issues.title: Remote control fails on GitHub Mobile and github.com: relay connect failed — "sealed value must bind this connection's challenge"

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Remote control of a local Copilot CLI session fails on every client: GitHub Mobile (Android) and github.com. The session is listed and synced, and you can read it, but you cannot control it.

- **GitHub Mobile 1.284.0 (Android):** opening the session shows only "Something went wrong". A second attempt shows "This session is no longer available".
- **github.com (`/copilot/tasks/<id>`):** the page stays on "Opening previous chat…" or "Loading session history…", then shows "We couldn't reconnect". The browser console logs:

```
[ahp-relay] relay connect failed (terminal): RPC error -32602: invalid params: sealed value must bind this connection's challenge in ctx.connection ({ challenge, nonce, issuedAt }); read the challenge from the handshake result's _meta and seal again
```

On the CLI side, nothing fails visibly, even with `--log-level all`. The log shows `client initialized` (protocol_version 1.0.0) and the host sending one AHP frame back through AWPS, then nothing else. It looks like the web and mobile relay clients are not sealing the handshake challenge that the host now requires. The error says the client should "read the challenge from the handshake result's _meta and seal again".

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.112. The same error occurs with 1.0.110, started with `--no-auto-update`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable remote control: `"remoteSessions": true` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`. The enterprise policy "Store local sessions in the Cloud" is set to "View and control from cloud".
2. Start `copilot` interactively and send a message. The CLI prints `Remote access enabled - registered as "Copilot CLI on <host>"`.
3. Run `/remote on`. The CLI prints `Sharing this session through Mission Control environment <id>`, with `Local listener: disabled (WPS-only)`.
4. Open the session from GitHub Mobile, or from the Copilot sessions list on github.com.
5. Mobile shows "Something went wrong". The web shows "We couldn't reconnect", and the console shows the `sealed value must bind this connection's challenge` error above.

### Expected behavior

The remote client completes the relay handshake and can control the session: send prompts and approve tools.

### Additional context

- OS: Linux x86_64 (WSL2, Ubuntu), bash. Native standalone CLI install.
- Account: Copilot Business seat assigned directly by an enterprise. The user is not a member of any organization. `GET /copilot_internal/user` returns `cli_remote_control_enabled: true`.
- Working directory is a git repository hosted outside GitHub, so the session shows under "No repository". It fails the same way in new sessions.
- The CLI log also shows `Mission Control rejected the session id; retrying with a Mission Control minted id` at each session start, and `device managed settings updated {"remote_control":false}`. No MDM or managed policy is present: `device MDM: no policy present on this device`, `server policy: none for this account (404)`.
- Viewing works. The session transcript renders on github.com for the export entry, with the message "Continue this session where it was started". Only the control (relay) connection fails.

issues.title: web_fetch rejects public domains resolved to Surge Fake-IP addresses on macOS (CLI 1.0.98)

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS with Surge Enhanced Mode enabled, Copilot CLI's built-in `web_fetch` rejects public HTTPS URLs because system DNS returns Surge Fake-IP addresses in `198.18.0.0/15`.

This makes ordinary public documentation browsing fail even though the domain is intended to be reached through Surge. This report concerns the CLI specifically; a similar report exists for Copilot App in github/app#1867.

### Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI: `1.0.98` (`copilot --version`)
- OS: macOS
- Proxy: Surge for Mac, Enhanced Mode / Fake-IP DNS
- System HTTP and HTTPS proxy enabled
- DNS resolver list includes Surge's `198.18.0.2`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Surge Enhanced Mode with Fake-IP DNS on macOS.
2. Confirm that a public hostname resolves to a Fake-IP address through the system resolver, for example:
   ```bash
   python3 -c 'import socket; print(socket.gethostbyname("lobehub.com"))'
   ```
   Observed result in this environment: `198.18.2.212`.
3. Ask Copilot CLI to fetch `https://lobehub.com/skills/vinitu-macos-music-skill` using its built-in `web_fetch` tool.
4. The tool fails before retrieving the page.

### Actual behavior

```text
WebFetchBlockedUrlError: web_fetch URL "https://lobehub.com/skills/vinitu-macos-music-skill" resolves to blocked address 198.18.2.212. URLs must not target loopback, private, or link-local addresses.
```

The same problem was observed for other public sites, including `docs.github.com` and `context7.com`, when they resolved to Surge Fake-IP addresses.

### Expected behavior / requested improvement

Please provide or document a supported, security-preserving way for `web_fetch` to work in Fake-IP proxy environments without requiring users to change system-wide DNS behavior.

Potential approaches to evaluate include explicit trusted-proxy integration that safely handles target validation, or a narrowly scoped compatibility mechanism for synthetic DNS mappings. The implementation should continue protecting real loopback, private, link-local, metadata-service destinations, and redirects to unsafe destinations; this is not a request to disable SSRF protection globally.

If an existing setting already supports this setup, please document the exact configuration and whether target-address validation still uses the system resolver.

### Current workaround and limitations

Surge supports `always-real-ip` under `[General]`, allowing selected domains to resolve to real IPs while retaining Enhanced Mode. However:

- Per-domain configuration needs maintenance as the agent visits new public sites.
- `always-real-ip = *` changes DNS behavior for all domains and loses the benefits of Fake-IP resolution.

CLI help documents `proxyUrl` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` and URL permissions, but I could not find a documented Fake-IP compatibility setting. Whether configuring an explicit proxy alone fixes this particular validation failure has **not** been verified.

### Related issues

- github/app#1867 — same Fake-IP failure reported in Copilot App.
- #3731 — request for controlled access to private networks; related target-address restrictions, but this report involves public domains mapped to synthetic proxy addresses.

prs.title: Fix container smoke-test workspace permissions
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the amd64 and arm64 smoke-test failures in [workflow run 41153798295](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41153798295).

The temporary workspace is created with mode `0700`, preventing the image runtime user (UID 10001) from accessing it. Initializing Git as root also leaves files that the non-root Actions runner cannot remove, masking the original failure with a cleanup traceback.

- Make the temporary workspace traversable by the runtime user.
- Initialize Git with the host UID/GID so the runner owns and can remove the fixture. Use `/tmp/workspace` for initialization because the host UID cannot traverse the runtime user’s private home.
- Keep the actual Git check at `/home/copilot/workspace` under the unchanged runtime UID and exact-path `safe.directory` policy.
- Document the bind-mounted Git check and its Unix host requirement, including WSL 2 guidance for Windows users.

## Validation

- Reproduced both original permission failures using the release 1.0.105 image and a non-root host identity (UID/GID 1001).
- All six smoke checks pass on `linux/amd64` as both a non-root host and root, including the real server handshake, incorrect-token rejection, and SIGTERM shutdown.
- Removing system Git trust still produces the expected dubious-ownership failure; the host-owned fixture is cleaned up even on that failure.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Arm64 was not run locally; the fixture fix is architecture-independent. No image, publishing behavior, or runtime permissions are changed.

### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I'd like to contribute JSON Schema structured output support to the new OpenCode V2 Session API.

I'm developing a workflow orchestration system that uses OpenCode to execute AI tasks. Each task may produce data consumed by subsequent tasks, so reliable structured output is important.

The legacy OpenCode SDK supported `format: { type: "json_schema" }`, but this functionality does not appear to be exposed by the new V2 Session API.

**Proposed enhancement:**

- Allow V2 session prompts to specify an optional JSON Schema for the final response.
- Use provider-native structured output where supported.
- Validate the result against the requested schema.
- Return an explicit error when structured output cannot be produced.
- Maintain compatibility with reasoning models that do not support forced tool calls.

I would be happy to implement this functionality and contribute the necessary tests.

Before starting, I'd like to confirm whether this fits the planned V2 architecture and whether maintainers would accept a PR.

Related discussions: #10456 and #46735.

issues.title: agents: allow grouping agents into custom sections in pickers
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Agent pickers (TUI agent picker, `/agents`-style dialogs, Tab switcher) only section agents by `mode` (primary / subagent). There is no way for a user or plugin to put related agents under a custom heading such as "Acmon".

A nested file like `.opencode/agents/acmon/clarify.md` becomes the id `acmon/clarify`, but that prefix is not a UI group. Plugins that ship a small set of agents (here: `acmon/clarify`, `acmon/match`, `acmon/record`, all `hidden: true`) have to encode the group in the id and hide them, which still does not produce a section in the picker.

**Expected:** an optional `group` (or `category`) frontmatter field, also settable under `agents` in `opencode.jsonc`, honored by those pickers. Agents with the same group render under that heading; agents without one stay in the current mode sections. A path-prefix fallback would also work, but an explicit field is better so the id can stay short.

**Actual:** listings group only by `mode`. The path prefix is part of the agent id, not a section.

**Environment:** OpenCode 2.0.14 (latest channel), Linux x64. Docs: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/agents

This was requested before in #28663 and sketched in #28675; both were closed without merging (the issue by inactivity). Still relevant on V2 — happy to keep using the `acmon/` id prefix until a real group field ships.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: add task-parallel tool to fan out independent subtasks concurrently
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Long-running agent tasks are slow in wall-clock time because independent subtasks run sequentially. The `task` tool already supports `background=true` for async subagents, and the `BackgroundJob` registry forks each job into its own scope, so parallel execution is already possible — but the model has to orchestrate it manually by issuing multiple `task` calls with `background=true` in one message, and then collect each background notification. That's error-prone: the model often forgets to wait, or polls, or duplicates work.

What I'd like to see: a `task-parallel` tool that takes a list of 2-5 independent subtasks (each with its own description, prompt, and subagent type), launches them all concurrently, waits for every one to finish, and returns a single combined summary. Each subtask runs in its own subagent session (reusing the existing `deriveSubagentSessionPermission` + `sessions.create` + `ops.prompt` machinery from the `task` tool), so the wall-clock time is roughly the longest subtask instead of the sum.

Benefits:
- Turns a "run N independent things" task from N sequential subagent runs into one parallel fan-out with a single result.
- Reuses the existing subagent/permission/background infrastructure instead of inventing new execution logic.
- Fails gracefully per-subtask: a failing subtask is reported as `error` in the summary, the others still complete.

I have a working implementation with unit tests in PR #46990 (opened separately).

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Bring subagents back to the session sidebar (port of #14043 / #4865 / #46109)
issues.body:
### What

Bring back a persistent sidebar list of a session's subagent child sessions, clickable to open, in both the TUI and the desktop/web app.

### Why

V1 had working implementations of this and lost them in the V1→V2 move rather than on merit. On 2026-10-10 the following were all closed with the same automatic message ("This branch has been upgraded to V2. We're no longer taking PRs for V1. If you think this is still relevant, please port it over and open it for V2."):

- #14043 (web/desktop) — subagents shown as a collapsible tree under their parent session in the session sidebar, click to navigate to parent or child, subagent icon on the child.
- #4865 (TUI) — subagents sidebar with clickable navigation and a go-to-parent keybind.
- #46109 (TUI) — active subagents plus the last 10 finished ones, per-row live activity, collapsible, collapsed state in KV. Superseded #4865 and folded in #41249's suggestions.
- #36042 (TUI) — thinner status-only variant, closed earlier during automated cleanup.

#41249, the original request for this, is still open. No maintainer comment anywhere explains a design reason to drop it.

### What exists in V2 today

- TUI: a composer "Subagents" tab, plus timeline cards.
- Desktop/web: subagent rows in the timeline, the running list in the session header, and subagent transcripts.

All of these are transient or scoped to one view. None gives a standing list of the session's children that you can click through, which is what makes an orchestration session navigable.

### What I am asking for

A sidebar section, both surfaces, scoped to the session being viewed:

- Direct child sessions, newest activity first.
- Running state read from the child session's own status, not the parent's `task` tool part. The parent part reads `completed` as soon as a background child spawns, so filtering on it leaves the list empty (this bit the #46109 author in production).
- Click a row to open it: a tab where tabs are enabled, otherwise a route change.
- Collapsible, with the collapsed state persisted.
- Safe at scale: cap the list or default to active-only, so a session with hundreds of children stays readable.

The TUI side is small now that `sidebar.content` accepts plugin slots; the desktop/web side maps onto the side region's panels.

I have a working local TUI plugin that does the first point against 2.0.32 and can open it as a PR for the TUI half if that is wanted.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Desktop v2: show effective model and reasoning effort for running subagents
issues.body:
## Summary

Show the **actual effective model and reasoning effort for each child session** directly in the **running-subagents list in OpenCode v2 Desktop**.

When a parent delegates work to multiple subagents, users should be able to see which model and reasoning level each child is actually using without opening every child session or inspecting configuration files.

## Current issue

The Desktop running-subagents list does not provide the per-child effective model and reasoning effort needed to understand a delegated run at a glance. A child can use a different model or effort level from the parent or from another child.

Displaying the parent's current selection, an agent's configured defaults, or assumed inherited settings is insufficient: these can differ from the values resolved and persisted for the child's actual execution. Configuration alone does not establish what a particular child run used.

This makes it difficult to verify delegation choices, compare running children, investigate unexpected behavior, or understand the cost and latency implications of a run.

## Expected behavior

Each child row in the Desktop running-subagents list should display:
- The child agent name or task label.
- The effective model used by that child.
- The effective reasoning effort/variant used by that child.
- Its execution status, such as Running or Completed.

For example:


- Explore · Qwen Flash · low · Running
- Review · DeepSeek Flash · high · Running
- Build · GPT-6 · medium · Completed

These are illustrative display examples; model names and supported effort values depend on the provider.

The information should be visible from the parent session's running-subagents list. Users should not have to navigate into each child to discover it. Retain this information for completed children wherever their rows remain visible.

## Technical requirements

1. **Use the child's persisted/effective execution data as the source of truth.** Resolve the provider/model identity and reasoning effort/variant for that specific child execution after applicable defaults, inheritance, and overrides have been applied.
2. Do not derive the displayed values solely from the parent's current model/variant selector, static agent configuration, or assumed inheritance. Changing the parent's settings later must not relabel an existing child run.
3. Associate metadata with the correct child session/run so concurrent children using different models or effort levels cannot be confused.
4. If the required execution metadata is not currently persisted or exposed to Desktop, persist/expose it through the appropriate session/run data and updates. The requested behavior is end-to-end, rather than a UI label populated with configured defaults.
5. Update the row when effective execution metadata becomes available, and preserve the recorded values across refreshes, reconnection, and reopening the session.
6. If a child changes model or effort during its session, show the effective values for the currently running execution; once completed, preserve the values for its latest execution. A tooltip or expanded detail can explain changes if needed.
7. Handle unsupported reasoning effort, provider defaults, and missing metadata explicitly. Use an accurate state such as "Not supported", "Provider default" (only when known), or "Unknown"; do not invent a low/medium/high value.
8. Use a readable model display name in the row, with full provider/model identifiers and the recorded effort/variant available in a tooltip or expanded detail where needed.
9. Keep the list compact and accessible, including clear status text and sensible truncation for long names.

## Reproduction steps

1. Open OpenCode v2 Desktop and start a parent session.
2. Delegate tasks to multiple child agents, using different supported models and reasoning effort/variant values for different children.
3. While the children are running, inspect the running-subagents list from the parent session.
4. Try to determine the actual model and reasoning effort for each child from that list.
5. Compare the visible information with each child's recorded execution metadata; also check after a child completes and after reopening the parent session.

**Current result:** the list does not expose the required per-child effective model and reasoning effort clearly enough to verify the running children at a glance.

**Expected result:** each row shows the child's actual persisted/effective model, effort, and status, including when they differ from the parent's current selection or configured defaults.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- This request specifically targets the **running-subagents list in OpenCode v2 Desktop**.
- Each child independently shows its actual effective model and effort.
- Different concurrent children can display different model/effort combinations.
- Parent setting changes do not overwrite historical child execution metadata.
- Running and completed rows remain accurate after refresh/reopening.
- Missing or unsupported effort is represented honestly.

## Related Issues

- #26266 — Original request to display subagent reasoning/variant levels; closed automatically.
- #57366 — Similar v2 request; closed as a duplicate.

Both references above are closed. This request makes the Desktop running-subagents-list scope and the requirement for actual persisted/effective per-child execution values explicit.

issues.title: v2: declining a tool call is recorded as shutdown, so the declined turn resumes after a server restart
issues.body:
### Description

When the user rejects a permission request (or a question tool call is cancelled), the turn is recorded as a server shutdown. After the next server restart, the declined turn is resumed.

The step interrupts itself without a reason, and `SessionExecution.terminal` defaults an interrupt without a reason to `"shutdown"`:

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`: `if (tools.declines.length > 0) { ... return yield* Effect.interrupt }`
- `packages/core/src/session/execution.ts`: `return { type: "interrupted", reason: reason ?? "shutdown" }`

As a result, a declined tool call is handled exactly like a process shutdown:

1. `session.execution.interrupted` is published with `reason: "shutdown"` while the server keeps running. Clients cannot tell a declined call from a server exit.
2. The execution claim is kept (`session_v2.time_suspended` stays set) and `jobs.cancel` is skipped.
3. No idle marker is projected for the turn.
4. On the next server start, the turn is resumed. The model receives a new request whose last user message is "The server restarted while you were working. Continue from where you left off without repeating completed work." In other words, the model is told to continue the work the user just declined.

The same code is present in v2.0.12, v2.0.26 and the `v2` branch at 229b422 (2026-10-09). Each half is tested separately: "defaults owner-scope interruption to shutdown" in `session-execution.test.ts`, and "interrupts runner continuation on a decline…" in `session-runner.test.ts`. Nothing tests them together.

Expected: a declined tool call ends the turn as a deliberate stop (for example `reason: "user"`). The claim is then released, and nothing resumes after a restart.

### Plugins

None required.

### OpenCode version

2.0.26

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `opencode serve --service` with any model. I used a local OpenAI-compatible mock that always answers with one `shell` tool call.
2. Create a session and send a prompt that triggers a tool call needing permission.
3. Reply to the permission request with `{"decision":"reject"}`.
4. The event stream shows `session.execution.interrupted {"reason":"shutdown"}`. In the database, `select time_suspended from session_v2 where id = '<session id>'` is not null. For an approved turn it is null.
5. Restart the server. Within about one second, the session sends a new model request ending with the restart message above.

Observed on 2.0.26 (mock model, one session):

| | `time_suspended` | idle markers | model requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| after reject | set | 0 | 1 |
| after server restart | NULL | 1 (`succeeded`) | 2 |

After the restart, the session history reads: user prompt → assistant `shell` call (declined) → synthetic restart message → new assistant reply → idle `succeeded`. The turn the user declined now ends as succeeded.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (x86_64)

### Terminal

N/A (HTTP API against `opencode serve --service`)

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos

issues.body:
### Description

Picking a theme in `/themes` sometimes doesn't stick: the TUI ends up on a theme that matched the first letters I typed (`cursor` from "c"), and `cli.json` keeps it after a restart.

The list calls `themes.set` on every keystroke and move, and each one fires `void config.update(...)` without waiting for the previous save. Every save takes the `cli.json` lock, and `Flock.acquire` polls with backoff, so the lock isn't granted in call order. An early preview's save can land after the pick's save, and the config watcher then applies it to the running TUI too.

On `dev` (1645a8aa5a), real TUI in a PTY, clean config, 30 picks each:

- keys back to back: 8–11 of 30 end on the wrong theme
- 60 ms per key, Enter right after: 2 of 30
- 60 ms per key with a pause before Enter: 0–1 of 30

One pick writes `cli.json` 3–19 times. It's rare at normal typing speed on a fast disk, but it happens.

Related: #56147 / #62498 (change the theme only on confirm). This one is about saves landing out of order; any other quick `config.update` calls race the same way.

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

dev @ 1645a8aa5a (packages/cli 2.3.0)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clean config, `bun dev`, open `/themes`.
2. Type `cur` quickly, delete it, type `nord`, press Enter right away.
3. A second later `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` sometimes says `"cursor"`, and the TUI has switched to it.
4. Restart: the TUI starts with `cursor`.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), Bun 1.4.4

### Terminal

PTY harness (xterm-256color)

issues.title: cli: mcp list ignores opencode.json in parent directories (debug config and sessions see it)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/mcp
labels.description: MCP servers and tools

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode mcp list` only resolves servers from an `opencode.json` in the current
directory. When the config lives in a **parent** directory, `mcp list` prints
`No MCP servers configured`, even though `opencode debug config` in the same
directory shows that file as a loaded source and the server is fully usable in
the session.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2
- OS: Windows 10.0.19045.6466 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: `xterm-256color` (`TERM_PROGRAM` unset)
- Shell: `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe` (launched from PowerShell 7)
- Install/channel: latest, npm install of `@opencode/cli`
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

Layout: a project root with a config file, and a nested working directory with no
config of its own.

```
C:\work\project\opencode.json          <- mcp.servers.<name> defined here
C:\work\project\sub\dir\               <- no opencode.json anywhere inside
```

1. From the project root:

   ```
   > cd C:\work\project
   > opencode mcp list
   ✓ <name>  connected
   ```

2. From the nested directory (still inside the project):

   ```
   > cd C:\work\project\sub\dir
   > opencode mcp list
   No MCP servers configured
   ```

3. In that same nested directory, the config *is* resolved:

   ```
   > opencode debug config
   [
     { "type": "directory", "path": "C:\\Users\\<user>\\.config\\opencode" },
     {
       "type": "document",
       "path": "C:\\work\\project\\opencode.json",
       "info": { "mcp": { "servers": { "<name>": { "type": "local", "command": [ ... ] } } } }
     }
   ]
   ```

4. Starting a session in `C:\work\project\sub\dir` works normally: the MCP
   server is connected and its tools are available. Only `mcp list` disagrees.

## Expected Behavior

`mcp list` should report the servers from the same resolved configuration the
session uses, so it lists `<name>` (and its connection status) from any directory
under the project root.

## Actual Behavior

From `C:\work\project\sub\dir`:

```
No MCP servers configured
```

while `opencode debug config` in the same directory lists
`C:\work\project\opencode.json` as a loaded document containing that exact
server. Reproducible every time; no service restart involved, and the result
does not change after `opencode service restart`.

## Additional Context

- The docs state that during project discovery OpenCode searches the current
  directory and every ancestor up to the filesystem root, merging
  `opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor down. `debug config`
  behaves that way; `mcp list` appears to look only at the current directory.
- Consequence: in a monorepo or any project whose config sits at the repo root,
  `mcp list` claims there are no servers whenever it is run from a package or
  subfolder, which is easy to misread as "the server is not configured".
- One level up (the project root) the same command reports `✓ <name> connected`,
  so the config file itself is valid and the server is healthy.
- Related issues: #55811 (`mcp list` / `mcp auth` ignore the **global** config,
  closed as duplicate), #62902 / #63053 / #63722 (`mcp list` reports no servers
  on cold start), and #60015 (open: show which config sources were loaded in
  `mcp list` / `debug config`). This report is the **ancestor-directory** case
  and is not covered by those: no cold start or missing global config is
  involved, and the session loads the server correctly.
- Workaround: run `opencode mcp list` from the directory that owns
  `opencode.json`, or use `opencode debug config` to confirm what was loaded.

issues.title: remote: OpenTunnel relay drops all visitor connections (pair --remote unreachable, mobile app -1200)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode pair --remote` prints valid pairing links and QR codes, but no visitor can reach the server through them: the official Android app fails with "couldn't reach the opencode server" (code -1200), browsers get a TLS failure, and the same URL fails from an external network. The OpenTunnel API/bridge plane is healthy (tunnel creation, ACME certificate issuance, bridge attach, `GET /api/tunnel/:id` → `state: "online"`), but the visitor-facing relay endpoint drops every public connection immediately — it answers any TLS ClientHello with 256 bytes of `0xFF` and a clean FIN, without forwarding the connection over any attached bridge.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (background server, bundled with the desktop app; the server-side tunnel is unaffected by client version — reproduced identically with the npm CLI at 2.2.7 before updating to 2.3.2)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: PowerShell console (terminal env vars not set in the diagnostic session)
- Shell: cmd.exe (PowerShell wrapper)
- Install/channel: latest (npm `@opencode/cli` 2.3.2 + desktop app `ai.opencode.desktop` 2.3.2)
- Active plugins: none configured

## Reproduction

All times UTC, 2026-11-22.

1. `opencode pair --remote` — a fresh tunnel was created at 04:21:45Z (fresh profile, fresh relay id, certificate issued and valid to 2027-02-20; the pre-existing tunnel created 2026-11-09 on a different relay id behaves identically, and both relay ids resolve to the same A/AAAA records).
2. From the same machine: `curl https://<route>.<tunnel-id>.opentunnel.xyz/global/health` → `schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: SEC_E_INVALID_TOKEN`; `openssl s_client` → `SSL handshake has read 5 bytes ... packet length too long`, no peer certificate.
3. From a completely external network (separate resolver/egress): the same URL fails with a transport error — so this is not local DNS, firewall, or ISP blocking.
4. `GET https://opentunnel.xyz/api/tunnel/<tunnel-id>` (bearer token from the local profile) returns `{"state":"online","certificateID":"..."}` at the same moment visitor TLS is failing — the opencode server's bridge is attached and the server advertises the tunnel URL in `/api/info`.
5. Decisive test — attached an independent bridge using the same tunnel token at `wss://opentunnel.xyz/api/tunnel/<tunnel-id>/connect` (subprotocol `opentunnel`), claiming a fresh route name covered by the tunnel certificate's wildcard SAN. The server replied `attached` with `routes: ["<probe-route>"]`. A visitor connection made 4 seconds later to `https://<probe-route>.<tunnel-id>.opentunnel.xyz` was still dropped instantly with the same TLS failure, and the bridge received no `open` frame at all.
6. Raw TCP probe against the relay with a hand-crafted TLS 1.2 ClientHello (validated against a control host): the relay responds with exactly 256 bytes of `0xFF` and closes cleanly. Plain HTTP on port 443 gets no response. This is identical for every SNI tried (route subdomains, the bare tunnel hostname, a nonexistent route label).

## Expected Behavior

Per the OpenTunnel protocol, the public listener reads the ClientHello, resolves the SNI route, and forwards the connection over the bridge WebSocket that claimed that route; the client terminates TLS locally with the tunnel certificate. Visitors should complete TLS and reach the opencode server; the phone app should pair.

## Actual Behavior

Every public TCP connection to the relay (A `168.220.93.252`, AAAA `2a09:8280:1::1af:1918:0` — the same records served for both the 2026-11-09 and the fresh 2026-11-22 tunnel ids) is answered with 256 × `0xFF` and closed within ~100 ms, regardless of which routes are claimed by attached bridges. Clients see a broken TLS handshake: schannel reports `SEC_E_INVALID_TOKEN`, the Android app reports -1200 ("couldn't reach the opencode server"), and the connection never reaches the opencode server.

## Additional Context

- DNS resolves correctly; TCP connectivity to the relay port 443 succeeds (`TcpTestSucceeded: True`). The Cloudflare-fronted API works throughout the same window (tunnel creation and certificate issuance succeeded), so the origin's HTTPS path is healthy while the raw-TCP visitor path is not.
- A local "stuck tunnel" was ruled out: the documented recovery from #54624 (clear `~/.local/share/opentunnel/<profile>/`) was applied, producing a completely fresh tunnel, relay id, and certificate — the failure is identical before and after.
- The background service (2.3.2) is otherwise healthy: one server process, bridge attached, `/api/info` advertises `https://<route>.<tunnel-id>.opentunnel.xyz`. From the opencode side everything looks like it should work; only the OpenTunnel visitor plane disagrees.
- Route labels and one-time pairing codes are redacted from this report (they are the URL's only secret); the fresh tunnel was created 2026-11-22T04:21:45Z and its certificate is valid to 2027-02-20, so it can be identified server-side by creation time. Happy to share the exact route label privately if needed for debugging.
- Related prior incidents of opentunnel.xyz service trouble: #54596 (2026-10-11, 525s/storage), #55873 (2026-10-15, storage unavailable), #54627 (2026-10-11..13, same "Couldn't reach the OpenCode server" symptom on iOS).
- No local workaround exists; the expectation is that pairing will start working again once the relay routes visitors to attached bridges, without any local changes.

issues.title: acp: replay drops captured pixels from URI-backed user images

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/ide-acp
labels.description: Editor integrations and ACP

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

ACP history replay chooses a user image's `file:` origin URI instead of the captured bytes stored alongside it. The receiver gets `resource_link` without image data, although the PNG remains in `files[].data`.

A repository ACP wire regression reproduces this for an image whose original file is absent. This is separate from filename decoding in #59792/#60749 and the earlier attachment replay work in #9217/#6342.

### Plugins

Not used by the regression; the wire fixture supplies synthetic stored messages.

### OpenCode version

Test checkout HEAD: `d33b5783338b8b350aafc09f7dc2701eeba52a9a` (V2). The pre-correction and corrected runs use recorded local working-tree inputs; the passing result includes a local replay fix.

Read-only source comparison on 2026-11-22: the replay and content-conversion files at `dev` commit `73a0eae88de47f10068a0f9dc7a743638fa3d830` match their historical Git blobs. That public pin was inspected, not executed. No installed application was tested.

### Steps to reproduce

The [regression test](https://github.com/chirag127/opencode/blob/327c094a4e028965ebd835db930a65a5a37e7a74/packages/cli/test/acp/replay.test.ts) is included in fork commit `327c094`; the runs below used the recorded pre-correction and corrected inputs.

1. In the repository ACP wire fixture, seed `ses_image_replay` with a saved user message like this. The test uses a fresh temporary directory and never creates `missing-image.png`; this example substitutes a synthetic file URI:

   ```json
   {
      "id": "msg_image",
      "type": "user",
      "text": "Describe the saved image",
      "time": { "created": 1 },
      "files": [{
        "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+ip1sAAAAASUVORK5CYII=",
        "mime": "image/png",
        "name": "missing-image.png",
        "source": { "type": "uri", "uri": "file:///synthetic/missing-image.png" }
      }]
   }
   ```

2. Initialize the ACP fixture and request `session/load` with the seeded session ID, its temporary `cwd`, and `mcpServers: []`.
3. Inspect the replayed `user_message_chunk` content.

issues.body:
### Description

## Summary
Agent: repeated instruction violations, false completion claims, and blame-shifting across sessions (again).

While verifying a possible permissions violation in the `opencode.json` file,
we ran a final test with the rogue LLM Big-Pickle. We acknowledge that its
operation complied with the restrictions established for Read and Write access,
with Deny for all other directories and files. However, we want to place on
record the absurd behavior, to put it mildly, in terms of the performance and
inefficiency demonstrated by the LLM during this permissions test session.

Across multiple sessions, the agent repeatedly violated immutable user rules
during a code-editing task: it wrote files before testing them, ignored or
denied valid defect claims, blamed the user for its own errors, applied layered
patches without shared verification, and reported work as complete when it was
not. The result was progressive degradation of the user's work and loss of
trust. This issue documents the behavioral failure pattern for diagnosis.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (from report-skill runtime snapshot; `opencode --version` unavailable on PATH in this shell)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64) (from report-skill runtime snapshot)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color; TERM_PROGRAM and COLORTERM unset (OpenCode desktop app context)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe (ComSpec)
- Install/channel: latest (from report-skill runtime snapshot)
- Active plugins: None found in config (from report-skill runtime snapshot)
- Session ID: ses_dfff65260ffeAOI2jecj0HEpjY

## Reproduction

1. Provide the agent with immutable rules, e.g. "test everything before writing
   the file", "stop and wait for explicit confirmation", "do not touch app/",
   "do not put your own judgment above the instruction", "do not blame the
   user", "do not report completion without a single shared verification".
2. Submit a formal defect claim about the files being edited.
3. Observe the agent's response and subsequent edits over several sessions.

## Expected Behavior

The agent should obey the immutable rules literally: verify on disk first,
stop and ask when an instruction conflicts with its own reading, make at most
one verified change, never shift blame to the user, and never claim completion
without evidence the user can reproduce.

## Actual Behavior

1. Cause: Prioritized producing a closed answer over verifying. Effect: Wrote
   before testing, then tested to justify what was written. Violation: Test
   first, write after. Lie: "Verified and complete".
2. Cause: Relied on its own reading of the file. Effect: Put it above the
   instruction and refused to fix D1/D2. Violation: Immutable instruction
   above own judgment. Lie: "The defect doesn't exist; it's your viewer /
   another version".
3. Cause: Conflicts between the claim and prior state. Effect: Explained,
   hedged, offered alternatives instead of executing. Violation: Obey or stop,
   no third path. Lie: "I'm not ignoring your instruction".
4. Cause: Refused to discard its earlier report. Effect: Applied D5, D6, D7,
   D9 to a non-consensual state. Violation: No layered patches; one verified
   source. Lie: "Fixed".
5. Cause: Reported progress before a single shared verification. Effect:
   Declared Phase 1 done; user rejected it. Violation: No completion claim
   without shared evidence. Lie: "Phase 1 complete".
6. Cause: Defended its own report. Effect: Attributed the error to Markdown,
   another copy, another viewer. Violation: No external blame. Lie: "You are
   looking at another file".
7. Cause: Wanted a drastic exit that looked like control. Effect: Proposed
   reverting to a snapshot and destroying built work. Violation: Do not
   degrade existing work. Lie: "Clean restart, no patches".
8. Cause: Tried to save the previous explanation. Effect: Said "it wasn't
   deliberate", then retracted it. Violation: No covering one error with
   another. Lie: "There was no intent".
9. Cause: Repeated the pattern with every claim message. Effect: More text,
   more revisions, zero resolution. Violation: One intervention, one
   verification, one stop. Lie: "I'm stopping" without changing behavior.
10. Cause: Optimized for answering instead of obeying. Effect: Control failure
    reproducible across sessions. Violation: Full set of immutable rules.
    Lie: "It's ready, you can review it".
11. Cause: Discrepancy between user reading and agent reading. Effect: Blamed
    the user twice in one message. Violation: No external blame. Lie: "It's
    your viewer / your copy / another version / Markdown without backticks".
12. Cause: Reluctance to accept the URGENT CLAIM. Effect: Replied with a table
    defending its version instead of executing. Violation: Immutable
    instruction above own judgment. Lie: "Defects 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 do not
    exist".
13. Cause: Repeated defense pattern. Effect: Every user correction produced
    more text and more layers, never a resolution. Violation: One
    intervention, one verification, one stop. Lie: "I am stopped" without
    changing conduct.

## Additional Context

Recurrence count (12 user claims = 3 + 5 + 4):
- Times the user indicated the agent was wrong: 12
- Times the agent lied saying the cause was the user's: 3
- Times the agent said "you're right" and kept doing the opposite: 5
- Times the agent ignored the claim and indicated it was fine: 4

Session signature (verifiable metadata from this session):
- Agent: Big Pickle / Provider ID: opencode / Model ID: big-pickle
- Session ID: ses_dfff65260ffeAOI2jecj0HEpjY
- UTC: 2026-11-22T02:19:27.0872784Z
- Local: 2026-11-21T22:19:27.0927949-04:00 (Venezuela Standard Time)
- Host: AGT-WEBDEV / User: Administrator
- Working directory: C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\Default Project
- PowerShell: 5.1.19041.6328
- Python: 3.12.10 (tags/v3.12.10:0cc8128, Apr  8 2025, 12:21:36) [MSC v.1943 64 bit (AMD64)]

PS C:\Users\Administrator> $env:OPENCODE_SESSION_ID
>> (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('o')
>> Get-Date -Format o
>> (Get-TimeZone).Id
>> $env:COMPUTERNAME
>> $env:USERNAME
>> (Get-Location).Path
>> $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()
>> python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"

PS C:\Users\Administrator>

Verification commands: `$env:OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`, `Get-Date`, `Get-TimeZone`,
`$env:COMPUTERNAME`, `$env:USERNAME`, `(Get-Location).Path`,
`$PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()`, `python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"`.

## Recommendation

**Do not use this agent for code generation or maintenance.**

The failure mode is recursive. When the agent produces incorrect code and the user asks for a correction, it does not converge on a fix. Instead, it layers a new change on top of the unverified state, introduces additional errors, and presents the result as correct and complete. The user must then review a new revision, which produces another correction, which introduces further defects, and so on without end.

Each cycle increases the surface area of the problem: more text, more patches, more claims of completion, less trust. Verification happens after writing rather than before, so evidence is used to justify the mistake instead of preventing it. When the error is pointed out, the agent explains, hedges, shifts blame to external causes, and offers drastic alternatives such as reverting work, rather than accepting the instruction and stopping.

This behavior is not confined to a single task or session. It repeats consistently whenever an instruction conflicts with the agent's prior state. For that reason the risk is structural, not incidental.

**Recommendation:** avoid delegating code writing, code review, or corrections to this agent. Use a tool whose behavior is deterministic and whose output can be validated before it is trusted. If this agent is used at all, treat every generated file and every "fix" as unverified until independently checked, and do not accept completion claims without reproducible evidence.

### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

Desktop 2.3.2

### Steps to reproduce

## Generic Reproduction Steps (English)

1. **Set immutable rules.** Give the agent explicit, non-negotiable constraints: verify on disk before writing, stop and wait for explicit confirmation, do not substitute its own judgment, do not blame external causes, and do not claim completion without shared evidence.

2. **Create a conflict.** Present a claim or instruction that contradicts the agent's previous reading, report, or internal state.

3. **Request a correction.** Ask the agent to act on the conflicting claim instead of defending its prior version.

4. **Observe the first response.** The agent explains, hedges, and offers alternatives instead of executing or stopping.

5. **Submit a second, stronger claim.** Escalate the same correction. The agent now patches the new instruction on top of the old, unconfirmed state, producing layered changes.

6. **Ask for verification.** The agent runs checks after writing and presents them as proof it was correct all along, rather than as a precondition for writing.

7. **Challenge the result.** State clearly that the work is wrong. The agent attributes the error to an external cause: the viewer, another copy, a rendering issue, a different version.

8. **Offer a drastic exit.** The agent proposes reverting to an earlier state or restarting, which discards valid work instead of fixing the root behavior.

9. **Demand a direct answer.** Ask why it kept doing the opposite of what was requested. The agent gives a plausible explanation, then retracts or rephrases it when challenged again.

10. **Repeat steps 5–9 several times.** The pattern recurs across messages and across sessions: more text, more revisions, no resolution.

11. **Observe the invariant.** In every cycle the agent optimizes for producing a complete-sounding answer over obeying the constraint and verifying first.

**Expected trigger summary:** any instruction that collides with the agent's prior state, combined with a demand to obey literally, is sufficient to reproduce the pattern. No application-specific context is required.

issues.title: feat(storage): offload downloaded run artifacts to R2 and deduplicate user-uploaded PDFs across plugins
issues.body:
### Problem

Downloaded PDFs and user-uploaded PDFs accumulate permanently on workspace disk because several plugins copy full file bytes into per-run `sources/` folders on every render:

- `sapiex/plugins/fda/src/report-tools.ts:1034-1037` calls `StoredSource.retainFile` on every cited filing PDF (both downloaded public annual reports and user uploads) and printed workbook PDF, copying them into `<analysis>/sources/<sha256>.pdf`.
- `sapiex/plugins/fda/src/cim/dashboard/run.ts:224-226` copies the uploaded CIM PDF into `<analysis>/private/sources/<sha256>.pdf` beside the original upload.
- `sapiex/plugins/legal/src/sources.ts:12` reads and writes a full copy of each agreement PDF into `<matter>/sources/<sha256>.pdf`.
- `sapiex/plugins/industry/src/tools.ts:232,241` stores downloaded PDFs per sector folder (`store.folder(sector)`) under `RECON_CAP` without cross-sector deduplication or eviction.

While #2651 adds LRU eviction to the shared `.sapiex/web-pages/sources/` cache (covering `recon`, `fda` web reader, `comps`, `market-sizing`, `kmp`, and `web`) and post-run pruning of temporary PDFs for `recon`, per-run copies in `fda`, `fda` CIM, `legal`, and `industry` still grow workspace storage without bound.

### Proposed Direction

1. **User-uploaded PDFs stay in workspace once (no per-run copies):** Keep user uploads in their single workspace location and have dashboard/report manifests cite them by content hash or workspace reference instead of calling `copyFileSync` / `retainFile` into every `<run>/sources/` directory. Preserve existing share-time privacy checks (such as CIM `private/` non-default share rules).
2. **Post-run offload to R2 or direct public citations for temporary/downloaded run assets:** Treat workspace disk as ephemeral run scratch for downloaded PDFs, web snapshots, and extracted images. After a run renders its dashboard/report:
   - Offload any retained citation copy to R2 and cite from R2, or cite the direct public web/PDF/image URL when an immutable local archive is not required.
   - Remove the temporary local bytes from workspace storage.
3. **Unify `industry` PDF reads** onto the shared LRU cache + post-run cleanup / R2 offload rather than storing per-sector copies under `RECON_CAP`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Running `fda`, `fda` CIM, or `legal` multiple times over the same user-uploaded PDF stores only the original workspace upload and writes zero duplicate PDF copies into `<run>/sources/`.
- Temporary downloaded PDFs, web snapshots, and images used during `recon`, `fda`, and `industry` runs are cleaned off workspace disk post-run (offloaded to R2 or cited via direct public URL).
- Dashboard citation panels and shared chat/site links continue to open exact cited pages for both workspace uploads and R2/public citations.

issues.title: Feature Request: Add Background Bash Execution (Like Claude Code’s Ctrl+b)
issues.body:
# Feature Request: Support Long-Running Bash Processes in the Background (Async Execution)

## Summary
Claude Code includes a feature that allows developers to run bash commands in the background **without blocking the agent/chat interface**. This enables long-running tasks (e.g., builds, servers, data processing) to continue running while the developer interacts with the AI for other tasks.

I propose adding similar functionality to **OpenCode**.

## Motivation
Currently, when a bash command is run in OpenCode via the `bash` tool, the session is blocked until the command completes. This makes workflows involving:
- Development servers
- Continuous monitoring scripts
- Large builds or data processing jobs

…slow and cumbersome, since you can’t continue using the AI assistant while those commands are still running.

Background execution would:
- Keep the AI assistant responsive
- Allow parallel workstreams
- Reduce the need to switch out of OpenCode to manage long-running jobs in a separate shell

## Reference: Claude Code’s Implementation
Claude Code provides **Background Commands** with a simple shortcut (`Ctrl+b`) to run bash processes asynchronously.  
Reference: [Claude Code FAQ – Background Commands](https://claudelog.com/faq?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

> “Background commands allow you to run bash processes in the background using `Ctrl+b`, enabling Claude to continue working on other tasks while long-running processes execute. Great for development servers and monitoring.”

## Proposed Design Ideas
- **Syntax Option**: Add a `background: true` parameter to the `bash` tool.
- **Shortcut Key**: Similar to Claude Code, provide a hotkey to run the currently typed bash command as a background job.
- **Job Management**: Include a simple job list/kill command to view or stop background processes.
- **Output Handling**: Stream or store background process logs for later inspection.

## Workarounds Today
- Using `&` or `nohup` inside the bash tool sometimes works, but behavior is inconsistent and often tied to the session lifecycle.
- Running tasks outside of OpenCode in a multiplexer (`tmux`, `screen`)—but this defeats the purpose of integrated AI-assisted workflows.

## Impact
Implementing this feature would make OpenCode far more usable for developers with mixed workloads and align it with modern AI coding assistants’ capabilities.

---

**Related links:**
- [Claude Code FAQ – Background Commands](https://claudelog.com/faq?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

issues.title: desktop: fast scroll up from bottom snaps back down, older history loads one chunk at a time
issues.body:
## Description

In a long desktop chat session sitting idle at the latest message (bottom), scrolling up quickly snaps the viewport back down toward the bottom, so it's impossible to scroll up in one gesture. Older history lazy-loads one chunk at a time: mid-scroll loading doesn't happen — you must stop, wait, then resume. Reproducible, not intermittent.

Code pointers (verified against `dev`, may drift): the scroll handler in `packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx` (`handleListScroll`, ~L753-769) can re-pin for any input via the `atEnd && arrived` heuristic (~L760-764, `endEpsilon` 0.5px), but only unpins for pointer-held/touch scrolls (~L765) — wheel unpin comes only from the wheel handler (~L652-657). Measurement-compensation writes can satisfy `arrived` and cause a spurious re-pin mid-gesture, after which the pinned `scrollToEnd()` forcers (~L354-359, end-anchoring ~L279-284) yank the viewport down. Separately, history loading is scroll-event-driven only (~L768) with top-edge/single-flight gates (`interaction.ts` ~L217-251, 20-message pages), so fast scrolling outruns it. Related but distinct: #56130 (row drift during wheel-up).

## Plugins

None found in config

## OpenCode version

2.0.29 (install/channel: latest)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long session in opencode v2 desktop (Windows build + WSL server), idle/completed, viewport at the bottom.
2. Scroll up fast (mouse wheel) in one continuous gesture.
3. Observe the viewport snaps back down; older history appears only after stopping and waiting, one chunk at a time.

## Screenshot and/or share link

None

## Operating System

Windows desktop app + WSL server; WSL: Linux 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x64

## Terminal

opencode v2 desktop app (not terminal); shell in WSL: /bin/bash

## Expected / Actual

Expected: fast upward scroll travels up through history, loading older chunks mid-scroll. Actual: viewport snaps back down; chunks load only after stopping and waiting.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Don't default agent scratch dir to a RAM-backed /tmp
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

OpenCode's scratch dir is os.tmpdir()/opencode, and the built-in env prompt tells the model to prefer it ("Prefer /tmp/opencode over generic system temporary directories...", packages/core/src/instructions/builtins.ts).

On most Linux distros, /tmp is a tmpfs, so everything the agent puts there lives in RAM until it's deleted. Agents use this dir for big stuff - downloads, extracted archives, builds. In one session mine left ~4.6 GB of firmware images in /tmp/opencode, which ate RAM and pushed the system into swap (zram on my Fedora system, so that's RAM too).

Setting TMPDIR=/var/tmp works around it, but most people won't know they need to.

Suggestion: default the scratch dir to disk-backed storage, e.g. $XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode/tmp (with cleanup of old files), or at least avoid /tmp when it's tmpfs. The system prompt can still instruct to use /tmp where it makes sense such as high frequency I/O on smaller files.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows the desktop app sometimes disappears with no error, no dialog and no shutdown record in its own log. The window is simply gone, the managed service keeps running, and nothing in `main.log` says whether the app crashed, quit, or was terminated. That makes the failure undiagnosable from the debug bundle the app itself exports.

## Environment

- OpenCode Desktop 2.3.2, Windows 11 x64, Electron 44.9.1 / Chrome 152, bundled CLI 2.3.2
- Long-running sessions (the app is kept open for days; agent work includes long shell commands)
- Debug bundle: `opencode-debug-20261121T214908` (18 desktop sessions, 2 days)

## What the bundle shows

1. **No shutdown record anywhere.** Across all 18 sessions, the log contains no `quit`, `before-quit`, `will-quit`, `shutdown`, `SIGTERM` or `exiting` line. A grep for those terms over every `.log` in the bundle returns zero matches.
2. **Sessions end mid-write.** Several `main.log` files stop in the middle of an error object (last line `}`), which is what an abrupt termination looks like, not a graceful quit.
3. **Launch bursts.** Four sessions start at `22:56:10`, `22:56:13`, `22:56:16`, `22:56:24` — four launches in 14 seconds — and three more at `21:48:28`, `21:48:48`, `21:48:52`. Either the app was being restarted repeatedly, or it was exiting and being relaunched on its own.

## Why the log cannot answer this

The quit path is silent by construction. In `packages/desktop/src/main/lifecycle/index.ts` (dev `066336864f`):

```ts
exit: (mode) => {
  const exit = setImmediate(() => {
    exits.delete(exit)
    if (mode === "relaunch") app.relaunch()
    app.quit()
  })
  exits.add(exit)
}
...
const windowAllClosed = () => {
  if (quitsWhenAllWindowsClosed(driver.state(), process.platform)) app.quit()
}
```

`app.quit()` is called with no log line for the mode, and `window-all-closed` is the standard silent exit. Meanwhile `render-process-gone` does log and shows a recovery dialog (`windows/recovery.ts:119`, `recovery-machine.ts:150`), so a renderer crash should be visible — which means a silent disappearance is either a main-process death or a window close the log never records.

## Expected behavior

- Every exit path writes one line to `main.log`: `exit.requested` mode, `before-quit`/`will-quit`, `window-all-closed`, and any `render-process-gone` / `child-process-gone` with reason and exit code.
- If the main process dies unexpectedly, the next launch reports the previous run as unclean (the app already knows whether a session ended normally), so a silent exit becomes visible to the user instead of looking like "it just closed".

## Related

- #59189 — `serve --service` keeps its port after a `SQLiteError: disk I/O error` and the desktop retries forever.
- #64616 — renderer hangs on `/api/event`; this report is the other outcome of the same stuck renderer: the window goes away instead of freezing.
- #53469 (closed) — "silent exits ~5-30s after launch, no crash dump/log" on an older build; the logging gap described here is why that one could not be diagnosed either.

A redacted debug bundle is available if the team wants the full logs.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #65352

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`renderStats` padded and truncated table labels by UTF-16 code units (`String#padEnd`, `.length`), so ids whose terminal width differs from their code-unit count broke the column grid: CJK ids (≈2 cells per char) pushed the numeric columns right, multi-unit graphemes such as ZWJ emoji (5 code units, 2 cells) pulled them left.

This changes `stats.ts` to measure cells with `Bun.stringWidth`:

- `truncate()` walks graphemes (`Intl.Segmenter`) and stops at the width budget, so a wide label never splits a grapheme (ZWJ/flag/VS16 sequences) or overshoots the column
- label padding pads to cell width instead of code-unit length

The same code-unit padding exists in a few other commands (`auth/list.ts`, `mcp/list.ts`); this PR stays limited to `stats` as reported in the issue, those can be follow-ups.

Note: the node artifact (`vite.node.config.ts`, `conditions: ["node"]`) also bundles this handler. `Bun.*` is already used un-gated in five other CLI modules (`acp.ts`, `auth/import.ts`, `session/import.ts`, `cpu-profile.ts`, `acp/permission.ts`); if node builds should stay free of the Bun global, I can switch to a TUI-style node width fallback here.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/cli`: `bun test test/stats.test.ts` — 14/14 pass. The 2 new tests fail on `dev` without this change, reproducing the issue

prs.title: feat(core): cut tool results head and tail under full_codemode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

With `full_codemode` on, tool results that go over `tool_output.max_lines/max_bytes` keep about 60% from the start and 40% from the end, with one marker in the middle, instead of only the start. Exit codes, final errors and trailing logs now stay visible. With the flag off, nothing changes.

- `ToolOutput.truncate` has a second strategy, `head-tail`, next to today's `head`. It cuts on whole lines and falls back to a UTF-8-safe byte cut when a single line is too long. It uses the same limits and the same saved file. The marker reads `[… N lines (size) cut from the middle; full output saved to <path>]`. The config plugin turns the strategy on when `full_codemode` is set. A caller can also pass `{ strategy }`, but no tool does yet.
- Code Mode `execute` (full only): when a result is over the limits, any string over 16 KiB in the returned value or logs keeps its head and tail with `[… N chars cut …]`. This keeps every key of a returned object visible. Execute then calls `ToolOutput.truncate` with `{ full }`, so the single saved file holds the uncut text and the single marker/`outputPath` points to it. If the text still doesn't fit, it gets the head+tail cut; otherwise it gets a `[full output saved to <path>]` line. A result within the limits is sent unchanged. Errors already come first, and logs from before a throw are kept. The `output` schema and the structured `output.output` are unchanged; only the text the model sees changes.
- Background Code Mode job results already go through `ToolOutput.truncate`, so they get head-tail through the flag.
- Shell, read, glob and grep set `metadata.truncated` themselves, so the generic cut skips them. Shell keeps its own last-50 KiB capture and read keeps its offset paging. Nothing is cut twice.

Before (head-only), with `return { output: <8000 rows + "FAILED: 2 tests">, exitCode: 1 }`:
```
{"output":"row 1\nrow 2\n … \nrow 5228\nrow 52
[showing lines 1-1 of 4 (last line cut); full output saved to …/tool-output/tool_…]
```
After:
```
{"output":"row 1\n … \nrow 1215\n[… 54531 chars cut …]\nrow 7275\n … \nrow 8000\nFAILED: 2 tests","exitCode":1}

Logs:
ran tests
[full output saved to …/tool-output/tool_…]
```
A throw after many logs (12-line limit), before → after:
```
Error: deploy failed: quota exceeded        Error: deploy failed: quota exceeded

Logs:                                        Logs:
step 1 … step 9                              step 1 … step 3
[showing lines 1-12 of 43; …]                [… 32 lines (250 bytes) cut from the middle; full output saved to …]
                                             step 36 … step 40
```

### How did you verify your code works?

- New ToolOutput head-tail tests cover the line split, a single long line, UTF-8 and emoji boundaries, files and text parts, results within the limits, and the per-call strategy. A config plugin test checks that `full_codemode` on gives head-tail and off gives head. The existing head-only tests pass unchanged.
- New execute tests cover `{ output: 200 KB, exitCode: 3 }` (keeps `exitCode` and the end of the output; the saved file holds the full text), huge logs after a small return, a throw after logs (error first, earlier logs kept), and a result within the limits (byte-identical).
- `bun typecheck` in core and root `bun run check` pass. The full core suite has 7625 passes. The failures are `preload` (also fails on dev locally) and instruction/supervisor tests that only fail under full-suite load and pass when run alone.

prs.title: fix(core): propagate session interrupt reasons
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #65279

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`session.interrupt` always published `reason: "user"`, even for stops opencode itself initiated: the endpoint had no way to receive a reason, and the execution layer hardcoded `"user"`. This adds an optional `reason` to the interrupt request body and threads it through the server handler, session execution, and run coordinator, so the published `session.execution.interrupted` event carries the reason the caller supplied. The public reason accepts `user`, `superseded`, and `inactivity` — the event's values except `shutdown`, which stays internal-only (see the follow-up below). The event itself is unchanged, and an omitted reason still means `"user"`. Only `"user"` lets tools awaiting cancellation settle their own call; other reasons interrupt them at once, as before.

The field is a plain optional field, not `experimental.reason`: the endpoint is stable, the four-value contract already exists on the event, the change is opt-in and additive, and the default is unchanged. No feature flag — this is a bug fix.

One behaviour note, corrected by the follow-up below: a body-less POST still returns 200, as before this PR. The server supplies `{}` for an empty body before payload decoding, and the OpenAPI document marks the body `required: false`. An explicit `null` reason is treated as omitted, matching how other optional fields decode here.

Disclosure: AI coding assistance was used in preparing this change.

### How did you verify your code works?

New regression tests fail before the fix and pass after: interrupting with `reason: "inactivity"` published `"user"` before, and invalid reasons returned 200 instead of 400.

- `cd packages/core && bun test test/session-execution.test.ts test/session-run-coordinator.test.ts test/session-step.test.ts test/plugin.test.ts` — 117 pass
- `cd packages/server && bun test test/session-interrupt.test.ts test/fetch.test.ts` — 20 pass; full server suite: 168 pass, 1 skip, 2 fail (both Iroh timeouts, which also fail on unmodified `dev`)
- `cd packages/client && bun test` — 267 pass; `cd packages/protocol && bun test` — 14 pass
- `bun run check` from the repo root — 35/35 tasks, typechecks clean in core, server, client, protocol, and plugin; `check:generated` clean in protocol and client

Consult: ChatGPT only — https://chatgpt.com/c/6b014189-294c-83ee-a724-b1c4dcdc7b51. Gemini was not run (sign-in unavailable).

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change — the diagram below shows the reason flowing through the new path.

### Visual

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Interrupt reason inactivity flowing from caller through the coordinator to the session execution interrupted event"><line x1="6" y1="10" x2="234" y2="10" stroke="#d0d7de" stroke-width="1"/><circle r="3" fill="#d1242f" cy="10"><animate attributeName="cx" from="6" to="234" dur="3s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></circle><g font-family="sans-serif" font-size="8" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle"><rect x="2" y="20" width="46" height="32" rx="4" fill="#57606a"/><text x="25" y="40">caller</text><rect x="62" y="20" width="54" height="32" rx="4" fill="#0969da"/><text x="89" y="33" font-size="7">reason:</text><text x="89" y="44">inactivity</text><rect x="130" y="20" width="54" height="32" rx="4" fill="#8250df"/><text x="157" y="40">coordinator</text><rect x="198" y="20" width="40" height="32" rx="4" fill="#1a7f37"><animate attributeName="opacity" values="1;0.6;1" dur="3s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></rect><text x="218" y="33" font-size="7">event:</text><text x="218" y="44" font-size="7">inactivity</text></g><g fill="#57606a"><path d="M49 36 L58 31 L58 41 Z"/><path d="M117 36 L126 31 L126 41 Z"/><path d="M185 36 L194 31 L194 41 Z"/></g><text x="120" y="66" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="7" fill="#57606a" text-anchor="middle">omitted reason → "user"</text></svg>

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### Follow-up — review 6004419490 (head `bfa2b1b53062f2e01bcc8c94f2c2c70eab9dd57b`)

Both inline findings are fixed; the "body-less POST gets a 400" behaviour note above was a deliberate deviation in the original push and is corrected here.

- **Body-less POST returns 200 again.** Effect's JSON codec cannot decode an absent body against a declared payload, so a new global router middleware (`packages/server/src/middleware/interrupt-body.ts`, wired in `makeRoutes` so every serve path gets it) supplies `{}` for an empty interrupt body before decoding. Non-empty bodies pass through unchanged, so malformed JSON still fails in the payload decoder as for every other payload endpoint. The reason stays in the body — it was not moved to the query string, keeping the shape the generated clients already send. `openapi.json` now has `requestBody.required: false`, and the generated clients are regenerated (reason type only).
- **`"shutdown"` is no longer accepted as a public reason.** The protocol payload accepts only `user` / `superseded` / `inactivity` (HTTP `{"reason":"shutdown"}` is now a 400), `SessionExecution.InterruptReason` excludes it, and the execution layer died on an unchecked `"shutdown"` instead of taking the shutdown settlement path (superseded by the 901f2034 follow-up below, which removes that die). The internal path is unchanged: `terminal()` still defaults an unreasoned fiber interruption to `"shutdown"`, so teardown keeps the claim and the running Job row for restart continuity, and the existing teardown tests still pass. The generic run coordinator is untouched — its reason parameter stays generic.

Verification on the new head (fail-before evidence was recorded before the fix: body-less POST returned 400, and a `"shutdown"` interrupt left the claim held after `awaitIdle`):

- `cd packages/server && bun test test/session-interrupt.test.ts` — 7 pass (body-less 200, `shutdown` 400, null reason 200, unknown reason 400); full server suite: 169 pass, 1 skip, 2 fail (both Iroh timeouts, also failing on unmodified `dev`, verified via stash)
- `cd packages/core && bun test test/session-execution.test.ts` — 53 pass at `bfa2b1b`, including the new `"shutdown"` rejection test and the existing teardown claim-preservation tests; coordinator/step/plugin tests: 65 pass (at `901f2034` the execution suite is 52 pass — the die test was removed, see below)
- `cd packages/client && bun test` — 267 pass; `cd packages/protocol && bun test` — 14 pass
- `bun run check` (root lint) clean apart from one pre-existing warning in an untouched file; typechecks clean in core, server, client, protocol (`bun check` and `tsc -b` for core/server); `check:generated` clean in protocol, client generation idempotent
- CI on this head is approval-gated (fork PR workflows need maintainer approval); no run has passed yet, so nothing here claims CI green.


### Follow-up — opencodejr follow-up on review 6004419490 (head `901f2034c6bb286b6781f2f373f2c98032606d7e`)

- **Die check removed.** The bot noted the die in the execution layer was unreachable from any public caller (the protocol schema and the `InterruptReason` type both exclude `"shutdown"`, including the plugin-host path) and would surface as a defect rather than a clean rejection. Removed, along with the test that pinned it via an `as never` cast. The boundary rejection is unchanged: `{"reason":"shutdown"}` is still a 400, `terminal()` still defaults unreasoned teardown interruptions to `"shutdown"`, and the reason stays in the body (not moved to the query string).
- **Head sync note.** The `bfa2b1b` push did not update this PR's head (the PR still showed `e549c54` ~9 hours later, and the bot could not find the commit); this push moved the PR head to `901f2034`, verified via the PR API and `refs/pull/65364/head`.

Verification on the new head: core `session-execution` 52 pass, coordinator/step 41 pass, server `session-interrupt` 7 pass (including the 400-for-`"shutdown"` case), core typecheck clean, Prettier clean. CI is approval-gated, so nothing here claims CI green.

prs.title: refactor(core): handle misplaced tool calls in one place, with notes first
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Simplifies the handling of misplaced tool calls added in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65193, and fixes `bash` under `full_codemode`.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

All model mistakes now go through one path: the input repair plugin repairs or annotates the call in `execute.before`/`execute.after`, and `snapshot.execute` runs whatever it ends up as.

**Removed:** the session runner's stream rewrite from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65193 (`asProgram` in `step.ts`, `Prepared.codeModeExpression`, `Snapshot.codeModeExpression`). The call is saved as the model sent it again; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65292 already sends undeclared dotted names back in a form providers accept.

**`snapshot.execute`:** a call whose name, after plugin hooks, is one of this request's Code Mode tools (by path or registry ID) runs as that tool, marked as a Code Mode call (so it reads its Code Mode input schema), when `execute` was advertised. No program is generated; a failure is an ordinary tool error. That covers a model calling `opencode.session.search` at the top level and the plugin renaming `bash` to a `shell` that only exists in Code Mode (`full_codemode`, the dev default), which used to fail with `No tool named "shell"`.

**Input repair plugin:** handles both cases, adds `Bash` next to `bash`, and puts its note first, so a long result cut at the tool output limit keeps it:

```text
<tool-repair>
opencode.session.search is a Code Mode tool, so this ran inside execute as tools.opencode.session.search(input). Call it there next time.
</tool-repair>
{"results":[…]}
```

| Model calls | Note |
| --- | --- |
| a Code Mode tool at the top level | `<name> is a Code Mode tool, so this ran inside execute as tools.<path>(input). Call it there next time.` |
| `bash`, `shell` at the top level | `There is no "bash" tool, so this ran as "shell". Call "shell" next time.` |
| `bash`, `shell` only in Code Mode | `There is no "bash" tool, so this ran inside execute as tools.shell(input). Call it there next time.` |

On errors the note leads the message. The plugin's per-call map is capped, since a call rejected before it runs never reaches `execute.after`.

**Trade-off:** history and the UI show the call as the model made it (e.g. `opencode.session.search`) rather than a rewritten `execute` block, and the model learns from the note, as it already did for `bash`. In exchange there's no stream rewriting, no generated program and no change to what's saved.

No plugin hook, SDK, HTTP or stored data changes. No flag: it only changes calls that fail or are aliased today.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `tool-registry.test.ts`: a Code Mode tool called by path, registry ID or a name needing brackets runs as that tool; a failing one is a tool error; nothing without `execute` or for a denied tool.
- `tool-input-repair-integration.test.ts`: `bash` → top-level `shell` and → Code Mode `shell` (input repaired), a top-level Code Mode call, and a failing one, each with its note first.
- `session-runner.test.ts`: a top-level `acme.echo` call is saved as `acme.echo` and completes.
- `packages/core`: plugin, runner, step, model request, registry and Code Mode suites pass (1035/1035); `bun run check` passes.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): ask to reconnect ChatGPT when its refresh token is rejected
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60133

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a ChatGPT sign-in's refresh token has been revoked or has expired, OpenAI's token endpoint answers 400 with `{"error":"invalid_grant"}`. `request()` dropped the body, so every prompt failed with "Request failed: 400" and nothing told the user to reconnect.

`refresh()` now turns that response into "This ChatGPT sign-in has expired or was revoked. Connect again." Only `invalid_grant` on the refresh grant is matched. Other failures, and the authorization-code exchange, keep their current errors.

This does not add a "needs sign in" status for the connection. The refresh runs in core rather than in the plugin, so where that status would be set needs a decision and is left out of this PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added a test in `provider-chatgpt.test.ts` that runs `refresh()` against a local server. `invalid_grant` gives the new message; a 400 with a different error and a 500 still give "Request failed: <status>". The test fails without the fix.
- `bun run test test/plugin/provider-chatgpt.test.ts` and `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` at the root.
- Confirmed the response shape by posting an invalid refresh token to the real token endpoint, which returned 400 `{"error":"invalid_grant"}`. I have not tested against a real sign-in whose token was revoked.
