issues.title: Opt-in package namespace (pi.namespace) for skills and prompt templates

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

An opt-in `pi.namespace` field in a package's `package.json`. Every name-keyed resource the package loads through package resolution — skills and prompt templates — resolves through one unified surface: both load under the composed name `<namespace>:<name>`, with `/myorg:<name>` resolving the package's template first and its skill when no template owns the name. `/skill:myorg:foo` remains available as the explicit form for skills when disambiguation is needed. The prefix composes at load time; resource content — SKILL.md frontmatter, template filenames — stays untouched.

### Why?

Package resources are named by independent authors with no coordination, and pi loads them into flat name-keyed maps right next to user and project resources. As the package ecosystem grows, same-name collisions are a when-not-if outcome. Today's precedence (first-found-wins, user/project first) means the package loses its invocation name behind a collision warning — the precedence is right, but the package has no way to vacate the bare name while staying callable without mutating the resource.

The current escapes mutate the resource itself: prefixing the SKILL.md name, or colon template filenames. Both fork the artifact from its source of truth — the escape does not survive syncing from upstream, so the bare name stays claimed on one side or the other.

A provider-declared prefix is the standard content-neutral answer to independently-chosen identifiers colliding — npm scopes, DNS, every package manager — and it needs core support because the collision maps and exposed-name composition live in the core loaders — the skills collision map inside `loadSkills`, the template dedupe in resource-loader; extensions receive already-loaded resources and cannot rename them.

### How? (optional)

Implemented on a fork ([maskshell/pi](https://github.com/maskshell/pi), branch `package-namespace`, single commit): manifest field → PathMetadata → validated path→namespace associations in resource-loader → rename-at-load before collision dedupe → unified `/myorg:<name>` invocation (template first, then exact skill match) with `/skill:myorg:foo` as the explicit form; user/project resources always keep the bare name. 31 new tests (the four touched suites pass 315); `npm run check` clean. Happy to open the PR once approved.

---

### Status: maintained as a release-tracked fork patch (2026-10)

This proposal is now shipped and maintained outside upstream: [maskshell/pi](https://github.com/maskshell/pi) carries it as a release-managed patch on the [`namespace-patch` branch](https://github.com/maskshell/pi/tree/namespace-patch/patch) — every upstream release is re-based mechanically, repaired when needed, re-verified (full check chain + touched suites), and published as the npm alias [`pi-namespace-patch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-namespace-patch) via trusted publishing with signed provenance. Same pi, one feature ahead; pin exact `X.Y.Z-namespace.N` versions.

It is exercised in production by the [solidforge](https://github.com/maskshell/solidforge-pi) toolchain (`/solidforge:*` skills). Release-tracking notes continue in the comments below, one per tracked upstream release.

issues.title: Resumed Kimi session cannot select tools present in outbound provider payload

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

On Pi 1.6.0 with provider `kimi-coding` and model `k3.1-pro`, one resumed session cannot generate calls to four tools that are present in the active loadout, effective system prompt, and `before_provider_request` payload. A fresh session with the same extension can select all eight tools.

This may be at the Kimi provider/model boundary rather than in core tool restoration. I have not isolated a standalone reproduction, so this report is primarily a diagnostic request with sanitized runtime evidence.

## Environment

- Pi: 1.6.0
- Provider: `kimi-coding`
- Model: `k3.1-pro`
- Extension: `pi-watch`, registering eight direct, default-active tools

The eight tools are:

- `watch_create_poll`
- `watch_create_stream`
- `watch_list`
- `watch_inspect`
- `watch_pause`
- `watch_resume`
- `watch_remove`
- `watch_tail`

## Expected behavior

In the resumed session, the model should be able to emit a native call such as:

```json
{"name":"watch_inspect","arguments":{"name":"example-watch"}}
```

## Actual behavior

The model selects only `watch_create_poll`, `watch_create_stream`, `watch_list`, and `watch_tail`. It does not generate calls to `watch_inspect`, `watch_pause`, `watch_resume`, or `watch_remove`.

When asked to call `watch_inspect`, it either substitutes another tool or reports that `watch_inspect` is unavailable. After being given the complete tool names, descriptions, argument schemas, and an explicit direct-call instruction, it still cannot emit the call. There is no tool execution error to report because the call is never generated.

## Diagnostic evidence

At `session_start`, all eight tools are active and registered:

```text
active=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
registered=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
```

Immediately before the agent turn, all eight remain active and all eight appear as entries in the effective system prompt:

```text
before_agent_start active=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
prompt=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
```

At `before_provider_request`, all eight are present in the payload's `tools` array:

```text
before_provider_request tools=watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail,watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list totalTools=46
```

Replaying the active branch's system-message tool deltas also reconstructs all eight tools. The lifecycle tools have no later `toolsRemoved` delta.

## What did not change the behavior

1. **Compaction:** compacting the affected session did not make the four tools selectable.
2. **Prompt-cache reset:** replacing `prompt_cache_key` with a new session-derived value did not help. Diagnostics confirmed `cacheReset=true`, and all eight tools remained in the payload.
3. **Tool-count reduction:** removing four unrelated web tools from the outgoing payload reduced it from 46 to 42 tools. All eight watch tools remained present, but the model still could not select `watch_inspect`.
4. **Explicit tool manual:** providing the exact names, schemas, semantics, and a direct invocation instruction did not help.

A fresh session with the same extension exposes all eight tools at the model boundary and can select the lifecycle tools.

## Related issue

#11062 describes default-active tools not being activated on resume. Its fix is present in this Pi version, and this case appears distinct: the affected tools are restored, listed in the prompt, and included in the `before_provider_request` payload, yet the model does not generate calls to them.

## Request

Could maintainers help determine whether Kimi's provider path performs any further tool projection/filtering after `before_provider_request`, or recommend instrumentation that can distinguish provider transport behavior from model-side tool selection?

No raw transcript, credentials, message contents, or local identifiers are attached. A minimal standalone reproduction has not been isolated; the failure was observed in one long-lived resumed session and disappeared in a fresh session.

— Dev Agent 2 (automated)

issues.title: apps/p2: the dock's height changes move a pinned transcript by whole frames

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

The transcript pins to the bottom by default. The dock (composer) floats over it, and `use-chat-scroll.ts` keeps room
for it in the scroller's `paddingBottom` (`dockRef`, `apps/p2/src/web/use-chat-scroll.ts:379-393`).

When the dock's height changes, that room is written and a pinned transcript is re-pinned with `toEnd` in the same
`ResizeObserver` callback, so it moves by the whole difference between two paints. At 1280x900 with nine lines:

- sending while a run is busy: the input becomes a queued chip, no row enters the transcript, the dock shrinks from
  303px to 159px, and the transcript is scrolled by 144px in the next frame. Everything the reader sees, including
  the message above, moves down 144px between two painted frames. Nothing glides, because there is no new row.
- sending while idle: the new message's row is appended and its push glides (320ms), but the room's 176px arrives a
  frame later as a plain scroll write. One send, two corrections at two speeds.
- typing nine lines does the same in reverse: the transcript moves up 176px in the frame the room catches up.

The comment in `dockRef` says a taller composer moves nothing the reader sees. That is true for a reader who scrolled
up (their position counts from the top) and false for a pinned one, whose position is the end: the room is exactly
what moves it.

### Steps to reproduce

Chromium, 1280x900, `npm start` in `apps/p2`, signed in, a conversation at the bottom.

1. Send a message that keeps the run busy for a few seconds.
2. Type nine lines in the composer, wait a beat, press Send.
3. The messages shift down by the composer's height difference (~144px) in one frame while the composer collapses and
   the chip appears. With one line, nothing moves.

### Expected behavior

One movement, with the same glide new rows use, or none.

### Root cause

- `dockRef` (:379-393) writes the room and calls `#sync()` -> `toEnd` in one callback: the pinned transcript is
  translated by the full difference in that frame. Appended rows have `#glide` (:250) for exactly this; the room has
  nothing.
- The observer watches the scroller as well; our own padding write resizes the scroller's content box (border-box), so
  the same height is observed again in the same frame and the end is followed a second time.
- The room is only restated from that observer, so it can be behind the dock: I measured `paddingBottom: 127px` with
  a 302px dock at send time, and the first correction then moved the transcript the wrong way.

### Suggested fix

All in `use-chat-scroll.ts`: restate the room from `docked.offsetHeight` wherever it may have changed (the dock's
observer, the transcript's commit), read before write, so a frame's changes are one move; when pinned, treat the room
as content displacement and draw it through the existing `#glide` (signed, and continuing from where a running glide is
drawn) instead of a bare `toEnd`; fix the comments to say the room moves a pinned transcript and not an unpinned one.

I have this working locally; I can open a PR if you want the change.

### Version

p2 0.0.3 (`apps/p2/package.json`), `main` at 597d7d6.

issues.title: searchTools() returns full tool descriptions — 36KB per call, ~25% of a long session's context
issues.body:
Measured in a real 3-day coding-agent session (Deepwork harness, pi-durable 1.5.x, thread ~4.7M chars of model-visible content):

- `searchTools` was called 73 times; its results cost ~950KB — ~25% of the whole thread's context (more than all file reads combined).
- Cause: `discover()` in `dist/codemode/codemode.js` maps each ranked hit to the tool's **full** `description`. One of our tools has a ~36KB description (an embedded .d.ts teaching contract), so every loosely matching query (`"workflow run status"`, `"task status"`) returns ~37KB. The same query is often repeated after context compaction, because the model loses the previous result.
- Consequence we could measure, not just guess: results are truncated at ~10K tokens downstream, which twice produced unparseable JSON that agents then `JSON.parse`-failed on.

Suggestions, in order of preference:
1. Return name + first paragraph (or a fixed budget, e.g. 500 chars) per hit, and let agents call `describeTool(name)` for the full text — the plumbing already exists.
2. Or add an option `searchTools(query, { full: boolean })`, default short.

Happy to send a PR if you point at the preferred shape.

issues.title: pi -p (headless) does not exit when a stdio MCP server stays connected
issues.body:
pi 1.4.0, macOS 27.0.1.

In headless mode (`pi -p`), pi prints its result but never exits when at least one stdio MCP server is connected successfully; the process hangs until killed. A stdio server that fails at startup does not block exit.

Repro:
1. Add any working stdio server to user-level `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`, e.g. `{"mcpServers":{"context7":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@upstash/context7-mcp"]}}}`
2. `timeout 90 pi -p --model zai/glm-4.7 'Reply with exactly: ok'`
3. Result prints, then the process hangs: exit code 124 via timeout. Disable the server entry: exit 0 immediately.

Verified with two unrelated servers (a custom python stdio server and @upstash/context7-mcp); failure at startup (nonzero exit) does not hang. Interactive sessions are unaffected.

Expected: in -p mode pi should shut down connected MCP children and exit after printing the result.

Workaround: wrap headless runs in `timeout`.

issues.title: isContextOverflow treats 429/5xx/quota errors as overflow; codemode marks still-running calls as cancelled

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
Two small things we patch locally on 1.6.0 (both patches originally from n8n-io/nod, Apache-2.0); filing them in case you want them upstream.

1. `pi-ai` `dist/utils/overflow.js`: `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` only excludes "rate limit" / "too many requests" / Bedrock throttling. An error such as `429 Too many tokens, please wait`, `insufficient_quota: token limit exceeded`, `usage_limit_reached ... too many tokens` or a 5xx whose body says "prompt is too long" matches an overflow pattern, so `AgentSession` starts a compaction on a rate or quota limit. We add to `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`:

```js
/^(?:[\w -]+ API error \((?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\):|(?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)(?:\s|:|$))/i,
/\(HTTP (?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\)(?: \(transport cause: [^)]+\))?(?: \[request phase: [^\]]+\])?\s*$/i,
/\b(?:insufficient_quota|quota_exceeded|usage_limit_reached)\b/i,
/\b(?:tokens? per (?:minute|day)|[tr]p[md])\b/i,
```

413 stays an overflow.

2. `pi-coding-agent` `dist/extensions/codemode/execute.js`: when a script fails or ends while tool calls it started are still running, those calls are reported as `cancelled`, but they may have already taken effect (e.g. a sent message). We track pending calls, wait for them within the script's remaining deadline (not after an abort), report a still-running one as `outcome unknown`, and append "Some tool results are still unknown. Check the outside state before repeating an action." so the model does not repeat a write.

Happy to open a PR for either if useful.

issues.title: durable: the compaction summary budget is ~13k tokens regardless of the model's context window (budget, not trigger)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Background

Automatic compaction has one setting, `CompactionSettings.reserveTokens` (default 16 384), doing two unrelated jobs:

1. **The trigger.** A blocking compaction starts above `contextWindow - reserveTokens` (background: above
   `blocking - backgroundTokens`).
2. **The summary budget.** The request that writes the summary is sent with
   `maxTokens = min(0.8 * reserveTokens, model.maxTokens)`.

So the size of the request that produces the summary is decided by the headroom kept for the trigger, not by what
the model can write.

## Problem

With the default reserve, `0.8 * reserveTokens` is 13 107.2 → **13 107 tokens** (floored) — for every model,
whatever its window. On a 1M-token model that is about 1.3% of the window. The summary is the only thing the model
keeps of everything before `firstKept`, so a long conversation is compacted into at most ~13k tokens no matter how
much room the model has — enough for a list of topics, not for the detail needed to continue a piece of work.
Raising `reserveTokens` to get a bigger summary also moves the trigger earlier, which is the opposite of what a
large window wants.

This report is about the **budget only**. The trigger is not proposed to change: blocking stays
`contextWindow - reserveTokens`, background stays `blocking - backgroundTokens`, and `keepRecentTokens` still
selects the cut.

Related: #9727 (closed) reported the same coupling at the same line of code; #9904 (open) asks for the trigger
side. This is a concrete formula for the budget half of #9727, not a re-argument of it.

## Proposal

`maxTokens = max(1, min(10% * contextWindow, model.maxTokens))` — 10% of the window, capped by the model's own
output limit, with a floor of 1. An unknown output limit (`maxTokens: 0`) keeps meaning "no output cap", as it
does today.

Catalog windows come in both families, so here is the same formula for each (10% floored; the table shows the window
term alone — see the note under it):

| context window | budget today | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| 128 000 (decimal "128k") | 13 107 | 12 800 |
| 131 072 (128 KiB) | 13 107 | 13 107 |
| 200 000 (decimal "200k") | 13 107 | 20 000 |
| 204 800 (200 KiB) | 13 107 | 20 480 |
| 500 000 | 13 107 | 50 000 |
| 1 000 000 (decimal "1M") | 13 107 | 100 000 |
| 1 048 576 (1 MiB) | 13 107 | 104 857 |

Note on the output limit. The formula keeps `min(..., model.maxTokens)`, exactly as today, so a model whose output
limit is below 10% of its window is capped by it — those models are unchanged by this proposal. In the generated
catalog (1 665 models that carry both numbers) 296 are in that state; the smallest output limits are 3 685, 4 000
and 4 096 tokens, and four Mistral models with a 128k–262k window and `maxTokens: 4000` keep a 4 000-token summary
(`min(0.8 × 16 384, 4 000)` = 4 000 today, `min(10% × window, 4 000)` = 4 000 after). The proposal only lifts the
flat 13 107 ceiling where the model can actually write more.

Two things to read out of it:

- **Small windows do not regress.** At 131 072 the proposed budget is 13 107 — exactly today's value (10% of 128 KiB
  and `0.8 × 16 384` coincide), and at 128 000 it is 12 800, about 2% below it. A model with a small window sees no
  meaningful change; nothing gets worse to make large windows better.
- **Large windows stop being clamped.** From ~131k upward the budget grows with the window again, so a 1M window
  whose output limit allows it gets ~105k for its summary instead of ~13k.

10% is the largest summary that does not compete with the rest of the request (the summarization request also
carries the serialized prefix), it scales with what the model accepts, and the output limit already bounds it per
model.

Long sessions get slow and expensive, and Pi only shows total tokens in the footer. There is no place to see how much is system prompt vs tools vs history, what the last cache miss cost, or how far away compaction is.

```
System prompt: 40 tokens (34.2%)
Tools: 55 tokens (47.0%, 2 tools)

Compaction
```

prs.title: fix(durable): size the compaction summary budget from the model's context window
prs.body:
## What

The pinned compaction summary request (`CompactionTask`, phase `select`) sizes its output as
`0.8 × reserveTokens`, capped by the model's own output limit.

This changes it to `max(1, min(10% × contextWindow, model.maxTokens))`:
10% of the model's context window, still capped by its output limit, with a floor of 1.

```diff
-				maxTokens: Math.min(
-					Math.floor(0.8 * policy.reserveTokens),
-					model.maxTokens > 0 ? model.maxTokens : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
-				),
+				// A summary may use 10% of the model's context window, capped by its output limit.
+				maxTokens: Math.max(
+					1,
+					Math.min(
+						Math.floor(model.contextWindow * 0.1),
+						model.maxTokens > 0 ? model.maxTokens : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
+					),
+				),
```

## Why

`reserveTokens` is the **trigger** headroom (`contextWindow - reserveTokens`), not a statement about how much a
model can write. Deriving the summary budget from it ties the two together:

| context window | default reserve | summary budget before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k | 16 384 | 13 107 tokens | 12 800 tokens |
| 200k | 16 384 | 13 107 tokens | 20 000 tokens |
| 1M | 16 384 | 13 107 tokens | 100 000 tokens |

On a large window the old formula summarizes a long prefix into ~1.3% of what the model can emit, so detail is
lost for no reason; the summary is the only thing the model keeps of everything before `firstKept`. 10% of the
window is the largest summary that does not compete with the rest of the request, and the existing output-limit
cap keeps it inside what the provider will accept. `maxTokens: 0` (unknown limit) keeps working as "no cap", as
before.

The trigger is deliberately **not** changed: blocking stays `contextWindow - reserveTokens`, background stays
`blocking - backgroundTokens`, and `keepRecentTokens` still selects the cut. This is only about the size of the
request that writes the summary.

Related: #9727 reported this coupling (closed); #9904 asks for the trigger side to be decoupled. This PR is the
summary-budget half and leaves the trigger alone.

## How

- `packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts`: the `select` phase's `maxTokens` (one expression).
- `packages/durable/test/harness-compaction.test.ts`:
  - `open()` gains an optional `maxTokens` (default 900, as before) so a test can register a model with a limit
    or with none;
  - new `describe("summary budget")` pinning the four window sizes, the output-limit cap, the unknown limit, the
    floor at 1, and one test that a 1000-token window with `reserveTokens: 300` still triggers a blocking
    compaction at 700 tokens *and* that its summary asks for exactly 100;
  - the existing manual-compaction assertion `maxTokens: 800` (which encoded `0.8 × 1000`) becomes `900`.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run packages/durable/test/harness-compaction.test.ts` — **114 passed** (`114 tests`, `1 file`,
  2.1 s). Run in a workspace mirror that aliases the workspace packages to their sources, because this checkout
  cannot produce `dist/`: `npm ci` succeeds, `npm run build` fails in `packages/ai` at
  `npm run generate-models && npm run build:offline`, and the package tests resolve `@earendil-works/pi-ai`
  through its `dist` entry.
- `npx biome check packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts packages/durable/test/harness-compaction.test.ts`
  — `Checked 2 files … No fixes applied.`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (repo root) — 1147 diagnostics, **0** in the two changed files. The rest come from the
  checkout's missing generated model data and `dist/` (the build failure above), not from this change.
- `./test.sh`, `npm run check`: not run — both need the build step above.

## Risk and rollback

- Risk is a larger summary request: at most 10% of the window instead of a fixed ~13k, always inside
  `model.maxTokens`. A model whose window is smaller than 10% of its output limit is unaffected (the cap wins).
- `maxTokens: 0` (unknown) now means "10% of the window" rather than "0.8 × reserve"; both were "no output cap"
  in practice because the provider limit is the real ceiling.
- Rollback: revert this commit. No data or stored checkpoint changes: the budget is read at `select` time and
  pinned into the task checkpoint.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep usage-backed estimate past post-usage context edits
prs.body:
## Summary

`estimateProjectedContextTokens` discarded the provider-measured usage estimate whenever **any** `context_edit` (or compaction) existed newer than the usage-bearing assistant — even when the edit only omitted the failed overflow-recovery attempt that by design follows the failed turn. That fallback (~chars/4 over the whole session) then reported a phantom over-limit context (~281% of the window in a real session), triggering spurious emergency-compression/overlay flows and blocking future turns.

**Fix:** a `context_edit` only invalidates the usage-backed estimate when its target is at or before the usage-bearing assistant (or the target is unknown). Edits targeting strictly later entries leave the measured prefix intact, so the valid provider-measured number is kept. Compactions keep the existing conservative behavior (always invalidate).

A regression test covers the overflow-recovery omission scenario.

## Tests

`packages/coding-agent` test suite (`vitest --run test/session-context-edit.test.ts test/compaction.test.ts test/agent-session-auto-compaction-queue.test.ts`) — all pass, including the new test (verified it fails without the fix).

# Harden transcript export compatibility checks and follow-up contract notes

## What happened?

After [#17970](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970) landed, the final review left non-blocking follow-ups in the test harness and supporting contract notes. These are reliability and maintenance issues, not a request to roll back the merged automatic-trigger presentation or to change scheduler/daemon interfaces.

The main items are:

- **The isolated local build can miss real workspace edits.** Its working-tree patch covers only selected packages and omits untracked files. A contributor changing a related package or adding a module can therefore test a stale dependency or fail to compile an import that exists in their checkout. The root also follows the caller's current directory, so invoking the test with a different Vitest root can select the wrong checkout. ([R3-1](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444797), [R5-3](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444810))
- **Failed setup can leave partial temporary trees and report two errors.** Cleaning an unregistered directory through Git fails before resetting the test's cleanup state, and the later cleanup repeats the same problem. Cleanup must preserve both Git registration and filesystem ownership; it must not resort to a global worktree prune. ([R5-4](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444813))
- **The legacy-renderer browser case still depends on a live CDN.** It downloads pinned 0.28.3 JavaScript and CSS during a `--retry=0` test job. Registry/CDN failures, an offline runner, or an environment that requires a proxy can turn a real compatibility gate into an unrelated network failure. ([R5-2](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444806))
- **Initialization is expensive, and some later work is duplicated.** The dedicated initialization includes dependency setup and a full workspace build. An actual local run took about 630 seconds in the test phase. A final renderer rebuild also happened just before deleting the same private tree. [R5-1](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444803) suggests trading this for direct TypeScript execution and a template-only build; that tradeoff must not replace real generated renderer constants and compiled public schema-ceiling behavior with an uncompiled or mocked check. ([R5-5](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444814))
- **The English budget history omitted attachment-reference validation** although the Chinese version and the guarded renderer behavior include it. The separate documentation follow-up [PR #18080](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18080) addresses that wording and the implementation-status paragraph in both languages. ([R5-6](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444817))

## What did you expect to happen?

- The test checkout should reproduce the contributor's relevant tracked and untracked source changes, while excluding ignored dependency/build outputs. Tests should demonstrate those boundaries with real inputs, and resolve the checkout from the test's location rather than the caller's working directory.
- Failed setup and teardown should remove the task-owned directory without duplicate errors. If Git registered the directory, its registration must also be released; unrelated worktrees and repositories must remain untouched. Repeated cleanup should be harmless.
- The real historical renderer must remain testable without live network access. An offline fixture/cache should prove its immutable identity, retain raw-byte and SRI checks, and continue to show that the real old reader opens V1 with full instructions and rejects V2 without displaying the instruction. Offline operation must not become a skip or weaken the renderer into a shape-only assertion.
- Any simplification of setup must preserve genuine compiled renderer and writer checks, including schema ceilings, identity, SRI, and unknown-schema rejection. A faster path that allows a document the actual renderer would reject is not an acceptable substitute.
- English and Chinese descriptions should remain synchronized. The remaining revision and contract observations from the [round 5 review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#pullrequestreview-6010045502) should also be checked against current main rather than being treated as already resolved.

## Client information

This concerns automated CLI/test infrastructure, not a production-model/login session.

- Platform: Linux.
- Local runtime used for the merge validation: Node.js v26.12.1; the main CI build/test jobs also use Node.js 22.
- The compatibility tests use actual published renderer assets in Chromium through Playwright.
- No interactive `/about` transcript or production-model credentials are applicable to this harness follow-up.

## Login information

N/A. The compatibility checks use local fixtures/stubs and do not require production model credentials or real model inference.

## Anything else we need to know?

These ideas were recorded as suggestions or deferred observations, not critical blockers. The original PR was approved and merged. Its main CI has passed, while a separate post-merge E2E workflow is being tracked independently. [#17267](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/17267) is a different pending-wakeup visibility issue and is outside this scope.

A retained local prototype already exercised complete tracked/untracked input transfer, real failed-registration and registered-worktree cleanup, module-anchored checkout discovery, and offline legacy assets. Its focused checks passed: formatter **13/13**, document-browser checks **13/13**, and document factory **80/80**. The final renderer and the old reader's V1-open/V2-reject behavior were genuinely exercised, not replaced by mocks. **Those edits have not been published or merged, and a full repository lint pass was not observed to completion for that prototype.** CI on the eventual follow-up head must remain a separate gate rather than reusing earlier results.

The implementation worktree and these pending test artifacts have been preserved. The merged PR's original local and remote branches were removed without discarding that work.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 发生了什么？

[#17970](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970) 合入后，最终审查留下了测试 harness 和配套契约说明中的非阻断后续事项。这些问题关系到可靠性和维护成本，并不要求回退已合入的自动触发展示，也不要求改变调度器或 daemon 接口。

主要包括：

- **隔离的本地构建可能遗漏真实工作区改动。** 当前 patch 只覆盖指定包，且不包含未跟踪文件。当贡献者修改相关包或新增模块时，可能在旧依赖上测试，或因找不到自己 checkout 中确实存在的导入而失败。根目录还取调用方的当前目录，使用不同的 Vitest root 可能选错 checkout。（[R3-1](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444797)、[R5-3](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444810)）
- **初始化失败可能留下临时树并产生重复错误。** 对未注册目录执行 Git 清理会在重置测试清理状态之前失败，后续清理又会重复该错误。清理必须同时保护 Git 注册状态和文件系统归属，不能转为全局 worktree prune。（[R5-4](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444813)）
- **旧版 renderer 浏览器用例仍依赖实时 CDN。** 它在一个 `--retry=0` 的测试 job 中下载固定的 0.28.3 JavaScript 与 CSS。registry/CDN 故障、离线 runner 或仅能通过代理联网的环境，都可能把真实的兼容性验证变成无关的网络失败。（[R5-2](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444806)）
- **初始化成本较高，且后续存在重复工作。** 专用初始化包含依赖安装和全仓构建，一次实测的测试阶段约为 630 秒。删除私有树之前还会再次构建 renderer。[R5-1](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444803) 建议改为直接执行 TypeScript 并只构建模板；这种取舍不能把真实生成的 renderer 常量及编译后的公共 schema 上限行为替换成未经编译或 mock 的检查。（[R5-5](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444814)）
- **英文历史体积说明遗漏了附件引用校验，** 而中文及 renderer 的实际行为已包含该项。单独的文档后续 [PR #18080](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18080) 正在处理这一措辞和两种语言中的实现状态段落。（[R5-6](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#discussion_r4656444817)）

## 期望如何改进？

- 测试 checkout 应完整复现贡献者相关的 tracked 和 untracked 源文件改动，并排除被忽略的依赖与构建产物。测试应使用真实输入证明这些边界，并从测试文件所在位置推导 checkout，而不是依赖调用方当前目录。
- 初始化和销毁失败时，应清理任务自有的目录且不产生重复错误。若目录已注册到 Git，也必须释放对应注册关系；不得影响其他 worktree 或仓库。重复清理应安全无操作。
- 真实历史 renderer 应能脱离实时网络验证。离线 fixture/cache 必须证明其不可变身份，保留原始字节数与 SRI 校验，并继续证明真实旧版阅读器能打开 V1、显示完整指令，却拒绝 V2 而不显示该指令。离线运行不能退化为跳过，也不能把 renderer 行为弱化到只验证外形。
- 任何简化初始化的方案都应保留真实编译出去的 renderer 和 writer 验证，包括 schema 上限、身份、SRI 和未知 schema 拒绝。不能为了加速而接受真实 renderer 会拒绝的文档。
- 英中文说明应保持同步。[第五轮审查](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17970#pullrequestreview-6010045502)中其余版本与契约观察项，也应按当前 main 重新取证，不能当作已经解决。

## 客户端信息

本问题涉及自动化 CLI/测试基础设施，不涉及生产模型或登录会话。

- 平台：Linux。
- 本次合入验证的本地运行时：Node.js v26.12.1；主 CI 的构建/测试 job 也使用 Node.js 22。
- 兼容性测试在 Chromium 中通过 Playwright 使用实际发布的 renderer 资产。
- 这项 harness 后续工作不需要也不适用交互式 `/about` 输出或生产模型凭据。

## 登录信息

不适用。兼容性检查使用本地 fixture/桩，不需要真实生产模型凭据或真实模型推理。

## 其他需要了解的信息

这些问题在审查中属于建议或延期观察，而非关键阻断项。原 PR 已获批准并合入。其主 CI 已通过，另一个合入后的 E2E 工作流正在独立跟踪。[#17267](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/17267) 是不同的 pending-wakeup 可见性问题，不在本 issue 范围内。

保留的本地原型已经验证了完整 tracked/untracked 输入复制、真实未注册/已注册 worktree 的清理、从模块定位 checkout，以及离线旧 renderer 资产。聚焦测试通过：formatter **13/13**、文档浏览器检查 **13/13**、document factory **80/80**。最终 renderer 及旧版阅读器的 V1 可读、V2 拒绝行为都经过了真实验证，没有用 mock 替代。**这些修改尚未公开或合入；该原型的全仓 lint 未观察到完整结束。** 后续 head 的 CI 仍是独立的门禁，不能直接复用先前结果。

当前实现 worktree 和这些待处理测试产物均已保留。原合入 PR 的本地与远端分支已删除，但没有丢弃这些工作。

</details>

# Update the sidebar design docs for the active-work color contract

## What happened?

PR #18072 intentionally made **active work** share the existing **running green**, while keeping **completed-unread blue** and **background-running amber**.

The two-language background-work design document still describes the previous behavior on current `main` (`68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0`):

- [English design: status-dot precedence](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.md#L128-L129) says "blue for other active work".
- [Chinese design: status-dot precedence](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d6038171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.zh-CN.md#L100) says the same in Chinese.
- The [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.md#L235-L236) and [Chinese](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.zh-CN.md#L182) acceptance criteria still say dot precedence is unchanged, despite the intentional color change.

This can direct a future contributor to restore the exact blue-active-work ambiguity that #18072 removed. The implementation itself is correct: [the active-work marker reuses the running class](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.tsx#L6155-L6162), and [that class uses the success color](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.module.css#L1344-L1346).

## What did you expect to happen?

Update both language versions together so they describe the current behavior: green for a running prompt or other active work, amber for background-running work, and blue for completed-unread status.

Revise the relevant acceptance criterion to reflect the intentional dot precedence while preserving the existing touch-layout and hover contracts. Keep both versions complete and synchronized; no further implementation or color change is requested by this documentation issue.

## Client information

Documentation/source issue reproduced on Linux against the cited `main` commit; no runtime client interaction is required to observe the contradiction.

## Anything else we need to know?

This is the follow-up to review suggestion R1-1: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072#discussion_r4656465334.

Related merged fix: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072.

A search found #17819, but that issue covers detached background-process liveness, not this documentation color contract.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 发生了什么？

PR #18072 有意让「活动任务」复用现有的「运行绿色」，同时保持「完成未读为蓝色」和「后台任务为琥珀色」。

在当前 `main`（`68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0`）上，后台任务设计文档的两种语言仍描述旧行为：

- [英文设计文档](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.md#L128-L129)仍写着「其他活跃工作为蓝色」。
- [中文设计文档](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.zh-CN.md#L100)也有相同的旧颜色约定。
- [英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.md#L235-L236)和[中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/docs/design/web-shell-sidebar-background-work-indicator.zh-CN.md#L182)验收条件仍写着圆点优先级不变，漏掉了此次有意的颜色调整。

这可能让后续贡献者按旧文档恢复 #18072 刚刚消除的「活动任务看起来像未读」问题。当前实现本身是正确的：[活动任务标记复用了运行类](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.tsx#L6155-L6162)，[该类名使用成功色](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.module.css#L1344-L1346)。

## 期望发生什么？

在同一改动中更新两种语言，使其描述当前行为：正在运行或其他活跃工作显示绿色，后台任务显示琥珀色，完成未读显示蓝色。

同步修改相应的验收条件，明确有意的圆点优先级变化，同时保持既有触屏布局与悬停契约。两版应完整、同步；本问题只要求修正文档，不要求再次改变实现或颜色。

## 客户端信息

这是文档与源码问题，已在 Linux 上按上述 `main` 提交复核；观察该矛盾不依赖运行时客户端交互。

## 其他需要了解的信息

这是评审建议 R1-1 的后续跟踪：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072#discussion_r4656465334。

相关已合入修复：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072。

检索到的 #17819 关注的是 detached 后台进程的存活状态，与本问题的文档颜色约定不同。

</details>

# Pin the active-work status color token in the sidebar CSS test

## What would you like to be added?

Add direct stylesheet regression coverage for the **success-color token** that gives the shared running/active-work status dot its intended meaning, using the existing warning-token CSS test as the pattern.

The coverage should exercise the current stylesheet source and retain the token's meaning across formatting changes. A negative mutation check should show that the assertion fails if the token is replaced by the ordinary blue token, and if the color declaration is removed, then pass again when the stylesheet is restored.

## Why is this needed?

PR #18072 makes active work reuse the running class, and its [DOM regression test](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.workspace-removal.test.tsx#L5384-L5392) correctly pins that class assignment. However, the visible color comes from the separate [`.sessionStatusDotRunning` stylesheet declaration](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.module.css#L1344-L1346).

On current `main`, the stylesheet-component tests contain no direct assertion for this class or its `--success-color` token, and their own setup explains that jsdom does not compute the CSS cascade. A later token swap or declaration deletion could therefore reintroduce a blue active-work indicator while the class-name assertion still passes.

The behavior on current `main` is correct; this is a request to protect it against future stylesheet mutations, not a report of a remaining runtime defect. The existing [background warning-token test](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.css.test.ts#L137-L150) demonstrates the established approach for this kind of coverage.

## Additional context

This is follow-up suggestion R1-2 from https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072#discussion_r4656465341. Related merged fix: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072.

A search for existing `sessionStatusDotRunning` issues found none. This is separate from the design-document color-contract follow-up and from #17819's detached-process liveness work.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 希望增加什么？

在现有侧栏样式测试里，为运行中/活动任务圆点所依赖的**成功色 token**补充直接的回归覆盖，沿用现有警示色 token 测试的模式。

覆盖应检查当前样式源码，并允许正常的格式排版变化。再做负向变异验证：把该 token 换成普通蓝色 token、或删除颜色声明时，断言都应失败；还原样式后应重新通过。

## 为什么需要？

PR #18072 让活动任务复用运行类，其 [DOM 回归断言](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.workspace-removal.test.tsx#L5384-L5392)正确固定了类名校验。但可见颜色取决于单独的 [`.sessionStatusDotRunning` 样式声明](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.module.css#L1344-L1346)。

当前 `main` 的样式组件测试没有直接固定这个类名或其 `--success-color` token，并且测试文件自己的说明已指出 jsdom 不计算 CSS 层叠。因此，未来若 token 被替换或颜色声明被删除，可能重新让活动工作显示为蓝色，而类名断言仍然通过。

当前 `main` 的行为是正确的；本请求是为了防止未来的样式变异破坏该行为，并非报告当前仍有运行时缺陷。现有[后台警示色 token 测试](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/68388f5d4129ab458d4638171b853a82cba525d0/packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/WebShellSidebar.css.test.ts#L137-L150)已经示范了同类覆盖方式。

## 其他上下文

这是评审建议 R1-2 的后续：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072#discussion_r4656465341。相关已合入修复：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18072。

检索未发现已有的 `sessionStatusDotRunning` 相关 issue。它与设计文档颜色约定的后续项，以及 #17819 的 detached 进程存活状态问题相互独立。

</details>

issues.title: chore(managed-agent): ToolPublicationDataStore exceeds the class-size ratchet (2485 > 2483)

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: scope/ci-cd
labels.description: Continuous integration/deployment

issues.body:
## What happened

The nightly SDK Java run (e.g. [run 44942840292](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44942840292), MySQL job) fails `ClassSizeRatchetTest`: `ToolPublicationDataStore` now measures **2485 lines** against its ratchet ceiling of **2483** in `packages/managed-agent-server/verification/src/test/resources/class-size-ratchet.properties:53`.

The overage was introduced by #18048 (`56ef3468`, "refactor(managed-agent): use plaintext identity segments in OSS object keys"), which added the 4-line `ossScope(JsonNode)` helper to the class.

## Why this needs a real fix, not a bump

The ratchet is deliberately one-way: the ceiling only ever moves down, so `class-size-ratchet.properties` must not be raised to 2485. The class needs to lose the overage instead — e.g. by moving the OSS-key naming (`ossScope` and the `managed-tool-results/` prefix assembly at its three call sites) into a small package-private helper, which would clear the gate with headroom to spare.

## Evidence

- Failing test: `com.alibaba.qwen.code.managedagent.architecture.ClassSizeRatchetTest` in the SDK Java nightly (`sdk-java.yml`, cron `47 19 * * *`).
- Current main: `wc -l packages/managed-agent-server/persistence/src/main/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/persistence/ToolPublicationDataStore.java` → 2485.
- Ceiling: `class-size-ratchet.properties:53` → `…ToolPublicationDataStore=2483`.

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): extract publication object key construction
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extracts tool-publication OSS object-key construction into a package-private component shared by the admission, terminal, and ordinary-slot write paths. Pins the exact plaintext layout through the helper and all three wired call sites, and lowers the global and per-class ratchet ceilings to the new 2481-line size without changing SQL identities, object layouts, or validation.

## Why it's needed

#18048 increased the publication data store from 2481 to 2485 lines, exceeding the 2483-line class-size ratchet. This makes the Managed Agent fast tier fail deterministically on main-derived merges, including #17910 even though that PR contains no Java changes. Extracting the new key-construction responsibility restores a green ratchet while preserving #18048's plaintext identity behavior; raising the ceiling would defeat the gate.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. From `packages/managed-agent-server` with JDK 21 and the sibling SDK installed, run `mvn -Dtest=ToolPublicationStoreTest,ClassSizeRatchetTest,ToolPublicationObjectKeysTest test checkstyle:check`; all 115 tests should pass, Checkstyle should report zero violations, and the publication data store should measure 2481 lines.
2. Confirm that the wired tests assert `managed-tool-results/{tenantId}/{workspaceId}/{sessionId}/{publicationId}/{slot}` for admission, terminal, and ordinary large-segment slots. As a mutation witness, temporarily changing only the terminal argument to the non-colliding `segment:stdout:0` makes both parameterized terminal cases fail at the new direct assertion; restoring it returns the suite to green.

Local results on the submitted revision:

```text
Tests run: 115, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
You have 0 Checkstyle violations.
BUILD SUCCESS
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

This is a non-UI refactor. The image contains the real local Maven results and the measured before/after class sizes; no interface comparison applies.

![Managed Agent ratchet verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/managed-agent-tool-publication-ratchet/managed-agent-tool-publication-ratchet/tool-publication-ratchet-evidence.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, JDK 21.0.9, Maven 3.9.11, task-isolated Maven repository under `/tmp`; no application service or external OSS instance was launched.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Low; this moves pure key assembly without changing its validated input fields or output. Helper-level exact-key coverage plus admission, terminal, and ordinary-slot assertions inside the 113-test publication suite cover the affected behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: The complete Managed Agent H2 suite, MySQL profiles, and hosted/fault profiles remain pending CI under the module's focused local-verification budget. #17910 is not modified by this PR.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

## Linked Issues

Related to #17910 and #18048.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 本 PR 的内容

将工具发布 OSS 对象键的构造抽取为包内私有组件，供 admission、terminal 和普通 slot 三条写入路径共用。通过 helper 和三处真实调用点固定完整明文布局，并将全局及类级棘轮上限下调到修复后的 2481 行；SQL identity、对象布局和校验规则均保持不变。

### 修复原因

#18048 将发布数据存储类从 2481 行增加到 2485 行，超过了 2483 行的类大小棘轮上限。这会使基于 main 的合并树在 Managed Agent fast tier 中确定性失败，#17910 即使没有任何 Java 改动也会连带失败，正如其 CI 所示。抽取新增的对象键构造职责可以在保留 #18048 明文 identity 行为的同时恢复棘轮检查；直接提高上限则会破坏该门禁的意义。

### 审核者验证计划

#### 如何验证

1. 在 `packages/managed-agent-server` 下配置 JDK 21 并安装兄弟 SDK 后运行 `mvn -Dtest=ToolPublicationStoreTest,ClassSizeRatchetTest,ToolPublicationObjectKeysTest test checkstyle:check`；全部 115 个测试应通过，Checkstyle 应报告零违规，发布数据存储类应为 2481 行。
2. 确认真实流程测试对 admission、terminal 和大型普通 segment 的 OSS key 精确断言 `managed-tool-results/{tenantId}/{workspaceId}/{sessionId}/{publicationId}/{slot}` 布局；仅临时将 terminal 参数改成不冲突的 `segment:stdout:0` 时，两个 terminal 参数化用例均在新增直接断言处报红，恢复后测试回到全绿。

提交修订上的本地结果：

```text
Tests run: 115, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
You have 0 Checkstyle violations.
BUILD SUCCESS
```

#### 前后证据

这是非 UI 重构，不涉及界面 Before/After。配图记录真实本地 Maven 输出及改动前后的实际类行数。

![Managed Agent 棘轮验证](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/managed-agent-tool-publication-ratchet/managed-agent-tool-publication-ratchet/tool-publication-ratchet-evidence.png)

#### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

#### 环境（可选）

Linux、JDK 21.0.9、Maven 3.9.11，Maven 仓库隔离在任务的 `/tmp` 目录；未启动应用服务或外部 OSS 实例。

### 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：较低；仅移动纯对象键拼装逻辑，不改变校验后的输入字段或输出。helper 级精确 key 测试，以及现有 113 项 publication 套件内新增的 admission、terminal 和普通 slot 断言覆盖了受影响行为。
- 未验证或不在范围内：根据模块的本地定向验证预算，完整 Managed Agent H2 套件、MySQL profiles 和 Hosted/fault profiles 留待 CI。此 PR 不修改 #17910。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无。

### 关联条目

prs.title: feat(web-shell): scope ChatSurface admission locks to the owning session and bind loadOlder
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This increment closes the two switch-readiness items explicitly deferred to the daemon main-column switch slice: it scopes the shared chat surface's in-flight submit latch and unknown-admission payload lock to the session that armed them (parking and restoring `{ token, inFlight, admissionLocked }` per durable session across round-trip switches, committing an accepted submit's identity-scoped draft before the stale-owner guard, and gating the mid-submit new-chat allocation exception on the contract's `allocatedSessionId` so a sidebar switch out of an unallocated new chat into an existing session clears the latch and rotates the owner token), and it binds the daemon controller's older-history pagination capability (`loadOlder(options?: { force?: boolean })`) to the session transcript history loader while forwarding `{ force: true }` on pagination-error retries. A bilingual design document (`docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.md` and `docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.zh-CN.md`) records the scoping and rationale.

## Why it's needed

The full daemon main-column switch is a multi-increment effort because the main column's local-slash/inline-shell submit orchestration, the streaming-tail projection, and the ~90 composer props all exceed the current contract. Before wiring any production column through the shared surface, two deferred gaps had to be closed so the switch cannot regress them: the surface's submit latches were component-scoped with no session owner (a stale unknown-admission lock or an abandoned in-flight submit could block or clobber the next session the user switched to, or be lost on a round-trip switch back to the owning session), and the daemon binding left older-history pagination unbound so a surface relying on the controller capability would silently lose pagination.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the unified-chat-surface test suite and both Web Shell TypeScript projects from `packages/web-shell`:

```bash
cd packages/web-shell
npx vitest run client/chat-core/ client/i18n.test.ts client/i18n-loading.test.tsx client/daemon/useDaemonChatController.test.tsx client/daemon/chat-controller.test.ts client/daemon/chat-intents.test.ts client/daemon/permission-signals.test.ts client/adapters/transcriptAdapter.test.ts
npx tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit
npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

Confirm all 10 test files (282 tests, including the six session-scoping cases in `ChatSurface.test.tsx` and the `loadOlder` case in `useDaemonChatController.test.tsx`) pass and both typechecks exit 0.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — additive switch-readiness increment; no production chat column renders through the shared surface yet (the visual before/after gate belongs to the column switch itself).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Vitest (`jsdom`) + TypeScript (`tsconfig.lib.json` and `tsconfig.json`) in `packages/web-shell`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Neither an unconditional empty-to-non-empty session exception nor an in-flight-only exception can distinguish a mid-submit session allocation (`'' -> allocated s1`) from a user clicking an existing session in the sidebar (`'' -> existing s2`) during the session-creation round trip; the exception is therefore gated on `controller.allocatedSessionId === controller.sessionId` for controllers that allocate a session inside `submit` before rendering the new id (the daemon adapter allocates sessions before `submitPrompt` and leaves `allocatedSessionId` unset, so any `'' -> id` transition on the daemon controller takes the switch branch), while durable sessions park and restore `{ token, inFlight, admissionLocked }` across round-trip switches.
- Not validated / out of scope: Wiring the daemon main chat column itself (requires carrying the streaming-tail projection, the local submit orchestration, and the rich composer surface through the contract or slots in subsequent increments, followed by the browser before/after gate).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Additive change to the shared surface, contract, and daemon binding; no daemon or Java route, OpenAPI, session-id namespace, or storage-key change. Design docs: [English](docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Part of #17460 (builds on #17520, #17684, #17709, #17794, #17895, #17952).

本增量关闭明确延后到 daemon 主列切换切片的两项切换前置项：把共享聊天表面的在飞提交闩与 unknown 准入载荷锁收敛到武装它们的会话作用域（在往返切换间按持久会话暂存并恢复 `{ token, inFlight, admissionLocked }`，在陈旧归属守卫之前提交 accepted 结算自身的身份作用域草稿，并以契约的 `allocatedSessionId` 作为新聊天提交中途分配例外的门禁，使首次提交在飞期间从未分配新聊天点击侧边栏切到已有会话时清除闩并轮换归属令牌），并把 daemon 控制器的更早历史分页能力（`loadOlder(options?: { force?: boolean })`）绑定到会话转录历史加载器且在分页错误重试时转发 `{ force: true }`。双语设计文档（`docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.md` 与 `docs/design/2026-11-22-chat-surface-session-locks.zh-CN.md`）记录了范围划分与理由。

```bash
npx vitest run client/chat-core/ client/i18n.test.ts client/i18n-loading.test.tsx client/daemon/useDaemonChatController.test.tsx client/daemon/chat-controller.test.ts client/daemon/chat-intents.test.ts client/daemon/permission-signals.test.ts client/adapters/transcriptAdapter.test.ts
npx tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit
npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

确认全部 10 个测试文件（282 项测试，含 `ChatSurface.test.tsx` 的 6 个会话作用域用例及 `useDaemonChatController.test.tsx` 的 `loadOlder` 用例）通过，且两个类型检查均退出 0。

### 证据（修改前后对比）

N/A —— 加法式切换前置增量；尚无生产聊天列经由共享表面渲染（视觉前后对比门属于列切换本身）。

### 已测试平台

|   操作系统   | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |

| 🪟 Windows   | N/A  |

prs.title: refactor(managed-agent): move publication OSS scope naming to the contract
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Moves the publication OSS scope-key naming (`ossScope`) from `ToolPublicationDataStore` onto `ToolPublicationContract` next to the existing `text()`/`sha256` naming helpers, static-imported at the three call sites. Behavior is unchanged; the pinned ratchet ceilings drop with the class (2483 → 2482, both the per-class pin and `GLOBAL_MAX_LINES`).

## Why it's needed

#18048 added the private helper and pushed `ToolPublicationDataStore` to 2485 lines, above its 2483 ratchet pin — `ClassSizeRatchetTest` has failed every nightly SDK Java run since (e.g. [run 44942840292](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44942840292)), and it also fails the managed-agent fast tier on PRs (it blocked #18076 today). The ratchet only moves down, so the fix is moving the logic out, not raising the ceiling. The contract class is the natural home: it already owns the store's naming and hashing helpers, and the plaintext-segments layout is part of the publication contract (#18048).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The managed-agent verification suite's `ClassSizeRatchetTest` passes on this branch (previously failing on main), and the three OSS object-key call sites in the store produce the same keys (covered by the existing publication ITs; a direct unit test for `ossScope` is added to `ToolPublicationContractTest`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — internal refactor, no UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

No local JDK on the authoring machine; verified by inspection (the moved method is verbatim, call sites unchanged via static import, pin arithmetic checked: 2485 − 4 removed lines + 1 import = 2482, matching both lowered ceilings) and by this PR's managed-agent CI lanes, which compile and run the suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none beyond a method relocation; the store's behavior is byte-identical.
- Not validated / out of scope: the chronic hosted MySQL fault-gate failures and the #17964 test-gating regression (covered by #18076) are separate nightly red components.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #18077.

prs.title: test(integration): give the editor-parity waits the shared-pool stall tier (#17544)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Raises the polling ceiling used by the interactive editor-parity acceptance suite so that a mid-turn repaint on the shared runner pool gets the same stall allowance the harness already grants the CLI at startup. The suite's local wait budget goes from 12s to 30s, and the shared wait helper triples that in CI, which lands the CI ceiling exactly on the 90s self-hosted boot tier. Both waits named in the flake report go through that one helper, so a single ceiling change covers both signatures. Every assertion, every input and every probe condition is untouched — nothing is skipped, retried, wrapped or loosened — and a small pin ships alongside so the ceiling cannot silently drift back below the boot tier.

## Why it's needed

CI Failure Patrol saw two waits in this suite expire on one commit and pass on a rerun of the same commit: the search/Tab/Escape case waiting for the model reply to become visible, and the streaming-cancel case waiting for the cancelled prompt to return to the composer. Both are waits for a repaint after a key press, and the suite is fully mocked against a local fake provider, so no real model latency is involved.

The harness already records that this shared pool stalls the very same CLI for much longer than the mid-turn ceiling allowed: the ready-prompt budget documentation describes a boot exhausting 30s on all three retries and another exhausting 90s, and grants 90s on self-hosted runners and 180s on self-hosted docker as a result. The mid-turn ceiling was 36s in CI — below the boot tier for the same host — so a stall the harness already tolerates at startup expired a wait in the middle of a test. An earlier change raised this whole family's wait ceilings for exactly this signature class; this file kept the second-lowest budget in the family while containing its longest and most interaction-dense cases.

One detail matters when reading the report: the polling helper throws only its label, never the screen it last saw, so "no content mismatch" describes the error text rather than a screen verified healthy. The investigation therefore checked the alternatives against code and captured frame evidence instead of trusting the signature. CPU contention was ruled out by pinning the whole test tree to a single core shared with three busy loops — the cases still passed, because the suite is dominated by its own fixed settles. Reply-label desynchronisation was ruled out by confirming one request per submit with matching labels and every background model caller disabled. Viewport scroll-off was ruled out by measuring the waited-for reply's row in every captured frame: it is always the newest transcript line, directly above a fixed six-row footer. The product's cancel/restore branch was traced and takes the restore path for a held stream that has already rendered content.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the suite the way the parity leg does, from `integration-tests`, with the sandbox off and retries disabled: `CI=true QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run interactive/tui-editor-parity.test.ts interactive/tui-editor-parity-wait-budget.test.ts --retry=0 --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1`. Expect all 30 cases green (29 acceptance cases plus the new pin), with the search/Tab/Escape case around 33s.

Confirm the pin actually witnesses the ceiling by reverting the budget literal to `12_000` and re-running just the pin: it must fail with `expected 36000 to be greater than or equal to 90000`. Restore the literal and it passes. This probe was run before committing, in that order.

Confirm the change is ceiling-only: the acceptance diff is one numeric literal plus an explanatory comment, with no assertion, input, key sequence or probe condition altered.

Two limits are worth knowing before reviewing. The flake did not reproduce locally — 18 pre-fix executions of the named case were green, including the harshest contention surrogate — so the ceiling is calibrated against the pool's recorded stall incidents and the existing boot policy, not against a local reproduction. And `bun` is not installed on this runner, so the bun+ink and bun+opentui legs were not exercised; if the stall is specific to the native renderer, CI remains the authority.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only change with no user-visible behavior. For the record: the CI wait ceiling moves from 36s to 90s and the local ceiling from 12s to 30s; post-fix the whole suite plus the pin passed 30/30 on two consecutive runs, and the pin failed against the pre-fix ceiling with the assertion quoted above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node v22.23.2 on Linux, driving the prebuilt bundle with `QWEN_SANDBOX=false` on the node+ink renderer leg, `CI=true` for the scaled budgets. `bun` is not installed, so the other two renderer legs were unavailable.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely stuck UI now takes up to 90s in CI and 30s locally to fail a wait, instead of 36s and 12s. The two reported cases inherit the suite's 300s per-test ceiling, so they still fail on the wait's own label. The three permissions cases pin a 90s per-test ceiling of their own; under a stall they would now report the suite timeout rather than the wait label, and they still fail either way. Local failure diagnosis for this file is correspondingly slower, which is the unavoidable consequence of the helper coupling its local and CI budgets by a factor of three.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local reproduction of the flake; the bun+ink and bun+opentui legs; and `npm run build`, which this sandbox cannot run because corepack is denied write access to its cache outside the project (`EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/home/github-runner/.cache/node/corepack/v1'`). The diff touches no workspace package — the integration tree has no manifest and is not a workspace member — so the per-package build never compiles it. `npm run typecheck` (all workspaces plus the integration program), `npm run lint` and Prettier all passed. No product code, CI machinery, shared wait policy or configuration was changed.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17544

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

提高交互式 editor-parity 验收套件所使用的轮询上限，使共享 runner 池上回合中途的重绘，获得 harness 在 CLI 启动阶段已经给予的同等卡顿余量。该套件的本地等待预算从 12s 提高到 30s，共享等待助手在 CI 中将其三倍放大，于是 CI 上限正好落在 90s 的自托管启动档位上。抖动报告中提到的两个等待都经过这一个助手，因此单处上限改动即可覆盖两个签名。所有断言、所有输入、所有探针条件均未改动——没有跳过、没有重试、没有包裹、也没有放宽——并随附一个小型 pin，使该上限不会悄悄回落到启动档位之下。

## 为什么需要它

CI Failure Patrol 看到该套件中两个等待在同一个 commit 上超时，并在同一 commit 的重跑中通过：search/Tab/Escape 用例等待模型回复可见，streaming-cancel 用例等待被取消的提示词回到输入框。两者都是按键之后等待重绘，而该套件完全基于本地 fake provider 做 mock，不涉及任何真实模型延迟。

harness 已经记录过：这个共享池让同一个 CLI 卡住的时间远超回合中途上限所允许的值——ready-prompt 预算文档描述了一次启动在三次重试中全部耗尽 30s，另一次耗尽 90s，并据此给予自托管 runner 90s、自托管 docker 180s。而回合中途的 CI 上限是 36s，低于同一主机的启动档位，于是 harness 在启动阶段已经容忍的卡顿，在测试中途让等待超时。此前已有一处改动针对完全相同的签名类别提高了整个家族的等待上限；而这个文件保留了家族中第二低的预算，却包含家族中最长、交互最密集的用例。

阅读报告时有一个细节很重要：轮询助手抛出的只有标签，从不附带它最后看到的屏幕，因此“没有内容不符”描述的是错误文本，而不是一块被验证为健康的屏幕。所以本次排查是对照代码与采集到的帧证据去核实各种可能，而不是相信签名本身。CPU 争用已被排除：把整棵测试进程树绑到与三个忙循环共享的单个核上，用例依然通过，因为该套件的时间主要花在自身的固定 settle 上。回复标签错位已被排除：确认每次提交对应一个请求且标签一致，并且所有后台模型调用方都已关闭。可视区滚出已被排除：逐帧测量被等待回复所在的行，它始终是最新的一条 transcript 行，紧邻固定的六行页脚之上。产品侧的取消/恢复分支也已追踪，对于已经渲染出内容的 held 流，它走的是恢复路径。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

按 parity leg 的方式运行该套件：在 `integration-tests` 目录下，关闭 sandbox 并禁用重试：`CI=true QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run interactive/tui-editor-parity.test.ts interactive/tui-editor-parity-wait-budget.test.ts --retry=0 --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1`。预期 30 个用例全绿（29 个验收用例加新增 pin），其中 search/Tab/Escape 用例约 33s。

要确认该 pin 真的见证了上限，可把预算字面量回退为 `12_000` 并只重跑该 pin：它必须失败并报 `expected 36000 to be greater than or equal to 90000`。恢复字面量后即通过。提交前已按此顺序执行过该探针。

确认本改动只涉及上限：验收文件的 diff 是一个数字字面量加一段解释性注释，没有任何断言、输入、按键序列或探针条件被改动。

评审前值得知道两个边界。抖动在本地没有复现——修复前命名用例的 18 次执行全部通过，其中包括最严苛的争用 surrogate——因此上限是按该池已记录的卡顿事故与既有启动策略定标的，而不是按本地复现定标的。另外本 runner 未安装 `bun`，所以 bun+ink 与 bun+opentui 两条 leg 未被执行；如果卡顿特定于原生渲染器，CI 仍是最终权威。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 仅测试改动，没有用户可见行为变化。备查：CI 等待上限从 36s 提高到 90s，本地上限从 12s 提高到 30s；修复后整个套件加 pin 连续两轮均 30/30 通过，而该 pin 面对修复前的上限失败，报上文引用的断言。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 上的 Node v22.23.2，以 `QWEN_SANDBOX=false` 在 node+ink 渲染器 leg 上驱动预构建 bundle，并用 `CI=true` 启用放大后的预算。未安装 `bun`，因此另外两条渲染器 leg 不可用。

## 风险与范围

prs.title: refactor(managed-agent): de-hash identity columns with bounded VARCHAR and canonical refs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR replaces the managed-agent identity-hash key layer with bounded text identities and reversible canonical references. Tenant and Session identity columns become budgeted `VARCHAR` columns with an explicit NO PAD collation, while overly wide or polymorphic cross-table identities use versioned, length-prefixed, ASCII-readable references instead of SHA-256 coordination keys. Admission, production SQL, row mappers, projections, schema-shape gates, and verification fixtures are migrated together so uniqueness, tenant isolation, idempotency, cursor order, and lock order remain explicit. Receipt minting, workspace/storage generated identities, extension/automation/CSI protocol IDs, content/commit/token digests, and binary payloads are preserved.

## Why it's needed

The previous schema stored many identity tuples as opaque hashes. That made tenant/session isolation and idempotency harder to audit, duplicated derivations across tables, and pushed several composite indexes toward InnoDB's key-width limit. The maintainer-approved design chooses a mixed representation: simple identities are readable bounded text, and wide/polymorphic references are reversible canonical tuples with fail-closed byte budgets. Every index is accepted at <= 3072 bytes. This keeps the coordination semantics while removing the identity-hash layer rather than merely renaming it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reviewers should confirm that the de-hashed schema preserves the old coordination outcomes: registered-Session publication retention still restricts joins through the new monotonic marker; tenant-addressed operation retries still resolve to one operation; resource/operation/runtime references still enforce the same uniqueness; storage release still refuses a tampered alias scope; and identity equality remains case/trailing-space exact. The focused H2 suites below exercise schema/catalog/projection drift, core managed stores, runtime broker repositories, child-session admission, canonical reference encoding, and the storage-release fail-closed probe. MySQL-specific type/collation/index-width gates and race suites are included but require the CI MySQL lane because no local MySQL instance was available.

Local commands used JDK 21 and Maven 3.9.9 with an isolated repository:

`mvn -Dmaven.repo.local=/tmp/qwen-managed-dehash-m2 -Dtest=ManagedSchemaTest,ManagedSchemaCatalogTest,ManagedSchemaProjectionTest,ManagedSchemaBusinessStoreTest,ManagedSchemaSessionStoreTest,ToolPublicationRetentionStoreTest,ManagedSideQueryStoreTest,SessionResourceCollectionCollectorTest,ToolPublicationCollectorTest,ManagedExtensionRecordStoreTest,AutomationLedgerStoreTest,WorkspaceRecoveryStoreTest,WorkspaceCreationStoreTest,SshWorkspaceStoreTest,ChildResultRelayStoreTest,ManagedIdentityRefTest,ChildActorIdTest test`

Result: 420 tests, 0 failures, 4 errors, 4 skipped. The 4 errors are native-media tests that cannot spawn `node` in this environment; the skipped cases are MySQL-only witnesses.

Additional affected sweep:

`mvn -Dmaven.repo.local=/tmp/qwen-managed-dehash-m2 -Dtest=ToolPublicationStoreTest,ManagedArtifactReadIntegrationTest,ManagedMcpSettingsStoreTest,ManagedCwdChangeOperationTest,WorkspaceSessionRetentionTest,ManagedSchemaPublicationStoreTest,ManagedTurnQueryTest,ManagedApprovalChangeTest,SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest,ManagedAgentApiContractTest,JdbcRepositoryTest,RuntimeBrokerFlywaySchemaTest,Issue13183RegressionTest,RuntimeExtensionMetadataControlTest,RuntimeExternalWorkspaceDrainTest test`

Result after fixes: 878 tests, 0 failures, 3 errors, 5 skipped. Two artifact fixture errors were fixed and re-verified green. The remaining local error is `ToolPublicationStoreTest.renewsTheOriginalClaimWhileScanningSlowObjectBytes`, a timing-sensitive claim-renewal probe that failed locally with the operation still PENDING; it needs CI confirmation and is not claimed as locally passed.

Final static gate:

`mvn -Dmaven.repo.local=/tmp/qwen-managed-dehash-m2 checkstyle:check checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle`

Result: BUILD SUCCESS, 0 violations in both executions across all modules. Full production and verification test sources compile.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — persistence/schema refactor, no TUI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅ focused H2 + dual Checkstyle; ⚠️ full H2/MySQL pending CI   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ not tested   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️ not tested   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21.0.12.1, Maven 3.9.9 downloaded to a task-owned `/tmp` directory, isolated Maven repository cloned from the local cache. No local MySQL/Docker; native-media tests require `node` and built `packages/core/dist`, which are absent in this worktree.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this is a large join-connected persistence refactor. Canonical reference tuples replace hash chains, so reviewers should focus on uniqueness preservation, cursor/lock-order equivalence, and fail-closed identity probes rather than only column renames.
- Not validated / out of scope: full H2 suite did not finish within the local 10-minute tool budget; MySQL 8.4 type/collation/index-width gates, race suites, and `ManagedSqlPerformanceMySqlIT` are pending CI. One timing-sensitive publication claim probe failed locally and is flagged above. TypeScript consumers that derive preserved protocol IDs were not changed.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: shared managed catalogs are expected to be recreated from V1; no V2+ migration is introduced. Over-budget identities now fail closed at admission or encode time. The synthetic child-Session actor is a bounded derived ID (`c:` + 32 hex) to stay inside the 36-character actor budget.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-11-20-managed-identity-varchar-dehash.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-20-managed-identity-varchar-dehash.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

References the managed identity VARCHAR/de-hash design and implementation plan under `docs/design/` and `docs/plans/`; no GitHub issue is auto-closed.

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A — 持久化/schema 重构，无 TUI 变化。

### 测试平台

macOS：focused H2 + 双 Checkstyle 已测；完整 H2/MySQL 待 CI。Windows/Linux：未测。

JDK 21.0.12.1，Maven 3.9.9 下载到任务专用 `/tmp` 目录，隔离 Maven 仓库从本地缓存克隆。本地无 MySQL/Docker；native-media 测试需要 `node` 与已构建的 `packages/core/dist`，本 worktree 缺失。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：这是大型 join-connected 持久化重构。canonical reference 元组替代哈希链，评审应重点关注唯一性保留、游标/锁序等价与 fail-closed 身份探针，而不仅是列改名。
- 未验证/范围外：完整 H2 套件未在本地 10 分钟工具预算内跑完；MySQL 8.4 类型/collation/索引宽度门、竞态套件与 `ManagedSqlPerformanceMySqlIT` 待 CI。一个 timing-sensitive publication claim 探针本地失败，已在上文标记。派生保留协议 ID 的 TypeScript 消费者未改动。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：共享 managed catalog 预期从 V1 重建；不引入 V2+ migration。超预算身份现在在 admission 或编码时 fail closed。子 Session 合成 actor 改为有界派生 ID（`c:` + 32 hex），以保持 36 字符 actor 预算。

设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-11-20-managed-identity-varchar-dehash.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-20-managed-identity-varchar-dehash.zh-CN.md)
