prs.title: fix(core): correct usage token accounting across the dashboard and /stats
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Token usage in the daemon status dashboard and in the cross-session statistics view now comes from the per-request usage ledger, placed on the local day each response actually happened, instead of from session summaries that carry a resumed conversation's replayed history and attribute all of it to the day the session last ran. A session record is dropped whenever its run's day span touches any ledger-covered day, so the same requests are never counted twice; a run with no ledger overlap at all keeps the previous attribution. The span rule deliberately accepts undercounting an unseparable part of a mixed-coverage run rather than double counting it. Reasoning tokens are counted once in the output breakdown, so input plus output equals the reported total. What a run persists is now only what that run itself spent, including when an interactive session resumes another conversation, and the read side keeps every run instead of collapsing them to the last one. Session counts, duration, tool calls, changed lines, skills and the per-project breakdown still come from session records over the same whole-day window, which the ledger deliberately does not carry.

## Why it's needed

On one real heavy history the dashboard reported roughly twice the tokens actually consumed for the current day, five times for seven days and seven times for thirty days; the cross-session view was 2.06x over seven days and 6.25x over thirty days, with average latency inflated too because the request denominator was inflated. Two causes dominated. A resume replays the stored conversation's telemetry into the live metrics, and those cumulative counters were then persisted as if the current run had spent them — a seven-minute resume of a long conversation was billed 45.7M tokens across 506 requests, and every further resume appended another full copy. And every token was attributed to the day the session ended, so a session that ran across three days landed entirely on one day: one session contributed 335M tokens to "today" while only 1.07M of them were actually spent that day. Separately, the output tile added reasoning tokens that chat-completions providers already include in their output count, so the breakdown did not sum to the hero total.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the daemon status Usage tab and toggle Today / 7D / 30D. The token totals, request count, input, cached and reasoning counters should equal an independent scan of the per-request ledger for the same window, and input plus output should equal the hero total. Each covered day's heatmap cell should equal that day's ledger tokens. Then open the cross-session statistics view, move to the Activity and Efficiency tabs, and cycle the range with `r`: the token total, session-independent counters, cache hit rate, average latency and per-model request counts should match the same ledger scan, and the period-over-period delta should compare only completed local days on both ledger-backed sides: the displayed window may include a partial today, but the comparison excludes that partial day on both sides rather than scaling or comparing it with full days. A single partial Today view shows no delta. To check the persist side, resume a long conversation and quit without sending anything: no usage record should be written. Run two turns of the same conversation in separate processes: both runs should survive a subsequent read, each carrying only its own spend. Note that the ledger lives under the runtime base directory, so when comparing against a frozen copy both the home and the runtime directory must be pinned, otherwise the UI reads the live, still-growing ledger.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Measured against an independent ledger scan on the same history. The "before" arm is the base revision's source driven directly; the "after" arm is this branch.

| Surface / window | Before | After | Ledger truth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-session stats, 7 days | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| Cross-session stats, 30 days | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| Dashboard output tile, today | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| Persisted record for a 400-response resume plus one live request | 401 requests / 400,000,005 input | 1 request / 5 input | 1 request / 5 input |
| Read side, two real runs of one conversation | 1 record / 30,778 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens |

On a frozen copy of the ledger, all three dashboard windows matched the oracle exactly (`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`, zero day mismatches), as did the cross-session view's tokens, requests, average latency and cache hit rate.

Rendered in a real terminal from this branch's bundle (PTY capture, cross-session tabs): Activity for 7 days showed `Tokens 11492.1m` and `Sessions 28` against an oracle of 11,492,141,679; Activity for 30 days showed `Tokens 40781.1m` and `Sessions 389` against 40,781,106,261 / 389; Efficiency for today showed `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`, `Avg Latency 5.7s` and per-model requests 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072 against 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072. Two real headless runs of one conversation, the second resuming it, produced records of 3 requests / 42,040 tokens and 2 requests / 30,778 tokens — the second did not re-bill the first.

A real Chromium session against this branch's daemon now covers the previously open browser gap. With two ledger rows and deliberately matching session records, Today rendered hero `1,100`, input `1,000`, output `100` and cache `60%`; 7D rendered `3,300`, `3,000`, `300` and `60%`, with the daily-session series labelled `runs ended per day`. The route independently returned the same numbers, and the browser emitted no page errors. A separate real PTY lifecycle used only a local mock model: one 5,000-token request in A, resume B with 10,000 stored tokens, one 7-token request in B, then `/exit`. The final file contains exactly two run-scoped records, A=5,000 and B=7. The stored 10,000 never entered either record, and exit code was 0.

Every new guard is mutation-witnessed: reverting it turns the corresponding test red, and the existing history reduces byte-identically to before (2,065 raw records, both arms returning 2,043 records / 379,387,040,763 tokens with identical per-session keys).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build and bundle, real Chromium and PTY capture, real headless and interactive CLI lifecycles against isolated temporary homes. Final focused suites: core 1168 passed, cli 165 passed, Web Shell 13 passed. The complete llm suite has 129 passes and three relaunch-provenance failures that reproduce identically on the base commit; its two exit-usage cases pass. Build, typecheck, lint and format gates are clean.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: summary windows now select whole local days, because day buckets cannot be split by hour, so the boundary day is counted in full instead of only the hours after a rolling cut-off; on the fallback path this is measurable and confined to that one day. The per-project token column stays record-derived — the ledger has no project dimension — so it now visibly disagrees with the corrected totals above it. A conversation that spans the upgrade keeps only its run deltas, so pre-upgrade activity for that id can be undercounted; undercounting an ambiguous overlap was chosen over double counting.
- Freshness and performance: `/stats` reuses aggregate tables only for completed local months and always re-reads the current and future month files, so every append is visible on the next open while completed months are parsed once. Concurrent opens also share pending reads. When a provider omits a total, it is synthesized according to the auth-aware reasoning/output convention rather than unconditionally adding thoughts. The period comparison uses only the completed local-day prefix, with the same number of disjoint complete days before it, so a partial today and DST-hour transitions cannot manufacture a change. Daemon requests retain their intentional 60-second source cache.
- Ledger scope on purpose: this daily/monthly source contains user-turn responses, not persistent telemetry for the internal `prompt_suggestion`, `forked_query`, `speculation` and `side-query:*` helpers. Those calls remain in live/session metrics, so the ledger is deliberately not an exhaustive bill for every internal compaction, memory or routing call.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux. The session-count and per-project tiles remain incomplete for sessions that never persist a usage record — on the reference history the ledger knows 633 sessions in seven days while the record file knows far fewer — which needs a ledger-backed session census and persisting usage at session end, both left as follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. One optional record field marks run-scoped writes; every reader that filters on the record version keeps working, existing history is neither rewritten nor migrated, and the dashboard payload shape is unchanged.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, and they record two first-pass findings that did not survive an independent check: a claimed session-identity divergence that the ledger disproved, and a proposed "sum the segments" dedup change that would have been a 3.1x regression on existing records.

## Linked Issues

No issue to close. Builds on the per-request ledger introduced for #4479 and on the session-swap telemetry transaction from #9833.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Daemon 状态用量面板与跨会话统计视图的 token 用量，现在取自逐请求用量台账，并落在每次响应**实际发生**的本地日上，而不再取自会话摘要——后者携带被恢复会话重放的历史，并把全部用量归到会话最后活动的那一天。一次运行的日期跨度只要触及任何台账覆盖日，其会话记录就会被丢弃，因此同一批请求不会被计两次；与台账完全不重叠的运行则沿用原有归属。对一个跨越覆盖与未覆盖状态的运行，此规则宁可少算无法安全拆分的部分，也不重复计算。输出明细中的推理 token 只计一次，因此输入加输出等于上报总量。一次运行落盘的用量现在只包含它自己花掉的部分，包括交互模式下 resume 到另一个会话的情形；读侧也会保留每一次运行，而不是收敛到最后一次。会话数、时长、工具调用、变更行数、技能以及按项目的明细仍取自同一个完整日窗口的会话记录——台账有意不携带这些。

## 为什么需要

在一份真实的重量级历史上，面板对当日报告了约两倍的实际消耗、7 天约五倍、30 天约七倍；跨会话视图 7 天为 2.06 倍、30 天为 6.25 倍，平均延迟也虚高，因为请求数这个分母被灌大了。主因有两个。其一，resume 会把已存会话的 telemetry 重放进实时指标，而这些累计计数随后被当作本次运行的消耗落盘——一次对长会话的七分钟 resume 被记为 506 个请求、45.7M token，且此后每次 resume 都再追加一份完整副本。其二，所有 token 都按会话结束日归属，于是跨三天运行的会话整体落在一天上：某会话向「今日」贡献了 335M token，而当天实际只花掉 1.07M。另外，输出 tile 还叠加了 chat-completions 类 provider 本已计入 output 的推理 token，导致明细之和不等于 hero 总量。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

打开 Daemon 状态的用量页，切换 Today / 7D / 30D。token 总量、请求数、输入、缓存与推理计数应等于对同一窗口的逐请求台账所做的独立扫描，且输入加输出应等于 hero 总量；每个被覆盖天的热力图格应等于该天的台账 token。然后打开跨会话统计视图，切到 Activity 与 Efficiency 页，用 `r` 循环区间：token 总量、与会话无关的各计数、缓存命中率、平均延迟以及逐模型请求数都应与同一次台账扫描一致，且环比两侧都只比较已完成的本地日：展示窗口可以包含未过完的今天，但比较会排除那一部分，不与完整日比较，也不按比例估算。只有不到一天的 Today 视图不显示环比。验证持久化侧：恢复一个长会话后不发送任何内容直接退出，应当不写入用量记录；在两个进程中各跑同一会话的一轮，后续读取应保留两次运行，且各自只带自己的消耗。注意台账位于运行时基目录下，因此与冻结副本对照时必须同时钉住 home 与运行时目录，否则界面读到的是仍在增长的真实台账。

### 证据（修前与修后）

以同一份历史上的独立台账扫描为准。「修前」臂直接驱动基线版本的源码，「修后」臂为本分支。

| 表面 / 窗口 | 修前 | 修后 | 台账真值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 跨会话统计，7 天 | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| 跨会话统计，30 天 | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| 面板输出 tile，今日 | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| 400 条历史响应的 resume 加一次真实请求的落盘记录 | 401 请求 / 400,000,005 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 |
| 读侧，同一会话的两次真实运行 | 1 条 / 30,778 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token |

在台账的冻结副本上，面板三个窗口全部与 oracle 精确一致（`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`，0 个日不符），跨会话视图的 token、请求、平均延迟与缓存命中率同样精确一致。

用本分支 bundle 在真实终端中渲染（PTY 抓屏，跨会话页）：Activity 的 7 天显示 `Tokens 11492.1m`、`Sessions 28`，oracle 为 11,492,141,679；Activity 的 30 天显示 `Tokens 40781.1m`、`Sessions 389`，oracle 为 40,781,106,261 / 389；Efficiency 的今日显示 `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`、`Avg Latency 5.7s`，逐模型请求 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072，oracle 为 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072。两次真实 headless 运行同一会话（第二次恢复它）分别产出 3 请求 / 42,040 token 与 2 请求 / 30,778 token——第二次没有把第一次再计一遍。

真实 Chromium 连接本分支 daemon，已补上了此前唯一缺失的浏览器验证。两条台账记录配两条等值会话记录时，Today 显示 hero `1,100`、input `1,000`、output `100`、cache `60%`；7D 显示 `3,300`、`3,000`、`300`、`60%`，按日会话序列明确标为 `runs ended per day`。独立 HTTP 读取返回同样数字，浏览器无 page error。另一组真实 PTY 生命周期全程只访问本地 mock 模型：A 发一次 5,000-token 请求，resume 带有 10,000 存量 token 的 B，再发一次 7-token 请求，最后 `/exit`。最终文件恰好有两条 run-scoped 记录：A=5,000、B=7；存量 10,000 没有混入任一记录，退出码为 0。

每个新增守卫都做了变异见证：还原它会让对应用例转红；而存量历史的归约结果与之前逐字节一致（2,065 条原始记录，两臂都返回 2,043 条 / 379,387,040,763 token，逐会话键相同）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 build 与 bundle、真实 Chromium 与 PTY 抓屏、隔离临时 home 上的真实 headless 及交互式 CLI 生命周期。最终触及套件：core 1168 passed、cli 165 passed、Web Shell 13 passed。完整 llm 套件 129 passed，另有 3 条在 base 上同样失败的 relaunch provenance 用例；退出用量两条用例通过。build、typecheck、lint、format 门禁全部干净。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：汇总窗口现在取整个本地日，因为日桶无法按小时切分，因此边界日被完整计入，而不是只计滚动截点之后的那几个小时；在回退路径上该影响可测量且只限那一天。按项目的 token 列仍是记录口径——台账没有项目维度——因此它现在与其上方已修正的总量存在可见的不一致。跨越升级时点的会话只保留运行增量，因此该 id 在升级前的活动可能被少算；对有歧义的重叠，选择少算而非重复计算。
- 新鲜度与性能：`/stats` 只复用已结束本地月份的聚合表；当前月及未来月份始终重新读取，因此每次追加都会在下一次打开时可见，而已结束月份只需解析一次。并发打开也共享未完成读取。如果 provider 未报 total，则按其 auth-aware 的 output 是否含推理进行合成，不无条件叠加 thoughts。环比只比较已完成本地日的前段及其之前等长、互不相交的完整日，因此未过完的今天和 DST 跨时制不会制造虚假变化。daemon 请求仍保留有意的 60 秒数据源缓存。
- 台账的范围是有意选择：其按日/按月内容只含用户回合回复，不持久化 `prompt_suggestion`、`forked_query`、`speculation` 与 `side-query:*` 内部 helper 的 telemetry。这些调用仍留在 live/session 指标中，因此台账刻意不是涵盖每次内部压缩、记忆或路由调用的完整账单。
- 未验证 / 范围外：Windows 与 Linux。对于从未持久化用量记录的会话，会话数与按项目 tile 仍不完整——参考历史上台账知道 7 天内有 633 个会话，而记录文件知道的远少于此——这需要台账口径的会话普查以及在会话结束时落盘用量，两者都留作后续。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增一个可选记录字段标记按运行写入；所有按记录版本过滤的读取方继续可用，存量历史既不重写也不迁移，面板载荷形状不变。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md)。两版完整同步，并记录了首轮两项未通过独立复核的发现：台账证伪的「会话身份分叉」，以及会在存量记录上造成 3.1 倍倒退的「分段求和」去重提案。

## 关联 Issue

无需关闭的 issue。构建在为 #4479 引入的逐请求台账与 #9833 的 session-swap telemetry 事务之上。

</details>

prs.title: test(managed-agent): gate the four durable existing-dir preflight tests to Linux
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gates the four durable existing-directory preflight tests in `LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryStateDirectoryTest` to Linux, matching the other eleven durable tests in the same class.

## Why it's needed

#17964 added the durable-state canonicality check (`directoryCheck` refuses a non-canonical recovery path) and gated the absent-directory tests to Linux — its commit message notes the macOS symlinked `/var/folders` TempDir trips the walk — but missed the existing-directory tests in the same class. Since then the nightly SDK Java leg fails deterministically: on macOS `@TempDir` lives under `/var` (a symlink to `/private/var`), so preflight FAILs on canonicality where two tests expect PASS/WARN; on Windows all four ERROR at `Files.setPosixFilePermissions` (no POSIX view). See nightly run 44942840292 (macOS job 136963609048, windows job 136963609253). The product behavior (durable store refuses symlinked recovery paths) is deliberate and unchanged — this only aligns test gating with the file's established pattern.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

On this branch the macOS and Windows legs of the SDK Java workflow should skip these four tests (previously 2 failures + 4 errors); the Linux leg still runs them. `sed -n '240,500p' packages/managed-agent-server/verification/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/runtimebroker/provisioning/local/LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryStateDirectoryTest.java` shows the annotations sit between `@Test` and each method, identical to the eleven existing gated tests.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only change; before/after is the CI leg outcome above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

No local JDK on the authoring machine; the change is a four-line annotation addition mirroring eleven existing usages in the same file, and the managed-agent CI lanes on this PR compile and run the class.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the two ownership tests lose macOS coverage (they would pass there with a realpath-normalized fixture); gating follows the file author's own precedent for the same root cause.
- Not validated / out of scope: the nightly's chronic hosted MySQL fault-gate family and the `ToolPublicationDataStore` class-size ratchet overage are separate issues, not addressed here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #17964 (introduced the test class and the canonicality check).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

把 `LocalRuntimeProviderFactoryStateDirectoryTest` 中四个 durable existing-directory 前置检查测试门禁到 Linux，与同类中其余十一个 durable 测试保持一致。

## 为什么需要

#17964 新增了 durable-state canonicality 检查（`directoryCheck` 拒绝非规范恢复路径），并把 absent-directory 测试门禁到 Linux——其提交说明注明 macOS 符号链接的 `/var/folders` TempDir 会触发该检查——但漏了同类的 existing-directory 测试。此后 nightly SDK Java 确定性失败：macOS 上 `@TempDir` 位于 `/var`（指向 `/private/var` 的符号链接），preflight 因 canonicality 返回 FAIL，而两个测试期望 PASS/WARN；Windows 上四个测试在 `Files.setPosixFilePermissions` 处 ERROR（无 POSIX 视图）。见 nightly run 44942840292（macOS job 136963609048、windows job 136963609253）。产品行为（durable store 拒绝符号链接恢复路径）是刻意的，不变——这里只是把测试门禁与该文件既有模式对齐。

## 评审验证

本分支上 SDK Java workflow 的 macOS 和 Windows leg 应跳过这四个测试（此前 2 失败 + 4 错误）；Linux leg 照常运行。直接查看测试文件可见注解与既有十一处门禁用法完全一致。

## 风险与范围

- 代价：两个 ownership 测试失去 macOS 覆盖（fixture 归一化后本可运行）；按该文件作者对同一根因的先例选择门禁。
- 未覆盖：nightly 的慢性 hosted MySQL 故障门家族与 `ToolPublicationDataStore` 类大小 ratchet 超线是独立问题，不在此处理。
- 破坏性变更：无。

prs.title: chore(scripts): stop generating unused core git-commit.ts
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Stops the build from generating a copy of the version and commit-hash module inside the core package. The generator now writes that module only for the CLI package, which is the only package that imports it. A new script test runs the generator in a temporary directory and checks that it writes the CLI copy and creates nothing under the core package.

## Why it's needed

The core copy was added so the Clearcut telemetry logger could report the CLI version and commit hash. That logger was removed in 37ad24b0d9 ("Remove Smart Edit tool and ClearcutLogger"), but the generator kept writing the core copy. Nothing in the repository reads it today: the generated module is imported only by the CLI's system-info view and the review sandbox (plus their tests), and the unit-test prerequisite guard checks only the CLI copy. Every build, bundle and skipped prepare still creates and rewrites a file that no code reads.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Search the repository for imports of the generated git-commit module. Only CLI sources and tests import it; nothing under the core package does.
2. Delete the core copy if your checkout still has one from an earlier build, then run `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck`. Both pass, and no core copy is created.
3. Run `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/generate-git-commit-info.test.js`. It fails against the previous generator (the core directory is created) and passes with this change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — build tooling only. The new test fails on the previous generator with "expected true to be false" for the core directory check and passes after the change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — build scripts and unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a consumer outside this repository that reads the core copy straight from a source checkout would no longer find it. Nothing in this repository does.
- Not validated / out of scope: the ignore rule for the core generated directory is kept on purpose. Existing checkouts still hold the stale file from earlier builds, and dropping the rule would surface it as an untracked file. Windows and Linux are covered by CI only.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Existing checkouts can delete the stale core copy; leaving it in place is harmless.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

构建时不再在 core 包里生成版本号和 commit hash 模块的副本。生成脚本现在只为 CLI 包写这个模块，CLI 也是唯一导入它的包。新增的脚本测试在临时目录里运行生成脚本，检查它写出了 CLI 那份，并且没有在 core 包下创建任何东西。

## 为什么需要

core 那份副本当初是为 Clearcut 遥测日志模块加的，用来上报 CLI 版本号和 commit hash。这个日志模块已在 37ad24b0d9（"Remove Smart Edit tool and ClearcutLogger"）中删除，但生成脚本仍在写 core 那份副本。如今仓库里没有任何代码读取它：生成的模块只被 CLI 的系统信息视图和 review 沙箱（以及它们的测试）导入，单元测试的前置条件检查也只检查 CLI 那份。每次 build、bundle 以及跳过 prepare 的安装，仍然会创建并重写这个没有代码读取的文件。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在仓库中搜索对生成的 git-commit 模块的导入。只有 CLI 的源码和测试导入它，core 包下没有任何导入。
2. 如果本地检出里还留着之前构建生成的 core 副本，先删除它，再运行 `npm run build` 和 `npm run typecheck`。两者都通过，且不会再生成 core 副本。
3. 运行 `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/generate-git-commit-info.test.js`。它在旧版生成脚本上失败（core 目录被创建），在本次改动后通过。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 仅涉及构建工具。新测试在旧版生成脚本上因 core 目录检查报 "expected true to be false" 而失败，改动后通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 仅涉及构建脚本和单元测试。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：如果仓库外有使用方直接从源码检出中读取 core 副本，它将找不到这个文件。本仓库内没有这样的使用方。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：有意保留 core 生成目录的忽略规则。已有的检出里仍留着之前构建生成的旧文件，去掉这条规则会让它显示为未跟踪文件。Windows 和 Linux 仅由 CI 覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。已有检出可以删除旧的 core 副本；保留它也没有影响。

## 关联 Issue

无。

prs.title: fix(ci): gate the Teams channel on its npm publishing bootstrap (#17898)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Holds the Microsoft Teams channel out of the npm release until a maintainer completes its one-time public bootstrap publish, using the same repository-variable gate the Mem0 extension already uses. The gate lives in the release package selection, so it rides the workflow-pinned checkout and applies even when the selected release ref predates this change; the release workflow contributes a single orchestration line exposing the variable, guarded to the upstream repository so a fork can never publish into the `@qwen-code` scope. The already-shipped guard and the release versioning behaviour are deliberately left untouched: Teams is still probed for an existing version, and its package and extension manifests still follow the release version. The developer documentation now names both bootstrap-gated packages and the variables that enable them.

## Why it's needed

The nightly `v0.28.0-nightly.20261119.f8d4f706ea` failed in its publish job (#17898). The Teams channel merged the same day and was the only new workspace in the release window since the last good nightly. Because it merged without `private`, it opted straight into the main npm release — but the publish job authenticates with npm trusted publishing alone, carrying no npm token, and npm only lets a maintainer bind a trusted publisher to a package that already exists. Teams has never been published, so the workflow cannot authenticate for it, and since the whole selection goes out through one recursive publish invocation under a fail-fast shell, that single package takes down the entire release rather than being skipped. This repository already documents both halves of that trap: the pnpm release design warns that a new non-private workspace opts into the release and its npm permissions and trusted publisher must be reviewed before merging, and the Mem0 extension design records the bootstrap-variable remedy for exactly this constraint. Teams was merged without either. Gating it defaults the release back to a working state immediately, while preserving the intent to distribute it once the bootstrap is done.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the default release selection no longer contains `@qwen-code/channel-msteams`, while `@qwen-code/audio-capture` and `@qwen-code/external-context-mem0` keep their existing behaviour, and that enabling the new variable on the upstream repository puts Teams back into the selection while a fork still never publishes it. Confirm the already-shipped guard still lists Teams among the packages it probes, so a partial release cannot be overwritten by a retry. The focused suites below cover all of this; each new clause was also mutation-probed by deleting or negating it and watching the corresponding test fail. After merge, a maintainer still needs to perform the one-time public bootstrap publish of Teams, bind it to the release workflow in the `production-release` environment, and then set `NPM_CHANNEL_MSTEAMS_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED` to `true`. Until then Teams is intentionally not distributed through npm; its documented local-extension install path is unaffected.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — release-pipeline behaviour, no user-visible UI change. Before: the publish selection handed a never-published package to a tokenless trusted-publishing invocation, failing the whole job. After: that package is skipped by default and re-enters the selection only when a maintainer enables its variable.

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status    |
| :--------: | :----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit and meta-test suites only (`scripts/tests` via the repository's Vitest config), plus the full build, typecheck and lint. The sandbox runs as a non-owner uid, so `COREPACK_HOME` and `npm_config_cache` were pointed at writable temporary directories for those commands; no repository file was changed to accommodate that.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Teams' npm distribution is deferred until a maintainer completes the bootstrap publish and sets the variable. That is the intended trade — a skipped package is recoverable in one release, whereas an unauthenticatable one fails every nightly. If Teams had already been bootstrapped and bound, this change would only delay its distribution by one release rather than break anything.
- Not validated / out of scope: the release workflow itself and a real npm publish were not run. This environment has no GitHub credentials, so the failed run's log could not be fetched, and publishing is a networked write that is out of bounds here. The diagnosis rests on the release-window diff, the publish job's tokenless trusted-publishing configuration, and the repository's own documented constraint and precedent; the regression witness is the selection gate and its mutation probes. The bootstrap publish, the trusted-publisher binding, and setting the repository variable remain maintainer actions. No change to Teams' runtime, its ingress, or its version alignment.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No published package is removed or renamed, and no consumer-facing contract changes. Teams was never available on npm, so nothing that users could have installed is affected.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17898

prs.title: feat(core): add local notes compaction with a strategy selector
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an opt-in local notes compaction strategy. Users can select **Summary** or **Notes and History** under **Chat Compression Strategy** in `/settings`, or set `model.chatCompression.strategy` to `summary` or `notes` in `settings.json`. Summary remains the default; changing the selection requires restarting Qwen Code.

Eligible main sessions gain `session_notes`, `session_history`, `get_context_remaining`, and `new_context`. The model can persist a bounded working checkpoint, start a smaller context from that checkpoint and the latest consumed user request, and recover omitted evidence from the active branch of its local session log. Successful notes rollovers make no summarization request. Notes revisions live in the existing JSONL transcript, with a generated Markdown projection for inspection; checkpoint persistence must succeed before active history changes. Resume, fork, rewind, archive, and deletion handle the matching notes state.

Missing, stale, or unusable notes fall back to summary for automatic and ordinary manual compression. An explicit `new_context` requires a fresh revision and reports an error if it cannot commit. `/compress <instructions>` continues to summarize, and `/compress-fast` keeps its existing behavior. The notes tool bundle respects recording availability and tool policy and is excluded from subagents, teammates, and nested code-mode calls. Ink and OpenTUI display a notes-specific transition notice.

## Why it's needed

Repeated full-history summaries can lose constraints, decisions, and tool evidence that a long task needs later. A local working checkpoint plus bounded history retrieval gives the model a way to carry forward its current state and recover details on demand. Storage and retrieval use the existing session log and require no additional memory backend. Selected notes and retrieved history still go to the configured model provider as normal inference input. Real-model quality, total token cost, and latency remain to be measured before considering a default change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the local build with no strategy configured and confirm summary behavior. Open `/settings`, search for `compression`, switch to **Notes and History**, and confirm the saved value is `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` and the restart notice appears. Restart and check that the four notes tools are available. Repeat with `summary`, including activation through `settings.json`.
2. In an isolated recorded session, have the model write notes and request a new context in separate tool-only responses using the returned revision. Repeat three times. Each new context should retain the checkpoint and current user constraints, with no summarizer request. Deliberately omit an earlier identifier from the notes, then recover it through history search/read. Resume the session and check that its latest notes revision and old history reference still work.
3. Check that missing/stale revisions, oversized notes, and notes/reset calls mixed with ordinary text or tools cannot install a new context. Disabling recording or denying a required notes tool should disable the complete bundle. After switching to a smaller model window, existing bounded notes should remain readable, while an oversized checkpoint must be shortened before it can authorize a reset.
4. Compare compression commands: `/compress` with fresh notes should use notes; missing/stale notes should fall back to summary; `/compress <instructions>` should forward those instructions to the summarizer even with fresh notes; `/compress-fast` should retain its current tool-output clearing behavior. Check that the next model request uses the committed context and that notes transitions show the notes-specific notice.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Actual tmux captures of `/settings`, with the search set to `compression`:

**Before — global `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`:**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**After — local bundle `0.24.1`:**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

The fresh-notes `/compress` case displayed `Started a new context from local notes` in the actual TUI. The complete deterministic headless/tmux run passed settings persistence, tool availability, history recovery/resume, six rejection cases, and all six manual-compression cases. After the final fixes, the rebuilt handoff rerun again committed **three distinct notes windows in 15 main requests with zero summarizer requests**; resume took three requests and restored the same notes revision and historical reference.

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run bundle` passed. Relevant core, ACP, settings/schema/i18n, and Ink/OpenTUI regression tests passed. The final focused rerun passed 23 core tests and 54 event-adapter tests; the commit hook also passed formatting and ESLint. A separate comment contains the E2E matrix and coverage limits.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js `v26.8.2`; local bundled CLI `0.24.1`; isolated temporary settings and runtime directories; deterministic localhost OpenAI-compatible provider; headless CLI and real tmux interaction. The user's normal settings and sessions were not modified by the tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: This changes core recording, compaction, and replay paths. Correctness depends on fresh notes, successful checkpoint persistence, and branch-correct recovery; note completeness still depends on the model. The Markdown file is a generated view, so editing it directly does not update canonical notes.
- Not validated / out of scope: Real-model task quality, token/cost/latency comparisons, full ACP/Web Shell E2E, other provider wire protocols, process-crash/disk/lease fault injection, and Windows/Linux execution. The deterministic E2E suite does not cover automatic/hard-overflow triggers, nested code mode, or fork/rewind/archive lifecycle operations; focused regression tests cover relevant runtime paths, without claiming end-to-end coverage. Cross-session memory, multi-file notes, and a notes editor are out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No settings migration is required. `summary` remains the default, existing transcripts remain supported, and enabling or disabling `notes` requires a restart. Ordinary compression can use summary fallback; an explicit `new_context` never silently summarizes.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up validation.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12257

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

增加可选的本地 notes 压缩策略。用户可以在 `/settings` 的 **上下文压缩方式** 中选择 **摘要** 或 **笔记与历史**，也可以在 `settings.json` 中把 `model.chatCompression.strategy` 设为 `summary` 或 `notes`。默认仍为摘要；修改选项后需要重启 Qwen Code。

符合条件的主会话获得 `session_notes`、`session_history`、`get_context_remaining` 和 `new_context` 四个工具。模型可以保存有大小限制的工作笔记，从笔记和最近已消费的用户请求启动更小的上下文，再从本地 session log 的有效分支找回遗漏证据。成功的 notes 换窗口不发起摘要请求。笔记版本保存在现有 JSONL transcript 中，并生成方便查看的 Markdown 文件；只有恢复 checkpoint 持久化成功后才替换当前历史。恢复、分叉、回退、归档和删除操作会处理对应的笔记状态。

自动压缩和普通手动压缩在笔记缺失、过期或不可用时回退到摘要。显式调用 `new_context` 必须提供新鲜的笔记版本，无法提交时返回错误。`/compress <instructions>` 继续生成摘要，`/compress-fast` 保持现有行为。笔记工具组遵循录制可用性及工具策略，并对 subagent、teammate 和嵌套 code-mode 调用关闭。Ink 和 OpenTUI 会显示专门的 notes 换窗口提示。

## 为什么需要

反复生成全历史摘要可能丢失长任务后续需要的约束、决策和工具证据。本地工作笔记加上有界历史检索，使模型能够保留当前工作状态并按需找回细节。存储和检索复用现有 session log，不需要新增 memory 后端。选中的笔记和检索出的历史仍会作为正常推理输入发送给配置的模型 provider。在考虑修改默认策略前，仍需评估真实模型的任务质量、总 token 成本和延迟。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 使用本地构建启动，不配置策略时确认仍使用摘要。打开 `/settings`，搜索 `compression`，切换到 **Notes and History**，确认保存的值为 `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` 并显示重启提示。重启后检查四个笔记工具可用。再切回 `summary`，并验证通过 `settings.json` 启用的行为一致。
2. 在隔离且开启录制的会话中，让模型先写笔记，再用返回的 revision 请求新上下文；两次调用分别放在独立且只含该工具的回复中。重复三次。每个新上下文都应保留 checkpoint 和当前用户约束，且不发起摘要请求。故意不把某个早期标识符写入笔记，再通过历史搜索和读取找回。恢复会话后，检查最新笔记版本和旧历史引用仍可用。
3. 检查缺失或过期的 revision、超限笔记，以及混入普通文本或其他工具的笔记/换窗口调用，都不能安装新上下文。关闭录制或拒绝任一必需工具后，整个笔记工具组应被关闭。切换到窗口更小的模型后，已有且满足固定大小上限的笔记仍应可读，但超过当前模型预算的 checkpoint 必须缩短后才能用于换窗口。
4. 对比压缩命令：笔记新鲜时 `/compress` 应使用笔记；笔记缺失或过期时应回退到摘要；即使有新鲜笔记，`/compress <instructions>` 也应把指定要求转交摘要模型；`/compress-fast` 应保留现有清理工具输出的行为。检查下一次模型请求使用已提交的上下文，且 notes 换窗口显示对应提示。

### 证据（前后对比）

以下为真实 tmux 捕获的 `/settings` 画面节选，搜索词为 `compression`：

**修改前：全局 `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`：**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**修改后：本地 bundle `0.24.1`：**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

使用新鲜笔记执行 `/compress` 时，真实 TUI 显示 `Started a new context from local notes`。完整的确定性 headless/tmux 测试通过了设置持久化、工具可用性、历史找回与会话恢复、六项拒绝场景以及全部六项手动压缩场景。最终修复后重新构建并复测交接，再次在 **15 次主模型请求中提交了三个不同的 notes 窗口，摘要请求为零**；恢复过程使用三次请求，恢复了相同的笔记版本和历史引用。

`npm run build`、`npm run typecheck` 和 `npm run bundle` 均通过。相关 core、ACP、设置/schema/国际化、Ink/OpenTUI 回归测试均通过。最后的针对性复测通过了 23 个 core 测试和 54 个 event-adapter 测试；提交钩子的格式和 ESLint 检查也通过。另附评论列出 E2E 场景矩阵和覆盖范围。

### 测试平台

| 平台 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS arm64、Node.js `v26.8.2`、本地 CLI bundle `0.24.1`；使用隔离的临时设置和 runtime 目录、确定性的 localhost OpenAI 兼容模型服务、headless CLI 和真实 tmux 交互。测试未修改用户日常使用的设置和会话。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：涉及 core 的录制、压缩和回放路径。正确性依赖笔记新鲜度、checkpoint 成功持久化以及有效分支恢复；笔记内容是否完整仍依赖模型。Markdown 文件只是生成视图，直接编辑不会更新权威笔记。
- 未验证或不在范围内：真实模型任务质量、token/成本/延迟对比、完整 ACP/Web Shell E2E、其他 provider 的通信协议、进程崩溃/磁盘/写入租约故障注入，以及 Windows/Linux 运行。确定性 E2E 未覆盖自动/硬溢出触发、嵌套 code mode 或分叉/回退/归档生命周期操作；针对性回归测试覆盖了相关运行时路径，但不代表完成了这些场景的端到端验证。跨会话记忆、多文件笔记和笔记编辑器不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无需迁移设置。默认仍为 `summary`，继续支持已有 transcript；开启或关闭 `notes` 需要重启。普通压缩可以回退到摘要；显式 `new_context` 绝不会悄悄改用摘要。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md)。两个版本完整同步，包括决策、约束、验收标准和后续验证。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #12257

</details>

prs.title: test(cli): deflake the admitted-mutation idle-timer case (#18053)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Stabilizes the hosted-harness idle-suspension test that checks an admitted mutation re-arms the session's idle timer. The test's idle window and its two waiting periods are scaled up by the same factor, so the proportion between them — and therefore everything the test proves — is unchanged, while the absolute tolerance around each timing boundary grows from roughly 400 ms to 1600 ms. Every assertion, request payload and expected status code is preserved exactly; nothing is skipped, loosened, retried or wrapped, and no production code changes.

## Why it's needed

CI Failure Patrol observed this test failing and then passing on a rerun of the same commit, which is the definitive flaky signature. The failure is a timing race, not a product defect: the test brackets a real suspension timer with two fixed sleeps, and both of its boundaries have only about 400 ms of slack. On a contended shard a 600 ms timer callback routinely fires hundreds of milliseconds late, which is enough to cross either boundary — the mutation then arrives after the session has already suspended, or the residency check happens after the re-armed deadline. Both directions were reproduced locally by injecting the overshoot a starved event loop produces, yielding `expected 200 "OK", got 404 "Not Found"` on the mutation and `expected 404 to be 200` on the residency check. The second matches the signature reported in the issue verbatim. In both reproductions the harness itself behaved correctly, so the nondeterminism lives entirely in the test's timing budget.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm the test still fails when the behaviour it pins is broken, and that it now tolerates the stall that used to break it.

First, discrimination: with this change in place, temporarily negate the middleware guard that resets the idle timer for admitted mutations. The test must still fail on its residency check with `expected 404 to be 200` (observed at 4941 ms). This is the important property — widening the window did not turn the assertion into a tautology. Restore the guard afterwards.

Second, tolerance: inject a fixed overshoot into the test's two waiting periods to emulate late timer callbacks on a loaded shard. A +700 ms overshoot breaks the pre-change test in both directions, but the post-change test passes (7541 ms); even a +1200 ms overshoot is absorbed (7952 ms). Without any injected stall the test passes repeatedly (7526 ms, 7549 ms, 6975 ms).

Third, no collateral damage: the whole idle-suspension block passes (17 tests), and the entire touched file passes (872 tests). The neighbouring cases are untouched, including the shared sleep helper.

A reviewer should also confirm the residency check still lands *after* the worst-case original deadline: with the new numbers the original timer can fire as late as 4400 ms and the check happens at about 4800 ms, so a harness that failed to re-arm would still be caught.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only timing change, no user-visible or TUI behavior.

Before, with a +700 ms late-callback stall:

```
× idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer
  → expected 200 "OK", got 404 "Not Found"        (pre-mutation stall)
  → expected 404 to be 200 // Object.is equality   (post-mutation stall)
```

After, with the same stall and with a 3× larger one:

```
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7541ms   (+700ms stall)
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7952ms   (+1200ms stall)
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7008ms   (no stall)
```

After, with the production reset guard negated (discrimination witness):

```
× idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  4941ms
  → expected 404 to be 200 // Object.is equality
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, run from the CLI package against the workspace sources. Build, typecheck and lint were run from the repository root. One environment deviation was necessary: the sandbox denies writes to the default corepack cache directory, so those three commands were run with `COREPACK_HOME` pointed at a writable system-temp directory to let the shim resolve the pinned pnpm. No repository or configuration file was changed for this, and no check was skipped.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the test now takes about 7 s instead of about 1.9 s, adding roughly 5 s to the file's runtime. That is the deliberate cost of buying 4× the timing tolerance; the per-test ceiling (15 s locally, 60 s on the contended pools) still leaves ample headroom, and the concluding wait keeps about 3 s of its own budget in reserve.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows were not run locally. The neighbouring idle-suspension cases use the same fixed-sleep pattern with even tighter margins and are left alone, since this issue names one test and the deflake workflow requires the diff to stay local to it. No production behavior, CI definition, configuration or dependency was touched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18053

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

稳化 hosted-harness 空闲挂起测试中「已准入的变更会重新武装 Session 空闲定时器」这一用例。把该用例的空闲窗口与两段等待期按同一倍数放大，因此它们之间的比例——也就是用例所证明的全部内容——保持不变，而每个时序边界的绝对容忍度从约 400 ms 增加到 1600 ms。所有断言、请求负载与期望状态码都被完整保留；没有跳过、放宽、重试或包裹任何内容，也没有改动任何生产代码。

## 为什么需要

CI Failure Patrol 观察到该用例在同一 commit 上先失败、重跑后通过，这是 flaky 的确凿签名。失败属于时序竞态，而非产品缺陷：用例用两段固定 sleep 去夹住一个真实的挂起定时器，两个边界都只有约 400 ms 余量。在高负载分片上，600 ms 的定时器回调经常晚数百毫秒触发，这足以跨过任一边界——于是变更在 Session 已挂起之后才到达，或者驻留检查发生在重新武装后的截止时间之后。两个方向都已在本地通过注入事件循环被饿死时产生的超出量复现，分别得到变更请求上的 `expected 200 "OK", got 404 "Not Found"` 与驻留检查上的 `expected 404 to be 200`。后者与 issue 中记录的签名逐字吻合。两次复现中 harness 自身行为都正确，因此非确定性完全来自用例的时序预算。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

确认用例在其所钉住的行为被破坏时仍然失败，并且现在能容忍过去击垮它的那种停顿。

第一，区分能力：在本改动基础上，临时把中间件中为已准入变更重置空闲定时器的守卫取反。用例必须仍在驻留检查处以 `expected 404 to be 200` 失败（实测在 4941 ms）。这是关键性质——放大窗口并没有把断言变成恒真式。验证后请还原守卫。

第二，容忍度：向用例的两段等待期注入固定超出量，以模拟高负载分片上迟到的定时器回调。+700 ms 的超出量会在两个方向上击垮改动前的用例，但改动后的用例通过（7541 ms）；即使 +1200 ms 的超出量也被吸收（7952 ms）。不注入任何停顿时，用例重复通过（7526 ms、7549 ms、6975 ms）。

第三，无附带损伤：整个空闲挂起区块通过（17 个用例），整个被改文件通过（872 个用例）。相邻用例未被触碰，包括共享的 sleep 辅助函数。

审阅者还应确认驻留检查仍落在最坏情况原始截止时间**之后**：按新数值，原始定时器最晚可在 4400 ms 触发，而检查发生在约 4800 ms，因此未能重新武装的 harness 仍会被抓住。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 仅测试时序改动，无用户可见或 TUI 行为变化。

改动前，注入 +700 ms 迟到回调停顿：

```
× idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer
  → expected 200 "OK", got 404 "Not Found"        (变更前停顿)
  → expected 404 to be 200 // Object.is equality   (变更后停顿)
```

改动后，同样的停顿以及 3 倍大的停顿：

```
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7541ms   (+700ms 停顿)
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7952ms   (+1200ms 停顿)
✓ idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  7008ms   (无停顿)
```

改动后，将生产重置守卫取反（区分能力见证）：

```
× idle suspension > an admitted mutation resets the idle timer  4941ms
  → expected 404 to be 200 // Object.is equality
```

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元测试，从 CLI 包针对工作区源码运行。构建、类型检查与 lint 从仓库根目录运行。有一处必要的环境偏差：沙箱禁止写入默认 corepack 缓存目录，因此这三条命令运行时把 `COREPACK_HOME` 指向可写的系统临时目录，以便 shim 解析锁定版本的 pnpm。为此未改动任何仓库或配置文件，也没有跳过任何检查。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险 / 取舍：用例现在耗时约 7 s，而非约 1.9 s，为该文件增加约 5 s 运行时间。这是换取 4 倍时序容忍度的有意代价；单用例上限（本地 15 s，高负载池 60 s）仍留有充足余量，结尾的等待也保留了约 3 s 自有预算。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：未在本地运行 macOS 与 Windows。相邻的空闲挂起用例使用同样的固定 sleep 模式且余量更紧，此处不予改动，因为本 issue 只指名一个用例，而 deflake 流程要求 diff 局限于该用例。未触碰任何生产行为、CI 定义、配置或依赖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

prs.title: fix(core): retain oversized transcript indexes in a bounded cache class
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gives transcript indexes whose byte estimate exceeds the shared 64 MiB index-cache budget their own bounded retention class (256 MiB, LRU eviction within the class) instead of refusing them admission on every request, and makes hook-turn aggregate retention account against the entry's own budget class so a cached large index cannot block hook retention on small sessions. The shared byte budget keeps capping small-session retention exactly as before; the two classes never evict each other by byte budget. Worst-case byte retention is the sum of both budgets (320 MiB), and the constant comment records the remaining residuals explicitly.

A review round on the merged head then closed three reproduced gaps in the new retention: a frozen cursor could serve rewritten bytes after an equal-size in-place rewrite (the page path now applies the same equal-size mtime validation the turn-index path already had); Managed message projections retained alongside a cached index now account their decoded bodies against the same class budget and are dropped when they do not fit (including projections decoded before their index is offered to the cache); and admitting a newer snapshot of the same file now evicts superseded older prefixes when the class budget is full, so an append no longer leaves every subsequent page reparsing while the dead prefix holds the budget. Capacity contracts in the design docs are updated in both languages.

A full high-effort review (17 agents + verifiers, two dry reverse-audit rounds) and a delta reverse-audit pair then hardened the retention further: superseded-snapshot eviction also covers equal-size orphans left unreachable by an in-place rewrite or replacement (within the entry's budget class only — cross-class eviction is deliberately absent because freeing shared bytes cannot admit an oversized index); the readPage projection retention delegates to the shared admission helper instead of duplicating its arithmetic; the projection byte estimate folds per record rather than stringifying the whole decoded history at once (bounding the transient allocation to the largest record); and a completed index build re-verifies its frozen snapshot before admission or eviction, so a build that finishes after the file was rewritten under it neither caches a torn index nor evicts the live newer entry as an orphan. Each guard ships a regression test verified to go red when the guard is removed.

The latest review round closed the remaining confirmed findings: both admission doors now sum the reclaimable superseded bytes and evict only when the new snapshot fits after the reclaim, so a refused admission no longer evicts the still-readable frozen prefix it cannot replace; projection and hook retention choose the budget class from the post-add entry total (a shared entry whose retained bodies cross the shared budget moves into the oversized class instead of being refused against a budget it no longer belongs to), through one helper shared by every retention site; and the snapshot-anchored half of the equal-size rewrite guard gained its missing regression test. The rewrite-then-append bypass found by the bot review is reproduced and documented as a pre-existing residual in both design-doc languages (page bodies are read live at the frozen offsets, so the equal-size mtime guard cannot see a rewrite followed by an append); frozen-prefix digest validation is listed as deferred work because it re-reads the prefix on every frozen page and touches the cursor contracts.

The next review round reproduced two concurrent P1s with one root cause — waiters on a shared index build received the raw build promise, bypassing the initiator's snapshot re-verification and admission — and a projection P2. The cache entry's pending is now a wrapper promise that runs build, re-verification and admission, so a snapshot rewritten under a shared build fails every sharer closed instead of serving torn bytes, and a projection can only attach after admission (the admission door also accounts any attached projection, the same contract as the restore-offer door). A transient stat error on the re-verification serves the built snapshot uncached instead of failing a ready page. The post-add class helper now reclaims superseded same-file snapshots when they block a projection's class crossing, fit-before-evict, so an appended Managed session's new projection replaces the old one instead of being refused and re-decoded per page. The identity arm of the orphan predicate gained its missing test (same-size replacement at a new inode with pinned mtime).

The following re-review found the last verification gap: the single-entry cap refusal and the stale-completion return still ran before the post-build re-verification, so a frozen cursor sharing a build whose entry was LRU-evicted mid-build or whose index exceeded the class budget could receive rewritten bytes. The re-verification now precedes every early return in the shared completion — cache-entry ownership only governs cache writes and deletes, never whether the built index is safe to serve. The same round extended the superseded predicate to the shrink direction (a truncated longer prefix is unreachable dead weight), applied the fit-before-evict reclaim to the restore-offer door's 32-entry count cap, consolidated the duplicated Managed test fixtures, added a route-level cross-request index-reuse test, and corrected the design docs (the count cap is a global LRU, not class-isolated; section references point at the real heading).

The bot's next review confirmed those fixes and deferred eight items; all eight are dispositioned in the following commit. The one fix-induced regression among them is corrected: the direction-agnostic superseded predicate let a frozen-prefix admission reclaim the live newer index, so the predicate is now temporal (strictly older snapshots reclaimable in either size direction; equal-mtime larger entries — the live index a frozen read sees — protected; equal-size equal-mtime identity-changed orphans unchanged). The unreachable admission-side projection accounting was removed (projections attach only after the shared verified admission; the offer door keeps its reachable call), the route-level reuse test now exercises the oversized class, the count-cap offer test covers both classes, the allowAppend success arm gained a concurrent test, and the docs correct the refused-admission rationale, a zh mistranslation, and mark the older selective-session-restore design superseded in part.

The bot's round-5 review added nine suggestions, all dispositioned in the next two commits. Substantive: the restore-offer count-slot reclaim became class-agnostic (a full 32-entry cap can now be relieved by a superseded same-file entry in the other class; the byte arm stays class-scoped), and in-flight build placeholders are exempt from the count-cap LRU with pending hits refreshing recency, so unrelated admissions no longer discard a completing index. The rest are test strengthening (entries-after-offer, deterministic equal-mtime reclaim, stale-completion witnessing via a cleared entry, retention-vs-rebuild entries assertions, shared-full hook refusal) and doc disposition: the legacy single-language restore design is restored to its pre-PR state while the bilingual design explicitly supersedes its three cache rules.

The bot's round-6 review then posted zero new findings and reached approve posture (downgraded to Comment only by the attributed main-side Java CI red). Its eight deferred items are dispositioned in the final commit: the hook-aggregate crossing-reclaim test (mutant-witnessed), removal of the redundant pending-hit recency refresh, the concurrent-projection test renamed to what it pins, the hook fixture typed, and doc precision fixes; the three behavior-preserving polish items (predicate/class DRY refactor, estimate caching, fixture consolidation) are deferred with reasons as follow-up work on converged code.

A further re-review then found that unreachable old indexes held the budget when the mtime did not advance (a backup replacement restoring an older mtime, or a same-millisecond truncation). The superseded predicate now reclaims entries the current file state has left unreachable — changed identity, length beyond the current file, or equal size at a different mtime — regardless of temporal order, while a frozen-prefix read still never reclaims the live newer index. Both reviewer scenarios were re-run at scale (106,085 records, 137 MiB index, default budgets): the second read after each mutation now hits in 10 ms / 5 ms instead of rebuilding. Regression tests pin mtimes explicitly for fast and slow filesystems; four clause-removal mutants each red exactly their test.

The next re-review (static plus a dynamic re-run of the round-9 scenarios) found three issues in that reclaim, all fixed with mutation-witnessed regression tests. (1) The reclaim branch issued a second, uncaught `fsp.stat` after the ownership check and the class budget math: a transient stat error there rejected the whole shared build with a raw system error, and a rewrite or concurrent admission landing in that await window could evict the live newer entry or overwrite a re-owned slot. The re-verification now returns the verified current file length through a shared helper, and the entire admission tail — ownership check, budget math, reclaim, cache write — runs synchronously against that one verified state. (2) The growth-accounting door passed the entry's own frozen snapshot length as the current file state, so a frozen hook aggregate or Managed projection could reclaim the appended live index as unreachable (and a replacement during the async decode could do the same through the identity clause). The unreachable clauses now require a verified current file state: the admission and offer doors pass it, the frozen hook/decode doors reclaim by temporal order alone. (3) The completion wrote over the placeholder key in place, leaving it at the LRU head the count-cap prune scans first; the completion now deletes before setting, landing at the MRU tail. Main is merged for the Java gate, which is green on main again.

The following re-review confirmed those fixes and reproduced one more P2: an in-place sync that appends on the same inode and then restores an older source timestamp broke the temporal reclaim clause in both directions — the live admission could not reclaim the shorter prefix (its mtime was newer), and a frozen read evicted the longer live index (its mtime was older). Supersession is now decided by length, never by mtime order: under the append-only read model a same-identity strictly shorter prefix is contained in the incoming snapshot and reclaimable fit-before-evict, while a longer same-identity index still serves the frozen offsets and is protected. The verified doors apply that rule plus the unreachable clauses; the frozen growth doors reclaim only same-identity strictly shorter prefixes and protect longer or foreign-identity entries, which may be the live index. The reviewer's scenario re-run at scale (106,085 records, 137 MiB index, default budgets, append + mtime −60 s): repeats now hit at 10 ms after one rebuild instead of rebuilding every read, and a frozen-cursor read no longer evicts the live index. Four regression tests (live reclaim + frozen protection double assertion, hook and Managed mtime-regression retention, shorter foreign-identity replacement during a paused decode) and seven mutants (M48–M54) witness the rule; the design docs state it in both languages.

The next re-review confirmed the length rule at scale and found one more P3 in it: an in-place truncation overlapping a frozen hook or projection read leaves the current full index shorter than the frozen snapshot at the same identity, and the growth doors reclaimed it as a historical prefix (one extra rebuild of the current page). Frozen growth now stats the live file when retention is accounted and reclaims only entries strictly shorter than the live length — the live index always equals that length, so it is protected; a failed stat refuses retention instead of reclaiming blind, the growing entry is excluded from its own reclaim scan, and slot ownership plus concurrent retention are re-checked after the stat so the fit/reclaim/write tail stays synchronous. Four regression tests (hook and Managed truncation races, a transient-stat arm, self-exclusion, and a hook-retention reclaim the admission door cannot preempt) and seven mutant runs (M55–M60) witness the rule; the design docs state it in both languages.

A default-config before/after A/B on the real daemon routes (review 6004557763) confirms the user-visible benefit: with the issue's 84k-record / 224 MB transcript (index estimate ≈ 104 MiB, over the 64 MiB shared budget), the base arm rebuilt the index on every page of both the workspace route and the singular route (~1.6 s/page); at this head the default Web Shell path (workspace route, daemon-local cache) serves repeat pages and 50-record cursor chains at ~17–23 ms after one build, unaffected by ACP child lifecycle, and the singular route stops rebuilding per page while its child lives. Measurements and method: issuecomment-7062923319.

The default Web Shell conversation path (`GET /session/:id/transcript`) originally read through the ACP child, whose module-local index cache died with the child on session switch, idle TTL, or daemon restart. The workspace route's daemon-local read is now extracted into a shared helper and the default route serves from it too, so the daemon-side index cache survives child exit. Ownership resolution, cursor compatibility (the persisted per-workspace key the ACP child also signs with), and the live-flush barrier are preserved. Real-daemon A/B: after SIGKILL of the ACP child the default route serves the next page in ~16 ms versus ~2.9 s cold rebuild before; the 14 singular-route tests are rewritten to drive the daemon-local path, with a no-child index-reuse regression and a revert-to-bridge mutation witness (issuecomment-7063366983 F1, review 6004557763).

## Why it's needed

#17889 measured that `GET /session/:id/transcript` costs the same wall-clock time regardless of `limit` and `cursor`: on a 199.9 MB / 84,352-record session every request — including `limit=1`, identical repeats, and cursor continuations — took ~4.2 s and stalled the daemon event loop for unrelated clients. The root cause is the cache admission policy: any index whose estimate exceeds the shared 64 MiB budget was refused outright, so the sessions that most need the cache could never enter it and reparsed the whole JSONL on every page. A 16.5 MiB control session proved the cache mechanism itself works (repeat requests hit in 0.6 ms); the only behavioral difference was the admission decision. This PR fixes that admission cliff for the daemon-local read paths (the workspace-qualified route Web Shell uses, restore projections, turn index, and long-lived ACP children), and keeps the new retention honest about snapshot validity and memory.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Unit suites (from `packages/core`): `npx vitest run src/services/session-transcript-reader.test.ts src/services/session-hook-history.test.ts` → 246 passed (reader 225 + hook-history 21); the 8 core reader/consumer suites → 748 passed, and the 2 cli route suites (multi-workspace-sessions + hosted-harness-session) → 1093 passed, all on the merged tree. The regression tests cover: oversized retention serves repeats/cursor pages without rebuilding; a second oversized index that does not fit the class budget is refused without evicting the first; oversized pruning never touches shared entries; appends invalidate a retained oversized index; mixed-class admission and hook retention account by class, not total bytes; the restore/offer path caches an oversized index for later pages; frozen cursors and snapshot anchors are rejected after an equal-size in-place rewrite in both budget classes; a newer snapshot makes room by evicting superseded same-file prefixes (shared-class and cross-class protection, both admission doors) while old frozen cursors still read their original prefix; equal-size orphans are evicted to admit the live snapshot; a stale equal-size build cannot evict the live newer entry; a refused admission (new snapshot cannot fit even after reclaiming the superseded prefix) keeps the prefix cached and its frozen cursor hitting, in both classes and at both doors; a retained Managed projection is accounted against the class budget via both the readPage door and the restore-offer door (tight budget re-decodes, generous budget retains and accounts), including a projection that moves its entry from the shared into the oversized class; hook aggregates cross the class boundary the same way; a projection that crosses into a full target class reclaims the superseded same-file entry; concurrent pages sharing a rebuilt snapshot all fail closed when it was rewritten under the build; a projection attached while the build was pending is accounted at admission; a transient stat error on the admission re-verify serves the page uncached; an equal-size replacement at a new inode with pinned mtime is evicted as an orphan; a truncated longer prefix is evicted to admit the live snapshot; the restore-offer door reclaims a superseded slot at a full 32-entry count cap; the concurrent fail-closed matrix covers resident, mid-build LRU-evicted, and over-cap completions; and a route-level test pins cross-request index reuse on the workspace-qualified HTTP surface in the oversized class; a frozen-prefix admission never reclaims the live newer index; a shared build only appended under admits for every sharer; the reclaim branch issues no second stat (a per-path call-position fault injector pins that a transient error at the hypothetical reclaim-stat position never fires, and a call-position hook reproduces the reviewer's rewrite-during-reclaim interleaving — frozen sharers serve frozen content, no newer build under the stale completion); frozen hook retention and frozen Managed projection retention refuse without evicting the live newer index (including a paused-decode inode-replacement race); and a completing placeholder lands at the MRU tail, surviving its own count-cap prune and the next unrelated admission. Four existing tests were updated to the new contract with their intent preserved.
2. Mutation witnesses (each mutation applied to the production source, run, and restored — fifty-nine in the main loop, plus verifier-executed mutants): reverting oversized admission, reverting hook class accounting, cross-class prune eviction, total-byte accounting at all three sites, reverting the offer hunk, reverting the equal-size mtime check, dropping orphan eviction, hardcoding the eviction class filter to oversized, deleting the class filter, removing offer-side eviction, making the projection admission helper a no-op, disabling the completed-build snapshot re-verification, evict-before-fit at the read door, evict-before-fit at the offer door, pre-add class selection, dropping the snapshot half of the rewrite guard, reverting the changed-snapshot throw to a return, moving the stale return back before it, reverting the shrink arm, removing the offer count-cap reclaim, reverting the predicate to direction-agnostic, restricting the older clause to smaller entries, ## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: worst-case index-cache byte retention rises from 64 MiB to 320 MiB per process (estimate caliber; an independent heap probe measured real heap ≈ 0.63× the estimate — heapDelta/estimate = 0.632 on a 30k-record probe — so 320 MiB of estimate corresponds to ~202 MiB of real heap). Retention stays bounded by the two class budgets, the 5-minute TTL, and LRU eviction; small-session retention is unchanged. Managed projections and hook aggregates count against the budget class the entry belongs to after the addition; an entry whose retained bodies cross the shared budget moves into the oversized class, and the combined entry is dropped from retention when it does not fit. A low-confidence review finding about coordinating the oversized budget with the experimental `--child-heap-mode enforce` 512 MiB floor is deferred to maintainer heap-policy discussion (the floor is not the default; default `observe` applies nothing).
- Behavior change beyond caching: a frozen cursor or snapshot now returns `transcript_snapshot_unavailable` when the file was rewritten in place at the same size with a moved mtime — the same validation the turn-index path already applied. Pure appends keep frozen prefixes readable. This closes a stale-snapshot hole that also existed for small cached indexes. Concurrent requests sharing an index build now share its verified completion: if the snapshot was rewritten or replaced under the build, every sharer receives `transcript_snapshot_unavailable` (previously waiters could receive the torn build result); a transient stat error (`EMFILE`/`EIO`/`EACCES`) on the post-build re-verification serves the built snapshot uncached rather than returning 500. The re-verification precedes every early completion return (cap refusal, stale completion), so no unverified build result is served except that documented best-effort path. Superseded-snapshot reclaim covers both size directions and the offer door's count cap.
- Not validated / out of scope: a uuid-preserving in-place rewrite followed by an append is not detected (pre-existing; the equal-size guard added here cannot see it because the size grew, and page bodies are read live at the frozen offsets even on a cache hit) — frozen-prefix digest validation is documented as deferred work in both design-doc languages. The legacy singular route with default `--channel-idle-timeout-ms 0` still reaps the ACP child after each page, discarding its in-process cache (documented in `docs/users/qwen-serve.md`; mitigation: a positive idle timeout) — the daemon-local workspace-qualified route and long-lived children benefit directly. The first cold read still pays the one-time full parse; appends invalidate the frozen key, and the newer snapshot is admitted by evicting superseded same-file prefixes when it fits after the reclaim (incremental tail extension remains a follow-up). Sessions whose index estimate exceeds 256 MiB (dense short records can reach this well below the 256 MiB file-size cap) still rebuild per page — the constant comment documents this cliff. The 32-entry count cap remains global, so an oversized entry can occupy a slot a warm small index held (at most three oversized entries fit the class budget).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The cache is process-internal; no API, cursor, or schema change. ## 为什么需要

#17889 实测 `GET /session/:id/transcript` 的耗时与 `limit`、`cursor` 无关：199.9 MB / 84,352 记录的会话上，每个请求——包括 `limit=1`、完全相同的重复请求、cursor 翻页——都耗时约 4.2 秒，并阻塞 daemon 事件循环、拖慢无关客户端。根因是缓存准入策略：估算超过共享 64 MiB 预算的索引被直接拒绝，最需要缓存的会话永远进不了缓存，每页都全量重解析 JSONL。16.5 MiB 对照会话证明缓存机制本身有效（重复请求 0.6 ms 命中），唯一的行为差异就是准入决定。本 PR 修复 daemon 本地读取路径（Web Shell 使用的 workspace 限定路由、restore 投影、turn index、长活 ACP 子进程）的准入悬崖，并让新保留机制对快照有效性与内存保持诚实。

3. issue 规模探针（源码级，路由最终委托的同一函数 `SessionTranscriptReader.readPage`，无 mock）：合成 84,352 记录 / 204.6 MiB 线性链 transcript，满足 reader 校验。修复前，缓存键逐字节相同的连续十个请求每次都记录 `index cache skipped oversized entry byteSize=108984066` 并全量重建（每次约 1.7–1.9 秒，事件循环间隙 378–439 ms）。修复后，首个请求构建一次并保留 103.9 MiB 索引；重复、游标页、向后页均命中缓存。
4. 先验后逐探针（同一 harness、默认预算）：A+3 填充会话占满共享类 62,021,256 B / 4 条目；A 从 12,000 增至 20,000 条，新估算回收旧前缀后仍放不下。被拒新快照构建一次（376.9 ms）；缓存统计不变；旧冻结游标 2.2 ms 命中无重建；填充会话 0.9 ms 保持热。先逐出后拒收的变异体在同一探针下失败。
5. 合并树重验：分支干净合并最新 `origin/main`；合并树上全量 build + bundle 与 core typecheck 通过，reader/消费方套件通过。

### 证据（前后对比）

非 UI 改动；84,352 记录 / 204.6 MiB 夹具上的请求级实测（连续请求、静态文件、Node v26.12.1）：

| 请求 | 修复前 | 修复后 | 修复后全量索引构建次数 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit=1` 首次 | 1837.6 ms，缓存空 | 1892.2 ms，索引保留（108,984,066 字节） | 1（一次性） |
| `limit=10` | 1743.2 ms | 10.4 ms | 0 |
| `limit=120` | 1721.7 ms | 15.0 ms | 0 |
| `limit=500` | 1724.0 ms | 36.2 ms | 0 |
| `limit=1` 重复 ×3 | 1824.9 / 1753.4 / 1694.8 ms | 11.2 / 9.1 / 9.3 ms | 0 |
| 游标页 `limit=10` | 1707.4 ms | 10.4 ms | 0 |
| `direction=backward&limit=1` | 1647.0 ms | 9.7 ms | 0 |
| 重复请求最大事件循环间隙 | 378–439 ms | 3.8–5.7 ms | — |

小对照（6,800 记录 / 16.5 MiB）不变：首次 155.5 ms，重复 0.7 ms。门禁：合并树 `npm run build && npm run bundle` exit 0；core `tsc --noEmit` exit 0；全部改动文件 prettier + eslint 干净。

真实 daemon 验证（从构建 bundle 起隔离 qwen serve，同一 84,352 记录 / 204.6 MiB 夹具注入工作区，真实 HTTP 路由）：workspace 限定路由首页构建一次（1811 ms）、重复命中缓存（12.8–17.8 ms）、游标页 16.2 ms、`limit=500` 58.8 ms / 625 事件；追加一条记录后新快照获准入、其重复命中（11.4 ms）；等长原地改写使冻结游标返回 `409 transcript_snapshot_unavailable`。一次性冷重建期间，并发小会话 ping 保持 5–11 ms，仅一处解析后同步段例外（最大 358 ms）；热请求不阻塞并发客户端，daemon stall 监控记录为零。先验后逐场景也在合并树 bundle 上经 HTTP 确认：A+3 填充会话占满共享类（冷 330.4 / 255.8 / 212.7 / 203.2 ms，A 热重复 6.1 ms）；A 文件从 30.5 MB 增至 50.8 MB 后，被拒新首屏构建一次 352.6 ms，旧冻结游标 200 返回仅 6.5 ms 无重建，被拒快照重解析 337.2 ms（已记录残余），填充会话 5.7 ms 保持热，stall 监控为零。首个无游标 backward 页付路由既有的 live-flush 屏障（ACP 子进程独立进程一次性冷构建约 1.9 s；backward 重复 24.2 ms，文件 size/mtime 不变）——已记录的 ACP 子进程残余，非 daemon 本地缓存。 真实环境确认的残余：冷构建的一次性解析后同步段（worker 线程索引为已记录的后续项）、legacy singular 路由默认 idle timeout 下的每页子进程回收（workspace 限定路由是 Web Shell 使用的表面）。

评审：完整 high 力度 `/review`（17 agent + 2 verifier）在 base 收敛，0 Critical、两轮干跑反向审计；增量反向审计对发现一条 Suggestion（陈旧等长 build 可腾退 live 较新条目），已修复并配并发回归测试；对该修复的最终反向审计确认收敛。最新一轮分类处置复审的三条边界（两条已修、先逐出后拒收本轮修复）与 bot 评审的五条内联建议（R1-1/R1-4 修复，R1-2/R1-3 测试覆盖关闭，R1-5 复现并作为先存残余文档化、摘要修复暂缓）。再一轮复审复现两个并发 P1（等待方绕过共享构建的验证；准入前挂载的投影脱离预算）与一个投影转类 P2；三者均根因修复（共享验证完成、准入时记账、转类回收），连同 bot round-2 建议（瞬时 stat 失败、identity 分支无测试）。再下一轮复审发现 cap/stale 提前返回绕过复验；以复验先于所有返回修复，同提交含收缩方向谓词、offer 计数上限回收、夹具合并、route 级复用测试与文档修正（bot round-3）。每个修复都配回归测试与已执行的变异见证。

### 测试平台

🍏 macOS ⚠️ 未测 · 🪟 Windows ⚠️ 未测 · 🐧 Linux ✅ 已测。

### 环境

Node v26.12.1、vitest 3.2.7、tsx 源码级探针。daemon E2E 验证见验证评论。与最新 `origin/main` 的合并树上全量 build + bundle + core typecheck。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：每进程索引缓存最坏字节保留从 64 MiB 升至 320 MiB（估算口径；独立堆探针实测真实堆 ≈ 0.63× 估算——30k 记录探针上 heapDelta/estimate = 0.632——故 320 MiB 估算对应约 202 MiB 真实堆）。保留仍受两类预算、5 分钟 TTL、LRU 驱逐约束；小会话保留不变。Managed 投影与 hook 聚合按加入后条目所属预算类记账；保留正文使条目跨过共享预算时移入超大类，合并条目放不下时丢弃保留。一条低置信评审发现（超大预算与实验性 `--child-heap-mode enforce` 512 MiB 下限的协调）留给维护者堆策略讨论（该下限非默认；默认 observe 不施加任何限制）。
- 缓存之外的行为变化：文件被等长原地改写且 mtime 前进时，冻结游标或快照现在返回 `transcript_snapshot_unavailable`——与 turn-index 路径已有的校验一致。纯追加保持冻结前缀可读。这也关闭了小缓存索引上同样存在的旧快照洞。共享索引构建的并发请求现在共享其经验证的完成：快照在构建期间被改写或替换时，所有共享者收到 `transcript_snapshot_unavailable`（此前等待方可能拿到撕裂的构建结果）；构建后复验的瞬时 stat 错误（EMFILE/EIO/EACCES）不缓存返回已构建快照，而非 500。复验先于所有提前完成返回（超限拒绝、陈旧完成），除该已记录的尽力路径外不返回未验证的构建结果。被取代快照回收覆盖两个大小方向与 offer 门计数上限。
- 未验证/超出范围：保留 uuid 的等长原地改写后再追加不会被检出（先于本 PR 存在；此处新增的等长守卫因文件变长而看不到它，且页正文按冻结偏移活读、缓存命中亦然）——冻结前缀摘要校验已中英双语列为后续工作。legacy singular 路由在默认 `--channel-idle-timeout-ms 0` 下仍每页回收 ACP 子进程、丢弃其进程内缓存（`docs/users/qwen-serve.md` 已记载；缓解：正 idle timeout）——daemon 本地的 workspace 限定路由与长活子进程直接受益。冷缓存首次读取仍付一次性全量解析；追加使冻结键失效，较新快照在回收后放得下时通过腾退同文件被取代前缀获得准入（增量尾部扩展仍是后续项）。索引估算超过 256 MiB 的会话（稠密短记录可在远低于 256 MiB 文件上限处触达）仍逐页重建——常量注释已写明该悬崖。32 条目计数上限仍全局共享，超大条目可占用 warm 小索引的槽位（类预算至多容纳三个超大条目）。
- 破坏性改动/迁移：无。缓存为进程内部；无 API、cursor、schema 变化。设计文档中英已更新：[untrusted-persisted-transcript.md](../blob/main/docs/design/untrusted-persisted-transcript.md) / [untrusted-persisted-transcript.zh-CN.md](../blob/main/docs/design/untrusted-persisted-transcript.zh-CN.md)、[hook-execution-records.md](../blob/main/docs/design/hook-execution-records.md) / [hook-execution-records.zh-CN.md](../blob/main/docs/design/hook-execution-records.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #17889 —— daemon 本地 transcript 读取路径的逐请求全量重解析成本模型已修复；legacy singular 路由默认 idle timeout 下的每页子进程回收与增量追加扩展仍为已记录的残余/后续项，故引用但不使用关闭关键词。

</details>

prs.title: feat(cli): let /theme take a theme name
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`/theme <name>` now switches straight to that theme, the same way `/effort high` or `/output-style Concise` work. It accepts built-in themes, custom themes and `auto`, ignores case, saves the choice, and applies it right away in the running session. An unknown name shows an error that lists the available themes and doesn't save anything. Plain `/theme` still opens the picker like before.

It saves to the workspace if the workspace already sets `ui.theme` (otherwise the user-level value would just be overridden), and to user settings otherwise.

Ink reads the theme on every render, so it picks up the change by itself. OpenTUI caches its palette, so I added an optional `ui.onThemeChanged` hook to the command context. The OpenTUI host uses it to re-derive the palette, the same call the theme dialog already makes.

On the completion question from triage: I went with `argumentHint: '[name]'` like `/effort`, not tab completion, so bare `/theme` + Enter still opens the picker instead of auto-picking the first theme. Happy to switch to completion if you'd rather have it.

## Why it's needed

Before this, anything typed after `/theme` was silently dropped, so the only way to change themes was the picker. Requested in #18061 (triage: community PR welcome).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

In `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/ui/commands/themeCommand.test.ts src/ui/opentui/commands-context.test.ts`. The new tests cover switching by name (case-insensitive, trimmed), saving to user vs workspace scope, an unknown name changing nothing, NO_COLOR still blocking it, and the OpenTUI context forwarding `onThemeChanged` to the host.

To check by hand: `/theme ansi light` → "Theme set to ANSI Light." and colors change. `/theme nope` → error with the list. `/theme` → picker.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: `/theme Dracula` opens the picker and ignores the name. After: it switches to Dracula and saves it. Unit-tested only; I didn't record a terminal session.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux, unit tests: `src/ui/commands`, `src/i18n` and the OpenTUI context/host suites, 1722 passed. `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier are clean.

### Environment (optional)

N/A, unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the new `ui.onThemeChanged` hook is optional, so other renderers and existing commands are unaffected. No completion (see above).
- Not validated / out of scope: running the OpenTUI renderer live (its native library isn't available in my environment). The `/config ui.theme` validation issue the triage mentioned is left for a separate issue.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #18061

---

## 中文说明

### 这个 PR 做了什么

`/theme <name>` 现在会直接切换到指定主题，用法和 `/effort high`、`/output-style Concise` 一样。支持内置主题、自定义主题和 `auto`，不区分大小写，会保存选择并在当前会话中立即生效。主题名不存在时会报错并列出可用主题，不会保存任何内容。不带参数的 `/theme` 仍然打开选择器。

如果工作区已经设置了 `ui.theme`，就保存到工作区（否则用户级设置会被覆盖而不生效），否则保存到用户设置。

Ink 每次渲染都会读取主题，所以会自动生效。OpenTUI 会缓存调色板，因此在命令上下文中新增了可选的 `ui.onThemeChanged` 钩子，OpenTUI host 用它重新生成调色板（与主题对话框已有的调用相同）。

关于 triage 提到的补全问题：参照 `/effort` 使用 `argumentHint: '[name]'` 而不是 Tab 补全，这样直接输入 `/theme` 回车仍会打开选择器，而不会自动选中第一个主题。如果更希望用补全，可以改。

### 为什么需要

之前 `/theme` 后面输入的内容会被直接忽略，只能通过选择器切换主题。需求见 #18061（triage：欢迎社区 PR）。

### 如何验证

在 `packages/cli` 运行 `npx vitest run src/ui/commands/themeCommand.test.ts src/ui/opentui/commands-context.test.ts`。新测试覆盖：按名称切换（不区分大小写、去除空格）、保存到用户或工作区、未知名称不做任何改动、NO_COLOR 时仍然拦截、OpenTUI 上下文把 `onThemeChanged` 转发给 host。在 Linux 上跑了 `src/ui/commands`、`src/i18n` 和 OpenTUI 相关测试，共 1722 个全部通过；`tsc --noEmit`、eslint、prettier 无问题。

### 风险与范围

新增的 `ui.onThemeChanged` 是可选的，不影响其他渲染器和已有命令。没有在真实 OpenTUI 渲染器中手动测试（本地环境缺少其原生库）。triage 提到的 `/config ui.theme` 校验问题留给单独的 issue。没有破坏性变更。
