issues.body:
## Summary
When a parent session yields while awaiting child subagent runs, a later revocation of the requester operator authority makes the child completion delivery fail permanently. The parent never receives the completion and stays in a waiting state. The failure is reported with a constant error string that does not say why the authority was revoked, so the failure cannot be attributed from logs.

## Environment
openclaw 2026.9.8, shipped bundle (dist).

## Where (verified against the shipped bundle)
File: dist/session-followup-completion-<hash>.mjs

- :174  async function withRequesterCronAuthority(params, run)
- :183  if (authority.operatorAuthority) throw new Error("Requester operator authority is no longer current");
- :195, :200  if (!current()) throw new Error("Requester operator authority is no longer current");

The same module contains the currency check isCurrent(authority), which returns false when:
- the operator authority is no longer current;
- authority.lifecycleGeneration !== getAgentRunLifecycleGeneration();
- the session authority set no longer contains this authority.

The module also exports revokeRequesterCronAuthority / revokeRequesterCronAuthorityBatch, i.e. revocation is an explicit, supported path.

## Observed behaviour
- A child run ends cleanly (status: done, execution: finished) while its recorded delivery status is failed, with failure text referencing the error above.
- The parent session that was awaiting children never wakes; no completion event arrives; the interface remains in a waiting-for-subtasks state indefinitely.
- The child result is not lost: it can still be read back from the child session.

## Gaps
1. The thrown Error carries only the constant message. No reason code, no cause detail, nothing that identifies which currency condition failed or which code path revoked the authority.
2. Because of (1), a failed delivery cannot be traced from logs alone; identifying the cause required reading the bundle source.

## Impact
- Parent-side waits can hang indefinitely with no signal to the requester.
- Automated flows that depend on yield/completion handoff stall silently.
- Self-diagnosis is not possible for operators.

## Requests
1. Include a machine-readable reason (and, where safe, a short cause detail) in the thrown error and in the recorded delivery failure.
2. Provide a recoverable or at least observable failure path (for example a delivery-failure event the requester can observe and re-attach to), instead of leaving the wait unresolved.
3. Document which actions revoke a pending requester authority.

## Reproduction caveat
We could not build a deterministic minimal reproduction, because the revocation path is not logged. The above is based on the shipped bundle source plus observed behaviour. We are happy to test a build that logs the revocation reason.

### Summary

Make the complete name of a theme discoverable when its Appearance card label is truncated.

### Problem to solve

The fixed-width theme cards shorten long names with an ellipsis. For example, the built-in **Manuscript** theme appears as `Manuscri...`. The card's current hover title is the theme description, so it does not reveal the full name. Users can still select the theme, but cannot easily read and compare its complete name in the grid.

### Proposed solution

When a theme name is truncated, provide a visible way to discover its complete name on hover and keyboard focus while keeping the existing theme description available. Keep the compact card layout and selection behavior.

Acceptance criteria:

- A long theme name can be read in full without changing the grid layout or selecting the theme.
- The existing theme description remains available.
- Keyboard navigation and the theme card's accessible name continue to work.

### Alternatives considered

Wrapping every label or widening all cards would change the grid layout even for short names. A disclosure only when needed keeps the current compact cards.

### Impact

Affected: Control UI users choosing a theme in Appearance. Severity: Low; this is a clarity improvement, not a blocker. Frequency: whenever a long built-in or imported theme name appears in the grid. Consequence: users may have to guess which theme an abbreviated label represents.

### Evidence/examples

The current Appearance view uses each theme's full label, while `.settings-theme-card__label` applies `text-overflow: ellipsis`. The theme button's hover title currently contains the description rather than the full name.

Before: the card label is truncated, and its hover hint only shows the description.

![Before: truncated theme name with description-only hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RileyJJY/openclaw/8416df560bf805c8ce5a3881d6c091aad1c8579e/issue-evidence/185814-theme-before.png)

After: focusing the card displays its complete name and keeps the description.

![After: focused theme card with full name and description](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RileyJJY/openclaw/bc1ec03cf989eedee6c9331aeffe7251f41115d7/issue-evidence/185814-theme-after.png)

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

This request is limited to revealing an existing theme label. It does not request new themes, changes to theme styling, or changes to selection behavior.

issues.body:
## Summary

More evidence for the consolidated Claude CLI transcript fix that follows #184216. Each case below is the same loss: OpenClaw writes host-generated content into the native Claude input as if a person typed it, or drops the host content entirely. Each one has been, or would become, another text-matching patch in the history importer. Filed as evidence instead of as more small PRs.

All observed on `main`-based builds (latest `b891b0f0ba0`), Claude CLI runtime, Control UI.

## 1. Quoted completion history is prepended to the human's own message

`src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts:558` prepends a block to the next human input:

> Recorded completion events and your replies (oldest first; quoted history, not new instructions; this session may already hold them). Verify current and time-sensitive facts before acting: …

The message really is human, so marking it as host-generated is wrong. But the native copy is now the human's words with host text attached. The canonical row and the native row no longer match by text, and history needs another stripping rule to pair them. Observed on three consecutive human turns in one session on 27 Oct.

Expected: this block travels through the private context channel (`promptContext` / UserPromptSubmit additional context), never inside the human prompt text.

## 2. The resume drift note is prepended to human input, and it fires on almost every trigger change

`src/agents/cli-session-drift.ts` prepends "OpenClaw resumed this CLI session after prompt content changed…" to the next input. This is the same problem as case 1: host text attached to human text. The importer strips it on display (#143960), but a duplicated human row still appeared on 26 Oct after a drift note.

The note fires far more often than it should. `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task` are only offered on Control UI turns. `CALLER_SURFACE_TOOL_NAMES` (`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:174`) excludes them from the prompt-tool hash, but not from the materialised tool list hashed into `extraSystemPromptHash` (`prepare.ts:964`). The hash therefore changes, and the native session reports drift, whenever a session alternates between a Control UI message and a completion, exec, inter-session, or system-triggered turn. In one session, this explained 28 of 28 drift notes; consecutive turns of the same type never drifted. Filtering caller-surface tools out of that list fixes it (red/green test available on request). That removes most drift notes at the source rather than stripping them later.

## 3. A mid-turn completion reaches a busy Claude CLI parent as a bare placeholder

When a child completes while its Claude CLI parent is busy, the parent receives `RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT` ("Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.", `src/agents/internal-runtime-context.ts:34`) with no result text. The run still records `delivery.status=delivered`. Reproduced in isolated Gateways on two builds (4 of 4 busy-parent runs; the parent states in its reply that it saw no result). Idle-parent and `sessions_yield` paths deliver correctly. The bare placeholder has also appeared as a standalone user row in production transcripts.

This looks like the Claude CLI form of #167276, which describes the same loss on the Codex harness. In both, the result travels in `internalEvents`, and the harness boundary drops it. A provenance fix that marks this input as host-generated would hide the placeholder correctly, but the content would still be lost. Any consolidated fix should carry the content as well as the origin.

## Pattern

| Case | Host content | Where it ends up |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Quoted completion history | Inside the human prompt |
| 2 | Drift note | Inside the human prompt; produced far too often |
| 3 | Child completion result | Dropped; only a placeholder arrives |

The provenance work after #184216 fixes inputs that are host-generated as a whole. Cases 1 and 2 are the remaining shape: host text attached to a human input. Case 3 is the inverse: host content that never arrives. If every host addition went through the private context channel and native input carried only what the sender actually authored, the importer would not need wording-based rules for any of these.

Related: #184216, #143960, #161012, #166080, #167276, #151962.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow explicitly selected scheduled agent turns to use plugin-provided system instructions instead of OpenClaw’s generic unattended-run preamble.

If the selected plugin provides no usable replacement, keep the existing default preamble.

### Problem to solve

TinyStaff’s scheduled tasks use plugin-provided instructions for reporting results and pausing when a human decision is needed.

OpenClaw also appends its generic unattended-run instructions. Trusted task instructions can override conflicts, but both sets remain present. There is no supported way to replace just this preamble without identifying and stripping upstream boilerplate.

The need is prompt customization, not a new scheduler or execution-policy framework.

### Requested behavior

1. Ordinary jobs retain their current behavior.
2. An operator can explicitly select a plugin to provide replacement system instructions for a scheduled agent turn.
3. When the selected plugin successfully supplies nonempty replacement instructions, OpenClaw includes them as system context and omits the generic unattended preamble.
4. If the plugin is absent, disabled, returns nothing, or its contribution fails, OpenClaw retains the default preamble.
5. Selection comes from trusted job configuration. Task text and external-hook content cannot select a replacement or disable protections.
6. Task identity, time/context information, external-content fencing, delivery rules, execution permissions, and scheduler lifecycle remain unchanged.

This should be an explicit choice, not something inferred from a session key or the presumed presence of a person.

### Scope and related work

Existing prompt hooks already contribute system instructions. The missing capability is a supported way for a selected contribution to replace the scheduled-run preamble. The exact job field and hook/API shape are for maintainer discussion.

TinyStaff’s business instructions, skill names, reporting tools, and task-state semantics remain in its plugin.

Required-plugin enforcement belongs in #147129. This proposal does not require plugin availability, validate application-specific prerequisites, or refuse execution when customization is unavailable. Deployments needing those guarantees must enforce them separately.

Related: #165811 concerns scheduled continuations into existing conversations. This request also covers isolated scheduled jobs and does not infer policy from the conversation target.

### Alternatives considered

- Override conflicting instructions in each task: works for precedence, but leaves both instruction sets present.
- Strip the preamble through prompt rewriting: depends on upstream wording and risks removing unrelated context or protections.
- Keep a downstream patch: requires maintenance and qualification on every upgrade.

### Impact and tradeoff

Integrations can supply one coherent set of scheduled-run instructions while ordinary jobs remain unchanged.

Fallback preserves execution when customization is unavailable, but the job may then run without the application-specific instructions. That is intentional for this feature; mandatory plugin guarantees are a separate concern.

This could replace the prompt-customization portion of TinyStaff’s downstream patch. It would not by itself justify removing the patch’s required-contract enforcement.

### Acceptance criteria

- Ordinary jobs retain the existing preamble.
- A selected plugin’s successful replacement appears in system context without the generic preamble.
- An absent, disabled, empty, or failed contribution retains the default preamble.
- An unrelated plugin cannot supply the selected replacement.
- Untrusted content cannot select or suppress the preamble.
- Existing context, fencing, delivery, and execution-permission behavior remains intact.

### Maintainer decisions requested

1. Should scheduled jobs support this explicit customization with default fallback?
2. Should it extend an existing prompt hook, and where should trusted job-level selection live?

No implementation PR is proposed before agreement on this scope.

issues.body:
## Summary
#89423 was closed as stale while waiting for a live repro. This is one, on the current release.

The macOS app node (`openclaw-macos`, mode=node) drops its Gateway WebSocket while a `system.run` is in flight. The agent gets `node disconnected (system.run)` with the outcome unknown, and the app reconnects within about 1–3 s. This happens even though the Gateway and the app run on the **same Mac over loopback** (no Tailscale/LAN involved, unlike #89423).

## Environment
- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (bun 1.4.4), LaunchAgent, `bind=loopback`, port 18789
- Mac app: 2026.11.5 (2611000590), mode local, node role, auth=token
- Hardware: Mac mini Mac16,10, 16 GB, macOS 26.5.0
- Gateway and node are on the same machine (`remote=127.0.0.1`)

## Frequency
Counted from `client connected … client=openclaw-macos … mode=node` in the gateway log:
- 09:xx: 40 reconnects
- 10:xx: 38
- 11:xx: 76 (heavy agent exec use)

## What fails
- Medium or long `system.run`: `log show`, `docker exec … python`, `sleep 15` loops, `osascript` (quit app / System Events). Roughly 50% of these failed in this session.
- Short commands (`pgrep`, `cat`, `curl -m 5`) mostly succeed.
- Running the identical commands through `exec host=gateway` on the same machine: 0 failures across about 20 commands.

## Evidence
- Gateway log: there is **no close/disconnect line with a reason**. The only trace is a fresh `client connected … mode=node` plus `gateway/node-connect WARN node command surface withheld … commands=canvas.*,screen.record,camera.*,codex.*` on every reconnect.
- Occasionally: `node.runnerInventory.update errorCode=UNAVAILABLE "node runner inventory publication lost its pairing ownership; retry"`.
- App unified log (`log show --predicate 'process == "OpenClaw"'`), at each drop:
  `nw_socket_handle_socket_event [C1xx:2] Socket received WRITE_CLOSE event`, immediately followed by a new connection to 127.0.0.1:18789. The peer (Gateway) side appears to close the socket.
- Not memory-related: it was also happening with about 60% memory free, after the host was cleaned up.
- Restarting OpenClaw.app didn't help. The first `system.run` after the restart (an osascript call plus `sleep 20`) dropped as well. The restart also changed the node device ID, which was re-approved automatically.

## Expected
`system.run` keeps the node connection open for the duration of the command, or the Gateway logs why it closed the socket.

## Workaround
Use `exec host=gateway` when the Gateway runs on the same Mac, and keep the node for computer control and browser only.

## Happy to provide
A full gateway log excerpt and a unified-log excerpt around specific drops, with device IDs and tokens redacted.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a macOS reboot, every Codex (OpenAI) turn fails before it starts with `ProcessInspectionError: Cannot inspect Codex processes ... permission`, because the orphan sweep keeps a registration from the previous boot whose parent PID now belongs to another user's process; restarting the Gateway does not help.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the OpenClaw 2026.11.6 Gateway on macOS with agents on the bundled Codex harness, so that Codex app-server children are registered in the plugin state namespace `codex` / `app-server-processes`.
2. Reboot the Mac (here: a macOS update). The Gateway is killed by the shutdown, so the exit cleanup of the registrations does not run; two rows from the previous boot remained.
3. After boot, the `parent.pid` stored in those rows (794) was in use by `/System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/usbaudio.bundle/Contents/MacOS/usbaudiod`, user `_coreaudiod`.
4. Start any Codex turn (chat message or cron job).

### Expected behavior

Codex turns start as they did before the reboot. A registration from the previous boot cannot name a live process and should not block the start. Observed reference: as soon as PID 794 was freed (`sudo pkill -x usbaudiod`; launchd restarted it under a new PID), the next Codex call's sweep deleted both rows by itself and Codex started, without a Gateway restart.

### Actual behavior

- Every Codex turn failed before the request was sent. Channel ingress for the affected lane retried every 3 minutes and failed the same way 19 times; a scheduled job failed with the same error.
- A Gateway restart did not help (the same rows are read again by the next sweep).
- Rows that remained (values as stored; `startedAt` is the UTC start identity; host boot time `kern.boottime` = `Sun Nov 22 06:58:56 2026` local, i.e. `21:58:56` UTC on Nov 21):
  - `{"parent":{"pid":794,"pgid":794,"startedAt":"Sat Nov 21 21:28:40 2026"},"child":{"pid":4633,"pgid":4633,"startedAt":"Sat Nov 21 21:30:20 2026","commandFingerprint":"…"}}`
  - same parent, child `4700`, `"Sat Nov 21 21:30:22 2026"`
- The children 4633 and 4700 did not exist any more.
- With the exported `readDarwinProcessSnapshot` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`: inspecting `[4633, 4700]` (or any absent PID) succeeds and returns only the caller's own row; inspecting `[794, 4633]` throws `DarwinProcessInspectionError("permission")`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10), bundled Codex plugin (`@openclaw/codex`, `dist/.setup/transport-stdio-jkj0OYDS.mjs`)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global (Node 24.22.1)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.2-sol (Codex harness)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> bundled Codex app-server (`@openclaw/codex`) -> openai

### Logs

```
ProcessInspectionError: Cannot inspect Codex processes. Check process inspection permissions (/proc on Linux, native process inspection on macOS), then retry.
spooled update … failed; keeping for retry: Cannot inspect Codex processes. Check process inspection permissions (/proc on Linux, native process inspection on macOS), then retry.
⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Cannot inspect Codex processes. …
```

### Impact and severity

All OpenAI/Codex turns on the host failed for about 80 minutes after the reboot (agents without a fallback stopped; others fell back to a different provider). It is likely to recur after any reboot that leaves a registration behind: PIDs restart from low numbers at boot, and a Gateway started at login gets a low PID that a system daemon may take after the next boot.

### Additional information

**Cause (from the 2026.11.6 dist):** `prepareCodexAppServerProcessRegistration` → `reapRegisteredCodexAppServerOrphans` → `sweepRegisteredCodexAppServerOrphans` calls `readCodexAppServerProcessSnapshot(deadline, [registration.parent.pid, registration.child.pid])`. On macOS `startIdentity` throws `permission` for the parent that this user cannot inspect, and the whole sweep — and with it every Codex start — fails, although the child that the registration exists to reap is already gone.

**Suggestions:**
1. Store a boot identity in each registration (e.g. `kern.bootsessionuuid` on macOS, `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` on Linux) and expire rows from another boot before any PID lookup.
2. When the parent cannot be inspected, check the child on its own: if the child is confirmed absent there is nothing left to reap, so the row can be dropped.

**Workaround we run (local patch, darwin only):** a row is deleted only when all of these hold — the `[parent, child]` inspection failed with `ProcessInspectionError("permission")`; both `parent.startedAt` and `child.startedAt` are more than 2 minutes before `Date.now() - os.uptime() * 1000`; a child-only inspection does not list the child; and `process.kill(child.pid, 0)` throws `ESRCH`. Every other outcome keeps the current fail-closed path. A first version that deleted on the start-time comparison alone was rejected in review: after a large clock step it could drop the row of a live child (a live row's parent is the Gateway itself and stays readable, but a dead parent can still leave a live orphan child), so the start time is only used together with the refused inspection and the confirmed-absent child.

**Related, different failure reasons:** #202176 (`unavailable` from transient processes in the census), #138043 (`deadline` with concurrent starts).

issues.body:
### Summary

Opt-in WhatsApp direct-chat batching that holds photos, voice notes, videos, documents, and stickers in the existing inbound debounce window, so a burst of text and media becomes one agent turn.

### Problem to solve

People rarely send one tidy WhatsApp message. A typical request is "look at this" + two photos + a voice note + "what do you think?", sent within a few seconds. `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp` batches rapid text, but media flushes immediately (the documented text-only policy), so the agent answers the first fragment before the rest arrives. The user gets several partial replies, and the agent never sees the photos, the voice note, and the question together.

### Proposed solution

A WhatsApp-owned boolean, `channels.whatsapp.debounceMedia` (default `false`, per-account override `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.debounceMedia`). When it is enabled and `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp` is greater than zero:

- In direct chats, image, video, audio, document, and sticker messages wait in the same window as text.
- The flushed batch keeps every attachment paired with its own caption in arrival order, and exposes every attachment to the agent (not just the last one).
- Each uncaptioned voice note in the batch is transcribed in place, and its media index is marked as transcribed so core STT does not repeat it.
- Groups, quoted replies, locations, and control commands such as `/stop` keep dispatching immediately. Group mention gating inspects each voice note before admission, so groups stay unchanged.

The window keeps its single owner (`messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp`); the new key only decides whether media may wait in it.

### Alternatives considered

- A generic `inbound_debounce` plugin hook (#106458) was closed because it moved WhatsApp-owned batching policy into a cross-plugin API; the maintainer pointed to a narrower WhatsApp-owned configuration. This proposal follows that direction.
- Image-only batching (#146117 / #146178) helps screenshots, but voice notes are the most common WhatsApp media in this flow, and a batch with several voice notes needs each one transcribed.
- `queue.mode` steering only helps once a run is already active; it does not hold the first message.

### Impact

Affected: WhatsApp direct-chat users who send text and media in bursts. Severity: UX friction (fragmented, premature replies; the agent misses context). Frequency: every mixed burst. Default behavior is unchanged.

### Evidence/examples

Prototyped and tested on a real linked WhatsApp account: five messages within 27 seconds (photo, text, text, captioned photo, voice note) arrived as one agent turn 21 seconds after the last message, with both images and the transcribed voice note, and produced a single reply.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, a PR with tests, docs, and live proof follows.

### Additional information

Related: #146117, #146178, #106458, #100970.

**Component:** `agents/runtime-execution-facts` (runtime-context emitter) + `agents/bash-process-registry` (exec session registry)
**Affected versions:** confirmed on **2026.10.7** (`v2026.10.7` -> `157d8c2`, matching the installed build) and still present in **2026.10.10-beta.3**. **Partially fixed on `origin/main`** @ `906e0b06be` ("fix(agents): preserve safe inspection and outcomes during recovery", #177943) - requirement (a) only. **That commit is in NO release tag and is in neither published bundle**, so the fix is unreleased. Requirements (b)-(d) are **still unfixed on `origin/main`**.
**Severity:** low — it misreports exec-session liveness in the prompt; it does not abort turns. But it is the same family as the settle-wake loop: state that says "running" and is never reconciled when the process dies.
**Related:** `OPENCLAW_ISSUE_settle_wake_late_kill_20261026.md`

> **Verification method.** Release status was confirmed three ways: (1) `git merge-base --is-ancestor 906e0b06be <tag>` against real fetched tags (`v2026.10.7`, `v2026.10.10-beta.2`, `v2026.10.10-beta.3` - all **NO**); (2) by grepping the **published npm bundles** for the new string (`npm pack openclaw@<version>` -> `grep -rl "No active exec-tool sessions" package/dist/` -> **0 files** in both 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.10-beta.3); and (3) by `git log -S "No active exec-tool sessions" origin/main -- src/agents/runtime-execution-facts.ts`, which returns **`906e0b06be` as the single introducing commit**. A shallow clone's empty tag list is not evidence of absence.
>
> **Correction (2026-10-26, third pass - supersedes two earlier revisions).** The attribution in this draft has flip-flopped and this revision is the one verified against the GitHub API. The fix commit is **`906e0b06be92f6b17d5e5dcfe3044b4e9b9b277d`** - "fix(agents): preserve safe inspection and outcomes during recovery" (#177943, merged 2026-10-20T12:11:39Z). Verified directly against `https://api.github.com/repos/openclaw/openclaw/commits/906e0b06be`: it is a real commit touching 56 files, one of which is `src/agents/runtime-execution-facts.ts` (+7/-1), and that file's patch contains both `includeEmptySnapshots` and the literal string `No active exec-tool sessions`.
>
> The sha **`e5c1ae9166c81367e6a8e5358f2ca379583389f2`** is **"feat(ios): hide automation sessions from ordinary session lists" (#178620)** and touches exactly 8 files, **all under `apps/` (iOS/Swift) plus `docs/platforms/ios.md`** - it cannot be the fix for a Node-side runtime-context fact. A second revision of this draft had asserted the opposite (that `906e0b06be` "does not exist" and `e5c1ae916` was correct); that assertion was wrong and is withdrawn here.
>
> **What `906e0b06be` does NOT fix.** It only makes the empty-snapshot fallback *possible* (requirement a). The registry still performs **no pid-liveness check** - `git grep -E "kill\(.*, *0\)|ESRCH" origin/main -- src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` returns **nothing** - so requirements (b), (c) and (d) remain open on `origin/main`.

---

## 1. Summary

The runtime context reports exec sessions as `running` forever, even after those processes have exited and the exec registry has already forgotten them. The stale fact is re-injected on every turn, unchanged, and no live state can correct it.

Observed on the reporter's host: the same two-entry block was re-injected **fourteen times, byte-identical**, listing two PIDs that had been dead for hours, while genuinely live exec sessions came and went without appearing.

## 2. Reproduction

1. Start a long-running exec session (e.g. `sleep 180`) from a turn.
2. Let it finish (or kill it).
3. Observe the runtime context on subsequent turns.

The session is still listed with `running pid=<pid>`.

## 3. Evidence that the fact is stale rather than live

On the reporter's host, two sessions were listed as running:

```
- plaid-reef running pid=1281178 cwd=/home/jimmylu/.openclaw/workspace-main :: sleep 180;
- quick-haven running pid=1281576 cwd=/home/jimmylu/.openclaw/workspace-main :: sleep 150;
```

Both PIDs were verified dead **six independent ways**:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `kill -0 <pid>` | fails (no such process) |
| `kill -9 <pid>` | exit 1 — "no such process" |
| `/proc/<pid>` | absent |
| `ps -p <pid>` | empty |
| host-wide scan for `comm=sleep` | no matching process at all |
| exec registry (`process list`) | **both sessions absent** |

The last row is decisive: the runtime-context emitter and the `process` tool's `list` action read the **same map** —

- `bash-process-references.ts` → `listRunningSessions()`
- `bash-tools.process.ts` → `listRunningSessions()`

— both imported from `bash-process-registry`. A live read of one map cannot show two sessions in the context while `list` shows neither. **The context is therefore not recomputed from live state; it is a persisted, replayed turn-start fact.**

A control experiment confirmed this: a session started during one turn (`pid 1290739`, verified alive) **never appeared** in the next turn's context, while the two long-dead sessions were still listed.

## 4. Root cause

### 4a. The installed emitter cannot supersede a stale fact

The 2026.10.7 bundle emits the exec-session block only when the registry is **non-empty**:

```js
// dist/messages-CfuAf9j-.mjs
if (sessions.length) {
  sections.push(["Active exec sessions:", sessions.join("\n")].join("\n"));
}
```

There is no empty-state fallback — `grep -c "No active exec-tool sessions" dist/messages-CfuAf9j-.mjs` → **0**. The same is true of the newer `v2026.10.10-beta.3` tarball (**0 files**), and its wording is still the old `Active exec sessions:`.

So once the registry becomes empty, the emitter produces **nothing**, and the last non-empty fact remains the effective one. Because the fact is persisted in the session transcript and replayed each turn, it can never be corrected: the only way to overwrite it would be to emit a fresh (empty) fact, which neither published build can do.

### 4b. Upstream main fixes the supersede problem

`origin/main` @ `906e0b06be` adds `includeEmptySnapshots`:

```ts
/** Retained carriers need explicit empty snapshots to supersede older facts. */
includeEmptySnapshots?: boolean;
...
if (sessions.length || includeEmptySnapshots) {
  sections.push([
    "Active exec sessions at turn start (snapshot):",
    ...
    sessions.join("\n") || "No active exec-tool sessions in this scope at turn start.",
  ].join("\n"));
}
```

and wires it at the call site:

```ts
includeEmptySnapshots: transcriptPolicy.appendOnlyRuntimeContext === true,
```

This is the fix for the observed symptom — but it is **unreleased**.

### 4c. A second gap remains even on upstream main: no liveness check on read

Neither `bash-process-registry.ts` nor `bash-process-references.ts` verifies that the process is still alive when listing:

```
grep -c "kill(pid, 0)\|ESRCH\|isAlive" src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-process-references.ts
→ 0, 0
```

`markExited()` (`bash-process-registry.ts:479` → `moveToFinished()`) is the **only** removal path when a process exits. If a process dies without that path being taken — e.g. the supervisor is torn down, or cleanup is interrupted — the registry entry stays in `runningSessions` forever and is reported as `running` even on upstream main.

Observed on the reporter's host alongside the stale fact:

```
service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; pending:
{"closingReceipt":true,"controlClose":true,"relayExit":true,"lineageEof":true,
 "extinctionUnconfirmed":true,"stdoutEnd":true,"stderrEnd":true}
```

`extinctionUnconfirmed: true` is exactly the condition where the supervisor cannot confirm the child's death — and therefore cannot call `markExited`.

## 5. Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| (a) | The exec-session runtime fact must be **supersedable**: when the registry is empty, emit an explicit empty fact so a previously persisted non-empty fact is replaced rather than replayed forever. *(Partially fixed on `origin/main` @ `906e0b06be`, unreleased - requirement (a) only; (b)-(d) still open.)* |
| (b) | When listing active sessions, **verify pid liveness** (`kill(pid, 0)`) and treat a dead pid as exited — the registry must not report a process that no longer exists. |
| (c) | A session whose process died without a terminal notification (e.g. `extinctionUnconfirmed`) must be reconciled into a terminal state rather than left `running`. |
| (d) | `process kill` should settle the registry entry, not only cancel the supervisor. Today the entry is dropped only by `process remove` (`deleteSession()` → `runningSessions.delete`); a plain `kill` leaves a phantom `running` session. |

## 6. Notes for maintainers

- The wording difference is a reliable version marker: `2026.10.7` emits `"Active exec sessions:"`, while `origin/main` emits `"Active exec sessions at turn start (snapshot):"`.
- The registry exposes a test-only reset (`resetProcessRegistryForTests`) via `globalThis[Symbol.for("openclaw.bashProcessRegistryTestApi")]`.
- The exec registry is consulted by the runtime-context emitter (`bash-process-references.ts`), the `process` tool (`bash-tools.process.ts`), and `gateway-active-work` — so a stale entry can affect more than the prompt.

## 7. Environment

- openclaw 2026.10.7 (`v2026.10.7` → `157d8c2`, the installed build) and 2026.10.10-beta.3 — both affected
- node v24.22.1, Linux 6.8.0-146-generic
- `origin/main` @ `2cfde9ae7` (2026-10-26) for the upstream fix reference; fix commit `906e0b06be` (#177943) is on `origin/main` but in no release tag

issues.body:
## Summary
On Discord, subsequent replies/progress appear to stop after a user sends a clarification during active tool/delegated work, while newer assistant text is visible in the web conversation. Discord can remain on an older task/progress message with typing activity. This affects later updates, not just the initial acknowledgment.

**Status: user-observed cross-surface discrepancy with correlated real completion-wake/admission failures; no deterministic end-to-end delivery-loss reproduction or root cause established.** This report does not claim every web commentary segment was eligible for Discord or that a generated final was permanently lost.

## Environment
Observed October 25, 2026. OpenClaw core/Discord plugin 2026.10.7; release-matched investigation source 157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e. macOS arm64, Node26.12.1. Prior read-only configuration observation found Discord progress mode and tool progress enabled. Effective per-turn queue/expectation overrides still need correlation. No live fixes or synthetic Discord sends were performed.

## User-reported sequence (not a deterministic reproduction)
1. Begin a multi-step task that uses tools and delegated children.
2. While it is working, send a clarification in the same Discord conversation.
3. Let child completions and requester continuation occur.
4. Compare newer assistant messages/progress in the web conversation against the Discord bottom/task message.

Paired screenshots around14:35–14:36 and14:49 Eastern showed newer web text while Discord remained on an older response. Private screenshots/business content are omitted. Some web presentation rows shared one assistant ID; apparent duplication is not evidence of duplicate generation or sends.

## Expected
Eligible replies/progress should reach the correct Discord turn/draft owner. Intentionally filtered commentary should not be confused with lost final delivery. Completion failures should settle/retry visibly rather than leave an apparently stuck progress message.

## Operational evidence
During the later affected continuation, bounded runtime logs report:
- 14:45:48,14:47:07,14:50:06 Eastern: completion wake `runtime_rejected`, with `queued steering message was not committed to the transcript before timeout`.
- 14:47:48,14:49:07: direct completion fallback failed with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.

These are real completion/admission failures correlated with the affected continuation, not conclusions inferred from screenshots. They do **not** establish that human input caused the failure, identify a Discord HTTP error, or locate a unique producer of SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED. The code has multiple producers, including prepared-source invalidation and command admission session disappearance/replacement. A separate expected-session revision mismatch emits UNAVAILABLE, not that code.

The earlier clarification final visibly arrived in Discord. Later recovered missing text includes intermediate commentary; no later generated final in the affected window has been recovered. Historical POST/PATCH/DELETE receipts and effective owner/adoption decisions remain unavailable. Supported message readback encountered provider/account-context prerequisites; no bypass was attempted.

## Offline investigation: what passes, and what it does not prove
- **13 scoped release-matched core cases pass**: real transcript commit, timeout/removal, consumed-but-unconfirmed input, explicit abort, admission guards and completion custody/retry. Removed queued input falls back once with original route/account; consumed input is not replayed. Rejection preserves retryable completion debt in tested paths. External model/Gateway boundaries are mocked where disclosed. No debt-loss invariant reproduced.
- **4 public Discord ingress/model/correction/lifecycle cases pass**, independently reviewed: raw inbound handling, real preflight/core dispatch, synthetic model stream, actual Discord delivery assembly against mocked REST. Active human correction durably commits once; exact REST sequence is preview POST → channel GET → original source final POST → preview DELETE → channel GET → corrected source final POST. Three POSTs mean one preview plus two different source-turn finals; zero PATCHes. Cleanup retires the test scheduler/MCP/resource host. This is ordinary partial-draft custody, **not child-owned retained progress**.
- Source-boundary checks show optional/unmentioned expectation may intentionally suppress queued progress while final delivery remains permitted, and retained child projections forward prepared tool activity rather than arbitrary commentary. Thus web presence alone does not prove Discord eligibility.
- The remaining full delegated-child composition stops **before accepted child registration**: the offline host does not supply a usable native in-process Gateway/source binding, and actual native spawn refuses credentials before any WebSocket. No accepted child/cohort/debt/adoption/wake is proved there. This is a test-host limitation, not a reproduced product delivery defect. No credentials or guard bypass were used.

The missing seam is real user-input admission + child registry/cohort + retained progress adoption + requester completion wake/fallback + eligible Discord final/retirement, in one supported isolated host. Need successful-commit control versus queued-timeout-removal and consumed input, retaining real source/session/transport guards. Do not relax lifecycle checks or replay consumed work to make it pass.

## Related reports (not established duplicates)
- #177852: intentional progress suppression for accepted unmentioned/room-event input; per-turn expectation must be checked here.
- #139217: web commentary absent from Discord, with finals arriving normally.
- #149640 (closed): older queued-followup stale-draft cleanup; installed2026.10.7 already has queued-settlement cleanup.
- #169076: older user input during sessions_yield admission/deadletter report.
- #178408: Slack post-yield tool-context failure; not proof of Discord delivery failure.

Separate from compaction-notice suppression #183657/#183658 and manual script refresh-owner #170985. No causal link to either established. No safe production mitigation selected.

issues.body:
### Summary

Agents can enter a repeated no-progress `sessions_yield` loop **without any pending child, task, or eligible completion event**. The tool correctly responds `status: "nothing_pending"`, but the agent calls it again until loop detection terminates the turn. This has been observed during both delegation and session-history work, across **multiple models and OpenClaw releases**.

This report concerns **tool selection and failure to recover after `nothing_pending`**, not a claim that the yield tool itself returned the wrong status. Root cause is **not yet isolated**.

### Environment

- Linux x86_64; Node.js 24.21.0; OpenClaw Gateway and CLI from the same official install.
- Local models exposed via llama.cpp / OpenAI-compatible provider.
- `tools.toolSearch.mode: "directory"` on current 2026.10.5 runs; prior failures also occurred before that setting was enabled.
- Loop guard is enabled.
- Package integrity audit matched **13,981 packaged files byte-for-byte**; the one absent member was an install-lifecycle marker. No duplicate Gateway, stale runtime, or mixed installation found.

### Recorded occurrences (original retained session traces)

| Date (2026) | OpenClaw runtime | Model | Observed behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 12 | 2026.10.1 | Gemma 4 12B | Session-history request: **22** `sessions_yield` calls, all `nothing_pending` |
| Oct 19 | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | LFM2.5 24B A2B (QAD_Q4_0) | Delegation request: **19** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 19 | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | Same LFM | Explicit spawn request forbidding yield: **28** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 21 | 2026.10.5 | LFM2.5 24B A2B (IQ4_XS), High thinking | **22** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 22 | 2026.10.5 | Same LFM, Tool Search `directory` | **28** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 22 | 2026.10.5 | Same LFM, Medium thinking | Workshop history review: **22** yield calls; model reasoning identified `sessions_list` as next action |

Representative result repeated:

```json
{
  "status": "nothing_pending",
  "message": "No pending completion or eligible active native task is owned by this turn. This call did not pause the turn or schedule a continuation. Continue unfinished work; return its final result when complete."
}
```

The generated prompt reports show `sessions_yield` in the **direct tool schema**, while `sessions_spawn` is deferred behind the Tool Search directory. Some normalized traces show the assistant's recorded reasoning identifying `sessions_spawn` or `sessions_list`, followed by an actual `sessions_yield` function call instead. Raw provider HTTP/SSE bodies were unavailable, so we cannot say precisely where that mismatch originates.

### Working control / evidence that spawn itself functions

On 2026.10.5 with the same primary LFM model, explicitly instructing the agent to:
1. `tool_describe` `openclaw:core:sessions_spawn`,
2. `tool_call` the described spawn schema with `agentId: "coder"` and a `task`,
3. wait for and report the completion event,

**succeeded end to end**. Separately, a different model successfully spawned that coding agent under the same Gateway. The requester allowlist was checked with an actual `agents_list` call, which returned the target agent.

### Expected / actual

**Expected:** When `sessions_yield` reports `nothing_pending`, the agent should proceed with the unfinished task using an appropriate tool (or report a blocker). It should not repeatedly issue the same no-progress yield.

**Actual:** Some runs repeatedly select `sessions_yield` despite the no-pending response, even when no child was ever created, until the loop guard terminates execution.

### Scope and uncertainties

- **Not** a 2026.10.5-only regression: original evidence shows this behavior on 2026.10.1 and 2026.10.10-beta.1.
- `sessions_yield` returning `nothing_pending` is appropriate. The defect/hazard appears in tool selection, tool presentation, or recovery from that response.
- Possible contributing interface asymmetry: `sessions_yield` direct-only, while relevant tools are deferred. This remains a **hypothesis**; no offending source change, model/provider/template boundary, or standalone deterministic reproduction has been isolated.
- Current installation is official and internally consistent; no reinstall, model switch, or source patch is justified by available evidence.
- Related but not identical: #106704 (yield misuse on first turn); #118776 (yield exposed where child/event-producing tools are absent).

### Request

Could maintainers review:
1. The **model-facing affordance/preconditions** for `sessions_yield` when there is no owned child or completion source;
2. The direct-only `sessions_yield` vs deferred session-tool presentation and Tool Search guidance;
3. Recovery behavior following repeated `nothing_pending` responses without sacrificing legitimate wait semantics?

We can provide redacted, selected runtime-event and prompt-report excerpts if maintainers indicate the preferred format.

OpenClaw 2026.10.5; macOS; Node 26.10.0; native bundled boot-md; SQLite session store. One observed occurrence on 2026-10-21 at 20:22 EDT. Reproducibility has not been tested with another restart.

2. BOOT.md uses native status, sends one startup message, and admits a main-session reconciliation turn.
3. Boot run finishes; native hook attempts to remove its temporary session.

boot: failed to clean up session: SQLite session entry changed before lifecycle removal for <temporary-boot-session>
hooks/boot-md: startup task failed; reason=session cleanup failed

Small cleanup/reporting defect: retained finished temporary session and misleading failure log. No observed lost startup message or duplicate execution. Installed boot handler finally calls applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation with expected session ID; exact-entry comparison in the SQLite projection rejects removal. The rejecting guard is located; the changing writer and root cause are not proven. Related finalization fallback appeared in the same run; causality is unknown and it is not a second blocker.

## Evidence and limits
The error excerpt above is sanitized from the observed Gateway log. Raw private transcripts, chat destinations, host names and user paths are not included. A maintainer can request a separately sanitized excerpt. No raw DB access, manual session deletion, installed patch, weakened guard or second restart was used.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

Since 2026.10.10, delegating work to native Codex helpers fails roughly once for every helper launched.

The parent agent starts helpers and ends its turn (`sessions_yield`). When a helper finishes, OpenClaw opens a separate wake-up turn on the parent's Codex thread. Two things go wrong with that turn:
- it runs on authority borrowed from the turn that already ended;
- the parent's original Codex turn is often still live on the same thread.

The wake-up turn then fails ("agent harness host capability is no longer active"). The helper's result is lost, any active `/goal` is paused, and the user's next messages are rejected ("Codex session became active in another runner", "still has background work after waiting for cleanup").

This is the underlying problem behind a family of errors that have been reported separately. They are all symptoms of one lifecycle bug: OpenClaw ties authority and thread ownership to a single turn, while native Codex helpers and background work routinely outlive that turn.

### Impact and severity

**Severity: blocks the core workflow on every delegated task, and locks the user out of their own assistant.**

Delegating work to parallel helpers is the main reason to give an assistant a substantial job. On 10.10 and later, that is exactly the moment it breaks:

- **Work silently stops.** Helpers finish their work, but the results never reach the assistant. Nothing tells the user that progress has halted; the conversation just goes quiet.
- **Goals are paused out from under the user.** A failed wake-up pauses the active `/goal` with "Paused after an error." On native Codex sessions the operator cannot resume it ("requires the built-in OpenClaw runtime"), so the user has to notice the stall and re-establish the goal by hand.
- **The user is locked out.** Messages sent afterward are rejected with errors telling the user to "stop its running work and retry", meaning stop the very work they asked for. The user gets no reply at all; the rejected messages are simply dropped.
- **It recurs constantly.** In my installation this happened ~100 times a day on a single long-running task. The assistant becomes something to babysit rather than something that gets work done: every few minutes, check whether it is stuck, abort it, resend the message, re-set the goal.
- **The cost is spent and thrown away.** Helpers run to completion and consume usage, and then their results are discarded.

The experience is that the assistant falls over the moment it is asked to do anything ambitious, and that the user has to spend their time diagnosing and recovering it instead of getting the outcome they asked for. It is deeply frustrating, and it undermines trust in delegating anything substantial at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.10 or later (observed through 2026.11.2), use the native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`) for an OpenAI model.
2. In a channel session (Discord in my case), give the agent a long task that it delegates. The agent calls `spawn_agent` for one or more helpers, then `sessions_yield` while they run.
3. Let a helper finish after the parent's turn has ended.
4. Observe the following:
   - the completion "announce" turn fails;
   - any active goal pauses;
   - a user message sent shortly afterward is rejected with no reply.

### Expected behavior

- A helper's completion is delivered to the parent reliably: once the parent's Codex thread is idle, as a turn with its own valid authority.
- If delivery fails, it is retried. It does not lose the result or pause the goal.
- The user's messages are always accepted and answered (queued if necessary). They are never rejected with an instruction to stop running work.

### Actual behavior

A representative sequence from 2026-11-09 (times are America/Los_Angeles; one session; IDs shortened):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 07:03:59, 07:04:05 | The parent calls `spawn_agent` twice. |
| 07:05:49 | The parent calls `sessions_yield`, ending its turn while both helpers run. |
| ~07:07:09 | A helper finishes. OpenClaw starts `announce:codex-native:<parentThread>:<childThread>:succeeded` on the parent thread. |
| 07:08:18 | `codex app-server notification ignored for inactive turn`, with `matchesActiveThread: true` and `matchesActiveTurn: false`. Codex is still emitting `item/started` and `item/completed` for the parent's original turn, while OpenClaw has already made the announce turn the active turn. Two turns are live on one thread. |
| 07:09:38 | `agent cleanup failed … step=codex-trajectory-flush error=agent harness host capability is no longer active`, then `lane task error … durationMs=148848 error="agent harness host capability is no longer active"`, then `Subagent completion direct announce failed`. The session goal changes to `paused`, with `lastStatusNote: "Paused after an error. Resume to continue. agent harness host capability is no longer active"`. |
| 07:14:09, 07:14:42 | Two user messages are rejected with `CodexAdoptedThreadActiveError: Codex session became active in another runner; wait for it to finish before continuing`. The log records `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads … cause=error`, and the user receives nothing. |

Error counts in the gateway log:

| Error | 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-09 (until ~07:30) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent harness host capability is no longer active` | 56 | 131 |
| `Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration` | 28 | 76 |
| `still has background work after waiting for cleanup` | 20 | 27 |
| `Codex session became active in another runner` | 0 | 6 |
| `Session … placement authority changed` | 0 | 3 |

### Regression boundary: 2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10

I counted these errors per day in the agent's transcript events, alongside `spawn_agent`/`sessions_spawn` calls. The transcripts capture only a subset of the gateway-log errors, but the pattern is unambiguous:

| Period | Version | Helper launches/day | Errors/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 8–21 | ≤ 10.9 | ~4 | ~0.5 |
| Oct 22–Nov 2 (proactive delegation enabled) | 10.9 | ~63 | ~2 |
| Nov 3–9 | 10.10 → 11.1 → 11.2 | ~97 | ~106 |

- Heavy delegation on 10.9 (~760 helper launches over 12 days) was essentially error-free.
- The first `host capability` / `background work` / `another runner` error in the entire history appears at 2026-11-03 11:16, a few hours after updating to 10.10 that morning. It has continued on every release since.
- Whatever changed between 10.9 and 10.10 in harness authority binding, announce delivery, or Codex thread retention is the most likely origin.

### Code-level observations (2026.11.2 dist)

- `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` (`src/agents/harness/host-source-authority.ts`) throws "agent harness host capability is no longer active" in any of these cases:
  - `attempt.admittedRunContext.operationalRunInstance` differs from the instance captured at bind time;
  - the captured admitted-run assertion fails;
  - the gateway is not current.

  The announce turn for a helper launched by an earlier turn appears to carry that earlier turn's delegated authority. It fails as soon as it touches a host capability, which in the trace above was the trajectory flush during cleanup.
- The announce turn is started while the parent's original Codex turn is still producing items on the same thread (see 07:08:18). That makes the follow-on errors expected:
  - "did not confirm unloading previous configuration",
  - "still has background work",
  - "became active in another runner".
- The `codex-trajectory-flush` cleanup failure has the same signature as #171197, which was closed as fixed in October. It is recurring on 2026.11.2.

### Suggested direction

The fix needs to be in the lifecycle model, not in individual guards:

- **The session, not the turn, should own outstanding helper work and background commands.**
- **Completions should be queued per session and delivered once the parent Codex thread is idle.** Simultaneous completions should be coalesced into one wake-up, instead of one competing announce turn per helper.
- **Wake-up turns should be admitted with fresh authority of their own,** rather than inheriting authority from the turn that spawned the helpers.
- **A failed delivery should be retried.** It should never discard the helper's result or pause the user's goal.
- **User messages should always be queued and answered,** never rejected with "stop its running work and retry".

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (b556fdf); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.2. The regression first appeared on 2026.10.10.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew Node 26.13.0)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`, codex-cli 0.164.0) → OpenAI

### Beta release blocker

No

### Additional information

Related reports that I believe are symptoms of this same underlying issue:
- #194403: helper-completion continuations lose authority and block conversations.
- #196061 and #196062: a silent turn with a retained command is falsely marked failed. That is one entry point into the stuck state, not the root cause.
- #171197: the `codex-trajectory-flush` "host capability is no longer active" failure, closed as fixed but recurring.
- #147759 and #167280: delayed or stalled prompts after native Codex handoff and stop.

Diagnostic signal: when the parent keeps its turn open and collects helper results with `wait_agent` instead of calling `sessions_yield`, the completion arrives inside the live turn and this path is not exercised. That is consistent with the announce/wake-up turn being the failure point.

issues.body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 x64, npm install
- Observed on 2026.11.2 (after an update whose finalization was abandoned), and still reproducible after upgrading to 2026.11.6 until affected jobs were recreated
- Multi-account Discord config (`channels.discord.accounts.{main,david,alondra,rip,default}`, `defaultAccount: "main"`)

## What happened

After the update, every cron automation whose owner was bound to a pre-update session key (`agent:<agent>:discord:direct:<chatId>`) **and** used announce delivery failed at agent-run start (<1s, before any model call):

```
Scheduled account "main" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration,
or recreate this automation from the intended account.
```

The account **was** present in config the entire time. Automations with unbound owners (`-`), dashboard-bound owners, or non-announce delivery kept running normally — so the discriminator appears to be the legacy owner-session binding + announce resolution path, not actual config state.

Source observation (2026.11.6 dist, agent-tools policy module): the scheduled-run check calls `plugin?.config.listAccountIds(params.config).some(id => normalizeAccountId(id) === accountId)` and throws `unavailableScheduledAccount(accountId)` when the configured account id is not in that list. For legacy-bound jobs this evidently returns a list without the account.

## Fixes attempted that did NOT work

- `cron edit <id> --account main` — receipts unchanged
- `cron edit <id> --clear-session-key --channel discord --account main` — receipts unchanged

## What DID work

Recreating each automation with `cron add` (fresh bindings, same schedule/payload/delivery). After recreation, all four previously-failing jobs ran green. One job had accumulated 50+ consecutive errors over ~30h, taking down our task-queue dispatch pipeline.

## Expected behavior

- Migration/finalization should normalize automation owner+account bindings across updates (or doctor --fix should repair them), so pre-update automations keep working.
- Alternatively, the scheduled-run account resolution should fall back to the live channel config (`defaultAccount` / configured accounts) rather than failing when a legacy session-key binding cannot be resolved.

Happy to provide sanitized receipts, config shape, or additional diagnostics.

issues.body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 x64, npm install, gateway runs as schtask-driven process
- Update run executed 2026-11-20 ~02:30 local installing 2026.11.2 (later moved to 2026.11.6)
- Single gateway, multi-account Discord config

## What happened

An npm-channel update run abandoned mid-flight. `openclaw doctor` subsequently reported:

```
Update 7df99fd3-... remains abandoned: the target build was not recorded, so
current version equality cannot prove this update completed.
Recorded warnings from update 7df99fd3-...:
  Model retirement repair deferred until plugin convergence.
  Update finalization timed out in doctor after 900000ms
```

And `openclaw status` showed: `Update run: Last update run failed (abandoned)` — while the gateway was already serving the new version.

## Impact

No owner-facing alert was produced. The abandoned state was discovered ~18 hours later, only because scheduled automations started failing with a related-but-distinct error (scheduled-account validation against incompletely migrated state; see companion issue). The practical blast radius was ~30 hours of dead cron dispatch on a production agent.

## Expected behavior

When update finalization fails, times out, or a run is recorded abandoned:

1. The gateway should surface this to the owner proactively (delivery through a configured channel), not wait for a human to run doctor.
2. Doctor --fix / update repair should be attempted automatically or offered as a one-command recovery.
3. Ideally: automatic rollback to the last-known-good state when finalization cannot complete.

## Workaround used

Manual diagnosis (openclaw doctor + update status), then completing the migration via a deliberate maintenance window: gateway stop -> `openclaw doctor --fix` -> gateway start. Happy to provide doctor logs or update-history entries if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

On an inbound Voice Call routed to GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`), the caller is never heard after the opening greeting. Voice Call holds caller audio back while the greeting plays and releases it only after the model sends `response.done` and playback drains. GPT-Live's public API has no `response.done`, and it keeps streaming silent audio after it speaks, so neither condition is ever met. No caller audio reaches GPT-Live for the rest of the call.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Voice Call (Twilio) with `realtime.enabled: true`, provider `openai`, `providers.openai.model: "gpt-live-1"`, and an inbound greeting (default "Hello! How can I help you today?").
2. Call in and ask something after the greeting, e.g. "What's on my calendar today?".

### Expected behavior

After the greeting, caller audio reaches GPT-Live, it hears the question and delegates to the OpenClaw agent, as `gpt-realtime-2.1` does on the same setup.

### Actual behavior

GPT-Live speaks the greeting and then nothing else happens. A recording of the Gateway ↔ `api.openai.com` frames on current main shows four `session.input_audio.append` before the greeting and none in the following 38 s. The audio sent to the caller is about 4 s of greeting and then silence. No error or warning is logged.

The model is fine: replaying the same `session.start` and greeting note straight to the GPT-Live API, with caller audio either flowing or paused for 8 s after the greeting and then resumed, it transcribes the question and sends `session.delegation.created` both times.

### Cause

`createRealtimeCallAudioController` (`extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-call-session-control.ts`): `isGreetingPlaying()` stays true until `finishGreeting()` (called from `onResponseDone` or a continuity reset) and until playback drains. The GPT-Live bridge never calls `onResponseDone`, and its continuous silent frames keep the pacer busy. `realtime-handler.ts` drops caller audio while `isGreetingPlaying()` is true.

### OpenClaw version

main at e76922592.

### Operating system

Linux x64

### Install method

source checkout

### Model

OpenAI `gpt-live-1` (realtime voice, Platform API key)

### Provider / routing chain

Twilio inbound → voice-call plugin → OpenAI GPT-Live (gateway relay, native delegation) → OpenClaw agent

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not the same as #164473: there the model hears the question and says it will check; here the question never reaches the model.

issues.body:
### Summary

Show separate **Last inbound activity** and **Last outbound activity** timestamps in the existing shared Channels account details.

### Problem to solve

A channel can be connected while an incoming message still goes unanswered. In a [2026.11.6 WhatsApp support thread](https://community.openclaw.ai/t/whatsapp-shows-on-ok-but-direct-messages-get-no-reply-2026-11-6/503), the operator saw `ON/OK` and had to check Gateway logs to tell where the message flow stopped. Control UI shows recent inbound activity in the account details, but the Gateway already exposes an outbound timestamp there too. An operator who wants to compare the two currently has to leave the account page and inspect the CLI or logs.

### Proposed solution

- In the existing shared account details, show **Last inbound activity** and **Last outbound activity** for each account using the timestamps already returned by `channels.status`.
- Use the current relative-time display. For a direction without a recorded timestamp, show **Unknown**. Keep connection health separate from both timestamps.
- Describe these as the most recent recorded activities for the account. The timestamps alone cannot identify which inbound message led to a reply or confirm delivery to a recipient.

I propose starting with the shared account view and leaving channel-specific views and Gateway behavior as they are.

### Alternatives considered

The CLI and logs give more detail when tracing an individual message. Showing the two existing timestamps in the account view gives operators a quick first check while keeping that deeper diagnostic workflow available.

### Impact

Operators troubleshooting a connected account with no visible reply can check whether inbound and outbound activity were recorded from the same screen. Per-account rows also help operators avoid confusing activity on one account with activity on another.

### Evidence/examples

- [Community report and DevRel response](https://community.openclaw.ai/t/whatsapp-shows-on-ok-but-direct-messages-get-no-reply-2026-11-6/503)
- [Stable 2026.11.6 Gateway snapshot sets both timestamps](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/gateway/server-methods/channels.ts#L413-L418)
- [Stable 2026.11.6 account detail renders the inbound timestamp](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/ui/src/pages/channels/view.shared.tsx#L154-L181)
- [Current main still renders inbound activity in the shared account view](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dbf7aaf95b63b2d4f37e356de42b84c87a5a2ab1/ui/src/pages/channels/view.shared.tsx#L175-L195)

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. If this scope fits, I can implement the shared view change and cover both timestamps, a missing timestamp, and accounts with different activity times.

### Additional information

The evidence combines a public user report and source inspection. This proposal was drafted with AI assistance.

issues.body:
## Summary

On an explicit restart, the Gateway logs `gateway is draining for restart` and then sits in systemd's `stop-sigterm` state for the **full `TimeoutStopSec` window** (5m30s here) before being killed. Two periodic tasks keep firing once per minute against resources that have already been closed, each logging a failure and apparently never unregistering their timers.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), Linux, Node 24
- systemd `--user` unit from `openclaw gateway install`, `TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s`
- 17 plugins loaded, no channel plugins with long-lived connections

## Observed

```
19:36:59  [agents/subagent-registry] subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart
19:36:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:36:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:37:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:37:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:38:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:38:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
19:39:55  [health]   refresh failed: Gateway health refresh owner is closed
19:39:56  [plugins]  workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: Gateway request entry is closed
```

`systemctl --user show` during this period:

```
ActiveState=deactivating
SubState=stop-sigterm
TimeoutStopUSec=5min 30s
```

The unit became `active` again at 19:41:35, i.e. only once the stop timeout had elapsed and systemd escalated. The subagent sweep, by contrast, correctly notices the drain and skips itself — so the drain flag is reachable; these two tasks just don't consult it or don't clear their interval.

## Expected

After the drain begins, periodic tasks whose owning resources have been closed should unregister (or check the drain flag as `subagent-registry` already does), so the process can exit promptly instead of waiting out `TimeoutStopSec`.

## Impact

Every explicit restart costs ~5 minutes of downtime rather than seconds. With `Restart=always` this also widens the window described in #144976, where a stop that exhausts the drain window is followed by an unrequested restart — these two timers look like a plausible way to exhaust it.

## Notes on related issues

- #144976 — slow drain followed by unwanted auto-restart; this report may be one cause of the slow drain, but the symptom is different.
- #101720 (closed) and #128948 (closed) — timers outliving their owner in other subsystems; same shape, different components.
- #153153 — `TimeoutStopSec` too small on installed units; here the timeout is already 5m30s and is fully consumed.

This was observed while restarting to recover from #152965, so the two came up together, but they are independent: the hang reproduces on a plain restart regardless of what prompted it. Filing separately as offered in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152965#issuecomment-5751556093.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (`fc23bc8`), a naturally occurring `web_fetch` fallback-resolution event caused a measured Gateway liveness delay while the Gateway main Node/V8 thread synchronously loaded and captured unrelated runtime plugins.

A V8 CPU profile captured the event. During the approximately 12-second overdue interval, almost the entire interval was attributable to `loadRuntimePluginCandidate`, reached from the `web_fetch` fallback-provider discovery path.

The deployment had `tools.web.fetch.provider` unset and no installed/configured `contracts.webFetchProviders` provider such as Firecrawl. Despite that, fallback discovery entered the generic plugin loader and produced capture trees primarily for Discord.

This appears to be a Gateway-liveness issue caused by synchronous plugin discovery/materialization on the main JS thread, rather than slow HTTP fetching.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.8 (`fc23bc8`)
- Node: 26.10.0
- V8: 14.6.202.34-node.34
- SQLite: 3.53.4
- Linux, containerized
- Plugin captures on persistent ext4
- `tools.web.fetch.provider`: unset / auto-detect
- No installed or configured `webFetchProviders` provider
- No Firecrawl fetch provider
- Brave is configured for web search, not as a `webFetchProviders` implementation

Relevant docs:
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/web-fetch.md
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/web.md

## Observed production event

A live, loopback-only Node/V8 CPU profile captured a natural Gateway heartbeat delay.

Approximate delayed interval:

`2026-10-07 13:27:11.662 UTC` through `2026-10-07 13:27:23.759 UTC`

Measured liveness overdue time:

`12.097 seconds`

During that interval:

- Gateway main OS thread was running/on-CPU for about 93% of the interval.
- Approximately 11.95 seconds inclusive were attributed to `loadRuntimePluginCandidate`.
- `/proc` sampling showed the main thread runnable for 57/60 samples, with only three brief filesystem D-state samples.
- GC accounted for only about 0.13 seconds.
- Host CPU scheduling pressure was low.
- No cgroup CPU throttling or memory/OOM pressure occurred.

Approximate sample-weighted hot self operations:

- `lstat`: 3.24 s
- `copyFile`: 0.98 s
- Node path normalization: 0.98 s
- `isCapturedPathInside`: 0.82 s
- `structuredClone`: 0.57 s
- GC: 0.13 s

## Resolved call path

The profile resolved this path:

`web_fetch`
→ `resolveWebFetchDefinition`
→ `resolveRuntimeWebFetchProviders`
→ `resolvePluginWebProviders`
→ `loadOpenClawPlugins`
→ `loadRuntimePluginCandidate`
→ `capturePluginGenerationArtifact`

The capture implementation performs synchronous filesystem inspection/materialization, including stat/lstat, realpath, directory enumeration, hashing, and copy operations on the Gateway thread.

Relevant current source:
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/plugins/web-provider-runtime-shared.ts

## Unrelated plugin capture generated during the profiled resolver window

A contemporaneous plugin capture generation contained:

| Candidate | Files | Allocated bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| Discord | 6,088 | 73,703,424 |
| Brave | 11 | 106,496 |
| DeepSeek | 15 | 106,496 |
| Total | 6,114 | 73,916,416 |

Discord accounted for nearly all captured files/bytes even though it does not provide `webFetchProviders`.

No Firecrawl capture tree or other actual fetch-provider implementation was present, and no fallback provider ultimately supplied page content.

This suggests generic runtime-plugin discovery/materialization was performed in order to determine that no usable fetch fallback provider was available.

## What was ruled out during the event

There was no overlapping:

- `SQLITE_BUSY`
- database-lock failure
- writer-admission/queue timeout
- meaningful SQLite transaction hold explaining the interval
- substantial GC pause
- cgroup memory pressure/OOM event
- CPU throttling
- host scheduler contention

The main thread was predominantly consuming CPU in the plugin-loader/capture path.

## Warm control

A later controlled test was performed on the already-warm Gateway without restarting it.

Direct readable page:

`https://example.com/?riker-web-fetch-ab=20261007`

Result:
- direct fetch + Readability succeeded
- approximately 1.731 s
- no liveness stall

A public HTTP-200 HTML fixture containing no usable readable text was then used to exercise provider fallback.

Result:
- fallback resolver was entered
- approximately 1.672 s
- no provider supplied content
- no new capture generation
- `loadOpenClawPlugins` / `loadRuntimePluginCandidate` did not reappear
- no >=2 s liveness delay

This demonstrates that provider-fallback entry itself is not always slow. The expensive path appears dependent on cold/process-state provider discovery.

## Reproduction status

The natural production event above is the measured reproduction.

The warm control proves the fallback condition but does NOT reproduce the expensive cold plugin-capture path.

A candidate cold reproduction, not yet independently confirmed as deterministic, is:

1. Start a fresh Gateway/process with:
   - `tools.web.fetch.provider` unset
   - no installed/configured ready `webFetchProviders` provider.
2. Before fetch-provider discovery has been warmed, invoke `web_fetch` against successful HTML for which Readability returns no usable text.
3. Profile the Gateway main thread and observe plugin-capture output.

Please do not interpret this candidate cold procedure as already confirmed deterministic; the strongest evidence is the naturally captured production event.

## Expected behavior

If direct HTTP succeeds but Readability cannot extract usable content and there is no eligible fetch fallback provider, `web_fetch` should determine that no fallback is available without synchronously loading/materializing unrelated plugins on the Gateway main thread.

If eligible `contracts.webFetchProviders` implementations do exist, discovery should load only those candidate plugin owners.

## Actual behavior

During the observed cold/provider-discovery path, `web_fetch` fallback resolution reached the generic plugin loader and synchronously captured unrelated plugins, predominantly Discord, blocking the Gateway main event loop long enough to delay its heartbeat by 12.097 seconds.

## Suggested fix

Use manifest/registry metadata to determine eligible `contracts.webFetchProviders` candidates before generic runtime loading.

Possible behavior:

1. If no eligible `webFetchProviders` candidate exists, return the no-provider result immediately without invoking the generic runtime-plugin loader.

2. If eligible candidates exist, load only the plugin owners declared as fetch-provider candidates rather than loading/capturing unrelated runtime plugins.

This should allow ordinary direct HTTP + Readability `web_fetch` to remain lightweight while keeping optional provider fallback.

## Related issues

These appear related but are not believed to be duplicates:

- #74915 — `web_fetch` provider discovery behavior
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74915

- #159499 — plugin-registry phases / event-loop stalls
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159499

- #162514 — plugin source-capture rebuild performance
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162514

## Additional evidence

A sanitized V8 profile and `/proc` sampling record exist from the observed event. They are not attached initially because production transcripts, private URLs, credentials, and complete production configuration should not be uploaded.

I can provide a minimized/sanitized profile artifact if maintainers need it.

No private URLs, authentication material, transcripts, or full production configuration are included in this report.
