### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Windows 10, openclaw 2026.11.5 aborts every config read with EACCES because the SQLite read-only worker cannot create its private snapshot staging directory, while 2026.9.5 on the same host with the same config and state DB exits 0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install 2026.11.5 into an isolated prefix: `npm install --prefix <dir> openclaw@2026.11.5`.
2. Redirect HOME, USERPROFILE, LOCALAPPDATA, APPDATA and XDG_CACHE_HOME to an isolated tree.
3. Put a working 2026.9.5 `openclaw.json` at `<HOME>\.openclaw\openclaw.json`.
4. Put the 2026.9.5 state DB (`user_version=17`, 13,135,872 B) at `<HOME>\.openclaw\state\openclaw.sqlite`.
5. Run `<prefix>\node_modules\.bin\openclaw.cmd config validate` -> exit code 1 with the error below.
6. Remove the state DB and rerun -> exit code 0 (only `Unrecognized key: agents.defaults.heartbeat` warnings), so the state DB alone flips the result.

```
Config needs correction: ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json
  - <root>: read failed at <HOME>\.openclaw\openclaw.json: Error: filesystem did not
    enforce the private directory DACL; snapshot staging root <XDG_CACHE_HOME>\openclaw:
    check filesystem health and write permissions or set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable
    filesystem
Resolve the read error shown above, then retry.
```

### Expected behavior

`openclaw config validate` should read the existing config and report it as valid, as 2026.9.5 does on this host:

```
Config valid: ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json
(exit 0)
```

Same host, same `openclaw.json`, same state DB (`user_version=17`, 13,135,872 B), only the package version differs.

### Actual behavior

`config validate` exits 1 and never reaches the config content:

```
Error: filesystem did not enforce the private directory DACL; snapshot staging root
<XDG_CACHE_HOME>\openclaw: check filesystem health and write permissions or set
XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable filesystem
```

`OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` changes the wording, not the outcome (exit 1):

```
Error: private object security was not enforced; snapshot staging root <XDG_CACHE_HOME>\openclaw ...
[FS_SAFE_NATIVE_FALLBACK] FsSafeWarning: windows-private-directory is using its portable fallback
because native support is disabled by OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE (disabled).
Expected @openclaw/fs-safe-win32-x64-msvc@0.26.13. ...
```

Measured rule-outs on the failing host:

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Missing native module | files present under `<prefix>/node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe-win32-x64-msvc` | still fails |
| Volume / filesystem | XDG_CACHE_HOME on C: and on D:, both NTFS | both fail |
| Loose inherited DACL | `icacls <root> /inheritance:r /grant SYSTEM:F Administrators:F <currentUser>:F` (SDDL becomes `O:...D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)`) | still fails |
| Owner is a group, not the user | `icacls <root> /setowner <userSID>` + `Set-Acl` owner = user SID | still fails |
| Mode switch | `OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` / `auto` | both fail, same exit code 1 |

Additional observations:
- After every failed run the staging root stays empty - no child directory is left behind, so creation aborts during its own verification step.
- The error string does not appear in `dist/*.mjs`; it is raised inside `@openclaw/fs-safe-win32-x64-msvc`.
- Hypothesis (not confirmed): on this machine the policy "System objects: Default owner for objects created by members of the Administrators group" is set to Administrators, so directories are owned by `BUILTIN\Administrators` unless ownership is set explicitly. If the fs-safe private-directory check requires owner == current user without SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege/SeRestorePrivilege, it cannot pass on this host.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (npm @openclaw/openclaw 2026.11.5; regression vs 2026.9.5)

### Operating system

Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, C: and D: both NTFS

### Install method

npm install --prefix <isolated dir> openclaw@2026.11.5, isolated HOME/USERPROFILE/LOCALAPPDATA/APPDATA/XDG_CACHE_HOME

### Model

N/A - config validate fails before any model is loaded

### Provider / routing chain

N/A - no gateway/provider in the path; failure occurs in local fs-safe private directory creation

### Additional provider/model setup details

None. This is not a provider/model issue. Native packages `@openclaw/fs-safe-win32-x64-msvc` and `@openclaw/proc-safe-win32-x64-msvc` are present; no gateway or provider is started by `config validate`.

### Logs

```shell
Version comparison on the same host, same config, same state DB:
- 2026.9.5 `config validate` -> `Config valid: ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json`, exit 0.
- 2026.11.5 `config validate` -> error above, exit 1.
- 2026.11.5 without the state DB -> exit 0.

Failure output (verbatim, 2026-11-18 23:12 local):

Config needs correction: ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json
  - <root>: read failed at <HOME>\.openclaw\openclaw.json: Error: filesystem did not
    enforce the private directory DACL; snapshot staging root <XDG_CACHE_HOME>\openclaw:
    check filesystem health and write permissions or set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable
    filesystem
Resolve the read error shown above, then retry.

`OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` variant:

Error: private object security was not enforced; snapshot staging root <XDG_CACHE_HOME>\openclaw ...
[FS_SAFE_NATIVE_FALLBACK] FsSafeWarning: windows-private-directory is using its portable fallback
because native support is disabled by OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE (disabled).
Expected @openclaw/fs-safe-win32-x64-msvc@0.26.13. ... Private Windows directory creation launches
the packaged .NET helper for each check or creation.
(exit 1)

Staging root DACL before / after hardening (both still fail):

before: O:LAG:S-1-5-21-<...>-513D:(A;ID;FA;;;BA)(A;OICIIOID;GA;;;BA)(A;ID;FA;;;SY)(A;OICIIOID;GA;;;SY)(A;ID;0x1301bf;;;AU)...
after : O:LAG:S-1-5-21-<...>-513D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)

Host: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, elevated Administrator.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Windows hosts running 2026.11.x where objects created by Administrators are owned by `BUILTIN\Administrators` by default; observed on 1 host.
- Severity: blocks workflow.
- Frequency: always (every config-reading command fails while a state DB exists).
- Consequence: the 2026.9.5 -> 11.x upgrade cannot complete, because the first post-install `config validate` fails and the schema/state migration is never reached. Production stays on 2026.9.5.

### Additional information

- Regression bounds: last known good 2026.9.5, first known bad 2026.11.5 (both measured on this host).
- Non-blocking secondary finding: in 11.x `agents.defaults.heartbeat` is reported as `Unrecognized key` during validate (exit 0); 2026.9.5 accepts it.
- Related: #180892 (Windows Doctor rejects native capture for DELETE-self permission on a volume-root ancestor - same fs-safe Windows private-directory family, different check), #156985 (Kubernetes /tmp emptyDir lacks sticky protection required by fs-safe).
- Duplicate search on 2026-11-19: no existing issue matches this error text; `"private object security was not enforced"` returns 0 results.

issues.body:
# Replayed inter-session messages should carry original sentAt/acceptedAt metadata

## Summary

When `sessions_send` targets a busy session, the input is persisted ("saved inputs") and re-delivered later by the delivery-recovery mechanism after a gateway restart or when the target session becomes idle. The replayed message body is injected **without any visible original-send timestamp**, so the receiving agent cannot distinguish a fresh instruction from a stale one that may be hours (or days) old.

## Real-world incident (multi-agent production gateway, 9+ agents)

On 2026-11-21 our agents exchanged ~51 inter-session messages that could not be delivered to busy sessions. They were retained (`Session delivery recovery blocked for 51 saved inputs; inputs retained.`) and replayed after the gateway restart at 08:48 on 2026-11-22.

Consequences observed:

1. An agent received a "P0 coordinate now" instruction **18+ hours late** and re-executed an already-closed investigation, burning tokens and nearly re-triggering remediation that had already been applied.
2. Another agent received a stale disk-alert copy ("Data volume down to 21.97 GiB") whose numbers no longer matched reality (volume had recovered to 52 GiB), risking a wrong triage.
3. Two approvals for the same action arrived twice (dedup worked on our side only because the receiving agent noticed).

The receiving agent's only clues were an in-body human-written time like "15:1x" (often absent) and `[Inter-session message]` headers, which carry **no timestamp at all**.

## Current behavior

The injected replay looks like:

```text
[Inter-session message] sourceSession=agent:dev-local:main sourceChannel=webchat sourceTool=sessions_send isUser=false
This content was routed by OpenClaw from another session or internal tool. ...
<message body>
```

No `sentAt` / `acceptedAt` / `originalDeliveryAttempt` fields are present.

## Proposed behavior

When a saved input is re-delivered (i.e., delivery happens materially later than acceptance), include machine-readable provenance in the routing header, e.g.:

```text
[Inter-session message] sourceSession=... sentAt=2026-11-21T15:05:32+08:00 acceptedAt=... deliveredAt=2026-11-22T08:49:12+08:00 replayed=true
```

Optionally add a one-line advisory when `deliveredAt - sentAt` exceeds a threshold (e.g., 10 minutes):

```text
NOTE: this message was queued for 17h44m before delivery; verify it is still actionable before executing.
```

The data already exists: the interrupted-inputs debug view shows `acceptedAt` per saved input (e.g., `"acceptedAt":1795310745011,"state":"interrupted","provenance":"inter_session"`). It simply is not surfaced into the delivered prompt.

## Why this matters

LLM agents treat prompt content as "now". Stale instructions that look fresh cause: duplicated work, execution of already-cancelled remediation, contradictory state across agents, and (worst case) destructive re-runs. A single `sentAt`/`replayed=true` annotation lets every agent apply a cheap freshness check without out-of-band coordination.

## Environment

- OpenClaw gateway (self-hosted, macOS), multi-agent setup with 9+ agents exchanging inter-session messages via `sessions_send`.
- Evidence logs: `Session delivery recovery blocked for 51 saved inputs; inputs retained.` (gateway log, 2026-11-22 08:49:12); delivery-recovery refusal guard `refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation` observed on 2026-11-21 22:11.


## Scenario 2 (added 2026-11-22): interrupted inputs regain queued custody and replay in a loop

A second, related failure mode observed in the same deployment:

- A nightly cron job (22:00) fans out `sessions_send` archive instructions to ~11 agents. One agent's main session accumulated **14 pending inputs in state `interrupted`** (timestamps spanning 6 days, verified via `sessions_history` → `pendingInputs`).
- Per the documented semantics, interrupted inputs are "saved without an active retry" but "eligible durable peer sends can regain queued custody on startup". In practice, **every time the session activates, the same interrupted inputs are re-injected into the prompt**; if that turn is itself interrupted (e.g. `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` preemption, which was frequent for this session), the input is not consumed, falls back to `interrupted`, and is injected again on the next activation.
- Result: the **exact same message was delivered 7 times** to the receiving agent between one evening and the next morning, with zero content increment each time — pure replay noise that burns tokens and risks duplicate execution of stale approvals.
- A companion artifact: two byte-identical copies of one approval message (ids differing, `acceptedAt` 13s apart) appeared in another session's interrupted-inputs view, suggesting the same save/re-inject path can also duplicate a single logical message.

Suggested fixes (in addition to the `sentAt`/`replayed` metadata proposal above):

1. Mark a saved input **consumed once it has been injected** into a model turn, even if that turn is later interrupted — re-injection should require an explicit retry decision, not automatic custody regain.
2. Cap re-injection attempts per saved input (e.g. 2-3) and surface a warning listing the stuck inputs afterwards.
3. De-duplicate identical saved inputs (same source session + byte-identical text within a short window) at admission time.

issues.body:
### Summary

When an agent whose session model is text-only generates an image in a chat (`image_generate`), the image is delivered, but the follow-up completion turn fails with `Image attachments could not be analyzed. Configure agents.defaults.imageModel or tools.media.models with an available vision model, then retry.` The announce then retries forever with `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`, and the chat session stays stuck until the Gateway restarts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a session model that the model catalog reports as text-only (in my case an OpenAI-compatible proxy model whose `/v1/models` entry lists `input_modalities: ["text"]`), with `agents.defaults.imageModel` pointing at the same text-only model.
2. In a chat session, ask the agent for a picture so it calls `image_generate` (chat runs it in the background).
3. Wait for the generation to finish.

### Expected behavior

The generated image is delivered and the agent's completion turn runs normally. The agent created the image itself, so no image-understanding pass should be needed to hand the file back.

### Actual behavior

- The image itself reaches the chat.
- The completion turn carries the generated file as an attachment. Because the session model has no image input, `agent-content-phase` sets `needsImageUnderstanding`, and `agent-image-understanding` throws `Image attachments could not be analyzed …` when no vision model produces a description.
- The direct announce retries every ~2 s and every retry fails with `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input` (thousands of log lines per hour, one loop per generated image).
- The requester session never sees the completion, so the agent believes the image is still pending: it repeats "it's on its way", re-sends earlier images, and promises new ones that are never generated. Only a Gateway restart stops the loops.

The same setup worked until the session model's catalog entry flipped from image-capable to text-only (an upstream proxy started advertising the model as text-only after its routing pool changed), which is how I noticed that the completion path depends on image understanding at all.

### OpenClaw version

main `bb44e168d34` (2026.11.6), also seen on `4126cf267df` and `a6983ed`

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04 (Node 24)

### Install method

Source build (`pnpm install && pnpm build`), systemd user service

### Model / provider route

OpenAI-compatible proxy (`openai-responses` API) whose model catalog entry is text-only; Matrix channel

### Logs

```text
[gateway] Offloaded image for text-only model. Saved: media://inbound/<generated>.png
[media-understanding] image: failed (0/1) reason=Model does not support images
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for session image_generate:tool:image_generate:<id> err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Image attachments could not be analyzed. Configure agents.defaults.imageModel or tools.media.models with an available vision model, then retry.", ...}
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for session image_generate:tool:image_generate:<id> err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input","errorCode":"UNAVAILABLE", ...}
... (repeats every ~2 s until restart)
```

### Impact

Every chat image request on a text-only session model leaves the session stuck. Configuring a vision `imageModel` works around the throw, but then every generated image is sent to a vision model only to describe a picture the agent just created. On my images that took 10-60 s each, and several vision models returned empty output or refused.

### Additional information

I have a small fix ready: skip the forced image-understanding pass when the turn's input provenance is an agent-mediated media-generation completion (`image_generate`, `music_generate`, `video_generate`, agent harness). The files are still offloaded as references for text-only models. I will open a PR that links this issue.

issues.body:
### Summary

On stable **2026.11.5**, unbound `agentTurn` automations that resolve to the `claude-cli` runtime fail on every run:

```
Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime claude-cli would run anthropic/<model> with stored account anthropic:manual. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <model>@anthropic:manual, or with openclaw doctor --fix.
```

The message names `openclaw doctor --fix` as a fix, but **`openclaw doctor` reports no finding for these jobs and `doctor --fix` doesn't bind them**. Only the per-job `automations edit` works. This is related to #191818 (which covers the pre-#180492 releases) and the 11.5-beta.1 report there. This issue is about the stable 11.5 recovery path.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), updated from 2026.9.7 |
| Install | npm global, launchd LaunchAgent |
| OS | macOS 15.7.9, x86_64 (Intel) |
| Node | managed runtime 24.19.0 |
| Auth | stored Anthropic profile `anthropic:manual` plus a native Claude CLI login (`claude auth status` → `loggedIn: true`) |
| Jobs | ~33 `agentTurn` automations with no `payload.model` (inherit the agent default, an `anthropic/*` model on `claude-cli`) |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have agentTurn automations without an explicit model, inheriting an `anthropic/*` default that runs on `claude-cli`, with a stored `anthropic:*` token profile configured.
2. Update to 2026.11.5.
3. Wait for a run, or force one. It fails with the error above.
4. Run `claude auth login`, confirm `claude auth status` shows `loggedIn: true`, and fully restart the Gateway. Runs still fail the same way.
5. Run `openclaw doctor`. There is no adoption/binding finding for these jobs. `openclaw doctor --fix` leaves them unbound.

Session-targeted jobs (`session:<key>`) are also affected. Their failures show in the session as "Session event execution failed" rather than the account error.

### Expected

- Per the docs (`automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`, "Inference account continuity"), unbound CLI-runtime automations use the CLI's own login. With a valid native Claude CLI login, they should run.
- If a binding is required instead, `openclaw doctor --fix` should detect and record it, since the refusal message names it as the remedy.

### Actual

Every run is refused. `doctor` doesn't see the problem and `doctor --fix` doesn't repair it. A native CLI login and a Gateway restart don't help.

### Workaround

Per job:

```
openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model anthropic/<model>@anthropic:manual
openclaw automations edit <jobId> --clear-model
```

The first edit records the binding. The second clears the explicit model so the job inherits the default again. The recorded binding survives the clear, and runs then succeed. Downside: the binding stays tied to the model chosen at edit time, so changing the agent default later may need a rebind.

### Asks

1. Make `doctor` / `doctor --fix` detect and bind (or adopt the native login for) unbound CLI-runtime jobs that the run path refuses. Or change the refusal message so it no longer points at `doctor --fix`.
2. Make the docs' "unbound CLI-runtime automations use the CLI's own login" statement match runtime behaviour when a stored profile also exists.

issues.body:
**版本环境**:
- OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), macOS (arm64), node v24.22.1
- `agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush`: enabled, model=qwen3.7-plus, soft threshold 4000 tokens
- 多 Agent 部署(15 workspaces),MEMORY.md 为各 agent 长期记忆文件

## 现象
连续两晚(2026-11-20、2026-11-21)**22:00:04 同一秒**,某一 agent 的 MEMORY.md 被截断为 **1 字节**(单个换行符),原文件 14KB+ 长期记忆全部丢失(靠 git/bak 恢复,未造成实际数据丢失)。

决定性特征:
- 两晚被清空的都是**同一个 agent**,其余 7 家 agent 的 MEMORY.md mtime 也全部=22:00:04 同一秒,但内容非空
- 22:00:00 有一个 cron job(归档调度)通过 sessions_send 批量唤醒多个 agent 的 message turn
- 仅 message turn 触发,心跳/CLI turn 不触发

**更严重的常态表现——静默回退(后续内容级比对实证)**:1 字节只是极端情形。对同秒被写的其他 agent:
- 2 家 agent 的磁盘现值与其 **24 天前(Oct 28)的备份逐字节一致**(cmp IDENTICAL)——每晚 22:00:04 的 flush 把 MEMORY.md 重写为注入上下文中的陈旧版本,磁盘记忆停滞 24 天零增长,期间增量被静默抹掉
- 1 家 agent 的现值为 flush 新生成的 LLM 摘要版(不等于任何历史备份,尺寸缩水)
- 历史 bak 序列显示常态缩水 -17%~-32%(疑似自 Oct 起持续)
- 全程无任何告警/日志提示写入内容异常,用户完全无感知

## 根因分析
pre-compaction memoryFlush 机制:上下文超阈时在 turn 开始触发"压缩前记忆刷盘",由 LLM 生成应保留的记忆内容并回写 MEMORY.md。

写入路径(short-term-promotion-memory-write 模块)为 `writeFile(content)` + `truncate(len)`,**对 LLM 生成内容无任何校验**:
1. 无空值校验——模型返回空/近空(如单个 `\n`)时直接提交,清空原文件(1B 截断案)
2. 无新鲜度/尺寸校验——以失真注入上下文为源生成时,输出为陈旧版本或缩水摘要也直接提交,静默覆盖磁盘上更新的记忆(回退案)

单家连中两晚 1B 的特异性因素已复现验证(cron receipts 取证,记录表可回溯 3 周无缺口):**双 session 并发干扰假说被证伪**——第一晚该 agent 名下独立定时任务全天 0 触发,不存在并发;第二晚 22:00:00 有并发但非必要条件。更符合「同一 agent 连中两晚」确定性的解释是**输入侧稳定性**:该 agent 的 MEMORY.md 在同秒被写 8 家中最大(14.7KB,其余 7-8KB),flush 由轻量模型(qwen3.7-plus)执行,大输入下稳定返回空/近空输出。但无论诱因如何,**生成内容不经校验直接覆盖磁盘**是确定性缺陷,空值/尺寸/新鲜度校验可同时拦截上述所有形态。

## 复现条件
1. memoryFlush enabled + 多 agent
2. 定时任务在同一秒批量触发多个 agent 的 message turn(部分为休眠/idle agent 被唤醒)
3. 被唤醒 agent 上下文超 soft 阈值触发 flush;LLM 生成质量不可控(轻量模型面对大输入/注入上下文陈旧时,输出空、旧版或缩水版)

## 期望行为(修复建议)
1. flush 提交前校验生成内容:空/近空(如 <N 字节)时**拒绝写入**并记 warning
2. 回退防护:新内容尺寸 < 磁盘现值某阈值(如 50%)、或磁盘现值 mtime 晚于注入快照时,拒绝提交或要求 merge
3. 写入前保留 `.bak`(或写临时文件+原子 rename+尺寸 sanity check)
4. flush 语义考虑 append/merge 而非全量 replace

## 影响
agent 长期记忆丢失:极端时整文件清空,常态时静默回退到陈旧版本(实测 2 个 agent 磁盘记忆停滞 24 天、增量被抹掉且完全无感知)。多 agent 生产环境下无 git/bak 时属不可逆数据损毁。

## 现行 workaround
外部守护脚本每 10 分钟巡检(automations command payload):增大/持平时刷快照;缩水时冻结快照+存证+告警;缩水>=50% 或 <100B 截断时自动从快照恢复+告警。

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.6** (fe06181), Node v26.12.1, Linux (Proxmox host, x64)
- Provider: `opencode-go` (OpenAI-compatible), primary model `glm-5.3-flash` with model fallbacks
- Prompt cache mode: `boundary-aware:openai-completions`
- Multi-agent setup: ~17 configured agents, cross-agent handoffs via `sessions_send` with inline wait; ordinary turns run 2-6 tool calls each
- Channels: Telegram forum topics + Home Assistant Assist through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.enabled: true`)

## Symptoms

Every model request logs `cache read dropped N -> 0`, so the full prompt (14k-27k tokens) is reprocessed from scratch on **every** call — including consecutive calls **within the same turn**. Each call costs 1-8 s of stream time (measured window: 41 calls, median 4.1 s, max 14 s), and a user message needing a 4-11 call chain takes 20-50+ s end-to-end. Synchronous clients (voice Assist) hit their timeout and disconnect mid-turn (`ClientDisconnectError`).

## Evidence (gateway journal, sanitized)

1. Within-turn drop with NO tracked change (request 3 of the same run, 5.5 s after request 2):

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] cache read dropped 14592 -> 0 runId=<redacted> request=3
for opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash via boundary-aware:openai-completions;
no tracked cache input change; requestGapMs=5544 promptTokens=18176 providerPrefix=prefix-match
```

2. historyRewrite because the user-message envelope is re-stamped on every request:

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] message 0 (user) differs from the previous request;
history must be append-only; changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw
```

```
cache read dropped 15104 -> 10240 ... historyRewrite(message 27 (user) differs ...;
changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=31690 promptTokens=17043 providerPrefix=message:2
```

3. Runtime-context carrier invalidating the provider history mid-turn (request 8 of the same run):

```
cache read dropped 13056 -> 0 ... request=8 ...
runtimeContextCarrier(runtimeContextCarrier changed provider history);
requestGapMs=2317 promptTokens=14866 providerPrefix=message:14
```

4. System-prompt digest change (expected after workspace file edits; listed for completeness):

```
cache read dropped 12160 -> 0 ... systemPrompt(system prompt digest changed (sections: Project Context)),
historyRewrite(message 27 ... envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=538656 promptTokens=17220 providerPrefix=message:0
```


### Steps to reproduce

Multi-agent gateway + any OpenAI-compatible provider with prompt caching. Send a message that makes an agent perform 2+ tool calls (or a `sessions_send` handoff with inline wait) and watch `[prompt-cache]` lines in the gateway journal. Drops appear on every request, including back-to-back requests in the same run.


### Expected behavior

Per `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`, consecutive request histories in the same session extend the previous request, and transient runtime-context carriers "remain outside the cached prefix" — a tool loop inside one turn should pay prefill once and reuse the cached prefix on follow-up calls.


### Actual behavior

The cache drops to zero on effectively every request, including same-turn follow-ups where the log reports `no tracked cache input change`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.6

### Operating system

Proxmox

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

Opencodego glm5.3 and all models wotch cache 

### Provider / routing chain

-

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity


- Every multi-tool agent turn re-processes 14k-27k token prefixes: 20-50+ s per user message.
- Voice/Assist integrations (synchronous clients with 60-120 s budgets) abort mid-turn — the answer never reaches the user.
- Billed tokens multiplied by the number of requests per turn.

issues.body:
### Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.9.2 (3928bad)**, macOS 26.5.1 (arm64), node 26.5.0, ~52 agents on one gateway
- Primary model: `openai/gpt-6-astra` via ChatGPT-subscription OAuth
  (`agentRuntime.id: codex`, `api=openai-chatgpt-responses`, `route=native policy=hidden`)
- Fallbacks configured and **healthy the whole time**:
  `kiro-gateway/claude-opus-4.5` and `qwen-local/Qwen`, both present in
  `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow`; no session-level model or auth overrides anywhere

### Summary
When a `server_is_overloaded` assistant error triggers the same-model transient retry, and that
**retry attempt** then dies with an error the classifier does not recognise, the run resolves to
`continue_normal` with `reason=none` and **the configured model fallback chain is never consulted** —
even though the primary is demonstrably down and the fallback provider is demonstrably up.

The classified reason from the *first* attempt is discarded by the *second* attempt's failure.

This is not #116315 (there the fallback model was missing from the agent catalog, and stale session
overrides bypassed the chain — neither applies here), and not #132611 (there `reason=overloaded`
reaches the chain correctly; here the reason never survives to the decision).

### Observed sequence (single run, from gateway.log)

```
10:23:37.660  embedded run prompt start: runId=4e10bbde... provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses route=native policy=hidden
10:23:40.168  embedded run prompt end:   runId=4e10bbde... durationMs=6983
              assistant message: stopReason=error, errorCode="server_is_overloaded",
              errorMessage="Codex error: Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later."
10:23:41.226  embedded run start:        runId=4e10bbde...   <-- same-model transient retry, same runId
10:23:44.947  embedded run prompt end:   runId=4e10bbde... durationMs=3444
              assistant message: stopReason=error, errorCode=<absent>,
              errorMessage="Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>"
10:23:44.953  embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=continue_normal reason=none
              attempt=1 retry=1 rotations=0 from=openai/gpt-6-astra
              rawError=Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>
```

The run then ends. No `rotate_profile`, no `fallback_model`. The end user gets a generic
`Agent run failed (model: openai/gpt-6-astra).` after ~28-67 ms of apparent work.

The identical shape reproduced in a second run the same minute (`runId=3b6290d4...`: 10:24:20
overload, 10:24:24 keyed-turn error, `reason=none`).

### Why the reason is lost
- `classifyAssistantFailoverReason` (`dist/embedded-agent-helpers-*.js`) builds its signal from
  `errorCode` / `errorType` / `errorMessage`. The overload attempt carries a structured
  `errorCode: server_is_overloaded` and classifies fine. The retry's error carries **no `errorCode`**
  and its text matches none of the message patterns, so classification returns `null`.
- `resolveRunFailoverDecision` (`dist/embedded-agent-*.js`) advances the chain only when
  `params.failoverFailure` is set, which follows from a non-null reason. With `reason=none` it
  returns `continue_normal` and the run ends.
- `mergeRetryFailoverReason` already threads the earlier reason through as `lastRetryFailoverReason`
  on the retry action, but the final decision is resolved from the **current** attempt's
  `failoverReason`, so the carried value never influences the outcome.

### Suggested direction
When an attempt exists only because a previous attempt was classified as transient, and that attempt
fails with an unclassified error, resolve the decision from the carried previous reason rather than
`none`, so the chain advances instead of the turn dying. Deliberately not proposing a specific patch
shape — the carried value already exists; the question is whether the decision should consult it.

### Secondary observation (may warrant its own issue)
The trigger for the failed retry is the keyed-turn guard
(`Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`, `dist/session-manager-*.js`).
PR #133094 (`fix(agents): preserve keyed turns across compaction`, merged 2026-08-30) is present in
this build, yet the guard still fires — on the **failover/transient retry** path rather than across
compaction. Possibly related to #142224. 9 occurrences on this gateway on 2026-09-14 alone.

### Impact on this deployment (2026-09-14, one gateway)
- 65 failover decisions logged that day: **100% `continue_normal` / `reason=none`;
  0 `fallback_model`, 0 `rotate_profile`.**
- `openai/gpt-6-astra`: 175 runs, 31 `server_is_overloaded` failures (~18%).
- `kiro-gateway/claude-opus-4.5` the same day: 339 requests, **339 x HTTP 200**.
  `qwen-local/Qwen`: 152 requests, **152 x HTTP 200**.
- So every one of those 31 failures had a healthy, configured, allow-listed fallback available and
  did not use it. End users received "the AI service is temporarily overloaded" and no answer.
- The first `server_is_overloaded` in ~4 months of stored transcripts is 2026-09-08 — the day this
  fleet moved 47 agents onto `gpt-6-astra`. Daily counts since: 10 / 6 / 9 / 15 / 31.

Happy to provide redacted trajectory excerpts, the full failover-decision log lines, or a config
dump on request.

### Related work checked before filing
- #116315 — `server_is_overloaded` on ChatGPT-subscription OAuth. Different cause: there the
  fallback model was absent from the agent catalog and stale session overrides bypassed the chain.
  Here the fallback models are present, allow-listed, healthy, and there are no session overrides.
- #132611 — fallback chain not consulted on `reason=timeout`. There `reason=overloaded` reaches the
  chain correctly; here the reason never survives the retry to reach the decision at all.
- PR #141843 (open) — classifies untyped 5xx as `server_error` instead of `timeout`. Adjacent code,
  but it would not cover this case: the retry's failure carries no HTTP status and no `errorCode`
  (it is an internal `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`), so it classifies
  to `null` rather than to the wrong reason. The point here is the *loss of the previous attempt's
  already-correct classification across the retry boundary*.
- PR #133094 (merged 2026-08-30, present in this build) — preserves keyed turns across compaction.
  The guard still fires here, on the failover/transient-retry path rather than across compaction.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in, single-owner escalation provider for Active Memory so a plugin can decide whether to start deep recall after the deterministic lane has no strong hit.

## Problem to solve

Active Memory has a sound two-lane architecture: the deterministic lane is cheap, while the deep lane runs a blocking embedded agent only when escalation is warranted. In the default escalate mode, however, the escalation decision is closed inside the bundled plugin and based on a built-in lexical intent matcher.

That leaves operators with only three choices:

- off: never run deep recall;
- always: pay for a blocking recall agent on every eligible turn;
- escalate: depend on the built-in matcher.

The matcher has already required language-specific repairs, including CJK support and the current PT-BR work in #135085 and #136502. A third-party plugin cannot replace only this decision: prompt-build hooks compose rather than claim the decision, and replacing the bundled Active Memory plugin also means taking ownership of its session isolation, privacy rules, timeouts, cleanup, caching, circuit breaker, status and deep-recall orchestration.

The missing capability is not another recall engine. It is a supported extension point for the small decision immediately before deep recall.

## Proposed solution

Expose an optional, lifecycle-aware Active Memory escalation provider through the plugin SDK.

Conceptually:

- a plugin registers one provider by id;
- Active Memory selects it through an optional escalationProvider config field;
- the provider runs only in escalate mode, after the deterministic lane has no strong hit and before the embedded recall agent starts;
- it returns recall, skip, or abstain;
- the provider receives an AbortSignal and a short bounded timeout;
- absent, missing, timed-out, failed or abstaining providers fall back according to an explicit, documented policy;
- off, always and strong deterministic hits retain their current behavior;
- existing configurations and defaults remain unchanged.

A dedicated provider is preferable to a general accumulating hook because exactly one component should own this decision. The SDK contract should not require or bundle any model. Implementations could be deterministic, local learned classifiers, or another policy chosen by the operator.

I plan to open a focused PR containing the SDK contract, registry/lifecycle handling, Active Memory integration, config/schema/UI hints, documentation and tests. It will not add a model, weights, network request or new runtime dependency.

## Alternatives considered

### Keep adding language-specific matcher rules

This preserves zero-dependency behavior but does not provide a scalable customization path. The PT-BR gap demonstrates that operators cannot currently supply a better policy without replacing the whole plugin.

### Run a generic LLM completion before recall

This adds another serial model request, authentication/failure surface, cost and latency to the path whose purpose is deciding whether to pay for deep recall.

### Replace the bundled Active Memory plugin

OpenClaw supports config plugins overriding bundled plugins, but this forces a third party to duplicate and track the full deep-recall implementation merely to change one decision.

### Use an ordinary prompt-build hook

Prompt-build hook results compose and do not offer a single-winner handled/cancel contract for this decision.

## Impact

Affected users and systems:

- multilingual personal-assistant deployments;
- operators with local or domain-specific recall-intent policies;
- latency-sensitive agents that cannot use always mode;
- plugin authors who want to improve escalation without owning memory retrieval.

Severity: medium. The current default works for covered formulations, but uncovered language or semantic forms can silently skip deep recall, while always mode adds a blocking agent run to ordinary turns.

Frequency: every eligible conversational turn reaches this policy after a weak deterministic result.

Consequence: either missed historical context, unnecessary latency, or downstream maintenance of a private Active Memory replacement.

## Evidence/examples

- PT-BR recall-intent gap: #135085
- PT-BR matcher repair: #136502
- Prior CJK matcher repair: #117419
- Blocking Active Memory latency report: #72015
- Active Memory documents that lane 1 makes zero model calls and lane 2 is a real agent turn:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-architecture.md
- Current decision is internal to:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The intended PR is additive and opt-in. It preserves the current built-in policy as the default and keeps model selection, datasets and classifier artifacts outside OpenClaw core. I will include focused provider lifecycle, sync/async, timeout, error, missing-provider, mode, strong-hit and embedded-run boundary tests.

## Summary
Possible recurrence of #192851 in OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (76cbb32), bundled Codex 0.164.0, after an OpenClaw.app-managed update on macOS arm64.

Every tested `functions.exec` call fails with `code-mode host closed its stdout`, including the minimal `text("ok")` without any nested tools. A new conversation and a full Mac reboot did not resolve it.

## Environment
- Mac mini M1, 8 GB RAM
- macOS 27.2.1 arm64
- OpenClaw CLI and Gateway: 2026.11.5 (76cbb32)
- Bundled Codex: 0.164.0
- Model: openai/gpt-6-astra
- OpenClaw.app-managed local Gateway; observed in Slack conversations

## Reproduction
1. Run the app-managed 2026.11.5 runtime on this Mac.
2. Ask the Codex-backed agent to execute `text("ok")` using `functions.exec`.
3. Observe `code-mode host closed its stdout` instead of `ok`.
4. Repeat in a new conversation: same result.

Expected: the code-mode call returns `ok`.
Actual: the host closes stdout, preventing all tools routed through this host. The separate desktop-control path still works.

## Signature evidence
Inspected the bundled `@openai/codex-darwin-arm64/vendor/aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/codex-code-mode-host` from the active 2026.11.5 runtime:

- `codesign -dv --verbose=4`: `flags=0x10000(runtime)`; Authority is `Developer ID Application: OpenClaw Foundation (FWJYW4S8P8)`.
- `codesign -d --entitlements - --xml`: prints the executable path but no entitlements.
- `codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2`: `valid on disk` and `satisfies its Designated Requirement`.

This looks consistent with the packaging/signing issue in #192851. Please verify whether the bundled host is re-signed without the JIT entitlements needed by V8. This is a suspected cause, not a confirmed root cause for every observed failure.

## Logs and timing caveat
The Codex `logs_2.sqlite` contains this host stderr immediately before the reboot, at 07:45 JST on 2026-11-19:

```text
Fatal process out of memory: Failed to reserve virtual memory for CodeRange
v8::internal::IsolateGroup::EnsureCodeRange
v8::internal::Heap::SetUp
v8::Isolate::Initialize
v8::Isolate::New
```

After the reboot at approximately 07:47 JST, router errors still record `code-mode host closed its stdout`, but no matching host-stderr/CodeRange entries were found for that later period. The earlier crash must not be treated as a newly captured post-reboot stack.

## Checks already performed
- Host binary exists and is executable; `--help` succeeds.
- `--listen stdio` waits for input; this does not prove V8 initialization works.
- Codex doctor reports installation/config/database integrity OK.
- launchctl data/rss limits are unlimited; no SoftResourceLimits or HardResourceLimits entries in the Gateway LaunchAgent.
- `memory_pressure` reported system-wide memory free percentage 42%; compression and swap were present, so this does not conclusively rule out memory-related causes.
- Temporarily setting `tools.codeMode.enabled=false` via OpenClaw management did not remove the exposed `functions.exec` failure in the existing conversation.
- No signature edits, entitlement changes, sandbox weakening, or manual replacement of bundled binaries were performed.

## Separate update inconsistency
After the update, the Node LaunchAgent still referenced runtime 2026.11.4 and repeatedly failed with a config-version mismatch. Reinstalling the Node service from CLI 2026.11.5 fixed it; the Node now runs and connects. The code-mode error persists independently.

## Impact
All tested code-mode-routed tool calls are unusable on this installation. Please investigate the 2026.11.5 macOS app signing/packaging path and provide a supported fix. The prior report #192851 is closed; this report documents the currently observed version. Exact last-known-good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a single-CPU host, a stock Gateway on 2026.9.9 or 2026.10.1 uses about 2.5× the memory of 2026.9.4 under the same three-turn chat (peak 706 MB → 1,815 / 1,938 MB, steady 474 MB → 1,151 / 1,227 MB), and is 3–5× slower to become ready and to answer the first message. The extra memory comes from 10–17 worker isolates and two helper processes that 9.4 did not have.

### Steps to reproduce

All runs use **stock images built with the repository's own `Dockerfile`** at each tag (`docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 .`), with no plugins, patches or config beyond the minimum below.

1. Build `v2026.9.4` (`3a9d69db306`), `v2026.9.9` (`bcfc88812a3`) and `v2026.10.1` (`e178c39e9aa`).
2. On a fresh named volume, write `/home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "agents": { "defaults": { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5", "workspace": "/home/node/.openclaw/workspace" } },
     "gateway": { "mode": "local", "bind": "lan", "auth": { "mode": "token", "token": "<token>" } }
   }
   ```
3. Start the Gateway with one CPU and a generous memory cap (so the real footprint is visible rather than an OOM):
   ```bash
   docker run -d --cpus 0.512 --memory 4g --memory-swap 4g \
     -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… -e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<token> \
     -v <volume>:/home/node/.openclaw <image> \
     node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18789 --bind lan --token <token> --allow-unconfigured
   ```
   (`--cpus 0.512` makes `os.availableParallelism()` return 1, as in a container with a fractional CPU limit.)
4. 15 s after `[gateway] ready`, send three turns with `docker exec <c> node openclaw.mjs agent --session-key main --message …` ("Reply with exactly: pong", "Reply with exactly: second", "What is 2+2? Reply with only the number.").
5. Sample `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current` every 2 s for ~260 s. Per-isolate heaps were sampled with a `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` preload that wraps `worker_threads.Worker` and calls `worker.getHeapStatistics()` every 10 s.

### Expected behavior

Memory and startup comparable to 2026.9.4 on the same host and workload: peak ~0.7 GB, steady ~0.5 GB, ready in ~13 s, first reply in ~7 s.

### Actual behavior

Same host, same config, same three turns (cgroup memory; one run per build):

| Stock build | Peak | Steady (~250 s) | Ready | First reply | Worker isolates started |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.9.4 | 706 MB | 474 MB | 13 s | 7 s | 1 (short-lived) |
| 2026.9.9 | 1,815 MB | 1,151 MB | 44 s | 33 s | 18 |
| 2026.10.1 | 1,938 MB | 1,227 MB | 43 s | 24 s | 17 |

Idle (no chat), 2026.9.9 alone peaks at 1,327 MB and settles at ~816 MB.

The main isolate does **not** grow (heap used ~233–240 MB on 9.9/10.1 vs ~237 MB on 9.4). The difference is worker isolates plus two child processes. Live isolates on 2026.9.9 ~230 s after the chat (`total/used` heap MB):

```
sqlite-store.worker.js              48/47
sqlite-store.worker.js              43/40
openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat      16/15
openclaw-state-read.worker.js       30/29
openclaw-state-read.worker.js       31/29
prepared-model-catalog.worker.js   118/114
session-transcript.worker.js        71/68
session-transcript.worker.js        72/69
session-transcript.worker.js        28/26
session-accessor.sqlite-archive     38/37
```

plus child processes `dist/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child session` (~76–85 MB RSS) and `dist/process/spawn-broker/worker.js` (~66 MB RSS). On 2026.10.1 the set is similar (three session-transcript workers at 50–64 MB, two sqlite-store, catalog 93 MB, two heartbeat workers, worker-native-lifecycle).

During the chat turns, short-lived workers also start (memory-search, provider-prompt-state, git-operation, disk-budget, additional transcript lanes), which produces the peak.

A heap snapshot of one session-transcript worker in a downstream 9.9 build showed ~970 loaded modules (~10.8 MB of module source, mostly config/schema/plugin-index code such as `io.factory`, `zod-schema`, `installed-plugin-index`, `bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated`) even though the worker entry's static import graph is ~120 modules. That suggests each transcript/state worker pulls in most of the config and plugin stack at runtime, so each isolate costs 30–120 MB whatever its task.

With one CPU these isolates cannot run in parallel, so the extra isolate start-up and module evaluation also shows up as latency (ready 13 s → 44 s, first reply 7 s → 24–33 s).

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (`bcfc88812a3`) and 2026.10.1 (`e178c39e9aa`); baseline 2026.9.4 (`3a9d69db306`)

### Operating system

Linux arm64 containers (Docker 29.7, upstream `node:24-bookworm` base) on macOS / Apple Silicon

### Install method

Stock Docker image built from the repository `Dockerfile` at each tag

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway → Anthropic API (API key, no proxy)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Minimal config shown above; no channels, no extra plugins configured.

### Logs

N/A: no errors. The Gateway is healthy; the problem is footprint and latency.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Full per-run CSVs (2 s cgroup samples) and worker traces available on request.

### Impact and severity

Hosts with ~1–1.5 GB per Gateway (small VMs, Raspberry Pi, containers with memory limits) cannot upgrade past 2026.9.4. We run per-user Gateways in 1.25 GiB containers: the measured 9.9/10.1 peaks (1.8–1.9 GB) and steady state (~1.2 GB) do not fit, and a downstream 9.9 build was OOM-killed at that limit seconds after `ready`. Start-up and first-reply latency also triple. Pinning to 2026.9.4 means losing fixes once 9.x leaves extended-stable.

Related reports covering parts of this: #159858 (idle worker heap ~650 MB), #160501 (catalog worker 260–350 MB), #162709 (session-transcript workers never retire), #157791 (Pi start-up/RSS), #159551 (1 GB VM), #156448 (empty Gateway baseline). This issue adds a controlled stock-vs-stock comparison across 9.4 / 9.9 / 10.1 at one CPU.

### Additional information

Things we checked that are **not** the cause:
- `--max-old-space-size`: removing it made the peak worse (main heap uncapped); the docs note it overrides worker `resourceLimits`, but workers' used heap was the same either way.
- Capping worker young generation (`resourceLimits.maxYoungGenerationSizeMb: 16`) trims ~10% of committed heap only; most of each worker's heap is in use.
- There is no config or env setting to limit worker pool sizes, worker heaps or idle retention (`docs/gateway/diagnostics.md`: "No configuration setting is needed").

Suggestions, roughly in order of impact for constrained hosts:
1. A low-resource mode (config or env, or automatic when `availableParallelism() === 1` / `process.constrainedMemory()` is small) that runs SQLite/state/transcript tasks on a single shared worker, or in-process, instead of one isolate per pool/lane.
2. Avoid loading the config/plugin-index stack inside transcript and state workers (pass the resolved values they need from the host).
3. Start pools lazily and retire idle workers quickly by default on constrained hosts; let the catalog worker retire (#160501, idle timeout 0 today).
4. Expose pool sizes and worker heap limits as config for operators who need hard bounds.

issues.body:
## Summary

An `isolated` agent-turn automation that runs often accumulates one retained session window per run under its base key `cron:<jobId>`, with no retention, and once that history is large it cannot be deleted through the supported path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6, PostgreSQL engine (also observed on SQLite before the port)
- One isolated agent-turn job (`sessionTarget: "isolated"`, `lightContext: true`, `thinking: "off"`) woken by a command-payload doorbell job every 60 s; it runs ~760 times a day

## Observed

- After ~6 weeks: 31,474 windows under `agent:main:cron:<jobId>`, ~891k transcript events (~3.1 GB raw, ~1.8 GB stored), ~192k trajectory runtime events. Every other session on the agent combined: ~4.7k events.
- `cron.sessionRetention` prunes only the `…:run:<runId>` rows (6 remained); the base key's superseded windows are kept, "bounded by the disk budget".
- The disk budget evicts the oldest historical sessions first, which would remove real conversations long before it reaches this automation's history.
- `openclaw sessions delete agent:main:cron:<jobId>` cannot complete: the delete archives every transcript generation first and fails with `Archive batch exceeds 268435456 bytes; use fewer sessions`. A single key cannot be split, and there is no option to delete without the archive.
- While the job is live, each delete attempt aborts the in-flight run (`OPENCLAW_RESTART_ABORT`) and then reports "still active; try again", because the doorbell starts a new run inside the wait.

## Requests

1. A retention policy for superseded windows of isolated automation base keys (for example, apply `cron.sessionRetention`, or a separate `cron.windowRetention`), so a frequently-run isolated job stays bounded without touching user conversations.
2. A bounded way to remove an oversized automation history: per-window deletion (or "keep the newest N windows"), batched archiving under the 256 MB cap, or a `--no-archive` option for automation keys.

Raw SQL is not a workaround: many tables reference `session_id` without a foreign key (FTS rows, event identities, active events, entry snapshots, memory origins), so deleting windows outside the lifecycle operation leaves orphans.

issues.body:
### Summary

`env` (including `env.vars`) has no rule in the reload planner, so its paths fall to the default `restart` kind
(`src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts`: `const kind = rule?.kind ?? "restart"`; the hot-reload docs say a path that
matches no rule defaults to a Gateway restart, and `env` is not listed in the reload table). A `config.patch` that only
changes `env.vars.SOME_TOOL_SETTING` therefore:

1. writes the file and answers **success** with `sentinel.payload.stats.requiresRestart: true`
   (`src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts`, `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` /
   `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult`; a restart-class plan is not awaited);
2. then, under the default `hybrid` reload mode, restarts the Gateway in process once it is idle
   (`src/gateway/server-reload-restart.ts`: `config change requires gateway restart (env.vars.X) — deferring until …
   complete` → `all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now` → `restart mode: in-process restart`).

Two consequences for anything that manages a Gateway from outside (an orchestrator, a control plane):

- `env.vars` are applied to the Gateway's own process env at config load (`src/config/config-env-vars.ts`). Most
  of them are read at boot or per child spawn anyway, so a full restart is usually more than the change needs. A `none`
  classification (applies at next start / next spawn), or `hot` with a re-publication of the config-owned env
  (`prepareConfigRuntimeEnv` already computes that diff from previous/next config), would avoid ~25 s of downtime
  per edit.
- The answer does not say *whether or when* the Gateway itself will restart. The `restart` field of the answer is
  only filled when the RPC schedules the restart directly (`gateway.reload.mode: "off"`); under `hybrid` it is absent
  even though the reloader is about to restart. A supervisor that reads `requiresRestart: true` as "I must restart
  it" then restarts it a second time on top of the Gateway's own restart.

### Reproduction (v2026.10.9; same code on v2026.10.10 and main; `gateway.reload.mode` unset = hybrid)

1. Start a Gateway; open a WebSocket client and note `hello-ok.server.bootId`.
2. `config.get` → `config.patch` with `raw: {"env":{"vars":{"PROBE_NEW":"1"}}}` and the returned `baseHash`.
3. Answer: `{ok: true, …, sentinel: {payload: {stats: {requiresRestart: true}}}}`, no `restart` field.
4. Log: `config change requires gateway restart (env.vars.PROBE_NEW) — preparing` then the in-process restart;
   ready again ~24 s later. A new handshake reports a different `bootId`.

Measured on five in-process restarts after such a patch: 23.5–27.8 s from the patch to ready.

### Asks

1. Classify `env` paths explicitly: `none` for `env.vars.*` (applied at next start / next spawn), or `hot` with a
   re-publication of the config-owned env. If restart stays the right default, list `env` in the reload table so
   callers can know before they write.
2. Make the self-restart visible in the answer: fill `restart` (or a new field) also when the reloader will restart,
   e.g. `{mode: "deferred", reason, …}`, and document `hello-ok.server.bootId` as the marker of the new generation
   (it changes on every start, in-process restarts included; the update CLI already relies on it in
   `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-drain.ts`).

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.11.6 with the PostgreSQL engine selected for the `state` and `agent` stores, `openclaw backup create` fails on the stores' local SQLite anchors, and the failed process leaves the Gateway state lease held. Every later `backup create`, `doctor --fix` and `gateway` start then refuses with "cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process" until the lease is recovered by hand with `openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (container image, Linux)
- `database.engine: "postgres"`, PostgreSQL 18.4, ported with `openclaw database port --to postgres` (phase complete)
- Gateway stopped; `backup create` run as the only OpenClaw process in the container

## Steps

1. Port an existing install to PostgreSQL (`openclaw database port --to postgres`).
2. With the Gateway stopped, run `openclaw backup create --output /backups --verify`.

## Observed

The backup fails with:

```
Backup scratch preserved at /tmp/openclaw-backup-owned-XXXXXX: Unrecognized backup scratch content: /tmp/openclaw-backup-owned-XXXXXX/state-snapshot-no-legacy/openclaw-state-db-0.sqlite.anchor
```

`gateway recover-lock --json` then shows the backup process as the holder of `gateway.state.lock` and `state.<hash>.lock` (in the backup's pid namespace, heartbeat no longer renewed). A second `backup create` refuses:

```
Cannot admit backup.create for <stateDir> in state root <stateDir>: cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process; heartbeat age does not prove that the holder stopped. holder <pid> at <host>/pid-ns <ns>, last renewed N s ago.
```

and so do `doctor --fix` ("Doctor could not enter maintenance") and `gateway`.

## Expected

- `backup create` recognizes the PostgreSQL store anchors in its snapshot scratch (or snapshots PostgreSQL-backed stores another way), and
- a failed backup releases the state lease it took, so a failure cannot block every later start.

## Notes

In a container whose entrypoint runs a pre-Doctor backup on each start, this turns one failed backup into a restart loop: each new container's backup or Doctor waits on the dead holder from the previous one. Skipping the backup when `database.engine` is `postgres` avoids it.

issues.body:
## Problem

Since OpenClaw 2026.10.10, `openclaw memory index` and `openclaw memory status` refuse to run while the Gateway owns the agent SQLite stores. The CLI requires exclusive offline state ownership. `memory search` still routes through the live Gateway, and the `memory.status` RPC only reports provider health. It does not reindex.

There is no supported Gateway RPC for an explicit incremental reindex of every configured agent. Confirmed against the 2026.10.10 docs and `extensions/memory-core` CLI: an all-agent incremental pass is `openclaw memory index` without `--agent` and without `--force`, and it still requires the Gateway to be stopped through its service owner.

Automatic index maintenance during normal memory activity is not a substitute. Idle agents stay stale until the next offline window.

## Impact

The only reliable pass is: stop the Gateway, run `openclaw memory index`, start the Gateway. On this host that window is about 25 minutes for seven agents (incremental, remote Ollama embeddings). During that window chat is down, and any cron that falls inside it is skipped or interrupted. The embedding host is a desktop machine, so the window cannot be overnight.

## Request

An authenticated, Gateway-owned incremental reindex of all agents (or of one named agent), with a completion and result API. Same semantics as `openclaw memory index` without `--force`. No second process opening the SQLite files, and no need to stop the service.

Please do not treat removing SQLite lock files or bypassing the ownership guard as a workaround.

issues.body:
## Summary

From a resolved command approval, let an authorized reviewer see whether that exact command execution completed, failed, did not run, or has no reliable evidence yet.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw already has an Approvals history page with durable decisions and resolver attribution. A history row answers “was it allowed?” but not “did the operation actually happen?” An allowed command can still fail, and an expired request is not proof the action was denied. Searching nearby chat or commands by text makes two identical requests hard to distinguish.

## Proposed solution

Start with Gateway-host command approvals. Reuse the existing command execution owner's receipt if it is reviewer-safe and exactly bound to the approval. Link to the authorized recorded result or show a small derived outcome beside the existing decision. If the owner cannot establish a match, say pending or unknown as appropriate. Never infer an outcome from the decision, command text, or timestamps. Do not expose command output/environment to an audience that cannot already read it. No new approval rules or parallel history store.

**Acceptance:** In an isolated test, record two identical ordinary command previews with distinct approval IDs. Only one has a confirmed completed execution; the other has missing evidence. Their history rows must remain distinct and show the appropriate result or unknown after reload. A separate approved-but-failed case must not say succeeded. A reviewer without access to the result cannot retrieve it through the history link.

## Alternatives considered

Point to the Activity run inspector: useful when exact execution identity is enabled and the user already knows the run, but doesn't give a link from the existing approval row. Match commands by string or re-label “allowed” as “ran”: both can misattribute effects.

## Impact

Reviewers and operators can distinguish approval from execution after reconnect or handoff. The cost is a bounded cross-owner correlation and authorization check; require an exact receipt, otherwise present unknown. This is a Control UI enhancement, not a new audit ledger.

## Evidence/examples

At [3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370), [approval history projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/approvals.ts#L188-L241) contains decision, reason and attribution, and [the expandable UI row](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/ui/src/pages/approvals/approval-history-row.tsx#L108-L141) renders those facts without an execution outcome. Both paths matched [upstream 3fd1657e7d72](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3fd1657e7d7249a2d0701f84d4eba63f9c4b00be). Rechecked 2026-11-21: the named source files are unchanged on main at e201b64f8d7. Nineteen [Gateway approval tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/gateway/server-methods/approval.test.ts#L140-L184) passed; those establish that history exists, not a browser or live-command repro of this enhancement. The ARTEX [trace fixture](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/blob/5bed53b6ae9bf3b29e29988f43e42d5ce3870587/intercept/trace_test.go#L13-L80) refused to bind an unrelated result and kept identical concurrent calls ambiguous. OpenClaw's [run inspector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts#L184-L232) remains the existing deep-inspection path.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

[#192180](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192180) already improved the history UI. [#199483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199483) corrected the false implication that an expired request denied execution. Preserve that distinction; this proposal is for independently supported execution evidence, not another wording fix.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw models auth login` (Gateway-backed login, used while the local Gateway is running since #168671) renders multi-line login steps with **literal `\n` sequences** instead of line breaks. The device-code box is a single run-on paragraph.

### Observed (2026.11.4, `openclaw models auth login --provider xai --method oauth`)

```
◇  xAI OAuth ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                          │
│  Enter this one-time code on the sign-in                                 │
│  page.\nhttps://accounts.x.ai/oauth2/device?user_code=XXXX-XXXX\nCode:   │
│  XXXX-XXXX\nCode expires in 30 minutes.\nContinue only if you started    │
│  this sign-in yourself. If a website or another person gave you this     │
│  code, cancel.\n\nxAI OAuth complete                                     │
```

Expected: message, URL, code, expiry and the phishing warning on separate lines (as the offline wizard path renders them).

Login itself succeeds; this is display only, but it degrades exactly the step that carries the device-code phishing warning.

### Root cause

`src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.ts`, `answerLoginStep()`:

```ts
const message = sanitizeTerminalText(step.message ?? step.title ?? "Continue");
```

`sanitizeTerminalText` (`packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts`) is documented as a **single-line** sanitizer and escapes `\n` → `\\n`. The Gateway wizard session builds the device-code message intentionally multi-line (`src/wizard/session.ts`, `deviceCode()` → `[message, externalUrl, "Code: …", "Code expires …", DEVICE_CODE_PHISHING_WARNING].join("\n")`), and progress steps also arrive multi-line (`\n\nxAI OAuth complete`). The CLI then hands the escaped string to `prompter.note()`.

Still present on `main` (line 86 of `auth-login-gateway.ts`). Affects every provider whose login goes through this path (xAI device code, OpenAI Codex device code, any multi-line note/progress step), not only xAI.

### Suggested fix

Same pattern as #198055 / #198058 for `id rebind`: sanitize per line and keep the layout, for `note`/`progress` (and arguably `text`/`select` messages):

```ts
const sanitizeMultiline = (text: string) =>
  text.split("\n").map((line) => sanitizeTerminalText(line)).join("\n");
```

Ideally a shared `sanitizeTerminalMultilineText` in `packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts`, since the same class of bug has now shown up in several commands (#198051, #198172).

### Related

- #198051, #198172 — same literal-`\n` class in `id rebind` / `nodes`
- #168671 — introduced Gateway-backed provider login
- #175096 — shared Gateway wizard terminal projection

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), Linux, Node 24.22.2, Gateway running (systemd user service).

issues.body:
## Summary

A built-in Goal with an explicit token budget should stop scheduling ordinary work while it can still deliver one useful partial-result status.

## Problem to solve

Correcting the Goal's usage counter does not decide what to do near a cap. The current continuation check admits another ordinary turn while the accounted Goal is active; once it becomes budget_limited, there is no dedicated reserve in that check. A user can get a terminal budget state without a clear account of what finished and what remains. This is separate from the accounting defect in #203350.

## Proposed solution

After #203350 is resolved, use the existing Goal continuation owner to reserve modest headroom for an explicit per-Goal budget. On the transition into reserve, stop admitting normal Goal work and deliver one short, visible handoff: completed output or references, what remains if known, token usage, and stop reason. A deterministic message from existing state is sufficient; no extra model call is required. Preserve Stop, ordinary chats, and explicit resume behavior. No global spend contract or child propagation.

**Acceptance:** In an isolated built-in Goal with a 100,000-token cap and a 15,000-token fixture reserve, settled usage of 45,000 allows the next ordinary turn. At 90,000, no third ordinary turn starts, and the user sees exactly one partial handoff. Duplicate settlement or restart does not publish it again. Unbudgeted Goals are unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

Stop only at the cap: no planned handoff. Prompt the model to remember to wrap up: it cannot enforce scheduler admission. Add a global budget hook: broader than this user-facing Goal transition.

## Impact

People running long, explicitly budgeted Goals retain useful partial work and know whether to extend the budget. Reserving room can stop marginally earlier even if another small task might have fit. This is an opt-in Goal behavior, not a new universal default.

## Evidence/examples

At [3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370), injecting accounted threshold values into OpenClaw's [Goal accounting](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/config/sessions/goals-transitions.ts#L26-L64) and [continuation check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/auto-reply/reply/goal-continuation.ts#L78-L94) gave next-turn eligibility **yes / yes / no** at **79,999 / 80,000 / 100,000**. Under the same threshold fixture, ARTEX's [ledger](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/blob/5bed53b6ae9bf3b29e29988f43e42d5ce3870587/agent/budget.go#L130-L171) gave **yes / no / no** and signaled wrap-up exactly once. Fixture outputs are below. This demonstrates control behavior, not delivery of a real handoff. The two OpenClaw files matched upstream main at [3fd1657e7d72](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3fd1657e7d7249a2d0701f84d4eba63f9c4b00be). Rechecked 2026-11-21: the named source files are unchanged on main at e201b64f8d7.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

File as an enhancement contingent on correct settled accounting, not as a repeat of the undercount bug. Related: [#179292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179292) is a broader per-surface cost policy. [#202270](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202270) is an uncapped Discord continuation loop; this request applies only to explicitly budgeted Goals.

issues.body:
## Summary

Give the owning parent an explicit way to start one fresh attempt for a failed delegated task, preserving prior attempt history and successful siblings.

## Problem to solve

When one child fails in a task split, the parent can spawn a new child or send a follow-up message, but it must reconstruct the old assignment or decide how to reuse its context. There is an exact resume path for a currently paused native child, not an equivalent retry of an already failed attempt. Retrying only the failed unit keeps the analysis and successful sibling results intact.

## Proposed solution

Start with one explicitly selected terminal, failed native child and the recorded original assignment. Start a new attempt with a new run ID linked to the prior attempt. Retain prior partial results; do not reuse consumed approvals, change permissions, or replay earlier tool calls automatically. Run through current admission rules. If the original assignment or workspace binding is not recoverable or permitted, refuse with a clear reason. Keep paused-child resume unchanged. Do not add an automatic retry loop or change Workboard's behavior.

**Acceptance:** Split an ordinary local document summary into two child tasks with a stand-in provider. One finishes, one fails before producing an answer. A parent-authorized retry of the failed run runs only that assignment, links the new attempt, and preserves the successful child's output and the failed run record. A child owned by another parent cannot be retried. Do not claim exactly-once effects of arbitrary external tools.

## Alternatives considered

Re-run the parent: redraws successful work. Manually respawn with copied instructions: works around the issue but loses obvious continuity with the failed task. Resume: existing and appropriate for a paused child, not a terminal failure. Use Workboard: appropriate for Workboard jobs, not a solution for a plain native delegation.

## Impact

Less repeated work and clearer history in multi-child tasks. Cost: a bounded retained assignment or reference, attempt linkage, and admission/UI work. Start only where the existing task owner can retain the needed facts safely.

## Evidence/examples

The [subagent tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts#L53-L66) lists list, wait, and cancel. The separate [sessions_send resume path](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-resume.ts#L34-L94) binds a currently paused native child. Both files matched [upstream 3fd1657e7d72](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3fd1657e7d7249a2d0701f84d4eba63f9c4b00be). Rechecked 2026-11-21: the named source files are unchanged on main at e201b64f8d7. ARTEX's [selected-item control](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/blob/5bed53b6ae9bf3b29e29988f43e42d5ce3870587/server/server.go#L1364-L1404) can reopen one blocked/exhausted/stopped item without re-running successful siblings; its domain planning is not part of this request. This is a source-backed feature proposal; the example is the acceptance scenario, not an executed cross-product retry proof.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

[#182682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182682) already covers a reviewer-requested corrective attempt on a Workboard card: reuse it for that case. [#44925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/44925) concerns missing results and automatic recovery/notification after timeout, not a parent-initiated retry of one chosen failed task.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw.app (2026.10.7 and 2026.11.6) on macOS shows "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery. Quit OpenClaw, run openclaw doctor --fix with the matching CLI, then reopen OpenClaw." on every launch. The only CLI on the machine is the app-owned 2026.10.7 runtime, the app never installs a newer one, and the Mac node stays disconnected.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on one Mac mini (Apple Silicon, macOS 27.2) with an app-owned local Gateway:

1. Starting state: OpenClaw.app 2026.10.7 in ~/Applications with an app-owned runtime (`~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.10.7-release-98a6b88...`, the only build). After a Gateway restart, `openclaw gateway status` reported "Service unit not found" / LaunchAgent not loaded.
2. `openclaw gateway install` → the service exited at startup with `Executable not found in $PATH: "tailscale"` (ENOENT); Tailscale serve is enabled and the binary is in `~/.openclaw/bin`, which launchd's PATH doesn't include. Worked around with `openclaw gateway install --force --wrapper ~/.openclaw/gateway-wrapper.sh` (adds ~/.openclaw/bin to PATH, then `exec openclaw "$@"`). Gateway healthy since.
3. The 10.7 app process had no menu bar icon and ignored quit/SIGTERM. After `kill -9` and relaunch it showed the "client credentials need recovery" alert.
4. `openclaw gateway stop`, then `openclaw doctor --fix` (10.7 CLI): completed, wrote a config backup. The 10.7 app then launched without the alert, but the Mac node stayed `connected: false` and there was still no menu bar icon.
5. Replaced the app with OpenClaw-2026.11.6-arm64.zip (notarized, Team ID FWJYW4S8P8). On launch: the same alert. `runtime/current` is still 2026.10.7, so no "matching CLI" exists. `openclaw update` says "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."
6. Removed the manual LaunchAgent (`openclaw gateway uninstall`) so the 11.6 app could own and upgrade the Gateway, then relaunched the app: the same alert right away; no Gateway or runtime installed.

### Expected behavior

After an in-place app update, docs (platforms/mac/bundled-gateway, "Credential recovery") say the app stops the previous app-managed Gateway, prepares credentials, and installs the updated service, with Doctor recovery only for inconsistent state. Expected: either the 11.6 app migrates credentials and installs its 11.6 runtime/CLI, or the alert points to a CLI that's actually available (e.g. the app's bundled runtime) so `openclaw doctor --fix` can be run at the matching version. The Mac node should reconnect afterwards.

### Actual behavior

Every launch of the 11.6 app stops on the credentials-recovery alert and does nothing else: no menu bar icon, no window, no runtime install (`~/.openclaw/runtime/` still contains only 2026.10.7), and `openclaw-mac status` reports the app isn't reachable. The only CLI available is 2026.10.7, which the 11.6 app doesn't accept as matching. `openclaw nodes status --json`: Mac node version 2026.10.7, `connected: false`; it's paired and approved in `openclaw devices list` with no pending requests. macOS also showed "bun was prevented from modifying apps on your Mac" (App Management).

### OpenClaw version

App 2026.11.6 (previously 2026.10.7); CLI/Gateway runtime 2026.10.7 (98a6b88)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon, arm64)

### Install method

mac app (in ~/Applications, app-owned runtime; no node/npm/bun on PATH)

### Model

claude-sonnet-5-5 (not model-related)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> claude-cli (not provider-related)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: macOS app with app-owned local Gateway, updating from 2026.10.7
Severity: Medium-High (Mac node and Computer Control unusable; app UI unreachable; Gateway and Telegram still work via a manual LaunchAgent)
Frequency: every app launch (10+ attempts across 10.7 and 11.6)
Consequence: no supported path forward; the alert's required "matching CLI" can't be obtained

### Additional information

Last known good: 2026.10.7 before a Gateway restart on 2026-11-21. Workaround in place: manual LaunchAgent via `openclaw gateway install --force --wrapper` keeps the Gateway and Telegram running; the Mac node can't connect.

Questions:
1. How do I get a CLI matching the app version when the only runtime is older than the app?
2. Is there a supported way to make the app redo its credential migration and runtime install (Retry setup from the CLI, or resetting client/credentials.sqlite and re-pairing)?
3. Could the App Management block on "bun" stop the runtime update?
4. Separate, smaller issue: should `openclaw gateway install` add ~/.openclaw/bin to the LaunchAgent's PATH when Tailscale serve uses the bundled tailscale binary?

Also posted on the community forum: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/macos-app-stuck-on-client-credentials-need-recovery-after-updating-to-2026-11-6-doctor-with-10-7-cli-doesnt-clear-it-mac-node-stays-disconnected/504
