issues.body:
## Summary

On a long-running self-hosted gateway (Kubernetes StatefulSet, single pod), child processes spawned for session / tool work are not reliably cleaned up when the owning session or turn ends. Over a day this accumulated into sustained high CPU, critical gateway RSS, SQLite lock contention and probe flapping. It also helped trigger repeated WhatsApp `pendingDeliveryNotice` ("I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat…") notices. We had to kill the processes and restart the gateway to recover.

**Version:** `2026.9.8` (56335df), custom image built from that tag. Linux x64 container, `tini -s` as PID 1, gateway as PID 12.

## What we observed (2026-10-05, before restart)

| What | Detail |
|---|---|
| 16 Codex app-server processes | 8 pairs of `node …/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js app-server --listen stdio://` plus the native `codex app-server` child. All were parented by the gateway, idle (≤0.1% CPU, 10–46 MiB each) and still alive after **~8h20m** with no Codex work running. Nothing reaped them until the gateway restarted. |
| Gateway RSS | Critical for 2h+ (`memory pressure: level=critical reason=rss_threshold`, 4.0–4.5 GiB vs a 3.14 GiB threshold). 109 critical and 193 warning events in 24h. |
| Probes | `/healthz` readiness failed ×74 and liveness ×11 over ~9h. |
| SQLite | `state.lease` lock contention (`sqliteErrcode=5`) on `state/openclaw.sqlite`, 6× in 2h. Several hit in the same second as WhatsApp 408 disconnects. |
| WhatsApp | 408/499 flaps → ambiguous final delivery → `pendingFinalDelivery` settles `unknown` → `pendingDeliveryNotice.state=owed` on 3 DM sessions (related: #154416). |
| Also present (not OpenClaw-spawned) | Two `python3` SQLite scans left behind by our own operator `kubectl exec` diagnostics (PPID 0). One sat at ~99% CPU for 50 min. We're mentioning them only because they added to the lock and CPU pressure. The ask below is about gateway-owned children. |
| backup sidecar | Unreaped `restic` zombie (our sidecar, `sleep infinity` entrypoint). Ours to fix, listed for completeness. |

## Post-restart observation (same day, fresh pod)

Each one-shot ACP prompt (`acpx <agent> exec "…"`, which goes through the gateway) started a supervised MCP service group: `service-child-relay` → `service-child-group-anchor` → `mcp/plugin-tools-serve.js` (~350–600 MiB RSS), plus a workspace MCP server (`python …/google_ads_server.py`). After 3 short pings, all **3 groups were still running 5+ minutes after the prompts finished**, adding roughly 1–2 GiB to the container. This looks like the same lifecycle gap. Per-session children seem to outlive the session/turn that started them.

## Second issue seen during restart

After the old pod terminated, the first gateway start in the new pod exited 1 with:

> OpenClaw refused shared state schema mutation at /home/node/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite because another Gateway owns that state directory.

The container restarted once and then came up. It looks like the previous gateway's ownership lease isn't released on SIGTERM, or isn't treated as stale even though that process no longer exists. We saw the same single boot restart on the pod's previous start.

## Expected

- When a session, turn or ACP connection ends, or after a bounded idle TTL, gateway-spawned children (Codex app-server pairs, `plugin-tools-serve`, workspace MCP servers and their relay/anchor wrappers) are shut down and reaped.
- A periodic reaper/watchdog finds children whose owning session is gone and kills them, logging a diagnostic line (pid, kind, owning session, age).
- The gateway releases the state-directory ownership lease on graceful shutdown, so a replacement pod doesn't fail its first boot.
- (Related, #154416) Ambiguous delivery caused by a transport reconnect shouldn't arm `pendingDeliveryNotice` when the adapter already returned a platform message id. A config option to set PDN to log-only would also help operators.

## Ask

Please look at process lifecycle and cleanup for gateway-spawned workers (Codex app-server, MCP service groups), and at lease release on shutdown. Something like `gateway status --children`, showing each child with its owning session and age, would also help operators find leaks without `ps` archaeology.

## Evidence

Our internal notes (not public; summarised above, with phone numbers and message content removed): `openclaw-runaway-scan-20261005.md` (process/RSS/probe/lock scan) and `openclaw-wa-pdn-20261005.md` (WhatsApp PDN timeline and code-path analysis). We can share specific redacted log excerpts if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap floor only ratchets up - per-run system prompt/skills strings stay reachable after runs (~25 MiB/h until the V8 cap aborts)

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.7** (npm `latest`), Node **v26.12.1**, Linux x64, 14.8 GB RAM
- systemd service, no `--max-old-space-size`, so the runtime V8 ceiling is the default ~2144 MB
- ~50 sessions across 3 agents, several high-traffic group chats
- `agents.defaults.compaction`: `mode=safeguard`, `maxActiveTranscriptBytes=12mb`
- `session.reset`: `{mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 4320}`

### Symptom

The gateway aborts with:

```
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

after roughly 20h of uptime. Four aborts in 14 days (Oct 18, 19, 24, 27). No kernel OOM kill in that period - it is always the V8 abort.

At the last abort: RSS 4.05 GiB, `heapUsed` 1.93 GiB, worker isolates ~0.5 GiB, pinned around the 2144 MB old-space cap for hours before dying.

### This is not steady-state workload: the floor only moves up

`diagnostics.stability` emits `diagnostic.memory.sample` every ~30s. Over the last 13 hours before the abort, min/max `heapUsed` per 4-hour block:

| window | min heap | max heap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Oct 26 18-20 | 1,716 MiB | 1,727 MiB |
| Oct 26 20-22 | 1,717 MiB | 1,811 MiB |
| Oct 26 22-24 | 1,738 MiB | 1,856 MiB |
| Oct 27 00-02 | 1,800 MiB | 1,905 MiB |
| Oct 27 02-04 | 1,819 MiB | 1,935 MiB |
| Oct 27 04-06 | 1,881 MiB | 1,946 MiB |
| Oct 27 06-08 | 1,916 MiB | 1,966 MiB |

Within a run the heap does come back down: the largest single-step change observed was **+123.7 MiB in 5 minutes, then -121.2 MiB five minutes later**. Transient allocations are reclaimed. What does not come back is the floor - it rises ~15 MiB/h and never recedes.

### Heap snapshot diff: the growth is prompt strings

Two native snapshots from the same process, 1h49m apart (480.0 MiB -> 527.7 MiB total `self_size`):

| node type | growth |
|---|---:|
| string | **+22.8 MiB** |
| object | +10.3 MiB |
| array | +5.7 MiB |
| code | +2.8 MiB |
| native | +0.2 MiB |

In the later snapshot, the duplicated text looks like this:

| content | copies | total |
|---|---:|---:|
| skills instructions block (`The following skills provide specialized instructions...`) | 215 | 6.2 MiB |
| full system prompt (`You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw...`) | 23 | 2.5 MiB |
| `<!-- openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->` block | 23 | 2.2 MiB |
| heartbeat scratch line (`Follow the heartbeat monitor...`) | 917 | 2.4 MiB |
| memory `## Goal` block | 65 | 1.8 MiB |
| memory `## Decisions` block | 65 | 1.8 MiB |
| base64 JPEG data URL | 11 | 2.0 MiB |

### Retainer path (BFS from GC roots)

```
(GC roots)
  -> global
  -> WeakMap
  -> Array (128 KiB)
  -> Object ... Object
  -> closure observeToolOutcome
  -> Context
  -> closure shouldEmitToolResult
  -> Context
  -> ... -> string (29.3 KiB, the skills block)
```

Of the 215 copies of the skills block, **208** are held on this path, **6** are internalized strings (reachable from `(Internalized strings)` under GC roots, therefore permanently live for the process), 1 via a separate array.

Code side:

- `observeToolOutcome` is the per-run closure created in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts:196`. It captures `terminalToolPresentation`, `turnTaintState` and `postCompactionGuard`.
- The strings are produced per attempt by `buildAttemptSystemPrompt()` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.ts`, which rebuilds `baseSystemPrompt` and `skillsPrompt` for every model attempt.
- `sessionPromptStates` (`openclaw.embeddedSessionPromptStates`, `MAX_SESSION_PROMPT_STATES = 64`) bounds session-level prompt state with an LRU prune. It does not bound the per-run object graph.

### Hypothesis

After a run completes, the observer closure (or whatever retains it - here a module-global `WeakMap` whose keys are still alive) keeps the run `Context`, and therefore the attempt prompt strings, reachable. GC keeps them; old space ratchets up ~15-25 MiB/h until the 2144 MB cap aborts the process.

### Expected

After `agent_end`, the completed run tool-outcome observer, prepared attempt and prompt strings should become unreachable, and old space should return to the process baseline (~0.5 GiB) instead of climbing monotonically.

### Question about the in-flight fixes

#184990 (`fix(agents): release completed run state from retained async contexts`), #184898 (`perf(agents): release settled replies and redundant run indexes`) and #185255 (`perf(agents): release settled context engine execution state`) merged Oct 26-27 and are contained in `2026.10.10-beta.4`.

Do they cover the `observeToolOutcome` path described above? If yes, this can be closed as covered and I will wait for the stable cut. If not, this looks like an additional retention site with the same shape.

### How this was measured

- `openclaw gateway stability` and `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.stability` for the 30s memory samples
- `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.heapSnapshot --params '{"reason":"..."}'` for the two snapshots
- `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.heapProfile` (60s, 16 KiB sampling) - not useful here; only ~2 MiB of new allocations land in a 60s window at this growth rate
- streaming parse of the snapshot `nodes` / `edges` arrays with BFS from GC roots for the retainer path

Happy to attach the raw snapshots, but each is ~400 MB; say the word and I will upload trimmed per-type aggregates instead.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.10, the Control UI still hides reasoning that is enabled through `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "on"` when a session has no explicit `/reasoning` override. The fix for this exact case (#173524, which closed #79469) is present on `main` but is not included in the `v2026.10.10` release tag.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "on"` and `ui.prefs.chatShowThinking: true`. Do not set a per-agent `reasoningDefault` or a per-session `/reasoning` override.
2. In Control UI, open a session that has no explicit reasoning override and send a prompt to a reasoning-capable model whose provider returns `reasoning_content`.
3. Observe the completed turn: no Thinking/reasoning block is displayed, before or after completion.
4. Send `/reasoning on` in the same session: reasoning then appears, and `sessions.list` reports `reasoningLevel: "on"` for that session.

## Expected behavior

Per `docs/tools/thinking.md`, Control UI shows native-provider reasoning for `on` and `stream` when View → Reasoning is enabled, and `reasoningDefault` is documented as the agent/global default reasoning visibility. A session that inherits `on` should therefore display reasoning without a per-session override.

## Actual behavior

Reasoning is generated and persisted, but not rendered. `sessions.list` returns `reasoningLevel: null` and `reasoningDefault: null` for sessions without an explicit override (58 of 62 sessions on this gateway), so the UI gate evaluates false. Only the 4 sessions with an explicit `/reasoning on` display reasoning.

## OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

## Operating system

Linux 6.12.100+deb13-amd64 (x64), Node 24.22.1

## Install method

npm global (`openclaw update`)

## Model

deepseek-v4.1-flash (OpenAI-compatible provider; returns `reasoning_content`)

## Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> OpenAI-compatible gateway -> upstream model

## Logs

Trajectory evidence from an affected session (reasoning is generated and stored):

```json
{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"Let me find ..."},{"type":"toolCall","id":"call_...","name":"exec"}],"usage":{"reasoningTokens":33}}
```

`sessions.list` row for a session without an override:

```json
{"key":"agent:ops:dashboard:...","reasoningLevel":null,"reasoningDefault":null}
```

After `/reasoning on` in another session:

```json
{"key":"agent:main:dashboard:...","reasoningLevel":"on","reasoningDefault":null}
```

## Source comparison

`v2026.10.10`, `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-reasoning.ts:128`:

```ts
const level = props.selectedSession?.reasoningLevel;
```

`main`, same file:

```ts
selectedSession?: { reasoningLevel?: string | null; reasoningDefault?: string | null };
const level = session?.reasoningLevel ?? session?.reasoningDefault;
```

`v2026.10.10` also has no `reasoningDefault` projection in `src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils.types.ts`, or `src/gateway/session-event-payload.ts`. On `main`, `session-utils-row.ts` adds:

```ts
reasoningDefault:
  resolveAgentConfig(cfg, input.agentId)?.reasoningDefault ??
  cfg.agents?.defaults?.reasoningDefault,
```

PR #173524 merged 2026-10-16T23:35:13Z. The `v2026.10.10` tag was created 2026-11-03T01:32:18Z but does not contain these changes.

## Impact and severity

Everyone who enables reasoning through the documented `reasoningDefault` setting sees no reasoning in Control UI on the latest stable release unless they send `/reasoning on` in each session. Reasoning is still generated and stored, so there is no data loss; the workaround is per-session and easy to miss.

## Additional context

This is a release/backport gap rather than a new behavior regression: the fix exists on `main` but did not ship in the 2026.10.10 release.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Bug (Talk realtime consult cannot use Codex subscription OAuth)

### Summary

With Browser Talk (`brain: agent-consult`, GPT-Live over WebRTC), every agent consult for an agent whose only OpenAI credential is a ChatGPT/Codex subscription OAuth profile fails right away with:

```
No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.
```

Typed chat turns in the **same session** (`agent:voice:main`) work fine through the Codex app-server harness with the same OAuth profile. The realtime voice leg works too (session.ready, speech in/out). Only the consult hand-off fails.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10), currently the latest stable

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 arm64, Node 24.22.1

### Config (relevant parts)

```json5
talk: {
  agentId: "voice",
  realtime: {
    provider: "openai",
    model: "gpt-live-1-codex",
    mode: "realtime",
    transport: "webrtc",
    brain: "agent-consult",
    providers: { openai: { speakerVoice: "cove" } }
  }
}
// agent "voice": default model openai/gpt-6.2-sol (session also tried on openai/gpt-6.1-sol)
// auth: exactly one openai profile, type OAuth (ChatGPT subscription); no Platform API key
// session entry: agentHarnessId "codex"
```

`openclaw models status --agent voice` reports:

```
Runtime auth
- openai via codex uses openai effective=profiles:… | status=indeterminate
Model route issues
- openai/gpt-6.2-sol [indeterminate] Auth readiness could not be confirmed for openai/gpt-6.2-sol.
```
(The OAuth profile itself is reported `ok`.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Agent with OpenAI available only through a Codex subscription OAuth profile and the Codex harness. Normal chat works.
2. Set `talk.agentId` to that agent, using GPT-Live with `brain: agent-consult`.
3. Start Browser Talk from the Control UI and ask something that triggers a consult (e.g. "What's the time?").

### Expected

The consult runs through the same harness/auth as a normal turn for that session (Codex, subscription OAuth), or it fails with a reason code that names the route/harness check that rejected it.

### Actual

Every consult fails in 8–21 ms, before any provider request, with `modelFallbackCandidate: false`. Repeated across several Talk sessions on the same day:

```
[diagnostic] {"errorName":"Error","taskKind":"turn","sessionKey":"agent:voice:main","runId":"talk-realtime-consult-…","modelFallbackCandidate":false}
  lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=18 error="No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai."
[plugins] OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.
```

The user did see one or two consults succeed earlier on, so it may be intermittent or depend on state. I couldn't find those successes in the logs, so I can't compare them.

### Analysis (from reading dist, may be wrong)

- The consult goes through `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `agentRuntime.runEmbeddedAgent(...)`, with `agentHarnessRuntimeOverride` taken from the session entry.
- The rejection comes from `selectProviderModelRouteAuth` (`provider-model-route-auth-*.mjs`). It only defers to the runtime auth owner (Codex) when `runtimeAuthOwner` is set, which requires `harnessAuthBootstrap === "harness"`, **and** either the model resolves to more than one route or `allowNativeAuthOnSingleRoute` holds. The second option needs **zero** ordered profiles.
- So an agent with exactly one OAuth profile and a single resolved route can't take the deferral branch. If that profile doesn't match the resolved route's auth requirement, it gets this error. That fits the `indeterminate` route status above.

### Related

- #202519: same error, same version, in another non-direct runner (queued Goal successor) after a successful direct Codex turn. Possibly the same root cause: the non-direct path resolves a different route catalog from the one direct chat uses.
- #161885: the Claude equivalent. Talk consults ignore `claude-cli` and fail with "No API key found for provider anthropic". This reproduces on the same machine on 2026.11.6 when the main agent (Claude via claude-cli) owns Talk.

Together these suggest Talk consults only work when the provider has a direct API credential. Subscription-only setups (Codex OAuth or Claude CLI) can't use voice delegation at all.

### Impact

Talk can't be used for anything that needs the agent (tools, lookups). The only workaround seems to be adding a paid Platform API key alongside the subscription.

### Summary

The local-model guide says a text-only check does not prove a model can finish a multi-step agent task, but it gives no way to check that. A read-only two-step tool recipe would let operators test it before making a local model the default.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

docs/gateway/local-models.md (troubleshooting steps, after "Inspect the failing request and server logs")

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Open docs/gateway/local-models.md on main (checked at 444399b60e6).
2. Read the troubleshooting list. Step 5 warns that a successful text-only check does not prove multi-step tool use.
3. Look for a way to test a task where the second tool call needs a value returned by the first. There is none.

### Expected docs behavior/content

A short section, for example "Verify a two-step tool task", that:

- uses two synthetic files in a disposable workspace (`catalog.json` maps a name to a record file, the record file holds an opaque value);
- uses a disposable config with only `read` allowed (`tools: { allow: ["read"], deny: ["skills_read"], toolSearch: false }`) and no fallback model;
- runs `openclaw agent exec` and checks that the agent read both files and returned the opaque value;
- explains how to tell a missing tool result (the result never reaches the server) from a model that gets the result and stops before the second call, by comparing the assistant stream OpenClaw receives with the request the local server logs.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The guide warns about the failure mode but has no recipe to reproduce or diagnose it.

### Impact

Local-model operators. A model can pass setup's connection check (which sends no tools) and make a correct first tool call, then stop before using the result. Without a recipe, operators find this only after making the model their default.

### Evidence

In a local Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M on llama.cpp test, the first lookup was correct in all six OpenClaw runs, and none made the dependent second call. This is a model limit, not an OpenClaw defect; it shows why the guide should give a way to check.

A draft of the section was checked with `openclaw agent exec` against a scripted loopback provider: only `read` was offered, the agent read both fixture files and returned the expected value. That validates the recipe, not any real model.

### Additional information

Docs only. No defaults, config contracts or runtime behavior change.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add Chat Completions transport test coverage for replaying a tool result, with its original call ID, before a dependent second tool call. Cover it with the optional tool-result name both enabled and disabled.

### Problem to solve

The Chat Completions transport must send a completed tool result back to the provider with the original `tool_call_id` so the next call can use the result. The replay integration suite (`packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-replay.integration.test.ts`, checked at 444399b60e6) tests reasoning fields, but not this two-request handoff, and not the `compat.requiresToolResultName` switch. A regression there would break every multi-step tool task on local or OpenAI-compatible providers without a failing test.

### Proposed solution

Add a parameterized case (`requiresToolResultName` false and true) to the existing replay integration suite:

- a loopback server returns a `lookup_record_id` tool call on the first request;
- on the second request it finds the `role: "tool"` message and returns a `fetch_value` call whose argument is the replayed result;
- the test asserts the second request carries the tool result with the original call ID (and the `name` field only when enabled), and that the parsed second call has the expected argument.

Test only. No behavior, default or setting change, and no claim about real-model skill.

### Alternatives considered

Rely on the existing reasoning replay tests. They do not check the tool result handoff or the name switch.

### Impact

Maintainers changing the Chat Completions transport. Severity: a silent regression would break multi-step tool use for affected providers. Frequency: every dependent tool call on that transport.

### Evidence/examples

A draft of this case passed in the focused transport file (18 cases). Targeted type-aware lint and formatting passed.

In a separate local llama.cpp test, the optional tool-result name reached the server but did not change its rendered prompt in two isolated replays, so both settings should be covered.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug: GUI shows an attachment card, external Telegram does not receive it.

### Summary

On a **native Telegram turn** (not WebChat), `message(action=send, channel=telegram, target=<chat>, attachments=[local zip])` failed with:

```text
Session "agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>" was not found.
```

The agent then emitted a final `MEDIA:<absolute path>` line. Control UI/GUI rendered the attachment card, but the Telegram topic never received the file. The user replied “waiting” in Telegram. No Telegram send receipt existed.

This is distinct from #198388 (WebChat targetless progress inheriting composite Telegram DM-topic `threadId`).

### Reproduction (sanitized)

1. Native Telegram DM forum-topic session, key shape `agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>`.
2. Agent assembles a valid local ZIP (~1.8 MiB, three JPEG members, `zipfile.testzip()` clean) and calls:

   ```json
   {
     "action": "send",
     "channel": "telegram",
     "target": "<chat>",
     "message": "...",
     "attachments": [{"type":"file","media":"/abs/path/final.zip","name":"final.zip","mimeType":"application/zip"}]
   }
   ```

   (also tried without explicit `channel`)
3. Result, twice:

   ```text
   {"status":"error","tool":"message","error":"Session \"agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<chat>:thread:<chat>:<topic>\" was not found."}
   ```
4. Agent falls back to final text containing `MEDIA:/abs/path/final.zip`.
5. GUI shows the attachment; Telegram user says the file is absent; no send receipt.

### Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`f521fcf`), Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, user systemd Gateway.
- Run/provider: `omniroute/nr-deepseek-41f` on the historical failing run; Codex runtime observed on the same session class during live diagnosis.
- Session was visible/readable through `sessions_list` / `sessions_history`; only the `message` send path reported the session as missing.

### Source-level trace (read-only)

- The exact error text is produced by `prepareInProcessSessionRead` in `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-session-read.ts` (`Session "${key}" was not found.`), used by in-process `sessions.get`.
- `message(action=send)` is dispatched through `message.action` (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.ts` → `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`).
- The failing call supplies a Telegram numeric `target` but no valid explicit thread; the session-key-derived implicit route points at the threaded Telegram session, and the session-read/projection lookup rejects it as not found.
- Final `MEDIA:` is parsed by `src/media/parse-output.ts` (`MEDIA_TOKEN_RE`) and can be projected to GUI without an external-channel send receipt.

### Expected

An explicit `message` send with a valid Telegram target and attachment either delivers to Telegram with a receipt, or fails before GUI projection with a clear actionable error. A final `MEDIA:` in a native Telegram session should either attach in Telegram or be surfaced as not-delivered.

### Actual

Tool error says the existing threaded session was not found; fallback `MEDIA:` renders only in GUI; Telegram gets nothing.

### Impact

Repeated file/zip delivery failures in native Telegram threads. Users see attachment cards locally but receive no file externally.

### Related

- #198388 — different WebChat composite `threadId` failure; do not conflate.
- #194024 — `Session ... was not found` family, but for subagent settle, not this message/attachment path.

No private chat IDs, names, photos, absolute paths, or transcript bodies are included.

issues.body:
### Summary

On macOS (Intel x64), `openclaw gateway stop` and `openclaw gateway stop --force` both fail with:

```
Gateway stop failed: ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected.
Use the Gateway update action for a managed handoff, or retry from an independent terminal
without inherited service markers.
```

The command is run from a **standalone Terminal.app login shell** (not spawned by the Gateway, no inherited service markers), so the suggested remedy cannot be followed. `--force` — documented as "Allow stop from a non-interactive shell" — does not bypass the check either.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) |
| Install | npm global, launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) |
| OS | macOS 15.8.1, x86_64 (Intel) |
| Node | v26.12.1 |
| Shell | zsh login shell in Terminal.app (ttys000) |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the macOS Terminal app from Spotlight (independent shell, no gateway ancestry).
2. Run `openclaw gateway stop` → fails with `ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected`.
3. Run `openclaw gateway stop --force` → fails with the identical error.

### Expected

`gateway stop` either succeeds, or at minimum `--force` overrides the ancestry heuristic as documented.

### Actual

Both variants refuse to act. The only working path is bypassing the CLI and driving launchd directly:

```
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<gateway-label>
# run offline maintenance (e.g. openclaw doctor --fix)
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<gateway-label>.plist
```

### Related symptom (possibly same root cause)

`openclaw doctor --fix` also reports process-inspection failures and therefore retains temporary updater runtimes:

```
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at <path>: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes:
ProcSafeError: layout-mismatch: invalid Darwin argument alignment
```

Three retained runtime directories (~1.8 GiB total) had to be cleaned manually.

### Analysis

Both failures point at the native process inspection layer (`proc-safe`) rather than the service itself: the ancestry check cannot complete, and the same layer reports a sysctl/kernel-struct layout mismatch on Darwin x86_64. This suggests the process inspection helper mis-parses Darwin process arguments on this platform/build.

### Impact

- Cannot stop the Gateway through the documented CLI path.
- Cannot reach an offline state to run `mcp probe`, `memory status`, or DB path repairs (they require exclusive offline state ownership).
- Workaround requires knowing the launchd label and plist path.

### Environment notes

- No inherited `OPENCLAW_*` service markers in the shell environment.
- `openclaw gateway status --deep` itself works and reports the service correctly.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Approval cards for config-mutation requests (triggered via the `openclaw` system tool's `config.set`) are not delivered to a TUI client, even when a TUI session is actively connected to the exact same session that another client (Control UI webapp, or Telegram) correctly receives the approval card on.

This is not a general "single-client-only" delivery limitation — Telegram-originated approvals are confirmed delivered in parallel to both Telegram and the Control UI webapp simultaneously, working as expected. The TUI specifically appears to be excluded from whatever approval-broadcast mechanism the other two surfaces participate in.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect to the same agent session (`agent:main:main` in our case) via both the TUI (`openclaw tui`) and the Control UI webapp at the same time.
2. From within that session, trigger an action that requires approval — in our case, a config mutation via the `openclaw` system tool (`config.set` on an arbitrary key, e.g. `telemetry.enabled`).
3. Observe: the approval card appears in the Control UI webapp. The TUI shows nothing at all — not even after the fact; reopening/refreshing the TUI view does not surface it retroactively either.
4. Separately, confirmed as a working comparison case: trigger an approval-requiring action from a Telegram-originated interaction. The approval card correctly appears in **both** Telegram and the Control UI webapp at the same time, in parallel.

Reproduced twice in a row with a harmless, side-effect-free test (`telemetry.enabled` true→false), specifically to rule out a one-off timing fluke.

### Expected behavior

A pending approval for a session should be visible on every currently-connected client attached to that session, including the TUI — not just whichever surface happens to be the one that "owns" delivery for that approval's trigger path. At minimum, a TUI client that's actively attached to a session with a pending approval should be able to see and act on it.

### Actual behavior

- Config-mutation approvals (via the `openclaw` system tool) triggered while a TUI client is attached to the session: **never appear in the TUI**, confirmed twice.
- The same class of approval, when the session also has a Control UI webapp client attached: **appears correctly in the webapp**.
- Telegram-originated approvals: **appear correctly in both Telegram and the webapp** at the same time — this works as expected and is the behavior we'd want the TUI to also participate in.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9

### Operating system

Linux (Debian GNU/Linux 13 "trixie", kernel 6.12.111+deb13-cloud-amd64, x86_64)

### Install method

Homebrew, systemd-managed gateway service

### Impact and severity

Medium. Not a data-loss or security issue, but a real reliability/usability gap: if the TUI is someone's primary or only open client at the time an approval fires, they have no way to know a pending approval exists at all — no card, no retroactive indicator. This could silently block requested actions (e.g. our config-mutation tests) indefinitely if no other client happens to be connected at the time.

### Possibly related

Not aware of an existing issue describing this specifically — this surfaced incidentally while diagnosing an unrelated pair of bugs (#167851, #167920) during a session that happened to have both a TUI and webapp client open on the same session at once.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Running a Gateway update from the Control UI on Windows (Scheduled Task install) stops the task/gateway and then hangs indefinitely at stage 4/7 ("Activating"). The Scheduled Task is left Disabled, no gateway process is running, and the npm package is NOT updated. Dialog shows: "Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it." Manual recovery: `schtasks /Change /TN "OpenClaw Gateway" /ENABLE` + `openclaw gateway start`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, npm-global OpenClaw 2026.9.5, gateway managed as Scheduled Task (logon trigger).
2. Control UI → update Gateway to the newer release (target 2026.10.2).
3. Update stops the task/gateway; dialog reaches "Activating" (completed 3 of 7 stages) and spins forever. Observed on two consecutive update attempts the same day.
4. Post-mortem after killing the dialog: Scheduled Task State=Disabled; zero gateway processes; `openclaw --version` still the OLD version; gateway log contains `update.run completed` RPC entries and the line "Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it."

### Expected behavior

Activation either completes (start the new build and verify) or fails loudly with an automatic rollback that restores the previous gateway AND re-enables the Scheduled Task. The task auto-start suspension performed before the update must be symmetrically resumed on every exit path (success, failure, interruption).

### Actual behavior

- Scheduled Task left Disabled; no gateway process; package version unchanged (update never landed).
- Control UI shows an endless spinner at "Activating" with no error surfaced to the user.
- After manual task re-enable + `openclaw gateway start`, the old build runs normally; a later CLI `openclaw update --yes` completes the update successfully.

### OpenClaw version

from 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), target 2026.10.2; CLI after manual recovery still 2026.9.5 until CLI update

### Operating system

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200

### Install method

npm global; gateway via Windows Scheduled Task (logon trigger)

### Model

main agent, glm-5.3 — issue is not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

local gateway → Control UI update flow → Windows Scheduled Task service manager

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it.   (update dialog step detail)

# gateway log around the same window:
update.run completed actor=openclaw-control-ui device=<redacted>
Runtime: stopped (state Disabled, last run 267014, last run time 2026-10-12T04:08:57.0000000Z)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Control UI dialog screenshot available on request (Chinese locale; stage list: Requested ✓ / Validating ✓ / Preparing ✓ / Activating (spinner) / Restarting / Verifying / Done).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Windows Scheduled Task installs using the Control UI update entry.
- Severity: high — gateway left down with a hung UI; unattended machines stay down until manual CLI recovery.
- Frequency: 2/2 attempts on 2026-10-12 (both update attempts failed identically).
- Consequence: users believe an update is in progress; no error is shown; remote/unattended gateways stay offline.

### Additional information

- The same target update completed successfully via CLI (`openclaw update --yes`) immediately afterwards, including service restart — so the failure is specific to the UI-driven/service-inspection path, not the package itself.
- Historical note (separate concern, possibly already fixed): an earlier 9.x gateway self-update persisted the retired transient key `plugins.installs` into openclaw.json; the running gateway does not validate, so the next cold start failed schema validation ("Unrecognized key: installs") and the logon-triggered auto-start aborted with "Refusing to run automatic gateway startup migrations because the selected config changed during startup" — which presents as "gateway did not auto-start after reboot". 2026.10.2's CLI update did NOT reproduce the writeback, and doctor auto-migrates the key now.
- Not a duplicate per issue search before filing (searches for "fs-safe-move EPERM", "update stuck Activating", "scheduled task disabled automatic rollback").

issues.body:
### Summary
Let operators set the model, thinking level, and input/output budget used by background Skill Workshop (self-learning) reviews, instead of the fixed values in `session-fork-run.ts`.

### Problem to solve
Since #173889 the background review runs with fixed settings: `thinkLevel: "low"`, `contextTokenBudget: 16_384`, `maxTokens: 2_048`, a 120 s cap, `bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight"` (still on `main` at `src/agents/session-fork-run.ts:507`). That change fixed a real problem — reviews competing with interactive turns during provider rate limiting — and we don't want it reverted.

But the right trade-off depends on the deployment. Some operators have a policy of never running agent work at low reasoning effort, and some care more about learned-skill quality than review cost, because a saved skill is later followed by the main agent as an instruction. Today the only choices are to accept the fixed settings or to turn learning `off`. `propose` mode (#181747) helps because drafts get a human or foreground check, but the quality of the drafts themselves is still capped by the fixed settings.

### Proposed solution
Optional keys under `skills.workshop.autonomous` (or the plugin's config), all defaulting to today's values so nothing changes on upgrade:
- `review.thinking`: `"low"` (default) | `"medium"` | `"high"` | `"xhigh"`.
- `review.model`: `"auto"` (default = the foreground model, as today) or a `provider/model` ref.
- `review.contextTokens` and `review.maxOutputTokens`: override 16,384 / 2,048.
- `review.timeoutSeconds`: override 120.

The existing rate-limit backoff, yield-to-foreground behavior and background lane stay as they are.

### Impact
- Affected: operators running Skill Workshop learning (`auto` or `propose`) who need a minimum reasoning level or higher-quality learned skills.
- Severity: medium. Learned skills are followed as instructions by the main agent, so low-effort drafts either need extra review or learning gets disabled.
- Frequency: every background review.
- Consequence: extra manual or scripted re-review of every draft, or loss of unattended learning.

### Alternatives considered
- `autonomous.mode: "off"` and only manual `/learn`: loses unattended learning.
- `propose` + `/learn drafts`: helpful, but it does not change the reasoning effort that produces the drafts.
- Local patching of the fixed values: fragile across updates.

### Evidence/examples
- Hermes Agent exposes similar settings: `auxiliary.background_review.{enabled, provider, model, reasoning_effort, max_input_tokens}` (`agent/background_review.py`; docs `user-guide/features/memory.md`).
- Related: #159687 (open PR: context budget / skip policy for oversized reviews).

### Do you plan to open a PR?
No.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A completed tool-backed assistant run in the Control UI can show its final user-facing answer with only the agent name/timestamp footer; hovering the completed answer on desktop reveals no Reply or Copy actions, even though completed terminal assistant replies are expected to own those actions.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.7 and open a Control UI conversation in desktop Safari.
2. Let an agent perform a tool-backed run that ends with a normal final user-facing answer.
3. After the run is fully complete, hover the final answer.
4. Observe that the footer shows only the agent identity and timestamp, with no Reply or Copy actions.

Generic example of the affected final-answer shape:

> Completed the requested changes and opened a draft pull request.
>
> - Updated the requested implementation.
> - Added the requested documentation changes.
> - Validation passed with no remaining review blockers.
>
> Verified the draft is open and unmerged. No deployment or unrelated changes were performed.
>
> One release-related item still requires owner review.

The run was complete and idle. Hovering this final answer in desktop Safari still showed only the agent name and relative timestamp.

### Expected behavior

The completed terminal assistant answer should expose the normal message actions on hover/focus, including:

- Reply to message
- Copy as markdown

This matches the current run-frame contract established by the Control UI E2E coverage: completed runs with terminal assistant text get exactly those two footer actions, while commentary/tool-only runs intentionally do not.

Related prior work: #126276.

### Actual behavior

The completed final answer renders with sender identity and timestamp only. Hovering does not reveal Reply or Copy.

This is distinct from intentionally action-less intermediate commentary/tool activity.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, Safari 26.6.2

### Install method

Self-hosted Gateway / Control UI in Safari

### Model

Not relevant to the UI defect.

### Provider / routing chain

Not relevant to the UI defect; the failure is in Control UI transcript presentation after the run is already persisted and complete.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The observed run was a normal tool-backed agent run with multiple tool/work blocks followed by a visible final assistant answer.

### Logs

```text
No runtime error observed. This is a deterministic missing-action presentation state on the completed transcript row.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Observed directly in desktop Safari on 2026.9.7:

- the final assistant answer is visible;
- the run is complete;
- hovering the final answer shows only agent identity plus relative timestamp;
- no Reply or Copy icons appear.

Current source also shows the relevant ownership boundary:

- `renderAgentRunFrame()` only passes footer actions when `frame.outcome.actionOwner` is non-null.
- `completedFrameActionOwner()` first looks for an explicit assistant message whose phase is `final_answer` or whose `stopReason` is `stop`.
- Its fallback only uses the last frame part when that part is an assistant `group` and `messageCanOwnCompletedFrame(..., false)` accepts it.
- If neither path yields an owner, the completed run renders without footer actions.

This is a source-valid mechanism for the observed symptom, but the exact persisted metadata of the live message was not inspected, so this report does not claim which rejection branch produced the null owner.

Relevant files on both v2026.9.7 and current main:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-agent-run-grouping.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-agent-run-frame.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-group.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-markdown.ts`

Existing E2E coverage in `ui/src/e2e/chat-agent-run-transcript.e2e.test.ts` explicitly expects a completed run with terminal text to have one footer action owner and exactly two buttons: `Reply to message` and `Copy as markdown`.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Control UI users reading completed tool-backed agent runs.

Severity: usability defect. The whole-message Copy and Reply affordances disappear for a final answer even though they are expected to be available.

Frequency: reproduced in one completed run; wider frequency is unknown.

Consequence: users must manually select text to copy it, which is especially inconvenient on mobile/touch, and cannot use the normal reply affordance for that message.

### Additional information

This is related to but narrower than #159523, which covers general WebChat text-selection/copy friction. The defect here is that the completed terminal message's normal action owner is absent, despite the current run-frame action contract.

No existing issue specifically matching this completed-run action-owner loss was found before filing.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw system event --mode now --session-key agent:main:main --text "…"` returns `{"ok": true}`, the agent runs the turn in the main session and writes its reply, and then delivery to iMessage fails with

```
Failed to route reply to imessage: iMessage message reference does not belong to the selected conversation.
```

The user receives nothing, and the caller cannot know: per the CLI docs the command returns when the Gateway accepts the event, not when delivery finishes. Normal inbound iMessage turns in the same session reply fine, and so does `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:main --message … --deliver --reply-channel imessage --reply-to chat_id:1 --json` (`deliveryStatus.status: "sent"`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.11.5 with `@openclaw/imessage` 2026.11.5 on the Mac that owns the Messages database (no `remoteHost`); `channels.imessage.actions` unset, so the `reply` action is on by default.
2. Exchange a DM with the agent so that `agent:main:main` has an iMessage delivery context.
3. Run `openclaw system event --session-key agent:main:main --mode now --text "Tell the user that X happened." --json` → `{"ok": true}`.
4. A few seconds later the gateway log has the two lines under Logs. No message arrives.

Done twice on 2026-11-21, about five minutes apart: once while an inbound message was being picked up in the same session, once with the session idle. Same result both times.

### Expected behavior

The reply to a system event is delivered to the session's iMessage conversation as an ordinary, non-threaded message.

### Actual behavior

Delivery is attempted and fails; the reply exists only in the cron result summary and the transcript.

Cause, as far as I can trace it in the installed build and on `main` (19082a44):

1. `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.ts` builds the turn's message context with `MessageSid: occurrenceId` — the event's own id — and takes `OriginatingChannel` / `OriginatingTo` from the session's delivery context.
2. Reply routing (`routeReplyOperation`) hands `currentMessageId` to the channel's `threading.resolveReplyTransport`.
3. The iMessage plugin's `resolveReplyTransport` (`extensions/imessage/src/channel.ts`) returns `replyToId = existingReplyToId ?? implicitReplyToId`, where `implicitReplyToId` is `currentMessageId` unless `replyToCurrent === false` or `replyDelivery.replyToMode === "off"`.
4. `resolveAuthorizedIMessageReplyReference` → `authorizeIMessageResourceReference` → `checkIMessageResourceBinding` looks that id up in `chat.db`. An event id is not a Messages GUID, so no row matches, the binding is `"mismatch"`, and `message-resource.ts` throws the error above.

I read steps 1, 3 and 4 in the source. I did not instrument step 2, i.e. I have not observed the event id arriving as `currentMessageId`; that link is inferred from `currentMessageId: ctx.MessageSidFull ?? ctx.MessageSid` and from the fact that the same session delivers when the turn comes from an inbound message or from `openclaw agent --deliver`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (76cbb32), @openclaw/imessage 2026.11.5

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (Apple silicon)

### Install method

OpenClaw.app-managed runtime (Bun 1.4.4)

### Model

google/gemini-4-neon

### Provider / routing chain

iMessage channel (imsg 0.21.1, local Messages database) → agent main → google/gemini-4-neon. The failure is in reply routing, after the model has answered.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
session-events {"source":"cron","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","eventId":"<uuid>","error":"Error: Failed to route reply to imessage: iMessage message reference does not belong to the selected conversation."}
cron {"result":{"status":"failed","executionStarted":true,"interruptedByRestart":false,"delivered":false,"deliveryAttempted":true,"deliveryAmbiguous":false,"admissionDeferred":false,"summary":"<the reply text>","error":"Error: Failed to route reply to imessage: iMessage message reference does not belong to the selected conversation."}}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: anything that uses a system event to have the agent tell the user something over iMessage — monitor and watchdog scripts, async task completions relayed with `--session-key` (the example in `docs/cli/system.md`), and presumably other session-event sources that go through the same context builder (not tested).
- Severity: message loss, silent. The turn runs and is billed, the transcript shows a reply, the user gets nothing.
- Frequency: 2 of 2 here.

### Additional information

Possible fixes, any one of which would avoid it:

- do not offer a session event's occurrence id to channels as `currentMessageId` (it is not a channel message id);
- in the iMessage plugin, only derive an implicit reply reference from a `currentMessageId` that is a Messages reference;
- let an *implicit* reply reference that fails authorization degrade to a non-threaded send instead of failing the delivery (an explicit one should still fail).

What I use instead for now: `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:main --message … --deliver --reply-channel imessage --reply-to chat_id:<n> --json`, checking `deliveryStatus.status`. `channels.imessage.actions.reply: false` should also avoid the reference according to `resolveReplyTransport`; I have not tried it.

Not the same as #193727 (different error, `remoteHost` without a local database, command replies). The `send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay` line that appears in the same log window is #115328.

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant; the two runs, the log lines and the working `openclaw agent --deliver` call are from the machine as described.

issues.body:
## Problem

An OpenClaw plugin that reviews integration calls from a Discord voice agent needs the speaker’s final words and verified Discord user ID for the exact run. The realtime consult can start with a provider-supplied prompt. The Discord adapter knows the speaker and processes transcript events, but the tool policy hook has no bound record containing both facts for this run. A typed integration request can be reviewed against the original message. The equivalent voice request lacks that evidence.

## Proposed behavior

Expose an optional, run-scoped voice input on the existing plugin policy surface. Attach the authenticated Discord speaker ID and the finalized user transcript from the same admitted voice turn. Consume the data through the existing conversation access policy. Keep it out of model-authored arguments, ordinary logs, and new durable storage. If the provider gives no reliable final transcript or call correlation, leave the metadata unavailable so a plugin can hold or decline just the integration call that depends on it.

## Alternatives considered

Parsing the generated consult prompt loses the distinction between original words and provider-generated context. Using the most recent room transcript can join a call to the wrong speaker or utterance. An upstream hook would let operators keep ordinary voice routing and use the same integration policy for typed and spoken requests.

## Prior art

Discord already admits and revalidates the speaker before launching an agent run. Its voice adapter also handles accepted transcripts separately from native consults. [Realtime consult source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/19082a44a/extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-consults.ts#L120) · [Discord voice ingress](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/19082a44a/extensions/discord/src/voice/ingress.ts#L91)

Related to #197647, which is about delivery of delegated results back to the speaker. This request is about the original user input available to a tool policy before a call runs.

issues.body:
## What problem this solves

The official Perplexity plugin currently exposes only the `web_search` provider contract. Operators can use Perplexity's Search API for retrieval, but cannot opt into Agent API cited synthesis or deep research as a native plugin tool without separately configuring Perplexity as a model provider or installing an external MCP server.

## Proposed solution

Add one optional read-only tool to `@openclaw/perplexity-plugin`:

- `perplexity_research`
- required `query`
- optional explicit `effort`: `low | medium | high | xhigh`
- returns the synthesized answer plus normalized citations/search-result metadata
- reuses the plugin's existing Perplexity credential resolution
- is declared optional and hidden unless explicitly allowlisted

This leaves the existing `web_search` provider, Search API defaults, and OpenRouter compatibility unchanged. It also avoids encoding an opinionated automatic decision tree: the calling agent or operator chooses the effort level.

## Alternatives considered

- Four separate ask/reason/research tools: larger prompt and manifest surface for the same API.
- Change `web_search` to use Agent API: breaks the structured retrieval contract and existing users.
- Require Perplexity MCP: valid external option, but not equivalent to extending the official plugin users already installed.
- Native Router API support: premature while Router remains private preview.

## Evidence / prior art

- The plugin SDK supports mixed plugins with `webSearchProviders` plus optional tools.
- The bundled Tavily and Firecrawl plugins already combine provider and tool contracts.
- Perplexity Agent API exposes effort presets and cited search-backed output.
- #126889 documents Agent API/model-provider and MCP setup, but does not implement a native plugin tool.
- #152778 handles only the retiring synthesized `web_search` compatibility route and intentionally does not add new tool surface.

issues.body:
### Summary

Realtime Talk agent consults (Control UI Talk / GPT-Live native delegation) ignore the per-model `agentRuntime` setting and the model fallback chain. When the agent's primary model is routed through a CLI backend (e.g. `anthropic/*` with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`) and there is no direct API credential for that provider, every consult fails immediately with an auth error, and it never falls back.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (c074824), macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0

### Config (relevant parts)

```json5
agents: {
  defaults: {
    models: {
      "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } },
      "openai/gpt-5.6-sol": {}
    },
    model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5", fallbacks: ["openai/gpt-5.6-sol"] }
  }
},
talk: { agentId: "main", realtime: { speakerVoice: "sol" } }
```

No `anthropic` auth profile or API key. `openclaw models status` reports `anthropic via claude-cli ... runtime-synthetic`. Normal chat turns in the same session work fine through claude-cli.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure as above (Anthropic only reachable through `claude-cli`, with a working OpenAI fallback).
2. Start Talk from the Control UI in the main session and ask something that triggers a consult.

### Expected

The consult runs through the same harness as a normal turn for that model (claude-cli), or at least uses the configured fallback (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`).

### Actual

The consult fails in about 46 ms and the turn ends with no reply:

```
lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=46 error="Couldn't sign in to anthropic. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic` ... (No API key found for provider "anthropic". Auth store: .../agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite ...)"
errorName=FailoverError runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Couldn't sign in to anthropic ...
```

The message is also misleading. It says a saved login has expired, but the provider is intentionally CLI-only.

### Likely cause

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` calls `agentRuntime.runEmbeddedAgent(...)` directly with the session's provider/model. It appears to skip both CLI-harness selection (`agentRuntime` per model) and the `runWithModelFallback`-style fallback that normal turns use, so a CLI-routed model goes to the embedded runner and needs a direct API credential. A `FailoverError` is raised but nothing acts on it.

### Workaround

Create a second agent on the same workspace with an API/OAuth-backed model and set `talk.agentId` to it. This only helps Talk sessions that aren't already scoped to an agent, and it splits conversation history. There's no `talk.consultModel`-style option to pick the consult model directly. Adding one would also help here.

Possibly related: #116058 (claude-cli / API path fallback inconsistencies).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The FaceTime audio pump respawns SoX in `clearPlayback()` (barge-in, `response-superseded`, non-completed outcome) and the next audio delta can be written a few milliseconds later. When that happens SoX plays only what was already queued on its stdin, exits with status 0, and the pump reports

```
[facetime] native audio bridge failed: SoX playback exited (0)
```

which ends the call (`call closed (talk-failed: SoX playback exited (0))`). To the caller the assistant simply hangs up mid-conversation.

Root cause: under Bun on macOS the child's stdin is a socket, not a pipe. SoX's `lsx_filelength()` tests `st.st_mode & S_IFREG`, which is non-zero for sockets (`S_IFSOCK` contains the `S_IFREG` bit), so `lsx_check_read_params()` takes `st_size` — for a socket, the number of bytes queued at that moment — as the total input length (`src/formats_i.c`). If nothing is queued when SoX opens its input, the length is 0 ("unknown") and streaming works. If audio is already queued, SoX reads exactly that many bytes and finishes.

### Steps to reproduce

Standalone (no call, same Bun binary the gateway uses, plugin's SoX arguments):

```js
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
const ARGS = ["-q", "--buffer", "8192", "-t", "raw", "-r", "24000", "-c", "1", "-e", "signed-integer", "-b", "16", "-L", "-", "-t", "coreaudio", "OpenClaw-Feed"];
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const p = spawn("/opt/homebrew/bin/sox", ARGS, { stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"] });
p.on("exit", (code) => console.log("sox exited", code));
// await sleep(20);              // uncomment: SoX stays alive
p.stdin.write(Buffer.alloc(15360));
for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) { await sleep(57); p.stdin.write(Buffer.alloc(15000)); }
await sleep(3000);
```

In a call: use a realtime provider whose first audio delta arrives together with `response.created`, and start a new response while the previous one is still playing by the pump's playback clock (the caller answers the instant the assistant finishes, or a tool call is followed immediately by another spoken response). `startResponse()` calls `pump.clearOutputAudio()`, a new SoX is spawned, and `writeOutputAudio()` runs about 10 ms later.

### Expected behavior

Playback continues on the new SoX process; the call stays up.

### Actual behavior

Measured on the machine (0 ms into SoX from Bun: 8 runs; 10 ms: 3 runs; 20 ms or more: 15 runs; the other rows 2–6 runs each; every run of a row gave the same result):

| Parent / child stdin | First write after spawn | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 0 ms, then 7 chunks 57 ms apart | SoX exits 0 at ~370–400 ms, having played only the first 0.32 s chunk |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 0 ms, one 2.5 s write | SoX plays all 2.5 s, then exits 0 |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 10 ms | SoX exits 0 |
| Bun 1.4.4 → SoX | 20 ms or more | SoX stays alive |
| Bun 1.4.4 → `wc -c` | 0 ms | all bytes received |
| python3 pipe → SoX | 0 ms | SoX stays alive |
| python3 `socketpair` → SoX | 0 ms | SoX exits after the first chunk (writer gets EPIPE) |
| python3 `socketpair` → SoX | 300 ms | SoX stays alive |

A child spawned by Bun reports its stdin as `S_ISSOCK`, `st_size` 15360 right after a 15360-byte write, and `(st_mode & S_IFREG) != 0`. The same child behind a python pipe reports `S_ISFIFO` and `(st_mode & S_IFREG) == 0`.

In the real call the macOS log shows the old SoX context stopped at 01:09:04.333, the new SoX starting I/O at 04.402 and stopping it itself at 04.702 after 15360 frames, and the gateway logging the bridge failure at 04.715.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (76cbb32), `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.11.5 from ClawHub

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (Apple silicon), SoX 14.4.2 (Homebrew 14.4.2_6)

### Install method

OpenClaw.app-managed runtime (Bun 1.4.4)

### Model

Realtime voice; agent google/gemini-4-neon

### Provider / routing chain

FaceTime plugin → realtime provider id `openai` with `baseUrl` pointing at a local OpenAI-Realtime-compatible relay → ElevenLabs realtime. The relay is not needed to reproduce: the standalone script above uses only Bun and SoX. A fast provider just makes the 10 ms window easy to hit, because its first audio delta arrives 0–5 ms after `response.created`.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[facetime] native audio bridge failed: SoX playback exited (0)
[facetime] call closed (talk-failed: SoX playback exited (0))
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: FaceTime realtime calls on Bun; any path that calls `clearOutputAudio()` shortly before the next audio (barge-in, superseded response, cancelled response).
- Severity: the call is dropped.
- Frequency: intermittent, timing dependent. Replaying the delta timings of one 7-minute call through the plugin's rules gives two respawns, one of them inside the window.

### Additional information

Possible fixes, any one of which removes the failure:

- give SoX a real pipe (for example spawn it behind a FIFO, or through a tiny `cat |` stage), so `st_mode & S_IFREG` is false;
- do not write to a freshly spawned SoX until it has opened its input (a short readiness delay, or queue the first chunks);
- treat a clean playback exit as recoverable and respawn once instead of failing the bridge.

Local mitigation I am running in the relay: the next response's events are held until the previous one has finished playing by the same clock the pump uses, so `startResponse()` never supersedes, and audio is forwarded no earlier than 120 ms after its `response.created`.

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant; every measurement above was taken on the machine as described.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With Telegram configured, every Gateway start logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability is deprecated`, and the Plugins catalog lists Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026. Steering an active run from a Telegram message also logs `Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated`. Both come from bundled or core code, not from a third-party plugin, so the operator cannot act on either.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build main at `19aff5bfd42` (`pnpm build`).
2. Configure `channels.telegram` with a bot token and `execApprovals.enabled: true` with one approver.
3. Run `openclaw gateway run` and read stderr.
4. Run `openclaw gateway call plugins.list --json` and look at the `telegram` entry's `compatibilityNotices`.
5. For the second warning: send a Telegram message to a session while a run in that session is still active, so the message steers it.

### Expected behavior

No `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warnings that name a bundled plugin, and no retiring-API notice for Telegram. Discord has neither since #174937 moved it to `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`.

### Actual behavior

- Step 3 logs one warning at plugin load. With `--trace-deprecation` the stack is `warnPluginSdkDeprecation <- createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` (module load).
- Step 4 returns 265 plugins. Exactly one, `telegram`, has a `deprecated-sdk-api` notice: "Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a plugin update.", apis `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`.
- Step 5 logs `Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated; use await fingerprintAsync() instead.` The call is core's: `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.ts`) re-reads its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated `fingerprint()`, reached from `runActiveReplySteer -> prepareReplyMessageJoin -> prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority`. The warning takes the label of the plugin frame it runs in.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.5 source build with local commits on two gateways; reproduced on main `19aff5bfd42`, and the three call sites are unchanged on main `da908d53390`.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 and macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout, gateway service

### Model

Not model-dependent (plugin load and steering preparation).

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-dependent.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

```shell
[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability is deprecated
[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated; use await fingerprintAsync() instead.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Isolated Gateway with Telegram configured (fake token, local API root), `--trace-deprecation`, 90 s window: 1 `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` line, from module load, while Telegram started its account.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests) shows the steering stack above: `fingerprint <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority (session-controller.message-join.ts) <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer (agent-runner-steer-adoption.ts)`.
- Across both gateways' logs since 2026-10-30: 7 `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` and 5 `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings, all labeled "Plugin telegram".

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every Gateway with the bundled Telegram plugin enabled.
- Severity: annoying. Nothing breaks today, but the warnings and the catalog notice tell operators to look for a plugin update that does not exist, since the plugin ships with OpenClaw.
- Frequency: once per Gateway start, plus once per steered Telegram run.

### Additional information

- The bundled Telegram plugin is the last caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. Every other bundled channel uses an `...Async` factory.
- Moving Telegram to the async factory alone has a side effect, filed separately: #191785.
- Related: #174937 (Discord), #190243 (same class, Matrix CLI paths).
- Also seen once, not covered here: `Plugin telegram: getMany is deprecated` from core's sync placement reads.

issues.body:
## `memory_search` hangs at 15 s when remote embedding stalls

### Summary
On the OpenClaw gateway (Linux, 2026.8.1-beta.2, observed across at least 2026.6.10–2026.9.2 with peaks on 2026-08-16, 2026-08-19, 2026-08-21, 2026-09-02), `memory_search` and the active-memory recall path occasionally hit a hard 15-second timeout that is short enough to consume the entire user-visible latency budget. The bottleneck is that the embedding client `fetch` call has no per-call timeout shorter than its embedded default (60 s for query / 120 s for batch), so a single stalled HTTP round-trip to `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` burns through the recall lane's 15 s `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` and surfaces as `MemorySearch timed out after 15s`. There is no configuration surface today to tune any of: the embedding-client per-call timeout, the embedding-client retry policy, or the recall-lane budget.

### Repro
1. Configure `memory.search.provider: "openai"` with `model: "text-embedding-3-small"`.
2. Force a slow edge on `api.openai.com` (or run behind a hanging egress proxy / DNS hang).
3. Invoke any of:
   - `memory_search` from an agent turn
   - `openclaw memory status` (which also exercises the embedding client)
   - Any active-memory recall path that triggers an embedding round-trip
4. Observe: hard failure at exactly 15 s (no retry, no fallback) and a `memory-lancedb embedding timed out` / `MemorySearch timed out after 15s` log line.

### Expected
A stalled embedding round-trip should either:
- fail fast (sub-second) and retry, **or**
- surface a recoverable "embedding provider slow" partial result instead of a hard 15 s cut-off, **or**
- be configurable via the memory-search config tree (`memory.search.remote.timeoutMs`, `memory.search.remote.retries`).

### Actual
- `EMBEDDING_QUERY_TIMEOUT_REMOTE_MS` is hardcoded at 60 s (`dist/...memory-lancedb.js`-like source). The recall lane, however, imposes `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000`. Result: when the embedding HTTP call stalls, the recall lane aborts first and the user sees a 15 s hang.
- No config key exists to tune either side. The `memory.search.remote.batch` node only exposes `enabled` (per `gateway config schema`).
- Behavior is reproducible across normal sessions and after a clean restart. Wiki corpus (`memory.search.wiki`) is unaffected.

### Suggested fix
Make the embedding client and recall lane configurable from `memory.search.remote`:
- `memory.search.remote.timeoutMs` (default 5000–8000 ms) — per-call fetch timeout for the embedding HTTP request
- `memory.search.remote.retries` (default 1) — number of retries on transient transport errors (the `RETRYABLE_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_TRANSPORT_ERROR_RE` regex in the embedding client is already in place and just needs a wrapper)
- Optionally `memory.search.remote.embeddingsBatchSize` to bound batch throughput

Additionally:
- Lower the recall lane's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` to fail fast and delegate to retry rather than burning the full budget on a single slow call, **or** raise it when a slow embedding call is detected so retry has room.

### Diagnostics already captured
- Stack: `memory_search` → remote OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` → local sqlite at `~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. No local QMD sidecar. Hindsight at `192.168.71.201:8888` is the recall sidecar (healthy).
- Symptom duration: 3–4 s normal, exactly 15 s on stall. Self-recovers per call (no persistent bad state).
- Re-enabling `memory.search.remote.batch.enabled = true` makes `openclaw memory status` itself hang at >30 s — confirms the 15 s is a layer above the embedding client and that batch-mode failures share the root cause.
- Observed in production across at least 4 distinct dates spanning 2 months.

### Workaround
None today. Schema does not expose per-call timeout or retry policy for the embedding client. Path forward for affected users is a local proxy (mitmproxy / nginx) fronting `api.openai.com` with explicit timeout + retry semantics, or an upstream patch.

issues.body:
Versions: 2026.10.7 and 2026.11.2 (same logic).

What happens
A client starts an agent run over the gateway WebSocket (`sessions.create` with `message`, or `chat.send` / `agent`). The agent makes tool calls, all succeed, and its final message is `NO_REPLY` (the caller accepts silence). The run's final assistant message in the transcript is instead:
"The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions."
The caller cannot tell this from a real answer without matching the English string, so a run that meant to stay silent reads as a completed run with odd content (or, to callers that check content, as a failure).

Why (source: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts, src/agents/reply-completion.ts)
1. Gateway-started turns resolve as reply "required": `resolveReplyExpectation` returns "optional" only for an explicit `terminalReplyExpectation`, heartbeat, `inputProvenance.kind` inter_session/internal_system, `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent`, or a trigger other than user/manual. The gateway agent attempt sets `trigger: "user"` (dist 2026.11.2 attempt-execution.runtime-*.mjs:336).
2. With "required", an explicit NO_REPLY stop after settled, error-free tools triggers the text-only settled-turn finalization (`resolveSettledToolTerminalContinuationInstruction`, allowEmptyStopContinuation). When finalization is empty twice (MAX_EMPTY_SETTLED_FINALIZATION_ATTEMPTS) or throws, and `preparedAttempt.silentExpected !== true`, the fallback text replaces the answer (2026.11.2 embedded-agent-*.mjs:7463 and :7518; 2026.10.7 :7338 and :7392). Native cron runs get `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` here (`runParams.trigger === "cron"`) and also run with `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional"`; gateway-started runs get the English text.
3. There is no supported way for a gateway client to say the reply is optional:
   - `SessionsCreateParamsSchema`, `AgentParamsSchema`, `ChatSendParamsSchema` and `sessions.patch` are closed and carry no reply-expectation field (packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-create.ts and siblings).
   - `silentExpected` is internal only (memory flush, experience review, recall) and also suppresses all visible output.
   - The in-process gateway path carries `replyExpectation`, but it is stripped before WebSocket transport (2026.11.2 in-process-gateway-*.mjs:136).
   - `agents.defaults.silentReply.group` applies to group chats; gateway chat is direct.
   - The only reachable lever is claiming `systemInputProvenance` / `inputProvenance` kind internal_system or inter_session, which is admin-only and changes how the turn is recorded and shown (system actor, "Internal system input", run-wait transcript-artifact filtering, skill selection). That is a provenance claim, not a reply policy, and not something a client should fake.

Repro
1. Over the gateway WS: `sessions.create { agentId, label, message: "<prompt that calls a tool and then answers NO_REPLY when there is nothing to report>" }`.
2. Agent runs one or more tools without error, final message `NO_REPLY`.
3. `sessions.get`: the last assistant message is the fallback text, with `__openclaw.idempotencyKey` = `<runId>:settled-finalization-fallback`.

Ask (any one would do)
A. A per-run reply expectation on the gateway API: e.g. `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional" | "required"` on `sessions.create` (initial turn), `chat.send` and `agent`, with the same semantics native cron gets (empty / NO_REPLY is a silent completion, no settled-turn fallback text).
B. Or: when a run's final assistant turn is an explicit NO_REPLY after settled tools, use `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` as the fallback for every trigger, not only cron (the cron branch already shows the intent).
C. In any case: a documented, stable marker that a final message is the synthesized fallback (today only the `:settled-finalization-fallback` idempotency-key suffix, which is an implementation detail), so clients can tell "agent produced no final answer" from a real answer without matching English text.

Related: #174620 (closed: optional turns now complete silently; this issue is that a gateway client cannot make a run optional), #188984 (same resolution problem for unmentioned group turns).
