issues.body:
## Current proposal and maintainer decision

This scope incorporates the later [author clarification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140213#issuecomment-5933164327) and [decision packet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140213#issuecomment-6345732181). It supersedes the original additive-CLI and durable-reference requirements retained below. Maintainer sponsorship and the choices below remain open.

Retain the existing primary/display `alias` and permit ordered secondary `aliases` as lookup names for one configured model, using existing resolution and collision rules. Secondary-only sets remain part of the proposed decision packet; they are not approved semantics.

- Preserve ordinary `models aliases add` replacement behavior; make secondary append explicit.
- Treat inherited primary and secondary aliases as one set, resolved before building the alias index. Unrelated parameter writes preserve the set.
- Removing the primary promotes the first remaining secondary deterministically.
- Preserve existing provider scope, case folding, collision precedence, configured-ID priority, and persistence timing.
- Saved-session migration, Automation round-trip guarantees and late-bound durable-reference retargeting are outside this slice. `modelPolicy.allow` is unchanged.

**Decision requested:** would a maintainer sponsor this bounded feature? Recommended defaults are that either authored alias field replaces the inherited set, `{aliases: []}` explicitly clears it, and removing the final name preserves suppression rather than reviving inherited/built-in aliases. These are proposals, not approved semantics; the linked decision packet records the remaining edge combinations and compatibility checks.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal retained for history — superseded scope</summary>

### Summary

Allow several stable semantic aliases to resolve to one configured provider/model while retaining the existing single `alias` field as the primary/display alias.

### Problem

Some multi-agent operators use model aliases as a policy API rather than as cosmetic shorthands. Roles such as `core_model`, `email_critical_model`, and `analysis_model` may intentionally target the same concrete model. This lets the operator hot-swap the implementation for several policy roles centrally without rewriting every agent, Automation/cron job, and session policy.

Today `AgentModelEntryConfig` exposes one `alias?: string`, the CLI replaces that alias when another is added for the same canonical model key, and the resolver reverse index stores one alias per key. The catalog cannot duplicate a provider/model under multiple keys because that provider/model is itself the map key.

### Proposed backward-compatible configuration

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      models: {
        "openai/example-model": {
          alias: "core_model",
          aliases: ["email_critical_model", "analysis_model"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Keep `alias` as the primary/display alias and add optional `aliases: string[]`. Existing configurations remain valid.

### Expected behavior

- Schema and types accept `aliases` and validate each entry using the existing alias rules.
- Resolver indexes primary and secondary aliases with the same case-folding, collision, provider-qualified, and precedence behavior as current aliases.
- `models aliases list` shows every configured alias.
- `models aliases add` appends a secondary alias when the target already has a different primary alias.
- `models aliases remove` removes either kind. Removing the primary promotes one secondary alias deterministically.
- Provider onboarding and unrelated configuration writes preserve the full alias set.
- Prompt/model-picker presentation can expose all applicable aliases.
- Agent, Automation/cron, and session configuration round-trips retain semantic alias strings rather than canonicalizing policy references to concrete model IDs.
- This does not change `modelPolicy.allow`; aliases remain metadata/resolution policy, not allowlist entries.

### Operational impact

Without this, a fleet hot-swap requires rewriting many durable records or collapsing distinct policy roles into one name. Partial rewrites can leave different agents and scheduled jobs on different concrete models while all configuration remains syntactically valid.

### Evidence and prior art

We have carried this backward-compatible behavior locally across OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2, 2026.8.1, 2026.9.1, and 2026.9.2. Tests cover:

- three semantic aliases resolving to one provider/model;
- the reverse index retaining all three aliases;
- CLI list/add/remove and primary promotion;
- configuration validation;
- provider-onboarding preservation;
- an Automation model reference surviving an unrelated read/write round-trip unchanged.

The current `main` branch was checked at `f5f1aaeb8027430e8e19054e4a4fe3f17b9d7d33`: `AgentModelEntryConfig` still has singular `alias?: string`, and the alias CLI and resolver operate on one alias per canonical model key.

### Likely implementation surfaces

- `src/config/types.agent-defaults.ts` and the corresponding Zod model-entry schema
- `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts`
- `src/commands/models/aliases.ts`
- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-onboard.ts`
- `src/agents/system-prompt-config.ts`

This is related to alias mutation/collision issue #127619, but distinct: that issue concerns several model entries sharing one alias identity; this request concerns one model entry intentionally exposing several alias identities.

### Alternatives considered

- Store concrete IDs in every agent/job: defeats central policy hot-swapping.
- Use one generic alias for all roles: loses semantic intent and prevents later role differentiation.
- Duplicate the same model in the catalog: impossible with canonical provider/model map keys.


</details>

issues.body:
### Summary

On a stock 2026.11.6 install the background Skill Workshop experience review never completes. Every run dies with `context_length_exceeded`, because the conversation excerpt budget is larger than the fixed context budget the review runs with.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (`06afb10d327`, tag `v2026.11.6`)
- Linux x64, Node 24.22.1
- Provider/model: `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
- 45 learned Workshop skills on the agent

### Observed

12 review runs in 7 days: 10 ended with `isError=true`, 0 completed successfully.

```
[provider-error] Model request failed sessionKey="agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review_..." provider=openrouter model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 name=Error code=context_length_exceeded
[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=skill-workshop-review:... isError=true failoverReason=context_overflow
[context-overflow-diag] ... error=Context window exceeded: estimated input 14409 leaves only 1974 output tokens within the 16384-token context.
```

### Root cause

Two constants inside the same feature disagree:

| Location | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `src/skills/workshop/review-run.ts:80` | `contextTokenBudget: 16_384` |
| `src/skills/workshop/review-run.ts:81` | `streamParams: { maxTokens: 2_048 }` |
| `src/skills/workshop/experience-review.ts:146` | `limits: { maxBytes: 32_768, maxEvents: 64, toolResultOverflow: "omit" }` |

A 32 KiB transcript excerpt is roughly 8-10k tokens. Add the review prompt, the authoring-standards prompt, the system prompt and the tool definitions, and the estimated input lands at ~14.4k tokens. With a 16,384 budget and 2,048 reserved for output there is nothing left, so the request is rejected before it can produce anything.

The excerpt budget is sized for a large context window; the run budget is sized for a cheap background call. Neither is wrong on its own, but the combination fails on ordinary sessions - this is not limited to oversized transcripts (#150238).

### Impact

Autonomous learning never runs on this install. Skills only change through explicit `skill_workshop` calls, so the "learn from experience" path is effectively dead while the failure is only visible as a `warn` line in the journal.

### Workaround

Raising `contextTokenBudget` to `65_536` in `dist/experience-review-*.mjs` lets the review complete. That is a local dist patch and is lost on every update.

### Related

- #194300 - configurable model, thinking level and token budget for background reviews (the fixed values come from #173889)
- #150238 - context budget / skip policy for oversized sessions

### Suggested fix

Either derive the excerpt budget from `contextTokenBudget` (remaining budget after prompt and tool overhead), or raise the default budget so the current excerpt fits. A preflight check that skips the review with one clear log line would also beat a provider error on every turn.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a runtime-enforced checkpoint policy for long foreground agent runs so that, after a configurable silent-time or tool-call budget, OpenClaw publishes a meaningful status update and cleanly yields before more work is dispatched.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw can stream tool activity and models can be instructed to send commentary during multi-step work. Neither mechanism guarantees that a direct foreground WebChat run will stop at a user-defined checkpoint.

In repeated real-world maintenance workflows, an agent was given explicit workspace instructions to:

- publish a user-facing status update at least every 30–45 seconds;
- stop after a small number of tool calls;
- report the verified state and exact next step before continuing.

The model sometimes followed those rules, but it also repeatedly continued with “one more check” and exceeded the intended stage boundary. One such run eventually ended with a timeout/abort before a final handoff. This is not primarily a tool failure: the missing control is a runtime-owned boundary around the *foreground agent loop*.

Current facilities solve adjacent problems but not this one:

- progress streaming shows activity but does not enforce a semantic checkpoint or yield;
- queue steering allows new user input at model boundaries but does not create a boundary on a quiet run;
- per-tool timeouts bound individual calls, not the number or duration of successive calls;
- the overall turn timeout aborts late and may provide no clean last-known-state handoff;
- TaskFlow provides durable background orchestration, but ordinary interactive WebChat work still runs as one foreground turn unless explicitly moved into a task flow;
- prompt or `AGENTS.md` rules remain model-behavior constraints and are therefore not reliable enforcement.

This makes users uncertain whether the agent is progressing, drifting into unrelated checks, or stuck. It also forces them to supervise or manually interrupt work that should be safely bounded.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Configure workspace instructions requiring a visible status every 30–45 seconds and a stop after a fixed number of tool calls.
2. Start a direct WebChat request that needs several diagnostic or implementation calls.
3. Observe that the agent may emit an initial preamble but continue beyond the requested time/tool budget.
4. The UI can show low-level activity, but there is no runtime guarantee of a concise checkpoint containing verified state, meaning, and next action.
5. If the foreground run later times out or is aborted, the user may receive no controlled yield or durable continuation point.

Because model behavior is nondeterministic, the exact number of calls varies. The reproducible architectural fact is that OpenClaw currently has no configurable foreground-loop checkpoint enforcement; compliance depends on the model following instructions.

## Proposed solution

Introduce an opt-in, runtime-owned checkpoint policy for foreground agent runs, with agent defaults and optional channel/session overrides. An illustrative shape could be:

```yaml
agents:
  defaults:
    foregroundCheckpoints:
      enabled: true
      maxSilentMs: 30000
      maxToolCalls: 4
      action: checkpoint-and-yield
```

The exact schema is only a suggestion. The behavioral contract is more important:

1. Track elapsed time since the last user-visible semantic update and the number of completed tool calls since that update.
2. When either budget is reached, do not dispatch another tool call.
3. At the next safe model boundary, require a compact checkpoint with:
   - the current phase;
   - the last verified state;
   - the meaning or risk;
   - the exact next step;
   - whether user approval is required.
4. Publish that checkpoint to the originating WebChat and persist enough continuation metadata to resume safely.
5. End/yield the foreground turn cleanly. A later user message or explicit continuation mechanism starts the next bounded stage.
6. If the model does not produce the checkpoint within a short grace period, emit a deterministic fallback status from runtime-known data and end the turn safely.

Safety constraints:

- Never cancel an in-flight tool solely because the checkpoint budget elapsed; enforce the boundary after the tool settles.
- Preserve existing per-tool timeout and abort semantics.
- Do not expose raw tool output, secrets, private paths, or hidden reasoning in the fallback status.
- Keep the feature opt-in and backward-compatible.
- Allow `status-only` as an alternative action for users who want periodic checkpoints without yielding.

## Alternatives considered

### Prompt or workspace instructions

This is the current workaround. It is useful guidance but cannot serve as enforcement because the same model that performs the work decides whether to stop.

### Existing progress streaming

Progress drafts improve visibility, but tool names or activity receipts do not provide a guaranteed semantic checkpoint or prevent another tool call from starting.

### Shorter overall turn timeout

A hard timeout limits total duration but terminates at the wrong abstraction level. It can interrupt useful work and does not guarantee a clean status, persisted checkpoint, or safe continuation.

### Per-tool timeouts

These protect individual tool calls. They do not bound a long chain of individually successful calls or extended model analysis between calls.

### TaskFlow/background tasks

TaskFlow is appropriate for work deliberately started as a durable background workflow. Requiring every non-trivial interactive request to be manually converted into TaskFlow leaves the common foreground WebChat path unprotected.

## Impact

- **Affected users:** operators using WebChat or another interactive channel for multi-step administration, coding, research, or maintenance.
- **Severity:** medium to high for consequential work; an uncontrolled long turn can waste time, increase risk, and erode operator trust even when individual tools are safe.
- **Frequency:** intermittent and model-dependent, which makes instruction-only mitigation difficult to validate.
- **Practical consequences:** repeated manual supervision, avoidable interrupts, lost handoff context after timeouts, unnecessary tool calls, and delayed work on other priorities.

This is especially relevant to service-first and approval-gated deployments where the operator expects short, understandable stages and must remain in control.

## Evidence/examples

Related issues cover important adjacent capabilities:

- #13207 — streaming progress and mid-run injection; its original report explicitly noted that manual checkpoint messages are behavioral/unreliable. It was later closed because streaming and queue steering shipped.
- #45522 — durable long-running orchestration and progress; closed after TaskFlow shipped.
- #100388 — WebChat compaction progress and diagnostics.
- #103461 — narrated agent status updates and activity receipts.
- #105622 — bounded tool execution and abort signals.
- #83966 — configurable timeout metadata for Codex plugin runtime tools.

None of these defines a runtime-enforced *foreground agent-loop* checkpoint based on silent time or completed-tool count, followed by a controlled yield and durable handoff.

Test environment where the gap was observed:

- OpenClaw `2026.8.2`
- Control UI / WebChat
- OpenAI Codex runtime
- multi-step maintenance and diagnostic workflows

No private infrastructure details or credentials are needed to reproduce the architectural gap.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

This request is not asking OpenClaw to expose hidden reasoning or raw logs. The desired output is a small, redacted operational checkpoint. It also does not replace TaskFlow; it provides a safe bridge between ordinary foreground conversation and work that should be promoted into durable background orchestration.

### Summary

The Control UI binds **Ctrl+Shift+A** (Windows/Linux) / **⌘⇧A** (macOS) to "Archive current chat" (docs: `web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md`, "Direct session shortcuts"). The chord collides with browser shortcuts, and it can't be disabled or remapped.

### What happens

On OpenClaw 2026.9.7, Control UI in Chrome on Windows: pressing Ctrl+Shift+A to open Chrome's tab search archives the current chat instead. Undo exists, but users who rely on the browser shortcut keep archiving chats by accident. In one case the chat was archived in the middle of a long-running agent task.

The docs already acknowledge this: "If your browser handles a chord itself, use the corresponding New Session control or Archive in the current chat's header menu." But when the page handles the chord first, the user loses the browser feature on that tab.

### Who else is likely affected (not verified for each)

- Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi), where this chord is commonly tab search.
- Firefox, which I believe uses Ctrl+Shift+A for the Add-ons Manager.
- Keyboard-heavy users in general, because Archive is a state-changing action on a chord that's easy to press by habit.

### Proposed

1. A setting to disable or remap the direct session shortcuts (Archive and New Session), e.g. in Control UI settings next to the side-panel shortcuts.
2. A default for Archive that doesn't collide with common browser chords. Alternatively, have the Archive shortcut need a confirmation, or only work while the chat header menu is open (the menu's existing **A** key already covers that case).

_Agent-written (Leviathan, an OpenClaw agent) on behalf of @MattFaus._

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Show the agent that ran the task on the task progress card

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (current release), Control UI (webchat) on Windows
- Card behavior verified against main source: the meta line is built in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-background-task-row.ts` (`renderTaskMeta`), strings in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-background-tasks.ts`

## Observed

The task progress card (and the Background tasks rail) renders: status label, runtime kind ("Subagent"), elapsed time / finished duration, relative time, tool-use count, current/last tool, delivery state, and the final summary. Nowhere does the card identify WHICH configured agent executed the task.

On gateways with several configured agents (a main agent plus dedicated subagent-type agents), every card looks identical, so attributing a finished run requires opening the task detail or cross-referencing the session list. Cards from different agents are indistinguishable at a glance.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a gateway with two or more agents.
2. Run a background/subagent task from each agent.
3. Compare the task cards in the chat view / Background tasks rail: the metadata line contains no agent identity for either run.

## Expected

The card's meta line (or a small badge/subtitle near the title) includes the agent that ran the task, e.g.:

`Completed · Subagent · <agentId> · 28m 38s · 34 tool uses`

## Suggested fix

`renderTaskMeta()` already receives the full task record, so this is a low-cost addition:

- If `TaskSummary` already carries the owning agent identity, render one more `<span>` in the meta line.
- If it does not, include the agent id (and/or session label) in the background-task payload the gateway sends, then render it and add the locale string (`en-background-tasks.ts` currently has no agent-related string).

Since the chat card and the Background tasks rail share the same strings and row renderer, one change covers both surfaces.

## Related

- Duplicate sweep done (issues + merged PRs, several phrasings): no existing request adds agent identity to cards. Closest threads are card finalization/visibility bugs (#147938, #142189) and UI polish PRs (#150881, #130183) — none touch agent attribution.

issues.body:
Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) shim as generated by the npm global install on Windows 11 x64; end-to-end failure originally observed 2026-09-08 on a 2026.8.x build; shim mechanism re-verified against the current install today.

Observed: multiline string arguments passed through the generated openclaw.cmd shim lose everything after the first line. The shim ends by re-invoking node with `%*` behind an `endLocal & goto #_undefined_# 2>NUL || ...` construction; the cmd batch parser cannot carry embedded newlines through that re-expansion, so a call like `openclaw.cmd ... --message "line1<newline>line2"` reaches openclaw.mjs as `--message "line1`. Demonstrated today with a batch file of identical construction: the child received only `ARGS=[--message "first line]`.

Consequence: any CLI flow that passes a multiline payload (for example --message into send/agent commands) silently truncates on Windows when invoked through the shim. The same call via `node openclaw.mjs` or the PowerShell shim carries the full text; that is our workaround. Secondary observation from the original incident: the shim surface also emitted CLIXML/XML-parse noise on the error stream under some invocation contexts (not re-chased).

Suggested fix: generate the Windows shim to route through PowerShell, or otherwise avoid cmd `%*` re-expansion for multiline arguments; alternatively document that multiline CLI payloads must go via node/openclaw.ps1 on Windows.

Related: #150974 (same generated shim, different failure: UTF-8 non-ASCII path on GBK consoles), #140631 (CLIXML noise in the PowerShell exec host).

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows 11 x64, Node v26.8.2. Observed 2026-09-26; reproduced live the same day.

Observed: a workshop SKILL.md whose description frontmatter was a multi-line plain scalar (continuation lines starting at column 0) caused the skill to be skipped entirely: `openclaw skills info <name>` reported "not found", the curator inventory undercounted (67 loaded vs 68 SKILL.md files on disk), and no warning appeared on any user-facing surface we checked (skills list, skills info, skills check, curator status). Rewriting the description to a single line, same text, made the skill load immediately with no other change.

Steps to reproduce (verified on 2026.9.6):
1. Create a throwaway skill directory in a per-agent workshop skills directory containing a SKILL.md whose frontmatter is:

   ---
   name: repro-skip-test
   description: First line of a plain scalar description
   continued at column zero which breaks strict YAML parsing
   ---

2. Wait for the skill watcher to register the change.
3. `openclaw skills info repro-skip-test --agent <agentId>` returns "not found". No warning is printed anywhere.
4. A known-good control skill in the same directory loads fine, so discovery itself works; the failure is specific to the frontmatter shape.

Context: #108432 (fixed by #108926, landed 2026-07-16) established that genuinely malformed frontmatter should warn with the file path and parse error instead of silently hiding the skill. On 2026.9.6 this shape produced a fully silent skip on every surface available to a user, so either the fix does not cover this frontmatter shape/loading path, or the warning exists internally but is not surfaced.

Suggested fix: cover multi-line plain scalars (and any YAML syntax error) on all loading paths, and surface the promised file-path + parse-error warning on every surface that reports skill inventory, including skills info/check and the curator inventory count (which currently undercounts silently).

issues.body:
After #203271, an install with no configured model rejects every chat message except `/model <provider/model>` with "No model is configured. Choose one in Settings → Models, send `/model <provider/model>` in chat, or run `openclaw models set <provider/model>`." The reply pipeline assumes a model before it reaches command handling, so model-independent commands do not run until a model is chosen.

Gaps until this is fixed:

- **Model discovery:** a chat-only user cannot list valid `provider/model` ids, because `/models` does not run.
- **`/new`:** it does not reset the session on an unconfigured install.
- **`/help`:** it returns the setup message instead of the command list.
- **`/status`:** it returns the setup message instead of the status card (which would say the model is not configured).

Fix: let the reply pipeline (`resolveReplyDirectives` → model selection state → inline actions → command handlers) carry "no model" so control commands run, and reject only when inference starts. No placeholder model.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), Control UI (webchat), macOS gateway, agent runtime claude-cli. Observed on the release; current `main` not checked.

## What happens
After an in-place reset (`/clear` / `/reset`, `sessions.reset`) of a dashboard session, the transcript shows the
"Session reset – the previous conversation was cleared" divider, but **above it** these items stay visible:

1. Answered `ask_user` question cards (question + selected answer) from before the reset
2. `SYSTEM` notices "Session observer assessments stopped for this run after utility model "…" failed repeatedly"
   (one per old run)

## Expected
Everything from before the reset is gone (as with ordinary messages), or at least these rows are not rendered above
the divider of a cleared conversation.

## Evidence that it is client-only state
- `chat.history` for the session right after the reset returns only `{role:"system", __openclaw.kind:"reset"}` and the
  new user message; no question or observer rows.
- `question.list` returns `{"questions": []}`.
- So the rows come from the browser's cached `question.requested`/`question.resolved` and `session.observer` events,
  which the reset does not retire (cancelled pending inputs had the same problem in 2026.11.5; there,
  `chat.pendingInputs.dismiss` was a workable workaround).

## Repro
1. In a dashboard session, let the agent ask an `ask_user` question and answer it.
2. Use a failing `agents.defaults.utilityModel` so the observer notice appears.
3. Run `/reset` (or Clear) in the same browser tab.
4. Old question cards and observer notices remain above the reset divider. A page reload removes them.

## Suggested fix
On the reset event for a session, drop client-side question and observer-notice state whose timestamp is before
the reset marker (same rule as for history messages).

issues.body:
**Version:** first seen on openclaw 2026.10.6, still reproducing on 2026.10.8 (2026-11-04: abort at 03:06:34 with age=379s, `dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=18 ...)` at 03:07:10, run status=ok, 434s). Same code in 2026.10.10 (latest) and 2026.11.5-beta.1: no progress calls in `dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js`, `DEFAULT_STUCK_SESSION_WARN_MS = 12e4` unchanged. Linux arm64, 16-18 dreaming workspaces.

**What happens**

The built-in "Memory Dreaming Promotion" cron runs `runShortTermDreamingPromotion` as an embedded run. It loops over every workspace in a plain `for (const { agentId, agentIds, workspaceDir } of workspaces)` loop (extensions/memory-core/index.js, ~L245-252). Each workspace takes about 15-25s, so with 16-18 workspaces the whole run takes 6-9 minutes.

The loop never calls `markDiagnosticRunProgress` / `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` / `emitCoreSemanticRunProgress`, so `lastProgress` stays at `embedded_run:started`. The stuck-session watchdog then:
- logs `stalled session ... classification=stalled_agent_run reason=active_work_without_progress` every 30s from about 120s on
- fires `action=abort_embedded_run` ("stuck session recovery") at about 360-383s (abort = max(300s, 3 x 120s warn))

The abort doesn't stop the plugin work. The loop keeps going and logs `dreaming promotion complete` 1-3 minutes after the abort, and diary files are written after that. The cron run record ends `status=ok`.

**Evidence (4 nights in a row, same every night, not tied to memory pressure)**
- 10/27: abort 03:06:32, complete 03:09:24
- 10/28: abort 03:06:40, complete 03:08:45
- 10/29: abort 03:06:23, complete 03:07:54
- 10/30: complete 03:06:10, 7ms before the abort would have fired
- Run durations over the last 5 nights: 371-564s, all status=ok. Output checked on disk: every workspace got its REM entry every night (144/144).
- Same pattern right after a fresh gateway restart at low RSS (~6.5 GiB, no heap warnings).

**Why it matters**
- Nightly false "stalled" / "aborted" log noise in any multi-agent install sends operators looking for a hang that isn't there.
- An abort that reports success but doesn't cancel the work is misleading. If the work ever really hung, recovery wouldn't free it.
- There's no workaround: `diagnostics.stuckSessionWarnMs` / `stuckSessionAbortMs` are retired (RETIRED_TUNING_PATHS), and cron `timeoutSeconds` doesn't feed the watchdog.

**Suggested fix**
1. In the dreaming promotion loop, report run progress once per workspace (and per phase), so the stall timer resets while real work is happening. This is the main fix.
2. Make `abort_embedded_run` pass an AbortSignal into plugin-hook embedded runs, and have the dreaming loop check it between workspaces, so an abort actually stops the work. Or, if a run can't be cancelled, don't log it as aborted.
3. Optional: let a cron/embedded-run declare an expected duration or stall budget, as asked for in #140401.

**Repro**
Multi-agent setup with dreaming enabled for 15 or more workspaces, then wait for the nightly promotion run. `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway | grep -E "Memory Dreaming Promotion|dreaming promotion complete|abort_embedded_run"`.

**Related (not duplicates):** #140401 (closed: watchdog threshold no longer configurable), #191822 (compaction not counted as progress), #171366 (Code Mode awaitResults aborted), #143396.

issues.body:
### Summary

`view_image` can't read images that a claude-cli agent saves in its own scratchpad directory.

### Problem to solve

On the claude-cli runtime, Claude Code gives the agent a scratchpad directory (`/tmp/claude-<uid>/<project>/<session>/scratchpad`) and tells it to put temporary files there. So that's where its screenshots land. `view_image` then refuses them with "Local media path is not under an allowed directory", and the agent has to copy the file somewhere else or fall back to Claude Code's own Read tool.

In my logs that refusal was 48 of 262 `view_image` calls (18%) over a week.

The allowed roots come from `buildMediaLocalRoots()` in `src/media/local-roots.ts` (tmp dir, media, state media, canvas, workspace, sandboxes) plus the agent workspace, and `readOnlyRoots` is only filled in for attachments. The scratchpad is none of those.

### Proposed solution

Either of these, whichever fits better:
- Add the claude-cli session's scratchpad to the media roots for that session only (the runtime already knows the session's path).
- Or a config list such as `tools.media.extraLocalRoots`, for directories an operator trusts.

### Alternatives considered

`tools.fs.workspaceOnly: false` does make `view_image` accept any absolute path (`hostReadRoot` in `media-tool-shared.ts`), but it opens every host file to the file tools, which is much broader than "let me look at my own screenshots". Pointing the agent at a directory under the workspace works, but it relies on the agent obeying a prompt instead of Claude Code's own scratchpad instruction.

### Impact

Every claude-cli agent that takes a screenshot and looks at it.

### Evidence/examples

Repro: on the claude-cli runtime, have the agent save any PNG into the scratchpad path from its system prompt, then call `view_image` on it. The refusal above comes back.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Happy to, once you say which of the two shapes you prefer.

### Additional information

OpenClaw 2026.10.5, claude-cli runtime, Linux. Checked against current main (cd3bcc0). Related but different: #47002 (config validator rejecting `mediaLocalRoots` for Telegram outbound media).

issues.body:
## Summary

On one node, every automatic update campaign since 2026-11-03 fails with `managed-service-stop-failed` ("Gateway process changed during maintenance drain"). The Gateway keeps serving fine the whole time, so the streak just retries every ~2 hours and has accumulated ~330 failed runs, each costing ~10 minutes (validating + canary + verify) with ~1.9 GiB snapshot + a fresh retained updater runtime each time (`/home/openclaw/.npm-global/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-*`).

## Details

- OpenClaw 2026.10.9 → target 2026.10.10 (Nov 3–5), then 2026.11.6 (Nov 5 → today). Same error each time.
- Trigger: automatic campaign, npm-global install, systemd **user** unit (`openclaw-gateway.service`, user-scope session bus).
- Platform: Linux x64 (Ubuntu-style, kernel 7.0.0-42), Node v24.22.2 for CLI, `/usr/local/bin/node` 24.21.0 in the unit's `ExecStart`.
- Failure JSON (saved): reason `managed-service-stop-failed`, recovery `{serviceRestartSafe: true, version: "2026.10.9"}`, failing step stderr: `Failed to stop managed gateway service before update: Error: Gateway process changed during maintenance drain`.

## Why I think it's a bug, not node-specific damage

- The unit is stable: `NRestarts=0`, `ExecMainStartTimestamp` unchanged for 14+ days, MainPID constant (1156) across repeated reads (tested 2 s apart via `systemctl --user show`).
- `openclaw gateway status --deep` is clean and connectivity OK; Telegram/agents continue serving during and between campaigns.
- Failure repeats deterministically at every campaign (~2 h), for two different target versions (2026.10.10 and 2026.11.6).
- One anomaly I can observe: the unit's cgroup holds **two** long-running gateway processes (PID 1156, `/usr/local/bin/node`, and PID 1439, `.openclaw/tools/cli-node/tools/node-v24.22.2/bin/node`, both running `index.js gateway --port 18789`, journal logs come from `node[1439]` while `MainPID=1156`). That is pre-existing, but may make whichever PID the updater reads during maintenance drain flip.

## Evidence

- `update_runs` history: 442 failed (first failure 2026-09-06, steady streak since 2026-11-03 14:07), 6 succeeded (last success 2026-10-31 15:58, also to 2026.10.9 — that same-day success shows the stop path can work on this node).
- Failed phase timeline of a representative run: requested 84.7 s → validating 382.5 s → previous gateway verification 22.2 s → activating 174.1 s → `managed-service-stop-failed`.
- Handoff log ends with `managed update update command exited code=1` + `recovery not attempted: no verified recovery result`, then the finalize step succeeds and the campaign ends; `auto-update deferred (recent attempt exists)` on the next check.

## Expected

Either the drain/stop retry tolerates the observed PID read (e.g. re-read both pids after the drain and re-validate identity before aborting), or the campaign backs off further after repeated identical failures instead of retrying every ~2 h for weeks.

Happy to run `openclaw triage -like` diagnostics or provide more artifacts (sanitized failure JSON, journal excerpts) if useful.

issues.body:
[PR #188973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188973) proposes a fix for this. I'm reporting the incident here so the issue and the proposed fix can be reviewed together.

### What happened

After one reboot, two separate client profiles on my Mac stopped working with this error:

```text
Client credential migration is incomplete or stale; run openclaw doctor --fix before using this client.
```

The filesystem device number changed from `16777232` to `16777229`. The shared database stayed at the same path and kept the same inode.

Checking the installed readiness guard showed that the recorded old device number was rejected. The same record, with only the device number changed to the current value, was admitted.

This is a Homebrew/npm global install (OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d44f263) on macOS 27.2). Running the following manually fixed both affected profiles:

```sh
openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix
```

Current startup code can try a Doctor repair automatically. On this install, it did not recover until Doctor was run by hand.

### What still happens on main

The device-number-only rejection was reproduced against main at [`1d9252c3770e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1d9252c3770e96372192b650601583134617296e), using the production TypeScript guard with an in-memory credential database and simulated filesystem metadata.

With path and inode held constant:

- Recorded device `16777232`, current device `16777229`: rejected.
- Recorded and current device both `16777229`: admitted.

Both read-only and writable admission behaved this way. Separate checks confirmed that a changed path, changed inode, or incomplete migration was still rejected.

This was a controlled guard reproduction on Linux, not another macOS reboot or a full client startup test.

### Where the check lives

[`prepareClientCredentialReceipt()` in `src/infra/client-credential-readiness.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d9252c3770e96372192b650601583134617296e/src/infra/client-credential-readiness.ts#L261-L271) rejects a mismatch in any of the recorded path, device number, or inode.

The compared file is the shared `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Its file identity is recorded inside the local `client/credentials.sqlite`.

The [Swift readiness check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d9252c3770e96372192b650601583134617296e/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawNativeState/ClientCredentialReceipt.swift#L147-L167) also compares the complete file identity. That code was inspected but not executed.

### Expected behavior

A reboot that only renumbers the volume should not make unchanged client credentials require migration again. Clients should keep working without manual repair, while genuine database replacement and incomplete migration should still be caught.

issues.title: [Bug]: skill loader substitutes invocation arguments for literal $0/$1/$2 in SKILL.md body text — silently corrupts dollar amounts, regexes and code samples with no diagnostic

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.4`
- Node 24, Linux
- Agent runtime: Claude CLI
- Skill invoked via the `Skill` tool with an `args` string
- Skill source is a plain `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter, loaded from a plugin skills directory

## What happened

A skill was invoked with an `args` string whose first whitespace-delimited token was a single capitalized word — call it `Acme`.

That skill's `SKILL.md` contains this line verbatim on disk:

```markdown
All scrapers priced at $0.0025/record under "collect by URL" API.
```

The text delivered into the model's context read:

```markdown
All scrapers priced at Acme.0025/record under "collect by URL" API.
```

The literal `$0` was replaced by the first token of the invocation argument. The `.0025/record` remainder was left intact, which is what makes it so easy to miss — the sentence still parses as English and still looks like a price.

The on-disk file was never modified. Verified afterwards:

```bash
grep -n '0025/record' <skill-dir>/SKILL.md
# 284:Fire all applicable scrapers **in parallel** ... All scrapers priced at $0.0025/record under "collect by URL" API.
```

So the corruption happens during load/render, not on disk.

## Expected

`SKILL.md` body text is instruction content and should be delivered to the model byte-for-byte. If argument interpolation into skill bodies is an intended feature, it should use an explicit, escapable placeholder syntax that cannot collide with ordinary prose — and `$0`, `$1`, `$2` are very much ordinary prose in technical documentation.

## Actual

Shell-style positional parameters appearing anywhere in the body are expanded against the invocation arguments.

## Inferred mechanism (not verified against source)

The corruption shape — `$0` → first whitespace-delimited token of `args`, with surrounding characters untouched — is consistent with the skill body being passed through shell-style parameter expansion with the argument string bound as positional parameters. I have not read the loader source to confirm which code path does this, so treat the mechanism as a hypothesis and the observation as fact.

## Why this is worse than a cosmetic glitch

1. **It is silent.** No warning at any log level. The reader has no way to know the instruction text they are acting on differs from the instruction text on disk.
2. **It corrupts the exact tokens that matter.** `$0`, `$1`, `$2` appear in: dollar amounts (`$0.0025`, `$0.50`), shell examples (`$0` for script name, `$1` for first argument — extremely common in documentation *about* scripts), `awk`/`sed`/`perl` snippets (`$0` = whole record, `$1` = first field), regex backreferences, and price tables.
3. **It can flip a factual claim without breaking syntax.** A per-record price of `$0.0025` becoming `Acme.0025` is noticeable. A cost threshold of `$0.50` becoming `Acme.50`, or an `awk '{print $1}'` becoming `awk '{print Acme}'`, is the kind of thing a model will act on.
4. **Skills are instruction surfaces.** If a safety rule, a spend threshold, or a command template in a skill contains a `$0`, the delivered rule is not the authored rule.

## Reproduction

1. Create a skill whose `SKILL.md` body contains a line with a literal `$0`, e.g.:
   ```markdown
   Records are billed at $0.0025 each. Use `awk '{print $1}'` to extract the id.
   ```
2. Invoke it through the `Skill` tool with a non-empty `args` string whose first token is a recognizable word.
3. Compare the rendered skill text in context against the file on disk.

Expected: identical. Observed: `$0` replaced by the first argument token; `$1` likewise.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these would resolve it:

- Do not expand shell-style parameters in skill body text at all. Pass `args` to the model as a separate, clearly delimited field (which already appears to happen — the invocation arguments were *also* delivered verbatim in a trailing `ARGUMENTS:` block, so body interpolation looks redundant).
- If body interpolation is intended, require an explicit non-shell placeholder (`{{args}}`, `${SKILL_ARGS}`) and leave bare `$0`/`$1` untouched.
- At minimum, log a warning when interpolation modifies the body, naming the skill and the substituted tokens, so the corruption is detectable.

## Impact in the reporting deployment

Caught by chance while exporting a skill's text for reuse elsewhere — the on-disk copy and the loaded copy disagreed. One price literal was affected in that skill. The deployment runs roughly 60 local skills, several of which document shell and `awk` one-liners, so the blast radius is wider than the single instance observed. No incorrect action was taken as a result of this particular corruption; it was noticed before it mattered. That was luck, not detection.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Updating 2026.11.4 to 2026.11.6 on macOS arm64, `openclaw doctor --fix` refuses at `plugin-doctor-post-session-state` with `Cannot find native binding`, because the published `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.6 packages contain only the linux-x64-gnu LanceDB binding.

### Steps to reproduce

1. macOS arm64 host on OpenClaw 2026.11.4 with `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` installed and owning the memory slot.
2. `npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.6`, stop the Gateway, run `openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive`.
3. Doctor converges the plugin to 2026.11.6, then stops at the plugin session repair step.

The packaging can be checked without an update:

```sh
npm view @openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.6 dist.unpackedSize bundleDependencies --json
# about 245 MB, 10 bundled packages: the seven @lancedb/lancedb-* packages, apache-arrow, openai, typebox
npm view @openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.4 dist.unpackedSize bundleDependencies --json
# about 0.5 MB, no bundleDependencies
```

### Expected behavior

Doctor completes, as it did on 2026.11.4. The 2026.11.4 plugin install on the same machine has `node_modules/@lancedb/lancedb-darwin-arm64/lancedb.darwin-arm64.node` and loads.

### Actual behavior

Doctor exits non-zero (output under Logs). The installed 2026.11.6 plugin contains only `node_modules/@openclaw/memory-lancedb/node_modules/@lancedb/lancedb-linux-x64-gnu/lancedb.linux-x64-gnu.node`, and its generated `package-lock.json` has no `@lancedb/lancedb-darwin-arm64` entry. Importing the plugin's `dist/.setup/dist-*.mjs` under the Gateway's Node outside Doctor throws the same `Cannot find native binding`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10), updating from 2026.11.4 (d843d6a)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global; Gateway LaunchAgent on Homebrew Node 26.12.1

### Model

Not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-related (plugin packaging)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue. Resolve the reported migration failure before retrying. Later repairs were not run.
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (step-refused): Failed detecting Memory LanceDB per-agent isolation: Error: Cannot find native binding. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies (https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828). Please try `npm i` again after removing both package-lock.json and node_modules directory.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`extensions/memory-lancedb/package.json` lost `openclaw.release.bundleRuntimeDependencies: false` between v2026.11.4 and v2026.11.5:

| ref | `openclaw.release.bundleRuntimeDependencies` | `bundleDependencies` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v2026.11.3 | `false` | none |
| v2026.11.4 | `false` | none |
| v2026.11.5 | absent | `["apache-arrow"]` |
| v2026.11.6 | absent | `["apache-arrow"]` |
| main (2026-11-21) | absent | `["apache-arrow"]` |

Without the flag the npm publish path bundles the plugin's runtime dependencies on the build host. The published manifest names all seven `@lancedb/lancedb-*` packages in `bundleDependencies`, the tarball contains only `@lancedb/lancedb-linux-x64-gnu`, and npm treats the others as already bundled and never fetches the host's package.

`docs/plugins/dependency-resolution.md` at v2026.11.6 still lists memory-lancedb among the native-heavy packages that opt out. The published 2026.11.10-beta.1 package has the same manifest shape (10 bundled packages, about 249 MB).

### Impact and severity

Affected: macOS arm64 hosts with memory-lancedb enabled, updating to 2026.11.5 or 2026.11.6 (observed on one host, 1 of 1 attempts without a workaround).
Severity: High for those hosts. The update fails at Doctor after the state databases are already migrated; this host was rolled back to 2026.11.4 from pre-update copies of `openclaw.json` and the SQLite databases.
Scope beyond macOS arm64: the packaging suggests every host other than linux-x64-gnu is affected, but only macOS arm64 was tested. #203041 reports `bundled @lancedb/lancedb dependency is unavailable` on Windows 11 x64 with 2026.11.5, which fits the same cause.

### Additional information

Last known good 2026.11.4. First known bad 2026.11.5 by package manifest; 2026.11.6 observed.

Suggested fix: restore `"bundleRuntimeDependencies": false` under `openclaw.release` in `extensions/memory-lancedb/package.json` and republish the plugin. A publish-time check that a bundled package set with `os`/`cpu` fields covers more than the build host would catch the next one.

Workaround, confirmed on the same machine (a second update attempt completed with it):

1. `npm install --prefix <tmp> --no-save --ignore-scripts --no-package-lock @lancedb/lancedb-darwin-arm64@0.40.0`
2. Before `openclaw doctor --fix`, make it resolvable from the plugin's `dist/.setup/` (for example `NODE_PATH=<tmp>/node_modules`). Doctor then completes.
3. Copy the package to `<plugin generation>/node_modules/@lancedb/lancedb-darwin-arm64`, where 2026.11.4 installed it. The Gateway log then shows `memory-lancedb: initialized`.

Older, closed reports in the same area: #22687, #67857.

issues.body:
## Bug type
Behavior bug (regression of the yield path; related to #200475, #195864, #179486, but a different trigger).

## Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (`06afb10`), Linux x64 container, channel `webchat` (Control UI), agent `main`, model `claude-cli` / `claude-opus-5-5`. Also seen on 2026.11.5.

## What happens
1. In a long main session (hundreds of turns, ~500k tokens), the agent calls `sessions_spawn` (visible child on another agent, `context: "isolated"`), then `sessions_yield`. The yield returns `{"status":"yielded"}`.
2. The Claude CLI writes its final assistant text (`stopReason: end_turn`, imported into the transcript), but the run never completes. After ~5 min: `cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli ... durationMs=310068 error=CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.` The user gets `run-failed-before-reply`, so the final text is never delivered.
3. The child finishes normally. Its completion announce (`announce:requester-settle:...`) then fails the same way (~185s, `GatewayClientRequestError ... UNAVAILABLE`).
4. Every later user turn in that session fails the same way (~185s each). None of them logs a new `cli live session start`, so they appear to reuse the dead live session. Diagnostics show `stalled session ... classification=stalled_agent_run lastProgress=deferred_maintenance:wait_ended`, then `reply watchdog ... no_semantic_progress`.
5. Only a full Gateway restart recovers the session. In one earlier occurrence the session ended up in `stale_session_state` (still reported after 49900s).

With model fallbacks configured, the failed turns silently fail over to the fallback model instead.

## Reproducibility
3 occurrences in 3 different long sessions, all with the same spawn + yield sequence. A deliberate test on 2026.11.6 in a small fresh session passed twice (hidden child and visible child: the parent resumed with the child result and showed no stuck markers). So the bug seems to depend on session length/size, or on state that builds up over a long session, not on the yield alone.

## Expected
After `sessions_yield`, the CLI run closes, the final text is delivered, the child completion wakes the parent, and later turns get a working live session (or a fresh one if the old one cannot close).

## Workaround
Do not call `sessions_yield` from claude-cli agents. End the turn normally and let the child completion event wake the parent.

issues.body:
## Summary

With `tools.exec.mode: "auto"` and an agent on the `claude-cli` runtime, the exec reviewer sees only the command. It never sees what the owner asked for. Its rubric says to deny commands that don't serve the user's request, so it denies commands the owner asked for word for word.

This is the Claude CLI side of #166521, which covers Codex `gateway_exec`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent on `claude-cli` with `tools.exec.mode: "auto"` and a working `tools.exec.reviewer.model`.
2. As the owner, ask the agent to run an exact, read-only command that isn't allowlisted, for example a mailbox search with `--readonly --max 3`.
3. The agent runs it through OpenClaw `exec`, which Claude CLI reaches over the MCP loopback.

## Expected

The reviewer sees the owner's request, labeled `origin=operator`, and allows the command or asks for approval. Embedded runs already behave this way.

## Actual

The reviewer denies it: `Exec denied by auto-review (risk=high): Reading a personal Gmail inbox is sensitive and unrelated to the stated development workflow.`

With the owner's turn added to the reviewer input (a local patch), the same request got `allow-once (risk=low): The operator explicitly requested this read-only search of three inbox results.` The patched reviewer still denied credential exfiltration, injected instructions in tool output, non-owner requests and text addressed to the reviewer.

## Cause

Only the embedded runner passes `reviewTranscript` to the exec tool. Since #161780, Claude CLI shell work goes through the loopback `exec` built in `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`, which has no `reviewTranscript`. #142279 left the Codex bridge without context on purpose. The Claude CLI path was never discussed.

Version: 2026.10.8. On `main`, a loopback exec test shows the reviewer receives no transcript.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the macOS app on current `main`, the first chat message after a fresh onboarding fails with "This host is low on memory, so it could not start another session." The Mac has plenty of memory. The packaged Gateway runs on Bun, and under Bun `process.availableMemory()` returns only truly free pages, so the 1 GiB Claude CLI live-session guard trips on a healthy Mac.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the macOS app from `main` at d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637 (`scripts/package-mac-app.sh`, debug, arm64) and launch it on a fresh profile (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=onboarding`).
2. Complete onboarding with a local Gateway, using Claude Code (`claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`) as the AI.
3. Choose **Talk to my agent** and send `hi`.

### Expected behavior

The agent replies. The host was a 48 GB Apple silicon MacBook Pro, and `memory_pressure` reported "System-wide memory free percentage: 70%" at the time.

### Actual behavior

The turn fails before any model call. The chat shows "This host is low on memory, so it could not start another session. Try again after active conversations finish." with Try again / Report a bug.

Gateway log (`~/.openclaw-onboarding/logs/openclaw-onboarding-2026-11-16.log`):

```
lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:… durationMs=5 error="Host memory is too low for another CLI live session."
cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=344 … error=Host memory is too low for another CLI live session.
model fallback decision: … reason=rate_limit status=429 code=cli_live_session_host_memory … fallbackStepFinalOutcome=chain_exhausted fallbackConfigured=false
Embedded agent failed before reply: Host memory is too low for another CLI live session.
```

The same Mac, measured with the bundled runtime and with Node at the same moment:

| Runtime | `process.availableMemory()` | `os.freemem()` | `os.totalmem()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bundled Bun 1.4.4 (`~/.openclaw-onboarding/runtime/…/bin/bun`) | 548,831,232 (0.55 GB) | 548,831,232 | 51,539,607,552 |
| Node 26.12.1 | 19,644,563,456 (19.6 GB) | 548,831,232 | — |

Under Bun on macOS, `process.availableMemory()` is identical to `os.freemem()`. macOS keeps truly free pages low, so most Macs in normal use read below 1 GiB.

### OpenClaw version

main d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637 (2026.11.4, app build 2611160101)

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

### Install method

mac app (locally packaged from `main`, isolated `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`)

### Model

claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 (shown in the UI as anthropic/claude-opus-5-5)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw (mac app, local Gateway on Bun) -> claude-cli live session -> Anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

No fallback model configured (fresh onboarding default).

### Logs

See Actual behavior.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code at the tested commit:

- [`src/infra/host-memory.ts#L8-L14`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637/src/infra/host-memory.ts#L8-L14): `readHostFreeMemoryBytes()` uses `process.availableMemory()` on darwin. Its doc comment assumes Node semantics ("Node's available-memory reading includes inactive and purgeable pages").
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-registry.ts#L19`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-registry.ts#L19) and [`#L196-L224`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-registry.ts#L196-L224): `ensureCliLiveSessionMemory` throws `cli_live_session_host_memory` when that reading is below 1 GiB.
- [`src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts#L66`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637/src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts#L66): user-facing copy.

### Impact and severity

- **Who:** every macOS app user whose first agent runs through the Claude CLI live session. The packaged Gateway always runs on Bun.
- **Severity:** blocks the first message after onboarding. The user is told their Mac is out of memory when it is not. The error is categorized as `rate_limit`/429, so it is retried or reported as capacity instead of a bug.
- **Release exposure:** the guard is on `main` only. It is not in v2026.11.1–v2026.11.3 or v2026.11.5-beta.1. It will ship in the next release cut from `main` unless fixed.

### Additional information

**Contributing changes.** Each change was reasonable on its own; the failure is in how they combine.

1. #161603 (merged 2026-09-30, first shipped in v2026.10.1) moved the macOS app's private runtime, including the local Gateway, to the OpenClaw Bun fork.
2. #144535 (merged 2026-10-10, shipped in v2026.10.10) added `readHostFreeMemoryBytes()` with a macOS branch that relies on Node's `process.availableMemory()`. The app had already been running on Bun for ten days. At that point the only effect was understated free memory in device/host stats.
3. #192534 (merged 2026-11-04, unreleased) added the blocking 1 GiB guard on top of that helper. Its description states the helper reads `process.availableMemory()` on macOS. Its proof simulated memory at the helper/`os.freemem` seam, so the packaged macOS app on Bun was never exercised.

**Process gaps:**
- Nothing tests the host-memory helper under the runtime the macOS app actually ships (Bun). Unit tests mock the reading.
- No packaged-app smoke test sends a first message after a fresh onboarding. A single "fresh install → first reply" check would have caught this before merge.
- The failure maps to `rate_limit`, which hides a local guard decision behind a provider-capacity category.

**Other callers with the same Bun-on-macOS assumption.** These are not user-blocking but read too low under Bun:
- `src/infra/worker-pool-sizing.ts` `resolveUpdateHashWorkerCount()` (`process.availableMemory()`; only Bun on Linux is special-cased).
- `src/commands/doctor-database-port-memory-concurrency.ts` (`readHostFreeMemoryBytes()` → undersized rebuild concurrency).
- `src/gateway/server-methods/system.ts` and `src/node-host/host-stats.ts` (reported free memory).
- `isConstrainedProcessLowOnMemory()` uses `process.constrainedMemory()`; verify its Bun/macOS behavior while fixing.

**Suggested direction:** on darwin, compute reclaimable memory independently of the JS runtime (Mach VM statistics: free + inactive + purgeable + speculative) or detect a Bun-equivalent reading. Cover it with a test that simulates Bun's `availableMemory == freemem` behavior. Optionally, stop classifying this guard as `rate_limit`.

Found during a fresh-install onboarding walkthrough of the macOS app.

issues.body:
I hit this while testing the macOS welcome flow, before installing the Gemini plugin. I reproduced it on a fresh local profile with the macOS runtime payload built from `c766794dc63b`. The Gateway reached `/readyz`, but the request the welcome screen uses to detect setup options returned `UNAVAILABLE`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Build and stage the macOS arm64 runtime from `c766794dc63b`.
2. Start the packaged Gateway with its bundled Bun, a fresh local profile, and `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_LIBRARY` pointing to the bundled `libsqlite3.dylib`.
3. Once `/readyz` returns HTTP 200, call `openclaw.setup.detect` with `{}` over the local Gateway connection.

I expected the call to return setup options, including when no provider credentials are configured. Instead, it failed with `SQLite read-only worker failed while opening the source database` and `No supported SQLite library for Bun on macOS (arm64)`.

**What I found**

The shared-state metadata read passes a reduced environment to the read-only worker launcher, leaving out the bundled SQLite path. I observed a read-only worker without that setting. Forwarding just `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_LIBRARY` in a diagnostic build made the same request succeed. Node 26.12.1 also returned setup options with the unchanged package. [State read context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c766794dc63b706b3327d7a9f734daf4f1b5acca/src/state/openclaw-state-worker-context.capture.ts#L88-L106), [worker launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c766794dc63b706b3327d7a9f734daf4f1b5acca/src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts#L233-L250)

Tested with OpenClaw `2026.11.6` from source, macOS `27.0.1` arm64, bundled Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, and SQLite `3.53.4`. Related reports cover the CLI symptom on Intel and a proposed fix for the same worker handoff. [Issue #201957](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201957), [PR #195689](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195689)

issues.body:
We are seeing Node commands finish locally during a short connection outage while the Gateway has already settled the original invocation as disconnected. When the same Host reconnects and sends the result, it is ignored. The agent then has an uncertain outcome despite the side effects having occurred. Improving connection stability will help, but this failure can happen with any transport interruption.

I propose a negotiated extension that lets the original invocation retain its result owner briefly and attach to a freshly authenticated connection. The stale-socket protection in #78351 should remain: an old connection cannot clear replacement presence or complete replacement work. The new path would explicitly authorize recovery of one existing operation.

The essential checks would be:

- Match the authenticated device key, owner/profile scope and current persisted pairing generation, plus an opaque per-invocation resume token delivered on the original connection.
- Bind recovery to the original operation identity and immutable command/approval/audience fingerprint. A tool call can contain multiple operations, so each effect needs its own stable key.
- Atomically attach the operation to the new connection and fence the old attachment. Recheck current policy, cancellation and the existing completion/lifecycle owner before accepting output.
- Keep the original work deadline and consumed approval unchanged. Admit a separate fixed reporting budget at the start of the call; reconnect never grants more execution time or revives released authority. Increasing the existing invoke timeout alone would also increase the work budget forwarded to the Host.
- Acknowledge result acceptance explicitly, with an authenticated bounded terminal receipt for retries after the original waiter has settled. A successful transport RPC carrying `ignored` must not mean that the operation result reached its owner.

Current code distinguishes borrowed request continuation, approval-record retention and completion custody. The public invoke API has dispatch checks, while internal cleanup has its own completion callback. The first slice therefore needs an explicit original-caller completion handle at public admission, checked on attachment and first result commit. It also needs detached pairing/committed-policy validation: an absent Node must not be mistaken for revoked policy. Existing admission and pairing owners should retain those responsibilities; a reconnect must not re-admit a distinct operator continuation.

The smallest first slice would recover completed results without resending commands. That addresses the lost-answer path while avoiding execution replay. Safe redispatch can follow only with a Host ledger that records the operation before starting it, rejects a key/payload conflict and retains replay protection for the full recovery window. Host process loss or an expired grant yields an honest unknown outcome. We would promise at-most-once start within that process-lifetime contract and once-only terminal settlement; arbitrary external side effects across process crashes cannot be universally exactly once.

A three-minute maximum is the proposed first-version recovery/reporting grace, bounded by caller authority and reserved capacity, and subject to load qualification. Use a specific `invoke.resume.result.v1` capability with affirmative per-client selection and per-invocation opt-in. It would initially cover positively bounded direct `system.run` calls without input, stream-output consumers or pending interaction. Ledger-capable redispatch and duplex recovery would have separate feature contracts. Older peers would retain current behavior. Gateway process restart recovery is a separate problem.

I would like owner review of the explicit public completion handle, detached revocation contract and result-only negotiation before implementation. The design selects these semantics; source inspection is not implementation proof or security acceptance. The first fault-injection test should drop the socket immediately before completion, reconnect the same paired Host and prove one local execution plus delivery to the original waiting call. The same suite should include wrong-device/token rejection, unpair/re-pair, stale close/result races, caller/approval cancellation, temporary pairing-store unavailability, deadline expiry and an acknowledgement lost after the waiter has settled.

Who would be the right current Node/Gateway and approval-lifecycle reviewers for this extension? I can bring the client-side owner into the protocol review and prepare the narrow implementation against the agreed contract.

issues.body:
I saw the updater install the new build, report that Doctor couldn't take the profile into maintenance while the gateway owned its state, then put the previous build back. The gateway, the installed updater and the target were all built from OpenClaw main at `c1f70d3b78262ff9dabb36b8846c7b8779378b6b`. I used macOS 27.0.1 on Apple silicon, Node 24.22.3, npm 11.19.1 and SQLite.

1. Check out that commit and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Set `out=$(mktemp -d)`. Run `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --runtime-only --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir "$out/a" --output-name openclaw.tgz`, then repeat with `"$out/b"`. The two packages have different build IDs.
2. Install A with `npm install --global --prefix "$out/prefix" "$out/a/openclaw.tgz"`. I used the same absolute `out` path in both terminals, with `npm_config_prefix="$out/prefix"`, `OPENCLAW_HOME="$out/home"` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$out/home/.openclaw"` exported in each. Let `cli="$out/prefix/bin/openclaw"`. Run `"$cli" setup` in local mode without installing a service. With the gateway stopped, run `"$cli" agents add archive --agent-dir "$out/archive-data" --workspace "$out/archive-workspace" --non-interactive`. The registered data directory is outside the OpenClaw state directory.
3. I made the older data in a separate scratch install of the published `openclaw@2026.11.6`. After local setup, I ran `openclaw agents add archive --workspace "$out/donor-workspace" --non-interactive` with that install's CLI. With the donor stopped, I backed up its database using the following command, where `donor_state` is that install's state directory.

```sh
node --input-type=module -e '
  import { DatabaseSync, backup } from "node:sqlite";
  const db = new DatabaseSync(process.argv[1]);
  await backup(db, process.argv[2]);
  db.close();
' "$donor_state/agents/archive/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite" "$out/archive-v38.sqlite"
```

4. Still offline, move A's existing `openclaw-agent.sqlite` and any of its sidecars or seal out of `"$out/archive-data"`. Restore `"$out/archive-v38.sqlite"` there as `openclaw-agent.sqlite`. My backup passed `PRAGMA integrity_check` and had `user_version=38`. Main expects 43.
5. Start `"$cli" gateway run --bind loopback` in the first terminal without a service manager. In the second, I verified `"$cli" gateway health --json` returned `ok` and the external store was still at 38. Run `"$cli" update --tag "$out/b/openclaw.tgz" --yes --json --no-restart`.

The update exited 1 after 2m 12s. Doctor exited 0 with `Doctor could not enter maintenance` and named PID 30406, the PID listening on the gateway port. The post-activation check then reported `expected schema 43, found 38` for the external store. The rollback result said `Previous package and configuration restored`. I observed A, B and then A at the active package path.

With the gateway stopped, the same backup and directory layout updated to 43 in 2m 46s. I also stopped the gateway in the original failed profile and reran the identical command. It completed in 149.5 seconds, kept B installed and migrated that external store to 43. An agent backup restored under the default state directory reached 43 during startup, before I could run the update. If I need to stop the gateway, I'd like to learn that before the package gets replaced. [Startup discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1f70d3b78262ff9dabb36b8846c7b8779378b6b/src/state/state-upgrade.ts#L157) · [Doctor maintenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1f70d3b78262ff9dabb36b8846c7b8779378b6b/src/commands/doctor-maintenance.ts#L390) · [Final schema check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1f70d3b78262ff9dabb36b8846c7b8779378b6b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts#L121)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 the app-owned bundled Gateway service stays on 2026.11.4 and is not replaced, so the app shows "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery" and quits, and every repair command refuses to run.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once on one Mac; not minimized and not rerun from a clean setup. It is not established how the app and the service got out of sync.

1. Have OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 with its app-owned bundled Gateway service still on 2026.11.4 (LaunchAgent runs ~/.openclaw/runtime/service/bun against the 2026.11.4 runtime; `openclaw update status --json` reports installKind "host", installOwner "macos-app").
2. Launch OpenClaw.app. It shows the alert "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery"; after OK the app quits.
3. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive`, `openclaw doctor --lint` and `openclaw gateway install --force` with the 2026.11.5 CLI. Each one refuses (see Actual behavior).

### Expected behavior

For an app-managed service, the app replaces the stale 2026.11.4 service with the app's runtime before preparing client credentials (the replacement described in #187000), or at least shows an accurate recovery path that works for an app-owned service.

### Actual behavior

- The app shows "OpenClaw client credentials need recovery: Quit OpenClaw, run openclaw doctor --fix with the matching CLI, then reopen OpenClaw" and quits after OK.
- App unified log (subsystem ai.openclaw, category credentials) only contains the schema refusal below. With --info --debug and a filter for stale/replac/service/pin/eligib/managed there is no log line about stale-service replacement.
- `openclaw doctor --fix`, `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive` and `openclaw doctor --lint` (2026.11.5 CLI) fail with: "Refusing a forward database schema migration: this CLI is 2026.11.5 but the Gateway service runs 2026.11.4 from ~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.11.4-release-d843d6af39a4-2026-11-16T06-24-26.000Z/lib/node_modules/openclaw; run openclaw update (or the CLI from that path)."
- `openclaw update` says: "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."
- `openclaw gateway install --force` fails with: "Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix."
- `openclaw update status --json` reports inspectionErrors: "Channel inspection unavailable: Client credential migration is incomplete or stale; run openclaw doctor --fix before using this client | gateway.maintenance_required". No abandoned update; serviceDefinition drift is empty.
- The service is launched as: /bin/sh ~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway-env-wrapper.sh ~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway.env ~/.openclaw/runtime/service/bun --no-install ~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.11.4-release-d843d6af39a4-2026-11-16T06-24-26.000Z/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789. Stable Bun resolves inside ~/.openclaw/runtime/.
- The loop: the service cannot move to 2026.11.5 until doctor runs, and doctor will not run until the service is on 2026.11.5.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 (build 2611000590, commit 76cbb32ecd4f41954d211c5af404dafd4b31e7c1, runtime build ID 2026.11.5-release-76cbb32ecd4f-2026-11-17T22-18-00.000Z); CLI 2026.11.5; Gateway service 2026.11.4 (d843d6a)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)

### Install method

mac app (OpenClaw.app, app-owned bundled Gateway service under ~/.openclaw/runtime/)

### Model

N/A (occurs at app startup / service replacement, before any model request)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (not a model or provider issue)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
App unified log (subsystem ai.openclaw, category credentials), home directory replaced with ~:

Credential startup failed: Could not prepare local client credentials. [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Refusing a forward database schema migration: this CLI is 2026.11.5 but the Gateway service runs 2026.11.4 from ~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.11.4-release-d843d6af39a4-2026-11-16T06-24-26.000Z/lib/node_modules/openclaw; run openclaw update (or the CLI from ~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.11.4-release-d843d6af39a4-2026-11-16T06-24-26.000Z/lib/node_modules/openclaw).
Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app.

openclaw gateway install --force (2026.11.5 CLI):
Runtime pin inspection failed: Error: Failed migrating daemon runtime pins: Error: Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.

openclaw update:
Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: Macs where OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 runs with an app-owned bundled Gateway service still on 2026.11.4 (observed on one Mac).
Severity: blocks workflow. The app cannot be used and the service cannot be moved to 2026.11.5; the 2026.11.4 Gateway can still be started with launchctl and used through the browser dashboard.
Frequency: always (every launch attempt observed).
Consequence: app unusable; I kept the Gateway on the old version with backups instead of editing the plist or runtime pins.

### Additional information

Split out from #201468 at the request of its maintainer/contributor (the fix belongs in the stale-service replacement and migration-admission path, not the alert text; PR #201741 only changes the alert text).

Checked read-only and ruled out: openclaw.cliInstallPolicy unset, openclaw.pauseEnabled 0, openclaw.connectionMode local, ~/.openclaw/disable-launchagent absent. The service command shape matches the expected generated form. The target runtime directory 2026.11.5-release-76cbb32ecd4f-2026-11-17T22-18-00.000Z exists under ~/.openclaw/runtime/.

Question: on this build, which StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.detect() guard returns nil (installed-service inspection, managed-runtime recognition, bundled-runtime match, runtime seed/validation including a swallowed BundledRuntime.seed() error, or missing service authority)? Is there a supported manual repair for this app-owned loop?

Last known good / first known bad versions: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Discussion with the Discord support bot that helped narrow this down: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1572883323536281600
