issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Setting a Markdown frontmatter key named `null` can remove a neighboring field and an inline comment.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use this Markdown file as the input to `openclaw path set 'oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/null' new --file note.md`:

   ```markdown
   ---
   null: old # keep
   "null": other
   ---
   Body
   ```

2. Compare the whole file before and after the edit. The two keys are distinct in YAML.

### Expected behavior

Only `old` changes to `new`. The [path mutation contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a3357794fa56cdd96e411272290aaf2752797925/docs/cli/path.md#mutation-contract) promises a source-range edit.

### Actual behavior

The resulting frontmatter contains only `null: new`. Both the inline comment and the quoted sibling disappear.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 source at `a3357794fa56`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu under WSL2, Node 24.22.1.

### Install method

Source checkout with pnpm 12.15.0.

### Model

No model involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Local oc-path plugin, Markdown editor.

### Logs

Three regression cases using the production path parser and editor failed on the unmodified source. The same deletion occurred with the plain keys `true`, `FALSE`, and `null` followed by their quoted spellings.

### Impact and severity

A successful edit to one field can silently remove another field from the file.

prs.title: fix(plugins): load the compiled public surface under node_modules
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a managed Git release (package installed under `node_modules`), a Gateway MCP request imported `extensions/deepseek/web-search-contract-api.ts` even though `dist/extensions/deepseek/web-search-contract-api.js` was present in the same release. Node refuses type stripping under `node_modules`, so the module load failed with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING` and the MCP loopback never started. Fixes #201874.

## User Impact

A managed Git install now loads the compiled public-surface artifacts, so the bundled web-search contract resolves and the MCP loopback comes up; the failing WebChat turn no longer dies with "Claude Code started without the OpenClaw MCP server". Source-tree development keeps its existing preference for the source artifact, so sidecars still share the active source instance there.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolvePluginRootPublicSurfaceLocation` derives `preferredArtifacts` from the registered entry: when that entry is TypeScript it prefers the source family (`.ts`/`.tsx`/…), and the source candidates are also appended to both the entry and plugin-root loops. That default is right for a checkout, but under `node_modules` Node can never execute those files, so the presence of the source artifact shadowed the compiled one.

The resolver now drops the source-family *preference* when the plugin root itself lives under a `node_modules` segment, so the compiled `artifactBasename` / `dist/<artifact>` candidates win; the TypeScript sources stay as the last-resort fallback, which keeps captured build trees that ship only sources resolvable. `resolveBundledPluginSourcePublicSurfacePath` (the development source root) is untouched.

## Evidence

Real-run A/B on this machine (Node 26.12.1, no tsx type-stripping available under `node_modules`), using a managed-layout copy: `<tmp>/node_modules/openclaw/extensions/demo/` holding `web-search-contract-api.ts`, `dist/web-search-contract-api.js` and a TypeScript `index.ts` entry. The probe calls the shipped resolver and then imports what it returns.

| Run | Source | Resolver result | Import outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `upstream/main` | `.../extensions/demo/web-search-contract-api.ts` | `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING: Stripping types is currently unsupported for files under node_modules` |
| After | this branch `352c344b` | `.../extensions/demo/dist/web-search-contract-api.js` | imports, `family = "built"` |

![Real-run resolver + import before/after under node_modules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201874/node-modules-artifact-proof.png)

Unit: `src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.test.ts` — new `loads the compiled artifact when the plugin root is under node_modules` fails on `upstream/main` and passes here; the paired control `keeps preferring the source artifact outside node_modules` passes on both. Suite 26/26; `public-surface-loader.test.ts` 16 passed / 1 skipped. `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK, `check:test-lines-ratchet` +43 / allowance 400, `oxlint` clean.

## What was not tested

- `src/plugins/public-surface-generation.test.ts`'s `loads captured dependencies and tsconfig source mappings…` case fails on this Windows checkout **with and without** this change (JITI tsconfig-path resolution), so it is not a regression signal here; the relative-mapping case and the rest of the suite pass.
- Not run inside a full Gateway + MCP loopback. The official reproduction is `scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` (`git-release` scenario), which is Docker-only and Docker is not installed on this machine; the probe above exercises the same resolver and the same Node type-stripping refusal against a managed-layout directory instead.
- No real model: the affected path fails at module load, before any provider call.
- No local typecheck: `run-tsgo` cannot resolve the workspace `@openclaw/proc-safe` package on this machine (it fails the same way on clean `upstream/main`).

prs.title: fix: deliver Nostr automation announcements to the owner
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts:249` the owner branch returned the outbound session route's `to` unchanged, so Nostr owner delivery carried the route form `nostr:<hex>` (`extensions/nostr/src/channel.ts:83`, adopted at `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts:518`) into a sender that requires a bare pubkey, while the explicit-target branch already strips that prefix with `stripSelectedProviderPrefix`.

Fixes #203403

Thanks @nousclawds4 for the precise report and code trace, and @chelsealong for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Nostr automations using `target: "owner"` can lose fallback announcements because cron passes a `nostr:`-prefixed session route to a sender that expects a bare pubkey. The run still reports `ok`, and the run record shows `Pubkey must be 64 hex characters or npub format`.

## User Impact

Owner-targeted fallback announcements now resolve to a sendable Nostr destination and reach the owner. `openclaw cron show` prints `nostr:<hex>` instead of `nostr:nostr:<hex>`. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron now applies its existing provider-prefix normalization to owner targets, as it already does for explicit targets.

## Evidence

Gateway proof ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203409#issuecomment-7074602226)): isolated Gateway from source, Nostr channel against a local fixture relay with generated keys, `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` with the owner npub, and a scripted model that answers without the message tool, so the fallback announce sends.

- Base `ae8155cf`: owner job `delivered:false`, `deliveryError: "Pubkey must be 64 hex characters or npub format"`, gateway `notification failed: Pubkey must be 64 hex characters or npub format`, relay receives no DM for it.
- This head: owner job `delivered:true`, `resolved.to` is the bare owner hex, relay receives one signature-verified DM to the owner pubkey that decrypts to the owner job's text.
- Controls, both sides: explicit npub target delivered; `nostr:not-a-pubkey` still fails with the existing `Nostr target must be a 64-character hex pubkey or npub value`.

The new owner-route regression failed before the source fix: expected `user:alice`, received `alpha:user:alice`. After the fix, the cron target suites passed (30 tests) and the Nostr channel suites passed (29 tests). The final owner test passed (6 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, the affected `services-cron` test typecheck, targeted oxlint, format check, and `git diff --check` passed. An earlier full test typecheck found a fixture typing error; it was corrected and the affected shard passed.

Prepared with Codex assistance; no human validation is claimed.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert fully undoes it and nothing is persisted. Blast radius: owner-targeted automation delivery on channels whose session route prefixes the destination with the channel id; other targets are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(update): Git installs update through prepared releases and a resident launcher
prs.body:
## Problem

A Git install updates in place under the running Gateway, through a managed-service handoff helper. When the new build does not start, recovery depends on that helper and on the old updater that is already installed, so a failed update can leave the Gateway down or stuck in `update-recovery-pending`.

## Change

Git installs now update through prepared releases and a resident launcher:

1. `update.run`, `openclaw update` and automatic updates admit the run, resolve the target and run preflight (Node engine, required tools, disk space, container installs refused before any change).
2. The next release is built beside the running one (`git worktree add --detach`, then the target's install and build). The running checkout is not changed.
3. `openclaw update check-release` runs the new code offline against the current config and state and reports broken plugin or config surfaces. It does not migrate state.
4. `openclaw update plugins` runs from the published release: the existing plugin maintenance owner (`updatePluginsAfterCoreUpdate`), with the new core's code and version. A plugin problem, or a target too old to have the command, is recorded as a `plugins` step with a next action and never fails the update. An already-current install still runs it from the serving code and restarts a running Gateway when plugins changed (`docs/install/updating.md`).
5. The release is published as a pending trial, and the Gateway restarts with a process-replacing reason.
6. The launcher switches the release link at the next child start, counts attempts, commits the trial when the new Gateway is ready, and otherwise rolls back and starts the previous release.
7. The Gateway that starts after the switch (new on success, old after a rollback) finishes the run and sends the outcome to a requester that received the start notice.

Routing:
- `update.run` reads the install kind from the existing install-status owner (`resolveStartupInstallStatus`). `update-run.ts` wraps `update.run`; `update.ts` is unchanged and still serves package installs.
- `openclaw update` branches after `prepareUpdateCommand`, so every existing refusal (external supervisor, host-owned, immutable, system package owner, interrupted update) applies first. A requested non-dev channel on a Git checkout still switches it to a package through the existing flow, and `--dry-run` keeps the existing preview.
- Package installs move to this path in the next change, which also deletes the old Git machinery that this PR leaves unused.

Converting an existing install:
- The old entry points of a converted install (`openclaw.mjs`, `dist/index.js`) forward to the release launcher through a marker beside the tree. Existing service definitions and PATH shims keep working without a rewrite.
- A first update driven by an older installed updater still migrates state as it does today. Released updaters require migrated state: 23 stable and 6 extended-stable tags contain that check.

Fixes found by the real-install runs below, each a separate commit:
- `openclaw update --sha` now sends the tracked upstream that the protocol requires.
- The new path restarts with `update.run` / `update.auto`, so the process is replaced instead of restarted in place.
- A Gateway started by the launcher leaves its update successor to the launcher instead of spawning one outside it.
- Preflight skips dangling symlinks in agent homes, such as Codex `arg0` shims, when it sizes state databases.
- `check-release` writes its JSON result to stdout.
- Plain `openclaw update` keeps following the run while the restarting Gateway refuses connections with a retryable HTTP 503. Before, it exited 1 although the update succeeded.

Accepted edge cases:
- After `openclaw update` runs in a Git checkout, `openclaw.mjs` and `dist/index.js` in that checkout run the current release. A developer who edits the source of a checkout they also update from runs the release, not their edits.
- A stop request handled inside a launcher child exits with code 0, and the launcher starts the child again. A stop through the service manager stops the launcher and its child.
- On a Gateway with no service manager, the first update from a released version does not restart it. The released updater does this, and says so.
- Package updates now read the install status twice per request: once to route, once in the old handler.
- After a rollback, the previous release runs with plugins maintained for the new core. A plugin that cannot load stays off for that boot, as the plugin docs describe.

## Evidence

Real install on macOS (Apple silicon). Isolated HOME, state, config and port, a foreground Gateway, no launchd service. Every candidate was built from `git archive` of its commit; the final candidate is this branch's head before review.

| Step | Run status | Trial | Served after | Health |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.6 → A (released updater) | succeeded | (old path) | A, after a recorded manual start | 200 / 200 |
| A → B′ (B′ fails at startup) | failed, `new build failed to start` | rolled-back, 2 attempts | A, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |
| A → B | succeeded | committed, 1 attempt | B, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |
| B → C | succeeded | committed, 1 attempt | C, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |

- The same launcher process stayed the parent through every replacement. The previous release was kept after each commit.
- Phase times (seconds), from the persisted run steps:

| Step | Staging (build) | Validating | Restarting | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A → B′ (rollback) | 192.5 | 0.8 | 29.2 | 222.7 |
| A → B | 195.7 | 1.1 | 32.9 | 229.8 |
| B → C | 201.6 | 0.9 | 36.9 | 239.5 |

- `check-release` on a copy of a real state directory (Linux, no network): exit 0 in 3.0 s, 187 surfaces checked, shared state schema 40 → 40, agent databases 43 → 43.

Tests:
- New: `src/update/*.test.ts` (target, preflight, Git and package preparation, check-release, store, launcher, trial settlement and outcome notice, CLI request shape), plus a launcher-child case in `process-respawn.test.ts`.
- The gateway `update*` suites run against package installs. Tests that pinned the old Git handoff, Git preflight delegation, explicit Git targets and foreground parking are deleted. Tests of behavior that package installs still use (notice policy, owner checks, campaign adoption, platform admission) now run on a managed package install.

## Review

- `--no-restart` on a Git install now prepares the release in the CLI process instead of asking the Gateway, so the Gateway does not restart. The release starts at the Gateway's next start, and the CLI says so and exits 0, instead of reporting "Updated".
- The first conversion creates the `prefix/openclaw` link to the running tree before it writes the forwarding marker. Forwarded commands work between publish and the switch.
- The run row is written through the existing asynchronous update-run owner (`update-run-write.async.ts`). The synchronous second writer is deleted, so there is no SQLite work on the Gateway thread.
- Rejected: settling trials of the format-1 Git-release launcher (#199706). No released build contains it (not 2026.11.6 `latest`, 2026.10.33 `extended-stable` or 2026.11.10-beta.1 `beta`), and main-only code is not a shipped contract. Only a Git checkout that tracked `main` between 2026-11-17 and this change can have such a trial.
- The in-process path (`--no-restart`, or no Gateway answering) uses the requested channel, else the saved `update.channel` (`readUpdateChannelConfig`), else `dev`, as the existing CLI does. The Gateway path passes the checkout's tag and branch facts, as the existing handler does, so a configless checkout on a stable tag stays on stable.
- After publishing a Git release, `git worktree repair` records it at its final path, so `git worktree list` and a later `git worktree prune` see the serving release where it is.
- `prefix/openclaw` is repointed to the running tree when it does not already resolve there, so a link left from an earlier package install cannot become the rollback target.
- Rejected for this PR: carrying the package layout's `lib/node_modules/openclaw` link. That layout belongs to package-release installs, which this PR does not route; the next change moves package installs and owns it.
- A new build that exits 78 (it refuses the configuration) during a trial now rolls back like any other failed candidate. Outside a trial, 78 stays terminal.
- Rejected again, same reason as the format-1 trial: making `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` follow `prefix/openclaw`. Only the main-only Git-release conversion (#199706) creates that link, and no release contains it.
- A Gateway with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` set now refuses `update.run` with `restart-unavailable` before anything is recorded or prepared, as the existing handler does. The prepared release starts only in a new process, which that Gateway cannot start.
- `openclaw update --timeout <seconds>` on a Git install is the overall budget again: it bounds how long the CLI follows the run, reaches the Gateway as `update.run` `timeoutMs`, and target resolution, the release build and plugin maintenance get only what remains of it. Preflight and `check-release` keep their own short bounds.
- Rejected again, same reason as the format-1 trial: settling legacy `.trial` records in `stale-install.ts`. Only #199706 writes them; `settleGitReleaseTrial` is in no released build (2026.11.6 `latest`, 2026.10.33 `extended-stable`, 2026.11.10-beta.1 `beta`).
- Rejected: routing `--tag` on a Git install to the package flow. The existing Git flow ignores `--tag` ("--tag applies to npm installs only; git updates ignore it"), so the Git route keeps that behavior.
- After merging `main`: Control UI and desktop app requests on a Git install show the update in the app instead of the conversation (#203357), through the same `appUpdateNoticePublisher` owner as package installs.
- A manual `update.run` on a Git install during a scheduled campaign adopts the campaign through its existing owner: it applies the pinned commit, records `trigger: campaign` with the campaign ID, binds the run, and refuses a mismatched `--sha` or a campaign already applying, as package installs do.
- Rejected a third time: settling legacy `.trial` records (same reason as above).
- Rejected: restoring the plugin cohort across a trial rollback. Removing the cohort is the approved design (plugins are non-fatal). After a rollback the previous release runs with plugins maintained for the new core; a plugin that cannot load stays off for that boot. Listed under accepted edge cases.

prs.title: fix: stop sending chats to OpenAI when no model is configured
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh install with no model chosen, OpenClaw silently behaves as if `openai/gpt-6-astra` were configured. The Models page shows "Couldn't load models from openai", the utility model shows `Auto · openai/gpt-6-luna`, and chat turns are sent to OpenAI even though the user never picked OpenAI or signed in to it.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw no longer picks a model for you. With no model configured, a chat turn replies "No model is configured. Choose one in Settings → Models, send `/model <provider/model>` in chat, or run `openclaw models set <provider/model>`." before any chat-model call. `/model <provider/model>` in chat still works. `openclaw models status` and the Gateway startup log say the model is not configured. The Models page no longer tries to load OpenAI, and no utility model is derived from a primary that does not exist.

Existing installs keep working: on update from 2026.11.6 or earlier (config `meta.lastTouchedVersion`), `openclaw doctor --fix` writes the model the install was actually running as `agents.defaults.model.primary`: `openai/gpt-6-astra`, or the provider row the old release picked. This includes configs whose only provider row is a separated utility model, which the old release skipped in favor of OpenAI. The OpenAI model is written only when OpenAI credentials are available; without them those installs could not run anyway and now get the message above. Configs written by newer releases are left alone.

Plugin SDK: `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` returns `undefined` when no model is configured. `DEFAULT_PROVIDER` and `runtime.agent.defaults` are deprecated under a new compatibility record and keep their values. Bundled plugins (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Codex, voice-call, llama.cpp, Skill Workshop) are migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveDefaultModelForAgent` filled a missing primary with the compiled-in `openai/gpt-6-astra`, so every reader (catalog planning, utility derivation, turn admission, status) treated it as the user's choice. The owner now returns "no model" and readers either describe it or fail the turn with one shared message. The core provider default remains only for qualifying a bare model id (for example a legacy `responseModel: "gpt-5.4-mini"`).

Chat commands that need no model (`/help`, `/status`, `/models`, `/model`, `/new`) run normally with no model configured; `/status` reports the model as not configured. The reply pipeline now carries "no model" through command and directive handling, and only the agent turn itself (and model settings such as `/think` or `/fast`) gets the setup message. Fixes #203304.

## Evidence

- Fresh profile on this branch (no model, no credentials): Gateway log `agent model: not configured (...)`; `models.list` has no `openai` provider outcome and no refresh failure; `openclaw agent --message "say hi"` and a Control UI `chat.send` both return the setup message; no OpenAI request.
- Before (same mechanism on base and on the published 2026.11.6): `models status` reports `openai/gpt-6-astra` with utility `openai/gpt-6-luna (provider-default)`; the Gateway log shows `agent model: openai/gpt-6-astra`; `models.list` reports `openai: unavailable`.
- Upgrade from the published 2026.11.6 on a scratch profile whose config has no model:
  - with an OpenAI key in the environment, Doctor on this branch writes `openai/gpt-6-astra` as the primary; `models status` matches 2026.11.6; a chat turn runs against `openai/gpt-6-astra` (it fails only on the fake key with OpenAI's 401);
  - without OpenAI credentials, Doctor leaves config unchanged and `models status` reports no default model.
- Doctor migration tests: writes the legacy model for 2026.11.6 configs (including OpenAI listed after another row, and a utility-only row), never without OpenAI credentials, over a configured primary, for a config from a newer release, or when runtime already selects the same provider row; model-selection tests now expect no model instead of `openai/gpt-5.4`; voice-call refuses to invent a response model.
- No-model commands: `/help`, `/status` (shows "Model: not configured") and `/new` run through the real reply pipeline with no model, and a plain message gets the setup message without starting a model run. The new test fails on the previous head and passes here.
- `/status` with no model no longer crashes in the catalog lookup (regression test fails on the previous head).
- Forking a session with no model into a host-only harness still refuses when the creator requires a sandbox.
- Typecheck (core, extensions, and their tests), oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap and mock-export ratchets, and the staged-content guard pass. The CI-failing test files and focused gateway, auto-reply, TUI and changed-plugin suites pass locally.

<details><summary>Known local-only failures (unrelated, reproduce without this change's code paths)</summary>

- `src/plugins/plugin-preparation-exec-argv.test.ts`: `FsSafeError: private Darwin creation requires native descriptor ACL inspection (helper-unavailable)` on this host.
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.boundary.test.ts`: binds `127.0.0.10+` loopback aliases that this macOS host does not have.
- `src/agents/provider-request-header-redaction.test.ts`: failed once inside the full unit shard, passes alone (ordering).

</details>

## Merge danger

One-way door for config: Doctor writes a primary model into existing configs that relied on the implicit default (reverting the code leaves that explicit, equivalent setting in place). Two-way for runtime behavior. Blast radius: installs with no configured model and no Doctor run since update (they get the setup message instead of OpenAI), and third-party plugins that assumed `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` always returns a model (type change; they now receive `undefined`).



### Accepted edge case
Attachment preprocessing (for example audio transcription through a media provider the install has credentials for) runs before the turn's model is resolved, so a model-less turn can still transcribe an attachment before replying with the setup message. I tried gating it on an early guess of the turn's model; review showed the guess is wrong for inherited thread models and per-channel models, and the only correct answer comes from the model resolution that runs later. Reordering preprocessing after model resolution is a larger change than this fix. The case needs no model and usable media credentials at once; installs upgraded from 2026.11.6 with OpenAI credentials get a model from the Doctor migration, so it is rare, visible, and costs one transcription. Docs say so.

### Review follow-ups in this head
- An existing config with no recorded version stays eligible for the implicit-model migration across unrelated saves (it is stamped with the last implicit-model release); a brand-new file starts on the new rules. Regression test fails on the previous head.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject non-decimal tool usage limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The tool-usage CLI accepted hexadecimal and exponent notation as bounded integers, so inputs such as `0x10` and `1e1` could silently select a range even though these options are documented as integer day/count values.

## User Impact

Decimal integer values within the existing bounds continue to work, while non-decimal, fractional, zero, and out-of-range values are rejected before any Gateway request is made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `tools usage import --since` and `tools usage status --limit` now use the shared strict positive-integer parser. The help text keeps readable ASCII ranges, and the parser remains private to the CLI owner.

## Evidence

At head `88332fc3cbd3e0fc54aad7d8b1b20522cd6208bc`, the focused CLI suite passes all 17 tests, including both flags rejecting decimal-looking exponent and hexadecimal inputs before the mocked Gateway call. The shipped CLI also rejects `--since 0x10`, `--since 1e1`, and `status --limit 0x10` with the expected range errors; `tools usage import --help` displays `(1-90)`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, and targeted oxfmt pass.

The repository stores these tracked CLI files with CRLF. `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check` passes; the default check reports the existing CRLF representation as trailing whitespace and is not a semantic whitespace change. Exact-head GitHub checks are pending after the push.

The remaining product question is maintainer-owned: a prior review of the same proposal requested demonstrated user harm before changing acceptance of non-decimal notation. This PR now supplies shipped behavior proof and restores help text, but it cannot make that product decision on behalf of maintainers.

prs.title: fix: keep prompt-history diagnostics accurate between turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On routes that replay transient runtime context, an ordinary next turn can produce a false prompt-history rewrite warning after the previous attempt is disposed. An incomplete diagnostic baseline can also misclassify repeated removal of an old context carrier and miss a simultaneous unrelated history edit.

## User Impact

User impact: normal transient replay is attributed correctly, while unrelated prompt-history edits remain detectable. This changes diagnostic bookkeeping only—not provider prompt bytes, persisted transcripts, tool availability or permissions. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep comparison facts with the existing bounded diagnostic baseline rather than disposable attempt state. Removed-carrier identities travel with their exact converted request in weak metadata, so its first observation receives complete facts without retaining raw payloads or mutating another affinity's baseline.

## Evidence

**Draft: revised complete-range local review remains incomplete.** The initial review finding is reproduced and addressed, but passing regressions do not substitute for the unfinished independent review.

- The original attempt-disposal regression remains green. Two review regressions fail on reviewed snapshot `261df6be184c` and pass after repair: identical repeated carrier removal reports no change; an unrelated history edit still throws.
- Session/affinity isolation, reset, eviction and raw request/message collection pass at the diagnostic owner. Owner/consumer validation passes 91 cases across six files; a final 53-case owner/real-runner run passes after a private callback-parameter rename.
- Real `runEmbeddedAgent` acceptance completes two turns in each of retained and provider-opt-out transient replay modes. Actual outgoing carrier flags prove the selected modes; the existing scripted model fixture performs no network fetches. No live-provider, billing or packaged-binary claim.
- Core and affected test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, assertion/line-budget ratchets and diff checks pass.
- Simplification: the diagnostic observer alone compares baselines; conversion no longer changes every matching affinity's tracker. Whole-change production delta +43/-31; tests +347/-182 (net +165, including formatter indentation in the reused runner fixture).
- The initial full local ClawSweeper review found the first-baseline gap addressed here. The revised complete-range local review did not finish: two attempts on `6f68d50b09b2f65280b4f91bf98107de1a40d745` terminated with a Codex execution failure before producing a complete review. This is not a clean review, and this PR remains draft until that required gate succeeds. Exact published-head CI is also pending.

- On final source `6f68d50b09b2f65280b4f91bf98107de1a40d745`, the required prefix-stability suite passes all 16 tests and both production/full-tree unused-file scans report zero unused files.

Adapted from release-only source repair `2298d4d135e1e9b5c1f77f416e532bffd3e48a6d`; original contributor credit is preserved for RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.

prs.body:
Closes #203371

## What Problem This Solves

If I start on an installed provider plugin’s page, I have to go to Models separately to find its sign-in.

## User Impact

An enabled provider plugin with a guided sign-in has **Sign in** under **Settings → Accounts → Models**. It opens the existing Models dialog with that plugin’s methods.

The provider picker uses the plugin’s labels. The declared method label also supplies the default guided action text, and explicit action-label overrides keep their existing presentation. After guided sign-in, **Choose a model** lets me start a new chat with an available model and keep my current default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin already declares its sign-in methods. OpenClaw can use that metadata for the entry point and the visible action text. Plugins without guided sign-in keep their existing Settings controls.

## Evidence

![GitHub Copilot plugin settings comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2cad13314f90dfc632e8548622fd445333712126/images/2026/11/82b2580b-f9c5-418a-8417-5b25204c0eb9.png)

- In the built Control UI, **Sign in** opened Gemini’s existing dialog with **Sign in with Google** and the action-label override omitted.
- 70 focused tests, UI typechecking, and Swift syntax passed. The tests cover guided label defaults, explicit overrides, and account connection through the OAuth callback. The live Model Setup probe hit a host Codex detection timeout.

prs.title: feat(microsoft-foundry): support typed System One decisions
prs.body:
Related: #155131

## What Problem This Solves

Operators with a Microsoft-Decision-1.1 Foundry deployment cannot select it for OpenClaw's typed Decision evaluations. Foundry chat and image support do not use the System One Decision endpoint.

## User Impact

Operators can select `microsoft-foundry-systemone/microsoft-decision-1.1` for Boolean, Choice, and Score evaluation with text or JSON evidence. They supply a Foundry resource hostname, a deployment alias, and a resource-scoped API-key SecretRef. Chat and image routes and automatic Decision assistance remain unchanged. The Decision route does not yet support images or Entra ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Foundry plugin owns a separate Decision V2 provider identity and credential so the route cannot inherit chat or image credentials. This builds on the Decision infrastructure Vincent Koc helped land in #181574 and reuses the shared System One decoder from the TypeSafe work in #188251. The adapter binds the prepared route to the live credential owner's resource and deployment, then sends one guarded HTTPS POST without redirects, capture, or fallback.

## Evidence

- **Full-build follow-up on [`dd5248aaa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203048/commits/dd5248aaac2cc0ecf7bb7fd1b4b33d7adc38ded2).** Local `pnpm build` (Linux x64, Node 24.22.2, pnpm 12.15.0) completed the Control UI and runtime postbuild, including native loading of 56 built plugin control-plane modules and the doctor closure checks. The full build exited 1 at the public Plugin SDK declaration-size check: **5,406,764 bytes** against a **5,385,536-byte** cap. With the same lockfile and declaration generator, PR merge base [`3dc2ddf1a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3dc2ddf1a2e6eade02e6d73be12bd2e0305a34ee) already measured **5,406,367 bytes** (declarations only; no baseline runtime build). The head is 397 bytes larger, matching the size increase of `decisions-http-runtime.d.ts`. No Azure requests or hosted CI runs for this follow-up.
- **Review follow-up on [`dd5248aaa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203048/commits/dd5248aaac2cc0ecf7bb7fd1b4b33d7adc38ded2).** The SDK guide now describes admission and resource binding as one check at the start of each request. The guarded DNS fixture still verifies that the admitted request can finish and the next request must pass a fresh binding check. Generic HTTP status and caller-cancellation coverage lives in the shared executor; the Foundry suite retains its distinct HTTP 415 mapping, route and credential assertions. All 159 focused tests passed (110 Foundry, 26 shared Decision HTTP, 23 TypeSafe transport; eight files, 106 seconds wall time), plus scoped TypeScript, source-only lint, formatting, docs MDX and diff checks. This follow-up changed only docs and tests. See the full-build follow-up above. No new Azure or hosted CI run was launched.
- **Admission fix, local proof on [`d1fefe287`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203048/commits/d1fefe287833cbdd4e25546867f134b2ea523596).** The shared Decision HTTP executor admits each request once. In the guarded DNS fixture, the started request used the original host, deployment, and synthetic credential after the live deployment changed; the next request with the old binding sent nothing. The SDK regression failed on `cb46332` and passed on `d1fefe287`: the admitted request finishes and the next request reports the authority error. All 163 focused tests passed (114 Foundry, 26 shared Decision HTTP, 23 TypeSafe transport), plus scoped TypeScript, lint, formatting, and diff checks. The local runtime compile and postbuild completed; the build timed out during the Control UI step, so the complete build is unverified. No new Azure request or hosted CI proof on this commit.
- **Live Gateway, two turns on [`cb46332`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203048/commits/cb46332e5c05345685fd4a7cdf3481763cc1b402).** In a fresh OpenClaw 2026.11.6 session, native `decision_evaluate` used the configured System One provider through a Store SecretRef. A synthetic duplicate-charge ticket returned all three V2 types: Boolean `P(true) = 0.9997561537008779`, Choice `billing`, and Score `0.0009255192282724577` on a 0–2 rubric (near the single-customer/no-outage level). A second call in the same session used legacy untagged JSON, the first turn’s `billing` choice, and a synthetic follow-up withdrawing the refund request. It returned `P(refund_still_requested) = 0.000015177557853765349`. Neither Boolean included an explicit `answer`. Both calls reported `microsoft-decision-1.1` and `ok`, with **345 input / 4 output** tokens total. No real ticket or refund action was involved.
- **Earlier local verification on `cb46332` (before the admission fix):** 163 focused tests passed (114 Foundry, 26 shared Decision HTTP, 23 TypeSafe transport), plus scoped typecheck, lint, formatting, and the repository runtime build. A compiled Gateway run through a local TLS proxy returned typed results on one request. The regression test for late caller-admission refusal confirmed no request was sent. The local Nix system build and flake checks passed. The deployed Gateway remained ready, with chat, utility, image, and Talk settings unchanged and automatic Decision assistance off.
- **Scope:** this exercises live credential routing and the response contract with synthetic inputs. It does not establish model accuracy, calibration, comparative latency, coverage of every transport mode, hosted CI, or upstream release qualification.

<details>
<summary>Redacted two-turn session transcript (JSONL)</summary>

The excerpts retain the actual tool arguments, returned results, and assistant replies. They omit the deployment and resource hostname, credentials, private session and run identifiers, duplicate wrapper events, and internal provenance. The ticket is fictional.

```jsonl
{"turn":1,"role":"operator","excerpt":"Run the first half of a live Foundry System One acceptance test for draft openclaw/openclaw #203048. [Private operational context omitted.] Make exactly ONE call to this session's native `decision_evaluate` tool (not HTTP, CLI, subagent, or a simulated answer), contractVersion 2 and tagged JSON state. [The synthetic state and rubric are preserved in the actual tool call below.]"}
{"turn":1,"role":"tool_call","tool":"decision_evaluate","arguments":{"contractVersion":2,"state":{"type":"json","value":{"ticket":"DEMO-104","customerMessage":"I was charged twice for one subscription renewal and want the extra charge reversed.","serviceStatus":"operating normally","customerCountAffected":1}},"questions":{"duplicate_charge_reported":{"type":"boolean","instructions":"Does the customer explicitly report a duplicate charge?","criteria":{"true":"Duplicate charge explicitly reported","false":"Duplicate charge not explicitly reported"}},"destination":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Select the destination for this ticket.","criteria":{"billing":"payments, refunds and invoices","technical":"uptime/bugs","account":"sign-in and identity"}},"severity":{"type":"score","criteria":["single-customer payment problem with no outage","multiple people impacted or a workaround unavailable","service-wide critical outage"]}}}}
```

prs.title: fix(worktrees): protect active owners during conditional cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators cleaning up old session checkouts cannot safely authorize removal from a stale inventory alone. A terminal session can resume without a worktree run lease, and ordinary snapshots omit arbitrary ignored files that non-force Git removal can still delete.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into `--owner-terminal-before <epoch-ms>` (which implies `--if-lossless`). Removal requires a terminal session whose current activity, completion, and checkout activity are no newer than the cutoff, which must be at least 24 hours old. The RPC equivalent is `ownerCleanup: { terminalBefore }` paired with `ifLossless: true`.

This mode intentionally retains ignored files outside snapshot custody, including `node_modules`, collapsed directories, and nested filesystems. This can substantially limit reclamation on existing checkouts; it never falls back to force. Existing seven-day GC and lifecycle cleanup policies are unchanged. This patch adds no database schema/config migration. No deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse existing owner cleanup/mutation fences for the initial claim and final custody check, deletion, and settlement. Controller/placement activity and owner/binding changes stop removal even without a worktree lease.
- Validate custody before pinning an incomplete-removal recovery ref. Preserve nested-repository, hidden-edit, unpublished-work, explicit-protection, and stopped-retry behavior.
- Return the current attempt's structured retention reason without overwriting newer activity. Unknown effects retain recovery custody rather than permitting blind replay.
- Project the existing completion timestamp. Use production binding semantics: the canonical workspace is the source workspace, not necessarily the checkout.
- Keep shared cleanup policy types in the existing leaf contract, avoiding an import cycle and another state/lock owner.

## Evidence

### Regression and static checks

- On exact base `89596c51481e17fb7ba044adfcf44df53567ded4`, the real active-controller-after-listing regression and ignored-only-copy regression both failed because removal returned true. Both pass with the fix.
- All 30 conditional-cleanup tests and 31 CLI tests pass. Coverage includes post-inspection owner/binding/controller/placement/activity changes, both lease-exclusion directions, cutoff equality/recent completion, unreadable/nonterminal owners, ignored dependencies, dirty/unpublished/hidden edits, nested repositories, explicit protections, stopped retries, and cancellation/failure/unknown settlement.
- Existing owner-policy (19), narrow owner-reader (9), protocol-schema (5), RPC (13), and registry/service/removal suites pass, reusing unaffected evidence. Post-delete cancellation rejects the call but durably records completed removal; it does not produce a false retention receipt.
- The public RPC handler, generated validator, real session/placement database, and real Git checkout retain ignored data and then actually remove a repaired eligible checkout (`ENOENT` verified).
- Production typecheck, five affected test type graphs, targeted lint/format, generated-protocol checks, docs checks, line ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass. Generated predicates were regenerated.
- The initial CI import-cycle finding was repaired by moving unchanged shared types into `types.ts`. Madge reports zero cycles; positive RPC and mixed-owner CLI GC integration passed after that type-only repair. Current-head CI architecture, production/test types, lint, docs and protocol checks have passed; overall CI remains a separate gate.

### Latest-stable existing-data upgrade and installed CLI — passed

Official npm `latest`, rechecked November 21, 2026, resolved to `2026.11.6`, source `06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638`. Registry SHA1/SHA512 and all 18,061 installed application-payload files matched the published tarball. The repository's canonical full build/packer produced candidate head `3d79cf4423db8da7ecc618b5560f5e6248e2a28a`; all 19,137 installed payload files matched its tarball after replacement in the same private npm prefix. Candidate SHA256: `eac77e5987f122afd7c114264846308c9bf6110ffe3622df651e9bcccb253343`.

After an initial attempt was blocked by shared workspace ancestor permissions, the operator authorized a separate private 0700 proof root with safe ancestors. Fresh native stable fixtures were seeded there rather than rewriting earlier absolute bindings. HOME/XDG/config/state/cache/temp were pinned to that root using a fresh allowlisted environment without inherited OPENCLAW_/OCM_ overrides. Normal Git checkout was selected through existing `worktreeAcceleration:false` to avoid creating additional undisposable subvolumes.

Native stable writers produced six terminal session bindings, one historical snapshot, both removed-lossless and retained-dirty receipts, and synthetic settings. Native `backup create --verify` succeeded. After installing the candidate, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` completed the supported migration, explicitly reporting agent schema v38 -> v43; no SQL was hand-migrated. The post-upgrade assertions passed:

- all six original session bindings and original settings retained (Doctor added defaults);
- public worktree listing and both pre-existing cleanup receipts preserved;
- historical snapshot Git object unchanged;
- public config read returned the original workspace;
- public `worktrees restore` restored historical tracked bytes;
- eligible public conditional removal actually removed one checkout; absence verified;
- resumed-owner and ignored-only-copy public removals retained their checkout and bytes;
- ignored-file refusal left no pending-removal marker; the dirty fixture remained intact.

Sanitized installed-CLI receipts (timestamps omitted):

```json
{"case":"eligible-after-upgrade","removed":true,"cleanup":{"outcome":"removed-lossless"}}
{"case":"resumed-after-inventory","removed":false,"cleanup":{"outcome":"retained-busy","reason":"owner is unavailable, active, changed, or not terminal and idle before the cutoff"}}
{"case":"ignored-only-copy","removed":false,"cleanup":{"outcome":"retained-busy","reason":"ignored-files: checkout contains files or nested filesystems outside snapshot custody"}}
{"case":"actual-nested-btrfs","removed":false,"cleanup":{"outcome":"retained-busy","reason":"ignored-files: checkout contains files or nested filesystems outside snapshot custody"}}
```

The installed-CLI resumed case proves current persisted owner facts; the active-controller-without-lease race remains separately proven by the native integration regression.

### Actual nested Btrfs public path — passed

Reused the previously created, explicitly owned Btrfs subvolume through a reversible rename into the current-schema fixture, then restored it to its original path. No new subvolume, mount, elevated operation, or binding rewrite was needed. Its inode/device identity and tracked sentinel were checked before and after. Git remained clean; the installed public conditional removal returned `removed:false` with the custody reason above, preserved the sentinel and subvolume, and left no pending-removal marker. An ordinary eligible checkout actually removed in the same upgraded state. Both original directory locations were restored.

### Disclosed proof side effect and remaining cleanup

**Full filesystem isolation is not claimed.** Despite the pinned environment, Doctor reported deleting 27 recognized legacy read-cache files and the empty `/tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache` directory, outside the authorized proof root. The existing `src/flows/doctor-session-archive-cache-check.ts` owner was inspected: it asks `resolveExistingPreferredOpenClawTmpDir()` without the captured proof root and repairs that shared cache. The deleted files' provenance is unknown. No further Doctor run, cache restoration, or unrelated code change was attempted. This off-root effect is recorded separately for operator follow-up; it is not hidden by the successful migration assertions.

The old owned nested Btrfs fixture remains protected at its restored location because its earlier deletion attempt returned EPERM. Only that fixture requires operator-scoped filesystem cleanup; its parent must not be recursively deleted. No additional subvolumes were created in the private proof. No Team access, deployment, service restart, or production database operation was performed. Operational reclamation/adoption remains separate work; one disposable checkout removal is not a Team-space recovery claim.

Remote ClawSweeper's prior review on `1f577fe3469bc65a183fb4ef519fbcb17c6e5a67` found no actionable source defect and requested the upgrade/entry-point evidence now supplied above. Exact-current-head remote review is being requested after this evidence update. Independent local review was explicitly waived. First-head Android JDK-download HTTP403 evidence remains separate from current-head CI.

Author simplification retained one existing owner and no new locks/store. Non-generated production changes are +414/-156; tests are +494/-4. The 91-line allocation above the 400-line test allowance covers distinct real DB/Git/controller boundaries and positive public removal; the native fixture suite takes about 53 seconds. Owner protection and ignored-file custody are the smallest coherent safe cleanup stage and must ship together.

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix: let update cleanup retry preserved database snapshots
prs.body:
Related: #202591

## What Problem This Solves

After a package update, a temporary filesystem denial while removing pre-migration database snapshots can move them away from the location saved in update history. Later `openclaw update cleanup` does not find those copies, even after a newer update succeeds, so they remain on disk without appearing in its report.

## User Impact

Later update cleanup can retry these snapshots once the existing verified-update retention rules allow it. No configuration, schema, permission, dependency, or recovery-policy change is required. Copies already relocated by an older updater remain a manual-inspection case; this change does not guess ownership of those directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a failed snapshot removal at its recorded path in the existing package cleanup owner. Ordinary package and launcher backup retirement remains unchanged, and cleanup continues to apply the existing run-history, pending-recovery, directory-identity, and PostgreSQL-capture checks.

## Evidence

**Required upgrade proof is blocked; this PR remains draft.** The current stable package `2026.11.6` was published on November 19 and is not eligible under the existing seven-day package-age policy until November 26, 2026 at 16:52:13 UTC. The maintained disposable Docker runner is also unavailable in the current validation environment. Neither restriction was changed or bypassed. The published-driver × candidate upgrade cell and subsequent fixed-installed-updater cleanup cell are not passed.

- Full local ClawSweeper committed-range review of `648619c733533fc34bac169b68c10d7d28ff4fcb..bd4dcf15c3bfd39a2c5c9b6066053def07da3514` completed with no correctness or security findings. This was independent source review; executed proof below is recorded separately.
- Exact candidate unused-file analysis passes with no unused files.

- A regression invokes the real package-backup cleanup owner, injects an EACCES at filesystem removal, then invokes the real update cleanup command against synthetic update history. It fails on the unchanged base because the recorded snapshot is absent from the report, and passes with the repair, removing the retained copy.
- 61 tests pass across snapshot cleanup, package swapping, and package filesystem operations; six existing platform-specific cases are skipped. This includes normal package retirement, cleanup authority, protected snapshots, PostgreSQL capture cleanup, and the new retry path.
- Focused production/test-import typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, assertion-safety ratchet, line-cap ratchet, and diff checks pass. No allowance was increased.
- Author simplification retains one cleanup owner: five production lines, one end-to-end regression, and the affected existing expectation updated. No new helper, state, or fallback is introduced.
- Proof uses owned temporary files and actual cleanup code, not a deployed installation. A full published-package upgrade and exact published-head CI have not been run in this worker. The fix must be present in the installed updater performing the failed cleanup; a newer candidate alone cannot repair an older updater's rename.

prs.title: fix(android): activate nearest clickable ancestor for non-clickable labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Android accessibility trees, visible text labels and icons inside a clickable list row or button often do not advertise `ACTION_CLICK` on the child node itself—only the enclosing container row does. When `mobile.ui.act` receives an `Activate` action targeting one of those child label refs, `AccessibilityActionExecutor` fails with `ActionNotSupported` even though a human tapping that label would trigger the row's click handler.

## User Impact

User impact: Mobile UI automation `Activate` actions on a non-clickable label or icon now click its nearest clickable ancestor (up to 8 levels up), matching what a human tap does, while other actions keep strict per-node capability checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded `nearestMatchingAncestor` helper (default `maxDepth = 8`) in `AccessibilityActionExecutor.kt`. When `MobileUiAction.Activate` targets a node without `ACTION_CLICK`, it walks ancestors until it finds the first clickable ancestor, performs the action on that ancestor, and recycles every allocated parent `AccessibilityNodeInfo` in a `finally` block.

## Evidence

- Verified unit tests covering nearest clickable ancestor selection, returning `null` when no ancestor is clickable, and stopping at `maxDepth` (`./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.accessibility.NearestMatchingAncestorTest"`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).

prs.title: fix(android): honor bounded server retryAfterMs reconnect hints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway refuses a connect attempt with a retryable error containing `retryAfterMs` (for example while starting up or backing off), the Android app ignores `retryAfterMs` and reconnects using only its local exponential backoff schedule. That can either retry too aggressively against a busy/starting Gateway or ignore explicit server-side pacing.

## User Impact

User impact: Android reconnects respect server-provided `retryAfterMs` hints (clamped to 1–60 seconds with positive jitter so retries are never shortened below the server's window), while explicit user-initiated reconnects and network-restore retries still interrupt the wait immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parses `error.retryAfterMs` onto `GatewaySession.ErrorShape`, computes `gatewayConnectRetryDelayMs` only for `retryable == true` errors clamped to `1_000..60_000 ms` (with up to +20% jitter capped at 60 s), and waits for `maxOf(gatewayReconnectDelayMs(attempt), gatewayConnectRetryDelayMs(error))` inside the existing `awaitGatewayReconnectSignal` select loop.

## Evidence

- Verified unit tests covering `retryable`-only parsing, 1–60 s bounds, non-shortening jitter, server-delay honoring on connect failure, and immediate interruption by `retryAfterNetworkRestore()` / `reconnect()` (`./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.gateway.GatewayReconnectDelayTest" --tests "ai.openclaw.app.gateway.GatewaySessionReconnectTest.retryableConnectFailureHonorsServerDelayAndExplicitReconnectInterruptsIt"`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).

prs.title: feat(linux): support bootstrap-token pairing and bounded retryAfterMs reconnect pacing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Linux desktop app currently connects only with stored device tokens, shared tokens, or passwords, and reconnects on fixed exponential backoff even when a Gateway returns a retryable `retryAfterMs` hint (for example while starting up or backing off). Users pairing with a one-time setup bootstrap token cannot authenticate with full bootstrap scopes, and reconnecting clients can hammer a busy or starting Gateway instead of respecting its server-provided wait window.

## User Impact

User impact: Linux desktop users can authenticate during setup with a one-time `bootstrapToken` (signing device auth with bootstrap scopes without treating the single-use token as reusable Control UI dashboard auth), and automatic reconnects respect server-provided `retryAfterMs` hints clamped to 1–60 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds `GatewayAuth::BootstrapToken` and `select_auth_with_bootstrap` / `signed_device_with_scopes` so bootstrap-token handshakes send `auth.bootstrapToken`, sign the v3 device payload with `BOOTSTRAP_FULL_SCOPES`, and never reuse the one-time token as a `NativeControlSession` credential.
- Honors `retry_after_ms` on retryable `SharedClientError::Gateway` failures in `reconnect_delay` (clamped between 1 s and 60 s), falling back to existing exponential backoff when no hint is provided.

## Evidence

- Verified `cargo fmt --check` and focused Rust unit tests (`cargo test -- gateway_control_auth gateway_device_identity reconnect_delay_honors_bounded_retry_after_hints connect_params_sign_bootstrap_token_with_bootstrap_scopes`: 22/22 passed, covering bootstrap token wire auth/signatures, auth selection precedence, Control UI refusal of one-time bootstrap tokens, and 1–60 s `retryAfterMs` clamping).

prs.title: fix: preserve caller identity during direct tools.invoke plugin calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin tool that calls back into Gateway methods (such as `github_read`) is invoked directly via `tools.invoke` (RPC or HTTP) outside an active agent run, there is no `GatewayToolCallerIdentity` in async context. The plugin's in-process Gateway call is then rejected as lacking an admitted tool invocation even though the operator was already authorized to invoke the tool.

## User Impact

User impact: Operators and clients calling plugin tools directly through `tools.invoke` get the same scoped caller identity and session tool-surface boundary that an agent run provides, while nested calls inside an existing agent run keep their original caller identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracts `runDirectToolCall` (`src/gateway/tools-invoke-caller.ts`) and wraps direct `tools.invoke` execution with `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity` whenever no active caller identity is already present. The synthetic caller identity stays strictly bounded by the session's resolved tool surface (`assertToolAllowed`), the current invocation's `receiptAuthority`, and the operator's `operatorRunAuthority` and abort signals.

## Evidence

- Verified that a direct `tools.invoke` request for `github_read` outside an agent run succeeds, returns the issue content without leaking credentials, and keeps existing rejection checks for unauthorized direct RPC calls passing (`pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-plugin-github-tool.test.ts`: 23/23 passed).
- `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors) and `oxfmt --check` passed on all touched files.

prs.title: test(android): wait for fixture chat history like sibling layout tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`android-test-play` failed on `main` in scheduled run [44980759580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44980759580/job/137080868008): `ChatMediaTranscriptLayoutTest > captionedPhotosStayReadableBesideTheActualChatComposer` threw `ComposeTimeoutException: Condition still not satisfied after 1000 ms` at `ChatMediaTranscriptLayoutTest.kt:96`, the initial wait for the screenshot-fixture chat history.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The Android Play unit test job stops failing intermittently on this wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wait is timing-dependent, not a product regression: no `apps/android` commit landed between the green scheduled run 44976289659 (3c8c7bf781) and the red one (1eacdff456), and the next scheduled run 44985131982 (ae8155cf5f) passed `android-test-play` again.

In `ScreenshotFixture` mode the chat history loads on `NodeRuntime`'s `Dispatchers.IO` scope and reaches `MainViewModel.chatMessages` / `chatHistoryLoading` through `stateIn(viewModelScope)`, which runs on Android Main. Line 96 used the default 1 s wall-clock `waitUntil` and read the flows without idling Main, so a loaded runner could miss the deadline. prs.title: fix(update): restore WAL journal mode after database rollback
prs.body:
Fixes #202772

## What Problem This Solves

Update rollback restores verified SQLite snapshot images, which are single DELETE-journal files by design. Publishing them without reconciling filesystem policy leaves restored databases in `journal_mode=DELETE` on WAL-policy filesystems. Issue #202772 reports repeated activation Doctor maintenance-lease failures after rollback on official v2026.11.6, resolved by manually restoring WAL mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

After publishing the verified database images, rollback re-establishes WAL policy while existing database exclusions remain held. It uses `openNodeSqliteDatabase` for native admission and the existing WAL owner's journal-mode primitive, without starting checkpoint maintenance. The client credential store is excluded: its exclusive custody design requires DELETE mode, which its restore path verifies. Conversion failures are collected without preventing credential rebinding. Native and supervised callers warn about failed conversions and name the manual recovery without reporting that completed database restoration failed. Original recovery snapshots remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Successful reconciliation restores WAL policy instead of retaining snapshot-only DELETE mode. Credential-store custody semantics are unchanged. If reconciliation fails, restored state and credential recovery are retained, with a visible warning rather than a silent journal-policy mismatch.

## Evidence

Contributor's real update CLI protocol on a scratch `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (Linux, Node 26.12.1): a **v2026.11.6** (`06afb10d32`) gateway created the WAL state; `openclaw update migrate --backup-root` snapshotted 4 databases; `openclaw update restore --backup-root` executed the real rollback.

| Phase | Build | Observation after `update restore` |
|---|---|---|
| RED | v2026.11.6 (unpatched) | `state/openclaw.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"delete"}` |
| GREEN | initial fix (`edfd2dfbeb`) | `state/openclaw.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"wal"}` and `client/credentials.sqlite → {"journal_mode":"delete"}` |

Contributor's initial red/green unit regression: `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/update-database-restore.test.ts`, 24/24 passing at `edfd2dfbeb`. This is prior-head evidence for normal reconciliation, not a claim that the expanded final tests ran in that invocation. Current tests also inject SQLite conversion failures and verify that credential recovery completes before warnings. Test-lines allocation: measured net +80, credit 80.

Maintainer review on November 22, 2026 inspected the complete restore, filesystem policy, credential restore, production callers, tests, and main drift. CI run 44854728160 at `2d71258976290aff0771285f452e3f377d697934` exposed PR-caused raw-SQL, direct SQLite construction, and assertion-safety violations. These were not classified as inherited failures.

Correction `3518797cc69be73bebad8f64bdc7068da1590c24` reuses the existing native-opening and WAL owners, removes duplicate raw SQL and the unchecked assertion, and preserves contributor history. Exact-head CI run 44987208495 confirmed those guardrails pass, but exposed the original ESM-only SQLite mock failing to intercept the createRequire-based owner, plus a redundant type conversion lint violation. Neither was treated as inherited.

Correction `92838225a67549d0a0852fe70d51ec834e45c8af` injects the failure through the shared native SQLite prototype while preserving real restoration and credential recovery; the spy is restored in finally. It removes the obsolete mock and reduces the measured test allocation to 80. Fresh independent exact staged-candidate review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The signed correction is published for secretless fork-CI proof in run 44988447802, with fork approval granted. Review is not test execution; publication alone is not passing proof or merge approval.

Gap: the reporter's macOS/APFS host and live npm-global update loop were not reproduced here. Contributor proof covers Linux supervised migrate/restore and the journal-mode invariant; subsequent Doctor contention is reported in the issue, not independently reproduced by maintainer review.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #202772, locate the rollback restore path in `src/infra/update-database-restore.ts`, and implement the policy-driven journal-mode re-establishment with the credential-store exclusion. The implementer understands the code: restored snapshot images are DELETE-journal by design, the exclusion window makes this process the only holder, and `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` on each restored non-credential database returns it to its pre-snapshot mode. The real runtime observations above are contributor-provided; the final-head maintainer review is separately identified.

prs.title: test(gateway): give run-authority test clients a complete connect handshake
prs.body:
## Problem

Gateway Node shards are red on `main` (scheduled run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44980759580, jobs `checks-node-compact-large-40`, `-41`, and at 3c8c7bf781 also `-8`, `-16`, `-6`). Every PR inherits these reds and has to triage them. 14 tests fail in 6 files:

- `server.sessions.create.lifecycle.test.ts` (4), `server.sessions.create.authority.test.ts` (2), `server.sessions.create-notices.test.ts` (1)
- `server-methods/question.test.ts` (4), `server-methods/session-catalog-gateway-copy.test.ts` (1)
- `talk/handlers/index.test.ts` "role-required Talk session creation" (2)

All fail with `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'client.connect.client.id')`, which the handlers return as `FORBIDDEN`.

## Root cause

#203357 (e76922592a73) added `clientId: client.internal?.syntheticClient ? undefined : client.connect.client.id` in `captureGatewayOperatorRunAuthority` (`src/gateway/operator-run-authority.ts:621`). Production is correct: `GatewayClient["connect"]` is the handshake `ConnectParams`, where `client` is required, and every real or spread client carries it. The failing fixtures built a partial `connect` (`{ scopes }` or `{ role, scopes }`) and hid the missing `client` with `as never` / `as GatewayWsClient["connect"]` casts. #203357 fixed one such fixture (`question.own-run.test.ts`) but not these.

## Fix

Build those fixture connects with the existing shared `gatewayConnect()` test fixture (`src/gateway/server/client-fixtures.test-support.ts`), so they are complete handshakes. Test-only change, no production code, net −3 lines.

## Evidence

- Base `origin/main` 6375a3690778: `ocx test` on the 6 files: 14 failed / 185 passed, 4 unhandled `client.connect.client.id` rejections.
- Head: same command, `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 192 passed (192)`.
- `pnpm check:test-types` passes; oxlint/oxfmt clean on changed files.
