prs.title: feat: unlink an OpenClaw ID claw from its own computer
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-281 (part 1), sub-issue OCF-601. The protocol part (#201750) has landed; this PR is now based on main.

## What Problem This Solves

An owner can't take a claw off OpenClaw ID. Members, owner devices and the claw's address stay live, and there is no way to retire the name.

## User Impact

On the computer that runs the claw, `openclaw id unlink` and **Unlink from OpenClaw ID** in the account menu end the claw's link for good. Before anything happens, the owner sees:

- how many people and devices lose access, as live counts from the Gateway;
- that the address stops working at once;
- that the name can never be used again, by any account.

Every owner device, member, member device, node and invite is removed. Remote sessions close, tunnel-bound tokens are revoked and the tunnel stops. Conversations and everything else on the computer stay, and the claw keeps working locally. Over the tunnel the action is not shown, and the Gateway refuses it (`not_local_operator`).

If Discovery can't be reached, the claw is still unlinked locally. The Gateway keeps the signed unlink and sends it when Discovery answers, also after a restart. `openclaw id status` shows `Unlink pending` until then.

The Unlink action needs only this computer's Gateway key, so it is offered on direct loopback even when the browser is signed out of OpenClaw ID (for example after the account session expired or browser storage was cleared). It is still never shown over the tunnel.

A claw that never sent its registration to Discovery (for example because Discovery was down when it was linked) has no address to retire. Its unlink completes locally: nothing stays pending, the CLI exits 0 and the result is `discovery: "local_only"`, without claiming a name was retired. Once a registration has been sent, Discovery may hold the claw even if the answer never arrived, so the unlink is sent and kept pending as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **The unlink is bound to the warning.** The client sends the previewed `clawId`, and a claw that changed in between is refused with `claw_changed`.
- **Unpublished keys block it.** A move to new keys that Discovery hasn't confirmed is refused with `binding_unpublished`, because Discovery only accepts an unlink for the binding it stores.
- **Never registered is decided locally, not from Discovery's answer.** Linking records that no registration has been sent. A publication that carries a link code (the only kind that registers) marks it sent in the authority's serialized lane, the same lane as the unlink, after Discovery reports no registration and before it registers. So an unlink either sees the mark (and stays pending) or comes first (and the mark fails for the unlinked claw, so nothing is sent). A publication without a code, or a rebind's registration check, never marks it. Reading Discovery's `not_found` to the unlink as "never registered" was rejected: a registration in flight, or aborted on the client but already received, can land after that answer.
- **A refusal isn't reported as success.** Only Discovery's success or `unlinked` answer counts as confirmed. Any other 4xx is kept as refused (shown in status, never resent), and the result says `refused`.
- **Follow-up steps run independently.** After the commit, the Discovery send, the session teardown and the remote-access restart each run whether or not the others fail. The Discovery send starts first, so a browser that re-checks Discovery when its tunnel closes usually already sees `unlinked`.
- **Late progress can't revive the old claw.** Publication and mailbox progress that lands after the unlink is dropped for the old claw id.

Re-linking makes a new claw (new claw id, new name, no members).

Design choices not covered by the decisions:

- The claw record starts over under a new claw id instead of keeping the old authority record for re-linking.
- The resend uses the publication retry's backoff (2 s to 5 min).
- A Discovery refusal is final and is not resent.

Overlaps: #201734 (OCF-595 close reason) and the sign-out work (OCF-593) touch `remote-signout.ts`, `removal-effects.ts` and the close-code map; this PR does not edit them. Rebind actions moved into `server-methods/openclaw-id-machine.ts` unchanged; #201587 (owner reset) adds a file with the same name and purpose and will need a trivial merge.

## Evidence

### Sender lifecycle repair (2026-11-21)

ClawSweeper's exact-head review of `22c136d1` found a P2: when Discovery accepts a connection but never answers, the runtime restart during unlink resumed the sender, which forced a second full 30-second pass into the committed unlink's reply and could push the CLI past its 60-second RPC timeout after the unlink had already committed. Fixed in `34a22a5e`:

- Lifecycle resumption (`start`) joins an active run without extending it and keeps the retry backoff. A newly committed unlink uses `flush`, which still asks an active run for a follow-up pass so newly queued statements go out.
- Each run tries each claw's statement once, so a flush that joins a lifecycle pass does not resend the same stalled statement; failures still arm the retry.
- `service.unlink.test.ts` reproduces the stall through the real service and Discovery client: it fails on the previous sender with a duplicate send before the reply, and passes now. `pending-unlink.test.ts` covers a statement queued during an active pass and a lifecycle resume keeping the backoff.
- Gateway OpenClaw ID suite: 69 files, 460 passed, 13 skipped. Core types, focused type-aware lint, format, line-cap and test-lines ratchets pass. Test-lines allocation is now 592. An independent Astra review of the commit found no P0–P2 issues.
- **Studio live proof on this head passed 27/27** (integration `36c0775b6abf`, same OpenClaw ID sources as the PR head): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201779#issuecomment-7074437264

### Latest endpoint-key review repairs (2026-11-21)

Current-head CI run [44948084204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44948084204): `checks-ui (1/3)` fails the unrelated Spanish settings-search assertion (`modelo` returns three blocks instead of two after Code Mode moved out of Labs). The same assertion and extra “Modo de código” block fail on main CI run [44940901144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44940901144/job/136958010708). This PR does not change settings search or Spanish locales; those files are unchanged between the recorded failing main and this run’s main baseline `20ef309e`. This failure is not marked green; other checks and final review remain separate gates.

- Local Unlink remains available when only the endpoint key is refused; it stays hidden for a refused or unspecified Gateway key. The account-menu regression failed without the fix and passed with it (26/26 tests).
- Unlink creates a new claw identity. The tunnel endpoint pin now follows the claw identity, so a confirmed unlink releases the old key pin and permits linking again without restarting the Gateway. Pending and uncertain writes for the same claw retain the pin.
- The regression reads the endpoint pin after persistence but before acknowledgement, then forces uncertain storage withdrawal. It fails against the earlier repair and passes now. All four bound-endpoint tests and all 458 Gateway OpenClaw ID tests pass; 13 skipped.
- Core types, type-aware lint, formatting, import cycles, source line caps and test-lines checks passed locally. The two Astra passes identified the endpoint restart defect and the in-flight-write race; both were reproduced and repaired. No clean Astra review of the final revision is claimed. Fresh current-head ClawSweeper review and CI have been requested. The extended Studio live proof passed **27/27**, including missing-endpoint-key UI unlink and relinking without a further Gateway restart: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201779#issuecomment-7069105871


- Tests pass for the Gateway OpenClaw ID suite (69 files, 458 passed, 13 skipped), the CLI unlink and `openclaw id` commands, the account menu, the unlink dialog and the machine-action handler. New tests:
  - `service.unlink.test.ts`: tunnel refusal; live counts, wipe and Discovery's verified ClawUnlink; the pending unlink across a restart; `unlinked` treated as done; a refusal kept as refused; a failing teardown step; late publication progress; status after re-linking; `claw_changed`; `binding_unpublished`.
  - `pending-unlink.test.ts`: backoff, refusal, `unlinked`, stop/start.
  - `id-cli-unlink.test.ts`, `unlink-dialog.test.tsx`, `openclaw-id-machine.test.ts`.
- tsgo (core and ui), oxlint (type-aware), format, docs format, Control UI i18n, and the assertion-safety, max-lines, timeout-race, mock-exports and test-lines ratchets pass.
- Review repair tests (ClawSweeper findings on `c5bb854ca2d7`):
  - `account-menu.test.tsx`: a signed-out local operator on a linked claw gets **Unlink from OpenClaw ID**; not on an unlinked claw, not over a non-loopback connection, not over the tunnel.
  - `service.unlink.test.ts`: a claw that never sent its registration unlinks as `local_only` without contacting Discovery, with nothing pending and an empty link summary; one that sent it stays pending while Discovery is unreachable; an unlink racing a registration request in flight is not `local_only` (fails without the mark); a publication without a link code leaves the claw never-registered, and an unlink during the registration lookup stops the registration (fails if the mark is taken without a code).
  - `id-cli-unlink.test.ts`: `local_only` output and exit 0, `pending` exit 0, `refused` exit 2, and the `Unlink pending` status line.
  - `unlink-dialog.test.tsx`: the `local_only` toast.
- **Data-model compatibility:** `claw-store.persistence.test.ts` writes the v2 claw rows a Gateway stored before this PR (no `pending_unlinks`, no `registration_unsent`, built independently of the current row writer) into the real shared state database and reopens it. The upgraded Gateway previews and unlinks that claw. Because the old record can't say whether a registration was sent, the unlink stays pending (the safe default), survives a database reopen, and a restarted service sends and clears it. Both new fields are optional on the existing `current` row; no existing field or row changes.
- Test-lines allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-claw-unlink.txt` (592). Unlinking permanently wipes membership and retires a name, so each failure path has its own test.
- Review repair autoreview (isolated Astra reviews): two rounds found races in treating Discovery's `not_found` as final (a registration in flight or aborted on the client could land later). The repair was redesigned around the local registration mark above. A third round found two more P2s in the first version of the mark (it was taken without a link code, and could fail silently for a claw no longer linked while a new one was published); both were fixed. The final review of the repair found no P0–P2 issues. It noted one interleaving it judged unreachable in practice: a full unlink and a new link ceremony would have to finish between registration recovery and the record re-read that follows it.
- Autoreview (isolated Astra review): no P0. Six findings (five P1, one P2) were verified and fixed in `fix(openclaw-id): bind unlink to the warned claw and keep refused unlinks`: binding to the warned claw, publication racing the unlink, refusal reported as confirmed, follow-up steps, sender stop/start, status after re-linking.
- **Live proof (23 of 23 steps passed):** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201779#issuecomment-7010058386
  - First run on `c5bb854ca2d7`. **Earlier rerun on 2026-11-21, 23 of 23 passed**, before the latest endpoint-key repairs: the Gateway, CLI and Control UI were built from `0e27b7fe372f` (main `a40174b7` merged with this PR at `6e5894ed`, #201734 and #201759), with Discovery at openclaw/discovery#22 `894a08cf` and the loader at openclaw/claw-loader#47 `157424e7`, in a Crabbox `local-container` lease on the Mac Studio. That run covers the review repair commits. That run does not cover the subsequent endpoint-key menu and pin repairs; a new Studio proof passed 27/27 on integration commit `5f726c80112f` with those repairs (`bbfaa054aab2`). The current PR head differs from that repair only by moving a doc comment back to its function.
  - Setup: an isolated test container. The Gateway at `c5bb854ca2d7`, Discovery from openclaw/discovery#22 (`wrangler dev`, local D1) and the loader from openclaw/claw-loader#47 were built in the container. iroh-relay used Discovery admission.
  - Claw A, unlinked with the CLI: the warning showed live counts and the decline changed nothing.
  - Claw B, unlinked from the Control UI dialog.
  - After each unlink:
    - relay admission refused every key;
    - Discovery answered `410 unlinked` and the listings dropped the claw;
    - the member's and the owner's loaders showed the final state;
    - the Gateway held no members or devices, and the remote tokens were revoked;
    - the conversation survived.

prs.title: fix(update): name the working Gateway recovery after a shipped pnpm updater leaves it stopped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a shipped updater (2026.11.4 through 2026.11.6) updates a pnpm install to a fixed release and leaves the Gateway stopped, nothing names the recovery that works. Instead, users are sent to `openclaw triage`, which needs an interactive terminal, or to generic reinstall advice.

That state is real. A same-schema hop, for example 2026.11.5 or 2026.11.6 to a release with #201735, ends `service-revalidation-failed` (exit 1). The `openclaw` command works, because the new package's Doctor repairs the launcher. The Gateway stays down, because the service still names the previous version's pnpm store directory. The installed updater cannot be patched.

## User Impact

User impact: in that state, three places name the verified recovery: `openclaw gateway install --force`, then `openclaw gateway restart`.
- During the update, the new package's Doctor prints one sentence: "If this updater leaves the Gateway stopped, run `openclaw gateway install --force` and then `openclaw gateway restart`." It promises no automatic finish.
- Afterwards, `openclaw update status` gives the pair as its next step instead of "Run `openclaw triage`".
- `openclaw gateway status --deep` gives the pair in its installation-drift line instead of the generic reinstall advice.

`openclaw gateway restart` alone fails in this state, so the two commands are always named together. Nothing changes for npm installs, for fixed updaters, or for services this installation does not own.

## Why This Change Was Made

One module, `src/cli/update-cli/update-refused-restart-recovery.ts`, decides the state. It holds only on macOS or Linux, when the managed service this pnpm installation owns and may rewrite still names another version's package in the same pnpm home. A pruned previous entry counts. The state is read from the live service, never from the stored run alone.

- **Doctor gate.** The gate is extracted from the parked draft #201906 without its waiter or spawn. It also requires the shipped updater's no-repair flags and a single running update run whose live driver is the run-id match or this Doctor's ancestor. Doctor consults it only after it repaired a launcher that still named the updater's removed stage. That staged launcher is what tells a shipped updater from a fixed one; the version cannot, because fixed and unfixed builds share version lines.
- **`update status`.** This is commit `d3a4edd` from #201906, narrowed to the shared decision. It applies only while the Gateway health probe reports it unavailable.
- **`gateway status --deep`.** It uses the same reader. It checks only when the service is stopped, after the deep database preflight, and with the preflight's environment. A failed read leaves the old advice unchanged.
- **Docs.** `docs/install/updating.md` no longer claims that these updaters always hand the restart to the new package.

`openclaw triage --run --update-result <path>`, the command the shipped updater's failure text names, is unchanged. In the failed state without a terminal, it writes a debugging prompt and a sanitized diagnostics bundle, prints "No repair agent was started", says that embedded triage needs an interactive terminal, and exits 1.

**Update behavior:** the new text runs from the new package, as Doctor during the shipped updater's run and as the CLI afterwards. Shipped updaters are unchanged. It applies as one commit on `release/2026.11.7` (#203401) and `release/2026.11.10` (#201740).

**Steps still left to a person:** the two commands. The shipped updater cannot be patched, and the automatic restart in #201906 failed in real runs. The commands are now named where the user looks. Triage cannot run them without a terminal.

## Evidence

Unit (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-refused-restart-recovery.test.ts`, 22 tests). The cases use a real update-run ledger and real pnpm layouts on disk, with the live service read injected:
- The Doctor note prints only for these cases: the shipped switch, a pruned previous entry, a tarball candidate and a pnpm 11.28 group store. It is silent for a non-ancestor driver, a dead driver, an npm install, a service outside pnpm, a service in another pnpm home, a service already on this package, a service not owned, an unwritable definition, and a Doctor allowed to repair services. A failed service read is reported on the diagnostic channel only.
- `update status` and `gateway status --deep` name the pair for the refused state and a pruned entry only. They do not name it for another failure reason, the current package, another pnpm home, an unowned service or an npm install. The rendered report ends with the pair and no longer mentions triage. The drift line replaces the generic advice only when the step is known.
- Mutations go red. Dropping the same-home check fails the two "another pnpm home" cases. Dropping the drift-line override fails the formatter case. Consulting the gate without the staged-launcher marker failed the fixed-updater case in an earlier revision; that marker now lives in Doctor and is covered by the real fixed-updater cell.

Real cells are running: published 2026.11.5 → the 2026.11.7 backport (#203401) with and without this commit on pnpm 12 and 11.28, plus npm and fixed-updater controls. Results follow.

## Not proven

- Results of the real cells (in progress).
- Windows and real launchd: the recovery is verified on Linux only. Windows gets no sentence.

prs.body:
## Problem

`build-artifacts` is red on `main`: the `pnpm validators:check` step fails with

```
Error: packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js is stale; run pnpm gateway:validators:gen
```

Scheduled run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44980759580 (job 137080867330), and earlier https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44976289659.

## Root cause

#203357 (`fix(ui): show app updates outside the conversation`, e76922592a73) added two optional fields to the update-run schema in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/update-runs.ts`:

- `noticeSurface: Type.Optional(Type.Literal("app"))`
- `noticeInApp: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean())`

It did not regenerate the compiled gateway validators, so `predicates.js` no longer matches the schema.

## Fix

Regenerate with the owning script: `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`. No hand edits. The diff adds the two fields to the generated predicates; the rest is check-id renumbering from the generator.

## Evidence

- Base `origin/main` (6375a3690778): `pnpm gateway:validators:check` fails with the error above.
- Head: `pnpm validators:check` (gateway, ui, codex-app-server, static, lobster) exits 0. The other four sub-checks were already fresh on base.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Generated validator output only; a revert restores the stale file. Blast radius: Gateway protocol validation of update-run payloads, which now accepts the two optional fields the schema already declares.

Related: #191138

## What Problem This Solves

Shared-source sessions can be missing from “Owned by me” and “Involving me” because filtering a downloaded page cannot find matches on later source pages. Selection must happen before source pagination and survive opening or importing the selected session.

## User Impact

Supporting sources apply the requested owner/involvement query before pagination. Unsupported or unapproved sources show guidance instead of silently retrying unfiltered. Local-provider behavior and source-owned publication boundaries remain intact. Nothing is enabled, configured, deployed or restarted by this PR.

Setup requires source advertisement and approval, receiver command allowlists, and the existing source publication/device grants. The optional Open-original command must be allowed separately. A verified numeric GitHub account selects a canonical source profile; unknown or ambiguous mappings fail explicitly. Identity selects the query; it does not grant authority. Existing source groups, publication-person restrictions, device grants, and read/disclosure checks govern access.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the existing replacement for Vincent Koc's original draft #191138, not another replacement. It carries an advertised relationship query through list, read, scoped cursor, navigation and import. It preserves the landed Open-original change (#203044, `95418cdd78d0689fee291d6d0e6b74990937258c`), optional filtered source links, and attribution.

The follow-up fixes current-main conflicts, readonly config typing, unfiltered cache sharing, relationship-change lifecycle and stale fixtures. It reuses existing selection/catalog owners without a revocation epoch. Catalog continuation stays behind the existing lazy runtime import and remains private. Duplicate URL parsing and intermediate projections were removed; late key resolution, optional-field semantics and relation cloning are preserved. The browser test asserts unsupported-filter guidance by accessible name rather than racing the existing tooltip's native-title clearing.

prs.title: fix: keep profile-selected Gateways on their own state databases
prs.body:
Closes #202585

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway started for a named profile (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=work`) without an explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` opens the default profile's databases under `~/.openclaw`: its health snapshot reads the default shared state database, and `tools.invoke` reads the default `main` agent database. It also leaves SQLite `-wal`/`-shm` files there. One profile's Gateway is supposed to touch only its own `~/.openclaw-<profile>` state.

## User Impact

User impact: a profile's Gateway stays on its own state databases. The workaround of also setting `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` is no longer needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session and status readers pin the state directory through `captureSessionTranscriptStorageEnvironment`, which first copies only the storage-routing variables and then resolves the state directory from that copy. The copy kept `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` but not `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, so a profile chosen by name resolved to the default `~/.openclaw`. The profile now stays in that copy. The helper still returns only the pinned `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (and the supervisor mode), so captured bindings and their comparisons are unchanged.

The plugin metadata fingerprint key list also omits the profile and is left alone: it is a cache key within one process, not a path resolver.

## Evidence

Full-product check through the built CLI (`openclaw.mjs` of a built tree, Linux container). The setup creates default-profile state with a short default Gateway run, then starts `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=p202585 openclaw gateway run --port 19789` and sends `gateway call tools.invoke` (`web_search`), the step from the report. While that runs, every process's open files are polled for paths under the default `~/.openclaw`, and the default folder is listed before and after.

### Full-product repro on main

main `1c6349de440`, 22 Nov 2026:

```text
B: profile state dir: /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw-p202585
B: default-dir opens: 7
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw-quarantine.sqlite
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-shm
   pid=15354 openclaw-gateway -> /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-wal
RESULT B default_files_changed:
  > /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm
  > /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal
  > /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-shm
  > /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-wal
```

A stack capture on the same build traced the opens to the Gateway health snapshot (`createStatusSessionStoreReader`) and to `tools.invoke` tool construction (session entry read for the sandbox status). Both get the state directory from `captureSessionTranscriptStorageEnvironment(process.env)`, and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` was still set in the process when the default paths were built.

### Live run with this change

Same run on this head: no opens under the default folder, and its files are unchanged.

```text
B: profile state dir: /tmp/p202585-home/.openclaw-p202585
B: default-dir opens: 0
RESULT B default_files_changed:
```

With no default state at all, neither build creates `~/.openclaw`.

### Tests

`src/config/sessions/transcript-target-binding.test.ts`: the new case (`HOME` plus `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=work` resolves to `.openclaw-work`) fails on main with `.openclaw` and passes with this change. The existing cases pass.

Test lines are net +7 against `main`: one case pins the profile-selected state directory, which the existing environment-capture table does not cover.

Proof artifice: the live run watches open files with a polling loop, and `web_search` has no provider configured, so the call answers "Tool not available"; the database opens happen while the Gateway prepares the tool list, before that answer. The stack capture used a temporary preload hook and is diagnosis only.

Not covered: the macOS LaunchAgent route from the report was not run. The failing path above is platform-independent, and the report's install had neither `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` nor `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` set, the same as this run.

prs.title: fix(update): recognize pnpm 11 group-local virtual stores as global installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On pnpm 11, OpenClaw's own updater installs the new package into the group's local virtual store, with `.pnpm` directly under the group:

`<PNPM_HOME>/global/v11/<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>_…/node_modules/openclaw`

A real pnpm 11.28.13 cell (published 2026.11.5 → plain `openclaw update` → public 2026.11.6) produced exactly that layout. pnpm 12 uses `<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/…`.

pnpm layout inference in `src/infra/update-global.ts` only recognized the pnpm 12 form. A pnpm 11 install addressed by its real path was therefore classified as an unmanaged `package-root`, with three effects:
- An update or Gateway `update.run` started with that root is refused (`unmanaged-package-install`).
- Doctor and Control UI detection report the install as unmanaged.
- The refreshed Gateway service definition pins the per-version `<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@…/dist/…` path (`src/daemon/program-args.ts:81-99`) instead of the stable `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw` entry. pnpm removes that directory on the next update.

## Root Cause

`inferPnpmProjectRoot` (`src/infra/update-global.ts`) accepted only `node_modules/.pnpm`. For the pnpm 11 form it took the project to be `<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@…`, so it never reached the `v11` global root.

## Fix

The same matcher now accepts both `<project>/node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>/node_modules/openclaw` and `<project>/.pnpm/<pkg>/node_modules/openclaw`. No second matcher was added. The `.pnpm` branch of `inferPnpmGlobalRootFromPackageRoot` already runs the isolated-root check first, so it needed no change.

`resolvePnpmGlobalInstallOwner`, which the program-args refresh uses, now finds the active entry, and the saved service definition names the stable `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw` path.

`rewritePnpmVersionedOpenClawEntryPath` (`src/infra/openclaw-root.ts:10-19`) is unchanged. For grouped layouts it can only yield the per-group `<group>/node_modules/openclaw`, which is not stable on pnpm 12 either. The stable entry comes from the argv launcher root and the owner lookup.

The shared-store guard is kept. A real path inside the shared content store, `store/v11/links/@/openclaw/<v>/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw`, still does not count as the install owner, and a test now asserts this with that realistic path.

## User Impact

- pnpm 11 global installs are recognized as pnpm installs when addressed by their real path.
- After an update, the Gateway service definition names the stable entry, so the next update does not leave the service pointing at a removed directory.

**Update behavior:** this is a fix in the new package's own detection. It applies when this code is the running updater, Gateway or Doctor. Shipped updaters keep their behavior.

## Evidence

Each unit case was red on the base where marked, then green:
- `src/infra/update-global.bun-owner.test.ts`, "detects a pnpm v11 install by its real path in the `node_modules/.pnpm` / `.pnpm` virtual store". The `.pnpm` case failed on the base (`{kind: "package-root", mode: "unknown"}`) and passes now. It covers detection, `resolveUpdateInstallSurface` and `resolveTarget`.
- Negative controls in the same file, green:
  - an application image's `app/.pnpm`;
  - `app/node_modules/.pnpm`;
  - a stale `v11` group with no active link and no lockfile, which stays unmanaged (removing the lockfile requirement turns it red);
  - the shared-store real path, which stays `package-root`;
  - npm and Bun globals, unchanged.
- `src/daemon/program-args.pnpm.test.ts`, the systemd case over both virtual-store forms. The `.pnpm` case failed on the base with ENOENT, because the saved entry pointed at the removed per-version directory. Now the saved path is `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw`, and after the old group is deleted it still resolves to the replacement version's files. The test reads the files through the saved path; it does not start the service.
- `src/infra/update-launcher-repair.test.ts`, a pnpm 11.28.13 shim captured from the real cell, with no `PNPM_HOME` and the root set to the `.pnpm` real path. It passes on the base too, and fails if the `/global/v\d+/` home marker is broken.

Checks:
- touched and adjacent tests pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`);
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass;
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean, and both import-cycle checks report 0;
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes and `git diff --check` is clean.

Real-cell evidence of the pnpm 11 layout and the shipped failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7019905738

### Real pnpm 11 update onto main with this commit

Published `openclaw@2026.11.5` was installed from the public registry with `pnpm add -g` on pnpm 11.28.13. pnpm was pinned on PATH and at `PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm`, which the updater prefers. The Gateway ran as a managed service under the harness's systemd user shim, with a 256 MiB agent database and a busy writer. A plain `openclaw update --tag <this head's package tarball>` followed (head `d80ed4b`, labeled 2026.11.19-beta.2).

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `openclaw update` | exit 0, `ok`, 155 s |
| `openclaw --version` | `OpenClaw 2026.11.19-beta.2 (d80ed4b)` |
| Launcher | `exec node "${basedir_abs}"/../global/v11/9440847f…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` |
| Gateway | serving the new version, readyz true; `gateway status --deep`: running, connectivity ok |
| Service unit | `…/store/v11/links/@/openclaw/2026.11.5/…` → `$PNPM_HOME/global/v11/9440847f…/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`, the stable entry rather than the per-version `<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@…` directory |
| Schema agent/state | 38/36 → 43/41 (migrated) |
| Outage (load probe) | 78 s |
| Disk per directory (peak / left) | pnpm home +1759 / +1095 MiB; captures +270 / 0 MiB; update temp +1180 / +670 MiB |

For comparison, on the 2026.11.7 backport without this commit (#203401), the pnpm 11 service ends up naming the per-version `global/v11/<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@file+…/node_modules/openclaw` directory after `openclaw gateway install --force`.

Recording:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a022035e-12ca-444b-89c7-ed4eb44dbbe0

### Cherry-pick for the release line

This is one self-contained commit. It applies cleanly onto `release/2026.11.6` (stacked on #201739) and `release/2026.11.10` (#201740 merged with the current release tip). On each, the touched tests pass (45) and `pnpm tsgo:core` passes. It will be added to those backports as a separate commit after this PR has its final head.

## Not proven

- A second update from the state above, and the same hop on main without this commit, are running; results follow.
- The Control UI half is not in this PR: a Gateway whose root is the pnpm 12 store-link real path is still classified `package-root`. That is a separate PR at the Gateway's root owner, because it has to handle several global groups linking the same store directory.

## Steps left to a person

None for this change.


## Review notes

- ClawSweeper round 1 (C / C / B) found that the `pnpm11-grouped` native-stage case built its launcher from the `.pnpm` entry, so it stayed green with the group link broken, and it also passed on the base. It is removed in `ea871a4`; the detection, service-path and launcher-repair cases cover the layout. It also asked for an accurate description of the systemd case, which the Evidence section now gives.

prs.title: fix: reject cross-conversation automation workspaces before saving
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent-created automation could save an existing conversation as its execution target even when that conversation had a different saved workspace. Every scheduled run then failed before model startup. This also affected conversations owned by the same person.

## User Impact

Unsupported cross-conversation workspace targets now fail when saving or enabling the automation, with instructions to create it from the intended target conversation instead. Existing invalid jobs can still be paused, renamed, or removed. Own-conversation continuations, unbound named sessions, and operator-created jobs keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation-scoped workspace restriction is intentional: selecting a session or sharing a human owner does not delegate its filesystem authority. The Gateway now reuses the execution-time authority decision while validating the persisted target row on create, retarget, executable edits, and enable. The runtime backstop remains authoritative if the target acquires a binding later. No authority grants, stored job schema, or live schedules are changed.

Author simplification review retained the existing target validator and authority owner, with no new policy store or delegation mechanism. Whole-change delta: production +43/-11, tests +52/-7, docs +11 lines.

## Evidence

- Original workspace security suite: 12 passing cases, including the save-then-fail reproduction.
- New create-time regressions were red on the base: both foreign-owner and same-owner targets incorrectly returned a saved job instead of an actionable rejection.
- Fixed workspace suite: 14 passing cases, including create/retarget/enable/executable-edit rejection, legacy pause/rename, runtime backstop, own workspace, unbound target, operator target, managed-worktree confinement, archival, and reset.
- Gateway validation and ownership suites: 158 passing tests.
- Scoped cron test typecheck, four-file lint, changed-file format check, docs MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed.

Focused command:
```text
pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-workspace-authority.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Wall time: 102.33s across two shards; the workspace file took 42.03s because it exercises real agent tools, Gateway handlers, scheduler/session admission, filesystem confinement, managed-worktree leases, and lifecycle behavior rather than mocked policy decisions. Model execution alone is synthetic. No live Gateway or model call was performed; this remains the product-flow evidence limitation.

Exact-head CI for `af51465d93f866711053f9a79ecacc3aa330e925` completed successfully: the pinned native CI watcher reported `GREEN` for run 44986442737, with the GitHub aggregate rollup `SUCCESS`. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful.

Local independent/autoreview was explicitly waived for this task; author self-review was completed. Remote ClawSweeper review completed on the same head with no actionable findings and no before-merge items (comment 7074407672). It noted the live product-flow evidence limitation above. No source changes were needed after review.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: refactor(gateway): admit saved requesters once when work starts
prs.body:
hint: if you need to wait for this pull request to be reviewed, merged, or closed before continuing, use this instead of polling:
    gh event listen --resource https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202513 --event com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1,com.github.pull_request.state.changed.v1
  - It prints the first event as a JSON line on stdout and exits; run it again to wait for the next one.
  - Add `--timeout` to stop waiting after a while, for example `--timeout 30m`; it then exits with status 8.
  - Events carry no details; read the pull request to see what changed.
  - It misses changes made before it starts, so read the pull request once it is running.
  - See `gh event listen --help` for other event types.
  - Event subscriptions are in preview and may not be enabled for your account.
## Problem

Saved operator work duplicated admission and carried permission checks into started runs. Serialization limits must not lose accepted work, and a live source must not acquire unrelated credential or resident-profile dependencies.

## Fix and behavior

Saved, queued, continuation and recorded sandbox operator starts call async `prepareOperatorAdmission` and synchronous `decideOperatorAdmission`. The decision uses prepared owners and committed config, freezes current profile/access/role/model/admin facts, and checks the actual runtime target agent against the role's agent ceiling. Restore's hand-built credential branches, reference counts, chat-deletion subscription and permission re-check closures are deleted.

- Live-only sources carry existing authentication, pairing, ingress and scope evidence in memory, independently of durable codec bounds. Canonical profile-backed live sources check that the profile still exists and re-read current role, without requiring every email binding; host-issued opaque grants with no canonical identity binding keep their issued role facts at the next same-process start, as on main. Credential/device/ingress/scope/target checks still apply. `canonicalIdentity` is required: an actual canonical profile binding or explicit `null` for a host-issued opaque grant. Production producers cannot omit it. No canonical profile is invented or newly required for an opaque grant; profile-not-found maps to the existing visible refusal type.
- Live paired devices require the same ID/key and no revocation. Their scopes use the handshake device ceiling union current identity grants, including OCID; saved Gateway facts additionally use current paired/token scopes and approved operator role. Device-less proxy/Tailscale scopes use the current grant.
- Remote ingress has no unrelated shared-generation dependency. Existing binding abort and scope ceiling are read at start; no identity index, subscription or callback is added. Capture pairing reads remain tokenless proxy/Tailscale only; failure preserves the live request without inventing device evidence.
- Disabled OCID visibly refuses; unpublished enabled lookup, missing generation state and pairing/profile-owner outages defer accepted work. Pending profile mutation is detected before waiting for its held writer.
- Cron's requesterOwner comes from the same decision/config. Parent-bound sources preserve the non-member owner rule; independent Gateway sources require admitted admin. Configured channel-owner receipt capabilities remain their existing separate domain.
- Already-admitted publication, completion and delivery transfer their frozen decision rather than admitting again during persistence or effects. Real session/creator/owner/target/physical-store/claim/receipt/plugin/Gateway fences remain. A claim is checked by the producer accepting work, not a restored authority callback.

Mixed-person collected inputs drop the requester sender identity and inherited command-owner capability. Single-sender starts recompute current owner status; mixed drains cannot reconstruct sender authority. No collected-run flag or queued parameter is needed in command-owner admission. An owner message cannot lend owner tools to another sender’s collected text.

Revocation affects the next start. Started work may finish; Stop still cancels. Initial dispatcher/connect migration and authority callback deletion remain later steps.

## Saved compatibility and explicit edges

Exactly one optional saved field is added: the trusted-proxy fallback password hash (`sha256Base64Url`). Fingerprints remain unchanged. Current role scopes intersect saved scopes; new snapshots stop writing `rolePolicy`, while old optional fields still decode.

- Browser origin is connect-only. Saved work follows its person, not its browser (owner decision2026-11-20). Old fallback rows without the hash retain legacy grant comparison, including `browserOriginAllowed`; an origin edit can still refuse that old row until it drains/is re-saved.
- Legacy Tailscale rows without device evidence preserve saved scopes when the grant fingerprint is unchanged; changed grants intersect current identity scope. New paired rows use exact evidence.
- A live ingress binding may abort on a role change, including widening; refusal at the next start preserves main's binding semantics.
- Native durable producers still omit recovery sources (`reply-source-admission.ts`, `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts`, `get-reply-run-execute.ts`). Restart replay refuses these in `queued-chat-inputs.ts`: retained bytes are cancelled/unrecoverable, no reply is generated, and the warning asks for a new send. Existing native in-memory operator queue starts share admission; this PR does not broaden native restart behavior.
- Shared HTTP bearer system actors and Cron standing/management grants are explicit control rows, not new operator sources. Node-role serialization stays outside this step.

## Owner narrowing and plugin grant proof

Removing a sender from `commands.ownerAllowFrom` before a queued turn starts **downgrades the turn to non-owner; it still runs without owner tools**. The same rule applies to Goal successors, with no Goal-only refusal. This is an intentional owner-approved behavior change from main: main stopped the Goal through the deleted live owner callback; later Goal turns now continue without owner tools. Stop and data/target fences remain.

The table adds a real configured-owner removal case and a typed `plugin-grant` kind registered through the production plugin API/PluginInstance and active Gateway registry. Its rows cover:

- resumed grant mismatch → visible refusal;
- no-resume current authorization denial → visible refusal;
- no-resume current authorization allowance with a new grant ID → admitted, executing scope capped to saved WRITER;
- missing plugin policy owner → unavailable, original durable bytes retained, exact owner restored and existing deferred retry used;
- ended resumption before start, held grant signal revoked after admission (run still completes), and explicit Stop.

Plugin policies are not role-required in this fixture, so removal of the explicit saved-grant/owner checks cannot be masked by a role-required policy guard. Mutations touch only that plugin owner; successful execution requires nonempty observed tool-run scopes and the expected current plugin grant. No authority/receipt is manufactured and no production hook or schema field is added. Removal-sensitivity is source-reviewed, not locally executed. The matrix remains four Gateway boots.

## Defined coverage

Typed `Record<Kind, Row>`: **40 operator/control kinds, 151 cases**, three real auth-mode pools and one real restart sentinel (**four Gateway boots**). Each kind defines before-start, after-start and Stop cases with row-specific control/independence assertions. Accepted durable WS/plugin rows use real `continueSessionQueuedInputs`; native channel uses its real in-memory queued lifecycle. No manufactured authority or production test hooks.

Additional cases cover grant/token/role/ingress narrowing, widening, empty scopes, unavailable-owner retry, legacy fallback/Tailscale, exact device key/revocation/approval, current OCID grant union, live credential rotation, and a real Goal whose role excludes its agent: the admitted turn finishes, the next turn visibly refuses with no provider request. The matrix also covers an owner-plus-non-owner native GROUP collection with no owner tools and a live continuation after removal of a secondary email. A profile-deleted-before-start row requires the existing visible refusal type, retained cancelled input and no queued provider call; it deletes the actual canonical row through the existing profile transaction/publication owner. Existing owner-specific tests retain alias/access-plugin/model/admin/channel-owner contracts not duplicated by the matrix.

## CI repair and evidence

### Latest CI repair

For CI run44870171223 on42f562bcbee1, every failing test file was classified from its assertion logs. Real defects repaired:

- Queued starts retain the existing current context/config reader after the submitting request scope closes.
- Accepted chat target-sharing custody uses the independently admitted child's frozen authority, not a closed parent.
- Cron restores its source once **before** session allocation and consumes that frozen role for sandbox placement.
- Native owner successors carry source facts independently of an occurrence; owner loss narrows later turns to non-owner without refusing them.
- Saved plugin grants reach the existing shared access owner. With `resume`, the owner checks the original grant. Without it, current `authorize` allows the current grant even when its ID changed, refuses a denial visibly, and defers only when the owner is unavailable. Normal current required-role semantics apply; no old policy-set or grantId equality check is imposed on `authorize`. Saved scopes still cap authority.
- Publication's data view no longer retains a live permission callback; immutable creator/owner and physical-store predicates remain. The owner-change regression fixture now uses the canonical owner mutation.

Model-policy tests pinning mid-flight cancellation/latching were removed or rewritten; initial ceilings, next-start denial, independent siblings, device/data/commit/Stop fences remain. The matrix's helper cycle and missing import are repaired, and the real Gateway matrix now uses the existing isolated-fork host-broker owner; **40 kinds/151 cases/four boots remain**. Exact stale mock baseline entries were removed, reported typed consumers migrated, and no scanner/ratchet allowances increased.

The owner's separate real-Gateway source preservation proof passed against main on42f562bcbee1 (`e2e-202513.md`); that is not a new-head matrix execution claim.

Old-head CI assertions were classified file by file: real live-context/profile and next-target regressions were fixed; obsolete mid-flight/snapshot/wording expectations were rewritten without restoring permission callbacks. Main was integrated; removed-export consumers, fixture types, mock exports and session-identity comparisons were migrated. Both new import cycles are cut with leaf contracts, without scanner or ratchet exemptions.

Opaque manufactured test grants now use `createTestOperatorAuthority` in the existing admitted-run test-support module, so the null default lives in one test builder rather than per fixture. Production factory/module-identity tests, intentionally invalid raw authorities and direct channel-input API fixtures retain explicit required identity facts.

Direct touched-file oxfmt/oxlint and normal pre-commit hooks passed. **No local test suites, builds or typechecks ran.** New-head CI is the behavioral/type proof; no green-CI claim. The existing shutdown-deadline and unrelated aggregate-workspace-overflow failures remain untouched for the owner’s comparison against main/other PRs; no thresholds or snapshots were changed.

## Test consolidation and deltas

Removed matrix-subsumed cases (files remain for their distinct contracts):

- `operator-run-recovery.test.ts`: shared credentials rotating before restoration/after admission; device removed/token revoked re-admission; admitted-facts device-revoked/role-changed variants. Real matrix token/password/device/role before-/after-start cases replace these; retired-claim, mutation, alias and other distinct cases remain.
- `operator-run-recovery.native.test.ts`: tokenless proxy device remove/revoke/remove-without-token variants; replaced by real proxy-device/live-device/live-device-revoked matrix rows.
- `operator-run-recovery.trusted-proxy.test.ts`: widened identity grant, removed proxy user and leaving trusted-proxy mode; replaced by widened-grant, trusted-proxy refusal and the real mode-transition restart sentinel.
- `operator-run-recovery.effects.test.ts`: two duplicated direct/native-Cron write setups became one six-case table; **all six device/email reassignment/email restoration write contracts remain**.

Credential, ingress-consent, session-owner and completion/Stop builders are shared; duplicate decision-observer/frozen-shape scaffolding was removed. No further cuts to the requested matrix or unique aliases/access-plugin/model/admin/physical-store/receipt/claim/token-reissue/reconnect proof. The remaining test budget is accepted to retain these contracts.

Production TypeScript versus the PR merge base with `origin/main` (src/extensions/packages, excluding tests/support): **+2,575 / -2,897, net -322**. Tests/support: **+6,650 / -4,590, net +2,060**; allocation **1,660** beyond normal400. The added owner/plugin proof preserves the accepted remaining test budget rather than deleting distinct coverage.

Latest head `edec027fd5245a7e45bd19dc50b2a459c2b8b014`: the matrix now uses five Gateway boots; the focused OCID case passes with a bounded-role assertion (not an identity-only cap difference); full 44-file verification and `check:changed` remain incomplete—no green-suite claim.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session observer digests authenticate with the session owner's linked account
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201585

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where, on a multi-user Gateway, every Control UI session observer digest for a session was sent through the agent-level auth order instead of the session owner's linked model account. When that agent-level profile is an unusable placeholder, every observer utility call returns 401 and the observer disables itself for the run, even though the session's own turns run fine on the user's linked account.
- Affected surface: Control UI session observer digests (`gateway.controlUi.sessionObserver`) on multi-user Gateways where sessions run on per-user linked model accounts.

- **Related:** #195172 (who pays for unattended utility-model calls); ClawSweeper confirmed current main drops the session's selected account on the observer path and no PR owns this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The observer's utility model resolution and route-currentness checks now consume the session's established route — effective provider/model plus the session-sticky auth selection (linked account first, then the configured primary's profile on the same provider) — exactly like dashboard session titles already do per docs/gateway/config-agents/models.md (`utilityModel`). The derived utility modelRef carries the session's `@profile`, so preparation authenticates with the session owner's account.
- **Out of scope:** Explicitly configured `utilityModel` routes are preserved unchanged (the resolver returns them as configured); no changes to regular chat routing, auth order, or persistence. Agent-level utility consumers outside the observer (for example activity recaps) keep using the agent-level auth order.
- **Highest-risk area:** Route-currentness comparison (`modelStateIsCurrent`) must use the same session-scoped resolution as the claim that produced the state's ref, otherwise digests get demoted mid-run.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Both the model-slot claim and the currentness check share one `resolveUtilityModelRef(agentId, state)` helper; the route snapshot is captured once at admission from the session entry and refreshed on re-admission, so the comparison inputs cannot diverge.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** Two interleaved sessions on one agent, each with a different linked account and an unusable agent-level auth profile, now get observer digests authenticated to their own accounts (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5@<session-profile>` per session) instead of a shared 401 loop.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/session-observer.ts` (shared resolver), `src/gateway/session-observer-lifecycle.ts` (route capture at admission), `src/gateway/session-observer-model-slots.ts` + `src/gateway/session-observer-audience.ts` (session-scoped claim/currentness), `src/agents/session-model-ref.ts` (`resolveSessionAuthProfile`, extracted from the dashboard-title contract and now shared by both callers). Regression: `src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts` "routes observer utility digests through each session's linked model account". Real-gateway proof: `test/session-observer-linked-accounts.e2e.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree (openclaw main @ 1eacdff456a), Node 26.12.1. A real Gateway server (repo e2e gateway harness, in-process, loopback bind) with the real agent runner, session store, auth profile store, session observer, utility completion, and credential selection. The agent-level auth order for `anthropic` is one deliberately unusable placeholder profile; two sessions carry `authProfileOverride` linked accounts. Only the Anthropic Messages endpoint is a loopback fixture that records the exact `x-api-key` each request authenticated with.

- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Real-gateway proof: interleaved linked sessions publish observer digests
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/session-observer-linked-accounts.e2e.test.ts
  # GREEN (with this patch): 1 file, 1 test passed (94.6s)
  # RED (implementation reverted to origin/main, same test file):
  #   AssertionError: observer digest for alice: expected undefined to be defined
  #   (no digest published; observer utility calls hit the agent-level placeholder
  #   and got 401 until the observer disabled itself — the issue's exact behavior)
  # Unit regression + type check via validate.sh (same-directory tests + tsgo:core): all green
  #   5 files, 70 tests passed; e2e proof re-run inside validate.sh: 1 passed
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  Provider trace (loopback Anthropic Messages endpoint, x-api-key per request):
    observer digest request (claude-haiku-5-5, session alice) -> key sk-ant-linked-alice, status 200
    observer digest request (claude-haiku-5-5, session bob)   -> key sk-ant-linked-bob,   status 200
    chat turn (claude-opus-5-5, session alice) -> key sk-ant-linked-alice, status 200
    chat turn (claude-opus-5-5, session bob)   -> key sk-ant-linked-bob,   status 200
    placeholder key used for observer digests: 0

  Published session.observer digests (real Gateway WS broadcast):
    agent:main:session-alice -> headline "Linked account alice assessed this run", health on-track
    agent:main:session-bob   -> headline "Linked account bob assessed this run",   health on-track
  ```
  Each digest names the account its own provider request authenticated with, so a session can only pass by going through its owner's credential.

- **Observed result after fix:** On one real Gateway with the agent's `anthropic` auth order pointing at an invalid placeholder profile, two interleaved sessions on linked accounts both completed their turns on their own credentials and each published observer digests authenticated with its session owner's linked account; the placeholder profile was never used for a digest. Agent-level utility consumers outside this PR's scope (activity recaps) still observe the placeholder's 401, matching pre-change behavior for that path.

prs.title: fix: let exec auto-review approve commands you asked for on Claude CLI and Codex
prs.body:
Closes #203250
Closes #166521

## What Problem This Solves

With exec auto-review on, agents running on Claude CLI or the Codex harness have commands denied even when the owner asked for exactly that command. The reviewer only sees the command, not the request, and its rules say to deny commands that don't serve the user's request. Owners have to approve by hand or switch auto mode off.

## User Impact

On Claude CLI and Codex `gateway_exec`, the exec reviewer now sees the message that started the run, labeled with its origin. A command the owner asked for can be allowed. A command that doesn't match the request, or that only a non-owner or another session asked for, is still denied. A review transcript supplied by a plugin is ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

Embedded runs already give the reviewer a bounded excerpt of the conversation. These two paths now give it the run's committed user turn from the run's own transcript recorder, which already records the sender and provenance. A turn whose transcript write was blocked gives no context. That is narrower than the embedded excerpt: no history and no tool results. The Codex harness host sets it on its exec options, after any plugin values. Claude CLI carries it through the run's MCP grant, which is minted per turn, so a warm CLI process gets each turn's own message.

The reviewer prompt, its rules and the approval flow don't change.

Accepted edge: a message steered into a running CLI turn isn't added; the reviewer sees the turn's original message.

## Evidence

- Two new tests, one per path, fail on `main` and pass with the change. On `main` the Claude CLI reviewer receives no transcript, and the Codex harness reviewer receives the plugin's forged context. With the change both receive exactly the owner's turn as `origin: operator`. A third test checks that a blocked turn gives the reviewer nothing.
- Existing tests for the MCP loopback, grant store, tool resolution, harness host, CLI runner preparation and reviewer transcript pass (66 files, 658 tests, run before the last review fix; the focused tests and typecheck were rerun after it). Typecheck, lint and format pass on the touched files. `host-capability.ts` was already over the `max-lines` limit on `main` (701 of 700). This change adds 2 lines.
- Source gateway, real Claude CLI agent, `tools.exec.mode: "auto"`, two turns in one session: for each turn the reviewer received that turn's message, `origin: operator`.
- On a 2026.10.8 install with a local patch that gave the reviewer the session's messages, and a real reviewer model, an owner-requested read-only mailbox search went from `deny (risk=high)` to `allow-once (risk=low)`. An owner-requested command that sent an SSH key to an external host was still denied.

<details><summary>Not covered</summary>

- The source-gateway run had no reviewer model credentials, so it shows what the reviewer receives, not the verdict. The verdicts come from the 2026.10.8 run.
- Codex is covered by the harness test, not a live Codex run.
- Origin labels come from the existing classifier the embedded path uses. It treats an authenticated profile sender as `operator` even without admin scope; this change does not alter that.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cron): classify failure-alert deadlines by handoff and delivery ack
prs.body:
Fixes #203140

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway deadline wrapping a cron failure alert's strict announce classified its timeout only from the recipient-reached flag, which turns true when a receipt becomes visible to the caller. A provider acknowledgment that arrived after the deadline — or whose publication lagged it — therefore recorded `not-delivered` and queued the in-app fallback even though the provider had accepted the alert. In the mirrored ordering (ack visible, conversation-history write stalled past the deadline) the outcome degraded to `unknown` instead of the `delivered` receipt that had already landed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable batch now reports two facts the deadline classifier was missing: the provider handoff (fired before `sendDurableMessageBatchCore`, after which the provider may still complete the send) and the complete payload acknowledgment. Deadline classification becomes three states: a deadline before the handoff predicts non-delivery and keeps the fallback; a handoff without the complete acknowledgment leaves the outcome `unknown` and no longer queues a duplicate in-app fallback; a complete acknowledgment settles as `delivered` with the history-write failure staying a diagnostic. Partial acknowledgments and fail-fast history errors keep their current outcomes, and conversation-only alerts (where the history write is the delivery) are unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators see the alert's real delivery state: a sent failure alert is no longer reported as not delivered, and the duplicate in-app fallback no longer appears on top of a delivered external alert. Pre-handoff deadlines still prove non-delivery.

## Evidence

Red/green at the owning boundary, head `63ba9b5cf2` (Node 26.12.1, Linux).

| Scenario | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Handoff + complete ack before deadline, history write stalled | `unknown` | **`delivered`** |
| Handoff, no complete ack at deadline | `not-delivered` + in-app fallback | **`unknown`**, no fallback |
| Deadline before handoff | `not-delivered` + fallback | unchanged (control) |

`pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`: 31/31 pass at head `63ba9b5cf2`. The new "settles a handoff whose complete payload was acked before the deadline as delivered" and "does not queue the in-app fallback for a handoff without a complete acknowledgment" cases fail on the unpatched classifier (verified by reverting the classification, showing `delivered: false/status: not-delivered` where `delivered: true/status: delivered` is expected), while the pre-existing stalled-admission controls (`recipientReached=false/true`) still pass with their established outcomes. `test-lines` ratchet: net +66, allocation credit 66 via `config/test-lines-allocations/203140-failure-alert-deadline.txt`.

Gap: the live Telegram observation from the issue was not reproduced here (no channel credentials on this host); the deterministic deadline orderings the reporter built exercise the same classification path at the owning boundary.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #203140, locate the deadline classifier in `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts`, and thread the handoff/acknowledgment facts from `src/cron/delivery.ts` into it. The implementer understands the code: the classifier now distinguishes proven non-delivery (before handoff) from unproven non-delivery (after handoff, no complete ack) and confirmed delivery (complete ack), and only the last two suppress the in-app fallback. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: preserve neighboring fields when editing Markdown frontmatter
prs.body:
Closes #203240

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path set` could silently delete a neighboring field when editing Markdown frontmatter. For example, setting the plain key `null` in a file that also had a quoted `"null"` key reported success while removing the quoted field and an inline comment.

## User Impact

Editing a field named `true`, `false`, or `null` now changes just its value. Adjacent fields, comments, and the Markdown body stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

YAML interprets the plain key `null` as a null value and the quoted key `"null"` as a string. Looking up the string could therefore return the wrong field's end offset. The editor now takes the value range from the pair on the addressed line after checking the key's original spelling.

## Evidence

Ran the built CLI against a temporary Markdown file. Both versions reported success and read back `new`, but the older build wrote only 23 of the expected 44 bytes. The fixed build wrote all 44 bytes and the file matched the expected output byte for byte:

```markdown
---
null: new # keep
"null": other
---
Body
```

Three regression cases failed on the unmodified PR base. All 513 oc-path tests passed with the fix, including those cases. The runtime build and staged change checks also passed.

prs.title: fix: log when Feishu chat tool is excluded for non-bundled installs
prs.body:
Closes #203210

## What Problem This Solves

When the Feishu plugin is installed from a non-bundled source (such as ClawHub or a workspace/config override), delegated agent turns silently drop `feishu_chat` at the host-restricted conversation-read gate without logging any warning or recording a plugin diagnostic. Operators see `tools.chat` enabled by default in configuration and docs, other Feishu workspace tools work normally, and direct HTTP tool invocation succeeds, leaving no clue why `feishu_chat` is missing from agent turns.

## User Impact

User impact: operators running non-bundled Feishu installs now get a one-time warning and plugin diagnostic explaining why `feishu_chat` was excluded in delegated turns, and the Feishu workspace tools documentation explains this bundled-origin restriction.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keeps `recordToolDiagnostic` as the single diagnostic deduplication owner (extracted into `src/plugins/tool-diagnostics.ts` with `createPluginToolDiagnosticReporter` to stay within the `tools.ts` line cap) and makes it return whether an entry was newly inserted so `warnOnce` logs only once per plugin registry.
- Invokes `diagnostics.warnOnce(...)` at both the pre-factory registration gate and the post-factory returned-tool filter in `src/plugins/tools.ts`, using pure predicates and message formatting from `src/plugins/compat/conversation-read-tools.ts` (and removing the unused `registrationIncludesHostRestrictedConversationReadTool` wrapper).
- Documents the bundled-origin restriction for `feishu_chat` in delegated turns in `docs/channels/feishu/advanced-configuration.md`.
- Adds resolver-level regression tests in `src/plugins/tools.conversation-read-diagnostics.test.ts` exercising `resolvePluginTools` through both exclusion paths and bundled no-op behavior.

## Evidence

### 1. Real running Gateway proof (Before `main` `0058b08e8` vs After `d25f78935`)

Started an isolated Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback --token <redacted> --allow-unconfigured` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`) loading a non-bundled `feishu` plugin via `plugins.load.paths` (`origin: "config"`) that registers both `feishu_doc` and `feishu_chat`, then created a session (`sessions.create`) and executed repeated delegated tool resolutions (`tools.effective` ×2, `tools.invoke feishu_doc`, `tools.invoke feishu_chat` ×2):

- **Before (`main` `0058b08e8`):**
  - `tools.effective` #1 & #2 admitted `feishu_doc` and excluded `feishu_chat`
  - `tools.invoke feishu_doc` → `ok: true` (`"ok"`)
  - `tools.invoke feishu_chat` #1 & #2 → `ok: false` (`Tool not available: feishu_chat`)
  - Matching exclusion warnings in Gateway stdout and log file: **`0`**

- **After (PR `d25f78935`):**
  - `tools.effective` #1 & #2 admitted `feishu_doc` and excluded `feishu_chat`
  - `tools.invoke feishu_doc` → `ok: true` (`"ok"`)
  - `tools.invoke feishu_chat` #1 & #2 → `ok: false` (`Tool not available: feishu_chat`)
  - Matching exclusion warnings in Gateway stdout and log file across all 5 delegated calls: **`1`** (deduplicated once per plugin registry, with no message content or credentials exposed):
    ```text
    2026-11-21T21:20:17.763-03:00 [plugins] plugin tool excluded in delegated turn (feishu: feishu_chat): conversation-read tools require bundled plugin origin (registration=config, manifest=config)
    ```
    Structured JSON log entry (hostname redacted):
    ```json
    {"subsystem":"plugins","logLevelName":"WARN","message":"plugin tool excluded in delegated turn (feishu: feishu_chat): conversation-read tools require bundled plugin origin (registration=config, manifest=config)"}
    ```

### 2. Base-red / head-green regression & checks

- **Base (`main` `0058b08e8`) with `src/plugins/tools.conversation-read-diagnostics.test.ts`:** **FAIL (`2 failed | 1 passed`)** — both non-bundled pre-factory and post-factory exclusion tests fail with `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`, while bundled no-op passes.

prs.title: feat: rename saved model accounts in Models
prs.body:
Related: #202695

## What Problem This Solves

People can connect two model-provider workspaces that use the same email. In Settings → Models, those accounts can look identical, making it hard to tell which workspace or subscription you’re looking at.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway administrators can rename a saved account without signing in again or restarting the Gateway. Leave the name blank to restore its default. Known subscription plans appear beside the account name; names controlled by configuration and accounts owned elsewhere remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admin-only Gateway operation updates only the selected saved profile’s display label. It leaves credentials, authorization, profile IDs, and routing priority unchanged and publishes the new label to the running Gateway. A plan badge uses a known stored tier, not a new usage request. Reconnect name preservation moved here from #202667, which can shrink to the optional sign-in naming prompt after this lands. No sign-in prompt is included here.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI and isolated Gateway: two synthetic same-email accounts could be named independently; Enter saved, Escape sent no write, and clearing restored the default. Names and plan badges rendered correctly, and browser reload read back the result without restarting the Gateway.
- The isolated Gateway, real CLI, and synthetic HTTPS provider verified token rotation, ordinary reconnect, and reconnect with `--force`: the name survived all three. A different account replacing the same slot did not inherit the name. The implementation reuses main’s account matcher and adds no sign-in prompt or config write.
- Gateway tests covered non-admin denial, inherited and config-managed profiles, exact-row and priority preservation, and authorization-grant continuity. The protocol generation and compatibility checks passed without a protocol version change. All 72 focused tests passed, along with targeted lint, UI typecheck, and protocol checks.

- The follow-up reuses the existing form and chip styles. The Control UI budget check passed against the same base with zero added raw CSS (previously +359 B). prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve device pairing for node-role clients using backend metadata (#147149)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #147149.

When a signed `role: "node"` client connects using default GatewayClient metadata (`client.id: "gateway-client"`, `client.mode: "backend"`), `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing` in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.ts` previously returned `true` because it checked only client mode, locality, origin, and authentication method without checking the connection role. Consequently, `authorizeGatewayConnectDevice` skipped device pairing record creation. When node surface preparation subsequently invoked `requestNodePairing`, the missing paired device record caused `requestNodePairing` to throw `Error: node pairing requires a paired device`, terminating the connection without creating or queuing a device pairing request.

As documented in `docs/gateway/protocol/handshake.md`:
> Remote, browser-origin, node, and non-backend clients follow their normal pairing and scope-upgrade policies.

This change ensures that `role: "node"` clients never skip device pairing in `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing`, routing them through standard device pairing and approval policies regardless of whether client metadata matches the default backend shape.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.ts`: Add `if (params.connectParams.role === "node") return false;` to `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing`.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts`: Add unit test coverage verifying that `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing` returns `false` when `connectParams.role === "node"` and `true` when `connectParams.role === "operator"`.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.test.ts`: Add integration test verifying that a `role: "node"` client presenting backend metadata successfully pairs its device identity and establishes connection.

## Behavior Proof & Live Transcript

### 1. Default-Metadata Node Client Connect & Pairing
A fresh node client connects over loopback presenting default backend metadata (`gateway-client` / `backend`), a newly generated Ed25519 device identity, and declared command `["system.which"]`.

- **Before fix:** `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing` returned `true`. Device pairing record creation was skipped. `requestNodePairing` threw `Error: node pairing requires a paired device`, closing the connection (`code: 1000`) with zero pending requests.
- **After fix:** `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing` evaluates `connectParams.role === "node"` and returns `false`. Standard local device pairing executes, the device record is created/approved, declared commands are queued pending approval, and the client receives `hello-ok`.

```text
[gateway-proof] node_connect client={id:"gateway-client",mode:"backend"} role="node" commands=["system.which"]
[gateway-proof] handshake_auth shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing=false role="node"
[gateway-proof] device_pairing status="approved" deviceId="dev_separate_node" roles=["node"]
[gateway-proof] node_surface_pairing requestId="req_node_surface_01" commands=["system.which"] status="pending"
[gateway-proof] connect_result connected=true pairedDevice=true pendingDeviceRequests=0 pendingNodeRequests=1 approvedNodes=0
```

### 2. Existing Paired-Node Reconnect Behavior
The paired node client reconnects with the established device identity and matching token. The Gateway re-authenticates the existing pairing record and reconnects without re-prompting device pairing:

```text
[gateway-proof] node_reconnect deviceId="dev_separate_node" isPaired=true existingRoles=["node"] status="ok"
[gateway-proof] reconnect_result connected=true pairedDevice=true pendingNodeRequests=1 approvedNodes=0
```

### 3. Unchanged Local Operator Control-Plane Access
An operator client connecting with `role: "operator"` and default backend metadata continues to utilize the documented loopback pairing exemption for internal control-plane RPCs:

```text
[gateway-proof] operator_connect client={id:"gateway-client",mode:"backend"} role="operator" shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing=true
[gateway-proof] operator_result connected=true skipPairing=true role="operator" scopes=["operator.admin"]
```

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts`: 41/41 tests pass.
- `npx vitest run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.test.ts -t "creates a paired device for a node-role client presenting backend metadata"`: Passes (verifies device creation and `roles: ["node"]`).
- `npx oxlint src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.test.ts`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: Clean typecheck (0 errors).

prs.title: fix: stop showing Retry when a Template or version is not found
prs.body:
Closes #198764

## What Problem This Solves

When someone opens a missing, mistyped, or retired Template link (or requests a Template version that does not exist on ClawHub), the Templates UI still shows a **Retry** button on the error alert even though retrying can never succeed. Although #198816 updated the Gateway error text for ClawHub 404 responses, the Gateway did not mark those responses as non-retryable or distinguish them structurally from transient catalog outages.

## User Impact

User impact: opening a missing Template or version now shows the not-found message without a pointless Retry button, while keeping navigation back to the catalog and preserving Retry for transient catalog failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds a structured `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` Gateway error detail code and emits `{ retryable: false, details: { code: "TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND" } }` from `mapClawHubError` on ClawHub HTTP 404 responses, leaving transient failures (such as 503s or unknown upstream errors) untouched.
- Updates the Templates catalog detail view, detail panel, and preview modal to hide the **Retry** button when `isTemplateNotFoundFailure` matches the error, without affecting retry behavior for transient errors.

## Evidence

### 1. Real running Gateway + live `clawhub.ai` + real browser (`1573eeea9`)
