prs.title: fix: stop PR CI watchers blocking on superseded security checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR CI watchers can reject an otherwise successful replacement run because a cancelled CodeQL matrix placeholder has a different name from its expanded jobs. This blocked #203197 on the stale Security High matrix placeholder.

## User Impact

Maintainers can wait for CI without treating a proven superseded cancellation as a current failure. Current failing or unfinished checks and incomplete evidence still block completion. No product configuration or runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing run/suite replacement proof to cancelled checks outside the attached CI workflow. Require a newer completed, successful run, matching workflow and event, and exact PR/head/suite evidence for both runs. Reobserve the rollup after metadata reads and retain the existing bounded evidence budget. Old-run identities reuse the attachment cache across polls, while successor success is re-read each poll because reruns retain their run IDs. This preserves the existing 32-read bounded-progress contract. There is no check-name allowlist or blanket cancellation ignore.

## Evidence

- The production CLI replay failed on the base with exit 15 and the cancelled Security High matrix placeholder, then passed with the fix.
- All 16 focused CodeQL cases pass, including current failures, unresolved checks, incomplete rollups, running/failed replacements, and wrong PR/head/workflow/event/suite evidence.
- Remote review follow-up: 32/33 cancelled-run backlogs reproduced TIMEOUT on the first revision, then passed with persistent old-run identities. Negative regressions reject a successor that fails between polls and a deferred foreign-PR association; each poll remains bounded to 32 metadata reads.
- Script typecheck and focused test typecheck pass.
- All 251 tests in the three watcher suites pass (109.55s test duration; 110.34s wrapper wall time). The main suite contains subprocess/API-boundary, deadline, ownership, pagination and failure guards.
- Targeted script/test lint, formatting and git diff checks pass.
- Author simplification pass: reuse the existing replacement owner and bounded read budget; no name matching, new API, or alternate classifier. Production delta: +81/-16 lines; test delta: +128/-7 lines.

prs.title: fix: recover Linux cloud workers with stale process IDs
prs.body:
Closes #200021

## What Problem This Solves

Linux cloud-worker resume can become stuck when its saved `node.pid` is stale or reused. A permission-denied liveness probe or a procfs read during process exit currently escapes as a raw errno instead of either recovering a dead worker or giving the operator the existing release-and-reprovision guidance.

## User Impact

User impact: Dead Linux workers can proceed through the existing receipt cleanup and resume replay, while a live process with missing, unreadable, or mismatched identity remains fenced with actionable recovery guidance. Ambiguous procfs failures, including a live process whose working directory was deleted, cannot authorize a duplicate launch.

Windows and macOS behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Linux `EPERM` now correctly means that a process exists and must still pass identity verification. Procfs `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` is confirmed with a second liveness probe; only a subsequent `ESRCH` takes the dead-process path. Other identity-read failures stay live but unverified and fail closed.

## Evidence

- The generated-script regression failed before the fix with raw `EPERM`, `ENOENT`, `ESRCH`, and `EACCES` failures. It now covers verified cross-user liveness, confirmed disappearance at each procfs read, ambiguous errors with a still-live process, unreadable identity, and exact liveness-probe counts — **22 passed**.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-resume.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment-replay.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **82 passed** across the resume, enrollment-replay, and warm-image suites.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — passed.
- Targeted Oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent local review covered base `6577f41b9ab` through final head `ffe5084d25b379826389cccd703d77dd241bc884`. It identified the deleted-cwd duplicate-launch risk during review; that was repaired and the final review reported no findings.

Faults and procfs races are injected into the real generated resume script; they were not reproduced using a separate OS user. No native Windows/macOS execution or full repository suite was run.

prs.title: fix(update): keep the openclaw command and Gateway working after a pnpm update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: after `openclaw update` on a pnpm install (`pnpm add -g openclaw`), the `openclaw` command fails with `Cannot find module …/.openclaw-update-native-…/openclaw.mjs` and the Gateway stays stopped. This is a backport of #201735 to the 2026.11.7 line, now in preparation. It is a proposal for the release owner; it supersedes #201739, which targeted the already shipped 2026.11.6 line. Published 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not contain the fix. ## User Impact What a pnpm user gets when they update to a 2026.11.7 built from this branch: - **The `openclaw` command keeps working on every hop we ran.** The installed updater still publishes a launcher that points into its removed update stage, and this package's Doctor repairs it during the same update. - **The Gateway restarts by itself only when the hop migrates the database schema.** The installed updater (2026.11.6 or older) hands the remaining steps to the new package only then. 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.6 have the same schema as 2026.11.7 (agent 38, state 36). On those hops the installed updater still refuses the restart (`service-revalidation-failed`, exit 1) and leaves the Gateway stopped. The updater that is already installed cannot be patched. - **On those hops, two commands bring the Gateway back.** This was verified in every cell below: `openclaw gateway install --force`, then `openclaw gateway restart`. `openclaw gateway restart` alone does not work, because the service still names the previous version's store directory. Once 2026.11.7 is installed, later pnpm updates run its own updater, which relocates the launcher and revalidates the service against the pnpm install root itself. ## Why This Change Was Made This is one commit with the net change of #201739 (which adapted #201735 to this line), plus a merge of the current `release/2026.11.7` tip. It does the following: - rewrites pnpm's quoted launcher shim (`"$basedir_abs"/''`) by value, so every quoting form relocates; - refuses to publish a launcher that still names the stage; - repairs an already broken launcher from Doctor and Gateway startup; - matches the unchanged service definition against its own install root after pnpm repoints the global entry. The fingerprint, name, profile and manager-UID ownership checks are unchanged. **Update behavior:** the fix runs when this package is the updater, the Doctor or the Gateway. Updates driven by an installed 2026.11.6 or older updater get only the Doctor launcher repair, plus the Gateway restart on schema-migrating hops, as described above. **Steps still left to a person:** the two Gateway commands on same-schema hops from a shipped updater. They cannot be automated inside that updater, which is already installed. The parked draft #201906 tried an automatic restart after the updater exits; it failed in three real runs and is not part of this PR. A follow-up commit on main makes Doctor, `openclaw update status` and `openclaw gateway status --deep` name the two commands in that state. It is proposed for this branch separately once proven. ## Evidence ### Real pnpm updates through the shipped entry point Each cell installed published `openclaw@` from the public registry with `pnpm add -g`, ran the Gateway as a managed service under the harness's systemd user shim, with a 256 MiB agent database and a busy writer, then ran a plain `openclaw update --tag `. The target is installed in the same layout class as a registry target. Afterwards the cell ran `openclaw gateway install --force` and `openclaw gateway restart`, only if the Gateway was not serving. Cells on this head, `2a2eb41`: | Start → target | pnpm | `openclaw update` | `openclaw --version` after | Launcher target after | Gateway after the update | Service unit after the update | Schema agent/state | After `gateway install --force` + `gateway restart` | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2026.11.6 → head | 12.21.0 | exit 1, `service-revalidation-failed`, 154 s | `OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (2a2eb41)` | `global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` | stopped | `store/v11/links/@/openclaw/2026.11.6/…` | 38/36 → 38/36 | both exit 0; running, connectivity ok; unit on `global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw` | | 2026.11.5 → head | 12.21.0 | exit 1, `service-revalidation-failed`, 153 s | `OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (2a2eb41)` | same | stopped | `…/openclaw/2026.11.5/…` | 38/36 → 38/36 | both exit 0; running, connectivity ok; unit on `global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw` | | 2026.11.6 → head | 11.28.13 | exit 1, `service-revalidation-failed`, 166 s | `OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (2a2eb41)` | `global/v11/9440847f…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` | stopped | `…/openclaw/2026.11.6/…` | 38/36 → 38/36 | both exit 0; running, connectivity ok; unit on the per-version `global/v11//.pnpm/openclaw@file+…/node_modules/openclaw` (see below) | | **Negative control:** 2026.11.6 → bare tip `d3b5796` | 12.21.0 | exit 1, `service-revalidation-failed`, 165 s | **fails**: `Cannot find module …/.openclaw-update-native-fPbx97/…/openclaw.mjs` | `"$basedir_abs"/'../.openclaw-update-native-fPbx97/…/openclaw.mjs'`, the removed stage | stopped | `…/openclaw/2026.11.6/…` | 38/36 → 38/36 | not run; the command itself is broken | - **Outage.** The load probe measured the Gateway from its stop until it served again: 238, 254 and 247 s. That window includes the update and the two commands, which the cell ran immediately after the update. For a user, the outage lasts until they run them. On the bare tip the Gateway was still down when the load window closed (342 s). - **Disk.** Sampled per directory through the update, as peak / left afterwards: - pnpm home: +855 / +855 MiB on pnpm 12, +1155 / +1155 MiB on pnpm 11 (the new package version); - update captures: +268 / +268 MiB; - the update's temp directory: about +900 / +630 MiB. These are the cell's own paths, not the shared VM disk. - **pnpm 11 service path.** After `gateway install --force`, the pnpm 11 service names the per-version `.pnpm/openclaw@…` directory instead of the stable entry, and the next update removes that directory. #202017 fixes this on main and is proposed for this branch. - **Cells on `b84ccfe`.** The same cells were also run on `b84ccfe`, this commit before the test-only tip merge, with identical outcomes. Recordings (cell log live, then a summary from the raw cell files; container paths under `/home/appuser`): 2026.11.6 → head, pnpm 12: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1906bd3-9e57-43de-b730-92203d5163ed 2026.11.5 → head, pnpm 12: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39444f59-9415-42ba-beb0-04b26bc55919 2026.11.6 → head, pnpm 11.28.13: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fafe8515-9746-4e99-89be-ba2c8c207004 Negative control, 2026.11.6 → bare tip: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9eb03318-e0eb-4806-bd3a-ad6937120e54
What the 2026.11.6 → head cell printed after the update, then the two recovery commands ``` $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (2a2eb41) $ openclaw gateway status --deep (excerpt) Runtime: stopped (state inactive, sub dead, last exit 0, reason exited) CLI 2026.11.7 at ~/…/global/v11/…/node_modules/openclaw differs from the Gateway service's 2026.11.6 at ~/…/store/v11/links/@/openclaw/2026.11.6/…/node_modules/openclaw. Run `openclaw update` or use the CLI from … Run `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw gateway install --force` from the active CLI. Connectivity check: failed $ openclaw gateway install --force Installed systemd service: ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service Previous unit backed up to: ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service.bak exit 0 $ openclaw gateway restart Restarted systemd service: openclaw-gateway.service exit 0 $ openclaw gateway status --deep (excerpt) Command: /usr/local/bin/node --max-old-space-size=4096 ~/…/global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port … Runtime: running (pid …, state active, sub running) Connectivity check: ok ```
Negative control: the same hop onto the bare release/2026.11.7 tip ``` $ openclaw --version Error: Cannot find module '~/…/pnpm-home/.openclaw-update-native-fPbx97/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs' $ grep exec ~/…/pnpm-home/bin/openclaw (excerpt) exec node "$basedir_abs"/'../.openclaw-update-native-fPbx97/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs' "$@" ```
Full raw logs are not attached, because the artifact store rejected uploads from the test host. ### Checks on this branch Run on head ``2a2eb41``, with the bare tip as comparison where something failed: - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the launcher repair, runtime relocation, native stage, all `package-update-swap*`, package filesystem, service install root, Gateway startup plugin, update-restart module outcome and eager import closure tests: 17 files, 222 tests pass. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` report 0 cycles. `pnpm check:docs` and `git diff --check` pass. - The branch packs: `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` runs `runtime-postbuild` (14 phases) and the tarball integrity check passes. The bare tip packs too. This line has no compatibility-inventory pack failure; 2026.11.10 had one. - `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes with the release context that a PR into `release/*` gets in CI, where the test-line budget is skipped. Run as a main-line branch, only `test-lines` fails: the bare tip is already 695 lines over its ceiling, and this branch adds the 424 net regression-test lines that #201735 added on main. CI on `2a2eb41`: every check passes (75 pass, 58 skipped). ## Cherry-pick for the release line One commit, `b84ccfe`, on top of `release/2026.11.7`, followed by a merge of the newer tip (`e0477dd`, a single test-file change). prs.title: fix(update): keep the openclaw command and Gateway working after a pnpm update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `openclaw update` on a pnpm install (`pnpm add -g openclaw`), the `openclaw` command fails with `Cannot find module …/.openclaw-update-native-…/openclaw.mjs` and the Gateway can stay stopped.

This backports #201735 to `release/2026.11.10`. It is a proposal for the release owner. Published 2026.11.10-beta.1 does not contain the fix.

## User Impact

What a pnpm user gets when they update to a 2026.11.10 build from this branch:
- **The `openclaw` command keeps working.** The installed updater still publishes a launcher that points into its removed update stage, and this package's Doctor repairs it during the same update.
- **The Gateway restarts by itself when the hop migrates the database schema.** The installed updater hands the remaining steps to the new package only then. From 2026.11.5 or 2026.11.6 (agent schema 38, state 36), 2026.11.10 migrates to 42/40, so these hops end with the Gateway serving the new version, with no user step.
- **A same-schema hop is expected to leave the Gateway stopped.** An example is a hop from 2026.11.10-beta.1, which was not run here. The installed updater refuses the restart (`service-revalidation-failed`), as it did on every same-schema hop on the 2026.11.7 line (#203401). There, `openclaw gateway install --force`, then `openclaw gateway restart` brought the Gateway back. `openclaw gateway restart` alone does not work.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries the #201735 change (the same commits as before) plus merges of the current `release/2026.11.10` tip. It does the following:
- rewrites pnpm's quoted launcher shim by value, so every quoting form relocates;
- refuses to publish a launcher that still names the stage;
- repairs an already broken launcher from Doctor and Gateway startup;
- matches the unchanged service definition against its own install root after pnpm repoints the global entry.

The fingerprint, name, profile and manager-UID ownership checks are unchanged.

**Update behavior:** the fix runs when this package is the updater, the Doctor or the Gateway. Updates driven by an installed 2026.11.6 or older updater get the Doctor launcher repair, plus the Gateway restart on schema-migrating hops.

## Evidence

### Real pnpm update onto this head

Published `openclaw@2026.11.5` was installed from the public registry with `pnpm add -g` (pnpm 12.21.0). The Gateway ran as a managed service under the harness's systemd user shim, with a 256 MiB agent database and a busy writer. A plain `openclaw update --tag <this head's package tarball, 2026.11.10-beta.2>` followed.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `openclaw update` | exit 0, `ok`, 143 s |
| `openclaw --version` | `OpenClaw 2026.11.10-beta.2 (c979fec)` |
| Launcher | `exec node "${basedir_abs}"/../global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` |
| Gateway | serving 2026.11.10-beta.2, readyz true; `openclaw gateway status --deep`: connectivity ok |
| Service unit | `…/store/v11/links/@/openclaw/2026.11.5/…` → `…/global/v11/926ea0a5…/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js` |
| Schema agent/state | 38/36 → 42/40 (migrated) |
| Outage (load probe) | 74 s |
| Disk per directory (peak / left) | pnpm home +1064 / +794 MiB; captures +268 / 0 MiB; update temp +896 / +651 MiB |

No recovery command was needed. Recording:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c56b7b9-1536-4a37-b242-a03e3b3264c0

Full raw logs are not attached, because the artifact store rejected uploads from the test host.

### Checks

Run on `2d90bc4`, the first tip merge; `c979fec` adds the next tip, a single CI test file. The pack ran on `c979fec` as well.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` passes on the launcher repair, runtime relocation, native stage, all `package-update-swap*`, package filesystem, service install root, Gateway startup plugin, update-restart module outcome and eager import closure tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` and `tsgo:test:root` pass. `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` report 0 cycles.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes in release context.
- The branch packs, including `runtime-postbuild`. The earlier compatibility-inventory pack failure came from the release tip, and it is gone on the current tip.
- The earlier red checks came from the release branch (the `cachesInstructions` type error and a runner download failure). Both are gone after the merge: the type lanes above pass locally on this head.

## Not proven

- A fixed version installed from a registry. The target was this head's tarball offered with `--tag`, in the same project-store layout as a registry target.
- Windows. Automatic launcher repair is macOS and Linux only.
- Real launchd, and systemd as PID 1. The cells used the harness's systemd user shim.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

prs.title: fix(update): keep a launched candidate's restart failure free of a data-risk mark
prs.body:
## Problem

After a migrated update, `finishUpdate` holds `rollbackBlockedReason = state-migrated-no-rollback` for the rest of the run. `completeUpdateCommandResult` stamps any later `status: error` with that block as `dataAtRisk`. The run then ends with "Keep the Gateway stopped: data at risk (state-migrated-no-rollback)".

The commonest error at that point is a restart health failure. The candidate started and answered as the new version, then missed core readiness inside the budget: a slow sidecar, a refused agent database, a plugin reload. That candidate is running on the state it migrated. Nothing shows the state was damaged. Yet the run records a data risk, and the guidance tells the operator to keep a running Gateway stopped. Since #201668, `openclaw update repair` can verify consistent state and record a receipt that resolves the mark, but only after extra verification, and only after the operator has first been given misleading guidance. The mark comes from the restart failing, not from anything observed about the data.

The same failure also printed `Rollback: reinstall OpenClaw <previous version> ...` from the restart verifier, even though older code cannot read the migrated state.

This is audit entry 1 ("blanket `rollbackBlockedReason` stamp"), for its highest-traffic producer: the restart.

## Rule

A data-at-risk mark needs positive evidence. After `restart-health-failed`, the block is released only on launch evidence read **after** readiness failed:

- the native service runtime still reports the process that answered. This reuses `readFailedUpdateGatewayState`, which keeps the recorded identity only while the same PID is still running, so a candidate that exited or was replaced during polling is no evidence;
- that process owns **every** listener on the Gateway port (fresh port inspection, the restart inspector's ownership rule). A version answered by another process on any bind address is no evidence, and neither is an unattributed listener;
- that process's recorded version equals the candidate's version, with no build mismatch, and its recorded build equals the candidate's build whenever the update knows it;
- the version it replaced is known and differs.

When it is released:

- the result is the restart-health failure (`readyz-unhealthy`). Restart stays unsafe (`runtime-verification-failed`), with no `dataAtRisk`;
- rollback is not attempted. It would hand the migrated state to a build that cannot read it. `rollbackOutcome` records `not-attempted: state-migrated-no-rollback`, so status and report readers keep the migration fact.

While any rollback block is set, or the recorded rollback outcome is a refusal (the final-recovery pass), the restart verifier drops the reinstall advice. It prints `Rollback: unavailable; update state was migrated, ...` for `state-migrated-no-rollback`, or `Rollback: unavailable; rollback safety could not be verified, ...` for `rollback-state-unverified` (for example, PostgreSQL state with no pre-activation baseline).

Everything else keeps the mark exactly as before:

| Restart observation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate still running with its PID and owning the port, answered as the new version, health failed | data at risk, rollback attempted (and refused by the migration check) | restart-health failure, no data risk, no rollback |
| Restart accepted, but no process ran (queued task, start never happened) | data at risk | data at risk |
| Restart command failed | data at risk | data at risk |
| Candidate answered, then exited while readiness was polled | data at risk | data at risk |
| Another process replaced the one that answered | data at risk | data at risk |
| A different process owns the port that answered | data at risk | data at risk |
| Port busy, listener owner unattributed | data at risk | data at risk |
| Managed PID owns one bind address, another process owns a second | data at risk | data at risk |
| Update knows the candidate build, answer named none | data at risk | data at risk |
| Match flag left by an earlier observation, wrong version | data at risk | data at risk |
| Port answered as the candidate, but no service PID (including after a Gateway-triggered update recorded its own PID) | data at risk | data at risk |
| Same version, different build | data at risk | data at risk |
| Version unchanged by the update, or previous version unknown | data at risk | data at risk |
| Split-root update (original-service compensation) | data at risk | data at risk (unchanged path) |
| Runtime or record unreadable | data at risk | data at risk |

An accepted restart or "start attempted" is not treated as launch evidence. That gap is why #201529 was closed.

## Change

- `update-command-verification.ts` owns the recorded activation facts and the restart failure report:
  - `releaseLaunchedState` applies the rule above. When it releases the block, it records the `not-attempted: state-migrated-no-rollback` rollback outcome in the run ledger, where status and final recovery read it (`result.rollbackOutcome ??= recorded.verification.rollbackOutcome`). If that record fails, the block stays.
  - The health-fact producer now always writes `pid`. Before, a PID-less observation omitted the key, so the merge kept the previous process's PID.
  - The failure advice honors the rollback refusal.
- `update-command-post-update.ts`: forwards `rollbackBlockedReason` to the restart, and one call after the existing `activationVerified` branch skips rollback when the block is released. Three lines, so the file stays within its 700-line cap after main's growth.
- `update-command-service-context-types.ts`: the restart parameter type. The restart verifier receives it through main's existing parameter spread; `update-command-service.ts` is unchanged.
- `scripts/tests/update-restart-module-outcome.mjs`: the vm fixture exposes the new export from the real verification module, as it already does for its siblings.

No config key, stored field, schema value or exit code changes. `rollbackOutcome.reason` is free text, and this reuses the existing reason. The only text change is the verifier's rollback line, shown only when a block is set.

## What is left to a person

For the converted case:
- The run ends as a restart-health failure. The existing next step names `openclaw update repair`, `openclaw gateway status --deep` and `openclaw triage`.
- Repair is no longer blocked by a data-risk mark it cannot clear.
- Whatever makes the candidate unhealthy (a channel, an agent database, a plugin) still needs its owner's fix. The readiness report names it.

For the cases that keep the mark, the existing steps remain. They stay manual because no running build has been shown to own the migrated state, and starting one automatically is exactly what the mark exists to prevent.

## Evidence

Exact base `0eb6488cd3c`, head `b1407681922`. The recordings are from that head. Later commits only merge `main` (including #201668 and #200578) and move the rollback-outcome record into the verification owner. That move is covered by the ledger assertions in the same tests, which pass on the final head. The same test files run at both. Only the four product files above are swapped.

- Red, base, finalizer rows: for both launched-candidate rows the finalizer still calls rollback (which the migration check refuses) and stamps the data risk. All thirteen negative controls pass, so they hold the existing behavior. The split-root contract test fails because the owner function does not exist on base. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20422972-71ad-4b40-9ed9-d72fecef60ff
- Red, base, verifier: the stale PID survives a PID-less observation, and reinstall advice is printed while rollback is refused, in the restart pass, the final-recovery pass and the unverified-baseline case. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecf03a68-8faf-40a2-a18b-4f0d91483413
- Green, head: all 21 pass. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3588d94c-cb49-4794-b3d2-10731f349167

Each guard is mutation-proven. With the guard removed, the named control fails:

| Guard removed | Failing control |
|---|---|
| live runtime re-read (recorded snapshot only) | candidate exited, process replaced |
| listener owned by the managed PID | listener not owned, listener unattributed |
| every listener owned (any one is enough) | listener shared |
| known previous version | previous version unknown |
| candidate build required when known | build not answered |
| version equality (match flag only) | stale match flag |
| `versionMatch !== false` | build mismatch |
| `serviceRunning === true` | candidate exited (recorded) |
| service PID | no service PID |
| version changed | version unchanged |
| split-root exclusion | split-root contract test |
| producer clears `pid` | `clears an earlier process's PID when the running service reports none` |
| refusal-aware rollback advice | `offers the previous version only while rollback is allowed (refusal=restart)` |
| recorded refusal honored in final recovery | `... (refusal=recorded)` |
| refusal-specific wording | `... (refusal=unverified)` |

Checks on head:
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean.
- The line-cap ratchet passes; `update-command-post-update.ts` stays within 700.
- Affected suites, 10 files, 0 failures: `update-command-post-update-repair`, `-post-update-recovery`, `-post-update`, `-verification`, `-service`, `-database-rollback`, `-lifecycle`, `-original-service`, `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome`, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure`. These ran on the same product tree before the rebase over unrelated main commits (UI locales, automations, Doctor image candidate, Gateway history, plugins). None of them touch update, port, restart or daemon code.

Review so far:
- An independent review found no blocker. Its findings are addressed: the stale PID merge, keeping the migration fact on record, the split-root path, the unchanged version, and weak assertions.
- ClawSweeper round 1 found two P2s, both addressed. Facts read before readiness polling could describe a candidate that had since exited; the live re-read now covers that. The verifier printed reinstall advice despite the refusal; that is now refusal-aware.
- ClawSweeper round 2 (patch tier C) found three more, all addressed. A version answer was not tied to the managed PID; the listener ownership check now does that. The final-recovery verifier pass still offered reinstall; it now honors the recorded refusal. The base comparison said "rolled back"; it now says the finalizer calls a rollback that the migration check refuses.

- ClawSweeper round 3 (last round) found four. All four are fixed in this head, because each one either dropped the mark on ambiguous evidence or printed a false message. A version answer could come from a non-owned listener on another bind address; every listener must now be owned. An unknown predecessor version passed the "changed" check; it now has to be known. A version answered without a build passed while the update knew the build; the build is now required. "State was migrated" was printed for the PostgreSQL no-baseline refusal; that refusal now has its own wording.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Hidden listener (rating round 4, P2):** when process visibility is restricted, `lsof` can return only the managed user's listener and omit another user's listener on a different address. If that hidden listener answered the version probe, the ownership check still passes. Attributing the reply needs the Gateway's health reply to name its PID or boot identity per listener, which is a protocol change. That is a decision for Jason, so it is not done here.
- **PostgreSQL without a pre-activation baseline (round 4, P2):** the first restart-verifier pass still offers "reinstall the previous version", which the rollback owner later refuses. Base prints the same line in the same state; this PR neither introduces nor widens it.

- Real-path proof of the restart verifier feeding this check. The finalizer tests fake the restart outcome and write the facts the verifier would record. The producer-side PID behavior and the advice are tested on the real verifier.
- A real Docker cell (see below).
- The remaining audit catch-alls, by owner: migration/rollback (`update-command-rollback.ts` default and catch, `update-command-database-backup.ts` rollback-start and `assertRollbackSafe`), Doctor classifier and preflight (`doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts`), Git legacy pre-Doctor mark (`update-runner-git.ts`), and service recovery admission (`update-command-service-recovery.ts`).

### Not proven

**No real Docker cell.** This PR's proof is unit and mutation tests only: red on base, green on head, and every guard mutation-killed. No packaged update with a live, write-loaded Gateway exercises this path. Within the agreed one-hour bound I tried these environment-level faults (no product test hook):

- **Startup that never completes** (for example a plugin or sidecar that hangs): rejected. The updater classifies a still-starting Gateway as `readiness-pending`, not `restart-health-failed`, so it never reaches this path.
- **Child-runtime loss** (removing the Node binary after the candidate starts): rejected. It is timing-dependent, and the runtime owner schedules its own restart.
- **An isolatable second agent whose database belongs to `main`:** the most promising. Readiness reports `agent-database:<id>` with `coreReady: false` while the Gateway owns its port and answers its version, and real agent-schema migrations exist between `v2026.11.6` and main. I wired it into an update-matrix harness copy and built head and base packs. It was not run: the Docker lock was taken by release-critical cells, then the session was interrupted. Two things remain unverified: the fault was never observed, and the update's Doctor might refuse or repair that database before the restart.

The unit tests run the real `finishUpdate`, rollback selection, run ledger, live-runtime and port re-read, final recovery and guidance code. Only the service manager, the restart outcome, the rollback executor and the port inspection are faked.

prs.title: fix(ui): clarify what the Usage error rate counts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Usage error rate and Errors count can be read as including failed attempts that never produced a recorded message, even though both metrics only cover recorded message errors.

Fixes #200598

## Why This Change Was Made

The error-rate and Errors tooltips now identify tool-result errors and assistant messages stopped for error, abort, or timeout, and say attempts without a recorded message are excluded. Error accounting stays unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can interpret the rate and count as recorded-message metrics, not measures of every attempted turn.

## Evidence

- The same English, light-theme Control UI route and mock Gateway fixture show `0.00%` and `0 errors`; the browser case checks the recorded-message boundary in both tooltips. This verifies display behavior, not a provider failure.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/usage/view.test.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`: 30 focused Usage tests passed. The duplicate tooltip unit case was removed; browser coverage remains.
- `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/proof-usage-error-rate.e2e.test.ts -t 'defines which recorded errors the Usage rate and count include'`: 1 focused Control UI E2E test passed and verifies both tooltips.
- `node --import tsx scripts/test-projects.mts --changed 1eacdff456ad0964d9b8cd65945913c6ebf50c4b -- --reporter=verbose`: 23,328 passed, 4 skipped, and 1 unrelated Workboard locale assertion failed (`vor 1min` vs `vor 1 Min.`) in a test file unchanged from the validation base and outside this PR's diff.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: passed.
- `pnpm format:check -- ui/src/e2e/proof-usage-error-rate.e2e.test.ts ui/src/i18n/locales/en-usage.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`: passed.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/proof-usage-error-rate.e2e.test.ts -t 'defines which recorded errors the Usage rate and count include'
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

### Existing error-rate comparison

These screenshots compare the Error rate tooltip on base `eb7ca3d33375fafc67dae7de9a545dac53d156d7` and the original PR head `e6352991abc3841988907adf9288b6357c728259`. The relevant UI files are unchanged between that base and validation base `1eacdff456ad0964d9b8cd65945913c6ebf50c4b`. Both captures use English, light theme, 1440 × 1100, and the same local mock Gateway fixture. The current head `10fc760077be196ed1542849e6db88d7ad7b7d3d` keeps the Error rate wording and extends the same boundary to the Errors count tooltip; the browser case verifies both. The fixture does not exercise an external provider failure.

Before

## What Problem This Solves

Temporary diagnostic carrier — **do not merge**. The cron failure-alert integration test observed an unsettled outcome after its existing wait. This adds failure-only diagnostics to distinguish transport completion, callback settlement, persistence warnings, and the existing public projections. It does not claim a root-cause fix.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203299. This branch deliberately retains that parser history and the same logging-policy base so CI can reproduce the original cron cohort; only the final commit adds this diagnostic.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. The diagnostic commit changes two test files only. All existing assertions, three outcome cases, polling defaults, the 45-second case deadline, and final Gateway drain remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture emits at most three fixed-label records on failure, without raw identifiers, paths, error messages, or configuration. Its case-owned spies preserve original receivers, promises, and thrown errors; synchronous, idempotent abort cleanup retires them before later tests can run. Callback fulfillment is reported separately from persisted state.

## Evidence

- Independent source reviews and the applicable native correction review completed with no remaining actionable source findings. The latest native pass completed successfully; earlier findings and their dispositions are retained.
- Targeted formatting and diff checks passed. Exact Oxlint 1.89.0 native non-type-aware rules passed on both files; full lint remains pending because the local JS-plugin dependency is unavailable. Twelve source-extracted checks preserved diagnostic field values, order, and references.

prs.title: fix: stop a failed Git checkout update from claiming data at risk without evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` updates a Git checkout in place (the legacy runner, used when the Git release layout is unavailable) and anything fails after its Doctor starts, the run records "data at risk (state-migrated-no-rollback)". The runner sets that mark before Doctor runs and never compares state. So a Doctor that failed before writing anything, missing Control UI assets, or a HEAD check failure all tell the user to keep the Gateway stopped, and `openclaw update repair` then refuses to start it.

## User Impact

A Git checkout update whose Doctor fails without changing state no longer reports data at risk. If the previous checkout can be restored, the updater restores it and starts the previous Gateway, as before. If it cannot be restored (for example a tracked file was edited during the update), the Gateway stays stopped with a true message, and `openclaw update repair` is no longer blocked. A real state change, or a Doctor that reports its own data-risk verdict, still records the mark.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rule: an update records "data at risk" only on positive evidence that state changed and was not verified. An inconclusive read, a timeout or an unknown failure becomes a warning or a true restart-unsafe outcome.

- **Git runner** (`src/infra/update-runner-git.ts`): starting Doctor now records only "restart unsafe: state-migration-started". The CLI already compares pre- and post-activation state schemas after every post-activation failure (`inspectActivatedUpdateState`, and `rollbackFailedUpdate` before any restore). That comparison is the owner of the "state migrated" evidence; the runner's default duplicated it without evidence.
- **Doctor verdict carried** (`runPackageUpdateDoctor`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-package.ts`): the Doctor child writes its own typed `maintenanceRefusal` verdict. The package/Git Doctor runner never read it, and the runner's blanket mark covered it by accident. It now raises `DoctorMaintenanceRefusalError` when a settled Doctor step carries a `data-at-risk` verdict, as the fresh-Doctor path already does. The Git runner records `recovery.dataAtRisk` from it and still reports `doctor-failed`. Lost requester authority or a recording failure keeps its own error and reason.
- **Other consumers of that throw:**
  - The package swap gets a failed verification step and restores the previous package, through the existing `runPackagePostInstallVerification`.
  - Fresh-profile initialization keeps a Doctor refusal a pre-activation `target-state-initialization` refusal, so nothing is marked before activation.
- **Final recovery** (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-failure-recovery.ts`): the automatic restart was refused only when a data risk was recorded. Without the runner's mark it would have started a candidate whose Doctor failed. It now also refuses `state-migration-started`. Other unsafe reasons (for example `runtime-verification-failed`) still restart, as before; audit entry 14 lists cases where restarting is right.

No new config key, stored field, schema value, JSON field, exit code or permission.

| Situation (in-place Git update, Doctor fails) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| State unchanged, checkout restorable | rolled back; previous Gateway started (the CLI's rollback overwrote the mark) | same |
| State unchanged, checkout rollback refused (tracked file edited) | `dataAtRisk: state-migrated-no-rollback`; "Keep the Gateway stopped: data at risk"; `update repair` refuses forever | no data mark; restart unsafe (`state-migration-started`); Gateway kept stopped; guidance names `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw triage`; repair is not blocked |
| Doctor migrated state, then failed | mark `state-migrated-no-rollback` (blanket) | mark from evidence: the CLI's schema comparison and database restore (unchanged code paths) |
| Doctor child reports `data-at-risk` (e.g. `incomplete-migration`) | blanket `state-migrated-no-rollback` | the child's own reason (`incomplete-migration`), reason `doctor-failed` |
| Unsafe recovery not involving a started Doctor | final recovery restarts | same |

## Evidence

Behavior checked through the real entry point: a Git checkout (dev channel) installed and built in a Docker container with real systemd, a managed Gateway service, and a busy agent-database writer. A real `openclaw update` runs on the legacy runner (the release slot holds a non-link path, so the updater warns and updates in place). The fault is external: the activation Doctor exits 1 at startup while the Gateway is stopped. It writes nothing; a NODE_OPTIONS preload in the update's environment does this, with no product hook. At the same moment a tracked file in the checkout is edited, as an editor or formatter would. Afterwards the cell reverts the edit and runs a plain `openclaw update`.

- **RED on base:** pending (cell queued; this body is updated when it finishes).
- **GREEN on head:** pending.
- **Base, simple case (Doctor fails, checkout clean):** the run is already rolled back on base, with the previous Gateway serving and no mark. This is why the red case needs the refused rollback.
- **Unit and CLI regressions:** red on base production code, green on head. Recordings: [unit red (base)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47932d9d-6b79-4e14-97c2-446eb1de3acb), [unit green (head 8e7b5d8; later commits only merge main)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6568bf6b-e76a-49ad-8ad3-d2b8ecb7aaaf).
  - `update-runner-git.test.ts` "retains the candidate after migration starts": 5 rows red on base (`dataAtRisk: state-migrated-no-rollback`), all green. The `doctor-data-at-risk` row keeps the child's mark (negative control).
  - `update-command-post-update-recovery.test.ts` "records no data risk when a Git checkout's Doctor fails": a real Git checkout and real `finishUpdate`.
    - `operator-edited`: red on base (`expected 'state-migrated-no-rollback' to be undefined`), green.
    - `restorable`: guard; rolls back on both.
    - `unsafe-without-doctor`: negative control; final recovery still restarts.
  - `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts` "carries a failed Doctor child's own data-risk verdict":
    - `runner` row red on base.
    - `revoked-runner` row red on the first head (which wrapped the authority error).
    - The package-verification, none and deferred rows are guards.
  - `update-command-initialization.test.ts` "pre-activation route": the refusal row is red on base; the uncertain-child row is a guard.
  - `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` `git` scenario: a candidate Doctor really migrates two databases, then fails with a `data-at-risk` verdict. It still reports `doctor-failed`, and the pre-migration databases are restored.



<details><summary>Mutation table (each guard removed; the named test fails)</summary>

| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| Runner keeps the blanket pre-Doctor mark (base) | runner "retains the candidate…" (5 rows), CLI `operator-edited` |
| Runner drops the child's typed verdict (`recovery.dataAtRisk = refusal.reason` removed) | runner `doctor-data-at-risk` |
| Runner reports a refusal with a failed step as `unexpected-error` | database-rollback `git` scenario |
| Doctor runner does not carry the verdict | package-doctor `data-at-risk, runner` |
| Doctor runner carries any verdict kind | package-doctor `deferred, runner` |
| Doctor runner wraps an error raised after the child settled | package-doctor `data-at-risk, revoked-runner` |
| Final recovery ignores `state-migration-started` | CLI `operator-edited` (restart attempted) |
| Initialization passes the refusal through | initialization refusal row |
| Initialization swallows other errors | initialization uncertain-child row |

</details>

Checks run on the head:
- Pass: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on touched files, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`.
- Pass: `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts`, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`.
- Affected update suites through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: 16 files, 420 tests. The run first flagged five database-rollback fixtures that call `runPackageUpdateDoctor` directly; they now use `try/finally` so their post-Doctor writes still happen, as the real swap does.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine. An independent reviewer read the diff against the behavior contract:
  - Fixed: a test assertion that failed at the first head, wrapping of authority errors, and a stale rollback reason.
  - Left (below): the inspection catch.

Full raw logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected the upload (`http 401`); the decisive excerpts are above.

Base proof was taken at `138482e6517`. `origin/main` then moved to `36681444353`, but the range touches only the Git release runner and a package space test, not these paths, so the reproduction was not rerun.

## Test files audited

All of each touched file was read:
- `update-runner-git.test.ts`: one table's expectations changed.
- `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts`: one table added.
- `update-command-initialization.test.ts`: one table added.
- `update-command-doctor-rollback.test-support.ts`: the Doctor exit code is now a fixture parameter; one table added.
- `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: two Doctor fixtures moved into `try/finally`.

No test was removed or skipped.

## Steps still left to a person

None added. When a checkout's rollback is refused, the Gateway stays stopped (as before), and the message names `openclaw update repair`, which re-runs the candidate's Doctor and starts the Gateway, and `openclaw triage` for the agent-assisted route. Before, repair refused forever in that state.

## Not proven / left

- **Inspection catch (audit P0-0):** `inspectActivatedUpdateState` still turns a failed state read into `rollback-state-unverified` for in-place Git updates, because `candidateOpenedState` is always true for that runner. Before this PR the blanket mark hid it. It is now the remaining evidence-free mark on this path, and it is not changed here.
- **Doctor classifier:** `src/commands/doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts` maps `GatewayLockError` to `gateway-state-unverified` and the preflight catch-all to `incomplete-migration`. Those need typed errors at their producers; another PR handles them.
- **Package flow:** it still decides from its own state comparison and does not record the Doctor child's verdict (unchanged).
- **Handoff path:** the handoff helper exits 79 on any unsafe recovery (audit entry 14). This PR does not change that.
- **Killed Doctor (separate defect):** an exploratory cell that SIGKILLed the activation Doctor left the Gateway down. Doctor custody was reported as `active-mutation`, and both repair and the next update failed on a stale artifact lock. Reported separately.

prs.title: fix: keep automation scripts running through plugin reloads
prs.body:
Closes #201903

## What Problem This Solves

A cron Code Mode evaluation that overlaps a plugin reload can make its next tool call through the disposed plugin instance. The evaluation then fails closed even after the replacement has been reported as applied, causing the affected automation to record an error.

## User Impact

User impact: Cron script evaluations now retain the plugin generation they started with until execution and cleanup finish. Plugin replacement waits for that work, and an evaluation whose preparation resolves to an already-retired generation retries against the current generation instead of calling disposed hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron runtime cache now validates and retains plugin work as part of its runtime lease, releasing that hold only after evaluation, cancellation, catalog cleanup, and MCP cleanup settle. Stale retries re-read the cache so concurrent waiters share one replacement preparation rather than overwriting and leaking a newer runtime.

No new lifecycle owner or configuration was added; the change uses the existing plugin-work retention and runtime-cache ownership.

## Evidence

- New regressions reproduce the stale-hook failure before the fix and now prove that a paused two-tool-call evaluation drains before hook disposal, cancellation releases its hold, and two waiters share a fresh preparation without executing the disposed generation or leaking runtime disposal.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts src/cron/trigger-script.preparation.test.ts src/cron/trigger-script.admission.test.ts src/cron/trigger-script.mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **44 passed**.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json` — passed.
- Targeted Oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent local review covered base `6577f41b9ab` through final head `ec9629fccc2d6e1b62c7b20e09174ba0b069a4b0`; the late-custody and concurrent-stale-retry findings were repaired, and the final review reported no findings.

The tests execute the production cron evaluator, real headless Code Mode execution, global hook dispatch, and plugin retention/disposal lifecycle. A full Gateway reload with a live model/provider was not run.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only sessions never get the daily session reset
prs.body:
Closes #185942

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `session.reset` set to `daily` (or `idle`), Talk voice consults never apply the reset. Typed messages evaluate session freshness and roll the session over; a voice consult reuses whatever session exists, so a voice-only user keeps sending previous days' history on every consult (the reporter saw about 110k prompt tokens per request) until they happen to type.

## User Impact

User impact: a voice consult on a session past its reset boundary now rolls the session over in place before it runs (same session id, a reset boundary in its transcript), so it no longer replays expired context. This applies to browser Talk, meetings, voice calls and FaceTime, which share the consult runtime.

- Automatic resets triggered by voice consults keep queued user requests; typed-chat resets, explicit `/new` / `/reset` and Stop keep their existing cancellation behavior.
- The reset runs in the session controller's lane (it waits for work on the old session instead of cancelling it). Cancellation, caller authority and the Access program are checked before native cleanup starts. Once admitted, the reset settles even if the call closes.
- When the session-memory hook is enabled, the ended day reaches session memory: the excerpt is captured before the reset and published with `session:auto-reset` after it (the bundled session-memory hook saves its usual excerpt, 15 messages by default, as for typed chat).
- Short session keys (`voice:consult`) reset the same stored row that consults read.
- Grants of the ended conversation do not carry over: `clearRotatedSessionMetadata`, the helper every in-place rollover uses (voice, Gateway agent turns, the CLI agent command), now also drops native-runtime consent, the elevated level, the active goal and pending worktree/project intents, as typed rollover's retained state already does. The Gateway and CLI automatic resets had the same gap; their reset suites pass unchanged.
- The consult's own surface picks the `resetByChannel` override, as a typed turn's ingress channel does: browser Talk `webchat`, phone and FaceTime `voice` (both send `voice`, so `resetByChannel.voice` covers both). A stored delivery route only routes replies.
- Native agent harnesses (ACP) restart their conversation just before the reset commits, as on a typed reset; once admitted, the reset finishes even if the call closes, so the two stay in step; coding-tool (CLI) session ids are cleared with the reset, as on a typed reset.

Limits:
- A voice reset ends the agent's context, not the live call's tools: unlike a typed reset it does not close the session's MCP servers or browser tabs, and it does not fire the plugin `session_end` / `session_start` hooks or shutdown tracking, which voice never fired on main.
- Session sharing is not re-checked per consult. On main, consults that arrive as Talk RPCs are refused at RPC ingress for a caller who lost participation, while Gateway-held consults (browser Talk tool calls run by the Gateway, relay-delegated consults) run the agent with the call's retained authority and no participation check (`client-agent-consult.ts` `assertConsultCurrent`, `client-run-authority.ts`, `prepareAgentRunAdmission`). The reset uses those same guards plus the Access program, so it adds no access the following run lacks; a per-consult participation check at the call owner is a separate follow-up.
- A spoken transcript saved before the consult counts as activity, so an idle window can be extended by the speech that ends it; tracked in #191870. The daily reset is unaffected.
- After a reset, only the agent stops receiving the old history. The realtime voice model keeps the history it was given when the call started, until the call ends; a call started after the boundary still gets the previous history at startup.
- If reloading the call's history fails right after a reset, the consult that triggered the reset fails and can be asked again; the next consult retries the reload.
- When typed chat or another Talk call rolls the session over, an open call keeps sending the agent the history it loaded at call start; only a reset this call applies reloads it.
- Each consult that reaches session preparation counts as activity for the idle reset, including one the model preflight then refuses (a caller allowed to use Talk but not the selected model).
- The native harness (ACP) restart is covered only by the storage test, which verifies the harness-reset call through a mock; it does not prove an external ACP conversation restarted. The live run uses an OpenAI agent model.
- Two consults that both read the stale session at once: the second can fail when the first has already reset it, and can be asked again.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts`) prepared the session entry without any freshness evaluation. It now asks the freshness owner typed turns use (`resolveSessionEntryResetFreshnessAsync`, read-only) whether a reset is due, treating a reset owed by a deferred rollover as due, as typed setup does, and if so resets the entry on the call's own store with `resetSessionEntryLifecycle`, inside `runSessionMutation` (`kind: "reset"`, policy `wait`), re-checking freshness after the wait so a session that became active meanwhile is left alone. Cancellation, caller authority and the Access program are checked before native cleanup starts; once admitted, the reset settles even if the call closes, and the entry check at the write rejects a session changed meanwhile (the Access check is `assertOperatorAccessProgramAllowed` on the entry re-read after the wait); the new session's start time is taken when the replacement entry is built, after any wait for the old turn. Inside the lane it re-reads the entry and stops if the session changed, is model-locked or blocked. It captures the session-memory excerpt, then admits the reset once, before any effect: cancellation, caller authority and the Access program on the re-read entry. An admitted reset then settles even if the call closes, so the native conversation and the transcript stay in step: it restarts native harness conversations through the Gateway's harness cleanup (`resetSessionAgentHarnesses`, with the agent's retained registries; a harness-declared cleanup failure stops the reset so it stays due, other hook failures are logged by the registry, as for typed and Gateway resets), commits the reset (the entry check still rejects a changed or blocked session), then publishes the excerpt with `emitSessionAutoResetHook`. The reset targets the store's qualified key (`resolveSqliteSessionKey`, which reads use). `clearCommittedSessionResetRuntimeState` takes `preserveControllerInputs` so the reset keeps waiting inputs. Browser Talk then reloads the call's history (`client-agent-consult.ts`), and a failed reload is retried on the next consult. The plugin SDK keeps its consult contract; the internal callbacks, authority are not part of it.

Not changed: typed chat, the reset policy, explicit reset and Stop.

Upgrade: no stored-data format changes. Existing sessions need nothing new: the live proof creates the session with released OpenClaw 2026.11.6 and then runs this change on that state.

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same run on this change

Built Gateway, a real browser Talk call (headless Chrome, WebRTC, OpenAI realtime with `brain: agent-consult`) and an OpenAI agent model, with the bundled session-memory hook on (`llmSlug: false`). Day one: released OpenClaw 2026.11.6 with `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, one typed session asked to remember "PELICAN-DAY1". The Gateway clock then moves two days ahead and the call asks aloud: "Check with your agent: what code word did I ask you to remember earlier in this conversation? If you have none, answer none." Both runs use the same day-one state, on `main` `f02d9dc2725` and on `main` plus this change.

```
main:        agent request carried 20 messages including "PELICAN-DAY1"
             spoken answer: "PELICAN-DAY1"
             session memory: no file saved (no reset happened)
this change: agent request carried 7 messages (the exchanges the reset keeps and the question), no "PELICAN-DAY1"
             spoken answer: "none"
             session memory: memory/2026-11-24-0328.md saved for the ended conversation, containing
             'user: "Please remember this code word for later: PELICAN-DAY1. Reply only with OK."'
```

Proof artifice: the Gateway clock is shifted two days with a preload, and the spoken question is synthesized speech (OpenAI TTS) played into headless Chrome.

### Tests

- `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts` › "configured session reset": a stale daily session is reset on the call's own store and a same-day one is not; a reset owed by an earlier rollover (`updatedAt: 0`) is applied, also with automatic resets off; a blocked stale session is left for admission to reject; earlier queued input is kept; a caller that cancels or loses its authority during preparation, or whom the session's Access program refuses, leaves the session and its native harness untouched; a reset already in native cleanup finishes when the caller cancels or closes the call; each consult counts as activity; with the bundled session-memory hook registered, a daily reset saves a memory file holding the message the reset dropped from view, and the other rows save none; a short session key resets the qualified row; a phone consult (`voice`) with `resetByChannel.voice` off keeps its session; each reset restarts native harness conversations once. On `main` the reset, owed-reset, queue, authority and activity cases fail; the same-day, blocked and cancel cases pass, as they describe unchanged behavior.
- `src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.terminal-writes.test.ts` › "stops quoting call-start history once a consult rolls the session over": through the real browser runner and consult runtime, neither the resetting consult nor the next one quotes the call-start history. On `main` it fails (`expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, false ]`).
- With this change both suites pass, along with the Talk handler, consult-admission, mailbox, reset-cleanup and consult-runtime suites. Final-content bench checks found no PR-caused failures; two checks (Plugin SDK surface budget, dead-export scan) fail identically on the base. Test lines are net +276 against `main`: the reset is new runtime code with distinct guards, each a separate failure (owed reset, short key, channel policy, Access refusal, cancellation and lost authority before and during native cleanup, queue preservation, saved memory, native harness restart, activity), folded into the existing table-driven storage suite (its real per-store session fixture and consult runtime are reused, no new helper), plus one browser test in the existing terminal-writes suite for the history the agent receives; the earlier 169-line browser parity test was dropped because the storage suite covers its cases.

prs.title: fix(ci): publish docs mirrors through pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The docs sync workflow pushes generated commits directly to `openclaw/docs` main. That prevents the mirror from following the organization's PR-only publication policy.

## User Impact

Docs updates become pull requests with the validated source revision and payload recorded. Publication waits for the target's strict `Publication merge admission` status from GitHub Actions. The target gate must be activated before this publisher can complete; unresolved or blocked candidates remain available for inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

One native Git-owner policy now owns guard, prepare, and publish. It preserves source ancestry checks, rebase/dependency validation (including the current slugify closure), and MDX validation, then freezes a single-parent candidate. The writer creates an immutable branch, performs a normal exact-head squash, and verifies the actual merged tree and source metadata before reporting publication.

Open PRs, orphan branches, uncertain responses, base movement, and exposed bypasses produce visible holds. The source token never posts the target admission status. Manual and automatic runs share a noncanceling queue.

## Evidence

- Nine real Git/native-owner/HTTP fixture tests pass (21.962 seconds), covering normal and uncertain merges, branch-creation races, stale bases, missing/invalid admission, retained candidates, unowned paths, and incorrect/retargeted receipts.
- Targeted workflow parsing, all five workflow shell blocks under ShellCheck, pinned oxfmt, Python syntax, and whitespace checks pass.
- Existing native prepare fixtures were updated, but Vitest and actual pinned-owner hosted execution remain unverified locally: the native worktree is code-only with no qualified dependency installation.
- Independent semantic review passed at `e7f85dab1dd7f543163b74e25bebcb6f5de678c7`. Automated P0–P2 review completed with one P1 declined: it assumed Actions only emits check runs. The target explicitly [posts a commit status](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/blob/c00cdb39d3a008fa7c2ac8875508eba8ee480591/.github/scripts/i18n/publication_admission.py#L60-L66), using [the target Actions token](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/blob/c00cdb39d3a008fa7c2ac8875508eba8ee480591/.github/workflows/publication-admission.yml). Both implementer and independent reviewer verified that contract; changing to check-run polling would break it.
- No manual workflow dispatch, target merge, deployment, or settings change was performed.

The old direct-main writer is removed. Net changes: production +284 lines, tests +320 lines, operational docs +3 lines. Production growth owns durable candidate recovery, server admission, and verified publication; the existing generator and dependency validator remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(codex): align native delegation prompts with effective collaboration policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex-backed OpenClaw agents can have native collaboration disabled by their **effective Codex-home config** (`agents.enabled=false`, `features.multi_agent_v2=false`) while prebuilt OpenClaw developer instructions still recommend unavailable native `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent`. This misdirects delegation despite the allowed OpenClaw `sessions_spawn` tool being present. Prompt-reporting must also reflect the **actual** instructions given to Codex, rather than an earlier unverified seed.

## Fix

- Read the effective native collaboration policy in the existing Codex lifecycle preflight; preserve the OpenClaw `sessions_spawn` route when native collaboration is disabled and keep native delegation when V2 is explicitly enabled.
- Refresh only the generated policy fragment without overwriting parent-local, workspace, or prompt-hook instruction carriers.
- Reconcile the authoritative prompt build's developer/thread instructions and refresh the existing System Prompt report after preflight, so thread/start, diagnostics, trajectory, and `llm_input` observe the same effective policy. Handle a later preflight after client replacement.
- Apply the native-home policy at normal attempts and the existing native thread/fork lifecycle. No new authorization, privileged tool, channel delivery, production config, or external service behavior is added.
- Drop the redundant mock-only lifecycle assertion matrix; retain the real normal-attempt protocol regression.

## Evidence

- **Red baseline (Windows, isolated checkout):** before the latest fix, `run-attempt.test.ts` case `routes AGENTS.md natively and MEMORY.md through tools` failed because `systemPromptReport.systemPrompt.chars` was **2715**, but actual thread-start instructions were **3223** characters. This reproduces the review's prompt-report mismatch.
- **Green after fix (same isolated PR checkout):** **3/3 targeted tests passed across 2 files**: the previously failing AGENTS.md/MEMORY.md report test and both `normal attempt uses native-home collaboration settings` cases (V2 disabled/enabled). The added checks compare the report's character count and SHA-256 to actual `thread/start` instructions and check that `sessions_spawn` remains offered.
- **Original PR verification:** `thread-prompt.test.ts` 25/25, `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` 19/19, `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` 14/14, earlier isolated protocol normal-attempt 2/2 (see original PR validation notes / commits). These are scoped tests, not a whole-project test claim.
- **Current-upstream integration and green regressions:** merged upstream `main` from 2026-11-03 into the PR branch without conflicts; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` exited 0. On the merged tree, the previously failing AGENTS.md/MEMORY.md report regression **passed 1/1**; after updating the test to include the separate parent-local inference relay introduced by newer main, the disabled/enabled native collaboration cases **passed 2/2** (Vitest extension-database-workers, latest test commit `792d35458e8`). The report's length and SHA-256 are compared with the composed **native thread policy + the actual conversation/tool-binding relay**, not the `thread/start` string alone. Changed-file Oxfmt passes; Oxlint **0 warnings / 0 errors**; `git diff --check` passes.
- **Native binary evidence (earlier reproducible isolated probe):** Codex app-server 0.164.0 `config/read` returned disabled native collaboration and a V2-enabled control from a synthetic, credential-free native-home configuration; the OpenClaw thread-start regression uses a deterministic native protocol transport fixture. This is **not** a live Gateway-to-model-inference E2E.

## Remaining verification / reviewer attention

- **Latest-head CI verified (2026-11-22):** The five returned PR-triggered workflow runs for `792d35458e8b2f26ea4343c7dae6ff6e86332250` completed successfully: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558287182), [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558286842), [macOS Periphery Dead Code report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558286876), [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558286747), and [OpenGrep PR Diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558286822). This is CI evidence for that exact head, not proof of current-base integration, a production-equivalent Windows build, or the live runtime behavior requested below.
- **Live behavior proof remains unverified:** The requested real Gateway-to-Codex disabled-collaboration run with successful `sessions_spawn`, enabled control, effective-instruction/prompt-report agreement, and retained-session continuation after latest-stable upgrade and app-server restart remain outstanding. A controlled Windows preflight on the clean exact-head checkout on 2026-11-22 did not establish a separate authorized model connection or complete an executable Gateway build. No model request or live delegation/restart/continuation test was performed; the preflight build was cancelled, not diagnosed as a product build failure. Production Gateway configuration, sessions, and channels were not changed.
- **Current integration status (2026-11-22):** GitHub reports `mergeable: false`. Integration with the current base remains outstanding. The earlier successful CI runs must not be treated as evidence that the PR is currently merge-ready.
- Confirm that prompt hooks and parent-local text remain untouched when the generated policy refreshes, and that the same effective instruction string reaches thread/start and the System Prompt report after client replacement.

Related: #170320.
