prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): make the SDK surface check pass on main again
prs.body:
## Budget increases awaiting owner approval

This PR stays a draft until each line below is approved. Every line is an export that a bundled plugin imports today, added by the PR named beside it. None is in a tagged release. An unapproved line comes out of the budget and the export is removed or moved instead.

Public entrypoints `163 → 164`

- [ ] `openclaw/plugin-sdk/resource-profile` (new subpath). Added by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478. Imported by `knowledge` (3 files).

Public exports `3896 → 3905`, callable exports `2245 → 2253`

- [ ] `reply-runtime` · `isReplySessionInitConflictError` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201363. Imported by `discord`.
- [ ] `interactive-runtime` · `agentControlText` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764. Imported by `discord`, `feishu`, `line`, `mattermost`, `msteams`, `slack`, `telegram`.
- [ ] `interactive-runtime` · `stampAgentControlValue` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764. Imported by `telegram`.
- [ ] `interactive-runtime` · `stampAgentControls` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764. Imported by `telegram`.
- [ ] `gateway-runtime` · `prepareGatewayPublicationReaderV1` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201073. Imported by `session-share`.
- [ ] `gateway-runtime` · `loadGatewayReaderIdentityV1` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201075. Imported by `session-share`.
- [ ] `agent-harness-runtime` · `AgentHarnessRuntimeUpdateRequiredError` (class, so it adds to exports but not to callable exports). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201130. Imported by `codex` (2 files).
- [ ] `native-command-registry` · `loadCommandArgMenuModelCatalog` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201254. Imported by `discord`, `slack`, `telegram`.
- [ ] `resource-profile` · `getResourceProfile` (function). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478. Imported by `knowledge` (3 files).

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` fails on `main`. Anyone who changes `src/plugin-sdk/` gets a red `check:changed` for exports they did not add, and the budget has stopped telling reviewers when the public plugin SDK grows. Between 17 and 21 November, eight merged PRs added one public entrypoint and 17 public exports (9 callable) with no budget line.

## User Impact

User impact: none on released versions. Nothing removed here is in a tagged release: no `v*` tag contains any of the eight PRs, and the check reports no removal from the shipped `v2026.11.6` inventory.

Plugin developers building against `main` lose eight names that no plugin imports:

- `onResourceProfileChange` on `openclaw/plugin-sdk/resource-profile`. `getResourceProfile` stays.
- The type names `ResourceProfile`, `GatewayPublicationReaderV1`, `ControlUiDraftProposal`, `ControlUiDraftProposalOutcome`, `ControlUiComposerTaskStep`, `ControlUiComposerTask` and `ControlUiComposerHandle`. The functions and the composer API they describe keep the same signatures. A plugin can no longer import these names to annotate its own helpers.

Maintainers get a passing surface check once the lines above are approved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each unbudgeted export got one test: does anything outside core import it by name? Nine do, from bundled plugins, so they are budgeted with a comment naming the PR that added them. Eight do not, so they leave the public surface instead of raising the number.

| Removed from the public surface | Added by | Who imported it | What happens to it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource-profile` · `onResourceProfileChange` (function) | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478 | No plugin. Docs and one core test only. | Deleted together with its listener set in `src/infra/gateway-resource-profile.ts`. |
| `resource-profile` · `ResourceProfile` (type) | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478 | Nobody. | Stays as a local type in the owner module. |
| `gateway-runtime` · `GatewayPublicationReaderV1` (type) | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201073 | No plugin. One core test, which imports it from the Gateway module. | Re-export removed. |
| `control-ui` · five composer types | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | No plugin. The Control UI host imported `ControlUiDraftProposal` by relative path. | Kept as local types in `src/plugin-sdk/control-ui.ts`. The host now takes the proposal type from its own composer task owner. |

Two judgment calls for the owner:

- **`onResourceProfileChange` is deleted, not hidden.** The resource profile is resolved once at Gateway startup and changing `gateway.resources.profile` needs a restart, so no listener can observe a change in a running Gateway, and no plugin subscribes. Keeping the function in core with no caller would fail the dead-export scan.
- **The seven type names are a real trade.** Hiding a type name lowers the count without shrinking the contract; plugin authors lose a convenient annotation. No bundled plugin registers a composer action today (only docs and the UI e2e test do), so nothing in the repo pays that cost yet. Restoring any of them is a one-word change plus one budget line.

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/resource-profile` now exports a single function for a single bundled consumer. It could live on an existing subpath and save the entrypoint line; I kept the dedicated subpath because the SDK guide asks for narrow purpose-built subpaths.

## Evidence

**The check, before and after** (Blacksmith Testbox, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`):

| | Budget on `main` | `main` at `ead1aff00c1` | This branch | Budget in this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public entrypoints | 163 | 164 (fails) | 164 | 164 |
| Public exports | 3896 | 3913 (fails) | 3905 | 3905 |
| Public callable exports | 2245 | 2254 (fails) | 2253 | 2253 |
| Public deprecated exports | 221 | 221 | 221 | 221 |

The check also reports `shipped Plugin SDK v2026.11.6: no unauthorized removals` on this branch.

**Where the drift came from.** The budget was exact at `422ff062032` (17 November, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201014): 163 entrypoints and 3894 exports. A name-by-name diff of every public entrypoint between that commit and `ead1aff00c1` gives 19 added exports and none removed. Two of the 19 were budgeted by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203044. The other 17:

| Entrypoint | Export | Kind | Commit | PR | Bundled-plugin importers | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reply-runtime` | `isReplySessionInitConflictError` | function | `ee37dd3b033` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201363 | `discord` | budget |
| `interactive-runtime` | `agentControlText` | function | `cd2ae19272a` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764 | 7 channel plugins | budget |
| `interactive-runtime` | `stampAgentControlValue` | function | `cd2ae19272a` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764 | `telegram` | budget |
| `interactive-runtime` | `stampAgentControls` | function | `cd2ae19272a` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201764 | `telegram` | budget |
| `gateway-runtime` | `prepareGatewayPublicationReaderV1` | function | `5795128db2d` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201073 | `session-share` | budget |
| `gateway-runtime` | `loadGatewayReaderIdentityV1` | function | `06d62b47d25` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201075 | `session-share` | budget |
| `gateway-runtime` | `GatewayPublicationReaderV1` | type | `5795128db2d` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201073 | none | removed |
| `agent-harness-runtime` | `AgentHarnessRuntimeUpdateRequiredError` | class | `1680f545048` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201130 | `codex` | budget |
| `native-command-registry` | `loadCommandArgMenuModelCatalog` | function | `3e0d3687c5d` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201254 | `discord`, `slack`, `telegram` | budget |
| `control-ui` | `ControlUiDraftProposal` | type | `a3d7e40f295` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | none | made local |
| `control-ui` | `ControlUiDraftProposalOutcome` | type | `a3d7e40f295` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | none | made local |
| `control-ui` | `ControlUiComposerTaskStep` | type | `a3d7e40f295` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | none | made local |
| `control-ui` | `ControlUiComposerTask` | type | `a3d7e40f295` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | none | made local |
| `control-ui` | `ControlUiComposerHandle` | type | `a3d7e40f295` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201695 | none | made local |
| `resource-profile` (new entrypoint) | `getResourceProfile` | function | `ce74e42351e` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478 | `knowledge` | budget |
| `resource-profile` | `onResourceProfileChange` | function | `ce74e42351e` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478 | none | removed |
| `resource-profile` | `ResourceProfile` | type | `ce74e42351e` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202478 | none | removed |

The callable flags come from the same type checker the report uses, dumped per export on the Testbox. They sum to the reported 9.

**Checks on this branch** (Blacksmith Testbox leases `tbx_01m7zcczy5f1361bk2edv35v7s` and `tbx_01m7zemk1gar5vxdwnexbwrghz`; the tree checked there is the tree of commit `4700c01fadd`):

- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passes with the numbers above. `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` pass. So do the test type programs, `pnpm tsgo:test:src` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff` from `ead1aff00c1` to this head reports exactly the eight removals and no additions. It lists 12 more exports only because their declarations mention the now-local types: 11 on `control-ui` and `getResourceProfile`. Acknowledgement digest `ea9bfe83`.
- Focused tests pass: `src/infra/gateway-resource-profile.test.ts` (16), `src/gateway/server.auth.publication-reader.test.ts` (44, 2 skipped), the three `extensions/knowledge` suites that mock the subpath (22) and `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` (4).
- oxlint on the touched TypeScript files and `oxfmt --check` on all ten files are clean.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` fails, and fails the same way on `main`. The scan output is identical on the base commit and on this branch: `FeishuBotAddedEvent` and `formatFeishuMediaContent` in `extensions/feishu`, and `htmlTagAttributeValues`, `isLikelyImageAttachment` and `safeHostForUrl` in `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/html.ts`. Nothing this PR touches appears in it, which is the part that matters here: the removals left no orphaned export behind.

Size: production code +10 −34, budget script +13 −3, tests +8 −28, docs +8 −16.

**Public consumers of the eight removed names.** The `plugin-sdk-impact` ClawHub query (21 November) found no static reference to any of them across 2,694 eligible public plugin releases (2,267 fully analyzed, 426 partly, 1 failed). ClawHub labels that coverage incomplete, so read it as strong evidence, not proof.

**Review.** Local autoreview (Codex engine) on the committed range `ead1aff00c1..4700c01fadd`, priorities P0 to P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings, verdict "patch is correct" (0.88). The reviewer said it could not check repository-wide callers or builds from its bundle; the Testbox runs above cover those.

**Not verified**

- The budget lines are not approved yet; see the top.
- No full `pnpm build` and no pull request CI. Draft PRs skip most CI jobs.
- `deadcode:exports` stays red until the feishu and msteams exports above are handled. That is separate work.
- Bundled-plugin usage comes from a repository-wide search and `tsgo:extensions`, not from the Plugin Inspector scan that `plugin-sdk-impact` describes. Plugins that live outside this repository and outside ClawHub are invisible to every check here.

### Should this check run in pull request CI?

Recommended, as a follow-up, not in this PR.

- **Today:** the only workflow step is in `workflow-sanity.yml` under the `generated-doc-baselines` job, which runs on `workflow_dispatch` only. The other caller is `scripts/check-changed.mts`, which runs it when an SDK path changes, but only for someone who runs `check:changed`. Nothing runs it on a pull request or on a push to `main`. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201254 recorded the red check in its own body (`public exports 3897 > 3894`), and nothing in CI stopped the merge.
- **Cost:** one type program over all 389 SDK entrypoints. On a warm Testbox the check itself took 7 seconds. On a fresh box, two back-to-back passes (the check, then a per-export dump) took 2m37s together. Checkout and dependency install come on top. Peak memory was 3.9 GB resident (`/usr/bin/time -v`), so the script's 8 GB heap flag is headroom, not what the run uses.
- **Where:** a `plugin-sdk-surface` row in the `check-additional` matrix built by `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` (next to `plugin-sdk-api-diff`), selected when the changed paths match the `PLUGIN_SDK_SURFACE_PATH_RE` set that `check-changed` already uses. Public entrypoints may not use wildcard re-exports (that budget is 0), so an export count can only change through those paths.
- **How often:** in the last 14 days, 127 of 4,577 commits on `main` touched those paths, about 9 a day.
- **Also worth doing:** run it on pushes to `main` so a type-level change elsewhere (a re-exported value becoming callable or deprecated) is caught within one commit.

prs.title: feat: move a conversation that has no project into one
prs.body:
Closes #202268

## What changes

On main, moving work from the default workspace into an existing project requires another conversation and a manual transfer of local edits.

Say **“let’s work on OpenClaw”** in the default workspace. The model moves this conversation into the registered project with `session_project`. The model can carry out the rest of that message in the project’s managed checkout. For a move-only request, the reply confirms the destination. The conversation keeps its messages. The tool is available by default for eligible sessions, subject to tool policy. The Gateway refuses a second move.

Choose **Move to project…** in the conversation menu to do the same move yourself. When a matching checkout has file changes, the dialog previews how many will be copied. The project checkout restores those changes before repository setup. The original checkout stays in place, and earlier links still open its files.

Project moves share the checks for active runs, background processes, terminals, and child sessions with PR workspace preparation.

Sandboxed conversations can move with Docker or Podman. For other sandbox backends, the picker explains why the move is unavailable and the Gateway refuses before saving a project or creating a checkout.

## Control UI comparison

Captured in the built Control UI with a synthetic project and two file changes. Main screenshot at `e309df612e`.

| Conversation menu on main | Project move dialog in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main conversation menu without a project move action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/8ea3ec35-58db-4f9b-8e2a-0143e9ef7810.png) | ![Move to a project dialog showing Changes to 2 files will be copied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/ac26f04c-e00c-4972-b493-62ce632fe8eb.png) |

## Evidence

### Live model handoff

The live Qwen3-8B capture at `4b990ab` shows the same conversation in Juniper and the release code from its README. The model called `session_project` and finished the read in the project checkout.

![Control UI showing the same conversation in Juniper and the release code returned from its README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b31285503734f99cc587a206f8819c0fb4cd455b/images/2026/11/51b055c2-4807-4c96-ab56-c24d904eb87e.png)

### Sandbox admission

On `9546f55`, an isolated Gateway with a real loopback SSH sandbox showed the Docker or Podman requirement in the picker and refused the direct move request. The session kept its original workspace and ID, had no project worktree, and replied to the next message.

The carry fixture exercises the Docker move handoff after the initiating turn ends. Live Docker and Podman carry remain pending.

### Upgrade compatibility on `9546f55`

Each published binary created a conversation, saved a user message and reply, and registered Juniper in its own profile. On startup, the Gateway built at `9546f55` loaded that profile. The same conversation then moved into Juniper through the built Control UI and got a new reply. These checks used synthetic repositories and a scripted local model.

| Starting release | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [2026.9.37](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.37) (extended stable) | Passed |
| [2026.10.33](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.33) | Passed |
| [2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.6) | Passed |

Each run preserved the session ID, both original messages, the project record, and the source commit. Repository setup saw the copied edit. The untracked file survived and the original files stayed in the source checkout.

The Control UI capture shows the same upgrade scenario at `4b990ab`.

![Control UI after the upgrade showing the released version’s reply, the successful move to Juniper, and the new reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b31285503734f99cc587a206f8819c0fb4cd455b/images/2026/11/e49925c6-e928-43c6-bc47-120f555523b5.png)

### Build and tests

- Full build and Plugin SDK declaration budget passed. The declaration graph was **5,284,258 / 5,385,536 bytes**.
- 139 focused tests passed across Gateway moves, worktree carry, sandbox preparation, handoff, tool and prompt behavior, and the Control UI. Core typecheck, scoped lint, and formatting passed.
- The test-line allocation includes 47 lines for the regression that checks the session and worktree after an SSH move is refused.
- A paired Qwen3-8B measurement found that the compact project tool description and guidance save 95 input tokens.
- Shared tool-display metadata keeps direct JSON imports out of startup. A paired build with that change removed put chat boot 136 B over main.

prs.title: fix(update): keep the openclaw command and Gateway working after a pnpm update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backport of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201735 (proposal for the release owner; do not merge without the release owner's decision).

On pnpm-managed installs (`pnpm add -g openclaw`), `openclaw update` can leave no working `openclaw` command, because the launcher points into the removed update stage, and on pnpm 11.28/12.21 a Gateway that is refused restart and stays down. This was measured with published 2026.11.4 updating to public 2026.11.5.

## User Impact

User impact: pnpm installs update to a working CLI and a Gateway that serves the new version. Launchers already broken by an earlier updater are repaired by this release's Doctor and Gateway startup, without a user command.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries the same commits as the main PR, cherry-picked cleanly onto this branch. It relocates and verifies pnpm's quoted shim form (`"$basedir_abs"/'target'`). It refuses to finalize a launcher that still names the stage, and fails an update whose published launcher cannot start instead of reporting success. Service revalidation now matches the unchanged definition against its own installation root after pnpm repoints the global entry into its versioned store. The fingerprint, name, profile and manager-UID protection is unchanged.

This branch now also includes the apostrophe and quoting fix. Launcher relocation parses each shell word, rewrites its value and quotes it again, so a pnpm home or global directory containing `'`, `"`, `$`, a space or a backslash relocates correctly, including pnpm's `'\''` spelling of the stage in `NODE_PATH`. A repair reports success only when nothing in the launcher still names the stage. It also includes the later review fixes from the main PR:
- the pre-stop guard checks only the launchers the swap publishes;
- a shim resolves physically only when it assigns `basedir_abs`;
- repair checks ownership on the same bytes it rewrites, skips FIFOs and other special files, and handles pnpm's home-level shim;
- the recovery command is `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@<installed-version>`;
- the launcher-name helper is a leaf module (`package-update-launcher-names.ts`), so the native stage adds no import cycle;
- a `$'` in a live path stays literal during relocation;
- the pre-stop refusal names the direct pnpm reinstall, the Gateway reinstall and restart, and `openclaw triage`.
On this branch the cherry-pick dropped the import change for `package-update-release-switch.ts`, which does not exist on 2026.11.6.

The main PR lists the remaining follow-ups; they are not part of this backport.

## Evidence

- On `release/2026.11.6`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the launcher repair, runtime relocation, native stage, all `package-update-swap*`, package filesystem, service install root, Gateway startup plugin, update-restart module outcome and eager import closure tests passes (258 tests). `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` report 0 cycles, and `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- End-to-end proof is on the main PR, from real pnpm 12.21.0 cells: published 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 updating to the fixed build (the first hop), and fixed build to fixed build. Both end with a working CLI and the Gateway serving the new version.

## Not proven

- **Target layout from a registry: now covered.** A real cell ran published 2026.11.5 → a plain `openclaw update` → published 2026.11.6 from the public registry only. The updater installs a registry target in the project-store layout (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), the same layout class the earlier tarball-target cells used. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7018135106.
- **Still unproven:** a fixed target installed from a registry. It cannot be exercised before a fixed version is published; the fixed builds were proven as tarball targets.
- **Still unproven:** pnpm 11, which ignores the `virtualStoreType=project` setting the updater passes, so its target layout may differ. A pnpm 11 cell is being prepared.

prs.title: fix: let GPT-Live voice sessions use substantive delegation guidance in Voice Call and Discord
prs.body:
Closes #202910

## What Problem This Solves

When a realtime voice session runs on GPT-Live and `consultPolicy` is `"substantive"`, Voice Call tells the model to "call openclaw_agent_consult", a tool GPT-Live does not have: it delegates natively. Voice Call's built-in default prompt has the same problem on every GPT-Live call: it tells the model to "call openclaw_agent_consult" and "call openclaw_end_call". Discord voice cannot use `"substantive"` at all, because its schema only allows `auto` and `always`, and `always` is rejected on GPT-Live. So on GPT-Live there is no working way to ask the model to hand facts, memory and tool questions to the OpenClaw agent instead of answering them itself.

## User Impact

User impact: `consultPolicy: "substantive"` now works on GPT-Live in both Voice Call and Discord voice. The model gets delegation guidance that matches how it delegates, and Discord accepts the same three values as Voice Call. Existing configs are unaffected: `auto` and `always` keep their current prompts and checks, and `always` is still rejected on GPT-Live.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each surface made part of this decision on its own. Voice Call passed `substantive` to the shared session policy as `auto` (so the GPT-Live check passed) but built the prompt from the raw config before it knew which model would answer. Now:

- The shared session policy (`resolveRealtimeVoiceSessionPolicy`) carries `auto | substantive | always` unchanged and stays the only place that rejects `always` on GPT-Live.
- The shared prompt builder (`buildRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultPolicyInstructions`) takes `handlesAgentConsult` and, for native-delegation models, emits a "Delegation policy" block that does not name `openclaw_agent_consult`. Both public SDK helpers gain an optional field, so existing callers are unchanged.
- Voice Call adds the consult block in the realtime handler after it resolves the routed model and session policy, instead of at startup. The block now comes after the agent context and call brief, the same position Discord already uses.
- Voice Call's built-in default `realtime.instructions` is reworded on native-delegation models ("delegate it to OpenClaw before answering"); the handler already appends the GPT-Live hang-up guidance. Only a configured value exactly equal to the default is reworded: custom `realtime.instructions`, including a copy of the default with added text, are sent as written. GA models keep the default byte for byte.
- Discord adds `substantive` to its schema, type and help text, and passes `handlesAgentConsult` into the shared builder. Config metadata and docs are regenerated.

Host-side enforcement of `always` (Discord `realtime-consults.ts`, Voice Call `scheduleForcedAgentConsult`) is unchanged.

<details><summary>GPT-Live wording</summary>

```
Delegation policy:
- Delegate every request that needs facts, memory, current information, tools, workspace state, or the user's own context, even if you think you know the answer.
- Answer directly only for greetings, acknowledgements, and brief latency checks.
- After delegating, do not answer the question yourself before the result arrives; one short backchannel is fine.
- When the result arrives, speak it once and do not repeat an answer you already gave.
```

GA models keep the existing "Consult behavior" blocks byte for byte.

</details>

## Evidence

The new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass on this branch. The Discord GPT-Live case reproduces the bug directly: on main the session instructions contain `openclaw_agent_consult`.

| Test | `origin/main` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discord GPT-Live, `substantive`: no `openclaw_agent_consult`, has Delegation policy | fails: `expected 'You are OpenClaw\'s Discord voice int…' not to contain 'openclaw_agent_consult'` | passes |
| Discord GPT-Live, `auto`: no consult block | passes | passes |
| Voice Call GPT-Live, `substantive`: bridge instructions start with Delegation policy, no tool name | fails: `expected 'Be helpful.\n\nUse native agent deleg…' to match /^Be helpful\.\n\nDelegation policy:…/` | passes |
| Voice Call GA, `substantive`: Consult behavior block reaches the bridge | fails: `expected 'Be helpful.' to match /^Be helpful\.\n\nConsult behavior:\n/` | passes |
| Shared builder: Live wording, `auto` and `toolPolicy: none` add nothing | fails | passes |
| Voice Call GPT-Live, default base prompt: no `openclaw_agent_consult` / `openclaw_end_call` (GA unchanged) | fails on the previous head `1afa441b5` | passes |
| Voice Call GPT-Live, customized default (default + "Always speak Spanish."): sent as written | fails on `ca74c8806` (`expected false to be true`) | passes |
| Discord schema accepts `auto`, `substantive`, `always` | `substantive` fails: `Invalid option: expected one of "auto"\|"always"` | passes |

Red-on-base was run by swapping the 10 changed source files for their `origin/main` versions with the new tests in place, then restoring and `cmp`-checking them.

### Real GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`, OpenAI Platform key)

Isolated test Gateway built from this branch (own `OPENCLAW_HOME`, mock agent model, no production config). A local script plays Twilio for one inbound call: it posts the inbound webhook, opens the issued media stream and sends a recorded "What's on my calendar today?" as G.711 μ-law. A test-only TLS relay records every frame between the Gateway and `api.openai.com`.

Tool names in what GPT-Live receives, counted from the recorded frames:

```
$ count-tool-names runs/<head 1afa441b5>/wire.jsonl
session.start: openclaw_agent_consult/openclaw_end_call = 2 | Delegation policy: yes | "delegate it to OpenClaw": no
$ count-tool-names runs/<this head>/wire.jsonl
session.start: openclaw_agent_consult/openclaw_end_call = 0 | Delegation policy: yes | "delegate it to OpenClaw": yes
```

The `session.start` sent on this head (identity/agent-context lines shortened):

```
You are OpenClaw's phone-call realtime voice interface. Keep spoken replies brief and natural. When a question needs deeper reasoning, current information, or tools, delegate it to OpenClaw before answering.

Agent context: You speak for an OpenClaw agent that can run many sessions at once, ...

Delegation policy:
- Delegate every request that needs facts, memory, current information, tools, workspace state, or the user's own context, even if you think you know the answer.
- Answer directly only for greetings, acknowledgements, and brief latency checks.
- After delegating, do not answer the question yourself before the result arrives; one short backchannel is fine.
- When the result arrives, speak it once and do not repeat an answer you already gave.

Use native agent delegation for OpenClaw work. To end the current call, say out loud that you are hanging up and delegate; ...
```

That these instructions make GPT-Live delegate: the same `session.start` and greeting note replayed straight to the GPT-Live API, then the question as audio:

```
$ node live-probe.mjs <recorded wire> A
variant A: delegated=true
caller transcript:  What's on my calendar today
assistant transcript:  Hi there. Hello! How can I help you today? Checking for you. You've got one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m.
event types: session.started, session.output_transcript.delta, session.commentary.appended, session.input_transcript.delta, session.delegation.created, session.usage.updated, session.closed
```

`session.delegation.created` arrived about 3 s after the question. The answer came back through `session.commentary.append`, as the bridge does.

Control on a GA model (`gpt-realtime-2.1`, same kit and same call): the question is transcribed, the model calls `openclaw_agent_consult {"question":"What's on my calendar today?", ...}`, the mock agent runs, and the call speaks "You have one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m."

**Full Voice Call GPT-Live run:** blocked on main by a separate bug, now fixed in #203388 (issue #203387). With that fix, the same real GPT-Live inbound call hears the question, delegates through Voice Call's call-owned agent consult, the agent runs, and the answer is spoken (evidence in #203388).

The original note: On inbound calls, Voice Call withholds caller audio until the opening greeting finishes. It detects that through `response.done` and drained playback. GPT-Live sends neither: its public events contain no done event, and it keeps streaming silent audio. So no caller audio reaches GPT-Live after the greeting: the recorded wire shows no `session.input_audio.append` for 38 s. The probe above with input paused for 8 s after the greeting (variant B) still delegates once audio resumes, so the model is fine. This will be a separate issue and PR.

### Real Discord voice session on GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`, `consultPolicy: "substantive"`)

Isolated test Gateway built from this head (`c0e237f75`), own `OPENCLAW_HOME`, a throwaway test bot in a private test guild, OpenAI Platform test key, mock agent model. The same TLS relay records the Gateway's GPT-Live frames. A person joined the voice channel and asked "What's on my calendar today?".

On `origin/main` the same config does not load:

```
$ openclaw config validate
Config needs correction: $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  - channels.discord.voice.realtime.consultPolicy: invalid config: must be equal to one of the allowed values (allowed: "auto", "always")
```

On this branch (Gateway log, ids redacted):

```
discord voice: occupied autoJoin joining guild=<guild> channel=<voice> humans=1
discord voice: realtime bridge starting mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1 voice=marin consultPolicy=substantive toolPolicy=owner ...
discord voice: realtime bridge ready mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1 voice=marin
discord voice: realtime lifecycle server:session.delegation.created
discord voice: agent turn start guild=<guild> channel=<voice> ... agent=main user=<owner> owner=true model=route-default chars=137
discord voice: agent turn answer (61 chars) guild=<guild> channel=<voice> ... agent=main
discord voice: realtime audio playback stopped reason=player-idle ... audioMs=5600
```

GPT-Live frames from the same session:

```
session.start: openclaw_agent_consult/openclaw_end_call = 0 | Delegation policy: yes
5.1 s s2c session.delegation.created {"offset_ms":3400,"delegation":{"id":"<item>","type":"delegation","target":"client"}}
8.5 s c2s session.commentary.append {"delegation_id":"<item>","content":"You have one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m."}
caller transcript:  Calendar today
assistant transcript:  One sec, checking that. You've got one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m.
```

The `session.start` instructions end with the Discord voice prompt, the agent context, and the GPT-Live "Delegation policy" block shown above. GPT-Live delegated the question, the agent ran (one request to the mock model), and the answer was spoken in the channel.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.6 → this branch, same home)

One isolated home (`OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pinned) with config written for stable:

- Voice Call on GPT-Live, `consultPolicy: "auto"`, and a customized copy of the default prompt: `realtime.instructions` = the built-in default + " Always speak Spanish."
- Discord voice on `gpt-realtime-2.1` with `consultPolicy: "always"`.

Steps: install `openclaw@2026.11.6` plus `@openclaw/voice-call@2026.11.6` and `@openclaw/discord@2026.11.6`, run the Gateway and one real GPT-Live inbound call. Then on the same home: this branch's CLI, `config validate`, `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, the branch Discord build installed with `plugins install npm-pack:<tgz> --force --accept-capabilities` (the checkout's bundled Voice Call overrides the installed one), run the Gateway and the same call.

```
stable:  OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10) | Config valid
         loading voice-call from $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/extensions/voice-call/dist/index.js
         loading discord from $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/extensions/discord/dist/index.js
branch:  OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (c0e237f) | Config valid | doctor --fix: no repairs needed
         loading discord from $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-discord-<hash>/node_modules/@openclaw/discord/index.js
         loading voice-call from <checkout>/dist/extensions/voice-call/index.js
         sessions --all-agents: the session from the stable run is still listed
after upgrade:
  plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.consultPolicy   auto
  plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.instructions    <default> Always speak Spanish.   (unchanged)
  channels.discord.voice.realtime.consultPolicy              always
  channels.discord.voice.realtime.model                      gpt-realtime-2.1
```

Config diff after the upgrade: every user-authored key is unchanged. Doctor only added its standard `meta.migrations.*`, `wizard.*`, plugin `enabled` and skill entries.

GPT-Live `session.start` on both versions, base prompt section compared byte for byte:

```
stable custom base present: true len 395
branch custom base present: true len 395
custom prompt identical on stable and branch
```

So the customized default is sent as written after the upgrade and is not reworded.

Checks on this branch (rebased on `5a3e6b1cb`):

- After the review fix (`c0e237f75`): `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 50 files, 628 tests passed (400s); `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on `extensions/voice-call`, format, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (+87): pass.
- Before it: `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 50 files, 627 tests passed (396s). Discord config schema + voice selection: 39 passed (44s). `src/talk`: 39 files, 355 passed (601s).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`: pass. oxlint on `extensions/voice-call` and `extensions/discord`: pass. Format check, `check:test-lines-ratchet`, `check-test-mock-exports`: pass.
- `config:channels:check`, `config:docs:check`: pass after regenerating `config-baseline.sha256` for the rebase. The earlier docs, config-example and schema checks from the first revision passed; the only new docs change is one paragraph.

Gaps:

- Voice Call end-to-end on GPT-Live (question → delegation → spoken answer over a call) is shown in #203388, which this PR does not include.
- Upgrade proof: Discord `always` was checked through config load and schema validation on the branch, not through a live Discord session after the upgrade (the live Discord session above covers `substantive`). The CLI's `plugins install npm-pack:` for Voice Call over the stable install did not finish within 180 s on this host; the checkout's bundled Voice Call takes precedence, as the load path shows.
- The shared exact-speech note (`src/talk/exact-speech-protocol.ts`) still says "Do not call openclaw_agent_consult or any other tool for this message." It is a negative instruction shared with Talk, so it is left as is.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` fails identically on `origin/main`; this PR does not change those counts.

prs.title: fix(gateway): count posted messages as session activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message appended to an existing session outside a run — `chat.inject`, a guest agent posting a reply into a shared session, a template receipt — never updated the session entry. Clients derive "unread" from `lastActivityAt`, so the session stayed marked as read while the new message sat in the transcript. Fixes #202707.

The stamp must not over-reach in the other direction: a hidden transcript row (private CLI/ACP completion, delivery mirror, subagent coordination) is bookkeeping, not a message the user can see. Advancing `lastActivityAt` for those rows would mark a read session unread with nothing visible in it.

## User Impact

A *visible* posted message now counts as session activity, the same as a reply from a normal run: the session reorders and shows as unread. Hidden rows keep the previous activity timestamp, so a private completion no longer produces a spurious unread dot or sidebar reorder — the visible-side-effect suppression that private coordination promises (see #175559) stays intact. Replayed or declined appends stay untouched, and a session that was reset or deleted while the write was in flight is not resurrected by the bump.

## Why This Change Was Made

`injectGatewayAssistantMessage` appended the transcript and broadcast the `chat` event, but nothing patched the session entry: `lastActivityAt` is otherwise advanced only by run lifecycles (`session-run-lifecycle-projection`, `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun`) which an injected turn never enters. The append itself already bumps `updatedAt` through the transcript-turn owner; only the unread-driving field was missed.

The fix stamps `lastActivityAt` in that same owner-built patch (`session-transcript-turn-state.ts`), so it commits atomically with the transcript append and the existing broadcast path. A replay or a declined append never reaches the fresh-append touch, so neither bumps the entry. An earlier revision patched the entry in a separate write after the append; review correctly flagged that a failure there would skip the broadcast and a replay would not repair it, so that write is gone.

**Private completion visibility (#175559).** The first revision of that atomic stamp applied to every fresh append, including rows that `projectAgentHarnessTranscriptMessageForDisplay` marks `display: false`. That silently widened "session activity" to cover invisible writes. This revision restores the original intent: `updatedAt` keeps its existing fresh-append condition, while `lastActivityAt` is gated on at least one appended row with `display !== false`. `display: false` is the single marker the projection sets for private completions, delivery mirrors, progress-card refreshes and subagent coordination, so the predicate tracks visibility exactly rather than guessing from provenance. Both directions are covered in `src/agents/command/transcript-persistence.test.ts` through the shipped CLI and ACP writers.

## Evidence

Live A/B on Windows 11, isolated Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under a temp dir, port 28794, mock OpenAI-compatible provider on 28795). One `chat.send` creates the session and settles; then `chat.inject` posts one visible message; then a private completion (`privateCompletion: true`) is appended through the shipped CLI transcript writer (`persistCliTurnTranscript`) against the same live agent store. Every row is read back from `sessions.list`.

| Build | after `chat.send` settles (`updatedAt` / `lastActivityAt`) | after `chat.inject` | after hidden private completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream/main` (`7e5cad36`, before the PR) | `1795230952360` / `1795230952349` | `1795230955735` / `1795230952349` — **unchanged**, posted reply stays read | `1795230979068` / `1795230952349` — nothing stamps it |
| earlier revision `00615d97` | `1795231119338` / `1795231119291` | `1795231122966` / `1795231122966` — bumped | `1795231145910` / `1795231145910` — **bumped, spurious unread** |
| this revision | `1795231279552` / `1795231279505` | `1795231283258` / `1795231283258` — **bumped** | `1795231305825` / `1795231283258` — **`updatedAt` advances, `lastActivityAt` frozen** |

![Live three-way comparison: posted message bumps activity, hidden completion does not](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/202707/visible-activity-proof.png)

Unit, through the shipped writers (`src/agents/command/transcript-persistence.test.ts`): the new `keeps {CLI,ACP} private completions out of unread activity` legs fail against the unconditional stamp (`expected 1795230519323 to be 1795230458484`, `expected 1795230521782 to be 1795230461666`) and pass here; `counts a visible {CLI,ACP} transcript append as unread activity` passes in both.

`counts a posted assistant message as session activity` is clock-free. It seeds `lastActivityAt` to `Date.UTC(2020, 0, 1)` through the fixture's own session writer and asserts the append advances past that stamp, so the 5 ms wall-clock sleep the test guide forbids is gone without softening the assertion — a missing stamp now fails on an exact value instead of on elapsed time.

| Test file | Source under test | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts` | source fix reverted to `upstream/main` | **1 failed / 10 passed** — `AssertionError: expected 1577836800000 to be greater than 1577836800000` |
| `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts` | merged head | **11/11 passed** |
| `src/agents/command/transcript-persistence.test.ts` | merged head | **10/10 passed** |

Gates on the merged tree (`upstream/main` `ae8155cf` merged in, merge commit only): `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK (0 changed source files), `check:test-lines-ratchet` +78 / allowance 400. Typecheck runs in CI only for this revision: this revision was verified in an isolated worktree whose shared `node_modules` makes `pnpm tsgo:core` refuse to start (`Declaration input escapes checkout`), so the local tsgo claim from the previous revision — exit 0 on the same source hunk, which is unchanged — is not re-run here.

## What was not tested

- No real model: the rig uses a mock OpenAI-compatible stub; no provider credentials exist in this environment.
- The hidden leg drives the shipped CLI transcript writer out of process against the live Gateway's own agent store. It does not run a real subagent settle or an ACP child end to end, so the private-completion *trigger* is still covered by the existing suite rather than by a live run.
- The unread dot itself is not rendered; the evidence is the persisted `lastActivityAt` that `deriveSessionUnread` consumes.
- The replayed-append path keeps the entry untouched by construction (the bump sits after the `replayed` early return) but has no dedicated live leg.
- Windows only; no macOS or Linux live run.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` was not re-run locally for this revision: the isolated worktree's shared `node_modules` trips the tsgo declaration-input guard, so CI owns the typecheck. The shipped source hunk is unchanged from the revision where it exited 0.

prs.title: fix(config): repeated $include entries make config loading take minutes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config loading takes minutes when config files include the same child file several times across a few levels of `$include`.

## User Impact

User impact: a config tree with repeated includes now fails fast with an error that names the limit and the recovery step, so the CLI, the Gateway and config reloads stop spending minutes on it. Real configs stay far below 1024 include file loads.

```
Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Recovery for an existing installation that hits the limit is the step the error names. Include merging concatenates arrays, so a file included twice adds its array entries twice. For example a file that sets `mcp.servers.docs.args: ["mcp-server-fetch"]` and is included twice gives two arguments. Removing a repeated reference therefore keeps the merged config only when the file sets no arrays, or when the user moves the array entries that the repeat added into the remaining files. A repeat that comes after a different file (A, B, A) also applies A over B again. The upgrade run below shows the recovery on a config tree whose included files set no arrays.

## Why This Change Was Made

`$include` already has a depth limit of 10 and a cycle check, and each file is capped at 2 MB. Both checks look at one include chain. A file may still list the same child file several times (`"$include": ["./b.json", "./b.json", ...]`), and each repeat reads, parses and merges the whole subtree below it again. The work grows as fan-out to the power of depth. Nine levels that each include the next level four times load 349,524 files, built from eleven files of about 100 bytes.

The include resolver now counts file loads in one resolution and throws a `ConfigIncludeError` once it reaches 1024 loads. The check sits next to the depth check in `loadFileSync`, and the error flows through the same config validation path as the depth and cycle errors. The docs list the new limit next to the depth limit, together with the same recovery step.

## Evidence

The proof script generates nine levels where level i includes level i+1 F times, then runs `openclaw config validate` from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config validate`) with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at that tree. Wall time includes about 30 s of dev-mode CLI startup on this machine.

| Fan-out | Include file loads | main `00b62dd` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 | 28.0 s, Config valid | 31.0 s, Config valid |
| 2 | 1,023 | 30.0 s, Config valid | 30.8 s, Config valid |
| 3 | 29,524 | 67.3 s, Config valid | 29.7 s, include error |
| 4 | 349,525 | 389.9 s, Config valid | 30.9 s, include error |

Branch output for fan-out 4:

```
Config needs correction: .../fan4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json
```

Calling `resolveConfigIncludes` directly on main for the same trees took 0.56 s, 7.3 s and 80.3 s for fan-out 2, 3 and 4. On this branch fan-out 2 resolves in 0.39 s and fan-out 3 and 4 throw the include error.

### Upgrade from stable 2026.11.6 (recorded 2026-11-21)

This section publishes the existing 2026-11-21 upgrade run after checking its raw logs and confirming that the PR still points to `e65d63e`; these timings were not rerun on 2026-11-22.

This run installs `openclaw@2026.11.6` (npm `latest` on 2026-11-21, commit `06afb10`) into a local npm prefix. It then upgrades in place to this branch built from source (`pnpm build:runtime` at `e65d63e`, run as `node openclaw.mjs`, which prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (e65d63e)` because the branch sits on an older main). Both CLIs share one state dir and one HOME inside the proof dir. The stable release runs every step first. The branch then runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` as the upgrade step, followed by the same steps. Node 24.22.1 on Linux. Every command runs in a bubblewrap sandbox that mounts the proof dir at `<proof>` below a sticky `/tmp`, because OpenClaw rejects temp roots below the world writable parent directory on this host.

Configs:

- `normal`: a modular config with eleven files. It uses include arrays (`logging`, `agents.defaults`), sibling overrides (`gateway.port`, `messages.responsePrefix`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`), and nested includes three levels deep (`openclaw.json` to `agents/index.json5` to `agents/defaults.json5` to `shared/timezone.json5`, and the same shape under `messages`).
- `fanout4`: nine levels where each level includes the next level four times (349,525 include loads).
- `recovered`: `fanout4` after following the error's advice, so each level lists the next level once (10 include loads). No included file in `fanout4` or `recovered` sets an array, so listing each file once gives the same merged config.

| Config | Command | 2026.11.6 | this branch `e65d63e` after `doctor --fix` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| normal | `config validate` | 2.6 s, Config valid | 4.0 s, Config valid |
| recovered | `config validate` | 2.7 s, Config valid | 3.9 s, Config valid |
| fanout4 | `config validate` | 193.2 s, Config valid | 5.8 s, include load error, exit 1 |
| normal | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 33.5 s, ready | 25.1 s, ready |
| recovered | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 24.7 s, ready | 25.0 s, ready |
| fanout4 | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 825.3 s, ready | 14.3 s, exits 78 with the include load error |

`config get --json` for `gateway`, `agents.defaults`, `logging`, `messages` and `ui` on the normal config, and for `ui` and `gateway` on the recovered config, print byte identical output on both CLIs. The gateway token prints as `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` on both. Merged values on both:

```
agents.defaults  {"workspace":"./workspace","userTimezone":"America/Chicago","thinkingDefault":"medium","timeoutSeconds":1200, ...}
logging          {"level":"info","consoleLevel":"warn"}
messages         {"responsePrefix":"[proof]","ackReaction":"eyes","ackReactionScope":"all", ...}
gateway          {"port":18891,"mode":"local","bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"}}
ui (normal)      {"seamColor":"#336699"}
ui (recovered)   {"seamColor":"#000000"}
```

`agents.defaults` shows all three include levels merged. `userTimezone` comes from the third level, `thinkingDefault: "medium"` from the later array entry and `timeoutSeconds: 1200` from the sibling override.

Authored files. The sha256 of all 33 authored config files was taken before the stable run and again after the branch run. The included files of all three configs and the root files of `fanout4` and `recovered` are byte identical. The stable Gateway added `openclaw.json.last-good` next to each root file, a byte copy of that root file. The branch `doctor --fix` upgrade step rewrote `normal/openclaw.json` and saved the authored file as `openclaw.json.bak.1` (same sha256 as before the run). The rewrite keeps every `$include` entry and every authored value. It adds `agents.entries.main`, `skills.entries`, `wizard` and `meta`. The same `doctor --fix` from 2026.11.6 on a fresh copy of the authored normal config makes the same kind of rewrite with the same `$include` entries and the same added top level keys, so this comes from doctor itself. The branch `config validate` and `config get` steps after doctor leave every file unchanged, and the branch Gateway refreshes `normal/openclaw.json.last-good` to a byte copy of the rewritten root file.

```
$ sha256sum (before stable run -> after branch run), changed lines only
  ./normal/openclaw.json            e3f172b6...  ->  9993e283...  (doctor --fix rewrite)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.bak.1      e3f172b6...  (the authored file)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.bak        e5c387d5...  (doctor's intermediate write)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.last-good  9993e283...
+ ./fanout4/openclaw.json.last-good 1bcbea34...
+ ./recovered/openclaw.json.last-good 1bcbea34...
```

Branch `config validate` output for `fanout4`:

```
Config needs correction: <proof>/configs/fanout4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair, or fix the keys above manually.
Run openclaw config schema to inspect supported settings and values, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Branch `gateway run` on `fanout4`:

```
OpenClaw config is invalid
File: <proof>/configs/fanout4/openclaw.json
Problem:
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.

Inspect: openclaw config validate
Audit, status, health, logs, and doctor commands still run with invalid config.
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to repair the config, then retry.
```

It exits with code 78. After the recovery edit, the same Gateway on `recovered` reaches ready in 25.0 s, and `config get ui` prints `{"seamColor":"#000000"}` on both CLIs.

### Tests

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/includes.test.ts src/config/includes.top-level-key.test.ts src/config/include-write-boundary.test.ts src/config/mutate.agent-delete-include.test.ts`: 42 passed on `e65d63e`, including a new test that pins the array concatenation for a file included twice. Both limit tests match the full error text, recovery step included. With the previous message they fail. On main the two new tests fail. The budget test resolves 1025 loads without an error, and the fan-out test runs for 101 s and resolves without an error. On this branch they take 660 ms and 352 ms.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK at `4e62b0f`, net +34 test lines. `e65d63e` adds 7 test lines (+41), within the 400-line allowance. On `e65d63e`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Skills first-visit requests within budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills can exceed its first-visit request limit when background sidebar assets finish before the page is ready. [Main CI recorded 30 completed requests against the limit of 28](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381/job/136875600229).

The Skills library imports upload-size constants through the protocol barrel, which also brings runtime schema code into the browser.

## User Impact

Skills reads its existing upload limits without fetching two unnecessary schema chunks. Upload limits, wire schemas, and existing exports stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the four constants into a dependency-free module owned by the protocol package. The schema re-exports them for existing callers; the UI imports the constants directly and imports its schema types with `import type`.

## Evidence

The same production-bundle browser scenario on the failing CI commit and the candidate showed:

| Skills first visit, 100 ms request latency | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Requests completed by ready | 28 | 26 |
| Schema chunks requested | 2 | 0 |
| Bytes completed by ready | 468,803 | 406,256 |

The local base passed because two sidebar requests finished after readiness; CI counted those same assets before readiness. The candidate removes the two schema requests without raising the existing limit.

All four existing route scenarios passed, including deferred skill-reader loading. Candidate ready-window counts were 26/28 for Skills, 29/31 for Skill Settings, 53/56 for Plugins, and 54/61 for Plugin Settings. The 23 library tests, targeted format/lint, UI typecheck, and protocol registry check passed.

The local ClawSweeper committed-range review found no code or security defects. Runtime results were collected separately from that source review. Temporary diagnostic logging was restored after execution, and the three candidate source files were verified by hash.

The [exact-head canonical performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44922622564/job/136902172794) passed. Its dispatch base is newer than this fix's parent, so the parent comparison below uses the [parent's existing canonical CI measurement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381/job/136875599061). Both runs used Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.3, and the same lockfile and performance/build code. These are separate CI runs, not interleaved timing samples; the values are normalized asset sizes.

| Cold boot JS, gzip bytes | Parent `6577f41` | Candidate `817f310` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 90,879 | 90,879 | 0 |
| Chat | 1,333,702 | 1,333,796 | +94 |
| New Session | 820,757 | 820,851 | +94 |

No thresholds were changed. Acceptance of the two 94-byte increases is pending.

An earlier absolute-budget diagnostic against the E2E bundle failed. That fixture deliberately omits compression sidecars and uses synthetic build metadata, so its CSS totals are not release measurements. An additional exact-parent remote probe stopped before measurement because its preflight expected the source SHA as HEAD instead of the wrapper's transport carrier; no result from that attempt is counted.

The canonical build and both selected UI E2E shards passed. [Real-Gateway CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44922622564/job/136902172446) reported a 120-second timeout in `required-human-action.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (`manual-in-panel`, last phase `manual-page-closed`). This matches the [prior main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44369795594/job/135034001765) at `fd5471bc2d57192072bc8fcec7f7980846dcfb31`: same test/case and 120-second timeout. The test's actions, assertions, and timeout are unchanged from that failure; only failure telemetry was added in [#201386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201386). This is retained as an inherited CI failure, not claimed fixed here. Its exact stalled click still needs separate diagnosis.

<summary>Focused validation</summary>

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

prs.title: fix: let chat history reload when a session changes during a read
prs.body:
Closes #203148

**Human review required before merge.** This changes an error returned during session authorization.

## What Problem This Solves

If a session is replaced while the Gateway checks access to its history, the pending read loses its snapshot. The Gateway withholds the transcript and returns a generic `UNAVAILABLE` error. The response gives the caller no explicit indication that a fresh read could succeed.

## User Impact

History clients receive the existing `chat.history` retry advice for this conflict, including a 250 ms delay. The failed request returns no transcript. A subsequent request goes through authorization again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite reader can identify when an active sharing acquisition has been superseded. Give that cause a distinct type and use it during history authorization to return the same error shape as other temporary history failures. A released acquisition has the same error text, so matching the text would also classify a different failure. The change is limited to the typed cause on `chat.history` and leaves each new read to the caller.

## Evidence

- On the parent, a scoped WebSocket client read a stored transcript. Replacing its session during reconciliation produced `UNAVAILABLE` without `details.method`, `retryable` or `retryAfterMs`. A separate request returned the replacement transcript.
- With the fix, the first frame contains the method and retry advice, with no payload. A fresh request returns only the replacement transcript. An invited reader whose membership was removed receives a terminal denial on the fresh authorization check. Unknown authority, a generic error with the same text, and `chat.send` stay outside the new classification.
- All 31 tests passed across the Gateway history, committed sharing, SQLite lifecycle publication and retained-history sharing suites. Scoped lint and formatting, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed on Linux with Node 24.22.1. The reproduction used a real local Gateway and synthetic SQLite data. The second request was explicit. Automatic client behavior was outside the test.

prs.title: fix: recover Linux stream automations after command-anchor crashes
prs.body:
Closes #202900

## What Problem This Solves

A Linux stream automation can stop permanently when its command anchor crashes: it immediately exhausts its restart budget, and disabling and re-enabling it cannot recover the retained cleanup failure. Simply clearing that failure is unsafe: a detached child can remain alive after both the source and anchor disappear.

## User Impact

Stream automations recover through their existing backoff after the command anchor dies, including across shutdown and restart. Old descendants are stopped and reaped before replacement. No configuration or data migration is required.

Strict Linux child scopes retain one additional native relay process. Losing that final custodian remains fail-closed: neither retry nor manual enable overrides unconfirmed extinction. macOS/Windows, owned workers, and intentional root-exit handoffs keep their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing relay now retains kernel subreaper custody outside the command anchor for strict, non-handoff Linux child scopes. After anchor loss, it adopts and reaps detached descendants and supplies an independent extinction certificate. The host joins that certificate, output/lineage closure, and relay exit before releasing cleanup. Cron continues using its existing restart owner and backoff; no exhaustion bypass is added.

Certificate observation stays with the retirement owner. Existing startup/private-input settlement moves into preparation to preserve the enforced module-size limit without changing its admission or cleanup behavior.

## Evidence

**Verified result (2026-11-21 16:51 UTC):** The [completed exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203149#issuecomment-7065332600) rates patch quality **4/6 platinum**, proof **5/6 diamond**, with no actionable findings and ready for maintainer review. The [exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44926099508) is successful on `0c080a7fc16a7f0c341eb400df78e93a0d635b99`; the full observed check inventory has no failed or active checks. This PR is open and non-draft; it has not been merged or deployed.

### Forced-cancellation review repair

The [second hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/44923917782), on `f2430a8c0f37f957dbda9dff0a03895fc014e2db`, accepted both prior fixes and rated the real terminal proof 5/6, but found a P2 cancellation-result regression. That finding is repaired in `0c080a7fc16a7f0c341eb400df78e93a0d635b99`: after independent extinction is certified, an explicitly requested cancellation uses the existing requested-signal result instead of becoming an unexpected-anchor-loss error. Unexpected anchor loss still rejects its missing command result; loss of final custody still rejects cleanup.

The new native regression runs a real child that ignores SIGTERM, then closes its strict scope within a 500ms cleanup budget. On the reviewed head cleanup succeeds but `run.wait()` rejects; on the repaired head it returns `reason: manual-cancel`, `exitSignal: SIGKILL`, and the child is absent. The unexpected-loss regression now explicitly requires the error rather than swallowing it. **88 native/supervisor cases pass** (40.9s wrapper), including the failed-custody and deadline controls. Core/services-test types, touched-file lint/format, session-identity and line-cap guards pass; the runtime build and real Gateway matrix were rerun on this repaired tree. The final exact-head review and CI now pass, as recorded above.

### Review and CI repairs

The [initial review of 3789e953445a](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/44921819901) identified two P2 defects, both reproduced locally and repaired in `f2430a8c0f37f957dbda9dff0a03895fc014e2db`:

- Prepared and overlay matrix runtimes now bind **both** compiled native owners through the existing sealed-runtime manifest. This restores the intent of [d782bc046eba / #181621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d782bc046ebaa39fcea10fc98798c04d74f899a3): source-loader compiler children cannot share exclusive kernel child-wait ownership. The loader prohibition is unchanged; the companion fixture supplies the same complete native closure.
- Custody receipts now enter through the host's existing generation-validated dispatcher. The retirement owner no longer adds a second filtering listener. The session-identity guard passes without a baseline change or renamed comparison.

Repair proof: the previously failing matrix file now passes all 4 cases; the selected matrix/resolver/native-host group passes 74 tests (45.2s wrapper), sealed-build consumers pass 70 tests, and the real cloud-worker mid-turn-loss composition passes (85.8s wrapper). That last local fixture initially lacked Debian `ps`; genuine signed-repository procps 4.0.2 and its library were staged only in task scratch, then the same test passed through the real native utility. No application guard or test assertion was relaxed. Core, scripts, tooling-test and E2E-test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, line-cap, session-identity and runtime-process-lifecycle checks pass. The runtime build and full disposable Gateway matrix were rerun after repair. Initial CI run [44920799768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44920799768) remains failed evidence for the first head; the final head has its own successful CI receipt above; the original failed run is not backdated green.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal receipts from the repaired real Gateway run</summary>

The following is the terminal receipt projection from the same public CLI/Gateway reproduction, completed 2026-11-21 16:28 UTC on the repaired tree. Addresses, paths, process/job identifiers and credentials are omitted; statuses and observed cleanup results are retained. The published file blobs were compared with that tested tree. The before-state and source regression are described above; this is not an in-process mocked Gateway.

```json
{"case":"midrun-recovered","at":"2026-11-21T16:27:57.933Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false,"oldExtinct":true}
{"case":"same-gateway-disable-enable","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:02.756Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":0,"restartExhausted":false}
{"case":"gateway-stop","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:03.168Z","exitCode":0}
{"case":"shutdown-reopen-recovered","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:10.774Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false}
{"case":"detached-descendant-reclaimed","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:47.538Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false,"oldExtinct":true,"noOverlap":true}
{"case":"custodian-loss-fail-closed","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.256Z","streamStatus":"error","failures":1,"restartExhausted":true,"noReplacement":true}
{"case":"gateway-stop","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.644Z","exitCode":0}
{"case":"cleanup","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.648Z","allRecordedProcessesAbsent":true,"portRebound":true}
```

The source emitted `{}` periodically with a deliberately nonmatching predicate, so these cases made no model turn. Faults targeted only fixture processes after checking their birth identity and ancestry. The real custodian-loss control remained in error and could not admit a replacement.

</details>

The real disposable Gateway reproduced the original failure before the change. The repaired source passed the same production CLI/Gateway flows:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command anchor killed mid-run | Error/exhausted with zero restart attempts | Old processes extinct, restart after normal 30-second backoff |
| Disable/enable in the same Gateway | Remained exhausted | Running again, restart counter reset |
| Anchor killed immediately before shutdown; same state reopened | Persisted cleanup error/exhaustion | Clean stop and running source after reopen |
| Detached descendant outlives root and anchor | Descendant remained alive | Adopted and reaped before replacement; no overlap |
| Final custodian killed | No equivalent additional custodian on base | Cleanup remains unconfirmed; manual enable does not start a replacement |

The final proof used a nonmatching stream predicate: no channel or model execution was needed. Every recorded fixture process disappeared, both Gateway stops exited 0, and the fixture port rebound successfully. This is Linux source proof with the normal pinned OpenClaw Bun runtime and a Node 24.20 feeder, not packaged-release or Node-26 parity.

- Native regression fails on base `0c475b963b585012a180030bdabbfb0016027505` with the missing closing receipt, and passes on the candidate. The existing deadline test now stalls the final custodian rather than the recoverable inner anchor; it still requires a failed cleanup result.
- Initial published-head focused run: **122 passed, 1 platform-specific skip**, across 12 files, 64.8 seconds wrapper wall. The changed native file also ran independently; baseline wrapper 38.6 seconds, initial candidate 37.2 seconds. Per-file CI seconds were not collected.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, core and selected services-test typechecks, touched-file typed lint/format, line-cap/assertion-safety guards, import-cycle check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Review history:** Auto Review was attempted on the full local candidate against the pinned base, P0–P2, with relevant unchanged owner context. The same managed route timed out after 1,200 seconds without a report. That attempt supplies no clean-review verdict. All three findings across the two subsequent hosted review cycles were repaired. The final exact-head review is linked above and reports no actionable findings, patch quality 4/6 and proof confidence 5/6.
- No failure-alert destination was configured in the reported reproduction. The existing alert path is unchanged; configured external terminal-source notification delivery is not claimed as live-tested.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and scope</summary>

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host*.test.ts src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay.native-owner.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.cleanup-history.real.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.root-exit.real.test.ts src/gateway/cron-stream-watchers.extinction.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron.stream-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

`node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.test.ts","src/process/supervisor/supervisor.cleanup-history.real.test.ts"]'`

The repair changes 14 existing files. No production cleanup path was replaced with a PID census or a fabricated receipt. Necessary growth is the independent native custody join and its regression coverage; the input-startup movement is behavior-preserving. Broader platform/CI proof remains with normal PR CI.

</details>

Requested by Donniefi. Original report and reproduction details by @warm-cloth.
