prs.title: fix: retain safe causes when provider catalog discovery fails
prs.body:
Related: #165888

## What Problem This Solves

Provider catalog failures discard the safe cause needed to distinguish authentication, HTTP, timeout, and unexpected failures during model discovery.

## User Impact

Operators receive bounded diagnostic fields when discovery skips an unavailable catalog. Existing discovery outcomes, authentication handling, sibling discovery, and deadlines are preserved. This improves diagnosis; it does not claim to repair the underlying refresh failure or update the installed runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner catalog boundary and outer discovery deadline share a fixed warning containing a validated provider identifier, phase, closed failure reason, elapsed milliseconds, and optional numeric HTTP status. Exception messages, stacks, URLs, response bodies, and credentials stay out of the warning. Adversarial thrown values cannot replace the existing graceful failure.

Current head is `b01a3e78cab7f79b97f655e402033ae8b9ee4698`. It integrates upstream main's timeout handling, flattened test layout and per-provider failure isolation (request-wide rethrow, unavailable outcomes) while retaining the five-file diagnostic repair, plus a test-line allocation for its +198 test lines. No dependency, scanner, or runtime deployment change is included.

## Evidence

- Head `b01a3e78cab` adds one test-only commit to `0ad55a7ea34`. The leakage fixture's credential URL is now assembled at runtime, as `src/infra/update-candidate-admission.test.ts` does on main, because a literal credential URL trips the PR input-safety scanner. The thrown value and every leakage assertion are unchanged.
- Focused tests on `b01a3e78cab`: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-outcome.internal.test.ts` and `src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts` pass (32 tests), and the format check passes.
- CI on the previous head `0ad55a7ea34` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42517944280)) had no failing checks, and both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks passed. CI on `b01a3e78cab` is waiting for a maintainer to approve the fork workflow runs.
- ClawSweeper reviewed `b01a3e78cab` with no findings and asked for real behavior proof, which is below.
- Local review: not run. Neither autoreview nor a local ClawSweeper is set up in this checkout.

### Real behavior proof

Entry point: the CLI run from source with no Gateway, `node scripts/run-node.mjs models list --refresh --all --json`, in a throwaway `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Four `models.providers` entries (`bifrost`, `litellm`, `llama-cpp`, `lmstudio`) point at loopback fake servers: one healthy, one HTTP 404, one HTTP 401, one that never responds. Every API key, response body and URL query string carried a private marker.

After, on `b01a3e78cab`, stderr:

```
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=live-catalog reason=http elapsedMs=36 httpStatus=404
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=llama-cpp phase=live-catalog reason=http elapsedMs=12 httpStatus=401
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=lmstudio phase=live-catalog reason=timeout elapsedMs=5004
```

After, with `litellm` hanging past the 180 s discovery deadline:

```
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=provider-discovery reason=timeout elapsedMs=180001
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=live-catalog reason=timeout elapsedMs=180688
```

The file log carries the same events as JSONL, for example `{"provider":"litellm","phase":"live-catalog","reason":"http","elapsedMs":36,"httpStatus":404}`.

Before, on merge base `61120568f82`, the same runs log no cause for the 404, the 401 or the 5 s timeout. At the deadline the outer boundary logs exception text:

```
[models/provider-isolation] provider discovery failed for litellm: provider catalog timed out after 180000ms: litellm; skipping provider
```

- Healthy sibling: stdout lists both `bifrost` models in all four runs, and `providerOutcomes` are identical before and after (`ready`, `unavailable`, `auth-rejected`, `unavailable`).
- Leak check: the private marker appears 0 times in stdout, stderr and the log file in all four runs.
- Baseline red: with this PR's two test files copied onto the merge base, `provider-catalog-live-outcome.internal.test.ts` fails 9 of 10 and `models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts` fails 1 of 22. On `b01a3e78cab` they pass 10/10 and 22/22.

Two things the proof showed that this PR does not change:

- A provider that hangs to the deadline produces two warnings about 0.7 s apart, one per boundary, because the inner fetch timeout equals the remaining outer budget.
- The existing `[fetch-timeout]` line still prints the provider base URL without its query string, on both the baseline and this head.

No approval, merge, or production rollout is claimed.

prs.title: fix: keep browser disabled when only hardening relay authentication
prs.body:
Closes #202959

## What Problem This Solves

Running `doctor --fix --non-interactive` after setting only `browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth=false` enables the browser plugin and adds it to an explicit plugin allowlist. A setting intended to restrict relay authentication should not itself request browser activation.

## User Impact

That exact hardening-only browser block no longer enables or allowlists browser. Explicit browser configuration, plugin entries, and browser tool references retain their existing activation behavior; disable and deny controls still apply.

If you relied on that sole flag to activate browser control, also set `browser.enabled=true`. Existing enabled/allowlisted browser entries are not removed. This does not change noninteractive allowlist repair generally or classify other hardening-only combinations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser-owned setup probe now distinguishes the reported hardening-only shape from activation intent, while continuing its plugin-entry and tool-reference checks. Shared activation/materialization policy is unchanged. Both browser recovery guides document the narrow exception to the existing root-browser configuration rule.

## Evidence

The reported behavior was reproduced through the real Doctor CLI on Linux/Node 24.20.0, then rerun on this fix with isolated HOME, state, config, workspace, logs, named profiles, and loopback ports. No serving Gateway or real user state was changed.

| Real Doctor input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sole `allowLegacyAuth:false` | Browser enabled and allowlisted | Browser remains absent |
| No browser block | Inactive | Inactive |
| Hardening plus `defaultProfile` | Enabled | Enabled |
| `browser.enabled:false` | Inactive | Inactive |
| Browser plugin explicitly disabled | Inactive | Inactive |
| Browser in `plugins.deny` | Inactive | Inactive |

Actual Gateway processes confirmed browser loaded before the fix and absent afterward; the configured-browser positive control still loaded it. All reached ready, shut down cleanly, and released their ports.

Latest-stable source-upgrade proof used signed tag `v2026.11.6` at `06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638`, with its normal frozen-lockfile installation. Candidate Doctor preserves newly added hardening without enabling browser and retains browser entries written by stable Doctor. The separate documented Skill Workshop migration was explicitly accounted for; repeated candidate Doctor preserved the entire plugin policy exactly. The npm package was age-gated, so this is exact-source Doctor upgrade proof, not packaged-updater certification.

The regression failed on the original probe and passes with the fix. Browser tests: 10 passed; shared auto-enable and Doctor consumers: 75 passed. Full build, browser production and extension-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, docs inventory, and whitespace checks passed. The build emitted nonfatal UI bundle-budget warnings; no UI code changed.

**Review limitation:** native Auto Review captured the complete local candidate against `0c475b963b585012a180030bdabbfb0016027505`, but its 600-second attempt and authorized 1,200-second retry timed out without a validated report. Publication follows the repository's explicit timeout-without-report continuation rule; normal maintainer judgment and enforced GitHub checks remain required. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44918557130) passed for `a15d4d19eead04b159203db4214fe38fb4c0423b`: 21 jobs passed and 31 were skipped by scope. prs.title: fix(ui): show archived session state on first paint
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a cached archived conversation can restore its transcript before the archived-session banner arrives, leaving the composer area empty for an initial frame. The scheduled [main CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381) catches this in both archived and deleted-parent sessions.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185788

## User Impact

Archived conversations show their existing status and Unarchive control with the first composer paint. Cached controls retain their existing pending-authority behavior until reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The banner is required session presentation. Render it synchronously with the composer instead of behind an empty lazy-loading fallback. The existing fixture now requires immediate rendering while retaining its focus, callback, disabled-action, and progress assertions.

**Draft: the measured Chat boot budget overrun is unresolved.** No budget has been changed.

## Evidence

- Unmodified base `3a20a7bcffff7bee97d774980c4ab3ee0507ec2d`: archived and deleted-parent fail the existing first-paint assertion; active and read-only pass.
- Candidate: all four unchanged bundled Chromium scenarios pass, including live-state replacement after reconnect.
- Strengthened fixture: four expected failures on the old renderer; four passes with the fix.
- Scoped format (oxfmt/Bun parity), lint, and UI typecheck pass.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `3a20a7bcffff..bf6f6fd9c153`: complete, no actionable correctness/security findings. It did not rerun tests; the budget overrun remains a landing blocker.
- Proof used the real production bundle with synthetic Gateway data on a task-owned Boat Linux lease. The before capture holds the actual banner bundle request open; no DOM replacement or production test hook.

| Same-host bundle comparison | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial startup JS gzip | 90,879 B | 90,879 B |
| New Session boot JS gzip | 820,757 B | 820,757 B |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,333,702 B | 1,334,099 B |
| Chat boot JS requests | 21 | 21 |

The current Chat cap is **1,333,899 B**: the candidate adds **397 B** and exceeds the cap by **200 B**. This failure is introduced by the patch. Existing CSS warnings are unchanged or improve by 3 B; they do not explain the Chat failure.

The change removes four production lines net and two test lines net. Before/after images: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203136#issuecomment-7064713198

prs.title: fix: keep dismissed automation failures out of the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202650
Closes #202652
Closes #202653
Closes #202661

## What Problem This Solves

A failed automation can come back after you dismiss it if browser storage is full, two tabs dismiss different failures at once, or you pause and re-enable the automation. Opening the same Gateway from a different browser or address also brings the failure back.

## User Impact

A dismissed run stays hidden for your account on that Gateway, including when you switch browsers, addresses, or devices. A dismissed auto-disable stays hidden after a successful manual run. A later failed run still appears. A dismissal that the Gateway refuses because a restart is in progress is saved for the same browser profile to submit when the Gateway returns. Update notices can reappear after a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway saves the latest dismissed failure for each automation in the signed-in operator’s existing profile preferences. The profile writer merges acknowledgements in one transaction, and the existing preference event refreshes open tabs. A structured restart refusal uses the existing per-profile reconnect queue with the exact failure timestamp. Pausing an automation leaves its last-run identity intact. For an auto-disabled job, dismissal covers the failed run and the automatic disable shown in the same row.

The Inbox imports existing account-scoped browser dismissals. Those records contain job IDs, so the first import uses the failure timestamp the Gateway knows for that job. Later imports preserve the first receipt. Import requires a browser record tied to the signed-in profile.

## Evidence

The current comparison uses main `3c8c7bf781fb` and this PR at `83ba861a5079`. The targeted Plugins readiness check passed on both builds.

On the PR head, 208 focused tests passed, including Inbox, profile preferences, and Gateway method order. Both Inbox opening latency cases and the Gateway protocol and generated validator checks passed.

I created Inbox dismissals and saved a theme on the published `2026.9.37`, `2026.10.33`, and `2026.11.6` builds, then started PR build `7f66802e9ad` on each isolated copy of the saved Gateway and browser state. All three imported the dismissal, preserved the theme, kept the original failure hidden after re-enable, reload, and a fresh browser, and displayed a later failure.

### Product captures

The paired captures compare main `e6d441549fe2` with the Inbox persistence implementation at `2720891948c5`, each against a copy of the same isolated Gateway state. The stable-upgrade captures use `2eda19b546a`. The isolated Gateway comparison below also covers that upgrade at `18b3695e8ad`. The receipt regressions compare main `5fe76f0073b4` with PR head `2dfaed67aaab`.

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser storage full after two dismissals | ![Main shows Archive check again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ae8c7e84-96fc-4c48-a11d-b035dfa86004.png) | ![Both failures stay hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/e57fbd94-8c5e-4178-9f0f-32a72cc2874f.png) |
| Automation paused and re-enabled after dismissal | ![Main shows Archive check with Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/acd96639-1811-4223-99ff-a6f924fc3fcb.png) | ![Only Index check remains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/aa7d9fbd-47aa-4bde-ac9f-030104e74e03.png) |
| Same Gateway opened at another address in a separate profile | ![Main shows both failures in the other browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/b90930a5-0eae-4bd7-a4c5-8e285976d63d.png) | ![The other browser shows only Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/4e67960e-177d-4273-8b25-ca05c0f31de6.png) |

- **Two tabs.** Main lost one dismissal when both tabs clicked at the same timestamp. The PR build hid both rows in both tabs, and the Gateway held both run timestamps.
- **Browser migration.** A dismissal carried over from the old browser while the job was paused. It stayed hidden in a fresh profile after re-enable. A genuine later failure appeared even when another browser still held an old dismissal.

| Imported dismissal in a fresh browser | A later failed run |
| --- | --- |
| ![Only Index check after importing the Archive check dismissal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/a0fe65c8-c529-4cb5-ba12-18860a11450d.png) | ![A new Archive check failure appears](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ff223519-afd7-49df-a707-ddd3e830c4a3.png) |

### Control UI behavior against isolated Gateways

I built main `3ac8d23a2cb6` and PR head `18b3695e8ad` and exercised both in Chromium against isolated Gateways.

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismiss a failed automation, reload, and restart the Gateway | Stays hidden in the original browser | Stays hidden in the original browser and in a fresh browser after restart |
| Dismiss with browser storage full | Returns on reload | Stays hidden on reload |
| Two tabs dismiss separate failures | Both stayed hidden in this run | Both stayed hidden and the Gateway stored both receipts |
| Upgrade from v2026.11.6 with a browser dismissal and a profile setting | The setting and original browser dismissal survive, and the failed run appears in a new browser | Imports the dismissal, preserves the setting, and hides the original failure in a new browser. A later failed run appears |
| Update notice and execution approval | The snoozed notice returns after restart. Pending approval requires a decision | Same behavior |
| Dismiss a seeded mention | Stays gone after reload and restart in a fresh browser | Same behavior |

A real Gateway refused the dismissal as shutdown began at `3106387303e`, and the original request never stored a receipt. At `18b3695e8ad`, I reproduced the same structured refusal during a real shutdown. After restart the dismissal was submitted, the Gateway saved it, and a fresh browser showed the failure hidden. The focused regression was red on `3106387303e` and green on the exact head. The runtime build, 108 focused tests, and targeted lint and format passed.

Overdue automation dismissal stayed browser-local on both builds. Built-browser fixtures covered model-auth dismissal, read-only scope guidance, and OpenClaw ID recovery notices and the other OpenClaw ID rows that require action. The browser outbox suite passed on both builds with simulated delivery rejection. The update test seeded a release check result. The mention test seeded an already-received mention and used the real Gateway for dismissal and persistence.

### Auto-disable followed by a manual run

In a built Control UI with an isolated Gateway and a scripted model response, a real one-shot automation failed and was automatically disabled. I dismissed its Inbox row, ran the job successfully without re-enabling it, and reloaded the page. At `05a4906c5d4`, the row came back. At `3106387303e`, it stayed dismissed and appeared again only after a later failed run.

The new regression failed on `05a4906c5d4` and passed on `3106387303e`. The 107 focused Inbox and Gateway preference tests passed on `3106387303e`, along with the runtime build and targeted lint and format checks.

### Upgrade from v2026.11.6

I dismissed Archive check in the published v2026.11.6 Control UI, saved a profile theme preference, and paused the job. I replaced the stable Gateway with a build of `2eda19b546a` using the same test state and browser profile. The Gateway imported the dismissal for the paused run and preserved the theme preference. Re-enabling the job kept the original run ID and timestamp, and a fresh browser profile on `localhost` kept the row dismissed after reload. Running the job again produced a new failed run and a visible Inbox row.

| Dismissal on v2026.11.6 | Relaunched browser on the PR build | Later failed run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Stable Inbox after dismissing Archive check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/489910f9-3477-48ae-95ac-ba5d4aba4d08.png) | ![Only Index check after import and reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/ce7c7cf3-07fb-42f3-ad74-3739d91f6b48.png) | ![Archive check appears for a new failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcf459336474b7f522107bd24a0615360b425109/images/2026/11/851cc5c1-ecbf-4d08-8fc2-1441b8c7788b.png) |

### Protocol and performance checks at `2eda19b546a`

- 218 focused tests and three selected browser tests passed, along with the UI typecheck and Gateway validator check. The legacy advertised method list keeps its order with the new RPC appended.
- Compared with main `8253356c9864`, the SQLite worker ratchet stayed at 166 main-thread calls. The Control UI comparison passed. Chat boot JavaScript went from 1,333,213 to 1,333,042 gzip bytes, with 21 requests on both sides. The existing absolute CSS overruns are present on main.
- Skills and Plugins readiness timed out on the original CI base as well. Skill Settings and both Inbox latency cases passed on the merged head.

### Receipt regressions on main and the PR

The main checkout at the CI base `5fe76f0073b4` received only the two test cases. The same tests passed on `2dfaed67aaab`.

| Regression | Main `5fe76f0073b4` | PR head `2dfaed67aaab` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Import a browser dismissal for a job outside the selected inventory | Failed because the Inbox made no `cron.acknowledgeFailure` adoption request | Passed. The browser ID remains until the Gateway confirms the import |
| Merge simultaneous receipts and keep the original timestamp on legacy adoption | Failed because the preference writer returned no acknowledgement timestamp | Passed. Both receipts persist and the adoption returns the original timestamp |

- The cron-event fixture waits for the lazy import and first preference read. The original incident-row, event-projection, and inventory-read assertions passed. All 69 focused tests passed.
- The deferred-storage scan checks storage before entering the loop. Targeted lint passed on main and the repaired head. The Control UI comparison passed, with Chat boot JavaScript 315 gzip bytes smaller than the CI base.
- The Skills ready-window check saw 30 requests against its limit of 28 on both main and the repaired head. Skill Settings passed on both replays. Both Inbox latency cases passed on the repaired head.

In an independent two-tab storage probe, an artificial delay between reading and writing let one-time legacy cleanup erase a concurrent dismissal of a different browser-local alert.

The live run used desktop Chromium with independent browser profiles. Native apps, a second physical machine, and PostgreSQL were outside that run.

The generated validator diff contains 4,333 added and 4,298 removed lines, mostly predicate renumbering.

prs.title: feat: show what a backup contains before restoring it
prs.body:
Closes #202779

## What Problem This Solves

Two backups can each pass verification with one asset even though one contains just the configuration and the other contains state. Choosing one for recovery currently requires opening the manifest separately.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw backup verify <archive> --inventory` to see the recorded asset kinds and SQLite snapshot owners before restoring. The same flag works with `--from` and `--json`. In JSON, an empty snapshot list means the archive recorded zero snapshots. A legacy archive with no recorded list returns `null`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Verification already reads and validates the manifest. The opt-in report projects the asset kinds, database roles, and agent IDs after verification succeeds, without another archive scan.

## Evidence

Debian 13, isolated OpenClaw state, synthetic config. I created local archives with `backup create --only-config` and `backup create --no-include-workspace` and verified those same files before and after. The commands below use the CLI source entry (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`), shown as `openclaw`. Output is filtered with `jq` as indicated.

**Before** · `ec270048434`

```console
$ for archive in config.tar.gz state.tar.gz; do openclaw backup verify "$archive" --json | jq -c '{ok,assetCount,sqliteInventoryVerified}'; done
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"sqliteInventoryVerified":true}
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"sqliteInventoryVerified":true}
$ openclaw backup verify config.tar.gz --inventory --json
OpenClaw does not recognize option "--inventory".
```

**After** · `7177df8f278`

```console
$ for archive in config.tar.gz state.tar.gz legacy.tar.gz; do openclaw backup verify "$archive" --inventory --json | jq -c '{ok,assetCount,inventory}'; done
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"inventory":{"assetKinds":["config"],"sqliteSnapshots":[]}}
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"inventory":{"assetKinds":["state"],"sqliteSnapshots":[]}}
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"inventory":{"assetKinds":["config"],"sqliteSnapshots":null}}
$ openclaw backup verify populated.tar.gz --inventory --json | jq -c '{ok,inventory}'
{"ok":true,"inventory":{"assetKinds":["state"],"sqliteSnapshots":[{"role":"global"},{"role":"agent","agentId":"main"}]}}
$ openclaw backup verify latest --from archive --namespace fixture --inventory --json | jq -c '{ok,inventory}'
{"ok":true,"inventory":{"assetKinds":["config"],"sqliteSnapshots":[]}}
```

The legacy fixture omits the SQLite inventory field. The populated fixture includes a synthetic agent database, and the offsite example uses an encrypted filesystem storage location.

The four focused backup and CLI test files passed on the PR commit (116 passed, one Windows-only path test skipped on Linux, 247 seconds wall time). Core type checking, changed-file lint, formatting, and whitespace checks also passed.

prs.title: fix: stop webhook runs from leaving a session behind each time
prs.body:
Related: #202621

## What Problem This Solves

Every isolated webhook run (`POST /hooks/agent` or a mapped agent hook) leaves its automation session behind for good. A Gateway that receives webhooks all day piles up hundreds of these sessions, which push real conversations off the first page of the session list.

## User Impact

User impact: an isolated webhook run now removes its own session when it finishes, like any one-shot automation. Persistent hooks keep their session, and a hook whose session key points at an existing `cron:` session, such as a stored automation's, leaves that session in place. Background commands an isolated hook run leaves running stop when its session is removed, as they already do for one-shot automations. Sessions leaked before this change are not removed (see Evidence → Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

Webhook runs build their one-shot job by hand and never store it. Every other one-shot path defaults to deleting its run session after the run; the webhook job skipped that default, and nothing else can reach it, because cron retention only prunes per-run keys and `cron.remove` only knows stored jobs.

This change sets that flag for isolated webhook jobs and makes the post-run cleanup delete only the session the run owns (`cron:<jobId>`). Without that second part, a hook keyed at an existing `cron:` session would delete it, for example a stored automation's.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`: isolated hook jobs set `deleteAfterRun`; persistent hooks do not.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/session-cleanup.ts`: for isolated targets, cleanup deletes only `cron:<job.id>`, canonicalized by the same `resolveCronAgentSessionKey` the runner uses. Stored isolated jobs always run under `cron:<job.id>` (`src/gateway/server-cron-agent-run.ts`), so their cleanup is unchanged. Persistent `session:` targets keep their existing rule.
- Cron retention is not widened. Deciding from key names alone which existing `cron:` rows are disposable would also catch a stored job's `session:cron:<name>` target or a persistent `cron:` hook key, and would delete accumulated rows in one burst on upgrade.
- Cleanup runs at the end of each run, so it does not depend on the cron scheduler and also works with `cron.enabled: false`.
- Accepted edge case, unchanged from stored one-shots: a run whose required delivery is refused keeps its session for inspection.

</details>

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, real model.** An isolated Gateway (`--profile`, fresh state) built from this branch, with hooks enabled and `ollama/qwen3:1.7b` served by Ollama in Docker. Every webhook was sent with `waitForCompletion: true`, and every run completed `ok`. The same script ran once with the two production files reverted to `main` and once with this change:

| Step | `main` | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 isolated `POST /hooks/agent` | 3 `agent:main:cron:<jobId>` sessions left | 0 left |
| Persistent hook `hook:persist:1` | kept | kept |
| Stored automation run, then an isolated hook keyed `cron:<thatJobId>` | automation session kept | automation session kept |
| Final session list | 3 leaked `cron:` rows, the automation's session, `hook:persist:1` | the automation's session, `hook:persist:1` |

**Regression tests, red on `main` and green with this change** (Linux, WSL Ubuntu 26.04, Node 24.22.2, base `369cdbaed`):

- A hook run pointed at `cron:daily-report` must not delete it. On `main` it fails: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called +0 times, but got 1 times` (the stored automation's session is deleted). With this change it passes.
- An isolated hook run deletes its own `cron:<jobId>` session: passes on both (the cleanup path itself already works once the flag is set).
- An isolated webhook job asks for that cleanup, a persistent one does not. On `main` it fails: `- "deleteAfterRun": true` expected, missing. With this change it passes.

The runner cases drive `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` with the real delivery dispatch, which owns post-run cleanup, and observe the `sessions.delete` request.

**Affected suites with this change:**

- `run.session-lifecycle`, `delivery-dispatch.double-announce`, `service.remove-session-cleanup`: 89/89 passed.
- `server.hooks`, `hooks.early-failure`: 48/48 passed.

**Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt on changed files pass; `git diff --check` clean; test-lines ratchet OK (net +36, within allowance).

**Gaps:**

- The real-Gateway run above used direct `/hooks/agent`. Mapped agent hooks build their job in the same dispatcher, which the gateway test covers, but were not run live.
- On Windows 11, tests in `run.session-lifecycle.test.ts` that drive the isolated runner time out, also on unmodified `main`, so the runner proof above was taken on Linux.
- Sessions leaked before this change remain. Telling which old `agent:<id>:cron:<id>` rows are disposable needs job-binding-aware cleanup, so it belongs in its own change; archiving them (`sessions.patch archived=true`, the reporter's workaround) keeps them out of the session list meanwhile.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```text
# red: production files from origin/main, tests from this branch
pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts -t "an isolated hook run"
pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts -t "keeps session-mode in the idempotency dispatch scope"
# green
pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts src/cron/service.remove-session-cleanup.test.ts
pnpm test src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.early-failure.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:core:test
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main
# real Gateway (hooks.enabled, allowRequestSessionKey, prefixes hook: and cron:; Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768)
pnpm openclaw --profile hook202621 gateway run --port 19789 --bind loopback --auth token
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19789/hooks/agent -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOOK_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the word pong.","agentId":"main","deliver":false,"waitForCompletion":true}'
pnpm openclaw --profile hook202621 sessions --all-agents --json
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: check a recorded data-at-risk mark before repair or the next update acts on it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an update step fails after it may have touched state, the updater records a "data at risk" mark on that run, for example `rollback-state-unverified`. Most of these marks come from a failed read or a timeout, not from real damage. The published 2026.10.33 and 2026.11.5 updaters keep writing them, and nothing ever checked a mark:

- The update report said "Keep the Gateway stopped" even when the Gateway was running.
- `openclaw update repair` then refused to start the Gateway for that run every time, naming only `openclaw gateway status --deep`.
- The next `openclaw update` ignored the mark completely. When the installation was already current, it exited 0 without a word.

## User Impact

User impact: a recorded data-at-risk mark is now checked against the state on disk, without the user having to run anything first.

- **State consistent:** the next plain `openclaw update` prints one line, resolves the mark and continues. That includes automatic updates and updates that find the installation already current. `openclaw update repair` does the same and also starts a Gateway the marked update stopped.
- **Real inconsistency:** the update or repair still refuses and changes nothing. It says what is wrong and whether the Gateway is running, records the finding on the run, and names `openclaw triage` first and the manual command last.
- **Killed-update refusals from #201361** now also name `openclaw triage` before the manual command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One verification owner** (`src/infra/update-data-at-risk.ts`) answers "is the state on disk consistent with the installed version?".
  - It reuses the runtime schema preflight: a child process reads the database in one native read transaction, with no copy, so it is safe beside a live writer. It also uses the existing recovery-admission readers.
  - Findings: a database newer than the installed build, a database behind it (unfinished migration), unfinished update recovery, an interrupted restore directory, retained `.migrated-<run>` files from the marked run's database rollback (state may be only partly restored), or unreadable state (unverifiable).
  - An `active-mutation` mark (Doctor writers that may still be alive) is not resolved from schemas alone. Before Doctor it is deferred to Doctor. After the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state and agent ownership, no earlier writer can still hold the state, and the schema check decides.
- **History is not rewritten.** A consistent verification records the step `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<marked run>` on the run that checked. Readers in `src/infra/update-run-data-at-risk.ts` treat "marked, later verified" as resolved. No new field, schema or protocol. Published updaters store the mark as the `finalize:data-at-risk` step, which the current reader already decodes, so their marks are handled the same way.
- **Repair.** Before it touches the Gateway, repair verifies every unverified mark in recent history, not only the run that stopped the Gateway. Git release updates and refusals before mutation never stop it. Any inconsistent finding keeps every Gateway as it is, whichever run stopped it. The managed-handoff interrupted-update path reads the same receipt before it restarts.
- **Next update.** Admission runs the same check after foreground admission and before it creates its run, so already-current updates are covered too.
  - Consistent: one line, plus receipts on the new run.
  - Newer state or unreadable: a warning, and the update continues, because its own schema checks still guard activation and updating is the fix for newer state.
  - Anything else: refusal. The refusal happens after the run exists, so the finding is recorded for the agent `openclaw triage` opens.
- **Messages.**
  - Update failure guidance states whether the Gateway was observed running or stopped, which version is installed and whether the update was rolled back, and says the mark is unverified.
  - With the Gateway running, it says nothing is needed now. With it stopped, it names repair to bring it back.
  - Refusals put the next steps before the finding, so the recorded warning's 500-character limit cannot cut them off.
  - Update-path guidance that asks you to stop the managed Gateway names `openclaw gateway stop --force`, because a non-interactive shell refuses the bare command. That covers the repair, status and maintenance-error messages and their docs; #201331 changed one more line in `update-recovery-guidance.ts`.

<details><summary>Genuine refusals kept, and their negative controls</summary>

- **Database newer than the installed version.** Repair refuses and leaves the Gateway as it was (owner test with real SQLite; Docker cell `inconsistent-repair`). The next update warns and continues, and its target schema check still refuses a target that cannot open that state.
- **Unfinished migration** (database behind the installed version): owner test with real SQLite. The next update refuses, and the finding is recorded on the refused run.
- **Unfinished update recovery or an interrupted restore directory:** owner tests with real fixtures. Repair and update admission already refuse these first.
- **Partial database rollback** (the marked run left `.migrated-<run>` files): owner test. Another run's leftover does not count.
- **`active-mutation`:** never resolved by a schema check alone. It is checked only after the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state ownership.
- **Unreadable state or an unlistable state directory:** reported as unverifiable, never as consistent or as an interrupted restore.
</details>

## Update behavior for published updaters

The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched:

- Marks written by 2026.10.33, 2026.11.5 and main are read through the same `finalize:data-at-risk` step.
- A published updater still writes false marks; P0-0 and the catch-alls in the audit belong to other changes.
- When the state is consistent, the first update or repair run by a CLI containing this change resolves the mark without user action.
- A published Gateway's managed-update helper still logs its old text on exit 79. The helper this change ships logs "gateway left stopped: data at risk (...) recorded and not yet verified; run openclaw update repair to verify the state and restart the gateway".

## Steps still left to a person

- **A Gateway left stopped by a marked update when no further update or repair runs.** The Gateway is down, so no Gateway-driven path can run. The next `openclaw update` (or an automatic one, if the user re-enables it) resolves the mark; starting the Gateway takes repair. Agent route: `openclaw triage`. Follow-up: verify the mark inside the failing update's own recovery before it decides the restart.
- **Managed handoff exit 79 (P1-4).** Not changed; see the design below.
- **A real inconsistency.** By definition it needs a decision: finish a migration, restore a backup, or install a newer build. The message leads with `openclaw triage`, and the finding is recorded on the run.
- **An interrupted restore directory or partial rollback leftovers.** No command finishes these safely. The existing docs procedure applies, and the agent gets the file paths.
- **`active-mutation` while the earlier Doctor writers are still alive.** Doctor's maintenance admission waits for them and refuses while they hold the state. Once they exit, one repair or update resolves the mark.
- **An unreadable agent database registry.** Rollback leftovers beside agent databases cannot be looked for, so update and repair refuse and name `openclaw triage`. Retrying once the registry is readable resolves it.
- **`openclaw update repair` in Git release mode.** It refuses as on `main` and leaves the service untouched; the message names `openclaw triage`. A plain `openclaw update` still resolves the mark, as the `green-repeat` cell shows.

## Follow-ups

- **Verdict inside Doctor restoration admission.** After a mark was deferred to Doctor, Doctor restores a Gateway it parked before the post-Doctor recheck runs. Moving the check into Doctor's restoration admission closes that gap. Owner: Doctor maintenance restoration.
- **Unresolved-mark lookup independent of the 100-row history window.**
- **Git release-mode repair ownership** belongs with #201538 (`fix/update-git-release-running-build-from-evidence`). Two pieces are needed:
  - The ownership change this PR reverted, which accepts `openclaw-launcher.mjs` services whose release is a linked worktree of this checkout.
  - The Doctor stale-Gateway check, which must compare the running Gateway with the active release's build, not the checkout's.

  The landing review's two findings that #201538 must address are recorded with the diff in the release-mode worker's notes: the stale-build stop, and sibling `git worktree` checkouts that share a common Git directory.

## P1-4 design (managed handoff exit 79)

- **Why it diverges:** the direct CLI restarts a stopped Gateway after a failure with no data risk (`update-command-failure-recovery.ts`). Under the handoff, the helper stopped the service, not the updater, so `preManagedServiceStop.stopped` is false in the child. The updater then reports `serviceRestartSafe:false`, and the helper exits 79 and leaves the Gateway down.
- **Fix that keeps the exit-79 contract:** a candidate updater running under `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_RUN_HANDOFF=1` could take the helper's recorded `service-stop` as its own stop evidence. It would then run the same restart and verification and report `service: "healthy"` with `serviceRestartSafe: true`. The helper already restores nothing in that case and exits non-79.
- **Why it is left out:** it only helps once the installed updater contains it, and it needs its own red and green handoff proof. It is left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

Behavior checked, on the exact head unless noted. Base for red is `origin/main` `f4b42cc9ae7`, or `f5b717d232f` where stated.

- **Owner (real SQLite)**, `src/infra/update-data-at-risk.test.ts`:
  - Current state is consistent beside an open `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer, and the in-process copy path (`prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation`) is never called.
  - Newer schema, behind schema, unfinished recovery, interrupted restore and partial-rollback leftovers are inconsistent.
  - Unreadable state and an unlistable directory are unverifiable; `active-mutation` is never resolved.
  - Red first: the no-copy and unlistable-directory cases failed on the first implementation, which used the maintenance copy path and labeled listing errors as an interrupted restore, then passed.
- **Repair** (`update-repair-service.test.ts`, real ledger and finalization):
  - A false mark with the Gateway stopped is verified, the receipt recorded, and the Gateway started.
  - The same with the Gateway running is verified, not restarted.
  - A mark on a run that never stopped the Gateway is verified once; a second repair does not check it again.
  - Inconsistent and unverifiable verdicts keep the Gateway as it was and print the exact refusal. One case uses a realistic UUID and path to prove the next steps survive the 500-character limit; another reports a running Gateway's version.
  - Reviewer-found regression: a Gateway another run stopped stays down when a later mark is inconsistent.
- **Next update** (`update-command-run.test.ts`):
  - A consistent mark prints one line and records the receipt on the new run, and a later update does not check it again.
  - An unfinished migration refuses and records the finding on the refused run.
  - Newer state warns and continues.
- **Guidance** (`update-recovery-guidance.test.ts`): exact text for running, stopped, rolled-back, failed-rollback and unobserved Gateways. Red on base `f5b717d232f` (11 cases fail), green on head.
- **Killed-update refusals** (`update-command-killed-run-refusals.process.test.ts`): every refusal names the agent route before the manual command.
- **Timeout attribution.** Two `update-command-database-rollback` cases and one `update-repair-cancellation` case timed out at 120 s in a 15-file local batch at load ~30. Run alone on the same machine:
  - The `git`/`git-edited` cases took 69 s/54 s on head against 71 s/59 s on base, and printed no data-at-risk verification.
  - `update-repair-cancellation` passed 7/7 on head.
  - Base failed a different case in that file in its own loaded batch. The timeouts were machine load, not added cost.
- **End to end:** the Docker cells below. The package and Git release-mode green cells ran on `787cf1befff`. The commits after it are merges of `main` (release tooling, UI, and the pnpm and Git-checkout update fixes #201735 and #201701) and touch no mark, verification or repair path.

## End-to-end: package install (installed tarball, real managed Gateway under a systemd shim)

`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_INSTALLED_RECOVERY_CUT=data-at-risk`. It installs the packed tarball, starts a managed Gateway, kills real `openclaw update` runs at fixed points, and writes the mark a failed rollback read leaves onto the killed run, in the row shape published updaters persist. Everything after that point goes through the installed CLI.

| Step | Red: base `f4b42cc9ae7` | Green: head `787cf1befff` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `after-mark-update`: next plain update after a false mark (Gateway stopped by the killed run) | exit 1. The update refuses: "the Gateway that update stopped is still not running" | exit 0 in 262 s. Prints `... verification found the state schemas match installed OpenClaw ... so that mark is resolved.`, records the receipt, installs the next version, and the Gateway serves it |
| `marked-repair`: repair after another false mark with the Gateway stopped | not reached | exit 0 in 53 s. Repair verifies the mark, records `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<run>` on its own run, then starts the Gateway and verifies it (new PID, `marked-repair-probe` 0) |
| `inconsistent-repair`: the marked run's rollback left `openclaw.sqlite.migrated-<run>` | not reached | exit 1 in 18 s. `... The Gateway is stopped. Repair left the Gateway as it was. Run \`openclaw triage\` for an agent with the recorded facts, or by hand: keep that file and the update's backup; ... Found: the database rollback of update <run> left .../openclaw.sqlite.migrated-<run> ...`. The Gateway stays stopped and no receipt is written |
| `restored-repair`: the leftover removed | not reached | exit 0 in 50 s. Receipt recorded; the Gateway starts and serves |

The green cell took 736 s under host load 18 to 22. Gateway outage in each repair case is the repair's own time (53 s and 50 s), which ends with a verified serving Gateway.

`autoreview` does not run on this machine. Two independent read-only reviewers reviewed the diff and the tests; their findings and what changed are listed below.

## Tests changed or removed

- `update-repair-service.test.ts`: the "named data risk" case of "does not start a Gateway after %s" is replaced by the verified, inconsistent, unverifiable and later-mark cases. The old behavior (refuse forever) is what this change fixes.
- `update-recovery-guidance.test.ts`: assertions on "Keep the Gateway stopped" are replaced by exact rendered text.
- `update-command-post-update-repair.test.ts`, `cleanup.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`, `update-repair-command.test.ts`, the killed-run tests and `update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts`: expectations follow the new text.
- `update-data-at-risk.test.ts`: "never resolves a mark that records live Doctor writers" is replaced by a case that proves both halves: unverifiable (deferred to Doctor) before Doctor holds the state, consistent after. The old expectation was the repair loop that round 2 finding 4 reported.
- `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`: "reports stale stop failure" gains an `identity-uninspectable` case. When service identity cannot be inspected, the stop is skipped, and the error must say so rather than "did not stop".
- `service-layout.test.ts`: the Git release-mode ownership cases are removed along with the reverted change; they move to the follow-up.
- Net test growth is +923 lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/update-data-at-risk-verification.txt` records 523 beyond the 400 allowance, with the reason.

## Reviewer findings

**First review (before the next-update and release-mode work):**
- The owner copied the database (the default preflight purpose was maintenance): fixed red then green.
- A listing failure was labeled an interrupted restore: fixed red then green.
- Some bare `gateway stop` instances remained: fixed in the update path.
- Repair only verified the stopping run's mark: fixed.
- The handoff reader ignored the receipt: fixed.

**Second review:**
- Repair could start a Gateway after reporting an inconsistent later mark (blocker): fixed, with a regression test.
- The 500-character limit cut off the next steps: the next steps now come first, multiple databases collapse to "(and N more)", and a realistic-length test covers it.
- `active-mutation` and partial-rollback marks could be falsely resolved: both now refuse resolution, with tests.
- A dangling "By hand:" in `refuse()`: fixed.
- Verification ran before foreground admission: moved after it.
- Only the newest mark got a receipt: all unverified marks are now resolved at once.
- `Keep the Gateway stopped` in `update-command-database-backup.ts` rollback-start messages: left as is. It belongs to the restore/rollback catch-all fixes (audit P2-1), not this change.
- No unit test for the handoff receipt reader: not added; that path is covered only by its existing refusal test.

## Not proven

- A mark written by the published `openclaw@2026.11.5` binary itself. The Docker cells use a copied record in the exact row shape that `v2026.11.5:src/infra/update-run-write.ts` and its codec persist.
- Windows.
- The managed handoff (`update.run`) trigger end to end; the Git cell uses the CLI trigger.
- An `active-mutation` mark end to end. It is covered by the owner test and the repair test (red on the previous head, green now), not by a Docker cell.
- Inherited failure, not caused here: `update-command-rollback.test.ts` "excludes a competing config writer..." fails on base `4c11507` as well.

## Rating round 1 findings and what changed

The round 1 rating was F/F/F; the reviewer saw no end-to-end evidence yet. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Rollback leftovers of agent databases were missed.** Real: the scan only listed the shared directory. Verification now walks the state directory, bounded in depth and entry count, for the marked run's `.migrated-<run>` files. A walk that cannot finish is unverifiable. Tested with both a shared and an agent leftover.
2. **The staged handoff helper's history read could reject an advanced schema.** Real: it ran for every run. It now reads history only when the run carries a mark. If that read fails, the mark stands, as before this change, so an unmarked recovery restarts as it did.
3. **A refusal did not reach the helper that restarts the Gateway.** Real: repair returned `coreUpdate: completed`. A mark refusal now makes repair report `coreUpdate: "pending"`, which the helper already treats as "post-core repair did not complete", so it leaves the Gateway stopped. Covered in the repair tests.
4. **A newer shared database cannot reach the verifier in the Docker cell.** Real: repair's own admission refuses newer shared state first. The Docker negative control now uses a rollback leftover, which reaches the verifier. A newer shared database is still refused by that existing admission, with its existing message.
5. **A newer database masked an unfinished migration.** Real: the warn-and-continue exception now applies only when no database is behind.
6. **"Repair changed nothing" overstated what repair did.** Real: Doctor and plugin maintenance had already run. It now says "Repair left the Gateway as it was".

## Rating round 2 findings and what changed

Round 2 rated proof D, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Rollback files beside an external agent store were missed.** Real. Leftover detection now reads the agent database registry (`readRegisteredAgentDatabases`) and checks the exact `<db>.migrated-<run>{,-wal,-shm,-journal}` family beside the shared database and every registered agent database. A registry read failure is unverifiable. Tested with a shared leftover and one beside an agent store outside the state directory.
2. **Doctor could cycle the Gateway before the check.** Real. Repair now checks unverified marks before Doctor maintenance starts and refuses there, so Doctor never parks or restarts the Gateway on an inconsistent mark (`expectRefusedBeforeDoctor`). An unfinished migration, and now a live-writer mark, are deferred to Doctor and checked again after it.
3. **The original-runtime handoff fallback could restart past a refusal.** Real. `assertRestartSafe` in the interrupted-handoff helper now checks every unverified mark in history, not only the interrupted run's, and falls back to the run's own mark when history cannot be read.
4. **`active-mutation` marks could never be resolved.** Real: repair told you to run repair again, and the next repair said the same thing. Before Doctor, the mark is now deferred to Doctor. After the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state and agent ownership, no writer the marked run left can still hold the state, so the schema check decides. One repair resolves it (red on the previous head, green now).
5. **The state-tree walk could exhaust its entry limit on large release-mode installs.** Real. The walk is gone; finding 1's registry check replaces it, so `git-install/releases` is never read.
6. **History was read with a cold synchronous snapshot before admission.** Real. The next-update check uses the async worker history read (`listUpdateRunsAsync`).
7. **Ahead and behind together named only the ahead database.** Real. The refusal names both, and its next step is to restore the pre-update backup, since neither `openclaw update` nor `doctor --fix` settles both.
8. **An unknown runtime was reported as stopped.** Real. The Gateway is reported stopped only when the runtime says `stopped`; otherwise its state is reported as unknown.

The low-value-test note on `update-recovery-guidance.test.ts` was not taken: the exact rendered text is what the brief asks to prove, and each case covers a distinct Gateway state.

## Rating round 3 findings and what changed

Round 3 rated proof D, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **A live-writer mark hid a rollback leftover.** Real. The `active-mutation` deferral is now the verifier's last check, so a leftover, an interrupted restore, or a schema finding reports first. Owner test: an `active-mutation` mark beside a leftover now returns the leftover (red on the previous head).
2. **The interrupted-handoff helper checks history-wide marks.** Rejected in round 3; the landing review showed it was real (see below) and it is now fixed. `assertRestartSafe` runs after `finalize()`, and finalize verifies every unverified mark first and records receipts. A false earlier mark is resolved in the same finalize and does not hold the Gateway. Only a mark that finalize could not resolve keeps it down, which is the intended outcome.
3. **Restoration ignored receipts from earlier repairs.** Real for consistency. `restoreRepairGateway` now reads receipts across recent history, as admission does. No dedicated test: in the repair harness, a repair whose start failed does not leave a stop intent for the next repair to restore. So the path the reviewer describes is not reachable through repair today.
4. **A refusal after Doctor finished finalization with exit 0.** Real. A mark still refused after Doctor now fails finalization: abandoned runs are not acknowledged, the handoff is not completed, text mode prints `Update finalization failed.`, and the command exits 1 with the refusal. The next repair retries it. Repair test: red (repair `succeeded`), green (`failed`, and a later repair resolves the mark and starts the Gateway).
5. **Files a completed rollback keeps on purpose were treated as a partial restore.** Real. `restoreUpdateDatabaseBackup` keeps the displaced `<db>.migrated-<run>` files after a successful restore and records a completed `database rollback` step. A mark whose run has that step no longer counts those files. Owner test covers it.
6. **A registry read failure replaced a schema verdict.** Real. The round-3 fix let an unfinished migration hide unchecked agent leftovers; the landing review caught that and the fix below replaces it. Shared-database leftovers are checked without the registry. Agent leftovers are checked after the schema verdict, and when the registry cannot be read, the schema finding is reported instead of a generic registry error. An unfinished migration or newer state still cannot hide an agent leftover. No separate test, because the registry read failure cannot be produced from a fixture without mocking the reader.
7. **The skipped-stop message inferred liveness from the stop flag.** Real. The message now comes from the existing liveness check, so an already-offline service passes. When the stop was skipped, the error says `Stale Gateway PID <pid> was not stopped: <reason> Observed: service=..., PID=..., port ...=...`. Doctor test: red on the previous code (`did not stop`), green now.

## Landing review findings and what changed

The landing review on `231fdd86e36` rated proof C, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Release-mode ownership stopped a healthy Gateway** (P1, `service-layout.ts`). Real, and reproduced under real systemd. Reverted; see "Git release-mode repair: moved to a follow-up".
2. **Sibling `git worktree` checkouts could claim each other's service** (P2, `service-layout.ts`). Real. Reverted with finding 1.
3. **Unchecked agent leftovers were deferred or continued past** (P1, `update-data-at-risk.ts`, the coordinator's fix-6 blocker and its sibling). Real.
   - An unreadable agent registry with an unfinished migration returned the deferrable migration verdict, so Doctor maintenance could park and restart the Gateway without anyone having looked for agent leftovers.
   - An unreadable agent database returned `unverifiable` before the leftover scan, and a plain update continued past a leftover it never saw.

   The verifier now looks for leftovers first, beside the shared database and every registered agent database, before any other check. When the registry cannot be read, the result is `unverifiable` with `leftoversUnchecked`. It keeps any schema finding beside that fact ("the agent database registry could not be read, so database rollback leftovers beside agent databases are unchecked; and <schema finding>"), and is never `finishable` or `newerState`. Every consumer of the verdict refuses on it:
   - **Repair before maintenance:** it is not deferrable, so repair refuses before Doctor and leaves the Gateway as it was.
   - **The next plain update:** it refuses on `leftoversUnchecked` instead of warning and continuing.
   - **Finalize after Doctor:** any result other than `consistent` refuses and fails finalization.
   - **Managed handoff:** it restarts only on a receipt, and receipts are written only after a `consistent` verdict.

   Tests, red on `231fdd86e36` and green now:
   - unreadable registry with an unfinished migration, with and without an agent leftover, at the owner and through repair before Doctor;
   - an unreadable agent database beside its leftover;
   - a readable registry, unchanged;
   - the plain-update refusal.
4. **The interrupted-handoff entry guard blocked on older marks** (P1, `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.ts`). Real. The entry guard now judges only the interrupted run's own mark, as on `main`. The history-wide check stays after `finalize()`, which verifies older marks and records their receipts. Handoff lifecycle test: an interrupted managed update with only an earlier false mark recovers and restarts. Red on `231fdd86e36` (`gateway left stopped: data at risk (rollback-state-unverified)`), green now.
5. **The rollback-completed exception read a step compaction evicts** (P2, `update-run-data-at-risk.ts`). Real. It now also reads `diagnostic:database rollback`, which only a completed restore writes ("Restored pre-migration databases from ..."). The ledger's compaction keeps that step and its text. Owner test with a ledger compacted past the ordinary step: the retained `.migrated-<run>` file no longer counts. No new stored field.

## Rating round after the landing review

On `33e6184dbc6`: proof C, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Doctor can restore a parked Gateway before the post-Doctor check** (P1, `update-command-finalize.ts`). Real but narrow. A mark deferred to Doctor (an unfinished migration, or live Doctor writers) lets Doctor maintenance park a running Gateway, and Doctor restores it before the post-Doctor recheck runs. `main` has no recheck at all, so this is no worse than `main`.
   - Changed here: the refusal after Doctor no longer claims the Gateway was left as it was. It now says `Repair did not start or restart the Gateway after this check.` Tested in the after-Doctor refusal case.
   - Not changed: making the verdict part of Doctor's restoration admission changes Doctor's restoration owner. It is listed as a follow-up.
2. **The original-runtime branch of the interrupted handoff restores without the history-wide check** (P1, `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.ts`). Rejected for this PR. With no plugin cohort, no finalize runs there, so no receipt can be written. A history-wide check would bring back the stuck state the landing review reported, where a false older mark keeps the Gateway down. The branch behaves exactly as on `main`.
3. **An inaccessible rollback path was read as absent** (P2). Real. Leftover probes now separate "not there" (`ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`) from "could not look". The latter goes down the same `leftoversUnchecked` refusal path. Owner test with an unreadable directory: red, then green.
4. **An unfinished migration was deferred while another database could not be read** (P2). Real. An unreadable database next to a behind or newer one is now `unverifiable` and never deferrable, with both findings in the detail. Owner test with real SQLite: red, then green.
5. **The repair's own row can push the oldest of 100 marked runs out of the window** (P2). Not changed. Only a mark at row 101 is affected, and that is the same history window `main` reads everywhere. The stopping run's mark is read by run ID, so it is never skipped. Listed as a follow-up.

## CI on `787cf1befff`

Three jobs in run [44525460079](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44525460079) failed, and none of them came from this change:
- `check-test-types-core-2` and `check-test-types-core-3` failed with eight TS2739 errors in `test/scripts/release-*` fixtures. `main`'s own CI run [44524514068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44524514068) at `dbc1aa04e88` (the `main` merged here) shows the same errors in the same jobs. #201811 fixed them.
- `checks-node-compact-small-3` failed in `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` ("Expected workflow step Download full release validation manifest"). This change touches no workflow or release tooling.

Merging current `main` cleared them. The root test-type stripes pass locally on the merged head.

The later `package-acceptance-workflow` failure came from #201802 removing a workflow step without updating its test. It was inherited from `main`, and #201805 fixed it by restoring the step. This head merges `main` after #201805.

## End-to-end: Git release mode (installed checkout, real managed service, busy database)

These cells drive the update-matrix harness in Docker. Each one installs a real Git checkout, converts it to release mode through a real `openclaw update`, and runs a second real update under database write load. It then writes the mark that a failed post-activation schema read leaves, in the published row shape, onto that update's run while the Gateway keeps serving. Everything after that point goes through the shipped CLI.

| Cell | Code | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `red-repeat` (inside the `red-repair` cell) | base `cf9a9839e03` | The plain repeat update reports `already-current`, exits 0 and says nothing about the mark. |
| `green-repeat` | head `787cf1befff` (earlier also `b7f71419149`) | The plain repeat update, already current, prints `Update <run> recorded data at risk (rollback-state-unverified); verification found the state schemas match installed OpenClaw 2026.11.5 and no migration or restore is unfinished, so that mark is resolved.` It records `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<run>` on its run (read back through `openclaw update status`) and exits 0 in 145 s. Busy load held throughout: 1278 write commits at 8 MiB/s on a 512 MiB database and 1278 readiness probes, with 0 failed and 0 outages. The Gateway served the same build before and after. |

`green-repeat` does not depend on the reverted release-mode ownership change. A plain update's mark check runs at update admission and never asks whether the service belongs to this checkout. The same cell's repeat step on base passed that path silently, with no ownership refusal.

### Git release-mode repair: moved to a follow-up

This PR no longer changes release-mode repair ownership. An earlier head accepted a Git release-mode service as the checkout's own (`src/daemon/service-layout.ts`). The landing review found two problems with that change, both of which make release-mode repair worse than on `main`:
- Once the service is accepted, Doctor's stale-Gateway inspection reads the expected build from the source checkout, not from the active release. It then stops a healthy Gateway that serves the release, and repair exits 1. A real-systemd cell reproduced this on `1e39a2c5828` ([raw output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201668#issuecomment-7014449579)).
- Two independent `git worktree` checkouts share a common Git directory, so one could claim the other's release-mode service.

The change is reverted here. Release-mode repair behaves as on `main`: it refuses and changes nothing. The refusal is now true for this case. It names the Git release launcher, says this checkout cannot yet confirm that the release is its own, says the service was left untouched, and leads with `openclaw triage` (rendered-text test in `update-command-service-maintenance.test.ts`). The ownership change and both findings move to the release-mode follow-up (#201538), which also carries the Doctor stale-build fix.

Two related message fixes stay in this PR. Doctor's stale-Gateway stop now reports a stop that was skipped (`was not stopped: <reason>`) and one it could not confirm (`could not be confirmed stopped`) instead of always `did not stop`. Both have red/green tests in `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`.

Raw terminal lines from every cell are in [this PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201668#issuecomment-7010468460). The full outputs (`fix.stderr`, `repeat.stderr`, update status JSON, asciinema casts) are kept locally, because the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine.

prs.title: fix: distinguish followup admission failures from revoked access
prs.body:
Related: #200072

## What Problem This Solves

When continuing a child task, OpenClaw can report that access was revoked even when the first continuation attempt was denied. It also loses which side rejected the continuation, making the operator's access check harder.

## User Impact

Callers can distinguish an initial rejection from later loss of access, identify the parent or child endpoint, and receive a safe next step: ask an authorized operator to check continuation access for both conversations.

Permissions do not change, and hidden-session details remain private. This diagnostic fix does not repair early session-resolution failures, explicit message source-admission failures, automation management scope, or unrelated Goal/completion-delivery failures. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a bounded `followupAccess` result containing phase, endpoint and public policy code through the existing custody and completion owners. Raw policy messages, policy details, session keys, identities and causes are not added to that diagnostic. The operator guidance addresses the retained review's P3 finding without suggesting recreation or granting additional authority.

## Evidence

The published source tree passed **160 focused tests across 12 files** (166.64 seconds), including all five diagnostic/privacy/authorized-continuation cases and all ten prepared-harness source-delivery cases. The latter includes the seven cases that failed in the previous CI snapshot; the selected upstream base supplies the missing fixture catalog. This is focused local proof, not a full-CI or live-native-acceptance claim.

Production types and three consuming test-type projects passed, along with focused lint on all nine changed TypeScript files, formatting on all ten changed files, documentation parsing, the +295/400 test-line budget and the feature-only diff check. The earlier original-base regression produced four denied-path failures and one authorized pass; that earlier RED is not presented as a new baseline replay.

The published tree is `8ae4c20cf731622ff5e6d1a97661debff0509662`, validated against review base `2b9b23b9f3afbd8ebb233c097e13b847df0b73a3`. GitHub now shows only the intended **10 files (+412/−13)**; the former 59-file base-context difference has been reconciled.

ClawSweeper completed its [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200155#issuecomment-6921500449) of `f78ef5226a8dc0cee020adbc0ca342d49b1f9b47` on November 17, 2026 at 17:14 UTC: **no actionable findings**, the prior P3 guidance finding resolved, and ready for maintainer review. The exact-head CI gate, dependency review and security-sensitive review have passed.

Remaining evidence limits: the review explicitly notes missing isolated real-Gateway/native behavior evidence, so native acceptance remains incomplete. An earlier interrupted canonical local-review attempt remains unconfirmed and is not counted as a completed or clean local review. These results cover the bounded diagnostic patch, not the other session-resolution, explicit-reply, automation or Goal failure surfaces.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```bash
pnpm test \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup-diagnostics.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-owner-continuation.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-helpers.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.incognito.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/completion/session-followup-completion.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-communication.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-send-reply-flow.requester.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json --incremental
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/concepts/session-tool.md
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 2b9b23b9f3afbd8ebb233c097e13b847df0b73a3 --staged
git diff --cached --check 2b9b23b9f3afbd8ebb233c097e13b847df0b73a3
```

All commands exited 0. Focused lint used `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; formatting used `pnpm format:check` on the feature-only changed paths.

</details>

## Worked on by

prs.body:
## Problem

`ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts` "bounds skills ready-window asset requests" fails intermittently on slow CI runners with `expected 30 to be less than or equal to 28`. It hit unrelated PRs (#203126, #203308) and scheduled `main` (6577f41b9aba; the 7 runs after it passed).

## Root cause

No commit added a Skills first-visit chunk. The 30 assets are the same 28 plus `app-sidebar-customize.js` and `presentation.js`: the Customize sidebar, which every Plugins-hub page shows, including Skills (`ui/src/app-navigation.ts:76`, since #199825). It loads lazily (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-owner.tsx:72`) after the Skills page module arrives (about 560 ms in). On a fast CPU the page reports ready first (28 assets). On a slow runner, rendering the skill rows takes longer than the two sidebar files take to load, so they finish inside the ready window (30 assets).

Keeping 28 needs a chunking change, and each option costs elsewhere: `presentation.tsx` is shared by about 16 chunks (chat cards, command palette). Moving it into `deferred-ui-support` adds bytes to Chat startup. Moving it into catalog or hub chunks makes chat load catalog code. Loading the sidebar earlier makes 30 constant.

## Fix

Raise the Skills ready-window limit to 30 with the reason in a comment. This is the same race #194827 accounted for with its Settings sidebar on `skill-settings` (31). No shipped bytes change.

## Risk

On fast runners the count stays 28, so the limit has 2 slots of slack there: a real regression of 2 assets on the Skills ready path would pass on a fast runner.

## Evidence

- Before, 4x CPU throttle: 28 assets (no reproduction). Before, 10x CPU throttle: 30 assets, the same list as CI; the test fails as in CI.
- After, 10x CPU throttle: 30 ≤ 30, pass. All four route cases pass at normal speed.
- oxfmt and oxlint on the changed file.

## Approval

This raises a performance budget. Maintainer approval (Ayaan, 2026-11-22): "Approved, we can merge past red CI if we can prove we didn't cause it."

prs.title: fix(voice-call): hear the caller after a GPT-Live opening greeting
prs.body:
Closes #203387

## What Problem This Solves

On an inbound Voice Call routed to GPT-Live, the caller is never heard after the opening greeting. Voice Call withholds caller audio while the greeting plays and releases it once the model sends `response.done` and carrier playback drains. GPT-Live sends no response-complete event and streams audio continuously (silence after it speaks), so neither condition is ever met and the rest of the call is deaf.

## User Impact

User impact: Voice Call on GPT-Live hears the caller after the greeting, so questions reach the model and get delegated to the OpenClaw agent. GA realtime models (`gpt-realtime-*`) keep their current `response.done` behavior unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Voice Call already ends host-requested speech by audible output actually played to the caller plus a quiet window (`hostSpeech` in `realtime-call-playback.ts`), not by a model receipt. This applies the same rule to the opening on native-delegation models:

- `createRealtimeCallAudioController` takes `finishGreetingOnQuietOutput`. When set, the pacer's played-out audio (`onAudioSent`) drives it: the opening ends 1.5 s after the last audible frame reaches the carrier, or after 5 s if nothing audible ever plays.
- The realtime handler sets it from the session policy's `handlesAgentConsult` (GPT-Live). GA models never set it, so their path is untouched.
- The release logs one line: `[voice-call] realtime opening greeting finished (quiet output|no audible output)`.
- Docs: the opening-greeting paragraph in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md`.

The model itself behaves correctly. Replaying Voice Call's `session.start` and greeting note straight to the GPT-Live API, with caller audio either flowing or paused for 8 s after the greeting, it transcribes the question and delegates both times. Details are in #203387.

## Evidence

### Tests

| Test | `origin/main` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening without response receipts ends once played-out audio goes quiet (native consult) | fails: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` | passes |
| Same, GA model (no `response.done`): caller audio stays withheld, unchanged | passes | passes |
| Native-delegation opening that never becomes audible is released after 5 s | fails: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` | passes |

Red-on-base was run by swapping the three changed source files for their `origin/main` versions with the new tests in place, then restoring and `cmp`-checking them. The test harness now passes routed-model capabilities to the call registration when a test asks for native delegation.

### Real GPT-Live inbound call (`gpt-live-1`, OpenAI Platform key)

Isolated test Gateway (own `OPENCLAW_HOME`, mock agent model, no production config). A local script plays Twilio: it posts the inbound webhook, opens the issued media stream, waits 12 s and says "What's on my calendar today?" as G.711 μ-law. A test-only TLS relay records every frame between the Gateway and `api.openai.com`. The mock agent answers every turn with "You have one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m."

Without this fix (same Voice Call greeting code as `origin/main`):

```
input_audio.append: 11 delegation.created: 0
caller: -
assistant: Hi! I'm here. Hello! How can I help you today?
mock agent requests: 0
```

With this fix:

```
[voice-call] realtime opening greeting finished (quiet output) callId=<call> providerCallId=<call-sid>
12.9 s s2c session.delegation.created {"offset_ms":14400,"delegation":{"id":"<item>","type":"delegation","target":"client"}}
18.0 s c2s session.commentary.append {"delegation_id":"<item>","content":"You have one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m."}
caller:  What's on my calendar today
assistant:  Hi! I'm here with you. Hello! How can I help you today? Okay, checking your calendar now. You've got one event today: a dentist appointment at three p.m.
mock agent requests: 1
```

The question is heard, delegated through Voice Call's call-owned agent consult, the agent runs, and the answer is spoken on the call.

### Checks

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 50 files, 626 tests passed (424s). `realtime-handler.test.ts` after the final harness typing change: 40 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`: pass. oxlint on `extensions/voice-call`: pass. Format check, `git diff --check`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (+67, allowance 400), `check-test-mock-exports`: pass. `pnpm build`: pass.

Gaps:

- Outbound GPT-Live calls go through the same audio controller and are covered by the unit path, but were not run live: an outbound call needs a real carrier.
- GPT-Live sometimes adds its own line before the verbatim greeting ("Hi! I'm here."). That is model behavior and outside this change; the quiet window simply ends after the last audible line.
