prs.title: fix: make onboarding next steps runnable when OpenClaw runs from npx
prs.body:
Closes #202822
Related: #192331, #202183, #201182

## What Problem This Solves

When someone tries OpenClaw with `npx openclaw@…`, as in the docs' "Try it in one command", and has not installed the CLI, there is no `openclaw` command on their PATH. In the closing lines of a foreground run, onboarding already prints the "keep the Gateway running in the background later" hint as `npx openclaw@<version> gateway install`, but the skipped-AI Next steps, the Local setup line, and the other foreground closing lines still use a bare `openclaw`. Copied into a new terminal, they fail with `openclaw: command not found`.

## User Impact

User impact: when onboarding runs from npx (or another temporary runner copy such as pnpm dlx or bunx), the skipped-AI Next steps, the Local setup line, and the closing lines printed while the Gateway runs in this terminal use the same `npx openclaw@<version> …` form as the existing background hint, so they no longer depend on an installed `openclaw` command in a new terminal. pnpm dlx and bunx runs get this npx form too, so they still need `npx` to be available. Outside temporary runners, output is unchanged unless a named profile or `--container` is in use; then these lines include `--profile <name>` or `--container <name>`, as the background hint already does. No new config, flags, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `084b631` (line numbers below are on that commit), `src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.ts:91-95` already decides whether the CLI runs from a temporary runner copy (`isDisposableEntrypoint`) and, if so, prints the npx form. The next line, `:96`, and the other closing hints print fixed text. This change moves that decision into one exported helper in `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.ts`, the module that already owns the check and the npx form, and uses it for these next-step commands:

- the reopen, pending-Gateway, and setup-only lines in the foreground summary;
- the skipped-AI Next steps, in both places that print them;
- the setup-only note during guided onboarding;
- the Local setup `gateway run` line.

The existing background hint now uses the same helper, with unchanged output. The three wizard locales use placeholders for these commands.

The docs' "Try it in one command" section still suggests installing the CLI for later use, and that stays true. These hints now also work before that step, the same way the background hint from #192331 does.

#202183 (draft) routes the skipped-AI next steps and the `gateway run` line through `formatCliCommand` so a named profile is kept; it does not change what npx runs print. Outside npx, this PR prints the same named-profile commands on those lines, since both go through `formatCliCommand`, and its three `nextStepsWithoutAi` strings match #202183's (head `11ac9b6`). #201182 is a related, different problem: it is about the wording and grouping after skipping AI, not about whether the printed commands run.

Unchanged on purpose: `formatCliCommand`, which the plugin SDK exports; the first-screen `openclaw onboard --classic` hint, shown before setup starts rather than as a next step; the team-setup error messages; the "You can always find me later — run `openclaw` in a terminal" note that some runs print at the end instead of opening the browser, since which command those runs should point to is a separate change; install-cli and install.sh installs, which do not run from a temporary runner copy; the docs.

Known limits: like the existing background hint, the printed command pins the running version.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `formatUserCliCommand(args?)` returns `npx openclaw@<VERSION> <args>` when `isDisposableEntrypoint(process.argv[1])` is true, and `formatCliCommand("openclaw <args>")` otherwise. With no arguments it returns `openclaw` or `npx openclaw@<VERSION>`, without a trailing space. Both forms keep the `--profile` or `--container` flag that `formatCliCommand` adds.
- `formatDurableInstallCommand` had one caller outside its module, the background hint. After the move it is used only inside the module, so it is no longer exported, and it is renamed `formatNpxCliCommand` because it now formats any command. The reinstall message in `resolveDurableServiceCli` is unchanged.
- `setup-apply.ts` loads the helper lazily in the branch where installation was explicitly skipped, like that file's other lazy imports.
- The skipped-AI commands in `onboard-guided.ts` are computed only when the Next steps are printed.
- Against `084b631`: production +59/−31 in 7 files, tests +276/−13 in 4 files.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on the published 2026.11.10-beta.1, whose files for these lines match main `084b631`. "After" results were taken on `084b631` with this PR's change applied: the real run used a package built from `084b631` plus this PR's production changes (the same production files as commit `fdd35b6d16ea`), and the focused tests ran on that commit's full diff.

Real runs through npx, AI skipped, before and after:

- **Setup**: Ubuntu 26.04.1 x86_64. Each run used a fresh throwaway HOME copied from `/etc/skel`, under `env -i` with a minimal environment that included HOME, USER, LOGNAME, `SHELL=/bin/bash`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, TERM and a PATH of the system directories plus a Node v24.22.1 install from nodejs.org. `openclaw` was not installed. Onboarding choices: Quick start, One agent, Skip for now. The printed command was then copied into a new login shell (`bash -l`) with the same environment and stdin from `/dev/null`.
- **Before** (`npx --yes openclaw@2026.11.10-beta.1`):
  - The Local setup block said ``Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `openclaw gateway run` to start it in the foreground.``, and the Next steps block listed bare `openclaw onboard`, `openclaw channels add`, and `openclaw dashboard`.
  - In the new login shell, the copied `openclaw dashboard` exited 127 with `openclaw: command not found`.
  - In the installed 2026.11.10-beta.1 package, the reopen text and the npx form of the background hint are both present, matching `onboard-quickstart-host.ts:91-96` on `084b631`.
- **After** (a package built from `084b631` plus this change with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`, package version 2026.11.5, run with `npx --yes --package <package> openclaw`):
  - The Local setup block said ``Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 gateway run` to start it in the foreground.``, and the Next steps block listed `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 onboard`, `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 channels add`, and `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 dashboard`.
  - In the new login shell, the copied `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 dashboard` resolved instead of failing with `command not found`: npm fetched the published 2026.11.5 and started OpenClaw. That OpenClaw then exited 1 with its own message, "This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data."
- Limit of this test environment: the branch's `package.json` still says 2026.11.5, so the package built from it prints `@2026.11.5`, and the copied command fetched the published 2026.11.5, an older build than the one that had just written this HOME's state. That build refused the newer state, and its message says the state was written by OpenClaw 2026.11.5, the same version label. A published build prints its own version, so the copied command would start the same build that wrote the state; this run shows only that the printed command resolves and starts OpenClaw.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output (before and after)</summary>

Box drawing is removed and a line wrapped by the terminal width is joined. The isolated HOME path is written as `~`. The `_: line 5:` prefix from the `bash -c` wrapper is omitted from the "command not found" line. The "Tool profile" line in the After block comes from #201043 on main, is not printed by the published 2026.11.10-beta.1, and is not changed by this PR.

Before (`npx openclaw@2026.11.10-beta.1`):

```text
Local setup
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `openclaw gateway run` to start it in the foreground.

Next steps
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Add AI later: re-run `openclaw onboard`
After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw channels add`
Open the dashboard: `openclaw dashboard`
```

Before, new login shell:

```text
openclaw dashboard   -> stderr: openclaw: command not found (exit 127)
```

After (package built from `084b631` plus this change):

```text
Local setup
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Tool profile: full (tools.profile). This profile allows every tool, including files, commands, the web and plugins.
Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 gateway run` to start it in the foreground.

Next steps
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Add AI later: re-run `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 onboard`
After AI connects, add a channel: `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 channels add`
Open the dashboard: `npx openclaw@2026.11.5 dashboard`
```

After, new login shell (selected stderr lines; the parts of two lines that name local paths are replaced with `…`):

```text
npx openclaw@2026.11.5 dashboard   -> exit 1
npm warn exec The following package was not found and will be installed: openclaw@2026.11.5
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data.
OpenClaw state database … uses newer schema version 40; this build supports 36.
Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) installed at ….
```

</details>

Focused tests:

- `src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.test.ts` runs the foreground summary with a real temporary entry point under `.npm/_npx/…`:
  - the background hint keeps its npx form (positive control), and the reopen line uses the same form;
  - reopen with a named profile, outside npx and through npx, matches the full expected line, with no trailing space;
  - default reopen output is unchanged;
  - zh-CN and zh-TW reopen lines are interpolated;
  - the pending-Gateway line is formatted in en, zh-CN, and zh-TW, and its default English output is unchanged.
- `src/commands/onboard-guided.quickstart.test.ts`: the skipped-AI Next steps use the npx form in both places that print them (default handoff and chat handoff), and in zh-CN and zh-TW for the default handoff; the default Next steps block is unchanged word for word.
- `src/system-agent/setup-apply.test.ts`: the Local setup line for explicitly skipped installation prints the npx form.
- `src/commands/onboard-guided.skip.test.ts` only gains the same environment pinning as the files above.
- Existing tests in these files keep their assertions. The reopen and pending expectations now pass the default commands, and the files pin `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT` for the cases that compare default output, so that output does not depend on the environment the tests run in.
- On `084b631` with only the test change, the 13 new npx and named-profile cases fail at their own assertions; the 3 new non-npx controls and all existing tests in the four files pass. With this change, all pass.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time (Vitest-reported time): `onboard-quickstart-host.test.ts` 41.4 s (0.09 s; the wall time includes a one-time compile cache warm-up), `onboard-guided.quickstart.test.ts` 12.4 s (2.66 s), `onboard-guided.skip.test.ts` 19.7 s (12.72 s; this file only gains a file-level env stub), `setup-apply.test.ts` 14.1 s (4.03 s).
- Consumers pass: `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.test.ts`, `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.update-race.test.ts`, `src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.plugin-generation.test.ts`, `src/commands/onboard-interactive-runner.test.ts`, `src/wizard/i18n/index.test.ts`, `src/system-agent/setup-apply.concurrency.test.ts`, and `src/system-agent/operations.setup.test.ts`.
- Targeted checks: oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, the test typecheck shards, `git diff --check`, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` pass. `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports three unused exports, and reports the same three on `084b631`; none is in a file this PR changes.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 084b631` passes locally, including the repository ratchets.
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not covered:

- The foreground closing lines (reopen, pending) use the helper that the skipped-AI run exercised live, and are checked by focused tests only; no live capture of that branch is attached.
- The setup-only lines are not covered by a focused test; they use the same helper.
- The chat handoff print of the skipped-AI Next steps is covered by the focused test only.
- macOS and Windows were not run.

prs.title: fix: show how to run openclaw when install-cli.sh leaves it off PATH
prs.body:
Closes #202309
Related: #201383, #201430, #200425

## What Problem This Solves

After installing with the local-prefix installer (`curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash`), the output ends with `OpenClaw installed (…)` and a support link. The command lives in `~/.openclaw/bin`, which is not on a new shell's PATH, and nothing says so, so the next step in the docs, `openclaw onboard`, fails with `openclaw: command not found`.

## User Impact

User impact: when the install prefix's `bin` directory was not on PATH when the installer started, the `install-cli.sh` success summary now says so, prints a shell-specific command that adds it for the current shell, and gives the next step as a full-path command (for example `<home>/.openclaw/bin/openclaw onboard`). When the installer starts onboarding itself (`--onboard`), the PATH lines still appear but the extra next-step line does not. When the directory is already on PATH, and with `--json`, the output is unchanged. The installer still does not add this directory to shell startup files. No new flags, config, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

`install-cli.sh` adds `<prefix>/bin` to PATH only inside its own process (`scripts/install-cli.sh:1337-1338` on `0b4d5d0`; line numbers below are on that commit), and its success summary prints two lines (`:1372-1373`). A piped installer cannot change its parent shell's PATH, so the summary is the only place to tell the user. This change remembers the caller's PATH before that line and, in the summary, prints the current-shell PATH guidance `install.sh` already prints for its own bin directory (`warn_shell_path_missing_dir`: wording, shell-specific commands, and quoting; without its nvm and startup-file branches), followed by the next step in the quoted full-path form `install.sh` uses for follow-up commands (#79074).

The change stays in `install-cli.sh`. It is distributed as its own standalone script whose only shared source is `install-policy.sh` (`install.sh` also downloads the published `install-cli.sh`, but only to reuse `install_node` without running its `main()`, so this change does not reach it); the `install.sh` renderer lives in `install.sh`, depends on that script's own output helpers, and its call site is being changed in #201383. Sharing one renderer would mean moving that function, with its nvm, managed-Node, and startup-file branches, into `install-policy.sh`. This PR leaves `install.sh` and `install-policy.sh` unchanged.

Unchanged on purpose: shell startup files; `--json` events (no new event, and nothing is added to stdout or stderr in JSON mode); the existing `OpenClaw installed` and `Support` lines; the `--onboard` onboarding handoff.

Related, different code paths:

- #201383 keeps the existing `install.sh` PATH warning visible in its final summary. This PR does not touch `install.sh`.
- #201430 changes the `--onboard` handoff in the same function. This PR does not touch that branch and prints its next-step line only when the installer does not start onboarding itself.
- #200425 does not change `install-cli.sh`.

Known limits: like `install.sh`, the check compares PATH entries literally, so a prefix that is on PATH only through a symlink, a trailing slash, or an unexpanded `~` still gets the hint. A prefix containing `:` cannot be placed on PATH at all. The full-path command uses Bash quoting. Unlike `install.sh`, the installer does not check for existing config, so a reinstall that leaves the directory off PATH also prints the `onboard` line. With `--onboard`, the PATH lines are printed before onboarding starts.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- The caller's PATH is captured in `main()` right before the installer prepends its own directories (`:1337`). The `--set-npm-prefix` step, which can also change the process PATH, runs later and does not affect the check.
- The hint is written inline in the success summary rather than as a new helper, because it has one caller.
- The next-step line is the complement of the onboarding condition (`:1375` on `0b4d5d0`, `:1412` with this change): it is printed whenever the installer does not run onboarding itself, including `--onboard` with `OPENCLAW_NO_ONBOARD=1`, and `--runtime-only` with or without `--onboard`. This follows the `install.sh` handoff for an unconfigured install when onboarding is skipped ("Skipping onboard (requested); run … onboard later").
- `docs/install/installer.md` gets one `install-cli.sh` flow step that describes the new summary.
- Against `0b4d5d0`: `scripts/install-cli.sh` +37/−0, `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts` +141/−0, `docs/install/installer.md` +7/−0.
- As of 2026-11-20, a three-way merge with #201430 (head `a0f9a14`) and #201383 (head `65a1354`) applies cleanly in either order.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `0b4d5d0`. "After" results were taken on `0b4d5d0` with this PR's change applied: the real installs used the same `scripts/install-cli.sh` as commit `de8d645fa044`, and the focused tests ran on that commit's full diff.

Real installs, before and after:

- **Setup**:
  - The installer was assembled with `node scripts/build-installers.mjs`. On 2026-11-20, the file assembled from `0b4d5d0` was byte-identical to the published `https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh` (sha256 `f5042f5965486206b9b97653cd745ec13d6e2b4080a0ec23429fed5f0205d85b`).
  - Each fresh install ran as `cat install-cli.sh | bash -s -- --runtime-only --version 2026.11.6` (the npm `latest` at the time) on Ubuntu 26.04.1 x86_64, in a new isolated HOME copied from `/etc/skel`, under `env -i` with `SHELL=/bin/bash` and `PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`.
  - `--runtime-only` was used to isolate the CLI-install path. The success summary runs the same code in a default run (`scripts/install-cli.sh:1366-1373`).
  - The PATH checks ran in a new login shell (`bash -l -c …`) with the same environment.
- **Before** (`0b4d5d0`):
  - The install exited 0, and the output ended with `OpenClaw installed (OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)).` and the support link.
  - In the new login shell, `command -v openclaw` found nothing, and bare `openclaw --version` exited 127 with `openclaw: command not found`.
  - The full path `<isolated-home>/.openclaw/bin/openclaw --version` printed `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`.
- **After** (`0b4d5d0` plus this change, new isolated HOME):
  - The install exited 0. Between the two existing lines, the summary printed the PATH lines and the full-path next step.
  - In a new login shell, `command -v openclaw` still found nothing before any change, and the printed full-path command with `onboard --help` worked.
  - After running the printed `export` line exactly as shown, `command -v openclaw` resolved to `<isolated-home>/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` and `openclaw --version` printed `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`.
  - A fresh login shell that did not run that line still did not find `openclaw`, as expected: the installer does not add this directory to startup files.
- **Rerun on that same HOME with its `bin` directory already on PATH** (the installer's reinstall path, same version): exit 0; the output ended with exactly the original two lines, with no PATH lines and no next-step line; bare `openclaw --version` worked.
- **`--json` rerun on that HOME, with the original PATH (its `bin` directory not on PATH)**: exit 0; the JSON events still ended with `{"event":"done","ok":true,…}`, and neither stdout nor stderr contained any PATH hint text, so the change adds nothing to `--json` output.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output (before and after)</summary>

The isolated HOME path is replaced with `<isolated-home>`; the before and after installs each used their own isolated HOME. `stderr:` labels lines written to stderr, and the `bash -c` script-name prefix on the "command not found" line is omitted.

Before (`0b4d5d0`), installer stdout:

```text

Installing OpenClaw (2026.11.6)...

added 361 packages in 11s
```

Before, new login shell:

After (`0b4d5d0` plus this change; the assembled `install-cli.sh` has sha256 `3253d70626d0e0d4fc9c23d733ef95a19005c5cf3a980d8ca2a379313040e724`), end of installer stdout:

- A new table in `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts` runs the real `main` while fixture functions replace download, installation, and unrelated post-install work; the production PATH-summary code remains intact. It covers:

prs.title: fix: keep a stopped Twitch account offline when a late reply finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Twitch account is stopped or disabled while the agent is still writing a reply, the reply that finishes afterwards reconnects the bot to Twitch chat. It posts the reply from an account the operator just turned off and leaves an open chat connection that no later stop will close until the account is started and stopped again.

## User Impact

A stopped or disabled Twitch account stays offline. A reply that finishes after the stop is logged as undelivered with the existing "Please start the Twitch gateway first" message, the same message the Twitch outbound send path already gives for a stopped account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway stops an account by aborting the account task and running the plugin stop, which removes the account's chat manager while admitted replies are still allowed to finish. The reply delivery callback looked the manager up with the helper that creates one when it is missing, so the late reply published a fresh manager and opened a new chat client. The callback now uses the plain lookup that the outbound adapter already uses. #127103 established that a retiring manager must stay unpublished and that outbound delivery should report the missing manager until a replacement starts. This change applies that rule to the reply path.

## Evidence

A new test runs the real Twitch monitor and the real client manager registry against a fake chat socket. It admits one message, holds the reply open, stops the account in the Gateway order (abort, then the plugin stop that removes the manager), and then lets the reply finish.

Before the change the late reply was reported as sent (`expected { visibleReplySent: true } to deeply equal { visibleReplySent: false }`) and the registry held a new, connected manager. After the change the reply reports `visibleReplySent: false`, no second chat client is constructed, nothing is said in chat, and the registry stays empty.

<details>
<summary>Commands and results</summary>

Base: `5e7675ea08cd6ff6de5713e7d5a0dcf6c7a84332`

- `npx vitest run extensions/twitch/src/monitor.stop.test.ts` before the fix: 1 failed.
- Same command after the fix: 1 passed.
- `npx vitest run extensions/twitch` after the fix: 15 files, 144 tests passed. The existing delivery tests now resolve the mocked manager through the same lookup the monitor uses.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on the three changed files: clean.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: exit 0, no TypeScript errors.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` could not run on this host (git 2.34 lacks `cat-file -z`). The change adds 152 test lines.

</details>

Not tested: a live Gateway against real Twitch chat. The chat host is fixed to Twitch's servers in the plugin, so the stop and late reply sequence was exercised with the real monitor and registry and a fake chat socket.

prs.title: fix: agent Channels panel says no channels were found while the first read is still running
prs.body: Closes #147816 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the agent **Channels** panel says "No channels found." while its own button says "Refreshing…", because the load hint and the empty state were rendered from `snapshot` alone and never consulted the read that was still in flight. Both messages were also left standing under the error callout after a failed read, so a panel that had failed looked like a panel that was empty. ## User Impact The panel now describes one state at a time. While a read is in flight the section button is the only surface that says so, and after a failure the error callout is the only surface that says so. An operator no longer reads "Load channels to see live status." as an instruction to start a load that is already running, and no longer reads "No channels found." as a result the panel does not have yet. Empty and populated results are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made `renderAgentChannels` already received `loading` and `error`, but only `snapshot` and `entries` gated its two messages: ```ts !params.snapshot ? t("agents.channels.loadHint") : nothing // ignores loading/error entries.length === 0 ? empty(…) : rows // ignores loading/error ``` Both messages describe a settled, successful read, so both now require one. This is the same shape the sibling `renderAgentSkills` already uses for its own load hint (`!reportReady && !params.loading`), so the two panels now agree. Width of change: one file, one guard. No new i18n keys, no new state owner, no change to the channels store or its request lifecycle. ## Evidence Reproduced through the real Control UI with the repo's own mocked Gateway, at the viewport named in the report (1440 × 1100, dark, English). The two "before" captures hold the first `channels.status` response or reject it; the "after" captures are the same two scenarios against this branch. **Loading — the hint and the empty state no longer appear beside the button** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | **Failed read — neither message is stacked under the error** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | Rendered text per state, taken from the same runs: | State | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | read in flight | `refreshing=true loadHint=true empty=true` | `refreshing=true loadHint=false empty=false` | | read rejected | `error=true loadHint=true empty=true` | `error=true loadHint=false empty=false` | | settled empty | — | `empty=true` only | | settled populated | — | channel row present, no empty state | `ui/src/e2e/agent-channel-runtime-status.e2e.test.ts` gains two cases covering the in-flight and failed reads through the same mock-Gateway entry point, and the file's existing fixture is hoisted so all three cases share one Gateway surface. Checks run on this branch: | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `ui/src/pages/agents/view.test.ts` | 23 passed | | `tsgo` ui project | exit 0 | | `oxfmt --check` on both files | clean | | `ui:i18n:verify` | exit 0 | **Not run:** the `ui-e2e-bundled` Vitest project does not start in my environment — its runner stalls with no output before any test executes, for this file and for the pre-existing `agent-channel-runtime-status` file alike. The captures above therefore come from driving the same repository helpers (`startBundledControlUiE2eServer`, `installMockGateway`) and Chromium directly rather than through the Vitest wrapper. CI covers the shard.

prs.title: fix: let chat retry a stale subscription during approval replay
prs.body:
Related: #175915. The client-side retry in #175924 is already in place.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a newly created conversation can fail with “session approval replay unavailable” even though the Gateway detected a transient change and the chat could recover by retrying.

## User Impact

The existing chat retry can reopen the conversation without creating another session or resending a message. Permission denials still stop recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-replay catch replaces the existing typed stale-subscription response with a terminal generic error. After rolling back the provisional observer, let only the exact stale-subscription error reach the existing outer response handler. Other replay failures keep their current responses. No authorization check, retry policy, or UI code changes.

## Evidence

- The regression test checks the actual subscription handler for the original structured response and absence of a leaked provisional observer.
- The downstream image backport passed its [browser and Gateway verification](https://gitlab.com/xrow-public/helm-openclaw/-/merge_requests/309). That validates the pinned released image, not this upstream commit.
- All nine focused Gateway tests passed locally, including the new rollback and retry-response regression and the existing access-denial cases. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.

prs.title: fix(exec): background tasks appear stale during long runs
prs.body:
Related: #59719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long-running background `exec` tasks can be reported as stale after 30 minutes even while their process is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: task audit and status surfaces keep showing active detached commands as live until they actually finish, fail, time out, or are cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background exec task records currently write `lastEventAt` only when created and finalized. This adds a 60-second, unref'd liveness heartbeat through the existing public task-progress writer. The timer is cleared before terminal finalization, and heartbeat write failures are warning-only so they cannot fail the underlying command.

## Evidence

- Current-main focused regression: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-task-tracking.test.ts` — 10/10 passed.
- Local seam coverage: exec task tracking + process E2E — 24/24 passed.
- `oxfmt` clean for both changed files.
- `oxlint` clean for both changed files.
- Added fake-timer coverage proving one heartbeat is recorded while live and no further heartbeat occurs after finalization.

No UI changes.

prs.title: fix: recover complete JSON records from noisy tool output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in JSON record recovery can lose valid records after malformed warnings or terminal framing. Delimiters inside strings and control sequences must not end unrelated warnings, and discovery masks must not invent valid JSON.

## User Impact

Strict recovery admits the original JSON bytes and returns original UTF-16 offsets. Default extraction and the existing prefix API retain their behavior. This prerequisite does not enable the downstream diagnostic redactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Original JSON admission, lexical ownership, and record selection have separate responsibilities. Actual lexical exits retire their matcher context together; warning expiry removes only that warning's contribution. Accepted framing is atomic, while a span entered inside a genuine string remains part of that string. Only an eligible, emitted containing record suppresses its children; crossing records retain their own completion.

The terminal scanner reuses a failed-search frontier in its existing consumers, preserving complete-sequence matching. The prefix API remains separate from strict recovery. The latest correction addresses CI lint findings with checked stack invariants, equivalent control flow and preserved synchronous work instrumentation.

Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203266. No compatibility, timeout, performance-budget, or CI exception is requested.

## Evidence

- Signed candidate `c9392c99228481444c6fc0ca8dff3774e0932851`, tree `5b810574d6d70371eb99ac359430c6b3ee9b398e`, against `dae3d844a0c76a91df1a543538ae959abf83ed57`.
- Independent corrected-candidate source assessment is clear for draft proof. The fresh applicable native lint-correction review completed 1/1 assignment with zero findings. All seven changed files were supplied whole; prior full-candidate evidence covers the unchanged contracts. This is not a new combined full-range automated verdict. The request to require discovery-view closing bytes remains rejected because discovery selects openers while original bytes own boundaries; explicit opaque spans control visibility.
- Targeted formatting, exact test allocation, diff and privacy checks passed. The lint correction passed 7,782 dependency-free before/after comparisons and independent source checks. These are not Vitest or typed-lint proof. A local Oxlint 1.89.0 check stopped during config loading because `eslint-plugin-solid` is absent; no local lint pass is claimed.
- **Current-head hosted proof:** run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44975653721 checked out this candidate through merge `afb58204903a308b362fe5997aa427299f4e997c` against the recorded stack base. The three changed test files passed all 100 parser cases, 21 admission/work cases and 50 terminal cases under each of Node 24.22.1 and Bun 1.4.4, with zero skips in those files. The surrounding 35-file cohort passed 708 tests with one unrelated skip in each runtime (job 137065287497).
- Typed Oxlint, production types and test types passed on this candidate. The package-test type graph completed 6/6 graph and 1/1 root units. The UI performance comparison passed: Chat and New Session each grew 3 gzip bytes; startup JS was unchanged; total CSS fell 3 gzip bytes. Existing absolute CSS-budget warnings are not represented as cleared.
- Build-artifacts job 137065286451 passed: package builds, SDK declaration generation/export checks, CLI bootstrap checks, Control UI build and deployment tests, Node/Bun CLI smoke checks, startup-memory checks and plugin-singleton smoke. The selected TUI check passed one case with eleven skips; this is not full TUI coverage or a full application/release declaration build.

prs.title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Studio benchmark:** Chat matched the first person mention. New Session still falls short of p95 parity (77.28 vs 71.63 ms across 50 matched observations per variant). The current CI and existing asset budgets passed; the performance gap is open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Performance acceptance for this landing

Use production builds and alternate samples on the same host. The known-good reference is `491c2944` (merged person mentions); keep an identical-reference control and the previous skill head `0283e5b6`. Collect at least 10 paired Chromium samples per route, cold and warm separately, and record renderer CPU median/p95, structural work counts and request/asset sizes.

Chat and New Session must stay native for a long unrelated draft containing `$HOME`, with zero whole-draft skill scans on subsequent unrelated typing. In rich mode one ordinary key after a 64 or 128 KiB word must not require work proportional to the word. Confirm exact `$command_name` output, late catalog changes, Markdown/escaped text, cursor, undo and chip selection.

Person-only typing, selection, undo, mixed typing and large paste must stay within the identical-reference sample spread, with no repeatable regression in median or p95. Time cold first skill from the first `$` through selection and an interactive editor; compare with the analogous first person mention and the old skill head. Validate the real Gateway flow as well as the repeatable benchmark. Enforce the startup asset gate without raising the limits.

## Evidence

### Studio qualification of the final product tree

Paired production Chromium, renderer CPU in ms, synthetic Gateway for timings, with identical baseline as a control. Kept the original tails. Repeated five scenarios whose original runs overlapped other validation.

| First use | Known-good person mention | Candidate skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chat, 10 pairs | 84.50 / 88.26 | 84.25 / 86.96 |
| New Session, all 50 pairs | 68.95 / 71.63 | 67.63 / 77.28 |
| New Session, 20 pairs | 69.25 / 71.63 | 67.83 / 104.45 |
| New Session confirmation alone, 10 pairs | 69.62 / 72.99 | 68.53 / 72.21 |

Values are median / p95. New Session originally had two higher samples (104.45 and 117.36 ms); neither recurred in the ten untraced confirmation pairs or the separate trace. The cause is unconfirmed, so this does not claim full p95 parity. The following 30 untraced pairs retained the earlier observations and produced no candidate samples above 77.28 ms. The 50-pair identical person-mention control was 68.43 / 73.93 ms. A local matcher experiment removed 400 name normalizations on the first dollar with 200 skills, but the measured paired median improved only 0.91 ms, within control variation; that experiment is not part of this PR. For ordinary typing, undo and mixed paste, differences were within the matched run's variation.

- An unrelated 69,014-character draft stayed native. Skill scans over 12 unrelated keystrokes fell from 38 to zero in Chat and 27 to zero in New Session. The rich editor reads four old document positions after an ordinary key, down from 65,540 in the long-word case.
- An isolated real Gateway and production Chromium accepted exact skill references in both routes. Chat also demonstrated downstream expansion. The bundled Chat E2E checks handoff and the raw payload for two skills; the 390 px New Session E2E and 12 focused Chromium tests passed after consolidating duplicate coverage.
- The paired build against main passed the existing asset limits: Chat −10 B gzip, New Session +372 B gzip, no new startup requests. The test-only follow-up removed 97 counted lines and passes the exact CI ratchet with 34 lines to spare.


### Current candidate

- Signed head \`86339fea5f6d65f5b3eb4c5e61eeee3fee5fb027\` matches the production build verified in Chromium against an isolated real Gateway on Chat and New Session. Raw \`$HOME\` stays native; person avatar selection and undo still work; the installed skill was copied and accepted by the Gateway as the exact raw reference. The test model endpoint was local; explicit expansion was verified in Chat only.
- On the 69,014-character literal-dollar draft, twelve unrelated keys caused 38 → 0 full lexical scans in Chat and 27 → 0 in New Session. One rich edit after a 65,536-character word went from 65,540 → 4 document reads; the revised count stayed 4 at 32,768 and 131,072 characters.
- The current-main merge build passes all asset budgets without changing limits. JavaScript request counts stayed 21 for Chat and 17 for New Session. Gzip change: Chat −10 B, New Session +372 B, largest JavaScript asset +430 B. The older budget evidence below refers to its pinned historical base.
- Late catalog, token boundary and Markdown coverage passed in Chromium. A trusted browser case also proves the fast path invalidates correctly when a controlled writer changes earlier text to a known skill without changing the draft length. Typechecks, focused lint and independent P2 review passed.

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

The existing inspected visual evidence is retained; this repair changes computation and correctness, not the chip design. Captures use the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; mobile is an emulated 390px viewport.

Before — implementation baseline (`491c2944`):

![Before: raw skill references](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c4e4c3-1f4d-46fa-8017-bcb02d634e13)

After — highlighted skill names and icons:

![After: highlighted skill references](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4de3ea02-abd4-4fb9-b1c0-4f0f5c6b3fb8)

<details>
<summary>New Session at an emulated mobile width</summary>

![New Session skill references at 390px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/209f61df-ec7c-476b-bdce-3dd520544a58)

</details>

Requested and designed with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/124475c8-50a5-40d7-876f-139275c99a14)

prs.title: fix: keep links whole when a long reply is split into messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a long reply is split into several channel messages, the split can land on a space inside a link. On Slack, a native link such as `<https://example.com/a/b|the docs>` that straddles the split arrives as literal text: the first message ends with `<https://example.com/a/b|the` and the next one starts with `docs>`. The same happens to a mention token with a space in its label. For a regular Markdown link such as `[the release notes page](https://...)`, Slack and Telegram users get two links in two messages, one labelled "the release notes" and one labelled "page".

## User Impact

Links and mention tokens near a message split stay whole and clickable. The split moves to the space before the link whenever that space fits in the message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared splitter already prefers breaks outside parentheses and keeps a `<...>` token together when it measures a candidate chunk. The first split pass ignored link labels and `<...>` tokens, so it picked the last space in the window even when that space was inside one. This change treats spaces inside a link label or a `<...>` token like spaces inside parentheses. A break outside them wins, and a break inside them is still used when the window has no other choice, so every chunk stays within the limit.

One existing Slack test pinned the old split of `beta beta <@U1|some one> <https://x|a b> x` at limit 23, which delivered `<@U1|some ` and `one>`. It now expects `beta beta `, `<@U1|some one> `, `<https://x|a b> x`.

## Evidence

Behavior checked on this branch against `main` at `85444ce1827`.

- Slack, limit 4000, one token moved across 70 positions around the split. Damaged splits on `main` then on this branch: Markdown link split into two links 20 then 0; native `<url|label>` link turned into escaped text 2 then 0; `<@U0123ABCDEF>` 0 then 0. No chunk exceeded 4000 in either run.
- Telegram, limit 4000, the same Markdown link sweep: link split into two anchors in 18 of 70 positions on `main`, 0 on this branch.
- Differential run of the splitter on `main` and on this branch over 24,000 random Markdown inputs (three seeds): output is identical for every input without a link or `<...>` token. Inputs with one changed in 885, 918 and 905 cases. No chunk exceeded its limit and no source text was lost.
- Timing of Telegram chunking for a 387,379-character reply with 1,600 links: 1718 ms on `main`, 1669 ms on this branch (one run each). Scaling stays linear from 45k to 387k characters.
- New tests fail on `main` and pass here: `breaks before a link label or angle token that does not fit` in `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` and `keeps a native link whole when a long reply splits next to it` in the Slack format tests.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
npx vitest run packages/markdown-core/src/render-aware-chunking.test.ts extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts
# main: 3 failed | 92 passed. This branch: 95 passed.

npx vitest run packages/markdown-core/src extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format extensions/signal/src extensions/googlechat/src extensions/whatsapp/src extensions/sms/src src/plugin-sdk
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <changed files>
node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <changed files>
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:extensions
```

On this host, 22 Signal UNIX socket tests and 4 WhatsApp inbox tests fail on `main` as well (socket and database worker setup under a group-writable parent directory). Three plugin-sdk lock and filesystem test files (4 tests) also fail on `main` here. The same tests fail with and without this change. `memory-host-events.test.ts` failed once in the full parallel run and passed on its own on this branch (11 of 11).

</details>

Not tested: a live Slack or Telegram workspace. The proof runs the real channel formatters (`markdownToSlackMrkdwnChunks`, `markdownToTelegramHtmlChunks`) without sending messages.

prs.title: fix(gateway): give published pull requests a real title when none is supplied
prs.body:
Related: [#202982](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202982), which fixed the duplicate pull request from the same incident and left this default out as a separate decision.

## What Problem This Solves

When you publish a session's work and nobody names a title, the pull request is opened as `Publish openclaw/<branch>` with the body "Published by the Gateway after authoritative workspace reconciliation." **Publish** in the Control UI never sends a title, and an agent calling `github_publish` may omit it. A search of this repository finds 32 pull requests with that placeholder title, 27 of them opened since 2026-11-01. Reviewers cannot tell what those pull requests do without opening them.

## User Impact

A pull request published without a title or body now takes them from the first commit its branch adds to the base, the same choice as `gh pr create --fill-first`. Of the 32 placeholder pull requests above, 29 had such a commit (26 of the 27 since 2026-11-01); for example `Publish openclaw/dawn-crab` would have been "fix(plugins): preserve completion authority after producer release".

What does not change:

- A title or body supplied in the request is used as before.
- Publishing again to an existing pull request never edits its title or body.
- The publication commit keeps its subject: the requested title, or `Publish <branch>`.
- A branch with no commit of its own is still titled `Publish <branch>`. That covers uncommitted-only work and repository checkpoint publications from cloud sessions, which have no local history to read. See the open decision below.

No config option, protocol change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The placeholder dates from the first publication broker ([#126306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126306)), where the request title doubled as the publication commit subject and the branch name filled in when the Control UI sent none. It was never a decision about pull request titles.

The first commit is the one fact the publisher already holds that describes the work and is already public: it is pushed with the branch. Trailers are left out of the body because the pull request states its own credit. The read is best effort and bounded to the limits a requested title and body must meet, so a default can never fail a publication.

Alternatives not taken:

- **Refuse an agent publish without a title.** It adds a failure to a path that can now succeed with a real title, and would not help the Control UI.
- **Use the session title.** A session title can come from a private conversation, and the publisher deliberately discloses the session link only for publicly shared sessions. Putting the title on a public pull request is a disclosure decision for a maintainer, not a default to slip in.
- **Add a title field to the Control UI publish flow.** A product change; it is the natural answer for the remaining commit-less case.

Open decision for a maintainer: what titles a pull request whose branch has no commit of its own. This PR keeps `Publish <branch>` there.

## Evidence

**Behavior, through the real request path.** The local-checkout cases in `src/gateway/github-publication-session-access.test.ts` send `sessions.github.publish` through the Gateway request handler against a real Git checkout, with no title or body. They now assert what the pull request is created with and what the publication commit is called.

- On the base (`8a6f2dd62d2`) the 8 cases that publish fail: the pull request title is `Publish openclaw/first-publication-<id>` where the task's commit subject is expected.
- With this change the file passes (27 tests): the title is the first commit's subject, the body is that commit's body without its `Reviewed-by` trailer, and the publication commit subject is still `Publish openclaw/...`.

**Focused proof on a Blacksmith Testbox** (`ci-check-focused-testbox.yml`, final tree):

- 41 test files passed: every `github-publication*`, `github-personal-publication*`, `github-repository-publication*` and `github-pr-workspace-preparation*` suite, the `github_publish` tool test and the prompt prefix stability test.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed for lint, format, core typecheck, dead-export scan, import cycles and the line-cap ratchets. Its test typecheck caught one more test caller of the content owner (`github-user-identity.enterprise.test.ts`); after that two-line update, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, that test file, the boundary test and lint passed.

**Local review.** Autoreview (shared helper, Codex engine), local mode, base `8a6f2dd62d2` to the working tree, priority P0 to P2: scoped-clean, no findings. It ran before the two-line test caller update above, which changes no production code. This is self-reported.

**Size.** Production: +77 / -12 across the content owner and both executors; the first-commit read lives in the content owner, and the executor's own line count does not grow. Tests: +12 / -2. Docs: +2.

**Where the 32 comes from.** `ghx pr list --state all --search '"Publish openclaw/" in:title'`, then the first non-merge, non-publication commit of each pull request.

**Gaps.**

- Not exercised against GitHub itself: doing so would open a real pull request. The test uses real Git and a stubbed GitHub API.
- The Control UI is unchanged, so there are no screenshots.
- Hosted CI has not run on this head; most jobs skip while the PR is a draft.
- Accepted edge: a first commit that mentions `@someone` in its body now carries that mention into the pull request body, as `gh pr create --fill-first` does.

prs.title: fix: let guests file GitHub issues from project conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A guest can ask an agent to file a GitHub issue in the project they are working on, but the Gateway's GitHub tool only handles pull requests. Even a guest with write access to their conversation has no issue-filing action to use.

## User Impact

User impact: a guest can ask the agent to file an issue in their own conversation’s registered public repository and get the issue URL back. No worktree, PR, or GitHub credentials in the sandbox are required. A read-only guest cannot file, and a conversation without a registered project does not guess a destination.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add one action to the existing GitHub tool, not another credential path. The Gateway derives the destination from the registered project, checks current requester access, and submits the title and optional body as the selected publisher. It does not retry a write whose result is unknown.

## Evidence

The previous production validator rejected a valid `create_issue` request. The new validator accepts it and rejects a caller-supplied repository. Four isolated Gateway integration tests exercised the real tool-to-Gateway dispatch, including allowed filing without a worktree, denial after a project goes private, and a lost response without a second POST. The protocol, tool, and prompt-stability suites, core typecheck, targeted lint/format, and Gateway protocol package build passed.

GitHub responses in those tests were simulated. Live guest-to-GitHub acceptance has not been demonstrated, and this PR does not deploy the change. Local P0/P1 autoreview could not start its reviewer inside read-only isolation, so no independent local review result is claimed.

[Hosted review of `95550fa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203369#issuecomment-7071915945) reported no findings. The [failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44967920114/job/137041591502) expected the formerly active synthetic name `OPENCLAW_E2E_HOOK_SOURCE_OLD` after reload and received `[]` at `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts:524:69`. I ran the same test file in a clean, detached checkout of the branch base `5d249c0e836fe407b21f1e15518808776ffdfc9c` with independent frozen dependencies and one worker. The same assertion failed at the same line; the other two cases passed. This reproduces the failure without the issue-filing change. The required CI gate is still red.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4be480e2-b217-4798-871a-e9fd64fc329c)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Maintainer verification

The issue action now holds the current project registration through dispatch, rechecks public eligibility for guests, and confirms the same conversation, requester, host, and selected GitHub account before submitting. A regression verifies that removing the registration before dispatch sends no issue request. 22 focused Gateway tests, typed lint, test typecheck and independent P2 review passed. GitHub responses were simulated; no public issues were created.

<!-- openclaw-publication:2ea88a17-80f1-417a-a604-0b7ff5ce6b14 -->

### CI attribution

The [exec-approval job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44973399121/job/137058364378) is the sole failing job. The same hook-source assertion reproduces on the exact main parent; the job's two teardown messages share the shutdown error recorded before this PR in [#200148](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200148). The checked hook, environment and supervisor files are unchanged. Security, the session-identity check, both Android Access lanes and the focused GitHub issue tests passed. No real issue was filed.

prs.title: fix: let an updated Mac app move its Gateway to the new version instead of quitting
prs.body:
Root cause: after an in-place update, `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.run` (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.swift:15`, merge base 08f45d611b7d) stops the previous build's service, runs the bundled `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive`, and only then installs this build's service. Every CLI run reads the installed LaunchAgent (`src/cli/run-main.ts:844`, `src/cli/run-main-service-installation.ts:114`), running or not. The stopped service still names the older package, so Doctor's preflight (`src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts:467`) refuses the pending schema migration with "Refusing a forward database schema migration: this CLI is X but the Gateway service runs Y". The app then restores the old service and quits. The replacement from #187000 was proven with a same-version candidate, so its proof never reached this guard.

Fixes #203065

Thanks @skrubbb for the report, @Speculorum9 for the update timeline that showed the stop, the refusal and the restart in order, and @BObereder for another affected install.

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw.app updates itself and the new version also upgrades the stored state schema, the app cannot move its own bundled Gateway to the new version. It stops the old Gateway, the credential step refuses to migrate because the old service is still installed, and the app puts the old Gateway back and quits with a credential recovery error. Every relaunch repeats this, so the Gateway stays on the previous version (for example 2026.11.4 under a 2026.11.5 app).

## User Impact

User impact: after an app update that changes the state schema, the app migrates the state, installs its new Gateway and keeps running. A separately installed newer CLI, such as a global npm install, still refuses to migrate state that an older Gateway service needs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app already knows which service it just stopped. It now passes that service's entrypoint to the Doctor run in `OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT`. The CLI stops treating the installed service as an older owner of the state only when that path resolves to the same file the LaunchAgent runs. With no value or a different path, the refusal added in #186971 stays as it is, so ordinary and flag-only Doctor runs still refuse. The app sets the variable only on the replacement's Doctor child and removes any inherited value on the normal startup path. Doctor still has to take the state lease, which a running Gateway holds.

Not changed: the in-app Retry setup repair still runs a plain `doctor --fix`. The app quits during credential startup in this failure, so Retry setup is not reachable here, but it would still refuse if it ran while an older service is installed.

## Evidence

- Real CLI run from source on macOS, in an isolated home with a LaunchAgent for a 2026.7.1 package and a state database one schema version behind (40; this CLI supports 41). Command: `OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT=<stale package>/openclaw.mjs node --import tsx src/entry.ts doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive`.
  - Before (merge base): "Refusing a forward database schema migration: this CLI is 2026.11.6 but the Gateway service runs 2026.7.1 from <stale package>". The state stays at schema 40.
  - After: the migration runs and the state is at schema 41.
  - Controls on this branch: no variable, or the entrypoint of a different 2026.7.1 package, still refuse and leave the state at 40.
  - Doctor then stops at "Client credential migration is incomplete or stale" in this synthetic home. The same database with no service installed stops the same way, so that comes from the hand-made fixture and not from the service check.
- Regression test in `src/cli/run-main-service-installation.test.ts` writes a real LaunchAgent for an older package and checks the migration guard with no name, a different entrypoint and the stopped entrypoint. It fails on the merge base, where the stopped entrypoint is still refused, and passes here. The file passes 9/9.
- Adjacent suites: `src/cli/worker-policy-regression-service-installation.test.ts` and `src/cli/gateway-cli/systemd-activation.test.ts` pass 31/31; `src/commands/startup-client-credentials.test.ts` and `src/commands/doctor-systemd-activation.test.ts` pass 29 with 2 skipped. In `src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.test.ts` the four "protects older service state" cases pass (ordinary and flag-only Doctor still refuse). Ten backup and SIGINT tests in that file failed locally on state-lock and backup errors; the file does not import the changed module, so CI is the reference for them.
- Swift: the replacement tests now check that credential preparation receives the stopped service's entrypoint and that `replacing(...)` takes it from the installed LaunchAgent. A new `ClientCredentialStartup` test checks that the Doctor child gets the variable only when one is passed, and that an inherited value is dropped. I could not build the macOS package locally, so these depend on CI.
- oxfmt and type-aware oxlint are clean on the touched TypeScript files, and `git diff --check` is clean. A direct core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`) reported only 713 declaration-emit diagnostics (TS2883, TS4023, TS4058, TS4078, TS4094) caused by my local dependency layout, none in touched files.

Merge danger: two-way door. The app and its bundled CLI ship together, and the CLI only acts on the variable when it names the installed service's exact entrypoint, so a revert brings back today's refusal. If it were wrong, the blast radius is the Mac app's in-place update of its own Gateway: state could be migrated before the new service installs, and the existing post-update check retries that install.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the right-docked Home actions clear of the window controls
prs.body:
Root cause: ui/src/styles/assistant-panel.css:34 places the right-docked Home panel at `top: var(--shell-topbar-height, 0)`, which is 0 on desktop, so its header shares the window's top-right corner with the caption buttons the Linux/Windows desktop shell draws there (apps/linux/ui/window-chrome.css:12-16, 138px x 52px).

Fixes #162448

Thanks @lanesawyer for the report and screenshot, and @AyhamJo7 for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux and Windows desktop windows the caption buttons (minimize, maximize, close) are drawn over the top-right corner. The right-docked Home panel starts at the top of the window, so its three header actions (open Home, dock, close) sit underneath those buttons: the glyphs overlap and the caption buttons receive the clicks.

## User Impact

The Home panel's actions can be used again when it is docked on the right. Panels docked at the bottom, macOS, fullscreen windows and plain browsers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The right-docked panel now starts below the caption strip when the shell publishes a nonzero `--openclaw-native-window-controls-width`. It is offset by `--openclaw-native-titlebar-height`, and the header keeps its full width. The shell sets that width to 138px on Linux and Windows and to 0 on macOS and in fullscreen (apps/linux/ui/window-chrome.css:3, 7-8, 80-81). Plain browsers set neither variable, so those layouts keep `top` at the existing topbar height. No new variable.

An earlier version reserved the caption width as trailing header padding, as the page toolbar does. At the dock's 320px minimum width, that left the Home and Ask tabs overlapping the actions, so it was replaced. The fixed panel's no-op `min-width/min-height: 0` is dropped to keep the stylesheet inside the CSS size cap.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and Control UI (isolated state, Chromium, 1280x900), Home docked right. The desktop shell is emulated the way `window-chrome.js` does it on a dashboard (root classes, `data-native-platform`, and the shell's own `window-chrome.css`), with a red box of `--openclaw-native-window-controls-width` x titlebar height at the top-right standing in for the caption buttons. Base is `c2e7b54ab`, after is `ac57af08a2`.

- Before (base `c2e7b54ab`, 440px and 320px): all three actions (x 1184, 1214, 1244) sit inside the caption area (x 1142-1280, y 0-52), and trial clicks are intercepted.
- After (`64b95c339f`): the panel starts at y=52, actions at y=63.5, and trial clicks reach the buttons at both widths. At 320px the title ends at x=1132.7, before the first action at 1184.
- Unchanged at both widths: macOS width 0, fullscreen width 0, plain browser, bottom dock.
- The regression opens the dock at 320px; it fails on base and passes here. The titlebar suite passes 10/10.
- Control UI CSS: +49 B raw, +20 B gzip.

Screenshots and the measured boxes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202733#issuecomment-7070712972 (final head at 440px and 320px: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202733#issuecomment-7071406079)

Merge danger: two-way door, CSS only; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: the right-docked Home panel header on Linux and Windows desktop windows.

prs.title: fix(meetings): keep tool-free replies separate from requester chats
prs.body:
Related: #182956

## What Problem This Solves

An agent-mode meeting configured with `realtime.toolPolicy: "none"` still forks the requesting chat's history. Switching an existing meeting consult to that policy can also reopen its previously forked transcript, rather than starting from the supplied meeting conversation.

## User Impact

Meeting replies under this policy no longer inherit unrelated requester-chat history. Other tool policies keep their existing context behavior, and existing transcripts are left intact.

This separates requester history, not all agent context: configured workspace instructions still apply. Use a separate agent when a meeting needs a different workspace audience. This does not activate a live call or implement OAuth transcription.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing isolated consult mode and give these consults a distinct, stable per-meeting session key so an old fork is not resumed. The shared runtime continues owning requester lineage, delivery, model locks, sandbox policy, and memory audience. No new configuration option, authorization protocol, or state store is introduced.

The meeting binding's runtime input now names only the `agent` capability it actually consumes, allowing the real-runtime regression fixture to remain structurally typed.

OAuth transcription is already proposed in #162757, and native tool-free consultation support is proposed in #182956. This PR deliberately does not duplicate either change or claim to solve workspace/bootstrap or tool-catalog isolation.

## Evidence

- The base regression reproduced reuse of a seeded, previously forked consult transcript. The fixed path uses a clean child, retains the meeting question and requester lineage, preserves the old transcript, and resolves the existing native conversation-scoped memory audience.
- Final local verification: **43 tests passed** across meeting bindings (6), meeting shutdown/cancellation (12), real SQLite consult storage and audience handling (9), and prompt/tool-prefix stability (16). The wrapper completed all three selected Vitest shards in 44.27 seconds; the storage suite reported 15.24 seconds and the new storage regression 1.668 seconds.
- Production and affected-test typechecks, targeted lint, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review against base `e566e993323385ce5c2ed64cffeecd4bd2ab07bb` found no actionable issues; a final formatter-only adjustment followed review. The change reuses existing owners and removes no supported context behavior from the other policies.
- Tests use synthetic data and stub the final embedded model dispatch; storage, session preparation, and memory-audience resolution run through their real owners. No live Gateway, provider credential, or meeting was changed. Live audio, remote hearing, transcription authentication, and production deployment are not covered by this evidence.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts \
  src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts \
  src/meeting-bot/realtime-shutdown.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.other.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts \
  src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts \
  src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts
```

The sandboxed macOS storage run initially refused its own SQLite maintenance process, including in an unchanged baseline test. Normal host process access resolved that test-environment restriction; no database or test assertion was weakened.

</details>

prs.title: fix(onboard): stop pointing Funnel runs at token auth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reported in #201385 by an affected user with a natural reproduction.

`openclaw onboard --non-interactive --tailscale funnel` fails and tells the operator to rerun with `--gateway-auth token`. Following that advice fails the same way, because Funnel always switches the Gateway to password auth.

## User Impact

User impact: the Funnel rejection now names the password requirement instead of pointing at token auth, so the printed next step actually works.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyNonInteractiveGatewayConfig` forces `authMode = "password"` whenever `tailscaleMode === "funnel"` (`src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.ts:80-89`), then rejects with `"Missing --gateway-password for password auth. Pass --gateway-password or use --gateway-auth token."` (`:145-148`). For a Funnel run that second sentence is unreachable advice. The rejection is now Funnel-aware and points at `--gateway-password` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`.

Scope note: this changes the rejection text only. Funnel winning over an explicit token request is existing, tested behaviour (`keeps password auth when a token-only rerun targets an existing Funnel`), so this PR does not turn that override into an error.
