prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta for git installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reported in #201335 by an affected user with a natural reproduction.

Installing with `install.sh --install-method git --beta` still installs the latest stable release. The flag is accepted, nothing warns, and the ref that gets checked out is `latest` instead of `beta`.

## User Impact

User impact: `--beta` now installs the beta channel for git installs, the same way it already does for npm and Bun installs. Explicit versions and branches are unchanged, and a flag-selected `--beta` whose beta dist-tag is unavailable (e.g. no npm on a fresh host) falls back through latest resolution instead of failing to check out a nonexistent `beta` ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh`) builds its request from `OPENCLAW_VERSION` alone. `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1` (`scripts/install.sh`), and that flag is read by the npm and Bun engine paths — after the git ref was already resolved. The resolver now prefers the beta channel when `USE_BETA` is set and the request is a channel (`latest`/`next`/unset), keeping an explicit pin or branch authoritative. Because the git ref resolution precedes `ensure_node`, a fresh host without npm made the beta dist-tag lookup fail and returned the literal `beta`; flag-selected beta now falls back through latest resolution, while an explicit `--version beta` keeps its literal meaning.

Scope note: this PR covers the `--beta` half of #201335.

## Evidence

**Real registry + real checkout (base vs this head).** Channel selection is exercised without any stubbed npm: the installer read the public registry and checked out real upstream tags.

```
$ npm view openclaw dist-tags --json
{ "latest": "2026.11.6", "beta": "2026.11.10-beta.1", "extended-stable": "2026.10.33", "alpha": "1.10.0-alpha" }
```

The checkout target was a blobless clone of `github.com/openclaw/openclaw` (`--filter=blob:none`, the same form the installer uses), driven through `--git-dir`; `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` were isolated and a settings file plus a workspace marker existed before the runs and survived them.

Base (upstream main `416b357`), `--beta` on a git install — the flag is accepted but latest is installed:

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.6
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.6
```

This PR's head, same command, same registry, same checkout (an upgrade from latest-stable to beta):

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.10-beta.1
· Fetching requested version
· Checking out v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> status --porcelain | wc -l
0
$ cat "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
{ "gateway": { "mode": "local" }, "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "<isolated>/ws" } } }
```

Latest-stable baseline on the same checkout without `--beta` (this head): `Using git ref: v2026.11.6` → `Checking out v2026.11.6`, HEAD `v2026.11.6`.

**Missing-beta fallback (stubbed npm).** The public registry always publishes a `beta` dist-tag, so the fallback cannot be produced against it. That case keeps the stubbed-`npm` environment (controlled `dist-tags`, local git checkout with `v2026.11.5` and `v2026.11.6-beta.2`): base (policy before the fallback) prints the literal `beta` and the checkout fails, this head falls back to latest.

```
# base commit (policy before the fallback)
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: beta
# this PR's head
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.5
```

**Unit/regression coverage.** The `resolves the git install ref` cases in `test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts` source the real `scripts/install-policy.sh` in bash with a stubbed `installer_npm`, including the flag-selected beta fallback and the explicit-beta literal cases.

Base (policy change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts`:

```
× resolves the git install ref: --beta selects the beta tag
× resolves the git install ref: --beta without a requested version
AssertionError: expected 'v2026.11.5' to be 'v2026.11.6-beta.2'
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

```

复现: base(416b357) --beta → Using git ref: v2026.11.6；head → v2026.11.10-beta.1 且 HEAD 切到该 tag
证据类别: 真实 npm registry + 真实 GitHub 仓库 checkout，本机可得: 是（上述 transcript）
契约核对: git 安装的 ref 由 scripts/install-policy.sh 的 resolve_git_openclaw_ref 独占决定，调用点 scripts/install.sh:2997
风险: 1 生产脚本 + 1 测试；不跨层、不触碰状态机
```

Implemented with an AI coding agent (OpenClaw contributor workflow). All quoted output above is from runs on this machine; the settings file and workspace marker were created before the runs to show they survive the checkout.

prs.title: fix: count settled model tokens toward Goal budgets
prs.body:
Closes #203350

## What Problem This Solves

A built-in Goal could keep running past its token budget when its context size stayed flat or shrank. The budget counted growth in the conversation, not the model tokens used to do the work.

## User Impact

Budgeted built-in Goals now count tokens from settled turns and stop scheduling more work once the budget is reached. If the Goal cannot count settled usage, including after an unmetered CLI fallback, it records why pursuit stopped instead of assuming zero. This is a continuation limit, not a cap on the cost of an in-flight model call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing turn settlement records the token total for the Goal that was active at admission. Retries of the same settlement do not count twice. Existing Goals keep their recorded tally; no historical usage is backfilled. Unbudgeted Goal behavior and native Codex accounting are unchanged.

## Evidence

- On the base, the first 45,000-token settlement left the persisted Goal tally at zero. With the fix, three settlements at fixed context record 45,000, 90,000, and 135,000. An isolated Gateway with a loopback provider emitted exactly three model requests against a 100,000-token budget, with no fourth request.
- Focused checks cover measured zero versus missing usage, duplicate settlement across actor restart, built-in requester wake, CLI continuation, Goal Resume, and session display. The requester-wake Gateway E2E passed. Core and targeted test typechecks, lint, formatting, and docs checks passed.
- `pnpm build` passed on the source tree published at `9e04b58ae6e4`. It also printed non-blocking Control UI CSS size and chat boot request budget warnings.
- The first CI run found a duplicated Goal settlement identity check. The repair at `a742bc391e38` reuses the existing check and shrinks the allowlist from 20 to 16 pins for that file. The session-identity ratchet, lint, core typecheck, 85 continuation tests, and the rebuilt requester-wake Gateway E2E all passed locally on the repaired tree. A separate prior-head `check-guards` job never reached its checks because the runner could not resolve the Node download host.
- The two failing CI shards on `a742bc391e38` identified an absent-settlement crash in built-in harness tests and stale Goal-search expectations. Both reproduced locally. The repair at `7215efb0dc36` passed all 101 focused tests across built-in harness, session search, continuation, and the isolated Gateway cap proof. The session-identity ratchet, core and affected-test typechecks, lint, and format also passed.
- **Stable upgrade:** The published 2026.11.6 package (`06afb10`) created and settled three synthetic Goals in a disposable SQLite store. Candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the agent store from schema 38 to 43. The candidate preserved all three Goal IDs, objectives, creation times, statuses, recorded usage, and the 2,000-token budget. A fresh context increase did not alter old tallies. It now persists `usage_limited`, retains ordinary session counters without charging them to the Goal, and tells the operator how to resume. prs.title: fix: keep chat image generation working on text-only models
prs.body:
Closes #203374

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent with a text-only session model generates an image in a chat and no vision model can describe it, the image arrives but the agent's follow-up turn fails with "Image attachments could not be analyzed" and then retries forever ("Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input"). The chat session stays stuck until the Gateway restarts, so the agent keeps saying the picture is on its way, re-sends old images, and promises new ones that are never made.

## User Impact

User impact: chat image generation no longer gets the session stuck on a text-only model. When a vision model is configured, the agent still inspects its generated image (including `deliveryMode="review"` candidates) exactly as before; when no description can be produced, the turn continues and the agent is told it has not seen the image.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion turn that hands a generated image back to the agent attaches the file for inspection, so on a text-only model it goes through image understanding, which throws when no vision model returns a description. That throw is fatal for an ordinary user photo, but for an `image_generate` completion it wedges the delivery loop. For that one source, a missing description now degrades instead of throwing: the pixels stay out of the text-only turn and the message gains a short note telling the agent the image was not inspected and not to claim otherwise. Image understanding still runs first, so configured vision models keep working, and every other input (user photos, other inter-session sources, revoked authority) behaves as before.

## Evidence

- Focused tests in `agent-image-understanding.test.ts`: a generated-image completion is still described when a vision model is configured; with no vision provider or an empty description it continues with the uninspected note instead of throwing; undescribed images from another inter-session source still throw; revoked request authority still throws for a generated-image completion. All tests in that file and in `agent-run-media.test.ts` pass, and removing the degrade branch makes the two new degrade cases fail (mutation-checked).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.

This revision was then run as a separate, channel-less Gateway (own state dir and port) built from this branch, with the same text-only session model and `imageModel` and a real ComfyUI image provider: the agent called `image_generate` in a session, the image finished in 13 s, image understanding failed as expected (`Model does not support images`), and the completion turn still finished normally (`stopReason=stop`) 5 s later with no announce failure. The agent replied "Done - the image of a red apple on a wooden table has been generated and sent.", describing only what it requested and not claiming to have seen the result.

prs.title: fix: keep FaceTime playback open after interruptions
prs.body:
Related: #202916

## What Problem This Solves

A FaceTime response can start sending audio immediately after an interruption. On macOS, Bun can give SoX a socket for stdin. SoX 14.4.2 can read the queued byte count as the entire input length, play only the first chunk, and exit successfully. The FaceTime bridge treats the early exit as a playback failure.

## User Impact

The replacement playback stream can accept the rest of the response when audio arrives immediately after an interruption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use SoX's pipe input with a fixed system command so its raw reader receives an anonymous pipe. The playback pump closes retired stdin before killing SoX so the relay can exit even when it is waiting for input. The native capture path keeps its existing shutdown handshake.

## Evidence

The playback boundary is verified on Apple silicon macOS 26.6.2 with SoX 14.4.2 built from the verified source archive and OpenClaw's pinned Bun. A live call with the actual FaceTime carrier and Core Audio device remains a separate manual verification item.

| Production playback pump after `clearOutputAudio()` | Exited before the fixture closed stdin | Bytes received by real SoX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base `5a3e6b1cb` | Yes | 15,360 of 120,360 |
| Patch `544eb6cce` | No | 120,360 of 120,360, byte-identical |

The fixture used synthetic PCM and redirected the device sink to a raw file. A short test-only producer/consumer ordering delay made the first chunk arrive before SoX opened stdin. A separate macOS probe confirmed the socket reported 15,360 queued bytes as its file size. A warmed-relay teardown probe confirmed the relay exited after stdin closure and SoX termination.

- The two touched playback lifecycle cases failed on the base. The full FaceTime suite passed on the patch (212 tests across 26 files), and the real-SoX boundary probe passed separately. The native helper fixture used the macOS Command Line Tools SDK for its ad-hoc signing test.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, targeted lint and format checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Bash syntax checks and the FaceTime package dry run also passed.
- An independent local review of the two-file change found no actionable issues. Hosted CI and complete call validation remain pending.

Thanks to `withlightsg` for isolating the reproduction and providing the byte-count control.

prs.title: fix: stop skills list ending with a failed-refresh warning
prs.body:
Closes #202990

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw skills list` succeeds but ends with `[skills] passive skills refresh failed: WorkerTaskError: worker task pool closed`. Every run prints it, so a plain read looks like a failure.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw skills list` and other short commands that touch Skills no longer end with a failure message. A passive refresh that fails while discovery is running, for any other reason, is still logged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command exits and retires the Skills worker while a watcher-triggered passive refresh is still running, so the worker pool rejects it. The timer callback logged every rejection as a warning. `closeSkillsWatchers()` sets `state.closing` while it retires the pool, so the callback now stays quiet when discovery is closing.

I did not find out what triggers the directory-change event during a read-only command. This change only affects how the interrupted refresh is reported.

## Evidence

Scenario: `openclaw skills list` run from source with `pnpm openclaw`, against an empty config and a clean state directory, six times in a row on each commit. Base is `32145db9a` and after is this PR's head `8f1fcafcf`.

Before, 6 of 6 runs end with:

```text
[skills] passive skills refresh failed: WorkerTaskError: worker task pool closed
```

After, 0 of 6 runs print it, and the listing and exit code are the same.

- New test `does not warn when shutdown interrupts a passive refresh` in `refresh.shutdown.test.ts`. A directory change arms a passive scan, the pool is retired while the scan is held at its worker request, and the real pool then rejects it. On the base commit it fails with the message above; with this change it passes.
- `src/skills` passes (82 files passed and 2 skipped; 884 tests passed and 3 skipped). `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass.
- Not covered: Gateway shutdown and Windows.

prs.title: fix: keep automations running when Doctor moves shared accounts
prs.body:
Related: #200600 and #200653 (same refusal family, different migration path).

## What Problem This Solves

An automation using the legacy main/shared account store can stop after Doctor moves those credentials into central storage, reporting that its unchanged account was signed in again or replaced. Restarting does not restore the saved authorization.

## User Impact

Existing authorizations survive that one-time relocation without switching accounts. Actual account replacements, local overrides and missing lifetime history remain blocked. This is preventive: already-central stores keep their existing identities, and this change does not automatically rebind jobs broken by an earlier relocation.

**Verification boundary:** the requested scope is synthetic and offline. The real migration, persistence and authorization guard have been exercised, but not a full released-binary upgrade followed by Gateway/model execution. A native independent source review completed and its actionable finding was fixed. Subsequent canonical Auto Review attempts were interrupted by Gateway restarts without a terminal report; no clean helper-validated review is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The authorization owner currently includes physical database paths and credential lifetimes in its identity. Doctor now records the logical origin of an enrolled legacy shared store and retains only credential-free lifetime metadata at its old location. The authorization owner recognizes the migrated main/shared pair only while the local profile is absent and both lifetimes still match. It keeps observing the real physical owners and leaves the cron guard unchanged.

The origin is recorded separately from the existing location record, preserving that record's old-reader shape. Interrupted source cleanup preserves its original migration receipt. There is no account-rebinding sweep, operator setting, schema-version bump or credential fallback. Credential retirement and its metadata reduction are grouped under the migration owner to keep the orchestration module within the existing size limit; no size limit was raised. The credential-writer inventory follows the extracted cleanup’s two bounded SQL branches and permits only the original exclusive migration caller; it grants no file-wide exemption.

## Evidence

- Both new integration regressions fail on base `899f48ffc6933e10712a47a136b371cce755e88e` at the actual post-migration account guard, then pass with the fix. They cover main OAuth/API-key bindings, inherited OAuth, real refresh settlement, local override/removal, explicit replacement (including identical API-key bytes), symlinked state roots, interrupted finalization and missing metadata. Saved jobs remain unchanged.
- A synthetic job was captured and persisted through the real owners, migrated by `migrateSharedAuthStore`, and accepted with the **original authorization ID in a fresh process**. The copied shared credential/state JSON and timestamps were unchanged. The full twelve-phase offline matrix also passed replacement and missing-lifetime controls.
- Affected auth, relocation, cron and Doctor suites passed: 89 tests across six files before the final helper extraction; the final two regressions and seven affected relocation cases were rechecked afterward. Final production/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Native independent review found one P2: a cold API-key-only shared write could cache ownership without the origin. This was reproduced at the real guard and fixed in the bootstrap worker and receipt adapter. The committed test now starts two fresh Node processes: the first writes an unrelated profile before acquiring all original bindings, and the next reloads and acquires them again. All 23 tests in the four affected bootstrap/cron/path suites passed after that repair.
- Follow-up CI repair: the exact cleanup writer and its sole maintenance caller are registered in the existing credential-writer guard. A new regression failed before registration and now rejects unrelated callers and additional writes. All 115 writer-guard tests, the full database-worker ratchet against the pinned base, scripts/tooling typechecks, targeted lint and formatting passed. A focused independent source review found no actionable issues. Runtime behavior is unchanged by this repair.
- No production state, real credential, login or hosted provider was used in these fixtures. This proves the reproduced defect, not the cause of the original reported incident.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, cost and proof boundaries</summary>

The committed regression is `src/cron/inference-binding.shared-migration.test.ts`:

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/inference-binding.shared-migration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

The final regression file passed both tests in 35.02 seconds within the affected-suite run (30.63 seconds of test execution). The complete four-file, 23-test run took 90.68 seconds wall time. The cost covers real SQLite ownership, Doctor migration and two fresh native processes; a warm helper test cannot prove cold-cache hydration. Storage and authorization are not mocked. The writer-guard suite passed 115 tests in 1.67 seconds (2.60 seconds wrapper wall time); its new regression covers the audited caller/sink boundary. Hosted CI is still pending for the latest head.

The separate-process rehearsal used synthetic state roots and blocked IP networking; only local Unix IPC was permitted. One parallel re-run failed before test startup with native-compiler process exhaustion (EAGAIN); the serialized final seed/migrate/reload sequence passed. No guard or resource limit was disabled.

Related #200653 repairs private upgrade-copy paths. This candidate preserves the distinct legacy shared-store relocation, including main's change from one physical authorization owner to two. It does not claim historical account recovery when the required lifetime evidence has already been lost.

</details>

Reported and reproduced with Vitor Cepeda Lopes.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/eef4c664-b63a-4562-a94c-501e2aeedc9b)

prs.title: fix(state): keep stalled lease work alive (needs maintainer acceptance)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A 57-second operator heap snapshot stalled the main thread while two `projects.clone` operations held 30-second state leases. Neither lease was taken over, but both owners declared their own leases lost and terminated their clones with SIGTERM. Users saw failed clones caused solely by the owner's stall.

## User Impact

This candidate lets a parent-timer lease recover once after missed renewals if the exact acquisition owner still holds the row. **Validation limits: CI failed on the initial head; the archive inventory was repaired locally, with one additional macOS provisioning timeout remaining. CI was not rerun.** A takeover, missing row, or failed recovery still loses the lease. **Draft: needs maintainer acceptance of the durable-expiry recovery semantics before readiness or merge.**

## Root cause and design

On base `f4f365140c10`, `src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts:122` creates a UUID owner per acquisition; `:149` schedules at leaseMs/3. `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.ts:130` schedules parent renewals, and `:137` immediately reports loss when the committed expiry has passed. Acquisition deletes an expired row and inserts the new owner in one transaction (`src/state/openclaw-state-lease-store.ts:71`).

Tracing the actual clone path exposed additional expiry requirements: the owner's admission calls `assertActive` (`src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts:226` on the base), actor renewal verifies unexpired ownership before SQL (`src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker.ts:233`), host admission requires unexpired renewal facts (`src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker-owner.ts:130`), and the store UPDATE has an expiry predicate (`src/state/openclaw-state-lease-store.ts:246`). The batched UPDATE in `openclaw-state-lease-renewal.worker.ts:80` serves the separate independent-worker heartbeat, not the clone's actor renewal.

The timer now joins any pending renewal and rereads the shared committed expiry. If none is pending, it issues exactly one explicitly named `recover` lifecycle request with `recoverExpired: true`. Only that request omits the old expiry requirement. Its UPDATE still matches `(scope, lease_key, owner)` inside the existing write transaction. Success logs one recovery warning with scope, key, overdueMs and attempts, then resumes the existing schedules. Failure retains the original expiry-message shape. There is no recovery retry loop or additional timer class.

The SQL option is a separate recovery variant of the existing store UPDATE: conditionally omit the expiry predicate only for recovery. A blanket predicate removal would broaden ordinary renewal contrary to the narrowed design. The existing batch statement, cadence, scopes and admission transport remain unchanged. The parent timer moved into `openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts` to keep the existing heartbeat file below its lint limit; the old export and callers were cut over together.

Off-thread scheduling does not solve the observed stall: native worker requests wait for host admission (`src/infra/sqlite-writer-admission-client.ts:90`), and the owner-context admission callbacks run on the host (`src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.ts:471`). Moving a timer cannot deliver those callbacks while the main thread is frozen.

## Failure-mode analysis

| Mode | Verdict and reclaim behavior | Code and proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Clock skew between writers/readers | Owner matching remains safe against reviving a different acquisition. This does **not** make arbitrary clock skew or multiple active hosts/Gateways safe: an ahead clock can take over early; a behind clock can delay takeover; a new expiry already past the observing clock still loses. PostgreSQL remote persistence is qualified for one Gateway, not active-active Gateways. No new distributed-clock guarantee is claimed. | Clock samples: `openclaw-state-lease-store.ts:69,231`; matching: `:244`; recovery result check: `openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts:119`. Existing native starvation and delayed assertion/result tests cover locally expired checks. Cross-host clock skew is not runtime-tested under the no-host constraint; unsupported active-active operation remains a validation limit. |
| (b) In-flight renewal and publication before reply | Safe: when renewal is pending the timer joins that exact promise; it does not issue recovery. It rereads the committed shared expiry after settlement. If publication already extended expiry before observation, it merely rearms expiry. Expiry is assigned `now + leaseMs`, not added to the previous expiry. No concurrent reclaim/double extension. | `openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts:44,100,112`; worker publication `openclaw-state-lease-worker.ts:62`; store `:232`. Lifetime `pending-recovered` asserts no recovery call; async timer “joins renewal before sealing public methods after commit publication” covers published expiry with delayed reply. |
| (c) Takeover, takeover then release, third acquisition | Safe: acquisition owners are UUIDs per invocation; takeover transaction deletes the expired row and inserts the acquiring owner. The recovery UPDATE cannot match a successor; a deleted row affects zero rows; a third acquisition has a different token. Cleanup cannot delete a successor. | `openclaw-state-lease.ts:122`; store `:71,87,244`; release owner predicate in store. Real SQLite regression table covers `takeover`, `released`, and `reacquired` after a synchronous stall, retaining successor rows after old-owner cleanup. |
| (d) Frozen owner's child kept writing | Unchanged accepted limitation. Durable expiry does not stop a child while its parent is frozen. A competitor may acquire and start work during that interval. The old owner discovers loss on resume and aborts. Recovery supplies no fencing of already-running children or external effects. | Clone signal handed to child work: `src/projects/project-clone.ts:183`. Takeover regression proves the resumed parent loses; no test claims child-process fencing. |
| (e) Expiry used as an operation deadline | Consumer inspection found ownership/cancellation signals, not a fixed operation deadline based on leaseMs. Clone passes its separate `timeoutMs` to the operation. Ordinary effect/write/verify checks still require an unexpired lease. Direct native and independent-worker heartbeat modes keep their old renewal rules. A caller checking between resume and recovery still fails. | `openclaw-state-lease.ts:164`; clone `:183`; worktree cancellation composition `src/agents/worktrees/allocation.ts:227`; plugin lifecycle guards `src/plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.ts`; MCP OAuth and transcript consumers inspected. Existing delayed assert/result and lease-loss consumer tests retained. |
| (f) PostgreSQL versus SQLite | Same Kysely UPDATE and exact owner predicate. SQLite retains the existing immediate write transaction; PostgreSQL retains its adapter's transaction custody. The explicit flag changes only the old expiry predicate. Normal batching remains the existing shared statement on both paths. | `openclaw-state-lease-store.ts:234`; `openclaw-state-lease-worker.ts:221`; `openclaw-state-lease-storage.ts:94`; `src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.ts:111`; `src/infra/kysely-sync.ts:152`. Actual local SQLite proof and PostgreSQL compile-only SQL check. All four repository CI PostgreSQL conformance lanes passed on the CI head; no PostgreSQL server was contacted from this worktree. |

## Accepted edge cases

- `isExpired` and `assertCurrent`/`assertOwned` semantics are unchanged. A point-of-effect check between resume and recovery reports expired and can abort the lease before recovery.
- A competing owner can take over while the frozen owner's child is still running. The old owner then loses on resume, as today.
- Ordinary in-flight renewal that settles with an error or without a future published expiry loses; it does not start a second recovery attempt.

## Measurement

Local synthetic SQLite measurement through the actual store function:

| Operation | UPDATE statements | Rows affected |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary renewal of expired row | 1 | 0 |
| Recovery of same overdue acquisition | 1 | 1 |
| Recovery after owner replacement | 1 | 0 |
| Unchanged normal batch of two due leases | 1 | 2 |

No extra SQL statement or row is touched on a normal renewal. Recovery adds one conditional UPDATE only when expiry is observed with no pending renewal; joining a pending renewal adds zero writes. Successful recovery touches the same three timestamp columns on one matching row. It adds no schema, index, persistent bytes, timer type, background worker or normal-path database read. PostgreSQL compilation produces the same predicate with `$n` parameters: seven parameters for ordinary renewal, six for recovery. The normal timer adds one shared-memory expiry load and a wall-clock check to choose between renewal and recovery; the flag adds a query-builder branch. This is statement/work-count evidence, not a latency or PostgreSQL execution benchmark.

## Evidence

Red, before production edits, on `f4f365140c10`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'recovers the timer owner'
FAIL recovers the timer owner's stalled main thread without aborting its work
OpenClawStateLeaseError: state lease core:test-maintenance/maintenance was lost; retry the operation
assertActive src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts:177
assertCurrent src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts:226
Tests 1 failed | 19 skipped
Duration 8.05s; wrapper wall time 37.67s (cold worker compilation)
```

The regression now shares a table with the three takeover lifecycle cases. It blocks the real main thread for 1.1 seconds against an injected 1-second lease, proves the lease signal remains live, and observes later durable renewal. Lifetime coverage also asserts `onLost` is not called and exactly one recovery warning is emitted.

Green on the final TypeScript candidate, with worker-generation source verification passing:

```text
50 lease and lease-loss consumer test files selected
Test Files: 50 passed across 5 Vitest shards
Tests: 549 passed, 3 existing skips
[test] passed 5 Vitest shards in 543.58s
settles a stalled timer owner after recover   PASS 2054ms
settles a stalled timer owner after takeover  PASS 1708ms
settles a stalled timer owner after released  PASS 1854ms
settles a stalled timer owner after reacquired PASS 2400ms
```

Selection was all `src/state/*lease*.test.ts` plus every test file containing `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST` or `state lease expired` under `src/` and `test/`, run through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <50 files> --maxWorkers=1`. This includes existing IOERR/renewal failure, pending renewal, native expiry, cleanup/uncertainty, project clone cancellation, project registry, worktree, plugin lifecycle, config-reload and transcript export consumers. Two PostgreSQL cases and one existing peer-admission case were skipped by their existing environment qualification; no new skip was added.

An earlier all-green owner/lifetime run was correctly invalidated by the wrapper because source was edited during the run. The 543.58-second run above held source fixed and passed final generation verification; the invalidated run is not counted as final proof. Summed test execution was 48.495 seconds for the heartbeat integration file and 380 ms for the lifetime file. Existing long worker startup/notification tests make the heartbeat integration file exceed 30 seconds; the new four real-stall cases add 7.916 seconds of test execution and reuse the existing worker/state fixture.

Test expectation changes: the lifetime “pending” case now asserts no loss at observed expiry while renewal is pending, then settles the pending renewal without a new expiry and asserts the original loss message. Existing failure, IOERR, idle and release diagnostic outcomes remain unchanged. No ordinary expired-owner expectation was changed to successful recovery.

Targeted checks passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental`; type-aware `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.source.json` on all ten touched TypeScript files; repository formatter check on those files and the documentation; `git diff --check`. The test wrapper regenerates its worker bundles through the repository compiler; no tracked lease-worker bundle is derived from the unchanged renewal scheduler.

## Decision needed

Owning store/lifecycle: `state_leases` in the shared-state database, the captured async lease owner, its actor renewal transaction and parent timer. The invariant changes from “observed expiry alone irrevocably loses the parent-timer lease” to “observed expiry may recover once if the same acquisition owner still holds the row.” Durable expiry remains the admission condition for effects; token matching alone does not authorize effects.

Every relaxed expiry check, and what remains:

| Check | Explicit exception | Remaining guards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent expiry observer, `openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts:101` | Wait for a pending renewal or issue one recovery instead of immediate loss. | One pending promise, one recovery decision; future shared expiry required after successful settlement; otherwise original onLost. |
| Owner admission, `openclaw-state-lease.ts:226` | `recover` skips `assertActive`'s expiry test. | Original source admission, disposed/closed/phase checks, caller cancellation and prior lease loss; no effect can use this purpose. |
| Host facts, `openclaw-state-lease-worker-owner.ts:136` | `recover` facts do not require expiresAt. | Exact lifecycle kind, identity equality, original live owner and source, transaction/commit grant transport, unknown-outcome custody. Ordinary renew/write/verify remain expiry-required; release cleanup is unchanged. |
| Worker durable verification, `openclaw-state-lease-worker.ts:233,257` | Recovery skips the ordinary unexpired verification at transaction/commit stages. | Both host grants remain; the exact owner-matched UPDATE and its affected-row check execute in the same write transaction; mismatch/missing row loses. |
| Store renewal predicate, `openclaw-state-lease-store.ts:247` | Only `recoverExpired: true` omits expires_at > now. | Exact scope/key/owner predicate, existing write scope, transaction, admission and durable commit publication. |

Alternatives considered: blanket expiry-predicate removal would broaden ordinary renewals; off-thread scheduling still waits on host admission; raising leaseMs merely moves the stall threshold. The selected recovery variant preserves batching and avoids a second competing lease owner or persistent recovery state.

Autoreview design question (P2): “Allow overdue recovery before stopping renewal on callback completion,” at `openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts:145`. If a stalled callback immediately returns before overdue timers run, drain stops renewal and final ownership validation still reports expired. This draft preserves that behavior as the agreed point-of-effect-before-recovery edge. Extending recovery into drainage/completion would be a further lifecycle decision. This finding is recorded for maintainer acceptance rather than silently changing the decided edge case. The review returned an incorrect-patch verdict on this point; it is not described as clean.

Pr-simplify completed: the old timer export was removed and both callers consume the extracted timer owner directly. No new recovery store, compatibility wrapper or parallel scheduling owner was introduced. Normal batch scheduling is unchanged. New cases share the existing integration table and lifetime fixture; exact warning-list assertions consolidate the previous separate count/content assertions.

| File | Kind | Added/removed | Net |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md` | docs | +8/−2 | +6 |
| `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` | tooling | +1/−0 | +1 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-context.ts` | production | +2/−0 | +2 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.lifetime.test.ts` | test | +56/−26 | +30 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.test.ts` | test | +65/−2 | +63 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.ts` | production | +1/−130 | -129 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-store.ts` | production | +3/−2 | +1 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts` | production | +167/−0 | +167 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker-owner.ts` | production | +12/−3 | +9 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker-storage.ts` | production | +11/−3 | +8 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker.ts` | production | +25/−7 | +18 |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts` | production | +11/−2 | +9 |

Totals versus `f4f365140c10`: production +232/−147 (**+85**), plus tooling +1/−0 (**+1**); tests +121/−28 (**+93**); documentation +8/−2 (**+6**). The aspirational net-test-lines <= 0 target was not met. Reaching it here would require removing distinct existing proof or unrelated cleanup; no coverage was deleted to meet the count. The explicit recovery path and its size are part of the maintainer decision.

Pre-commit Codex autoreview completed at P2 with the one design-dependent finding above and no other findings. No implementation finding has been accepted and left unfixed. Initial draft-head Codex autoreview of `e3bf46f1c59be6b26a406b4c9e6b6dd27fddea89` completed **scoped-clean at P2**: no additional actionable P0–P2 findings. It explicitly considered the documented callback-completion edge. The earlier design question remains above for maintainer acceptance; no accepted implementation finding remains.

Rollback: revert the two candidate commits together. No schema or data migration is required; existing rows retain their format and earlier binaries resume the prior expiry semantics. No retention, deletion, durability or permission policy is changed beyond the proposed recovery interpretation. Validation limits: no operator Gateway, production state or operational remote host was contacted; local PostgreSQL work was compile-only, while the authorized repository CI ran its PostgreSQL conformance lanes; no claim of child-process fencing, arbitrary clock-skew safety or active-active Gateway support.

## CI result and packaging repair

One native `scripts/pr ci-dispatch 202973` request ran [44877465850](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44877465850), attempt 1, at `e3bf46f1c59be6b26a406b4c9e6b6dd27fddea89`. It completed **failure**, in 1,429 seconds (61 successful jobs, 3 failures including the aggregate gate, 27 skips; 21,277 aggregate job-seconds). All four PostgreSQL conformance jobs, all five Windows test jobs, docs, lint and production/test typechecks passed. The two test-job failures were:

| Job | Failure evidence classification | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-16` | unknown: no matching job on main | `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-1` | new: matching main job passed; selected scope not compared | `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` |

The failure report was fetched once with `pnpm test:ci-failed <exact-run-url> --json`. The closed-runtime inventory check was reproduced locally red and named the omitted `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-timer.ts`. The owning guide requires explicit maintenance of `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`; it is not generated. The final repair adds exactly that one entry, with no lease-code or test change. This omission is attributable to the timer extraction, not claimed as inherited CI.

Post-repair local proof (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`): eager-import **23 passed** (34.61 s); provisioning **17 passed, 1 existing skip, 1 timeout** (990.93 s); wrapper total 1,105.07 s, with final source-generation verification passing. The timeout was the macOS-only “materializes full cold/warm PR siblings, then preserves native sparse transitions” case: observed 423.316 s against its existing 120 s timeout. It was skipped by the Linux CI environment and is additional local platform proof, not a claimed reproduction of the Linux CI failure. Its timing relationship to the candidate has not been established on the base. No timeout, assertion, skip or test source was changed. No claim that passing replay proves the entire CI run fixed.

The one-line inventory repair completed focused Codex autoreview **scoped-clean at P2**. Pr-simplify on the repair retained only the required explicit archive entry; no lease implementation or test changed. The full 50-file / 549-test lease and consumer proof therefore remains valid for the unchanged lease code. Final repaired head `1252d107b3b9d25975a22b2a3eecb59e0fc5f0a7` completed committed-head Codex autoreview **scoped-clean at P2**, with no accepted/actionable findings. It assessed the inventory delta and the reported timeout; the unchanged lease range retains its prior scoped-clean review. The earlier callback-completion design question remains in Decision needed.

The requested `node scripts/watch-pr-ci.mjs 202973 <head> --after 44877247546 --completion ci-run --interval 120` was invoked, but discovery filters for pull_request events (`scripts/watch-pr-ci.mts:371`) and cannot attach the workflow_dispatch run. That read-only watcher was stopped; the repository-supported `gh run watch 44877465850 --repo openclaw/openclaw --interval 120 --exit-status` observed the same exact run to completion. No workflow code was changed.

There was **no second CI dispatch or rerun**. The final inventory repair is covered by focused local proof and review; the completed CI run covers the preceding head. CI is not claimed green for the repaired head. This PR remains draft and needs maintainer acceptance; no readiness or merge action was taken.

prs.title: fix: export Meme Maker PNGs with system Chromium on Linux
prs.body:
Closes #202635

## What Problem This Solves

Meme Maker reports that PNG export needs Chromium on Linux even when the distribution's Chromium browser is installed. SVG export works on the same machine.

## User Impact

Linux users can export a PNG using their system Chromium installation without downloading a second browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

If the usual Playwright or Google Chrome launch fails on Linux, Meme Maker now checks the standard system Chromium paths and launches the browser directly.

## Evidence

On Debian 13 with system Chromium and an empty Playwright browser directory, the existing PNG rendering test failed before the fix. With the fix, all three local rendering tests passed, including checks for image dimensions and caption pixels. The reported Drake render command produced a 1200 × 1200 PNG using a cached fixture image with the patch applied to upstream main.

Formatting and whitespace checks passed. The broader check on the contributor checkout stopped at its unrelated plugin compatibility removal gate.

### Linux CLI reproduction

I ran the renderer from the PR parent and the reviewed commit in separate directories on the same Debian host. Both used the same installed dependencies, empty Playwright browser directory, and cached synthetic JPEG for the Drake template. The launch trace below includes only the executable path.

```text
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)"
Chromium 156.0.8078.79 built on Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)
Playwright browser directory: empty. Google Chrome: absent from PATH and /opt/google/chrome/chrome.
```

prs.title: refactor(android): simplify paired-device token summaries
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Paired-device summaries retain per-token metadata objects even though their only production readers need total and active counts. That stores token roles, scopes and timestamps the screen never reads and makes rendering scan the list repeatedly.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Paired-device status and count text stay identical. Device identity, displayed roles/scopes, pairing admission, confirmation, mutations and canonical readback are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Calculate tokenCount and activeTokenCount at the existing decoder, remove GatewayDeviceTokenSummary and its decoder, and drop the unused device approval timestamp. Migrate all constructor fixtures and use the scalar counts in the screen. This removes 15 production lines without introducing another wrapper.

Preserve token admission through the existing nonBlankString helper, including nonblank primitive roles. Preserve the existing trimmed-long revocation semantics, including zero, negative values and numeric strings. The literal localization source key remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Six affected suites pass in both phone flavors: 32 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. Both compiles, Kotlin lint and staged-content guards pass on exact tree `abddb298c3fbb453c1adf29f20749b204d0de2a2`.
- Both flavors also passed on the frozen baseline with the new contract tests. Runtime refresh coverage includes malformed collections/rows, blank and primitive roles, and revoked timestamp coercion. UI coverage retains Paired, Active and Needs Token with 0/0, 2/3 and 0/2 counts.
- JUnit-reported suite times total 29.429 seconds (Play) and 24.169 seconds (ThirdParty), excluding Gradle/build overhead. Existing real Compose dialog/overview tests dominate this scope.
- Fresh independent source review and full local ClawSweeper review of `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69..a078528bf513c5b46bea73f9fc65c4c9af9ead8b` found no actionable issues. PR-head CI remains separate from local proof.

## Render Control

The same real Compose screen rendered with synthetic fixtures under Robolectric, at the frozen baseline `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69` and candidate `a078528bf513c5b46bea73f9fc65c4c9af9ead8b`. These are not device/emulator captures. The two inspected PNGs are byte-identical (SHA-256 `abcd58253e8ce98840ac46194be60f0bb52c640bd9a825a2a489d203992f71ee`).

Before:

![Baseline paired-device statuses and token counts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2db9a866-5431-4cca-921b-0d6237c681cd)

After:

![Unchanged paired-device statuses and token counts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfef6e6c-238c-42ea-ad77-96ffee898113)

## PR CI

Published-head [CI run 44876322430, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44876322430/attempts/1) passed at unchanged head `a078528bf513c5b46bea73f9fc65c4c9af9ead8b`. All nine executed jobs passed; the remaining 37 were intentionally skipped.

prs.title: improve: clear mention notifications once you see their messages
prs.body:
Related: #194147 (complementary in-app mention alerts; not a dependency).

## What Problem This Solves

A mention stays in your Inbox even after you have seen its message in the conversation. Clearing the notification requires a second, manual dismissal.

## User Impact

User impact: a mention clears automatically when its source message becomes visible in a foreground chat pane, including either desktop split pane. Off-screen messages, hidden mobile panes, background tabs, and prepared transcript rows stay unread. Manual dismissal still works.

A visible portion of the source message counts as seen. This does not remove messages or alter browser/OS notification history. No setting, migration, permission, retention, or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message bubble reports viewport visibility only after its transcript row is presented and initial positioning has settled. Exact message, session, and agent identity select the existing authenticated Inbox entries, which clear through the existing durable dismissal owner and synchronize across browsers. Shared projections and the pooled intersection observer avoid a separate Inbox or read-state store.

The change is deliberately separate from #194147, which draws attention to mentions in other sessions but leaves Inbox entries untouched.

## Evidence

The regression fails on base `c53f0575b`: a source message is on-screen, but no dismissal is sent. It passes with this change: only that mention clears; the older, off-screen entry clears after scrolling to its source.

- Built Control UI browser checks: **4 passed** (2 new mention-read scenarios plus 2 existing mobile Inbox scenarios). New scenarios took **2.21 s** and cover off-screen sources, identical message IDs in different sessions, hidden mobile panes, desktop splits, and late Inbox arrivals while document visibility changes. Document visibility is driven through the browser fixture's platform boundary, not a physical-device test.
- UI owner and affected consumer tests: **109 passed**, 6 files, **6.42 s**.
- Existing Gateway named-recipient/cross-browser dismissal regression: **1 passed**, **17.88 s**; the other 31 tests in that file were not selected.
- UI typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, Control UI controller guard, and `git diff --check`: passed. PR CI supplies broader coverage; CI timing is not yet available.
- Independent source reviews cover the original feature and the follow-up integration repair. The fresh P0–P2 review of the repair found no actionable findings; source-only, with no reviewer-executed checks. Local Auto Review was interrupted and produced no completed report. Delayed native-observer delivery and dismissal rejection were inspected rather than covered by new dedicated tests.

### CI integration follow-up

Exact-head CI and hosted review of `d19a81929a86` found two PR-caused integration defects: incomplete application fixtures and a type-inclusive static import cycle. Both are repaired in `bd689fab92c1`:

- Both affected fixture constructors reuse the existing test-only context normalizer. The production application contract remains required; no production fallback was added.
- The read-presentation context now lives in a dependency leaf shared by the renderer and visibility hook. Its previous definition is removed.
- Reproduced the failing fixture scope before editing: **11 failed / 24 passed** across five files. The same scope now has **35 passed** (**14.00 s**).
- Reproduced the static cycle: **1 before → 0 after** with `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`.
- Browser transcript geometry regressions: **2 passed** (**0.38 s**). Rebuilt Control UI mention-read scenarios: **2 passed** (**2.29 s**, including off-screen, split-pane, hidden-mobile and document-visibility behavior).
- UI typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Focused tests used the documented Node runtime selector after the local Bun worker failed before executing tests. Updated-head PR CI is pending; the previous red run is not treated as inherited or as a pass.

<!-- mention-visual-evidence -->
### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: both mention entries remain while the source message is visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f775311c-9f22-465f-9a9f-6419200cb651)

**After**

![After: the seen mention clears and the off-screen mention remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a94ab6e-4cef-4503-b937-99f5055e6642)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: visible source and stale Inbox count highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4bdf9d4-00fa-4950-ba88-c5c9948e7a90)

**After**

![After: visible source and reduced Inbox count highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7798808-1da4-4fb4-8566-d10d0cfe641e)

Actual built Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, 1280 × 820, dark mode. Before: base `c53f0575b`. After: initial implementation `d19a81929a86` (captured before publication). The later fixture/context-location repair does not change appearance; mention behavior was rechecked in the rebuilt UI.
<!-- /mention-visual-evidence -->

Simplification: no new persistence, RPC, timer, or notification manager. The additional presentation context distinguishes readable rows from resource-preparation rows without changing existing media admission.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(setup): don't block a failed model setup's restore as a config size drop
prs.body:
Closes #202461
Related: #202459

## What Problem This Solves

When model setup has already saved its config and a later step fails, for example because the Gateway does not apply the change, setup tries to put the previous config back. If the config was small before setup and setup more than doubled it, OpenClaw's config write guard blocks that restore as a suspicious size drop, so setup fails without undoing its change.

## User Impact

User impact: when setup activation or the onboarding wizard fails after saving its config and the only reason its restore is blocked is `size-drop`, setup now restores the small config it started from instead of ending with "OpenClaw blocked this config update …". That message asks the user to correct the proposed update and retry, but the blocked update is setup's own restore, so there is nothing for the user to correct. The other write guards can still reject the restore, for example when setup had also added `gateway.mode` to a config that had none (see Not covered). From reading the code, before this change a credential that setup had already activated also stayed active: setup rolls it back only after the config restore succeeds (`src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts:159-163`); Not covered says what the tests and runs below show about that step. No new options, config, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup's restore is one conditional write built by the shared helper `captureSetupInferenceFileUndo`, and its write options never included `allowConfigSizeDrop`. The config write guard rejects a write as `size-drop` when the file is at least 512 bytes before the write and less than half that size after it, so restoring a small pre-setup config after setup added a provider and its model catalog trips the guard. The helper now sets `allowConfigSizeDrop: true` on that restore write. The setup activation and onboarding wizard restores both go through this helper, so the allowance is set once, where the restore write is built, rather than at each caller.

Setup reaches this restore when its config write succeeds and a later step fails. For example, a running Gateway does not apply the write (#183964 describes a hand-written first-run config with `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`), or, with default reload settings, defers it, as in the Gateway runs below. Credential activation can also report a false "connection changed" error after a plugin install, which #202459 addresses; the released CLI run below hit that error before its restore.

Boundaries of the allowance:

- It is hardcoded in the helper and applies only to the helper's conditional inverse write. That inverse is computed from this setup's own before and after configs, can only undo this setup's own changes, and refuses to write if any of those keys changed since. No caller sets the option, and a caller's own value is overridden. The other write guards still apply: `unreadable-config-before-write`, `gateway-mode-removed`, the pinned config path, and the check that newer settings have not superseded this setup. The accepted restore still records its `size-drop` reason in the config write audit. Merged #143147 hardcodes the same allowance, with a comment, for an avatar replacement that can shrink the config.
- #155427 made the message for this rejection path-free; it did not change whether setup's restore may shrink the config. This PR leaves that message as is.
- #81828 asked to let `skills.update` callers request `allowConfigSizeDrop`. This PR adds no such option: no RPC, CLI, or caller parameter can turn this allowance on or off. Draft #202108 sets the same allowance for the restore of its new first-agent step.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts`: in `captureSetupInferenceFileUndo`, the restore write's options gain `allowConfigSizeDrop: true` after `expectedConfigPath`, with a one-line comment. No new exports, parameters, or files.
- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts` and `src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`: one new case each (see Evidence).
- Against `cf95c48d9d`: `setup-inference-transition.ts` +2/−0, `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` +28/−0, `setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts` +27/−0.

</details>

## Evidence

Runs added for the review. They used synthetic API keys and loopback fake model servers only; paths, ports, and tokens are redacted.

- Behavior, on a Gateway built from source at `cf95c48d9d` (not the npm package): a failed activation whose restore drops the config below half. Before this change the guard blocked the restore (`size-drop:1106->535`); with this change the restore was written.
- Behavior, on the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` CLI: `openclaw onboard` reached the same restore, but that config was not small enough to cross the size-drop line, so the guard did not block it.
- Upgrade from the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` to a package of this change: doctor migrated the databases, and the existing settings and the stored credential still work.

The upgrade item has a complete run on the released package. The before/after behavior samples come from a source-built Gateway; no run on a published entry point crosses the size-drop line.

### Gateway run: before and after, with a restore below half

Each run started from a fresh, isolated state directory and HOME. The Gateway was built from source at `cf95c48d9d` (`pnpm build`), not the npm package, and listened on loopback with default config reload. The client was `openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate` with a synthetic OpenAI API key. The built-in OpenAI provider reached an OpenAI-compatible fake server at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1` through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` in the Gateway process environment; the config did not contain that address. OpenClaw applies config `env.vars` to the process environment and keeps a value already set there (`src/config/config-env-vars.ts:624`), so the provider sees the same variable either way. No fault was injected: with default reload, the Gateway deferred applying setup's write (both runs' Gateway logs show "config reload deferred", and the after run's reply says so), and setup then restored. The config before setup was the minimal Gateway config our harness writes: `gateway` settings and a log file path (327 bytes on disk in both runs). OpenClaw's config writer adds `meta` when it writes the restore, and the restore also keeps an empty top-level `agents` object (see below), so the restored file is larger than this start.

- Before (the build without this PR's change): the RPC failed with "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update …". The config write audit holds one rejected write whose only blocking reason is `size-drop:1106->535`, and the rejected payload (535 bytes) was saved next to the config as `openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-21T17-34-21-915Z`. The config on disk stayed setup's candidate (1106 bytes, the size of setup's write; it was still the same after a second setup attempt and a Gateway restart). Each of the two setup attempts sent one model request to the fake server.
- After (the same build plus this PR's production change): the RPC reported "The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in." No write was rejected and no `.rejected.*` file was saved: the audit records the restore as a `rename`, with `size-drop:1106->535` listed under `suspicious` and not as a blocking reason. Without `meta`, the restored config equals the config before setup except one added empty top-level `agents` object (`"agents": {}`), which the earlier runs also left. After a second setup attempt with another synthetic key and a Gateway restart, the config on disk was unchanged and the running config had the same top-level keys as the restored config; none of the keys only the candidate had (`auth`, `plugins`) were present. Each of the two setup attempts sent one model request to the fake server.
- Builds: both carry the local package version label `2026.11.7`, a `package.json` change only, not a published version. Apart from that label, the after build differs from the before build only by this PR's production change; its diff has the same SHA-256 (`66cfd15b…`, `git diff --binary --full-index`) as the production diff of `2ff2bd4ee53f`. In the built output, the restore write's options (`expectedConfigPath: …, allowConfigSizeDrop: true`) occur 0 times in the before build and once in each of the restore helper's two bundled copies in the after build.

```text
# before: cf95c48d9d source build without this PR's change; Gateway console log
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.models, agents.defaults.model, auth.profiles, plugins.entries.openai, meta)
[reload] config reload deferred: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during prepare: Plugin openai reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup; the previous plugin configuration remains active.
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.; retrying automatically after admitted work and cleanup settle
Config write rejected: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:1106->535). Rejected payload saved to <state>/openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-21T17-34-21-915Z.
[gateway] request handler failed: Error: Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it p...
# before: client output of openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate --json
"message": "Error: Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it p...",
# after: the same build plus this PR's production change; Gateway console log
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.models, agents.defaults.model, auth.profiles, plugins.entries.openai, meta)
[reload] config reload deferred: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during prepare: Plugin openai reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup; the previous plugin configuration remains active.
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.; retrying automatically after admitted work and cleanup settle
Config write anomaly: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:1106->535)
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (meta)
[reload] config source revision 3 accepted (write)
[gateway] request handler failed: Error: The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in.
# after: client output of openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate --json
"message": "Error: The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in.",
```

<details>
<summary>Earlier Gateway runs that stayed above the line</summary>

Earlier Gateway runs from the same harness also wrote the fake server's address into the config's `env.vars`, and three of them, including a before/after pair, also wrote `gateway.reload.mode: "off"` (the #183964 shape). With those extra bytes, every restore stayed 27 to 49 bytes above half of the setup-written file: for example `1239 -> 668`, where half is 619, and `1196 -> 625` against 598 in the one run with default reload settings, where the Gateway deferred the activation. Those restores were written both before and after this change, so the change does not alter a restore that stays above the line.

</details>

### Released CLI onboard (`openclaw@2026.11.6`)

With the released npm package, `openclaw onboard` (manual setup, Groq, the Groq provider plugin installed from npm, a synthetic key against a loopback fixture) failed with the false "connection changed" error that #202459 addresses and then wrote its restore. Onboard's two earlier writes took the config from 1297 to 1492 bytes; setup's write took it to 2049 bytes, and the restore to 1508. Half of 2049 is 1024, so the guard did not block the restore.

<details>
<summary>Starting config of this run</summary>

That run's starting config also held a Groq provider block that we add to route Groq to the fixture, which made up most of its 1297 bytes. Without that block, and if the restore again removed the same 541 bytes (2049 − 1508), the restore would still stay above half (computed from this run's readings; not run).

</details>

### When the size-drop guard blocks the restore

The restore is blocked for this size-drop reason only when the config before setup is small compared with what setup adds: the setup-written file must be at least 512 bytes and the restored file less than half of it. The minimal Gateway config above is one such start; a config that already holds more than setup adds is not. How often real setups start from a config that small is not measured.

### Upgrade from `openclaw@2026.11.6` with existing settings and a stored credential

In an isolated HOME and state directory, the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` npm package ran `openclaw onboard --non-interactive` with the built-in OpenAI provider and a synthetic API key. Then `config set` wrote `skills`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` (900, not the default), and `logging.level`, and a file was placed in the workspace. Next, a package built from `cf95c48d9d` plus this PR's production change (the repository's packaging script, local version label `2026.11.7`) was installed over it, and `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran.

- Doctor exited 0 and printed neither its maintenance-deferred notice nor a migration refusal. It saved pre-migration SQLite backups and reported "Upgraded agent database schema … v38 -> v43". `config validate` passed before and after the upgrade.
- Stored credential: `openclaw infer model run --local` went through a loopback proxy that checks the API key against the stored synthetic key. Before the upgrade it succeeded with the stored key; a control request to the same proxy with a different synthetic key got HTTP 401; after the upgrade `infer` succeeded again with the stored key. A credential probe read the same result before and after: `readable`, `present`, `type: api_key`, key hash matching the synthetic key given to onboard, profile id `openai:api-key`.
- Settings: hashes of the `gateway` settings, `skills`, `logging`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, `agents.defaults.model`, and the auth profile list were the same before and after, and the workspace file was unchanged. The whole config without `meta` did change: doctor reported writing its own config migration records ("Updated config", with a backup).
- Environment: the CLI commands in this run set `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT` to a unit name that does not exist. The variable is the documented selector for this install's systemd service; pointing it at a missing unit is our test-isolation use, not a documented one. It keeps the CLI from taking another, older Gateway service installed on the host under another account for this install's service. Without it, doctor refused the forward database migration, naming that service's older version; from the code, doctor cannot rule out that service sharing this state, the conservative case that #190194 keeps. From the code, the variable only changes which systemd unit counts as this install's service; it does not skip migrations or backups. The same CLI environment also set `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external`, `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, and `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BONJOUR=1`.

### Focused tests

For the focused tests, "Before" results were taken on main `cf95c48d9d` with only the test changes applied. "After" results were taken on `cf95c48d9d` with this PR's change applied, the full diff of commit `2ff2bd4ee53f`.

Two new cases with no padding or invented config fields. Each asserts that the setup-written file is at least 512 bytes and that the restored file is less than half of it, so the case keeps exercising the size-drop guard if the fixtures change.

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, "restores a size-dropping first config write when its activation is not applied": the same flow as the existing case from #183964 (activation completion deferred, no reloader, so the Gateway never applies the write and setup restores), but the starting config is small and has no provider, and the sign-in adds the provider with its model catalog. It expects "The previous connection was restored on disk" and the restored config to equal the starting config apart from `meta`.
- `src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`, "wizard recovery restores a size-dropping provider write": the onboarding wizard's config target starts from `{ gateway: { mode: "local" } }`, writes a candidate that adds one provider with one model, and the activation is rejected ("promotion refused"). It expects that error to be rethrown and the restored config to have no `models`.
- Before: exactly these two cases fail; the other 48 cases in the two files pass. Both fail with "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update …", and the guard logs one rejection for each, with the size drop as the only reason: `size-drop:1674->438` for the activation case and `size-drop:811->235` for the wizard case.
- After: all 50 cases in the two files pass, and the run logs no config write rejection.

<details>
<summary>Mutation check, timing, consumers, targeted checks, local review</summary>

- Mutation check (not part of this PR): with only the production lines reverted on the final tree, both new cases fail again the same way.
- Time, per changed test file with this change (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, 42 tests, 112.83 s Vitest duration (the new case: 2.38 s); `setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`, 8 tests, 18.97 s (the new case: 1.04 s). The consumer run below took 73 s.
- Consumers pass: `src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.test.ts`, `src/gateway/config-reload.activation.integration.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-setup-auto.test.ts`, and `src/wizard/setup.inference-verification.test.ts`, plus the changed wizard recovery file.
- Targeted checks: `oxfmt --check` and oxlint pass on the three changed files; the two tsgo typecheck commands selected by `pnpm check:changed --dry-run` pass; the test-lines ratchet reports `Net test lines: +55; allowance: 400`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Local review: autoreview on the full diff against `cf95c48d9d` reported scoped-clean: no accepted or actionable findings (overall: patch is correct, 0.94). pr-simplify on this diff suggested no changes.

</details>

CI: the workflow runs for this fork PR (CI, CodeQL, OpenGrep and others) are waiting for maintainer approval (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` has not passed yet. Other checks, including dependency-review, security-sensitive-review, and PR context and evidence, pass.

Not covered:

- Credential rollback after the restore: the focused tests activate no credential before the restore (no Gateway claims the write in the activation case, and the wizard case's activation fails at once). In the Gateway runs, there is no credential reading: the CLI's credential listing refuses to run while the Gateway is running ("This command is offline-only"), so the rollback is not shown there either. The rollback ordering described under User Impact is from reading the code.
- From the code, if setup added `gateway.mode` to a config that had none, the restore is still blocked by the `gateway-mode-removed` guard and setup reports the same message; this PR only allows the size drop.
- The Gateway's automatic Codex setup also calls this helper. This PR does not test that entry (its tests mock the helper) and does not claim it is fixed.
- The run that crosses the size-drop line uses a Gateway built from source, not the npm package; the released-package CLI run reached the restore without crossing the line.
- Model calls went to loopback fake servers with synthetic keys; no real provider account was used. This change is in the config restore after a failed activation, not in the model call.
- The tests and runs used Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64) with Node v24.22.1 only; the change is one write option with no platform-specific code.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.
