prs.title: fix: send WhatsApp videos and large media on slow connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a slow upload connection, sending a WhatsApp video (or any media file of a few MB) fails with `Media upload failed on all hosts`, even though text and small images keep working. The agent then falls back to text only, so the user never gets the video they asked for.

## User Impact

User impact: WhatsApp videos, documents and other large media send normally on slow connections instead of failing after a few seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Baileys only puts a timeout on an upload socket when the message options carry `mediaUploadTimeoutMs`, and OpenClaw never set it. With no proxy, Baileys then uploads through Node's `https.globalAgent`, whose sockets time out after 5 seconds idle (Node 19+). The OS accepts a multi-MB body into the socket send buffer almost at once, so the socket looks idle while a slow uplink drains it. After 5 seconds Node fires `timeout`, Baileys aborts with `Upload timeout`, the remaining hosts fail to connect over the still-saturated uplink, and the send fails. Small images finish within 5 seconds, which is why only larger media broke.

This change passes a 60-second `mediaUploadTimeoutMs` on every media send, quoted ones included. That replaces the 5-second idle default on the upload socket. Text sends are unchanged. Stickers still go through the structured-send path without the option; they are small enough not to hit this.

## Evidence

**Live:** on a Gateway with about 340 KB/s upstream (OpenClaw 2026.9.7, Baileys 7.0.0-rc14, Node 26), a 4.4 MB H.264 video failed every time. Instrumenting Baileys' per-host upload loop showed the first host failing with `Upload timeout` and the next hosts with `ETIMEDOUT`. With an explicit upload timeout, the same video sent as a normal video in about 14 seconds.

**Repro test, red before the fix and green after:**
- `session.media-upload.test.ts` adds a slow-uplink case using the existing local HTTPS upload origin and a real `createWaSocket` session. The origin answers only after the full body arrives, and `https.globalAgent`'s idle timeout is shortened to keep the test fast. Without an upload timeout, Baileys fails with `Upload timeout`; with `WHATSAPP_MEDIA_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` the same upload succeeds.
- `send-api.test.ts` checks that video, document, image and quoted media sends pass `mediaUploadTimeoutMs`, and that text sends do not.
- Before the fix: 7 failing (the slow-upload case, the four media-option cases, and two voice-delivery call-shape assertions). After: all pass.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/session.media-upload.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/send.voice-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 52 passed (7 failed with `send-api.ts` reverted)
- `pnpm test:extension whatsapp`: 1,059 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/whatsapp`: passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/whatsapp/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit`: passed
- oxfmt: clean

`pnpm check:changed` was killed for running out of memory on my machine, so the gates above were run individually; PR CI runs the full set.

</details>

prs.title: feat(workboard): request changes on the same card
prs.body:
Related to #182682.

## What problem this solves

A reviewer can find an unmet requirement after a Workboard worker finishes. A completed card with a linked worker session offers no direct way to ask for a correction on that card.

## User impact

Open a finished autonomous card in Review or Done, choose **Request changes**, and enter revised instructions. Workboard starts one new attempt on the same card. Earlier attempts, proof, artifacts, comments, and dependency links remain available under current retention limits. Pending dependents wait while the card is Running and follow the existing completion rules afterward.

## Implementation

The action uses the existing Workboard start RPC and worker dispatch. The store checks the reviewed card revision and atomically prepares the new attempt, claim, and launch. It can replace an unexpired claim on a Review card when the claim belongs to its completed worker run. A newer reviewer claim and other cards' occupied capacity still prevent dispatch. The worker receives the instructions, card history retains them, and late lifecycle events from earlier attempts are ignored.

## Evidence at `e1437a743c0ca40d5d4aeac2b9fd574e74408b37`

- Reproduced the retained-claim rejection with the regression before the fix. After the fix, **40 focused tests passed**. Coverage includes replacing the finished run's claim, protecting a newer reviewer's claim, and respecting capacity occupied by another card. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent scoped review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Started a built Gateway at `743062e30ff53765ea7b91edfba9e46bc119f720` with a persisted SQLite Workboard and a loopback fixture model. A real worker finished in Review while its claim was still valid. Restarted with the candidate Gateway using that same SQLite state. The card, execution, unexpired claim, accepted launch, and prior evidence all read back.
- In Chromium on the candidate's built Control UI, used **Request changes** from Review, then again from Done. The real worker sent the respective new instructions to the fixture provider in both runs. The same card persisted three attempts, its original session, and its prior proof, artifacts, comments, and dependency link. The linked dependent was still outside Ready at the Review readback.
- Both Gateways and browser sessions used isolated local state and fictional fixture data. The provider was local and synthetic.

### Review card in Chromium

The upstream baseline and candidate use the same persisted fixture card. The candidate screenshot shows the instructions just before **Start new attempt**.

prs.title: fix: start sessions from ready templates during background refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A first send at an already accepted repository commit can wait behind a background template refresh for a newer commit, even though its own template is ready. The same cache-wide wait affects managed checkout materialization and sandbox projection preparation.

## User Impact

Startup uses the ready generation for the session's accepted base while a different generation builds. HEAD, index, source files and prepared dependencies stay on that accepted commit. Requests that need an unavailable generation still join or build it normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preparation sharing now includes the requested content and backend. The template owner validates an idle exact generation without waiting for a different commit's build lease, then atomically acquires reader custody for the validated generation ID. Managed validation remains read-only. Existing publication, uncertain-process custody and retention owners remain responsible; no new persistence, schema, product configuration or cache.

Scope directed by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), not Peter. This is the startup-wait follow-up to #202803. Projection reconciliation and pre-attempt storage phase accounting are separate follow-ups; MCP timeout investigation belongs to another owner.

## Evidence

Current source head: `381949bf9b9da21a082bec88b3d0b392da4acdef`; performance campaign head: `d9b466b067c8904015041e814de59fb90059a751`; baseline: `ab054758bb2a6eac5c4caab6722437e0da777d12`. Focused owner suites: 31 tests pass. The real-Git regression is red on baseline for both consumers: managed startup falls back to ordinary Git and fails the one-private-clone assertion; sandbox startup waits until timeout. Candidate startup completes while the build gate is held, with exact A HEAD, index, source and dependencies. Existing cancellation, concurrent preparation and unknown-native-outcome custody tests remain green. Full `pnpm check:changed` passes. Isolated Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. Previous-head CI gate was green (run 44884649486; gate publisher 44885786877). Pre-rebase CI run 44900735659 completed successfully at `4d246ad046bc5de32b77c316b81f3a32e3bc2f70`; new-head CI [44935797495](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44935797495) completed successfully for `381949bf9b9da21a082bec88b3d0b392da4acdef`. ClawSweeper revision 4 reports zero open items and no findings on that same head. Native review validation and preparation are complete; landing uses `scripts/pr`.

The predeclared workload uses two A/A controls and five serial counterbalanced pairs per kind, a synthetic 62,000-file/~1.1 GB Btrfs workspace, a 35 GiB synthetic storage fixture, and real Podman. One idle native clone and directory fsync complete before their return is delayed 30 seconds. This models slow storage completion, not the kernel's metadata-reservation cause. Required outcomes: exact accepted-base contents, zero inline template builds, foreground completion while storage remains pending, lower send latency, and no >20% total CPU/allocation regression. Any other worse metric requires explicit owner acceptance.

Rerunnable committed workload: `scripts/perf/worktree-creation-measure.ts --base-advance --first-send-layout --first-send-image <local-image> --startup-refresh managed|sandbox --repo <synthetic-repo> --output <new-directory> --samples 1`, with the repository TypeScript loader and matching compiled filesystem worker. The warmed case prepares a separate untimed session; the measured retained-A session remains unprepared. It was declared in this body before its first run.

### Warmed-process comparison

Five serial counterbalanced pairs per kind, plus two A/A controls per kind. Resource totals cover the measured B idle pass plus the C refresh/send overlap once; the nested send row is not added again. All ten candidate sends finished while the 30-second storage-completion delay remained pending, with zero inline template builds. All 48 measured/control/warmup projection and installed-skill comparisons matched fresh preparation.

| Metric | Managed baseline → candidate | Sandbox baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-send median | 43.84 → 8.38 s (-80.9%) | 45.28 → 9.08 s (-80.0%) |
| First-send minimum–maximum | 43.37–44.62 → 7.70–8.81 s | 43.72–51.41 → 8.31–10.37 s |
| Template preparation median | 30,285 → 167 ms | 33,868 → 86 ms |
| Idle-pass median | 4.62 → 4.43 s (-4.0%) | 4.92 → 5.14 s (+4.6%) |
| Total CPU median | 39,494 → 38,383 ms (-2.8%) | 40,887 → 36,455 ms (-10.8%) |
| Main-thread CPU median | 2,486 → 2,609 ms (+4.9%) | 2,710 → 2,568 ms (-5.3%) |
| Transient main allocation median | 279,659,104 → 287,566,240 bytes (+2.8%) | 250,972,232 → 257,981,672 bytes (+2.8%) |

With five samples, the maximum is also the nearest-rank p95. A/A first sends were 43.45/43.32 s managed and 43.06/44.95 s sandbox. The main-CPU/allocation increases and sandbox idle-median increase are disclosed and covered by the separate performance-owner acceptance recorded below.

### Compiled Gateway, real transport and model

An isolated compiled Gateway used the ordinary idle scheduler, real WebSocket requests, Podman, and a real OpenAI model reply. Both heads reached a successful terminal model event and retained exact A HEAD, clean index, source and installed dependencies, with zero inline template builds. The retained harness searched the entire history for the response sentinel, which also appeared in the input; exact assistant reply text is therefore not claimed by that assertion.

| Delayed-refresh scenario | Baseline → candidate startup | Baseline → candidate model completion | Template preparation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Managed, existing warm slot consumed first | 38.57 → 11.77 s | 41.84 → 14.63 s | 28,557 → 90 ms |
| Sandbox, first chat.send into existing A session | 38.96 → 8.55 s | 40.89 → 10.71 s | 30,249 → 54 ms |

These are one real Gateway pair per scenario, not estimated p95s. Both candidate model replies arrived before the delayed refresh completed; both baseline replies arrived after it. Sandbox projection reconciliation stayed 4.16→4.22 s, separate from the template wait.

The managed flow uses an initial-message create, whose admitted startup owner materializes accepted A. A prior ordinary create consumes the one ready checkout slot in 340/370 ms while C is delayed. On baseline, the following startup waits for C. On candidate, A can also replenish that slot while C is still pending, so startup consumes it immediately. The direct startup-owner regression separately proves one private template clone when no slot is involved. An initial managed qualification with the slot still available completed on both heads (14.62→15.25 s model completion); that unaffected-path observation is retained and is not claimed as a red reproduction.

### Profiles and disclosed costs

Source profiles still include first-idle esbuild work in both arms (maximum consecutive non-idle spans 4.42→4.40 s managed; 5.12→4.51 s sandbox). They are not shipped-runtime blocking claims. The compiled Gateway has no such multi-second spans. Its qualified managed candidate records existing GC spans up to 83.6 ms and a 105.5 ms timer delay during the idle interval: the latter aligns with a 106.5 ms profile sample gap marked `(idle)`, followed by a 78.6 ms timer delay dominated by `(program)`. Those are disclosed native/descheduling observations, not evidence of a newly added synchronous JavaScript section. No >50 ms section was attributed to the new exact-generation selection code. Foreground module-loading/GC pauses remain (maximum observed timer delay 196 ms); reconciliation and pre-attempt storage accounting are separate follow-ups.

The original cold-source campaign is retained rather than discarded: managed median 49.28→22.43 s, CPU -10.6%, main CPU -6.7%, allocation -13.8%; sandbox median 52.11→24.30 s, maximum 64.44→68.58 s (+6.4%), CPU +4.4%, main CPU +13.1%, allocation -0.75%. Two sandbox sends outlasted the fixed barrier even though template preparation completed promptly. Profiles exposed synchronous source compilation; the separately predeclared warmed case above qualifies the running-process behavior. These disclosed observations remain part of the evidence considered in the separate owner decision below.

**Owner acceptance: ACCEPTED**, separately for this PR, as recorded verbatim below.

### Review repairs and scope

The benchmark preserves ordinary base-advance behavior when `advance.txt` does not exist at A (old script red with ENOENT; corrected script completes). Both new scenarios also complete without repository-local Git identity; C supplies explicit synthetic author identity. These address all three numbered items in the prior ClawSweeper review. Final-head re-review is required before merge.

Production delta is +52 lines across the existing checkout/Git-policy, template-cache and registry-worker owners. Growth carries exact-generation validation into atomic reader admission. Publication, retention and uncertain native custody keep their existing owners; no schema, persistence, product configuration or cache is added. A caller whose accepted generation is unavailable still follows normal preparation. A session with no accepted base continues to resolve its base through the existing owner; this change does not redefine base selection. Release-note context: first sends can reuse their own ready managed or sandbox generation while a newer base refreshes in the background.

The second ClawSweeper review found that source-only Git policy filtered the explicit read-only validation setting. Current head preserves the operation owner’s `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` setting through its existing whitelist; inherited Git variables remain filtered. The extended real-Git advanced-default cases make template file metadata stale and assert unchanged index bytes and mtime: source-only fails on the previous head, both policies pass with the repair. The 24 focused policy/startup/filter cases and full `pnpm check:changed` pass; isolated Codex P0–P2 review is clean. A command-line alternative was rejected by the file-size gate and is not in the final change. The performance campaign above predates this narrow read-only correction; no new call, scan, wait, or cache is added. The separate owner acceptance is recorded below.


### Conflict integration with #193214

Rebased onto `e695c13a939e6a2e08c255a2ac829a64c7f33f41` after GitHub reported conflicts. The two conflicts preserve lane 2746's cold-cause attribution in the shared validation helper and call its extracted Git-status owner with the explicit read-only environment. The other two commits replay unchanged. All 80 affected tests pass across sandbox templates, template cache, Git filters/policy, managed prewarm and incoming cold-cause diagnostics. The complete `pnpm check:changed --base e695c13a939e6a2e08c255a2ac829a64c7f33f41` passes, including typechecks, dead-export scans, lint and ownership guards. Fresh isolated Codex review of the complete rebased patch and relevant unchanged owners is scoped-clean through P2. The +1 net production line versus the previous patch is formatting around the extracted status call; no extra operation, scan, configuration or owner was added. Existing performance evidence remains tied to its original measured heads.

## Performance-owner decision (verbatim)

Performance-owner decisions by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), NOT Peter.

**#202960: ACCEPTED.** Own-base ready-template startup selection cuts first-send medians 43.84→8.38 s (managed) and 45.28→9.08 s (sandbox). Production on Team shows 9–100 s first-send waits on template refreshes today, so this is the most user-visible fix in flight. The disclosed costs (+2.8% main allocation, +4.9% managed main CPU, +4.6% sandbox idle median) are accepted as small against an ~80% first-send latency cut. Land it via scripts/pr once exact-head CI is green and ClawSweeper has zero open items. Rebase if needed; lane 2746 landed #193214 (cold-cause enum) in a neighboring area.

prs.title: fix: keep session writes responsive during worker bundle cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing or pruning a worker bundle can recursively delete an extracted installation or staging tree through the Gateway's shared libuv filesystem pool. Slow unlinks can then hold up unrelated session reads and writes. Moving bundle construction into a worker thread does not isolate that pool.

Related: #202874.

## User Impact

Worker-bundle cleanup no longer contributes bulk unlink/rmdir work to the Gateway filesystem pool. Preparation still waits for cleanup to settle, and pruning keeps its existing retention and file protections. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the three whole-tree cleanup sites through the existing `nativeWorktreeFilesystem.remove` child-process owner and its content-operation budget. Keep ordinary tarball and temporary-file deletion nonrecursive. This completes the separately requested bundle follow-up without another cleanup service, cache, or setting.

The child startup/CPU/allocation tradeoff accepted in #202874 also applies here. That PR's production-shaped synthetic proof measured bulk-removal pool occupancy 4/4 → 0/4 and injected-slow-unlink patch/fs-write maxima 1,442/1,388 ms → 13.9/4.7 ms. Those are the existing owner's measurements, not a new bundle benchmark; compiled-release startup cost was not measured.

## Evidence

The existing archive-staging and retention/pruning tests now forbid recursive staging removal through the shared pool while retaining their real filesystem assertions. On exact parent `182493a8ef52cfce34ca8abd3de05909492b8dfb`, three cases fail at that boundary and file-only pruning passes. With the fix, all 24 bundle and real worker-thread consumer cases pass. Live public-npm verification was not exercised.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/bundle.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/node-bootstrap-artifact-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed; 46.92 s including cold worker compilation, approximately 9.5 s executing tests. CI timing pending.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 182493a8ef52cfce34ca8abd3de05909492b8dfb`: passed, including production and affected-test typechecks, lint/format, and all three unused-export scans.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no P0–P2 findings; reviewer did not execute tests.
- Simplification: one existing owner replaces three recursive call sites. Production delta +8/−3, net +5 lines, for the owner import and staging/file branch; test delta +14, extending existing cases. No UI-imported module changed.

prs.title: fix(update): explain missing macOS developer tools when Git is unavailable
prs.body:
Related to #202701.

## What Problem This Solves

On `main`, switching a macOS npm install to the dev channel can fail during cloning when the updater selects Apple's Git stub and no developer directory is active. An existing source checkout can be reported as an unmanaged install for the same reason.

## User Impact

This PR reports that `/usr/bin/git` needs the macOS developer tools and stops before invoking the stub. The message tells users to run `xcode-select --install` or select an installed Xcode, then retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater checks the active developer directory when its existing executable search selects `/usr/bin/git`. The existing search order still gives `/usr/bin` precedence over inherited PATH entries. Whether the updater should trust a standalone Git is a separate decision for maintainers.

## Evidence

### Native macOS CLI

Built an npm package directly from PR head `04f1650` and ran its CLI on macOS arm64. For the refusal paths, an OS sandbox hid the Command Line Tools directory from the process. Apple's real selector returned exit `2` while `/usr/bin/git` remained executable. The pinned main comparison at `b4a41aa` denied Git execution in its isolated process.

| CLI path | Pinned main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm install switching to dev | Attempted cloning, then exited `1` with `update-failed`. | Exit `1`, `git-version-unsupported`. No clone step or new checkout. |
| Update from an existing source checkout | Exit `0`, skipped as `unmanaged-package-install`. | Exit `1`, `git-version-unsupported`. Checkout HEAD stayed at `04f1650`. |

The head trial ran these commands.

~~~sh
openclaw update --channel dev --yes --json --no-restart
node ./openclaw.mjs update --yes --json --no-restart
~~~

Both refusals printed this message to stderr.

~~~text
Update refused: /usr/bin/git requires the macOS developer tools. Install the Command Line Tools with xcode-select --install or select an installed Xcode, then retry openclaw update.
~~~

With the installed developer tools visible, `git version 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)` completed the npm-to-source switch using an existing checkout that tracked a private Git mirror pinned to the PR head. The updater returned `status: "ok"` with exit `0` and the checkout resolved to `04f16506ea34fa8bf28b38711300c0f1fc0d04b5` after the switch. The head check, package swap, and runtime verification each exited `0`.

### Released npm updaters

Each published updater installed the package built from `04f1650` with `openclaw update --tag head.tgz --yes --json --no-restart`. The 9.x extended-stable updater also needed `--channel stable` to select the local artifact. Each run used an isolated, loopback Gateway and stopped it for the update.

| Starting release | Exit and installed commit | Before/after checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2026.9.37` (extended-stable) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `0eee1704-d0dc-4434-85fa-89bea492f31b` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `0a6b4676c814…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |
| `2026.10.10` (10.x) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `8cdf8ef3-dd70-415e-8038-295cefe92ea7` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `56a57ab3d0b8…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |
| `2026.11.6` (latest stable) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `8ed50274-09e7-4323-94d4-dbe4cdf4a074` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `64147b95291c…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |

The cards were read through the Gateway RPC. The CLI returned the same `messages.ackReaction` value (`🧪`) and configured workspace path. The 10.x and latest-stable runs retained their stable channel. The 9.x run saved stable as explicitly requested.

### Regression tests

The same two test files ran on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1. The base was pinned main at `b4a41aa` with only the two test-file changes applied. The passing run used `2bb9c2ac0`, whose Git tree matches signed PR head `04f1650`.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-install-layout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner-git-commands.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

| Regression | Pinned main with the new tests | Candidate with the same tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source update with no confirmed package owner and missing developer tools | 1 failed, 8 passed. The CLI exited `0`; the assertion expected `{ code: 1 }`. The test command exited `1`. | 9/9 passed. The test command exited `0`. |
| macOS system Git with no selected developer directory (`selected: false`) | 1 failed, 6 passed. Git was invoked (`true`); the assertion expected `false`. The test command exited `1`. | 7/7 passed. The test command exited `0`. |

Full core lint stripe 5 passed locally on macOS arm64 at `04f1650` in 36.44 seconds. Exit `0`, 0 errors, and 7 warnings in files outside the PR diff.

Failed and overdue automations add to the Inbox count. Their run details live on the Automations page.

Vyctor asked for the failure indicator on the clock. The rail shares the Automations sidebar’s failure styling and uses the same definition of a current failure. prs.title: fix: keep local embeddings working during post-port memory rebuilds
prs.body:
Closes #201575

## What Problem This Solves

After `openclaw database port --to postgres` finishes porting stores, the built-in post-port memory rebuild fails for agents whose embeddings use a configured local service (such as bundled `llama.cpp` or an OpenAI-compatible local provider). Because the post-port rebuild loads the destination configuration without preparing the runtime config snapshot, local-service acquisition throws `Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.`, leaving affected agents' derived memory indexes dirty until the operator manually runs `openclaw memory index --agent <id>`.

## User Impact

User impact: post-port memory rebuilds now prepare the freshly published destination runtime config before indexing so configured local embedding providers start and index normally without requiring a manual `openclaw memory index` follow-up, while preserving per-agent SecretRef isolation and concurrent rebuild behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replaces the non-preparing `createConfigIO(...).loadConfigAsync(...)` read in `rebuildPortedAgentMemory` (`src/commands/doctor-database-port-memory.ts`, `+8/-6`) with `assertCurrent()`, `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()`, and `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader({ assertCurrent, observe: false, skipPluginValidation: true })()`, reusing the same runtime-config snapshot owner as standalone `openclaw memory index`.
- Clearing any pre-port snapshot under verified offline ownership guarantees that runtime readers (`api.runtime.llm.acquireLocalService` / `readRuntimeConfig`) consume the freshly published destination configuration rather than reusing a stale pre-port snapshot.

Operators can inspect the recorded provenance of locally installed plugin archives on PostgreSQL-backed profiles.

## Why This Change Was Made

The live SQLite metadata shortcut now checks the captured state backend and leaves PostgreSQL reads to the existing engine-aware worker.

## Evidence

A regression test wrote synthetic npm-pack provenance to PostgreSQL under a live Gateway owner. Before the source change, the read returned no row; after the change, it returned the recorded fields (2/2 tests passed). Focused metadata, install-record, and source-identity suites passed (27 tests; one macOS-only test skipped on Linux). prs.title: fix(config): preserve omitted model reasoning so discovery can supply it
prs.body:
Fixes #203150

## Problem

A sparse configured model row that pins only sizing fields — for
example, `{ "id": "gpt-6.2-sol", "contextTokens": 500000 }` merged into
the existing OpenAI provider — caused the Gateway to advertise only
`off` and `ultra` instead of the model's native thinking efforts, even
though the ChatGPT subscription catalog returns the full effort list
for GPT-6.2 Sol. `gpt-6.1-sol` does not have this problem with the same
override.

Root cause: `applyModelDefaults` (`src/config/defaults.ts`) filled an
omitted `reasoning` from the bundled plugin manifest, or `false` when
the model has no matching manifest row (the installed OpenAI manifest
covers 6.1 Sol but not 6.2 Sol). The synthesized `false` was then
treated downstream as an authored value — `modelCatalogRowToEntry`
records it as `configuredReasoning: false` — which `thinking.ts`
prioritizes over discovery, and which blocks the full-catalog runtime
enrichment in `prepared-model-runtime.full-catalog.ts`.

## Solution

Preserve the authored omission through materialization: when neither
the operator nor the manifest catalog supplies `reasoning`, leave it
unset instead of synthesizing `false`. The catalog-composition and
thinking-profile layers already treat an absent `reasoning` as
"unknown, let discovery decide" (`overlayCatalogMetadata` only
overlays defined values; `thinking.ts` falls through to
`candidate.reasoning` when no `configuredReasoning` is present).

- An explicit `reasoning: false` remains authoritative as an opt-out
  (existing test `keeps a configured catalog opt-out authoritative
  over runtime reasoning` still passes).
- A manifest catalog row still seeds `reasoning` for covered models.
- Adding individual manifest rows would only mask the defect; this
  repairs the authored-versus-synthesized precedence at catalog
  composition, as the review on #203150 directs.

## Tests

New regressions (red on base, green with the fix):

- `src/config/defaults.test.ts` —
  `preserves omitted reasoning for manifest-absent models so discovery
  can supply it (#203150)`: a sparse `gpt-6.2-sol` row keeps
  `reasoning` undefined while `contextTokens` is preserved; explicit
  `false` stays `false`, explicit `true` stays `true`.
- `src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts` — `lets discovered reasoning
  supply efforts when the configured row omits reasoning (#203150)`:
  an entry with no `reasoning`/`configuredReasoning` plus a runtime
  entry with `reasoning: true` yields the native efforts
  (`off/low/medium/high`).

Updated expectations that pinned the old synthesized default
(`reasoning: false` for sparse rows with no catalog match):

- `src/config/defaults.test.ts` (`falls back to generic defaults when
  no catalog row matches`)
- `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts` (`defaults output tokens
  without inventing context`)
- `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.inline-defaults.test.ts`
  (`expectedDefaults`)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.runtime-choices.test.ts`
  (`bounds configured-row indexing through hydrated implicit OpenAI
  picker reads`)

Verification (local, `--maxWorkers=1`, direct `vitest` — the
`run-vitest.mjs` wrapper stalls on this VM's bun worker compile; see
below):

- `src/config/defaults.test.ts`: 38/38
- `src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts` + `defaults.test.ts` +
  `prepared-model-runtime.inline-defaults.test.ts`: 61/61
- Sibling suites (model-catalog, model-catalog-route,
  model-catalog-view, model-selection.catalog-overlay,
  model-selection.configured, defaults.ollama-output-cap,
  model-alias-defaults): 146/146
- `model.compat-route`, `update-command-invalid-config`,
  `normalize-paths`, `redact-snapshot`,
  `models-list-result.runtime-choices`, `server-reload-handlers`,
  `setup-apply`, `setup.test.ts`, `artifacts.images`: 251/252 —
  1 unrelated failure in `server-reload-handlers` (`keeps a supervised
  on-exit child alive exactly once across lazy cron reload`,
  `service child cleanup identity lost`, a process-supervision timing
  failure — confirmed failing on the base commit too, pre-existing
  environment failure, unrelated to this change)
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings/errors; `oxfmt --check`: clean;
  `git diff --check`: clean; `tsgo:core`: exit 0.

## Still unverified

- Isolated-Gateway live proof (the issue's `models.list` check with a
  ChatGPT subscription OAuth login) was not run here: no subscription
  credentials on this machine. The fix is covered at the materialization
  + thinking-profile boundaries instead; the live check is a
  maintainer-side verification step.

## Environment notes (not part of the change)

- `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` stalls on this VM: after a
  `[vitest-workers] local cache miss` the bun worker goes zombie and
  the runner aborts after 120s of no output (two identical stalls).
  Direct `vitest run` with the same scoped configs completes the same
  suites. No repo files were changed for this.
- This worktree's `node_modules` was copied from the sibling
  `openclaw-203131` worktree (same base) and repaired with
  `pnpm install --prefer-offline`; three missing top-level UI links
  (`@solidjs/vite-plugin`, `solid-js`, `@solidjs/web`) were relinked
  from the existing `.pnpm` store so the vitest configs load.

## What Problem This Solves

A local session offered **Move to cloud…** even when the person opening the menu had no configured cloud profile they could use. On a Gateway with no paired devices either, this opened an empty picker with no way to continue.

## User Impact

The sidebar, Sessions page, and chat header omit **Move to cloud…** when no cloud profile is available to you. A paired device alone does not advertise a cloud move. **New child session**, moves back to the Gateway, and recovery of an existing move are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session menus now use the same profile grants as the destination picker. The Gateway includes a yes/no answer in the roster the UI already loads; opening a context menu does not fetch the device or machine catalog.

prs.title: fix: keep one model’s cooldown deadline off other models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a short API-key block overlaps a longer rate limit on one model, the model picker can show the longer cooldown for the whole provider. Its cached catalog can then keep healthy routes unavailable after the key has recovered.

## User Impact

A rate-limited ClawRouter model keeps its own deadline. Other models on the same key become selectable when the actual key-wide block ends. No configuration change or cooldown reset is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway checked which models were blocked, but included an unrelated model’s deadline when reporting how long a sibling was blocked. It now filters by model before choosing the latest applicable deadline. Account-wide billing and credential blocks remain enforced; no UI or storage changes are needed.

## Evidence

Reproduced through `models.list` with a synthetic 15-hour model rate limit and a one-minute billing block on the shared key. Before the change, the sibling also reported 15 hours. Afterward, it reports one minute and becomes available after the billing block expires; the original model still reports 15 hours. The catalog and auth/fallback expiry suites, targeted Gateway typecheck, lint, and formatting passed. This reproduces the reported symptom, not the original account’s historical state.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: test(android): close owned runtime fixtures after each test
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

The cron guard, device-pairing and approval runtime suites create their own NodeRuntime instances but never hand them to the existing teardown owner. Across 41 tests, those factories create 45 runtimes with independent coroutine scopes and database resources. NodeApp does not own these directly constructed fixtures.

## User Impact

Production behavior and all test assertions are unchanged. Each test now retires its runtime fixtures before Robolectric tears down the sandbox, preventing their background work from escaping the test lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track instances in the existing factories and close them from JUnit teardown through closeNodeRuntimeTestFixture. That helper already owns disconnect, coroutine cancellation/join and database closure. No new cleanup framework, production seam or test case is added; the fix adds 24 net test lines to make lifetime ownership explicit.

## Evidence

- A temporary TestWatcher observed the actual runtime jobs after test teardown. One existing test from each suite failed on the baseline with one active runtime job, then all three passed with the cleanup. The observer cleaned up in finally and is absent from this PR. This proves job retirement, not a measured heap or RSS reduction.
- Both phone flavors compiled and passed all 41 affected tests, with zero failures/errors/skips. JUnit-reported suite times total 9.867 seconds (Play) and 8.717 seconds (ThirdParty); these exclude Gradle/build overhead.
- Kotlin lint and staged-content guards passed on exact tree `6675e6e2dd9a5df0b6c1f37da0680c8ca57cbb08`. Fresh independent source review found no issues and confirmed all assertions are unchanged.
- Full local ClawSweeper review of `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69..23d80eda7101f0bbd2b952ff79be67c41af25ae8` found no actionable correctness or security issues.
- Local tests use isolated fixtures. No live Gateway, credential, permission, dependency or production lifecycle change is claimed. PR-head CI remains the integration gate.

## PR CI

[CI run 44861136241](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44861136241/job/136714909089) completed with one Access 16K setup failure and its aggregate failure. UTP 32.5.1 could not resolve JUnit Platform 1.13.3 and Kotlin 2.2.10 before instrumentation tests ran. The tested merge `b52cacdbd108acaecee8b942764983d7df815006` and main parent `7e5cad36da3525a056b14aca8b9b022e6180bfb7` have identical dependency, repository, wrapper and CI workflow blobs; this PR changes only JVM test teardown. The exact external/cache cause is not established. Other jobs passed or were skipped; failed CI is retained as a gap, separate from the successful local proof.

Recovery: the failed-job retry completed successfully as attempt 2 at the same commit. It was triggered after a fresh scheduled run passed Access with identical dependency, repository, wrapper and workflow blobs. The original failed attempt and its evidence remain recorded above; no source or dependency change was made for the retry.

prs.title: fix: send Telegram media from the selected agent on multi-agent setups
prs.body:
Closes #202794

## What Problem This Solves

On a setup where every agent is configured explicitly (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`), `openclaw message send --channel telegram --media <file>` fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner`, even though the account is bound to one agent and the same command without `--media` sends fine.

## User Impact

Sending a local image or file to Telegram from the CLI works again on multi-agent setups, using the agent the account is bound to. Text-only sends and single-agent setups are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host already selects the agent for the send and hands it to the Telegram action, but the action did not pass it on. Without a session key, staging the attachment then had no owner to resolve. The action now passes the selected agent into the outbound session, as the Discord and Nextcloud Talk plugins already do. The session and media-access setup moves into `action-delivery-context.ts` because `action-runtime.ts` is over its line cap and the ratchet rejects growth.

## Evidence

Scenario: `openclaw message send --channel telegram --account default --target 123 --message "test chart" --media <file in the ops agent workspace> --json`.

Run from source with `pnpm openclaw` against an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port). The config has two agents with explicit ownership (`main`, `ops`), a binding of the `default` Telegram account to `ops`, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "ops"`, as in the report. Telegram's Bot API is a local stand-in (`channels.telegram.apiRoot`) that logs each method it receives, so no bot token or Telegram account was used. Before is this PR's parent commit `504f4a6ed` (Gateway and CLI), after is this PR's head `bdd98b6ff` (Gateway and CLI).

Before:

```text
AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "AgentSelectionRequiredError: ..." } }
```

After:

```text
{ "action": "send", "channel": "telegram", "dryRun": false, "handledBy": "plugin", "messageId": "1",
  "payload": { "ok": true, "messageId": "1", "chatId": "123", "receipt": {} } }
```

The stand-in Bot API logged one `sendPhoto` for the "after" run and none for the "before" run.

- New test `sends local media for the selected agent on an explicit multi-agent fleet` in `action-runtime.test.ts` calls the registered Telegram `send` action with the selected agent and a local image on that fleet. On the base commit it fails with the same `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; with this change it passes.
- `action-runtime.test.ts` and `channel-actions.contract.test.ts` pass (58 tests). `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` on the four changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass, and the pre-commit line-cap ratchet passes.
- Not covered: a real Telegram bot. The repository's Telegram Test Server proof (`telegram-e2e-userbot`) needs credentials from the maintainers' leased pool, which I do not have, so a maintainer would need to run that scenario on this head if it is required before merge.

NodeRuntime stores connection readiness twice: in GatewayConnectionDisplay and in a separate mutable Boolean flow. Every status update must keep both synchronized, while runtime decisions already use the display.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. The ViewModel keeps its Boolean StateFlow API, false initial value, runtime switching and subscription lifecycle. Connection, retry, permission and authentication policies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate runtime Boolean and its write. Derive the existing ViewModel stream from the authoritative display through its existing runtime adapter, and migrate the debug voice harness's two direct reads. Update five UI fixtures to seed the same state the application uses.

- Both phone flavors compiled and passed eight affected suites: 87 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. Kotlin lint and the staged-content/freshness guard passed on exact tree `f1bbefff47f0c6d1471d9bec99b01d0ac5ebab73`.

prs.title: improve(ci): start long upgrade checks before the final validation wave
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two fully drained Full Release Validation (FRV) traces ended on a tool-bridge compatibility upgrade check that waited more than 23 minutes for matrix admission. These are required independent checks, not a reason to remove coverage.

## User Impact

At the existing 48-job hosted cap, replay models **5m36s and 5m32s less total FRV wall time** in those two traces. Two other traces model **zero total benefit**, including the newest one, whose first-hop job is already the longest path. These are conditional scheduling estimates, not measured after-change savings or a universal speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge` to the existing long-job order, after `plugin-update` and before `legacy-operator-state`. Preserve package recovery, first-hop and restart-auth priority, every complete row, baseline identity, timeout, independent retry/failure, fresh-container isolation, current concurrency caps, and stable remainder order. No new planner, cache, timing data, setting, jobs, or runner capacity.

This builds on #198925 (`8656c447df05`, existing first-hop/legacy priority) and #199911 (`f947bdc94981`, early package recovery), rather than replacing their deliberate policy. It is independent of #202688 (48→64 cap); the incremental gain after that change is reported separately below, never added twice. Author simplification: one list entry plus its evidence comment; extend the existing real-CLI regression rather than add another suite. Production +2/-0, tests +3/-1, docs +5/-0.

## Evidence

All four traces have 92/92 successful targeted rows and fully drained parents, but other validation failures mean **none is claimed as passing release qualification**. Durations include runner setup, downloads, test execution, upload and cleanup. Replay uses the base planner order and earliest-free slots; its cap-48 residual versus observation is 0–3 seconds. Preserve that residual and all sibling/collector barriers in both projections.

| Parent / candidate child | Observed matrix | Base48→proposed48 | Total FRV gain at48 | Incremental total gain after64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|[44773914831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44773914831) / [44777975959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959)|3150s|3148→2812s|336s|287s (2633→2346s)|
|[44790287992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44790287992) / [44794544663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663)|3032s|3029→2697s|332s|329s (2556→2227s)|
|[44635836314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44635836314) / [44639105831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44639105831)|2912s|2910→2902s|0s (8s hidden by CI)|0s|
|[44832835993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44832835993) / [44835864437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835864437)|2704s|2704→2704s|0s (first-hop dominates)|0s|

- Candidate44777975959, C=Q `3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22`: matrix17:07:51–18:00:21 UTC Nov20. [Final ACPX row136440786047](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959/job/136440786047) starts17:31:52 (1441s after matrix start), then runs1709s. Internal sibling floor17:39:49; external CI17:33:59; candidate tail44s and parent tail83s. Base parent ends18:02:28; proposed48 projects17:56:52. With64 plus this change, restart-auth2346s becomes the matrix floor, limiting incremental gain to287s.
- Candidate44794544663, C=Q `fae2f8f16fbd335566c2d9aa500887dedef4da8d`: matrix18:49:39–19:40:11. [Final ACPX row136497002115](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663/job/136497002115) starts19:13:13 (1414s admission delay), then runs1618s. Internal sibling floor19:23:17; external19:22:14. Preserve3s residual,51s candidate tail and observed parent tail: proposed48 matrix ends19:34:39,332s earlier. With64 plus this change, first-hop2026.10.1 at2227s becomes the floor.
- Newest candidate44835864437, C=Q `35207ad56a84cc44cd596556955ce73feaf4d5f8`: first-hop2026.9.9 already occupies2704s in the first wave; no ordering-only gain is claimed. Sealed plan digests for this parent and44790287992 match their drained manifests, with no active children or requested cancellation.

### Coverage, capacity and uncertainty

The current-main 93-row output has **identical complete row objects before/after; only order changes**. Historical replays preserve their exact92-row inventory instead of inventing durations for current-only first-hop2026.11.6 and2026.11.10-beta.1; historical2026.9.36 is absent from the current inventory. Consequently these are frozen-workload estimates, not measured forecasts for all93 current rows.

No extra setup or concurrency is introduced. Work may overlap registry/artifact requests differently, so constant complete-job durations and available runners remain assumptions. Retained32-cap sensitivity on the same four duration sets is nonregressing (+141,+310,+17,+9s matrix gains in the table order), not an observed32-way campaign. Placing ACPX after legacy instead would regress one such replay by44s; that ordering was rejected. An unmeasured workload or severe contention can still erase the benefit.

## Proof

The existing real-CLI regression is red on base solely because ACPX rows remain late, then green with this entry. It asserts complete rows including labels, baseline/scenario identity, timeout, old priorities and stable remaining order. No new test case or timing fixture is committed. Changed suite:13 tests,22ms test bodies,274ms Vitest duration,982ms runner wall time.

All 740 tests across six affected planner, baseline, source-preflight, package-acceptance and release-workflow suites pass (134.41s runner wall time). Targeted tooling-test typecheck, two-file type-aware lint, three-file formatting, documentation MDX and `git diff --check` pass. Local independent review is waived by the task owner. No FRV or native campaign was dispatched. Logs are decision evidence, not a post-change runtime benchmark.

**Ready for review, verified November 21, 2026 at 03:26 UTC**, head `93897401daea0182b165e9138a9942deaa1541b7`: [CI44859542084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859542084) and [CodeQL44859541709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859541709) succeeded. Full current check rollup: 48 success, 65 skipped, 1 neutral; no failed or pending checks. GitHub reports OPEN, MERGEABLE, CLEAN. [ClawSweeper completed this exact revision at 03:22:27 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202894#issuecomment-7056571971), with no findings and no before-merge items. Its remaining performance uncertainty is explicitly retained above; RFR does not claim measured production savings or authorize merging.

<details>
<summary>Exact replay inputs and method</summary>

Compare the planner at `684018d110ef6d5e38c9530616a65f74950837fe` with this PR using the input below. For historical replay only, expand `update-first-hop-compat` into the explicit version lanes from `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json` at `3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22`, followed by `update-first-hop-compat-missing-load-path`. This restores the exact measured 92-row inventory; do not remove or invent current production coverage.

```json
{
  "lanes": "release-typed-onboarding doctor-switch update-channel-switch skill-install update-corrupt-plugin upgrade-survivor update-first-hop-compat published-upgrade-survivor root-managed-vps-upgrade update-restart-auth plugins-offline plugin-update plugin-binding-command-escape",
  "upgradeSurvivorBaselines": "openclaw@2026.10.33 openclaw@2026.11.5 openclaw@2026.11.6",
  "upgradeSurvivorScenarios": "base package-publication-recovery package-verification-recovery package-stranded-first-hop legacy-operator-state acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge feishu-channel bootstrap-persona channel-post-core-restore plugin-deps-cleanup configured-plugin-installs custom-plugin-siblings stale-source-plugin-shadow tilde-log-path meeting-transcripts-sqlite versioned-runtime-deps cron-scheduled-authority"
}
```

Fetch all jobs pages from each candidate run (`gh api --paginate --slurp repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/RUN/jobs?per_page=100`). Match each planner label to the final parenthesized label in its targeted-lane job name. Assert 92 matches, 92 successful conclusions, and identical complete row objects before/after. In planner order, assign each full `completed_at - started_at` duration to the earliest-free one of 32/48/64 slots. Compare the maximum slot finish, then retain observed residuals and the sibling/collector barriers above. No duration-weighted or oracle reordering is used. Actual proposed planner output also matches the modeled order. Observed timestamp/ID admission order differs from source order for some ties; the table deliberately uses source planner order on both sides.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(android): give installed skills one data owner
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Installed-skill refreshes wrap their list in a second object, while the decoder and data contract live inside runtime orchestration instead of the existing skill-management owner. Maintaining the installed list therefore requires changes across both responsibilities.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Unknown or failed state remains distinct from a successfully loaded empty list; skill flags, Gateway switching, enable/disable behavior and install verification retain their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the installed-skill contract and decoder into SkillManagement, remove the single-field GatewaySkillsSummary wrapper, and migrate every runtime, ViewModel, UI and test consumer to the list directly. The existing trimmed-string boolean reader moves unchanged to the shared JSON owner so the decoder can reuse it. All allowlist, agent-filter, trust and provenance fields remain intact.

Concurrent policy work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166166 touches these fields; this PR preserves the current policy.

## Evidence

- Both phone flavors compiled and passed six affected suites: 88 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. Kotlin lint and staged-content/freshness guards passed on exact tree `77baf6a26cc0f4418a66046a96c8124dbabb66f0`.
- The five existing skills suites also passed on the frozen baseline before the change. The added decoder contract covers malformed rows, fallback names, missing-item counts, primitive/string flag semantics and install readback.
- Fresh independent source review and full local ClawSweeper review of `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69..6b612cd77be06d81d172d536730aee06106477ad` found no actionable issues.
- Local proof used a byte-identical source tree in an independent checkout. Runtime/UI tests use isolated fixtures; no real Gateway or install is claimed. PR-head CI remains the integration gate.

## PR CI

Published-head [CI run 44859282461, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859282461/attempts/2) passed at unchanged head `6b612cd77be06d81d172d536730aee06106477ad`. All nine executed jobs passed; the remaining 37 were intentionally skipped.

Initial attempt: The Access 16K job in [CI run 44859282461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44859282461/job/136709026864) failed before tests ran: UTP 32.5.1 could not resolve JUnit Platform 1.13.3 and Kotlin 2.2.10. The actual tested merge `ed3a95ba8ccb2f8b1968d36c2de2eb48424e4050` and its main parent `684018d110ef6d5e38c9530616a65f74950837fe` have identical Gradle dependency, repository, wrapper and CI workflow blobs. This is independent of the Kotlin refactor; the exact external/cache cause is not established. The run is now complete: every other non-aggregate job passed or was skipped. Local proof above does not replace those results.

prs.title: feat(sessions): choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automatic idle or daily reset always carries the last six user/assistant messages into the new session, and there is no way to change that number. Some deployments want more continuity after a reset, others want a clean start.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `session.reset.tailMessages` (also in `resetByType` and `resetByChannel` entries) to choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps. The default stays 6, so nothing changes unless the key is set. `0` starts the new session empty. `/new` and `/reset` still always clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tail size was a constant inside the transcript selection. It is now resolved with the rest of the reset policy, so the per-type and per-channel overrides work the same way as `mode`, `atHour` and `idleMinutes`. The four places that write an automatic preserve-tail boundary pass the resolved value: the channel reply path, `openclaw agent`, the gateway agent turn and cron's stale-session rollover.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/config/zod-schema.session-config.ts`: `tailMessages` (integer, at least 0) on the reset policy object, with label and help text.
- `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts`: `SessionResetPolicy.tailMessages`, type override first, then base, then `DEFAULT_RESET_TAIL_MESSAGES = 6`.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-replay.ts` and `session-reset-boundary-event.ts`: the preserve-tail request takes an optional `tailMessages`; omitted means the default. The default constant stays in `transcript-replay.ts`, and `reset-policy.ts` imports it, so the extracted PR wrapper module keeps no new dependency.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `session-hooks.ts`, `src/agents/command/session.ts`, `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-patch.ts`, `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-session-persist.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/session.ts`, `run-session-state.ts`: pass the resolved value. In `session-hooks.ts` the redundant `explicitReason` parameter is dropped: for explicit resets it always equalled `previousReason`, so `session.ts` does not grow.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/session.md`, `docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md`, regenerated config baseline.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `src/config/sessions/session-reset-boundary-event.test.ts`: with 4 turns, the boundary keeps from turn 2 by default, from turn 4 with `2`, from turn 1 with `10`, and nothing with `0`.
  - `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.test.ts`: default 6, base value, chat-type override, channel override, and the schema rejects `-1`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `config:docs:check`: clean. `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` passes.
- Test-line budget: +33 net test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/session-reset-tail-messages.txt`. The tests cover two separate contracts that no existing test covers: the boundary tail for each size, and the policy resolution order (default, base, chat type, channel, negative rejected). The policy cases are one table. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.
- Head `bd7c2b6a778` only moves the default constant and consolidates tests after the live runs below; runtime behavior is unchanged from the proven `891d01a7db3`.
- After merging current `main` (`891d01a7db3`): tsgo checks, `config:docs:check` and the 9 focused session, reply, gateway and cron test files (148 tests) pass again.
- 44 test files that import the changed modules (sessions, reply session, agent command, gateway agent turn, cron isolated agent): 574 passed. One test, `src/cron/isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` "runs a linked current job as a child of its conversation", fails on this macOS machine identically on `main` without this change. `src/config/io.observe-recovery.test.ts` (2 tests) does the same.

Live run against a real Gateway:

- Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1. Candidate: this branch (`e8c6e67a793`), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` and installed with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz>` (`openclaw --version`: `2026.10.9 (e8c6e67)`, tgz sha256 `ecf411c1…da63`). The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, which logs every request body, so no provider key is used.
- Config: `session.reset = { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 1 }`, plus `tailMessages` per round.
- Each round: `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof-<round>` sends turns 1–4 to a fresh session, waits 80 s, then sends turn 5. The table shows the user/assistant messages the model received on turn 5, the first turn after the idle reset. Per-turn runtime-context messages are left out.

| `tailMessages` | Model input on turn 5 | Reset event |
|---|---|---|
| not set | T2, A, T3, A, T4, A, **T5** (6 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 2 |
| `2` | T4, A, **T5** (2 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 4 |
| `0` | **T5** (none kept) | `reason: idle`, no `firstKeptEntryId` |
| `20` | T1, A, T2, A, T3, A, T4, A, **T5** (all 8 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 1 |

In every round, turn 5 stayed in the same session id and the transcript has one `reset` event between turn 4 and turn 5, so the difference comes from the reset tail and not from a new session.

Upgrade from the latest stable release, with existing settings and transcripts:

- A second clean VM with published `openclaw@2026.10.10` (`7dc3350`, the `latest` dist-tag). The same idle policy without `tailMessages`. Turns 1–4 were sent to `agent:main:proof-upgrade` on 2026.10.10. Before the update, 2026.10.10 rejects the new key: `session.reset: Unrecognized key: "tailMessages"`.
- Updated with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz>` to this branch merged with current `main` (`891d01a7db3`, tgz sha256 `73e97dcb…256d`).
- Results:

| Check | Before update (2026.10.10) | After update (candidate) |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw config validate` | valid | valid |
| `session.reset` | `{mode: idle, idleMinutes: 1}` | unchanged |
| Session `8e82ddde` | 16 events, 4 user messages | unchanged: same id, 16 events, 4 user messages |

- Compared with `openclaw.json.pre-update`, the updated config differs only in `wizard.*` and `meta.*` bookkeeping and in `plugins.entries.memory-core.enabled`, which `main`'s doctor adds during any update. This change does not touch that key.
- Then `openclaw config set session.reset.tailMessages 2` was run, and turn 5 was sent to the pre-upgrade session. The model received `T4, A, T5`. The transcript of the same session id gained one `reset` event, `reason: idle`, first kept turn 4. The setting applies to a transcript written before the upgrade.

Both VMs were purged afterwards.

prs.title: fix(ui): skip archive exit animations outside the sidebar viewport
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving a session group that is already outside the sidebar viewport could temporarily bring its fading copy into view. The virtual list repositioned itself for the removal while the copy kept occupying space, moving the neighboring visible row down by 32 px.

## User Impact

The visible rows stay in place when an offscreen group is archived. A group that is still partly visible continues to animate, including when only a child is visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session window already compensates for removing offscreen rows. Start an archive exit only when the entire tree's rectangle intersects the sidebar viewport, so there is no invisible copy competing with that adjustment.

## Evidence

[The Chromium failure also appeared in the Usage PR's CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44964363782/job/137030541268). An isolated Chromium reproduction on main showed the same +32 px displacement after two layout frames. At the same scroll position, the first neighboring row moved from 5 to 37 px before and stayed at 5 px after.

The regression failed on main and passed with the correction. Six archive cases, two virtual-window cases and 17 archive/Undo/stability browser scenarios passed in Chromium on Studio. The UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting also passed. The partial-visibility case explicitly exercises a clipped parent with a visible child.

![Before: the archived copy enters the viewport and moves its neighbor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/394cc3b7-053b-41c3-9bc0-dd4ad7f37dfa)

![After: the neighbor stays at its original position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e026fdf-6ab5-49a8-bdcc-3677e798c63d)

prs.title: improve: show complete 30-day Usage reports sooner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When saved usage summaries are missing, opening Usage for one agent can show partial totals for tens of seconds before the full month is ready. Switching to a date preset also waits 400 ms before the request starts, even though both dates are already known.

## User Impact

User impact: In five matched local browser runs, the complete 30-day report appeared in **6.65 s instead of 30.61 s (4.61× faster)**. The first usable rows appeared sooner, partial totals stayed labeled, and the final totals and rankings were unchanged. This is a cold-backfill improvement, not a 4.61× speedup for visits with existing summaries. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backfill used to sleep for at least a millisecond after every small page, even when Linux confirmed the data was already in memory. Queued background work now yields without that timer when no wait is due, accounts for small payloads together, and settles its remaining byte budget before returning. Physical or unmeasured disk reads retain conservative pacing. Direct foreground refreshes do not opt in.

The refresh queue also skips windows it can already prove fresh. Loading context for visible rows no longer repeats a full aggregation unless the filter uses that context. Session progress no longer refetches unrelated provider plans, and a preset applies both dates at once without changing how manual date edits work.

## Evidence

A trusted click in the compiled Control UI opened a real Gateway report for one agent. The synthetic store contained 6,000 session families across four agents. All five candidate runs matched the independent ledger: **9,866,184 tokens, $210.82, 251 active families, 30 daily buckets and 50 ranked rows**. All 6,858 transcript windows had saved summaries by shutdown.

| Click to usable result | Baseline median | Candidate median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Missing summaries: first labeled partial and usable rows | 1.94 s | 1.30 s |
| Missing summaries: complete report and usable rows | 30.61 s | 6.65 s |
| Revisit after backfill | 43.6 ms | 42.3 ms |

Every cold pair improved; the slowest complete report fell from 30.90 s to 7.20 s. Median provider-plan requests fell from 35 to 1, and Gateway CPU during the cold open fell from 21.81 to 14.87 CPU-seconds.

**Other interactions and tradeoff:** In a separate five-pair run of the pacing candidate, an already-summarized first open changed modestly (808 → 752 ms), and returning from 7d to 30d took 38 ms instead of 437 ms. During backfill all 40 matched foreground history reads per build returned the expected 64 messages; their p95 increased slightly (44.8 → 47.2 ms). A real 8 MiB disk read still requested 500 ms of pacing. These are local Linux/Chromium results, not production latency estimates.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce and inspect</summary>

The primary comparison used baseline `9aae2826269d` and tested revision `5e40bd98e5491`. Build both clean checkouts with `pnpm build sourcePerformance` and `pnpm ui:build`, then follow **Real-Gateway Usage opens** in [`scripts/README.md`](../blob/HEAD/scripts/README.md#real-gateway-usage-opens). Seed with `--unprojected` and compare with `--pairs 5 --deadline-ms 180000`. Use separate runs for `--preset` on a projected fixture and `--foreground-history` during backfill. Cold means a fresh Gateway and browser context, not a flushed OS page cache.

The final build also passed a real Model providers open and explicit refresh. Local verification included 484 Model providers and Usage tests, targeted Gateway/worker tests, typechecks, formatting, and scoped lint. No full local CI run. Both base and candidate post-build reports had the same pre-existing CSS-size and chat boot request budget warnings; no limits were raised.

</details>

### Independent checks before landing

The timed comparison will use isolated built Gateways and the same 6,000-family synthetic data for main and the integrated PR. Run five alternating pairs; keep missing-summary opens, completed-summary revisits, and 7d → 30d presets separate. Compare median, p95, sample spread, Gateway CPU, and RPC counts. Every completed report must match the independent ledger and ranked rows; partial totals must stay labeled.

During missing-summary backfill, verify ordinary history reads return the right session and all 64 messages, and compare latency only for cadence slots that overlap backfill in both roles. Verify the provider plan is not reread on session progress, manual date edits remain debounced, and a completed preset refresh preserves its requested interval. Verify agent visibility and context-dependent filters separately. A reproducible regression in correctness or foreground responsiveness blocks landing.

The Linux resident-read speedup is evaluated separately from macOS, where residency is unavailable and conservative pacing still applies. For the cold Linux fixture, the complete result should arrive materially sooner (at least 2×), without extra work or an identifiable regression in warm or foreground flows. On macOS the requirement is equivalent correctness and no persistent regression, not the same residency speedup. Record actual wall time, counters, and limitations for each host.

### Independent Studio results

The timing comparison ran production Gateway and UI builds from main `663669a43b29` and integrated tree `465ae4aa3e6a` (published source `04eef5235bf9`) on arm64 macOS 27.2, Node 26.13.1 and Chromium 156. No external providers or live data were used. Each primary comparison used five alternating pairs on the same 6,000-family fixture. All reports matched the independent ledger, daily buckets and ranked rows; partial totals stayed labeled.

| Studio workload | Main median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No saved summaries: complete report | 36.09 / 38.72 s | 36.16 / 37.28 s |
| 7d → 30d preset | 469 / 502 ms | 134 / 303 ms |
| History reads during backfill | 9.0 / 46.9 ms | 8.4 / 45.6 ms |
| Warm revisit in an already loaded browser (16 per build) | 97.3 / 146.0 ms | 48.0 / 146.8 ms |

On macOS the first useful rows without summaries arrived in 2.02 s instead of 3.31 s at the median, and provider-plan requests fell from 36–37 to one. The cold run is the portable fallback path; the Linux resident-read result above is the author's separate comparison. Preset changes still issued one session usage RPC and no longer issued a provider RPC. All 40 matched history reads on each build ran wholly inside backfill and returned the expected session and all 64 messages; none were skipped or censored.

The original fresh-process revisit showed a p95 of 111.9 → 150.0 ms; after a symmetric Back settle it was 111.6 → 130.5 ms. A same-build fresh-process control varied substantially (median 129.7 → 42.2 ms). The repeated warm diagnostic kept each browser and Gateway loaded and measured WebSocket send and paint on the renderer clock. The slower tail did not persist in that setup; neither the original slowdown nor a durable warm speedup is established.

A separate restart stress used two concurrent logical agent scopes on a 600-family fixture. Each wrote 50 durable checkpoints before a clean process restart, then finished the remaining 121 and 122 windows without cross-scope totals or duplicate discovery work. This did not interrupt a transaction.

The original Studio build passed 116 focused tests. Follow-up `bf87fedbd81a` shares the existing mtime/generation check, fixes the type of the preset test fixture, and removes obsolete ratchet exceptions. The exact failing typecheck and identity ratchet, scoped lint and formatting, and 78 targeted tests passed on that patch.

**Final exact-source smoke:** Production Gateway and WebUI built from the final source `bf87fedbd81a`, integrated over the same pinned base as `bd1f503877dd`. In fresh 6,000-family fixtures the missing-summary report labeled partial totals and completed with the exact independent ledger and rows. Each of eight matched history slots per build returned the expected session and 64 messages, with no errors or missed slots. The projected 7d → 30d flow also matched its ledger; the candidate made one session request and no additional provider request. These were correctness smokes (one pair per case), not a new performance comparison.

**CI attribution:** The only failed job in the final attempt, apart from its aggregate gate, was [the offscreen archive animation test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44964363782/job/137030541268). Its test, sidebar renderer, window and CSS files are identical in the tested merge and its main parent. The same 32 px assertion reproduced in an isolated main Chromium run. [#203368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203368) carries the separate correction.

Requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/be791297-37f7-4808-b3f2-80de77c9c1ee)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: refactor(android): move model availability policy out of chat UI
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Android chat sending and Wear handling import the chat picker to use shared model identity and availability rules. Keeping those rules in the UI makes non-UI callers depend on presentation code.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Model selection, unavailable-model messages, and send-blocking decisions retain the existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the three unchanged policy helpers into the existing model catalog owner and migrate all callers. The picker keeps its presentation and search behavior. This removes the controller and Wear dependencies on the picker without adding a file or abstraction. Production code grows by three import lines; the benefit is the removed dependency edges. Nullable controller identities and bounded Wear input parsing keep their distinct contracts.

## Evidence

- Both phone flavors compiled. Existing model-picker, controller model-selection, Wear proxy, and composer-layout suites passed: 216 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. App Kotlin lint and staged-content/freshness guards passed.
- Exact source tree `e6a775b8224c778ce433a8b3ff2eb8be4db3dd00` matches signed commit `0caff03a2f74c485f5c7da1acfde3c7927157b4d`. Local proof used an independent checkout at the frozen baseline; PR-head CI remains the integration gate.
- Independent source review verified unchanged helper bodies and import-only caller migrations. Full local ClawSweeper review of `6b0df8b93610b320210488d93e6e205aafb84e69..0caff03a2f74c485f5c7da1acfde3c7927157b4d` completed with no findings.

Gradle disabled that repository and could not resolve UTP dependencies; native tests did not execute. Every other non-aggregate job in the completed attempt passed or was skipped. No dependency, repository, or workflow inputs change in this PR.

prs.title: fix(telegram): send attachments from the selected agent
prs.body:
Closes #202794.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Gateway with explicit ownership and two agents, a Telegram send from the CLI can deliver text but fail while preparing an attachment. The durable send loses the agent selected by the caller.

## User Impact

A CLI send can stage attachments using the selected agent's workspace media policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the host-selected agent from the Telegram action context to the existing durable-send session context.

## Evidence

Windows, Node 24.22.3, and an isolated loopback Gateway. Built the CLI with `pnpm build qaRuntime` on base `9bb091e873e4` and again with the three independent patches. The changed Telegram production files in the repaired build match this PR.

Ran the built `openclaw message send` CLI twice against the running Gateway. The Telegram plugin sent Bot API HTTP requests to a loopback fixture with a synthetic token. The text-only run was the control and the attachment was a 68-byte PNG in the selected agent's workspace.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default --target 12345 --message fixture --json
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default --target 12345 --message fixture --json --media <workspace>/pixel.png
```

| Build | Text exit and requests | Attachment exit and requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | `0`, one `sendMessage` | `1`, `AgentSelectionRequiredError`, zero upload requests |
| Fix | `0`, one `sendMessage` | `0`, one multipart `sendPhoto` carrying all 68 bytes with the same SHA-256 as the original file |

The regression invokes the registered action and a loopback HTTP receiver. On the base it failed with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` while staging the file. This PR is a draft pending a Telegram Test Server capture. The local proof establishes the CLI-to-Gateway-to-Bot-API request path.

The final registered action regression passed on the patched source. The two related outbound suites passed 20 cases and the Telegram action contract passed 16 cases.

```sh
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'uploads media using the selected agent'
```

### Hosted Telegram receipt

On 2026-11-21, the built OpenClaw CLI sent one synthetic 160 × 120 PNG through an isolated Gateway with two explicitly owned agents and the selected bot account bound to `ops`. The relay verified that the bot and exact dedicated group matched, checked the uploaded file against the source bytes, and forwarded the multipart request to Telegram's hosted production Bot API.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs message send --channel telegram --account default \
  --target '<test-group-id>' --message 'OPENCLAW_202868_FEB497BE' \
  --json --media '<synthetic-png>'
```

```text
CLI exit: 0
Telegram method: sendPhoto
Telegram HTTP status: 200
Source PNG bytes: 42215
Source SHA-256: d09291df46dd559f166d2ea7aa743ecabe43c62a121f624e6fcc83b1da979a42
Photo sizes in Telegram's message receipt: 2
Telegram Desktop: received photo with caption OPENCLAW_202868_FEB497BE
```

At 10:48 UTC+08, Telegram Desktop displayed the incoming photo and the same caption in the dedicated test group. The previous base-failing result comes from the local Gateway and loopback Bot API run. This section adds a post-fix delivery observation on Telegram's production service. The separate Telegram Test Server run is still pending.
