prs.title: fix(cli): reject a blank working directory when editing an exit-triggered automation
prs.body:
Related: #129714

## What Problem This Solves

An edit that supplies an empty or whitespace-only `--on-exit-cwd` can succeed and replace the saved schedule without the requested working directory. The watched command would then use the default directory.

## User Impact

An invalid directory value stops the edit before any automation settings change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate `--on-exit-cwd` at the edit command boundary, using the same nonblank check as automation creation.

## Evidence

Windows, Node 24.22.3, and an isolated loopback Gateway. Built the CLI with `pnpm build qaRuntime` on base `9bb091e873e4` and again with the three independent patches, including this PR's initial commit `bd32067ccefe`. The follow-up reuses the existing `parseCronStringOption` validator for the same guard. The registered Commander regression passed again after that follow-up.

Created a disabled `every` automation. Ran this edit and read the saved record through `cron.get` in the same Gateway.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs automations edit <id> --on-exit 'node --version' --on-exit-cwd ' ' --json
```

| Case | Edit exit | Saved schedule |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Base | 0 | Changed from `every` to `on-exit` with no `cwd` |
| Fix | 1 | Original `every` schedule retained |
| Fix, valid directory control | 0 | `on-exit` with the supplied directory |

The fixed CLI returned `--on-exit-cwd must not be blank`. The job stayed disabled during the proof.

The new Commander regression failed on the base because the edit resolved successfully. It also checks that the rejected command makes no Gateway RPC.

All 78 cases in the focused CLI suites passed on the repaired source. The compiled runtime and touched-file formatting also passed.

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/schedule-options.positional.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/schedule-options.onexit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.body:
Related: #168163

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw automations add '@daily' …` rejects the schedule as an invalid `--at` value. The same Gateway accepts `--cron '@daily'`.

## User Impact

The positional alias and the `--cron` spelling create the same repeating schedule, including its timezone.

## Why This Change Was Made

Send positional strings that start with `@` through the existing cron expression validator. Croner still decides which aliases are valid.

| Base, positional | 1 | CLI returned `Invalid --at` before creation |
| Base and fix, `--cron '@daily' --message fixture` | 0 | `{"kind":"cron","expr":"@daily","tz":"Asia/Taipei"}` |
| Fix, positional | 0 | `{"kind":"cron","expr":"@daily","tz":"Asia/Taipei"}` |

The new regression failed on the base with `Invalid --at`.

prs.title: refactor(android): keep Talk route policy with its parser
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk configuration parsing depends on setup-readiness code that imports the parser back. Its route value also owns presentation text used only by the Talk status display. This makes the routing contract depend on its consumers.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Talk selects the same native/relay routes and displays the same status text, including existing fallback behavior for older Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the model fallback predicate private to the configuration parser, and put route descriptions beside the status presentation owner. Remove the reverse dependency and preserve the enum and decision order. Existing direct predicate assertions now exercise the real parser boundary. Production code is four lines smaller and test code eight lines smaller. Native localization regeneration changes only three source-location records; IDs and text stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- Both phone flavors compiled and passed the existing Talk config, setup-readiness and manager suites: 138 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. App Kotlin lint and staged-content/freshness checks passed.

prs.title: fix: match the web first-run setup to the Mac welcome
prs.body:
Closes #202132

## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh install, the web dashboard on main chooses and tests an AI connection automatically. Users can’t choose what to try first, and a failed connection shows the Gateway’s full error.

## User Impact

The web setup follows the Mac welcome flow through **Welcome to OpenClaw**, **Where should your assistant run?**, and **Connect your AI**.

- **ChatGPT** tests a detected Codex login. If the login is unavailable or the test fails, the card offers **Sign in with ChatGPT**.
- **Claude** offers Claude Code when detected and keeps Claude API-key entry available. The same key option is available under **Another provider**.
- **Run a model locally** offers detected models, local server setup, and downloads. OpenClaw tests the exact model selected during preparation, including an installed Ollama model that is idle.
- **Another provider** offers API keys, other sign-ins, and detected connections.

**Check again** refreshes the list. A successful test saves the selected model and shows **You're all set!**. Failures show a short message with the Gateway error under **Show details**. Setup keeps an existing configured model.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard discovers providers without testing them, then starts the existing Gateway wizard for the selected connection. First-run setup and Model Setup share the handoff from preparation to activation. The Claude card offers the same API-key form independently of CLI detection, so a failed login leaves a recovery path. The ChatGPT card can reuse the existing Codex login on the Gateway host.

## Evidence

| Flow | main (`d77a6d28a6`) | This head (`464979947f`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose an idle Ollama model | First-run setup relies on automatic discovery, which lists loaded Ollama models. | With a real Gateway and Ollama, the dashboard prepared the selected unloaded model, verified it, and saved that exact model as the default. |
| Recover from a signed-out Claude CLI | The dashboard tests a detected connection automatically and shows its failure details. | The Claude card keeps its API-key entry available after a failed CLI test. The Anthropic API key also appears under **Another provider**. |

The main screenshot uses a mock Gateway. The candidate screenshots come from the packaged Control UI in the VM. Claude Code was signed out. The browser accepted synthetic key input through both recovery paths. The regression tests cover submitting the key and completing setup.

| main | This head |
| --- | --- |
| ![First-run setup automatically checks a connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12cc96d6a097981b1da22bb84542d9be0de99bb/images/2026/11/0d226443-2664-425f-86f0-1b3766706e78.png) | ![The Claude card shows an API-key field after the CLI login fails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9b75494d8e49b21632465740aaf0285deb4024d1/images/2026/11/974aa30e-b6ac-4196-8f71-cd7c0c66b139.png) |

| main with the automatic test marked | This head with the recovery field marked |
| --- | --- |
| ![Automatic connection test highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9b75494d8e49b21632465740aaf0285deb4024d1/images/2026/11/2c959286-b1e2-45ad-9c20-775aecd8adb0.png) | ![API-key recovery field highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9b75494d8e49b21632465740aaf0285deb4024d1/images/2026/11/de611efb-4372-4655-b2e1-783ba7a0c831.png) |

![Anthropic API key selected under Another provider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9b75494d8e49b21632465740aaf0285deb4024d1/images/2026/11/63b6f43b-9966-4ab2-bac6-6550aacfa598.png)

### Stable upgrade on macOS

A private arm64 macOS VM ran the published `v2026.11.6` Gateway with synthetic saved state. The native `openclaw update` command installed the package built from this head into the same npm prefix and state directory. The candidate Gateway reached readiness.

| Saved data | Stable `v2026.11.6` | Candidate `464979947f` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default model | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` | Same |
| Auth profiles | `anthropic:upgrade-primary` and `anthropic:upgrade-backup`, both API-key profiles | Same IDs, provider, type, and configured profile entries |
| Codex `appServer.homeScope` | `user` | `user` |

The source package reports the checkout’s version label `2026.11.5`. Its installed build metadata identifies the exact candidate commit.

### Tests

- 221 focused UI tests and five Control UI browser scenarios passed. Coverage includes both Claude key recovery routes and exact activation of an idle Ollama model absent from discovery.
- UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and docs MDX passed. The packaged candidate passed the tarball integrity check.

prs.title: fix: prepare high-resolution chat images before upload
prs.body:
Related: #198250
Related: #137469 (hydration-failure policy unchanged)

## Scope and Current Finding

This patch prepares supported JPEG/static PNG attachments when bytes or dimensions exceed browser preparation targets. **The synthetic comparison does not reproduce a downstream delivery failure: pinned baseline and corrected code both deliver the image successfully to the mock provider.** The prior claim that the fixture was unsuitable for downstream decoding is not supported by this executed proof.

The original installed-version loader incident is separate evidence. The current pinned upstream synthetic baseline succeeds, so this PR demonstrates browser preparation policy, not a reproduced downstream delivery repair.

Whether below-byte-limit, above-4096px images should be reencoded in the browser remains an owner policy decision. Do not interpret the preparation-width regression as a demonstrated delivery bug fix.

## Behavior

Bounded header reads feed the existing serialized resize worker; eligible images are reduced to 4096px longest side. Byte-valid images above the browser JPEG 40MP/PNG 25MP decode budget now pass through unchanged, preserving server-supported uploads. Above-budget images requiring byte reduction still reject before browser decode. No backend limit changes.

Original files are not overwritten. Existing file-name/MIME handling, cancellation, encoded-byte and batch reservations remain in place; this is not a claim that reencoding preserves embedded metadata. JPEG marker scans are bounded; unsupported SOF encodings reject explicitly. APNGs needing resize are not flattened. Other formats and the no-limit bypass remain unchanged.

## Executed Evidence

Product head: `5ebf4fbb5e522e409ac13b529e90f2f23717e692`.
Base: `19082a44a49109a0d93645b68caa0cb6a10b8837`.
[Comparison run](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44962049979), tooling SHA `acd57051623e4b2b19689760fe8b0da3b7fdf5d1`. Hosted formatting output was reflected exactly; all five product-source SHA256 values match the tested candidate.

- 20 Chromium tests passed: high-pixel file/data-URL preparation, orientation/portrait, bounded/corrupt headers, APNG preservation, worker/input behavior, and byte-valid 8000×6000 JPEG/5120×10472 PNG pass-through.
- Lint/format, eight UI test-type shards, allocation (+228/400), max-lines and both runtime builds passed.
- Real WebChat picker, data-URL paste and file drop passed through real Gateway to the fixed-response mock provider. Assertions require one image capture, independent decoding with expected aspect/pixels and bounded dimensions/bytes, unchanged original and assistant-only final reply.
- Pinned baseline picker delivery also passed. Fixture: 8160×4590 JPEG, 220315 bytes, SHA256 `8922a206ede73c00cfbd45416b9b478f8c56a86741a6adbff7094db3b0b40a49`; Chromium canvas solid #2468ac, JPEG quality 0.9. Browser width changes 8160→4096; this is not a downstream failure reproduction.
- The retained corrected paste capture decoded to 1200×675, 22924 bytes, RGBA [35,104,171,255]. Some compact annotation tails truncate later records; full successful assertion execution is evidenced by exit 0, not a claim that every raw record was retained.
- Prior valid lifecycle/admission evidence covers cancellation, timeout, custody and ordering. Prior production/full-tree unused scans found 0/0; this follow-up changes no imports, files or graph.

All fixtures are synthetic. This is mock-provider transport/image proof, not live-model vision-quality or phone proof. Normal upstream CI remains independent and was pending after this push.

<details>
<summary>Prior failures and resource limits</summary>

Earlier [phase 2](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44956221862) failed at a stale private readiness selector before image exercise. The [next run](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44958218912) reached a 4096px preview but failed with zero matching provider captures; its unscoped reply locator could match the user's prompt. The current harness uses public session readiness/navigation and assistant-only reply selection, then actual provider capture. Those previous failures are not represented as passes.

The earlier browser baseline failed its 4096px preparation assertion with 8160px; current real-Gateway baseline success limits that finding to preparation behavior. Initial lint/format/accounting failures were corrected in the retained earlier runs.

A 64MP experiment peaked at 1510352 KiB RSS/840276 KiB PSS across Chromium including fixture generation; it did not justify 64MP browser admission. Prior 40MP probe whole-tree PSS peaks: baseline 408591 KiB, fixture generation 668023 KiB, fixture-retained 396452 KiB, preparation/output verification 650231 KiB, settled 476453 KiB. Preparation RSS 1314848 KiB. These are approximate whole-browser phases, not decoder-only allocation; shared pages/retained fixture overhead overlap. Successful hosted decoding does not establish low-memory-device or cross-browser safety. That unchanged bounded worker evidence was reused, not rerun.

Current pinned-base and candidate builds have identical CSS warnings: 344811 B gzip vs 337312 B ceiling; 1781668 B raw vs 1740234 B; largest 58551 B gzip vs 58315 B. These warnings are demonstrated pre-existing in this comparison, not dismissed as harmless. Both builds exit 0.

</details>

## Review

Manual static review covered the complete five-file patch, callers/reservations, cleanup, header bounds, cancellation, no-limit behavior and regressions, plus the two-file compatibility follow-up. Local Autoreview/ClawSweeper were unavailable in the qualified route; no automated-review clearance is claimed. Independent maintainer review and normal CI remain applicable.

prs.title: improve: shorten WAL pins during cold transcript archival
prs.body:
Related: #200076

## What Problem This Solves

Preparing a large cold transcript keeps its read snapshot open while decoding, publishing, syncing, and rereading each archive chunk. This does not block the writer, but it pins the WAL and delays reset, increasing subsequent checkpoint work.

## User Impact

Cold archival releases its read snapshot earlier while producing identical archives. On the existing 50,000-event fixture, median snapshot hold time drops 29.3%, from 4.851 s to 3.429 s. No schema, config, environment, dependency, writer, or hot-to-cold flip changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot still reads, JSON-encodes, compresses, and hashes every chunk. It retains the compressed buffers alongside the existing metadata. After the snapshot closes, each chunk follows the original decode-verify → publish → file-verify order. Encoding limits, recursive splitting, and pass-budget errors stay inside the snapshot. The writer still performs its existing session revalidation before committing.

A later publication/verification failure rejects preparation and commits nothing. Cleanup ownership is unchanged: `publishEncodedSessionTranscriptArchive` and `trackSqliteArchiveWorkerCleanup` handle staging files. Already-published cold files can remain unreferenced, as explicitly documented in the cold-storage retention contract; ordinary disk-budget pruning does not delete them. There is no existing orphan-chunk sweep to claim or extend here. A retry can reuse identical content-addressed files. No new cleanup or consistency check was added.

Production grows by **6 net lines**: the compressed buffer array, retention, and the post-snapshot loop/comment. The additional benchmark code provides opt-in stage profiling without production instrumentation; the focused regression adds 44 lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before measurement: use the existing synthetic 50,000-event / 220,291,661-byte fixture; stop if decode verification, publication, and file verification account for less than 20% of the baseline snapshot. Otherwise compare five alternating baseline/candidate fresh-process runs, requiring shorter snapshot holds and identical chunk SHA-256 values and archive metadata, with memory reported. The OS page cache is warm from the benchmark's existing pre-measurement digest; “cold” describes transcript storage, not a cold filesystem cache.

### Initial breakdown

Baseline `eac1324110867ef3c37f61d00e1c99d967a575fa`; times are milliseconds. The initial measurement used temporary timers around the unchanged statements; the repeat uses the included `--snapshot-profile` loader. Profiling overhead is excluded from the alternating comparison below.

| Inside snapshot | Initial | Reproducible profiler repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native row reads (including SQLite payload decompression) | 2697.644 | 3353.066 |
| JSON encoding and envelope assembly | 495.803 | 521.578 |
| zstd compression | 63.750 | 65.303 |
| Chunk SHA-256 | 0.769 | 0.796 |
| Decode verification | 558.838 | 585.828 |
| Publication (write/fsync/link/directory sync/internal readback) | 539.497 | 434.554 |
| Separate file verification | 1.512 | 1.674 |
| Other control/schema/query-building/timer overhead | 129.534 | 132.038 |
| **Snapshot total** | **4487.347** | **5094.838** |
| **Movable stages** | **1099.847 (24.51%)** | **1022.056 (20.06%)** |

Both measured runs clear the requested 20% threshold.

### Five alternating pairs, without stage instrumentation

Fresh copies of the same closed fixture; one baseline then one candidate per pair; run serially. Apple M3 Ultra, 512 GiB RAM, Node v26.12.1. Recorded one-minute host load ranged from 19.98 to 33.86, so the observed spread is included.

| Metric | Before median | Before max | After median | After max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot hold, ms | 4851.053 | 4904.111 | 3429.372 | 3772.077 |
| Complete preparation, ms | 4899.007 | 4951.498 | 4234.544 | 4616.213 |
| RSS increase from preparation entry to return, MiB | 238.829 | 265.688 | 163.842 | 190.330 |
| Process peak RSS through preparation, MiB | 1109.859 | 1113.438 | 884.000 | 913.297 |

Snapshot samples (before → after, ms): 4851.053 → 3772.077; 4518.085 → 3405.281; 4275.216 → 3241.668; 4904.111 → 3429.372; 4860.802 → 3456.215. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the reported maximum.

Peak retained compressed buffers: **1,011,884 bytes (0.965 MiB), 14 chunks**, compared with one chunk at a time before (largest 84,405 bytes). Compression remains inside the snapshot. RSS is measured with `process.memoryUsage().rss` before/after preparation; process peak uses `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` and includes earlier import/digest work. It is not a heap-allocation measurement.

All ten runs produced exactly equal prepared archive metadata, chunk metadata, and chunk SHA-256 values. Snapshot-only mode fixes `Date.now()` so `archived_at` is also identical. The ordered manifest SHA-256 is `19b27f7b16387c43f64a750d9916ee210489d3c9cd6e0b6fd9d3f868b9a00ed5`; the production publication/verification path validates the actual files.

### Reproduction

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --prepare --state-dir <new-seed>
# Use a fresh copy of the seed for each invocation.
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --snapshot-only --snapshot-profile --source-root <baseline-checkout> --state-dir <fresh-profile-copy>
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --snapshot-only --source-root <baseline-checkout> --state-dir <fresh-baseline-copy>
```

prs.title: fix(plugins): warn when a manifest stops an enabled standalone plugin file from starting with the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #202830

## What Problem This Solves

An enabled plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` starts with the Gateway while it has no manifest (#171330). Once an `openclaw.plugin.json` that declares no `activation` sits beside it, it silently stops starting unless its config activates it. A plugin that only registers hooks, such as a `before_tool_call` tool policy, then never loads, while `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor` keep showing it as enabled with no warning.

## User Impact

User impact: operators get a warning naming the plugin and the fix (`set activation.onStartup to true …, or false to keep it lazy`) wherever plugin diagnostics already appear. Which plugins load does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest registry is where a manifestless standalone file gets its synthetic `onStartup: true`, so the same place now warns when an explicitly enabled (`entries.<id>.enabled` or `allow`) standalone file has a real manifest that declares no `activation` at all. Any declared trigger (`onStartup` either way, `onCapabilities`, `onChannels`, …) silences it, since the author then chose how it starts. Plugins that policy keeps inactive (`plugins.enabled: false`, `deny`, an allowlist that leaves them out) get no warning; the adjacent `channelConfigs` metadata warning now shares that check.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** one repro script run unchanged on throwaway Gateways: a hook-only plugin file whose `before_tool_call` blocks `session_status`, enabled through `plugins.entries`, called through `POST /tools/invoke`.

| Manifest beside the file | Runtime (`plugins.list` RPC), main → PR | `plugins inspect` / `doctor`, main | `plugins inspect` / `doctor`, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |
| without `activation` | `unloaded` → `unloaded` (200, tool ran) | no warning | **warning on both** |
| with `activation.onStartup: true` | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |
| with `activation.onCapabilities: ["hook"]`, no `onStartup` | `active` → `active` (403 blocked) | no warning | no warning |

Warning text, as printed by `plugins inspect` (and by `doctor` under `[config] warnings: plugins.entries.hook-probe:`):

```
standalone plugin file has a manifest that declares no activation, so it starts with the Gateway only when its config activates it (registering hooks does not); set activation.onStartup to true to keep starting it with the Gateway, or false to keep it lazy
```

Apart from these two lines the main (`dce3c29`) and PR outputs are identical across all four phases, so load behavior is unchanged.

Tested on `4ebe01004e` (based on `dce3c29`; merges cleanly onto current main `684018d110`, which has not touched either file since).

- Tests: a table in `manifest-registry.diagnostics.test.ts`: warns for a file enabled through `entries` or `allow` whose manifest declares no activation; silent for `onStartup: false`, `onCapabilities: ["hook"]`, a disabled entry, `plugins.enabled: false`, `deny`, and an allowlist that excludes it. The warning cases fail on main and pass here; lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude) on the first commit (`cdbaeee892`), clean; the two follow-up commits address ClawSweeper's findings (accurate wording, no warning for policy-inactive plugins or manifests that declare any activation).

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Why a warning rather than a behavior change: the docs (`docs/plugins/manifest/capabilities.md`) say leaving `onStartup` out no longer startup-loads a plugin, so making manifest-bearing files start again would contradict the documented contract. The gap is that nothing connects the two states for an operator. #117243 asked for a broader exclusion diagnostic and was closed as documented; this PR covers only the transition #171330 introduced, where the same file's startup behavior flips when a manifest is added, and needs no startup-plan data.

Not covered: installed (non-`load.paths`) plugins whose manifest has no trigger that can match. Detecting those needs the startup plan and per-trigger reasoning, so it is left to maintainers.

Repro script: four phases (no manifest, manifest without `activation`, manifest with `onStartup: true`, manifest with only `onCapabilities: ["hook"]`), each restarting the Gateway and recording the boot line's plugin list, a `gateway_start` hook log line, `/tools/invoke session_status`, the `plugins.list` RPC runtime state, `plugins list`, `plugins inspect` and `doctor --non-interactive`. The probe also carries the usual `record-missing` provenance warning in every phase, unrelated to this change.

</details>

prs.title: fix(templates): preserve Unicode in template draft inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When drafting a Template from an agent, an emoji or multilingual text in the agent inventory can turn into replacement characters if its UTF-8 bytes arrive in separate CLI output chunks. The inventory can still look valid and feed the damaged identity text into the draft flow.

## User Impact

Create a Template preserves names, emoji, and other Unicode text in the inventory it uses to prepare a draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory now sets UTF-8 encoding on child stdout so Node's streaming decoder carries partial characters across chunk boundaries before parsing the JSON. All inventory lookups pass through this reader. [Node documents this behavior for readable streams.](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.20.0/docs/api/stream.html#readablesetencodingencoding)

## Evidence

I ran the bundled inventory script on Linux with Node 24.18.0. A fixture child process running the `agents list` lookup wrote valid JSON to a real stdout pipe in two writes, with the split after the first byte of the four-byte `🧭` emoji.

| Inventory script | Split write | Single-write control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream base `eac13241108` | `����` | `🧭` |
| Fixed | `🧭` | `🧭` |

All four runs preserved the ASCII identity name `Research assistant`. The standalone probe ran `node "$workspace/before.mjs" "$workspace" --agent demo --draft 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 --json`, repeated it with `after.mjs`, and read `.agent` from stdout. Only the child CLI responses and chunk timing were supplied by the fixture. The probe ended at inventory output, before the Control UI review card.

The regression command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/create-template-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed on the base with four replacement characters and passed with the fix in 3.10 seconds wall time. Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, Node syntax, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 issues. The production change replaces one line and the existing test covers the split pipe.

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix: let plugin counters show a label set at 0 before its first event
prs.body:
<!-- Template: .github/pull_request_template.md at ed8f4e680cbfc32182fee0b9286ef40c112bb1c3 -->

Closes #202816

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that publishes counters through `api.metrics` cannot show a known label set at 0 before its first event. `counter(name).inc(labels, 0)` is dropped, so the series appears only after the first non-zero increment. Dashboards and `absent()` alerts then cannot tell an idle label set from one that is missing.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can call `inc(labels, 0)` to export a label set at 0 on the Prometheus scrape, the usual way to pre-initialize counters. Core metrics and existing plugin series are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exporter's store skips counter increments of 0 before creating the series. Core counters rely on that: the model cost counter receives `costUsd ?? 0`, and skipping 0 keeps an unknown cost from showing as a measured $0. So the change applies only to plugin counter samples: a value of 0 uses the store's existing `max` mode instead of `add`. A new label set is created at 0 under the usual per-family and total limits. An existing series keeps its value and its cached output. Negative and non-finite values are still refused. The plugin families section of the Prometheus docs now says what `inc(labels, 0)` does.

## Evidence

- A scrape from a real Gateway with a path-loaded plugin shows the new `{outcome="error"} 0` series on this branch and not on main (Runtime output below).
- New store test, red on main for the missing `{outcome="error"} 0` line, green with the fix, red again with the fix reverted. It also checks that negative, NaN and Infinity values create no series, that core `counter(..., 0)` still creates none, and that a later 0 on an existing series does not re-render it.

Setup: isolated Gateway built from the checkout, own state folder, token auth with a throwaway token, loopback port 19455, `diagnostics-prometheus` enabled, and a path-loaded plugin `zero-proof` with `allowMetrics: true`. Five seconds after its service starts, the plugin logs and calls `inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)`, then `inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)`. No model, channel or provider. prs.title: fix(discord): keep /codex detach and rebind after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Closes #178330
Related: #175379

## What Problem This Solves

In Discord, `/codex detach` and re-running `/codex bind` with another workspace reply with success, but the change is not saved. After the Gateway restarts, the conversation is bound again with the workspace from the first bind, as if the detach or rebind never happened. #178330 has the reproduction on a real Discord bot.

## User Impact

User impact: in Discord, `/codex detach` and `/codex bind` to another workspace now stay in effect after a Gateway restart, and one such command no longer leaves Discord's binding storage memory-only for the rest of the Gateway process.

- If a binding change reaches Discord after the Discord plugin instance that created the relevant binding manager has shut down, the change is now refused with an error instead of reporting success and reverting at the next restart. Discord's deprecated synchronous binding helpers refuse it as well. This holds while Discord is still saving binding changes to its store; Not covered lists the cases that keep the previous behavior.
- No config, schema, or stored-data change; stored bindings load at startup as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries forward the Discord-only repair from #178622, which its author closed unmerged on November 5 and whose branch was then deleted. The production change is that PR's repair ported to current `main` with the same logic, and its author, HeZ2z, is credited as co-author of the commit. The differences from #178622 are listed in the details below.

When I closed my earlier #178333 on October 20, I expected a complete fix to overlap with the core-side approach in #177691, in which runtime-owned plugin-state stores refuse retired runtimes with a typed error, a change to public SDK behavior. Since then, ClawSweeper's last review of #178622 (November 4) found the Discord-only repair complete in scope, without new configuration or public SDK surface, and listed nothing before merge; #178622 and #177691 were both closed by their authors without being merged; and the focused reproduction still fails on current `main` (see Evidence).

Discord's binding code opened its store with the runtime of whichever plugin instance was current at write time. `/codex` commands run in the Codex plugin's instance, where Discord's runtime is not available, so the write failed. The failure was handled as a storage failure: the change was kept in memory only, Discord stopped saving binding changes for the rest of the process, and the command reported success.

The thread-binding manager now keeps the runtime of the Discord instance that created it and writes through that runtime whichever plugin calls it, as the Telegram repair merged in #175379 does. Session-wide helpers that change bindings outside a manager (idle timeout, max age, and unbind by session) look up the account's manager and use the runtime it keeps.

Unlike Telegram's, Discord's binding storage switches to memory-only after a failed write, so Discord also has to tell a retired owner apart from a storage failure. After a failed store write, it reopens its store through the kept runtime with the V2 opener, which the plugin SDK documents as bound to the plugin lifetime. If that reopen is refused and the store has not yet confirmed the targeted row, the write is refused: it is not kept in memory, and persistence is not switched off. If the reopen succeeds, the failure is handled as a storage failure, as before. While Discord is still saving to its store, the synchronous compatibility paths check the kept runtime before they write. As #178622 noted, a typed retired-runtime error needs a core public-contract change and can come later; this PR changes no core production code, public SDK contract, or config.

Thanks to HeZ2z, the author of #178622, for the repair and its regression tests, and to the author of #177691 for the earlier discussion of this bug.

<details>
<summary>Changes from #178622</summary>

- Production: the same logic in the same five files under `extensions/discord/src/monitor/` (`thread-bindings.state.ts`, `thread-bindings.manager.ts`, `thread-bindings.persistence.ts`, `thread-bindings.session-shared.ts`, `thread-bindings.lifecycle.ts`). One comment in `thread-bindings.persistence.ts` is reworded to describe the documented V2 opener behavior.
- Tests: five of #178622's six regression cases moved into the existing `src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts` as a `describe` block next to the Telegram cases from #175379, plus one new case for the synchronous session idle-timeout helper. The Discord helpers the tests use come from the existing `runtime-api.js`, except two that `extensions/discord/test-api.ts` now exports: the thread-binding test harness and the state reset used to simulate a restart.
- Diff against `9f20b63e7796`: 7 files changed, 362 insertions(+), 20 deletions(-) (production: 5 files, +98/-19; tests and test exports: +264/-1).

</details>

## Evidence

**Real Discord run, before and after.** On main, `/codex bind` to a second workspace and `/codex detach` both replied with success, and the next full Gateway restart undid each of them: the stored row stayed on `<dir-a>` and the bot showed `<dir-a>` again. With this PR, the stored row moved to `<dir-b>` after the rebind and was gone after the detach, and `/codex binding` after each restart showed the same.

- Setup: a dedicated test bot in a DM over real Discord, on Ubuntu x86_64 with Node v24.22.1. "Before" is a local `pnpm build` of main `9f20b63e7796`; "after" is a local `pnpm build` of this PR's head tree (`9f20b63e7796` plus this PR's diff; the 7 changed files match `e942926e771a` blob for blob). Each start ran `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --tailscale off --port <port> --verbose` from that checkout.
- Commands: only `/codex` text commands, plus one `/session unbind` in the before run, typed as plain-text messages (not native slash-command interactions; the config sets `commands.native: false`) from a Discord user account in the web client. The first bind in each run was approved with the Allow once button; no standing approval was seeded. No ordinary message was sent, so no model turn was made; the bug and this fix are in the binding writes these commands make, which a model turn does not reach.
- Restarts: each table row below is one Gateway start, 5 per run. Between rows the Gateway was fully stopped (SIGINT, clean shutdown, port released) and started again from the same isolated state directory. After each stop, the Discord binding rows were read directly from the state database.
- Test machine: another account on this host runs a system-level Gateway service, so the isolated Gateway and CLI ran with `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT` set to a unit name that does not exist (see #190177). This is specific to the test machine and unrelated to the code this PR changes.

Before (main `9f20b63e7796`):

For the focused tests and checks below, "Before" results were taken on main `9f20b63e7796` with only the test change. "After" results were taken on the same commit with this PR's full diff (commit `e942926e771a`).

Focused tests: six new Discord cases in `src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts`.

- Detach from another plugin instance (Codex): the stored row is deleted, and the binding stays gone after a simulated restart.
- Rebind from another plugin instance: the new binding is stored and comes back after a simulated restart.
- After such a change, Discord's own next binding write is still stored.
- With Discord's plugin registry retired, a detach from another plugin instance is refused, and memory and stored rows are unchanged.
- The same refusal through the deprecated synchronous unbind-by-session helper and through the deprecated synchronous idle-timeout helper.

Results:

- The focused reproduction still fails on current `main`: on `9f20b63e7796` with only the test change, 6 of the file's 9 cases fail and 3 pass. Each Discord case fails at the check it targets: the detach and rebind from the Codex instance report success, but the stored row is unchanged; Discord's next own write is not stored; and the three retired-owner cases accept the change instead of refusing it. The three existing Telegram cases in the file pass.
- With this change, all 9 cases in the file pass. Vitest reported about 6.9 s for the file.
- Mutation checks (not part of this PR):
  - with the manager no longer keeping its runtime, all six Discord cases fail and the three Telegram cases pass;
  - with the retired-owner check turned into a no-op, only the three refusal cases fail; the other six pass;
  - with the synchronous refusal detection always false, only the synchronous idle-timeout refusal case fails.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: passed (260 files, 2,649 tests).
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels`, run once as a cross-check although no shared channel surface changed: passed (49 files, 221 tests).
- Targeted checks:
  - `oxfmt --check`, oxlint, and `git diff --check` on the changed files: clean (oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors);
  - `pnpm check:changed --base 9f20b63e7796` (34 steps, including `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and the mock-export ratchet): passed;
  - test-lines ratchet: OK, net +259 of the 400-line allowance.
- Local review: autoreview on the full diff against `9f20b63e7796` reported scoped-clean with no findings (overall: patch is correct, confidence 0.85).
- CI: the workflow runs for this fork PR (CI, CodeQL, OpenGrep and others) are waiting for maintainer approval (`action_required`), and `openclaw/ci-gate` reports failure until they run.

Not covered:

- The focused tests simulate a restart by clearing Discord's in-process binding state and rebuilding the manager from the store; the Real Discord run above takes the rebind and the detach through full Gateway stop/start cycles.
- The after Discord run did not include `/session unbind`; only the before run did.
- The refusal cases retire Discord's plugin registry directly in the test; a real plugin reload or disable was not run.
- Once Discord's binding storage has switched to memory-only, async commits and synchronous updates go straight to memory without checking the kept runtime, as on `main`, so a retired owner's change there is not refused. If the kept runtime is refused partway through a store write after the targeted row was already written, the change is kept, as on `main`.
- Tests ran on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Node v24.22.1) only; the change has no platform-specific code.

prs.title: feat: let Talk and Discord request GPT-Live-1.1 with ChatGPT sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #202806

Related: #202133, #174084.

## What Problem This Solves

When a ChatGPT subscriber selects `gpt-live-1.1-codex`, OpenClaw treats it as an unlisted GPT-Live model and asks for Platform credentials. The subscriber cannot explicitly request that model through the existing Codex voice route.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk users can select `gpt-live-1.1-codex`, including in native iOS Talk, and Discord operators can choose it in realtime voice settings. The Codex selector prefers ChatGPT sign-in and can use a Platform key when the subscription profile is unavailable. Users can still select a public API model directly. Existing model defaults stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI plugin recognizes the selector from Codex CLI 0.171.0 and reuses its existing Codex model catalog, voice profile, and WebRTC call creation. iOS submits its offer through Talk's existing client WebRTC path. Discord uses the Gateway-owned WebRTC bridge. Existing iOS builds with GPT-Live WebRTC can use the selector. If a ChatGPT offer fails, the provider reports a safe, route-specific error to the gateway. The released browser Talk UI displays a generic WebRTC setup error.

## Evidence

- **Browser Talk.** The released Control UI running in Chromium connected through the isolated gateway, sent and received audio, and received input and reply transcript events. [Redacted browser results and HTTP 403 behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202807#issuecomment-7054806575).
- **Live OAuth relay.** Applied the exact PR diff to an isolated OpenClaw 2026.11.6 runtime and used its Gateway relay over WebRTC. The probe verified the selector on the outgoing ChatGPT offer and waited for audio and a completed assistant transcript. The server did not report its selected model. This was a headless relay test. Native iOS Talk and a human Discord call with this revision are pending.
- **Failure handling.** With test credentials, the runtime fixtures exercised configured and environment Platform keys when a subscription profile could not load. The source-mode tests exercise HTTP 403 in the Talk broker and a network rejection in the Gateway relay. They verify the public message omits provider details and each failed ChatGPT offer sends one request. No live Platform call was made.
- **Comparison against base.** Copied the three published test files onto base `8271ec9ee5d4` and ran the same 11 selected cases with Node 24.22.3 and Vitest on the base and published commit `01245008b74c`. Base missed the catalog entry, did not project the OAuth startup error, and failed selector assertions. All 11 cases passed on the PR commit. The broader focused source-mode run passed 114 tests.
- **Model contract.** [Codex CLI 0.171.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.171.0/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L118) uses this selector as its v3 default. In an independent Codex WebRTC probe, a deliberately nonexistent selector also returned audio. The evidence establishes OpenClaw's requested selector and transport, and the backend model identity remains unverified.
- **Hosted CI.** The local full build stopped at its memory preflight. [Required CI is waiting for a maintainer to approve the run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44844277283).

<details>
<summary>Redacted live relay output and regression results</summary>

```json
{"requestedModel":"gpt-live-1.1-codex","oauthOffer":true,"responseStatus":201,"serverSessionStarted":true,"nonzeroAudioFrames":146,"assistantTranscriptDone":true}
```

```text
Base auth routing: 6 failed | 19 skipped (exit 1)
Base Talk broker and Gateway relay: 4 failed | 1 passed | 38 skipped (exit 1)
PR auth routing: 6 passed | 19 skipped (exit 0)
PR Talk broker and Gateway relay: 5 passed | 38 skipped (exit 0)
```

</details>

## Maintainer decision

The fallback intentionally covers both listed Codex models when the ChatGPT profile cannot be loaded. The existing Platform key selection can run before sending an offer. A network error or rejection after sending a subscription offer is reported to the caller without a second request on the Platform route.

prs.title: improve: open a new session from the mobile web rail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The mobile web drawer has a New session shortcut in the Sessions header, but not when the drawer shows People or another section. Starting a session from there means switching sections first.

## User Impact

Tap the plain **+** directly above Home to open a new session for the selected agent. The original **+** stays in the Sessions header without an outline. Search, desktop, and native layouts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rail stays in place as the drawer changes sections. Both shortcuts use the same New session link and permission check, so they open the same composer without creating a session until the user submits.

## Evidence

Six focused browser tests passed, including opening `/new` from both mobile shortcuts, keeping a draft on re-entry, opening from People, and preventing navigation without creation access. The Control UI typecheck passed. Visual proof used the actual web UI at an emulated 393 × 852 viewport with synthetic Gateway data; no physical device was tested.

prs.title: fix: show gateway sign-in instructions on separate lines
prs.body:
Closes #200749

## What Problem This Solves

When you sign in to a provider with `openclaw models auth login` while the Gateway is running (for example xAI or OpenAI device-code sign-in), the multi-line instructions are shown as one run-on paragraph with literal `\n` sequences in it. The code, its expiry, and the warning not to enter a code someone else gave you are no longer on their own lines, so the warning is easy to miss.

## User Impact

Gateway-backed sign-in shows the instructions the way the Gateway wrote them: the message, the code, the expiry, and the device-code warning each on a line of their own. Login itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway builds these steps as several lines. The CLI passed the whole message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, which is a single-line sanitizer and turns every newline into the two characters `\` and `n`. It now sanitizes each line and joins them again, the same way `sessions-import.ts` and `transcripts/read.ts` already do, so terminal control characters are still removed from every line.

## Evidence

Scenario: `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a running Gateway.

Run from source with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port) started from the same commit, using OpenAI's real device-code endpoint. The sign-in was never approved. The one-time codes below are replaced with `XXXX-XXXX`; nothing else is edited. Before is the base commit `81a962707` (Gateway and CLI), after is this PR's head `79e8a8df7` (Gateway and CLI).

Before:

```text
◇  OpenAI Codex device code ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                         │
│  Enter this one-time code on the sign-in page.\nCode: XXXX-XXXX\nCode  │
│  expires in 15 minutes.\nContinue only if you started this sign-in      │
│  yourself. If a website or another person gave you this code, cancel.   │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

After:

```text
◇  OpenAI Codex device code ────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                       │
│  Enter this one-time code on the sign-in page.                        │
│  Code: XXXX-XXXX                                                      │
│  Code expires in 15 minutes.                                          │
│  Continue only if you started this sign-in yourself. If a website or  │
│  another person gave you this code, cancel.                           │
│                                                                       │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The later "Waiting for device authorization…" note had the same problem before (`cancel.\n\nWaiting for device authorization…`) and renders on its own lines after.

- New test `renders a gateway device-code step on separate lines and still strips terminal controls` in `auth-login-gateway.test.ts` drives a real `WizardSession` device-code step through `runGatewayLoginWizard`. On the base commit it fails because the note text contains literal `\n`; with this change it passes. It also checks that an escape sequence in the message is still removed.
- The whole `src/commands/models` suite passes (35 files, 324 tests). `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:core`, pass.
- Not covered: completing a sign-in with a provider account.

prs.title: fix: show device-code sign-in steps on separate lines when the Gateway runs the login
prs.body:
Root cause: src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.ts:86 (base 29ce933e9e) passed every Gateway login step message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, a single-line sanitizer that turns each newline into a visible backslash-n, so multi-line steps such as the device code reached the terminal as one run-together paragraph.

Fixes #200749

## What Problem This Solves

When the local Gateway is running, `openclaw models auth login` (for example `--method device-code`) showed multi-line sign-in steps with the text backslash-n instead of line breaks. The sign-in instruction, the code, its expiry and the warning not to continue with a code someone else gave you all ran together in one paragraph. Sign-in still worked, but the step that carries the phishing warning was hard to read.

## User Impact

User impact: people signing in to a provider through the CLI while the Gateway runs see each line of the sign-in step on its own line again. The wording and the sign-in flow do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway builds the device-code step with real newlines on purpose (`src/wizard/session.ts:103-113`), and they reach the CLI intact in the RPC payload. The one place the CLI prints Gateway login steps then sanitized the whole message as a single line. Without the Gateway, the login prints the provider's note directly through the terminal prompter (`src/wizard/clack-prompter.ts:170`), so line breaks were fine there.

The CLI now sanitizes each line of a step message separately and joins the lines with real newlines. This happens once, where every Gateway login step is prepared, so note, progress and prompt messages all get it. Color codes and other control characters are still stripped from each line. The URL, the code box and error text still use the single-line sanitizer, so a backslash-n the provider actually sends stays literal.

Thanks to @digitalfrost84 for the report and the precise diagnosis, to @deepujain for this fix, and to @AyhamJo7 for the same fix in #202790.

## Evidence

Real built CLI and Gateway, isolated state, OpenAI device-code sign-in against a local fixture (no real account). Full transcript excerpts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200884#issuecomment-7070954091

- Before (base 29ce933e9e, Gateway running): the instruction, code, expiry and warning joined by visible backslash-n sequences in one wrapped paragraph, with 11 literal backslash-n in the transcript.
- After (this PR, Gateway running): the instruction, `Code: P749-ABCD`, `Code expires in 15 minutes.`, the warning and `OpenAI device code complete` each on their own line, with 0 literal backslash-n.
- Offline login (Gateway stopped): base and this PR print the same transcript.
- Single-line steps (`Starting device code flow…`, the URL box, the code box) are unchanged. A provider code that contains a real backslash-n (`P749`, backslash, `n`, `ABCD`) still prints literally.
- Regression test `keeps the line breaks of multi-line login steps while stripping terminal controls` fails on base and passes here.

Merge danger: two-way door. This only changes how the CLI prints Gateway login text and writes no state. If it were wrong, the worst case would be Gateway-backed `models auth login` output for any provider.

prs.title: fix: stop old Doctor recovery copies from holding tens of gigabytes of disk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` saves a full copy of OpenClaw state before repairing. OpenClaw kept the newest three of those copies for up to 30 days. On an installation with a large database each copy is several gigabytes: one host held three copies from a single week, 23 GiB in total, and neither Doctor, a finished update, nor `openclaw update cleanup` would remove any of them.

## User Impact

Standalone Doctor now keeps its newest two completed recovery copies, however old they are. Older completed copies are removed automatically the next time standalone Doctor saves a copy or an update finishes its cleanup, and `openclaw update cleanup` lists them as removable.

Things to know:

- **Why two and not one.** Some Doctor repairs change database rows without a backup of their own (Telegram general-topic conversations, the incognito session key repair, auth migration receipts, the agent-deletion journal quarantine). After a second repair, the older copy is the only one from before the first.
- **Less history.** Previously up to three generations were available for 30 days. Take a verified backup when you need more than two generations.
- **The second-newest copy no longer expires.** It used to become removable after 30 days; it now stays until a newer copy replaces it.
- **First run after upgrading removes the backlog.** Existing copies older than the newest two are deleted on the next standalone Doctor capture or finished update.
- Unfinished copies, copies that a pending update recovery refers to, and copies taken by updates keep their existing protection. If recovery records cannot be read, nothing is removed.
- No new options and no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three-copy limit came from #174415, which bounded a Docker rollout loop that had filled a disk under the earlier 30-day-only rule (#162364). Neither change names a failure that needs three copies; three was a bound. Doctor only ever reuses the newest copy.

The retention rule has one owner, shared by Doctor's automatic retirement, capture reuse, `openclaw update cleanup` and a finished update's automatic cleanup, so the change is a single rule there. The age check is removed because it no longer decides anything. Automatic retirement already existed on both paths; no new deletion path was added.

## Review notes

An independent review of this head found one P2, accepted as a documented edge and not changed:

- **A container's activation copy can be retired one generation sooner.** A container seals activation copy A; two later standalone repairs against the same state seal B and C. A is now removable at three copies, where the old rule kept it until a fourth copy or 30 days. The container's next start then saves a fresh full copy. The collector has never read the activation marker (it lives in the container's own `/tmp`), so this protection gap predates the PR; only the count at which it shows moved from four to three. The activation start itself still protects its own copy.

It found nothing else at P0–P2: the newest two stay protected, pending-recovery and unfinished-run protections are unchanged, and unchanged-capture reuse still protects the reused copy.

## Evidence

Head `9453022c1243`, base `main` `4bedaedbcc06`. Real-product runs used Crabbox `local-container` leases on a Mac Studio with packed npm installs and isolated state.

- **It works (leases `cbx_96d9392c4e19`, `cbx_603b162080bc`).** Five standalone `doctor --fix` runs with a state change before each:
  - base: three copies kept after each run;
  - head: two copies kept after each run;
  - base, then upgrade to head: three copies before any Doctor run, two after the first, config and workspace intact.
- **Upgrade lanes on head (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh`):**
  - published package survivor from `openclaw@2026.11.6`: passed (lease `cbx_290f08c55afb`);
  - `git-release` from the lane's default baseline: passed, 27 phases;
  - `git-release` from tag `v2026.11.6`: fails on base and head alike (`preflight-no-good-commit`: the 2026.11.6 updater cannot build the candidate), so it says nothing about this change.
- **Red on the base, green with the fix** for the retention suite; every consumer of the rule passes (retention owner, `update cleanup` preview and removal, a finished update's automatic cleanup, Doctor's capture flow including the container activation marker, capture reuse, update status recovery reporting).
- Core and test typechecks, lint and format on touched files, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

**Not proven: the Docker image upgrade path.** `scripts/e2e/container-image-upgrade-docker.sh` fails on this arm64 host for base and head, so it gives no verdict:

| Side | Runs | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | 3 of 3 | `Invalid persisted transcript payload` in the fixture's `default` verify |
| head | 2 of 3 | the same |
| head | 1 of 3 | passed that check, then `Expected exactly one retained-schema backup` (3 found) for `state/openclaw.sqlite` |

The base never reached the second assertion, so the one differing head run cannot be attributed either way. Those backups are Doctor's `.pre-startup-migration` files, which this PR does not touch, but that is reasoning, not a measurement. A run on an x86 Linux host, base against head, would settle it.

Also not proven: a real Docker rollout, macOS and Windows. Historical release notes under `docs/releases/` still describe the old rule for the releases that shipped it.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: keep neighboring chats apart when a sidebar group expands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Expanding a group of chats at larger text sizes could briefly paint the following chat on top of the last child. Collapsing the group could briefly leave a blank gap. The list looked correct once it settled, so checking only the final layout missed both problems.

## User Impact

The next chat follows the actual height of the group as it opens and closes. Offscreen rows are still virtualized, existing sort and focus behavior is preserved, and archiving still moves the remaining chats smoothly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser knew the size of the visible chat trees before the sidebar updated their absolute positions. Mounted trees now lay each other out in normal flow; the virtual window reserves space only for omitted rows. The archive animation releases its own slot instead of coordinating a separate transform on neighboring rows.

## Evidence

The regression samples consecutive animation frames while opening and closing a four-chat group three times at 140% text size. On the baseline, titles collided and the geometry probe recorded both overlaps and gaps. With the fix, the distance between the bottom of the group and the next row was **0 CSS pixels on every sampled frame**. A separate replay on top of #203183 still failed without this fix.

Actual Chromium frames from the production Control UI with synthetic Gateway data: desktop, 1280 × 900, light theme, 140% text; matching sidebar crops from main `010b5348381e` and this change `a1e36550fc60`. The captured baseline predates #203183, so its child completion icons appear on both sides of this comparison.

### Early Undo while a row is fading

In the before video, **Prepare release** appears twice and **Review docs** drops an extra 32 px. With the correction the fading copy is removed before the restored row takes its place. Closes #203341

## What Problem This Solves

A local model can pass a text check and make a correct first tool call while still failing a task that depends on the returned value. The local-model guide warns about this but doesn't show how to check it.

## User Impact

Local-model operators get a read-only two-step recipe and a way to distinguish a missing tool result from a model that stops before using it. No defaults, config contracts, or runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(voice-call): pace interruptible prepared statements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent calling someone to deliver a long prepared statement can generate audio faster than the telephone plays it. The bounded queue then overflows and closes the stream. The statement must also remain interruptible: the listener should be able to ask a question, continue the unfinished statement, or stop it entirely.

## User Impact

This draft adds paced delivery for OpenAI response-mode prepared openings and later `speak` requests, retaining the interrupted passage for resume. The `say` steering route keeps its existing 500-character limit. Caller speech is not discarded for the duration of a managed statement. Resume repeats the last unacknowledged short passage rather than skipping unheard words; it is not word-exact seek.

**Not ready to merge:** the latest human test resumed and progressed, but also showed unexpected caller-speech detections and unwanted continuation during caller exchanges. A clean human interruption → answer → explicit continuation → complete reading → stop test remains outstanding. The earlier uninterruptible eight-passage success does not validate this revision. Production is unchanged.

Other providers, short openings and continuous/native-delegation paths retain their existing behavior. Arbitrarily long spontaneous model replies are not covered: the host must have prepared text to split. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One plugin-local coordinator supplies bounded, sentence-aware passages and waits for generation completion plus carrier playback acknowledgement before advancing. Caller speech pauses delivery; unique marks prevent cleared/stale acknowledgements from skipping the interrupted passage. The call-bound `openclaw_statement` tool can resume or stop, but cannot start or replace a statement: only the host supplies complete prepared text. Explicit stop, continuity reset and teardown discard it.

The initial revision exposed model `start` as well, and broadly instructed the model to use the tool for prepared statements. A human test then logged repeated tool calls before reading audio. The follow-up removes that recursive route and clarifies that only the quoted Answer text—not internal playback directions—is spoken. Repeating full session instructions inside each passage was also removed. The rejected-start regression attempts replacement while paused and verifies that resume retains the original passage.

The previous proposal to suppress early caller input is withdrawn. There is no longer a request to approve discarding caller speech throughout a long statement. Normal code-owner review and CI requirements remain.

The existing six-line package-build compatibility correction remains: bundle the pure SHA-256 helper for declared supported hosts lacking its SDK subpath. Retire that alias when the declared host floor supplies it. The prepared-statement coordinator is scoped to the OpenAI response-created/done and silent tool-result contract; it is not claimed as a generic continuous-provider capability. Existing overflow protection stays enabled.

## Evidence

- **Deterministic playback:** paced completion, pre-ready caller input, interruption, answer playback before resume, repeating the unacknowledged passage, late cleared marks, explicit stop, later host speech, teardown, and unchanged short/continuous behavior are covered. The 180-second production-composition replay at 4x generation speed still distinguishes unsegmented overflow from paced delivery.
- **Follow-up tests:** 10 passed / 2 files (`realtime-reading` and `realtime-reading-overflow`). After moving the rejected-replacement assertion into the paused-state scenario, the final reading group passed 8 / 8 (9.31 s wrapper; Vitest 7.05 s). Earlier implementation had 48 focused tests / 4 files; these are bounded local results, not broad exact-head CI.
- **Checks:** targeted strict typecheck, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, docs lint and commit guards passed. Canonical plugin package built; isolated Gateway reload verified the exact compiled candidate path and source digest. No production deployment occurred.
- **Review:** autoreview found the earlier provider-eligibility P2, addressed by restricting registration/coordination to the OpenAI non-native response path. A subsequent scoped review of host-only initiation found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The later prompt clarification has real-model evidence below, not a claim of an additional independent review.
- **Real model, no phone:** an OpenAI realtime probe generated audio, answered the train-colour question, invoked resume, reached the final phrase, and invoked stop on a later statement. It checked that playback directions were not spoken. Caller interruption and carrier acknowledgements were simulated, so this is not telephone timing or human-audibility proof. Earlier probe iterations caught spoken wrapper text and an overlapping probe turn; these were corrected before the final probe.
- **Latest human-answered call (21 November, ~23:29–23:33 UTC):** the corrected candidate started the reading, paused, handled conversation, resumed the retained passage on a continuation request, and progressed through multiple further passages. Unexpected input detections and later unwanted resumptions prevented a clean pass. Possible acoustic echo is only a hypothesis, not an established root cause. The test was ended; full delivery and a caller-directed permanent stop on this revision remain unproven. No more human calls are planned tonight.

The immediate next work is to diagnose the unexpected input/continuation behavior from this call and add the appropriate boundary regression before another human test. Keep the PR draft.

Hosted validation is not complete. The latest PR-context check rejected the previous body because its validation section was titled “Verification” rather than the required “Evidence”; this body corrects that presentation issue. Earlier broad CI was `action_required` with zero jobs, and the author has read-only upstream permissions. Maintainer workflow approval remains a separate gate; no permission or CI bypass was attempted. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix(usage): show model attribution without stored session metadata
prs.body:
Fixes #198488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing provider and model information in Usage session rows and exports when measured usage exists but session-level attribution is absent or incomplete.

## User Impact

Missing fields now use representative measured attribution without inventing a provider/model pair. Stored values remain authoritative. If one field is stored, the missing field is filled only from matching measured entries; if none match, it stays empty. No configuration, migration, or protocol changes are required.

For mixed-provider sessions, this fallback is representative metadata only—not attribution of every token or cost. Aggregate accounting and provider filters are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial row assembly only copied stored metadata. Packed overview summaries arrive later, and metadata restoration replaces report rows with visible rows while retaining their usage. One shared helper fills final response metadata after hydration/restoration and filtering/aggregation.

The helper selects the greatest totalTokens among eligible measured entries, keeping the first on ties. Eligibility preserves an existing provider or model. When neither field is stored, both come from the same dominant entry. Repeated application is idempotent and does not mutate source usage.

The response regression is a sibling test file because usage.sessions-usage.test.ts is at its line cap. It uses the existing isolated Gateway-methods lane. Documentation describes both representative attribution and partial-pair consistency.

## Evidence

- Base: 3ab80aba158a5c5488d9323f4352aa593fb9af1c (tree 7e4dc64cd2172b6045e63b7f35f5d38b5af13a34).
- Final candidate: 3ffbb5d752358a4b3500738ac7cc79fd4789f089 (tree 32cf975c2eb0b50588d8135fc10d5abc23516507).
- The Windows runtime proof below is supplied by @MertBasar0 and bound to afe57af5e5fdd7391263110cc8efd4dbb86a583d (tree 8393447bc9453ff991178b99a42920976a9189c5). Roboclaw did not execute those Windows commands. The final commit adds only 15 lines to one test file; every other repository file, including all production code, is byte-identical to afe57af5. The proof remains labeled with the commit actually built.
- Original RED/GREEN: detail, packed overview, and restoration failed on the pinned base due to absent attribution. Partial-pair consistency cases then failed on f303c818 (eight assertions across two tests) and passed with afe57af5.
- Final Linux verification: 53 tests pass across usage.sessions-usage.test.ts, usage-overview-report.test.ts, session-cost-usage-worker-overview.test.ts, usage-overview.test.ts, and usage.row-attribution.test.ts. Runner wall time: 22.01 seconds including preparation; attribution test bodies: 0.840 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Final test-file lint, format check, Gateway-methods test typecheck, and git diff --check pass. Prior core production typecheck and full-candidate review remain applicable to unchanged production code.
- Independent OpenClaw Auto Review: the full afe57af5 candidate was P0–P2 scoped-clean; a fresh review of the final test-only delta against afe57af5 is also scoped-clean, with no findings.

### Reporter measurements and explicit regression coverage

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the [follow-up live-store measurements and requested controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198488#issuecomment-6875408820). Their live-store counts, mixed-provider frequency, and client-workaround observations are reporter-provided evidence, not numbers reproduced by this PR's Windows fixture.

Both controls are in src/gateway/server-methods/usage.row-attribution.test.ts:
- **fills final detail row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**
- **fills final overview row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**

The existing **missing** case supplies two providers with 10 and 30 tokens and requires the 30-token entry's provider and model, while independently checking aggregate totals. The new **null-model-usage** case supplies totalTokens=0 and modelUsage=null and requires both row attribution fields to stay empty. Detail additionally asserts that the returned modelUsage is literally null; packed overview represents it as zero model entries and keeps attribution empty. Existing usage=null and modelUsage=[] controls remain. The null fixture is intentionally outside the current optional-array TypeScript summary type, with a localized documented expected type error; no production type was widened.

### Publication status and remaining verification

UI E2E passed locally on Windows as reported by @MertBasar0 below; this is not a passing CI claim. The inherited unused-export failures are documented rather than suppressed. Preflight found no competing #198488 PR. Main b9dacb674914f74b57155edc02cdd13f8f963486 still has the unchanged row assembly, loading, and restoration defect.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, built Gateway

A built Gateway answers the real `sessions.usage` RPC through `openclaw gateway call`. The Claude turns that create the session usage records are served by a **stub Claude CLI**, so no real inference runs. The RPC, the usage pipeline, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:
- Windows 11 Home 26200 x64, Node v24.19.0. `pnpm build` of each commit from a clean checkout: base `3ab80aba` (tree `7e4dc64c`) and candidate `afe57af5` (tree `8393447b`).
- Isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, state dir, config and workspace. Model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Sequence: `openclaw gateway run` → `openclaw agent` turn in session K (kept) → turn in session D → `openclaw sessions delete <D> --yes` → `openclaw gateway call sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:100, startDate, endDate}`, re-polled until no row reports `computing: true` → the same call with `projection: "overview"`.

| | Base `3ab80aba` | Candidate `afe57af5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail, deleted session D | `modelProvider`/`model` empty; `usage.modelUsage` = `claude-cli`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, 2 tokens | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Detail, kept session K (stored metadata) | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, deleted session D | empty | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, kept session K | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Rows with `modelProvider == null` and measured usage | 1 of 2 (detail), 1 of 2 (overview) | 0 |
| `aggregates.byProvider` | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens (unchanged) |

Notes:
- The deleted row first reports `computing: true` while its usage is summarized; the values above are after it settled, in both builds.
- Mixed-provider, partial stored pair and empty-usage cases are covered by the regression suite, not by this run.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports the same three unused exports on base `3ab80aba` and on the candidate: `REQUIRED_ACTION_STOP`, `mergeNodeRepositoryPublication`, `WorkspaceTransferOperation`. All are in files this PR does not touch, and the new `usage-row-attribution.ts` is not flagged. So the `check:changed` red is pre-existing.

prs.title: fix(ui): continue a lone sidebar session list as it scrolls
prs.body:
Related: #200217, #186714, #197587

## What Problem This Solves

A sidebar session list that stands alone (Group by none, or Other with no other groups) stops at its first page behind Show more. With hundreds of sessions, browsing older ones means clicking Show more again and again.

## User Impact

- **One list on its own:** it still opens at its first page (30 sessions when grouped by none, 15 for a lone Other). Scrolling to its end shows the next 15 loaded sessions, and each later visit to the end shows 15 more. Show more stays for keyboard users and for a list too short to scroll.
- **Several groups:** unchanged. Each group pages with Show more, so a large group never buries the ones below it. This includes #200217's case of Other next to a named group.
- A list whose end is already on screen, or comes into view as the mobile drawer opens, keeps its first page until you scroll or press Show more.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection decides which sections render, including when an empty Other heading still shows (more pages to load, owner filters, a non-Active status, or a drag). The renderer draws every section it returns, so the projection knows when one section is the whole list and marks it to continue on scroll. Show more and Collapse load lazily, the first time a section has rows to reveal or hide, which keeps the chat boot JS inside its budget. The new code is in that lazy module: it watches the section's end and shows one more page each time the end scrolls into view in a scrolled list.

This covers loaded sessions only. Fetching older pages from the Gateway, and where that control sits, is #197587's part; the two changes meet only at the list's end.

## Evidence

Group by none, 100 sessions, after scrolling to the end of the list twice:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the list stops at Conversation 30 with Show more](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/1a2df424-1b27-4cdd-a775-6fdb6450154a.png) | ![After: the list continues past Conversation 30](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/b3af6ea3-531a-444c-9a0e-d570a87d96c9.png) |

Before is main.

- Regression tests:
  - `sidebar-flat-list` E2E: the flat list opens at 30 and shows 45, then 60, as its end scrolls into view. It fails with the scroll handling removed (stays at 30).
  - Projection test: only a lone section continues on scroll, and a shown empty Other heading counts as a second section.
- E2Es that page a lone list with Show more press it without Playwright's scroll into view, since that scroll would reach the list's end and show a page by itself.
- Passed locally in headless Chromium: 8 sidebar unit/browser files (`app-sidebar*` projection, visibility, freshness, memo, feedback, stress, sessions, people), 18 sidebar, session-management and chat E2E files, UI typecheck and UI test typecheck, lint, and formatting.

Browser proof uses synthetic sessions and a mocked Gateway. The full local suite and a live Gateway run were not run.
