prs.title: feat: browse and search Skills by ClawHub category in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub’s website lets people find skills by category, but the Control UI only offers a flat Skills list and an unrestricted search. Someone looking for a Research skill can’t browse that category or limit a query to it as they can with Plugins and Templates.

## User Impact

Skills now shows category sections with **View all**. Selecting a category browses the whole category, including skills outside the overview; typing searches within it. Unclassified skills remain visible, and ordinary search and discovery still work with registries that do not advertise categories.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway reads the registry’s taxonomy rather than maintaining a separate list. The overview uses one trending-feed request and one taxonomy request, not a request per category. Search keeps its registry ranking. Companion API: https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4868.

## Evidence

- [Before/after screenshots: desktop, mobile and scoped search](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202756#issuecomment-7051955937). Real Chromium with deterministic gateway fixtures: the flat overview became grouped on desktop and at 390 px. View all found a skill absent from the preview. Seven browser cases passed across four suites, including pagination, retry, stale responses, search focus, navigation, installation and recovery.
- The real OpenClaw reader replayed HTTP responses captured from the companion backend. Mixed-source ranking, cursors and install identities stayed the same; Finance and Research memberships came through, and an unclassified external row stayed ungrouped.
- Before the CI repair, 120 focused UI and 41 gateway/registry tests passed, plus core/UI typechecks, protocol checks, scoped lint/formatting, controllers, i18n and docs links. The full local `pnpm check:changed` stopped at its 4 GiB SQLite checker heap limit. The unchanged checker passed separately with 12 GiB: live calls 166 → 166; deprecated-only calls 15 → 15. Later gates did not run through that aggregate.
- [First-visit CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44827592778/job/136604849420) measured 30 assets on Skills (limit 28) and 33 on Skills Settings (limit 31). The repaired bundle groups catalog skeletons with the cards and skill grouping with its shared helpers. All four unchanged route-budget cases passed locally with the reader still lazy. The four category browser cases, both recovery cases, 65 focused tests, UI types, scoped lint and formatting also passed.
- Test growth fell from +557 to +471 lines after consolidating fixtures and duplicate assertions. The remaining **71-line allocation** above the normal 400 keeps two distinct regressions covered: registry HTTP through the gateway (mixed-source order, install identity, cursor and older registries) and Chromium interaction (keyboard focus, narrow layout, retry and rejection of stale pages). The route budgets and default test allowance are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(skills): accept comments after multiline quoted descriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Creator rejects an otherwise valid skill when its multiline quoted description has an inline comment containing angle brackets after the closing quote. Authors running Python without PyYAML hit this error in both validation and packaging.

## User Impact

Skill authors can validate and package these skills using a standard-library-only Python environment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dependency-free validator now applies its existing quote-aware comment handling to the assembled quoted value, so an editor's note after the closing quote is excluded from description validation. Both commands use the same validator. The change adds nine net production lines and three test cases.

## Evidence

On Linux with Python 3.12.3 and no PyYAML installed, the real validation and packaging commands rejected both single- and double-quoted fixtures on OpenClaw v2026.11.6 and base `150edeea6e0`. With this patch both commands exited 0, the ZIP integrity checks passed, and the archived `SKILL.md` matched the input byte for byte. A fixture with angle brackets inside the description still exited 1 and produced no archive. A plain multiline description with a trailing comment succeeded on both the base and the patch.

PyYAML 6.0.1 independently parsed both valid fixtures and returned the folded description without the comment. The distinction follows the [YAML 1.2.2 rules for comments](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#66-comments) and [quoted flow scalars](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#73-flow-scalar-styles).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused checks</summary>

Create `meeting-notes/SKILL.md` with this content and run the same commands on the base and the patched checkout.

```yaml
---
name: meeting-notes
description: "Summarize team
  meeting notes." # <editor note>
---
```

```sh
python3 -m venv --without-pip /tmp/skill-proof-venv
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py meeting-notes
/tmp/skill-proof-venv/bin/python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py meeting-notes out
python3 -m zipfile -t out/meeting-notes.skill
```

On the base both Python commands exited 1 with `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`. On the patch validation reported `Skill is valid!` and packaging wrote the archive. Replacing the quote pair with single quotes gave the same before/after results.

- `python -m pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/skill-creator/scripts` passed 12 tests and 57 subtests. The two new positive subtests failed on the original parser. The standard-library unittest run also passed all 12 tests without PyYAML.
- Targeted Ruff lint and `git diff --check` passed. Ruff format flagged the same pre-existing test line in the base and candidate.
- Codex autoreview covered the uncommitted two-file patch against `150edeea6e0` at P0–P3 and returned `scoped-clean`. The reviewer assessed the supplied patch and did not independently rerun the CLI.
- Local CLI evidence is from Linux. Broader checks are left to GitHub CI.

</details>

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix(model-usage): read piped UTF-8 reports on non-UTF-8 terminals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Piping a UTF-8 CodexBar report into the Model usage skill can fail when Python's standard input uses a different encoding. A report containing a non-ASCII project name can fail before the skill prints any model costs.

## User Impact

The skill can summarize the same UTF-8 report from a pipe or a file, including reports with a UTF-8 byte-order mark.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stdin import decodes bytes as UTF-8, matching the existing file import and using the same BOM handling.

## Evidence

I ran the bundled CLI with Python 3.12.3 on Linux and forced CP1252 for standard I/O. The UTF-8 fixture contains the project name `東京支店`.

- Before, both `e5ccb878a104` and the stable `v2026.11.6` tag exited 1 on the pipe with a `charmap` decode error. The same bytes worked through the file import with CP1252 and through the pipe with UTF-8 standard I/O. This isolates the failure to stdin decoding.
- After, the pipe exits 0 and reports `claude-sonnet-4-6` at `1.25` USD. The committed regression fails on the base for both plain UTF-8 and UTF-8 with BOM, and passes for both on the fix.
- `pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/model-usage` passed all 12 tests. Targeted Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Codex autoreview of the complete patch against `e5ccb878a104` returned scoped-clean at P0–P3.
- The proof uses a synthetic report and Python's CP1252 stdio setting. Native Windows and live CodexBar collection were outside this check.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce with the shipped script</summary>

```bash
cat > cost.json <<'JSON'
[{"provider":"claude","projects":[{"name":"東京支店"}],"daily":[{"date":"2026-11-20","modelBreakdowns":[{"modelName":"claude-sonnet-4-6","cost":1.25}]}]}]
JSON

cat cost.json | PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python3 skills/model-usage/scripts/model_usage.py --provider claude --input - --mode all --format json
PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python3 skills/model-usage/scripts/model_usage.py --provider claude --input cost.json --mode all --format json
```

[Python standard stream encoding](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/sys.html#sys.stdin) and [CodexBar cost report format](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/blob/main/docs/cli.md#cost-json-payload).

</details>

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix: keep terminal formatting out of Meme Maker SVGs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meme Maker accepts captions copied from colored terminal output and reports that it saved an SVG. The saved file can contain raw control characters that prevent SVG viewers from opening it.

## User Impact

Local SVG and PNG renders preserve the visible caption text when it includes terminal formatting, so users can paste colored output directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clean captions at the shared local layout step, before wrapping and sizing. Node's terminal-code stripper removes formatting sequences and the XML 1.0 character filter removes any remaining characters that SVG cannot represent. XML escaping continues to preserve printable punctuation and Unicode text. The existing CLI regression now parses the output and verifies that the caption survived.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24.18.0 and a downloaded Drake template, both main (`dce3c298384`) and the v2026.11.6 tag's renderer exited 0 and wrote SVG that Python's XML parser rejected.
- The repaired CLI produced valid SVG and a 1200 × 1200 PNG with Chrome for Testing 156. Both files were byte-identical to renders from the same captions with the terminal and XML-invalid characters removed manually. The SVG readback preserved the ampersand, accented and Chinese text, and emoji. FFmpeg decoded the PNG.
- The CLI regression failed before the fix because Resvg rejected an ESC character. After the fix, the focused suite passed both default tests. Its opt-in browser case was skipped in the default run and the separate real Chromium CLI proof covered the PNG path.
- Focused TypeScript, lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues on the same two-file patch before a base update that left the owning files unchanged. The change adds six net production lines and eleven net test lines.

<details>
<summary>Local reproduction</summary>

Run from the repository root with an isolated cache directory.

```bash
proof_dir=$(mktemp -d)
XDG_CACHE_HOME="$proof_dir/cache" node skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs \
  render drake --text $'before\033[31mRED\033[0m after' --text 'Control' \
  --out "$proof_dir/meme.svg"
python3 -c 'import sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse(sys.argv[1])' \
  "$proof_dir/meme.svg"

OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: show clean initials when a Team Reports avatar fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a member photo cannot load, Chromium draws a broken-image icon over the initials on the Team Reports People list and person page. On the smaller list badge it partly covers the letters.

## User Impact

People still see who the report is about: the initials occupy the same badge when the photo is missing. Loaded photos, member names, link targets and hit areas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared badge already reserves the square and centers the initials. Let the square GitHub photo use its intrinsic height instead of stretching even a failed image to the full badge. The badge is decorative for assistive technology; the adjacent name provides the identity. No script, new request or per-page workaround is needed.

## Evidence

Navigated Reports → People → Person and back in the real Control UI with a synthetic roster, local 404 and successful photo responses, at 390 and 1440 CSS pixels. The failed badge now matches the initials-only state. All four loaded badge crops were pixel-identical before and after; all badge positions and sizes were unchanged (36 × 36 on People, 72 × 72 on Person).

### Clean comparison

When a conversation’s workspace was removed, the message field and toolbar still invited people to compose a reply they could not send. The restore action was tucked inside that field.

prs.title: fix: write Blobster previews to the requested directory
prs.body:
Related: #199950

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw agents render-blobster` can return success after writing a preview to the wrong directory. When `--out` contains a symlink followed by `..`, the command collapses the path before opening it and can overwrite a neighboring file.

## User Impact

On POSIX, Blobster previews land where the supplied path points. The JSON summary reports that destination, and a missing directory before `..` produces an error before anything is written.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the shared filesystem resolver introduced in #200031 at the one output boundary used for SVG and PNG. The design reader already delegates traversal to the filesystem.

## Evidence

- Linux, Node 24.18.0, isolated state and the design guide's sample JSON. On main `3d0900e4ac0`, the built CLI read `selected/../design.json` and overwrote the lexical neighbor when rendering to `selected/../preview.svg`. The bundled skill CLI did the same for PNG.
- After rebuilding, both renderers wrote to the directory named by the symlink traversal and reported the correct path in JSON. Both neighboring files kept their original bytes. The rendered SVG and PNG matched the baseline artifacts byte for byte, and ordinary output still created its parent directory. An output with a missing segment before `..` exited 1 and preserved the neighboring file.
- The regression failed on the base at the overwritten-neighbor assertion. The fixed command and shared resolver suites passed all 40 tests. Core and command-test type checks, targeted formatting, and lint passed, and independent autoreview through P2 returned no actionable findings. macOS and Windows were outside the local run.

<details>
<summary>Commands and timing</summary>

```sh
pnpm openclaw --version
node openclaw.mjs agents render-blobster selected/../design.json --out selected/../preview.svg --json
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts src/infra/home-dir.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts src/commands/agents.commands.blobster.ts
```

Replay the CLI command from a temporary directory with `selected` pointing to `physical/nested`, the guide's sample saved as `physical/design.json`, and a sentinel file at `preview.svg`. Use the checkout's absolute entry path when running from the fixture directory. The passing Vitest run took 65 seconds wall time, including a cold compiled-worker build. CI timing is pending.

</details>

prs.title: chore(deps): refresh dependencies through the November 13 cutoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw’s runtime, native apps, and build tooling are pinned to older dependency releases. This sweep picks up compatible updates while keeping the seven-day supply-chain cooldown in place.

## User Impact

The Gateway and bundled WebSocket consumers move to the [ws 8.23.0 security release](https://github.com/websockets/ws/releases/tag/8.23.0). Other changes refresh install, native, release, and CI dependencies without introducing new settings, migrations, or user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit fixed an inclusive cutoff of **2026-11-13 22:51:20 UTC**. It updates 91 distinct npm pins or existing overrides, 22 Fastlane transitive gems, and five Cargo locks, plus qualified scanner and container pins. It adds no cooldown exclusions or patches. TypeBox advances to 1.4.5, the newest qualifying release that preserves OpenClaw’s namespace contract. parse5 8.1.x and fs-safe 0.27.2 were deferred after the UI build and a filesystem test found regressions. Updates under separate review ([Android #200037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200037), [Actions #201745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201745), and [Ruff #198356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198356)), and major or toolchain updates without compatible consumer proof, are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Fixed-cutoff audit: **230** newly resolved pnpm identities, **47** new identities in standalone npm locks, **154** introduced Cargo lock entries, and all **22** updated gems. Compared retained dependency edges; no downgrades or too-young new identities were found. Frozen pnpm/npm and Bundler installs and locked Cargo metadata passed.
- The CI artifact build, production typechecks, focused Gateway/provider/lockfile and filesystem tests, workflow validation, lint, and formatting passed locally. The repository’s paired Control UI budget check passed in a clean exact-commit checkout using CI’s Node 24.22.1. The Vercel and Sandbox CLIs materialized from the pinned lock and exposed the expected release subcommands; no deployment ran.
- Locked Rust workspace, watch engine, and both iroh binding suites passed. The Linux desktop suite has one failure reproduced on the exact base (an Ubuntu multicall fixture); opt-in logind cases exceeded the local socket path limit. Fastlane Supply and Deliver loaded from the frozen mobile locks. Native-platform CI is still required.
- OpenGrep changed-path scanning and SARIF conversion, zizmor validation, PostgreSQL and Node container smoke tests, and a local Litestream restore/rollback passed. The local OpenGrep Vitest suite stalled in the host Git wrapper; the direct scanner checks do not count as a passing Vitest run.
- Local Codex autoreview covered all 105 changed paths of the committed tree against `d5a99b07e88e`; no actionable P0/P1 findings were reported. Build and registry checks provide separate evidence.

Co-authored by [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

prs.title: fix(tlon): require approval before responding in group DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon group DM messages carry author claims that the Tlon transport does not authenticate. OpenClaw could treat a claimed ship in a group DM as if it matched the verified 1:1 DM allowlist, admitting unapproved input to the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner enables a group DM once per club by default, then the agent can respond automatically in that club. Operators can require approval for each message, disable clubs, or allow and deny specific club IDs. Existing clubs need one-time enablement after upgrade; claimed authors and legacy approvals do not grant standing access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Club admission now depends on the club's own policy and recorded decision. Claimed participants never provide owner or command authority. Approved club messages use a club-specific group session, and replies return to the club. The change also decodes Tlon's wrapped settings events so saved decisions work across restarts.

Enabling a club accepts unverified input delivered under that club ID with the agent's ordinary permitted tools. It does not authenticate the author or membership; the owner prompt and Tlon docs explain that tradeoff.

This is a replacement for #196109. Thanks to @mmaps for identifying the group DM author-claim boundary and preparing the first fix. This version keeps approval friction to once per club by default and adds explicit stricter modes and club reply routing.

## Evidence

- The two regression cases failed on the base and pass with this change: an allowlisted claimed author cannot admit an unknown club, and a club turn uses a group route rather than the claimed author's direct route.
- In an isolated Gateway with a real model, a bot-side Tlon club event claiming allowlisted `~nec` produced one owner prompt and no agent turn. A verified `~bus` DM approved the club; the saved message ran through the model, which read a proof file and replied inside the club. A later message claiming the owner received an automatic club reply without another prompt. After Gateway restart, the saved club rule still allowed an automatic reply.
- Upgrade check: the published `@openclaw/tlon@2026.11.5` plugin created a legacy pending club request in isolated ship state. The replacement plugin loaded it; owner approval replayed the saved message without adding the claimed ship to the DM allowlist or enabling the club. The next message prompted for a new club decision.
- Startup persistence check: with no saved club rules, an explicit file-config allow rule migrated into the real Urbit settings store as a JSON string. A regression test failed before this serialization repair and passes after it.
- All 322 Tlon tests in 35 files pass. Tlon production and test typechecks, focused lint and format, docs MDX/config examples/internal links, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- The generated config baseline records six intentional Tlon schema paths for club policy and rules at the channel and account levels. Relative to current `main`, core and plugin counts are unchanged; `pnpm config:docs:check` passes. The merged current-main tree also passes all 322 Tlon tests and the Tlon production typecheck.
- CI on merged head `dfc6c43b` passed the config baseline, docs, Control UI e2e, and `openclaw/ci-gate` checks; the earlier one-request Control UI asset-budget failure did not recur.
- Local autoreview of the complete staged source change against base `053fb62c` reported `scoped-clean` for P0–P2 with no actionable finding at `b293ba33`. The later commits add generated baseline files and merge current `main`; the Tlon source patch is unchanged. Its assessment covered the supplied patch, not a live Tlon round trip.
- Authenticated remote ingress proof: a test-only Gall agent on isolated fake `~ten` sent a native remote `%chat-club-action` poke over Ames to fake `~zod`, claiming author `~nec`. The remote poke was acknowledged and `~zod` stored the club message. The isolated Gateway emitted one approval prompt to verified `~ten` DM and no agent turn before approval. After that DM approved the club, the real model read a proof file and replied `papaya` into `~zod`'s club. A second remotely delivered message claiming owner `~ten` received an automatic club reply without another approval prompt; saved `clubRules` contains the allow rule and no pending approval.
- Remaining Tlon transport gap: stock club gossip failed to reach the peer in hand-assembled desks and Tlon's published prebuilt fake-ship fixture. I also booted fresh non-fake Urbit comets in an isolated VM. Two comets on the same updated `%groups` desk hash (`a6eta`) exchanged Ames `|hi` and a direct DM invitation. In both directions, `chat-club-create` returned an Eyre poke ACK and recorded the club locally, but the invited comet's club list stayed empty. The older desk additionally logged `%bad-fact-mark` for club actions during its update. The sender ship did not receive the bot's club reply in the fake-ship proof, although it was present in the bot ship's club. Authenticated remote club ingress through a native Gall poke and the OpenClaw admission/reply boundary are proven; stock Tlon club propagation and a peer-visible reply remain unproven. Confirm that round trip on working Tlon ships before merge.

prs.title: feat: switch sessions with Command-1–9 and Control-Tab in the desktop apps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching conversations needs the mouse, or Command-K and typing part of a name. With several sessions running at once, this is the most frequent navigation in the app, and the desktop apps have no direct key for it, unlike Slack, Linear, or browser tabs.

## User Impact

User impact: in the macOS app and the other desktop apps, Command-1 through Command-8 (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) open that session in the sidebar, and Command-9 opens the last one. Control-Tab goes back to the session you were in before; hold Control and press Tab again to go further back, or add Shift to go the other way.

**Changed default:** in the macOS app's Gateway menu and the web identity menu's Gateway picker, Gateway shortcuts move from Command-1–9 to Control-Command-1–9 (Control-Option-Command for a new window), so Command-1–9 can open sessions.

Web browsers keep both chords for their own tabs, so nothing changes in a browser tab.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar owns the visible order (pinned, groups, expanded children, then the rest, minus collapsed sections and catalog sessions), so the sidebar handles the keys and opens sessions through its normal row navigation. The keys are bound only when the page runs in a desktop host (`isNativeWebChromeHost()`), the same split New Session already uses for Command-N. They work from the composer, ignore key repeat and text composition, and leave open dialogs alone.

Control-Tab walks a most-recently-used list of up to 20 sessions opened in this window. Holding Control freezes that order for the walk, as app switchers do; releasing Control makes the session you stopped on the most recent one. Sessions that can no longer be opened are skipped. Before a second session has been opened, Control-Tab moves to the next sidebar row.

In the macOS app the Dashboard web view sees key equivalents before the main menu, so the page claims Command-1–9 and the Gateway menu items move to Control-Command so both keep working. The shortcuts dialog lists the new keys in desktop apps only.

Related: #182559 (jump to the next session waiting for you) is navigation by state; this is navigation by position and recency.

## Evidence

Keyboard shortcuts dialog (Command-/), Sidebar section, in the Control UI with the macOS desktop host emulated by the existing `installNativeWebChrome` fixture, Chromium at 1440×900 and 2×, synthetic sessions. Before is `main` at 39250610246, after is this branch.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the Sidebar section lists only the multi-select click chords](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4477ce9-c0c5-49eb-a12a-1db31d1040ee) | ![After: the Sidebar section also lists Command 1–9 to open a sidebar session and Control-Tab to switch to a recent session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2509f99d-4377-4b30-9c1f-67ce31430537) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Sidebar rows outlined: no session switching keys](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb598459-6395-4cfb-bb27-5b64c6add9ff) | ![New rows outlined: session switching keys, desktop app only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13027694-19eb-4800-b49c-ed7bca1c7b7e) |

- **E2E** `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-session-shortcuts.e2e.test.ts`: with the desktop host emulated and focus in the composer, Command-3, Command-9 and Command-2 open the third, last and second sessions; Control-Tab returns to the previous one and back; holding Control and pressing Tab twice walks two back, and releasing Control keeps that session; Control-Shift-Tab walks the other way. A second case checks that a plain browser page leaves Command-2 unclaimed and ignores Control-Tab. Passes.
- **Unit** `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-shortcuts.test.ts` (13 tests): position targets and Command-9, the held-Control walk and its final promotion, skipped unavailable sessions, the 20-session bound, AZERTY-style digit keys, repeat/modifier/composition/browser/modal guards, the next-row fallback, and listener removal. `app-sidebar-native-gateways.test.ts` now expects the Control-Command hints. Both pass.
- **Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` pass.

### macOS app, rebuilt from this branch

`swift build --product OpenClaw` at e8e413f0983 (debug build), attached to a throwaway `clawproof` profile Gateway on loopback with five synthetic chats. Each key press came from a synthetic key event while the Dashboard web view had focus:

![Rebuilt macOS app: Command-3 opens the third sidebar chat (Charlie), Command-1 opens the first (Echo)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64ce7c6b-3613-48b7-9971-b761418f2aa1)

- Command-3 from Main session opens Charlie, the third row.
- Command-1 from Charlie opens Echo, the first row.

### Full key sequence in WebKit

Playwright WebKit on Linux with the desktop host emulated, same branch: Command-3, Command-9 (the last chat), Command-2, quick Control-Tab twice, Control held while Tab is pressed three times and then released, and Control-Shift-Tab. A corner badge names each key; it exists only for the recording.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3db42b09-6ccc-4c1c-b224-86bcf4434275

### Not yet proven in the app

- The held-Control walk and the Gateway menu's Control-Command accelerators. The `swift build` binary has no app bundle, so macOS handed keyboard focus back to the previously active app about a second after each activation, and later key presses never reached the Dashboard. A packaged debug app (`scripts/package-mac-app.sh`) should allow a full in-app recording.
- The Gateway shortcut move itself needs an owner decision: Command-1–9 go to sessions, and Gateways move to Control-Command-1–9 (Control-Option-Command for a new window).

The two Swift edits only change the Gateway menu items' modifier masks and the native card's hint text. The claim that the Dashboard web view sees Command-digits before the menu comes from WebKit's `WebViewImpl::performKeyEquivalent`, which hands key equivalents to the page first when the web view is first responder and passes them on to the menu only if the page leaves them unhandled. The Dashboard's own Command-W handling relies on the same order.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On New Session, tapping project search on a phone moved the text left of the **Recent** heading and shrank the field. In the redesigned device-folder picker, the **Absolute path on device** label started left of the path it described on both phone and desktop.

## User Impact

The search text stays aligned when you tap and type, and the field stays 40 px tall on phones. The device-path label now lines up with the entered path without moving or resizing the input. Selecting a folder still collapses it to the compact project control; reopening it preserves the path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker panel sets the field spacing in every input state. The device-path label uses the same text inset as its input. Both fixes belong to the current picker; neither restores the retired form or changes access to the folder browser.

## Evidence

Paired production builds: main `e6b0b9bda569` and candidate `3f7d26a69d15` (identical tree to published `cf379a3d649d`). Both were exercised in Chromium with the same synthetic Gateway, devices, and projects. No real device was browsed, project registered, or session created. Physical-device keyboards and cloud placement were not tested.

### Device folder: writer without admin access

The first dark pixel of the label moved **x=44 → 52** on phone and **x=624 → 632** on desktop, matching the path at both widths. The CSS text origins likewise align at x=51 and x=631. The field stayed **304 × 40** at 390 × 844 and **304 × 32** at 1440 × 900. The writer entered an absolute path, pressed Enter, reopened the compact selection, and returned with Back without a directory listing.

### Project search: touch focus in onboarding

At 390 × 844, the first dark pixel of both placeholder and typed query moved **x=44 → 52**, matching **Recent**. The focused field height changed **24.8 → 40 px**. At 1440 × 900 field and heading stayed at x=475. Typing filtered the project options; the sibling device search was also exercised.

Both focused regressions failed by 8 px on the pinned main build. All seven bundled device-folder and project-access tests passed after the fix. UI and UI-test typechecks, scoped formatting, CSS lint, and TypeScript lint passed. Local autoreview could not start its reviewer in this checkout. The native comparison on the two production builds passed: total CSS fell from 1,781,614 to 1,781,379 raw bytes (−235) and from 344,799 to 344,786 gzip bytes (−13). Both builds remain above the fixed total CSS ceilings.

**Historical evidence only.** [#203269](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203269) retired the persistent stacked label, field and hint. The original [before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9dd1134e-3e83-42c8-a899-f0306dd2c7a4) / [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d557bf8-1672-437d-9889-b9eb4689fb18) and [annotated before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52e1d16b-9e2a-4cb3-9b5d-cd163583effc) / [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cceea9f-ba03-4a17-99e3-c853142b43e1) document a 7 px offset in that old layout, not the current interface.

prs.title: fix(ui): simplify activity summaries and separate agent milestones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mixed tool groups in chat enumerate every category, making a short work summary read like an inventory. Agent launches and completions also sit too close to neighboring tool groups.

## User Impact

- A group that reads and changes files, runs commands, searches, and reads memory now summarizes as **Read and changed files, ran commands**.
- Agent milestones remain separate, with a 16 px gap to adjacent tool blocks instead of 8 px.
- Expanding a group still shows every operation in its original order. Isolated command text is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the headline by the work performed, rather than cap the number of categories. File reads and changes combine when their states agree. Completed searches and memory reads become supporting detail beside file work; completed generic “used tools” adds no extra phrase beside a specific category. Search-only groups, memory updates, active operations, and uncertain outcomes retain their own labels.

The spacing applies only at milestone/tool boundaries, not to every operation inside an expanded list. No agent lifecycle regrouping, command rewriting, or runtime behavior change is included.

## Matched 8 px and 16 px comparison

Chromium, 1200 × 890, same release-checklist fixture. Main `8b6ffa48341c` shows **8 px** on either side of the completion; `d5b404200b7f` shows **16 px** on either side and the short agent name stays on one line. The fixture uses a synthetic transcript through the real Control UI. The final selector-only update (`a75182d15eb6`) was remeasured and visually inspected; it has the same 16 px gap and one-line completion name.

## Evidence

- 86 focused UI tests passed. Updated existing summary/consumer expectations and added five selection cases for standalone discovery, active/failed searches, and memory writes. No pixel-locking tests added.
- 19 existing browser checks passed across nested tool presentation and turn outcomes, including approval states.
- Two temporary visual checks passed against the production UI build in dark and light themes; expanded details retained the supporting operations.
- UI production build, UI typecheck, scoped lint, Stylelint, formatting, i18n verification, and controller guard passed.
- Native `codex review --uncommitted` found no actionable defects. Local autoreview also completed one Codex pass against `a3357794fa56cdd96e411272290aaf2752797925` plus the final local changes, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview assessed the supplied diff without executing project code; runtime evidence is listed above. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review remains required by the maintainer fallback route.

The published CSS uses the existing 8 px spacing token twice at milestone boundaries (16 px). The follow-up passed the paired production asset check and the 39 targeted unit and 19 browser cases. The images below are the original 24 px proposal and show the same grouping and labels; their spacing annotation is historical.

Screenshots below use the same synthetic transcript through the real Control UI and mocked gateway transport, with the same viewport, crop, scale, and theme. Before: `a3357794fa56cdd96e411272290aaf2752797925`. After: `dbd9f69f08ec161ca5923ae1a48e9a5a82fc056f`. This verifies presentation, not a live model or subagent run.

## What Problem This Solves

When activity moved a chat in the Sessions sidebar, the inline name field could lose focus and save what you had typed so far. Further typing went nowhere. A keyboard-focused chat link could also lose focus when it moved, leaving Enter with nothing to open.

Keeping the same DOM element was not enough: moving it could blur the editor and end native text composition. The sidebar now holds only display order during an inline edit, including nested chats. prs.title: fix: show earlier attachments in Session files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Files in a long chat could show only the recent uploads. A file shared at the beginning could be missing until someone scrolled back through the conversation.

## User Impact

Session files now includes older attachments without loading earlier chat pages. New uploads also appear while Files stays open, without waiting for the active run to finish. Files keep their native previews, and “Show in chat” goes to the source message. A partial-list notice remains when the Gateway really cannot supply the whole list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Files already requests the session’s artifacts. The Gateway collects attachment references in that same transcript pass and reuses its revision-aware cache. There is no new table, migration, history preload, or extra catalog request. A 4 MiB ceiling bounds the extra metadata; if it is reached, the panel retains both the collected references and attachments from the loaded chat. Older Gateways retain their existing fallback.

## Evidence

- Parity of the two SQLite artifact reads: the same admitted attachment IDs and sequence numbers survive both cached metadata and include-download queries. The fixture fails with the old visitor and passes with the repair; 22 Gateway tests and nine focused UI checks passed. Both import-cycle guards report zero cycles.
- The production asset check passes on the repaired candidate 33712df50015. In the paired build, Chat used the same 21 requests and stayed below the JavaScript gzip cap. Six Files browser checks also passed with the shared deduplication rule.

- In Chromium, with the same paginated chat fixture, the original project brief was missing on `abd8b92cfa` and present on `b63c38fb27`. Both versions made one catalog request. This verifies the Control UI, not a native macOS run.
- 58 focused UI tests, the real Gateway integration test, core and UI type checks, and the UI production build passed. The build reported advisory bundle-budget overages; no budgets were raised.
- In a local synthetic session with 1,204 messages and 27 messages carrying attachments, the catalog RPC took 13.9 ms on the first request after appending history, then 3.7 and 2.6 ms. The response was 6,469 bytes. These are local observations, not a production latency guarantee.

### Live upload while Files stays open

Both captures show the same Chromium fixture after a PDF arrived in chat during an active run. On the previous PR head the panel stays stale; on the repaired head it shows the new upload once, keeps the earlier files, and still makes only one catalog request.

| Previous PR head | Live update |
| --- | --- |
| ![The new upload is already in chat but Files still lists two files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48c0be91-1319-4973-9043-766407c077d2) | ![Revised diagrams.pdf appears alongside the two older files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65f38e2e-5bfa-4074-8cc3-eae34ae1a2b6) |

- Both complete and capped catalog regressions failed before the repair. The repaired code passes 53 focused UI tests, 33 Gateway artifact tests, UI type checking, and changed-file lint.
- Chromium also opened a catalog-only image in the native lightbox through the mocked artifact download, then fetched the older chat page on “Show in chat” and displayed the source. The grid action stayed inside its tile. These are Control UI interactions against a fixture Gateway, not a native macOS run.
- The local UI bundle comparison passes with no additional raw or gzipped CSS versus the PR base. No budget changed. The local independent review helper did not start with the worktree-scoped temporary directory; this follow-up does not claim a fresh automated review.

### Clean comparison

prs.title: fix(workboard): write tools return the whole card with all its comments and history on every call
prs.body:
Closes #162498

## What Problem This Solves

Every Workboard write tool (`workboard_comment`, `workboard_move`, `workboard_heartbeat`, `workboard_release`, `workboard_claim`, `workboard_proof`, ...) answers with the whole card: notes, every past comment, events and proof. An agent that keeps a card current pays for that history again on each call, and the result grows with every comment. #162498 measured 21 KB on average per `workboard_comment` call, and #180394 measured ~28 KB per heartbeat.

## User Impact

Write tools now answer with the same compact card summary `workboard_list` uses (id, title, status, claim state, links, diagnostics), plus the id of what they added: `commentId`, `attachmentId` or `proofId`. `workboard_claim` still returns its token. `workboard_read` still returns the full card. Agents that read history from a write result need `workboard_read` instead. Nothing in the repo did that: the dispatcher, worker prompts and Control UI use the store or the read path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Most write tools share one result helper, which returned the full redacted card. This PR changes that helper's contract once, keeping the card nested under `card` so its status is never mistaken for the tool result's. The writes outside the helper (create, link, claim, proof, decompose) get the same summary. `summarizeCard` moves next to the helper unchanged, so list and write results share one shape.

## Evidence

**Real deployment:** over 3 days and 184 agent sessions, `workboard_comment` results over 12 KB totalled 2.32M characters in 92 calls. The largest single result was 35,302 characters, 24.7K of them past comments and 5K events.

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways, tools called through `POST /tools/invoke`. A card gets 30 comments of 700 characters, then each tool runs once on it. The numbers are `details` JSON characters.

| Tool, on a card with 30 comments | 2026.11.6 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `workboard_comment` | 27,145 | 222 (`card`, `commentId`) |
| `workboard_move` | 27,277 | 171 |
| `workboard_claim` | 27,719 | 341 (token still returned) |
| `workboard_heartbeat` | 27,760 | 292 |
| `workboard_proof` | 28,029 | 343 (`proofId` still returned) |
| `workboard_release` | 27,967 | 171 |
| `workboard_dispatch` (due card with 30 comments, promoted) | 27,181 | 238 |
| `workboard_read` (control) | 32,706 | 32,706, all 31 comments |

Tested on `86a84515286` (rebased onto main) against 2026.11.6.

- Tests: new `tools.compact-results.test.ts` checks that comment, move, heartbeat and release results stay small and leave out metadata and notes while read keeps them (fails on main, passes here). `tools.test.ts` assertions that read history from write results now read it from the store. On `86a84515286` the workboard suite passes (32 files, 333 tests), and lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude) on the pre-rebase head `3b0d6fc24e8`, no P0–P2 findings, clean.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Credit: @-mentions are left out on purpose. #162498 (21 KB on average per comment call) and #180394 (heartbeat/release, ~28 KB per heartbeat) both measured this.

Alternatives considered: a per-tool `compact` flag or a comment-only patch would leave move, heartbeat, release and the rest echoing the card. Trimming comments inside the full card would still send notes, events, proof and attempts. The list summary already exists and is what agents use to choose work, so writes reuse it.

Repro script (needs `openclaw plugins enable workboard` on the test Gateway): creates a card through `/tools/invoke`, adds the comments, then prints each write tool's result size, with `workboard_read` as the control.

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep nested chats steady in the session sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A nested chat looked like a task rather than a conversation: finishing a run replaced its usual identity with a green check. A fresh child-list read could insert a blank row, and a title update replaced the title element even when the chat stayed in place.

## User Impact

Child chats now look like ordinary session rows, just indented. They use the same text, avatars, unread dots, activity rings, and attention indicators. A new or removed chat takes or releases its own space; a pending read doesn't move its neighbors. Sorting, nesting, and which chats are visible are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removed the separate child badge, timer, and layout rules. Kept the title mounted as its text changes, and moved loading feedback onto the existing disclosure rather than allocating a row for it. Background subagents still don't appear as navigation rows.

## Evidence

Chromium exercised the real Control UI with synthetic Gateway data. Across desktop and emulated phone widths, light and dark themes, touch and pointer input, and enlarged text, the retained title stayed in place through refresh and completion. prs.title: fix: refresh pinned agent cards when their reply arrives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pinned agent in the session sidebar could say “No agent reply yet” after the latest reply had already arrived. This was reproducible in the phone and tablet drawer: the roster had the reply, but the open card still showed the empty state.

## User Impact

The reply appears in the existing card without closing and reopening it. A genuinely empty agent still shows the empty message. No additional Gateway request is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar decided whether to repaint roster cards by comparing agent names and avatars, but not the assistant preview it displays. A reply-only change could therefore be discarded as visually identical. The comparison now includes that text. Session sorting, row geometry, and the roster’s source of truth are unchanged.

## Evidence

On current-main baseline `010b5348381e`, the focused regression delivered a settled roster snapshot with an assistant reply and observed the visible card staying empty. On `0a4680fbc1a7`, the same receipt updated the text while preserving the preview element. The open tooltip bounds matched before and after.

The full app’s pin, hover, keyboard, and unpin flow also passed at 390, 768, 1366, and 1440 pixels. The UI build and typecheck, 111 focused tests, Solid guards, and formatting passed. prs.body:
Closes #200034

## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Enter to confirm an IME composition in a Control UI input dialog (group name, session rename, device alias) saves the unfinished text and closes the dialog.

## User Impact

User impact: IME users can finish composing a name before saving. Ordinary Enter and Save are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dialog input now ignores composition Enter, using the shared `lib/ime.ts` helper the login gate already uses.

## Evidence

- New `input-dialog` case: composition Enter (`isComposing`, `keyCode` 229) is prevented, ordinary Enter is not. Red on base, green with the fix.
- `input-dialog.test.ts` (12 tests), `tsgo:ui`, oxfmt, oxlint and the test-line ratchet pass.

## Real behavior proof

Real Control UI "New group" dialog in Chrome 157 on Linux, mocked Gateway (repo e2e harness), head `01a0fa0` vs the same tree without the fix. Composition driven through Chrome with CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` of `に`, then `page.keyboard.press("Enter")`. The keydown is trusted with `isComposing=true`.

```text
base: composition Enter -> dialog closed, sessions.groups.put {"names":["に"]}
head: composition Enter -> dialog stays open, 0 requests
head: ordinary Enter after commit -> dialog closes, 1 put {"names":["Client work"]}
head: Save click after composition Enter -> dialog closes, 1 put
```

Not a native OS IME candidate window; Gateway state is synthetic.

prs.title: fix(update): retire database snapshots of earlier updates after a verified update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An update can leave a full copy of the databases in a `.databases` directory. Only the creating run's own verified completion removes it. Nothing removes one that a failed update, an update without automatic restoration, or an older updater left behind. On one host, eight of them held 63 GiB.

On today's `main` (after #200578 and #201711):

- Package installs still write `<package-backup>.databases` beside the package backup. A verified update removes its own; a failed one, or one whose restoration was unavailable, keeps it.
- Git installs now run from releases and take no database snapshot. But updaters before #200578 rebuilt the checkout in place and left `<checkout>/.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-<uuid>.tmp.databases` directories. No code on `main` names or removes those (the affected host has four, about 34 GiB).
- #201711 removes Doctor backups, `.migrated-<runId>` files and original-state captures. It does not touch `.databases` directories.

## User Impact

User impact: after a later update is verified healthy, update cleanup removes the snapshot directories earlier updates left behind, both automatically and through `openclaw update cleanup` (and the Gateway's `update.cleanup`, including dry run). This includes the ones older updaters left in a Git checkout's `.artifacts`. The ones it keeps are listed with their size and reason. The latest verified update's own snapshot waits for the next verified update. Snapshots of a Git checkout outside the home directory are not found and stay, as do snapshots no listed update recorded. With `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"`, cleanup drops a snapshot's PostgreSQL capture schemas before deleting it, and keeps and reports the snapshot when that drop fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

A snapshot directory's name carries a transaction id, not a run id, and nothing inside it names a run (`schema-discovery-ownership.json` maps databases to owners only). The only record linking it to an update is the `database snapshot` location in update history. Cleanup now reads that location and treats a snapshot as superseded once a verified successful update started after its run finished. That is the rule original-state captures already follow, decided by run order and never by file times.

- Kept and reported: a snapshot of an unfinished run, of a run with a pending recovery, of the latest verified run or anything after it, and a snapshot-named directory no listed run recorded (`orphan-database-snapshot`; only file times could order it).
- Automatic cleanup never releases the triggering update's own snapshot, also when a clock set back makes an earlier verified run look like its successor.
- Deletion reuses the capture retirement path: no symlinks, same directory identity as when selected, same cleanup authority.
- PostgreSQL server captures keep the lifecycle their owning update gives them (#196236). A snapshot's `<image>.postgres` export manifests are the only record of the capture schemas on the server. Cleanup passes the export directories that hold a manifest to the existing `discardPostgresSchemaCaptures` first, with the configuration cleanup already reads. If the drop fails, the directory stays and the item reports `failed` / `database-snapshot-retirement-failed` with `PostgreSQL capture cleanup remains pending at <directory>`; a later cleanup retries. A `.postgres` directory without a manifest is a mirrored source directory or the rest of an interrupted removal, and does not block cleanup.
- Previous install roots are in scope only when a run recorded a location that still resolves. Update history shortens the home directory to `~` and redacts other install roots to `[path]`, so a checkout outside the home directory cannot be resolved. When the OpenClaw home and the OS home differ, `~` names two directories and attributes none.
- An earlier install root that is unreadable, or whose path is no longer a directory path, is skipped instead of failing the whole cleanup inventory.

Decisions for the maintainer:

1. Attribution parses a path-redacted diagnostic. A structured, unredacted receipt in the run record would also cover checkouts outside the home directory, but needs a schema change and would not help snapshots already on disk.
2. A run's own verified success does not release its snapshot here, because the updater says non-restorable snapshots remain available after activation. Captures do release on their own success.
3. Orphans are report-only; `--include-unmanifested` cannot select them.
4. Status now counts these snapshots under update captures. Doctor's `core/doctor/update-snapshots` check still advises manual removal.
5. The server-capture drop uses the current configuration's connection, as `openclaw update finish` does for its own receipt. Accepted: if the configuration now names a different PostgreSQL server than the one the snapshot was captured on, `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` finds nothing there, the snapshot is deleted, and the capture schema on the old server stays.
6. A superseded snapshot is removed without checking that the live databases it copied still exist. Original-state captures follow the same rule; Doctor backups and moved-aside copies do check. A review asked for that check here; it is not added, because a later update was verified healthy on that state. Say so if snapshots should get the check too.

## Evidence

Head `3d509d0`, rebased onto `main` `4bedaed`. The real runs below used `9334a04`; `3d509d0` differs from it in one test file only.

**Tests** (each red on the base, green on the branch)

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-snapshot-cleanup.test.ts` (new, 7 tests) runs the real `updateCleanupCommand` and `cleanupCompletedUpdateRecovery` over a temp home with real update-history rows:
  - dry run reports each snapshot's run, bytes and reason and deletes nothing;
  - `--yes` and automatic cleanup remove only the two superseded snapshots (a legacy Git one under a previous checkout root, a package one outside home);
  - kept: pending recovery, latest verified run, a failure after it, an unfinished run, an orphan, and the triggering run's own snapshot; untouched: a non-updater name, a redacted-root snapshot, a recorded path replaced by a symlink, and home-relative snapshots while two homes are in play;
  - a former install root replaced by a regular file (`ENOTDIR`) no longer aborts cleanup;
  - the server-capture drop receives only the export directory that holds a manifest, while that manifest still exists; when it rejects, the snapshot stays `failed` and the command exits 1.
- `src/infra/database-engine/backup-schema-capture.test.ts` against real PostgreSQL 17 (`scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs`, disposable `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` container): a real update capture creates a `restore_…` schema and `updateCleanupCommand({ yes: true })` runs twice. With an unreachable connection the schema and manifest both remain and the item reports `failed`. With the real connection the capture schema is dropped, the live store's schema remains and the directory is gone. Run on `84954c9`, not repeated after the later two commits.
- On the rebased branch all 7 tests in the first file fail with the wiring reverted to `main`, and the PostgreSQL test fails the same way. The triggering-run and manifest cases were each red without their fix.
- `pnpm check:changed` on `9334a04`: exit 0. Net test lines against the merge base: +400 of 400 (`9334a04` failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` at +409; `3d509d0` folds one test into another).

**It works: legacy Git snapshots** (Crabbox `local-container` on the Mac Studio, `node:24.22.1-trixie`, lease `cbx_d34709ead512`, run `run_534ff1aa121f62943602014dc138d057`, exit 0)

- An updater from before #200578 (`44ec89e`) updates a source checkout in place four times while the Gateway runs by hand: twice under `~/Projects/openclaw/.worktrees/live-main-ba9f1ea`, twice under `~/Projects/openclaw` after the install moves. Each run keeps its `.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-<uuid>.tmp.databases` (17.8 MB together).
- The four update-history rows, written by those real updates, were then rewritten in the state database to the shapes recorded on the affected host (run `failed` / `post-update-failed`, a failed `database rollback` step): two with the Oct 27 2026 wording, two with the Oct 3 to Oct 20 wording. This is the only state edit.
- The Gateway service is installed and the checkout updates to `main` `4bedaed`. All four directories remain, and `main`'s `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run --json` lists no `database-snapshot` artifact.
- The next update, to this PR, finishes verified (`serviceRunning`, `versionMatch`, `settled`, `coreReady`, no plugin errors). Its automatic cleanup reports `Removed …/.worktrees/live-main-ba9f1ea/.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-26124ce4-….tmp.databases (4272383 logical bytes)` and the other three. No snapshot directory remains.
- Caveat: the update to `main` exited 1 (`post-update-failed`: the old checkout build refused the new state schema) although the Gateway then served from the release. So this run shows that `main` neither lists nor removes these directories, not that they survive a verified update on `main`. That failure happened before any code from this PR was installed.
- Substituted: the container has no systemd, so the service manager is the repository's upgrade e2e stand-in.

**It works: package install** (lease `cbx_c94e7446a4a3`, run `run_f7324d80b838230c88083cd349e11a46`, exit 0)

- `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.6`, then `openclaw update --tag <tarball>` to `main~6` (`a27f0c3`) and to this PR with the Gateway service running. Both finish verified. Each run snapshots to `~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-backup-<pid>-<ts>.databases` and removes it on its own verified completion; none remain and the dry run is empty.
- This shows a package upgrade from stable works on the PR. It did not produce a kept package snapshot: with the Gateway run by hand, 2026.11.6 refuses the update (`gateway-stop-unverified`) before taking one.

**It does not break existing upgrades** (repository upgrade lanes, `scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh`, run from lease `cbx_fc8ff4647655` through the Studio's Docker engine, candidate `9334a04`)

| Lane | Baseline | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| published upgrade survivor (package) | `openclaw@2026.11.6` | passed, 660 s |
| `git-release` (Git install, kill points `stage build publish link-switch launcher-restore`) | tag `v2026.11.6` | passed over two runs |
| `recovery-cleanup` | `openclaw@2026.11.6` | failed at `package-swap`, inherited |

- `git-release`: the first run passed every phase through `git-kill-build`, then failed in `git-kill-publish` because the harness missed its kill window (`"missed":"the link moved before the release smoke was seen"`). The second run, with kill points `publish link-switch launcher-restore`, passed (`Git release survivor passed: route baseline.`).
- `recovery-cleanup`: `State schema inspection failed … during pre-migration database backup for …/client/credentials.sqlite … hardlink publication target changed`, then a clean package rollback. #202590 saw the same signature on `main` (lease `cbx_e9fabf91f712`). It was not rerun on `main` here.
- All three leases were stopped.

**Earlier proof** on `5fb7e5a`, before the rebase (leases `cbx_5fe14464ed65`, `cbx_892d7fe68601`, `cbx_f37a9e6d9f22`): base kept three in-place Git snapshots after a verified update and did not list them; head listed them as `awaiting-later-verified-update` and removed them after the verified update.

**Not proven**

- No run against the affected host's own update history.
- A kept package snapshot (failed update, or restoration unavailable) retired through a real update; covered by the test file only.
- `openclaw update cleanup --yes` removing a snapshot candidate through the real CLI: automatic cleanup always got there first.
- The server-capture drop through a full `openclaw update` cycle on a PostgreSQL install.
- Windows `~\` expansion, receipt wording of updaters before Oct 3 2026, and an install root failing with `EACCES` (same guard as `ENOTDIR`, no test).
- Update history's secret redaction can mask part of a long checkout path (seen once as `/srv/p…law/.worktrees/…`). Such a receipt does not resolve, so that snapshot stays.

prs.title: fix: let Side chat finish long answers or stop just the answer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Working Side chat answers were cut off after a minute. The panel hid the timeout behind a generic error and had no way to stop just the side answer without clearing the thread.

## User Impact

User impact: wait for a longer answer, stop it without losing earlier answers or your next draft, and retry in place after a timeout or a temporary model failure. The main session is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing runner detects model inactivity; Side chat keeps a short preparation deadline and a five-minute overall limit. Stop targets the caller’s exact side question, not the main run or the thread history. Model execution now lives separately from question admission and cancellation.

## Evidence

Gateway tests exercised a 75-second answer, stalled preparation, a terminal timeout, late cleanup, exact-question cancellation and stale Stop. The Control UI against a synthetic Gateway exercised Stop, draft preservation, timeout copy, Retry, image retry, session switching and mobile selection. Production core and UI typechecks passed. Independent local review could not start in its read-only sandbox; no live provider or deployment was used as proof.

Desktop Side chat, Chromium, light theme, synthetic session. The first pair shows the same timeout before and after the change.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An installed plugin’s icon in the Customize sidebar briefly disappears when another plugin changes. The label and link stay in place, but the icon flashes back to a loading tile.

## User Impact

Unchanged shortcuts keep their icons. A plugin that gains artwork still shows its new icon without requiring a reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar treated each fresh inventory object as a replacement for its artwork. It now retains the artwork for the same installation; a catalog identity, version, install time or icon-availability change still reloads it. An in-place icon file edit with none of those changes is picked up when Customize is reopened.

## Evidence

Three updates renamed the notes plugin without changing Calendar. In the before recording Calendar’s blue icon disappeared three times for nine frames each. prs.title: fix(ui): give installed skills their own page
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed skills open inside ClawHub discovery today. The Installed chip duplicates the Installed skills button, and a discovery query can carry over into the inventory.

## User Impact

The existing **Installed skills** button opens a dedicated page with its own search. It uses the same page container, rows, icons, and status indicators as Skills discovery. **Skills** takes you back to your discovery query and position; a skill opened from Installed takes you back to that inventory and its filter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate chip and separate discovery from inventory navigation without changing how skills look or are managed. The inventory shares the existing Skills route renderer and agent-scoped reads. Its first grid waits for the workspace and library reads to settle so late library rows cannot move workspace rows that are already visible. This does not change ClawHub categories or Skills settings.

## Evidence

- [Before and after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202766#issuecomment-7052344401), clean and annotated, from the Control UI with a synthetic Gateway. The final inventory matches the published after image pixel for pixel in the installed content area.
- Browser walkthrough verified opening Installed while searching, filtering the inventory, opening a skill, and returning through both levels with the discovery query, exact scroll offset, and keyboard focus restored. Also verified direct reload and the single-column layout at 390 px.
- Chromium’s `layout-shift` observer recorded no entries while delayed reads settled at 400, 820, and 1280 px, in either arrival order, from the Installed button and a fresh direct link. Before the follow-up, a late library response could move workspace rows down by 160, 124, and 64 px respectively. These measurements used the running Control UI against deterministic Gateway fixtures, not a production deployment.
- 45 focused UI tests, including both first-load orders, and 4 Chromium component tests passed. UI translation, controller, and stylesheet checks passed on the original implementation. Production bundling remains unverified: the regular build could not write Vite’s temporary config under the read-only dependency tree, and Vite’s runner stopped in the social-card plugin before transforming app modules.
- Local independent review could not run with the task’s configured scratch directory; hosted review has picked up the draft.

prs.title: feat(discord): match final GPT-Live transcripts to voice requests
prs.body:
Related: #203328

## What Problem This Solves

GPT-Live can ask OpenClaw to delegate a Discord voice request before it delivers the user's final transcript. Plugins that review a proposed integration call need the original words and the verified Discord speaker on the same run.

## User Impact

Plugins with conversation access can read the finalized utterance alongside the Discord sender ID and run ID for the GPT-Live subscription route and batch voice. A subscription delegation with an explicit user-turn ID waits for its matching final transcript. If the final transcript never arrives, OpenClaw asks the speaker to repeat the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The subscription transport sends `delegation.created.item.user_bidi_turn_id` and `turn.done.turn.id`. The existing parser discarded those fields. This change preserves them, reuses the bounded delegation queue to wait for the corresponding user transcript, and carries the text through the existing consultation and hook contracts. The Discord speaker ID continues to come from the authenticated voice receiver. Older delegations without a turn ID continue to work and omit the finalized-transcript field. The GPT-Live Platform API route retains its existing behavior.

## Evidence

- A live subscription probe with two synthetic utterances observed both matching IDs. In each case the delegation arrived before its final transcript, and the unpatched controller started the consultation before that final event.
- A patched probe made a live subscription call with two distinct test utterances. GPT-Live delegated the second one, and the patched controller waited for its `turn.done` and delivered only the matching finalized transcript to the stub. GPT-Live answered the first utterance directly.
- All 167 focused tests passed. The provider regressions cover either event order, a mismatched or assistant transcript, duplicate delegation IDs, and a late transcript after timeout. The Discord case verifies each of two speakers receives only their own transcript and sender ID. The hook test checks that the transcript stays behind the conversation-access policy.
- Formatting, scoped Oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. The test probe uses a stub consultation handler and makes no integration calls.

prs.title: docs: show how to test roles locally with a same-host proxy
prs.body:
Closes #202751

## What Problem This Solves

Someone evaluating multiplayer roles on one machine has no documented way to give test accounts their own sign-in. Token and password auth sign everyone in as the shared owner, which cannot hold a role, and the trusted-proxy pages assume a real identity provider. Two details also trip up a same-host setup: the Gateway rejects a loopback client address from a proxy, and a role only caps scopes, so an account without an `identityScopes` grant connects with none.

## User Impact

Operators can try roles locally with a short, tested recipe, and the recipe states plainly that this setup lets any local process act as any allowed account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new "Test roles locally" section in the multiplayer quick setup uses only existing settings: trusted-proxy auth with `allowLoopback`, `allowUsers`, `identityScopes`, `gateway.roles`, the local Gateway password for maintenance commands, and `users.setRole` by profile ID after each first sign-in. The proxy example is a Caddy basic-auth site that overwrites `X-Forwarded-User` and sends a fixed documentation address (`192.0.2.10`) as the client address. The warning repeats the `allowLoopback` risk from the trusted-proxy page in this context, and lists how to keep the test narrow.

## Evidence

The recipe was run on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b) on macOS with Caddy 2.11.9. Ports in the run were 18830 (Gateway) and 18831 (Caddy) instead of the 18789 and 8080 in the docs; nothing else differs.

- The Gateway config from the recipe passes `openclaw config validate` (`"valid":true,"warnings":[]`). The Caddyfile passes `caddy validate`.
- First sign-in creates each profile with the default role. `users.setRole` by profile ID then assigns `administrator` and `member`; by email it is refused.
- After reconnecting, Alice has `operator.admin`, Bob has `operator.read` and `operator.write`, and Bob is denied an administrator method.
- Through the proxy without credentials: HTTP 401. Bob sending his own `X-Forwarded-User: alice@example.test` through the proxy still connects as Bob.
- A local client that skips the proxy and sends forged headers straight to the Gateway port connects with `operator.admin`. This is the behavior the warning describes.
- `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` (the new JSON5 block is schema-checked) and `pnpm check:changed` pass. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` finds no broken link in `docs/start/multiplayer.md`; it reports 7 broken links elsewhere that are already present on `main`.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `review --local-range` against `origin/main` at head 6262add, `review_status: complete`, checkout access verified. Overall B, patch B, proof not applicable (docs only). No findings; security cleared ("describes an existing opt-in loopback trust mode with an accurate impersonation warning").

<details>
<summary>Runtime output (2026.11.5, credentials not printed)</summary>

```text
=== 1. First sign-in through Caddy (creates each profile)
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
=== 2. Profiles after first sign-in
alice@example.test id=219e263c-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
bob@example.test id=4f383f74-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
=== 3. Assign roles by profile id
alice -> administrator: ok
bob -> member: ok
--- users.setRole with an email instead of a profile id:
invalid users.setRole params: must have required property 'profileId'; at root: unexpected property 'email'
=== 4. Reconnect
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
[alice] exec.approvals.get -> OK
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"]
[bob] exec.approvals.get -> DENIED {"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"missing scope: operator.admin",...}
=== 5. Spoofing checks
[anon] HTTP 401
[bob-forging] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"]
[direct-forged] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
[direct-forged] exec.approvals.get -> OK
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: show why a trusted-proxy sign-in was rejected when the web app has no device identity
prs.body:
Closes #202750

## What Problem This Solves

When a Control UI connection without a device identity fails a trusted-proxy check, the Gateway replies "web app requires device identity (use HTTPS or localhost secure context)" and drops the trusted-proxy reason. Operators following the trusted-proxy troubleshooting guide look for reasons such as `trusted_proxy_missing_header_*` or `trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed`, but neither the response nor the Gateway log shows one, and the message points at HTTPS instead.

## User Impact

The rejection now includes the failed check as `details.authReason`, and the Gateway's close log records it as `authReason`. The error code, message and the decision to reject are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The device-less Control UI branch in the connect handler sent `CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` without reading the auth result. It now adds the auth reason when auth did not succeed, the same field the general unauthorized path already returns. Successful auth adds nothing, so token and password clients that only lack a device identity see the same response as before.

## Evidence

- Base, live: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b, same code path as `main` at b8b173b6697), trusted-proxy Gateway on loopback. A device-less Control UI connect with a missing required header, and one with a user outside `allowUsers`, both return the same error with no reason. The Gateway log for both has only `failureCause=control-ui-insecure-auth`, and no `trusted_proxy_` string.
- Head, live: the same two probes against a Gateway built from this branch (same trusted-proxy settings, scratch config and state) now return `authReason: "trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-eval-proxy"` and `authReason: "trusted_proxy_user_not_allowed"`, and the Gateway close log records the same reasons. Code, message and rejection are unchanged.
- Head, tests: `pnpm test src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts` passes (50 tests). The existing loopback case now asserts `authReason: "trusted_proxy_loopback_source"`, and a new case asserts `authReason: "trusted_proxy_missing_header_x-forwarded-proto"`.
- Mutation check: with only the fix reverted (`git apply -R`), both assertions fail with `authReason` missing from the details.
- Related tests pass: `src/gateway/server.auth.modes.test.ts` (asserts the same error code for token auth without a device) and `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-policy.test.ts`.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `review --local-range` against `origin/main` at head 547d90f, `review_status: complete`, checkout access verified. Patch B, "patch is correct", no findings, security cleared ("unauthenticated clients already get the same `authReason` values on the unauthorized path"). Proof D and overall C because a local-range review sees only the commits, not the runtime output above.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format and the other guards pass. The dead export scan fails on `extensions/knowledge/src/scribe-schedule-dialog.ts: CronSchedule`, a file this change does not touch.

prs.title: fix: show sender phone number for quoted WhatsApp messages (#202554)
prs.body:
Closes #202554

## What Problem This Solves

When replying to a quoted message in a WhatsApp group where the quoted sender is identified by an internal `@lid` (such as `1234567890@lid`), the agent's inbound reply context displays the opaque `@lid` JID rather than the contact's phone number or display name, even though the receiving account already has the contact's reverse mapping stored in its local credentials folder (`authDir`).

## User Impact

User impact: When someone quotes another user in a WhatsApp group, the AI agent correctly sees the sender's phone number (e.g. `+15555550123`) in the quote context instead of an unreadable `@lid` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound quote extraction (`describeReplyContext`) was not provided with the receiving account's `authDir`, so the participant lookup fell back to the unmapped identifier. Additionally, `resolveComparableIdentity` retained the raw identifier in the `label` property even after resolving the phone number, causing the downstream reply envelope formatter to render the stale raw `@lid`.

This patch:
1. Passes `authDir` from delivery intake and message enrichment into `describeReplyContext`.

## What Problem This Solves

When a shiny lobster sits beside a regular one in the Lobsterdex, their names line up, but the descriptions and first-visit dates do not. A longer name makes the difference more noticeable.

## User Impact

Readers can compare neighboring cards across the row. The artwork, copy-link targets, and visit history are unchanged; no action or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each card used to divide extra height independently between its text rows. Cards on the same shelf now share rows sized to their actual content. A longer name or description can wrap without imposing a fixed height on every card. The sprite’s block margins preserve its existing 94 px artwork slot without adding an empty grid item to every card.

## Evidence

In Chromium at **390px and 1440px**, measured from Copper’s first text line to Harbor’s in the same row:

| Name | 0 px | 0 px |
