prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI breaks under browser auto-translate
prs.body:
Closes #191961

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI shows a "panel failed to load" error in Edge when browser auto-translate is on.

## User Impact

The Control UI no longer breaks under auto-translate. It already localizes itself. Browser translate of chat text is off for the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auto-translate rewrites text nodes under the Solid renderer, so `insertBefore` throws. The shell now sets `translate="no"` and `notranslate`.

## Evidence

- No test: the change is two static HTML attributes, covered by the proof below.
- Not tried in Edge: headless can't run its translate. Two reporters on the issue confirmed translate as the cause.

## Proof (partial)

Built Control UI (Sessions page) in real headless Chrome through the UI e2e harness, with a simulated translator that wraps every text node the browser reports as translatable in `<font>`, like a page translator:

```
            html translate attr   html.translate   text nodes replaced
main        null                  true             109
this PR     "no"                  false            0
```

Not shown: Edge's own translator, and the original `insertBefore` crash. Neither reproduces in headless, and the simulation did not trigger it on main either. This only shows the opt-out reaches the built page.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Pick the open issue you can fix most confidently with no PR yet, and open a PR.

**Agent:** Checked open bug issues for linked PRs. #192031, #186832, #173611 already have PRs. #191043 and #193262 need maintainer decisions or Windows repro. #191961 has a confirmed cause in the thread: Edge translate rewrites text nodes while `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded.

**Agent:** `translate.ts` already sets `lang` at runtime, but Edge decides at load. Chose `translate="no"` plus `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">` in `ui/index.html`. Tradeoff: no browser translation of chat text.

**Agent:** Added a test beside the `index.html` boot test. Red on main, green with the change. `oxfmt` clean.

</details>

prs.title: fix(acp): a failed identity save leaves a new backend session on every request
prs.body:
Closes #127371

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an ACP request succeeds on a backend identity that was never saved when the identity write fails, and the next request opens yet another backend session.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed identity save now fails the request and closes the new handle, instead of silently opening a new backend session on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ensure write is now strict like session init: it must return the stored ACP entry before the handle is cached. Init and ensure share the close and persisted-entry helpers. Control and refused publications keep their handle open, as before.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway with the `acpx` backend. The backend is a tiny ACP agent I wrote over stdio (official SDK, no session resume), not a real harness. The storage failure is injected: a SQLite trigger aborts `acp_sessions` updates that store a new backend session id for session A (`database or disk is full`). Sessions A and B were created with `/acp spawn toy --mode persistent --thread off`, then the Gateway was restarted:

```text
main (74f111a):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=0  pong   # opened toy-1351073-1, prompt sent, identity never saved
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=0  pong   # closed toy-1351073-1, opened toy-1351194-1, prompt sent
gateway log: acp-manager: failed persisting ACP metadata for <A>: Error: database or disk is full

PR (5059270):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=1  OpenClaw couldn't save your conversation because the disk is full. ...
                                                                    # opened toy-1349192-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=1  (same)   # opened toy-1349284-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <B> --message "B request 2"   exit=0  pong     # prompt to B's own toy-1349059-1, untouched
-- trigger dropped, storage restored --
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 3"   exit=0  pong     # opened toy-1349394-1, prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 4"   exit=0  pong     # same toy-1349394-1, no new backend session
```

- `manager.runtime-handle-ensure.reset.test.ts`: red on main (resolves), green here, for a failing write and for no returned entry.
- `pnpm test:changed`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, lint and format pass. `check:changed` fails only the dead-export scan on files this PR does not touch.
- Test lines +38, under the ceiling.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking in the Control UI Browser panel (for example filling a captcha) gives no immediate feedback. The first sign a click registered is the remote page's next frame, about 70-100 ms on loopback and a full round trip on a real link.

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: #187032 and #187075 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence

Real run, head a5fb8f5 vs base b9251d1: isolated Gateway, managed headless Chrome 156, built Control UI. Text selected via `openclaw browser evaluate`.

```text
                          base                      head
Ctrl+C, text selected     clipboard unchanged       copied + "Copied!" toast
local Ctrl+V paste        "local-clipboard-before"  "Order 4821 shipped to Rotterdam"
Actions menu              Copy URL only             + Copy selection (copies the same text)
nothing selected, Ctrl+C  nothing happens           clipboard unchanged + "Nothing is selected" notice
tab switched 340 ms into a 3 s selection read
                          n/a                       clipboard unchanged, no toast
                                                    (same read without the switch: copied)
```

| before | after |
|---|---|
| ![before: menu has no Copy selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/867adabe-de77-4830-a000-59755316dee7) | ![after: Copy selection in menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9be0888b-c393-458d-a298-7c53e45e9b3d) |
| ![before: Ctrl+C shows nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdf6c8c6-a6fb-4d50-9d4d-11414d006076) | ![after: Copied toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9e5613d-7a80-483d-a76d-726cce174b0e) |

![after: Copy selection disabled with nothing selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19edf76-ca99-4c19-a129-c2ff78a6696d)

prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck; the current-head Gateway run is under Real behavior proof below. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

### Real behavior proof

Current head `1bb85c8a42c`, built with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, port 28789, throwaway token). A command job (`openclaw cron add --command`, then `openclaw cron run`) printed one line per second for 20 s, including a synthetic token, a synthetic private key split across polls, and one stderr line. I polled `cron.liveOutput` with `openclaw gateway call`, sending back the returned `cursor` and `runAtMs` (trimmed):

```
11:22:28 cursor=0   -> active:true reset:true cursor:14  "line 1 stdout\n"
11:22:31 cursor=14  -> active:true cursor:56  "line 2 stdout\nline 3 stdout\nline 4 stdout\n"
11:22:34 cursor=56  -> active:true cursor:174 "line 5 stdout\napi token=sk-pro…7890 used\nline 6 stdout\nline 7 stdout\nwarn 7 on stderr\n"
11:22:37 cursor=174 -> active:true cursor:310 "line 8 stdout\nline 9 stdout\n-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…redacted…\n"
11:22:40 cursor=310 -> active:true cursor:381 "…redacted…-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\nline 13 stdout\n"
11:22:43 cursor=381 -> active:true cursor:426 "line 14 stdout\nline 15 stdout\nline 16 stdout\n"
11:22:46 cursor=426 -> active:true cursor:471 "line 17 stdout\nline 18 stdout\nline 19 stdout\n"
11:22:49 cursor=471 -> active:false cursor:0 ""   (run ended, buffer discarded)
```

Each poll returned only new complete lines, stderr arrived in order, the token and the private key (across polls) were masked, and `active` flipped to `false` when the run ended. `cron.runs` then recorded the finished run with its full, unchanged summary. Not re-run on this head: the Control UI panel (the screenshots above are from an earlier head).

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

prs.title: fix(openai): Ark Responses fails on the turn after a tool call
prs.body:
Closes #116691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a custom `openai-responses` model on Volcengine Ark fails with `missing input.status` on the turn after a tool call.

## User Impact

Ark and BytePlus ModelArk Responses routes keep working after tool calls. Other custom routes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed `function_call` and `reasoning` items now get `status: "completed"` on Ark hosts instead of having status stripped. Other custom routes still strip it (#100831).

## Evidence

Real behavior proof, with one stand-in: no live Ark call (no key). The real Gateway and `openclaw agent` CLI use provider `custom-volces` (`api: openai-responses`, base URL host `ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`), with the Gateway's `HTTP_PROXY` pointing at a local stand-in endpoint. It returns Ark's 400 `MissingParameter ... input.status` (text from the issue log) when a replayed `function_call` or `reasoning` item has no `status`. A tool call turn, then a second user turn on the same session:

```text
main (2b9dd45):
$ openclaw agent --agent main --model custom-volces/doubao-seed-evolving --session-id ark-1 --message "read IDENTITY.md"
LLM request rejected: The request failed because it is missing \`input\.status\` parameter\. Request id\: req\-2 | MissingParameter   exit=1
  #2 -> 400 MissingParameter  replay: reasoning[status=<none>], function_call[status=<none>], function_call_output
$ openclaw agent ... --session-id ark-1 --message "read it again"
LLM request rejected: ... | MissingParameter   exit=1
  #3 -> 400 MissingParameter

PR (ee08560):
$ openclaw agent --agent main --model custom-volces/doubao-seed-evolving --session-id ark-1 --message "read IDENTITY.md"
Done, I read the file.   exit=0
  #2 -> 200  replay: reasoning[status=completed], function_call[status=completed], function_call_output
$ openclaw agent ... --session-id ark-1 --message "read it again"
Done, I read the file.   exit=0
  #3 -> 200, #4 -> 200  (older reasoning and function_call replayed with status=completed)

Other custom host (llm.example.com), main (#5) and PR (#6) alike:
  -> 200  replay: reasoning[status=<none>], function_call[status=<none>], function_call_output
```

- Policy test red on base, green here (Volcengine and BytePlus hosts, custom route still strips). Touched tests, tsgo core and core:test, oxlint, format pass.
- Test lines net -11.
- Gap: not run against the real Ark API (no key). The Ark requirement is from the issue report and docs.

prs.title: fix: align Activity tabs and panels on phones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a 390 px phone, Activity’s search, chart and session list start 28 px farther in than the page description. The Sessions tab label starts even farther in, leaving less room for the session feed, Current work and Run inspector.

## User Impact

Activity uses the phone’s existing page margins. Tabs keep their original hit areas, and people in the filter menu share a label column even when their avatars are different sizes. Desktop layout is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell already supplies the phone gutter. Activity now drops its extra inset there and positions the narrow tab strip by its label rather than its button edge. The page stylesheet groups related layout rules and inherits toolbar sizing and alignment where those values already match. No shared shell, tab styles or performance budgets change.

## Evidence

At 390 × 844, the subtitle stays at x=12. The search, chart, session list, Current work and Run inspector move from x=40 to x=12; the list’s trailing edge moves from x=350 to x=378. Relative to the subtitle’s first glyph at x=13, the Sessions label moves from +35 px to −1 px. It retains its 65.89 × 24.05 px hit area. The people picker’s label spread falls from 2 px to 0 px. At 1440 × 900, the reading column stays at x=346–1404.

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing the Systems inventory could take keyboard focus off a device. Pressing Enter then selected nothing, even though the device was still visible. This also happened when a different device changed status.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(ui): keep provider-pattern model maps editable in form mode
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Control UI → AI Agents → Agent Defaults → Models shows "Unsupported schema node. Use Raw mode." on a valid config, because provider model schemas (bundled vLLM) inject `patternProperties` into the models map and the form analyzer rejects that keyword.
- Solution: Admit `patternProperties` in the analyzer only where the existing editor can render the node (named properties or an object-valued/`true` `additionalProperties`); pattern-only object maps keep their Raw-mode fallback.
- What changed: `ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.ts` (representability-gated keyword admission), `ui/src/lib/config-form-utils.ts` (`patternProperties` declared on the shared `JsonSchema` type), `ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts` (real-Chromium coverage: editable models map, pattern-only fallback, mixed named+pattern fallback), `ui/src/e2e/config-form-provider-pattern.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` + `test/vitest/vitest.ui-paths.mjs` (built-UI e2e registered in the real-gateway shard).
- What did NOT change: Pattern-only object maps (e.g. the knowledge plugin's `stores`, `additionalProperties: false`) still report unsupported and keep the Raw-mode notice — the review counterexample is covered by tests at both the analyzer and browser level. Form validation and patch behavior are otherwise untouched.

Fixes #202721

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A valid config with a bundled-provider `patternProperties` refinement on `agents.defaults.models` was pushed into Raw mode, so the Models map was not editable in Form mode.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, worktree at `issue-202721` on `origin/main` (599bc4222a4), **system Chromium 138.0.7204.157 driven by the browser Vitest project** (Playwright provider, no download needed; the repo's `playwright-chromium.ts` helper selected it). The production analyzer and the real Solid editor were exercised before and after the patch.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # analyzer-level reproduction from the issue (synthetic schema, no config needed)
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/components/config-form.analyze.node.test.ts
  # real-Chromium editor coverage (map editor edit/patch + Raw fallback notice)
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-browser.config.ts ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ chromium  src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts (36 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  36 passed (36)
  ```
  In a real Chromium instance: a models map carrying `^vllm/.+$` patternProperties renders the `.cfg-map` editor (no Raw-mode notice), editing an entry's alias patches `["models", "vllm/local", "alias"]`, and a pattern-only map (`stores: {team:{agents:["main"]}}` with `additionalProperties: false`) keeps the Raw-mode notice, renders no `.cfg-map`, and issues no patches. Analyzer-level: before the patch the same synthetic schema failed with `expected [ 'models' ] to deeply equal []`; after, `unsupportedPaths` is empty for the models map and `["stores"]` for the pattern-only map.
- **Observed result after fix:** Provider-pattern model maps render as editable maps in real Chromium; pattern-only maps AND mixed named+pattern maps with `additionalProperties:false` keep their Raw-mode fallback; `tsc -p ui/tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports zero errors in the changed files; all 37 config-form browser tests and 20 analyzer-adjacent node tests pass.
- **What was not tested:** The new built-UI e2e (`config-form-provider-pattern.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, driving the shipped Control UI against a real isolated Gateway: edit → save → reload persistence, with `assertServedUi` proving the served bundle is this checkout) is registered in the real-gateway shard but could not execute on this host: the suite's spawn-broker relay requires systemd 254+ Delegate support, and the existing merged `browser-pair-code.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` fails identically here (`service child cleanup identity lost`), so this is a host limitation, not a regression. It is expected to run in CI. No live vLLM endpoint was involved (not needed for the analyzer/renderer boundary).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Real-browser component test + built-UI e2e (runs in CI)
- Target test file: `ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts`, `ui/src/e2e/config-form-provider-pattern.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: (1) provider-pattern models map renders an editable map with key-path patches in real Chromium; (2) pattern-only maps and mixed named+pattern maps with `additionalProperties: false` keep the Raw-mode notice; (3) e2e: edit → save → reload persistence against a real Gateway serving this checkout's built UI.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: both render outcomes from the review findings are pinned in a real browser, and the issue's user path is pinned end to end at the built-UI boundary.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `SUPPORTED_FORM_SCHEMA_KEYS`/`SUPPORTED_CONSTRAINT_ONLY_KEYS` in `config-form.analyze.ts` never listed `patternProperties`; once `modelParamsSchema` started contributing it (#129434), every provider-pattern model map failed the analyzer's keyword policy and fell back to Raw mode. A global exemption would have over-admitted pattern-only maps the editor cannot render, so admission is gated on renderable structure instead.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test covered a map schema carrying `patternProperties`.

prs.title: fix(ui): paint the archived composer banner in the first frame
prs.body:
## Problem

After a reload, an archived chat (or a chat whose parent was deleted, which is also archived) first painted an empty, zero-height composer for about two frames. Then the "Unarchive" banner appeared and the composer grew to its real height (0 → 62 px). The cached archived presentation from #185788 exists to avoid exactly this shift.

`ui/src/e2e/chat-pane-state-snapshot.e2e.test.ts` catches it: the `archived` and `deleted-parent` cases fail on `main` at line 134 (`paints.every((paint) => paint.archived === archived)`). Main CI skips UI suites when UI files are unchanged, so `main` looks green, but every UI PR hits it in `checks-ui-e2e`.

## Root cause

#202800 (commit "perf(ui): defer inactive composer banner rendering") moved the disabled banner into `chat-composer-disabled-banner.tsx` and loaded it with `lazy()` behind a `ChatLazyBoundary` (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer-view.tsx:46` and `:130` on `main`). For an archived session, the banner is the whole composer (`composer-replacement`), so the first frames have a visible composer shell with nothing in it until the chunk resolves.

Frames sampled on `main` during the reload (archived case):

```
{"archived":false,"height":0}, {"archived":false,"height":0}, {"archived":true,"height":62}
```

## Fix

Import `ChatComposerDisabledBanner` statically in the composer view again. The module split from #202800 stays; only the lazy load and its boundary go. The banner's own imports (`chat-pane-header-view.tsx`, `chat-composer-controls.tsx`) were already in the chat boot set, so the boot cost is the small banner module itself. `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` is regenerated with `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` (one added line).

The chat boot JS gzip budget in `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts` rises by the measured cost: 1,334,416 B, +777 B over the paired base 1,333,639 B, plus 64 B headroom. The #202534 budget was measured before #202800 and already included this banner inline; #202800's saving was then consumed by later changes. Painting the archived state correctly in the first frame is worth the 777 B.

The unit test `chat-composer-disabled-banner.test.ts` goes back to asserting the banner synchronously, which pins the first-frame paint.

## Impact

Archived and deleted-parent chats paint the Unarchive banner in the first frame after reload, with no composer height change. No behavior change for other banners except they also paint without the lazy-load gap.

## Evidence

- `chat-pane-state-snapshot.e2e.test.ts` (ui-e2e-bundled): `main` 2 failed / 2 passed (archived, deleted-parent fail at line 134); this branch 4 passed.
- `chat-composer-disabled-banner.test.ts`: `main` 4 failed (banner not present synchronously); this branch 4 passed.
- Consumers: `chat-composer-subagent`, `chat-composer`, `chat-view`, `chat-pane-bridge`, `control-ui-chunking` unit tests pass; related e2e `subagent-task-notice`, `session-management.archive`, `session-management.archived-actions`, `chat-worktree-restore` pass.
- `control-ui-performance` on the first head flagged only the +777 B chat boot gzip as new; the other violations (CSS totals, largest CSS, 21 chat boot requests) also fail on the base run of the same job.
- Unrelated reds on the first head: `ui/src/pages/config/settings-search.test.ts` fails the same way on `main` locally (Spanish locale entry); `ui/src/e2e/dashboard-fullscreen.e2e.test.ts` passes locally on this branch (11/11).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxfmt and oxlint on changed files pass.

No before/after screenshot: the defect is a two-frame gap during reload, which a static screenshot cannot show; the per-frame samples above are the visual evidence.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully undoes it; no state, config or contract changes. Blast radius if wrong: Control UI composer banners only.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep the Gateway responsive when an edited message has long slash or www. runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent edits a Discord message with the `message` tool and the new text mentions someone and holds a long run of slashes or `www.` without spaces, the Gateway freezes before the edit is sent. In a Gateway run against a local Discord server, an edit with a 32,000-character run of `/` held the Gateway main thread for 8.6 seconds, `/healthz` waited 10 seconds and another user's chat turn took 12 seconds. The text comes from the model, so a prompt injection in fetched content can ask for such an edit. Normal replies and `message` sends split the text into 2,000-character chunks first, so each scan there sees at most 2,000 characters and they did not stall in the same run.

## User Impact

User impact: Discord edits with long slash, `www.` or letter runs are prepared in milliseconds, and other chats keep working while they are sent. Mentions, bold text and links in Discord messages render exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before a Discord message is sent or edited, OpenClaw marks bare URLs in the text so mention rewriting and bold normalization leave them alone. `findDiscordUrlRanges` in `extensions/discord/src/url-ranges.ts` does that marking. It had two quadratic paths.

1. After it found a URL start (`//`, `www.`, `mailto:` or a scheme), it scanned to the end of the URL. The next search then started right after the URL start, so every `//` or `www.` inside that URL started another scan to the same end. A run of 16,000 slashes produced 8,000 ranges, each scanned to the end of the run.
2. The scheme pattern `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:\/\/` was retried at every letter of a long word. Each try walked to the end of the word before it failed.

The fix keeps the same pattern and checks with two changes.

- After a range is found, the search continues from the end of that range. A URL start found inside a range only produced a range nested inside it, so the covered text is the same.
- A scheme is only tried where a run of scheme characters begins (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9+.-])`). The run may start with digits, `+`, `.` or `-`, and the range still starts at the run's first letter, as it did before.

## Evidence

Time for `prepareDiscordOutboundText` (render, then mention rewrite) on `@alice here is the output:\n<body>\nthanks` with a configured `alice` alias. Single calls in one process.

| Body | Chars | main `4b74fd5` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prose (`word ` repeated) | 32,034 | 0.7 ms | 0.6 ms |
| `/` repeated | 8,034 | 628 ms | 2.0 ms |
| `/` repeated | 16,034 | 2,385 ms | 1.3 ms |
| `/` repeated | 32,034 | 9,174 ms | 3.8 ms |
| `www.` repeated | 16,034 | 1,491 ms | 1.7 ms |
| `www.` repeated | 32,034 | 4,679 ms | 1.7 ms |

`findDiscordUrlRanges` alone at 16,000 characters:

| Input | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` repeated | 2,535 ms (8,000 ranges) | 1.9 ms (1 range) |
| `www.` repeated | 1,279 ms (4,000 ranges) | 0.9 ms (1 range) |
| `http://` repeated | 686 ms | 1.1 ms |
| `a` repeated | 345 ms | 0.2 ms |
| `-a` repeated | 168 ms | 0.2 ms |

Equivalence checks:

- A differential fuzzer ran 1.8 million random strings built from URL starts, scheme characters, punctuation, parentheses, `<`, `>`, `_`, `@`, spaces and non-ASCII letters. For every string the branch returned exactly the main ranges that sit outside every earlier main range, and both covered the same characters. It found 0 differences. 1,343,173 of these strings produced ranges, and the branch left out 1,005,719 nested ranges.
- `renderDiscordMarkdown` followed by `rewriteDiscordKnownMentions` ran on 100,000 random replies with mentions, `__bold__`, `**`, links and code spans. The output digest is identical on main and on this branch. 15,792 of those replies were changed by the rendering.

Tests on this branch:

- `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/url-ranges.test.ts`: 2 passed. On main both fail. The first test shows main returning a nested `www.c.d` range inside an outer URL. The second takes 14,775 ms on main against its 500 ms bound and 12 ms here.
- `npx vitest run` on the Discord markdown, mentions, outbound and send tests (18 files): 205 passed. The 6 failures in `send.voice.test.ts` also fail on main on this machine. They come from a group-writable parent directory that the temp-workspace guard rejects.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: clean.
- The change adds 25 test lines, inside the 400-line allowance.

### Gateway run with a local Discord server

Both builds ran `openclaw gateway run` from source (main `4b74fd5`, this branch `28dff50`, Node 24.21.0) in an isolated state dir on loopback. The bundled Discord plugin connected to Crabline 0.2.0 (`@openclaw/crabline`, the repo's local Discord provider server with REST v10 and the Gateway WebSocket) through `DISCORD_API_URL`. Crabline generates a synthetic bot identity, so no Discord account or token was involved. The model was a mock OpenAI-compatible provider on loopback. The config sets `mentionAliases: { alice: "135000000000000777" }`. A user message injected into the Crabline guild channel started each agent turn. The model output was `@alice here is the **build output** you asked for:` followed by a line of 32,000 `/` and `thanks, ping @alice if it looks wrong`. While each turn ran, one process polled `/healthz` every 100 ms and another sent chats one after another to `/v1/chat/completions` from a separate user. Each build first ran one short warm-up turn and one warm-up chat.

Three turns per build:

- reply: the model returns the text as its reply.
- message tool send: the model calls the `message` tool with `action: "send"` and the text.
- message tool edit: the model calls the `message` tool with `action: "edit"` on an earlier bot message and the text.

| Turn | Measure | main `4b74fd5` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reply | longest `/healthz` wait | 52 ms | 60 ms |
| reply | longest other chat turn | 2,507 ms | 3,264 ms |
| reply | stall reports | 0 | 0 |
| message tool send | longest `/healthz` wait | 95 ms | 203 ms |
| message tool send | longest other chat turn | 3,147 ms | 1,589 ms |
| message tool send | stall reports | 0 | 0 |
| message tool edit | longest `/healthz` wait | 10,044 ms | 1,682 ms |
| message tool edit | longest other chat turn | 12,194 ms | 2,678 ms |
| message tool edit | stall reports | `elapsedMs=8591 task="gateway:rpc:message.action"` and `elapsedMs=10141 task=unattributed` | `elapsedMs=1700 task=unattributed` |
| message tool edit | tool call to tool result | 11.4 s | 2.0 s |

The reply and the send each reached Discord as 18 messages on both builds (2,000, 15, then 1,949 characters each, and 869). The core outbound path splits the text into chunks of at most 2,000 characters before the Discord plugin rewrites mentions, so each call of `findDiscordUrlRanges` sees at most 2,000 characters there. The edit action passes the whole text to `prepareDiscordOutboundText` and then sends one PATCH. On main that call held the Gateway main thread for 8.6 s. Crabline answers an edit over 2,000 characters with `Invalid Form Body` as Discord does, so the model received `{"status":"error","tool":"message","error":"DiscordError: Invalid Form Body"}` on both builds.

Check of the bot messages Crabline holds for the reply and the send, read back over its REST API (`joined_equals_model_reply_with_mentions` compares the concatenated messages with the model text after `@alice` becomes `<@135000000000000777>`):

```
long_reply_messages=18 chars_per_message=2000,15,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,1949,869
first_message_starts_with_mention=true mentions_rewritten=2 plain_at_alice_left=0
bold_kept=true slash_chars_received=32000 slash_chars_sent_by_model=32000
joined_equals_model_reply_with_mentions=true newline_joined_equals=false
first_message_head="<@135000000000000777> here is the **build output** you asked for:\n//////////////"
last_message_tail="///////\nthanks, ping <@135000000000000777> if it looks wrong"
```

These lines are the same on main and on this branch for both turns.

Gateway log on main during the edit turn:

```
main-thread stall: elapsedMs=8591 task="gateway:rpc:message.action" taskMs=8591 stallStartMs=1795260815735 stallEndMs=1795260824326
main-thread stall: elapsedMs=10141 task=unattributed stallStartMs=1795260814195 stallEndMs=1795260824336
[tools] message failed: GatewayClientRequestError: DiscordError: Invalid Form Body | UNAVAILABLE
```

On this branch the only stall report in the edit turn is `elapsedMs=1700 task=unattributed`, and the same `Invalid Form Body` line follows.

Not tested: a live Discord bot. The Gateway run above uses the bundled Discord plugin against Crabline's local Discord server.

prs.title: fix: make release harness readiness checks reliable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release validation can mistake another service on port 44080 for its mock model server, and the dashboard fullscreen test can check sibling loading indicators before those widgets finish rendering.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. Release validators get an independently allocated mock listener and a readiness assertion that waits for all widgets without weakening the existing checks. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing process/log-bound readiness helper to allocate and return the mock port, then propagate that port to the existing model configuration and assertion. Poll the existing board-wide loading assertion rather than assuming the selected frame becoming ready means every sibling is ready.

Simplification review retained the existing owners: no new allocator, retry policy, timeout, or production state. The three-file delta is +54/-6; necessary growth is the occupied-port regression and its fixture support.

## Evidence

- Occupied-port regression: the actual container program and real mock startup/readiness helper fail on the base with EADDRINUSE / wrong listener, then pass with the repair. The test checks the allocated port and sends an inference request to that listener. CLI/Gateway operations remain fixture doubles; this is not a full Docker run.
- Focused shell and assertion suites: 29/29 pass. Targeted typecheck, both touched TypeScript lint checks, formatting, Bash syntax, shellcheck, and test-line budget (+48 against 400) pass on the unchanged patch.
- Dashboard controlled held-sibling reproduction: the existing full touch/scroll/resize flow fails at the original count=0 assertion with one sibling still loading, then passes with polling under identical skew. Diagnostic instrumentation is not included.
- Remaining local gap: clean uninstrumented dashboard attempts, including the final focused attempt on this base, fail during initial roster setup before the changed helper executes, with Browser closed and cascading fixture cleanup errors. The cause is not established; this is neither a dashboard suite pass nor a proven unrelated infrastructure failure. Exact-head PR CI remains required. Full Docker/package release validation is also not claimed here.
- Local ClawSweeper unavailable; local autoreview completed on the exact three-file snapshot against 9aae2826269df5e45f42fe50631689f4ff2647ea, scoped P0–P2 clean (no actionable findings). Its source-only scope did not execute tests or include the mock server implementation; that helper contract was separately inspected. One hosted ClawSweeper review will be requested if not automatically queued.

This is a scoped maintainer-authorized release-harness repair; it does not publish a release or launch release validation.

prs.title: fix(openai): embed system prompt in input on ChatGPT Responses when uncached (#202372)
prs.body:
Closes #202372

## What Problem This Solves

On `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` and other models using the ChatGPT Responses backend (`openai-chatgpt-responses`), top-level `instructions` are not cached by the provider, but the request builder always placed the system prompt in `instructions` and disabled input prompt conversion. This resulted in the entire system prompt being reprocessed uncached on every turn, causing excessive subscription quota usage and avoidable prefill latency.

## User Impact

User impact: Restores prompt caching for system prompts on GPT-6.2 models accessed via ChatGPT OAuth subscriptions by embedding the prompt in leading developer input as indicated by `cachesInstructions: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog already configures `cachesInstructions: false` for GPT-6.2, but the ChatGPT Responses adapter hardcoded `includeSystemPrompt: false` and always populated `instructions`. Consulting `cachesInstructions` enables system-prompt input conversion and omits the uncached `instructions` field when `cachesInstructions` is `false`, while preserving existing `instructions` behavior for models that support and cache it.

## Evidence

### Wire Comparison (`openai-chatgpt-responses`)

| Field | Base (before fix) | Head (with fix, `cachesInstructions: false`) |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | `"You are an autonomous agent."` (uncached on 6.2) | `undefined` (omitted from payload) |
| `input[0]` | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` | `{ type: "message", role: "developer", content: [{ type: "input_text", text: "You are an autonomous agent." }] }` |
| `input[1]` | Next user turn message | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` |

### Multi-turn WebSocket Continuation & Cache Reuse Trace

Verified over unmocked `WebSocketServer` via `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`:

1. **Turn 1 (Cold request, initial developer prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 1" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `instructions` omitted; system prompt placed in leading developer input for prefix caching.

2. **Turn 2 (Continuation with unchanged prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "previous_response_id": "resp_1",
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 2" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `previous_response_id` continues the stored chain. The delta input carries only the new user turn without duplicating the developer prompt or breaking prefix caching.

3. **Turn 3 (System prompt changed to `System Prompt 2 (Changed)`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 2 (Changed)" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] },
       ...
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: Continuation is safely invalidated (`previous_response_id` omitted) and a full replay is dispatched with the new developer prompt.

### Automated Test Suite Execution

- **Reproduction**: Unit test proved red failure on base (`AssertionError: expected { model: 'gpt-6.2-sol', ... } to not have property "instructions" (received "You are an autonomous agent.")`) and passes green with the fix.
- **Suite Results**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`: **35 passed** (including uncached prompt placement, cached prompt retention, and multi-turn WebSocket continuation).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.replay.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-streaming.test.ts`: **9 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-protocol.test.ts`: **5 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-uncached-instructions.integration.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-payload-policy.test.ts`: **28 passed**
- **Standards & Code Quality**:
  - `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `run-format.mts` & `git diff --check`: Clean.

## What Problem This Solves

When an invited OpenClaw ID member uses a keyboard on a phone, the bottom of the focus ring disappears on **Skip for now** and **Not now**. Both buttons sit flush with the bottom of the New Session page.

## User Impact

Members can see the whole focus indicator while choosing whether to add a name or photo. The buttons keep their size, and the desktop welcome and chat composer are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both steps replace the mobile composer. The welcome now uses the same 10 px bottom gap inside the scrollable step, so it remains reachable on short screens without counting the phone's safe area twice.

## Evidence

At 390 × 844, both buttons ended at y=844 before and y=834 after. The 2 px outline and its 2 px offset previously extended 4 px beyond the page; now the full outline has 6 px of clearance. With a simulated 34 px bottom safe area, both buttons end at y=800, 10 px above the safe edge. At 1440 × 900 the name and photo button positions did not change.

Chromium rendered the real Control UI with a synthetic member; no live account, upload, sign-in, or physical device was used. prs.title: fix: stop worker sessions from looping on a wait tool they can't use
prs.body:
Related: #203292 ## What Problem This Solves When a session runs on a worker (a paired node started with `openclaw connect --session-host`), the model is offered `sessions_yield`, the tool that pauses a turn until a child finishes. On a worker that tool can never work: every call returns `Yield not supported in this context`. Models keep calling it anyway. On current `main` with gpt-4.1, a plain "spawn a child session" request on a worker made 54 failing yield calls in a row before I stopped it, and it never reached the spawn. ## User Impact Worker sessions no longer get stuck repeating a tool that always fails. The model ends its turn normally, and child results still arrive by the usual completion delivery. Sessions that run on the Gateway host keep `sessions_yield` exactly as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Yield pauses the turn through an `onYield` owner. On the Gateway host the Gateway runs the model loop, so it can pause it. On a worker the loop runs on the node, and the Gateway only executes the tool. There is no loop for it to pause, so worker turns never get an `onYield`. The obvious fix is to special-case `sessions_yield` in the worker tool filter. That puts the knowledge in the wrong place. The yield tool is the one that knows it has no owner. So the tool now declares itself unavailable when it has no `onYield`, using the same `unavailableReason` mechanism `portal` already uses on workers. The worker tool surface already withholds unavailable tools. The worker prompt and delegation guidance are built from that surface, so they drop the yield instructions too and fall back to "completion is push-based, end the turn". Making yield actually work on workers would need a new worker protocol feature. Nothing needs it today, since children deliver their results without it. This fixes the loop, not the spawn. With yield gone, the model in my run went on to call `sessions_spawn` with `objective` and no `task`. It got the bare `Worker tool arguments are invalid` and asked me what to do. #203292 makes that error name the bad fields so the model can correct itself. Together, the two PRs make "spawn a child" on a worker recoverable end to end. ## Evidence Live, plain upstream gateway from source, gpt-4.1, same prompt, session placed on a worker node: | | `main` (1d9252c) | this PR | |---|---|---| | `sessions_yield` calls | 54, all `Yield not supported in this context` | 0 | | Gateway log | — | `Worker tool sessions_yield withheld` | | Outcome | looped until stopped by hand | tried to spawn, then ended the turn and asked the user | **Before (`main`):** the session runs on `r13-main-worker`. Every yield fails with `Yield not supported in this context`, and the model keeps calling it. **After (this PR):** same prompt, on `r13-fix-worker`. No yield calls, and the loop is gone. The "Couldn't launch subagent" error in this screenshot is a different bug, and this PR doesn't touch it. Now that the model can no longer get stuck on yield, it reaches `sessions_spawn`. It sends `objective` instead of the required `task`, and the worker answers only with the bare `Worker tool arguments are invalid`. With nothing telling it which field is wrong, the model gives up and asks the user. #203292 fixes that error: it names the invalid and missing fields, so the model can correct the call and retry. Tests (each fails on `main` and passes with this PR): - a real worker turn execution: `sessions_yield` is in neither the authorized worker tools nor the system prompt, and `sessions_spawn` still is; - full tool assembly keeps the unavailable marker without `onYield`, and adds none with it; - the worker tool filter withholds yield without an owner and keeps it with one.
Commands and scope - `pnpm exec vitest run` on the changed and related suites: tool registration, requester yield, worker turn execution, worker gateway tool runtime, MCP HTTP, restart-resume yield, worker runtime, and the vitest project config tests. All pass. - `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the changed files. - Only worker turns change behavior. The `unavailableReason` marker is read only by the worker tool filter. Non-worker runs without `onYield` still see the tool, as before. - Not covered: #180941, the same loop with `nothing_pending` on sessions where yield works but nothing is pending. That is a model-selection problem, and this PR doesn't change it.

prs.title: fix(update): reclaim abandoned updater runtimes on a busy host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each update of a package (npm) installation keeps a copy of its running code in an `openclaw-update-runtime-XXXXXX` directory and leaves removal to the next update or `openclaw doctor --fix`. On a host that always has other OpenClaw processes running, that removal never happens. One host accumulated 12 runtimes (46.5 GiB), each refused for one of two reasons:

- `no recognized runtime marker`: a runtime is recognized only by projecting the inspecting installation's own package root into it, so a runtime created from any other install root is never recognized.
- `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: ...)`: without knowing who created a runtime, the process census treats every OpenClaw process it cannot rule out as possibly the creating updater.

Still true on `main` at `4bedaedbcc06`, after #200578, #200657, #200732 and #201711:

- **Package installs: yes.** `update-command.ts` calls `retainRuntime` for every package update. The base run below reproduces both refusals on `4bedaedbcc06` with nothing more than `openclaw logs --follow` and `openclaw mcp serve` running.
- **Git installs: no longer.** Since #200578 a Git update returns before retention (`if (gitRelease) { … return; }`), so it creates no runtime. Git installs still run the cleanup, and benefit only for runtimes a package install left on the same host.
- **Containers: unchanged.** The census refuses inside a container on both commits, so nothing is reclaimed there.
- #200657 and #200732 exempt specific processes (Gateway children, macOS node hosts and the app). They do not cover ordinary CLIs, agents or test workers, and do not address cross-installation recognition. #201711 removes update backups, not runtimes.

## User Impact

User impact: updater runtimes left by package updates are now removed by the next update or `openclaw doctor --fix` even while a Gateway, agents, test runs, or other OpenClaw commands are running, and whichever installation runs the cleanup. A runtime is kept while the update that created it is still running, or while any process's executable, arguments, working directory, or preload points into it. Runtimes created by updaters older than this change carry no record and keep the previous checks, so those already on disk may still need manual removal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the update command creates a runtime, and it loads code from it until it exits. The updater now writes `owner.json` (PID, process start time, Linux PID namespace) into the runtime when it creates it. Cleanup uses that record instead of guessing:

- The record marks the directory as an updater runtime for any installation.
- Creator alive (same PID and start time, and not an exited process awaiting its parent): kept, with `the creating update (PID n) is still running`.
- Creator exited: the census runs with `creatorExited`, where a process holds the runtime only through a path into it. Pathless OpenClaw processes and commands that cannot be classified but name no runtime no longer hold it. Resolved preload aliases and unresolved runtime references still do.
- A bare preload (`--require preload`, `--import @scope/preload`) is resolved the way Node resolves it for that process: the nearest `node_modules` above its working directory, followed through links. It holds the runtime it resolves into. With the creator exited, one that resolves elsewhere, or cannot be loaded from that working directory at all, holds nothing. A process whose working directory cannot be read stays unknown and blocks.
- A record from another PID namespace, or a creator whose identity cannot be read, falls back to the previous conservative census.

Accepted edges, named in code: a reboot that reuses both the creator's PID and its start time keeps that runtime until the impostor exits; `NODE_PATH` is not read when resolving a bare preload.

No config options, schema, or state changes. The record is a file inside a directory the updater already owns. Nothing in the diff served the deleted in-place Git runner.

## Review notes

- **Unresolved bare preloads (ClawSweeper P2, fixed).** The finding was real. With the creator exited, `node --require preload service.js` whose `node_modules/preload` links into a retained runtime was released, and cleanup would have deleted code that process loads. Holding every unresolved preload again, as #191284 did, would block busy development hosts once more, so the census resolves the specifier instead.
- **`owner.json` and "State and caches: SQLite, not new JSON/JSONL/sidecar stores" (ClawSweeper P2, rejected).** The record stays a file, deliberately. It is a marker inside a disposable directory that describes that directory, like the files already there: the updater writes `retained-files.json` and `update-native-gate.mjs` beside it, cleanup already recognizes a runtime by reading the projected `package.json`, and update captures carry `.openclaw-private-update-capture` the same way. It must be readable by a Doctor from any installation and any state directory, and it must disappear with the directory. A state-database row would belong to one state directory, would outlive or be orphaned from the directory it describes, and would defeat cross-installation recognition. The repository's `database-first legacy-store guard` passes on this branch.
- **Exited updater not yet reaped (independent review P2, fixed in `d558fbd2b5a1`).** An exited updater whose parent has not waited for it keeps its `/proc` start time, so cleanup reported it as still running. Cleanup now checks definite death first. No other P0 to P2 finding.

## Evidence

Head `d558fbd2b5a1`, rebased on `4bedaedbcc06`.

**Tests.** `src/infra/temp-artifact-cleanup.test.ts`, `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-retained-runtime.test.ts`: 110 passed, 1 skipped before the last commit, plus the new unreaped-updater case. With the three source files reverted to `4bedaedbcc06`, the new cases fail (missing `owner.json`, pathless processes still holding, linked preload not held); the unreaped-updater case failed on `57b15c68dc30` with `the creating update (PID …) is still running`. `pnpm check:changed` exits 0. Net test lines: +192.

### Works: real package updates and Doctor, base against head

One scenario through the real CLI on `4bedaedbcc06` and on `d558fbd2b5a1`, each in its own Linux container (Crabbox `local-container` on a Mac Studio, `node:26.12.1-trixie` `sha256:97fa0f1b5903…`, leases `cbx_f486a644f87c` and `cbx_66152598d597`). Both exited 0 with 30 of 30 checks passing against the expectation for that commit.

- Installation: the commit packed with the repository's Docker e2e packer and installed with `npm install -g` into two prefixes.
- Updates: three real `openclaw update --tag file:<tarball> --yes --no-restart` runs to repacked copies of the same build with the next version numbers (2026.11.7 to 2026.11.9). Each finished `status=ok mode=npm` with 18 steps and retained a 638 MB runtime.
- Busy host, alive throughout: the second installation's Gateway and its workers, `openclaw logs --follow`, and `openclaw mcp serve` from the installation being updated. None points into a runtime.

| Step | Base `4bedaedbcc06` | Head `d558fbd2b5a1` |
|------|------|------|
| Update 1 exits and leaves runtime 1 | no `owner.json` | `owner.json` is `{"name":"openclaw","pid":11621,"startTime":16911363,"pidNamespace":"pid:[4026533140]"}`; PID 11621 has exited |
| A Gateway runs from runtime 1's own code (working directory inside it, then by absolute path from outside); `doctor --fix` | kept: `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 5770, 5771, 5784, 5785, 74247, 74465, 75104, 76032)`, the first four being the unrelated CLIs | kept: `(PIDs: 74328, 74546, 75187, 76111)`, exactly that Gateway and its three workers |
| That Gateway stops; update 2 starts (the next update) | runtime 1 kept, old refusal logged | runtime 1 removed |
| `doctor --fix` from the second installation while update 2 runs | runtime 2: `no recognized runtime marker; inspect it before manual cleanup` | runtime 2 kept: `the creating update (PID 96252) is still running` |
| Update 2 has exited; `doctor --fix` on the updated installation | both runtimes refused: `other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 5770, 5771, 5784, 5785)` | `Removed abandoned updater runtime: /var/tmp/ocproof/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-c8KWva` |
| Update 3, then `doctor --fix` from the second installation (a different install root) | runtimes 2 and 3: `no recognized runtime marker`; three runtimes, 1.9 GiB, left on disk | `Removed abandoned updater runtime: /var/tmp/ocproof/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-vkyoLa`; no runtime left |

Substitutions: the scenario moved `/.dockerenv` aside so the container stood in for a host (the census refuses inside a container on both commits). There is no service manager, so the Gateway was started by hand and belongs to the second installation, because a standalone `doctor --fix` cannot enter maintenance while a Gateway holds the same state directory.

### Does not break upgrades: the repository's upgrade-survivor lanes

`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` on `d558fbd2b5a1`, each lane in its own Crabbox `local-container` lease on the Mac Studio, the lane's containers started through the lease's engine socket.

| Lane | Baseline to candidate | Lease | Result |
|------|------|------|------|
| `base`, published baseline | `openclaw@2026.11.6` (latest stable) to head tarball | `cbx_4f848b2216ea` | passed |
| `base`, published baseline | `openclaw@2026.10.33` (extended-stable) to head tarball | `cbx_847f3ca83458` | passed |
| `package-verification-recovery` (failed activation, repair, repeat repair, next update) | `openclaw@2026.9.9` to head tarball; the lane requires 9.8 or 9.9 | `cbx_a0cd2603af56` | passed |
| `git-release` with all kill points (`stage build publish link-switch launcher-restore`) and the crash release | Git checkout at `7db69bedeab6` (2026.11.5 on `main`, the lane's default) to head | `cbx_2a1c8d419045` | passed, 26 phases |
| `recovery-cleanup`, published baseline | `openclaw@2026.11.6` to head tarball | `cbx_8b5d4578ae43` | failed, inherited |

- Inherited: `recovery-cleanup` fails identically on `4bedaedbcc06` (lease `cbx_e9fabf91f712`). Both stop in `update-candidate` at `package-swap` with `State schema inspection failed (exit) … during pre-migration database backup`, then roll back. Updater-runtime retention completed before that on both.
- `git-release` on `4bedaedbcc06` (lease `cbx_28e8be9d37f0`) failed once at `git-candidate-crash-release` (`updater exit 1`), a phase the head run passed; it was not repeated.
- Setup failures, not verdicts: two earlier `git-release` attempts on head stopped before any head code ran, one because the shared partial clone lacked objects the baseline updater fetched, one because the 2026.11.5 updater reported `Gateway service inspection is unavailable` under host load. `git-release` from the `v2026.11.6` tag cannot run: the tag is on a release branch that is not an ancestor of `main`, so the baseline updater's preflight rebase fails.

Not proven: a Git install upgraded from the `v2026.11.6` tag (see above; the Git lane ran from 2026.11.5 on `main`), a service-managed Gateway outside the lane's service-manager stand-in, macOS and Windows (the start-time read uses the existing cross-platform lock helper; the new tests run on Linux), and reclaiming inside a real container, which this PR does not change. The package base-against-head scenario updated between repacked copies of one build, not from a published release; the lanes cover that.

prs.title: fix: restore the new-window icon size in Reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Reports, the icon for **Open in a new window** was about half the size of the theme icon beside it. Both controls had the same hit area, but padding intended for the text tabs squeezed the new-window glyph.

## User Impact

The new-window action is easier to recognize on phones and desktops. Its hit area, keyboard position, accessible name, destination, and the spacing of the text tabs stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply text-tab padding to the report navigation’s segmented items, not to every link. The icon link can then use the same 16 × 16 SVG box as the theme button without an icon-specific override.

## Evidence

In the real Control UI Reports iframe, the new-window glyph went from 6 × 6 to 12 × 12 CSS px inside the same 34 × 34 target. Using the adjacent theme glyph’s top edge as the guide, the dark-theme gap fell from 3.67 to 0.67 px; in light mode it fell from 3.00 to 0.00 px. The glyph stayed centered, and only its pixels changed in the matched frames.

Exercised Reports, People, and Work sessions with populated synthetic data at 390 × 844 and 1440 × 900 in Chromium. prs.title: fix: keep scheduled jobs recovering while accepted work runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After the native scheduler reconnects and starts a job, recovery can remain occupied until that accepted job finishes. If the replacement native worker fails during that time, another reconnect is blocked by unrelated running work.

## User Impact

Scheduled jobs can recover from another native-worker failure while previously accepted work is still running. Ordinary initial startup keeps its existing waiting behavior. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release the recovery owner once startup publication and run-queue registration complete. The existing run queue continues to own execution, failure handling, and shutdown settlement; no duplicate drain owner is added.

## Evidence

- Two real-native regressions pass: replacement loss while an accepted job is held, and shutdown during launch. The replacement-loss case is red without the fix. Final-byte focused run: 2/2; 82.10 seconds including compilation. Earlier startup/recovery sibling run: 11/11.
- Exact-final-byte isolated Gateway/WebSocket/native-worker/real-model proof passes: 1/1, 42.828 seconds test time (148.45 seconds including compilation). One actual model invocation completed successfully and its return remained held; after the replacement worker was terminated, third dispatch occurred in 681 ms and ready in 937 ms. The 3000 ms assertion was unchanged. Gateway remained responsive and shutdown completed cleanly. The hold is after a real provider response, not during provider execution.
- Targeted type-aware lint/typecheck, formatting, and diff checks pass. No test budget allocation needed: 150 added test lines.
- Canonical local autoreview, P0–P3, reported no actionable findings on the exact patch against base a40174b768cfd3318dfecdc61da3e1ef0087effc, with complete run-queue, execution, and lifecycle context. Its assessment was static and did not include the full unchanged scheduler-actor module; a separate earlier independent review covered that module. Hosted review and exact-head CI remain to be observed.
- Patch SHA256: 7f160aa903b123477676620155818c2f76883cf7efb8c86ed264faf14ae60a73. Current main adc087617bb418d85823139dec790df5d990900e has unchanged affected scheduler/queue/lifecycle and fixture source, and does not contain this repair.

Historical limitation: the original hosted 3000 ms scheduler failure (job 136821853726) remains causally unproven. This change fixes the separately reproduced accepted-startup-work recovery blockage; passing local proof is not retroactive attribution or clearance of that historical failure. CI timing is pending.

prs.title: fix: show why a model tool call was rejected as malformed
prs.body:
Related: #202672

## What Problem This Solves

When a model streams a tool call whose arguments never arrive as a complete JSON object, the turn fails with a malformed-tool-call error. The `provider-error` log line for that failure showed only the error code and the provider's message id, so an operator reading the logs could not tell a truncated argument buffer from a buffer that was never JSON-encoded at all, and could not see how large the rejected buffer was or whether the string-literal repair had been attempted.

## User Impact

User impact: the `provider-error` log line for a rejected tool call now carries `argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, and `repairAttempted`, so operators can distinguish truncation from a never-encoded buffer without opening provider payloads. No argument text is added to the log, so the content-exclusion contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` already builds content-free diagnostics (`argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, `repairAttempted`) and attaches them to the error `cause` plus a mirrored `errorBody`. `assignTransportErrorDetails()` built the `provider-error` metadata from only `causeCode` / `code` / `type` / `requestId` / `responseId` / `status`, so those diagnostics never reached the log.

This change propagates the bounded diagnostics into that metadata and adds the transport-to-log regression coverage requested in #202672. The propagation is deliberately narrow:

- Only the fields produced by `parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` are surfaced, and only for the `malformed_tool_call_arguments` code.
- The argument hash is accepted only when it matches the base-36 digest shape OpenClaw produces, so a provider-crafted `cause` cannot smuggle argument text into the log.
- `errorBody` is **not** logged. For other error classes it can carry provider prose (prompts, tool results), so it must stay out of the log.
- Rejection behaviour, JSON repair, streaming, recovery, and failover are unchanged.

## Evidence

New coverage:

- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — *"surfaces bounded tool-call diagnostics in the provider-error log"* drives a truncated `tool_use` argument buffer through the loopback HTTP transport and asserts the `provider-error` metadata carries `argumentChars` / `argumentHash` / `repairAttempted` matching the terminal error body, that no `toolcall_end` is emitted, and that the rejected argument text appears in neither the log nor the error body.
- `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — *"logs bounded tool-call diagnostics without the rejected argument text"* pins the metadata contents for a rejected buffer, and *"does not log tool-call diagnostics that are not an OpenClaw digest"* proves a non-digest hash is dropped rather than logged.

Existing coverage kept green: the truncated-sibling case in `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` still requires truncated sibling arguments to stay rejected, the bounded diagnostics to survive in `errorBody`, private argument text to stay excluded, and no sibling `toolcall_end` to be emitted.

Focused tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Whole package suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/ai/
 Test Files  167 passed (167)
      Tests  2455 passed | 3 skipped (2458)
```

Format and lint on the touched files:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <same files>
✓ No problems in 3 files
```

<details>
<summary>Log line before and after</summary>

Before, the failure was indistinguishable from any other malformed tool call:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_...
```

After, the metadata additionally carries the bounded diagnostics (no argument text, only a length, a digest, and a flag):

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_... argumentChars=52 argumentHash=jiqoxq1e07seo repairAttempted=true
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep Skills discovery within its request limit and show the installed count
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
On first visit, the Skills page loaded the Gateway protocol validators only to read three upload size limits, which pushed the page toward its request limit. The collapsed Installed shelf did not say how many skills were installed, and the Plugins category strip kept its initial scroll edges after the categories loaded. The browser and benchmark checks for these pages had also drifted from current behavior: they waited for installed rows that start collapsed, and they expected installed plugins in ordinary browsing.

These problems reproduced on the base of [the Template sign-in PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013); this companion keeps their repairs out of that feature.

## User Impact
The Installed shelf shows its count, for example "Installed skills (1,000)". Skills and Plugins stay within their existing first-visit request limits, and the Plugins category strip reports correct scroll edges once its categories arrive. No migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Move the three skill upload limits into a module that constructs no validators. The protocol schema re-exports them, so the wire contract and existing imports are unchanged.
- Show the installed count in the shelf heading. The truncated name preview is hidden from assistive technology, which reads the count instead.
- Recompute the category strip's scroll state when the loaded categories change.
- Share the Skills readiness and interaction steps between the benchmark and the browser test. Both now require the complete installed count and the registry results, then open the last of 1,000 installed skills and check its Markdown on the full page route.
- Align Plugins navigation coverage with current discovery: installed providers appear in search, not in ordinary browsing or its later pages.
- No request limits, timing windows, or retry thresholds were changed.

Earlier revisions of this PR also carried repairs that have since landed on `main` separately, so they are no longer part of this diff: SDK declaration size ([#203000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203000)), SQLite ownership checks off the Gateway thread ([#202765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202765)), the compact Skill workshop heading ([#202784](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202784)), the Plugins request repair ([#202795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202795)), and the internal Chat file-link helpers ([#202879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202879)). The diff is now 12 files.

## Evidence
[Clean and annotated Skills screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202715#issuecomment-7050055796) show the installed count before and after. They predate the merges with `main`; the Workshop heading they also show is now provided by #202784.

Current head `efc8e461e887`, whose tree is identical to the locally validated `7696518cb333` (merged with `main` at `c56a9d40e778`). Local macOS Chromium with synthetic inventory and loopback services, not hosted Linux CI:

- 14 of 14 focused browser cases passed without retries: ten Plugins workspace navigation cases and the four first-visit request-limit cases, against the unchanged caps (Skills 28, Skills Settings 31, Plugins 56, Plugin Settings 61).
- The Skills case becomes ready with 1,000 installed skills plus registry results, opens `/skills/installed/data-skill-0999`, and renders that skill's Markdown.
- UI, scripts, and core typechecks, formatting, and lint passed.

On the preceding head `2ec20111e2a`, against `main` at `247b9581b1d`: the full build passed, and the release-size comparison measured Chat and New Session each 104 gzip bytes smaller, with startup size and all request counts unchanged. Changed-file checks passed there once two unused Chat exports were made private; that fix now comes from #202879 instead.

prs.title: feat: prepare worker placements for recovery after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a worker is confirmed lost, Codex recovery needs to know which placement it is replacing, even if the Gateway restarted. The shared database has no field for that fact yet.

## User Impact

This prerequisite adds storage only; it does not enable recovery or change existing placements. Shared state advances from v40 to v41 (the agent schema is unchanged). Older builds require restoration of the verified pre-upgrade backup before downgrade.

Related: #201026, #201032. The existing shared branch and both PRs are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing placement row and migration owner: one nullable field on SQLite and PostgreSQL, no backfill, no automatic loss inference, and no reader or writer for the new field in this PR. The placement owner can later record the predecessor with its existing placement update; a separate store would add another write and rollback boundary. No repository reset, permission change, or new retention policy is included. [Maintainer design acceptance](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0).

## Evidence

- Fixtures from the published stable v36 and beta v40 SQLite schemas preserved the seeded rows and original schema when commit was refused, then upgraded successfully through the existing owner. The new field was NULL; this was not a package-update/restart run.
- Isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed 16 focused cases, including old schemas with and without the optional repository table. Repository fragment SQL is unchanged. Generated schema checks, focused typechecks, lint, formatting, and the test-line budget (+248 net; 400 allowed) passed on the tested patch against `4b74fd5a979d`. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the reviewed scope.
- **Upgrade cost:** one nullable ALTER on `worker_session_placements`, no backfill or row rewrite; SQLite retains existing idempotent index checks and quick/placement integrity checks. The scoped SQLite backup copies placement rows and publication metadata; the package updater retains its existing full rollback capture. PostgreSQL takes its normal DDL lock and publishes the version. Largest-deployment row counts and backup/lock timings were not available; packaged update/restart and a Swift build are still unverified.

Original implementation: @galiniliev, selectively ported from `a1b9b73924b6`.
