prs.title: fix: bring the Gateway back when a failed Windows update rolls back
prs.body:
Related: #169844

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, when an update fails and OpenClaw rolls back, the rollback refuses with `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN: Scheduled Task changed.` and stops. The Scheduled Task stays **Disabled** and the Gateway stays down until someone re-enables the task by hand. Nobody changed the task: the only difference is the updater's own `/DISABLE`.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed Windows update rolls back to the previous version with the Scheduled Task re-enabled and the Gateway running, instead of leaving the Gateway down.

Installs only get this once the updater they update *from* contains the fix (the installed updater runs the rollback check). Until then the manual recovery is `schtasks /Change /TN "OpenClaw Gateway" /ENABLE` followed by `openclaw gateway start`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Task Scheduler exports omit `Settings.Enabled=true` and serialize an explicit `<Enabled>false</Enabled>` in schema order (after `StopIfGoingOnBatteries`). The rollback guard hashed the task after re-inserting `Enabled=false` at the *start* of `Settings`, so the backed-up (enabled) task and the live task disabled by the updater always hashed differently. The install-recovery receipt checks compared raw strings with the same position dependence.

Registrations are now compared without `Settings.Enabled` (plus the parsed enable state where it matters), in one small `schtasks-xml-enabled` owner. Rollback receipts cross updater/candidate versions, so the receipt hash format is unchanged and verification additionally accepts the live task once `Settings.Enabled` is dropped. The test-only normalizer that already encoded this export rule is retired in favor of the production helper.

Production LOC: +74/−40 (+50 is the extracted module; `schtasks-control.ts` was at its 700-line cap). Tests +60. Regression: since #152120.

## Evidence

- Root cause from M24 Windows evidence: the backed-up task XML and the live task differ only by `<Enabled>false</Enabled>` after `StopIfGoingOnBatteries`; same failure on `b229b266453^` (pre-#200578), so it is not a recent regression.
- New tests, red on base and green with the fix:
  - `service-definition-backup.test.ts` "restores after Task Scheduler exports the update's own disable in schema order" (base: `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN: Scheduled Task changed.`), and it pins the receipt hash format older updaters verify.
  - `schtasks-install-rollback.test.ts` "restores an enabled task whose export places the update's disable in schema order" (base: restore fails).
  - `schtasks.integration-xml.test.ts` export canonicalization for `\r\n` and `\r\r\n`.
- All 26 `schtasks*` / `service-definition-backup*` / `service-policy-preservation` test files: 431 passed. `pnpm check:changed` passed.
- Reviews: autoreview scoped-clean; an independent Codex review first caught that changing the receipt hash would break cross-version rollback (fixed in the second commit), then found nothing on the final head.
- Live Windows proof (Crabbox, Windows Server 2025, npm global, Scheduled Task): update 11.6 → fixed build, then to a deliberately broken build whose Gateway exits on start.

  | Updater | Rollback outcome | Version after | Scheduled Task | Gateway `/readyz` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | main `b8b06c4824f` (today's matrix) | failed: `Scheduled Task changed` | previous | Disabled | down |
  | pre-#200578 `df2faf7d476` | failed: `Scheduled Task changed` | previous | Disabled | down |
  | this PR `9448fef5b3a` | succeeded: previous package and configuration restored | previous | Running | 200 |

  The manual recovery above was also checked on the same box (Disabled/down → Running/200).

prs.title: fix: keep empty device search results visible during refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Systems, a background device refresh could make “No devices match your search” disappear and reappear even though neither the search nor the devices had changed. A confirmed empty inventory could blink the same way.

## User Impact

The last device search result stays visible until an updated inventory replaces it. The first load still shows loading rather than claiming there are no devices, and a failed first read still offers recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Systems already retains the last successful inventory during a refresh. The sidebar now uses that inventory for its empty result, just as it does for populated rows. The list still reports that it is busy; this changes neither requests nor their timing.

## Evidence

With “work laptop” in the search box, two unchanged inventory notifications each erased the result for **eight consecutive recorded frames** on desktop. After the change the text stayed visible throughout both reads. The same two blinks reproduced in the phone-width drawer and were absent during both refreshes after the fix.

Real Control UI in Chromium, light theme, 1280 × 800 and emulated 390 × 800. The clips show matching desktop sidebar crops at the original 60 fps. prs.title: fix(gateway): clean up transient isolated hook base sessions after run (#202621)
prs.body:
Closes #202621

## What Problem This Solves

Every isolated webhook run (`POST /hooks/agent`) creates an ephemeral agent execution session that was never cleaned up after completion. Over time, gateways running automated webhooks accumulate hundreds of orphaned base session records (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>`) that cannot be purged by standard cron retention sweeps.

## User Impact

User impact: Prevents unbounded session record leaks and database bloat on gateways handling webhook triggers, ensuring transient isolated hook sessions are immediately purged after execution while preserving history for persistent hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Isolated hook runs create ephemeral jobs with `sessionTarget: "isolated"` but previously omitted `deleteAfterRun`. Setting `deleteAfterRun: value.sessionMode !== "persistent"` marks transient hook runs for post-run base session cleanup in `cleanupCronRunSessionAfterRun` once finished, while keeping conversation history intact when `sessionMode === "persistent"`.

## Evidence

Verified that the new unit test fails red on base (`expected undefined to be true` for `call.job.deleteAfterRun`) and passes green with the fix.

Targeted test suites:
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` (21 passed)
- `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts` (33 passed)
- Linters and formatting: `oxlint` (0 errors, 0 warnings) and `run-format.mts` clean.

Open **+**, tap a plugin’s name, then choose its action. For example, **Better Prompt → Better** and **Better Prompt → Better and send** share one row in the menu. prs.title: fix: let agents on a dedicated worker start child sessions
prs.body:
Hi! I'm exploring running our planning workflows ([RFE Creator](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/rfe-creator), [Strat Creator](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/strat-creator) and [Epic Creator](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/epic-creator)) as multi-agent OpenClaw agents on dedicated workers in OpenShell, using OpenClaw Enterprise. This is the first fix from what I hit along the way. Next up is a related worker one: the model can loop on `sessions_yield`, which the worker offers but always refuses.

## What Problem This Solves

On a dedicated worker, an agent cannot start a child session from an ordinary request.

The model is not the problem. The prompt is. The worker's `sessions_spawn` accepts `task`, `label`, `agentId`, `model` and `runTimeoutSeconds`. The system prompt describes the full Gateway tool instead: objective-style briefs, `context`, `taskName`, `visible=true`, ACP options. The model follows the prompt and sends `objective` instead of `task`. The worker refuses with "Worker tool arguments are invalid". No field name, so the model cannot tell what to fix, and no child is created.

## User Impact

Agents on a dedicated worker start child sessions from an ordinary request. This is the core pattern in our skills: a coordinator spawns reviewer children and collects their results. Today, on a worker, every one of those spawns fails unless the skill restates the worker schema. When a model still sends a field the worker refuses, the refusal names it. Prompts outside workers do not change. No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two problems, two commits. Fix one, and the other remains: a correct prompt still leaves a bare refusal when a model drifts, and a clear refusal still costs a failed call on every spawn.

- **The refusal names the fields.** The worker keeps its strict check and reports each failing field in the format the non-worker validator already uses (`- task: must have required properties task`). The formatter is shared, not copied.
- **The prompt describes the worker tool.** The worker turn passes a `workerPlacement` flag to the prompt builder, the same flag `sessions_spawn` already uses to pick its worker schema. On a worker, the guidance says the whole brief goes in `task` and every child is a visible session, and ACP spawn guidance is omitted, as sandboxed runs already do.

Alternatives I considered, happy to switch:
- **One spawn hint true for both tools.** Smaller, but Gateway runs, which are most runs, lose the `context` and `taskName` guidance.
- **Derive the guidance from the `sessions_spawn` definition in the tool list.** Cannot drift from the schema, but a larger change to how prompt guidance is built.

Out of scope: letting the worker's `sessions_spawn` accept more Gateway options. That is a product call; if it lands, the worker prompt text here should follow.

## Evidence

Live runs on a dedicated worker, gpt-4.1, same plain request, new chat each time. Without the patch, every run failed. With it (on OpenClaw Enterprise, which builds on an earlier runtime; the code paths are unchanged on `main`), 3 of 4 runs created the child: 2 on the first call, 1 after the named refusal and a retry. The fourth hit the `sessions_yield` loop above.

**Before, on current `main`.** The model sends `objective` and `output`; the worker refuses with the bare message.
[before-objective-refused.png]

**After, first call.** The model sends `task`; the child is created and replies with the marker.
[after-task-accepted.png]
[after-child-reply.png]

**After, named refusal.** The model adds `runtime`; the refusal names it, and the retry without it creates the child.
[after-named-refusal.png]

Tests, each failing without the change it covers:
- **Worker runtime:** the refusal names the missing and unexpected fields.
- **Prompt:** worker spawn hint, delegation guidance, session routing and ACP guidance, each with a non-worker control.
- **Wiring:** the flag reaches the rendered worker prompt through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSystemPrompt`.

I also have an end-to-end test (paired node worker, scripted model) that I left out to keep this small. Happy to add it if you want it.

Not validated live: an agent's main session (`prefer`-mode delegation), ACP-enabled workers, models other than gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o-mini.

prs.title: fix: keep background handoffs out of chat reply errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a subagent result could not be delivered, chat could show “Couldn’t finish this reply” and “Report a bug” several times above an answer that actually arrived. The same warning also marked questions that genuinely had no answer.

## User Impact

Background delivery reports fold into the work details instead of interrupting the conversation. Open the disclosure to read the retained findings. A reply that really stopped still has its own failure notice. There is no toast or inbox item.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion writer knows whether a handoff was independent or was needed to finish a waiting request. Chat now uses that distinction rather than comparing the wording of failures. Previously saved, individually identifiable background reports get the same treatment; older ambiguous reports remain visible rather than hiding a possible blocked reply. This changes presentation, not delivery, retry behavior, or the saved transcript.

## Evidence

The same saved-history scenario showed **three failed replies on the baseline and one with the fix**. In an isolated real Gateway and Chromium, the test opens both retained background findings, inspects the unanswered follow-up, preserves an unsent draft during inspection, and checks the distinction after reload. The transcript entries are synthetic; the browser, storage, history API, and UI are real. The test does not induce a live provider outage or a subagent transport failure.

Baseline: `20ef309ec843d`. Tested change: `8945958b7c2a0`. Dark desktop, 1280 × 900, matched chat-pane crops. The final focused browser run passed in 41 seconds. The two backend suites (80 tests), neighboring UI suites (44 tests), UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting passed. CI timings are not yet available.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: three reply warnings for one unanswered question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/558c5024-0082-46e8-9720-9d394fe1cca8)

**After**

![A genuinely blocked reply still has its own error details](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69567758-e662-4f74-b61e-79838b45cdba)

prs.title: fix: hide structured tool calls from session history by default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant recalls a session, `sessions_history` can return structured tool calls and their arguments even when tool activity wasn't requested. Tool-result messages were already hidden, but tool blocks inside other messages weren't.

## User Impact

Session recall omits structured tool calls and results by default. Set `includeTools: true` to see them. Message IDs, pagination, ordinary text, readable reasoning, and markup embedded in text are preserved. By default, recall also omits opaque thinking blocks that contain no readable reasoning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history tool filters structured blocks using OpenClaw's existing block-type contract before applying its response byte cap. It retains the parent message, even if the content becomes empty, so an existing message ID remains usable as an anchor. The shared classifier recognizes the lowercase `toolcall` spelling produced by the Claude CLI importer. Filtering affects the model-facing recall only; it does not rewrite imported JSONL, stored transcripts, or Gateway history.

## Evidence

- Two regressions failed on base `915669080` and pass with the fix: paged recall with and without tool activity, and an anchored tool-only row alongside user text and a structured tool result.
- 32 history tool tests and 16 prompt-prefix stability tests passed (54s and 62s wall time locally). Formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Self-reviewed the full diff. A separate P0–P3 Auto Review attempt against `915669080` timed out without a verdict; ClawSweeper found no correctness issues on the prior head `9705247ca1af`; its [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44940933995) passed. Follow-up-head CI and review are separate.
- The updated tool description is reflected in the three generated Codex fixtures. `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passes after regeneration.

- **End-to-end Gateway proof (rerun with the Claude CLI fix):** Two real OpenClaw agent turns wrote ordinary text, structured `session_status` calls, and tool results to the isolated Gateway's transcript. A separate real agent recalled that session via `sessions_history`. At the model-facing tool response, omitted and explicit `false` each hid both calls and results; `true` returned both. All three retained the visible reply. The default anchored read retained the tool-only message ID with `content: []`, the next page used `nextOffset: 1` and returned two strictly older rows, and a subsequent Gateway history read still contained the original tool call.
- The combined Gateway proof passed (16.4s test time; 53.7s including startup/transform). The Gateway, agent loop, tool execution, and transcript storage were real; the model endpoint was a deterministic loopback Responses provider, not hosted inference.
- **Claude CLI import proof:** A synthetic Claude JSONL transcript was linked to an isolated Gateway session and read through the actual importer. Raw Gateway history exposed lowercase `toolcall`, `tool_result`, and both opaque thinking variants. The registered `sessions_history` tool omitted all four with `includeTools` omitted or false, preserved readable reasoning and final text, and returned all blocks with `true`. A signature-only row kept its message ID and empty content when recalled by anchor. The imported offset view remained a terminal snapshot, and the source JSONL was unchanged. The focused regression failed on the previous PR head and passes with this change.

**Runtime output (isolated Gateway, deterministic loopback model):**

```text
Claude CLI JSONL → Gateway import → sessions_history → agent: omitted/false hid toolcall, tool_result and both signatures; true retained them; readable reasoning, final text, signature-only anchor and terminal snapshot passed; JSONL unchanged.
Gateway chat.send → real agent → sessions_history → provider tool output: omitted=false; explicit false=false; opt-in=true; anchor content=[]; nextOffset=1, older rows=2
```

The booleans in the second line indicate presence of tool activity in the returned content. Only assertion output is shown; endpoint and process logs are omitted. Hosted-model recall has not been run.

Exact-head [prompt snapshot check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44949200153/job/136983657136) and [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44950250315) passed.

Contributor: @TheAngryPit

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af8f1f56-dbda-4b18-b0b2-a2c7ca957d04)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(ui): keep pinned sessions visible when switching a chat to Draft
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changing a chat from Shared to Draft can make unrelated pinned chats briefly disappear and reappear. This happens when a pin is outside the sidebar’s current list page and the Gateway is still checking whether it can be shown.

## User Impact

Unchanged pins stay visible and in the same order while sharing changes. Pins that the Gateway confirms are no longer accessible still disappear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar reuses the already-rendered pin as a temporary fallback rather than rebuilding it on invalidation. The Gateway still decides what the user can access. The sharing write, redacted invalidation, and authoritative reads are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Bundled Control UI in Chromium: Shared → Draft reproduced a three → two → three pin sequence on `307d9c45fb25`. On `5f63a93492d5`, all three original DOM rows stayed mounted in pin order through the held descriptor read. The sidebar list RPC still ran; expanded state and loading presentation did not change.
- Neighboring controls: title updates, recency ordering under Other, sharing back, confirmed access loss, pin/unpin, and reconnect passed. Focus and scroll on an unaffected row survived revalidation.
- Isolated real Gateway and Chromium, 204 synthetic sessions: the actual visibility write produced both scoped and redacted change events, the sidebar refreshed, the off-page pin was re-described, and all three original nodes stayed mounted. No live Team state or provider calls were used.
- 37 focused unit tests, four browser cases, UI production and test typechecks, scoped lint/format, and local autoreview (P0–P2; no actionable findings) passed.
- The [original performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44547630986/job/135643427324) failed only the chat boot gzip limit: 1,332,763 B on the original patch vs. 1,332,622 B on its CI base (limit: 1,332,637 B). The repair passed the unchanged paired gate locally with Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, and Pako 3.0.3: 1,332,599 B on the clean base → 1,332,604 B on the repair, 33 B below the limit. Requests stayed at 21 → 21 and chat boot CSS stayed at 139,073 B. The existing request-count and total/largest CSS overruns were not new blocking violations. No budgets or check policies changed.

### Clean comparison

**Before**: Research notes temporarily drops out of Pinned.

![Before: two of three pins are visible while Draft is selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17369836-14de-4cbb-9318-aae6562063d9)

**After**: Research notes remains visible in its original position.

![After: all three pins are visible while Draft is selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8636ebc-ac19-42da-8cb0-8ef5217f6ae4)

### Annotated comparison

![Before: callout points to the missing pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9153a6c8-fbc0-4ef7-900b-0b1b45074d43)

![After: callout points to the retained pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e44800b2-abde-4ce7-a1df-a303009ba35c)

Both frames show the same in-flight revalidation in the real Control UI, with synthetic Gateway data and a held descriptor reply (Chromium, 1280×820, dark). The same visible result was reproduced on the repair.

Reported by [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b6c9890-c898-4067-afd7-e6d4e8db39cb)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8fd8a130-03d0-40a5-a4c7-84433ec3ba78)

prs.title: feat: dismiss browser completion notifications after viewing replies
prs.body:
Related: #202178

## What Problem This Solves

Browser/PWA completion notifications can remain after the corresponding reply has been read, leaving stale alerts to dismiss manually.

## User Impact and Read Boundaries

Dismiss only the notification for an exact final reply visibly viewed in the foreground. Preserve unrelated sessions, newer/unseen replies and legacy alerts without reliable identity. Cleanup is local to the same browser/service-worker registration, not cross-device recall.

Payload and transcript identity match on agent/session/run/message/recipient. Message identity prefers the persisted idempotency key and otherwise uses the row ID. Session opening, history loading and notification tags alone do not acknowledge a completion.

The layout review finding is corrected: read presentation requires an active row, settled initial position and release of the transcript's hidden state. Resource preparation remains independently enabled. Layout/foreground/connection/profile ownership fences queued callbacks synchronously.

At most 512 page-memory visibility receipts are retained for six minutes (five-minute push TTL plus margin). The worker's after-display hint reconciles late pushes while a page is visible. Closing all pages forgets receipts; there is no durable cross-restart acknowledgement guarantee. Support is limited to the serving Gateway's origin and registration scope.

## Evidence

Current head: `45b07b2be25bbbeddafde2ba4511c3a15f88bd12`.

- [Final-head formatting, allocation and input-equivalence proof](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44847422160): **passed**. The runner verified the exact formatter-only transformation from the preceding tested head plus allocation 704 → 706, with every other tracked entry unchanged. No browser/test rerun is claimed at this formatting-only head.
- [Behavioral proof at 81b1d5daa9e6853930dd70637261d89998ecda84](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44846626872): Chromium upgrade/notification test, 2 identity tests, 8 runtime tests and the required scoped canonical lint wrapper **passed**. That run's sole failure was the formatter line-wrap now corrected and verified above.
- Chromium installs the pinned released v2026.11.5 worker, retains its identity-less notification, updates the same registration without clearing storage, verifies the running candidate's embedded build identity, and preserves exact legacy notification data. It then verifies unread/newer/other-session preservation, exact foreground-read dismissal, emulated foreground return and delayed-delivery reconciliation. Listener installation is acknowledged before injection. The redundant key-inequality test was removed; observable identity-separation coverage remains.
- Reuse inventory SHA-256 versus the behavioral head, excluding only the exactly verified formatter/allocation files: `ce5102240c16f636e511e8c8dca8085292eeede95f053412ec2497073a982668`. Final browser-test bytes SHA-256: `18202c2d781d9021027d5964ed34384d218bb82a836d343eb5403646085ed1e4`.
- Production/dependency/configuration inputs independently match the previously tested layout repair at `e0b0cb680c18b19585d52f72d65cb00e5f9dab89`; only two tests, the historical worker fixture and allocation differ. Inventory SHA-256: `8de953c2417347cb9d5fd655abe535e218627ef3b20b9b79feaa5675f36cc227`. The [full production build and real-renderer regression](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44801786340), [affected layout suites, UI production types and UI build](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44800188759), and independently unchanged [core-type proof](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44797497267) retain their original scopes. Historical format/lint failures in the core-type run were separately repaired; its entire run is not described as passing.
- The real-renderer regression covers hidden initial positioning, settlement, inactive preparation/forecast rows, queued callbacks, parking and disposal.
- Final ratchet: 1,106 net test lines, 400 allowance plus 706 explicit allocation. The pinned historical-worker fixture is separate from test logic. No assertions, checks or baselines were disabled.

## Tested Scope and Remaining Decisions

This is desktop Chromium behavior using real ServiceWorker/Notification APIs, CDP-injected push, mocked Gateway transport and emulated visibility transitions. It does not establish real encrypted Web Push transport, native OS notification shade/suspension, Safari/mobile behavior, or a complete old UI/Gateway upgrade. No device access or mobile acceptance is claimed. Android-specific validation is not automatically a prerequisite for this browser feature; the stated tested scope remains for reviewer acceptance.

[Final-head upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44847326518) remains `action_required`; maintainer admission and required upstream results are separate from the fork evidence. Maintainer acceptance of automatic exact-read dismissal, receipt lifetime/capacity and serving-origin scope remains pending.

Previously disclosed non-failing test-length and CSS/chat-boot diagnostics remain. Renderer Solid strict-read warnings were [traced to unchanged lifecycle call sites](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44803275112); no warning suppression, baseline runtime comparison or performance improvement is claimed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep CLI run tools working after a plugin reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A CLI-backed agent run (for example Claude CLI) loses all of its OpenClaw tools when any plugin is reloaded or reinstalled while the run is in progress. Every tool call, including core tools that have nothing to do with the reloaded plugin, fails with `Internal error` (JSON-RPC -32603) until the run ends. In our case, reinstalling the Gemini OAuth plugin from inside a Claude CLI turn made `exec`, `message` and `session_status` fail for the rest of that turn, so the agent could not verify its own install or report back.

## User Impact

User impact: a CLI-backed run keeps working tools after a plugin reload or reinstall. Its tool calls continue on the newly published plugin generation, the same way embedded runs continue on it at their next step.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

#### High Level TLDR

The MCP loopback grant for a CLI run remembers the plugin set the run started with. After a reload retires that plugin set, every later tool request from the run keeps building its tool list from the retired plugins, hits the retired plugin, and fails as a whole. Now the first request that hits a retired plugin set builds its tools again on the current one, and the grant's later requests stay there.

#### Root Cause

- `mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant` stores `requestScope: getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope()`. For a CLI run this scope carries the run's prepared plugin generation as its `pluginRegistry`.
- For CLI grants with Cron management construction, `mcp-http.ts` builds tools inside that scope (`withPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope(boundClientGrant.requestScope, constructAsCaller)`), and plugin tool resolution prefers the scope's registry (`openclaw-plugin-tools.ts`: `requestRegistry ?? getActivePluginRegistry()`).
- After a reload retires that generation, the retired plugin's tool factory throws `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`. That error counts as a request-wide lifecycle failure (`isRequestWideFailure` → `isPreparedModelRuntimePluginLifecycleFailure`), so the whole request fails, not only that plugin's tools. Nothing caches a failed build, so every later request repeats it for the rest of the run.
- Embedded runs already handle this: after a reload they re-run outside the retired generation (`runOutsidePluginRuntimeGenerationScope`, see `run-orchestrator.ts` and `prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts`). The plugin turn handover logs `whole-run hold yields to the reload` for CLI runs, and its comment says a later fresh call "rebinds to the current registry". The MCP loopback never did that rebinding.
- Gateway log from the incident (identifiers removed):

  ```
  Plugin replacement queued behind 2 retained work item(s) for plugin gemini. Running turns on gemini continue on the new version at their next step.
  [agents/plugin-turn-handover] plugin gemini reload requested; whole-run hold yields to the reload
  Plugin replacement applied: gemini
  [mcp-loopback] request handling failed: Plugin gemini was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.   (repeated on every tool call until the turn ended)
  ```

#### Change

- New `src/gateway/mcp-http.grant-generation.ts` owns how a run-bound grant enters its request scope:
  - `resolveInMcpGrantRequestScope` builds tools in the grant's scope. On a retired-generation failure (`isPreparedModelRuntimePluginLifecycleFailure`, or an expired registry scope) it waits for a reload that is still in flight, marks the grant's scope as retired, and builds once more outside the plugin generation (`runOutsidePluginRuntimeGenerationScope`). That keeps the exact Gateway caller and authority. Any other error propagates unchanged, as does a second failure.
  - `runInMcpGrantRequestScope` runs tool execution in the grant's scope, outside the generation once that scope has been marked retired. That way execution matches the tools that were built.
- `mcp-http.ts` uses these two helpers at its two existing `withPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope(boundClientGrant.requestScope, …)` call sites.

#### Scope boundary

- No change while a grant's plugin generation is current. The fallback only runs after the pinned generation has already failed. Before this change, that state failed every request.
- The tool cache is unchanged. Tool lists built before a reload can still be served for up to the 30-second cache lifetime, and the reloaded plugin's own tools from that cached list then report `tool runtime is no longer active` at the tool level. Other tools keep working, and it clears when the entry expires. This is a separate, self-healing issue and not part of this PR.
- Grants without a request scope, and owner or non-owner listener tokens, are untouched.

## Evidence

#### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior fixed:** after a plugin reload, a run-bound CLI grant can still call tools from both an unrelated plugin and the reloaded plugin.
- **Environment:** the real MCP loopback HTTP server, the real plugin loader with two on-disk probe plugins, real plugin instances, the real grant store, and a grant minted inside the original generation scope with Cron management construction, as a CLI run does. One plugin's generation is replaced and its old instance is disposed.
- **Command:** `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/mcp-http.plugin-reload.test.ts`
- **Before (base `2e3fd02ff12`):**

  ```
  × keeps a run-bound grant's tools working after a plugin reload retires its generation
    → {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error"}}: expected 500 to be 200
  ```

  This is the same error the agent saw live.
- **After:**

  ```
  ✓ observes plain results by reference across registry replacement despite observer errors
  ✓ observes shared results by reference across registry replacement despite observer errors
  ✓ keeps a run-bound grant's tools working after a plugin reload retires its generation
  Tests  3 passed (3)
  ```

#### Verification

- MCP loopback, grant store and request-scope suites: 25 files, 191 passed, 10 failed. The same 10 also fail on the unmodified base in this environment. They are exec-sandbox tests (`Linux child ownership requires a process owner without source-loader hooks`; cgroup controllers are not delegated on this host) and slow-body timeout tests in `mcp-http.exec-completion`, `mcp-http.exec-egress` and `mcp-http.test`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint, import cycles, architecture, plugin boundary and other guards pass. Two failures are unrelated to this change and also present on base: `typecheck core` (`src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts(309,13)`: `revalidateOnCompletion` does not exist in `InProcessGatewayCallOptions`), and the dead-export scan (`extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser/*`).
- Local `$autoreview`: no findings.

#### What was not tested

- No isolated Gateway run with a real CLI model turn reinstalling a plugin mid-turn. The regression test drives the same loopback and grant path with real plugins, but not a live Claude CLI process.
- No benchmark. The only per-request cost added is one `WeakSet` lookup on the grant's scope.

prs.title: fix: remove old chat questions and notices after reset
prs.body:
Root cause: ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-build.ts:500 (notices) and :577 (question summaries) placed the browser-only observer notices and answered question summaries by timestamp, without checking the reset divider the same build emits at :262. So after `/reset` they stayed above "Session reset" until reload.

Closes #203215

## What Problem This Solves

After a chat reset, the Control UI can still show an earlier answered question and a system notice above the reset divider. The Gateway history is already clear, but the browser can still have those rows cached.

## User Impact

The reset divider starts the cleared transcript. Questions and notices from later activity still appear in the same chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript already reads the reset marker from Gateway history. The same projection now uses its timestamp to filter cached questions and notices from earlier turns.

Thanks @NovaeonStudio for isolating the two stale rows and checking the Gateway history.

## Evidence

On Windows, I ran a local OpenClaw Gateway in Chromium with a scripted chat provider and a failing utility provider. I answered a question, waited for the actual observer warning, then sent `/reset`. On `adc0876`, both old rows stayed above the divider. On `ed525f7`, both disappeared, and a new question could still be answered. In both runs, the Gateway returned the reset marker and an empty question list. I also kept an answered question in a second session across the reset and confirmed the cleared transcript after reconnecting.

Re-checked on a real isolated Gateway with the built Control UI in Chromium, using the same scenario: a scripted model that runs commands and then asks one `ask_user` question, plus a utility model that always fails so the observer notice appears. The post-reset question is asked in the same tab, before any reload. Base is main at 2c473901162a; this branch is 48dddba794:

| Step | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| A after `/reset`, same tab | old question card and observer notice above the divider | only the divider, `/reset`, and the reply |
| New question in A after the reset, same tab | n/a | question card and notice shown below the divider |

When people open a Template to review its contents, plugin rows briefly show package IDs as titles, then switch to friendly names. The change makes it harder to scan which plugins the Template includes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Template details and the inline preview now share the same exact-release presentation state. prs.title: fix: keep the Windows openclaw command on the current release after Git updates
prs.body:
Related: #200578

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, a Git install's `openclaw` command keeps running the build made when the installer ran. After #200578, every Git update should repoint the installer's `openclaw.cmd` at the release launcher. On Windows it never did, so `openclaw` keeps running the checkout's old build and its old updater. At the next state schema bump that build would refuse every command, including `openclaw update`. macOS and Linux are not affected.

## User Impact

- The next Git update on Windows repoints `openclaw` at the current release.
- That update still exits with its real exit code.
- New Windows Git installs write a wrapper the updater recognizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`install.ps1` built the wrapper path with `"dist\\entry.js"`. In a double-quoted PowerShell string that is a literal double backslash, so the wrapper reads `node "C:\repo\dist\\entry.js" %*`. The updater compared that line exactly against `C:\repo\dist\entry.js`, so it skipped the wrapper every time. The installer's own `Test-PreviousGitWrapper` regex rejected the line for the same reason. The fix:
- The updater compares normalized, case-insensitive Windows paths.
- The installer writes single backslashes.
- The installer's regex accepts wrappers already written with the double backslash.

Once the rewrite happened, a second problem showed up live. `openclaw update` usually runs through the very wrapper it rewrites. cmd.exe rereads a running batch file at its saved byte offset, so when the update returned, cmd resumed in the middle of the new line. The update then exited 1 with `The system cannot find the path specified.` even though it had succeeded.

The new wrapper is:
- `@goto run`;
- a `@rem` line padded so the old file's length lands exactly on `@exit /b %errorlevel%`;
- `:run`;
- `@node "<launcher>" %*`.

A fresh run jumps to the launcher. The cmd.exe that ran the update exits with the update's own exit code. The updater and the installer recognize both formats, and a later update rewrites the wrapper byte for byte.

POSIX wrappers are unchanged: they `exec`, so bash never reads the rewritten file.

## Evidence

- **Regression test.** The wrapper `install.ps1` writes is repointed at the launcher. In the new file, the old file's byte length lands on the exit line, and a second update rewrites it unchanged. The test fails on base and passes with the fix.
- **Live, Crabbox Windows Server 2025 (AWS).** Base `install.ps1` writes the wrapper, then one `openclaw update --channel dev` from a checkout at the driver commit:

  | Driver | Wrapper after the update | `openclaw --version` | Update exit code |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | base `9156690807f` | still `node "C:\g\oc\dist\\entry.js"` (checkout build) | checkout build | 0 |
  | first fix, rewrite with no padding | launcher | release | 1, `The system cannot find the path specified.` |
  | padded rewrite (`ac2174e34e5`) | padded launcher wrapper | release `0810295` | 0 |

  Through the padded launcher wrapper, `openclaw --version` exits 0 and an unknown command exits 1.
  The final head (`b4828c4ce9f`) adds only the unit-proven skip that leaves a wrapper already on the launcher unchanged.

- `test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts` passes locally with pwsh.
- Reviews on `b4828c4ce9f`: autoreview scoped-clean, and an independent `codex exec` review found nothing. Earlier rounds found the repeated-rewrite padding growth and the vacuous second-call test; both are fixed.

Not in this PR. The evidence is on #200578.
- **Switching a Git install back to npm** (`Occupied slot does not resolve to its original installation.`) needs more than a slot exception. Package publication recovery also requires the executor's installation to be the npm directory, so the fix belongs with the package update owner. Verified workaround: `npm i -g openclaw@<version>`, then `openclaw gateway install --force`.
- **POSIX Git-on-main installs already locked out by schema 41.** An older updater left their wrapper on the checkout. Recovery: `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs update --channel dev`.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): pasted clipboard images do not attach in terminal sessions
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #202645

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users pasting a copied image into the terminal-mode chat input (for example a Codex session opened from the session catalogue) would get nothing — the image was silently dropped, while picking the same image via the attach button worked.
- **Related:** #202645; the clawsweeper review confirmed the gap ("file selection stages attachments, but the input never forwards pasted images to that path") and asked for real paste behavior in the shipped product rather than a synthesized event.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** A paste carrying image files into the embedded terminal composer input now stages those images through the exact same path as the attach button and drag & drop: upload admission, quoting, editable attachment chips, and explicit submit (no PTY input before Send). Text-only pastes keep the native input path.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to the desktop (non-embedded) terminal panel, PTY paste behavior, or upload policy; non-image clipboard files are not intercepted (matches the composer-level image-paste precedent in the command palette).
- **Highest-risk area:** Accidentally swallowing text pastes or double-pasting into the PTY.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The handler returns early when no image items are present (native paste untouched), and the existing upload owner already refuses any PTY write before explicit submission — both covered by the regressions and by the real-gateway run below.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With a live terminal session open, copying a PNG and pasting into the chat input shows an editable attachment chip; Send submits the text plus the quoted uploaded path; no PTY input happens before Send.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-upload.ts` (`handlePaste`), `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-view.tsx` (composer `onPaste` wiring); regressions in `terminal-file-upload.test.ts` ("leaves text-only pastes on the native input path") and the real-Chromium e2e `ui/src/e2e/terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts` ("stages a pasted clipboard image in the chat terminal composer and submits only on Send"), which now copies a real canvas-encoded PNG into the browser clipboard and pastes it with a trusted `Ctrl+V` instead of dispatching a synthetic `ClipboardEvent`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree at commit `36b2aa96b8e` (base `origin/main` @ `a3bd84cc506`), Node 26.12.1, Linux, Google Chrome 151. Two lanes: (1) the committed real-Chromium ui-e2e lane; (2) a **real OpenClaw gateway built from this checkout** (`node dist/index.js gateway --port 18811 --bind loopback` on an isolated state dir) driven by a real Chrome through the shipped Control UI — chat → side-panel launcher → embedded Terminal with a real PTY-backed `bash`. Lane (2) substitutes no gateway response: every `terminal.*` frame below was recorded from the live WebSocket.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # component + view regressions and the full terminal directory suite
  pnpm --dir ui test src/components/terminal/
  # real-browser e2e lane: real PNG in the browser clipboard + trusted Ctrl+V
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts
  OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo pnpm tsgo:ui
  # real gateway + real Chrome paste proof: once on this patch, once with the two
  # source files reverted to origin/main and the Control UI rebuilt
  node <evidence-dir>/real-paste-proof/real-paste-proof.mjs --label after
  node <evidence-dir>/real-paste-proof/real-paste-proof.mjs --label before
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  pnpm --dir ui test src/components/terminal/: Test Files 13 passed (13), Tests 170 passed (170)
  ui-e2e terminal-upload.e2e.test.ts (real Chromium, real clipboard PNG + Ctrl+V): Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 3 passed (3)
  OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo pnpm tsgo:ui: exit 0

  real gateway + real Chrome, AFTER (this patch):
    terminal.open ok=true sessionKey=agent:main:main sessionId=66ea07f7-7bd3-48b2-883c-f568a739ba43
    copied to the browser clipboard: real PNG 64x64 (navigator.clipboard.write of a canvas-encoded image)
    trusted Ctrl+V on the shipped .tp-composer input ->
      terminal.upload ok=true params={"sessionId":"66ea07f7…","name":"image.png",
        "contentBase64":"<283 bytes png=true 64x64 sha256=a6dcd8219ff86df9e7e8a59174ac9c20d2e8ac1f13aa748cbec2d769e078becd>"}
      staged on the gateway host: /tmp/openclaw-terminal-upload-vTsPdm/image.png
        283 bytes, PNG magic 89504e470d0a1a0a, IHDR 64x64, sha256 a6dcd821…
      attachment chip rendered: "image.png"; composer draft preserved: "cat"
      terminal.input frames before Send: 0
    text-only Ctrl+V (negative control): terminal.upload 1 -> 1, input value "catplain-text-probe" (native path)
    Send clicked -> terminal.input "cat /tmp/openclaw-terminal-upload-vTsPdm/image.png" then terminal.input "\r"
    real PTY output after Send (prompt redacted):
      $ cat /tmp/openclaw-terminal-upload-vTsPdm/image.png
      <binary PNG dump: …PNG… IHDR … IDAT … IEND…>
    attachment chips after Send: 0

  real gateway + real Chrome, BEFORE (both source files reverted to origin/main, UI rebuilt):
    identical steps, identical clipboard contents ->
      terminal.upload observed=false; no .tp-attachment chip; composer draft unchanged ("cat")
      Send delivered only terminal.input "cat" + "\r" — the pasted image never reached the gateway
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Copying an image and pasting it into the embedded terminal composer of a live chat session stages the image through the real gateway (`terminal.upload` → a real file on the gateway host), renders an editable attachment chip, keeps the draft text, and sends nothing to the PTY until Send; Send then writes the quoted staged path followed by a separate carriage return, and the real shell `cat`s the staged PNG. Text-only pastes are untouched. On the pre-patch build the same keystrokes drop the image entirely.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** The real-gateway BEFORE run above (screenshots `before-04-after-ctrl-v-attachment-chip.png` vs `after-04-after-ctrl-v-attachment-chip.png` in the evidence dir), plus the earlier unit/view-level RED (`red-tests.log`: `Tests 3 failed | 26 passed (29)`, `upload.handlePaste is not a function`).
- **What was not tested:** The OS-native clipboard → browser handoff (a human copying from an OS application) is not drivable headlessly; the proof writes the PNG through the browser's own `navigator.clipboard.write` and pastes it with a trusted `Ctrl+V`, so the ClipboardEvent is built by the browser, not by the test. Chromium re-encodes clipboard images, so the staged payload is compared by PNG container + geometry (64x64) + sha256 rather than byte equality with the source file. The gateway ran with a loopback model provider so the chat session could materialize; the terminal lane never calls a model. macOS / Mac app clipboard behavior (no macOS host available); HEIC-only native WebKit delivery is a separate boundary (#165117 / #170362). Full CI lanes have not run for this PR: the workflow run is held in `action_required` awaiting maintainer approval, which is also why `openclaw/ci-gate` currently reports failure.
- **Proof tier:** L3 (shipped entry point: real gateway + real browser + real PTY, before/after)
- **Proof limitations:** OS-native clipboard handoff is out of headless reach; the model provider is a loopback stub used only to materialize the chat session.
- **Review state:** Addressed the clawsweeper review of `8e02718e95e` in commit `36b2aa96b8e`: removed the redundant pasted-image replay from `terminal-panel-handoff.test.ts`, replaced the synthesized `ClipboardEvent` with non-PNG bytes in the e2e by a real clipboard PNG pasted with a trusted `Ctrl+V`, and added the real-gateway before/after paste proof recorded above. The second blocker (approving the held CI workflow for the reviewed head) needs maintainer action.

prs.title: fix: wait for three conversations before showing the community invite
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
The first time someone opens the Control UI, the sidebar promotes the community before they have used a conversation. Freshly imported history or conversations used by someone else should not make a newcomer look active.

## User Impact
The invitation stays out of the sidebar until the signed-in person has sent messages in three distinct conversations. Three messages in one count once. No pop-up opens. Previously dismissed cards stay dismissed in that browser, and **Profile → Help → Discord** remains available without waiting. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made
Ownership and recent activity can both exist without the person sending a prompt. The Gateway now filters its existing prompting-participant records, including merged profile aliases. The sidebar requests one compact row and uses the Gateway's total before pagination; it neither fetches transcripts nor keeps a second participation counter. Cron, system, subagent and dock sessions are excluded. Missing or failed reads do not qualify a new visitor.

## Evidence
- Gateway filters and catalog-import integration: 37 tests passed on the final filter. A real import containing a question did not qualify the importer. Other-person-only, assignment, ownership, mentions, timestamps, and merged aliases were checked separately.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium + local synthetic inference: observed **0 → 1 → 2 → 3**, including three replies to prompts in the first conversation. prs.title: fix: a running Gateway stops cleanly after an update replaces its files
prs.body:
Related: #185730, #160674, #203185

## What Problem This Solves

When an update replaces OpenClaw's files while a Gateway is still running (a foreground Gateway, `update --no-restart`, or a manual npm install over a running Gateway), the old Gateway's shutdown still loaded several modules for the first time. Those files were already gone, so shutdown failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, cleanup was left unfinished, and the process sat for about 325 seconds until the hard-exit watchdog killed it. #203185 fixed two of these imports; this fixes the rest of the class and adds a guard so it cannot quietly come back.

## User Impact

A running Gateway whose installation was replaced in place now stops in about a second with a clean exit, instead of failing cleanup and waiting about five minutes for its watchdog. Restart intent, memory index cleanup, process cleanup and final log flushing finish normally. Gateways already running 2026.11.5 or 2026.11.6 still have the old code in memory, so this helps from the next in-place replacement of a release that contains it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node resolves each importer's first import of a module against the files on disk, even when the target module is already loaded elsewhere in the process. Loading a module somewhere else at startup therefore does not help; the importing call site itself has to resolve before the swap, or use a static import. Each late import now resolves where its owner starts work:

- The state worker's restart-intent and agent-lease cleanup handlers are static imports, because SIGTERM reads restart intent there and retiring agent databases can release leases during shutdown. Both join the PR wrapper inventory.
- memory-core closes index managers through a small manager-runtime loader module, which peeks the manager runtime it already loaded, instead of first-loading the runtime provider just to close nothing.
- The cron dispatch worker loads run finalization together with the scheduler or run queue that claims runs, so a run that finishes during shutdown can record its result.
- Plugin source capture roots start loading their temporary-artifact cleanup when acquired, not when released.
- The Gateway's process-broker close loads the process supervisor and read-only worker close functions when the broker starts.
- The shared-state broker's canonical-state close is loaded by the existing shutdown-runtime owner at Gateway startup, so one-shot CLI processes keep loading it only when they need it.
- Process supervisor warnings during host stop use a log loader that the shutdown-runtime owner starts at Gateway startup.
- The Gateway passes its already-loaded log flush to the final settled-exit step.

The ~325 s wait is the existing retained-cleanup contract (#191251, in 2026.11.5): when close fails and resources remain, the process waits for its hard-exit deadline instead of exiting early. 2026.11.6 appeared to exit in 1 s only because its CLI error path crashed on yet another missing chunk; once close succeeds, neither path is reached.

Rejected alternatives: preloading modules elsewhere in the process does not satisfy Node's per-importer resolution; eagerly priming the state-database cache when any broker is created changed one-shot CLI behavior (a regression test caught 143 unexpected worker messages); retaining the old release directory until exit belongs to install layout, not shutdown.

Accepted edge cases: other handlers that only ever run for the first time during shutdown may remain (the guard covers the idle Gateway's shutdown graph, with channels, providers and cron skipped). Workers started after SIGTERM (the hard-exit watchdog and log-file workers) and bare dependency imports resolve in the replacement tree by stable names, so they load rather than fail. The CLI error path's late `startup-maintenance` import after a failed Gateway run is left as is.

## Evidence

Live on Crabbox Linux (AWS, lease stopped): a foreground Gateway from a published-style package, every hashed dist chunk deleted under the running process, then SIGTERM:

| Build | Exit | Time to exit | `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `e695c13a939` | 137 (watchdog SIGKILL) | 327 s | 7 |
| this branch | 0 | 1 s | 0 |

A resolve-hook probe on the same Gateway (no deletion) listed modules first imported after SIGTERM. Base showed restart-lifecycle worker, memory-core runtime provider, process supervisor, state-database cache and the logger; this branch shows none from the shutdown graph.

New guard `test/scripts/gateway-shutdown-late-imports.built-cli.e2e.test.ts` runs the built Gateway with that probe, waits for startup maintenance to settle, stops it, and fails on any hashed dist chunk first imported after SIGTERM by a module loaded before it. On the box it passes on this branch (11.2 s) and fails on base with three late chunk imports. It is registered in the CI policy watch for the shutdown owners. The test is not deletion-based because deleting chunks would mutate the shared `dist` other tests read; the probe also sees late imports that an earlier failure would hide.

Focused tests pass: memory-core entry, manager, probe and race tests (new regression for closing without loading the runtime provider fails on base), state worker imports, agent execution cleanup, PR wrapper import closure, cron dispatch/scheduler workers, source capture, SQLite worker store, shutdown runtime, gateway run loop (179), one-shot exit, supervisor. `check:changed` passed (typecheck, type-aware lint, format, ratchets, dead-export scan).

Reviews: autoreview scoped-clean on the final head. Independent read-only Codex reviews across five passes found P2s that are all fixed here: the guard could mask cyclic late imports, supervisor warning paths, agent lease cleanup and cron finalization still first-imported handlers, the guard needed a Windows skip and a realistic stop budget, and the CI watch missed the memory loader files.

CI notes: `gateway-skill-authoring-plugin.e2e` and `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e` also fail locally with this branch's production files reverted to the base, so they are not caused by this change.

Production LOC: +109/−76 (net +33) across the shutdown owners. Tests +158/−3, CI watch and PR wrapper inventory +19.

prs.title: fix: resume the same provider sign-in after returning from the browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Returning from a provider’s browser sign-in should not send someone through login again. Reloading first-run Model Setup could open another provider tab; reopening Mac onboarding could replace the view that owned the attempt. A Mac sign-in that offered optional redirect paste could also stay on that prompt after the browser had finished.

## User Impact
Return to the same sign-in in the Control UI or Mac onboarding. A restored web page still offers a link if the original tab was lost. The Mac setup window can be minimized and brought forward without replacing a busy setup. Manual input remains available only when requested by the provider wizard.

## Why This Change Was Made
The clients read the original wizard session; focus does not start another login. The Mac observer reads without submitting an answer and hands a changed result back to the existing completion and model-verification path. The existing request/attempt identity and Gateway lease scope the result. There is no new credential store, activation mechanism, RPC or provider callback handler.

## Evidence
- Chromium: 3 end-to-end tests passed with a synthetic Gateway/provider page. The return regression opens one provider tab, switches focus, reloads the setup page, reads the same session ID without starting another login, then reaches the onboarding destination on the terminal result without a second activation.
- WebUI: 21 tests passed across the wizard runner and reconnect suites, including late replies after cancellation and after switching Gateways. Focused TypeScript lint and format passed.
- macOS: the app and native test bundle compiled. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint passed on the three changed production files. Native fixtures cover the normal callback, late replies after cancellation or a route change, and minimizing/reopening the same AppKit window.
- **Not verified:** native test execution and interactive Mac sign-in require a disposable macOS runner; no real provider account, callback URL or code was used for the browser proof. No full-repository typecheck or CI result is claimed. Independent local autoreview was stopped before a verdict because its preparation scanned the whole checkout, outside the requested validation scope.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): retain dismissed failures across cron pause
prs.body:
Closes #202652

## What Problem This Solves

Dismissing a failed automation in the Inbox, then pausing and enabling its schedule, brings the same failure back even though no new run occurred. This happens when the All agents inventory refresh treats the paused job's hidden row as a resolved failure.

## User Impact

A dismissed failure stays hidden across pause, enable, and page reload. A later failed run or automatic-disable incident still appears. Existing saved dismissals are retained; recovered or removed jobs stop retaining them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dismissal retention now follows the underlying failure instead of whether its row is currently visible. Failures are identified by their recorded run or automatic-disable time, and existing job-only dismissals are bound to the currently known failures. A row may represent both a failed run and an automatic-disable incident; dismissing it acknowledges both, so clearing one cause does not revive the other. Paused-job visibility and other Inbox categories are unchanged.

## Evidence

The actual built Control UI was exercised in Chromium through the repository's E2E harness with synthetic Gateway WebSocket responses. On the base revision, dismiss → pause → enable returned the old row and failed the assertion. With the fix, the old row stayed absent and a distinct later failure appeared. This verifies the UI boundary, not a live scheduler or provider.

Before: the same dismissed failure returns after enabling.

![Before: Archive check returns in the Inbox after pause and enable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b3fe9cd-d7f3-434d-9c77-e6185894ca21)

After: the same failure stays dismissed.

![After: the Inbox remains empty after enabling the same failed job](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9d1d592-cfc3-44e0-8a4f-8245a5268544)

Both captures use the same 1440×900 viewport, light theme, synthetic job and All agents scope. Before is `dc73ec0bac`; after is this patch. No layout or styling change.

The permanent store regression covers persistence across a paused reload, a later failure, recovery, removal, and legacy job-only dismissals. Additional regressions reproduced automatic-disable transitions, failed and successful manual runs, and legacy history without a run timestamp. The repair retains each present failure independently so enabling or manual recovery does not revive an acknowledged incident.

<details>
<summary>Validation details</summary>

- Base regression: two expected failures because pausing removed the saved dismissal.
- Final related suites: 4 files, 61 tests passed.
- Changed store suite: 41 tests passed, 2.40 s Vitest duration / 5.52 s command wall time with one worker. Net test growth: 124 lines. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Browser base: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 1`, expected 0; exit 1.
- Browser fix: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 0`, `Distinct failed run after pause/enable: 1`; exit 0. [New failure screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/179b166c-a974-41f4-84b2-904f52002d17).
- Changed checks, UI production/component test types, lint, format, controller guard, test-line budget and diff checks passed. The three dead-export scans passed with zero entries and were reused on the final changed-check rerun. Earlier line-cap and test-table typing failures were corrected without dropping coverage.
- Independent local review was completed after correcting its automatic-disable findings.

Focused suite command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-store.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-items.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-cron-events.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

## Upgrade from v2026.11.6

The published `openclaw@2026.11.6` Control UI and the bundle built from `c53c398db97f` ran at the same origin in the same Chromium context. The release tarball matched the registry SHA-1 `1399d4ec476c2bb47ceb5e1c70d8aa6c89f22cfc`. Both used synthetic Gateway responses for the same account and job.

In the release UI, dismissing **Archive check** from the Automations tab wrote the original browser record. Reloading with the PR bundle migrated that record. Pausing the job and reloading the page retained the dismissal. Enabling it kept the old failure hidden, and advancing the failed-run time by one minute produced one visible row. The browser test also compared the saved theme, theme mode, sidebar agent mode, and current Gateway selection before and after the upgrade.

```text
old release browser dismissal [ 'archive-check' ]
upgraded dismissal [ 'archive-check@1795197600000' ]
paused reload retained dismissal
Same failed run after pause/enable: 0
preserved named settings: [ 'theme', 'themeMode', 'sidebarAgentsMode' ]
Distinct failed run after pause/enable: 1
Tests  1 passed (1)
```

In the macOS Dashboard, Plugins reserves space for the titlebar even though its scrollable area already starts below it. That pushes the content down, and the scrollbar can touch the rounded workspace edge.

## User Impact

The Plugins heading starts closer to the titlebar and the scrollbar clears the corner. The Dashboard’s visible chrome is 4 px shallower without moving the native window controls or resizing the AppKit toolbar.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell now reserves the titlebar space once and shares the painted edge with the rail, Chat pane, and window drag region. The scrollbar track starts below the workspace radius. The existing header rules preserve the native control centerline without duplicating the Mac selectors.

prs.title: fix: stop old question cards and system notices showing after a chat reset
prs.body:
Root cause: ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-build.ts:500 (and the question summaries at :577) draws the browser-only observer notices and answered question summaries by timestamp, without checking the reset divider the same build emits at :262. So after `/reset` they stay in the chat above "Session reset" until you reload.

Fixes #203215

Thanks @NovaeonStudio for the clear report.

## What Problem This Solves

If you type `/reset` in a Control UI chat, the conversation is cleared and a "Session reset" divider appears. But answered `ask_user` question cards and "Session observer assessments stopped" notices from before the reset stay visible above the divider until you reload the page.

## User Impact

After a reset, the chat shows only what happened after it. Questions and notices that come after the reset still show, and other sessions are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Those question cards and notices are kept only in the browser and are placed in the chat by time. The transcript already marks where a reset happened. The chat view now leaves out any of these browser-only rows that are older than the latest reset divider. Because it keys off the divider and not one particular history response, a question asked after the reset (even one that arrives while history is still reloading) is never hidden.

Size: Control UI gzip +39 B, all in `control-ui-boot-chat-styles` (the only chunk whose code changed once hashes are ignored). Production +10/−4 lines, tests +73 (one regression).

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway, built Control UI, and Chromium, with a scripted model that runs commands and then asks one `ask_user` question, plus a utility model that always fails so the observer notice appears. Base 2c473901162a against this branch:

| Step | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| A after `/reset`, same tab | old question card and observer notice above the divider | only the divider, `/reset`, and the reply |
| New question in A after the reset, same tab | n/a | question card and notice shown below the divider |
| Session B, same tab | its question and notice shown | its question and notice shown |
| A after reload | clean | clean |

Regression test `chat-pane-retired-event.test.ts` mounts a real pane. It sends a question and a notice, then refreshes history so the cursor read returns `kind: "reset"` and a full transcript that starts with a reset marker. It checks that both old rows are gone and that a question asked after the reset shows. It fails on base (`expected [ 'notice', 'before-reset' ] to deeply equal []`) and passes here.

Screenshots (before/after) and the observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203288#issuecomment-7068707855

**Merge danger:** two-way door. This changes display only and writes no state, so a revert fully undoes it. If it's wrong, the worst case is a Control UI chat hiding a question card or notice that should show after a reset.

prs.title: fix: keep your place while reading Activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an older session received a live update, Activity moved it to the top—even if you were reading it. The row could jump completely out of view.

## User Impact

You can scroll through older sessions without losing your place. Titles, status, and recaps still update. When you return to the top and stop scrolling, the latest sessions appear automatically. There is no refresh button.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activity holds the displayed row order and day groups while you read, not the underlying data. Returning briefly to the top and reversing direction does not reshuffle the list. Once scrolling settles at the top, the feed resumes its newest-first order using the existing list animation, which respects reduced motion. Changing filters starts a fresh list.

## Evidence

[Before and after: the same live update at phone width](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201448#issuecomment-6991169321)

In production-bundled Chromium with synthetic Gateway updates, the reading row moved 881 CSS pixels on desktop and 922 on an emulated phone before the fix. On both layouts it now moves less than 1 pixel in the same scenario. The tests also cover recap growth above the reader, new arrivals, reversing at the top, automatic catch-up, and a filter that introduces a previously unseen session. The 28 existing Activity view tests and UI typecheck passed. Independent re-review found no remaining P0–P2 issues after a filter-scope correction. Not tested on a physical phone or against a live Gateway.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bdd83cdc-a237-4dad-b47d-cc0eca0d9a96)
