prs.title: feat(update): run every Git install from releases and delete the in-place Git runner
prs.body:
Slice 4b of the update foundation. Follows #199706 (slice 4), #201917 (releases outside `node_modules`) and #201538 (half-switched Git updates).

## Problem

Since #199706, POSIX Git checkouts with a Gateway service update through releases: a detached worktree at `<state>/git-install/releases/<id>/openclaw`, behind the link `<state>/git-install/openclaw`, started by a launcher that switches back after two failed starts. Three cases still used the in-place Git runner, which rewrites the checkout the Gateway runs from:

- Windows checkouts;
- package-to-Git switches;
- checkouts with no Gateway service.

That runner is RC1 of the update RCA: in-place replacement at a path running processes use. Keeping it meant keeping its rollback, retention, pack transfer, staging and handoff code.

## Change

Every Git install now updates through releases. The in-place Git runner and its command-side rollback are deleted on every platform in one cutover. `openclaw update` no longer moves the checkout `HEAD` or rebuilds its `dist`. (`scripts/update-gateway.sh`, a separate maintainer script, still rebuilds a checkout in place; it is unchanged.)

- **Windows:**
  - The release link is an NTFS junction, which needs no administrator rights. It is owned by the existing `package-release-slot*` code; the win32 exclusions there and in the release lease are removed.
  - Windows cannot rename onto a junction, so a switch removes the old junction and then renames.
  - The Windows task supervisor starts its Gateway child through the release launcher, so the child's starts count toward the trial.
- **Package-to-Git:**
  - The checkout is cloned and the target is built as the release on trial. Its fallback is the npm package that was serving, kept intact: if the Git build fails to start twice, the launcher switches the link back to the package, and the Gateway and `openclaw` on PATH run the npm build again with no manual step. A deferred (`--no-restart`) switch keeps the same fallback. The package counts as this install's only while its `openclaw.mjs` is exactly this install's forwarding entry; retention never touches it.
  - The global npm package's `openclaw.mjs` is rewritten once to import the release launcher, so the existing npm bin shims run the release. Without that, `openclaw` on PATH would keep running the old npm build, whose updater treats the install as npm.
  - The rejected alternative, re-pointing the npm package path at the release, would name the release through `node_modules/openclaw` again, the cause of #201874.
  - Installs whose switch was done by an older updater have the npm package path linked to the checkout, which releases never rebuild. A Git release update replaces that link (only a link to the checkout) with a directory holding `openclaw.mjs` and `dist/index.js`, both starting the launcher; the second keeps a service definition that names the package path working after a `--no-restart` update. Without this, the CLI and its updater stayed on the version the switch built (found by the package-to-Git upgrade lane).
- **No service:** a checkout run by hand updates through a release too. The next `openclaw gateway` runs it.
- **CLI on PATH:** after a Git release update, the installer's `openclaw` wrapper (POSIX and Windows) is rewritten once to run the release launcher, and a global npm, pnpm (`pnpm add -g openclaw@link:`) or Bun (`bun link`) link to the checkout is replaced the same way as the npm link above. The launcher selects a `--no-restart` release on the next Gateway run and counts `openclaw gateway` / `openclaw gateway run` as trial starts; other commands (`gateway status`, `--version`) never count.
- **Service definition:** `serviceUsesUpdatedRoot` reads the service definition, not the running process. A `--no-restart` Git release update whose service still starts the checkout writes a definition that starts the launcher without starting or restarting the Gateway (`stage`; systemd reloads unit metadata only). Every OpenClaw restart route on macOS (`openclaw gateway restart` and the Gateway's own restart) re-bootstraps the job when the loaded command is known to differ from the plist on disk; otherwise it kickstarts. Only a failed write leaves an owed `service-definition` step.
- **Conversion stop:** a Git update stops a Gateway whose service does not yet name the launcher before the release activates, so the existing install rebinds it. A Dashboard update on macOS runs inside the Gateway's LaunchAgent, which cannot rewrite itself while loaded; without the stop, the update reported success, the Gateway kept the old checkout and the result asked for `openclaw gateway install --force`. This replaces `main`'s macOS in-place fallback (247b9581), whose runner this PR deletes. An update the previous definition does not start is reported as pending, not succeeded. Services that already name the launcher still switch without a stop.
- **Restart:** the converted service restarts once, not twice. Git release updates no longer warn to restart a live Gateway by hand: a release replaces no root the Gateway uses.
- **No manual steps (Ayaan, 2026-11-20):**
  - Releases built under `lib/node_modules` by `7db69bedeab6`-era updaters (#201874): bundled plugin public surfaces there load the built `dist/extensions/<plugin>/` JavaScript, so those installs update by themselves; the manual bridge in the #201874 comment is no longer needed.
  - A killed npm link swap leaves the link under npm's backup name; the next Git update restores it and retries.
  - The launcher finishes a Windows link switch killed between removing the old junction and renaming the new one.
  - npm -> Git -> npm: destination ownership recognizes this install's exact forwarding `openclaw.mjs`, so switching back is admitted.

## Impact

- One update path for Git installs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- `openclaw` on PATH runs the current release after an update.
- **Accepted edge cases:**
  - Two checkouts that share one state directory share its single release install.
  - After a package-to-Git switch, the old npm package keeps its disk space until a switch back to npm replaces it.
  - A Gateway run for another profile through the default `openclaw` on PATH counts toward the default install's trial (accepted by Ayaan, 2026-11-20).
  - `--no-restart` selects the new release at the next start without the two-start switch-back.
  - A checkout installed at `<state>/git-install/openclaw` (the release link path; the installer default is `~/openclaw`) is left in place, and every update fails visibly with nothing changed, naming the fix: move the checkout or reinstall with another `--git-dir` (accepted by Ayaan, 2026-11-21).
  - The first update of an install whose service still names the checkout has a one-time outage while the Gateway stops and the LaunchAgent or unit is rebound (26 s on the macOS Dashboard run).
  - If a macOS release's `launchctl print` omits the job's arguments, a definition staged by `--no-restart` applies at the next login or update instead of the next restart.
  - Unchanged follow-up: when local commits conflict with every newer commit, the preflight reports `already-current` instead of naming the conflict. This predates the PR and gets its own PR.

## Size

Against the merge base, 32 commits:

- Production code: +821 / −2,166 (56 files).
- Tests: +1,391 / −8,893 (74 files). Cut tests covered steps a Git release no longer takes (checkout rollback, in-place staging, service stop before checkout); each is listed in the contract.
- Upgrade-survivor scenario: +836 / −104 (4 files): baselines `v2026.11.5`, `7db69bedeab6`, `main`; package-to-Git; no service; SIGKILL at stage, build, publish, link switch and launcher restore.
- Docs: +132 / −104.

## Evidence

Final head `99ecf23e04e8`. Each row names the head its end-to-end proof ran on; later commits change tests, the e2e helper's lint, the restart warning text, the macOS reload probe's unknown case, the npm/pnpm/Bun link lookup and the deferred-switch staging (unit-proven, red on base).

| Invariant | Result | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Release built where it serves; no `node_modules` in the link or realpath | Pass | Linux upgrade-survivor lanes; macOS launchd (isolated profile on a maintainer Mac); hosted Crabbox Windows Server 2025 |
| Gateway serves the new release and `tools.invoke web_search` works after every update | Pass | every hop on all three OSes |
| SIGKILL at stage, build, publish, link switch, launcher restore leaves a serving install | Pass | Linux kill-point lane (`8f63330`) |
| Two failed starts switch back and restore `.pre-` state | Pass | Linux lanes; macOS `8f63330` (`failed to start twice; switched back`); Windows `9cbc4b5`, automatic through the Scheduled Task, 67.5 s outage. Older-supervisor and pending cases: unit tests red on base (`6003675`, `75e7bd5`) |
| The release updates itself | Pass | Linux; macOS `8f63330`; Windows `9cbc4b5` |
| The checkout is never written (HEAD, status) | Pass | every lane and OS run |
| Every shipped layout reaches releases with no manual step | Pass | `v2026.11.5`, merge-base `main` (`8f63330`); `7db69bedeab6` (`6003675`) |
| npm → Git switch; `openclaw` on PATH runs the release | Pass | Linux `75e7bd5` |
| No service: the next `openclaw gateway` runs the release | Pass | Linux `8f63330` |
| `--no-restart` keeps the Gateway up; the next restart runs the release | Pass | macOS `8f63330`: 0 s outage, `gateway restart` reloads launchd arguments |
| macOS Dashboard update (`update.run`) on a LaunchAgent that names the checkout, twice, then a terminal update | Pass | `80d9587`, isolated profile on a maintainer Mac: each update served its new commit, launchd runs `openclaw-launcher.mjs`, `web_search` passed, checkout unchanged, no manual step needed. Red on `3c14869` (Gateway kept the checkout, manual install step) |
| Linux `7db69bedeab6` → head and npm → Git | Pass | `80d9587` |
| Windows junction; a release held open is retained, then collected | Pass | hosted Crabbox (Windows Server 2025) |
| Windows without admin rights | Not run | S4U Limited stays admin on the Crabbox image |

## What Problem This Solves

Personal sections give a conversation a second place in the sidebar without changing its shared group. This retires that extra layer of organization.

## User Impact

**Add to section** is gone from the session menu, and **New section** is gone from **Filter & sort**. Existing personal section headings disappear. Conversations stay in their original groups and remain accessible under the usual filters. Pins, rail shortcuts, shared groups, and child conversations are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI no longer renders, looks up, edits, or syncs personal sections, including edits queued before the upgrade. It does not turn old sections into pins or shared groups, delete conversations, or change the Gateway’s history-retention protection for existing references.

## Evidence

In the same Chromium fixture, **Release notes** appeared under both **This week** and **Engineering** before the change, and only under **Engineering** afterward. **Ship checklist** stayed pinned. prs.title: fix: publish a valid gateway hostname for long hostnames
prs.body:
Closes #202665

## What Problem This Solves

When a machine's hostname is longer than 63 characters, OpenClaw truncates it for the wide-area DNS-SD zone. The truncation can leave a trailing `-`, so the advertised SRV target (and its `A` owner) is not a valid hostname, violating the LDH rule the module already enforces for configured domains.

## User Impact

The gateway now advertises a well-formed hostname, so clients that validate the SRV target as a hostname (TLS/SNI, strict HTTP clients) are not handed an invalid name.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dnsLabel()` stripped leading and trailing hyphens before truncating to the 63-character limit, so truncation could re-expose a trailing `-`. The label is now re-trimmed after truncation.

## Evidence

**Launched Gateway (shipped entry point), not a test harness.** I built this head with `scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup` and ran:

```
node dist/index.js gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `discovery.wideArea.domain = openclaw.internal`, and a `--require` preload that sets `os.hostname()` to a 68-character name (`aaa…a-bbbbb`) and reports a Tailscale IPv4 interface. The Gateway logged:

```
[discovery] wide-area DNS-SD updated (openclaw.internal. → …\dns\openclaw.internal.db)
```

and wrote this zone (truncated host label is `aaa…a`, 62 chars, no trailing hyphen):

```
$ORIGIN openclaw.internal.
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa IN A 100.64.0.1
_openclaw-gw._tcp IN PTR aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp IN SRV 0 0 18789 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

I served that exact file with CoreDNS 1.15.0 and resolved it with a real DNS client:

```
PTR ["aaa…a._openclaw-gw._tcp.openclaw.internal"]
SRV [{"name":"aaa…a.openclaw.internal","port":18789,"priority":0,"weight":0,"type":"SRV"}]
A   ["100.64.0.1"]
```

Base comparison: the same 68-character hostname through `startGatewayDiscovery()` on `HEAD~1` (a base `dist` build was not available on this host) publishes `aaa…a-` (63 chars, trailing hyphen) as the SRV target and `A` owner — not a valid hostname.

Scope note: CoreDNS also serves the trailing-hyphen label from the base zone (DNS wire format allows any octet in a label), so this is not a hard resolution failure. The defect is that OpenClaw advertises a name that is not a valid hostname.

- Red on base, green on head: `keeps truncated host labels as valid DNS hostnames` in `src/infra/widearea-dns.test.ts` asserts the SRV target matches `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` and that its `A` record exists (selected via the SRV target, not the `ns1` nameserver record). Full file: `10 passed | 1 skipped`.
- `oxlint` on both changed files exits 0; formatter check is clean.

Known environment limitation, unrelated: `src/infra/widearea-dns.boundary.test.ts` fails on this Windows host with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename …` inside `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s atomic replacement. I reproduced the same failure against the base source with this change reverted.

Not run here: full `pnpm check` / repo-wide typecheck. Required CI workflows on this external PR are waiting on maintainer approval, which I cannot grant.

This change was AI-assisted and verified against the evidence above.

prs.title: improve: offer a name for an added provider account
prs.body:
Related: #202626

## What Problem This Solves

When you connect another account for the same provider, the saved profiles can show identical emails. The account list leaves you to recognize an opaque ID or check usage to tell work from personal. Reconnecting a previously named account can also drop its name.

## User Impact

User impact: an interactive CLI sign-in or Models sign-in offers an optional name after saving another account. Press Enter to keep the prefilled label. Chat `/login` still signs in without prompting, and reconnecting a recognized account keeps its saved name, including `--force`. If a name cannot be saved, the sign-in stays connected and Models or the Gateway-backed CLI shows what happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt surfaces opt in to optional text; the chat adapter does not. Credential persistence completes before the question, so dismissing the name or failing to write it cannot undo the sign-in. A custom name uses the existing profile `displayName`: config-authored names keep precedence, and saving a label does not create an auth-order declaration. The suggestion uses an existing provider-supplied name or email when available. If neither exists, the provider label is suggested and is saved when accepted. Subscription tiers are not assumed to be workspace names.

## Evidence

**Main integration (`72a8d6a99174`):** After #202626 landed, this branch incorporated `main`, including the #202795 Plugins asset-budget fix. The merge keeps the shared-store reconnect matcher authoritative for saved names; a different API key or token or an unresolved secret reference does not inherit an existing name. The original visual flow is unchanged. All 130 focused shared login, auth naming, wizard, and Models runner tests passed on the integrated tree; targeted typed lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent full-diff local Codex review through P2 found no actionable findings. Fresh hosted CI is still required on this head.

On unpatched main (`31ce94f0a`), seven new account-name cases failed at the absent prompt or lost name; the first-account and chat controls passed. With the change all ten pass against the real isolated auth store, including the additional review regression for a provider that supplies no name or email. The hosted CLI prompt-error case also fails before its fix and passes after. Shared auth, reconnect, chat-adapter, and WizardSession/Clack checks pass. Focused TypeScript, lint, format, diff check, and a bounded local runtime build pass.

The real CLI in a PTY and the real Models UI through an isolated Gateway use a synthetic local provider, not real OpenAI credentials. The CLI saved both profiles and one Enter kept the default. Models submitted **Work** with Enter and read back both saved profiles, with **Personal** unchanged. The screenshots show the same added-account interaction before and after. The production UI build completed, and the report-only budget check still flags limits that were already exceeded before the UI change. No budget was changed.

A real Models regression reproduced a stale name form after clicking **X**. With the fix, that click reaches the sign-in confirmation without another input, and both accounts remain saved with the new one unnamed. The narrow UI regression also fails before the fix; the runner, Models, and login-dialog suites pass afterward.

After repairing the draft ancestry onto `c1f70d3b7`, all 14 authored files matched the tested patch byte-for-byte. The affected core and UI suites were rerun on that base: 68 tests passed.

Independent excerpt review identified the missing fallback-label save and Models dismissal problems; both were fixed and reverified. The full diff was self-reviewed. The packaged Auto Review executable was unavailable in this worktree, so no completed Auto Review report is claimed.

[Follow-up review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048414949) found that replacing the account in an explicit `--profile-id` slot could inherit the old account’s name. Matching reconnects now keep the name; a replacement does not, and gets the optional offer when another account exists. The replacement case failed before that fix; all 55 tests in the three affected auth suites now pass, including explicit same-account reconnect. Focused typecheck, lint, format, and the CI mock-export ratchet also pass.

### OAuth accounts without a provider matcher

The [maintainer follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f4153f88310ff6f004f34b2daa66531114c02760) keeps the provider matcher authoritative. Without a matcher, a reused OAuth slot keeps the saved name only when the provider-supplied account ID and OAuth registration match. A different or unknown account can be named without inheriting the old label. Credential writes, profile selection, config-authored labels, and API key/token behavior are unchanged.

Both regression cases failed against `66e6da85`: the naming prompt was skipped for a different account and when no account ID was available. After the fix, both cases and the same-account control passed; 61 tests passed across three focused auth suites. The naming suite took 33.34s locally; CI timing on the follow-up is pending. Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local Auto Review found no P2-or-higher issues in the follow-up diff. Tests used synthetic credentials, not a live xAI sign-in.

### Failed name saves are visible and nonfatal

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048687460) found that a name-write failure only reached the Gateway log. The saved sign-in now sends an optional plain note through the existing wizard channel. Models displays it rather than silently acknowledging it; the Gateway-backed CLI prints it. The note says the account is connected, explains that the name was not saved, and shows where to set a display name in configuration. Dismissing it still retrieves the successful sign-in receipt. No Gateway protocol change.

Three real-store cases reproduced missed or rejected name writes with no client notice; one Models runner case reproduced the hidden notice and one reproduced the stale cancellation receipt. All are green with the repair. The seven affected test files pass 160 tests, including the Gateway CLI reader and wizard cancellation logic; core/UI typecheck, lint, format, mock-export ratchet and diff check pass. The real Models before/after below runs a loopback Gateway and Chromium with synthetic credentials and injects a null name-write result only. Before, Models went straight to confirmation. After, the warning is visible; clicking **X** still finishes sign-in, and read-back confirms both accounts remain saved and the new account has no custom name.

### Latest-stable existing-state upgrade

Built and ran latest stable `2026.11.6` from the exact source tag `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d3272`) with frozen dependencies. Used an isolated profile and synthetic OAuth fixture only. Seeded and read the state using the stable CLI, then ran the candidate’s supported `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check` on the same isolated state (exit 0). Before any post-upgrade sign-in, all of these matched the stable readback:

| State | Stable and immediately after upgrade |
| --- | --- |
| Profile IDs | `example-upgrade-proof:personal`, `example-upgrade-proof:work` |
| Saved names and effective labels | Personal → Personal; Work → Office override (configured) |
| Saved auth order and first profile | Work → Personal; Work first |
| Resolved selected model | `example-upgrade-proof/example-v1` |

A real CLI sign-in then saved **Travel** as a third account without changing either existing profile or selected model. Reconnecting **Work** did not prompt for a name, refreshed that same profile ID, and kept both the saved **Work** label and the **Office override** config preference. Normal sign-in promotion changed first-profile order only after those new sign-ins. No live credentials, external provider endpoints, or inference were used; no naming migration was added.

### Required CI background

The reviewed-head [compaction job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514993232) failed `compact.queued-successor.test.ts:781` (during branch read: expected false to be true). A separate unmodified checkout of the published base `c1f70d3b7` reproduced that exact failure (18 pass, one fail). The [UI E2E job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514992833) failed the same plugin and skills readiness selectors and skill-settings request budget (33 > 31) that a local base replay reproduced without the PR’s UI change. These broader checks are not waived or fixed here.

### Models: failed account-name save

**Before**

![Models confirms sign-in without showing the unsaved name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f2a5099-38b1-49c4-b76b-5fb413167d64)

**After**

![Models explains the name was not saved while the account remains connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88dc74bd-e151-4b37-8231-adba6c7d143d)

### CLI: adding a second account

**Before**

![CLI: sign-in saves the account without a name offer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1ee446-cd8c-4422-8493-6e76abef1e69)

**After**

![CLI: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a36c4cb-22fc-4df8-b779-de8d4d22f5b6)

### Models: adding a second account

#### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Models: the saved sign-in goes straight to confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69ee5150-d068-4f26-a327-526f1cad6d46)

**After**

![Models: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8d92a88-cef3-4f54-9ddc-c0851ce87c16)

#### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Models before: highlighted sign-in confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fce90167-fda2-4555-86cd-9ff7c5fac3de)

**After**

![Models after: highlighted name field that accepts Enter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5028fe10-f765-410c-945c-93468e2dcdfe)

Report, starting patch, and design requirements supplied by Vítor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/56f989b2-27a6-40b1-b1c0-7620a6f39e55)

prs.title: fix(crabbox): avoid extra runtime loading during version checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Checking a supported Crabbox executable eagerly loads the command error-formatting runtime and its dependency graph even when there is no error to format.

## User Impact

Successful binary discovery avoids that unnecessary load. Binary selection, fallback notices, redaction and cancellation behavior stay the same. This change makes no RSS or latency savings claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The version probe now imports the existing error formatter only when its runner throws. Cancellation is checked both before and after that import, so an abort still wins over an indeterminate probe result. The added await justifies the second cancellation check; no new formatter, cache, SDK surface or configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

Validated base `1d9252c3770e96372192b650601583134617296e` against signed head `783960a6cc3c962453c68e778387fd6ffd183526` (tree `1e606a2019932fad6771cab24230771cdf31bc8d`). Production delta: **+2 lines**; isolated regression: **90 test lines**.

- **Node 24.22.1 and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork:** all 103 tests in the managed-binary, new import-boundary, provider-binary and command suites pass on each runtime. The three cold-path tests fail against the original owner on both runtimes; the two held-import cases are intentionally excluded from that baseline control.
- **Targeted checks:** owner/test lint and types, mock-export validation, formatting and diff checks pass.
- **Normal full builds:** baseline and candidate `pnpm build` pass with declarations enabled. The candidate rebuilt runtime output and declarations; normal content caches were allowed. Build durations are not performance evidence.
- **Independent local review:** local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout was dirty; the prescribed autoreview fallback completed one P0–P2 pass on the committed range above with no findings. That review is source-only. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44946274868) passed. Hosted ClawSweeper acknowledged pickup; no substantive review was posted before merge.

The acceptance rule was recorded before execution: fresh supported/returned-failure/early-abort source cases must not evaluate the command module; a thrown runner must load it; cancellation during held evaluation must reject with the exact reason without calling the formatter. The compiled public CLI success case must remove the rendered error owner while the thrown-error control must retain it and preserve the redacted fallback result. All conditions passed.

Fresh Node processes exercised the compiled public CLI facade through its existing injected command runner. The existing main-module census and compiler-owned rendered-source metadata bind the exercised entry and owner chunks; capture acknowledgements and all four child exits were successful.

| Compiled case | Error-owner chunks loaded, base → head | Parsed `dist` modules, base → head | Parsed `dist` source bytes, base → head |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Supported binary | 1 → 0 | 926 → 224 | 6,922,699 → 1,221,570 |
| Thrown runner with fallback | 1 → 1 | 926 → 928 | 6,922,699 → 6,923,195 |

The thrown path adds two chunks and 496 parsed source bytes at the lazy boundary. Its result is byte-for-byte equivalent after JSON serialization, including the canonical redacted notice. These are parsed-module counts/source sizes, not retained-memory measurements or proof that every logging module disappeared. The injected runner keeps this an import/selection boundary test, not a live provider test.

An initial TS6059 failure was confined to the temporary typecheck harness's `rootDir`; correcting it and verifying unchanged source, dependencies and build output allowed the remaining checks to pass without repeating completed proof.

The baseline build reported nonfatal existing Control UI CSS budget advisories; the candidate reused the unchanged UI content cache. This PR changes no UI inputs.


Merged as `20ef309ec843db5914a4f5d657bba7ae82510b35`; both landed file blobs match the tested head above.

prs.title: fix(onboard): reject --secret-input-mode ref when the provider API key flag differs from the env var
prs.body:
AI-assisted: yes

Closes #201401

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --secret-input-mode ref` with a provider API key flag (for example `--anthropic-api-key`) while the provider's environment variable holds a *different* value would silently end up with a reference to the stale environment variable; the explicitly passed key was discarded with no warning, and onboarding reported success.
- **Related:** #201401; the Gateway credential flags already reject this exact mismatch (`src/commands/onboard.ts`), so provider flags now follow the same contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** When `--secret-input-mode ref` is used and both the provider flag and its env var are set to different values, onboarding now fails with the same error shape the Gateway credential flags use, instead of silently keeping the env value. Matching values, env-only, and flag-only (plaintext) flows are unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to reference serialization, plaintext flag precedence, or the Gateway credential checks themselves.
- **Highest-risk area:** The shared non-interactive resolver used by provider methods, custom-provider onboarding, and reset validation.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The comparison is added only to the existing ref-mode branch, after the existing malformed-input check (preserving the current malformed-input error precedence), and both values are normalized the same way as today. The error message contains neither value.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=A openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key B` (A ≠ B) now exits 1 with `--anthropic-api-key does not match ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Set the environment variable to the same value or omit the flag.` and persists no credentials; when A = B the env reference is stored exactly as before.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.ts` (single comparison in the ref-mode branch) and the new regression tests in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.test.ts` (`stores the env reference when a ref-mode flag matches the env var`, `rejects a ref-mode flag that differs from the provider env var without leaking either value`).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree of this PR branch, shipped CLI entry point (`node scripts/run-node.mjs`) with local runtime build; plus a released-stable install (`openclaw@2026.11.6`, `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`) for the upgrade run. `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` pointed at temp dirs; synthetic (non-secret) key values.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # mismatch case (should now fail, before it silently stored the env reference)
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-stale-env-key \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk \
    --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-rotated-flag-key
  # matching case (should keep working, with --skip-health)
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-same-key \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-same-key
  # regression tests
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/api-keys.test.ts

- **Regression test red on base → green on head (recorded):**
  - **RED** (base `0a399569bae`, fix reverted, new tests present): `rejects a ref-mode flag that differs from the provider env var without leaking either value` fails — the resolver returns `{ key: "stale-env-key-should-not-leak", source: "env", envVarName: "CUSTOM_API_KEY" }` instead of rejecting (`AssertionError: expected { …(3) } to be null`). `1 failed | 13 passed`.
  - **GREEN** (head `101d96db8b9`): `14/14 passed`, including both new regression tests.
- **Existing-install upgrade run (latest-stable → head):**
  - Onboarded with the released stable `openclaw@2026.11.6` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-existing-ref-key … --secret-input-mode ref --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-existing-ref-key` → exit 0. Credential profile `anthropic:default` stored as `keyRef: {"source":"env","provider":"default","id":"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"}` (no key material persisted — only the env reference); settings written to `openclaw.json`.
  - Pre-upgrade snapshot: `sha256(openclaw.json)=2372378dd0d4…`, `sha256(openclaw-agent.sqlite)=737a1d5c2164…`.
  - Upgraded to this PR's head and re-ran onboarding against the same state dir:
    - matching re-onboard → exit 0; credential SQLite **byte-identical** (sha256 unchanged); keyRef unchanged.
    - mismatching re-onboard (`--anthropic-api-key sk-ant-rotated-flag-key` vs env) → exit 1 with the new rejection, neither value leaked; credential SQLite still **byte-identical**.
  - Settings diff after upgrade: only non-destructive changes — `meta.migrations` gained `skillWorkshopPlugin`/`skillLibraryToolSplit`, and `lastTouchedVersion`/`lastRunVersion`/`lastRunAt` version/timestamp fields advanced. Workspace, agent identity, model config, auth profile, and gateway config unchanged.
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-stale-env-key ... --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-rotated-flag-key
  → exit 1
  --anthropic-api-key does not match ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Set the environment variable to the same value or omit the flag.
  (no credential profile persisted; neither key value appears in the output)

Unit suite `api-keys.test.ts` 14/14 green via validate.sh (oxfmt + oxlint + tsgo:core). prs.title: fix: resume project sessions after background commands exit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A project-backed chat can get stuck waiting after its background command finishes. The completion reaches the right session, but the Gateway rejects the follow-up with `Session changed while preparing its project; retry the task.`

## User Impact

A background command's completion can resume the same chat without the user having to prompt it again. No configuration changes or migrations are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detached session-event callbacks can inherit a workspace-readiness guard bound to the original turn. That guard correctly rejects work from the retired turn, but must not be used for admission of a new turn. Clear the inherited guard at the detached admission boundary, alongside the existing context resets. The original guard, operator authority, destination checks, and cancellation behavior remain intact.

## Evidence

- A regression using a real background child process reproduces the admission rejection on the base and passes with the fix. It verifies the completion reaches the current session after rotation and that the retired turn's guard still rejects.
- 50 focused tests passed across exec follow-up, session-event handoff, and Gateway workspace readiness. Targeted lint, typecheck, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- The isolated Gateway check used a synthetic provider. A real-model end-to-end replay is pending; this PR is a draft.

prs.title: feat: generate PixVerse image videos through ClawRouter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter can advertise a PixVerse image-input route, but OpenClaw cannot currently select it through video generation. Falling through to another provider after an uncertain paid submission could also create a second video.

## User Impact

Users whose selected ClawRouter key grants the exact input profile can generate image-to-video with `clawrouter/pixverse/v6` or `clawrouter/pixverse/c1`. One local PNG, JPEG, or WebP image is submitted through the Router. Direct PixVerse behavior and ordinary pre-submit fallback stay unchanged.

The Router route must actually be enabled and present in the selected key's fresh catalog. This client change does not activate it. Shipping SDK-to-Worker/SQLite composition remains a separate qualification step. The current video request API has no caller signal; this PR does not claim caller-abort or pre-header disconnect propagation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new registration admits only `clawrouter.pixverse-image-input.v1` with matching offer/endpoint metadata, native image-video formats, and the two supported models. It snapshots at most 8 MiB of image bytes plus 32 KiB of multipart framing and scalar controls. Caller image IDs, URLs, receipts, and grants are rejected.

The Router owns upstream upload/create and its separate fixed upload/generation policies. The client sends one composed POST with an operation-owned idempotency key, then polls only the original video ID with the original selected Router key. Returned media URLs remain opaque.

A narrow SDK helper reuses the existing terminal-failure registry. Once create invocation begins, escaping response, polling, asset-validation, deadline, and cleanup failures stop automatic media fallback before callbacks or another provider. Frozen errors retain identity; non-Error reasons retain their exact cause. Independent body and cleanup failures remain ordered. No error-name/status heuristics or provider-secret fallback are added.

## Current Candidate and Reconciliation

Signed candidate **`b0d33f09ba5d8d0e6db804f01cbf79dcf269a351`**, tree **`3ef374ed98c55f0e3e55e55b5d9868771fed1bd7`**, ordered parents **[`caf56e1f5e5bda520fa2f2472f731f71f5d24cc9`, `a90c174919aca859d2145b2e6bede683ec87177a`]**. The native materializer resolved exactly chunk grouping and skills-library readiness using bound source/base/fork blobs. Provider implementation and documentation remain byte-identical to `caf56`; frozen install inputs remain unchanged.

The incoming explicit Search-settlement and held-library setup replace obsolete empty-grid polling. Recovery opens the installed shelf before selecting its detail. Failure, no-false-empty, reload and zero-write assertions remain. Incoming attachment visibility sampling is preserved. These are source-supported test corrections, not an attribution of the prior hosted Escape failure.

The two retained grouping mappings keep neutral truncation with the existing plugin-catalog group and catalog-discovery with settings controls. Incoming routed Skills pages, single SkillTile owner, installed/browse separation, 1,000 records, category counts/cursors/deduplication and request/DOM identity stay intact. The original 100 ms delay, deadlines, **28/31/56/61 asset ceilings**, and zero eager-reader/tooltip guards remain. Inventory opens during benchmark preparation; the measured action is filtering only.

## Verification and Timing

- **Fresh on signed `b0d`: 54 contract/registered HTTP cases pass**, 32.011 s wall / 28.85 s Vitest. The 22 video-runtime cases pass in 6.223 s wall / 4.41 s Vitest. Real unfinished HTTP responses, operation deadlines, original release and terminal no-fallback joins require the transport layer; compiler/registration startup contributes to invocation walltime. Fake clocks alone cannot establish those joins. Hosted seconds for this head remain pending.
- Core production types (8.951 s), extension production types (9.901 s), extension test types (14.355 s), and the owning core-test-other graph (7.126 s) pass. The actual test graphs are checked as well as production types.
- Test-line guard passes against frozen `a90`: **711 net LF growth <= 400 + 317 existing justified credit**. Allocation is unchanged. Diff checks pass.
- Exact **`a90` to `b0d` SDK/API comparison passes in 104.624 s**, with no public API changes. Diff SHA256 `16eb6f4a2c62f6fc310b2c62864e833978757dfe9129c7a2e7c7452086055595`; evidence SHA256 `9013348bb0678a3ed217d9d54ec59a6eda2e423ee4ecf02625d806c52858e581`. This does not replace full-build qualification.
- **Explicit proof reuse:** this candidate's entire UI tree `9eb3281881f00253f99acd467826546617d47d0a` and scripts tree `cc5867378b8c2bff90e1342c4f73e73791f51e53` equal OpenCode `dad3cce339d3173679979a1c92c1a5e3c2c92380`, with matching package/lock/runtime inputs. Its 10 chunk-boundary cases and four original production asset cases passed (45.044 s wall / 43.04 s Vitest); two strict local interaction cases also passed. These remain executions on `dad3`, not new PixVerse runs or hosted parity. UI fixture compilation, real Chromium readiness and held-reader release explain the over-30-second file invocation.
- Prior normal built-registry acceptance on `5b` used `generateVideo(params)` without provider-lookup overrides: malformed create produced one composed POST and zero direct requests, while a missing offer reached the configured direct upload/create/GET; acquisition cleanup and process closure passed. That receipt remains historical. Shipping SDK-to-Worker/SQLite composition is separately coordinated.

## Investigated Build Failure and Remaining Gates

The exact signed **`b0d` full build failed exit 1 after 218.093 s**, without timeout or capture fault. Public SDK declarations are **5,394,718 > 5,385,536 bytes** (9,182 over). Raw output: 621,087 B, SHA256 `f408ca8dafb7f0cf32a4a48072dd8e774ca0b2b12ce01127010635bab4ac9408`. Runtime/plugin/UI phases completed, but the full build did not pass.

The same execution reports largest CSS 58,500 > 58,315 B; total CSS 345,436 > 337,312 gzip / 1,783,340 > 1,740,234 raw; chat 21 > 20 requests and 1,334,208 > 1,332,637 gzip. New Session is within its recorded ceiling at 822,164 <= 822,243 gzip. No unmodified `a90` baseline-build attribution, budget increase, API removal or green-build claim is made.

All prior source, failed runs and diagnostic receipts remain retained. In particular, `caf56`'s hosted 390px Escape failure remains causally unresolved; a local strict pass is not baseline or Linux parity proof. The separate scaffold archive-timeout retry completed successfully on unchanged `caf56`. Native preparation records `tests.result: fail` with this exact-head investigated evidence. `github_pending` is not successful hosted qualification. prs.title: feat(memory): opt topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker
prs.body:
Closes #179954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: curated memory kept in topic files under `memory/` is indexed with the size-based chunker, so unrelated one-fact bullets are merged into ~400-token chunks. A query pulls in neighboring facts and the mixed embedding ranks specific facts lower than the same bullets in `MEMORY.md`.

## User Impact

User impact: a topic file under `memory/` can opt into per-entry chunking by carrying one marker line. Files without the marker are indexed exactly as before; there is no new config key.

```markdown
<!-- chunking: entries -->
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Shape agreed with @steipete in the issue (option 1, chunking only):

- The marker uses the existing HTML-comment carrier style and is stripped before indexing like the other annotations. It must sit on its own line, so prose or code samples that mention it do not opt a file in. Only `memory/` files honor it.
- `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input to the existing `perEntry` predicate; the chunker itself is unchanged.
- Recall metadata eligibility and path provenance are untouched (`memory-path-provenance.ts`, `curated-annotations.ts` extraction). The marker does not make a file a curated root, so trigger and importance annotations stay ignored in topic files. Project scope was already read for topic files and now applies per entry in marked files, which follows from the chunk boundaries.
- Adding or removing the marker changes the file content hash, so the normal per-file reindex handles it. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` is not bumped because unmarked files chunk as before.
- Docs updated in `memory-builtin`, `memory`, and `memory-architecture`.

## Evidence

Tests (all pass; the three behavior tests fail on the base without the change):

- `manager-index-preparation.test.ts`: marked file chunks per entry with the marker stripped; unmarked file stays one size-based chunk; marker in prose, unknown mode, and non-`memory/` paths are ignored; trigger/importance stay null and project scope still applies as for an unmarked topic file.
- `manager-per-entry-marker.test.ts` (real manager, SQLite index): file indexed size-based, marker added then a normal sync gives per-entry chunks, marker removed then a normal sync returns the original size-based chunks.
- `curated-annotations.test.ts`: marker detection, stripping keeps line numbers, marker never reaches recall metadata.
- Full `extensions/memory-core`, `packages/memory-host-sdk`, `src/plugin-sdk` vitest run: 463 files pass, 9 skipped, 2 fail (see below). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck/format/guards and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

Paired corpus: the same 24 synthetic one-line bullets (team facts), once in a topic file with the marker and once without. Chunks were produced by the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (400 tokens, 80 overlap) and embedded with a local embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-4B 4-bit served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plain queries, cosine similarity, vector ranking only). The unmarked file becomes 2 chunks (20 and 8 bullets); the marked file becomes 24 chunks.

| Query | marked: top score | marked: bullets returned | marked: target rank | unmarked: top score | unmarked: bullets returned | unmarked: target rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which food should we avoid when booking a team dinner? | 0.602 | 1 | 1 | 0.395 | 20 | 1 |
| How many API calls per minute are allowed? | 0.892 | 1 | 1 | 0.529 | 8 | 1 |
| Who do I ask to change the analytics warehouse schema? | 0.779 | 1 | 1 | 0.501 | 20 | 1 |
| When is the database backup restore-tested? | 0.710 | 1 | 1 | 0.533 | 20 | 1 |
| What is the Friday deploy rule? | 0.731 | 1 | 1 | 0.584 | 20 | 1 |
| How long do we keep logs? | 0.823 | 1 | 1 | 0.492 | 20 | 1 |

With such a small corpus the right chunk is found either way. The difference is what comes back: one bullet at a clearly higher similarity versus 8-20 unrelated bullets in one chunk at a lower score. The gap grows with file size, since a larger unmarked file has more diluted chunks competing with each other.

Shipped-CLI proof (head `f81c3b246`; built `openclaw.mjs`, local oMLX embeddings `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ` through `memory.search.provider: "omlx"`, throwaway `HOME` and state dir, real index untouched). Corpus: `MEMORY.md` (3 bullets), `USER.md` (2), `memory/people-marked.md` (6 bullets + marker), `memory/people-unmarked.md` (6 bullets). `openclaw memory index --agent main`, then `openclaw memory search --json`:

| File | base `bec3ad81d` chunks | PR chunks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `USER.md` | 2 | 2 |
| `memory/people-marked.md` | 1 (lines 1-11) | 6 (1-5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-11) |
| `memory/people-unmarked.md` | 1 (lines 1-9) | 1 (lines 1-9) |

| Query | base top hit | PR top hit |
|---|---|---|
| who is allergic to peanuts | 0.490 `marked:1-11` | 0.633 `marked:6` |
| who manages the Cluj warehouse | 0.577 `marked:1-11` | 0.794 `marked:7` |
| who is allergic to shellfish | 0.443 `unmarked:1-9` | 0.518 `marked:6` (then 0.445 `unmarked:1-9`) |
| vendor contract with the catering company | 0.503 `marked:1-11` | 0.730 `marked:9` |

Upgrade compatibility (same state dir: index with base `bec3ad81d`, switch to the PR build, run `openclaw memory index` again without `--force`): `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and the unmarked file keep identical chunk counts and chunk hashes (sha256 digests `6f2efb3f`, `f8bc8e7a`, `f9c76450`) through every step. The marked file is rewritten to 6 per-entry chunks when it is next touched or edited (7 after appending a bullet); adding the marker to the unmarked file gives 6 chunks and removing it restores the original single chunk with the original hash, with all other files untouched. A file that already carries the marker keeps its old chunks until it changes (or `--force`); the marker is new, so no existing corpus is affected. No index-identity warning and no rebuild were needed. Full tables are in the PR comment.

CI: type, lint and package-boundary checks pass on the earlier head. `test-lines` now passes locally (`slack: 237`, baseline untouched) after consolidating duplicated detector test rows; the add/remove-marker reindex test is unchanged.

Fence detection requires only spaces/tabs after a closing delimiter (as `packages/markdown-core/src/fences.ts` does). Upgrade from the latest stable (`v2026.10.8`) to this branch, with existing settings, files and index data preserved, is documented in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186649#issuecomment-6468411633).

Known gaps, none caused by this change (each reproduces with the three source files reverted to `main`): `manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` ("KNN child loaded unrelated runtime: kysely") and two `qa-runtime.test.ts` waitForHealth tests fail locally. `pnpm check:changed` reports two further failures. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails identically on a clean `main` (public entrypoints 160 > 158), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run locally because `rg` is not installed. No Ollama was used; the embedding model above is the local provider.

prs.title: fix: test upgrades from released PostgreSQL installs
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

[OpenClaw 2026.11.5](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openclaw/v/2026.11.5) ships PostgreSQL shared state and agent stores. Published-driver CI now installs that npm release with both stores on PostgreSQL and checks that users can open the same session and transcript after the installed updater activates the candidate.

## Root Cause

Published-driver CI seeded SQLite only. PostgreSQL migration fixtures checked individual schema changes without exercising the released npm updater and candidate activation on populated PostgreSQL stores. The operator guide still described stable PostgreSQL upgrades as inapplicable.

## Real behavior proof

Ran the new fixture against disposable PostgreSQL 17 with the published 2026.11.5 npm package and a candidate built and packed with the CI artifact commands. The fixture wrote a session and transcript through the released Gateway, verified its backup, ran the installed `openclaw update --yes --json --no-restart --tag <candidate.tgz>`, and started the candidate Gateway. The updater recorded `succeeded` at `finished` and replaced the installed build.

```sh
node scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/published-driver-postgres.mjs candidate.tgz artifacts
```

```text
Published 2026.11.5 PostgreSQL state 36 → 40, agent 38 → 43; Gateway history preserved
```

The fixture requires a disposable PostgreSQL DSN in `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN`. It checks the original store identities before opening the candidate Gateway.

## Verification

- The base workflow resolver emitted no PostgreSQL selection. The patched resolver emitted `postgres=true` for the 2026.11.5 candidate. Older and frozen candidates stay out of this case.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-published-driver-update-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 31 tests.
- Candidate build and tarball integrity, workflow sanity, targeted formatting and lint, and `git diff --check` passed. The final local upgrade fixture took 4m18s.
- The first CI run flagged the fixture's promise rejection typing. The follow-up passed the type-aware script lint and repeated the full upgrade and planner suite. [Updated-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44633456653)

- The required PR CI gate passed. Ordinary PR CI skipped the published-driver update job by design. The PostgreSQL step has local proof above. Exact-head proof on a GitHub-hosted runner is pending. [Skipped job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44633456653/job/135946915075)

## Evidence

Local autoreview covered the initial patch at P0 through P2 and found no actionable defects. The follow-up changes error handling types and preserves the same upgrade path. The production and full-tree unused-file scans both passed.

## What was not tested

This case uses foreground Linux Gateways and synthetic RPCs. Managed service restart, PostgreSQL rollback restore, Windows package update, and paid model calls are outside this case.

`openclaw browser set credentials <user> <pass>` followed by `open <url>` does not get past HTTP Basic auth:

- managed headless profile (`main` and `2026.11.5`): `page.goto: net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS`
- extension-relay profile (`2026.11.5`): `Protocol error (Fetch.enable): Fetch interception is owned by another session or is being released`

The navigation fence intercepts each guarded tab's documents on its own CDP session but neither asks for nor answers `Fetch.authRequired`, so the challenge falls back to Chromium's default handling, which headless cancels. Playwright's `setHTTPCredentials` handles auth on a second session; on an extension relay that second `Fetch.enable` is refused because the relay grants a tab's Fetch domain to one session only (intended, covered by `relay-bridge.fetch.test.ts`).

## Change

- `pw-session-http-auth.ts` (new): per-`BrowserContext` credentials for the fence, `interception()` (adds `handleAuthRequests` while credentials are set), `answer()` (one `Fetch.authRequired` listener per interception target), `onChange()` (re-enable an already-fenced tab when credentials change), and a relay-browser marker.
- Fence: enables `handleAuthRequests` when credentials exist, forwards `Fetch.authRequired`, answers it. Server challenge → `ProvideCredentials`; the same request challenged again → `CancelAuth` (rejected credentials end as the server's 401 page, no loop); proxy challenge or no credentials → `Default` (unchanged behavior).
- `set credentials`: stores credentials for the fence on every transport. Direct CDP still calls `context.setHTTPCredentials` (tabs the fence never touched, e.g. popups, keep working). Relay connections skip it, so no second `Fetch.enable` is attempted.
- `settleInterception` moves unchanged into `cdp-fetch-interception.ts` so the fence stays under its line cap.

Not changed: credentials are still context-wide and in-memory, as before. Per-origin scope and SecretRef sources are proposed separately in the issue.

## Evidence

Candidate `90943efefd7567fc0f6d460c0bed0b73fab6e4fd` on `main` @ `0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2` (no `extensions/browser` or package changes on `main` since). Built CLI (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs`), throwaway `HOME`/state, headless Chromium (Linux, Playwright 1.62 image), managed profile `openclaw`, local Basic-auth fixture on `127.0.0.1`:

| Build | Sequence | `open` | `snapshot` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`44267df`) / `2026.11.5` | set credentials → open | `net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` | empty |
| main (`44267df`) / `2026.11.5` | open → set credentials → open | `net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` | empty |
| this PR | set credentials → open | `opened` | `heading "BASIC-AUTH-OK"` |
| this PR | open → set credentials → open | first `open` fails (no credentials yet), second `opened` | `heading "BASIC-AUTH-OK"` |
| this PR | wrong password → open | `opened`, no loop | `generic: unauthorized` (server 401 body) |

Tests that fail on `main` and pass here:

- `pw-session-navigation-fence.http-auth.test.ts`: fence enables `handleAuthRequests`, answers `ProvideCredentials` / `CancelAuth` on repeat / `Default` for proxy; credentials set after fencing re-enable the existing interception (and clearing turns it off again).
- `pw-tools-core.state.http-credentials.test.ts`: relay contexts never call Playwright's `setHTTPCredentials`; direct contexts call it and also feed the fence.

Without the production change: 4 failed / 4. With it: 97 passed across 7 files (new tests plus the existing fence, state, navigation-guard and relay Fetch suites).

Checks on the candidate tree: `pnpm build` ✅ · `tsgo:extensions` + `tsgo:extensions:test` ✅ · oxlint `--type-aware --deny-warnings` on the changed files ✅ · oxfmt `--check` ✅ · line-cap ratchet ✅ (fence file shrinks) · test-mock-exports, test-timeout-race ratchet, import-cycles ✅. The full `pnpm check:changed` run did not fit the 12 GiB container I have (SQLite worker ratchet), so I ran the steps above individually; happy to fix anything CI reports.

Not verified: a real browser with the OpenClaw extension on the fixed build. The relay path is covered by the unit tests above and the existing relay contract test (`relay-bridge.fetch.test.ts`). The same fence change, applied to a local `2026.11.5` install, also passes with a real Chromium-based browser on macOS over direct CDP (both sequences, wrong password ends on the 401 page).

prs.title: fix: stop offering Retry for removed chat automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After you remove an automation, its original chat card still says “Automation unavailable” and offers Retry. Retrying cannot bring the automation back.

## User Impact

The card keeps the name and says **Removed**, with no Retry button, settings link, or switch. Other automations in the group keep their controls. A temporary loading failure still offers Retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card now distinguishes an exact not-found response for that job from a failed request. The Gateway intentionally gives the same response if the viewer loses access. If access is restored, the card updates normally.

## Evidence

In Chromium, four saved rows changed from switches to four retry buttons on main, and to four status-only rows on the fix. Both captures use the actual bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses, the same dark theme and a 1152 × 780 viewport. Before: `1d9252c3770`; after: `3d6eb66d131`.

prs.title: fix(doctor): warn about Docker and image problems for per-agent sandbox configs
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who enable sandboxing per agent (`agents.entries.<id>.sandbox`) would get a clean `openclaw doctor` report while that agent's sandboxed turns fail. Doctor only inspected `agents.defaults.sandbox`, so with per-agent-only sandboxing it never reported Docker being unavailable and never warned about (or offered to repair) a missing sandbox image — including a per-agent `docker.image`. The first visible symptom was a failed sandboxed turn. The Linux Codex bwrap namespace note was skipped the same way.

- **Related:** #201988 (issue body already pinpoints `resolveEnabledSandboxBackend` vs the runtime's agent-first mode resolution); no competing open PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now enumerates every sandbox source it must treat as enabled — `agents.defaults.sandbox` (including the gateway-role-required admission from #202230) plus each agent entry with its own sandbox config whose resolved mode is not `off` — and resolves each source through `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`, the same runtime config owner sandboxed turns resolve through, instead of duplicating the fallback chain. Doctor therefore inspects exactly what the runtime would use: nullish (`??`) image selection (an explicitly empty `docker.image` is preserved and reported as an invalid empty value rather than silently falling back to the default image), strict backend matching, and the `shared` scope's exclusion of agent docker/browser overrides. For each source it reports engine unavailability and missing images with the config path and per-agent disable hint, and dedupes identical (engine, kind, image) checks so defaults+agent overlap never double-prompts. Defaults-only messages are unchanged for normally-configured setups.

- **Intended outcome:** per-agent-only sandboxing produces the same Docker-unavailable warning and missing-image repair prompt that `agents.defaults.sandbox` already gets, naming the offending agent entry.
- **Out of scope:** no changes to runtime sandbox resolution, no new config surface, no UI changes.
- **Highest-risk area:** message/behavior drift for the existing defaults-only paths.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** all existing `doctor-sandbox` unit tests — including the gateway-role-required tests added by #202230 after this branch's original base — pass on the rebased branch; new tests pin per-agent behavior (entries + legacy list rosters, mode inheritance, per-agent image, explicitly-empty image, shared-scope overrides, bwrap note).

## User Impact

Users enabling sandboxing per agent now learn about broken sandbox prerequisites from `openclaw doctor` before a turn fails, and can repair them with `openclaw doctor --fix` — including per-agent images. Reviewers should focus on `src/commands/doctor-sandbox.ts` (`resolveEnabledSandboxSources`) and the regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Follow-up round: rebased onto current `main`, ClawSweeper's P2 finding addressed (per-agent images/mode/backend now resolve through `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`, the runtime's config owner, instead of a competing resolver), and the requested upgrade + repair behavior demonstrated on a real host. Internal proxy/registry-mirror endpoints are redacted below.

- **Real environment tested:** built CLI (`pnpm build:runtime`; buildstamp head `35eaa22` — identical source to final head `291f4fc`, the amend only reflowed test-file whitespace), isolated state dir `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-201988-upgrade-state` holding only `agents.entries.work.sandbox = { mode: "all" }` (default image, `agents.defaults.sandbox` unset); real Docker client + daemon 20.10.0; Linux host; `openclaw@2026.11.6` installed via npm into an isolated prefix for the stable side of the upgrade scenario.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm build:runtime
  # 1. stable CLI on the per-agent-only state dir (pre-upgrade behavior)
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-201988-upgrade-state <isolated-prefix>/openclaw doctor --non-interactive
  # 2. patched CLI: detect -> fix -> verify repaired state
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-201988-upgrade-state node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-201988-upgrade-state node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
  docker buildx build --builder <mirror+seccomp-unconfined> \
    -t openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim --load -f scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile scripts/docker/sandbox
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-201988-upgrade-state node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  # 3. warning variants on the patched build
  DOCKER_HOST=unix:///tmp/nonexistent-docker.sock OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  #    (config variants: docker.image "evidence-sandbox:missing", then "")
  # 4. regression tests + types
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker.test.ts \
    src/agents/sandbox-merge.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health.update-scope.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  (patched CLI, per-agent-only config, default image absent — stable v2026.11.6 printed NO warning here)
  Doctor: Sandbox
  ◇  Sandbox ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │  Sandbox base image missing: openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim. Run openclaw  │
  │  doctor --fix to build it with scripts/sandbox-image-build.sh.           │
  │  Sandboxed turns will fail until the image is available.                 │
  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

  (doctor --fix auto-approves and runs the shipped repair path)
  Running scripts/sandbox-image-build.sh...

  (Docker unavailable, DOCKER_HOST pointed at a dead socket)
  ◇  Sandbox ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │  Sandbox mode is enabled for agent "work" (agents.entries.work.sandbox,  │
  │  mode: "all") but Docker is not available.                               │
  │  ...                                                                     │
  │  - Disable sandbox mode: openclaw config set                             │
  │    agents.entries.work.sandbox.mode off                                  │
  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

  (missing custom per-agent image)
  │  Sandbox base image missing: evidence-sandbox:missing. Build or pull it  │
  │  first. Sandboxed turns will fail until the image is available.          │

  (explicitly empty per-agent image — the P2 finding's case; no default-image probe/build offer)
  │  Sandbox base image resolves to an empty string                          │
  │  (agents.entries.work.sandbox). Sandboxed turns will fail until a valid  │
  │  image is configured.                                                    │
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** after the image was built, patched `doctor --non-interactive` reruns with a clean `Doctor: Sandbox` section and exit 0 — detect → shipped repair path → repaired state verified end to end. Tests: **41/41 pass** across `doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode`, `doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker` (including the gateway-role-required test added by #202230), `sandbox-merge`, `doctor-health.update-scope`. Types/lint: tsgo test-types shard `commands-doctor` exit 0, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0, `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` clean.
- **Before evidence (red-on-base):** the new test file run against `origin/main`: **7 of 8 tests fail** (per-agent health surface absent). Run against the pre-fix PR head `0c5907f7b07`: only the empty-image test fails — the old resolver probed `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` where the runtime preserves `""` (exactly the P2 mismatch). Stable `openclaw@2026.11.6` on the same state dir: `Doctor: Sandbox` runs but prints no warning at all while the default image is missing (first symptom remains the failed sandboxed turn, as reported).
- **What was not tested:** no podman backend run against a real podman daemon (covered by unit tests with synthetic engine descriptors). The stock `doctor --fix` → `docker build` path could not complete against this host's daemon: the daemon has no internet route for the pinned `FROM debian:trixie-slim@sha256:...` (`registry-1.docker.io ... i/o timeout`; daemon-level proxy/mirror config requires root), and docker 20.10's default seccomp profile rejects Debian trixie's apt hooks (verified side-by-side: identical `apt-get update` exits 0 with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`, fails with the daemon default). Both are host-level constraints, reproduced and logged; the image build itself was completed through BuildKit with the internal mirror + unconfined seccomp using the identical shipped Dockerfile/context.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** host-level daemon constraints on the stock `doctor --fix` build path (disclosed and evidenced above); everything else ran through shipped entry points.
- **Review state:** P2 finding addressed; awaiting CI + re-review

prs.title: fix(talk): answer the first talk.catalog read with its snapshot
prs.body:
## Problem

A brand-new chat on a fresh profile logs a refusal for its first Talk catalog read:

```
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.catalog errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Talk catalog is warming; retry shortly
```

The first `talk.catalog` request for each agent (and each provider/model override) always answers retryable `UNAVAILABLE` (`details.reason: "talk-catalog-warming"`), even when the catalog build finishes a few milliseconds later. The Control UI retries and recovers, but every new chat produces an error round trip and a red log line.

## Root cause

`readTalkCatalog` (`src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.ts:204` on `main`) starts a detached build for a key with no snapshot and returns `entry.snapshot` (still `undefined`) at once, so the handler answers "warming" (`catalog.ts:486`). This stale-while-revalidate shape came from #172556, which is correct for refreshes but also applies it to the very first read, where there is nothing to serve.

## Fix

- When a key has no snapshot, the handler awaits the in-flight build, bounded by the existing 5 s refresh deadline (`CATALOG_REFRESH_DEADLINE_MS`), then answers with the snapshot.
- The deadline timer that already logs slow builds now also releases waiting readers. No new timer or constant.
- Concurrent first reads for one key join the same build (the existing `pending` single flight).
- "warming" remains only when the deadline passes without a snapshot, or the first build fails. The Control UI retry stays for those cases.
- For session-scoped reads, the wait happens before `withPreparedSessionResolve`, so disclosure inside the authorization callback stays synchronous.
- Refreshes of an existing snapshot are unchanged (stale-while-revalidate).
- Tests: the retry-first-read helpers are removed; tests now expect the first read to return the catalog, plus a new case for a build past its deadline.
- Docs: `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md` describes the new first-read contract.

## Impact

- New chats and Talk settings get the catalog on the first request; the Gateway log has no `talk.catalog` UNAVAILABLE line for a normal startup.
- Risk: a first request can now hold for up to 5 s when a provider readiness check is slow (it then answers "warming" as before). Session-scoped callers now start the agent's catalog build before session resolution rejects an unknown or hidden session; the build is cached per agent and single-flighted, and the response is still the same rejection.

## Evidence

- Red on `main`, green here: `test/talk-catalog-session.test.ts` (real `sessions.resolve` path), `src/gateway/server.auth.guest-dictation.test.ts` (real WebSocket), `catalog-speech.test.ts`, `provider-discovery.test.ts` all got `talk-catalog-warming` on base for the first read; all pass on this head.
- Touched and importing suites pass: `catalog-speech`, `catalog`, `provider-discovery`, `file-transcription`, `index`, `method-scopes.own-session`, `server.auth.guest-dictation`, `talk-catalog-session`, `talk-browser-defaults`, `ui/src/api/gateway-talk-catalog.node`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean.
- Isolated Gateway (fresh profile): base (`main`) vs this head, same steps: start a Gateway on a fresh profile, create a new chat (`sessions.create`), then the chat's first `talk.catalog` (with its `sessionKey`) and a settings read (no `sessionKey`).
  - `main`: chat first read returns `UNAVAILABLE` `talk-catalog-warming`; the Gateway log has `[ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.catalog 43ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Talk catalog is warming; retry shortly`.
  - This head: chat first read returns the catalog; settings read returns the catalog; the Gateway log has no `talk.catalog`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `FORBIDDEN` or `INVALID_REQUEST` line.

## Decision

The maintainer chose this contract change (bounded first-read wait instead of an immediate warming response) so that a new chat on a fresh profile produces no refusal in the Gateway log. Warm reads stay immediate, and the client retry stays for builds past the deadline.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state, config or protocol change; a revert restores the old warming-first behavior. Blast radius: `talk.catalog` callers (Control UI chat composer and Talk settings, native clients) on first read per agent.

prs.title: fix: slow macOS dashboard reconnects when the app keeps refusing native sign-in
prs.body:
Related: #168743 ## What Problem This Solves When the macOS app keeps refusing native sign-in for an open Dashboard page, that page reconnects to the Gateway every 9 to 15 seconds for as long as it stays open. On 2026.11.5, which already includes #185963, one Mac still produced hundreds of `code=4008 reason=native authorization unavailable` closes overnight. #185963 stops closed and replaced pages; a page that is still open has no limit. ## User Impact A native Dashboard or chat page that the app keeps refusing now retries quickly about ten times, then about once every five minutes. Coming back to the window (focus, or the window becoming visible again) still retries at once, but it no longer starts a new fast series. The page still connects by itself as soon as the app grants it again, and short refusals recover exactly as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Control UI client marks every native refusal as retryable, and its reconnect loop has no attempt limit, so the 15 second backoff ceiling repeats forever. The page's native auth adapter now counts consecutive refusals. From the tenth one, the refusal carries a five minute retry floor, which the shared reconnect loop already honors for retryable errors (300 to 360 seconds with jitter). Any native grant resets the count. The count lives in the native auth adapter, which is created once per page, not in the connection client. Page activation (focus, visibility, Retry) replaces the client. With the count on the client (the first commit, `2d4b7f498c1`), every activation started a new fast series, and the packaged app still logged 38 closes in 600 seconds. Recovery is not removed: no stop, no new state, no new setting, and the page activation recovery is unchanged. This bounds the retry side for every native page. In the app runs below, hiding the app, restarting its SSH tunnel and showing it again leaves the visible Dashboard page refused until the Dashboard is reopened. Whether that is the path on the reporter's Mac is not known (the window state was not recorded). The app-side cause is a separate fix and is not part of this change. Maintainer decision: the issue carries `needs-product-decision` because ending retries would change the recovery contract from #159860. This change keeps that contract (retries never stop) and only lowers the pace after ten consecutive refusals. ## Evidence - Packaged macOS app (release 2026.11.5, its own WKWebView and native auth bridge), Dashboard served by a test Gateway with the Control UI of the commit under test, 600 seconds of a refused, visible page: - main `9ebaece1079`: 66 closes, steady to the end. - first commit `2d4b7f498c1`: 38 closes, with new fast bursts after the window became visible again. - this branch `1426dc12ce3`: 12 closes. After the first ten refusals: one scheduled attempt (308 seconds after the previous one) and one attempt for each of the two times the window became visible again. Activating the app afterwards gave exactly one refusal. Reopening the Dashboard connected about 1.2 seconds later. - Real Gateway and headless Chromium with a refusing native bridge stub, 420 seconds: main made 35 attempts, one every 12.5 to 14.6 seconds; this branch made 11 (ten fast, then one at +378.2 seconds). A focus event gave 3 attempts within 3 seconds on main and 1 on this branch. - Regression test `slows reconnects after ten consecutive native refusals until a grant` in `ui/src/app/native-gateway-auth.node.test.ts` (real `GatewayBrowserClient` and application gateway store, fake native bridge). It checks ten fast refusals, one immediate attempt on page activation without a new fast series, the five minute floor, recovery on a grant, and fast backoff again after the grant. It fails on main (13 sockets after a minute and one activation, expected 11) and on the first commit alone (19 sockets five minutes after the activation, expected 11), and passes on this branch. - Mutation checks: reverting the second commit's source fails the same way as the first commit (19, expected 11); removing only the grant reset fails the last step (13 sockets, expected 14). - Related suites pass on this branch: `native-gateway-auth.node.test.ts`, all of `ui/src/api`, `gateway-page-activation.test.ts`, `gateway-store.auth.test.ts`, `local-error-copy.test.ts` (16 files, 284 tests). - `pnpm check:changed` at `1426dc12ce3` against a freshly fetched `origin/main` (merge base `9ebaece1079`): format, lint, UI and core test typechecks, i18n and the ratchets pass. The dead export scan fails the same way on `9ebaece1079` without this change (two unused exports in `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.authority.test-support.ts`). - Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner), base `9ebaece1079`, head `1426dc12ce3`, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified; outcome: patch is correct, no findings, rating C (proof D, patch B) in the second round; remaining findings: none. Its proof rating does not see the runtime output below and asks for a macOS app run. Gaps: the main and first-commit app runs are from one session and the `1426dc12ce3` run from a later one, on the same two Macs. The Mac was in normal use during the `1426dc12ce3` window: other apps covered the test window twice (12:36:52 to 12:38:00 and 12:43:15 to 12:43:49), and the test window was not refocused. The packaged app is the release build; only its served Control UI changes between runs. ### Runtime output #### Packaged macOS app Setup: release `OpenClaw.app` 2026.11.5 with its own profile connects over an SSH tunnel to a test Gateway on another Mac (own state dir, loopback port 19743). The Gateway's `gateway.controlUi.root` serves the built Control UI of the commit under test, so the app's WKWebView and native auth bridge run that client. Steps: open the Dashboard, hide the app, restart the app's SSH tunnel, show the app, watch 600 seconds, activate the app once, reopen the Dashboard. Counts come from the test Gateway log: `lines` are the logged `closed before connect ... code=4008` lines in the window, `closes` adds the `suppressed=N` closes the Gateway folds into each line.
