prs.title: fix: keep setup housekeeping out of the first conversation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After someone named their assistant, the first chat could report edits to internal files and sign off with a fixed line about OpenClaw. Neither helped the person start their task.

## User Impact

A new assistant can continue the person's request, or briefly invite the next one. Routine setup, cleanup, and an empty recommendation list need no recap or completion card. A failed setup step still explains what did not work; changes to the person's own files still get an explicit result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stock first-run instructions produced the sign-off. A command alone cannot distinguish housekeeping from a user-requested file edit, so this changes the instructions rather than filtering chat text or hiding tool events. Live activity, expandable details and history are unchanged. The previous stock template remains recognizable on restart; existing workspace files are not rewritten.

## Evidence

Real first conversations with a model and isolated Gateways on macOS. The base reported an identity file update and the scripted sign-off. The final template ended with an invitation, with no completion card and the bootstrap file removed. Also exercised a failed identity sync (visible warning and retry offer), a follow-up request, and a requested grocery-list write (visible confirmation and verified file contents).

Clean comparison — base `dacf5604e46`, change `3961e1c583f`. Same synthetic name and avatar choice; cropped Control UI captures.

**Before:** ![Internal file recap and scripted sign-off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/161f0eb9-e83c-4021-b727-bdf34b869118)

**After:** ![Ready for the next task with activity still available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98734c82-8793-4fbb-932a-1ee700807897)

**Annotated before:** ![Maintenance recap highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3106ca61-2202-4b7c-bfa4-9f01635369ce)

**Annotated after:** ![Conversation handoff highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/256437ea-c6b7-4d64-b64c-d7aec14b66be)

prs.title: fix: retain both errors when approval test cleanup fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When approval-forwarding verification fails and its deny/drain cleanup also fails, the cleanup rejection replaces the original assertion error. Developers investigating a failed test lose the acceptance or delivery failure that triggered cleanup.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior changes. Approval test failures retain both diagnostic errors, while cleanup still runs exactly once. No configuration, migration, dependency, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A test-local helper preserves both failures in an `AggregateError`, keeps the cleanup error as its cause, and rethrows a sole verification or cleanup failure unchanged. The existing six-scenario integration flow uses the helper without changing assertions, waits, deadlines, or the existing forwarding-settlement fix. Focused regressions cover acceptance/delivery plus cleanup failures, single-error identity, and the successful path.

Only `src/gateway/server.approval-forwarding.test.ts` changes (+75/-20). The existing settlement fix is not duplicated.

## Evidence

- The real approval-forwarding test file passed all 4 tests, including its original six-scenario Gateway integration flow, on the reviewed main adaptation. The exact published test file matches the validated file (SHA-256 `35c0fdd965c965fc79cad06cc219e236e49f40982bad699f3dddbf5773dd85ca`).
- Targeted Gateway-server test typecheck, file lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed (exit 0). Earlier red/green proof exercised the original `try/finally` error-masking behavior versus the diagnostic helper.
- Full final-range canonical local autoreview (`--engine openclaw`) completed exit 0, scoped-clean, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Independent main-adaptation review also found no actionable issues. These are local reviews, not claims of completed hosted review or PR CI.
- Reviewed base: `9f35510e10ecf1b4cd1a2dd824e96245cd33ca5a`; reviewed head: `60a0aa51b36743437b973e1d00b4e2e251f1202d`. Exact range diff SHA-256: `a5d7c36fcd598a530f9608c05a6fbcc074f6c4e68362226a5827c197cad5bb28`.

**Limits:** The historical negative RPC payload is unavailable. This diagnostic change does not establish the original incident's cause, reproduce that incident, or restore risk clearance. A separate controlled execution of frozen commit `408a7b5` demonstrated an authority-overlap mechanism (old path: exit 1, `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`, revision 1→2; existing eight-line settlement wait: exit 0 across all six cases). That separate experiment is not historical attribution, and no frozen-checkout changes are included here. The PR is ready for review; hosted CI and any hosted review follow-up remain pending.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changing the chat priority and sending a message while a turn is running can inject the message at the old priority. The picker shows the new setting even though the running turn keeps the one it started with.

## User Impact

A chat message sent after a saved priority change queues as a new turn rather than steering under the old setting. The current turn keeps running. The follow-up uses the session priority when it starts, subject to model and account support. Unchanged-priority steering is unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat the saved priority as part of the execution settings checked before a message can join a running turn. This reuses the existing follow-up queue on both harnesses. It does not add same-turn priority switching: ordinary Codex `turn/steer` carries only input, and the experimental live settings RPC requires opt-in and does not reprepare the Ultrafast context limit.

## Evidence

- Both Gateway regressions (Normal → Fast and Fast → Ultrafast) failed on the base by steering the active turn, then passed with the fix by preserving follow-up custody without stopping that turn.
- 215 focused tests passed across Gateway custody, session continuation, Codex steering/tier parameters, and OpenClaw Responses policy. Core typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks completed. Local Codex AutoReview was scoped-clean at P0–P2 for the reviewed candidate; unchanged owner files were outside its review bundle.
- The real Codex 0.166.0 and 0.169.0 binaries, tested against a local Responses mock, kept the active request tier unchanged with ordinary steering. Opting into `turn/settings/update` changed later requests to `priority` and then `ultrafast` in the same turn. This is wire-request evidence against a mock, not a live serving or billing check. ## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw’s managed stock Bun installs and images still select Bun 1.4.4. Bun 1.4.5 fixes the bundled HTTP/3 library issue in [GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/security/advisories/GHSA-p268-p2w7-qr8x). The advisory requires an HTTP/3 server running on Bun; the stock OpenClaw Gateway runs on Node.

## User Impact

New builds that use these pins will pick up Bun 1.4.5. This does not change the default Gateway runtime, the minimum accepted Bun version, the pinned OpenClaw fork, or existing deployments. Anyone running a separate Bun HTTP/3 server should upgrade that server’s runtime directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update the stock Bun pins for the root build image, optional GBrain sidecar, CI and install smoke, and macOS test bootstrap. Refresh the CI archive checksums and matching test fixtures. The optional sandbox installer already selects the upstream release without a fixed Bun version, so there is no sandbox pin to change.

## Evidence

- Docker Hub registry metadata verifies the Bun 1.4.5 OCI image index at `sha256:3aa040e5445efa09d75bb428a64ba50db13e2b3ac9b6b0c7f145615f62b2ee18`. The manifest bytes match the registry digest and retain the Bun 1.4.4 image’s `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` platforms.
- The upstream Bun release and npm registry confirm the archive checksums and npm version. Focused pin consistency, YAML parsing, Node and Bash syntax, staged commit checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Draft: focused repository suites, image builds, and CI are not yet verified. No containers or packaging ran on the production host. Remote proof was unavailable because the configured Crabbox provider was not authenticated. Local independent autoreview could not start with the permitted temporary-directory layout.

prs.title: fix: stop asking for Local Network access when setting up OpenClaw on this Mac
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone opens the Mac app for the first time and picks **On this Mac**, macOS asks "Allow OpenClaw to find devices on local networks?" even though running and chatting on this Mac never uses the local network. The question appears on the "Where should your assistant run?" page, before the person has said anything about another computer. Opening the Connection window in local mode triggered the same network search.

## User Impact

User impact: setting up and chatting on this Mac no longer makes OpenClaw ask for Local Network access. OpenClaw asks only when the person chooses **Nearby** to look for a Gateway on another computer, or opens the Connection window in Remote mode, where nearby Gateways are listed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dialog comes from the Bonjour gateway search (`GatewayDiscoveryModel.start()` → `NWBrowser`). Onboarding started it on both the hosting-choice page and the find page, together with the check for a Gateway already running on this Mac. The local check reads this Mac's Gateway port (`lsof`/`launchctl`), so it needs no network permission.

- Onboarding: the hosting-choice page now runs only the local port check. Network search starts when **Nearby** is opened on the find page and stops when it is closed or the person leaves the page.
- Connection window: network search runs only in Remote mode and follows mode changes.
- Camera, microphone, Accessibility and Screen Recording already follow the in-context path (`nodes.permission-missing` → chat permission card → Device Settings). This PR leaves that path unchanged.

Accepted limitation: the bundled Gateway (`bun`) still announces itself over Bonjour by default (`discovery.mdns.mode: minimal`), so macOS may still ask about **bun**. Changing that is a Gateway default and affects how other devices find this Mac, so it belongs in a separate decision.

## Evidence

- New mounted test `LocalNetworkDiscoveryTests`:
  - Local onboarding: on the hosting page and on the find page before **Nearby** is chosen, no search starts. Choosing **Nearby** starts it, and closing it stops it again.
  - Connection window: no search starts while the connection is not set up. Switching to Remote starts it, and switching back stops it.
- Red on base: the onboarding test fails on `origin/main` (search started on the hosting page and on the find page before **Nearby**). The Connection window test fails with only the mode check reverted.
- Updated `GatewayDiscoverySelectionFlowTests`, which had encoded the old behavior where search started on the hosting page.
- Sandboxed local run (`sandbox-exec` with `scripts/macos-health-render.sb` plus loopback and per-user temp access, default profile, private HOME): 209 tests in 11 suites passed: LocalNetworkDiscovery, GatewayDiscoverySelectionFlow, OnboardingAISetup, OnboardingViewSmoke, GatewayDiscoveryModel, OnboardingPage, OnboardingRemoteAuthPrompt, ConnectionWindow, HealthStoreState, OnboardingFirstRun and OnboardingDashboardHandoff.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and swiftformat on the touched tests: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.

prs.title: improve: set up this Mac in fewer steps on first launch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Setting up OpenClaw on this Mac took extra clicks that did nothing: **Next** on the welcome screen, **Next** again on a separate "Where should your assistant run?" page, and then, after the AI connection had already passed its live test, a final "You're all set!" tour that waited for **Finish** before the dashboard opened.

## User Impact

User impact: on a fresh Mac, one click on **Use this Mac** starts local setup, and a verified AI connection finishes onboarding and opens the same dashboard destination as before, with no tour and no confirmation click. **On another computer** and **Set up later** remain on the welcome screen.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The welcome screen now hosts the hosting choice. **On this Mac** stays preselected, so the primary button reads **Use this Mac** and commits local setup in one action. Choosing another computer leads to the existing remote finder; nothing local starts.
- **Getting things ready** is unchanged: it already shows per-step progress and an in-place **Try again**. A mounted test now drives a preparation failure followed by **Try again** and checks the user stays on that step.
- When the live AI test passes, the success transition runs what **Finish** used to do: complete onboarding and open, once, the destination AI setup already chose (guided setup for a newly verified model, the normal dashboard for a pre-existing one). It runs only after verification, which needs the Gateway answering, so the dashboard never opens before the service is ready. Primary-model verification and the pending-activation recovery path are untouched; relaunch recovery now finishes the same way instead of stopping on the tour.
- The final tour and its now-unreachable local rows are gone. "You're all set!" remains only for flows without an AI handoff (**Set up later**, node invitation, browser Gateway, joined OpenClaw ID claw). Builds with OpenClaw ID still offer the optional reachability step before finishing.
- Cleanup: the Channels and Skills route constants used only by the tour are removed from `DashboardRouteMap`; docs describe the current first run (the "automatic first run" text was stale since #196759).

| Required actions to use this Mac | Base (`main` dacf5604e46) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome | Next | **Use this Mac** (choice + start) |
| Where should it run? | Next (separate page) | — |
| Getting things ready | automatic, Try again on failure | automatic, Try again on failure |
| Connect your AI | choose + live test | choose + live test |
| After verified AI | tour + **Finish** | dashboard opens automatically, once |
| Clicks outside AI choice | 3 | 1 |

## Evidence

Base behavior was confirmed first: on `main` the existing tests show the five-page local order `[0, 1, 2, 3, 9]`, a mounted window needing **Next** twice to reach AI setup, and `fresh inference waits for the optional native steps before finishing once` (connected AI does not finish until **Finish**).

On this branch, in a sandboxed run of the real `OnboardingView` (private HOME/state, no network, no operator home or preferences):

- **One action:** a mounted window presses **Use this Mac** once and lands on AI setup (or the preparation gate); the welcome page's primary title is **Use this Mac**.
- **Preparation failure then Try again:** with unreadable service ownership, the mounted window shows the failure on **Getting things ready**, presses **Try again**, and stays on that step with the error and retry visible.
- **Remote choice:** a mounted window selects **On another computer**, presses **Next**, and reaches **Find your OpenClaw** with connection mode still unconfigured and no daemon command beyond status.
- **Success opens the destination once:** a real activation through a fixture Gateway finishes onboarding on its own and calls the dashboard opener exactly once (`.dashboard` for an existing model, `.custodianOnboarding` for utility setup); relaunch and cold-launch receipt recovery do the same; a superseded resume still cannot finish.
- 73 focused onboarding tests pass; 224 tests across the onboarding suites pass except two that write to the system temp directory, which the sandbox denies (unrelated to this change).

### Clean comparison

Real SwiftUI views rendered by `OnboardingRenderTests` at the default 630×752 window, light mode, fixture state, no live Gateway. Before: `main` dacf5604e46. After: this branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: welcome screen with feature list and a Next button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10e1ad4a-60ee-42fd-ba72-ba13cb360fd7) | ![After: welcome screen with On this Mac preselected and a Use this Mac button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fc60e7e-d820-4041-946a-81c162000304) |
| ![Before: separate Where should your assistant run page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09c9852d-3f87-4cf1-9d27-ba55702a563d) | ![After: the next screen is Getting things ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/208632b9-01f0-4b4c-96ab-6db352eb1375) |
| ![Before: You're all set tour with channel, skill and launch-at-login rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55bdca2a-0e2e-4a96-8c49-d72d11ed705e) | No page: a verified AI connection closes onboarding and opens the dashboard. |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Next opens a second page; hosting choice not on this screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84cc3ea6-16a2-4d2f-8e86-a28c7799a87b) | ![Hosting choice on the welcome screen; one click starts local setup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/091e00a8-662a-44f1-b8f3-eb29360c5490) |
| ![Second screen asks where to run; another Next commits this Mac](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c74b5b0f-ae5e-400a-bc32-e7db66e9e720) | |
| ![Tour, then Finish opens the dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a14c67e-55bb-4de1-acef-210b19db21bd) | |

Gaps: the screens come from the view renderer, not a packaged app, so the preparation page shows the unbundled build's copy. A packaged bundled-runtime failure followed by a successful **Try again** was not run end to end on a disposable Mac; the mounted test covers the in-place retry with an ownership failure. Full native CI, Periphery and the OpenClawKit package tests are left to PR CI.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` (base and branch)
- Focused tests through `swiftpm-testing-helper` under `scripts/macos-health-render.sb` with private HOME/state: `Onboarding*Tests`, `first mounted*`, render tests with `OPENCLAW_ONBOARDING_RENDER_DIR`
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (0 violations)
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`
- `format-docs --check`, `check-docs-mdx` on the two docs pages; link audit shows no issues in changed pages

</details>

prs.title: fix(auth): CLI clients refuse to start after a macOS reboot renumbers the state volume
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw node run` and other CLI clients stop with "Client credential migration is incomplete or stale; run openclaw doctor --fix" after a macOS reboot, even though the shared state database did not change.

## User Impact

User impact: clients keep working after a reboot that renumbers the data volume. A node under a service manager no longer crash-loops until someone runs `openclaw doctor --fix` by hand (we observed one restarted about 32,500 times over four days). A shared database that was really replaced (new inode or new path) is still refused, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local client credential receipt binds itself to the shared `state/openclaw.sqlite` with `{path, dev, ino}`, and readiness refused any mismatch, including `st_dev`. On macOS APFS, `st_dev` is assigned at mount time and can change across reboots. Some Linux mounts do the same. In the observed case the device number changed while the database kept the same path and inode, and every client start failed closed.

Path plus inode is the stable part of that identity. It is what detects a replaced database (restore, rename-over, new file). This change compares only path and inode, and treats a changed `dev` as the same file:

- **Canonical receipts:** writable admission rewrites the recorded `dev`, so the receipt heals itself. Read-only admission accepts the file and writes nothing.
- **Independent native receipts:** their `source.identity` embeds `<dev>:<ino>`, so only the inode is compared. Before this change, a writable admission after a renumbering also wiped the local derived rows and rebuilt them from the native source, which dropped tokens refreshed since the copy. Now an unchanged source keeps its rows, and only the receipt's identity and binding are refreshed.
- **Migration paths** that compare the same binding (fresh bootstrap, recovery, independent→canonical cutover) use the same comparison. Recovery still rewrites the receipt when only `dev` changed, so `doctor --fix` records the current device.

The restore and rewrite flows in `client-credential-restore.ts` still compare their captured identities exactly. They run inside one Doctor operation and are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Why not a stronger identity signal, and what about the macOS app?</summary>

A generation stored inside the database would also survive a reboot. But canonical readiness deliberately does not open the shared database. A realpath'd path plus inode already distinguishes the replacement cases this guard exists for. What remains is a different filesystem, mounted at the same path, holding a file with the same inode. A whole-volume clone or restore is the realistic version of that, and it carries `client/credentials.sqlite` along with the shared database, so the pair stays consistent.

The macOS app's native check (`ClientCredentialReceipt.swift` `assertReady`) still compares the full binding. After this change, any CLI client admission on the profile refreshes the receipt, and that also clears the app's check. Relaxing the Swift comparison can follow separately.
</details>

## Evidence

The new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass with the fix. The inode-change guard tests pass on both.

- `client-credential-store.test.ts`: a receipt with a shifted `dev` and the same path and inode is admitted. Writable admission rewrites `dev`; read-only leaves the receipt untouched. A shifted inode still throws the `doctor --fix` error in both modes and leaves the receipt untouched.
- `client-credential-native-bootstrap.test.ts`: an independent receipt with a renumbered device keeps the locally refreshed token in both modes. Writable admission refreshes `source.identity` and `sharedFile`.
- `client-credential-bootstrap.test.ts`: rebinding the same anchor file after a `dev` change succeeds, records the current `dev`, and keeps local identities and tokens.
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` (the startup path `node run` uses): after a `dev` change, preparation finishes without entering Doctor maintenance, and credentials stay readable. Existing recovery tests that used a `dev` shift to force recovery now shift the inode, which still requires recovery.

Commands run locally:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/client-credential-*.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.device-*.test.ts src/commands/startup-client-credentials*.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`

Results: 17 test files passed, 2 skipped (PostgreSQL-only suites with no local server). Typecheck, lint, and format are clean. An independent local review of the branch reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(goals): allow Goals on OpenClaw cloud workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting or resuming a Goal in an otherwise usable OpenClaw cloud-worker conversation is rejected before the worker can admit its input. Goal admission recognizes Codex workers but omits built-in OpenClaw workers in `worker-turn` mode.

## User Impact

This change enables Goal Start and Resume admission on OpenClaw cloud workers. The Goal, input turn, and operation receipt commit together after runtime admission. Setup failure, a lost placement claim, or a blocking/throwing input-policy hook must not create or reactivate the Goal. Explicit runtime choices retain their precedence.

Automatic continuation to completion is not yet proven: it failed after Resume in the live Azure run described below. No new configuration, persistence schema, migration, or required user action is introduced. Policy rejection remains terminal for that input's operation ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generalizes the existing runtime Goal admission, input staging, source guard, and acknowledgment owner to include OpenClaw workers while preserving local/Codex behavior and visible-spawn eligibility.

- `e29da7a951c` prevents blocked-message audit persistence from applying a Goal mutation or successful Goal-operation receipt. It retains an existing worker-turn placement when runtime policy is implicit, without overriding explicit choices.
- `55f66bba1c6` fixes the three fixture lint errors caught by CI without changing behavior.
- `07610fc6348` merges `main` at `bd67a3f9a18` into the PR branch. The sole conflict resolution retains the authenticated-operator check for both runtime-admitted Goals and active steering.

The same owners handle these decisions; no parallel manager or compatibility path was added. Hook fixtures share the existing Goal test-support owner rather than exceeding the worker-support file's line cap.

Original implementation by @galiniliev. The linked work session covers review and follow-up corrections.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1982ca1f-7dc1-485c-9af9-265bbf8c3d61)

## Evidence

**Original live failure:** Live Pause/Resume did not lead to durable automatic completion on `07610fc63480827693622e419b074237d1d41ea2`. Resume returned a success receipt, but the automatic worker turn lost authority during transcript commit. The Goal returned to paused with zero settled continuation turns. The [required CI gate passed on the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44789793338), but that does not override the failed live case. Trace which authority expired, fix the responsible lifecycle path, and rerun the live case through durable completion before landing.

### Live Azure proof with Factory credentials

On November 21, the isolated Azure Gateway ran OpenClaw `2026.11.5` from `91d99b8a5474fefbc0f1521d50ca39757356a7ba`. Package SHA-256 `1e9f14732f36f166784cd00b1fa67874a4e5fa1559e4063b87dbf960c35bd030`. Worker bundle SHA-256 `9738fbaa616f47c59b6f14fe7ce87ae420d40d51f6a9c8b3509653f648846715`. The tested commit `91d99b8a5474fefbc0f1521d50ca39757356a7ba` is the hosted PR head. Required CI for this head is pending.

The existing Factory TOML was reused with only the token helper path relocated. The helper bytes matched the original, and the managed identity token matched the expected identity and audience. OpenClaw resolved its credential through an exec SecretRef that invoked the same helper. Native Codex used the TOML's token command on the Azure worker.

| Live case | Result | Redacted observations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenClaw worker-turn Goal | **PASS** | One Resume of paused Goal `f22282d9b055` led to a distinct automatic worker turn. SQLite confirmed the same Goal completed with one settled continuation and one human turn. An independent Azure lease read verified the final marker on the worker. |
| Native Codex with the Factory TOML | **PASS** | The enrolled node advertised the exact versioned app-server command derived from the TOML and helper. Run `2d8e8b38a32b` settled successfully. An independent Azure lease read verified the marker on the worker, and SQLite retained the assistant marker at sequence `4` after reclaim. |
| Implicit Codex placement | **UNRUN** | The Factory route specifies Codex in provider configuration. The live session reported `runtimeSource: provider`. |

<details>
<summary>Redacted Goal timeline in UTC</summary>

- `14:44:40.556Z` Resume acknowledged for run `196d908a2f2a`.
- `14:44:51.147Z` Automatic successor `7fed8a0ca50d` started on placement `1bdfd3ce86d0`, generation `5`.
- `14:45:05.082Z` Worker commit `28` persisted assistant transcript sequence `30`.
- `14:45:05.143Z` Successor settled successfully.
- `14:45:06.604Z` SQLite readback confirmed Goal `f22282d9b055` complete with one settled automatic continuation.

</details>

Azure verified zero workers after reclaim. The temporary Factory identity bindings, allocator role, and Gateway were removed. The empty Container Apps environment was `ScheduledForDelete` at the final cleanup readback.

### Live Azure worker-turn proof

OpenClaw `2026.11.5` ran from PR head `07610fc63480827693622e419b074237d1d41ea2` in a disposable Azure Container Apps Gateway. The installed package reported that commit and matched SHA-256 `a2f538a76b57afc596f51aa07195f8ea508d2cd3dbe905032670a0b6d472f861`. The Azure Sandbox worker bundle SHA-256 was `090e62ef54d1e3e0cc27c0dc54c7d818f6dc6199a44d490ec90d069ad327e452`. The Gateway enrolled a Linux node, and a separate Azure lease read found a model-created file on the worker. The worker hostname differed from the Gateway hostname, and the same path was absent on the Gateway.

| Scenario | Result | Observed state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start in an idle worker session | **Pass** | Active worker-turn placement with zero user turns, no Goal, and no receipt. Successful `chat.send` left one user turn, an active Goal, and a SQLite Start receipt with the same Goal ID. |
| Pause and Resume to automatic completion | **Fail** | The same Goal moved from active to paused. Resume returned a successful receipt and the model finished phase two. The next automatic worker turn ended with `worker turn authority changed` during transcript commit and `worker turn cancelled`. The Goal returned to paused with zero settled continuation turns and one human turn. A later Resume also ended with the Goal paused. |
| Worker setup rejection | **Pass** | A separate idle worker's disposable workspace was temporarily moved. `chat.send` returned `UNAVAILABLE` and said it had not committed Goal input. Before and after were identical for the admission checks. No Goal, zero user turns, and no SQLite operation receipt. The workspace was restored. |
| Blocking input policy | **Pass** | A live `before_agent_run` policy blocked both requests. Start left no Goal. Resume left the same Goal paused. Neither committed a successful operation receipt. Each transcript showed the policy's replacement input and omitted the original blocked text. |
| Implicit Codex selection on an unpinned worker session | **Unrun** | Access to a real implicit-Codex model route was unavailable. The OpenAI Platform credential returned HTTP 401, and the inference route used for this run returned HTTP 403 for `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.6-luna`. An explicit provider override control exercised a different policy source. |

<details>
<summary>Redacted live receipts</summary>

```text
18:32:45Z  Linux cloud node enrolled, version 2026.11.5
Start      worker-turn / idle / Goal absent / user turns 0 / receipt absent
           accepted / Goal active / user turns 1 / SQLite Start receipt present
Pause      same Goal paused / active run false / user turns 1
Resume     accepted / SQLite Resume receipt present / phase two completed
18:33:46Z  worker transcript commit failed: worker turn authority changed
18:33:46Z  node worker exit 1: worker turn cancelled
After      same Goal paused / settled continuations 0 / user turns 1
Rejection  UNAVAILABLE: Goal input was not committed
           before and after: Goal absent / user turns 0 / receipt absent
Policy     Start blocked: Goal absent / receipt absent
           Resume blocked: same Goal paused / receipt absent
```

</details>

Azure Sandbox inventory returned zero leases after the run. The temporary allocator role was removed and verified.

- **42 focused tests passed on the refreshed candidate tree**: 30 active-steer cases and 12 OpenClaw/Codex worker Goal cases. [AWS proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_81ddacf6dccee860355778f6a757edaf) verified tree `a526a6fb09d0f0bce1c85d2a3f2e38f0fe73de33` before running tests. Independent P0–P2 Codex autoreview of `07610fc6348` against `bd67a3f9a18` found no actionable findings in the supplied static review scope; `git diff --check` passed.
- The [pre-refresh CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44268778221) on `55f66bba1c6` passed the required gate, build artifacts, production types, and `check-lint-core-5`. The PR itself has not been merged into `main`.
- The earlier [AWS proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_41a4959c0545f270058daff7d98c3c01) passed seven worker Goal RPC tests and 71 recorder/runtime/prompt-stability tests. Both review defects were reproduced before correction through the public RPC path. Blocked Start and Resume now preserve Goal state without replaying a successful receipt, and the simulated unpinned implicit-runtime worker case passes.
- Earlier touched-file formatting, `git diff --check`, line-cap and test-budget checks passed (+320 test lines / 400 allowance). No baseline exception or weakened behavioral assertion was added.

**Proof limitations:** Gateway RPC, SQLite, queue ownership and worker admission are real in the focused AWS tests; worker transport and inference are simulated in those tests. The separate live Azure run had the failure and unrun case above. Upgrade proof was not run.

<details>
<summary>Validation provenance and retained failure evidence</summary>

- Incoming head `fba536ef71b` passed **66/66** Goal cases in isolated AWS run `run_549134cf99b8dbe6e387ea3d7d6452f5`.
- A corrected-suite run passed **69/70** before the implicit-runtime fixture received synthetic auth. The remaining failure was fixture auth setup. After that correction all seven worker cases passed on focused tree `21807b430e96bd7e5560df007e0e202593d7332c`; this was not an exact-SHA run of later fixture changes.
- The original correction and the CI fixture repair received independent P0–P2 static review with no actionable findings. CI at `e29da7a951c` failed on three PR-caused fixture lint errors, fixed in `55f66bba1c6`. The old failed run was not rerun or relabeled green.
- Standalone package declaration build failed on both the unmodified incoming source and the correction due to six nonexported types in unchanged `hook-model.types.ts` and `plugin-metrics.ts`. Local full typechecks and lint boundary preparation encountered the same diagnostics; a broad dead-export scan reported untouched paths. [Retained baseline reproduction and changed-check run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0e1590525e4d25f537239ce61cae0811). These results are distinct from the successful build/type/lint checks on `55f66bba1c6`.
- The original author's first run passed 65 tests and failed `keeps pursuing after an owner's silent exec completion`: expected `Exec completed` but received an automatic Goal nudge. Bounded first-15-case replays passed on base (111 seconds) and candidate (99 seconds). This remains unclassified; later passing runs are not a claimed repair.
- Refresh proof used an isolated, no-hydration AWS Crabbox lease, pinned Node/pnpm, and the exact candidate tree. Ran `chat-steer-now-handler.test.ts`, `sessions-steer-active.test.ts`, and the OpenClaw/Codex worker cases of `server.chat-goal.test.ts`. The lease was released.

</details>

prs.title: fix: reopen the model picker on Favorites when last chosen
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you closed the model picker on Favorites while using an unstarred model, opening it again took you back to the model’s provider. Getting back to your shortlist took an extra click.

## User Impact

Choose Favorites once and the picker reopens there, even if the active model is not starred. Choose a provider tab instead and the next open shows the active model’s provider. Removing the last favorite still returns you to that provider without switching models.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker already remembers whether you chose Favorites. This removes the extra requirement that the active model also be in the list. It does not add a preference, star any models, or change the selection.

## Evidence

In the real Control UI in Chromium with a synthetic catalog, GPT-4.1 stayed active while GPT-4o was starred. After closing on Favorites, main (`d5a99b07e88e`) reopened on OpenAI; the fix (`ae92921c2e13`) reopened on Favorites with only GPT-4o listed. Both builds reopened on OpenAI after choosing the Anthropic tab instead.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Picker reopened on OpenAI with GPT-4.1 selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/065348fb-1291-406e-a6ec-a68de3e136ae) | ![Picker reopened on Favorites with only GPT-4o listed; GPT-4.1 remains active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/385ca74e-dd7e-43bb-84d9-96d4b7699988) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The selected OpenAI tab is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df95fbb5-4cb1-4b4f-8b56-8e6cb121609b) | ![The remembered Favorites tab is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cf307cd-bed9-41bc-8c3b-b409ed6afc06) |

The focused regression failed on main and passed with the fix. All 20 Favorites tests passed, including removal of the last favorite. The bundled UI built, and formatting and lint passed for the changed files.

Reported and designed with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e40befd8-7dd7-4f98-baaa-e95a33df3ce7)

prs.title: fix: retain complete native release-validation evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release validation could lose the node-local diagnostics needed to investigate cancelled skill execution. Native extension batches also emitted unframed output and stopped later groups after an ordinary failure, so their logs could not establish complete failure evidence.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Maintainers receive bounded, redacted cancellation diagnostics and complete, attributable native extension results. This does not fix or waive the original skill cancellation, scheduler, or provider failure. No dependency, config, schema, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture node diagnostics before fixture teardown and attach them to the original assertion, including when E2E console output is suppressed. Reuse one bounded stream relay for native invocation framing, continue planned CI groups after ordinary exit 1, and emit a completion receipt only after process-group settlement and worker disposal. Accept blank separators within already-framed failure reports; completeInvocations and all other evidence-admission rules stay unchanged. Historical unframed logs remain rejected.

## Evidence

- Parent independent review accepted both exact patches; integration preserves their stable patch IDs. No automated review requested.
- Skill diagnostics: 2/2 focused tests; real reporter-boundary injected failure preserves the original assertion and emits sanitized diagnostics before cleanup. Typecheck, lint, and formatting passed. Original cancellation remains unreproduced.
- Native evidence: 107 parser/waiver tests; six selected native test files passed. Real failing-plus-passing extension batch emitted planned=completed=invocations=2, failedInvocations=1; production parser accepted exactly one signature. Historical raw failure still returned no signatures. Red regressions failed against the original parser and producer.
- Main integration: frozen dependency install; root tooling/scripts typechecks, all touched-file formatting and diff checks passed. Unchanged source proof reused rather than rerun.
- Workflow actionlint and downstream owner/input/conflict checks passed. Full workflow lint retains pre-existing zizmor findings (30 medium, 2 high) in unrelated action references; this patch adds only a sparse-checkout source path and makes no security suppression. This gate is not represented as green.

The producer must also reach the release candidate; repairing only the validation tool cannot frame old candidate output. A newly authorized full validation run is still needed for release qualification.

### CI correction

The extracted relay is also a transitive Darwin tooling test input. The exact CI failure named only `scripts/lib/ci-test-output.mts`; an explicit path include now retains it after the planner exclusions. That unchanged source-closure assertion is red on the original PR head and green on the correction.

Additional local workflow verification retained 126 passing completion tests and 30 passing macOS launch tests. The remaining run had 1,306 passes and two fixture-launch failures: the dependency-repair synthetic pnpm wrapper was parsed as shell (`import: command not found`), and the synthetic hourly iOS command exited 2. Both use the long private Node path in generated shebangs; neither test or command is changed by this patch. These are retained failures, not passing evidence or waivers. An earlier broad run was interrupted before all shards completed.

prs.title: improve: avoid rereading workspace files when opening a Template
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Opening a Template made the Gateway read its declared workspace files twice: once to verify the downloaded release, and again to generate the excerpts shown in the catalog.

## User Impact
The same Template detail page now takes fewer local file reads. The UI, catalog ordering, SOUL.md preview, skill summaries and inline automations are unchanged. The Gateway still downloads and verifies the archive. No migration or configuration change is needed. This is not a general page-latency improvement: a fresh-connection replay showed a slower tail.

## Why This Change Was Made
The Gateway now builds workspace excerpts from the bytes it already reads for verification, and returns them only after the whole release passes verification. Explicit file previews and install checks are unchanged. The earlier UI, pagination and archive-free inventory changes are excluded: the live registry did not supply the complete display data the current UI needs.

## Evidence
For `myfitnessclaw@0.2.5`, seven archive replays per build measured **30 → 20 local workspace file opens per detail**. Both builds made four registry requests, including the same 896,242-byte archive. Parsed detail responses matched, and all 12 Chromium opens showed the title, excerpt and enabled Add action; Show more opened the full SOUL.md on both builds.

| Measurement (main → candidate) | Median | p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Chromium, live registry via relay, five repeated opens per build | 875 → 825 ms | 1,358 → 1,338 ms |
| Live registry via relay, eight warm details on fresh connections per build | 610 → 632 ms | 682 → 730 ms |
| Captured release, 59 warm details on fresh connections per build | 47 → 47 ms | **54 → 72 ms** |
| Captured release, 60 details on persistent connections per build | 44 → 41 ms | 48 → 45 ms |

The first Chromium open in each fresh browser context took about 1.59 seconds on both builds. The measured local win is fewer file reads, not fewer downloads or a guaranteed speedup. Focused catalog, reader and Gateway tests, targeted lint/format, core typecheck and the runtime build passed. The performance-only tree was checked against `7af829afeef7d`; later main integration did not change these files. Independent local autoreview of the committed four-file range (base 7a4298bfb55f, head ccdc4f509f43, P0–P2) finished with no actionable findings. GitHub’s test merge 5e1290d4ac76 against main 3bf86304325f changes only those four backend/test files; the Files tab may compare against the older PR base snapshot.

Contributors: @Patrick-Erichsen and @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f55045c5-faef-4527-8ff5-3df5e0579516)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fe7d5b2a-04ad-4825-aade-61e9464fbab4)

prs.title: fix: stop AI setup labels from promising accounts that were only detected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw looks for AI you already have, it only finds things on the machine: a `claude` or `codex` executable, a Codex `auth.json` file, an `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` variable, or a local model server. The WebUI turned those findings into verdicts it never checked: an environment key or a saved Codex file showed **Account ready**, Codex without that file showed **Sign-in needed** (Codex can keep its login in the system keyring), and an unreadable or unrecognized Claude Code login showed **Native login** in the chat model picker. The macOS setup page promised “nothing new to sign up for” when Claude Code, Codex, or a key is merely present.

## User Impact

User impact: AI selection labels in the WebUI and the macOS app now describe what was found, not a login, plan, or working reply. A plan or API label still appears when Claude Code reports one, and every choice is still tested with a real reply before it is used. Authentication, billing, ranking, and activation are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **WebUI setup list:** the status chip no longer derives readiness from the discovery `credentials` flag. Rows show **Recommended** (ranking) or **Detected**. The row detail from the Gateway still names the evidence (`OPENAI_API_KEY set`, `installed; stored credentials found; login status unverified`).
- **WebUI model picker:** when Claude Code’s login origin is unknown (unrecognized login type, or `claude auth status` could not be read), the badge names the client, **Claude CLI**, instead of **Native login**. Confirmed subscription (`Max`, **Subscription**) and API labels are unchanged.
- **macOS onboarding:** the subtitle says OpenClaw *can* reuse Claude Code, Codex, or a key and checks for a reply before using it. The progress line no longer claims to check CLI logins. Result rows already show the Gateway’s detail text and are unchanged.
- Codex semantics were checked in `openai/codex` `rust-v0.169.0` (the pinned app-server; `d32063f96c2d`), `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs:709-726`: File, Keyring, Auto, and Ephemeral credential stores. The presence or absence of `auth.json` proves neither a login nor a logout.

| Situation | Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code installed, no login | WebUI setup | Recommended | unchanged |
| Codex installed, no `auth.json` | WebUI setup | **Sign-in needed** | Detected |
| Codex `auth.json` / env API key / local server | WebUI setup | **Account ready** | Detected |
| Claude Code subscription or API confirmed | WebUI picker | Max / Subscription / API key | unchanged |
| Claude Code login origin unknown or unreadable | WebUI picker | **Native login** | Claude CLI |
| Tool or key detected (local Gateway) | macOS setup | “nothing new to sign up for” | “can reuse … checks that it replies” |

## Evidence

**Real detection data.** On the Studio, `detectSetupInference()` (the `openclaw.setup.detect` body) ran against base with fake `claude`/`codex` version scripts on `PATH`, an isolated `HOME` and state directory, and synthetic environment keys. It returned `claude-cli` (no `credentials`, recommended), `codex-cli` with `credentials: false`, or with `credentials: true` plus a synthetic `auth.json`, and `openai-api-key` / `anthropic-api-key` with `credentials: true`. Those exact candidate fields feed the WebUI captures below through the Control UI E2E mock Gateway. The picker captures use synthetic `models.authStatus` native-auth metadata, not a live Claude account.

Before = `origin/main` `cc849dd810e`; after = this branch. Same viewport, theme, and fixture data.

### Clean comparison

**WebUI setup: Claude Code and Codex installed, no login**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Codex shows Sign-in needed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d902ce02-3385-4611-aef7-a475187a0500) | ![After: Codex shows Detected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78f195e9-bbf8-4c4a-aa8e-807962ef26fe) |

**WebUI setup: environment API keys plus a saved Codex file**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: API keys show Account ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f04f157a-525e-44fe-858f-a7336b31962e) | ![After: API keys show Detected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8031dad-bd6d-4858-9eb1-8a00b608b863) |

**WebUI model picker: Claude Code login origin unknown**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Native login](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdbe00b7-030b-4a53-b03f-2c0543e58390) | ![After: Claude CLI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce7c5a3a-a0d3-455f-9a05-ff8a13a6aeab) |

**macOS onboarding: Connect your AI** (`OnboardingRenderTests` bitmap in `scripts/macos-health-render.sb`; no live Gateway, so detecting state)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: macOS copy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37d13a06-2e8e-4fdc-b42c-6459c099133a) | ![After: macOS copy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5bb4eee-bd55-4d69-8bf4-b5641fed75bd) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5496983-6701-4303-9e47-e56a6f5e1fbc) | ![After annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c034248-fb17-4fe9-a086-974cdda95ad1) |
| ![Before annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cd4742d-0da5-4b7c-b7aa-43e5495c59d7) | ![After annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac8b5f1d-d59f-4406-a3de-fb97e273f0b2) |
| ![Before annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7c4d681-267a-4855-bc6d-36246090cfd4) | ![After annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ec0d100-67f2-4cf3-97fd-029c59edd4ab) |
| ![Before annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba53aaf5-51f1-4b0f-a7b2-333724927836) | ![After annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aec972f-6376-4a04-a40e-fc6ad76013c9) |

The confirmed-subscription (**Max**) and API (**API key**) picker badges were captured in the same run and are identical before and after.

**Tests**

- New setup-list case in `ui/src/pages/model-setup/view.test.ts` and the updated native-origin cases in `ui/src/lib/model-provider-auth-label.test.ts` fail on base (`Sign-in needed`, `Native login`) and pass on this branch.
- Focused unit tests for model setup, auth labels, runtime labels, chunking, and the chat picker: green.
- Control UI E2E: `chat-claude-native-auth` and `model-setup` (green).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline change), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (inventory updated), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed UI files, and `git diff --check`.
- macOS: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests`, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (clean).
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, `cc849dd810e` → `6dc094a9285`, P0–P2): no findings.

**Not verified locally (left for CI):** full `tsgo` and the UI project typecheck, repo-wide checks, and the macOS native test suite, which must run in the disposable `macos-swift` runner. The new macOS caption still needs translation from the native localization sync. The subtitle was already unlocalized before this change.

<details><summary>Out of scope / follow-ups</summary>

- The macOS chat **Model sign-in** sheet (shared `OpenClawKit`) lists Claude CLI native auth as **Connected** because `models.authStatus` reports native entries with `status: "ok"`, including when Claude Code’s status could not be read. Fixing that changes the Gateway status contract and the shared iOS code.
- Claude Code `third_party` auth (Bedrock/Vertex) maps to the API billing kind, so the picker heading says **API key**. This is rare and was left unchanged.
</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): report host live-session refusals as host limits, not provider rate limits
prs.body:
## Problem

When a Claude CLI conversation cannot get a warm process because the host has no room for another one (16 busy live sessions, or less than 1 GiB free memory with only busy sessions to close), the live-session registry refused the turn as a `rate_limit` failure with a synthesized HTTP 429.

That one wrong fact had two visible effects:

- **Text.** For the session limit (no code), the chat reply and the WebUI failure card said `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.`: the provider was blamed for something the host did.
- **Retry policy.** CLI run settlement treats `rate_limit` as a provider fact, so both refusals put the conversation's saved Claude login into a rate-limit cooldown. A later message could then be refused for the cooldown (and a successful fallback could make the session prefer the fallback model) even after memory or a session slot was free again. The host-memory copy said "try again after active conversations finish", but the policy said "the provider is limiting you".

#192534 kept the `rate_limit` category on purpose and named it as a limit; this PR fixes it at the producer.

## Solution

- `cli-live-session-registry.ts`: both local refusals are now `FailoverError`s with reason `overloaded`, **no HTTP status**, and a code naming the cause: the existing `cli_live_session_host_memory` and a new `cli_live_session_limit` for the 16-session cap. `overloaded` keeps the original behavior that the turn can fail over to another model, and the existing policy never records it against a saved login (`resolveAuthProfileFailureReason`) and never makes a session prefer a fallback (sticky fallback is `rate_limit`-only). No provider request had been sent, so failing over does not replay work; this is unchanged from before.
- `failover/error.ts`: the two refusal codes keep their host-authored copy beside them (`CLI_LIVE_SESSION_REFUSAL_TEXT`, read by `renderFailoverCodeUserCopy`). New copy for the session limit: `⚠️ This host is already running as many sessions as it allows, so it could not start another one. Try again after active conversations finish.` The host-memory copy is unchanged.
- `agent-runner-failure-reply.ts`: for an `overloaded` failure, a host-authored failover code renders its own copy before generic "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" text (the cooldown code keeps its existing path), so the reply text and the policy describe the same cause.

A real provider 429 is unchanged: it stays `rate_limit`/429, cools the saved login down, and shows rate-limit copy.

## Impact

Gateways that use a warm CLI runtime (today Claude CLI). In the WebUI chat and in channel replies, a host refusal now explains the host and suggests waiting for active conversations; the saved login stays usable for the next message. One explanation reaches the reply and the run-failure card (the card's notice is the same reply text; the existing transcript projection already keeps the toast from repeating a failure shown by the card).

The macOS onboarding model test is not affected: its setup probe runs with an auth-binding callback, which never takes a warm live session.

No config, schema, protocol or stored-state change. `overloaded` is an existing failover reason; the codes are diagnostic strings on the existing error.

## Evidence

New `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-capacity.test.ts` drives the real producers (the registry's memory admission and its 16-session cap; a real CLI 429 through `createCliExitFailoverError`) into the real consumers: `settlePreparedCliRun` (saved-login cooldown) and `handleAgentExecutionError` (chat reply text and the run-failure card notice), for both the Control UI and channel routes. No provider calls.

| Case | Base (`2aca1a1c159`) | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host memory refusal | `rate_limit`/429; saved login cooled with `rate_limit`; text: host-memory copy | `overloaded`, no status; no cooldown; same host-memory copy |
| 16-session limit | `rate_limit`/429; saved login cooled with `rate_limit`; text: "The AI service needs a short break…" (Control UI and channel) | `overloaded`, no status; no cooldown; host session-limit copy |
| Provider 429 | `rate_limit`/429; cooled; rate-limit copy | unchanged |

The new test fails on base for both local cases (reason/status and saved-login cooldown for each, plus the session-limit copy on both routes) and passes on this branch. Updated `execute-plugin.test.ts` host-memory expectation (`overloaded`).

Focused runs (green): `cli-live-session-capacity`, `execute-plugin`, `cli-live-session-registry`, `host-memory`, `agent-runner-failure-reply`, `failover/user-copy` tests; oxfmt on the changed files; line-cap ratchet; `git diff --check`.

Left to CI: full `tsgo`, type-aware oxlint (locally it starts by rebuilding the plugin-sdk package, so it was stopped), and the broad suites.

No UI component changed, so there are no screenshots; the WebUI card renders the reply text shown above.

prs.title: fix: connect AI without being asked about conversation history or memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connecting your first AI used to come with history decisions. In the Control UI and the macOS app, the AI setup screen asked whether to show existing Claude Code and Codex conversations. Then, as soon as onboarding continued, a dialog offered to import memory from other coding agents. Someone who only wanted a working model had to decide what to do with their personal history first.

## User Impact

User impact: you can connect an AI without being asked about conversations, session copies or memory. Login records nothing beyond what it did before. Fresh installs keep native conversation discovery off, and a saved discovery preference stays as it is. When you want these features, they remain in Settings: **Appearance → Session sources** to browse native conversations in place, the sidebar catalog menu to copy a session into OpenClaw, and **Memory → Import memory** to migrate memory. Each one still shows its source and effect and can be cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Control UI (`ui/src/pages/model-setup`):** removes the "Find existing sessions" section. Activation and provider sign-in no longer send `nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled`.
- **macOS (`OnboardingAISetupView.swift` and its model):** removes the matching "Show existing native conversations" checkbox and stops sending that parameter.
- **Onboarding mode (`app-shell-view-state.ts`, `onboarding-memory-import-solid.tsx`):** removes the automatic memory import dialog, along with its strings, styles, test and retention scene. The voluntary `/memory-import` page stays unchanged.
- **Gateway behavior:** unchanged. When the Gateway still needs a first-time choice (`nativeSessionCatalogPreferenceRequired`) and no choice arrives, it already records "off" (`resolveSetupNativeSessionCatalogPreference`). When a preference is already saved, no consent is required and nothing is written. So a login never turns on discovery and never overwrites an existing choice.
- **Kept on purpose:** the Gateway protocol fields `nativeSessionCatalogs`, `nativeSessionCatalogPreferenceRequired` and `nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled` stay. prs.title: fix: avoid a Gateway restart when removing a saved model login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removing a saved model login can prompt the operator to restart the Gateway even though the credential was removed. The config rebuild can be canceled when the credential change retires an individual model owner during database preparation.

## User Impact

The Gateway can finish applying the change and refresh model authentication in place when these operations overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Database preparation follows the lifetime of the config rebuild that owns it. The existing generation checks still prevent publishing retired model snapshots, and the same rebuild processes the credential change before publishing the replacement. Owner-scoped builds still cancel when their owner retires.

## Evidence

Three CI failures showed an added logout `warning` field after the prepared-model rebuild aborted following config commit. The new regression pauses database preparation, delivers the credential change, and checks that the rebuild publishes a current snapshot. [CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44766012493/job/136392052494)

`git diff --check` and `node --check` passed for the touched files. Codex autoreview of the local change against `dacf5604e469` reported no P0–P2 findings. Local E2E, red/green regression execution, lint, typecheck, runtime timing, and repeat runs were unavailable in this checkout. PR CI will supply runtime proof.

prs.title: fix: fill each plugin category preview when installed plugins are hidden
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub picks up to eight plugins per category. Control UI then hides installed plugins, including disabled ones. On one real gateway this left Channels with three installable plugins and Models with one, although ClawHub lists more than 200 in each category.

## User Impact

When the registry supplies a continuation cursor, the Plugins page fills short previews with the next installable plugins in the same ranked order (pins first, then downloads). The overview appears immediately. Registries without cursors keep the previous behavior. The [companion ClawHub change](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4867) is merged; production did not return cursors when checked on November 20.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI knows which plugins are installed; ClawHub owns the ranking. The Gateway requests an optional `previewCursor` on each overview category and passes it through `plugins.catalog.browse`. The client asks for the next page only when a category has fewer than eight available entries. Installed IDs never go to ClawHub. Continuations are limited to two concurrent requests, three pages per category, and 32 requests per overview. View all, Search, Featured and Trending keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Real Control UI in Chromium against a mocked Gateway and synthetic catalog. The first comparison uses base `5458e9614f17` and the initial fix, with the same fixture, viewport and crop (1440 × 1180, light). This is not a live Control UI–Gateway–ClawHub run.

### Clean comparison

![Before: Channels shows three plugins and Models shows one](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebcca46c-7b06-4ab4-82ab-3ed1247e429a)

![After: Channels and Models each show eight plugins; Memory is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19dabf7-4918-4842-8d2a-3277c2d5e3e8)

[Annotated before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a66e81e7-35ed-4e35-ac52-161831aaa29e) · [Annotated after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9569b40e-53d6-45aa-9f3c-4b5d627507a6)

### Loading state

A category reserves only the missing card slots while its next page is pending, even if all its initial candidates are installed. Loaded cards stay visible. If the continuation fails or runs out of results, unused slots collapse once and the page keeps the available cards.

[Clean loading state: before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd01e48f-c184-4953-9da8-fedeaf3b3dd5) · [Clean loading state: after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1070441-5d71-405c-ae8d-09fd5288976f)

![Before the layout repair: Memory begins 320 px above its settled position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eebd266e-1d13-48ed-adf6-8cbaa91b1243)

![After the layout repair: placeholders reserve the final section positions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bbcb077-bd14-4ad0-8014-74e4611b4aa5)

Chromium layout-shift scores during two sequential refills. Paired values are for one / zero initial Models. The loading screenshots isolate the layout repair before main's artwork update; post-integration browser checks confirmed stationary headings in all seven cases.

| Width | Before repair | After repair |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 400 px | 0.1237 / 0.1719 | 0 / 0 |
| 820 px | 0.1461 / 0.1846 | 0 / 0 |
| 1280 px | 0.0740 / 0.1114 | 0 / 0 |
| 1440 px | 0.0689 | 0 |

At 1440 px, Memory moved down 320 px before the repair and stayed fixed afterward. At 400 px, reserving two summary lines makes short rows less dense: the settled Models and Memory headings sit about 96 px and 192 px lower, respectively.

### Validation

Results below are for the current head, which merges main `c56a9d40e77`.

- 207 Plugins unit tests and 34 Chromium tests passed: 25 Plugins, 5 plugin-skill preview, and 4 first-visit asset-budget cases. UI typecheck, controller guard, lint, stylelint and formatting passed for the changed files. The catalog (37), Gateway plugins (32) and management-service catalog (39) suites passed.
- Stylesheet budget: the previous head added 122 B of raw CSS against an allowance of 64 B, so `control-ui-performance` failed. Two responsive rules re-declared visibility that the base grid already provides. Removing them makes the stylesheet 107 B smaller than main (1783393 B to 1783286 B in the same-toolchain comparison). The seven sparse-shelf cases at 400, 820, 1280 and 1440 px record the same heading positions and visible counts as before the removal, with zero layout shift.
- Skill reader: main now loads the reader on demand (#202795), so this PR no longer touches it. An earlier head carried an equivalent change, which was dropped in the merge. Cold visits use 55 requests on `/plugins` and 54 on `/settings/plugins` against the unchanged budget of 56.
- The published source tree matches the locally tested tree. Production verification is outstanding: the live overview returned zero cursors across 22 categories at the November 20 check.

prs.title: fix(android): connect through HTTPS proxies requiring Basic login
prs.body:
Related: #162240; related recovery report: #173578.

## What Problem This Solves

Android cannot sign in through an HTTPS reverse proxy that requires HTTP Basic, even when browser access works. A direct-LAN setup code does not supply the proxy-authenticated user identity, and the app can hide the useful rejection behind a generic reconnect message.

## User Impact

Adds a separate proxy-login control to manual and QR/setup-code onboarding and saved-Gateway editing. Credentials are encrypted and limited to the confirmed HTTPS destination. Android CA trust and hostname verification remain required; an existing certificate pin is additional.

For per-user access, the proxy must validate Basic credentials, strip its Authorization header, and forward the authenticated identity on HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades. GitHub is not required. Gateway roles and pairing remain server-owned. Proxy credentials never enter Gateway token/password fields or setup codes.

Password rotation preserves pairing. Switching proxy usernames requires Forget and re-add; Forget clears local credentials/cache, not server pairing or server history. Image requests retain proxy authentication without falling back to a Gateway Bearer token; an ingress-only proxy that cannot authenticate the upstream HTTP route can leave images unavailable.

This is Basic support, not browser-only SSO/OIDC, per-account proxy Bearer tokens, a new Gateway authentication mode, or a local-account database.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing ingress-authorization and secure-preferences owners, one shared setup-confirmation component, and the existing image loader. Failed credential writes preserve saved Gateway authentication and drafts. Recovery distinguishes node connectivity from operator sign-in and handles both AUTH_VERIFIED_USER_REQUIRED and AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED with trusted_proxy_user_missing.

The simplification removes decorative assets, duplicate design material, unrelated client-side setup-expiry plumbing, proxy-specific retry/pairing timers, and the separate favicon RPC rewrite. Existing Gateway expiry and reconnect policies remain in charge. The current-main integration preserves fingerprint-entry recovery and structured method diagnostics; the unrelated Doctor repair is already upstream and is no longer part of this diff.

Original implementation by @DonnieFi. Earlier repair and native verification with @IWhatsskill.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/220c0918-a800-4d03-9de9-76bfe07ee90d)

- [Earlier native Android verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0c87876b-823a-435d-a74e-59e628d7e6ab)

## Evidence

**Unverified candidate: Android build/tests, Kotlin lint, fresh native screenshots and an installable APK remain outstanding. Do not treat the earlier evidence below as proof of this candidate.**

- Published head: `fae0c5d322b8b59d971071870797b90195716ede`. Updated against main at `a81218e17a0bed096972ea4b47de9eba62fb72fd`; all four reported conflicts were resolved.
- Current diff: 26 files, 1,629 changed lines; tests and fixtures account for 445 changed lines, counting additions plus deletions. The earlier PR was 41 files / 3,880 changed lines against its then-base. The test reduction reuses existing fixtures instead of removing production behavior.
- ClawSweeper’s Kotlin compilation finding at the previous head is repaired: the Basic realm quotes are escaped. The remote one-line repair and co-author credit were read back; this is not yet a successful compilation claim.
- GitHub has not executed this head’s CI: [run 44939646031](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44939646031) is held with `action_required` and needs repository workflow approval. This is separate from security-sensitive merge approval.
- Unexecuted regression tests cover Basic/Gateway credential separation; missing/rejected login; verified TLS, hostname, pin and redirect boundaries; no image-read Gateway-Bearer fallback; atomic storage/rotation/account binding; partial Forget; saved-Gateway failures; onboarding cancellation/restoration/draft preservation; and both verified-identity rejection shapes.
- Native string generation/verification and git diff --check passed. Android proof preflight could not start Gradle: the sandbox has no working JDK or Android SDK. No Android test execution or APK build is claimed.
- Auto Review could not start because its installed helper was unavailable. Independent review preparation did not produce a complete review. No clean review is claimed.

prs.title: fix: finish remote OpenClaw ID sign-out when the claw doesn't answer in time
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-593 (found by the OCF-333 staging proof). Companion loader PR: https://github.com/openclaw/claw-loader/pull/46

## What Problem This Solves

On a claw opened remotely through OpenClaw ID, **Sign out of OpenClaw ID** can leave the tab blank for good. This happens when the claw's loader doesn't answer within 10 seconds, for example while the Gateway is frozen or unreachable. The loader hides the page as soon as sign-out starts, so the Control UI's "Sign-out was not confirmed" error appeared in a page nobody could see. The OpenClaw ID session also stayed signed in.

## User Impact

User impact: when the loader doesn't answer in time, the tab now goes to the loader's signed-out page instead of staying blank. With the companion loader change, it then continues to the OpenClaw ID sign-out. Nothing claims the claw confirmed the sign-out.

## Why This Change Was Made

When its 10-second deadline passes, remote sign-out now opens `/_loader/?stay=1&end_issuer=1` instead of throwing. That page belongs to the loader, so it shows only what the loader recorded.

- With the companion loader PR, a signed-out browser continues to OpenClaw ID's sign-out page.
- A loader without it just shows "You're signed out".
- A loader that never received the sign-out ignores the parameter.

When the loader does answer, nothing changes. The loader PR also makes it answer within the deadline when the Gateway is frozen, so this path is the fallback. Each PR is safe to merge alone. The experimental-features doc now says what happens when the claw can't confirm sign-out.

## Evidence

**Live staging proof** in an isolated test container. The isolated Gateway and Control UI were built from this head (`89ccb0ab`; a later commit changes only the docs wording), against real OpenClaw ID, Discovery and relay staging, with a throwaway claw and synthetic accounts.

| Gate | Chromium | WebKit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **This PR alone** (deployed staging loader, Gateway frozen with SIGSTOP during sign-out): the tab moves to `/_loader/?stay=1&end_issuer=1` and shows "You're signed out"; no claim of server confirmation. The issuer session stays active, as expected, because the deployed loader has no `end_issuer` support | PASS | PASS |
| **With claw-loader#46** (Gateway frozen): the tab reaches OpenClaw ID `/logout`, the issuer session ends, the loader reply is `gatewayConfirmed:false` after about 9.05 s | PASS | PASS |
| OCF-333 normal sign-out gate with claw-loader#46 (all 13 steps) | PASS | PASS |

Before this change (OCF-333 run on `main`), the tab stayed blank for more than 60 s and the issuer session stayed active.

The full report and browser evidence are kept privately by the maintainer and are available on request.

**Focused tests:**

- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/remote-sign-out.test.ts` has a new case: a loader that never answers. It failed on `main` (unhandled "Sign-out was not confirmed" rejection) and passes here.
- `remote-sign-out.test.ts` and `account-menu.test.tsx` pass (32 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files are clean.

**Review:** an autoreview found no P0–P2 issues.

prs.title: fix: keep session durability faults scoped to their session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-creation durability tests can reject an unrelated model-catalog database commit while injecting a failure into the session's initial-input commit. This makes the idle-commit-refused case report two injected failures instead of one and obscures the durability behavior being tested.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Developers get a fault-injection test that targets the intended session while still checking that unrelated catalog writes persist. No migration or configuration action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope the refusal hook to session-actor-admission publication facts for the exact test session. Add a deterministic regression that commits a real independent catalog update inside the input-command interval, then verifies the catalog persisted and the original session failure/persistence assertions still hold.

## Evidence

- Deterministic original-hook regression: red with the catalog-save warning and two refusal hits. Same regression with the scoped hook: green; unrelated catalog content persists and the intended refusal still occurs once.
- Actual Linux Node 24.22.1 run: all nine selected durability/fault and committed-input cases passed; the separate concurrent-create test was intentionally excluded from this targeted fixture proof.
- Targeted gateway-server typecheck, file lint, formatter, and git diff whitespace checks passed using a physically contained frozen install. No lockfile or dependency changes.
- pr-simplify and test-audit completed. Canonical local autoreview (OpenClaw engine, through P3) reviewed the final local snapshot against base 346078f73f1935f278eed581fc3d85fbbb1da633: scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review follows the ready PR.
- Reviewed patch SHA-256: 83ee7dec3a426d4b34b87f75a3c981da0e414ec5a291f514723cc8b1f5d7cdc9. Current main adc087617bb418d85823139dec790df5d990900e still has the original hook and has no changes to this test since the reviewed base.

**Separate unresolved failure:** the original concurrent-create RPC timeout is not fixed or cleared by this PR. One bounded actual-Node diagnostic with communication/title siblings passed (18 passed, nine fixture cases skipped); both create replies arrived in about three seconds. The original failed process lacks the phase/worker/host telemetry needed for causal attribution. Passing replay is not a fix; this PR neither relaxes the deadline nor changes that test.

Maintainer-directed release-validation repair; limited to the demonstrated fixture interference. No diagnostic instrumentation is included.
