prs.title: feat: OpenClaw ID protocol for unlinking a claw from its own computer
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-281 (part 1), sub-issue OCF-600

## What Problem This Solves

An owner who wants to take a claw off OpenClaw ID for good has no way to do it. The only option is an operator script with a Cloudflare token, so the claw's address, members and relay access stay behind.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. This adds the signed statement, the Discovery endpoint contract and the error that the Gateway, Discovery and the loader use to unlink a claw from its own computer (follow-up PRs).

## Why This Change Was Made

Unlinking follows the owner-reset rule that the person at the machine wins: the Gateway signs `ClawUnlink { claw_id, binding_seq }` with the Gateway key (K_gw) of the current binding.

- `verifyClawUnlink(statement, binding)` (Discovery): K_gw of the stored binding, same claw, exactly the stored `binding_seq`. Lower is `rollback` (replay, old binding), higher is `not_yet_valid`, and an older K_gw after a rebind is `wrong_signer`.
- `verifyClawUnlinkForPin(statement, pin)` (loader, apps): signed by the K_gw the pin stored, for the pinned claw, not below the pin's `binding_seq`. Only a verified unlink may clear a pin. An unverifiable one keeps the pin, so Discovery cannot use a fake `unlinked` to wipe a client.
- `unlinkClaw` `POST /v1/claws/{claw_id}/unlink` with a new `statement` auth class: no bearer and no request signature, because the statement is the credential. The Gateway can store the signed statement as a pending unlink and send it after its link is cleared. Part 2 (OCF-597, unlink from OpenClaw ID home) can accept an R- or owner-device-signed `ClawUnlink` on the same endpoint. The docs say what part 2 must add for owner-device evidence.
- Error `unlinked` (410) carries the stored `unlink`, so a pinned client can verify it.
- The Gateway refuses to unlink while a moved or reset binding is not yet published (`binding_unpublished`), because Discovery accepts an unlink only for the binding it stores.

Added to v1-draft in place, like owner reset (`docs/versioning.md`, "Claw unlink"). Existing statements and vectors are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 34 files, 280 tests pass. They cover the regenerated fixture, the `unlink` verifier vectors (forged signer, other claw, replayed older binding, never-published binding, bad signature, signature under another type's domain) and `unlink_pins` (pinned K_gw, later binding, forged signer, pin without `k_gw`, other claw, older binding, bad signature, cross-type).
- `tsc -p packages/openclaw-id-protocol/tsconfig.portable.json`, oxlint (type-aware) and docs formatting are clean.
- Autoreview (isolated Astra review): no P0. P1 (an unlink signed during an unpublished rebind could never be accepted) is fixed with the `binding_unpublished` rule. P2s (no bad-signature coverage; part 2 owner-device evidence understated) are fixed. The cross-type vector is built without a type assertion (assertion-safety ratchet).
- Consumers: Discovery and claw-loader PRs vendor this branch's head (linked from OCF-602 and OCF-603). They must be re-vendored from main after this merges.
- End-to-end proof across Gateway, Discovery, loader and relay with this protocol at `dc3ad1d47c42`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201779#issuecomment-7010058386 (23 of 23 steps passed). It covers a K_gw-signed ClawUnlink accepted, a replay answered `410 unlinked`, a forged signer refused (`wrong_signer`), and pinned loaders verifying the served `unlink` and clearing their pins.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(subagents): wake a yielded requester for each ready child result
prs.body:
## Problem

A requester that calls `sessions_yield` after spawning several completion-mode subagents was woken only when every member of the frozen yield batch was ready. A sibling that keeps running, or that pauses on its own `sessions_yield` while a background command runs, held every finished result back.

Production incident (2026-11-21): a dashboard parent spawned 3 children and yielded at 16:20 IST. Two children finished at 16:26:58 and 16:29:41 with reports that needed a decision. The third kept cycling through exec-yield and resume. The Gateway log has no `announce:requester-settle:…` run for that parent. The parent ran again only at 18:32, when the user typed into the chat. A copy of the state database shows why: both finished rows were `terminal`/`ok` with `delivery.status: pending` and a pending `requesterSettleWake` (`batchRunIds` = all 3, `rearmGeneration: 1`). The third row was still `running`. The gate in `subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts` returned `false` unless every frozen member passed `isRequesterSettleMemberReady`. #200967 had already made an exception for siblings that wait for a message. An exec-yielded or running sibling is the same bug class.

## Change

Rule: every ready result wakes the yielded parent. Siblings that are still working keep their wake, with the same `rearmGeneration`, and wake the parent again when they finish. Each result is delivered once.

- **Settle wake:** removed the all-or-nothing gate and the message-wait exception (`isEndedSubagentMessageWait` is deleted). The wake delivers the ready members of the frozen batch as one partition, and lists the members that are still working. A member whose partition has already started dispatch records its own batch, so a later partition never offers it again. When a partition holds only results that were already delivered and siblings are still pending, it settles without a redundant wake.
- **Wake message:** a partition that leaves members pending no longer says "every subagent has settled… do not call sessions_yield again". It names the siblings that are still working (label, task name or run ID, at most 5, each truncated) and tells the parent: if the request needs those results, call `sessions_yield` to wait; otherwise act on the ready results without reporting the batch as finished.
- **Lifecycle failure path:** `offeredBatch` now offers only ready members, so failure settlement can never consume the wake of a sibling that is still running or exec-yielded.
- **Yield transfer:** when a child ended before the yield and a sibling is still running, `afterRelease` now schedules the settle for the finished child. Before, nothing woke the parent until the sibling ended.
- **Followup owners** (`sessions_send` wait-for-reply, `agent-step`, nested `agent-run-subagent`): the caller is waiting for a single reply. Only the partition that leaves no member pending continues the followup. Earlier partitions wake the session as ordinary settle turns. `successor()` accepts that last partition as a subset of its cohort, so it no longer throws and records the result as a permanent failure.
- **Automation authority:** a yield that carried cron-management authority keeps it for the partition that leaves no member pending. Earlier partitions run without borrowing it, and settling them shrinks the retained cohort instead of discarding the authority.
- **Silent waits:** while siblings are still working, the parent may stay silent (`NO_REPLY`) and wait. Such a turn is not treated as a missing visible reply, so it is not retried.
- **Goal return:** an earlier partition leaves the Goal cohort when it settles. The partition that settles the cohort last resumes the Goal once.
- `isRequesterSettleMemberReady` moved to `subagent-run-liveness.ts`, its only owner, and replaces the deleted message-wait predicate.
- Docs: `tools/subagents/announce.md` and `concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`.

Product decisions, under the rules "no stranded user" and "no false done":
- A stopped child is a settled outcome, so its report now wakes the parent right away instead of waiting for its siblings.
- A followup caller gets one reply, after all results are in. The session itself is still woken for each result.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts`, real registry, lifecycle, yield tool and wake entry point): spawn 2 children, yield, finish one, keep the other exec-yielded. The parent is woken with the finished result, and the wake names the working sibling. The sibling's continuation then wakes the parent again with only its own result. A sweep adds no third wake. A second case covers a child that ended before the yield, while the requester's turn held it.
- Base `eb7ca3d33375`: both cases red (`expected [] to have a length of 1`: no wake).
- Head: both cases green.

**Owner tests:** cron authority (`requester-cron-authority.test.ts`: the early partition neither borrows nor consumes the authority, and the last partition is admitted with it), followup partition (`subagent-announce.requester-settle-followup.test.ts`: early partition runs with no followup successor, last partition carries it). Goal partition (`goal-continuation.test.ts`: early partition does not resume the Goal, last partition resumes it once).

**Updated tests that asserted the all-at-once rule:** `requester-settle-cross-turn` (paused member), `subagent-control.worker` progress card (one wake per result; the card retires once), `requester-wake-settlement` (stopped child).

**Real-Gateway E2E**, incident shape. Scratch `ocx src` Gateway under `env -i`, OpenAI `gpt-5.5` on the OpenClaw runtime. Parent spawns `alpha` (replies at once) and `beta` (`exec` with `background: true` running `sleep 90`, then `sessions_yield`), then yields.

| | alpha ended | first parent wake | beta yielded | beta ended | second parent wake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 19:47:10 | **19:48:53** (one combined run, after beta) | 19:47:13 | 19:48:50 | none |
| head | 19:40:08 | **19:40:11** (`announce:requester-settle:…:<alpha>:yield-1`) | 19:40:12 | 19:41:55 | 19:41:59 (`…:<beta>:yield-1`) |

The parent's replies on head were `alpha: ALPHA-RESULT-7`, then `alpha: ALPHA-RESULT-7 / beta: BETA-RESULT-9`. The live Peanutto launchd pid and `openclaw.json` hash did not change.

**Live sibling suites** (`subagent-yield-pause`, `subagent-followup-yield`, `subagent-yield-resume`, real OpenAI `gpt-5.5`): the same tests fail on base `eb7ca3d33375` and on this branch, with the same assertions (missing `completion.resultText` after a resumed or paused child completes, a Gateway shutdown timeout, an interim reply in the follow-up watch case; follow-up-yield failed 2 of 2 on base). One run of this branch showed a parent that wrote its final report as soon as the first result arrived; the wake message now says to keep waiting when the request needs the remaining results, and that failure no longer appears. The real-Gateway restart e2e files (`test/gateway-*-restart*.e2e.test.ts`) fail locally on base too (11 of 26 on base, 9 of 26 here, same assertions).

**Gates:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files. Every test file in `src/agents/subagents` and `goal-continuation.test.ts` was run across the unit-fast, infra, agents-support, spawn-boundary, core-isolated and e2e projects. Two infra tests failed once under host load and passed when run alone, on head and on base.

## Size

Production code is +96 / −56. The gate, the message-wait exception and its predicate are deleted. The added lines are the partition support the old gate did not need: pending members in the message, the followup last-partition rule, Goal cohort shrink, and pre-yield scheduling, and cron-authority cohort shrink. A census of `batchRunIds`, `requesterYieldBatch`, the frozen branch and `selectConnectedSettledSubagentWave` found every remaining reader still in use. v8 coverage could not attribute lines under the compiled-worker test runner (0 files collected in two attempts), so the census was done by reading the code.

## Accepted edge cases

- If a Goal cohort's last partition is rejected for an unrelated reason (for example, a rearm-generation mismatch), the Goal return stays retained until Stop or a lifecycle rotation. That is the same outcome as a failed final delivery today.
- A nested requester whose early partition answers without yielding reports that answer to its parent. The later result wakes it again as a separate completion.

## Merge danger

- **Two-way door.** No schema, stored-row or config change: the wake rows keep their existing fields and generation. A revert restores the all-at-once wake for every cohort, including rows written while this change ran.
- **Blast radius:** requesters that yield on two or more completion children (dashboard, chat and nested subagent requesters). A defect here would show as an extra or a missing wake for the parent, not as a lost child result: every result stays saved in its child session.

prs.title: fix: say "signed out" when an OpenClaw ID browser signs out
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-595

## What Problem This Solves

When you sign out of OpenClaw ID in a browser, the Gateway closes that browser's connections. It closed them with the same reason it uses when an owner removes a member: `1008 "removed from this claw"`. The Control UI and the Gateway log then said the browser was removed from the claw, when it had only signed out.

## User Impact

User impact: a signed-out browser now sees and logs "signed out of OpenClaw ID". A removed member still sees "removed from this claw". Sign-out still keeps membership and leaves other peers connected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection-close effect now takes a cause. Remote sign-out passes `signed-out`. The Gateway then closes with the internal reason `openclaw-id-signed-out` and the message `signed out of OpenClaw ID`. Membership removal and owner expiry keep `openclaw-id-removed` / `removed from this claw`.

The close code stays `1008`. I checked every client that reads the close code or reason, and none needs a separate code:

- Control UI (`ui/src/app/gateway-store.ts`) shows the Gateway's close reason as-is in the disconnect message. Its `1008` handling does not look at the reason text.
- claw-loader (`src/loader/states.ts` `CLOSE`, `sw.ts`) matches tunnel-session close codes (`not_a_member`, `revoked`, ...), not Gateway WebSocket close frames. It relays those frames to the page without reading them. The loader needs no change.
- Native Apple and Android clients do not compare against `removed from this claw` or `openclaw-id-removed`. The macOS "Removed from …" copy comes from its own removal record, not from the close frame.

## Evidence

- New unit test: closing with the `signed-out` cause invalidates only the signed-out peer's connection, with `{ reason: "openclaw-id-signed-out", code: 1008, message: "signed out of OpenClaw ID" }`. The removal test now also pins the removal message.
- The remote sign-out route test now requires sign-out to close with the `signed-out` cause.
- Both tests fail on the base commit and pass with this change.
- The other `closeConnections` consumer tests (membership, member role, tunnel API, owner expiry) still pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` and oxlint on the touched files are clean.
- Not run: a live staging sign-out. The issue was found by the OCF-333 staging proof, and this fix only changes the close reason.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/openclaw-id/removal-effects.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/remote-signout.test.ts   # base: 5 failed; fix: pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/openclaw-id/{removal-effects,remote-signout,service.membership,authority.member-role,tunnel-api,owner-expiry}.test.ts   # 44 passed
pnpm tsgo:core
```

</details>

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: keep the first setup and chat free of automatic side panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone who had the Home side panel open on an earlier visit (or in the macOS app's saved window state) and then sets OpenClaw up again gets that panel imposed on them: Home opens beside the model setup page and the onboarding conversation, and after **Exit setup** the first chat opens with an empty Ask OpenClaw panel docked on the right plus the community promotion card in the sidebar. The first conversation starts cramped and full of things that do not help connect or chat.

## User Impact

User impact: during first-run setup and the first chat it opens, the side panel stays closed until the person opens it from the menu, button, or Mod+Shift+H. The chat shows the agent, the composer with attachments, connection status, help, and the rest of the app; the community card waits for the next open. Saved panel preferences are not rewritten, so an established user who reopens the app gets their panel back.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell records one fact when it shows a first-use setup route (`/settings/model-setup?firstRun=1|explicit` or `/custodian?onboarding=1`, the same markers the first-run redirect and onboarding already use). For the rest of that page:

- the assistant dock does not restore its saved open state and does not auto-minimize the onboarding conversation into the dock when setup ends (by a real reply that hands off, or by Exit setup); an automatic close request does not overwrite the saved choice;
- any explicit open or close (menu, sidebar Home button, shortcut, palette, plugin activation, update-failure triage) works as before and releases the hold;
- the sidebar does not show the community invitation.

Home availability still follows `chat.history` (`isHomePanelAvailable` is unchanged), and send errors, setup errors, and the channel nudge stay visible. The macOS app hosts this same UI; no native code changes.

Accepted edge: the quiet state lasts for that page (window) session. Reloading in the middle of the first chat restores the saved preference; on the default first chat (`/chat/main`) Home is already the page's own conversation, so it stays closed there anyway.

## Evidence

Scenario: a saved `open` Home dock preference, then first-run model setup → onboarding (one real turn) → Exit setup → first chat, against the mocked Gateway at 1280×800, dark theme. Before = `origin/main` @ cc849dd810e; after = this branch.

### Clean comparison

**Model setup**

**First chat after Exit setup**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: empty Ask OpenClaw panel and community card in the first chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63a76c07-8e33-4252-8e57-a19ca3fac314) | ![After: first chat with only the conversation and composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e131730-81f1-4a63-8b49-c0d39427688d) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Home panel opening on its own during setup highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5e0e7b0-6bc3-4701-b537-051b9e68b906) | ![Setup without a panel highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f7a1ab4-3779-4d97-9552-3ac436b22abe) |
| ![Automatic Ask OpenClaw dock and promotion in the first chat highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f5f58f8-a6ca-4a8a-b6cc-c0cebd2e3245) | ![First chat without panel or promotion highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f9dcdb1-33fa-48b6-b47b-f9c08345612c) |

Behavior checks (new `ui/src/e2e/first-use-home-panel.e2e.test.ts`, red on `origin/main`, green here), run for the web app and with the macOS web-chrome host flags:

- setup and onboarding: side panel closed despite the saved `open` preference;
- first chat: no side panel and no community card; composer and **Add attachment** present; `/help` shows the command list without sending; a rejected `chat.send` stays visible as **Not sent**; the saved preference is byte-for-byte unchanged;
- reopening on another session restores the open Home panel (established preference);

prs.title: fix: let people choose their AI during first-run setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the dashboard's first-run setup opens (the macOS fresh-install handoff and the WebUI onboarding route), it immediately asked the Gateway to set up AI on its own. With two detected options, opening the screen already picked one, ran a live test, and — if that failed — moved on to the next provider, and could even install the Codex plugin. The person never chose an account, provider, or billing route.

## User Impact

Opening first-run setup now only shows the AI access the Gateway detected; nothing is installed or turned on. The person picks one. If it fails, the card names the failed choice and offers **Retry** (same choice) or the other options; setup never switches by itself. **Set up automatically** keeps the previous ladder for anyone who explicitly asks for it. Existing configured models are kept exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The custodian setup card now reads `openclaw.setup.detect` (read-only) on open, the same detection the native macOS AI page and Model setup already use. A configured model still goes through `openclaw.setup.auto`, which only reports it (including the shared Codex login notice). A chosen option uses the existing `openclaw.setup.activate` with its detected `modelRef`, so activation cannot drift to another model. The automatic ladder (`openclaw.setup.auto`) is unchanged on the Gateway and runs only from the explicit **Set up automatically** button. After ChatGPT sign-in, setup re-reads detection instead of re-running the ladder.

Offered options follow the native macOS rule: primary-model candidates whose credentials are not definitively logged out, recommended first. No Gateway, protocol, or config changes.

Accepted edge case: if the model is removed between the detect and auto reads on an already configured Gateway, `setup.auto` would pick one. This needs a concurrent config removal within milliseconds on an onboarding screen; it is named in a code comment instead of guarded.

## Evidence

Scenario: two detected options (Codex, Local model), no configured model. Before = `main` at dacf5604e46; after = this branch. Captured with the Control UI E2E mock Gateway (synthetic data, native macOS setup capability emulated as "This Mac").

prs.title: fix(macos): open the agent chat after verified primary model activation
prs.body:
## Problem

In the macOS app's native setup sequence, a fresh primary-model activation that passed its live test finished by opening `/custodian?onboarding=1`: the OpenClaw setup assistant with **History** and **Exit setup**, a channel nudge and a "what next" card. The user had to pick "Talk to your agent" before reaching the conversation they set up the model for.

Base behavior on `main` (99b756206cd): `OnboardingView.finish()` sent every non-existing completion to `.custodianOnboarding`; `OnboardingDashboardHandoffTests` and `OnboardingAISetupTests` (`managed Gateway restart…`, codex-cli fresh primary) asserted exactly that.

## Change

- The verified completion now carries its destination by activation role:
  - fresh **primary** activation → `.chat`
  - **utility-only** activation → `.custodianOnboarding` (OpenClaw help, which already routes a utility-only setup to add a primary model); a utility model never enables the main chat
  - verified **existing** model → `.dashboard` (unchanged)
- `.chat` uses the existing `AppNavigationActions.openChat`: native windows go through `WebChatManager` (composer focuses on appear), the dashboard preference goes through `DashboardManager.show` with the existing `__openclawComposerFocus` route hint. Session and agent come from the activated Gateway's server lease (`mainSessionKey` + `defaultAgentId`), fenced by the existing primary/lease checks.
- The role comes from the same verified result that binds attempt, model and server (`ActivateResult.verifies`, owned completed receipts, provider-auth reconciliation). `finishConnected` no longer has a default destination, so every completion path chooses one explicitly.
- Removed the now-unused `verifiedExistingInference`.
- Docs: `start/onboarding.md`, `platforms/macos.md`.

### Preparation that only lived in the setup assistant

Checked what `/custodian?onboarding=1` does after a native activation:
- `openclaw.setup.auto` returns `configured` without changes once `setupComplete` is true.
- The onboarding welcome only proposes the consent-gated `setup` operation when the config has no authored setup; app-managed Gateways have Gateway auth, so they get the navigation guide (talk to agent / channels).
- Workspace bootstrap and the hatching ritual run on the agent's first real turn (`ensureAgentWorkspace`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`), not in the assistant.
- Channels, memory import and macOS permissions are optional, consent-based and remain in Settings.

No essential step is skipped, and no consent decision is applied automatically. The assistant's "Wake up, my friend!" hatch draft is not prefilled; the composer opens empty and focused.

### If the window fails to open

`finish()` marks onboarding complete and retires the owned activation receipt before opening, as before. A failed open shows the existing chat/dashboard error; the menu bar icon reopens OpenClaw and nothing re-runs activation. The new handoff test asserts the receipt is gone after finishing.

## Evidence

Control UI e2e with synthetic Gateway fixtures (mock gateway; synthetic welcome text), 1280×860, the two destinations the dashboard window opens. Before = `main` route `/custodian?onboarding=1`; after = this branch's route `/chat/main?__openclawComposerFocus=1`. Asserted: before has History=1, Exit setup=1; after has History=0, Exit setup=0, exactly one composer, and `document.activeElement` is that composer. The native SwiftUI chat window was not captured (native app runs are not allowed on the operator desktop).

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: setup assistant with History and Exit setup after activation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b928e28-7145-43f9-85af-9686921ceca6) | ![After: main agent chat with a single focused composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8638f87d-d0de-4aba-aba0-ac59009572e9) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Setup-assistant chrome and next-step card highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d57b498e-f6ae-4c31-9ba3-ffac7430f019) | ![Main conversation header and its one composer highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1e066fc-c97f-4cc0-991f-a54502a93088) |

## Verification

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests`: app and test targets compile.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: clean.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Tests updated or added (run in the `macos-swift` CI job; the native launcher refuses operator desktops):
  - `OnboardingDashboardHandoffTests`: real detect → activate through a fake Gateway, finish once → `.chat` (primary) / `.custodianOnboarding` (utility); receipt retired; cold-launch completed receipts keep the role destination.
  - `OnboardingAISetupTests`, `OnboardingUtilitySetupTests`: role → destination mapping for claude-cli / existing-model / api-key, restart-reconciled codex-cli.
  - `WebChatDocumentRouteTests`: focus-only route search.

Pending: native test execution in CI; full `tsgo` and repo-wide checks left to integration.

Out of scope: Linux/Windows. The Control UI's own model-setup first-run page (`?firstRun=1`) is handled separately in #202593; no file overlap.

prs.title: fix(ui): open the configured agent's chat after first-run model setup
prs.body:
## Problem

After first-run setup in the Control UI verified a primary model, `FirstRunSetup.completeNavigation` always opened the setup assistant at `/custodian?onboarding=1`. Someone who started from the web entry never landed in the chat of the agent they had just configured. Reaching it through the bare chat route can restore whichever conversation was open last, including the last-route restore in the macOS app's embedded shell.

## Solution

- `completeNavigation` now resolves the configured agent's main session from the identity the Gateway advertises in `hello.snapshot.sessionDefaults` (`defaultAgentId`, `mainKey`, `mainSessionKey`, scope). It goes through the existing `resolveUiConversationIdentity` owner, using the activation owner's agent, and opens the session with `openPreferredApplicationSession`. That selects the exact session and navigates to its exact path (for example `/chat/<agent>`), never the bare `/chat` route. Nothing hard-codes `agent:main:main`.
- Utility-only activations still hand off to the setup assistant (`/custodian?onboarding=1`).
- Unchanged: the activation receipt lifecycle (it survives Gateway restarts and reloads and is cleared only at the single handoff), the explicit **Open setup agent** action, deep-link and first-run landing rules, remote-profile receipt binding, and the "Continue setup" path for an already-configured model.

## Impact

- Affects the WebUI and the macOS app's embedded Control UI. Linux and Windows are not in scope. The native Swift onboarding handoff (`OnboardingDashboardHandoff`) is unchanged.
- A primary-model activation no longer opens the onboarding assistant view automatically. That view carries the optional "Reach OpenClaw outside this app" channel nudge. It still opens for utility-only setup and through its explicit route, but people completing primary setup on the web won't see that nudge by default anymore.

## Evidence

- **Base reproduction** (main `dacf5604e46`): the new e2e test `opens the chosen agent's main chat after a web-entry activation reloads mid-handoff` failed with `expected '/custodian' to be '/chat/atlas'`. The scenario opens an earlier `agent:atlas:dashboard:*` conversation, enters through `/`, activates a candidate that requires a Gateway restart, and reloads mid-handoff.
- **With the fix:** the same test passes. The reloaded page lands on `/chat/atlas` and shows that agent's main transcript, not the earlier conversation. It makes 1 `setup.verify` call and no further `activate`/`wizard.next` calls, so the model is applied only once. The receipt is cleared.
- **Unit:** `ui/src/pages/model-setup/**`, `ui/src/lib/sessions/route-navigation.test.ts` and `ui/src/app/native-route-memory.test.ts` pass (185 tests + 2 browser tests).
- **E2E (mocked Gateway, bundled build):** `model-setup-reconnect`, `model-setup-cancel`, `custodian-channel-onboarding`, `model-setup-recovery`, `model-setup-explicit`, `model-setup-activation-feedback`, `model-provider-login`, `custodian-auto-setup` and `initial-connect-splash` all pass, with one exception. `initial-connect-splash` › "keeps finalized recording pixels intact…" is a synthetic `setContent` video check that fails the same way on unmodified main on this host, so it is unrelated.
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and `git diff --check`. The full `tsgo` and repo-wide gates are left to CI.
- **Visual (synthetic fixtures):** after an activation that required a restart plus a reload, main lands on the onboarding assistant (`/custodian?onboarding=1`). This branch lands on Atlas's main chat (`/chat/atlas`). The screenshots were shared in the review thread; embedding them here is still pending.

## Not covered

- No live proof against a real isolated Gateway with a real provider. The proof uses the mocked Gateway e2e harness.

prs.title: fix: stop automatic updates from retrying the same failure every hour
prs.body:
Related: #202954

## What Problem This Solves

When an automatic update keeps failing the same way before it changes anything, the Gateway tries the same release again every hour, indefinitely. On #202954 every automatic update since 2026-11-03 was refused with "Gateway process changed during maintenance drain"; the install built up about 330 failed runs, each spending about 10 minutes of validation and a ~1.9 GiB state snapshot while the Gateway kept serving normally.

## User Impact

User impact: an automatic update that keeps failing identically now backs off instead of retrying hourly forever: it retries after 1 hour, then 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours, then once a day. The Gateway log names the next attempt time and the next step. A new release, a successful update, or a manual `openclaw update` resets it. Two identical activation failures still pause automatic updates for that release, as before. No config change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The campaign already reads the newest update-run records to pause after two identical activation failures (Doctor, post-update verification, Gateway startup on the new version). Refusals before anything changes never matched that rule, so they had no backoff at all. This extends the same history-based streak to every identical failure for the same release, using the failure's reason code when there is no activation signature. The run ledger stays the only record; no new state or config. The root cause on #202954 was fixed separately by #203152; this removes the unbounded retry cost for any future identical refusal.

<details><summary>Alternatives and retention check</summary>

- Rejected a doubling counter in `update.checkState`: a second owner for a fact the run ledger already records.
- Rejected gating at campaign announcement in `update-startup.ts`: it would duplicate the history read the apply path already does.
- Retained updater runtimes do not pile up: each retention attempt reclaims older marked runtimes (`maintainRetainedUpdateRuntimes`, `repair: true`) before creating its own. The candidate state snapshot is per attempt, so the cost was repeated work, not a leak.
- Production change is in `src/infra/update-startup-auto-run.ts` (+44/−25, part of it the reflowed history read); docs in `docs/install/updating/automatic-updates.md`.

</details>

## Evidence

- New tests seed identical `managed-service-stop-failed` automatic runs under a fake clock and probe just before and after each wait: 1 failure keeps the hourly cadence, 2 waits 2 h, 5 waits 16 h, 6 waits the 24 h cap, and a new release starts immediately. Three of the four fail against the current code (the 1-failure control passes on both) and all pass with the fix.
- The existing activation-pause matrix still passes unchanged; the campaign-run file passes 20/20, and the four related update-startup test files pass 99/99.
- Core typecheck, type-aware lint and formatting are clean. Autoreview came back scoped-clean and a separate independent review found nothing after one test-ordering gap was fixed.

prs.title: ci: add fixed Linux Gateway cold-turn calibration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The performance workflow has no fixed hosted lane for comparing the Gateway's settled memory, first-turn memory peak, and first streamed answer latency. Same-build trials on a separate Linux runner showed up to 56.9 MiB of paired cold-peak variation, so a hosted baseline is needed before enabling a 25 MiB regression gate.

## User Impact

Maintainers can dispatch `gateway-cold-turn-calibration` against an exact OpenClaw revision. The mock workload records the measurements and links them to the packaged build and Kova revision in the workflow artifact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mode reuses the existing Kova workflow setup on Ubuntu 24.04. It publishes run-scoped artifacts, with the Kova verdict and raw bundle retained for investigation. It verifies the build commit and successful cleanup for every repeat. The mode is for measurement and has no regression threshold.

## Evidence

The workflow shell fixtures verified mock-only routing and rejected a mismatched build, missing repeats, and cleanup failures. A failed command with an emitted report still bundled its evidence. Actionlint and the scoped shell check passed. The scoped autoreview identified a missing failed-run bundling path, which the fixture now covers.

- [Kova scenario and Linux evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/Kova/pull/277)
- [Exact workflow smoke against a pinned OpenClaw revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44937107662)

The final revision completed three repeats on one Ubuntu 24.04 worker. Every repeat captured the same ready Gateway's settled RSS at +120 seconds, its active cold-turn peak and the first streamed answer, then destroyed its environment. The packaged OpenClaw SHA and the merged Kova pin matched the receipt, and teardown removed the local runtime.

| Measurement | Observed range | Spread |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Settled Gateway tree RSS | 1,356.0–1,367.6 MiB | 11.6 MiB |
| Observed cold-turn peak RSS | 2,189.5–2,249.2 MiB | 59.7 MiB |
| First streamed answer | 3,670.6–3,809.5 ms | 138.9 ms |

All three receipts retain the original Kova scenario verdict. The measured cold-peak and first-answer spreads exceed the proposed 25 MiB and 100 ms cutoffs. This lane collects calibration evidence with regression enforcement disabled.

- [Final hosted calibration and artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44938217312)
- [Passing PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44938244206) and [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44938244152)

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

When a queued Telegram answer drains without the original dispatcher, the answer can arrive as a standalone message. For example, if message 11 arrives while message 10 is being processed, the recovered answer should reply to 11 when the chat's reply policy permits it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queue admission now records which channel issued the inbound message ID and the turn's effective threading policy. During delivery, channels without a transport-specific resolver use those facts to prepare the reply target. Channels that resolve their own reply references continue to receive the routing context at send time.

## User Impact

A recovered Telegram answer can reply to its triggering message. Explicit reply targets and opt-outs still work. Routing WebChat output to Telegram leaves gateway IDs out of platform reply references, and Tlon can keep its configured thread root. Older queue entries with ambiguous message origins retain their previous delivery behavior.

## Evidence

Validated against upstream `a3357794fa56`. The two regression suites on unchanged upstream produced five failures and 46 passes. One failure showed that the dispatcher-less final lost the queued Telegram message ID.

The same regression test ran on upstream and on this change. It supplied a synthetic admitted follow-up with no dispatcher and exercised the production reply decision, origin routing, SQLite-backed durable delivery and Telegram sender. The loopback Bot API recorded exactly one unquoted `sendMessage` in each run. Upstream failed the final reply-target assertion. This change passed.

| Telegram message that triggered the queued answer | On upstream | With this fix |
|---|---|---|
| `11` | The HTTP request omitted both reply-target fields. | The HTTP request included `reply_to_message_id: 11`. |

The affected threading, queue admission, and delivery suites passed **311 tests across 8 files** (136 in the infra project and 175 in the auto-reply project). The separate HTTP regression passed **1/1**. Formatting, the repository's line-cap check, and `git diff --check` passed.

A contributor previously exercised a real gateway restart against a stub Telegram API. The authenticated Telegram Test Server run requested in review remains pending. The QA broker credentials are unavailable to this fork. [Earlier gateway restart evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142470#issuecomment-5594377607) · [Review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142470#issuecomment-5590977736)

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the dispatcher-less Telegram HTTP check</summary>

Save the following file as `extensions/telegram/src/followup-http-proof.test.ts` in a dependency-ready checkout. Run it first at `a3357794fa56` and then at `2868e23fef3e`. The test uses the repository's local Telegram HTTP fixture.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/followup-http-proof.test.ts --pool=forks
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  createTestRegistry,
  resetGlobalHookRunner,
  resetPluginRuntimeStateForTest,
  setActivePluginRegistry,
} from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-test-runtime";
import { withOpenClawTestState } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-state";
import { telegramPlugin } from "./channel.js";
import { useTelegramHttpFixture } from "./send.telegram-http.test-support.js";
import {
  createAccounting,
  createDefaults,
  createSettledExecution,
  createTurn,
} from "../../../src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test-helpers.js";
import {
  resolveFollowupDeliveryDecision,
  deliverFollowupDecision,
} from "../../../src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.js";

describe("Telegram queued final on the origin route", () => {
  const fixture = useTelegramHttpFixture();
  it("sends the queued final as a native reply to the triggering message", async () => {
    await withOpenClawTestState({ prefix: "queued-http-proof-" }, async () => {
      resetPluginRuntimeStateForTest();
      resetGlobalHookRunner();
      setActivePluginRegistry(
        createTestRegistry([{ pluginId: "telegram", source: "test", plugin: telegramPlugin }]),
      );
      const cfg = {
        channels: { telegram: { ...fixture.cfg.channels.telegram, replyToMode: "all" as const } },
      };
      const turn = createTurn({ config: cfg });
      Object.assign(turn.queued, {
        originatingChannel: "telegram",
        originatingTo: "123",
        originatingChatType: "direct",
        originatingReplyToMode: "all",
        messageId: "11",
        messageIdChannel: "telegram",
      });
      Object.assign(turn.queued.run, { messageProvider: "telegram", config: cfg });
      const text = "QUEUED_FINAL_142470";
      const decision = await resolveFollowupDeliveryDecision({
        turn,
        execution: createSettledExecution(text),
        accounting: createAccounting([{ text }]),
      });
      expect(decision.kind).toBe("deliver");
      const defaults = {
        ...createDefaults(async () => {
          throw new Error("unexpected dispatcher");
        }),
        opts: undefined,
      };
      await deliverFollowupDecision({
        turn,
        defaults,
        decision,
        runId: turn.runId,
        runFollowup: async () => {
          throw new Error("unexpected retry");
        },
      });
      const sends = fixture.requests.filter(
        (r) => r.method === "sendMessage" && r.fields.text === text,
      );
      expect(sends).toHaveLength(1);
      const params = sends[0].fields.reply_parameters;
      const native = (typeof params === "string" ? JSON.parse(params) : params)?.message_id ?? null;
      const legacy = sends[0].fields.reply_to_message_id ?? null;
      const observed = native ?? legacy;
      console.log(
        JSON.stringify({
          transport: "loopback Bot API",
          dispatcher: false,
          triggeringMessage: 11,
          method: "sendMessage",
          nativeReplyTarget: native,
          unquotedReplyTarget: legacy,
          replyTarget: observed,
        }),
      );
      expect(observed).toBe(11);
    });
  });
});
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(android): Talk button demands a realtime provider on a native Talk setup
prs.body:
Fixes #189985

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android Talk button says to configure a realtime provider when Gateway Talk is already system/stt-tts, and composer dictation fails with a generic error when the on-device recognizer cannot start.

## User Impact

User impact: a native Talk setup can start from the Talk button without a realtime provider. If the on-device dictation engine fails before any speech is heard, the composer tries the platform recognizer instead of stopping on "Dictation failed." Realtime Talk still asks for its provider. A no-speech result, or an error after speech has started, is not retried on the other engine.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Talk button was using realtime catalog readiness before it looked at `talk.config`. Native routes, including system/stt-tts, no longer inherit that gate. A failed config read does not fall back to demanding a realtime provider. Composer dictation still prefers the on-device recognizer, then uses the platform recognizer only when that engine is missing or fails before speech starts.

This is the Android admission path for #189985. It overlaps the Android files in #165481 and does not change the gateway talk catalog.

## Evidence

- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayTalkSetupReadinessTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatDictationControllerTest`: 18 tests in each class, 0 failures.
- `:app:ktlintMainSourceSetCheck` and `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck` passed.
- The readiness tests cover system/stt-tts, native fallbacks, realtime relay, a failed config read, and an unresolved route.
- The dictation tests cover an on-device client error before speech, an error after speech starts, an unavailable on-device engine, and a no-speech result.
- No emulator or phone pass. The dialog needs a gateway already set to system/stt-tts, and that config was not changed.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: perf(cron): compile narrow automation validators
prs.body:
## Outcome: STOP — do not merge

The frozen trial completed all 20 children and 220 measured cycles. It failed the predeclared rule: **100 of 256 aggregate cells were adverse; 55 met the 20% STOP threshold.** Only two of four required median RSS wins passed. This candidate is rejected and is being closed unmerged. No samples were replaced, thresholds changed, performance reruns requested, or regression waiver applied.

Complete numerical evidence, including every raw child value, all 256 aggregate cells, all 640 paired deltas, and arm/paired spread:

- [40-job evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203232#issuecomment-7067753518)
- [1,000-job evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203232#issuecomment-7067756890)

### Observed result

| Metric | 40 jobs: A → B | Change | 1,000 jobs: A → B | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median RSS after cold grace | 341.6875 → 344.855469 MiB | 0.927154% | 379.425781 → 338.453125 MiB | -10.798596% |
| Median RSS after warm grace | 396.769531 → 431.496094 MiB | 8.752326% | 530.699219 → 472.257812 MiB | -11.012152% |
| Median sampled maximum RSS | 411.683594 → 446.007812 MiB | 8.337524% | 547.28125 → 491.417969 MiB | -10.207417% |
| Median overall wall time | 22187.5345 → 18540.976223 ms | -16.435167% | 20483.355204 → 21653.212735 ms | 5.711259% |
| Observed maximum overall wall time | 23231.228771 → 20795.190006 ms | -10.486052% | 21144.618107 → 27315.261688 ms | 29.183046% |
| Median overall process CPU | 10928.925 → 8357.516 ms | -23.528471% | 11290.474 → 11096.985 ms | -1.713737% |
| Observed maximum overall process CPU | 13439.302 → 10503.383 ms | -21.84577% | 12303.317 → 14198.895 ms | 15.407048% |

The 40-job size had 20 adverse cells, including 5 STOP cells. The 1,000-job size had 80 adverse cells, including 50 STOP cells. The larger fixture used less RSS but increased median overall wall time by 5.711259% and its observed maximum by 29.183046%. The smaller fixture's median RSS after warm grace increased by 8.752326%. These are observations from five pairs per size; they do not establish the persistent cause of any individual timing difference. They are sufficient to reject this candidate under its frozen rule.

### Collection integrity and terminal failure

All 33 declared stages exited zero without timeout, signal, or forced termination. The four preparation children and 20 measured children passed the complete oracle, compiled-entry and observed-start checks. Source, dependency, and generated-output seals matched before/after in both arms. All prepared/copied fixtures and compile caches were removed, both temporary arm checkouts were removed, and the staged runtime was removed. The report records `complete=true`, `error=null`, and `cleanupUnknown=false`.

The original collector and native command **exited 1**: after writing and closing the complete archive and printing `PERFORMANCE_FINAL`, line 527 called `sys.exit` without importing `sys`. That terminal bookkeeping error is preserved. The native command subsequently joined and explicitly released its workspace owner. Independent verification accepted the complete recorded data after checking all archive hashes, external declaration bindings, exact stage/sample order, final seals, normal child cleanup, and native join. The controller is not relabeled as an exit-zero run, and this failure was not used to replace samples.

- Archive: 1,993,261 bytes; SHA-256 `9b1cc58de2aa0115a3a4619f08997cecc511b74353070c88852a7228b16a767c`.
- Report SHA-256: `0f4d40630c10a33b1f946f65b068f4165c760ec572d666a5468e0827cd24b678`.
- Frozen analysis: 393,816 bytes; SHA-256 `c02a7d9abde57725708505401146a5dd2a2af7e84df47863ea6c118924c13bba`.
- Declaration SHA-256: `9a373c7064ad37091d6a1a3a4f5449be686340226934a927e9ce4bf7fa2c33af`.
- Native failed-command capture SHA-256: `1ba4382d71a70a0d4c6e636e3963d80679eec701806fc0c20b7adf789f1dc562`.

Normalized dependencies matched across arms: 117,184 entries, 2,804,998,627 bytes, SHA-256 `639fafd534133fb2f6ed34e5f859d7aee68ab1f36c12551aee84ec88819b827b`. The declared exclusions are only `.modules.yaml` and `.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`; their individual per-arm hashes are recorded. Static relative-ESM cron worker closures were seven files in each arm: A 1,263,240 bytes, B 1,254,794 bytes. This 8,446-byte reduction is structural evidence, not an explanation of the measured RSS differences or a complete dynamic graph.

Both full builds passed with declaration generation enabled. The three nonfatal CSS warnings were identical in A and B: gzip 1,745 bytes over the fixed ceiling, raw CSS 5,927 bytes over, and largest CSS hard-ceiling headroom −289 bytes. Both also printed the same five budget violations (largest CSS, total CSS gzip/raw, chat boot request count, and chat boot gzip). These observed advisories already occur in the measured baseline. Build-log hashes: A `762dd41a3fb34a78150a269a7cfcf33bdd5d72381082e94c17f0e903df884dac`; B `ec32c2ca53eb8b8e0d3b0d49dbd3e79e16dd2c2725f370db4de9113195c6009a`.

### Diagnostic follow-up

In the 40-job warm-grace samples, median main-isolate heap used fell from 45.936630 to 37.699989 MiB and allocated heap capacity fell from 112.53125 to 105.78125 MiB while process RSS increased. Main-isolate external memory remained about 9.475 MiB. These counters do not attribute process RSS to a specific worker or native owner. Named follow-up: isolate retained worker, code, and native allocations before choosing another import optimization. No leak cause or worker culpability is established, and no diagnostic rerun is part of this rejected trial.

### CI and review disposition

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44936024642) completed with 62 successful jobs, 20 skipped jobs, and 3 failed jobs. `check-dependencies` flagged the three new generated declaration exports in the script-only Knip model; the declarations need the same application-owned treatment as the existing generated companions if this design is revisited. Its full-tree scan also flagged two Discord test-support exports. `check-docs` found 18 heading issues in `docs/releases/2026.11.5.md`; the aggregate CI gate failed with these checks. The docs and Discord files are byte-identical between A and B; that is source attribution evidence, not a separate baseline CI pass. The owned Knip finding remains unresolved because this performance candidate is rejected. No green-CI claim or waiver is made. The separate native CI watcher exited 13 because it could not attach; direct GitHub run/job results above are authoritative.

[The exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203232#issuecomment-7067420380) reported no actionable findings and requested the declared performance evidence. The completed trial supplies that evidence and rejects the proposed optimization. Any future import-boundary design requires a new declared experiment; this result is not a basis for a retry until green.

<details>
<summary>Frozen pretrial description and declaration — historical, preserved verbatim</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

Reading scheduled jobs loads the schema construction library and session schemas into the cron reader even though the reader only needs three validation checks. This adds eager work to automation reads and their cron workers.

## User Impact

Automation validation and stored data formats stay unchanged. This draft tests whether removing those imports reduces the memory used by real automation reads without increasing CPU use or latency. No measured benefit is claimed yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing static-validator generator now emits the three checks from their canonical schemas into an independent module. Four existing call sites consume that module, including the mutation-side access-program check. No new cache, configuration, schema version, public API, or handwritten validation policy is introduced.

The equivalence claim covers actual call-site normalization: persisted values cross JSON or structured-clone boundaries, and the automation-result parser copies the scalar result shape before validation. It does not claim that TypeBox's interpreter and compiler agree on arbitrary objects with inherited properties.

## Evidence

Generation and focused correctness passed on Node 24.22.1 and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork: 28 tests across four cron files and 24 tests across two wrapper-boundary files per runtime. The three parity tests were rerun after their lint-only correction. Core and cron-test lint/types, generator, formatting, and syntax checks passed. The full build, with declaration generation enabled, passed on source tree `dc1369d19b16be0bd61e871612631fbfed3d94e1`; subsequent changes affect only the benchmark. The final benchmark passed its affected script lint/type/format/syntax checks and four functional children: prepare plus a fresh 11-cycle child at each size. Every cycle matched the complete selected-store, Doctor inventory, history, and projection oracles; the canonical compiled worker path, observed worker start, and normal worker/broker cleanup passed. Both unused-file scans passed with zero entries. The final controller exited nonzero because that scan added 282 Jiti cache files (969,706 bytes) beneath `node_modules/.cache/jiti`. A separate read-only reconciliation excluded only those exact new files and reproduced the original dependency seal; compiled output and source seals stayed exact. The original failed final receipt is retained, rather than relabeled as a successful controller run. No paired acceptance trial has run.

Final functional/check receipt SHA-256: `7e99ca2ca6c094e9cce1aa1ff842002b6d3e77aa92b7f53a71268bdecd0164fb`. Cache reconciliation SHA-256: `c54eb9e4cb2e874648763a10daad781847bc46ba2b84fdc46f722f9d99110093`. The reconstruction restored dependency seal `c424b9a1fd86db086722c9df27a00a30c4122133bb51cf8bd63a1ecdea96ca42`; compiled-output seal remained `7a43221844557faa2f0a1d0528f4d3f6837215686ef7455bfc5de64e5bcb187f`.

The built cron reader has seven files totaling 1,254,794 bytes in its static relative-ESM closure, with no external TypeBox edge. This is a structural observation, not an RSS measurement or a complete dynamic-import graph. The build emitted nonfatal UI CSS warnings (gzip +1,745 bytes, raw +5,927 bytes, largest-chunk headroom −289 bytes); baseline attribution is pending the independent A/B builds.

The initial committed-range review and both benchmark-correction reviews completed with no findings, including the final signed head. It reviewed the changed source and benchmark with their unchanged caller, schema, compiler, and lifecycle contracts. Private collection orchestration was reviewed separately; source review does not establish a performance benefit.

Formatted scope: authored runtime −3 net lines; generated runtime +113 and declarations +13; generator +27 and wrapper inventory +1; existing benchmark +455 net; tests +150. Generated code replaces schema construction at the read boundary. The benchmark changes are verification tooling, outside the shipped runtime.

### Pre-run acceptance declaration

This pre-run declaration binds the signed candidate commit/tree, exact baseline, binary diff, committed benchmark hash, collection controller, and analysis program. No scored child has run; collection will begin only after this declaration is published and its live body is verified.

- A: `a757a08f5f2674d584d738c45393df495a9a47da`.
- B: signed commit `f579c811c9c45906f83c79fd94144e942af7d8a1`, tree `e3f159863383b615bc402c07578e6cd8e1c3daec`.
- Binary full-index diff from A to B, with external diff/text conversion/rename detection disabled: SHA-256 `a936a01690501864e198adc2dd76bc4d7151a5237e5bcec294b16f0cf33a73e0`.
- Committed benchmark SHA-256: `e31ca310b209c7512ed0c897bdb0e0d2576664db4960bb826fc4e475fc4d599d`.
- Collection controller SHA-256: `43a277273b21043e6d493533c7ad7e6f33a16495f377a491051eec42caf602be`; analysis SHA-256: `73d0d50024c3922d04e804adb914b703d1c5f76348d9d81e0a7d6a87e8abacbe`.
- Workload: committed `scripts/perf/cron-reader-reuse-measure.ts`, running native Node 24.22.1 against the actual `dist/cron/store/read-only.worker.js`.
- Sizes: 40 and 1,000 synthetic jobs. Each includes all three access-program values, persisted meaningful outcomes, and complete history records covering all five automation outcomes.
- Collection: five fresh-process pairs per size, alternating AB, BA, AB, BA, AB; 40-job pairs first, then 1,000-job pairs. Twenty scored children total; no replacements, dropped samples, adaptive order, or post-result threshold changes.
- Each child executes one cold cycle, five seconds of natural idle, ten warm-process cycles, then five seconds of natural idle. Each cycle performs selected-store reads, a real Doctor inventory, full history reads in batches of at most 200, and canonical history-result projection. Complete normalized outputs must match the prepared oracle at every cycle.
- Fresh-process does not mean cold filesystem caches. There is no OS cache flush. Fixture preparation and any functional qualification are excluded from scored children and may warm filesystem caches.
- Node options and execution arguments are empty. Each child gets a fresh `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` directory; `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` is explicitly empty. No source loader, inspector, forced observer GC, allocation profiler, or worker heap-limit change is used.
- Export resolution, bundle hashing, and fixture creation run only in preparation. Measured children consume the prepared export/worker metadata; the controller binds it to the selected compiled build and fixture hash. Operation clocks exclude output verification; cycle, phase, and overall clocks include it. Doctor's own worker/copy cost remains in the actual flow.
- The RSS sampler uses `process.memoryUsage.rss()` every 20 ms. Its maximum is a sampled maximum, not the OS high-water mark. Full memory fields are recorded at the two fixed grace boundaries. Natural production GC may differ between arms; it is not forced equal.
- Process CPU and RSS include the measured Node process and its worker threads. Separate broker/copy subprocess CPU and RSS are outside this measurement. Wall time still includes awaited subprocess work. This is component evidence, not whole-Gateway or device memory evidence.

### Frozen computations and decision rule

Each size is analyzed independently. For each of the 64 metrics below, calculate the median and nearest-rank p95 across the five child summaries per arm: 128 aggregate cells per size, 256 total. With five children, p95 is the observed maximum, not a robust tail estimate. Within-child warm summaries are computed before arm summaries; the ten warm cycles are not independent process samples.

| Metric family | Child summaries | Metrics per size |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Timed imports, cold phase, warm phase, overall work, cleanup | Wall, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each | 15 |
| Four cold-cycle operations | Wall, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each | 12 |
| Four warm-cycle operations plus complete warm cycles | Within-child median and p95 of wall, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each | 30 |
| Two natural-idle grace periods | Process CPU and main-thread CPU for each | 4 |
| Memory | RSS after cold grace, RSS after warm grace, sampled maximum RSS | 3 |

Primary success requires strictly lower B median RSS after both the cold and warm grace at both sizes: four required wins. Every one of the 256 scored aggregate cells must also hold or improve. Any adverse cell yields HOLD; an increase of at least 20% in any cell yields STOP. For positive A, the exact cutoff is `B * 5 >= A * 6` using decimal arithmetic, with no tolerance. If A is zero, B must also be zero; positive B is STOP.

Missing primary wins yield HOLD. Small adverse estimates are reported as uncertainty in this batch, not proof of a persistent product regression. No noise allowance, cost relabeling, rerun, or waiver is implied.

Publish all raw per-child values and all 640 paired metric deltas, absolute and percentage, with paired medians/ranges and arm spread. Zero-baseline percentages remain explicitly undefined. The requested five-second grace wall durations remain raw diagnostics and validity checks; they are not scored operation latency. Heap, external memory, array buffers, load, worker lifecycle, source/build/dependency identities, and module closure are diagnostics; they do not replace the scored RSS/CPU/latency gates.

Invalid oracle output, runtime/adapter/source/dependency drift, wrong resolved worker entry, missing observed cron worker start, missing cycles or grace samples, a grace shorter than 4,990 ms, timeout, signal, forced termination, or unproved owner/fixture cleanup invalidates collection. The same compiled resolver used by cron must return the selected compiled worker entry; lifecycle counters separately prove that `read-only.worker.js` started in the fresh child. These counters report script names, not full paths. Preserve complete raw evidence and report invalid collection separately; do not silently replace a failed child.

Both arms receive independently built outputs and normalized equivalent dependencies. Record source, generated-output, and dependency seals before and after collection, including explicit metadata exclusions. The native task owner must join; successful benchmark cleanup must close database handles, lifecycle singletons, retained native workers, and the broker. The controller removes only its exact prepared/copied fixture and compile-cache paths after known cleanup. Any uncertainty stops subsequent work and preserves the relevant state.

</details>

prs.title: fix(templates): Template Add creates an agent with a reserved system ID that cannot be deleted
prs.body:
Closes #196713

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Template Add creates an agent with a reserved system agent ID (`openclaw`, `crestodian`) when the Template declares one, and that agent cannot be deleted afterwards.

## User Impact

User impact: Template Add now refuses a reserved agent ID before creating anything, the same way `openclaw agents add` does, and the error says to choose another agent ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Add planner only checked for collisions with configured agents, and system agents are not configured entries. It now checks the same reserved list `agents add` uses and blocks the plan with `reserved_agent_id`. That covers the CLI and the Gateway, and both an ID from the Template and one passed with `--agent-id` / `agentId`.

An earlier revision renamed the agent to `openclaw-2`; following maintainer feedback it now rejects the ID instead.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep assistant actions below native window controls
prs.body:
Related: #162448

## What Problem This Solves

Home / Ask OpenClaw's right-docked panel can place its actions underneath the Linux desktop window buttons. With the regular navigation expanded and the window maximized, trying to close the assistant panel can instead close the app. This follows the reporter's [exact panel/layout diagnosis](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162448#issuecomment-6370618990), not the separate Side chat panel.

## User Impact

The assistant actions have their own click targets below the native caption row. The Linux/Windows right dock gives up 52px of height rather than squeezing its header, preserving space at the supported 320px minimum width. Existing zero-width caption tokens preserve web, macOS and fullscreen placement; bottom docking is unchanged.

**Native Tauri/WebKitGTK on X11 or Wayland is not verified.** The evidence below is Chromium with production Linux window chrome and synthetic Gateway/mocked Tauri commands, not a packaged-desktop test. Broad upstream CI is intentionally skipped while this PR is a draft; the focused fork proof ran in full.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixed-position assistant dock is separate from the shared headers that already reserve caption space. Its existing top inset now also respects the existing native caption-height/width tokens. No new state, platform detection, dependencies or header wrapper is needed.

## Evidence

[Successful before/after proof run](https://github.com/zackmsa777-a11y/openclaw/actions/runs/40709899627) on Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0:

- **Before:** the new regression fails specifically at `assistant-panel-caption-clearance` with the original CSS from `8889b596023c846cc9076078a000c25715f0ecf0`; setup failures cannot satisfy the proof gate.
- **After:** all **12 tests pass, none skipped**, across native-titlebar and assistant-toggle suites. The new flow covers expanded desktop navigation, maximize/restore, repeated close/reopen without native close, 320px panel width, bottom docking, mobile navigation, and independent native minimize/close actions.
- The proof candidate `a4095dd61ca7e304e00bf6ca6b3da2772ab93aa0` differs from this product commit `069ed9816926586fd203f8be9ff4b459818217e8` only by the fork-only workflow. That workflow and generated media are excluded from this PR.
- Inspected synthetic screenshots were also delivered in chat. No live account or model request was used.

| Before: caption buttons cover panel actions | After: separate caption and assistant rows |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: native caption buttons overlap assistant actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/412570c6-7191-495d-a1db-c8a374ee2137) | ![After: assistant actions are below the native caption row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e9b9a3e-4cca-449c-919a-9aacccc4d816) |

<details>
<summary>Focused checks, timings and review</summary>

Passed locally: targeted oxfmt, TypeScript oxlint, CSS stylelint, UI E2E typecheck, line/max-line ratchets, and `git diff --check`. Local Chromium could not launch in the execution sandbox, so runtime evidence comes from the linked fork Actions run.

Runtime command (with `--reporter=default --reporter=json`):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/native-desktop-titlebar.e2e.test.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/custodian-panel-toggle.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Baseline focused command: 34.00s wall (3.254s regression); repaired affected suites: 69.58s wall. Native-titlebar file: 34.486s test time, including the new 7.887s scenario; assistant-toggle file: 4.273s. Total proof job: 244 CI seconds including setup and both runs. Browser geometry, hit testing and real visible-control interactions are the owning boundary; a CSS/unit-only assertion would not catch covered click targets. Existing shared browser/server fixtures are reused.

AI-assisted implementation with independent source review; two fixture issues found during review were corrected before runtime proof. The separate local autoreview installation was unavailable. Simplification pass retained only the existing-owner inset and one regression scenario: CSS +9/-1, test +115/-2. No changelog changes. Broad upstream PR CI remains separate from this focused proof.

</details>

## Native Linux verification on November 21, 2026

I ran the production Control UI in the official OpenClaw v2026.11.6 Linux x86_64 Tauri package on Debian 13, WebKitGTK 2.54.0, X11 and Openbox. Both builds used base `8889b596023c`. The second build applied the exact assistant-panel stylesheet from this PR's head `069ed9816926`. The test used synthetic gateway data, expanded navigation, and a right-docked assistant panel.

| Window | Before the CSS change | With the PR stylesheet |
|---|---|---|
| Normal, 1280 × 900 | The native caption intercepted the centers of Open Home, Dock, and Close. | All five panel controls received pointer hits. Clicking Ask OpenClaw selected the tab. Clicking Close dismissed the panel and kept the same app window open. |
| Maximized, 1440 × 1000 | The same three buttons overlapped the caption. The center of Close assistant sidebar hit Close window. | All five panel controls received pointer hits. Clicking Ask OpenClaw and closing the panel again kept the same app window open. |

The center of the maximized panel's Close button moved from `(1418, 26)` to `(1418, 78)`. These measurements apply to the stylesheet in this PR. [Stylesheet at the tested head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/069ed9816926586fd203f8be9ff4b459818217e8/ui/src/styles/assistant-panel.css)

prs.title: fix: stop an update before installing when a running Gateway blocks its database migration
prs.body:
Related: #202700

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` must migrate a database, the new version's Doctor needs the Gateway stopped. A Gateway that the updater does not manage as a service keeps running through the update, for example a foreground `openclaw gateway run` under a custom `OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` profile, or one under an external supervisor. With such a Gateway, the update installed the new package and spent minutes on it. Doctor then could not get exclusive access, the final schema check failed, and the update put the previous version back.

## User Impact

User impact: an update that cannot migrate while that Gateway runs now stops before replacing anything. Its message names each database with its schema change (for example `38 -> 43`) and the Gateway PID, and says to stop the Gateway and rerun `openclaw update`. Updates that need no migration still run while the Gateway serves. A running service the updater owns is unaffected; the updater stops it, or under `--no-restart` its supervisor restarts it on the new package.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater already records each store's schema before activation. It now checks, right after its own service stop and before any package mutation, whether a live Gateway still owns the state while a store needs migration. A running owned service is exempt: the state lock allows only one owner, so that owner is the service. A stopped owned service does not exempt a separate foreground Gateway. That rule ("which stores must the candidate Doctor migrate") was previously inline in the final post-activation check. It now lives in one shared helper used by both checks, so the two can't drift. Both checks apply the same agent-store discovery and the same exclusion of retained (deleted-agent) stores.

Production growth (+121/−50) is required behavior plus that single shared rule. Managed-service admission would be a smaller place for the check, but it runs before candidate validation and before the updater's own stop. There it can't know which stores need migration, or whether a managed owner is about to be released. Activation after the stop is the one point where both facts exist.

## Evidence

Live on Crabbox Linux (AWS), using the reporter's setup: a custom `OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` profile, a foreground `gateway run`, and an external registered agent store restored from published 2026.11.6 at schema 38. Main `b8b06c4824f` was relabeled 2026.11.30/.31; this branch was built as 2026.11.29.

| Lane | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main → main, `--no-restart` | Reporter's failure reproduced: exit 1 after 163 s, `Agent database migration did not finish … expected schema 43, found 38`, rolled back to the previous version |
| fix → main, `--no-restart` | Refused in 138 s with `database-migration-owner-live`; no package replacement; installed version unchanged; Gateway still serving (`/readyz` 200); store still at 38 |
| same profile, Gateway stopped, rerun | Exit 0; new version active; store migrated to 43 |
| fix → main, default profile with a systemd user service (updater stops it) | Exit 0 in 228 s; store migrated to 43; `/readyz` 200, so no false refusal after the updater's own stop |

Regression test `admits activation only when Doctor can migrate` in `update-command-execution.test.ts` covers six cases:

- A live owner plus a pending migration is refused before mutation. This case is red on `origin/main` and green with the fix.
- With no owner, the update proceeds.
- With no migration needed, the update proceeds under a live owner.
- A retained agent store is excluded.
- A running owned service is exempt.
- A stopped owned service is not exempt.

Targeted typecheck (`tsgo:core`), oxlint, and oxfmt pass. Touched and consumer update tests pass locally, except the process-lane rows that require a built `dist` worker. Those rows fail identically on `origin/main` in a fresh worktree, so CI covers them.

The live lanes ran on `eff70f301bd`. Later commits only narrowed the exemption for running owned services. That change does not affect the custom-profile lanes, which have no owned verdict. The managed lane now skips a check that it previously passed after the service stop.

Reviews: autoreview is scoped-clean (P0–P2) on `022bf8a91d4`. Independent Codex read-only reviews found three problems, all addressed. Two are fixed here: retained agent stores were missing from the activation read, and a stopped owned service could exempt a separate foreground Gateway. The third is declined under the AGENTS.md compromises. It is a running managed Gateway blocked behind a foreground Gateway from another installation, which needs two Gateways on one state. That case keeps today's visible install-then-rollback, and proving which process owns the state would mean PID matching, which wrapper launchers break. CI is green on `022bf8a91d4`. Its last commit makes the native-maintenance test mock spread the real module, as the mock-exports ratchet requires.

Separate pre-existing issue observed, not changed here: a no-migration `--no-restart` update under a custom profile succeeds, but the foreground Gateway's self-restart then fails to load a lazily loaded chunk that the package swap removed.
