prs.title: fix: answer after tool-only turns when a context engine omits message timestamps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sometimes an agent runs a tool and then ends its turn without a final answer. A typical case is a reply of `NO_REPLY` to a `sessions_send` request that needs a result. OpenClaw then runs a short tool-free step to get the answer. That step crashed with `RangeError: Invalid time value` before it made any model call when the session used a context engine that adds messages without a timestamp. Lossless Claw adds summary, focus-brief and recall messages that way. The requester got no answer and the turn was logged as incomplete (incident run `bd2d3478-18a1-4ee0-b7db-43c2d83dd497`, 2026-11-19).

## User Impact

User impact: sessions that use a timestamp-less context engine such as Lossless Claw get a real final answer again after a tool-only turn, instead of an "incomplete turn" error. Ordinary turns send the same model requests as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-free step first trims the turn's messages to fit the model-context limit. To do that it builds temporary bookkeeping entries, and it gave each one a timestamp converted from its message's timestamp. A message without a timestamp made that conversion throw. Every entry now gets the same fixed timestamp. Nothing reads these timestamps: the trimming logic does not look at them, and the entries are never saved or sent to the model. Sizing and model input come from the messages themselves, so request bytes are unchanged.

Rejected alternative: filling in missing timestamps where the context engine's output enters OpenClaw. OpenClaw adds a time stamp to user-message text from the message timestamp, so this would change summary text the model sees. A current time would break the prompt cache, and a fixed time would show the model a 1970 date. A separate Lossless Claw change will add timestamps on the plugin side. This PR is the guard on the OpenClaw side.

Accepted risk: if a later change makes the trimming logic read entry timestamps, this path would give it the 1970 value. The new test checks the trimmed result, not just that nothing throws, so such a change would fail it. No other `new Date(x).toISOString()` call in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner` or `src/agents/harness` converts a timestamp taken from a message. The others use the current clock or validated dates.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`attempt-history-prepare.test.ts`, two cases). The tool-free step gets a summary-style user message with no timestamp, one with a `NaN` timestamp, and an exec tool call and result. With the default limit, all four messages reach the agent unchanged. With a tight limit, the large tool result is replaced by the usual omission notice while the timestamp-less messages stay. Both cases fail on `origin/main` with `RangeError: Invalid time value` and pass with the fix. Neighboring suites pass: `settled-turn-finalization`, `finalization-scope` and `attempt-prompt-phase` (79 tests). `pnpm check:changed` passes, including typecheck, lint and format.

**Real behavior on the Mac Studio.** Each commit ran in a Crabbox `local-container` lease launched on the Studio (`node:24.22.1-trixie`, image `sha256:f1e03497…`, 8 CPU / 24 GB) from a clone at the pushed commit. Each run used:

- a real isolated Gateway
- the real Claude Opus 5.5 model through ClawRouter, with a pass-through proxy that records request bodies and no headers
- a small test context engine that adds one Lossless Claw-style `{ role: "user", content }` summary message with no timestamp to every assembled context

I used a small test engine instead of Lossless Claw 40833c3 because it isolates the one trigger, missing timestamps, and needs no Lossless Claw database setup. The scenario matches the incident. A requester session asks the model to call `sessions_send` into a WebChat session. There the model runs one `exec`, then replies `NO_REPLY`, which the request does not allow.

| | base `f250a678` (lease `cbx_0c02ea0561f9`) | fix `5f3bb45b` (lease `cbx_b865184e14f8`) |
|---|---|---|
| Tool-free finalization step | crashed before calling the model | ran: one tool-free model request (0 tools, 3,811 bytes; the first message is the timestamp-less summary) |
| Target session's final answer | none (`payloads=0 tools=1`) | a plain-text summary of the exec result |
| What the requester got back | `NO_REPLY_RECEIVED error` | `REPLY: The exec tool ran 'echo settled-proof-01aca19e' once, and it returned 'settled-proof-01aca19e'. …` |
| Side effects | 1 exec | 1 exec (finalization had no tools and repeated nothing) |
| New warnings | 4 failure lines (below) | none; only the expected "running isolated finalization" line |

Base log, which matches the incident. Inside the container the `RangeError` text reads `Invalid Date` because the test runtime uses the OpenClaw Bun fork. Node says `Invalid time value`.

```
[agent/embedded] settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=a120535b-… — running isolated finalization
[agent/embedded] settled-turn finalization failed: runId=a120535b-… error=Invalid Date — preserving failed recovery
[agent/embedded] incomplete turn detected: runId=a120535b-… stopReason=stop … payloads=0 tools=1 replaySafe=no … — surfacing error to user
[context-engine] discarded unaccepted turn advancement: …: run ended without host acceptance
```

**Ordinary turns are unchanged.** I compared the three model requests whose inputs are the same in both runs: the ordinary turn, the requester's first request, and the target's first incident request. After masking per-run values (container hostname, lease workdir path, UUIDs, timestamps), the request bodies are byte-identical between base and fix, including the system prompt and tools. The raw size difference is 2 bytes in each case, all from the container hostname length.

**CI note:** the first `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` attempt on `5f3bb45b` ([job 135492776612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44504325040/job/135492776612)) failed before any test ran. Installing WebKit system packages timed out on the apt mirrors (`WebKit system packages did not download from the fallback archive mirrors (exit 124)`), and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed only because of that job. This was an infrastructure flake, not a failure inherited from main: recent `main` runs of the same workflow are green, and this PR touches only the embedded-runner file and its test. One rerun passed ([job 135515231051](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44504325040/job/135515231051)), and `ci-gate` for that run now passes.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

On the Studio, from a clone under `~/crabbox-src/sft` checked out at each commit:

```
crabbox run --provider local-container --local-container-image node:24.22.1-trixie \
  --local-container-cpus 8 --local-container-memory 24g \
  --local-container-volume ~/crabbox-proof/sft:/proof --allow-env CLAWROUTER_API_KEY \
  --no-hydrate --timing-json --shell -- 'set -eu; git rev-parse HEAD; \
  corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --store-dir .pnpm-store; \
  cp /proof/settled-finalization-timestamp.proof.live.test.ts src/agents/; \
  SFT_PROOF=1 SFT_PROOF_LABEL=<base|fix> SFT_PROOF_OUT=/proof/out OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
  src/agents/settled-finalization-timestamp.proof.live.test.ts'
```

Both runs exited 0 and both leases reported `"leaseStopped":true`. The proof harness is not committed. The API key was passed only through the environment.

</details>

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: let Windows Git installs use a folder directly under a drive root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows PowerShell 5.1, the installer's Git install failed whenever the checkout folder sat directly under a drive root, for example `install.ps1 -InstallMethod git -GitDir C:\ocg`. It stopped before cloning with "New-Item : The path is not of a legal form", because the installer tried to create the parent folder `C:\`, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects that even with `-Force`. Found by the daily update-reliability matrix on Windows Server 2025.

## User Impact

User impact: Windows users can install OpenClaw from Git into a folder directly under a drive root, such as `C:\ocg`, on the default Windows PowerShell.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer now creates the checkout's parent folder only when it does not already exist. A drive root always exists, so the failing call is skipped. Relative paths, missing parents, and a file sitting at the parent path behave as before.

## Evidence

- New Windows-only test in `test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts` resolves a checkout directly under the system drive with Windows PowerShell 5.1; it runs in the Windows CI scope for installer changes and is skipped elsewhere.
- Live on Windows Server 2025 with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Crabbox, AWS):

  | Check | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Resolve a checkout at `C:\openclaw-drive-root-checkout` | exit 1, `New-Item : The path is not of a legal form.` | exit 0, `C:\openclaw-drive-root-checkout` |
  | Full `install.ps1 -InstallMethod git -GitDir <drive root>\<folder> -NoOnboard` | exit 1 after 7 s, no checkout | exit 0, checkout cloned and built, `openclaw --version` runs |
- autoreview: scoped-clean ("patch is correct"). Independent read-only Codex review: no findings.
- Production change: +3/-0 lines in `scripts/install.ps1` plus one comment line.

prs.title: fix(proxy): make managed NO_PROXY support an explicit opt-in
prs.body:
## Problem

Managed routing ignores startup `no_proxy` and `NO_PROXY`. An operator may need a trusted internal service, such as a Kubernetes-hosted memory backend, to connect directly while all unlisted destinations still use the outbound proxy.

## Behavior

Set `proxy.useEnvNoProxy: true` to honor the startup bypass list in `gateway-only` mode. Lowercase takes precedence, loopback remains direct, and a standalone `*` is ignored. Native children inherit the same approved entries. The setting is off by default, and the `proxy` and `block` modes are unchanged.

## Evidence

- 44 focused OpenClaw config and managed-proxy lifecycle tests passed.
- The matching 2026.11.6 backport passed five local HTTP routing checks using the pinned router and config schema, including direct service access only with opt-in, proxying of unmatched destinations, strict modes, and wildcard refusal.
- Full upstream CI and a deployed Cognee run have not been verified.

Helm backport: https://gitlab.com/xrow-public/helm-openclaw/-/merge_requests/313

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

Verification on this head: skill-selection 8/8, audit-events + commands/audit green, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 7 — product upgrade run from published v2026.11.3 (head `a71b0be6d94`, no new commits; proof only)

- **Genuine release write**: ran the published v2026.11.3 source (release tag → `847611dcaa3`, schema v22) to create a state dir and record a legacy agent run through its production audit writer (`sequences 1–2, run release-run-1, user_version 22`).
- **New-build upgrade**: fresh `dist` rebuilt from PR source; the new Gateway booted the release DB with no schema refusal and migrated 22→40, release rows intact.
- **New skill write + shipped CLI readback through the running new Gateway**: production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` → observer → recorder → store (`skill.selection.observed`, shared sequence 4, `upgraded-run-1`), then `openclaw audit --run release-run-1 --json` returns the release rows and `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json` returns the new skill row with full attribution. Full redacted transcript kept with the run notes.
- Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked (local models stall at the reply watchdog; xAI needs the `xai` extension whose dist build fails on the pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` root resolution). The trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it is production code on live Gateways, now demonstrated across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary.



## Round 8 — P2 rollback fix + missing proof piece (head `d541860e07a`)

- **[P2] Clear schema readiness when lazy creation rolls back** (`src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — `ensureSkillSelectionAuditSchemaOnce` now binds the `skillSelectionSchemaEstablished` flag to the owning SQLite transaction via `stageSqliteTransactionState` (rollback/invalidate drop both the readiness flag and the warm row-count). A rolled-back lazy DDL no longer leaves a stale flag that skips recreation; the next write on the same handle recreates `audit_skill_selection_events` instead of failing with `no such table`. Postgres path binds the same way (no-op outside a transaction).
- **Regression test** — `recreates companion schema after lazy creation rolls back`: drops the companion table on a live handle, clears caches, runs a doomed `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` (lazy DDL + throw), asserts the table is gone, then asserts a follow-up `recordAuditEventInDatabase(skill_selection)` succeeds with the table present. Negative control: without the bind the follow-up throws `no such table`.
- **Missing real-behavior piece since Round 7 (22→40 boot already proven)** — production writer rollback/recovery exercised end-to-end on the same handle (drop → doomed lazy-DDL batch → recovered skill write → `audit.activity.list` readback path covered by `audit-events.skill-selection` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` suites). Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–7 (local ollama stalls at reply watchdog; xAI needs the broken `xai` dist); every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code.
- **Owner decision still open** — default collection (`logging.audit.enabled`, 30-day retention, 100k row cap) awaits maintainer approval under the audit doctrine; contributor-side approval only.

Verification on this head:
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection.test.ts` 8/8 (incl. new rollback-schema + existing rollback-count + v22 upgrade)
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts` + `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts` 17/17
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts` 21/21
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files



## Round 9 — re-verification on sync head + genuine release-upgrade proof (head `8de7c834dba`, no new PR commits since Round 8)

Since Round 8 (`d541860e07a`) the branch only absorbed upstream sync merges — `git log d541860e07a..HEAD` shows sync commits plus upstream fixes, zero PR-owned changes. Full re-verification on the merged head plus a fresh end-to-end proof against a genuine published-release state dir.

- **Contract re-verified**: async worker `listAuditEventsInDatabase` (`src/audit/audit-event-read.kernel.ts`, delegated from `audit-event-writer.worker.ts`), companion table `audit_skill_selection_events` (storage + schema + migration), 4-field run-usage receipt (`name`/`source`/`activation`/`skillFile`, session attribution via audit side-effect only). (`workspace-bootstrap-privacy` no longer exists on either side — absorbed by upstream bootstrap refactors; zero references repo-wide.)
- **Suites green**: `audit-events.skill-selection` + `skill-selection-hidden` + `runtime-skill-selection` + `agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e` (via include-override, excluded from default projects by the `*.e2e` glob) — 26/26; `audit-events` + `commands/audit` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` + `sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence` — 292/292; `tsgo:core` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

### Live-Gateway proof (new, genuine v2026.11.3 → PR-head upgrade)

State dir created by the **published release itself** (worktree of tag `v2026.11.3` @ `847611dcaa3`, deps installed, `gatewayWatch` dist built): release Gateway booted fresh (user_version 22, device identity issued, local credential custody created), one legacy `agent.run.started` recorded through the release production writer (`release-run-1`, seq 1). Release Gateway stopped; **PR-head Gateway booted the same dir** (fresh `gatewayWatch` dist): migration **22→40** with the release row byte-identical, companion table present, audit CLI serving.

Production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → `recordRunSkillUsage` (4-field receipt) → bus `skill_selection` event → the exact production recorder the Gateway subscribes (`createAgentEventAuditRecorder` + real async writer) → store with lazy companion path → shipped CLI against the running Gateway (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:18796`, `--auth none`, loopback):

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-15T22:52:33.227Z      skill_selection  -         -      observed  main   proof-run-r9  skill.selection.observed  skill:r9--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{..., "sequence":3, "kind":"skill_selection", "agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-r9", "sessionId":"proof-session-r9", "runId":"proof-run-r9",
"action":"skill.selection.observed", "status":"observed", "redaction":"metadata_only",
"selectedSkill":"r9--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1, `release-run-1`, preserved) → ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 2, `proof-run-r9`) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 3, full attribution) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 4). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–8; every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code on a live Gateway, this time across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary with release-created credential custody (the synthetic-fixture shortcut fails at the client-credential migration without it — verified).

Note: `openclaw audit` without an explicit `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` resolved to an unrelated Gateway on this host's default port; the proof pins the URL explicitly.



## Round 10 — P1 validator regen + real-model trigger (head 82915d6ae6d, no upstream drift)

prs.title: fix: preserve agent IDs in Doctor's session store restore command
prs.body:
Closes #202034

## What Problem This Solves

When a config backup contains a session store owner that is missing from the current config, Doctor prints a command to restore it. For agent IDs such as `123` or `true`, `config set` interprets the bare argument as a number or boolean and rejects the restore.

## User Impact

Operators can copy Doctor's restore command to recover a numeric or literal-like agent ID. Doctor still requires consent before applying the recovery itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor serializes the backed-up agent ID as a JSON string, preserves its quotes with the existing CLI argument formatter, and passes `--strict-json` to `config set`.

## Evidence

- In isolated macOS arm64 configuration, I ran Doctor and executed the exact restore command it printed in `/bin/sh` against the built CLI. The baseline rejected `123` as a number. The fix restored `123`, `true`, `null`, `infinity`, and `ops` as strings. Doctor preserved the config until the command ran, and the restore preserved other settings and the pre-write backup.
- OpenClaw `2026.11.6` generated an actual backup via `config set` followed by `config unset`. The fixed CLI recovered `"123"` from that backup with the same preservation checks.
- The new registered-CLI regression fails on the base and passes with the fix. All 53 tests across the config path, config roster, and Doctor recovery suites pass. The new case took 1.17 seconds. The changed roster and Doctor suites took 13.21 and 59.95 seconds respectively, and the combined run finished in 107.43 seconds including worker preparation. The Doctor suite checks real config writes, consent, and backups.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:changed`, targeted TypeScript, lint and formatting checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Captured CLI output</summary>

Baseline `87e11d625`, executing the restore command printed by Doctor

```console
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId 123
Config validation failed: agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId: Invalid input: expected string, received number
```

Fixed build `69febf640`, executing each suggested restore command and reading back the configured value

```console
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"123"
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"true"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"true"
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"null"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"null"
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"infinity"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"infinity"
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"ops"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"ops"
```

Backup created by OpenClaw `2026.11.6 (06afb10)`, restored using the fixed build

```console
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"123"
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: let people finish Mac setup without an unsupported remote-access step
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In macOS app builds that package the native OpenClaw ID transport (`OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`), local setup ends with a **Reach it from anywhere?** step. Its only button, **Sign in with OpenClaw ID**, is enabled, but the action behind it is not implemented in the app, so every click ends in "Setup did not finish." The final summary then invites the person back to the same step with a **Reach it from anywhere · Learn more** row.

## User Impact

User impact: someone who sets up OpenClaw on this Mac goes straight from **Connect your AI** to **You’re all set!**, which says **Running on this Mac**. They no longer see a button that cannot work. Back from the summary returns to AI setup. Turning on remote access stays an explicit choice after setup, through the existing Dashboard account-menu action (**Turn on remote access**). That action already checks whether this claw can use it and explains when it cannot. The remote paths are unchanged: **On another computer**, OpenClaw ID sign-in, node invitations, and invite links.

## Why This Change Was Made

A packaged transport does not mean the app can make a Mac reachable. Both onboarding services answered the remote-reach request by throwing `featureUnsupported`, so the step only showed a failure. This change removes the local remote-reach page, its summary row, the **Not now** title, and the unused remote-reach request and result. Local setup now has the same steps whether or not the transport is packaged. Remote and invite page orders stay the same. The WebUI already offers remote access only as an explicit action after setup, so it needs no change.

## Evidence

**Base reproduction** (`main` cc849dd810e, built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1` against a locally built arm64 `OpenClawIrohFFI` slice). A temporary test, not committed, drove the production `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInService` through the real `OnboardingOpenClawIDModel`:

```
N01-BASE pageOrder(local)=[0, 1, 3, 5, 9] unavailable=nil account=nil error=Setup did not finish. Try again or continue without OpenClaw ID.
```

The reach page (5) was in the local path, its button was enabled because no unavailable reason applied, and clicking it always failed.

**After** (same packaged build mode): local order is `[0, 1, 2, 3, 9]` or `[0, 1, 3, 9]`. 76 tests passed in the focused onboarding suites: `OnboardingViewSmokeTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDMemberJoinTests`, `OnboardingNodeInvitationServiceTests`, `OnboardingPageTests`, `OnboardingFirstRunTests`, and both render suites. Those suites cover the remote `[0, 1, 4, 3, 9]`, joined-claw, and Set up later orders. The new regression test `local setup goes from AI setup to the summary in every build` asserts the local orders; the packaged base produces `[0, 1, 3, 5, 9]` instead, so this test fails there.

### Clean comparison — final summary, local setup

| Before (main, packaged transport) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: summary shows Reach it from anywhere with Learn more](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62a61af5-0845-40f5-8c3e-34b4453f31e3) | ![After: summary shows Running on this Mac](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe18c4b-a2b0-42f2-8486-349ad46f14a2) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Remote-reach row highlighted in the before summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9e0d670-78bf-4109-b571-98e5dfec86ad) | ![Local-only summary row highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a69da73-6f38-4bfa-b264-720e60a60860) |

### Removed step (before only; it no longer exists)

| Reach page on main | Annotated | After clicking Sign in with OpenClaw ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Reach it from anywhere page with enabled Sign in button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55e955a7-8119-4c3f-9a6e-a6c73e08dea3) | ![Sign in button highlighted as enabled but always failing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7490b7ec-038b-49d9-8cc1-b7a2d4ff1cf3) | ![Sheet shows Setup did not finish](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3fb3624-8d9f-4b66-be04-6b13ab5f336a) |

These captures come from `OnboardingRenderTests` and a production-service sheet render: the real page views with fixture app state, the default 630×752 content rectangle, and navigation omitted. Before is cc849dd810e and after is this branch, both built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`. Rendering ran in the repository's native render sandbox (`scripts/macos-health-render.sb`), with no network, private HOME and state, and no preferences or Keychain access. "Launch at login · Unavailable under profile" appears because the sandbox uses a named profile.

<details><summary>Checks run and gaps</summary>

- `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1 swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` built on both base and branch.
- Focused sandboxed run: the suites listed above, 76 passed and 0 failed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: 0 violations.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated the inventory, removing only the strings for the deleted step and row. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed.
- Not run locally: the default (unpackaged) app build and the full macOS native suite. CI's `macos-swift` job covers them. This change has no packaging-dependent code paths, but CI will confirm the default build.
- Not exercised: the Dashboard **Turn on remote access** flow against a live OpenClaw ID backend. It is unchanged here.
- Simplification: removed the local reach page, its view, the summary row, the `openClawIDEnabled` page-order switch, the `.makeReachable` intent, and the `.reachable` result. Diff: 24 insertions, 114 deletions.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): show Template cards without waiting for artwork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Templates could leave titles and Add hidden for half a second after the catalog had arrived. Slow images then left blank spaces beside the titles, and on a sparse catalog the next section jumped as it loaded.

## User Impact

You can read and add Templates as soon as the catalog arrives. Each image has its own placeholder, and the next section appears in its final position.

## Why This Change Was Made

Titles and Add no longer wait for artwork. Each 64 × 64 slot shows a placeholder until its own image is ready. Missing or broken images keep their fallback; loaded artwork stays unboxed. The loading grid doesn't guess where later sections will begin.

## Evidence

[Desktop, mobile and dark-mode before/after captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202587#issuecomment-7045205416). Across five paired Chromium runs of the built Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, titles appeared **1.5–2.1 ms** after catalog data arrived, down from **502.7–506.4 ms**. The second section previously jumped 102 px on desktop and 306 px on mobile; it now first appears in place. Image arrival caused no measured movement. Reduced motion was also checked.

32 unit and 33 browser tests passed, as did the seven final loading cases, production UI build, typechecks, changed-file lint, and differential asset budget. The local full-tree dead-export check reports two existing, unrelated spawn test fixture exports on the base. No Gateway or API behavior changes.

prs.title: feat(signal): include recent group photos when mentioned
prs.body:
Closes #202570.

## What Problem This Solves

In a mention-gated Signal group, a person can post a photo and someone can ask OpenClaw about it a few messages later. The bot currently sees an attachment label in history and cannot inspect the photo.

## User Impact

An allowed mention can include eligible photos from the group’s existing `historyLimit` window. The photo and mention can come from different members, and the mention can be an ordinary unquoted message. Unmentioned photo posts stay silent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal keeps bounded attachment references in the existing account-local group history. When an allowed, non-command mention arrives, it retrieves up to four eligible images from the preceding 30 minutes and adds them to the normal turn attachments with their source message IDs. This makes the images available through the embedded model path as well as the ACP attachment path.

The lookup respects supplemental-context visibility, `ignoreAttachments`, and the configured media size limit. View-once and disappearing images are excluded. A delete event removes the pending reference. Unavailable media leaves the existing placeholder and the text request proceeds.

## Evidence

- Two new receive-handler cases reproduced zero history-attachment fetches on the original base. After the patch, 44 focused Signal tests passed across mention gating and inbound context (92.53 seconds for the two-suite run, including cold compilation). The cases cover a cross-sender, unquoted photo with an intervening message, the history cutoff, sender visibility, the image cap, deletion, and missing media.
- A build and an isolated Gateway replay passed on `838434a34`. The follow-up at `7cd285b8d` only renames a local formatter parameter and passes lint. A loopback Signal fixture sent a generated PNG, an intervening message, and a plain mention from another sender. The photo stayed silent and caused no attachment request until the mention. The Gateway fetched it once, the mock vision endpoint received the matching PNG bytes, and the Gateway sent the reply to the Signal fixture.
- Targeted Signal type checking and lint, formatting, MDX validation, and the line-cap ratchet passed. CI timing is pending.

The replay used a simulated Signal transport and model endpoint. Independent Antigravity review attempts timed out without a verdict.

### Live Signal and model validation

Passed on `7cd285b8dd2ac6fa2290e17d003d90b761028b8c`. The PR build ran in an isolated Gateway with `historyLimit: 10`, a real Signal account in a mention-gated group, and the live OpenAI Responses API. A test relay forwarded only the two test messages.

| Step | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| One member posted a synthetic image containing a random eight-character code, without mentioning the bot. | No attachment fetch, model request, or reply. |
| About a minute later, a different member sent a standalone text mention with no quote or attachment. | The Gateway fetched the earlier Signal attachment. The model request contained one `input_image`, and OpenAI returned HTTP 200. |
| The bot replied in the group. | The reply matched the code printed only in the image. The reply was also verified in Signal Desktop. |

#### Captured test output

The lines below come from the test relay’s recorded events. Elapsed milliseconds are relative to receipt of the photo. The relay compared the outgoing reply against the expected code stored separately from the model request.

```jsonl
{"elapsed_ms":0,"event":"photo","attachment_count":1,"mention":false}
{"elapsed_ms":63715,"event":"mention","distinct_sender":true,"quoted":false,"attachment_count":0}
{"elapsed_ms":63851,"event":"attachment-read","after_mention":true,"success":true}
{"elapsed_ms":72192,"event":"model-request","image_count":1,"status":200}
{"elapsed_ms":78366,"event":"send","accepted":true,"visual_code_matched":true}
{"elapsed_ms":78367,"event":"model-request-blocked","image_count":0}
```

During the 63.7 seconds between the photo and the mention, the relay recorded no fetch, model request, or reply. After the matching reply, the relay’s single-request limit blocked a separate text-only request.

The temporary Gateway and relay were stopped after the test. The PR remains a draft while the maintainer decision on cross-sender photo visibility is pending.

prs.title: fix: let config unset remove sections with default lists while the Gateway runs
prs.body:
Root cause: src/cli/config-cli-owner-patch.ts:84 builds the routed `replacePaths` consent from the authored config only (`collectReplacePaths(patch, previous)`), while the Gateway's guard at src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts:879-880 (`rejectDestructiveArrayPatchWithoutIntent({ currentConfig: snapshot.config, ... })`) checks the runtime view, where an omitted provider `models` list or a plugin schema default exists as an array. Deleting the section therefore "removes" an array the CLI never named, and the Gateway refuses.

Fixes #203175

Thanks @woodmanlegion for the detailed report and source trace.

## What Problem This Solves

With the Gateway running, `openclaw config unset models.providers.ollama` (or `config unset models`) fails with `config.patch would remove entries from array path(s): models.providers.ollama.models` when the provider has no `models` list in the file. The same happens for plugin config sections with array schema defaults, such as `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.managedNativeTools`. The same command works with the Gateway stopped, and the error suggests options the CLI does not have. Routed CLI writes are supposed to match offline writes (#184194; docs/cli/config.md: "Output and exit codes match the offline command").

## User Impact

`config unset` of a section holding a runtime-default array now removes it through a running Gateway, and the saved file is byte-for-byte what the offline command writes. No workaround (writing `[]` first, or stopping the Gateway) is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI already sends consent, in the existing `replacePaths` field, for every array removed below a subtree the command explicitly deletes or replaces. It now also collects those arrays from the Gateway's own `config.get` view (the one the guard checks, read at the same revision as `baseHash`), still only below the removed subtree. The Gateway guard, the request fields and authorization are unchanged. A `set` that would drop entries from an authored list is still refused, and a raw `config.patch` that truncates an authored array without `replacePaths` is still refused by the guard.

## Evidence

Built CLI and Gateway (dist), isolated state per side, the issue's steps run against a running Gateway (routed) and with no Gateway (offline) from identical starting files. Proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203235#issuecomment-7067338414

- Base (282121402940), routed: `config unset models.providers.ollama`, `config unset models` and `config unset plugins.entries.anthropic.config.managedNativeTools` exit 1 with `config.patch would remove entries from array path(s): ...`; offline the same commands exit 0 and the files differ.
- Candidate, routed: all three exit 0 (`Removed ...`), and after each of the 14 steps the routed file equals the offline file byte for byte.
- Controls on the candidate: offline results unchanged; `config set models.providers.vllm.models` dropping an authored entry is refused on both paths (`Refusing to replace ...`); unsetting a sibling provider or a sibling key leaves the other arrays untouched (files equal offline); a raw `config.patch` truncating `gateway.nodes.commands.allow` without `replacePaths` is still refused by the Gateway guard.
- Tests: `src/cli/config-cli-owner-patch.test.ts` now gives the synthetic owner a runtime view with default arrays inside and outside the removed subtree; it fails on base (inside path missing) and passes here, and the outside path is not consented. `src/cli/config-owner-route.process.test.ts` unsets an ollama provider without `models` through a real in-process Gateway.

Line deltas vs merge base: production +26 / -19 (one file, partly formatter rewrap), tests +23 / -7.

Merge danger: two-way door. CLI-only, no stored data, schema or protocol change; a revert restores the previous consent list. Blast radius: routed `config set/patch/unset`, `mcp` config commands and Gateway-owned `setup`; if wrong, a routed removal would consent to an array the Gateway materializes under the removed subtree, which the offline command removes too.

prs.title: fix(subagents): preserve yield settlement after child cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A requester could yield after some accepted children had already been delivered or expired and cleaned up, then fail with “accepted continuation children could not transfer terminal delivery.” Cleanup removed the registry rows but left their in-memory accepted completion receipts outstanding. Separately, completion delivery failures used `run-failed-before-reply`, making successful child work appear to have failed.

## User Impact

Requesters can yield after finished children are cleaned up and still receive the remaining results. If a result cannot be delivered, the notice identifies the delivery problem and reason while preserving the child’s actual success or failure. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration now retains the requester's existing operational instance for ordinary spawns, as follow-ups already do. Committed registry removal retires that instance's accepted completion receipt before releasing custody. Yield settlement transfers the remaining children and still rejects unknown missing children. This removes the sweeper's redundant full-batch-witness retention guard. Delivery failures use `subagent-delivery-failed`, report the child's execution outcome separately, and include a bounded delivery reason; expiry names the deadline.

No schema, configuration, persistent delivery-state, or cache change. Production code is net −12 lines. Normal delivery identity, private-result visibility, and the incomplete-cohort guard remain intact. Follow-up to #203198; does not alter the partial-wake policy in #203176 or the notice-custody retry work in #199455.

## Evidence

- Exact-parent reproduction at `9f35510e10ecf`, with only regression tests applied: 8 expected failures and 48 passes. Both delivered/cleaned and expired/cleaned mixed cohorts fail at the completeness check; successful-child expiry records the wrong notice type. The focused owner regressions pass with the repair.

prs.title: fix(agents): name dispatcher when correcting deferred text calls
prs.body:
Related: #183085, #183165, #186718.

## What Problem This Solves

In Tool Search `tools` mode, the bounded correction for a deferred OpenClaw tool call emitted as text asks the model to call it natively without explaining the dispatcher route. When a reply contains several text-form calls, a directly callable tool appearing first must not hide a later deferred target.

We observed the original gap after #183165 was installed: a deferred `web_fetch` arrived as XML, the generic correction ran, the model repeated the undeclared name, and the turn ended as `incomplete_turn`. Neither call executed.

## User Impact

An eligible retry names `dispatch_action`, the exact target in `id`, and target parameters in `args`. It mentions `tool_describe` only when offered. Mixed-call text selects the first eligible deferred target, regardless of preceding direct or execution-restricted calls. Direct-only calls retain their existing correction.

No extra retries, text-derived execution, initial-prompt changes, or tool-schema changes are added. This guidance covers deferred OpenClaw tools; it does not add deferred MCP/client-tool recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The strict parser retains an accepted call's name. The attempt owner selects a deferred target using the current native surface, authorized catalog, registered spelling, direct-name precedence, ambiguity checks, and execution restrictions. Candidate selection is separate from validating action announcements: `I'll call read now.` can precede a mixed list without hiding its deferred target. The existing recovery owner adds guidance after its normal safety guards.

The superseded private boolean detector wrapper/export is removed and its tests use the name-returning function. There is no new runtime module, configuration option, cache, parser grammar, or execution path.

The related changes address different stages:

- **#183165 (merged):** recognizes authorized deferred names in text-form attempts and activates bounded native correction. Our incident confirmed detection and retry worked, but the instruction omitted the dispatcher.
- **#186718 (open):** supplies dispatcher guidance when a **structured native call** names a deferred tool and would otherwise receive a bare “not found” error. Text-form output never reaches that resolver.
- **This PR:** supplies the authorized target and native dispatcher arguments to the **text-call correction**. It builds on #183165 and complements #186718, replacing neither.

## Evidence

Current head: `d3cff0c7deb434b88832ef0a63c0bada2ab7b421`. Original PR base: `ba557d2b264067f303d6bd6181a2c86144c30d11`.

The November 10 follow-up addresses [Yigtwxx's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196009#pullrequestreview-5838743805). [Reproduction scripts, actual appended corrections and sanitized results](https://gist.github.com/LeoStehlik/5a6a4677cae703dc16156958d999a2a0#file-followup-readme-md).

| Real CLI, injected text `[read, web_fetch]` | Previous PR head `bdcba982` | Current head `d3cff0c7` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Provider requests | 2 | 3 |
| Actual page fetches | 0 | 1 |
| Result | `incomplete_turn`, exit 1 | Success, exit 0; fetched marker returned |

The isolated CLI exposes `read` directly and keeps `web_fetch` deferred. Its scripted provider emits a native dispatch only after the **actual appended correction** names `web_fetch`, `dispatch_action`, `id`, and `args`. The verifier checks that no HTTP fetch precedes native dispatch and the final answer contains the real loopback page's marker. This proves orchestration, not model compliance. Baseline production inputs were clean; only the added regression test file was dirty. Current-head proof uses a clean committed checkout.

Validation on this revision:

- **259 focused tests across seven files pass**, covering owner-to-recovery composition, strict parser grammar, retry safety/budget, text-promotion siblings, stream normalization and prompt-prefix stability.
- Six new owner cases cover both JSON call orders, a `tool_calls` array, XML blocks, a direct-tool announcement before mixed calls, and an execution-restricted deferred call before an eligible one. Five fail on the prior PR head with generic guidance; the reversed-order control already passes. All six pass with the fix. Direct tools are also in the fixture's capability set, matching the runtime rather than assuming capabilities are deferred-only.
- Owner suite: 57 tests, 36.92s wall time (92% transformation of the existing compiler graph); parser suite: 74 tests, 1.61s. Hosted CI status is recorded below.
- Core, agents-other test and package test typechecks; scoped oxlint; formatting/MDX; line-cap, max-lines, assertion and test-line ratchets; and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full `pnpm build` passes on the committed head: 239.01s, exit 0, under an 8 GiB process-group limit. It retains Control UI size-budget warnings; this PR changes no UI sources.
- Fresh independent local agent review inspected the full original-base-to-candidate diff and found no actionable issues. Reviewed working-diff SHA256: `54521cf3c86582911f573858da1406e2cea9260e62843e476d7c5131117a7967`, then committed unchanged. This was an independent agent review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper tool run; the shared autoreview helper is not installed locally.

Simplification: the follow-up removes one net production line and adds 35 net test lines. The complete PR is +80 production / +206 test lines; its dedicated allocation records exactly those 206 regression lines, with the shared baseline unchanged.

Historical evidence remains in the same gist. The original single-call CLI proof demonstrated base failure and original-head recovery. Its small-context actual-model control succeeded on **both** base and original head, so it did not reproduce the observed roughly 134K-context production failure or establish a reliability/latency improvement. This follow-up does not make a new actual-model claim. No production Gateway or inference service was changed or restarted.


### November 10 review and hosted CI follow-up

[Yigtwxx's second review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196009#pullrequestreview-5842210576) rechecked `d3cff0c7deb`, passed the 57 owner and 74 parser tests, and used mutations to verify the selector and announcement regression cases. It reports no further findings. This is the current-head human review; the earlier ClawSweeper verdict remains tied to `bdcba982`.

The three red check entries represent **one failing test job and two aggregate gate failures**. [Run 42813130671, attempt 1, `checks-node-changed-7`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42813130671/job/129820321062) fails the configured/guarded `apply_patch` containment cases in `src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts`. Both expect the older shared “Keep patch paths within the bound root” guidance. The implementation now returns configuration-specific “Keep file paths within the bound root” or session-specific “Keep file paths within this session's recorded root” guidance introduced by merged #194473.

CI tested merge `e5aa0249f716269bc40cf16e10f7bbe5e1b0d08d`, combining this PR with main `ba5d43b4e6cd04f9e4fe5f04cc30ec645fbf6b38`. Inspection confirms both the stale expectation and its production owner are byte-identical on that main parent and the tested merge:

| File | Git blob on both revisions |
| --- | --- |
| `src/worker/worker-runtime-permissions.suite.ts` | `446f11c8c69a7aa1cc9c10dd3cfa0a7f5fbe5265` |
| `src/agents/apply-patch-containment-hint.ts` | `c6e5bf1a096dbb64df9cd96ab25a0c3a254bbb0c` |

Neither file is changed by this PR. The repository failure classifier reports `unknown` because no matching scheduled-main job was available; the inherited-main attribution above comes from the exact failed assertions, source comparison and independent review, not a green main run. The failure remains recorded: no rerun, weakened assertion or unrelated source change was made to clear it.

prs.title: feat(gateway): connect approved trusted-proxy CLI and TUI devices within their grant
prs.body:
Related to #199692. Stacked on #199698.

## What problem this solves

A CLI or TUI guest approved only for session access can ask for broader operator scopes on its first connection. That files a scope-upgrade request for access the administrator already chose to withhold.

## How it works

Set `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.narrowToDeviceGrant` to let a paired CLI or TUI connect with the intersection of the requested scopes and its approved grant. The Gateway checks the trusted-proxy identity, paired device key, and effective operator role. The connection must have no browser `Origin`. The hello response reports the admitted scopes, so the client can use its session permissions on the first connection. A request for broader scopes with no overlap still follows the scope-upgrade flow. An administrator can use this option with manual enrollment or configure enrollment separately through `trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove`.

The option defaults to `false` and applies only to devices with a current grant. Device enrollment and browser connections follow their existing policies. The TUI can store a device token under this opt-in. Human operators governed by named-role policy still receive no device token. Reserved Session Share grants use the dedicated publication-transport admission path.

Device tokens can authenticate a direct connection until revoked. `openclaw security audit` reports `gateway.trusted_proxy_narrow_to_device_grant` when this option is on. Keep the trusted proxy as the only Gateway ingress and remove a guest device when access ends. The core configuration baseline gains one boolean key, from 2,666 to 2,667. The trusted-proxy guide documents the option and its token behavior.

## Evidence

- **Main vs. PR head.** On `53fe7a0b11bd`, an approved session-only guest's broad TUI request files a scope-upgrade request. On `013f2b4e0e8f` with the opt-in enabled, the TUI receives only its paired session scope and a device token, with no pending upgrade. A CLI requesting `operator.read` receives `operator.sessions.read` when its grant covers session access. The option-off test on the PR head still files the upgrade. These cases run against the Gateway WebSocket server. The main run uses the option-off case from the PR test suite. [Exact base-to-head diff](https://github.com/daniel-lxs/openclaw/compare/53fe7a0b11bd656cfb8251dd4a311e9a59d10b52...013f2b4e0e8ffaa7d677eb65b849f2d22dab02c7)
- **Checks on `013f2b4e0e8f`.** 275 focused tests passed on macOS arm64. Separate suites covered the opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verifier, trusted-proxy grant narrowing, Session Share publication request admission, CLI and TUI scope selection, config, and audit behavior. Core typecheck and all 12 baseline ratchets passed.
- **Shipped TUI and stable upgrade.** The runtime run at `a5b50ef7ff73` upgrades two paired guests and their Gateway from the published `2026.11.6` package. It preserves the settings, credentials, and grants. One guest reuses its stable-issued token. The other receives a token on the first connection and reuses it on restart. Both can run `/sessions` on the admitted WebSocket after identity resolution. The Access and GitHub responses came from test fixtures. [Upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199699#issuecomment-7052127488)

prs.title: fix: create Feishu Drive folders at the root when no parent is given
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/feishu/src/drive.ts:312 `createFolder` looked up the Drive root folder with the raw `client.httpInstance`, which sends no tenant access token, so Feishu always answered `99991661`; the empty `catch` hid that and the request went out with `folder_token: "0"`, which Feishu rejects with `1061002 params error`.

Fixes #203208

## What Problem This Solves

`feishu_drive` with `create_folder` and no `folder_token` (the documented way to create a folder in the bot's Drive root) always failed with `1061002 params error`. The error pointed at the caller, while the real failure was an unauthenticated root-folder lookup that was silently ignored. `feishu_drive list` without a token, and `create_folder` with an explicit token, worked.

## User Impact

User impact: `feishu_drive create_folder` without a parent creates the folder in the bot's Drive root. If Feishu refuses the root lookup (for example, a bot with no usable root or a missing scope), the tool now returns that Feishu error instead of a misleading `params error`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root lookup now goes through the same authenticated SDK request path (`client.request`, via the file's existing `requestDriveApi`) that the other Drive calls, including `list`, use, so it carries the tenant token. A failed lookup is reported through the existing Feishu error handling instead of falling back to `"0"`, which Feishu never accepts. Explicit parent tokens are unchanged. `create_folder` is the only Drive action that resolves the root this way.

Thanks @yeliccc for the report, the exact diagnosis and the confirmed local patch.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`), isolated state, bundled Feishu plugin pointed at a local HTTPS Feishu fixture (fixture app id/secret; the fixture issues a tenant token, returns the root token only to authenticated requests, and returns `1061002` for `folder_token: "0"`), and a scripted model that calls `feishu_drive`. Observed request log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203234#issuecomment-7067234036

- Base `4a86f968f92f`: `create_folder` without a token sends an unauthenticated root lookup (`400 / 99991661`), then `create_folder` with `folder_token: "0"` -> `1061002 params error`.
- This PR: authenticated root lookup, folder created under the real root token.
- Controls: `list` without a token and `create_folder` with an explicit token send the same requests on both sides; when the root lookup is refused, the tool reports that Feishu error (`feishu_code 99991672`) and sends no `create_folder`.
- Regression test `extensions/feishu/src/drive.test.ts` (root create uses the authenticated lookup token; lookup failure is reported, no create) fails on base and passes here.

Production lines: +14 / -20 (`drive.ts`). Test lines: +27 (one regression).

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert fully restores the old behavior, no state or config is written. Blast radius: Feishu `feishu_drive create_folder` calls that omit `folder_token`.
