prs.title: perf(ci): avoid duplicate declaration path checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Extension package-boundary compilation repeats the same physical checkout check in the filesystem owner, emitter adapter, and private worker callback. These checks add filesystem work to every compiler lookup.

## User Impact

The candidate removes duplicate checks while retaining checkout confinement, diagnostics, package coverage, and receipt publication rules. The complete worker request is 19.7% faster at the median in the qualified five-pair comparison below. Whole-job and billing savings remain unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded filesystem already admits each physical lookup. Pass custom caller policy directly to that owner. The private worker has no narrower input policy, so use the existing identity-callback convention to request compiler-owned confinement. Keep the worker's request, output, and final input validation.

The committed benchmark executes the actual worker and emitter from the selected revision, including final input validation and receipt publication. It can also load immutable snapshots at the same module URLs.

## Evidence

- Initial emitter-only work counts: `existsSync` 154,478 → 108,108; native realpath 113,603 → 81,811, on identical 6,743-input graphs. These counts describe the first candidate, not the complete-worker revision.
- Existing native declaration tests passed: 14 passed, 3 Windows-only cases skipped on Linux. They cover declaration bytes, nested installs, aliases, external links, missing-path retargeting, and inherited config. The original emitter change passed scripts typecheck, lint, format parity, and Knip.
- The new worker proof executes valid requests and an imported directory symlink to an external declaration, for both check-only and declaration emission. The external declaration deliberately has a semantic error: a late input-inventory rejection cannot substitute for confinement during compilation. Both failures must remove the prior success receipt.
- Current head passed both selected suites: 27 tests passed and 2 Windows-alias cases were skipped on Linux. Scripts typecheck, scoped lint, and oxfmt/Bun parity passed.
- Fresh source review of the full range through `498945a1de3436b76d8d5c5c5897667cde9cff9d` found no actionable findings.

### Rejected emitter-only candidate

Five interleaved pairs at `224197005eb9dd3eb6acfd0733fc31d87cf3551c` completed with equal 6,865-input semantic graphs:

| Metric | Baseline | Emitter-only candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median compile wall | 2,905.514 ms | 2,716.773 ms |
| p95 compile wall | 3,248.526 ms | 3,045.516 ms |
| Median process CPU | 5.96 s | 5.53 s |
| Median peak RSS | 619,076 KiB | 620,100 KiB |

The 6.50% median gain missed the predeclared 10% gate. This candidate was rejected for landing; the result is preserved rather than rounded up or retested unchanged. Earlier incomplete raw-digest attempts are censored and are not acceptance evidence.

### Full-worker performance acceptance rule

At head `498945a1de3436b76d8d5c5c5897667cde9cff9d`, run the committed `scripts/perf/extension-boundary-compile-measure.mts` against immutable baseline and candidate worker/emitter snapshots, with the same prepared Discord config and unchanged sibling modules. Use one 8-CPU, approximately 16-GiB Linux VM, `GOMAXPROCS=2`, fresh processes and warm filesystem state. Keep instrumented counts/profiles/manifests separate from timing.

Collect five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs serially. The primary metric is complete worker wall time through receipt publication. Report median, p95 and range, plus process CPU and peak RSS. Require at least 10% lower median worker wall time, no median CPU increase, no p95 worker-wall regression, and no more than 10% median peak-RSS growth. Scope any saving to this worker request; it does not establish whole-job or billing savings.

Every timed run must match the full-manifest controls' consumed inputs and semantic lookup digest. Preserve every read, negative probe, directory and realpath lookup exactly; only positive `fileExists` facts for consumed inputs verified as regular files may vary. Report raw digests separately. Production receipt fingerprinting remains unchanged.

### Qualified full-worker result

Five interleaved pairs, Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, 8 available CPUs, 16,767,762,432 bytes RAM, `GOMAXPROCS=2`, fresh processes and warm filesystem state. Baseline owner blobs were verified against `5b12461c7b3265ef81a3ba0594041e2510e865ba`; candidate owner files differed only by the two reviewed callback changes. Instruments and CPU profile ran separately from timing.

| Metric | Baseline median | Baseline p95 | Baseline range | Candidate median | Candidate p95 | Candidate range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Worker wall (ms) | 7343.955 | 7764.948 | 6454.713–7764.948 | 5896.597 | 6100.544 | 5581.516–6100.544 |
| Process wall (s) | 7.79 | 8.23 | 6.94–8.23 | 6.37 | 6.55 | 6.05–6.55 |
| Process CPU (s) | 14.83 | 15.59 | 13.65–15.59 | 12.32 | 12.85 | 11.78–12.85 |
| Peak RSS (KiB) | 633,416 | 653,708 | 606,900–653,708 | 628,976 | 659,540 | 608,596–659,540 |

All four acceptance gates passed. Median worker wall improved 19.71%, p95 wall 21.43%, median CPU 16.93%, and median peak RSS 0.70%. Peak RSS is GNU time's reported maximum; its p95 moved from 653,708 to 659,540 KiB (+0.89%), while the median-RSS gate passed. This is a worker-request result, not a whole-CI or billed-cost estimate.

| Count (separate instrumented runs) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `existsSync` | 164,143 | 63,090 |
| Native realpath | 122,487 | 50,892 |
| Consumed inputs | 6,865 | 6,865 |

All ten timed samples had the same 6,865 inputs and semantic digest. The two raw variants differ by the previously investigated redundant positive existence probe. The baseline CPU profile independently showed realpath and existence checks among the active Node frames.

| Pair | Baseline worker ms | Candidate worker ms | Baseline CPU s | Candidate CPU s | Baseline RSS KiB | Candidate RSS KiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6999.073 | 5896.597 | 14.43 | 12.31 | 653,708 | 628,976 |
| 2 | 6454.713 | 5581.516 | 13.65 | 11.78 | 633,416 | 651,640 |
| 3 | 7531.568 | 5709.899 | 15.37 | 12.32 | 606,900 | 659,540 |
| 4 | 7343.955 | 6100.544 | 14.83 | 12.85 | 651,908 | 609,852 |
| 5 | 7764.948 | 5990.697 | 15.59 | 12.55 | 628,104 | 608,596 |

Rerun after preparing Discord declarations, alternating `REV` between the baseline above and the candidate head:

```sh
CI=true GOMAXPROCS=2 /usr/bin/time -f '%e %U %S %M' \
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/extension-boundary-compile-measure.mts \
  REV .artifacts/extension-package-boundary/compile/discord.tsconfig.json
```

prs.title: fix: retain child results behind live requester turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A child can finish successfully while its requester keeps working for more than thirty minutes. Completion expiry currently treats that queued result as abandoned even when its recorded blocker is still the requester's own live execution. Both the idle sweep and the announce timer can retire it.

## User Impact

Completed results keep waiting behind their live requester and enter normal admission when that turn ends or yields. Dead, unknown, or mismatched blockers still expire through the existing visible failure-notice path. There is no migration, configuration change, or new persistent delivery state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared delivery-deadline owner now reuses the existing physical-requester liveness check, and the announce timer re-evaluates that deadline when it fires. Stored deadlines, mailbox admission, requester transfer, and exactly-once receipts stay with their existing owners. No cache or database query is added; the liveness lookup runs only when the original deadline is due.

Production delta is +10 lines (+28/−18). That growth covers both expiry paths through one existing policy owner, plus adapting the existing array callback to the explicit blocker argument. Tests +257, docs +4, reproducible benchmark +180. Related ownership fixes: #203102, #203132, #203156, #202732; #203176 concerns yielded partition admission.

## Evidence

The idle-expiry and announce-timer regressions fail on base `fcfb1140877abb643a0584c8e71f7ab08045d738`. The final-head isolated Gateway end/yield pair passes: each admits the result once and records one completion receipt. A separate real 31-minute requester hold also passes with the child retained across expiry, exactly one delivery after end, and no delayed/failed notice. [Real-duration trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203198#issuecomment-7066519533).

Focused proof passed: lifecycle 220/220; liveness/expiry/expired receipts 25/25; cleanup 5/5; settle-wake policy 27/27; requester-wake E2E 49/49. Native build including declarations passed. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2; hosted Codex and final-head ClawSweeper reviews have zero findings/open items. [Exact-head CI 44928680746](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44928680746) succeeded.

`pnpm check:changed` passed the affected types, lint, formatting, and runtime guards. The global dead-export audit fails identically on the exact parent: Feishu `FeishuBotAddedEvent`/`formatFeishuMediaContent` were left unused by `483f025ea389d` (#203108); Teams `htmlTagAttributeValues`/`isLikelyImageAttachment`/`safeHostForUrl` were left exported by `ec270048434f3` (#203084). These are main regressions for their owners to repair; they are not relabeled passing.

Synthetic measurement used Linux Node 26.12.1, btrfs with SQLite NoCoW, a 34.37 GiB agent DB, 5,000 sessions, 195,223 messages, 336 settled retained runs, 62,000 files / 1.116 GB, and 100 live requester operations. Five interleaved A1/A2/B rounds per mode, three warmups then twenty measured owner sweeps per fresh process: 100 samples per arm per mode, all outcomes verified. No production system or data was accessed.

| Arm | Wall ms median / p95 | Process CPU ms median / p95 | Sampled allocation KiB median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline A1 | 13.821 / 17.943 | 35.657 / 41.553 | 1671.66 / 1981.77 |
| Baseline A2 | 14.331 / 24.793 | 36.325 / 51.043 | 1664.50 / 1745.09 |
| Fix B | 0.299 / 0.446 | 0.343 / 1.824 | 57.76 / 78.04 |

A/A median drift: +3.69% wall, +1.87% CPU, −0.43% allocation. Setup is excluded; CPU includes worker threads, while allocation is sampled host-isolate V8 allocation. The baseline incorrectly discards and writes a notice; the fix retains the live wait and avoids that work. These are expiry-owner costs, not a whole-Gateway speedup claim. Reproduce with the committed `scripts/perf/subagent-live-expiry-measure.mjs` harness.

prs.title: fix: recognize Portuguese requests to search earlier conversations
prs.body:
Closes #195855

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory misses explicit Portuguese requests to search or review earlier conversations, and questions using the past-tense spelling `combinámos`.

## User Impact

People using these phrasings can pass the existing recall-intent gate. Future instructions, greetings, generic fix requests, and searches of current documentation retain their negative classification. This does not force deep recall on every message or change contextual follow-up handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend two patterns in the existing Portuguese matcher. Conversation-search commands need an explicit match; `combinámos` distinguishes an unambiguous past agreement from the unaccented future-ambiguous form. The existing test tables gain seven positive controls and seven negative controls, with a separate allocation for their 14 lines.

This follows the Portuguese support in #135137; it does not replace that work or alter memory storage, authority, configuration, or diagnostic-prefix rendering.

## Evidence

[Current-head running-Gateway evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195859#issuecomment-6822774006) now supplements the unit regressions. Exact clean head `bd4b96093bcc70718b186e8f01b4459ba8b57df1` was built through the supported source CLI and exercised via persistent `chat.send`, `agent.wait` and stored history with default escalation. Both `Pesquisa nas nossas conversas o que ficou decidido` and `O que combinámos para amanhã?` produced the actual recall-model HTTP request before the terminal answer. A future reminder, current-documentation search and greeting produced only the answer request with the no-recall-intent outcome. All five reached terminal replies.

External inference was synthetic and returned `NONE` for recall. This proves routing through the running Gateway and production prompt hook, not retrieval quality, a memory-tool result or live-provider reasoning. Empty memory used keyword/FTS fallback because the embedding provider was not loaded. No daily runtime, credentials or production source was changed; task processes stopped and ports closed. No before-fix Gateway run is claimed; the RED evidence below is unit-level.

Tested against public `main` at `7ebc4f3e67137c34b0850dfa8cab2b8d68e6576d`, with the same final regression cases on both sides:

prs.title: fix: include remote models in catalog retention benchmarks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The catalog-worker retention benchmark creates a remote catalog, but its fixture does not select that catalog URL or declare a provider that can admit its models. A run can therefore succeed without exercising the requested remote inventory.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Developers get a benchmark that includes its synthetic remote catalog and fails if those rows disappear.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same catalog URL in configuration and input, and give the remote provider a distinct static manifest seed. Keep runtime provider selection unchanged. Check the active revision's row count and first/last metadata without adding per-row allocations.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182902

## Evidence

The unchanged pre-fix harness returned only 501 entries despite requesting 5,000 remote rows. On the same freshly built runtime, the corrected default returned 5,502 entries, including all 5,000 remote rows, for every request across five workspaces and two revisions.

Earlier remote-fixture measurements did not exercise the active remote overlay and are not directly comparable to this corrected workload.

- Six real built-worker cases passed: pre-fix reproduction, corrected default, periodic refresh, three providers, no-runtime-plugin control, and one-row boundary (26 requests total).
- Build, targeted script lint, script typecheck, erasability, and formatting passed on Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0. Source and built-artifact manifests matched before and after proof.
- Fresh P0–P2 autoreview and independent source/proof review passed for `25093440087987ccfbab5d18e3c351ef53d39c6b`.
- [Isolated Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44928723254): native command exit 0; lease cleanup verified. The workflow may show cancellation because native cleanup closes its hosting job.
- Exact-head hosted PR CI and ClawSweeper review passed. This PR makes no speed or allocation-improvement claim.

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506 Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main. ## What Problem This Solves On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable. ## User Impact User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow. The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators are regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported. Update behavior: this only changes what `update.status` reports and what Settings shows. How updates run is unchanged. An app-owned Gateway still refuses Gateway update requests with the app's hint, and package and Git installs keep their current update flow. ## Evidence ClawSweeper's last review left end-to-end proof open: before and after screenshots of the built Settings flow, and an upgrade from v2026.11.6 that keeps settings and data. The built-flow part now has a run on the current head, recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200910#issuecomment-7066419264). Fresh Gateways were built with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` from the base (`dc6e31a`) and from `1b71766`, both with the Mac packaging ownership marker, and the same Settings > Updates steps ran in Chromium on each. The changed Updating guide was built with `docs:build:preview` on both sides. Before, Settings offered "Update Gateway…", confirming it left the ownership refusal as an update error, and the guide did not mention the Settings display. After, Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" with the app's guidance and no Gateway update button, and the guide describes that behavior. The upgrade from a released version and the native app updater are still not exercised (see Not verified below). The screenshots below come from an earlier run of the same steps against Gateways built from `d119c6b` and `0f678cb`, using the exact ownership marker written by the Mac packaging script, with fresh Gateway state and no model or credentials. The current head (`1b71766`, on main `dc6e31a`) has the same hand-written changes as `0f678cb`; only the generated `predicates.js` was regenerated on newer main. Before: Settings shows "Update status unavailable" and offers "Update Gateway…". Confirming it leaves "Couldn’t update OpenClaw. Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." in the status row. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: null`. After: Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" and the guidance "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." There is no Gateway update button. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: {"kind":"host","host":{"owner":"macos-app","displayName":"OpenClaw.app","updateHint":"Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."}}`. With main's sources (`dc6e31a`) and this PR's tests, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" where it should say "Managed by OpenClaw.app". The 9 Gateway and schema cases that expect the owner fail the same way. On the current head, all of them pass.
Tests and checks on the current head (Node 26, macOS arm64) - `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`: 43 passed. The app-managed case took 34 ms. - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status.test.ts`: 71 tests across the 5 files, run with a 60 second test timeout because this machine is slow. In the full run, 69 passed and the two "reads recorded progress without reconciliation during restart" cases in `update-status.test.ts` (a file this PR does not change) hit that timeout. Rerun alone with a longer timeout, both pass on this head and on main's sources. - `gateway:validators:check` and `ui:validators:check` report no drift. `predicates.js` was regenerated from the schema rather than merged by hand. - `oxlint` with the repository config on the 11 changed TypeScript files reports no diagnostics. `oxfmt --check` on the 13 changed files and `git diff --check` are clean. `ui:i18n:verify` passes. - `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.ui.json` report the same set of type errors with and without this change. All of them come from packages missing in my partial dependency install, and none are in the changed files.
Not verified: - No run inside OpenClaw.app itself, and no upgrade from a released version (such as v2026.11.6) with settings intact. The browser runs above used Gateways built from source with the Mac packaging marker. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac. - A separately managed Gateway was not run in a browser; the existing `updates.test.ts` cases for the "Update Gateway…" action still pass. - The full `pnpm check:changed`, type-aware lint and a full typecheck were not run. The focused checks listed above used a scratch npm install of the versions in `package.json`.

prs.title: fix: let PostgreSQL-backed Gateways remove managed worktrees
prs.body:
Closes #202394

## What Problem This Solves

When a running Gateway stores its shared state in PostgreSQL, `openclaw worktrees remove` can fail before it snapshots or removes a managed checkout. The CLI reports a main-thread database error and leaves the checkout in place.

## User Impact

Operators can remove managed worktrees through a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway and recover uncommitted changes from the resulting snapshot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion synchronously checks the removal marker before it proceeds and verifies the current claim before Git or filesystem changes. Those reads now use the existing synchronous admission for native lock primitives. The entry check reads only the removal marker, and the host and worker share the batched claim check. Initial claim verification runs inside the existing cleanup scope so a failed check can release the attempt's claim.

## Evidence

- **CLI, real Gateway and PostgreSQL 16.15 on Linux.** Main at `6e113fecbf3` returned exit 1 from `openclaw worktrees remove <id> --json` and left the checkout active. The candidate returned `removed: true` and a snapshot ref. Git read the exact uncommitted file bytes from that ref, and `openclaw worktrees restore <id> --json` restored the same bytes.
- **Control UI, same PostgreSQL-backed Gateway flow.** Before, Delete showed the database error and left the checkout Active. After, the same checkout became Restorable and its directory was gone.
- **Regression and sibling tests.** The unpatched `4bddfe904dd` PostgreSQL case failed in the original lease read, and its SQLite control passed. The candidate passed all 70 tests across six files covering both engines, allocation, claim contention, removal safety, and recovery. The new two-case file took 11.9 seconds locally. The PostgreSQL case also verifies the main thread still rejects ordinary SQL.
- **Build and static checks.** The source runtime and Control UI built locally. Core, scripts, and the worktree test typecheck shard passed, as did targeted Oxlint and formatting. The full database-worker scan was stopped when local memory and swap filled. Hosted checks are pending.
- **Local review.** Codex autoreview reported no actionable P0 findings. The production diff adds 66 lines and removes 72 by sharing the claim queries. Test and test-infrastructure changes add 90 net lines.

**Before**

![Delete shows a PostgreSQL main-thread error and the checkout stays Active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/160f95df-d138-478d-b7e4-f6f5fbf536ad)

**After**

![The same worktree is Restorable after deletion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97112ee8-5dfd-481d-aa4f-b81dc568fc87)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaab1461-cb91-4912-99d8-f157757c74a6

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and test commands</summary>

The isolated state was created with `openclaw worktrees create` and ported with `openclaw database port --family state --to postgres`. The Gateway ran on loopback. Chromium used the same locally built Control UI assets for both runs. The candidate is based on `4bddfe904dd`. The removal and database bridge code was identical on that base and the live baseline.

```sh
pnpm openclaw --version
pnpm ui:build
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <isolated-port>
pnpm openclaw worktrees remove <id> --json
pnpm openclaw worktrees restore <id> --json
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <local-test-dsn> -- \
  src/agents/worktrees/service.remove.postgres.test.ts \
  src/agents/worktrees/capacity.postgres.test.ts \
  src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts \
  src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts \
  src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-safety.test.ts \
  src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The separate stale-PID cleanup warning during Gateway startup remains a follow-up from the report.

</details>

prs.title: fix(worktrees): explain cold template refresh decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a workspace template refresh becomes a cold rebuild after a commit change, its outcome currently explains the cache miss but not why incremental refresh was rejected. Operators cannot distinguish an invalid retained checkout, changed Git attributes, incompatible checkout policy, or a failed Git probe.

## User Impact

Managed and sandbox template outcomes now include bounded reason fields at the point where the existing code selects cold. This is an observability change; template selection, validation, dependency preparation, and lifecycle behavior are unchanged. No configuration or persistent-state changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing diagnostic record now carries `refreshRejectReason`, with `validationFailure` or `refreshErrorClass` where applicable. For example, a timed-out diff records `refreshRejectReason=diff-probe-failed refreshErrorClass=timeout`; a contaminated checkout records `refreshRejectReason=validation-failed validationFailure=dirty`. Values are closed enums, and Git output and error text are never copied into these fields.

The current lifecycle owners record the facts as they happen. This updates the existing diagnostics PR against the current template lifecycle. It does not implement previous-generation serving or claim a performance improvement.

## Evidence

Eighteen regression cases failed on unchanged base production code because the cold outcome lacked the expected reason. They cover missing retained checkout, each validation rejection, changed attributes, checkout-policy mismatch, and failed Git probes, including timeout, signal, nonzero exit, and truncated output. Real Git fixtures exercise both managed and sandbox template preparation and verify successful rebuilt content and commit identity.

The final touched suites pass 57 tests; another 27 unchanged template lifecycle and preparation timing tests passed in the same validation campaign. Independent Codex review is clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The complete `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` run passed all gates except an unused test import (removed; focused lint and formatting now pass) and three unrelated unused exports in Feishu/Teams. Those failures reproduce at exact main parent `1c86bd5173a36` and were introduced by #203108 (`483f025ea389d`) and #203084 (`ec270048434f3`). Main fixed them in #203186 (`adc4bb52fdfcf`); this branch now includes that fix. The final script, production, and full-tree export scans all pass with zero findings. Exact-head CI passed at `583969560ab0ef5e7367ec9ff15d247a88e4e151` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44928112951)). ClawSweeper reviewed that head with zero findings and zero open items. Native `scripts/pr` merged it as `4a86f968f92f263d0f60a53db65ed04084c8e6ab`.

Production grows by 90 lines to record the bounded reasons at their owners; test coverage grows by 235 lines and documentation by 10. The existing status validator and contamination tests moved to focused files to keep their owners within the line-cap budget.

prs.title: fix(cli-runner): let steering join an agent-command CLI turn
prs.body:
Part of #202510 (with #202511)

## What Problem This Solves

A channel message can never steer a CLI-backend turn started through the agent command path (for example the turn that resumes a conversation after `sessions_yield`): the join is refused with `execution-settings-changed` even though nothing changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The join gate compares the active turn's recorded execution selection with the incoming message's, field for field. Every producer records the caller's raw selection, except the CLI runner's capture in `src/agents/cli-runner/tool-authority.ts`: it records the cwd the runner already derived (defaulted to the workspace) and leaves `agentDir` empty when the agent command path did not pass one, while an incoming reply records the resolved agent dir and no cwd. This PR records the caller's `cwd` and the agent dir the runner will use (`params.agentDir ?? resolveAgentDir(...)`, as `prepare.ts` does later). The gate itself is unchanged: a different cwd or agent dir still refuses. The turn's tool authority input is untouched, so its fingerprint stays the same.

## User Impact

Once a sender is allowed to steer such a turn, their message joins it instead of waiting until it ends. On channels we only reached this check with the requester fix in #202511 applied (main refuses earlier); the two changes are independent.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after** (Telegram DM, claude-cli, owner's message during the turn that resumes after `sessions_yield`; main refuses this earlier at the requester check, so the before is #202511 alone):

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| #202511 alone | refused, `execution-settings-changed`; only `binding.agentDir` and `binding.cwd` differ |
| #202511 + this PR | accepted: the word lands in the same turn's DONE line |

Unit tests on `15a79a26d36`; live on the two stacked on `main@238160cf99b`.

- Test: `tool-authority.test.ts` captures an agent-command-shaped CLI turn and compares it with the real `isSameReplyExecutionSelection` against an incoming reply's selection: equal here, unequal on main; a different cwd or agent dir stays unequal. The existing projection test now expects the caller's cwd and agent dir.
- Review: `autoreview` `00bc7923f32..15a79a26d36`, P0–P2: clean.
- Checks: redgreen on the new test (fails with `tool-authority.ts` reverted, passes here); 3/3 in the file; `ocfix` lint and `tsgo` core and test graphs clean.

<details>
<summary>Live captures (fake Telegram Bot API, test user 1001, claude-cli)</summary>

The repro DMs a task: spawn a helper (`sleep 15`), reply STARTED, `sessions_yield`; when the result arrives, run `sleep 40` in the foreground, then reply DONE plus any words asked for meanwhile. While the resumed turn runs its `sleep 40`, it DMs "also include the word PELICAN<time> in your DONE line". Lines are the Bot API calls the gateway made and its steering log.

Before: #202511 alone on `main@238160cf99b` (06:38), plus a temporary diagnostic that dumped both selections:
```
06:38:46 steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=execution-settings-changed error="The execution settings changed before steering" activeRunId=announce:requester-settle:...:yield-1
diag: only differences between the two selections
  binding.agentDir  active (resumed CLI turn)=undefined              incoming (owner DM)="<profile>/agents/main/agent"
  binding.cwd       active (resumed CLI turn)="<profile>/workspace"  incoming (owner DM)=undefined
```

After: #202511 + this PR on `main@238160cf99b` (07:26), no `steering rejected` line:
```
07:26:07 inject      'Spawn one helper subagent ... Reply STARTED and then call sessions_yield ...'
07:26:39 sendMessage 'CHILD-OK'
07:26:41 edit status 'sleep-15-helper: completed / Exec running'   <- resumed turn starts sleep 40
07:26:48 inject      'While that runs: also include the word PELICAN072607 in your DONE line.'
07:27:21 edit status 'Exec' (done)
07:27:23 sendMessage 'DONE PELICAN072607'                          <- same turn, one DONE
```
Control, plain DM turn on the same build (07:28): steer accepted, `DONE PELICAN072823`.

</details>
<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Alternatives considered: comparing effective values inside the gate would touch the shared check and is wrong for ACP-placed sessions, whose cwd is node-owned; forwarding `agentDir` from `attempt-execution.ts` would change the turn's tool authority input and other consumers of `params.agentDir`.

</details>

Part of #202510 (with #202512)

## What Problem This Solves

In a channel DM, after the agent spawns subagents and calls `sessions_yield`, the turn that resumes with their results refuses the owner's own mid-turn message (`requester-mismatch`), so it waits until that turn ends. `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md` says guidance from the same person joins a subagent completion; on channels it does not.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resumed (`subagent_settle`) turn has no sender, so steering sees an unknown requester. The yielding owner's identity already reaches that turn, inside its yield admission scope (`requesterOwner`), but steering never read it. This PR reads it once when the turn's tool authority is captured, bound to that settle run's session, and adds one continuation kind: guidance joins when it arrives through host-attested channel ingress from that exact owner, while the turn is running and that sender is still a configured owner. Who yielded is fixed when the snapshot is taken, so the owner's own message, which as a fresh channel turn revokes the pending yield authority, does not end the guidance. Like the other continuation kinds it keeps the turn's own tool authority snapshot unchanged and does not let the guidance answer pending questions; the turn does not gain the owner's identity or tools.

## User Impact

The owner can redirect work while helper results are being processed. Other senders, other transports, follow-up results (`subagent_announce`) and runs in other sessions started inside its scope still queue as before. On CLI backends the turn is then held by a second, independent check, fixed in #202512.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after** (Telegram DM, claude-cli, the repro from the issue):

| Build | Owner's message during the resumed turn |
|---|---|
| 2026.11.5 | refused, `requester-mismatch` |
| this PR alone | passes the requester check; claude-cli then refuses with `execution-settings-changed` (#202512) |
| this PR + #202512 | accepted: the word lands in the same turn's DONE line, no follow-up turn |
| plain DM turn (control) | accepted |

Tested on `5f78308fc68`; live with #202512 stacked on `main@238160cf99b`. The embedded backend records the resolved agent dir already, so this PR alone is expected to suffice there (not run live).

<details>
<summary>Live captures (fake Telegram Bot API, test user 1001, claude-cli)</summary>

The repro DMs a task: spawn a helper (`sleep 15`), reply STARTED, `sessions_yield`; when the result arrives, run `sleep 40` in the foreground, then reply DONE plus any words asked for meanwhile. While the resumed turn runs its `sleep 40`, it DMs "also include the word PELICAN<time> in your DONE line". Lines are the Bot API calls the gateway made and its steering log.

Before (released 2026.11.5, 04:29):
```
04:29:33 steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=requester-mismatch disposition=followup-policy channel=telegram activeRunId=announce:requester-settle:main:agent:main:main:<id>:yield-1
 70.3s sendMessage 'DONE PELICAN042849 (the sleep 40 had already finished before this word arrived ...)'   <- the steer ran afterwards as its own turn
```

This PR alone on claude-cli (06:38):
```
06:38:46 steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=execution-settings-changed error="The execution settings changed before steering" activeRunId=announce:requester-settle:...:yield-1
```

This PR + #202512, `main@238160cf99b` (07:26), no `steering rejected` line:
```
07:26:07 inject      'Spawn one helper subagent ... Reply STARTED and then call sessions_yield ...'
07:26:39 sendMessage 'CHILD-OK'
07:26:41 edit status 'sleep-15-helper: completed / Exec running'   <- resumed turn starts sleep 40
07:26:48 inject      'While that runs: also include the word PELICAN072607 in your DONE line.'
07:27:21 edit status 'Exec' (done)
07:27:23 sendMessage 'DONE PELICAN072607'                          <- same turn, one DONE
```
Control, plain DM turn on the same build (07:28): steer accepted, `DONE PELICAN072823`.

</details>

- Tests: six rows in the existing `session-controller.message-join.test.ts` matrix. The owner joining, also after the yield authority is revoked as the owner's message does (and failing once the owner is revoked before submission), fails on main and passes here; another sender, the same id on another transport, a follow-up result and another run's scope stay deferred. 61/61 pass.
- Review: `autoreview` `c8931b32d3d..5f78308fc68`, P0–P2: clean.
- Checks: redgreen on `5f78308fc68` (fails with the four source files reverted, passes here); `ocfix` lint and `tsgo` core and test graphs clean.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Alternatives considered: giving the settle turn the yielding requester's `RequesterOrigin` would also make the existing same-requester check pass, but it recomputes `senderIsOwner` and the sender's tool policy for that turn and lets other collaborative senders join a now-known principal. Reusing `bindRequesterOwnerIdentity` does not work at this point because the gateway tool-caller identity is not installed yet when the snapshot is captured.

Not covered here: a yielding requester who is not a configured channel owner (the yield scope then carries no owner) still queues, and so does a result turn whose pending yield authority was already revoked by another channel message in the session between the yield and the result. Background exec completions and automation (cron) turns show the same refusal with different causes (no requester owner identity is carried for them); they are left for separate PRs.

</details>

prs.title: improve: reduce session sidebar work during streaming bursts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session events during streaming bursts can repeatedly recompute child activity for unrelated sidebar rows, consuming the Gateway main thread even when those rows do not change.

## User Impact

Unchanged child contributions remain reusable across session events and list subscribers. Row contents, audience visibility, and event ordering are preserved. No protocol, configuration, schema, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`bumpAgentRunIndexVersion` advances the run registry revision and emits a keyed runtime publication (`src/infra/agent-run-registry-state.ts:76–90`). The child owner already invalidates that key and its ancestors (`session-row-child-activity.ts:367–389, 415–417`), but did not acknowledge the registry revision. Its next read consequently took the broad fallback at lines 140–142 and dirtied **every cached child contribution**.

The fix acknowledges the revision through the existing runtime invalidation operation after invalidating the published key, stored session-ID aliases, and their ancestors. Keyed publications carry their runtime session identity, including the previous identity when a run moves. Broad and session-ID-only publications retain their existing handling. Production growth is **+18/−2, net +16 lines**: the additional lines carry the existing alias identity contract across the publisher/child-owner boundary. There is no new cache or coalescing point. Existing audience/exclusion identities, time-based expiry, and private-source isolation remain in control.

This builds on #200899, #201420, #201591, #201758, #202117, and #202337. The measured repeated term is child activity. Existing freeze, selection, and sidebar sharing reuse already prevents proportional recomputation in this workload; this change does not redo those optimizations.

## Evidence

### Original lane evidence (preserved)

The measurements and checks in this section are historical evidence from the original lane/head, not the repaired head. Autoreview found that its 10% child-event branch changed only `registeredAt`, which is not a projection input; those child publications were no-ops, while model publications still exercised the invalidation defect. The corrected campaign below toggles actual projected child activity.

The interleaved work-count regression fails on base `9bb091e873e4c` and passes with the fix. It moves a real registered run between three parents, alternates owner/viewer audiences with different child visibility, checks activity and release state, and requires untouched children to remain unprojected. The new test and five related event/projection suites pass: **36 tests in six files**. Targeted lint, formatting, scripts typecheck, gateway-root test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.

The existing `sidebar-presentation-measure.ts` rig now exercises 15,000 persisted synthetic entries (100 parents with 149 children each), eight active child runs and their eight parents, six loopback WebSocket subscribers across two profiles, and 100-row sidebar pages every 47 events. Each arm handles 4,700 logical events / 28,200 delivered event frames and 600 list requests. Target input is 470 logical events/s; six-recipient fan-out is heavier than 470 outbound frames/s. Mix: 60% chat deltas, 20% activity publications, 10% model updates, 10% child runtime updates. These event kinds use the prepared event/list owners and registry publishers; their proportions are synthetic because aggregate stacks do not provide actual production ratios.

Acceptance recorded before measurement: lower repeated child work, main-thread CPU, and allocation; matching normalized event/final-row bytes and FIFO counts; no 20% regression in timing summary. Five serial alternating AB/BA pairs, separate timing and sampled-allocation campaigns, warm fixtures, Node 24.22.1 on a controlled Boat Linux VM (observed 8 CPUs, 15,991 MiB RAM; one-minute load 1.06–2.04). Allocation sampling is 32 KiB and includes collected objects. A = base owner, B = candidate; the workload is identical in both processes.

| Pair/order | Main-thread ms / 1k events, A → B | Worst synchronous CPU ms, A → B | Worst synchronous elapsed ms, A → B | Sampled bytes/event, A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (AB) | 2594 → 1148 | 88.66 → 24.00 | 88.55 → 23.75 | 2225000 → 752649 |
| 2 (BA) | 2580 → 999 | 89.77 → 3.41 | 89.76 → 3.72 | 2220471 → 744726 |
| 3 (AB) | 2402 → 953 | 83.62 → 3.01 | 84.10 → 2.54 | 2224971 → 742542 |
| 4 (BA) | 2385 → 858 | 102.99 → 2.00 | 103.06 → 1.93 | 2215440 → 741371 |
| 5 (AB) | 2351 → 913 | 95.78 → 2.99 | 96.58 → 2.59 | 2213713 → 740573 |
| Median | 2,402 → 953 | 89.77 → 3.01 | 89.76 → 2.59 | 2,220,471 → 742,542 |
| p95 across five runs (maximum) | 2,594 → 1,148 | 102.99 → 24.00 | 103.06 → 23.75 | 2,225,000 → 752,649 |

Median main-thread work improves **60.3%**, worst on-CPU slice **96.7%**, and allocation **66.6%**. All five pairs match normalized event digests and final list digests; every recipient receives sequence 0 through 4,699 in order. Normalization removes only generated fixture profile IDs/avatar versions and snapshot timestamps.

Separate instrumented attribution (inclusive CPU; child is nested within present, so these rows are not additive):

| Path | Calls A → B | Main-thread ms / 1k events A → B | Worst synchronous CPU ms A → B | Worst elapsed ms A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Present, including child activity | 116,400 → 116,400 | 1922.55 → 181.45 | 25.689 → 20.001 | 25.093 → 20.274 |
| Child activity | 116,400 → 116,400 | 1749.28 → 29.81 | 24.896 → 1.011 | 24.989 → 0.372 |
| Select, including prepared rows/roster/policy/owners/sort | 600 → 600 | 17.23 → 12.51 | 1.955 → 1.009 | 1.309 → 0.543 |
| Freeze | 972 → 972 | 1.49 → 1.05 | 1.000 → 1.001 | 0.083 → 0.232 |
| Sidebar share | 600 → 600 | 0.21 → 0.43 | 1.001 → 1.007 | 0.016 → 0.033 |

Child contributions: **1,917,378 → 1,410 (−99.93%)**. Present still gets called for each consumer; its child owner now retains unchanged contributions. Freeze/selection/share counts are unchanged. These tiny unchanged paths are not improvement claims: instrumented share CPU rises 0.21 → 0.43 ms/1k and freeze maximum elapsed rises 0.083 → 0.232 ms. Their per-call CPU samples reach about 1 ms even for sub-ms wall durations; use the uninstrumented campaign for total/tail claims.

The controlled candidate sustains **470 logical events/s**; the baseline reaches 385–423 (median 414). Median event-loop delay improves at p95 **2.40 → 2.15 ms**, p99 **58.06 → 7.42 ms**, and maximum **98.11 → 17.09 ms**. Median GC elapsed/event is **0.0445 → 0.0277 ms**.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused checks</summary>

Save the original owner and run the same committed rig against each owner, alternating order for five pairs with fresh state directories (or the rig's existing `--repeats 5 --barrier-dir … --side base|fix` controls):

```sh
mkdir -p .local/session-surge/base
git show 9bb091e873e4c:src/gateway/session-row-child-activity.ts > .local/session-surge/base/session-row-child-activity.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sidebar-presentation-measure.ts   --surge --sessions 15000 --page-size 100 --clients 6 --operations 4700   --state-dir .local/session-surge/base-1 --output .local/session-surge/base-1.json   --source-file .local/session-surge/base/session-row-child-activity.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sidebar-presentation-measure.ts   --surge --sessions 15000 --page-size 100 --clients 6 --operations 4700   --state-dir .local/session-surge/fix-1 --output .local/session-surge/fix-1.json
```

Use separate fresh arms with `--allocations` for allocation and `--surge-detail` for coarse path attribution/work counts. CPU profiles are separate from the timing table. The rig records source hashes, load, CPU/wall slice pairs, event digests, and GC/event-loop metrics.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-presentation.fingerprints.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-event-parity.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-event-trees.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.subagent-index.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.incognito.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --incremental
```

</details>

### Remaining gaps

This is a synthetic production-shaped owner/transport workload, **not a booted Gateway or live-model test**, and does not establish production chat.history p95 or reproduce every reported one-second stall. An earlier macOS campaign on an overloaded shared host (load 50–66) also reduced median CPU 2,479 → 1,097 ms/1k and allocation 2.42 MB → 0.758 MB/event, but its timer-delay p95 moved 3.31 → 6.17 ms. That diagnostic prompted the controlled Linux campaign above, where p95, p99, and maximum all improve. The initial remote browser-hydration step failed on an Ubuntu PPA label change before the benchmark; the same VM then completed the Node-only workload through supported `--no-hydrate`, frozen dependency installation, and source-hash verification. No provider change or CI retry was used.

The original lane had production +4 lines and regression coverage +76 lines; its remaining diff extended the existing rig/probe to make the requested workload, FIFO checks, and attribution repeatable. No production systems accessed. The original lane performed no autoreview or merge; maintainer takeover qualification follows below. Exact-head CI is green on `98ea8fba6a487fe095ebd32347b5536e0ad1aa9f`: [test lanes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44857707529), [artifact build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44857707181), and the PR `openclaw/ci-gate`. No CI job was rerun. Superseded administrative auto-response jobs were cancelled; validation checks passed.


## Takeover qualification at `b0241f852b93`

Rebased onto `6760abc62f0ef2c5aff46abf150c46f59cf6518f` without conflicts, retaining #202764, #203040 and #203037. Original author metadata and evidence are preserved.

Both ClawSweeper findings are repaired. Keyed runtime publications now invalidate stored session-ID aliases and their ancestors before acknowledging the revision, including the previous ID when a run moves. The expanded real-owner regression is red on the original candidate and green after repair. The default 10,000-session/100-row benchmark previously timed out because computed backfill keys were outside the selected page; it now warms actual selected rows and completes. Codex autoreview also caught the no-op child-event fixture, now repaired by toggling `projectSessionActive`.

Acceptance recorded before the new campaign: identical normalized event/final-page hashes and FIFO delivery, reduced child work/CPU/allocation, no unexplained 20% median timing regression. A/A controls and five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs use fresh processes and separate untraced timing, collected-object-inclusive sampled allocation (32 KiB), and instrumented attribution. Baseline substitutes the exact main-parent production owners; candidate uses the repaired owners. Host: macOS, 32 logical CPUs, 512 GiB RAM, Node 26.12.1; no concurrent local tests during measurements. The subsequent CI repairs change one consumer expectation and the terminal-event fixture setup only; measured production and benchmark bytes are unchanged.

## Corrected workload measurements

Measured production/benchmark head `30fbd3c58e7a88e62b7785ecc8f391e21ccd8a3e` versus exact main parent `6760abc62f0ef2c5aff46abf150c46f59cf6518f`. macOS, Node 26.12.1, serial fresh processes, 15,000 persisted synthetic sessions, six loopback recipients, 4,700 events and 600 list calls per arm. Both arms use the same source-override loader. Child events now toggle actual projected activity. Timing, sampled allocation and attribution are separate.

| Pair/order | Main CPU ms/1k A → B | Max synchronous CPU ms A → B | Max synchronous elapsed ms A → B | Sampled bytes/event A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (AB) | 2228.59 → 959.05 | 47.945 → 2.611 | 48.031 → 2.610 | 2764151 → 1011237 |
| 2 (BA) | 2089.73 → 1099.69 | 46.275 → 2.383 | 46.437 → 2.389 | 2767777 → 1007070 |
| 3 (AB) | 2254.24 → 977.45 | 46.754 → 1.706 | 46.844 → 1.701 | 2760196 → 1007181 |
| 4 (BA) | 2105.99 → 1083.70 | 46.165 → 2.033 | 46.231 → 2.029 | 2759507 → 1005622 |
| 5 (AB) | 2521.28 → 1240.21 | 59.586 → 3.001 | 63.588 → 11.091 | 2763323 → 1008984 |

| Metric | Median A → B | p95 across five runs (maximum) A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main CPU ms/1k | 2228.5868 → 1083.7036 | 2521.2809 → 1240.2085 |
| Max synchronous CPU ms | 46.7540 → 2.3830 | 59.5860 → 3.0010 |
| Max synchronous elapsed ms | 46.8441 → 2.3893 | 63.5882 → 11.0907 |
| Sampled bytes/event | 2763322.8664 → 1007181.2085 | 2767776.5464 → 1011237.0911 |
| Loop p95 ms | 2.7709 → 2.3081 | 2.9778 → 2.8672 |
| Loop p99 ms | 48.5622 → 8.8474 | 55.0830 → 9.6993 |
| Loop maximum ms | 55.1813 → 14.2787 | 72.8105 → 25.3460 |
| GC elapsed ms/event | 0.0456 → 0.0288 | 0.0579 → 0.0365 |

A/A controls (two independent baseline processes):

timing: 2034.89 → 2305.35 (+13.29%).

allocation: 2766514.19 → 2760998.21 (-0.20%).

Host one-minute load range: 4.57–10.82. All 26 outputs match normalized event and final-page digests; each client receives sequence 0–4,699, 28,200 total frames and 600 lists. Source hashes are stable within each arm and match the pinned owner bytes.

Separate inclusive path attribution (nested CPU is not additive):

| Path | Calls A → B | Main CPU ms/1k events A → B | Max synchronous CPU ms A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| present | 116400 → 116400 | 1606.307 → 190.285 | 1.814 → 0.453 |
| child | 116400 → 116400 | 1418.420 → 38.131 | 1.789 → 0.048 |
| freeze | 3644 → 3644 | 4.239 → 3.315 | 0.046 → 0.034 |
| select | 600 → 600 | 10.691 → 7.590 | 0.500 → 0.423 |
| share | 798 → 798 | 11.546 → 11.719 | 0.649 → 0.717 |

Child contributions (count-only probe): **1,997,289 → 1,880**. Share attribution is effectively flat, 11.55 → 11.72 ms/1k; no improvement is claimed for that path.

### Verification and review

49 focused tests passed across fingerprint, event parity, invalidation, event trees, subagent index, incognito, selection and registry-publication coverage. Two affected browser tests and nine UI E2E tests passed. No browser-application Node import was added. CI exposed one additional stale consumer expectation in `agent-events.test.ts`; it now expects the intentional runtime session identity while retaining exact notification counts and irrelevant/repeated-update silence. Its targeted local rerun passed (one selected case; 45 unrelated cases excluded). Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for the substantive repair and the subsequent one-line expectation repair.

`pnpm check:changed` and the targeted script replay pass all gates except inherited Teams dead exports. After repairing the benchmark's own unused export through the existing probe object, its script scan is clean. A fresh isolated checkout of exact parent `6760abc62f0ef2c5aff46abf150c46f59cf6518f` reproduces the same production unused exports (`htmlTagAttributeValues`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, `safeHostForUrl`) and full-tree unused export (`safeHostForUrl`) in `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/html.ts`. Introducing commit [ec270048434f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec270048434f3194393a00dbf9a8951cf5711a7f) (#203084) moved the helpers into that file, making their production consumers local while retaining exports. This is a main regression for follow-up, not a passing check. This PR changes neither that owner nor Knip configuration. Exact-head PR CI is tracked separately; no failed job has been rerun to chase green.

### Terminal-event fixture investigation

The exact-head CI attempt at `f71562f0784ad` timed out waiting for `subagent-status` in the terminal-subagent websocket case. The same untouched case and its three predecessors reproduced on an isolated Linux VM with Node 24.22.1 and pinned OpenClaw Bun. macOS passed; the exact CI main parent (`165f1297b8c0e139257f85597dafd9127b983499`) and bounded diagnostic replays passed. These replays do **not** establish inheritance or prove the original timeout's cause. No CI retry was requested.

Source inspection identified a fixture precondition gap: persistence seeding does not establish the row in the gateway's asynchronous projection, and cold discovery intentionally uses `updated` rather than `subagent-status`. The fixture now performs and verifies one real `sessions.describe` request before completing the child. All terminal-event, status, timing, parent and exactly-once assertions and timeouts remain intact. Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this test-only correction. The corrected four-case predecessor/terminal sequence passes on macOS and on isolated Linux with CI’s pinned Node/Bun runtime. The VM was released. The same CI attempt also lost its baseline-ratchet hosted runner (GitHub annotation: “The hosted runner lost communication with the server”); there was no ratchet finding or log artifact. Fresh exact-head CI remains the landing gate; a passing replay is not presented as proof of the original intermittent cause.

### Deep-equal follow-up and limits

No deep-equal removal is included. The materializer can accept fresh worker entries or retained facts. The lineage owner already skips full entry comparison when stored identity is retained, then checks the two rewritten lineage keys. Fresh equal worker values have no equivalent producer change bit; lineage and selection can change independently of stored metadata, and the fallback-model comparison covers a derived value. Attribute residual comparisons by source before replacing that contract. The available aggregate does not identify a safely redundant comparison.

This is a synthetic resident-metadata/loopback-transport qualification, not a booted Gateway, live-model test, or production latency claim. It does not traverse bulk database payloads or workspace trees, so it does not emulate a 35 GiB database or 62,000-file btrfs workspace. No production data or production system access was used. Measurement acceptances are the performance-loop lead agent's under standing unattended authority, not personal acceptance by Peter.


### Supplemental isolated-Gateway streaming proof

At final head `b0241f852b93`, the committed `team-shape-fixture.ts` and `transcript-broadcast-measure.ts` drivers completed a real isolated source Gateway run with 10,000 generated sessions, 8,000 settled child runs, 23 concurrent agent turns, 20 sidebar WebSocket subscribers, and five rounds of 30-second keyed row churn. Each round recorded 430 successful metadata patches and 430 transcript appends: 115 measured primary turns, 2,150 patches, 2,150 appends, 820 list reads and 74,020 delivered session events in total. All 20 subscribers had identical settled event counts in every round. The driver exited successfully; its owned Gateway and model listeners were gone afterward. Shutdown reported plugin-service/log-close warnings, so this is not presented as clean lifecycle proof.

This addresses the requested real Gateway/agent/transport portion of the rank-up move using synthetic state and a deterministic loopback model endpoint. It is not an external-model run or an additional before/after performance campaign; the interleaved owner measurements above establish the reduction in unrelated child work. No Team access occurred.

Reproduction (fresh state directory and free local ports):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts --state-dir <fresh-fixture> --sessions 10000 --runs 8000 --settled-runs --cron 0 --approvals 0 --projects 0 --transcript-mib 1 --port 42842
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts --state-dir <fresh-fixture> --entry src/entry.ts --port 42842 --mock-port 42844 --scenario transcript-broadcast --runs 23 --clients 20 --exact-clients 20 --row-mode sidebar --list-interval-ms 5000 --chunks 35 --chunk-interval-ms 1000 --session-row-churn-seconds 30 --diagnostics --prompt-kib 1 --revision b0241f852b93d6e445424137aa8da45f9ec36955
```

### Final-head CI follow-through

Run 44926118094 surfaced an intermittent UI Inbox Escape-dismissal assertion at `ui/src/e2e/native-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:136`. The isolated case passes on both this head and exact CI main parent `010b5348381e4aaf2ac60d15023fd7ec9ed991b5`; all seven native-navigation predecessor/sibling cases also pass on that parent. The test and panel owners are byte-identical between these heads, and the mock-Gateway UI harness does not execute this PR's server projection changes. Its preceding CI run passed the same UI shard. The retained failure screenshot shows an open, focused Inbox without browser/script errors. The intermittent trigger remains unconfirmed. No assertion was weakened, no UI source was changed, and no inherited-failure waiver is claimed. The remaining test shard passed. One supported failed-check retry on the unchanged head then passed the UI shard and aggregate gate. [CI run 44926118094, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44926118094/attempts/2) is successful on exact head `b0241f852b93d6e445424137aa8da45f9ec36955`: 56 successful jobs and 28 skipped. This passing retry does not establish or repair the intermittent dismissal trigger; no inherited-failure exception was used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Keeps generated Control UI locales synchronized without bypassing protected-branch checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI Locale Refresh workflow generated worker memory from `5a5d4948bf2d68b9979aecdb99ebe8fad98013a9`, reconciled it once against `fe48a6f224f94c963a2f501e72aefbca38002613`, and published the current output through a reviewable automation branch.

## User Impact

Related: #186561 (merged service-worker handoff; native recovery follows a separate path).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native dashboard recovery loading the public page for an authenticated private chat, which can show “Conversation unavailable.”

## User Impact

Reloading, reconnecting, or restoring a native dashboard window returns to the private conversation with its supported navigation hints and fragment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical chat URLs serve public conversation documents. Native recovery now reuses the existing protected session-entry handoff for trusted chat URLs within the same origin and dashboard mount. Existing authentication, account-change, and TLS checks retain their owners.

## Evidence

- Reconciled with `main` at `125b9c817daaf6788d6dc73665f91514aa8a4277`, preserving the compact native toolbar changes. Targeted SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint, Swift syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The current source candidate against `125b9c817daaf6788d6dc73665f91514aa8a4277` compiled successfully with the supported Swift build-tests command. Tests were compiled, not executed.
- Sandboxed URL-contract tests passed on the earlier `087d1229ef49822acd43f771787b2a4be0fe2409` base: 8 functions, 17 expanded cases. The URL helper and three test files are unchanged in this candidate; this is not a current-candidate test execution or WebKit lifecycle result.
- Local OpenClaw Autoreview through Codex/OpenAI (`gpt-6-astra`, medium, P0–P3) reviewed the five-file local snapshot against `125b9c817daaf6788d6dc73665f91514aa8a4277`: complete, scoped-clean, no findings.
- The unchanged test-line ratchet passes against the pinned base: 6,657,655 counted lines, ceiling 6,657,668. Swift tests are outside its JS/TS patterns, so this change adds no allocation or unrelated headroom.

The pre-fix controller regression and installed-app recovery have not been executed; no desktop WebKit test result or merge readiness is claimed.

Rebased the one feature commit onto canonical `main` at `282121402940c47c87a68bf08bb6e66097818884`. The conflict now composes main's retained-document route with the PR's trusted, same-mount session-entry conversion, so a retired chat URL still re-enters the private dashboard shell. `git range-diff` shows only that integration adjustment; `git diff --check` passes. ## What Problem This Solves

The QA Gateway replay proxy still contains reconnect-handshake controls whose test cases were removed in [#160115](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160115). Those unused commands and their frame buffer add fixture code without serving a current test.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The existing real Gateway lost-response test and RPC-client cases remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unused hold/release commands, held-frame state and unconsumed snapshot field: 32 fewer support lines, with no production or test-case changes. Retain forwarding, committed-response loss, authentication, event recording and process cleanup. The audit ledger records the bounded fixture review and retained contracts.

## Evidence

- On Boat Linux (4 CPUs, 8 GiB; Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0), baseline and candidate both passed the real Gateway case (1/1) and RPC-client suite (10/10).
- A deliberate retry after a dispatched request failed made the retained Gateway test fail: it observed two requests and two committed sessions, plus unexpected successful resolution. Production bytes were restored.
- Syntax, targeted formatting/lint, the final two-file format check and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- Independent preservation review found no lost current contracts.
- All seven deadcode phases ran. Both unused-file scans and script exports passed. Dependency and production/full-tree export failures reproduced on the unchanged base: Feishu's `formatFeishuMediaContent`/`FeishuBotAddedEvent` and Teams' attachment helpers. The explicit full-export phase also matched the base. These checks remain recorded as failed; the initial dependency output additionally contained first-download chatter.

Updates `androidx.test.uiautomator:uiautomator` from 2.4.0 to 2.4.1 Updates `org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on` from 1.86 to 1.87
Changelog

Sourced from org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on's changelog.

Version 1.87

Release: 1.87
Date: 2026, 11th November.

Defects Fixed

  • PrivateKeyFactory, and so the ML-DSA and ML-KEM KeyFactory services, ignored the tag of the RFC 9881 / RFC 9935 private key CHOICE and applied no length checks, so mislabelled or inconsistent seed, expandedKey and both forms were accepted. Each form is now checked for its tag, exact lengths and consistency; the pre-RFC draft forms are still read.
  • X500Name.equals was quadratic in the number of RDNs for names that are equal but not byte-identical, and is reached from unverified CMS, TSP and S/MIME messages; the CMS signer and recipient stores could also be slowed with colliding ids. Name comparison is now n log n and the stores no longer hash their entries (CVE-2026-103611).
  • Tables keyed on ASN.1 object hash codes, which a sender can make collide - Extensions, X509Extensions, ExtendedKeyUsage, the CMS AttributeTable, the EST CSRAttributesResponse and the CMS digest algorithm sets - made parsing quadratic in the number of entries. They are now ordered maps and sets.
  • CMSSignedData digested the content once for every signer verified. Signers using the same digest algorithm now share one digest, and the new org.bouncycastle.cms.max_digest_algorithms property can bound the number of distinct digest algorithms computed over one message.
  • The verify side of the ML-DSA-CALCULATE-MU signature service, and MLDSASigner.verifyMu, did not absorb the message, so a correct mu was accepted only for an empty message, and the signer was left unusable afterwards. verifyMu now derives mu as generateMu does and compares in constant time.
  • KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("SM2", "BC") was built on the generic EC generator and could draw a private key of n - 1, which GB/T 32918.1 excludes. It now uses SM2KeyPairGenerator.
  • ESTResponse was quadratic in the number of repeated header lines, and a read limit only applied after the header block. Header values are now collected once and the header block counts against the read limit.
  • The C509 encoding of RFC 6955 proof-of-possession signature values and of the RFC 9883 privateKeyPossessionStatement attribute did not follow draft-ietf-cose-cbor-encoded-cert-21 and could not be reconstructed. Both now convert in each direction, and the draft-ietf-cose-c509-test-vectors-02 vectors drive the tests.
  • DANE SMIMEA support: JndiDANEFetcherFactory mangled the owner name of listed records so lookups failed, DANEEntryStore kept only one entry per owner name, and DANEEntrySelectorFactory mishandled addresses with a quoted local-part or no '@'. All three are corrected, and DANEEntry rejects a record that is not a full certificate entry.
  • TimeStampToken accepted a token whose signing-time attribute disagreed with the genTime in its TSTInfo. Such a token is now rejected (org.bouncycastle.tsp.allow_inconsistent_signing_time switches the check off), and TimeStampTokenGenerator sets signing-time from the genTime (CVE-2026-103615).
  • TimeStampToken.validate() accepted an MD5 message imprint and TSPAlgorithms.ALLOWED included MD5. MD5 is removed from ALLOWED, validate() rejects an imprint algorithm outside the allowed set, and TSPAlgorithms.LEGACY and org.bouncycastle.tsp.allowed_imprint_algorithms are provided for callers needing it (CVE-2026-103606).
  • CRL-based revocation checking mishandled a CRL entry reasonCode outside the RFC 5280 set: 11 left the certificate unrevoked and other values threw an unchecked exception. An undefined reasonCode is now processed as unspecified.
  • OERDefinition.enumItem(label, value) discarded the explicit enumerand value. The value is now kept and unnumbered items are numbered as X.680 sec. 20 specifies.
  • OERInputStream did not detect a stream ending inside an INTEGER or BIT STRING value, decoding the zero-padded buffer instead. Length-driven reads now fail with EOFException and do not allocate a declared length up front.
  • The OER codec encoded a signed INTEGER whose upper bound is exactly the maximum of a fixed-size word in the next word up; X.696 sec. 10.4 bounds are inclusive.
  • The ETSI TS 102 941 response code wrappers range-checked a truncated int value, so 2^32 was accepted as "ok". Out-of-range values are now rejected.
  • OERInputStream accepted an empty group of octets as zero in four places where X.696 requires at least one octet. Each now fails with an IOException.
  • OEROutputStream could not encode a CHOICE whose chosen alternative has a tag number of 63 or more.
  • OEROutputStream rejected a required SEQUENCE component as absent when it arrived wrapped in a defined OEROptional.
  • OERInputStream failed with a NullPointerException for an absent optional SEQUENCE component selected through a switch that has a default value.
  • OERInputStream truncated a SEQUENCE OF count to 32 bits. A count that does not fit in 31 bits is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream rejected a valid SEQUENCE OF on streams whose available() reported fewer bytes than the element count. The count is now bounded by the decoder's allocation ceiling instead.
  • OERInputStream could not decode a variable-size BIT STRING, and mis-sized a fixed one that is not a whole number of octets. Both forms of X.696 clause 13 are now decoded, and OERDefinition gains bitString() and bitString(lower, upper).
  • OEROutputStream wrote a negative INTEGER under a type with a non-negative lower bound as a different, positive value. It is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream.uint64() read its value as signed; it now reads unsigned.
  • The OER codec treated an INTEGER with a positive lower bound as signed, where X.696 sec. 10.2 gives it the unsigned encodings.
  • The OER codec encoded and decoded negative ENUMERATED values wrongly; both directions now follow X.696 sec. 11.4.
  • ASN1Enumerated rejected negative values, which X.680 allows. The checks are removed, isNegative() and longValueExact() are added, and valueOf() returns shared instances for 0 to 15.
  • A PBEKey stored in a BCFKS KeyStore was not reported as a key entry, so KeyStore.getEntry() returned null for it.
  • The CMS content-type decoders (SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthenticatedData, AuthEnvelopedData, EncryptedData) and the streaming CMS parsers let unchecked exceptions escape for short or malformed content. Malformed content is now reported through the declared CMSException or IOException.
  • A KeyAgreement asked for its shared secret before doPhase returned data rather than throwing IllegalStateException - for Diffie-Hellman, the private value itself. Every key agreement in the provider now refuses the request.
  • Mac.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance failed for the HMAC SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 object identifiers; both are now aliased.
  • A KTSParameterSpec naming an HKDF with parameters was accepted at Cipher init and failed with an unchecked exception from wrap or unwrap. The KTS Ciphers now report it at init as InvalidAlgorithmParameterException.
  • A DTLS handshake deadlocked when a handshake message ahead of the peer's ChangeCipherSpec was lost while the ChangeCipherSpec and Finished arrived, as retransmissions were discarded as belonging to the old epoch. They are now accepted until the handshake completes.
  • The lightweight key info factories encoded a GOST R 34.10-2012 key on a legacy CryptoPro curve under id-GostR3410-2001. The digestParamSet now decides, and is OPTIONAL on read and write per RFC 9215 (bc-csharp github #707).
  • Name-constraint checking canonicalised a host with an extra empty label, such as "example.com..", into a name that matched no constraint, escaping an excluded subtree. A tested name whose host carries an empty label is now refused where a constraint of that type is in force (github PR #2436).
  • SSLContext.createSSLEngine() from BCJSSE in the 1.86 bctls jar failed with NoSuchMethodError on JDK 9 and later, from a return type mismatch between the base and jdk1.9 copies of SSLEngineUtil. The copies now agree, and a new multiReleaseCheck build task checks every multi-release jar for such mismatches (github #2448).
  • The BCFKS key store derived its scrypt keys with the block size r in place of the parallelization parameter p, so stores with p != r were not RFC 7914 readable. Derivation now follows RFC 7914, older stores are still read, and org.bouncycastle.bcfks.scrypt_p_eq_r (default true) keeps written stores readable by earlier releases.
  • Building an evidence record was cubic in the number of data objects. SortedHashList and SortedIndexedHashList now sort once, with the same resulting order and root hashes (github #2456).
  • ERSDataGroup recomputed its hash on every request rather than using the ERSCachingData cache.
  • ERSArchiveTimeStampGenerator rebuilt its reduced hash tree on every call; it is now built once.
  • Grain-128AEAD returned corrupted plaintext, with no error, from a decryption driven in chunks carrying more than the tag length. One-shot decryption and encryption were unaffected (github PR #2447).
  • The certificate path validators looked up an indirect CRL entry by serial number alone, so where two issuers had revoked the same serial number a revoked certificate could be reported as not revoked. Entries are now matched on issuer and serial number, including for CRLs parsed by the JDK's provider and in the jdk1.4 distribution.

... (truncated)

Updates `org.robolectric:robolectric` from 4.17 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from org.robolectric:robolectric's releases.

Robolectric 4.18.1 is a minor release that fixes several issues and improves the Robolectric simulator.

It fixes data races that ThreadSanitizer reported when several threads link calls to the same shadow method at once (#11784, #11786). It also fixes ShadowServiceManager.waitForService, which never blocked and could throw IllegalMonitorStateException (#11758), and scheduled task time queries on ShadowPausedLooper, which returned wrong times on newer SDKs and could race when called off the Looper thread (#11780, thanks to Brett Chabot). Content providers are now installed for lazily created applications (#11775), and Choreographer display receivers are disposed, which fixes a CloseGuard leak and stale clock callbacks (#11688, thanks to @​utzcoz).

For the simulator, it handles mouse and keyboard input when running headless (#11750) and advances the system clock by the time spent rendering (#11783). It also adds two opt-in system properties, which the simulator Gradle plugin turns on: robolectric.bindRealServices=true binds to the app's own services the way the system does (#11748), and robolectric.installDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler=true installs an uncaught exception handler that logs crashes the way Android does (#11734).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/robolectric/robolectric/compare/robolectric-4.18...robolectric-4.18.1

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed (#11625, #11633). As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

Other Highlights

  • Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36 (#11578).
  • Robolectric no longer prints the "restricted method in java.lang.System has been called" warnings on JDK 24+ (#11482).
  • The shadow annotation processor now supports KSP (#10996).
  • Lots of performance improvements:
    • Resource values are shared between bags and themes instead of copied (#11726, #11595)
    • Faster shadow method lookups (#11723, #11593)
    • Cached resource reference resolution (#11586)
