prs.title: fix(skills): reject unsupported Meme Maker output formats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meme Maker accepts local output paths such as `example.jpg` and reports success after writing SVG data. An image viewer or uploader expecting the format in the filename can reject the file.

## User Impact

Meme Maker now reports unsupported filename extensions and points users to `.svg` or `.png`, without creating or overwriting the requested file. Paths without an extension still produce SVG.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local renderer checks the extension before fetching the template or creating the destination directory. The same case-insensitive extension selects the PNG renderer.

## Evidence

Verified with the actual CLI on Linux, Node 24.18.0, and the real Imgflip Drake template.

- Main `745288fe28e` and stable `v2026.11.6` both exited successfully and wrote a file that `file` identified as SVG despite its `.jpg` extension. The skill and test sources were unchanged on the refreshed main base `4126cf267df`.
- The fixed CLI exited 1 with guidance for a `.jpg` path, left the output directory and cache absent, and preserved an existing file byte for byte.
- With the downloaded template in an isolated cache, uppercase `.SVG` and an extensionless path produced identical SVGs. Uppercase `.PNG` produced a 1200 × 1200 image with Chrome for Testing 149.0.7827.55, and FFmpeg decoded it.
- The focused regression failed on main because the render exited 0. On the fix, the tooling suite passed three tests with the opt-in PNG case skipped. The real PNG run above exercised that format directly. Focused TypeScript, Oxlint, formatting, Node syntax, and diff checks passed. Local autoreview reported no actionable P0 findings. macOS and Windows were outside this run.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused test</summary>

```sh
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
XDG_CACHE_HOME="$scratch/cache" node skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs \
  render drake --text Before --text After --out "$scratch/example.jpg"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Production +8/−2, tests +9/−1.

</details>

prs.title: feat: keep lean Gateway worker growth inside a memory budget
prs.body:
Fixes #202376. Related: #202373.

**Stacked on #202422**, now merged as `28aa5c88fd45`; this PR now targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

On small machines, Gateway worker pools grow to fixed caps regardless of how much memory is left, so a busy small container or laptop can run out of memory or stall turns. The lean resource profile from #202422 had no way to hold worker growth back.

## User Impact

User impact: in the `lean` profile, extra workers start only when they fit a memory budget; otherwise the work waits for an existing worker. `standard` is unchanged. `openclaw status` and `diagnostics.lanes` show the budget, its basis, waits and refusals. A new optional `gateway.resources.memoryBudgetMiB` overrides the default budget.

This is an admission rule, **not an OOM guarantee**. Memory already admitted (the main thread, floor workers, growth inside running workers, child processes) is measured, not refused. The proof below shows that the budget alone does **not** keep lean under a 1.5 GiB limit: floor workers alone reach it. The shared core host (#202377) is needed for that.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Budget by limit source** (provisional shares):

  | Limit source | Default budget | Memory use compared with it |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | cgroup v2 `memory.max` | 85% of the limit | `memory.current − inactive_file` of the limiting cgroup |
  | Host RAM (no container limit) | 40% of host RAM | The Gateway process RSS, including worker threads, **not** child processes |
  | `memoryBudgetMiB` set (lean only) | That many MiB | As above, by limit source |

  A container limit is sized for OpenClaw. A bare 4–8 GiB host is shared with everything else, and #202422 now selects lean below 8 GiB.
- **Floors always run.** Each pool keeps one worker (two for shared-state reads, so a held settlement read cannot block a fresh one), plus its point-read lane once used. Fixed direct workers keep their normal counts: native lifecycle supervisor, both state heartbeats, SQLite broker carriers, Knowledge registry and storage, PostgreSQL bridges, and the #202377 shared host. Floors are never refused, so admission cannot deadlock.
- **Growth waits.** A pool worker beyond its floor starts only if *measured use + reservations not yet running + that worker's estimate* stays under the budget. Running workers are counted by measurement and are not double-charged. Refused work stays in the same pool queue and is never dropped. Deadlines and cancellation are unchanged.
- **Floor warnings.** At startup the Gateway records its measured working set (the main isolate plus anything already running) and adds the per-kind floor estimates. It logs one warning if that exceeds the budget, and another if measured use exceeds the budget while only floor workers run. Either way, no growth is admitted.
- **Coverage:** main-isolate pools, including plugin SDK pools, get floors plus admission. Fixed direct families get floor reservations. Pools nested in worker threads stay at their floor in lean; the flag travels in worker environment data, never `process.env` or child processes. Plugin workers created directly, not through a pool, are measured once running but cannot be refused through their synchronous API.
- **#202377 seam:** `registerHostedSlotPredicate()`. A pool's first floor slot, or a SQLite `agent` / `shared-state` carrier, that the shared host claims needs no isolate reservation. The host itself is one floor entry. Neither branch imports the other.
- `WorkerTaskPoolCore` changes are confined to one helper (`worker-task-pool-memory.ts`): a lazily bound budget that rebinds after an in-process restart, a count-based bulk limit, and wait accounting. The core file stays within its line budget.

## Evidence

**Studio proof.** Crabbox Linux `local-container` leases on the Mac Studio, Node 26.12.1, `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, inspector-free. The workload is the reused part 3 F personal-assistant harness (33 turns, 3 child runs, a Knowledge call, an automation, compaction, 5-minute idle). The harness copy changed only the arm selection (`gateway.resources.profile`), the budget snapshot reader and `memory.stat` sampling; SHA-256 sums of the original and modified harness are recorded. One fresh lease per case; all leases were released.

Rebased onto #202422 head `9d7f71d104cc` (including main’s #202407 allocator default). Range-diff against previous base `f110ba8d49c1` shows no feature-patch changes: only regenerated config baselines and schema context changed. Existing Studio evidence is retained; every case already set `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, matching #202407. No new benchmark was run.

All cases ran build **`75e5303b`**. Rebasing onto `e57f84aa` and then `f110ba8d` left every file in this diff byte-identical. Subsequent changes add the host-RAM basis and override, wrapper extraction inventory, typed singleton initialization, conditional cleanup of the lean environment flag, test allocation and docs. These do not change the measured lean cgroup admission rule. Every case ran in a cgroup v2 container, where the 85% rule is unchanged, so these results apply to the current head.

| Case (1.5 GiB unless noted) | Completed | OOM kills | Peak anon | Peak `memory.current` | Workers | Growth admitted / refused / waits | p95 (info) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lean r1 | **yes**, 33/33 turns, 3/3 children, Knowledge, automation | 0 | 1,501 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 23 | 0 / 663 / 523 | 1.9 s |
| lean r2 | **yes**, 33/33 turns, 3/3 children, Knowledge, automation | 0 | 1,472 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 22 | 0 / 653 / 517 | 2.3 s |
| lean r3 | **no**: killed during startup, before the first turn | **1** | 1,092 MiB (last sample) | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 10 | 0 / 0 / 0 | — |
| standard | **no**: turn left pending after 26 turns | 0 | 1,508 MiB | 1,536 MiB (limit) | 24 | no budget | 6.4 s |
| standard, 3 GiB | **yes**, 33/33 turns | 0 | 1,799 MiB | 2,875 MiB | 28 | **no budget snapshot or events** | 0.9 s |

**Refusals and waits by family** (lean r1 / r2):

| Family | Refusals | Waits | Total wait (ms) | Longest wait (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| session-transcript | 449 / 442 | 395 / 391 | 7,159 / 7,764 | 194 / 220 |
| fs-safe-copy | 207 / 207 | 123 / 123 | 3,731 / 4,055 | 137 / 147 |
| provider-prompt-state | 7 / 4 | 5 / 3 | 39 / 17 | 22 / 15 |

Nothing was still waiting at the end of either round.

**Floor-only operation.** Lean admitted **zero** growth in every round: every lean worker was a floor worker. Even so, 22–23 live floor workers plus the main isolate drove the working set to about 1.52 GiB and anon to about 1.5 GiB.

**Startup warning, before and after.**
- **Before** (`871607f8` smoke): the estimate was per-kind floors only. Floors were 420 MiB at startup and 1,064 MiB at peak, against a 1,306 MiB budget, so **no warning** fired, although measured use reached about 1,522 MiB.
- **After** (`75e5303b`): the estimate is the measured startup baseline (590 / 592 MiB in r1 / r2) plus floors. It exceeded the budget early (1,354 / 1,415 MiB), and **the warning fired** in r1 and r2. Estimates peaked at 1,696 / 1,715 MiB.
- r3 was killed before the estimate crossed the budget.

**Conclusion.** The budget does what it claims: in lean it held growth to zero and queued about 520 tasks per run without dropping any, and standard is untouched. But it **cannot keep lean under 1.5 GiB by itself.** Floor workers and the main isolate fill the limit. r3 shows the startup peak alone (main RSS about 1 GiB plus three Gateway child processes of 294 MiB in total) can be OOM-killed. That is outside what admission controls, and is the gap the shared core host (#202377) and later lean reductions target. Lean completed 2 of 3 rounds; standard at 1.5 GiB completed 0 of 1.

**Startup peak** (saved samples only, every 2 s). Each Gateway's first start is its memory peak, before any turn and before admission has anything to refuse:

| Time after start | r1 main RSS / children / cgroup anon / workers | r2 | r3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 s | 468 / 76 / 479 MiB / — | 492 / 182 / 562 / — | 478 / 176 / 542 / — |
| 6 s | 876 / 294 / 1,006 / 10 | 995 / 294 / 1,125 / 5 | 962 / 294 / 1,092 / 10, then OOM-killed |
| 8 s | 1,283 / 294 / 1,413 / 19 | 1,289 / 294 / 1,419 / 11 | — |

- Main RSS includes every worker thread's isolate; the probe did not record main-isolate heap, so heap vs native vs worker isolates is not separable from these artifacts.
- The three children are Gateway child processes of 76 MiB (8 threads), about 107 MiB (11 threads) and about 111 MiB (11 threads). Their command lines were deliberately not recorded by the harness, so their identity is not established here.
- After the harness restart, the same three children run at 35–46 MiB each.
- Startup peaks happen before admission applies; reducing them belongs to the lean reductions (#202379), not this PR.

**Local checks on the current head:**
- Focused tests: pool admission (refusal queues on the floor worker, growth is released after exit, the point-read lane stays mandatory, rebind after restart; standard sizing is covered by the existing pool suites, which supply no budget) and the budget owner (pending vs measured, floor warnings by estimate and by measurement, hosted-slot claims including late registration, direct floors, restart and flag reset, each budget basis). Status, schema, profile and worker-runtime suites also pass.
- Typechecks: `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test`.
- Lint: oxlint on all changed files, `check:import-cycles`.
- Config: `config:docs:check`, `check:base-config-schema`. Core config count 2666 → 2667 for `gateway.resources.memoryBudgetMiB`.
- CI follow-ups:
  - Both new modules are in the extracted PR-wrapper inventory (ClawSweeper P1); wrapper closure and provisioning tests pass.
  - The budget singleton is typed instead of asserted.
  - Lifecycle reset no longer touches worker environment data unless lean published it. That fixes a test teardown that mocks `node:worker_threads`.
- Test-lines allocation of 85 lines (`config/test-lines-allocations/202507-lean-worker-memory-budget.txt`). This is new scheduling policy, and its regression tests cover queueing without drops, the point-read lane, restart rebinding, floor warnings, hosted-slot claims and each budget basis. Several of those came from verified review findings.
- Independent review: 4 verified findings, all fixed with regression tests (rebind after restart, flag reset on standard, refuse growth while floors exceed the budget, no double release after a failed close).

<details>
<summary>Proof identity</summary>

Build `75e5303b5e02f3a9def163044b57e37862bb724d` → image `sha256:34a664c2759358ee69b816235655b5ef5ed045bce02b97f88baee55fcfa42efc` (base `node:26.12.1-trixie`).

| Case | Lease | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lean r1 | `cbx_d6ed442aad8f` | `run_05e039570e43d6ba95734a2872f284db` |
| lean r2 | `cbx_cee412424a66` | `run_1806267e46381f1fcc287f06be87ffa7` |
| lean r3 | `cbx_5732bb293fb0` | `run_540d5afffae8fdee1ae939ff171d924a` |
| standard | `cbx_45a75e0af362` | `run_b8550bc32ab07fd1f7359e52c0af456d` |
| standard, 3 GiB | `cbx_7ccc56124678` | `run_9a8b524f80504978ca1d9e8d7b91e972` |

All released. Kernel `memory.peak` includes lease preparation; sampled `memory.current` and `anon` are taken every 2 s. Usage is the cgroup working set; `memory.current` includes page cache, so reaching the limit is not by itself an OOM.

</details>






### Main retarget and proof status

Rebased only this PR’s nine commits from `9d7f71d104cc` onto main `2d13f968e794`, after foundation #202422 was squash-merged. `git range-diff` against prior head `ffd3fa8939ca` shows eight identical patches and only regenerated config-baseline hashes in the ninth; feature production code is unchanged. Existing and pending prior-head proofs retain their original tested SHA, not the rebased SHA.

Diagnostics `usageBytes` is the last growth-admission sample and remains `null` until the first growth admission attempt; an idle null is not a failed RSS read. No-cgroup proof setup on `ffd3fa8939ca` observed `memory.max=max`, host RAM 134,884,679,680 bytes, basis `host-40`, and budget 53,953,871,872 bytes (exactly 40%). The host admission/override and stable-upgrade proofs below now pass. Earlier harness failures: v2 used an invalid fresh-RSS comparison against an unsampled null; v3 stopped on concurrent session creation (`AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError`) before admission assertions. Both leases were deleted. The corrected isolated harness creates fixture sessions serially before concurrent turns; no product changes were made for these harness/setup failures.



### Host, override and upgrade proof — complete

Studio Crabbox `local-container`, Node 26.12.1, candidate package SHA-256 `d6b4993fda3fbc34810d768c7aae8a9fba2c520001863567c7e9af47493c50b4`, built from `ffd3fa8939ca`; production patches are equivalent to rebased head `059bab5adb9a` as described above. All cases serialized under the shared measurement lock; every lease deletion was confirmed.

- **Host basis PASS** (`cbx_4cfb988ede83`, followup-v4): `memory.max=max`, observed host RAM 134,884,679,680 bytes, `limitSource=host`, `basis=host-40`, budget 53,953,871,872 bytes, exactly 40%. Five real admission-event observations verified the Gateway PID and its process RSS (including worker threads, excluding child processes). A 512 MiB override reported `basis=configured`, budget 536,870,912 bytes.
- **Cgroup basis PASS** (`cbx_b03d26a12ef5`, followup-v4): 6 GiB limit, `basis=cgroup-85`, budget 5,476,083,302 bytes; the same 512 MiB override reported `basis=configured`, budget 536,870,912 bytes. Both basis cases rejected zero, negative, fractional and string values through `config validate` (exit 1), without accepting an invalid override.
- **Latest-stable upgrade PASS** (followup-v5): resolved npm latest stable `2026.11.6`, installed stable, created three synthetic Knowledge records and session state, then installed the candidate in the same prefix/state. Added the new resource settings once (stable predates them), selected `auto` under 6 GiB, observed lean and configured 2048 MiB, and verified all semantic user settings including resources, saved page bytes, record bodies/revisions and session messages. Package installation itself preserved the config bytes. Candidate startup adds doctor migration metadata, a wizard receipt and `plugins.entries.openai.enabled=true` through existing provider auto-enable normalization (not this PR’s behavior; a separate plain-main upgrade comparison was not run); the semantic comparison explicitly permits only these additions. v4's whole-file byte comparison was a harness error, not settings loss.

Artifacts: `studio-crabbox:~/crabbox-proof/lean-budget-202376-followup-v4/` (host/cgroup results and receipts), `...-followup-v5/` (upgrade result and receipt), including each `summary.json`, `out-*/upgrade-proof.json`, and `*-stop.log`. Earlier failed attempts are retained as history. v3 encountered a concurrent-first-session setup discovery error in the family tracked by #158379, before admission proof; serial fixture creation avoids it without changing product code.

### Current CI attribution

`checks-ui-e2e (2/4)` failed only `ui/src/e2e/route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts:120`, “bounds plugins ready-window asset requests at 100 ms from a settled New Session,” at the line-145 asset-count limit (92 tests passed). [Job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44836195528/job/136633900074). UI code is untouched. The failure is exactly **57 assets > 56**, matching the same assertion on main `2d13f968e794` in #202478’s paired fresh-production-build reproduction: Studio Crabbox run `run_7875f8579b36dd07c7fa99b0289ab3c7`, lease `6c28ab65a1e6` (released). The count is not higher on this PR. This is the prior-head CI result, not a hosted main CI run; the fresh rebased-head checks are recorded separately below. The CI gate failure follows this shard failure.





### Conflict-only rebase after review

After ClawSweeper’s 01:15:55Z verdict on `059bab5adb9a` (“no definite introduced defect”, 4/6), rebased once onto main `684018d110ef`, producing `483d2239059a`. Range-diff: eight identical feature patches; the override patch differs only in regenerated config baseline counts/hashes. No feature production or test patch changed, so that verdict and the documented prior-head behavioral proofs carry over; no new re-review was requested. prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when the complete workflow, dependency and policy inputs remain equivalent. This change admits that case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse an equivalent reviewed workflow for initial baseline proof while preserving authenticated ancestry, source identity, signed evidence and custody. This is maintainer tooling; it does not change the runtime product. No measured speedup or resolution of the macOS test deadlines is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Authenticate current main and compare complete workflow inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy. Carry provenance through native context and signed baseline bindings. Reuse same-commit facts only within each check; preserve fresh admission boundaries.
- Validate custody and preparation inputs before retiring active evidence. Preserve pending-proof acceptance retirement and qualified-baseline rejection. Keep the selected workflow's dependency revision independent of bootstrap, including creator reentry and unbound commands.
- Integrate frozen main `181656c5749804e8584af726d67eebdecaf017a7`, preserving verified-bootstrap completion and expansion order alongside workflow proof verification. prs.title: feat(voice-call): elevate one realtime call's consult tools with a keypad PIN
prs.body:
Related: #193571

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls run every consult at one fixed `realtime.toolPolicy`. Operators who keep it at `safe-read-only` (the safe default) cannot do owner-level work from a phone call, and raising the policy globally gives every admitted caller owner tools on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can turn on `realtime.elevation`, and on a call with a trusted number (an inbound caller, or the callee of an outbound call, in `allowFrom`), the person on the line can press `*`, a PIN, and `#` to give that one call the elevated consult policy (default `owner`) until hangup. Everything else keeps the configured `toolPolicy`. Elevation is off by default, so nothing changes for existing configs.

Risks and limits, kept visible:

- Twilio only. Digits come from Twilio Media Streams `dtmf` messages. Config validation rejects other providers while elevation is on.
- Only calls whose other party is in `allowFrom` can elevate: the caller of an inbound call, or the callee of an outbound call. Whoever answers an outbound call still has to enter the PIN; elevation is never automatic. Elevation requires `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"` or `"pairing"`. Caller ID can be spoofed (see #193571 for STIR/SHAKEN attestation), so the PIN is the credential; the allowlist only narrows who may try.
- Wrong PINs count per hashed number across calls (inbound and outbound share one budget) within `lockoutMs`, so hanging up and redialing does not reset the budget. After `maxAttempts` the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. Failure counts and lockouts are in memory; a Gateway restart clears them.
- Elevation ends when the call's media stream ends. A stream reconnect within the same call drops the tool policy back to `toolPolicy` (the caller re-enters the PIN), but the call's later consults stay in its isolated elevated session, because the call's transcript still carries answers from owner tools.
- A consult that is already running keeps the policy it started with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realtime handler already owns each call's telephony binding, so it now also owns that call's keypad state and passes the call's current consult policy to the consult tool handler, which uses it for `toolsAllow`. A new `DtmfElevationGate` collects digits after the prefix, submits on `#`, after 3 seconds without a key, or at 12 digits (not at the configured PIN length, so the length stays private), and compares with `safeEqualSecret`. On success the realtime model gets a short notice so it can tell the caller; on a wrong PIN it gets a "not accepted" notice; failures are counted per hashed caller number across calls (a window of `lockoutMs`), so redialing cannot reset the attempt budget. After `maxAttempts` the call is hung up and the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. During a lockout any entry hangs up the call without checking the PIN, so retries reveal nothing. A correct PIN clears that caller's failure count.

Digits never reach the realtime model, the transcript, or logs. Logs record only the outcome, attempt count, and the hashed caller number on lockout. Caller audio is withheld from the model between the prefix key and submission, in case the carrier leaves tones in the media.

The PIN is a secret input (`realtime.elevation.pin`, registered in `configContracts.secretInputs` and marked sensitive), resolved the same way as `twilio.authToken`. It must resolve to 4 to 12 digits; the startup error never echoes the value.

Config surface: this raises the plugin config budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 5080 to 5087 (the `realtime.elevation` object and its six fields). The feature is opt-in and needs an operator-set PIN, so it cannot ride on an existing field.

To stay within the line-cap ratchet for `realtime-handler.ts`, the existing caller-transcript buffer helpers and `withFallbackConsultQuestion` moved unchanged into `realtime-transcript-text.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

```json5
realtime: {
  enabled: true,
  toolPolicy: "safe-read-only",
  elevation: {
    enabled: true,
    pin: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "VOICE_CALL_ELEVATION_PIN" },
    prefix: "*",               // one key: 0-9 or *
    elevatedToolPolicy: "owner", // or "safe-read-only"
    maxAttempts: 3,              // 1-10
    lockoutMs: 3600000,
  },
}
```

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests, all passing locally:

- `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: eligibility (inbound + allowlisted only), prefix gating, `#` submit, `*` restart, inter-digit timeout, 12-digit submit, wrong PIN, failures counted across calls (redial does not reset), failure window expiry, success clears failures, lockout across calls and expiry, close drops pending entry.
- `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): consult before the PIN gets `safe-read-only`, after the PIN gets `owner`; caller audio is withheld while entering the PIN; the PIN never appears in manager events, model notices, or console output; a stream close drops elevation; `maxAttempts` wrong PINs hang up the call, and during the lockout the correct PIN on the next call hangs up without a notice.
- `runtime.test.ts`: a consult with call policy `safe-read-only` runs with the read-only `toolsAllow` list, and with `owner` runs with `toolsAllow` undefined (normal agent tool policy).
- `config.test.ts`: defaults, runtime and manifest schema agreement, validation errors, PIN resolution.
- `stream-frame-adapter.test.ts`: Twilio `dtmf` frame parsing; Telnyx frames stay ignored.

Also updated: two `realtime-handler.test.ts` assertions now expect the consult context to carry `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`.

Results:

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 52 files, 633 tests passed; database-workers lane 15 files, 182 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm lint:extensions`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane green except the dead-export scan, which reports only pre-existing entries outside this change (for example `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`).
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `runtime.test.ts` (added in 6f93e38): an elevated consult runs in the session `<caller session key>:elevated:<callId>`; consults before the PIN and on later calls keep the caller's normal session.
- **Reconnect isolation (8a6d57d, the P1 from the last review).** The gate remembers which call ids were elevated (pruned after a day), so `wasElevated` survives a new binding for the same call. `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "keeps a call marked elevated across rebinding while its tool policy resets". `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): elevate, end the stream, reconnect the same call; the next consult gets `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"` **and** `elevated: true`. Together with the `runtime.test.ts` case above, the reconnected call's consults run in `…:elevated:<callId>`, so its retained transcript never enters the shared per-phone session, and a later call without the PIN can't read it.
- **Outbound (4277a5a).** `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "opens only when the other party is allowlisted, in either direction", and "shares failures and lockout between inbound and outbound calls with one number".

Rebased onto `main` at ae0d37b3c4 (2026-11-17). The only conflict was the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (`config:docs:check` OK). On the rebased head:

- The PR's test files (`config`, `runtime`, `realtime-dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler`, `stream-frame-adapter`): 6/6 files pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: the only errors are `max-lines` in `extensions/crabbox/…/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` and `extensions/tlon/…/monitor/index.test.ts`, both on `main` and outside this change.
- Full `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: failures only in `index.call-scope.test.ts` and `src/manager.async-store.test.ts` (steering/end_call admission). Neither file is touched here, and the same tests fail or hang on unmodified `main` at ae0d37b3c4 on this host.

The feature code is the same as this branch; only the base differs. [voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=4fd2dbc6-8a0f-42a3-8fe3-adf072776006 tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=10084

```text
[voice-call] Realtime keypad elevation rejected callId=f10831ae-5c3a-477b-a906-6acf51b693bc attempt=1/3
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=f10831ae-5c3a-477b-a906-6acf51b693bc providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
```

What the calls show:

- **Read-only before the PIN.** `bf202c8f` and `7992d6c1`: the first consult asked for current alerts; the agent had only the read-only tool list, couldn't reach Grafana, and said so.
- **Elevation.** After `*<PIN>#`: `Realtime keypad elevation granted … toolPolicy=owner`. The next consult in each call used Grafana MCP tools and reported the firing alerts.
- **Reset on hangup.** `52e9a519` (call-back after `bf202c8f`): the consult ran with the read-only tool list again, and the owner tools (Grafana MCP) were not in its catalog.
- **Wrong PIN.** `f10831ae`: `Realtime keypad elevation rejected … attempt=1/3`, and the model received the "not accepted" notice. I stopped after one attempt to avoid locking out the test number; the 3-attempt hang-up and lockout are covered by `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts`.

**Found live and fixed in 6f93e38.** With the default `sessionScope: "per-phone"`, the call-back in `52e9a519` couldn't run owner tools, but its consult answered from results the elevated call had left in the caller's shared session. Elevated consults now run in a session scoped to the call (`…:elevated:<callId>`), so owner-tool results never land in the shared session. Re-checked live: `7992d6c1` elevated and fetched alerts into `…:elevated:7992d6c1…`; on the call-back `4fd2dbc6`, the agent had no record of them. The docs now cover this, plus `sessionScope: "per-call"` for no carry-over at all.

### Live outbound proof (2026-11-16, same host and build)

Outbound call to the allowlisted number (`mode=conversation`). The consult before the PIN had the read-only tool list (7 tools) and couldn't reach Grafana. After `*<PIN>#`, the consult ran in `agent:main:voice:call:49796487-…:elevated:49796487-…`, had the owner tool catalog (133 tools, including Grafana MCP), and reported the firing alerts. Those matched Prometheus `ALERTS` at the same moment.

```text
[voice-call] Outbound call initiated: callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a providerCallId=CA… mode=conversation preConnectDtmf=no initialMessage=yes
[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a (providerCallId=CA…, initialGreeting=queued)
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=9670
[voice-call] Realtime keypad elevation granted callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a toolPolicy=owner
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=17774
[voice-call] Call finalized callId=49796487-79b6-44d9-9429-b405a7e2d29a providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
```

### Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrading this host from 2026.10.7 to 2026.11.4 kept the existing voice-call config (Twilio store SecretRef auth token, realtime provider settings, allowlist, tool policy). `realtime.elevation` defaults to `enabled: false`, so existing configs load and behave as before.
- Operator note: when a newly installed plugin version adds a secret input path (here `realtime.elevation.pin`), the Gateway reads the secret-input registry only at startup. Until a Gateway restart, voice-call fails to start with `unresolved SecretRef`; `secrets reload` and a plugin reload are not enough. This is core behavior, not something this PR introduces.





### Live reconnect + callback proof, and upgrade from v2026.11.5 (2026-11-18)

Elevate → forced stream reconnect → consult → unauthenticated callback on a real Twilio call: after the reconnect the tool policy resets, but the call's consults stay in its isolated session, and the callback's shared session never sees the elevated answer. Also covers the upgrade and data-model proof from the current stable release (v2026.11.5) in a sandbox. Details and redacted logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200198#issuecomment-6979119355

prs.title: fix: unblock changed checks after channel module splits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After #203108 and #203084 moved Feishu and Microsoft Teams consumers into their owning modules, five stale exports caused the local dead-export gate in `pnpm check:changed` to fail for unrelated nearby changes.

## User Impact

Developers can run the local changed-file checks without these inherited export failures. There is no user-visible runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unused `FeishuBotAddedEvent` re-export from `bot.ts` while preserving its live `event-types.ts` export. Make the four locally consumed helpers private. Move the two test-only callers to existing attachment parsing entry points, retaining their mixed-case MIME and HTML fixtures. No other export, configuration, cache, or schema changes.

Production LOC is net −3 (+5/−8); test LOC is net +6. The simplification pass confirmed that all function bodies stay unchanged and only the obsolete module exposure disappears.

## Evidence

On exact base `1c86bd5173a36ff73718d0839cbd0edc7bc19dac`, the existing dead-export gate reproduced five production findings and three full-tree findings. This existing gate is the regression proof; no duplicate source-grep test is introduced.

All 100 focused tests passed across Feishu bot parsing/dispatch and Teams attachment suites. The changed Teams test file and its HTML sibling took 2.48 seconds together, with 24 tests passing. Feishu parser and dispatch configurations took 39.04 and 53.83 seconds including compiler setup. CI timing will be recorded after the exact-head run.

Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against that base was scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Repository-wide references and plugin barrels were checked; no Control UI importer uses these owners. The production function bodies are unchanged apart from export removal and signature formatting.

A bounded synthetic comparison of the actual Teams HTML summary and advertised-media owners used 5,000 distinct attachment inputs, five fresh-process A1/A2/B rounds, 20k warmup pairs, 50k timed pairs, and separate sampled-allocation runs. A1/A2/B median wall times were 8.798/8.903/8.782 µs per pair; CPU 9.457/9.597/9.477 µs; sampled heap 14,671/14,859/14,705 bytes. Results remain within A/A variation; no runtime performance improvement is claimed. These owners do no database or workspace I/O.

Final `pnpm deadcode:exports` passes all three scans with zero findings. `pnpm check:changed` passed completely in 639.44 seconds, including both extension typechecks, lint, formatting, structural guards, and all three dead-export scans.

prs.title: fix(ci): wait for cron recovery within the test deadline
prs.body:
## Superseded

Closed in favor of [#203169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203169), merged as [9264bd4c37ce](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9264bd4c37cea7a42a41dc3bea03b3ef1c297184) while this PR was being prepared. The landed change removes the same three-second polling deadline, waits for the required scheduler starts under the existing test deadline, and retains callback delivery and exactly-once assertions. No further change from this PR is needed.

## What Problem This Solves

The native cron recovery check can fail after three seconds while a replacement worker is still starting. [Main CI recorded this failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381): the third worker had opened, but had not received its scheduler-start command before the separate polling deadline expired.

## User Impact

This changes test synchronization only. Cron runtime behavior is unchanged; missing recovery or delivery still fails within the existing ten-second test deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait for both the expected replacement scheduler-start command and callback delivery using the existing abort-aware test helper. Preserve the exact worker count, exactly-once callback, persisted job-removal assertion, failure trace, and cleanup.

This is a maintainer main-CI repair. GitHub rejected direct landing because main requires a pull request.

## Evidence

- Both native-loss cases passed on the baseline and candidate in the same isolated Linux runner (Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs, 16 GB RAM). The baseline did not reproduce the CI failure, so this is not claimed as a local red/green reproduction or proof that all CI flakes are eliminated.
- Targeted format, lint, and cron test typecheck passed. The candidate file was verified before and after execution.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper found no actionable correctness or security findings. ClawSweeper reviewed `1c86bd5173a3..50805157cd91`; the final signed commit `4d30c5fc5a48` has an identical patch after integration onto `a4f721c182cd`. The intervening main changes do not alter cron, its test helpers, dependency inputs, or these validation commands.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/cron/service/scheduler-native-loss.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/cron/service/scheduler-native-loss.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json src/cron/service/scheduler-native-loss.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental
```

</details>

Updates `actions/setup-java` from 6.1.0 to 6.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

prs.title: fix(windows): report a Startup-folder login item as itself in gateway status
prs.body:
Closes #202094

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, a non-elevated `openclaw gateway install` cannot register the S4U Scheduled Task, so it falls back to a Startup-folder login item. On such a host:

- `gateway status` labels the service `Scheduled Task (registered)`.
- `gateway status` and `doctor` report `Service definition inspection could not be completed.` on every run. The service audit asks Task Scheduler for a task definition that does not exist.

## User Impact

User impact: on a login-item install, `gateway status` shows `Service: Startup-folder login item (registered)`, and neither command reports the false inspection failure. Real inspection failures are still reported, such as an unreadable Task Scheduler with no login item installed. Scheduled Task installs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New read-only predicate.** `isConfirmedStartupEntryOnly` (`schtasks-runtime.ts`) uses the typed `probeScheduledTaskState`. It is true only when the probe returns `missing` and a Startup entry is installed. Denied, timed-out or invalid probes return false. Lifecycle control (`shouldControlStartupEntry`) is unchanged and keeps its best-effort `isRegisteredScheduledTask` check.
- **Audit.** `auditGatewayServiceConfig` still audits the Scheduled Task definition first. Only if that read fails does it run the predicate, and it treats "no definition" as correct only on a confirmed login-item install. So Scheduled Task installs spawn nothing extra, and a failed Task Scheduler query is still reported when a Startup file exists.
- **Label.**
  - `readScheduledTaskRuntime` already routes a missing task with a Startup entry to `resolveFallbackRuntime`. It now records that as `windowsStartupEntry: true`.
  - `formatServiceLabel`, the label owner for both status paths, renders that fact as `Startup-folder login item`.
  - The new field also appears in `gateway status --json` under `service.runtime`, as an additive field.

Not changed:

- Update-owned service refresh still rejects the Startup fallback by design (`UPDATE_NATIVE_AUTHORITY`).
- In the live run below, both unfixed main and this branch printed `Gateway service definition changed during Doctor` when the CLI and the service came from different installs. That is a separate case, and this change neither causes nor fixes it.

## Evidence

**Regression tests.** I checked both against main by restoring the five source files from `upstream/main` with the new tests in place:

- `schtasks-runtime.test.ts`: a missing task plus a Startup entry yields `windowsStartupEntry: true` and the label `Startup-folder login item`. On main it fails: `expected { status: 'unknown', …(1) } to match object { windowsStartupEntry: true }`.
- `service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts`: a login item with no task produces no `definitionDriftError`. On main it fails: `expected 'Service definition inspection could n…' to be undefined`.
- `service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts`: when the probe returns `unknown` (access denied, HRESULT `-2147024891`) and a Startup file exists, `definitionDriftError` is still reported. With the first revision's best-effort check it fails.
- Control: the existing `reports failed native task inspection independently from legacy issues` test still passes. It covers a failed read with no login item.

**Affected suites.** I ran the daemon lane on Windows over `schtasks-runtime`, `schtasks-runtime.deadline`, `schtasks`, `schtasks-runtime-probe.windows`, `service-audit-schtasks.windows`, `service-audit` and `service-audit.definition-facts`.

- 204 tests passed.
- The 10 failures are systemd cases (KillMode, Delegate, base-unit directives, backup modes) that fail identically on unchanged `upstream/main` on this Windows host.

**Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are all clean.

**Live run.**

- Setup: Windows 11 26200, non-elevated. The login item was installed by `openclaw@2026.11.5` for a throwaway profile and removed afterwards.
- Before, with 2026.11.5:

```text
Service: Scheduled Task (registered)
Service definition inspection incomplete: Service definition inspection could not be completed.
Runtime: running (pid <pid>, Startup-folder login item installed; matching gateway process detected for port <port>.)
```

- After, with this branch built and run against the same install:

```text
Service: Startup-folder login item (registered)
Runtime: running (pid <pid>, Startup-folder login item installed; matching gateway process detected for port <port>.)
```

- `gateway status --json` (after): `"label": "Startup-folder login item"`, `"windowsStartupEntry": true`.
- `doctor --non-interactive`, run against the same stopped login item: an unfixed main build (7f059c01cd03; the touched files are unchanged up to this branch's base) prints the `Gateway service definition` box with `Service definition inspection could not be completed.`. This branch does not.

prs.title: fix(update): keep settled warnings out of failure reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An update failure report can keep showing an old step warning after the final update result explicitly clears or replaces it. The report concatenated recorded and current warnings, so settled diagnostics resurfaced in support reports.

## User Impact

Failure reports show the current warnings for each update step. An omitted warning list still preserves recorded diagnostics, and warnings from other steps remain visible. No configuration change or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the update ledger's existing warning projection before formatting the report, instead of maintaining a second merge rule. Failure selection, public diagnostic redaction, and the warning limit stay unchanged. Production code grows by three lines to reuse the canonical typed helper; regression coverage adds 31 lines.

## Evidence

The new regression distinguishes omitted, cleared, and replaced warning lists while checking unrelated warnings, the failed phase, and input immutability. Against the base implementation, clearing and replacement fail and omission passes.

All 148 focused tests passed across report preparation, ledger projection/compaction, and CLI progress. Targeted formatting and lint also passed on the existing [Testbox lease](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44923336371); the native wrapper settled with exit 0. Its external portal sync timed out after command success. Exact source commit: `4f55471a32fe47ada32083621555b1b2be974814`.

Local review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings; its supplied context omitted the projector implementation. A separate full-source review covered that implementation, the report preparer, tests, and CLI/Gateway callers and found no P1/P2 blockers. This is report-boundary regression proof, not a live package upgrade qualification.

Hosted ClawSweeper review did not run because its input scan refused material. Manual source inspection confirmed an existing synthetic credential-redaction fixture at `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.test.ts:203`, unchanged by this PR. An independent local TruffleHog 3.97.6 scan with network verification disabled found only that synthetic URI in each of the base and proposed test files; the hosted scanner is 3.99.4, so this does not claim a successful hosted scan or review. No scanner policy or hold was changed.

prs.title: fix(ci): wait for native cron recovery without a polling deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native cron recovery test can fail while a replacement worker is still opening normally. Main CI observed the third worker opening at 2,149 ms, then rejected recovery at 3,363 ms because the fixture imposed a separate three-second polling deadline.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. CI still verifies real native worker loss, replacement loss, exactly-once delivery, queue drainage, and removal of the completed job.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture waits for its existing real-transport observer to record the required scheduler starts, under the unchanged ten-second test deadline. It retains the exact worker count and all delivery and cleanup assertions. Production LOC: 0; test LOC: +9/-4.

## Evidence

- Both native-recovery cases passed at `61817eeb648dc93c00b8ca8b5c0af662bc99bf90`: 2.960s with one worker lost; 2.214s with the replacement also lost. The file completed in 16.04s; its wrapper in 16.94s. [Exact-head changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44924112612/job/136906757481) passed.
- Original failure: [main CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381/job/136875601520). Its trace shows the third worker opening, not a missing retry.
- Local autoreview (P0–P2) covered `5b12461c7b3265ef81a3ba0594041e2510e865ba..61817eeb648dc93c00b8ca8b5c0af662bc99bf90` with the complete test and scheduler/promise context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Independent read-only review also returned GO.
- Diff checks and commit-time formatting passed.
- The earlier manual workflow's dependency check reported five unused exports in Feishu/MSTeams, matching [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44919125909). Those source files, Knip runner/configuration, package manifest and lockfile are unchanged between the failed main revision and this PR. That manual-run failure matched baseline; the ordinary PR CI below is green.

prs.title: fix(plugins): match peer-link host roots by physical identity (#201589)
prs.body:
Closes #201589

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, installing OpenClaw into a mixed-case directory (e.g. `D:\Personal\OpenClaw`) left every peer-declaring plugin permanently blocked: the installer's junction stored a different casing of the same directory (`D:\Personal\openclaw`), and the host-root audit compared realpath results with `===`, so one directory under two spellings was rejected as `missing-openclaw-peer-link` and the channel never started.

- Solution: when the spellings differ, compare physical identity (dev/ino) through the existing `sameFsObject` owner before falling back to standalone-manifest identity.
- What changed: `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.ts` only; the shared matcher serves all three callers (peer-link audit, native namespace, native reference).
- What did NOT change: manifest-identity admission for relocated standalone copies, link repair/rebinding, rejection of genuinely distinct directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

Physical identity is the repo's established answer to Windows alias spellings: `src/plugins/path-safety.ts` already proves dev/ino identity for Windows physical aliases, and `sameFsObject` (`src/infra/path-case.ts`) is the canonical comparison owner (also used by `exec-safe-bin-trust.ts`).

- Alternative considered: case-folding gated by `isPathCaseInsensitive`. Rejected: it needs a filesystem probe per mismatch and only covers casing, while dev/ino covers any same-directory alias and never widens admission on case-sensitive filesystems.
- Stat failures fail closed inside the existing try/catch; no change to the standalone-manifest contract.

## User Impact

Windows installs whose directory casing differs from the plugin record keep their channels connected after plugin install/reinstall; `doctor` no longer reports a false peer-link mismatch for the same directory. No behavior change on case-sensitive filesystems.

## Evidence

Observed result — native Windows proof on a `windows-latest` runner (GitHub Actions, real NTFS): a fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.5` (latest stable, the reporter's version) into mixed-case `C:\proof\OpenClaw`, then `plugins install npm:@openclaw/feishu@2026.11.5` invoked through the lowercase spelling of the same install. The junction naturally stored the lowercase target — no manual fixture needed. BASE arm = pristine published package; HEAD arm = the same install with this PR's 5-line production diff mirrored into the published dist chunk (dist inventory entry recomputed); both arms share one state dir, so BASE→HEAD is also an in-place upgrade with existing settings.

```text
BASE (pristine 2026.11.5), openclaw channels status:
- Feishu default: enabled, configured, reason:Plugin feishu failed: configured plugin
  payload verification failed (missing-openclaw-peer-link) ... stopped, health:blocked
BASE gateway log:
- Plugin "feishu": ... peer link audit failed: ...\node_modules\openclaw
  points to c:\proof\openclaw\node_modules\openclaw instead of C:\proof\OpenClaw\node_modules\openclaw

HEAD (same install + mirrored diff), gateway log:
[gateway] startup trace: plugins.gateway-load.plugin.feishu ... loadFailedCount=0.0 ... registerFailedCount=0.0
[gateway] http server listening (15 plugins: anthropic, browser, canvas, cua-computer, device-pair, feishu, ...)
[feishu] starting feishu[default] (mode: websocket)
[feishu] feishu[default]: WebSocket client started
[info]: [ '[ws]', 'ws client ready' ]
HEAD openclaw channels status: - Feishu default: enabled, configured, running
HEAD openclaw channels status --probe: - Feishu default: ... running, connected
```

The channel connected to Feishu over a real websocket with real app credentials. The bot-identity health probe separately returned Feishu API error 21001 (platform permission policy on the test app, `bot open_id resolved: unknown`) — orthogonal to peer-link admission; the channel stayed `running, connected`.

Path identity captured on the runner (same object, two spellings):

```json
{"linkRealpath":"c:\\proof\\openclaw\\node_modules\\openclaw",
 "hostRealpath":"C:\\proof\\OpenClaw\\node_modules\\openclaw",
 "linkDevIno":[1422631540,1125899907154117],"hostDevIno":[1422631540,1125899907154117],
 "sameObject":true,"spellingsEqual":false}
```

| Cell (shipped CLI + Gateway, real NTFS) | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh mixed-case install + feishu plugin install | blocked: `missing-openclaw-peer-link`, `health:blocked` | admitted, feishu registered |
| `plugins install --force` reinstall (lowercase junction) | re-blocked (reporter symptom) | still admitted |
| Upgrade in place, existing state | — | gateway + channels config unchanged |
| Real Feishu channel connect (websocket, real credentials) | never starts (`health:blocked`) | `running, connected` |

Regression tests fold into `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.test.ts` (`openClawHostRootsMatch physical identity`, `it.each`): same dev/ino under two spellings → `true` (red on base, green with the fix); distinct inode / distinct device → `false` on both arms. Full file: `48 passed` on the plugins shard config.

Checks: `oxfmt --check` clean; `oxlint` 259 rules, 0 findings; targeted `tsc` program over the two touched files: 0 errors in them (648 residual errors in unrelated files from the limited program).

What was not tested: end-to-end message send/receive (the proof asserts admission and websocket connection, not conversation). The HEAD arm is the published stable with only this PR's production diff mirrored into dist (disclosed above), not a full source build.

prs.title: fix: let GPT-6 Luna chat again on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription route
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/model-catalog-metadata.ts:127 (and :57 in `clearRouteBoundCatalogMetadata`) on main fd4807ae11 turned any declared `inference` into `{ chat: false }` when the configured route differs from the catalog route, so GPT-6 Luna's `{ chat: true, decision }` catalog row became a chat veto on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription route.

Fixes #201513

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.11.5, people who use GPT-6 Luna through a ChatGPT/Codex subscription get "does not support chat" on every turn, from `openclaw infer model run --local` and from the Gateway, before any request is sent. Other OpenAI models on the same route still work.

## User Impact

User impact: `openai/gpt-6-luna` runs again on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription route, as it did on 2026.11.3. Models whose catalog says they cannot chat stay refused with the same message, and Luna's Decision settings stay tied to the OpenAI Platform route.

## Why This Change Was Made

2026.11.5 gave the bundled Luna row both chat and Decision capability (#176133). When the configured route differs from the catalog route, the catalog overlay drops route-bound facts, but it also replaced Luna's `chat: true` with `chat: false`. The overlay now decides inference once: on a changed route it keeps a veto only when the catalog row says `chat: false`, and otherwise drops the whole route-bound declaration, Decision facts included, so the model is treated as chat like the other OpenAI rows on that route.

Two changes on top of @MertBasar0's commit:
- The provider-config merge (`mergeProviderModels`) is left as on main. There a decision-bearing row is a discovered per-route grant, such as ClawRouter's granted Luna, and #186596 deliberately keeps vetoing it on another route because ClawRouter's catalog declares Luna typed-only (docs/providers/clawrouter.md). With the merge change, `utility-completion.clawrouter.test.ts` fails: the refreshed catalog lets typed-only ClawRouter Luna chat on a changed configured route.
- With only the veto dropped, an API-only route change (which skips `clearRouteBoundCatalogMetadata`) let Luna's Decision facts ride along to the new route. The overlay now strips base inference and sets it once.

Codex agrees on the subscription route: its backend `/models` metadata (`codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs:419-421`, `ModelInfo`) and `model/list` (`codex-rs/app-server/src/models.rs:16`, `model_from_preset`) carry no chat-or-Decision capability split, and `gpt-6-luna` is listed like any other agent model (`codex-rs/models-manager/models.json:1045`, `visibility: "list"`, `shell_type: "shell_command"`).

Thanks @Caitoz for the report and the precise analysis, and @MertBasar0 for the fix this builds on.

## Evidence

Real built CLI and Gateway with the issue's config verbatim (`openai-chatgpt-responses`, `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`, `auth: oauth`, `agentRuntime: openclaw`), a fixture ChatGPT OAuth profile and a local ChatGPT-backend fixture; the real bundled Codex app-server uses the same fixture. No real account.

- Before (main fd4807ae11; also v2026.11.5): `infer model run --local` fails with "This model doesn't support chat; pick another model." (2026.11.5: "Model openai/gpt-6-luna does not support chat inference"); Gateway `models.list` hides Luna and `chat.send` gets the same refusal. The fixture receives no model request.
- After (this PR): `infer model run --local` returns `FIXTURE-ACK`; Gateway lists Luna and `chat.send` answers `FIXTURE-ACK`; the fixture logs `POST /backend-api/codex/responses model gpt-6-luna`.
- Controls, same before and after: typed-only `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna` granted chat on ClawRouter's endpoint but configured on another route is still refused with the existing message and sends nothing; Luna on its own Platform catalog route reaches the provider; Luna on the native Codex runtime answers through Codex.
- Regression: one case in `model-catalog-inference.test.ts` (a `chat: true` + Decision row on a new endpoint or API keeps no inference). On main both routes fail with `expected { chat: false } to be undefined`; on the contributor commit alone the API route fails with `expected { chat: true, decision: … } to be undefined`.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201746#issuecomment-7059365788

Merge danger: two-way door. Only in-memory catalog metadata changes; nothing is written or migrated, and a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: models whose bundled catalog row declares `chat: true` together with Decision facts, used on a non-catalog route; today that is only `openai/gpt-6-luna`.

prs.title: fix: keep Windows plugins loading when the OpenClaw folder is spelled with different letter case
prs.body:
Closes #201589
Supersedes #201707 and #201754 (same production approach; this version keeps both authors as co-authors).

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, a plugin that declares `openclaw` as a peer dependency (Feishu, for example) stays blocked with `missing-openclaw-peer-link` when the OpenClaw install folder is spelled with different letter case in different places. One example is an install at `D:\Personal\OpenClaw` where the plugin's link was recorded as `D:\Personal\openclaw`. Both spellings name the same folder, but OpenClaw compared them as text. Reinstalling the plugin or running `doctor --fix` did not help, because the next launch from the other spelling rejected the link again.

## User Impact

Windows plugins that depend on OpenClaw now load whenever their host link points at the running OpenClaw folder, whatever letter case the link recorded. A link to a genuinely different folder is still rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

On Windows, OpenClaw's realpath helper keeps the spelling that a junction stored; it uses the on-disk spelling only on POSIX. The host-root check now treats two spellings as the same host when the filesystem reports the same device and file ID for both.

The check uses bigint `stat` results, because number inodes can round on Windows. It also never admits a zero file ID: that is what libuv reports when it cannot open a path, so two unreadable folders would otherwise match each other. Peer-link audit, native namespace admission and native reference admission all share this one check.

Both contributor PRs found the same identity approach. This PR keeps it, adds the bigint and zero-ID guards, and replaces the statSync mocks with a real symlinked host fixture.

## Evidence

Native Windows proof (Windows Server 2025 on Crabbox AWS, Node 24.22.1). Each lane installed OpenClaw under `C:\Personal\OpenClaw` and Feishu (`npm:@openclaw/feishu@2026.11.6`) through one launcher spelling, then ran `openclaw doctor` through the canonical spelling:

| Build | Feishu installed through | Junction target recorded | `doctor` peer-link findings |
|---|---|---|---|
| published 2026.11.6 | `c:\personal\openclaw\...` | `c:\personal\openclaw\node_modules\openclaw` | 6 lines (`missing-openclaw-peer-link`, "points to c:\personal\openclaw\node_modules\openclaw instead of ...") (reproduced) |
| published 2026.11.6 (control) | `C:\Personal\OpenClaw\...` | `C:\Personal\OpenClaw\node_modules\openclaw` | 0 |
| this PR, packaged at `36aa2cc8707` | `c:\personal\openclaw\...` | `c:\personal\openclaw\node_modules\openclaw` | 0 (fixed) |

The control lane shows that letter case alone triggers the failure. The fixed build keeps the same lowercase junction and admits it.

- Regression test: `admits another spelling of the host directory but not a different directory` fails on the base production code (the audit returns an issue) and passes with the fix. The whole file passes, 46/46.
- Local checks: `pnpm check:changed` typecheck and lint pass. Its dead-export scan fails only on unrelated files already on main (feishu `bot.ts` and `message-content.ts`, msteams `attachments/html.ts`).
- Reviews: autoreview (Codex) came back scoped-clean, and an independent read-only Codex review found no P0–P2 issues.

<details><summary>Scope notes</summary>

Production change: `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.ts` (+10/−1) and `src/infra/path-case.ts`, where `sameFsObject` widens its type to accept bigint stats with no behavior change. Test: `src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.test.ts` (+21).

Rejected alternatives:
- Case-folding paths would treat genuinely distinct directories as one on case-sensitive Windows directories.
- `realpathSync.native` returns UNC or 8.3 forms for subst, mapped and short-name paths.

Sibling survey: `plugin-native-admission.ts` and `linkOpenClawPeerDependency` still compare spellings, but a mismatch there only rebinds the link to the current runtime's spelling. It does not block admission, so they are left as they are.
</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): web_fetch results are wrapped twice in Code Mode and Tool Search
prs.body:
Closes #198109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Code Mode cell or Tool Search `dispatch_action` returns `web_fetch` fields, the result wrap sanitizes the tool's own envelopes as if they were spoofed, so the model gets `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]` frames and a second warning sentence, and whole pages go over the 20,000-character result budget.

## User Impact

User impact: agents using Code Mode or Tool Search see fetched titles and text as content inside one untrusted-content envelope, and a `{ title, text }` page result comes back inline instead of as a saved-result reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

`web_fetch` and `web_search` wrap their own fields with `wrapExternalContent`, and Code Mode guests keep that wrapper as documented. `renderToolSearchControlText` then wraps the whole result again, and `replaceMarkers` cannot tell the tool's envelope from a spoofed one.

This PR folds only envelopes OpenClaw issued, never syntax alone:
- `wrapExternalContent` now remembers a SHA-256 digest (over UTF-16 code units) of each envelope it issues for the `web_fetch` and `web_search` sources, keyed by its random id (bounded to 4,096 entries per process).
- Before the outer wrap, `foldIssuedExternalContent` looks up each start marker's id, decodes the candidate (raw or JSON-encoded up to three levels), and folds it into its body only if the decoded envelope, start marker through end marker, matches the stored digest. The warning line that `wrapExternalContent` puts directly before an envelope is removed with it; it is fixed text and not part of the digest.
- Anything else stays for the outer wrap to sanitize as before: a well-formed envelope with an unknown id, an issued id with changed bytes, an envelope from another source, a clipped envelope, or one evicted or issued before a restart.
- The outer wrap and the 20,000-character model cap are unchanged. The fold reads only the first 200,000 characters of a result, which is a new bound; nothing past it folds. Guest values and tool `details` are untouched.

**Why this is not #78521.** #78521 skipped the outer wrap when tool output already contained marker strings, so attacker text with fake markers went out unwrapped. Here the outer wrap always applies, and a fold requires the exact bytes the runtime produced, including its random id and its already-sanitized body. The tests and the live run below check that a copy of a real envelope with a fabricated id stays `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]`.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- A cell that slices a wrapped string (`res.text.slice(0, 300)`) clips the envelope. A clipped envelope does not match its digest, so it is sanitized as today; the whole `title` field in the same cell folds.
- The Code Mode result fit measures through the same function, so results that the duplicate framing pushed over budget now come back inline. Results that still don't fit are saved with a preview, as before.
- `web_search` builds its fields with the same wrapper, so it gets the same fold. I tested `web_fetch` live, not `web_search`.
- #194934 (open) edits the same function for a configurable limit. The overlap is small; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

A scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint stands in for the model, so no vendor model is involved: it issues one tool call and records the tool result it receives. `main` is unmodified source at db4b2edd6d0; the PR column is this branch. ## What Problem This Solves

Installed terminal checks need to bind package metadata, module parsing and the emitted dependency closure to the reviewed reference.

## User Impact

This changes proof tooling and tests. Product runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collector now supplies verified package scopes to the existing import collector, so nested package metadata determines module interpretation. The regressions also exercise the current reference producer and independently pinned closure requirements.

This is the package-contract prerequisite for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192954. The original PR remains open; its historical results keep their original source attribution.

## Evidence

- Signed head `fb5de5b6e82ab84018652b0de57887f35c04a1fa`; review base `0f95ac716c215259f6f097babd68ee822f7493ed`. Normal commit hooks, formatting and whitespace checks passed; checkout clean.
