prs.title: fix(models): read the published owner inventory for picker menus after a config republish
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

After any runtime config change, the Telegram `/models` picker (and the Discord and Mattermost pickers built on the same data) could show only a provider's configured or manifest models instead of its discovered inventory. Live, a Gemini OAuth provider with 6 discovered models showed its 3 manifest models after a click, while `models.list` on the same Gateway kept returning 6. It stayed that way until a Gateway restart. Published-policy readers now look up the published owner the same way they select it, so they get its full inventory again.

### Root Cause

`withPreparedModelCatalogOwnerPolicy` (`src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.ts`) does two lookups:

1. `resolvePreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshotWithPolicy(request, configPolicy, ...)` selects the owner snapshot. With `configPolicy === "published"`, it accepts the published owner even when `request.config` no longer matches the owner's config (`policy === "published" || preparedModelRuntimeConfigsMatch(...)`).
2. `publishedReadOnlyOwner` decides whether a read-only request materializes that owner's full inventory (`materializeRequestedModelCatalog`) or returns the raw snapshot. This always used `getPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot`, an exact-config lookup.

When the caller's config is older than the published owner, lookup 1 returns the published owner and lookup 2 returns `undefined`. The `request.readOnly && !publishedReadOnlyOwner` branch then returns the raw snapshot. Its `modelCatalog` holds only configured or manifest rows, because a generation keeps discovered rows apart until a reader materializes them.

Which callers hit this depends on the config they pass:

- `loadModelsProviderData` (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models-catalog.ts`) passes the command's `cfg`, which was captured when the turn or command started. After a republish that config is stale, so the picker got configured rows only.
- `models.list` (`src/gateway/server-model-catalog.ts`) passes `getRuntimeConfig()`, the current config. The exact lookup matches, so it kept returning the full inventory. That is why the two disagreed on the same Gateway.

Observed before this change: the picker's provider button showed the discovered count, and the model list behind it showed the 3 manifest rows. A safe Gateway restart rebuilt the owner and fixed it until the next config write. The plugin logged no failed discovery refreshes, and `models.list` returned 6 rows on 12 consecutive polls.

## Exact change

- `prepared-model-catalog.ts`: for `configPolicy === "published"`, `publishedReadOnlyOwner` now uses `getPublishedPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot(request)`. Exact-policy readers keep `getPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot`. One ternary plus a comment.
- `prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`: a regression test that publishes an owner under a newer config, reads it through `loadPublishedPreparedModelCatalogOwnerSnapshot({ readOnly: true })` with an older config, and asserts the full discovered inventory comes back with no discovery call and no activation.

## Scope boundary

- No config, schema, storage, protocol or SDK change.
- Exact-policy readers, writable reads and `refreshFullCatalog` paths are unchanged.
- Materialization reads the owner's already-built inventory (`readFullModelCatalog`). It does not start discovery, and the test asserts `loadFullModelCatalog` is not called.
- Not addressed here: why the picker reader gets a config older than the published owner. Passing the current runtime config to every turn-path reader would be a broader change. This PR makes the published policy behave the same for stale and current configs.

## Real behavior proof

Regression test, run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:

```text
base (d874bf532f4)  reads the published full inventory for picker menus after a config republish  FAIL
                    - "id": "discovered"   + "id": "configured"
                    Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
this head           Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Related suites at this head, all passing: `prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`, `server-model-catalog.test.ts`, `commands-models.test.ts`, `commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts`, `directive-handling.model.test.ts`, `local-request-context.test.ts`, `sessions-mutations.catalog-queue.test.ts` (4 Vitest shards, 121 tests).

## What was not tested

- Not deployed to a live Gateway yet, so the picker has not been clicked after a config write on this head.
- No before/after benchmark. The change swaps one in-memory owner lookup for another and, for stale-config published reads, adds the same materialization fresh-config reads already did.
- A wider run over 68 catalog, picker and channel test files hit failures in `src/sessions/session-diff-revisions.test.ts` (6) and `src/agents/simple-completion-execution.test.ts` (13). Both fail the same way on the base commit with this change reverted, so they are unrelated. That run also stopped at its 40-minute local cap, so some shards never finished.

## Verification

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both touched files: clean.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`: exit 0.
- `$autoreview` (commit mode, P1 cap): no accepted findings, "patch is correct".

prs.title: fix(models): select a first model when a browser sign-in finds none
prs.body:
## Problem

On a fresh profile with no model chosen, signing in with OpenCode Go (Settings → Models → Add account → OpenCode Go → browser sign-in) ends on a dialog that says only "OpenCode Go (browser sign-in) is ready". It names no model and offers no "Start a new chat". The agent still has no primary model, so chat then shows "Set up a model".

Two causes:

1. **A credential-only sign-in never chooses a model.** Nearly every browser and device sign-in (OpenCode Go, OpenCode, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Copilot, MiniMax and others) is declared `credentialOnly: true`. `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-login.ts` sends these to the credential wizard, which only saves the account. The dialog could name a model only from a later catalog read that looked for a `recommended` row. That read finished 2–4 s after the dialog appeared: in the incident log the dialog was closed at about +1.9 s and the catalog replies arrived at +3.9 s and +5.8 s. Even when the starter did appear, it only pinned the model on the new session, so the agent primary stayed unset.
2. **"Is a model available?" stood in for "has this agent chosen a model?"** #172826 decided both the setup prompt and the sign-in mode from `configuredModels.some(available)` (`login-controller.ts` `connectProvider`, `view-status.tsx` `needsModelSetup`). Any available catalog entry fails that check, for example a running local llama.cpp model or an installed OpenCode CLI. "Set up a model" then disappears even though the Models page still shows "Model: Select a model". Every other "Add account" button always opened in access-only mode. The predicate shipped in v2026.11.6.

## Fix

- **Gateway (`models.authLogin`):** when a credential-only sign-in is started with the existing `selectModel: true` flag and the agent has no configured primary, it saves the credential as before, then:
  - reads the agent's catalog for that provider, refreshed so the new account's own models are listed;
  - picks the hosted catalog's recommended available model, else the account's first available model;
  - hands the saved profile to the existing saved-sign-in activation owner (`saved-auth:<profileId>`). That owner live-verifies the route, writes the primary and returns `modelActivation`.
  - The primary is read from config after sign-in (`resolveNativeModelPrimary`), so an operator's choice made before or during sign-in is never replaced.
  - If verification fails, the error says the sign-in was saved and names the next step.
  - If the account lists no available model, the result is the same as today, and the Gateway logs this non-outcome.
- **Activation wizard body:** extracted into `runSetupActivation` in `system-agent-setup-wizard.ts`, so setup and sign-in share one implementation instead of two copies.
- **Control UI:** one predicate everywhere, "this agent has a configured primary" (`resolveAgentModelPrimary`: the agent's model, else defaults; the same source as "Select a model").
  - The Models page shows "Set up a model" until the agent has a chosen model.
  - Every Models-page entry point sends `selectModel` only for an agent without one.
  - `connectProvider(models)` and `needsModelSetup` are deleted.
  - A pasted secret still only saves.
  - The "no usable models" wording appears only when that is true.

## Engineering decisions (consulted Fable 5.2)

- **Reused the saved-sign-in activation; did not reroute to the setup activation.** Sending credential-only choices into the setup activation would drop the secure browser callback. It would also run each provider's non-credential-only sign-in path, which may return no starter model, so a good sign-in would end in an error. That is a regression for OpenAI, Copilot, MiniMax and the rest.
- **When there is no recommendation, fall back to the first available model.** Without the hosted catalog nothing is marked recommended, and stopping there would strand a first-time user (UX rule: no stranded user). The provider's catalog order picks the model.
- **Primary write shape:** the activation owner pins the account (`provider/model@profile`) on the agent entry. It may also write the Gateway's current implicit route into `agents.defaults.model`, as it already does for setup. That implicit route goes away with the separate "no invented default model" change.

## Impact

- A first-time user who signs in with OpenCode Go sees "<model> is ready for your agent." and "Start a new chat with <model>" in the same render. The agent's primary is set, and the new chat answers.
- An agent that already has a primary keeps it: the sign-in only saves the account, as today.
- No protocol or schema change: `selectModel` already exists on `models.authLogin`.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway E2E, new `ui/src/e2e/provider-browser-login-first-model.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`.** Real HTTPS Gateway, real browser callback sign-in (fixture provider), fresh profile, plus an available local model like llama.cpp. The test checks:
- the local model is listed and available, yet "Set up a model" shows;
- browser sign-in completes, and the dialog names the model and offers the starter within 1 s of "ready";
- the agent primary is `browser-login-fixture/ready@browser-login-fixture:default`;
- Start a new chat, then send "Write a limerick about OpenClaw.", and the reply arrives;
- the page never shows "Set up a model" or "Couldn't load models from openai".

Results:
- head: passes;
- 346078f73f19 (the incident build): fails ("Set up a model" never appears);
- the existing `provider-browser-login.real-gateway` E2E passes on head. Its fixture now saves an OAuth account, like OpenCode Go's Console sign-in.

Before (346078f73f19), 6 s after "ready":
![before: ready dialog without a model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c4fffe3-3635-46d7-8033-955b80d7ad49)

After:
![after: ready dialog names the model and offers Start a new chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d96c838-244f-4e63-a2b2-e65e691f1d56)

Before and after, Models page with only a local model available:
![before: no Set up a model prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2062c664-8be6-4508-86f4-8e213c57033c)
![after: Set up a model prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f578fb82-c526-467b-a23d-3f82af616277)

**Regression tests (red on merge base `a48440bbdf3e`, green on head):**
- `models-auth-login.test.ts` "a credential-only sign-in selects the account's recommended model only without a primary": the no-primary case fails on base and the explicit-primary case passes on both.
- `model-providers-page.login-select-model.test.ts` "a browser sign-in selects the first model only for an agent without one": the no-primary case fails on base, and the explicit-primary case (no takeover) passes on both.

**Gates:** `ocx test` over `ui/src/pages/model-providers`, `ui/src/pages/model-setup`, `ui/src/lib/agents`, `models-auth-login.test.ts` and `test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxfmt and oxlint on changed files.

**Not covered here:** the real OpenCode Console approval needs a human; it is next, on a fresh profile.

## Merge danger

- **Two-way door.** A revert restores the old behavior. Primaries written by the new path are ordinary config that the user can change.
- **Blast radius:** first sign-ins through the Control UI for agents with no configured primary. Agents with a primary are unaffected.

prs.title: fix: stop clean updates warning about skipped agent database path repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every successful `openclaw update` ends with the warning "Skipped agent database path repair during update Doctor. Run openclaw doctor --fix to repair agent database paths.", on every platform, even when no agent database registration needs repair. The update result counts it as a warning that needs attention and sends the operator to a broad repair command that then does nothing. In [#161921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161921) a reporter read the same line as "the remaining step" of a recovery.

Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` run while an update is active has the same defect with its own message ("Skipped agent database path repair while update `<id>` is in progress").

## User Impact

User impact: an update whose agent database registry is clean no longer reports this warning. When a registration does need the repair, the warning still appears and now says how many registrations are affected:

`Skipped agent database path repair for 2 registration(s) during update Doctor. Run openclaw doctor --fix to repair agent database paths.`

Update behavior is otherwise unchanged. Update Doctor still defers the repair, so nothing in `agent_databases` or on disk is rewritten or removed while the updater holds its rollback inventory. Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` repairs exactly what it repaired before. The candidate must contain this change; the installed updater needs no schema, config or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warning was written for Windows only ([#147762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147762)) and returned as a constant before the registry was read. [#170043](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170043) extended the repair to the `(multiple)` session-store marker on every platform and removed the platform gate, so the constant started firing on every update everywhere.

The repair now reads the registrations and classifies them one time. That one result decides both whether anything is deferred and what the standalone repair writes, so there is no second copy of the marker or Windows alias rules and no second scanner (the concern [#173395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173395) raised when it reworded this warning). Update Doctor stops after the count. It also skips the shared-state maintenance assertion, which only guards the write and could otherwise turn an update pass into a refusal.

Production lines: +39/-39 (net 0). Tests: +44/-25. Docs: +11/-4.

## Evidence

Checked on Blacksmith Testboxes (Linux, Node 24), base `95e9afcf2926`.

**Through the built CLI** (`pnpm build`, then `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1 node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive` in an isolated state directory):

- Base build, clean registry: Doctor prints "Skipped agent database path repair during update Doctor. Run openclaw doctor --fix to repair agent database paths." under Doctor warnings.
- This branch, clean registry: Doctor completes with exit 0 and no agent database path warning.
- Upgrade from the latest stable: state and a config value were created with `openclaw@2026.11.6` from npm, then this branch's Doctor ran its update pass on that state. Exit 0, no agent database path warning, the config value was still there, no SQLite file went missing, and `agent_databases` was unchanged (it was empty in that state).

**Focused tests** (Doctor state-integrity contribution and a real SQLite state database):

- Red on the base: with the two production files restored to the base, 5 of 10 tests failed, including the clean-registry cases (`expected [ Array(1) ] to be undefined`).
- Green with the fix: 10 of 10, plus the 60 update report tests.
- Deferral intact: with a `(multiple)` registration and with a Windows extended-length alias, update Doctor and an active update run both warn with `for 1 registration(s)`, and the `agent_databases` rows and the file on disk are unchanged afterward.
- Standalone repair unchanged: the existing repair tests pass without edits.

**Static checks:** oxlint on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src` and `pnpm format:docs:check` passed on the Testbox. PR CI on head `f06ff2c3520` passed `check-lint`, `check-docs` and the test shards; the first head failed those two jobs on formatting of one test file, which the second commit fixes (whitespace and one trailing comma).

**Local review:** autoreview (Codex CLI, `gpt-6.1-sol`, one pass) on the working tree against base `95e9afcf2926` at priority P1 returned `scoped-clean` with no accepted findings. After that review a test title was renamed and the test file was reformatted; nothing else changed.

**ClawSweeper "before merge" item (data-model compatibility proof):** this change adds no schema, column, stored value or config. The update pass now runs the same `agent_databases` read the standalone repair already ran, and writes nothing. The upgrade-from-2026.11.6 run above is the proof I could produce for existing data.

Gaps:

- **Exact-head CI is red on one job this diff does not touch.** `PostgreSQL conformance (pg16-smoke)` failed in run 44892796106: `src/gateway/server-database-engine-cron.postgres.test.ts > drains accepted cron finalization before graceful stop and preserves it on restart` timed out at 90 s. The same job passed on the previous head (run 44890204390, 50 s for that test) with identical production code, and the other three tests in the file ran faster in the failing run than in the passing one, so the runner was not slow. The gate classes it "unknown" because `main` has no matching job. I have not rerun it. No open issue or PR covers this test file. It also failed once on #202654 (run 44831772604, a different test in the same file: `recovers completed and interrupted one-shots after their Gateway process is killed`, an assertion on the `cron.run` result) and passed on that PR's next head.
- **A repairable registration was not reached through the built CLI.** A seeded registration with no file was removed by another Doctor step before the path repair ran. A seeded 0-byte `(multiple).sqlite` made the `media-persistence` state migration refuse ("no schema ownership metadata") and Doctor stopped before later repairs, in update and standalone mode; I did not run that on the base. A fresh CLI state has no agent database to register under the marker name. The deferred warning and the repair are therefore proven at the Doctor contribution and real SQLite level only, and no full `openclaw update` run was made.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` is red on this branch for an export this change does not touch: `recordAllowlistMatchesUse` in `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts` and `src/infra/exec-approvals-authorization.ts`. It is the same on `main`, and #203022 is open for it.
- The native Windows suite (`src/state/openclaw-database-paths.windows.test.ts`) and the PostgreSQL state suite did not run on the Testbox. Their assertions on these messages are substring matches that the new text still satisfies.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
pnpm test src/flows/doctor-health-contribution-runners.state.paths.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db-path-repair.test.ts src/infra/update-run-report.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:test:src
pnpm deadcode:exports
pnpm format:docs:check
pnpm build
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1 node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
```

Testbox Actions runs: 44887258911 (tests and static checks), 44893095158 (built CLI and upgrade from stable), 44894002742 and 44894727460 (seeded registrations).

</details>

prs.title: fix(protocol): carry provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than the identifier budget
prs.body:
Fixes #203099

## What Problem This Solves

Worker inference stream frames and transcript commits rejected provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than 256 characters because those IDs inherited the internal worker identifier budget. Compatible providers emit opaque IDs that can exceed it — a GitHub Copilot diagnostic run produced a 458-character ID, the frame check returned null, and the run silently fell back to a different model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider-issued tool-call IDs are opaque upstream strings, unlike internal session/run/turn identifiers: `toolcall_start` stream-frame ids, transcript `toolCall` ids, and their matching `toolResult` references now travel with the payload budget (the same shape that long provider response IDs required in #170461), while internal identifiers and `toolName` keep the identifier budget. A provider ID larger than the frame payload budget is still rejected, and the generated protocol predicates were regenerated to match.

## User Impact

Worker-backed sessions keep tool calls from providers that mint long opaque tool-call IDs (GitHub Copilot observed at 458 characters) instead of dropping the call and falling back to another model. Existing short IDs remain valid; no wire-format or migration change is required.

## Evidence

Red/green at the shipped validation boundary, head `3107acfbd8` (Node 26.12.1, Linux). The reporter's own frame sequence, run through the real `validateWorkerInferenceEventFrame` validator:

| Phase | Build | 256-char id | 257-char id | 458-char id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED | upstream main (unpatched) | true | **false** | **false** |
| GREEN | this branch | true | true | true |

Unit regression (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts`, 21/21 pass at head `3107acfbd8`): "carries provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than the identifier budget" fails on the unpatched schemas (the 458-char stream frame, the transcript toolCall content part, and the matching toolResult reference are all rejected) and passes with the fix, including the payload-budget rejection and whitespace-pattern rejections. `test-lines` ratchet: net +65, allocation credit 65 via `config/test-lines-allocations/203099-worker-toolcall-id-length.txt`. Generated protocol predicates regenerated via `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`.

Gap: the end-to-end Copilot turn (real provider minting the long ID) was not reproduced here — no Copilot credentials on this host; the reporter's shipped-dist observation and the validator-level red/green above cover the changed boundary.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #203099, locate the identifier-budget constraint in the worker protocol schemas, and implement the payload-budget widening for provider-issued tool-call IDs following the #170461 precedent. The implementer understands the code: stream-frame, transcript toolCall, and toolResult schemas share the widened provider-ID schema while internal identifiers keep the identifier budget, and the compiled protocol predicates are regenerated from the schemas. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(agents): warn when a protected store entry overrides an inherited exec value
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the secret egress proxy is enabled, a protected store entry whose name matches an inherited environment value (a config `env.vars` literal or a host env var) silently replaces that value with a process-local sentinel during exec environment assembly. Sentinels are regenerated on every Gateway restart, so operators lose byte-stable local values — a file-backed keyring password is the reported case (#196120) — with no visible cause. Protected-store precedence itself is intentional; the gap is that the override is silent.

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.store-env.test.ts` ("keeps config environment literals readable unless a protected store entry overrides them"): a config-only literal passes through byte-for-byte with egress enabled, and a same-name protected entry overrides it with a sentinel while the exec result now surfaces a warning naming the entry.
- Red on main without the fix: the warning assertion fails with `expected 'ok' to contain 'overrides the inherited "GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD"'` (17/18 other tests pass). Green with the fix: 18/18 in the file, wall ~92s, CI shard ~141s.
- The warning fires only when the sentinel actually wins (inherited value present, no explicit per-call env of the same name), so explicit overrides keep working unchanged.
- Docs updated in `docs/gateway/secrets/secret-store-and-egress.md`: same-name override, the warning, and the restart instability are now stated.

Fixes #202045

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway on a new install accepts connections only from its own computer. When an owner tries to create their first phone setup code, the dialog reports a configuration error and leaves them to figure out how to make the Gateway reachable.

## User Impact

**Connect a device** guides phone pairing through **Set up secure access** and announces that title to screen readers. Choose Tailscale Serve, a trusted home network, or an existing public HTTPS address. **Device** pairing keeps its existing setup error and **Reload** action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway sends a structured detail for the loopback refusal and keeps the error message available to the CLI and other setup flows. The Dashboard uses the detail only for phone pairing and keeps the instructions outside the title’s live region.

The Dashboard leaves configuration changes to the owner. Tailscale Serve keeps the Gateway on loopback and encrypts connections. The trusted-home-network option opens a plaintext LAN listener and explains how to undo it. Phone codes created over plaintext LAN have Limited access, which includes chat history and approvals.

prs.title: fix(config): persist memory search provider/fallback in canonical casing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory.search.provider` and `memory.search.fallback` are persisted with whatever casing the author typed (for example `"None"` or `"NoNe"`), so the value written to `openclaw.json` does not match the value the runtime actually resolves, and the same setting can mean different things depending on how it was typed.

## User Impact

User impact: a `memory.search.provider` value written through the config write path is now stored in the same canonical lowercase form the config schema resolves at runtime, so the file on disk and the effective setting can no longer disagree. This is a persisted-file change: the first write that sets these fields normalizes their casing on disk. Providers, adapters, and validation rules are untouched, and the case-insensitive sentinel `"none"` keeps resolving exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config schema already canonicalizes `memory.search.provider` / `memory.search.fallback` with `normalizeOptionalLowercaseString` when it parses a config, so the runtime always sees a lowercase value. The write path, however, persisted the authored projection without applying the same rule, which left a disk/runtime disagreement: the file could say `"None"` while the runtime resolved `"none"`.

The change adds a small seam at the config persistence point that applies the **existing** normalization rule to just the two fields, and only to the slots the write actually authored. It deliberately does not introduce a second casing rule, does not rewrite the rest of the config, and does not tighten startup or runtime validation.

### Persisted-config casing compatibility

This is the compatibility-relevant part of the change, so it is spelled out explicitly:

- **Only two slots are ever touched**: root `memory.search.provider` / `memory.search.fallback`, and the same pair on a single agent entry under `agents.entries.<id>`. Nothing else in the file is rewritten.
- **Only values this write authored are canonicalized.** The seam is anchored to the write's explicit value source, not to the file. A legacy value that the write did not set keeps its exact original bytes.
- **Whole-roster writes are refused.** A write that replaces `agents`, `agents.entries`, or `agents.list` as a whole does not canonicalize any provider inside it, so replacing a roster cannot silently rewrite members the author never set.
- **Sentinel and `auto` values are unaffected semantically.** `"none"`, `"auto"`, and the `fallback` slot are already case-insensitive at resolution time; they are now stored in the same lowercase form rather than in the author's casing.
- **Blank values are left alone.** A whitespace-only value is stored as authored and continues to resolve as unset; removing the key is the unset path's job, not a casing rule's.
- **Env-var templates are never re-cased.** A value containing an env reference (for example `${MEM_PROVIDER}`) is skipped entirely, so the referenced variable name is never altered.
- **The runtime-facing lookup is unchanged.** Adapter lookup stays a case-sensitive exact match; the change only aligns what is written to disk with what the config schema already resolves. A third-party adapter that registers a non-lowercase id behaves exactly as it did before this change.

## Evidence

An independent QA pass (single round, post-freeze) reviewed the exact committed bytes and returned **PASS-WITH-NOTES, 0 blockers**. The reviewer reproduced the base-commit baseline independently, confirmed the new regression test is sensitive to the fix (it fails when the seam is reverted, so it is not tautological), and confirmed the seam's rule is byte-for-byte the schema's rule.

**Targeted verification**

- New persistence regression test — 2 passed (root case, per-agent case). Reverting only the config-write file makes both fail (`expected 'None' to be 'none'`, `expected 'NoNe' to be 'none'`); restoring it returns 2/2.
- 5 config-write suites — 5 files passed, 171 tests passed.
- Typecheck — clean, no diagnostics.

**Full `src/config` shard, candidate vs base commit**

| | Test files | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate | `2 failed, 499 passed, 2 skipped` (503) | `2 failed, 5493 passed, 9 skipped` (5504) |
| Base | `2 failed, 497 passed, 2 skipped` (501) | `2 failed, 5480 passed, 9 skipped` (5491) |

The **same two files fail on both sides, with identical assertions and error signatures**, and neither is in this diff:

1. `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-excluded-rows.test.ts` — a UTF-8 vs UTF-16 row-filter expectation. The reviewer reproduced it independently at the base commit with all candidate files reverted (`1 failed | 13 passed`), and with the candidate (`1 failed | 14 passed`).
2. `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-memory.test.ts` — `PluginStateStoreError: ... OpenClaw state database lifecycle is retired`. It passes in isolation with the candidate and fails only inside the full shard, on base and candidate alike.

The `+2` file delta is exactly the two new test files, and the skipped count is identical on both sides. **No candidate-caused test failure exists in the shard.**

### Open review notes (6, all non-blocking)

These are disclosed in full so reviewers can judge them rather than discover them.

1. **Ancestor explicit paths also canonicalize.** An ancestor write (for example `agents.entries.<id>` or `memory.search` as a subtree) canonicalizes a provider value carried inside that subtree, even when that value was carried over from the previous file rather than authored in this write. It is bounded to the two authorized slots, never a whole-config rewrite, and semantically inert because the runtime already lowercases the same field. Same mechanism that makes an explicitly-set root provider canonical.
2. **Unresolved env templates still differ in memory.** The config schema lowercases an *unresolved* template (`${MEM_PROVIDER}` → `${mem_provider}`) in the parsed config, so file and runtime still disagree for unresolved templates. This seam correctly leaves the file alone; resolved templates are unaffected (`MEM_PROVIDER=NoNe` loads as `none`). The schema file predates this change.
3. **Blank values stay as authored.** A whitespace-only provider stays on disk as authored while the runtime resolves it as unset. Deliberate: this seam's job is canonical casing, and removing a key belongs to the unset path.
4. **Strict validation rejects an unknown provider id even on unrelated writes.** A write that does not touch the provider field can still fail if the config contains a provider id that is not registered. This was confirmed **not** to be caused by this change: with the seam call removed, the same write still fails with the same message. Realistic ids (`voyage`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`, `none`, `auto`, `gemini`) all write successfully. The validation rule itself predates this change.
5. **The new test file covers 2 of the behaviors in this diff.** There is no case for the `fallback` slot, for env-template preservation, for whole-roster refusal, or for a root-scope byte-identity assertion. The reviewer verified each of those behaviors directly, so this is a suite-completeness gap rather than a behavior gap.
6. **Mixed-case third-party adapter ids are lowercased.** The seam lowercases any explicitly-set provider string. This matches what the config schema already resolves at runtime, so it removes a file/runtime disagreement rather than creating one; the case-sensitive exact-match adapter lookup is unchanged, and all in-tree adapter ids are already lowercase.

### Scope of this diff

This branch carries 11 files: the persistence seam (`src/config/io.write-memory-search-provider.ts` + its call site in `src/config/io.write.ts`), the new regression test, and the config-schema and plugin-registry changes that define the canonical provider/fallback shape the seam reuses.

One note for reviewers: the branch is based on the `v2026.10.7` release line, where all touched files are byte-identical to the base commit, so the diff applies without conflict and introduces no unrelated churn.

prs.title: fix: tell users to stop the Gateway before removing a kept update backup
prs.body:
Related: #201711

## What Problem This Solves

After an update, the result lists old backups the updater kept because it could not prove it created them. For an unmanifested `.pre-startup-migration-*.bak` original, it suggests removing the file yourself with `openclaw update cleanup --include-unmanifested <path>`. That command refuses while the Gateway is running, and the Gateway is running right after the update finishes. So following the suggestion exactly always hit a "Stop the Gateway first" refusal before it worked.

## User Impact

User impact: the hint now says to stop the Gateway (`openclaw gateway stop`) before running the cleanup command, so the suggested steps work the first time. No behavior, refusal, exit code or JSON output changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each refusal already named its next step, so nothing was silent. But the hint skipped a precondition it could state up front. The explicit-retirement section of `docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md` already says to stop the Gateway first; the report hint and the docs summary paragraph now say so too.

Not done:
- Stopping the Gateway from inside cleanup: a lifecycle side effect a deletion command should not take on.
- Adding `--yes` to the hint: the interactive confirmation is the intended guard for an irreversible deletion.

Production change is one string (+1/−1). Docs +2/−1, test +6.

## Evidence

- Found by the update-matrix Windows lane (11.6 → main chain). The hint printed with correct PowerShell quoting. Running it with `--yes` while the Gateway was up returned `Stop the Gateway first (openclaw gateway stop), then retry.`. After stopping the Gateway, the same command removed the file, and the Gateway restarted ready.
- New assertion in `src/commands/update-backup-cleanup-policy.test.ts`: fails with the base report source, passes with the fix (35/35 in the file).
- Format check and `git diff --check` clean on touched files.
- Reviews of the exact head `16956a61400`: autoreview scoped-clean; independent read-only Codex review found nothing.

prs.title: fix: recover longer session history text within response bounds
prs.body:
Related: #64970

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

## User Impact

Callers can opt into `maxChars: 1..64000` for bounded visible-text recovery. Omitting it preserves the 4,000-character default. The 80 KiB response cap, access checks, physical-session checks, and existing reasoning/tool-preview limits remain in place.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. It preserves upstream truncation facts and marks a source-row group incomplete when the local byte cap splits its display siblings, rather than silently treating the surviving sibling as complete.

The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. Unlike the closed environment-override proposal in #65029, this is a bounded per-call option, not a new global setting or a higher default. It builds on the pagination owner in #97101 and structured truncation in #126342.

## Evidence

A Knowledge conversation-learning scribe operator reports that the fixed 4,000-character preview leaves some source intervals incomplete. This is a real-use report, not live validation of the patch; no private conversation content was used.

- **Current head:** `8ca678fa52adffaf2bb059c84e42a5c807c09a1c` integrates `a48440bbdf3e1f827e72eb7d674b63bcbb2fe4cf`. The published tree `2ee2ce64ef3f436feb4223bf09cb9709808906f9` matches the reviewed workspace. The two generated prompt snapshot conflicts were resolved with the canonical generator, not hand edits. The history implementation and regression tests are unchanged apart from inherited main changes in surrounding code.
- **Current-tree local checks:** all six prompt snapshots match the generator. Scoped TypeScript lint and formatting, base-relative whitespace, assertion-safety, and test-line budget (354/400) passed. The sandbox has an older patched Vitest than this main lockfile, so no fresh local runtime test pass is claimed here.
- **Prior-head proof** (`3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`): 95 affected tests, core and agents-tools test typechecks, and [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44606766159/job/135862438343) passed. The real-storage embedded regression failed before the adapter fix and passed afterward, recovering 16,000 characters and paging four rows without omissions or duplicates within 80 KiB per response. It is not a live Gateway/model run.
- **Review:** strict self-review of the complete nine-file, base-relative diff before push confirmed that the inherited changes were outside the PR delta and that regenerated snapshots contain the expected schema addition and derived sizes/hashes. The [completed exact-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) accepted the operator-supplied live proof without independently rerunning it. No findings or Before-merge items remain; the verdict is ready for maintainer review. Overall readiness is **4/6 (Platinum)**, proof confidence **5/6 (Diamond)**, and patch quality **4/6 (Platinum)**.
- **Current-head CI:** the [CI finalizer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44907727218/job/136859675158) and [consolidated `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44908717875) passed. Hosted production/test types, prompt snapshots, and the dependency and security review gates passed; the bounded check inventory does not establish that every job ran or passed.

Pit supplied the following exact-head evidence. The underlying measurements and verifier are retained by the operator and available on request; this run was not reproduced in the Linux sandbox.

### Isolated Gateway + real agent proof

Observed on macOS arm64 on 2026-11-21, testing PR head 8ca678fa52adffaf2bb059c84e42a5c807c09a1c (tree 2ee2ce64ef3f436feb4223bf09cb9709808906f9) against the unpatched selected base a48440bbdf3e1f827e72eb7d674b63bcbb2fe4cf. Both clean SSD worktrees were built with the frozen lockfile and the official build command (exit 0).

A fresh OCM environment used separate state/config/workspace/temp paths and an exclusive loopback port, with no channels, scheduled jobs or memory plugins. The owner performed a dedicated OpenAI device login for the test environment only; no credentials or private conversations from the daily setup were copied. A real OpenClaw agent ran through each live Gateway's normal agent endpoint and invoked sessions_history through its supported Code Mode bridge, not a mock or a direct operator invocation of the history function.

- maxChars:16000 recovered the synthetic 16,000-character message byte-for-byte. Source and recovered SHA-256: 6868e590b63de849692c4ce16ca1a7ad3dcc91311378e0615de4ee5f371a0cdb. contentTruncated=false; a separate 46-character control message was unchanged.
- Omitting maxChars preserved exactly the first 4,000 source characters plus the truncation marker (4,014 characters / 4,018 UTF-8 bytes), with truncated=true and contentTruncated=true. The unpatched baseline returned the same preview and hash: 48a905748127fa6fd3d3c81972d689ec13644ec95e29c67f6b7ec19d037bfda3.
- Three 40,000-character messages exceeded one page. With maxChars:64000, offset 0 returned two messages and offset 2 returned the remaining one: actual JSON result sizes were 80,796 and 40,514 UTF-8 bytes, both below 81,920. The first page had droppedMessages=true, hasMore=true and nextOffset=2; continuation completed without duplicates or omissions. Each recovered message matched its source SHA-256.
- A 200,000-character synthetic message remained explicitly incomplete at maxChars:64000: exactly the first 64,000 source characters plus the marker (64,014 characters), truncated=true and contentTruncated=true. Its actual JSON result size was 64,530 bytes; recovered-text SHA-256: b1acf38523b0fbc1749165b51cbc13dd66c758b0f1974e6b7ceee092c0e15cfc.

The four cases were first exercised in one normal agent turn. Because nested-tool display receipts omit large results, a second normal agent turn captured the same real results in bounded chunks; an offline verifier reconstructed the complete values, independently measured JSON bytes and hashes, and checked exact source equality and pagination. It passed. The initial guessed model was unavailable; supported same-account model discovery resolved setup before the successful proof runs.

Cleanup completed: test Gateways stopped cleanly, test port free, secondary auth profile removed and confirmed absent, and the OCM fixture destroyed. Only the two source/build worktrees and proof artifacts were retained. The personal Gateway kept its original PID/start time and unchanged config/launchd hashes. This is bounded local runtime proof, not adoption, broad security qualification, Unicode coverage, or proof that a live scribe has completed its backlog.

Native `scripts/pr` preparation remains unverified in this sandbox, where `gh` is unavailable.

RoboClaw independently reviewed the supplied contribution and added the scoped preview-bound fixes and regressions. The author-preserving local commit is `c923e10ebcbfd7e37f1629f3cf6e5c2dd75dea48`; the managed publisher created `b71a064d6faee5f6fbc66affadeb30266f515fc1` with an identical tree and the original contributor as co-author. Preservation of the original primary Git author remains unresolved.

prs.title: fix(setup): activate verified sign-ins when setup installs the provider plugin
prs.body:
Closes #202458
Supersedes #170165
Related: #166965

## What Problem This Solves

When setup installs a provider plugin and saves a new sign-in in the same run, the plugin installs and the connection test passes, but activating the sign-in then fails with "The connection changed before credential activation. Test the saved sign-in again." Nothing changed the connection in between; the setup run fails and the saved sign-in is left inactive. The same check also rejects access-only setup (`selectModel: false`) whenever it has a new sign-in to activate; that path is covered by an in-process test only (see Not covered).

## User Impact

User impact: when setup installs a provider plugin and saves a new sign-in in the same run, a sign-in that passes the connection test is now activated and setup completes, instead of failing with "The connection changed before credential activation" and leaving the sign-in inactive. Access-only setup with a new sign-in to activate now also completes, and still does not set a default model. If the saved connection really changes between the commit and activation, setup still stops with that message and leaves the sign-in inactive. No new options, config, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before activating the new sign-in, setup reads the saved config back and requires its inference route to strictly equal the route it verified. That verified route was built from the pre-commit candidate, which still carries the pending `plugins.installs` records for the plugin being installed. The commit moves those records into the installed-plugin index, out of `openclaw.json`, so after an on-demand plugin install the two never match. For access-only setup, the check also compared the saved config's route, which keeps the existing default model, with the route verified for the new provider, so it failed there as well.

The expected route is now built from `candidate` with a source-side candidate whose pending install records are removed (`stripPendingPluginInstallRecords`, the helper the commit itself and the rollback undo in this file already use), and both sides of the comparison go through `candidateRouteConfig`, as the pre-write check in the same function already does. For a setup that selects the model, including the plugin-install case, `candidateRouteConfig` returns the config unchanged. For access-only setup, it applies the model selection used for verification to both sides, so the check still covers the route of the provider that was just verified. The comparison is still a strict deep equality, followed by the unchanged owner revalidation (`revalidateOwner(route)`), so a real change to the saved connection between the commit and activation is still rejected on both paths.

This does not compare against the config that the activation callback receives since #175138, as the setup wizard's check in `src/wizard/setup.inference-verification.ts` does. `commitSetupInferenceActivation` initializes that argument from the pre-commit candidate and replaces it with the result of `configTarget.write(...)` only after the write returns, while a running Gateway can invoke activation from the write notification before that assignment. The argument can therefore still be the pre-commit candidate with its pending install records, so the expected route is built explicitly from the candidate with those records removed, as the rollback undo in this file already does.

Unchanged on purpose: in the regression test with a smaller starting config, the rollback after the false drift is also rejected by the config size-drop guard; rollback behavior is unchanged here.

#170165 has had no updates since 2026-10-12, currently conflicts with main, and is waiting on end-to-end proof; this PR carries the same fix for the plugin-install case forward on current main with before/after evidence, and credits its original author as co-author. Thanks to its author for the original diagnosis and fix. #166965 bundles the same activation change with separate catalog work.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.ts`:
  - A two-line `projectRoute` helper next to `project` applies `candidateRouteConfig` to both of its inputs. `verifiedRoute` now uses it, with the same meaning as before.
  - `activateCredential` computes `committedRoute` with it after its early return when there is no credential to activate, and the pre-activation check compares `projectRoute(current, latest.sourceConfig)` against it.
  - `isDeepStrictEqual` and `revalidateOwner(route)` are unchanged; no new exports or signatures.
- `src/system-agent/setup-inference.provider-install-owner.test.ts`: the existing install-owner test now saves a credential so it reaches activation, and gains a rejection case (see Evidence).
- `src/system-agent/setup-inference.groq-external.integration.test.ts`: the existing Groq case also runs access-only, with and without a provider endpoint change after the commit.
- `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`: one entry removed. The install-owner test's mock of `../plugins/provider-auth-choice.js` now passes the real module through (`importOriginal`) and replaces only `prepareAuthChoiceLoadedPluginProvider`, so it is no longer a closed mock.
- Against `c1dbc0ea30`: `setup-inference-activate.ts` +9/−5, `setup-inference.provider-install-owner.test.ts` +86/−9, `setup-inference.groq-external.integration.test.ts` +52/−7, `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` −1.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `c1dbc0ea30`. "After" results were taken on `c1dbc0ea30` with this PR's change applied, the full diff of commit `7be06ca12fe6`.

Focused tests:

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference.provider-install-owner.test.ts`:
  - The existing test installs a fixture provider plugin during setup but saved no credential, so it never reached activation. It now saves one synthetic API-key credential, keeps the rest of `provider-auth-choice.js` real, and on success asserts `ok: true`, the install record in the installed-plugin index, no `plugins.installs` left in `openclaw.json`, and the credential promoted (its setup marker cleared).
  - The fixture's starting config gets 275 bytes of unrelated settings (`gateway.controlUi`), so the before-fix failure shows the drift error itself rather than the rollback size-drop rejection.
  - New rejection case: after the commit and before activation, another writer restores the pre-setup config bytes. Setup must return `{ ok: false, status: "auth", error: "The connection changed before credential activation. Test the saved sign-in again." }`, the config bytes must equal the pre-setup bytes, and the credential must stay unpromoted. The test writes the config file once at that point; activation itself runs through the real owners, the same way the existing case replaces the plugin files during the connection test.
- `src/system-agent/setup-inference.groq-external.integration.test.ts` (Groq plugin already in the installed-plugin index, a new API key, a local test server):
  - The existing case also runs with `selectModel: false`. It asserts `ok: true`, no default model saved, and the Groq credential promoted with its setup marker cleared.
  - A new access-only rejection case adds a `models.providers.groq` block with another `baseUrl` to the saved config after the commit and before activation. Setup must return the same drift error and leave the Groq credential unpromoted.
- On `c1dbc0ea30` with only the test changes, exactly one case in each file fails, both because setup returns `{ ok: false, status: "auth", error: "The connection changed before credential activation. Test the saved sign-in again." }` instead of `ok: true`: the install-owner case without a change, and the Groq access-only case. All other cases pass, including both rejection cases. For the install-owner case, the assertion output shows `ok: false` and `status: "auth"`; its error text was printed in an earlier run with the same setup.
- With this change, all 6 cases in the two files pass.
- Mutation checks (not part of this PR):
  - With the expected route replaced by the current config's own projection (a self-comparison), both rejection cases fail because setup returns `ok: true`; the other cases pass.
  - In the Groq file, with both sides of the comparison built without `candidateRouteConfig` (the previous revision of this change), only the access-only rejection case fails, again with `ok: true`.
- Time: one focused run of both files (`pnpm test` with both paths and `--maxWorkers=1`) took 39.50 s Vitest duration (73.59 s for the command). Per test: 2.32 s, 0.93 s, and 1.06 s in the install-owner file; 11.98 s for the existing Groq case, and 7.22 s and 7.07 s for the two access-only cases, which repeat that case's setup with `selectModel: false`.
- Consumers pass: 103 tests in 8 files, including the changed Groq file: `setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, `setup-inference-activate.utility.test.ts`, `setup-inference-activate.openrouter-onboarding.test.ts`, `setup-inference-credentials.lifecycle.test.ts`, `inference-route-runtime.test.ts`, and `setup-inference.groq-external.integration.test.ts` under `src/system-agent/`, plus `src/commands/models/auth-activate.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-setup-auth-retry.test.ts`.
- Targeted checks: `oxfmt --check` passes on the three changed TypeScript files; oxlint with the core config (the command printed by `pnpm check:changed --dry-run`) reports 0 warnings and 0 errors; `pnpm tsgo:core` and all `pnpm tsgo:core:test` shards pass; `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` passes; the test-lines ratchet reports `Net test lines: +122; allowance: 400`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Local review: autoreview on the full diff against `c1dbc0ea30` reported scoped-clean, with no actionable findings (patch is correct, 0.85). pr-simplify on an earlier revision of the diff suggested two minor simplifications; both are applied.
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not included yet: a packaged end-to-end setup run and a latest-stable upgrade run. They are planned with Groq, whose provider plugin is not bundled in the npm package, each starting with the plugin absent:

- the setup before the fix, on the latest stable `openclaw@2026.11.6`;
- a fresh install of a package built from this change: plugin installation, verification, activation, and a reply;
- an upgrade from `2026.11.6` with existing settings to that package, then the same setup, with the existing settings checked afterward.

Not covered:

- The focused tests call setup in-process without a deferred-activation callback, so the deferred activation used when setup runs through a running Gateway is not exercised. The planned runs use the CLI `openclaw onboard` path and do not cover it either.
- Access-only setup is covered only by the in-process Groq cases, with no packaged run. On current main it is reached through the Gateway method `models.authLogin` (app-guided provider sign-in that is not credential-only), which runs through a running Gateway and is not part of the planned runs; no bundled provider was found that reaches credential activation with a new credential through it.
- Tests ran on Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64) with Node v24.22.1 only; the change is a config comparison with no platform-specific code.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `50e97a8c67d`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 368ae1dc | v2026.10.8 | 17:47:36 | 17:47:37 | 17:48:06 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| a7d22a6f | v2026.10.8 | 17:48:15 | 17:48:16 | 17:48:49 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 49b062ca | v2026.10.8 | 17:49:07 | 17:49:08 | 17:49:09 | completed | completed |
| 8fea48a4 | 2df6212 | 22:12:37 | 22:12:38 | 22:13:28 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 05f267e5 | 2df6212 | 22:13:34 | 22:13:35 | 22:13:55 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 0a54b7ad | 2df6212 | 22:14:01 | 22:14:02 | 22:14:37 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| c96579c8 | 2df6212 | 22:14:51 | 22:14:52 | 22:14:53 | completed | completed |
| 28ab70e0 | 2df6212 | 22:15:40 | 22:15:42 | 22:16:14 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 70f2a343 | 2df6212 | 22:24:50 | - | 22:24:53 | completed | completed |
| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

- `runtime.telnyx-answer.test.ts` starts the real runtime with Telnyx and realtime enabled and POSTs a `call.initiated` webhook to its listener. It mocks only the outbound HTTP edge and asserts the Telnyx commands for three paths: unset, Krisp, and rejected `suppression_start`. It replaces the constructor-forwarding test the review flagged.
- `providers/telnyx.test.ts` covers:
  - the request order and payloads,
  - engine field mapping,
  - the 5 second suppression bound,
  - fail-open on network errors,
  - hangup on a failed stream-less answer (and none on a failed inline-stream answer),
  - hangup on a failed `streaming_start`, even when that hangup fails,
  - unchanged outbound dials.

  The unset-answer case is folded into the existing streaming-answer test.
- `config.test.ts` covers the rejection cases.

## For the voice-call owner

This adds one optional block, with 10 config paths, under `telnyx`. It stays inside the existing Telnyx provider, and the defaults are unchanged. ClawSweeper recommends approving the optional capability. A maintainer decision on exposing it is the remaining item I can't close from the contributor side.

prs.title: fix(skills): report excess captions before rendering a meme
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a local Meme Maker command supplies more captions than the template has boxes, the command reports success and draws the extra captions on top of the last one. The resulting SVG or PNG can have unreadable text.

## User Impact

The command now tells users how many captions the template can hold and asks them to remove the extra `--text` arguments. It exits before writing an image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both local formats share the same caption layout. The local renderer validates the count against that layout before loading the template image and assigns each caption to its own box. Templates can still render with some fields left blank.

## Evidence

On Linux with Node 24.18.0 and Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4, the real CLI downloaded the Drake template into an isolated cache. Three captions for its two boxes produced an SVG and a 1200×1200 PNG on main. The last two SVG text elements had the same box center. Stable v2026.11.6 produced the same SVG byte for byte.

With this patch, the same input exits 1 for both formats. It creates neither an output file nor a template cache. One and two captions still produce valid SVGs and 1200×1200 PNGs. The hosted rendering service was outside the scope of this check.

<details>
<summary>Commands and local checks</summary>

Base `2d7934abf99`. The affected files were unchanged in upstream main `6e56a2a42ba` at publication. Candidate `e1950ef8968`.

```text
$ node skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs render drake --text "First caption" --text "Second caption" --text "Extra caption" --out meme.svg
error: Drake Hotline Bling has 2 caption boxes, but got 3 captions. Remove extra --text arguments.
exit=1
```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: the new regression failed on the base because the command resolved successfully. The patched suite passed all four tests with the existing PNG test enabled and isolated OpenClaw state. Local shard wall time was 12.30 s, including 0.98 s of test execution.
- Focused tsrs typecheck, repository Oxlint for the test file, Oxfmt, Node syntax, and `git diff --check` passed. The repository-wide changed plan classifies standalone skill scripts into all lanes. Broad verification is left to PR CI.
- Codex autoreview found no P0 issues. Production code is net +1 line for the count validation after removing the fallback that reused the last box. Test code is net +18 lines.

</details>

prs.title: fix(skills): show a runnable skill packaging command
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Skill Creator packager is run without its required skill folder, the usage output sends users to `utils/package_skill.py`. That file is absent from the checkout, so following the recovery instructions fails before packaging starts.

## User Impact

From the repository root, users can follow the displayed command and get a readable `.skill` archive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The packager now prints a single usage command pointing at its bundled script and identifies the working directory it expects. Removed the duplicate stale examples. The missing-argument exit code remains 1.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Python 3.12.3, ran the bundled command without arguments, then used the printed script path with a valid temporary skill. On main `2fa55d1c805` the printed path failed with exit 2 and `No such file or directory`. On the PR head the printed command exited 0, produced `demo-skill.skill`, and passed `python3 -m zipfile -t`. The affected files were unchanged at the updated base `2d7934abf99`.
- The new subprocess regression fails before the change for the same missing path and passes after. It follows the displayed path and reads the exact `SKILL.md` bytes back from the archive. All 13 tests passed with `python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/skill-creator/scripts`.
- Ruff passed on both changed files using `skills/pyproject.toml`. `git diff --check` passed, and local Codex autoreview found no actionable P0 findings. macOS and Windows were not exercised.

<details>
<summary>Local CLI output</summary>

```text
Before
Usage: python utils/package_skill.py <path/to/skill-folder> [output-directory]
python3: can't open file 'utils/package_skill.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory

After
Usage: python3 skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py <path/to/skill-folder> [output-directory]
Run this command from the OpenClaw repository root.
[OK] Successfully packaged skill to: final-output/demo-skill.skill
Done testing
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: enable personal MCP sign-in from browser chat
prs.body:
Related: #138113

## What Problem This Solves

A user can sign in to Control UI but still be unable to connect a personal MCP account from chat. Browser turns have a verified Gateway profile, while personal MCP discovery expects a channel sender ID and therefore omits the connect tool.

## User Impact

User impact: authenticated browser chat can offer personal MCP sign-in, with credentials kept separate for each profile even when profiles share a chat session. Shared MCP tools retain their existing behavior. Background work and subagents do not inherit browser credentials, and a turn with ambiguous personal participants cannot start a personal tool call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted human-turn owner supplies a private, session-bound browser identity to the native and harness MCP consumers. This preserves the meaning of `SenderId` for channel authorization and metadata. Personal tools check the admitted participant when execution starts and reject retained calls after disposal. Work already in flight follows the existing runtime contract.

This is an independently maintained, narrower alternative to #188164 by @apps3000 and #177356 by @Canvinus. Their work informed the separation of browser profiles from transport sender IDs and the authority/lifecycle cases to check. This branch does not depend on either PR or copy their commits. It reuses the existing personal-participant resolver and credential partitioning; it does not add a profile-first identity policy for other channels or repeated checks after every await.

Maintainer decision requested: should direct and visible Control UI turns use this private profile-to-MCP handoff while channel sender semantics remain unchanged?

## Evidence

Publication update (20 November): merged upstream `c72c65a94` in `a18e81e87`. The only conflict was between adjacent imports in `attempt-bundle-tools.ts`; both imports are retained. All contribution additions and deletions match the tested commit below, and the diff against the new base passes `git diff --check`. The 53 tests, type/lint checks, and runtime build below apply to `c50283d04`; they have not been rerun on the merged head. This remains a draft pending merged-head validation and live OAuth replay.

On the base revision, the direct and visible browser regressions fail because personal MCP preflight returns `false`; the five exclusion cases pass. With this patch, all 53 focused tests across five files pass, including separate sign-in identities for two profiles in one session, retained-call rejection, and shared-tool independence. Both targeted type graphs, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

The `qaRuntime` build passed, including runtime post-build checks (350 seconds). This draft requests review of the identity policy; the live OAuth replay below remains unfinished.

Live candidate limitation: this exact upstream implementation has not completed browser-to-provider OAuth consent or an authenticated MCP request. Our deployed workaround did complete real browser sign-in, but it populated `SenderId`; that observation is supporting defect evidence, not a live test of this implementation. See the [sanitized Pilot evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188164#issuecomment-6977193737).

Local autoreview checked the complete source change against the base at P0–P2 priority. Its final result had no actionable findings. The earlier shared-tool restriction was corrected, and the final review also covered connect-only servers. The reviewer inspected source; it did not run tests or a browser.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and check details</summary>

Base: `9903773c4da39eddddf8bc40ff954fad311e1feb`. Candidate: `c50283d04` (the tested file hashes match the committed source).

The final focused test command took 253 seconds including worker compilation. The baseline replay took 218 seconds and produced the two expected failures. The two type graphs took 99 seconds; lint plus SDK declaration preparation took 296 seconds.

Environment: isolated, secretless Linux x64 container with Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependencies, repository-pinned Bun, one test worker, and a 2 CPU / 5 GiB test limit. The runtime build used 6 GiB after the normal capacity check refused 5 GiB; no memory-check override was used. No live Gateway state or personal credential stores were mounted.

The regression uses the actual admitted-turn, participant, MCP manager, and harness materialization paths. It replaces OAuth credential status and provider authorization at the external boundary. It tests profile separation, shared-only acquisition, direct/visible turns, retained tools, anonymous/mismatched profiles, other sessions, memory work, and subagents. A materialization regression checks that ambiguous personal authority blocks personal tools while shared tools remain callable.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-webchat.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-shared.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-root","core-test-agents-other"]' --concurrency 1
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
```

The repository lint wrapper checked all seven changed TypeScript files. The formatter processed all eight changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

</details>
