prs.title: fix(skills): register a bundle command declared as a single Markdown file
prs.body:
Closes #202406

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude-compatible bundle can declare a single Markdown command file (or an array of files) in its manifest, for example `{"name":"fixture","commands":"./extra/review.md"}`. The [Claude Code manifest reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#commands) permits a command path to name a `.md` file or a directory, including arrays of paths. OpenClaw accepts the declaration and reports the bundle's `commands` capability, but the command never appears in the slash-command registry.

The command consumer passed every declared path to the directory walker, which cannot enumerate a file used as its root, so a directly declared file silently produced no command. This is a silent failure: the bundle advertises `commands`, yet the user loses the slash command with no diagnostic.

## User Impact

A plugin that keeps one command file outside the default `commands/` directory now registers that slash command in the live Gateway command catalog. Directory declarations and the additive default-directory behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/skills/discovery/command-specs.ts` resolves bundle command roots from the manifest and walks each with `walkDirectorySync`. `walkDirectorySync` calls `readdirSync` on the root, which fails with `ENOTDIR` for a file root and returns an empty entry list.

The fix has three parts, all inside the existing discovery owner:

- `listMarkdownFilesRecursive` selects a file root directly under the same dotfile and `.md` predicate it applies to directory entries, instead of handing it to the walker.
- `toDefaultCommandName` falls back to the filename when the relative path is empty (a file root makes `path.relative` return `""`), so a directly declared file still registers a command name.
- The consumer de-duplicates selected files by canonical path, so a declared file that is also reachable through the default `commands/` directory registers once, preserving the additive default-directory behavior.

The existing bounded file read, frontmatter handling, invocation policy and plugin-root containment are reused unchanged. Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (a documented declaration shape was accepted but never enumerated).

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway proof (real Gateway RPC)

A real Gateway built from this PR's head (`dist` at `d83bf19`, `OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d83bf19)`) runs against an isolated state directory and a bundle plugin whose manifest declares `"commands": "./extra/review.md"`, with a sibling `unselected.md` written next to it. The command catalog is read through the real `commands.list` Gateway RPC:

```sh
# Isolated state; bundle declared as a single file; sibling unselected.md present.
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PROOF/state" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PROOF/config.json" \
  node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19531 --allow-unconfigured
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PROOF/state" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PROOF/config.json" \
  node openclaw.mjs gateway call commands.list --port 19531 --params '{"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

The `commands.list` response (72 commands total) contains:

```json
{
  "name": "review",
  "nativeName": "review",
  "textAliases": ["/review"],
  "description": "Review the current change",
  "category": "tools",
  "source": "skill",
  "scope": "both",
  "acceptsArgs": true,
  "skillDisplayName": "review",
  "skillModelVisible": false,
  "skillReferenceable": false
}
```

- `/review` is served through the shipped Gateway command catalog after the fix.
- The sibling `unselected.md` is **not** in the catalog (`unselected` absent), so selecting one file does not load neighboring files.
- `review` appears exactly once.

### Source-level base/head comparison (discovery entry)

Real discovery entry point (`buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` + `loadPluginManifestRegistryCore`), run from source on the unmodified tree, over the four manifest layouts from the report. No mocked modules or fabricated manifest records. The `file` and `array` layouts also write an unselected sibling `unselected.md` to confirm it is not loaded.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/repro-202406.mts .
```

| Manifest declaration | BASE `217bb899f09` | HEAD `d83bf19` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"./extra"` (directory) | `['review']` | `['review']` |
| `"./extra/review.md"` (file) | `[]` | `['review']` |
| `["./extra/review.md"]` (array) | `[]` | `['review']` |
| `"./commands/review.md"` + default dir | `['review']` | `['review']` |

BASE reproduces the report exactly: the direct-file layouts return no command. HEAD registers `review` for every layout. The directory and default-directory layouts are the control group and are unchanged, and the unselected sibling is never loaded. The shipped Gateway run above is HEAD; the BASE column is the same discovery entry at the pre-fix commit.

### Regression test

`src/skills/discovery/command-specs.test.ts`:

- `registers a directly declared Markdown command file outside the default directory` — covers both the single-string and array declarations, asserts the filename becomes the fallback command name and the body is read. Red on BASE (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'review' ]`), green on HEAD.
- `does not duplicate a file already selected through the default commands directory` — asserts a file reachable through both the default directory and an explicit declaration registers once.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/skills/discovery/command-specs.test.ts
```

BASE: 1 failed | 5 passed. HEAD: 6 passed.

## Not tested

- A bundle whose declared command file is a symlink or hardlink; the directory path uses the walker's `symlinks: "skip"` policy and the file-root path uses `lstatSync`, so a symlinked file root is not followed. This matches the directory behavior but was not exercised end to end.
- Windows path semantics for a file root. The repro, Gateway run and tests ran on Linux; the fix uses `path.relative`/`path.basename`, which are platform-correct, but a Windows run was not performed.
- The shipped Gateway run used a source-built `dist` from this PR head, not the published npm package.

## Cleanup

The Gateway and reproducer ran entirely in a temporary directory (`os.tmpdir()/oc-proof-*`) with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, on a loopback-only port. No production Gateway, session, token or config was touched.

Claude bundles declaring a Markdown command file could omit that command from the slash-command registry. The initial fix also skipped a bundle whose default commands directory was a symlink.

## User Impact

Selected file commands and commands in an in-bundle symlinked directory are discoverable. Unselected sibling files stay out of the registry, and an overlapping declaration registers a file once.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery previously passed declared files to a directory walker. It now handles Markdown file roots directly and uses `statSync` to classify directory symlinks by their target. The existing realpath boundary check still applies.

## Evidence

The new symlink regression failed on the blocked patch (1 failed, 4 passed) and passed after repair. The original direct-file regression failed before its fix. prs.body:
Related: #201267

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, **Connect your AI** splits logins, API keys, and local models across several sections. ChatGPT sits under **More sign-in options**, and its browser sign-in opens a separate setup sheet.

## User Impact

- Pick ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, an API key, or a local model from one list. **More providers** opens the other options. Detected logins are labeled **On this Mac** or **On your Gateway** and are tested when picked.
- Sign-in, key entry, and the connection test appear in the provider card. Finish the open provider setup or use **Cancel** or **Choose another AI** before moving to another onboarding page.
- The ChatGPT card shows the browser sign-in and paste fallback inline. A failed connection test names ChatGPT and marks the card **Not connected**.
- Gemini offers an API key when a Google sign-in is unavailable. Its form stays bound to Gemini across Gateway changes. The setup mascot uses dark eyes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac groups the options the Gateway reports and shows the selected provider's steps on the page. The Gateway still owns detection, sign-in, and verification.

## Evidence

The macOS VM captures compare main (`4442518e379`) with the onboarding build (`603cee2b93a`). [Independent macOS VM verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201296#issuecomment-7026820075) also checked the picker and inline ChatGPT card.

prs.title: feat(a2a): implement the A2A protocol v1.0 specification
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the `extensions/a2a` channel plugin from partial 0.3-era support to a **conformance-validated implementation of the A2A protocol v1.0 specification**, tested against the official [a2a-tck](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck) conformance suite (remaining failures are limited to scripted-reference-SUT-only scenarios — see Evidence). All configuration remains backward compatible with the original plugin.

## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/a2a` plugin currently implements only a partial, 0.3-era subset of the A2A protocol. A2A has since shipped **v1.0** with breaking changes and new requirements:

- **New method surface**: `SendMessage`/`GetTask`/`ListTasks`/`CancelTask`/`SendStreamingMessage`/`SubscribeToTask` replace the 0.3 dotted methods, plus push notification config CRUD and `GetExtendedAgentCard` — v1.0 clients calling a 0.3-era server get `Method not found`
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` (spec §5.4) with gRPC-transcoding-style path bindings — required for REST-native clients, previously absent
- **Revised error model**: codes `-32001..-32009` with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details, and new HTTP status mappings (`TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502) — the old mappings no longer conform
- **Capability, media-type, and required-extension validation** (spec §3.3.4, §3.1.1, §4.6) — previously not enforced
- **Agent Card caching** (ETag/304, §8.6.1) and the **Extended Agent Card** — previously absent
- **Push notification webhooks** with idempotent delete (§3.1.10) and SSRF protection — previously absent

In short: without this change, the plugin cannot interoperate with A2A v1.0 clients and fails the official conformance suite. With it, it passes (see Evidence below) while every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default.

## Evidence

### a2a-tck conformance suite (official, black-box against a live instance)

Round 10 (latest, HEAD `086867253` — the stream-order fix — both declared transports `jsonrpc` + `http_json`, Bearer auth; [full rendered report](https://gist.github.com/beeven/d00d70490e12cea4d1450b26f472da37)):

- **Overall: 70.0% / MUST: 71.2%** — the only MUST requirements still failing are the two scripted reference-SUT contracts (`DM-ART-001`/`DM-MSG-001`)
- Per-transport: `agent_card` 10/10; `jsonrpc` 62P/5F; `http_json` 57P/5F — every remaining failure is a scripted-contract case
- `STREAM-ORDER-001` (round-9 finding: state-sequence regression when a reused messageId lands on a completed task) **passes on both transports** after `086867253`, with a regression test in the suite
- Round-to-round: 51.3% -> 65.8% -> 67.9% -> 69.1% -> 73.9% -> 75.0% -> 73.9% -> 71.4% -> 71.2% MUST. Round-over-round variance is coverage, not behavior: the real LLM returns COMPLETED or INPUT_REQUIRED non-deterministically for TCK's fixed prerequisite text, so requirements move in and out of the denominator between runs
- Round-9 confirmation traces (live gateway, token redacted):

```
# REST push-config list route — the round-8 regression, now fixed
GET /a2a/v1/rest/tasks/<uuid>/pushNotificationConfigs
-> 200 {"configs":[],"nextPageToken":"","pageSize":0}

# STREAM-ORDER-001 reproduction (reused messageId on a completed task)
jsonrpc  first stream : ok     [WORKING, WORKING, COMPLETED]
http_json reuse       : regress [COMPLETED, WORKING, COMPLETED]   <- before fix
http_json reuse       : ok     [WORKING, COMPLETED]               <- after 086867253
```

- Reproduction (public repo layout, local plugin injects Bearer auth which upstream TCK lacks):

```
cd a2a-tck && PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python ./run_tck.py \
    --sut-host http://localhost:38789 --transport jsonrpc,http_json -- \
    -p tck_local_openclaw --timeout=45 --timeout-method=signal
```

Artifacts: `reports/compatibility.json` / `compatibility.html` / `junitreport.xml`.

### Behavior proof over the real transport

Captured against a real Gateway built from this branch (`19e3466d0`) — real HTTP/SSE on the wire, real agent dispatch to a live model backend, real webhook POSTs to a local receiver (localhost endpoints and placeholder tokens throughout, nothing to redact). Full traces in [#issuecomment-6659323864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179380#issuecomment-6659323864); summary:

- **Allowed delivery**: three ordered webhook POSTs (WORKING → artifact → COMPLETED), all 200, per-task ordering held
- **Foreign peer refused**: unknown bearer → HTTP 401, no task, zero webhook POSTs
- **No POST after deletion in the real retry window**: registration deleted via REST inside the 250 ms backoff → receiver saw exactly one failed POST, no retries
- **No POST to the old URL after replacement in the retry window**: same config id re-registered to a new URL during backoff → old receiver silent, new receiver got the retries
- **No POST after shutdown**: SIGTERM while a delivery chain was live → terminal update delivered while the account was still stopping, then zero POSTs after `shutdown completed` with the receiver healthy for 17 s
- **Disabled extended card**: authenticated peer gets `-32004` UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION pointing at the config
- **Stream ordering (v4 contract)**: `SendStreamingMessage` = opening Task snapshot (WORKING) → updates → terminal close; subscribing to an INPUT_REQUIRED task folds all pre-subscription transitions into the snapshot and streams only post-subscription events
- **Follow-up retry identity**: identical messageId retry while the resumed turn was running resolved to the same task, history contains the answer exactly once
### Unit tests and typecheck (this repo)

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/a2a
Test Files  13 passed (13)
     Tests  151 passed (151)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test   # typecheck: green
```

New coverage added alongside the review fixes: REST binding HTTP tests (push-config create/list, shared per-peer rate limit -> 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, malformed body -> INVALID_ARGUMENT), per-subscriber stream queues each observing the full event sequence, replay-before-subscribe, interrupt-released blocking sends, `statusTimestampAfter` filtering, task-eviction observers expiring push registrations, 429 webhook retry, and the stream-order regression above.

### Config compatibility

- All pre-existing config keys verified unchanged (name/semantics/default) — existing deployments upgrade without touching config
- New keys are opt-in; `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` and the metadata sync check passes

## What's implemented

### Core protocol (§3)
- All **11 JSON-RPC methods** defined in v1.0: `SendMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `SubscribeToTask`, the four push notification config CRUD methods (`SetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig`), and `GetExtendedAgentCard`
- Backward-compatible **0.3-era dotted method aliases** (`message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/subscribe`, ...) so existing clients keep working
- **Agent Card** served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` with ETag / Last-Modified / Cache-Control caching and `If-None-Match` → 304 handling (§8.6.1)
- **Extended Agent Card** served behind the `extendedAgentCard` capability

### Transports
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` per §5.4, with gRPC-transcoding-style URL path bindings (path parameters take precedence over body fields)
- **SSE streaming** with resumable task updates
- **gRPC-style HTTP status mappings** per §5.4: `TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502

### Error model
- Full v1.0 error codes **-32001..-32009** with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details (reason / domain / metadata); JSON-RPC reserved codes (-32700..-32603) carry no ErrorInfo, as required

### Push notifications (§3.1.10)
- Full config CRUD with **idempotent delete** (repeated deletes succeed silently, per spec)
- Webhook delivery with **SSRF protection** (private-network targets blocked unless explicitly allowed)
- Configurable authentication schemes (bearer, basic, apikey)

### Validation
- **Capability validation** (§3.3.4): calling a method whose capability is disabled returns `-32004` `UnsupportedOperation`; enabling `extendedAgentCard` without configuring it returns `-32007`
- **Media-type validation** (§3.1.1): raw/url part media types checked against `inputModes` (with `type/*` and `*/*` wildcard support) before text-part checks, returning `-32005` with ErrorInfo metadata
- **Required extensions** (§4.6): extensions declared with `required: true` that are not activated via the `A2A-Extensions` header return `-32008`

### Outbound agent-to-agent client
- Full `Message | Task` oneof parsing with ErrorInfo reason surfacing in thrown errors

## Configuration compatibility

- **No breaking changes**: every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default
- New v1.0 features are **opt-in** via new keys: `capabilities.*` (skill discovery, extensions, push), `pushNotifications.*` (auth, webhook options), `rest.enabled`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`
- `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` so core startup validation accepts the new keys
- Config-surface budget: this consciously raises the `channel` baseline by **+30 entries** (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`, channel 3975 → 4005) — exactly the new opt-in A2A v1.0 keys (`capabilities.*`, `pushNotifications.*`, `rest.*`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`, and peers/auth knobs); no existing keys changed

## Notes

- Rebased onto latest `main` (`65fc2f00d`); the diff is limited to `extensions/a2a/` + the regenerated config metadata file, and upstream's `wait()`/`buildContext` refactors from #178508 are integrated
- Happy to split into smaller commits or adjust scope per maintainer feedback

prs.title: fix: keep QA context from skipping automation steps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation checks in the QA mock provider can skip their required tools when a request includes standalone sender or notification context. Some planners also count results from an earlier user turn, so the provider can report a completed step that the current scenario never performed.

## User Impact

QA developers can run the affected automation, hook, requester, and handoff scenarios without context being mistaken for a tool result. This changes QA tooling only; it adds no configuration, permissions, migration, or user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing linked-output and current-turn helpers throughout the remaining planners instead of independent raw output-kind checks. Generic named standalone context stays supported, while linked empty results, existing ID aliases, and explicit handoff call matching keep their contracts. No new predicate, state, or compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

- New HTTP regression groups fail on the unchanged baseline and pass with the repair: eight scripted planners retain their required first tool, and scratch progresses through linked aliases and an empty completion without reusing an earlier turn.
- The maintained provider factory and real loopback Responses endpoint reproduce the failure before the change and preserve the initial tool plan afterward across all eight planners, using both generic notifications and sender context. Tools are planned only; no automation, file, or shell side effects are executed.
- 248 affected and sibling tests passed, including malformed-output, native function/custom results, current-turn boundaries, WebSocket, fanout, and forked-context cases. Targeted types, lint, formatting, assertion safety, line-cap, test-line, and diff checks pass. No baseline allowance was increased.
- Author simplification keeps the existing completion owner and removes the parallel caller-side checks. The change adds no production helper or API.
- No external live model or deployed Gateway was used for this QA-only repair; exact published-head PR CI must pass before landing.
- Full local ClawSweeper review of `5e7675ea08cd6ff6de5713e7d5a0dcf6c7a84332..ea5a5dc5a8fe2c7dd77f4cd29d92a0bd875eb288` completed with no correctness or security findings. This is the complete committed range, not a smoke or hosted review.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that request only a provider API key currently initialize the model-specific authentication runtime as well. Provider-only lookup already has a narrower credential owner, so this loads code the request does not need.

## User Impact

Provider-only SDK credential lookup no longer initializes model-runtime preparation. Credential selection, cancellation, and model-specific authentication behavior are unchanged; no configuration changes are required. This is an internal loading-boundary fix, not a claim of a measured latency improvement or repaired authentication outage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve provider API keys lazily through the existing provider-auth owner, preserving the cancellation checks before and after the import. Model-specific requests keep their existing lazy runtime path. This adapts the maintained release-line repair in `2955325ff52c` and its mock-isolation clarification in `f889066b55b9` without adding an API, wrapper, fallback, or cache.

## Evidence

- Acceptance rule: provider-only lookup initializes the model-runtime module zero times; a subsequent model-specific lookup still initializes it once and returns its credential result.

- Focused SDK, Bearer-request policy, provider-operation deadline, and xAI auth/cancellation consumer suites pass: 70 tests across four files. HTTP and credential I/O use synthetic fixtures; no paid provider call is claimed.

prs.title: fix: start fresh native work after its broker disconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a native resource broker loses its IPC connection, the next worker/resource request can select that disconnected broker before its JavaScript disconnect callback runs. The request then fails instead of starting with a fresh broker.

## User Impact

Fresh native-resource requests select a new broker as soon as native IPC reports disconnection. Already-admitted work keeps its existing settlement and cleanup obligations. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing broker admission fact now includes the child process’s native `connected` state, matching the narrow repair already maintained on release/2026.11.7. It introduces no new lifetime owner, retry, timeout, or permission policy.

## Evidence

The regression disconnects an actual task-owned native broker, requests a fresh retained source before the disconnect callback runs, and completes a real resource round trip in a different broker. It fails on the unchanged base with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` and passes with this fix; all owned broker cleanup is joined.

- 47 tests passed across the native lifecycle, native handle, host transport retirement, and real resource transport suites. Existing tests continue to protect admitted claims, SQLite/native-child cleanup, failed close retries, and granted launch settlement.
- Final regression rerun: 238 ms test time, 36.47 s wrapper wall time including compiled-worker preparation. Full changed file: 17 tests passed; the existing late-attachment case accounts for approximately 15 seconds. CI timing remains pending.
- Targeted test/production-import typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, assertion safety, line-cap and test-line budget checks passed. No exceptions added.
- Linux / Node v26.12.1; repository runner used its configured compiled-worker runtime. No macOS/Windows qualification or deployed Gateway changes.
- Full local ClawSweeper review of `c949daa031c6ea961c4cf39bae8ba3df50a0e73e..d22969dca412673d140f95602998399b4f147ad5` completed with no correctness or security findings. This is the complete committed range, not a smoke or hosted review. The review input did not include the local execution receipts; the actual red/green production-caller results above were separately inspected and retained.

prs.title: fix(webui): let users turn off failed channels
prs.body:
## Why

When a WeChat login expires, the channel is still enabled, but its switch looks off. Clicking it retries the failed connection instead of turning WeChat off. The switch should show what the user can change; the **Failed** badge should show what happened to the connection.

## What changed

- Channel and instance switches now reflect the saved enable setting, not whether the channel is running. Failure badges and login recovery remain separate.
- A channel that is enabled but missing dependencies keeps its off switch next to the install button. No gateway or credential-handling changes.

### WeChat in Apps → Channels

| Before: login expired, switch incorrectly off | After: same failure, switch on | After turning it off and refreshing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![WeChat marked Failed with its switch incorrectly off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d68ff420-41d4-414c-b660-ec88e799abbf) | ![WeChat marked Failed with its switch on](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a229d9f-135b-426a-af5c-cff81371b1e4) | ![WeChat disabled after a page refresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd522c98-90fe-4920-80e4-2599a323ede2) |

## Verification

- Reproduced in Chromium against an isolated gateway using a local WeChat endpoint that reports an expired login. With the fix, one click disabled WeChat without scanning a QR code. Refreshed the page and verified the switch stayed off and the saved token and allowlist were unchanged.
- The 46 focused WebUI tests passed, including disable with and without channel support installed. WebUI typecheck, lint and production build passed.

Resolves [NAN-481](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-481/让-webui-能关掉已启用但运行失败的微信渠道)

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
**Ready for review.** All five shared operations met the performance budget against current `main` (`0dc8679ed` vs PR `68c11eaf0`). [20/20 CI checks passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44917107465).

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What users get

In a saved topic, **Message actions → Edit message** opens an inline draft. **Cancel** preserves the conversation and composer. **Resend** replaces the selected message and its suffix and generates a reply in the same topic. **Fork** still makes a separate topic. This does not undo external tool effects. Only persisted plain user text is editable; attachments, quotes, mentions, commands and special inputs are not silently converted to plain text. [User guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/68c11eaf0fe9696a4b5e9f4761e0311541446c2b/docs/webui.md#edit-a-sent-message).

## Current verification

Synced `main` at `0dc8679ed`. On desktop and a 390px viewport, opening the editor on a collapsed message exposes the full text and resend controls; cancel restores the original collapsed message and keyboard focus. Edit admission no longer decodes answer bodies to identify the discarded suffix. A concurrent SQLite writer test verifies that a history page and its ETag describe the same snapshot and an edit based on an obsolete page is rejected.

### Current `main` comparison (decision baseline)

Both snapshots were separately production-built on Windows and run against the same deterministic loopback model, fixture data, dependencies and browser. Eight fresh gateway pairs × 16 measured pairs per operation; startup and within-pair order were balanced. Differences are PR minus `main`, in ms. For all five shared operations the one-sided 95% upper bound on the paired median was below the existing margin. This measures typical latency on this runner, not every device or tail latency.

| Shared operation | Paired median Δ | One-sided 95% upper bound | Margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Latest history (8 turns) | -0.29 | +0.61 | 1.00 |
| Latest history (192 turns) | -0.83 | +0.25 | 1.00 |
| Ordinary input acknowledgement | -0.20 | +0.20 | 1.00 |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | -2.44 | +0.56 | 5.00 |
| Navigate → latest message painted | +0.60 | +4.90 | 5.00 |

`main` has no edit-and-resend operation, so it has no like-for-like timing for that new feature. Earlier results against an older integration parent and the previous edit implementation are [historical diagnostics](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-59285eab-02f7-45da-bd22-d08700295c79), not the readiness gate. [Measurement plan, all 640 raw pairs and confidence intervals for the current comparison](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-03da91ef-d8e0-464f-940a-7719408576c5).

## Correctness evidence on `e42f74689`

- One owner serializes ordinary input and edits. The SQLite transaction checks the page-independent source identity, original text, revision and retry receipt, then changes both model history and display history. Admission failure leaves the old histories intact. Once accepted, a model failure belongs to the new turn. A transport retry does not schedule a second model request.
- **White-box:** reviewed admission/dispatch, cancellation, storage/crash boundaries, outbound ownership, HTTP pagination and frontend draft/connection lifecycle. Fixed canonical `input_id` on replacement and a late idle event that could leave its original run marked active. The late event releases only that owner and does not publish into a replaced history. Final focused Python selection: 81 passed.
- **Black-box:** two Chromium clients, production-built UI, real local gateway/SQLite/WebSocket and a deterministic HTTP model. Mouse, keyboard and touch; cancel with an outstanding composer draft; middle, first and paginated edits; reload and actual disconnect/reconnect. The provider saw exactly 3, 0 and 174 retained user inputs respectively, followed only by the edited input, once per edit. Older retained rows remained pageable; the topic/identity did not change. Two editors of the same revision produced one winner; reconnect/retry, busy/stale source, provider refusal and ordinary fork were checked independently. No uncaught browser exceptions. No physical device or external model was used.
- **Formal concurrency check:** [two TLA+ models, assumptions and reproduction commands](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/tree/e42f74689b0e41915d0c7d52939092cd50f4b062/verification/history-edit). All invariants held over 484 admission states and 132 delayed-delivery/reconnect states, with no unexpected deadlock. Removing transactional source validation or the retired-generation fence gave the expected counterexamples. These are bounded single-owner models assuming atomic SQLite commits, not an exactly-once guarantee for external side effects.

## Historical CI and snapshots (`e42f74689`)

[Test Suite 44722331397](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397) passed, including `CI required`. PR head `e42f74689`; Actions checked out `5a0fd420d`, merging that head onto `db0306b40`. The local correctness and timing runs use the PR head; ordinary timing uses its frozen integration parent `cd75dbfaa`, not moving main. No check or size/coverage budget was relaxed. Attempt 1's Windows native upgrade/recovery test reached the second `metadata-loss` journey, then `inspect_profiles()` raised `ValueError` while checking readiness after the second restart. The exact target's push CI skipped native acceptance. The preceding PR candidate passed the same step. Only that Windows job and downstream aggregate were re-requested on the unchanged merge; the original failure is not attributed to the edit without evidence. [First attempt's failure report](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397/artifacts/14624090600).

<details><summary>Historical performance results and diagnosis on e42f74689 (superseded by the current table above)</summary>

### Performance

**At that snapshot, performance was not signed off:** Latest page, 8 turns, Latest page, 192 turns, Ordinary input → completed reply, Navigate → latest message painted, Edit → completed reply. Do not treat passing CI as performance approval.

Windows, real same-version gateway/WebUI with a deterministic loopback model. Ordinary operations vs `cd75dbfaa` (integration parent); edits vs `d06d326ad` (previous edit implementation). Four fresh gateway pairs, 16 measured pairs each, per metric. Snapshots on the same volume. AB/BA balanced at startup and randomized within adjacent pairs; warmups excluded, no other observations discarded. Reads decode eight real HTTP responses per observation. Render requires the expected message in view followed by an animation frame. Edit replaces turn 49 of 96, with one provider execution and the exact retained prefix. All durations are ms.

| Path | Baseline median | PR median | Paired Δ [two-sided 95% interval] | One-sided upper / margin | Gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 13.21 | 14.36 | +0.88 [-0.28, +1.62] | +1.54 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 14.70 | 15.27 | +0.64 [-0.51, +1.60] | +1.19 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Ordinary input ACK | 6.07 | 5.85 | +0.05 [-0.38, +0.53] | +0.48 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 70.04 | 72.48 | +1.91 [-1.51, +6.17] | +5.22 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 99.65 | 95.45 | -0.15 [-7.80, +7.20] | +5.30 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Edit ACK | 13.19 | 10.79 | -1.57 [-2.25, -0.85] | -0.92 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Edit → completed reply | 86.31 | 100.96 | +9.27 [+3.27, +14.12] | +14.02 / 5.00 | Not established |

The gate is the one-sided 95% upper bound on the paired median delta (candidate minus baseline), strictly below max(5% of the baseline median, 1 ms for reads/ACKs or 5 ms for completed turns/render). Intervals use 12,000 deterministic stratified bootstrap draws across observations within the four blocks. Cross-block and machine-to-machine variability, tails, physical-device latency and the latency of an external model are not bounded by this test.

On the previous `aa18f9e45` snapshot (48 pairs; gateway blocks separated in time), short/long reads had paired medians +1.67/+2.24 ms and upper bounds +2.80/+3.43 ms vs a 1 ms margin. Ordinary ACK, paint and edit completion also failed to establish non-inferiority. Profiling identified a duplicate SQLite snapshot-header lookup. This candidate reuses immutable headers only within one transaction and sends the regular 40-event page after replacement, with a cursor for the rest. The previous samples were retained, not pooled.


| Path | Baseline / candidate block medians (ms), in measurement order | Min–max of all samples: baseline / candidate (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 19.14 / 20.84; 11.75 / 14.21; 13.03 / 12.07; 12.95 / 12.93 | 6.92–24.56 / 6.77–26.59 |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 22.50 / 17.84; 13.20 / 14.74; 12.98 / 12.78; 14.03 / 14.99 | 7.40–25.67 / 8.04–26.99 |
| Ordinary input ACK | 5.75 / 6.21; 7.06 / 7.07; 5.77 / 5.41; 5.77 / 5.77 | 4.70–24.72 / 4.66–37.74 |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 66.80 / 70.06; 84.42 / 92.85; 68.16 / 69.86; 67.26 / 69.63 | 59.76–114.63 / 59.57–130.79 |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 90.60 / 90.45; 102.80 / 108.55; 102.30 / 100.40; 92.70 / 90.90 | 65.50–163.60 / 67.20–149.50 |
| Edit ACK | 11.10 / 10.02; 12.36 / 9.92; 16.95 / 13.63; 13.63 / 12.48 | 10.03–25.28 / 7.71–186.72 |
| Edit → completed reply | 74.88 / 87.17; 78.57 / 82.53; 114.81 / 123.42; 93.31 / 109.56 | 68.64–346.62 / 70.84–463.34 |

**Where to investigate next:** on an equal 48-input context, the interval between the fixture provider returning and the client receiving `turn_end` was 16.8–16.9 ms (old edit), 23.6–24.7 ms (candidate edit), and 22.6–24.6 ms (ordinary input on the integrated main baseline), as ranges of two diagnostic block medians. Independent tracing found prompt-context observation and four display-history appends on both current main and the candidate, versus two appends on the previous edit implementation. This explains a candidate path to optimize; it does not assign the full end-to-end difference to one function. Recheck the shared delivery path on a quiet runner without dropping context graphs, persistence or generation checks. In ordinary HTTP reads the candidate already makes fewer SQL statements (25/37 vs 27/39), selects the same 24/42 records, and does not load full model history. These diagnostics do not override the failed timing gates. [Raw paired timings and a relocatable Windows benchmark harness](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-e64c8f32-6625-410f-b27e-ac69baf99db7).

</details>

prs.title: fix(tools): number read_file lines by newline like edit_file
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` numbers lines with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on form feed, vertical tab, lone CR, NEL, U+2028, U+2029 and the ASCII separators `\x1c`-`\x1e`. `edit_file` reports and checks `line_hint` by counting `"\n"`. So the two tools disagree on any file that contains one of those characters. Form feeds are a common page break in C and Python sources (GNU style), and U+2028 appears raw in JS/JSON string literals.

For `"alpha\n\f\n    beta\n    gamma\n"`, `read_file` prints `4|     beta` and "5 lines total", while `edit_file` places `beta` on line 3. The `edit_file` schema tells the model to copy `line_hint` from `read_file`, so `edit_file(old_text="beta", line_hint=4)` fails with "line_hint 4 does not match the old_text location. old_text appears at line 3."

Two more places inside `edit_file` number lines the `splitlines()` way: trim-fallback matches (so an exact match and a trim match of the same block report different lines) and the "Best match ... at line N" hint shown when `old_text` is not found, which the model then uses as its next `line_hint`.

## Fix

- `read_file` splits on `"\n"` (after the existing CRLF normalization; a trailing newline does not add an empty line, so "N lines total" is unchanged for normal files). A file with lone-CR line endings now reads as one line, which is where `edit_file` already placed its text.
- Trim-fallback matches and the best-match hint compute their line number by counting `"\n"` before the match, the same expression the exact and quote-normalized matchers already use.

Not changed: the `grep` tool still numbers lines with `splitlines()`. It reads files without the CRLF normalization, so it needs a separate change.

## Tests

- New `test_edit_file_line_hint_matches_read_file_numbering` (exact and trim-fallback cases): `read_file` shows `3|     beta` and "4 lines total", and `line_hint=3` applies. On main both cases fail with `assert '3|     beta' in '1| alpha\n2| \n3| \n4|     beta ...'`.
- New `test_edit_file_best_match_line_matches_read_file_numbering`: the not-found hint says "at line 3". On main it says "line 4".
- `tests/tools/`: 1172 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `filesystem.py`.

prs.title: fix(matrix): keep HTML formatting in m.new_content for edits
prs.body:
## Problem

A streamed Matrix reply is sent once and then updated through `m.replace` edits of that first event (the throttled intermediate edits and the final one). `_build_matrix_text_content` puts `format` and `formatted_body` on each edit's top-level fallback, but builds `m.new_content` from `body` and `msgtype` only.

Clients that apply edits read `m.new_content`. From the spec, [Applying `m.new_content`](https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/#applying-mnew_content): "When applying a replacement, the `content` of the original event is treated as being overwritten entirely by `m.new_content`, with the exception of `m.relates_to`, which is left *unchanged*." Its example ends with "Note that `formatted_body` is now absent, because it was absent in the replacement event." So in Element and other edit-aware clients the finished reply shows raw Markdown (`**bold**`, headings, backticks, tables), although the first draft was rendered as HTML.

## Fix

When the text renders to HTML, put `format` and `formatted_body` inside `m.new_content` as well. This applies to the intermediate edits and the final one. Plain-text edits are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test_build_matrix_text_content_with_event_id_preserves_html_formatting`. On main it fails because `m.new_content` lacks `format` and `formatted_body`; it passes with the fix.
- `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests`: 123 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `runtime.py`.

Not tested against a live homeserver.

prs.title: fix(tools): read SVG files as text instead of image blocks
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` decides whether a file is an image with `detect_image_mime(raw) or mimetypes.guess_type(path)[0]`. `detect_image_mime` recognises PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP from their bytes; for anything else the file extension decides. So `logo.svg` comes back as an `image_url` block holding `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` instead of its source.

That block is not usable. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI accepts SVG as image input (both take JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP), and the Anthropic converter's `data:(image/\w+);base64` pattern does not match `svg+xml`, so the block is sent as a `url` source with a `data:` URL. The model never gets the SVG markup it asked to read or edit.

## Fix

Leave `image/svg+xml` out of the image check. SVG then goes through the text path like any other XML file and returns line-numbered source. Other extension-guessed images (for example a `.png` whose bytes `detect_image_mime` does not recognise) keep the image path, as `test_magic_and_extension_image_reads_are_unchanged` on main expects.

An SVG that is neither UTF-8 nor BOM-marked gets the existing `Cannot read binary file` error, because `.svg` is not in `_is_text_extension`.

## Tests

- New `TestReadFileTool::test_svg_file_returns_numbered_source`. On main it fails because the result is `[{'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,...'}}, ...]`; with the fix it returns `1| <svg xmlns=...`.
- `tests/tools/` on the rebased branch: all pass (1499 passed, 8 skipped).
- `ruff check` is clean.

prs.title: fix(mcp): render resource and audio blocks in tool results
prs.body:
## Problem

`MCPToolWrapper._render_call_result` handles text and image blocks and passes every other content block through `str(block)`. MCP tools also return embedded resources, resource links and audio. For those the model sees pydantic reprs, for example:

```
type='resource' resource=TextResourceContents(uri=AnyUrl('repo://octo/demo/README.md'), mimeType='text/markdown', meta=None, text="# Demo\n\nIt's a readme.") annotations=None meta=None
```

github/github-mcp-server's `get_file_contents` returns file bodies this way (an `EmbeddedResource` next to a short text message, or a `ResourceLink` for files of 1 MB or more). For a binary file or an audio block the repr includes the whole base64 payload, which goes straight into the tool result and the context. The docstring of `_render_call_result` already says base64 must not be forwarded for images; the sibling `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` renders the same resource types as their text or `[Binary resource: N bytes]`.

## Fix

In `_render_call_result`:

- `EmbeddedResource` with text contents renders as its text; with blob contents as `[Binary resource: N bytes]`, the wording `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` uses.
- `AudioContent` renders as `[Audio content: N bytes]`.
- `ResourceLink` renders as `[MCP Resource] <description or name>` plus its URI, the format `MCPResourceWrapper` uses for its tool description.

Image handling is unchanged, including image blobs inside an `EmbeddedResource`, which still become artifacts. A `ResourceLink` is rendered without its `mimeType` and `size`. As in `MCPResourceWrapper`, `N` is the length of the base64 string.

## Tests

- New `test_execute_renders_resource_blocks_as_text` and `test_execute_keeps_binary_payloads_out_of_result`, built from real `mcp.types` objects. On main both fail with the reprs above (the second shows `blob='JVBERi0xLjcK'` in the result); with the fix they pass. The fake `mcp.types` fixture gains the three real types the renderer now checks.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py`: 117 passed. `tests/tools/`: 1171 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `mcp.py`.

Not changed: `MCPPromptWrapper.execute` has the same `str()` fallback for prompt messages; that can be a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(provider): support OpenRouter native image generation API
prs.body:
## Reason for the Change

OpenRouter now provides image generation through its native Images API. Nanobot needs to use this API so OpenRouter image generation remains compatible with the current service and can expose more image-generation providers and models through the existing `generate_image` workflow.

## Summary

Update the OpenRouter image-generation client to use OpenRouter's native image API instead of the previous chat-completions image flow.

The implementation:

- Sends generation requests to `POST /api/v1/images`.
- Looks up model capabilities through `GET /api/v1/images/models`.
- Sends `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` only when the selected model advertises the requested values.
- Sends reference images using OpenRouter's native `input_references` format.
- Decodes `data[].b64_json` responses into nanobot image data URLs.
- Preserves a valid response `media_type` when one is returned.
- Keeps provider configuration and the existing `generate_image` tool interface unchanged.

The implementation was tested with these OpenRouter models:

- `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`
- `meta/muse-image`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-lite`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5`
- `black-forest-labs/flux.2-pro`
- `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality`

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_image_generation.py -q`
  - Result: 99 passed in 0.82s

The suite covers:
- Native `POST /api/v1/images` requests.
- `GET /api/v1/images/models` capability discovery.
- Supported and unsupported aspect-ratio and resolution values.
- `extraBody` overrides.
- Native reference-image inputs.
- Base64 response decoding and returned media types.
- Capability-lookup failures and responses without images.
- Missing OpenRouter API keys.

## Compatibility and Rollout

Existing OpenRouter provider credentials, image-generation settings, and the `generate_image` tool remain unchanged. Models that do not advertise a requested aspect ratio or resolution receive a request without that optional field, allowing the model to use its default behavior.

## Problem

When a user selects a model preset and quickly reopens the picker, the previous picker can return focus to the message input. The new picker then closes before the user can change the reasoning effort.

Clear the pending focus return on reopen. Ignore the previous picker's close callback when another picker has mounted. A normal selection still returns focus to the message input.

releases.body:
## Changes

- Connect over SSH to gateways that also advertise a public WebSocket URL. **Use existing SSH settings** now supports Windows hosts where Python 3 is available as `python`. The quick-pairing command remains Linux-only; gateway-native TLS and `trustedProxyAuth` are still unsupported over SSH. [#6682](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6682)
- See the latest activity when a turn is collapsed, and see which follow-up messages are still waiting for the agent. Reconnecting also preserves the state of running turns more reliably. [#6664](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6664), [#6719](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6719), [#6726](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6726), [#6715](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6715)
- Find Tools, Skills, and Chat Platforms in one **Apps** catalog. Choose the reasoning effort for your next message from the composer, without changing the shared preset. [#6700](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6700), [#6441](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6441)
- Long messages you send can collapse to keep the conversation easier to scan. Expand them with **Show more**, or copy the full text without expanding. [#6739](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6739)
- Align the footer controls in the settings sidebar, and keep the model picker open when you reopen it quickly after switching presets. [Settings sidebar fix](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/bc690f0394a00703d6f25a48c63ecb0170b2e091), [#6743](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6743)
- Dream can organize detailed knowledge in a Markdown wiki and keep a short memory summary in context. Existing memory files and custom Dream guides remain supported. [#4477](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/4477)

## Upgrade notes

- For a manual update, stop nanobot, back up your configuration and workspace, and update the gateway using the original installation method. If you use a separate WebUI client with a remote gateway, update both to the same version. [Update guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0dc8679edcc6061fbcdf3de13c7e16000e9d1b65/docs/updating.md#installation-owners)
- **Standalone API server:** `nanobot serve`, its `/v1` endpoints, and the `nanobot-api` Compose service are retired. Stop the old process or container before upgrading and keep the data volumes. There is no drop-in HTTP replacement. The gateway, WebUI, Python SDK, and outbound model connections still work; old API conversations can be read through the Python SDK. [#6614](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6614)
- **OpenAI provider settings:** If you explicitly selected an API using the old `apiType` or `api_type` setting, save your configuration with v0.4.1 before upgrading, or migrate to the current `api` field. Update any old launcher environment variables separately. The old default `auto` needs no action. [#6615](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6615)
- **Global shared session:** `unifiedSession` and `unified_session` are now ignored. Existing session data stays in place; new messages use per-chat or explicitly selected topic routes. [#6621](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6621)
- This release supports manual installation. In-app automatic updates are not enabled for it.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a model with a **1,048,576-token context window**, the stale-stream watchdog fires **during the prefill phase** — before a single byte has arrived — and kills a healthy request. The user is told the model "stopped".

The trigger for reaching such huge prefills in the first place is that `compression.threshold` is a **ratio of the context window**: with the default `0.5`, compaction on a 1M-token model would only begin at **524,288 tokens**, which normal sessions approach but never reach. Observed in practice: contexts grew to **259,764** and **400,608 tokens** with no compaction.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.2+1545` (build 2026-09-24), stable, gateway mode
- Linux 6.8.0-134-generic, x86_64
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible remote endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`
- Primary `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (1M ctx); fallbacks `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`
- `compression:` `enabled: true`, `threshold: 0.5`, `target_ratio: 0.2` — no `model_thresholds`, no `threshold_tokens`

## What happens

1. Long-running session. Compaction never triggers because `0.5 x 1,048,576 = 524,288` is never reached.
2. A turn starts with a very large prompt (observed up to ~400k tokens).
3. The provider must prefill that prompt before emitting the first token, so **nothing is sent for minutes**.
4. The watchdog gives up and kills a healthy connection.
5. The turn is presented to the user as a stopped / truncated reply.

## Evidence

Stale kill (exact log line, hostname/PID stripped):

```
WARNING agent.chat_completion_helpers: Stream stale for 300s (threshold 300s) — no chunks received. model=mimo-v2.6-flash context=~259,764 tokens. Killing connection.
WARNING agent.stream_diag: Stream drop on attempt 1/3 — retrying. provider=opencode-go base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
```

Repeated elsewhere as `Interrupted provider wait counted as stale after 235s with no output; consecutive stale attempts=1.`

Counts over 7 days: **1 stale kill**, **4 `Clean EOF, no finish_reason`**, **several `Stream drop on attempt 1/3`**.

Compaction after the threshold was lowered (confirming both the window size and the ratio behaviour):

```
Preflight compression: ~400,608 tokens >= 157,286 threshold.
```

`157,286 = 0.15 x 1,048,576` exactly — i.e. the config resolves the window as 1M tokens, so `0.5` really does mean 524,288.

### The model is not the cause

Direct streaming probes against the same endpoint:

| prompt | time to first token | frames | longest gap between frames | finish |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| trivial | 1.74s | 12 | 0.1s | `stop` |
| deliberately hard reasoning | 1.73s | 956 (954 carrying `reasoning_content`) | **0.3s** | `length` |

Reasoning is streamed continuously — there is no long silent "thinking" phase. The silence is **pure prefill**, so any allowance computed for remote calls has to scale with input size.

## Related

- #108237 — per-model / per-context-window `threshold` and `target_ratio` (this is the root enabler; `model_thresholds` as a local workaround came from it)
- #126217 — stream ends without `finish_reason` after text is delivered (also observed here; separate symptom)
- #104402 — reasoning-model stale floor killing long prefills (local-endpoint angle; this report is the **remote** angle)
- #133318 — Bedrock read timeout killing long-context reasoning turns (same class, different transport)
- #126304 / #136350 — `compression.threshold_tokens` defaulting to 256000 despite docs saying `null`

## Workaround applied locally

```yaml
providers:
  opencode-go:
    stale_timeout_seconds: 600
compression:
  model_thresholds:
    deepseek-v4.1-flash: 0.15
    mimo-v2.6-flash: 0.15
    glm-5.3-flash: 0.15
```

Both took effect without a gateway restart (verified: compaction fired at 157,286 immediately after).

## Suggested fix

1. **Treat pre-first-token as a distinct phase.** Before the first token the expected silence is `O(input_tokens)`; after it, a short idle timeout is appropriate. Today one flat wall-clock budget covers both, so large prompts are structurally punished.
2. **Scale the prefill allowance with the resolved context window / prompt size** rather than a fixed 300s for remote providers.
3. **Clamp `compression.threshold` when the window is very large**, or prefer absolute `threshold_tokens` consistently — a ratio that implies "half the window" is not a meaningful default at 1M tokens.
4. Optionally: when a stale kill occurs with `bytes=0` and the turn has an enormous prompt, say that in the user-facing message — "the prompt was too large to process in time" is actionable, "stopped" is not.

issues.body:
*Highest impact: it makes a correctly configured install answer nothing while
every check the user runs says it is fine. This is the one that cost us four days.*

## Affected component
`Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)` — the closest option; this is the
`api_server` platform, which the list does not name.


## Bug Description

With `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME` unset, the API server sends its own **advertised
display name** upstream as the model id, so every turn through `/api/sessions`
fails with a provider error naming a model the user never chose.

`_resolve_model_name` falls back to the literal string `hermes-agent`
(`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`, ~L1387 and ~L1648). That value is used for
`/v1/models` — which is correct — and then also as the model id for the request,
which is not.

Three things make this very hard to diagnose from a client:

1. **The CLI is unaffected.** `hermes -z "..."` answers correctly from the same
   config, so every check a user runs says the agent is healthy.
2. **The error names a model nobody chose.** `hermes-agent` is the project's own
   name, so it reads like a client bug or a broken install.
3. **A per-request `model` is silently ignored while this is unset.** Sending an
   explicit `{"model": "...", "provider": "..."}` still ran `hermes-agent`, and
   the response's own `runtime` block reported `route_source: "raw_request"`
   *alongside* `model: "hermes-agent"` — it recorded the override and did not
   apply it. Setting `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME` to a real slug fixed the
   per-request override too, so the two paths appear more coupled than intended.

The failed run is also reported as a **successful** `assistant.completed` whose
message content is the provider's error text, which is indistinguishable from a
model that chose to reply with an error string.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME` unset and `platforms.api_server.model_name`
   absent from `config.yaml`. Set a valid `model.default` and `model.provider`.
2. Confirm the CLI is healthy: `hermes -z "Reply with exactly: ok"` → `ok`
3. Send the same thing through the API:

```bash
SID=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"model id probe"}' "$GW/api/sessions" | jq -r '.session.id')

curl -s -N -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly: ok"}' "$GW/api/sessions/$SID/chat/stream" \
  | grep -A1 assistant.completed
```

4. Set `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME` to a real slug, restart the gateway, repeat
   step 3 — the turn now succeeds.

## Expected Behavior

The turn uses the configured `model.default` / `model.provider`, exactly as the
CLI does. A per-request `model` overrides it. If no model can be resolved, the
gateway fails at startup with a clear message.

## Actual Behavior

The run reports success and the assistant's message content is the provider's
error:

```
HTTP 400: hermes-agent is not a valid model ID
HTTP 404: Model 'hermes-agent' not found. The requested model does not exist in
          our configuration or OpenRouter catalog.
```

This continued for four days on our install. Sessions were created, runs
started, `assistant.completed` arrived — nothing anywhere reported a failure.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The advertised display name for `/v1/models` is being reused as the model id for
inference. The fallback for that display name is the project's own name, so an
unset variable produces a syntactically valid but meaningless model id.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Do not use the advertised display name as a model id — resolve the model from
   `model.default` / `model.provider` as the CLI does.
2. If no model is resolvable, fail at startup rather than per-turn.
3. Honour a per-request `model` independently of `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME`.
