issues.title: [Bug]: Queued busy VOICE follow-up skips auto-TTS despite completing and delivering text

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: tool/tts
labels.description: Text-to-speech and transcription

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug Description

A second `MessageType.VOICE` event received while the first turn is executing completes successfully and delivers its final text, but never invokes auto-TTS. The first reply is spoken normally. Two sequential voice events produce two spoken replies.

This is a **Core orchestration integration reproduction**, not an assertion that a remote TTS provider failed or that a messaging transport lost an uploaded file. It requires no chat-voice-routing extension and no agent-generated/manual TTS.

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.23.2, installed commit `ae2a81ccc00e9b7c06301523e5bb09608397149c`.
- macOS 26.2; Python 3.14.9.
- Affected component: Gateway / Core session-authority busy-follow-up delivery.
- Originally investigated for MAX; the independent reproduction uses a generic `BasePlatformAdapter` transport fixture, not the MAX plugin.
- Auto-TTS is enabled (`voice.auto_tts: true`; adapter auto-TTS mode `all`). Both inputs are VOICE events with synthetic already-transcribed text. Final responses contain no MEDIA or attachments.
- **Latest upstream runtime was not executed.** I did not update/restart the working installation just to file this report. I separately inspected upstream main `88a1c1f4b19d1bc2b9fe8db870dee9ba0803fad5`; its `session_ingress.deliver_response` still sends text/attachments without an auto-TTS step. This inspection is not claimed as latest-main reproduction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable automatic voice replies in a messaging chat.
2. Send a voice message that keeps the agent executing long enough to accept a follow-up.
3. While the first turn is executing, send another voice message to the same chat.
4. Let both turns finish with ordinary text-only final responses.
5. Compare with sending the same two voice messages sequentially, waiting for the first reply before sending the second.

The deterministic offline integration script below uses an `asyncio.Event` at the external agent-execution boundary instead of a slow external model. It exercises real `BasePlatformAdapter.handle_message`, scoped runner handling, disposable SQLite SessionAuthority admission/drain/turn settlement, and native waiter/busy-follow-up delivery. Only external agent execution, synthesis and transport IO are fixtures; scheduling and Core reply-delivery code are not replaced.

## Expected Behavior

With auto-TTS enabled, both completed VOICE turns should invoke synthesis and deliver audio, whether they were admitted sequentially or while the session was busy.

## Actual Behavior / repeated results

Each scenario was repeated three times by the initial investigation and then independently rerun from a byte-identical script in a fresh fixture directory. The independent rerun returned the same result:

| Scenario, per run | Terminal/completed SQLite admissions | Final texts | Synthesis invocations | Audio deliveries |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two sequential VOICE events (3 repeats) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Second VOICE while first agent execution is blocked (3 repeats) | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

- All expected-two-audio healthy controls pass.
- The queued expected-two-audio assertion fails in all three repeats.
- No captured Core/auto-TTS errors and no agent cancellation.
- Every synthesized fixture WAV is valid and reaches the transport fixture; the missing second audio is an **absent synthesis invocation**, not a filtered/generated file or failed upload.
- `router_loaded` is false. The agent fixture never invokes any tools or manual TTS.
- Reproduction exit: **1**, specifically `AssertionError: Expected 2 audio replies per 2 completed VOICE turns`.

## Root Cause Analysis

On the installed commit, the busy follow-up observer delivers via [`gateway/session_ingress.py#L508-L568`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ae2a81ccc00e9b7c06301523e5bb09608397149c/gateway/session_ingress.py#L508-L568). `deliver_response` extracts response content, sends final text, and calls attachment delivery, but does not run native auto-TTS. The normal base path has a separate [auto-TTS step](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ae2a81ccc00e9b7c06301523e5bb09608397149c/gateway/platforms/base.py#L4377-L4386).

The defect is reproduced independently of the TTS provider label. This report does **not** claim to explain all historical missing-voice incidents, streaming-related suppression, or voice-origin metadata loss after async delegation.

Related, different scenarios: #154530 concerns voice-origin async delegation completion delivered as an internal text event; #18539 concerns explicit MEDIA file delivery in a FIFO chain. Here a second actual VOICE event completes, but the automatic synthesis itself is never called.

## Debug Report / privacy and test boundaries

No full production configuration, personal conversations, credentials, or gateway logs are uploaded. Scoped diagnostics and a self-contained synthetic reproduction are provided instead of a broad debug bundle. No working Core/MAX plugin/converter/configuration was modified and no live messages were sent by the reproduction.

The script installs its network/subprocess guard **before importing Hermes** and confines file writes to the fixture directory. It read-selects the already-committed dependency environment and imports real bootstrap through its import-only `pm repair` branch, restoring argv immediately; it does not execute a repair/update command. This avoids production PM locks/dependency updates. The audio fixture writes a valid tiny WAV; it does not test actual speech generation or remote MAX transport.

Save the script as `repro.py` in an empty directory and execute it with the Python interpreter from the Hermes installation:

```sh
python repro.py /path/to/hermes-agent
# Expected on affected code: exit 1 at the final expected-two-audio assertion.
# results.json contains all six cases, SQLite outcomes, synthesis/audio counts,
# captured errors/cancellations, and SHA256 pins of the exercised Core files.
```

<details>
<summary>Standalone offline reproduction (200 lines)</summary>

```python
"""Offline Core integration fixture; not a MAX/provider end-to-end test.
Run: python repro.py /path/to/hermes-agent
Exit 1 means the expected-two-audio assertion failed (see results.json).
"""
import sys
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import os
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
from collections import Counter
DENIED = Counter()
def guard(event, args):
    if event in {'socket.connect', 'socket.getaddrinfo', 'socket.sendto',
                 'subprocess.Popen', 'os.system', 'os.posix_spawn', 'os.fork'}:
        DENIED[event] += 1
        raise RuntimeError('OFFLINE GUARD: ' + event)
    if event == 'open' and len(args) > 2:
        flags = args[2]
        if isinstance(flags, int) and flags & (os.O_WRONLY | os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT):
            if isinstance(args[0], (str, bytes, os.PathLike)):
                p = Path(os.fsdecode(args[0])).resolve()
                if not p.is_relative_to(ROOT):
                    raise RuntimeError('WRITE OUTSIDE WORKSPACE: ' + str(p))
sys.addaudithook(guard)  # Before bootstrap or any Hermes imports.
import asyncio, json, wave, hashlib, logging, uuid
RUN_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex
HOME = ROOT / 'test-home'
HOME.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
SCRATCH = ROOT / 'scratch'
SCRATCH.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
os.environ.update(HERMES_HOME=str(HOME), HERMES_ROOT=str(HOME), TMPDIR=str(SCRATCH))
for key in list(os.environ):
    if key.startswith('HERMES_SESSION_') or key in {
        'HERMES_PLATFORM', 'HERMES_UI_SESSION_ID', 'HERMES_SAFE_MODE',
        'HERMES_PLUGIN_HOST_PROCESS'}:
        os.environ.pop(key, None)
(HOME / 'config.yaml').write_text('tts:\n  provider: offline-fixture\n  output_format: wav\nplugins:\n  enabled: [offline-fixture]\n  isolation: in_process\nvoice:\n  auto_tts: true\n')
PLUGIN = HOME / 'plugins' / 'offline-fixture'
PLUGIN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(PLUGIN / 'plugin.yaml').write_text('name: offline-fixture\nversion: 0.0.1\ndescription: Offline synthesis fixture only\n')
(PLUGIN / '__init__.py').write_text('''from agent.tts_provider import TTSProvider
import wave
class Fixture(TTSProvider):
    name = 'offline-fixture'
    calls = []
    def synthesize(self, text, output_path, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append(text)
        path = str(__import__('pathlib').Path(output_path).with_suffix('.wav'))
        with wave.open(path, 'wb') as w:
            w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(24000)
            w.writeframes(b'\\x00\\x00' * 240)
        return path
provider = Fixture()
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_tts_provider(provider)
''')
CORE = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(CORE))
# Read committed dependencies without acquiring production PM write locks.
from pm.environments import committed_venv, site_packages
import site
site.addsitedir(str(site_packages(committed_venv(CORE))))
# Real bootstrap's documented stdlib repair import route skips dependency mutation;
# no CLI command/repair is executed. Restore argv immediately after import.
saved_argv = sys.argv[:]
sys.argv = [sys.argv[0], 'pm', 'repair']
import hermes_bootstrap
sys.argv = saved_argv
from hermes_constants import set_hermes_home_override
set_hermes_home_override(HOME)
from hermes_cli.plugins import get_plugin_manager
from agent.tts_registry import get_provider
from gateway.run import GatewayRunner
from gateway.hooks import HookRegistry
from gateway.config import GatewayConfig, Platform, PlatformConfig
from gateway.platform_registry import PlatformEntry, platform_registry
from gateway.platforms.base import BasePlatformAdapter, SendResult
from gateway.platforms.event import MessageEvent, MessageType
from gateway.session_authority import initialize_session_authority
get_plugin_manager().discover_and_load()
provider = get_provider('offline-fixture')
assert provider is not None
platform_registry.register(PlatformEntry(name='fixture', label='Offline transport',
    allowed_users_env='FIXTURE_ALLOWED_USERS', adapter_factory=lambda cfg: None,
    check_fn=lambda: True))
PLATFORM = Platform('fixture')
os.environ['FIXTURE_ALLOWED_USERS'] = 'test-user'
ERRORS = []
class Capture(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, record):
        if record.levelno >= logging.ERROR or 'Auto-TTS failed' in record.getMessage():
            ERRORS.append(record.getMessage())
logging.getLogger().addHandler(Capture())
class Adapter(BasePlatformAdapter):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, token='offline'), PLATFORM)
        self.sent, self.audio, self.completed = [], [], []
        self._auto_tts_default, self._auto_tts_mode = True, 'all'
    async def connect(self, **kwargs): return True
    async def disconnect(self): pass
    async def send(self, chat_id, content, reply_to=None, metadata=None):
        self.sent.append(content)
        return SendResult(success=True, message_id='text-' + str(len(self.sent)))
    async def edit_message(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return SendResult(success=True, message_id='edited')
    async def send_typing(self, *args, **kwargs): pass
    async def get_chat_info(self, chat_id): return {'id': chat_id}
    async def on_processing_complete(self, event, outcome):
        self.completed.append([event.message_id, str(outcome)])
    async def send_voice(self, chat_id, audio_path, **kwargs):
        with wave.open(str(audio_path), 'rb') as w:
            assert w.getnframes() == 240
        self.audio.append({'bytes': Path(audio_path).stat().st_size})
        return SendResult(success=True, message_id='audio-' + str(len(self.audio)))
    async def send_audio(self, chat_id, audio_path, **kwargs):
        return await self.send_voice(chat_id, audio_path, **kwargs)
async def until(predicate, seconds=15):
    async with asyncio.timeout(seconds):
        while not predicate(): await asyncio.sleep(.005)
async def scenario(queued, number):
    cfg = GatewayConfig()
    runner = GatewayRunner(cfg)
    runner.hooks = HookRegistry()
    adapter = Adapter()
    adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    runner.adapters = {PLATFORM: adapter}
    authority = await initialize_session_authority(runner, profile_id='default',
        instance_id='fixture-' + str(number))
    runner._wire_adapter_handlers(adapter)
    gate, started = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()
    turns, cancelled = [], []
    # Only the external execution boundary is replaced: no tools/manual TTS.
    async def external_agent(**kwargs):
        index = len(turns) + 1
        turns.append({'index': index, 'completed': False})
        started.set()
        try:
            if index == 1: await gate.wait()
            turns[index - 1]['completed'] = True
            return {'final_response': 'Fixture response.', 'messages': [],
                    'model': 'offline', 'provider': 'offline'}
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            cancelled.append(index)
            raise
    runner._run_agent = external_agent
    source = adapter.build_source(chat_id='test-chat-' + RUN_ID + '-' + str(number),
        chat_type='group', user_id='test-user')
    def event(i):
        return MessageEvent(text='Fixture voice transcript.', source=source,
            message_id='message-' + str(i), message_type=MessageType.VOICE)
    before, errors_before = len(provider.calls), len(ERRORS)
    with authority.db._read_ctx() as conn:
        seq_before = conn.execute('SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) FROM session_admissions').fetchone()[0]
    if not queued: gate.set()
    await adapter.handle_message(event(1))
    await asyncio.wait_for(started.wait(), 15)
    if not queued:
        await until(lambda: not adapter._background_tasks)
    await asyncio.wait_for(adapter.handle_message(event(2)), 15)
    gate.set()
    await until(lambda: len(turns) == 2 and not adapter._background_tasks)
    for live in authority.sessions.values():
        if live.task is not None:
            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(live.task), 10)
    assert authority.db is not None
    with authority.db._read_ctx() as conn:
        admissions = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(
            'SELECT status, outcome FROM session_admissions WHERE seq > ? ORDER BY seq', (seq_before,))]
    result = {'case': 'queued' if queued else 'sequential', 'run': number,
        'sqlite_admissions': admissions,
        'turns': turns, 'text_deliveries': [t for t in adapter.sent if t == 'Fixture response.'],
        'all_transport_text': adapter.sent,
        'synthesis_calls': len(provider.calls) - before, 'audio': adapter.audio,
        'processing_completions': adapter.completed, 'cancelled': cancelled,
        'errors': ERRORS[errors_before:], 'expected_audio': 2,
        'expected_two_audio_pass': len(adapter.audio) == 2}
    assert len(admissions) == 2 and all(
        r == {'status': 'terminal', 'outcome': 'completed'} for r in admissions), result
    assert len(turns) == 2 and all(t['completed'] for t in turns), result
    assert len(result['text_deliveries']) == 2, result
    assert not result['errors'] and not cancelled, result
    return result
async def main():
    results = []
    for repeat in range(3):
        results.append(await scenario(False, repeat * 2))
        results.append(await scenario(True, repeat * 2 + 1))
    hashes = {p: hashlib.sha256((CORE / p).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in [
        'gateway/platforms/base.py', 'gateway/platforms/base_auto_tts.py',
        'gateway/session_ingress.py', 'gateway/session_authority.py',
        'gateway/run_adapters.py', 'gateway/run.py', 'tools/tts_tool.py']}
    report = {'fixture': 'Core orchestration integration; external agent/audio/send only',
        'results': results, 'critical_sha256': hashes, 'denied_operations': DENIED,
        'router_loaded': get_provider('chat-voice-routing') is not None}
    (ROOT / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    assert all(r['expected_two_audio_pass'] for r in results if r['case'] == 'sequential')
    assert not report['router_loaded']
    assert all(r['expected_two_audio_pass'] for r in results), 'Expected 2 audio replies per 2 completed VOICE turns'
asyncio.run(main())

```
</details>

## Proposed Fix

Please route busy-follow-up final delivery through the same voice eligibility/deduplication and auto-TTS handling as normal final delivery, without duplicating audio already produced by the agent. No production patch is included in this report.

issues.title: Kanban attachment store has no programmable pre-store policy — the completion-staging copy is invisible to tool-layer guards

labels.name: type/security
labels.description: Security vulnerability or hardening

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## The class

A kanban attachment becomes durable through **three distinct blob writers**, and none of them has a programmable content policy in front of the write:

1. `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::store_attachment_bytes` — agent `kanban_attach`, `kanban_attach_url`, and CLI `attach` (the card that called this "the single write path" was right about intent but the dashboard doesn't use it);
2. `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py::upload_task_attachment` — the dashboard streams the upload straight to disk and calls `add_attachment` itself;
3. the completion-artifact staging copy inside `complete_task`/`request_review` (`_persist_scratch_completion_artifacts` → `_copy_capped` → `_insert_completion_attachment`) — bytes are copied into the durable attachments dir **by the engine**, so a plugin guarding the tool layer (`pre_tool_call`) never sees this door at all.

Consequence measured in the field (multi-profile fleet, anonymized): a worker declared a captured `docker inspect` dump in `kanban_complete(metadata={"artifacts": [...]})`. The engine copied it into `<kanban>/attachments/<task>/…json` — the dump contained a live service key that no filename denylist and no shape-based redactor can name (a prefix-less hex value inside a JSON env array). The file sat world-readable-by-umask for hours until a value-sweep found it. The board row + dashboard download link made it a durable egress door. Nothing in core could have been configured to refuse it.

**Repro on current `main` (synthetic, no live values):**

```python
# HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d), main @ 88a1c1f4
import hermes_cli.kanban_db as kb
conn = kb.connect(); tid = kb.create_task(conn, title="t", assignee="w", workspace_kind="scratch", workspace_path=str(home/"kanban"/"workspaces"/"w1"))
artifact.write_bytes(b'{"Env": ["SOME_KEY=<value-only-identifiable-secret>"]}')
kb.claim_task(conn, tid)
kb.complete_task(conn, tid, summary="done", force=True, metadata={"artifacts": [str(artifact)]})
# -> True; the blob is durable; grep finds the value in attachments/<tid>/; there is NO hook,
#    policy, or config knob that could have refused this store.
```

This is §3.2 hardening / accident-prevention layering, not a §2 boundary claim — the trust model treats any in-process scanner as a heuristic. That is exactly why the ask is a **generic seam**, not a second parser: operators who run value-based scanners want the store seam to consult their oracle.

## Relation to open work

- **#156844** (open): masks `.env` values on redacted surfaces and adds `gateway.refuse_secret_files` for **chat delivery**. Complementary, not overlapping: it never sees the board-store door (a blob stored on the board with no chat send is untouched by it), and its oracle is the profile `.env`; operators with a broader needle set (vault stores, harbor overlays) need an injectable provider, which is what a hook gives.
- **#109636** (open, conflicting): a static **filename denylist** (`auth.json`, `.env`, keychain exports) at these doors. Its own review already shows the class problem — `id_rsa`/`*.pem`/`*.key` pass, any value-bearing filename that looks innocent (`merlin-inspect-pre.json`) passes forever, and every addition is a core PR. A policy hook subsumes it: that denylist becomes a plugin consumer of `pre_attachment_store` instead of a frozen list in core.

## Proposed shape (PR follows)

New fail-closed directive hook `pre_attachment_store`, fired inside one new shared store lane (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_attachments`) that all three writers are routed through:

- kwargs `task_id, board, filename, content_type, size, source(attach|attach_url|dashboard|cli|completion_artifact), uploaded_by, path` — the staged blob exists at mode `0600` during callbacks and is unlinked on refusal;
- `{action: block, message}` refuses the store (message surfaced to the uploader verbatim — the subscriber names the finding, never the content), records an `attachment_policy_blocked` event;
- a subscriber may **redact the file in place and allow** — the attachment row records the post-hook size;
- timeout/raised callbacks fail closed via the existing `pre_tool_call` policy-hook machinery;
- with no subscriber the store path is byte-identical to today (no scan, no chmod, no dispatch).

Core ships no scanner and no secret parser — the oracle stays an operator plugin (ours: value needles from the deployment's own secret store, same oracle the file-sweep uses).

PR: #TBD (branch `fix/kanban-attachment-store-policy-hook`, tests red on base). Fleet interim control while unmerged: an estate `pre_tool_call` plugin that blocks the tool-layer doors — it demonstrably cannot cover door 3, which is what motivated this seam.

labels.name: type/bug

labels.name: duplicate

issues.body:
## Problem

A canonical Kanban implementation task with an existing owner, worktree, branch, and open PR can be routed to `triage` after the same block kind recurs twice. When `kanban.auto_decompose: true`, the gateway's next dispatcher tick treats that recovery triage card like a fresh unspecifed task and decomposes it into unrelated child tasks.

Observed on Hermes `b1858f33a`:

- canonical task already had an issue, owner, absolute worktree, branch, open PR, clean exact head, and bounded review loop;
- `block_task()` reached `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` and emitted `block_loop_detected`, moving the task to `triage`;
- gateway `_auto_decompose_tick()` selected every triage ID without checking triage origin or canonical implementation identity;
- five overlapping children were generated and the root owner changed;
- generated children had `workspace_kind=worktree` but no `workspace_path`, so dispatcher attempts failed immediately;
- this could have created duplicate editors/branches/PRs if a board default workdir had existed.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` uses `triage` both for fresh unspecified cards and for block-loop human intervention. `gateway/kanban_watchers.py::_auto_decompose_tick()` calls `list_triage_ids()` and decomposes both categories indiscriminately when auto-decompose is enabled.

## Expected behavior

Block-loop triage is a human recovery gate and must not be auto-decomposed. At minimum, auto-decompose should skip a triage card when any of these hold:

- the card entered triage through `block_loop_detected`;
- it has an existing workspace path, branch, current/open PR association, or durable implementation identity;
- decomposition would overlap an existing canonical owner/worktree/branch/PR;
- generated children cannot receive valid isolated workspaces.

The root owner and canonical implementation identity must be preserved. A human may explicitly invoke `hermes kanban decompose` if decomposition is truly desired.

## Acceptance criteria

- Distinguish fresh-specification triage from block-loop/recovery triage durably.
- Gateway auto-decompose skips block-loop/recovery triage.
- Existing owner, workspace, branch, and PR identity remain unchanged.
- No child tasks are created for the skipped card.
- Explicit manual decomposition remains available.
- Regression covers repeated same-kind block → `block_loop_detected` → gateway tick with `auto_decompose=true`.
- Regression covers a canonical card with a worktree/branch and proves zero fan-out/dispatch.
- If child fan-out is ever permitted, workspace allocation must be valid before children become dispatchable.

## Immediate containment

The affected live profile was set to `kanban.auto_decompose: false`; the gateway re-reads this safety toggle every tick. This prevents further automatic fan-out but does not replace the product fix.

issues.body:
**What breaks:** For the same profile, the Dashboard's model page and the Desktop's Settings → Model page show different provider lists. A provider can be selectable in one and missing in the other, so what you can configure depends on which app you open.

**Real case:** I run several profiles on one Mac. The root profile is signed in to OpenAI Codex; a second profile, `don` (a social-media agent), has no Codex login of its own and borrows the root one through the credential-pool fallback. I wanted to move `don`'s main model to an OpenAI model:

- **Dashboard → Change model · don:** "ChatGPT or Codex Subscription" models are listed. I picked `gpt-6.2-sol`, saved, and `don`'s `config.yaml` now has `provider: openai-codex`.

  ![Dashboard: Change model · don, Codex models listed](https://www.pedroberaldo.com.br/gh/hermes-dashboard-model-picker-profile-don.png)

- **Desktop → Settings → Model, applied to `don`:** the Provider dropdown only shows Nous Portal, Anthropic and Claude Subscription. `openai-codex` isn't there, so the same change can't be made from the Desktop.

  ![Desktop: Settings → Model, profile don, no openai-codex](https://www.pedroberaldo.com.br/gh/hermes-desktop-provider-picker-don.png)

Same profile, same machine, same moment, two answers. Nothing on either screen explains why.

**Workaround:** `hermes -p don auth add openai-codex` (a login owned by the profile). After that, both pickers list it.

**Why it happens (`main` at `88a1c1f4b1`):**
- Dashboard: `GET /api/model/options` defaults to `explicit_only=false` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/models.py:166`), so fallback credentials count.
- Desktop: the request sends `explicit_only=true` (`apps/desktop/src/api/models.ts:53`), and `_filter_explicit_provider_rows()` drops providers that `is_provider_explicitly_configured()` doesn't count. A credential borrowed from the root is not counted.
- Live on an install at `a15efb95f7b`: the same profile gets 5 providers from the Dashboard path and 3 from the Desktop path.

**Expected:** Both surfaces apply the same rule for a profile, whichever one the team prefers. If borrowed credentials shouldn't be selectable, the Dashboard should hide them too, ideally with a hint such as "signed in on the root profile only: run `hermes -p <profile> auth add <provider>`". If they should be, the Desktop should list them.

**Context:** #39398 kept provider selection profile-scoped on purpose, and #88609 discusses the same asymmetry. This issue doesn't argue for either side, only for one rule across both surfaces. Possibly related: #149002 (Desktop fallback-model picker not scoped to the selected profile).

Tested on: macOS 26.7, Hermes Desktop + dashboard, multiplex gateway.

issues.body:
## Observed failure

In a local/Desktop-origin Hermes session, an asynchronous delegated child's approval is successfully presented while a parent turn is active, then withdrawn unanswered immediately when that parent turn finishes. The child stops without executing the protected command. The user did not deny or stop the action in these observed windows.

Two log/SQLite-correlated incidents on 2026-11-21, same local/Desktop session:

| Event | Incident A | Incident B |
|---|---|---|
| Approval prompt delivery reports success | 11:09:38.166 | 12:21:28.885 |
| Parent assistant final persisted | 11:09:43.479989 | 12:21:30.023061 |
| Approval waiter wakes: state=set, choice=None | 11:09:43.504 | 12:21:30.037 |
| Child protected tool returns withdrawn | 11:09:43.511 | 12:21:30.041 |

Times are CST. Prompt answer windows were approximately5.34s and1.15s, not the configured300-second unanswered timeout. A separate foreground approval really did time out after300s that day; that is not being relabelled as this bug. The child errors correctly say withdrawal, not user denial:

```text
BLOCKED: Command approval was withdrawn before the user answered
(the turn ended before the prompt was answered).
```

Incident B's parent turn was reconciling a background process notification while the independent review child was running. The child later reported review blocked, not a test verdict. Async delegation delivery succeeded; this is not lost child-result delivery. No new protected command replay was attempted for this report.

## Source inspected / limits

The installed CLI entrypoint points to a managed installation whose current HEAD is ae2a81ccc00e9b7c06301523e5bb09608397149c (v0.23.2 lineage). Local profiles/instructions are customised. This is captured incident evidence and a source audit, **not a fresh clean-main synthetic reproduction**, nor proof that every live process had reloaded the current on-disk checkout.

Relevant source at that installation:
- gateway/run_turn_runner.py unregisters the session notifier in the turn's finally.
- tools/approval.py::unregister_gateway_notify wakes/removes queued entries when no dispatch-owned callback can keep them answerable.
- gateway/run_turn_runner_approval_transport.py deliberately publishes no background_notify for local-viewer/non-messaging surfaces.
- tools/approval_notify_lease.py falls back to the currently registered foreground callback when no background transport exists.

These paths are consistent with the observed lifetime failure; exact callback/lease state was not instrumented during the original incident.

## Expected

A supported background child must not lose a prompt already shown merely because an unrelated parent notification/reconciliation turn ends. Preserve exact request ownership and provide an actionable lifetime-safe approval surface, or reject unsupported detached approval-dependent work before promising continuation. Preserve real Stop/deny/timeout/session teardown; never auto-approve or weaken guards.

## Related, but different

- Closed#112026 included teardown of already-present child approvals and incorrect denial attribution. The current result text attributes withdrawal correctly, but the action still loses its answer window.
- Closed#133514 / open#144440 address missing/notifier-after-parent scenarios, primarily messaging/post-turn requests. Here local/Desktop delivery succeeds before ordinary parent completion cancels an existing wait.
- Open#153633 concerns an attached viewer not seeing a messaging child's prompt; #157332 concerns Relay pending-control projection. Neither establishes this local/Desktop already-visible prompt lifetime.

Public logs are sanitised: no command contents, project/person names, private paths, credentials or session/request IDs. AI assistance was used for this audit/report.

issues.title: [Bug]: Parent agent silently stops an incomplete task after a local subtask blocker

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/delegate
labels.description: Subagent delegation

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Problem
An agent can correctly recognize that one subtask is blocked, report that the overall job remains incomplete, and then end the turn without continuing other executable work or explicitly transitioning the overall task to blocked/stopped. The user has to ask why work stopped. A background child exiting normally is not evidence the parent goal finished.

This is separate from stale cron continuity (#147625). That PR only labels historical context and does not provide task-level continuation or liveness guarantees.

## Observed workflow
1. User requests a multi-step deliverable with verification and explicitly asks the agent to continue autonomously.
2. One validation subtask repeatedly returns inconclusive results.
3. Agent stops ineffective retries (appropriate), but also stops all work, despite independent remaining tasks.
4. Agent reports incomplete status or completion of an unrelated fix, then ends without an active executor or a clear overall stopped/blocked transition.
5. Work resumes only after another user prompt.

This is an observed behavioral failure, not yet a code-level root-cause reproduction. No claim that one particular scheduler method causes it.

## Expected behavior
- Distinguish completed, partially completed, blocked, stopped and actively executing states.
- On a local blocker, continue independent authorized work where safe; otherwise explicitly report that execution has stopped and what is required to resume.
- Never equate tool activity, process existence, silent child completion or exit code 0 with deliverable progress.
- Preserve an actionable parent checkpoint when a child returns incomplete.
- Support opt-in periodic progress/stall notices with explicit delivery policy; honor quiet/local-only workflows by default.
- Do not create an unbounded autonomous retry loop or keep spending merely to appear active.

## Suggested acceptance tests
- Child returns normal exit + incomplete checkpoint: parent does not mark task complete.
- One subtask blocked, another authorized and runnable: next action continues the runnable task or records a concrete reason not to.
- No executor remains while the task is incomplete: observable task status is not running.
- Repeated unchanged checkpoints: bounded escalation/strategy change, not infinite identical redispatch.
- Opt-in periodic update reports no progress explicitly; local-only workflows remain local.
- Cancellation and revoked authority stop work immediately; release/permission gates are not bypassed.

## Related work
Potentially related: #26410 (durable stall detection), #136930 (background work interruption), #102694 (guardrail termination reported completed). Please link/deduplicate if these cover the same lifecycle. #147625 addresses only stale continuity disclosure, not this broader parent-task lifecycle gap.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop (macOS) half-quits permanently — teardown completes, process never exits, singleton lock held, every IPC rejects 'Hermes Desktop is quitting.'

labels.name: comp/desktop

issues.body:
## Bug Description

On macOS (Apple Silicon), Hermes Desktop can enter a permanent half-quit state: the main process runs `before-quit` teardown to completion, latches its backend lifecycle into the aborted state, and then **never exits**. The process stays alive holding `SingletonLock` in `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/`, with zero windows, and every IPC handler rejects with `Error: Hermes Desktop is quitting.`

From the user's side this is unrecoverable without `kill`:

- The window shows `Hermes couldn't start: Error: Error invoking remote method 'hermes:connection': Error: Hermes Desktop is quitting.`
- Clicking retry / reset / repair does nothing. The renderer's `[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer; clearing latched failure` runs, but the in-memory abort latch is not something a reinstall can clear, so `repair attempt 3/3, primaryBackendAlive=false` loops and gives up.
- Relaunching the app does nothing, because the singleton is held by the zombie. A fresh `open` routes into the dead instance and exits silently.

The gateway is **not** involved. It stays healthy and connected the whole time; this is purely the Desktop's own quit path.

## Steps to Reproduce

I cannot yet trigger this deterministically, but it has occurred on 6 separate days on this install (2026-10-20, 11-01, 11-18, 11-19, 11-20, 11-22), always around an externally-driven `hermes gateway restart`, so the race is reachable with modest frequency:

1. On macOS, with Desktop running attached to the local gateway (`hermes gateway ensure`, the normal path).
2. Trigger a gateway restart out-of-band — `hermes gateway restart`, or `SIGUSR1` from the launchd supervisor. The gateway drains and relaunches correctly in ~14s.
3. Desktop's backend re-ensure runs against the draining/restarted gateway. In the captured incident the Desktop logged `[boot] Using Hermes at ...` at `11:45:39` and then produced no further boot output.
4. ~55s later, a `before-quit` runs (in this incident concurrent with a `Hermes-Setup` launcher fast-path `/usr/bin/open` on the bundle). Teardown completes; Electron never emits `quit`.
5. From that moment every renderer IPC fails with `Hermes Desktop is quitting.` indefinitely.

## Expected Behavior

A quit that finishes its teardown must actually terminate the process. If Electron's quit finalization stalls — the documented reason `createQuitFinalization` exists — the same bounded escape hatch should apply on macOS, releasing `SingletonLock` so the next launch works.

## Actual Behavior

`desktop.log` for the captured incident (`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`, WIB):

```
11:45:32,772  gateway.run: SIGUSR1 received ... performing a graceful gateway restart
11:45:34,451  Shutdown phase: drain done at +1.63s (drain took 0.00s, timed_out=False)
11:45:37,888  Gateway stopped (total teardown 5.06s)      <- gateway side clean
11:45:46,678  Gateway control socket listening            <- gateway back
11:46:08,665  [Telegram] Connected to Telegram (polling mode)

11:45:39,675  [hermes] [boot] Using Hermes at /Users/.../hermes-agent
11:46:34,648  [hermes] Error: Hermes Desktop is quitting.   <- latch set, process begins quit
11:46:34,648      at Object.run [as shutdown] (electron-main.mjs:5636:40)
11:46:35,133  [renderer error:main] Hermes couldn't start: Error invoking remote method
              'hermes:connection': Error: Hermes Desktop is quitting.
...
11:46:39,188  [bootstrap] reset requested by renderer; clearing latched failure   <- recovery attempt
11:46:41,321  [bootstrap] repair requested ... (attempt=1/3, primaryBackendAlive=false)
11:46:42,988  [bootstrap] repair requested ... (attempt=2/3, primaryBackendAlive=false)
11:47:24,004  [bootstrap] repair requested ... (attempt=3/3, primaryBackendAlive=false)
```

The process then kept serving the same rejected IPC every few seconds for **17 minutes** until I killed it. Observed state at that point:

```
$ osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "Hermes" to get count of windows'
0
$ ps -p <pid> -o etime            # alive, 53 minutes, 0.3% CPU
53:31
$ ls -la ~/Library/Application\ Support/Hermes/ | grep Singleton
SingletonLock -> NB-DK-0686.local-21478     # held by the zombie
```

`will-quit` never fired (`grep -c "will-quit\|\[quit\]" desktop.log` → 0), so the escape hatch below was never even armed.

## Root Cause Analysis

Two pieces combine.

**1. The latch is one-shot and permanent** — `apps/desktop/electron/local-backend-lifecycle.ts:77-82`:

```ts
const shutdown = createBackendShutdownCoordinator((): Promise<void> => {
  controller.abort(markExpectedTransition(new Error('Hermes Desktop is quitting.')))
  deps.cancelSetup()

  return waitForTeardown([...starts, ...[...children].map(stop), ...stops.values()], deps.timeoutMs ?? 7_000)
})
```

`createBackendShutdownCoordinator` (`backend-ownership.ts:321-355`) stores `completion` on first `run()` and never clears it, while the `AbortController` is aborted permanently. Correct for a real quit; the problem is the quit doesn't finish.

**2. The only escape hatch is Windows-only** — `apps/desktop/electron/quit-finalization.ts:41`:

```ts
if (!isWindows || finished || timer !== null) {
  return
}
```

That early return means `quitFinalization.arm()` (called from `will-quit`, `main.ts:16238-16245`) is a no-op on macOS and Linux. Its own doc comment describes exactly the failure I hit:

> Provides a bounded escape hatch for a Windows Electron process that has entered its final quit phase but never emits the completed quit event.

The mechanism is platform-agnostic; only the gate is not. Introduced in `a598d5273e` ("fix(desktop): bound Windows Electron quit finalization", 2026-09-19), which scoped it to Windows without recording a reason the bound can't apply elsewhere.

Note that in this incident `will-quit` never fired at all — so simply flipping `isWindows` would not have helped here. It needs to be armed from `before-quit` (after teardown is admitted), not only from `will-quit`.

## Proposed Fix

Two independent, small changes:

1. **Arm the deadline from `before-quit`, not just `will-quit`.** `quitFinalization.begin()` at the point `quitTeardown.begin(teardownTasks)` returns `true` (main.ts ~17774, where the quit is deferred), so the bound covers a teardown that settles but whose final `app.quit()` never produces `quit`.
2. **Drop the `isWindows` gate** (or widen it to `isWindows || IS_MAC`), with the timeout kept generous — the existing `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` is already past the 7s backend teardown budget.

Both are covered by `quit-finalization.test.ts`, which already tests the arm/cancel/no-rearm semantics; the platform gate is a constructor argument, so a darwin case is a few lines.

## Additional Logs / Traceback

The gateway logs confirm the restart itself is unrelated and healthy — included above. `hermes debug share`: https://paste.rs/zlYDr

Recovery that works reliably, for anyone hitting this meanwhile:

```bash
pkill -f 'Hermes.app/Contents/MacOS/Hermes'; sleep 2; open -a <path>/Hermes.app
```

A bare relaunch is not enough, because the single-instance lock routes the new launch into the wedged instance.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.3+293.g030036a (2026.9.24), canary, git install
- macOS 26.3 (Apple Silicon, M5)
- Electron desktop `mac-arm64` release bundle
- Gateway: launchd user agent `ai.hermes.gateway`, `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`, `ExitTimeOut=60`

issues.title: kanban block-recurrence breaker cannot distinguish a human unblock from an automated one — supervised tasks get one question before routing to triage

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

issues.body:
## Summary

The block-recurrence breaker treats a **human** unblock the same as an automated one, so a supervised task that legitimately blocks twice for the same *kind* — with a person answering in between — gets routed to `triage` as though an unblocker were spinning it.

The breaker's stated purpose is to stop a loop: *"Loop detected — stop letting the unblocker spin this task"* (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:5581`). That is the right goal for a cron or a retry loop. But a human answering a question and returning the task to the pool is not a loop, and the counter cannot currently tell the two apart.

## The mechanism

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:5577-5578` (line numbers against `main` @ `c3ffe2738`):

```python
same_cause = prev_kind == kind
recurrences = prev_recurrences + 1 if same_cause else 1

if recurrences >= BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT:      # == 2
```

`unblock_task` returns the task to the work pool but leaves `block_recurrences` and `block_kind` intact — they are reset only on successful completion (`:950`, `:5800`). So with `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT = 2` (`:134`):

| Step | `block_recurrences` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Worker blocks `needs_input` ("which timezone?") | 0 → **1** | blocked, correct |
| Human answers, unblocks | **1** (retained) | back in pool |
| Worker blocks `needs_input` again — *different question* ("which currency?") | 1 → **2** | **routed to `triage`** |

The second block is a legitimate new question from a supervised worker. It is indistinguishable, to the counter, from a cron re-blocking the same task for the same unresolved cause.

Net effect: a supervised lane gets exactly **one** question per task before the breaker fires. Any task needing two rounds of human input lands in `triage` and stops moving.

## Why this shows up in practice

On a fleet where workers block `needs_input` to ask the operator questions, multi-question tasks are ordinary rather than exceptional. We hit it repeatedly and worked around it in two places before fixing the cause — a watchdog archive-with-evidence fallback, and a convention that supervisors comment instead of unblocking. Both are the kind of workaround that exists only because the counter is over-eager.

Note the breaker still can't be simply loosened: raising `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` weakens the automated-loop protection it exists for. The counter needs to distinguish *who* unblocked, not count higher.

## Proposed fix

Add an opt-in `reset_recurrence` parameter to `unblock_task`, defaulting to `False` so nothing changes for existing callers:

```python
def unblock_task(conn, task_id, *, reset_recurrence: bool = False, ...):
    # when True: block_recurrences = 0, block_kind = NULL
```

Then pass `True` from **human-driven** unblock paths only:

- the interactive CLI `kanban unblock`
- the dashboard's status-to-ready transitions
- any decision-apply path where a person answered

and leave it `False` — the default — for every automated unblocker (sweeper crons, retry logic, watchdogs). An automated unblock still accumulates recurrences and still trips the breaker, which is exactly the behavior worth keeping.

The asymmetry is the whole point: the breaker should count *unattended* retries, and a human in the loop is evidence that the cause was actually addressed.

## Regression sequences worth pinning

Three cases, all of which a fix should cover:

1. **Supervised, must NOT trip.** Worker blocks `needs_input` → human/CLI unblock → one legitimate same-kind re-block → stays `blocked`, does not route to `triage`.
2. **Unattended loop, MUST still trip.** Two same-kind re-blocks with no human unblock in between → routes to `triage`. (Guards against the fix simply disabling the breaker.)
3. **Automated unblocker must NOT reset.** A sweeper-cron unblock followed by a same-kind re-block still increments and still trips — i.e. automated unblockers keep `reset_recurrence=False`.

Case 3 is the one most likely to be missed, and it is what keeps the fix from becoming a blanket bypass: if a cron can reset the counter, the breaker is gone.

## Environment

Reproduced on current `main`. We have been running this fix as a local patch since 2026-07-16 on a 10-lane fleet, with a functional scratch-DB test covering cases 1 and 2 (control escalates 2/2; human-reset does not). Case 3 is untested locally and would ride the PR.

Happy to send a PR with all three sequences as durable tests if this framing looks right to you.

issues.body:
Tracking issue for the staged fast-follow named in [#134889](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889)'s scope note: *"the browser dashboard and Desktop URL / Cloud / SSH modes still talk to standalone `hermes serve`."* [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (merged Oct 14, `eb75627f`) gave every **local** surface one gateway-owned session authority per profile. This issue tracks moving the remaining entry points onto that same authority and then removing the old in-process session host.

Design: [One Gateway: Entry-Point and Session Ownership Plan](https://gist.github.com/unsupportedpastels/765f9d551ce88ee01630c18367763e75). Profile-multiplexing direction: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) (one `hermes gateway run` serves every profile).

It traced EP-8 to EP-11, split EP-11, and added EP-13 to EP-17 and D6. **Update (Nov 6):** merged the handler ledger (EP-1, #148795), the acceptance harness (EP-2, #148774), the EP-15 fix (#148769), the EP-11a removal (#148775) and the V1/V2 tests (#148777, #148798). EP-13 (#148770) and EP-14 (#148794) are held for the cutover so `main`'s behavior doesn't change before it.

**Scope:** `hermes serve`, standalone `hermes dashboard`, Desktop remote modes (SSH / URL / Cloud), remaining direct agent constructors, and removal of the legacy host. **Out of scope:** the forced-migration campaign (soak, rollback window, `--force`); migrating background services is in scope as EP-18, storage redesign, protocol unification, a replacement browser UI and a mobile client.

## Done on `main` (not tracked here)

- Local Desktop runs `gateway ensure` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`); `5e783bde` removed code that only Desktop's own `serve` reached.
- `session.detach` is wired in `gateway/session_controls.py`.
- `SessionAuthorities` supports `add`/`remove` at runtime (`gateway/session_authorities.py`, `gateway/run_runtime.py`); see V1.
- [#141864](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141864) serves the Desktop webapp (`apps/desktop/dist-webapp`, not `web/`) from the gateway's own listener.

## Contract under test

- Every supported entry point reaches the canonical profile authority; none starts its own session runtime.
- Closing a client removes a viewer. It never stops accepted work.
- Authorized clients can join and leave the same conversation and see the same queue, execution state and pending controls.
- Profile selection resolves an authority inside the multiplexer; `serve -p X` never launches an independent gateway for X.
- Documented callback URLs, profile-scoped auth, `--force` and standalone migration support are unchanged.
- No legacy execution fallback remains at completion.

## Legend

🔴 open, no fix · 🟡 fix PR open · 🟣 fix in review (member PR) · 🔵 waiting on a maintainer decision · ⚪ not reproduced · 🟢 fixed on `main`

## Open findings

### Stage 1: caller map and parity harness (start here)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-1 | Caller map for `serve`. **Done at `edfa1c2a`.** One FastAPI app runs in two modes, chosen only by `app.state.gateway_runner` (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`). Only the gateway's own mount sets it (`gateway/run_api.py:96-97`), so every `hermes serve`, `hermes dashboard` and `serve --isolated` runs `standalone_lifespan` with no authority. `serve` never discovers or forwards to a running gateway, except single-session edits over `session.mutate` (`hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py:188-234`). Results feed D1 to D6 below. **Handler ledger merged in #148795 (`eccfff7b`):** `tests/hermes_cli/serve_handler_ledger.json` lists every serve HTTP route, RPC and WebSocket handler with its owner decision (625 rows, 520 undecided pending D1–D6); `scripts/gen_serve_handler_ledger.py --check` keeps it in sync with `main`. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-2 | Parity rigs on the combined tree. **Headless baseline recorded on `edfa1c2a`** (scratch home, one pytest process per file): 31 files, 289 tests passed, about 8 min. Covers entrypoint parity and boot contract (`tests/e2e/core/parity/`), two-tenant gateway and Desktop backend (`tests/e2e/core/tenancy/`), live hot-serve (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py`, 7), gateway turn liveness (`tests/e2e/core/chaos/test_gateway_turn_liveness.py`, 12), and the profile-isolation, handoff, recovery and admission/replay unit tests. `tests/e2e/core/tenancy/test_routing_truth_table.py` could not run on this host (its guard refuses temp dirs under `~/.hermes`); use the CI `e2e` job result. **Missing:** `verify_parity2.sh` is not in the tree, git history or any linked issue; the #134889 "Verified working" live checks were manual and have no scripts. **Not run here:** Desktop `apps/desktop/e2e/core` (`remote-topology`, `remote-secondary`, `local-gateway-attach`) needs a GUI; CI lane `e2e-desktop-core` runs it. Next: rerun the same file set on every combined-tree candidate; rebuild network drop mid-turn, cron→compress→input and SSE approvals as scripted e2e tests. **Acceptance harness merged in #148774 (`418de33e`):** `tests/e2e/core/serve_ownership/` runs a real `serve` and gateway with one control cell and three `known_failure` cells for the open ownership gaps; `HERMES_E2E_STRICT_ACCEPTANCE=serve-cutover` turns them into hard failures for the cutover. **Scripted rigs merged (Nov 7):** network drop mid-turn (#149888), cron→compress→input (#149889) and SSE approvals (#149896), all green on `main`. | P1 | 🔴 |

### Stages 2–3: `serve` uses the authority

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-3 | With no `gateway_runner`, `serve` selects `standalone_lifespan` and runs agents in-process (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`; comment at `hermes_cli/main.py:2598`). | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D1, D2) |
| EP-4 | `/api/ws` sends every RPC to the legacy `server.dispatch` when no authority is present (`tui_gateway/ws.py:362-390`). With an authority, non-session verbs that the authority answers with -32601 still fall back to legacy handlers in-process (`tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py:53-64`): 100 methods go to the authority, 163 fall back, 16 are blocked. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-5 | New work can enter `serve` without going through the authority's admission: [#138750](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/138750). The issue's line numbers have drifted; on `edfa1c2a` the console executor is `hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:278`, PTY spawn `:552`, action subprocesses `hermes_cli/web_server_gateway.py:475`. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-6 | Version skew: a new remote client's `prompt.submit` attachments are refused by an older `serve`: [#144186](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/144186). Traced: the retry strips only `submission_id`, then the legacy param model refuses `attachments` with `4000`. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on D5) |
| EP-13 | Session-bound legacy fallback methods on authority sessions. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`:** the authority answers -32601 for all 13, the fallback runs the legacy handler, and the handler can't find the session (authority sessions are never in `server._sessions`). 10 fail with `4001 session not found`; `tools.list` and `toolsets.list` silently ignore the session and return launch-profile data; `insights.get` isn't session-bound (it rejects `session_id` with 4000). Clients gate or translate 11 of the 13 before they reach the wire. Two still reach the server and fail silently: Desktop `image.detach` on chip removal (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/hooks/use-composer-actions.ts:922`, harmless) and ui-tui `input.detect_drop` for a dropped non-image path (`ui-tui/src/app/useComposerState.ts:339-379`), which pastes raw text instead of an attachment. `handoff.*` and `tools.configure` are refused by name client-side (feature gap). Defensive server fix: keep -32601 for these verbs in `tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py`, as already done for `session.`/`prompt.`. | P3 | 🔴 |
| EP-14 | `POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/trigger` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:762`) runs the job's agent inside the request thread (`cron/scheduler.py:3373`) outside admission, in both modes; the code marks the path deprecated. `POST /api/cron/fire` already forwards to the gateway. | P2 | 🔴 |
| EP-15 | `POST /api/health/retirement` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:160`) is live on the gateway listener and declares a busy gateway idle. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`** (real dashboard app bound the way `gateway/run_api.py:75-108` binds it, a claimed admission and one running agent; runner and authority are stand-ins): `GET /api/health/idle` returns `idle: true`, `prepare` returns 200 with a token, `commit` returns 200. Afterwards dashboard JSON-RPC answers 5035 "backend is retiring", cron `tick()` dispatches nothing and the fence admits no new work until restart, while the gateway keeps running. Cause: the idle proof (`hermes_cli/web_server_idle_proof.py:39-58`, `hermes_cli/web_server_idle_exit.py:104-136`) reads only the legacy session table, delegation, cron and the fence; it never consults the gateway runner or authority, and nothing under `gateway/` takes the fence. Latent: no in-repo client calls the route, and it needs an owner or local token. Fix direction: refuse when `app.state.gateway_runner` is set, or base idleness on `gateway/run_idle_exit.py:busy_reason` and fail closed. **Fixed by #148769 (`f190892f`):** with a gateway runner mounted, the idle route reports not idle and `prepare`/`commit`/`cancel` are refused; standalone `serve` keeps its idle retirement. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-17 | Bulk session REST (bulk delete, delete-empty, prune) writes `state.db` directly under a store-wide lock and returns 409 while a gateway owns the store, with no owner path. | P3 | 🔴 |

### Stage 4: remote Desktop and browser

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-7 | SSH mode starts `serve --isolated` and kills it on disconnect, so closing the client stops accepted work (`apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts:1142-1161`, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:9486`). Every disconnect path (quit, connection switch or edit, profile delete, recycle) kills the remote process with no check for a running turn. | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D4) |
| EP-8 | Desktop URL and Cloud modes reach whatever process the URL names; neither calls `gateway ensure`. The Docker image's dashboard service runs standalone `hermes dashboard` on 9119 (`docker/s6-rc.d/dashboard/run:52-54`). Desktop reads no `gateway_mode` or host role, so it can't tell which backend it reached. Hosted Cloud agents are inferred to match; Cloud infra isn't in this repo. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-9 | Standalone `hermes dashboard` chat (the sidebar's `/api/ws`, and the chat terminal when no profile is named) and its session REST use the legacy dispatcher, not the authority. A named profile attaches to the profile's gateway. *Reworded:* `ChatPage` can't reach `serve`, which is headless and doesn't serve `web/` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:126-149`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-16 | SSH, URL and Cloud remotes send raw method names: the 13 rewrites to `session.mutate` with revision/generation checks in `canonical-protocol.ts` apply only to `native_dial` sockets. `handoff.*` is refused locally but still sent to remotes. **Fixed by #148219 (`7bc10408da`):** Desktop now selects the canonical adapter from `session_authority: true` in `gateway.ready`, so the rewrites and the `handoff.*` refusal apply to any remote that advertises it. SSH still reaches `serve --isolated`, which serves the legacy names (EP-7). | P2 | 🟢 |

### Stage 5: remaining producers

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-10 | The slash worker runs a second `HermesCLI` per session: [#141196](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141196). Standalone backends only (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1070-1086`); the gateway serves `slash.exec` itself (`gateway/session_controls.py:390`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-11a | `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` `_run_agent` builds a bare `AIAgent`, but it's dead code: its only caller `_run_and_exit_oneshot` is called only from tests, and `-z` goes through `launch_gateway_chat` (`hermes_cli/main.py:3020-3026`). Removal candidate. **Removed by #148775 (`a2db0efb`).** `_exit_after_oneshot` stays (it writes `--cpu-profile` output) and `hermes_cli.oneshot.get_fallback_chain` stays importable. | P3 | 🟢 |
| EP-11b | `prompt.background` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1184`) writes a separate `bg_*` session row and skips the gateway's queue check; `preview.restart` (`:1249`) builds `AIAgent` with no session store. Standalone backends only; gateway connections refuse `prompt.*` fallback. | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |

### Stage 6: remove the legacy host (after parity)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-18 | Users who run `hermes serve` / `hermes dashboard` as an automatic background service need a migration path before removal. Hermes never installs one itself; the shapes are systemd units copied from the docs (`web-dashboard.md:186-197`, `desktop.md:668`) and hand-written launchd plists, Nix `hermes-backend` (NixOS unit, Home Manager user unit and launchd agent; `Restart=always`, `KeepAlive=true`), the Docker image's s6 `dashboard` longrun and the Compose `dashboard` sidecar, Desktop SSH `serve --isolated`, and operator-made Windows autostarts. `hermes update` restarts these but never migrates them, and its unit-name gate misses `hermes-backend`. Hazard: the attach path exits 0 when another backend owns the host, which respawn-loops under those restart policies, so a deprecated entry point must stay in the foreground. Main blocker is listener parity (the gateway serves the webapp on 9120, not the `web/` SPA on 9119, and lacks the Nix session-token file and the `dashboard.public_url` mapping). Proposed: a `serve.host_mode` switch, sentinel mode, `hermes gateway migrate --backends` with dry-run/rollback, and a report-only update hook until the cutover (Linear HACORE-159). **Merged (Nov 21):** #157376, #157387, #157393, #157403, #157430, #157453 and #157484. Opt-in only; follow-ups are listed in each PR's description. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-12 | The legacy session host still exists: `tui_gateway/server.py` (2,187 lines), `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`, `ws_legacy_fallback`. Remove only after EP-3 to EP-18 are green and EP-2 passes. Modules named `tui_gateway` that don't host sessions stay. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on stages 2–5) |

### Verification (believed done; needs evidence)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | Hot-added and removed profiles create and retire authorities. #134889 lists the served profile set as a start-time snapshot, but `main` now has `SessionAuthorities.add`/`remove`, driven by the `serve-profile`, `unserve-profile` and `rescan-profiles` control-socket verbs (`gateway/run_runtime.py:380`, `:459`). **Partly verified on `edfa1c2a`:** `test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py` (7 passed) drives `rescan-profiles` against a real multiplexer, and unserve is covered at the function level (`test_run_runtime_hot_serve_cleanup.py`). No test sends `serve-profile` or `unserve-profile` by name; add one to the live test, then update #134889's "Deliberate limits". **Verified by #148777 (`02849dba`):** the live test now sends `serve-profile` and `unserve-profile` by name and checks the authority is added and retired (including during a running turn). | P2 | 🟢 |
| V2 | [#109403](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109403), [#109405](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109405) and [#109412](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109412) closed unmerged. Check whether `main` covers each one's piece ([#109404](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109404)'s is covered by `session.detach`). **Checked:** all three pieces are on `main`; #148798 (`e8a469a1`) adds the Desktop tests that were missing. | P3 | 🟢 |

## Decisions to settle

| ID | Decision | EP-1 input | Gates | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Which existing startup/discovery path does `serve` reuse, and when does it start the owner versus forward to it? | `gateway_runner` is in-process only, so forwarding means a proxy, and that needs identity forwarding (D2). The evidence favors remote clients attaching to the gateway listener directly (it mounts the same app and auth), with `serve` as a launcher that uses control-socket discovery (`identify`, `session-ticket`). Blockers: `/api/ws` accepts loopback only; no remote ticket path. | EP-3, EP-4, EP-7, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D2 | Can owner-side authentication preserve current deployments without delegated identity forwarding? | Yes if the gateway authenticates clients itself; it already runs the same auth stack. No if `serve` forwards: tickets, the session token and cookies are process- or origin-bound, so a forwarder collapses every user into one identity. Missing on the gateway: the SSH `--isolated` token and owner nonce, the Desktop env token, the rendezvous-record token, and carrying `dashboard.public_url` to `webapp.public_url`. | EP-3, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D3 | Which legacy capabilities need mappings before their callers can move? | Of 254 legacy methods: 75 mapped, 14 partial, 163 legacy fallback, 2 refused (`agents.list`, `session.activate`). Gaps: EP-13 (reproduced: 2 client-reachable, both silent); no authority verb tears a session down like `session.close`; host-wide services (pet, projects, MCP, vault, voice, billing, connectors, group replica/peer) run in the owner process outside admission. | stages 2–5 | 🔵 |
| D4 | Which web/SSH changes are inseparable from keeping those entry points supported? | SSH options: (a) run remote `gateway ensure --json` and tunnel to the gateway, with a capability probe and fallback to isolated `serve`; (b) interim: keep isolated `serve` but stop killing it on quit or window close, relying on its 900 s idle retirement and existing reattach. | EP-7, EP-9 | 🔵 |
| D5 | What explicit migration behavior covers version skew and unsupported legacy operations? | No version handshake exists; Desktop infers canonical vs legacy from `?native_dial`. `gateway.capabilities` exists in the contract but no client uses it. Hosted-room peers' `protocol_versions` plus per-capability flags is a working model. | EP-6 | 🔵 |
| D6 | Is authority-less `serve`/`dashboard` still a supported host? If not, fence that backend instead of fixing each producer. | — | EP-9, EP-10, EP-11b, EP-17 | 🔵 |

Open question: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) closed Sep 21 with no successor found for its forced-migration gates. This tracker doesn't own those gates; it needs to know whether they're met before EP-12.

## Not tracked here

These are separate operational work, not prerequisites for removing the alternate owner: extracting an execution-host interface from the messaging runner, independent adapter supervision, moving storage off the event loop, durable event retention and idle-session eviction.

## Working rules

- Work is grouped into package issues by stage; each package lists its rows, prerequisites, consumers and acceptance evidence.
- Reproduce on current `main` before fixing; no repro means no commit, plus a ⚪ note here.
- PRs use `Refs #<this issue> (EP-n)`, never `Fixes`.
- If an entry point already meets the contract on `main`, mark it 🟢 and leave the code alone.
- Stop and add a 🔵 row when a slice needs a new framework or an unplanned auth/lifecycle policy.

## Found a problem? Report here

Comment on this issue with: `main` SHA, Desktop version if involved, surface and mode (serve / dashboard / SSH / URL / Cloud / browser), OS and topology, steps, expected, actual, and the relevant lines from `gateway.log`, `errors.log` and `desktop.log`. Redact tokens, cookies, tickets and session URLs.

issues.title: [Bug]: pnpm's version probe runs in the caller's directory, so the launch-time sync fails inside a project that pins npm

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`Pnpm` inherits `probe_cwd = False` from `BinaryPackage`, so `verify()` runs `pnpm --version` in whatever directory Hermes was started from (`pm/packages.py`, line 109 on main). pnpm 12 reads the nearest `package.json`, and if that file's `packageManager` field names npm, it refuses with `ERR_PNPM_OTHER_PM_EXPECTED` and exits 1. Verification then fails and pnpm can't be installed.

Users hit this through the launch-time dependency sync in `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py` (`ensure_tools_for_sync()`, line 674), which runs when `hermes` starts after an interrupted update or with a borrowed data root. If the shell is inside any project that pins npm, startup fails. `hermes update` is unaffected because `update_completion.py` runs its child with `cwd=root`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/proj
echo '{"name":"p","packageManager":"npm@10.9.2"}' > /tmp/repro/proj/package.json
cd /tmp/repro/proj
HERMES_HOME=/tmp/repro/home hermes pm install pnpm
```

From `/tmp/repro`, which has no `package.json`, the same command succeeds.

### Expected Behavior

pnpm installs and verifies no matter which directory `hermes` was started from.

### Actual Behavior

```
✗ pnpm: staged entry failed verification: .../tools/.staging-XXXX/tree/pnpm --version exited 1: Error: ERR_PNPM_OTHER_PM_EXPECTED

  × This project is configured to use npm
  help: Run a one-off command with "pnpm dlx npm <command>", or link a npm
        command that follows this project's pin with "pnpm shim add npm". — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Debug Report

Not attached. The steps above need no local state.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL2)

### Hermes Version

Reproduced on ae2a81ccc0. The code is unchanged on main at 95b7386558.

### Proposed Fix

Set `probe_cwd = True` on `Pnpm`, so the probe runs in the binary's own directory, where no project `package.json` applies. Running the probe from any other neutral directory would also work.

prs.title: fix(update): name autostashes parked by earlier runs before stashing again
prs.body:
## What happened

An update stashed 25 tracked files, pulled 76 commits, and the restore hit a conflict on one file
(`use-composer-submit.ts`: upstream added `editorHasFocus`/`refocusAfterSend` where the local change
added `submitAsNextTurn`). `_apply_stash_step` reset the tree to keep it runnable and parked the
stash, which is the right call. It printed the notice and exited non-zero.

An hour later the user ran `hermes update` again. That run stashed the three untracked test files it
found, restored them cleanly, and printed:

    Local changes were restored on top of the updated codebase.

Nothing mentioned that the 25 tracked files were still in `stash@{0}`. The second line reads as "my
changes are back", and the leftover was only going to be named once it was seven days old.

## What this changes

`_warn_orphaned_update_autostashes` takes `max_age_days`, and `_cmd_update_impl` calls it with `0`
right before it stashes, so every leftover `hermes-update-autostash-*` entry is named with its ref,
whatever its age. The restore line now says which stash it restored.

The seven-day wording stays for the default call, so the `--keep-stash` desktop flow sees no new
output beyond the entries it already has. Still not a GC: a stash can be the only copy of the user's
work.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_autostash_orphan_warning.py` gains
`test_a_fresh_park_is_named_when_the_age_filter_is_off`: a one-hour-old park is named with
`max_age_days=0`, and the same repo stays quiet under the default threshold.

    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_autostash_orphan_warning.py  -> 6 passed
    scripts/check --only ruff,health  -> ok

## Not in this PR

The conflict itself. Auto-merging is not something the updater should attempt: both sides were
additions at the same anchor, and guessing there is how a tree ends up neither updated nor local.
Naming the park is what makes the next step the user's call.

prs.title: Hermes schedules help on its own (trips, habits, owed replies), and each job asks on its own "Schedule this job?" card
prs.body:
Hermes can now notice a moment you'll need help with later (a flight, an appointment, a deadline, a habit) and set up a scheduled job for it without being asked. Every job the model creates or changes first shows you a card ("Schedule this job?" / "Change this job?") with what will run, when, and who sees the result, and nothing is saved unless you allow it.

This is step 1 of the proactivity work; the roadmap and research on other proactive assistants are in #158538. The Desktop/Web Inbox for job results is a separate PR (#158555).

## What changes for you

| You say | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| "dentist thursday at 3pm, I always forget" | an answer, nothing scheduled | a card for a reminder before the appointment |
| "flying SFO to Tokyo on NH7 next friday 11:25am, nervous about the airport" | travel tips | a card for a check-in reminder at T-24h (plus arrival help on some models) |
| "landing in Lisbon tuesday 6am, check-in isn't until 3pm" | tips | a card for an arrival reminder with transit and bag-storage help |
| "I keep forgetting to answer people on slack" | tips | a card for a weekday "clear your unanswered Slack" nudge, a few runs, never sends anything |
| "my dentist appointment yesterday went fine" | — | nothing scheduled |
| "please don't set reminders for me" | — | nothing scheduled |
| the model edits a job you approved earlier | applied silently | a "Change this job?" card listing each change old → new; deny leaves the job untouched |

Where no card can be shown (cron runs, `-q` one-shots, kanban workers, API server / webhooks, `approvals.mode: off`, yolo, or after "Always allow new jobs"), the model is not told to create jobs unasked and jobs save exactly as on main.

## What changed

- **Proactive guidance, only where a card will show.** One rule (`tools.approval.schedule_card_skip_reason`) decides both whether a card is shown and whether the system prompt carries the one-line "create the job, then say what you scheduled" guidance. The `cronjob_manage` description itself is neutral: what jobs are good for (appointments, trips, deadlines and owed items, habits with a run limit, re-checks with `monitor` / `[SILENT]`), cadence advice, and "a job never sends, buys or submits on the user's behalf".
- **Schedule cards on every surface.** Classic CLI, Ink TUI, Desktop, and the messaging adapters (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Teams, Matrix, Feishu, …) draw a schedule card instead of the "dangerous command" card, and keep it a schedule card after a reconnect, behind another queued card, after a click, and in the plain-text fallback.
- **The card shows the job that will be saved.** It is built from the finished, validated record: the saved name, when it actually fires (first run in your clock; a one-shot's real instant), run count, "created paused", the monitor script or URL that runs first, and **who sees the result** (this chat, a named home channel, an explicit target, or nowhere), plus where failure notices go when different. The job text is fenced on messaging cards so model-written markup can't change how it reads.
- **Edits ask too.** A model-initiated update that changes when it runs, what runs or who sees it shows "Change this job?" (Allow / Deny only; an "Always allow new jobs" grant never covers edits). Pause / resume / run / remove stay unasked. A run that completes while the card is open keeps its count.
- **Honest outcomes.** Invalid jobs fail before any card. A card answered after the first run it showed has passed saves nothing (instead of a different time or an error after consent). A decline is an answer, not a tool failure, so the loop guardrail doesn't push the model to keep trying.
- **Approval kinds** (`schedule`, `schedule_edit`, plus `access` / `network` cherry-picked from @emozilla's #156726) travel through the approval contract, managed workers, replay and every adapter.

## Live results (real CLI in tmux, real models on Nous Portal, head of this PR)

16 conversations per model, each from a fresh profile, every card approved; counts are jobs created.

| | Sonnet 5.5 | Gemini 3.8 Flash | GPT-5.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 helpful cases (dentist, flight, water, site re-check, report deadline, Tokyo trip, Slack replies, Lisbon arrival) | 1 of 8 (dentist) | 8 of 8 | 8 of 8 |
| 8 unwanted cases (past appointment, past trip in passing, "don't set reminders", hypothetical trip, a friend's story, finished task, a general cadence question, a plain question) | 0 of 8 | 0 of 8 | 0 of 8 |

On main, none of the three models created a job in the 5 helpful cases tried there (trip, Lisbon, Slack, site, report). Sonnet stays conservative: it offers in chat ("tell me the flight time and I'll set a check-in reminder") rather than creating. One run per cell: directional, not a rate.

Other live legs: the real system-prompt builder + `registry.dispatch("cronjob_manage", …)` under a temp `HERMES_HOME` for normal CLI (line present, card asked), approvals off with a UI, streaming API server, and a kanban worker (no line, no card, saved as on main); the real classic CLI card at 100×18 in tmux; the real messaging renderer (schedule card fenced, command card unchanged); Desktop approval cards earlier in this PR's history over CDP.

## Not covered

- Real Discord / Slack / Telegram clients (rendered strings only); Discord, Feishu and Matrix after-click card edits.
- Duplicate-proposal cases (needs a job to exist before the conversation starts) and ctaylor86's "propose a script job" / "reply stops one reminder" evals: tracked in #158538.

## Prompt surface

Stable system prompt: about +101 tokens per interactive surface vs main (the gated guidance line); tool schemas −1 token. Cron and unattended surfaces are unchanged. Needs a `hermes-agent-core` approval for the snapshot.

## Follow-ups (own PRs)

- #158541: damaged `[SILENT]` markers no longer reach your chat.
- #158555: Desktop/Web Inbox for job results, continuable in place.
- `cron.proactive: create|offer|off` (default `create`).

Credit: @emozilla (#156726 approval kinds), and the reviewers whose findings shaped this head: @kshitijk4poor, @salch-cred, @GottZ, @AtlasOmnia, @mr-magaia, @quotumorg, @ctaylor86, @eyedeaco, @askclaw-vesper, @mselcukozturk, @yqecea, @Adolanium.
