prs.title: fix(ci): fail fast on invalid macOS notarization credentials before building
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Catch dead notary keys fast. Before: Auth check: no pre-build check; Build & sign: 401 after 10 min. After: Auth check: notarytool history probe; Build & sign: runs only if valid. Change: 401/403/PEM → fail fast, 5xx/NSURL → warn.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dc63ca4-4077-45ea-9d95-584b2b23278d)

## What does this PR do?

Daily canary runs [44784160658](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44784160658) and [44876973873](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44876973873) spent ~10 minutes building, signing, and zipping `Hermes Agent Canary.app` before `xcrun notarytool submit` failed immediately with `HTTP status code: 401. Unauthenticated`.

This adds a pre-build notarization credential check (`scripts/ci/check_macos_notary_auth.py`) wired into `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` right after `Write App Store Connect key for notarytool`. Revoked keys, expired Apple Developer agreements, malformed or truncated `.p8` PEM files, or a key that isn't an EC P-256 PKCS#8 key now fail the macOS job in seconds before Xcode selection, signature-cache restore, or bundling, while transient Apple 5xx or network blips log a `::warning::` and let `Build and package` continue with its existing retry loop.

Points to review:
- **Deterministic vs transient classification:** `classify_notarytool_failure()` inspects explicit HTTP status codes before message keywords so Apple's HTTP 500 (`Error communicating with authentication service`) warns rather than failing fast; only HTTP 401/403, local PKCS#8 PEM validation errors, and deterministic `notarytool` key/argument errors exit 1, while 5xx/429, `NSURLErrorDomain`, timeouts, and unrecognized exits fail open (see commit message for the full matrix). The local key check reads the PKCS#8 envelope with the stdlib (the step runs bare `python`), and notarytool's own output is classified but never logged: the job log gets the verdict and exit status only.
- **Workflow anchor and checkout trust:** placed in `&darwin-steps` (covering both `build-darwin-arm64-release` and `build-darwin-arm64-commit` without re-declaring `APPLE_API_KEY` in step `env`). The helper runs from the trusted controller checkout (`.build/channel-controller` at `github.sha`), which channel builds and now release candidates check out, so a release of an older admitted commit on `main` or `release/*` keeps the preflight. Older `build_commit` checkouts lacking the script warn and skip; a release with the script in neither checkout fails closed.
- **CODEOWNERS:** edits `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml`, so landing requires one non-author `@NousResearch/hermes-agent-core` approval.

## Related Issue

Related to macOS canary notarization 401 failures in runs [44784160658](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44784160658) and [44876973873](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/44876973873).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/ci/test_macos_notary_auth_preflight.py \
  tests/ci/test_desktop_release_tag_admission.py \
  tests/ci/test_desktop_release_commit_admission.py \
  tests/ci/test_stable_release_graph.py \
  tests/ci/test_stable_release_commit_threading.py \
  tests/ci/test_workflow_job_graph.py \
  tests/ci/test_protected_canary_publication.py \
  tests/ci/test_channel_build_publication.py \
  tests/ci/test_check_os_marker_fakes.py \
  tests/ci/test_list_os_marked_tests.py -v
```

Manually on macOS with an App Store Connect `.p8` key:

```bash
APPLE_API_KEY=/path/to/AuthKey.p8 APPLE_API_KEY_ID=... APPLE_API_ISSUER=... \
  python3 -m scripts.ci.check_macos_notary_auth
```

Tested on Linux aarch64 (Python 3.14.9) at `33ca244682`: all 24 tests in `tests/ci/test_macos_notary_auth_preflight.py` (including real `bash` replay of the workflow's write + preflight steps with a fake `xcrun`, a release of an older commit, key validation against freshly generated P-256, P-384 and RSA keys, and checks that no key material or notarytool text reaches the log) pass, as does the 22-file related CI set that includes it (320 passed, 1 skipped), and `scripts/check --only ruff,health` is clean. Live `xcrun notarytool history` against Apple's API on a hosted `macos-15` runner with `release-signing` secrets was not run here and will be exercised by the next signed macOS release/canary run after merge.

prs.title: fix(approvals): retry a content-filtered guardian verdict on the first fallback
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The smart-approval guardian asks the auxiliary `approval` model for a one-word verdict. Some providers answer an ordinary flagged command with an empty body and `finish_reason="content_filter"`. On Codex I see this on routine `python -c` and heredoc scripts. `_smart_approve` treats any empty answer as an infrastructure failure and escalates. In an unattended run (cron, Kanban workers, `-q`) nobody can answer an escalation, so the command is refused and the job or card stops. The filter fired on the guardian prompt, so it tells the guardian nothing about how risky the command is.

With this change, a `content_filter` blank asks the first entry of the main fallback chain once, with the same system and user prompts. I read the chain through `get_fallback_chain(load_config_readonly())`, the same helper the auxiliary client uses for its main-fallback step. The fallback's verdict goes through the existing `_VERDICTS` mapping. Everything else is unchanged:

- no fallback configured: escalate, no second call
- the fallback is blank too: escalate
- the fallback call raises: the existing handler in `_smart_approve` logs it and escalates
- an empty answer for any other reason (`length`, `stop`): escalate without a retry, as today

The retry is logged at WARNING ("guardian answer blocked by a content filter; asking fallback ..."), next to the existing empty-answer warning.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched open and closed PRs and issues for the guardian's content-filter and empty-answer handling and found no duplicate.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/approval_smart.py`: in the empty-answer branch of `_smart_approve`, a `content_filter` finish reason calls the new `_fallback_verdict()` once. That helper takes the first fallback chain entry and repeats the verdict call with its `provider`, `model`, `base_url` and `api_key`, the same 16-token budget, the configured approval timeout and the same reasoning setting.
- `tests/tools/test_smart_approval_content_filter.py`: five tests with `call_llm` and the config mocked. They cover the retry (approve on fallback), a blank fallback, a fallback that raises, no fallback configured, and a `length` blank that must not retry.

## How to Test

1. Set `approvals.cron_mode: smart` (or run with `-q` and `approvals.single_query_mode: smart`), with a primary provider whose content filter blanks a verdict and any entry in `fallback_providers`.
2. Before: the log shows `guardian returned an empty answer (finish_reason=content_filter), escalating` and the unattended command is refused. After: the log shows `asking fallback <provider>` and the command runs or is denied on the fallback's verdict.
3. Unit test: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_smart_approval_content_filter.py`. On current main, 3 of its 5 tests fail (the retry, blank-fallback and error cases). The other two pass, because they pin the behavior that stays the same.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Not run: I ran only the 4 smart-approval test files (listed below).
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Python 3.14.9

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

On current main (ca22df7d08) plus this commit: `pytest tests/tools/test_smart_approval_content_filter.py tests/tools/test_smart_approval_reasoning.py tests/tools/test_smart_approval_policy.py tests/tools/test_smart_approval_injection.py`: 4 files, 30 tests passed, 0 failed. With the `tools/approval_smart.py` change reverted, the new file gives 3 failed, 2 passed. `python scripts/check --base ca22df7d08`: 17 checks, ok.

I run the same change as a local patch on v0.23.0 and v0.23.1. On one machine with a Codex primary and a fallback on another provider, the content-filter escalation refused unattended commands eight times in three days before the patch.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump solverforge-routing to 0.2.4
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Bumps the SolverForge Routing catalog entry from 0.2.2 to 0.2.4 (pin `cddc9903f14364a670f7234643a968c95c91b08f`, [release v0.2.4](https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/releases/tag/v0.2.4), engine [`engine-v0.2.4`](https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/releases/tag/engine-v0.2.4)). I maintain the plugin, and SolverForge and solverforge-maps, which the engine is built on.

What changed since the merged entry (#150783):
- **Trip changes no longer download roads again.** Removing a stop shrinks the trip's area, and the road cache was keyed by the exact area, so the re-solve went back to Overpass for roads it already had and failed whenever Overpass was busy. The engine now uses [solverforge-maps 2.3.4](https://crates.io/crates/solverforge-maps/2.3.4), which serves an area inside one already downloaded from that download.
- **The engine gets only the environment it needs** (proxy and CA certificate settings), so no API keys or tokens from the Hermes process reach it (0.2.3).
- The README states the supported platforms (Linux and macOS) and discloses the shared geocoder pacing lock in `~/.cache`, which the catalog Disclosure already listed (0.2.3).

Tools, Desktop UI and data are unchanged.

## Related Issue

None. This is a version bump of the merged entry from #150783.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

`plugin-catalog/solverforge-routing.yaml`:
- `sha` → `cddc9903f14364a670f7234643a968c95c91b08f`, `version` → `"0.2.4"`
- `image` and `screenshots` re-pinned to the new sha (same images)
- Disclosure: the engine release is `engine-v0.2.4`; it now says a trip inside an area already downloaded reuses it, and that the engine subprocess gets only proxy and CA certificate settings from the environment

Unchanged: `capabilities` (same 15 tools, no hooks), `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.2"`, `platforms` (Linux and macOS), `known_issues`.

Diff from the previous pin: https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/compare/6f8ea8251881a30fcd86f9607509034a60848de9...cddc9903f14364a670f7234643a968c95c91b08f

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/solverforge-routing.yaml` returns `OK: 1 file(s) valid`. Every image URL returns 200.
2. On a clean clone at the pin, `hermes plugins validate <clone> --install-deps` passes. No tracked file is a compiled binary.
3. CI is green on the pinned commit: https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/actions/runs/44401697719, and the plugin release run checked that the pinned SHA-256s match the engine release: https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/actions/runs/44402589021. The engine binaries come from https://github.com/blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing/actions/runs/44399499294.
4. New-user path in an empty `HERMES_HOME`:
   - `hermes plugins install blackopsrepl/hermes-solverforge-routing --ref cddc9903f14364a670f7234643a968c95c91b08f --enable`
   - `hermes solverforge-routing install` downloaded `engine-v0.2.4` and accepted it against the pinned SHA-256.
   - A five-stop Milan round trip through the installed engine downloaded its roads from Overpass and returned `0hard`.
   - The same trip without one stop, with all network access blocked, solved from the saved roads (`0hard`, four stops) and wrote no new road file. Engine 0.2.2 downloads the roads again for that trip.

## Checklist

- [x] One file changed, one entry
- [x] Full 40-hex sha, version matches the plugin's `plugin.yaml`
- [x] Capabilities match the registrations

prs.title: Add Frame (security scanning over MCP) to the plugin catalog
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/frame.yaml` for [Frame](https://github.com/lambdasec/frame), an open-source (Apache-2.0) security agent from lambdasec, the plugin's owner. The entry pins `lambdasec/frame-mcp` at `99688c3dafd18e0aff6706ef83dbdc1cd22bd230`, subdir `hermes/`: an Agent Plugins v1 package (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/frame/SKILL.md`), configuration only, no Python plugin code.

**What it does.** Runs Frame's MCP server so the agent can scan a codebase for vulnerabilities (taint analysis whose source-to-sink paths are checked with Z3, in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, C# and C/C++), verify that earlier findings are fixed, record baselines, generate verified fixes, and query the analysis engine (entry points and whether they are protected, data flows, callers, path guards). The `frame:frame` skill tells the agent when to scan and how to report.

**Hermes surfaces used.** A portable package's stdio MCP server and one skill. The `com.nousresearch.hermes` extension sets `trust: untrusted` (Hermes asks before the three tools not annotated read-only, `write_baseline`, `fix` and `exploit`, and refuses them unattended) and `timeout: 1800` for large scans; `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.2"` because of those keys.

**Disclosure (rule 13).**
- Downloads: `uvx --from frame-mcp==0.3.0 --with frame-security[scan]==1.1.7 frame-mcp` fetches both packages and their dependencies from PyPI on first run; pinned by version, not covered by the catalog sha. Needs uv.
- Files: reads what it is asked to scan; writes only the baseline file `write_baseline` names, and with `fix` only when `in_place` is set. Caches under `~/.cache/frame`.
- Network: plain scans make none. `scan` with `ai`/`hunt_authz`, `fix` and `exploit` send source code to the user's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint; `exploit` sends requests to the target the user names (the skill tells the agent to use it only on targets the user is authorized to test).
- Credentials: none read by the package. `FRAME_LLM_BASE_URL`, `FRAME_LLM_MODEL` and `FRAME_LLM_API_KEY` are passed through with `${NAME}` only when the user has set them.
- Processes: one `frame query --serve` child per scanned project for the engine queries.
- No telemetry.

**Validation.** `hermes plugins validate hermes/ --install-deps` at the pinned sha:

```
$ hermes plugins validate hermes --install-deps   # Hermes v0.23.2, fresh clone at 99688c3
✓ portable manifest — plugin.json parses (Agent Plugins v1)
✓ manifest fields — name present
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ server trust: frame — untrusted (Hermes asks before every write-capable tool 
call)
✓ security scan — safe
◆ Isolation — portable plugin (no Python): runs anywhere

Validation passed.
```

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add chanda (local long-term memory provider)
prs.body:
Adds one file, `plugin-catalog/chanda.yaml`, for the Chanda memory provider. I'm the owner of https://github.com/felipemarts/chanda.

**What it does.** Chanda is a local long-term memory server for agents (a Go binary over MCP, one SQLite file per memory). Writing needs no LLM: a hash, an embedding and rules. Reads use hybrid keyword and vector search. Facts carry validity periods and are superseded, not overwritten. Every record keeps its origin and trust zone. `forget` deletes in cascade and verifies the content is gone. The provider:
- delivers a pre-context on the first prefetched turn of a session (`prefetch()`, Chanda's `context` tool);
- exposes three provider tools: `chanda_search`, `chanda_get` and `chanda_timeline`;
- logs the session's user/assistant turns and an outcome when the session ends (`on_session_end`).

**Hermes surfaces used.** `ctx.register_memory_provider` and `ctx.register_hook("on_session_end", ...)`. The tools come from the provider's `get_tool_schemas()`, not from `register()`, so `provides_tools` is empty, as the validator expects. No core overrides, middleware or desktop code.

**Disclosure (rule 13).**
- Starts one local `chanda serve --profiles read,standard` child process over stdio while Hermes runs. It holds one SQLite file on disk, at the path in the user's `chanda.yaml`.
- Sends the first user message of a session, the provider tools' queries, and the session's user and assistant turns to that local process.
- Makes no network calls by default. If the user sets `llm.endpoint` in `chanda.yaml`, the Chanda process calls that endpoint for sleep consolidation and agentic search.
- The `chanda` binary is a separate install. `plugin.yaml` declares it as an external dependency pinned to `go install github.com/felipemarts/chanda/cmd/chanda@v0.1.0`, which the Go checksum database verifies. GitHub release binaries with `SHA256SUMS` are the alternative. Nothing is downloaded or updated by the plugin itself.
- Reads optional configuration from `memory.chanda` in `config.yaml` and from `CHANDA_*` environment overrides (binary path, config path, namespace). Neither holds secrets.
- No credentials and no telemetry.

**Validation.** `hermes plugins validate adapters/hermes/chanda_hermes --install-deps` on v0.23.2, against the tree at the pinned commit:

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.23.1' parses
✓ loadable — entry: __init__.py
✓ python dependencies — 1 requirements from manifest
```

prs.title: fix(kanban): stop the auto-decomposer storming loop-escalated cards + kind-independent loop recurrences
prs.body:
Two coupled fixes for a real operational failure mode of the kanban auto-decomposer.

**1. Loop-escalated triage cards were being re-armed by the decomposer every tick.**
When a task hits `block_loop_detected` it is moved to `triage` "escalated to a human" — but
`triage` is also the auto-decomposer's own work queue, so `auto_decompose_tick` pulled every
triage card, re-specified the looped card, and re-dispatched a worker ~1×/min indefinitely. We hit
this in production (a card with 15+ dispatch recurrences, zero human answers, churn storming the
dispatcher). `list_triage_ids()` now takes `exclude_loop_limited=True`, applied at the dispatcher
tick only (the sole automation caller); human CLI/dashboard paths are unchanged. The counter is
cleared only on explicit human re-arm (`specify_triage_task`), recorded as `loop_counter_reset` on
the `specified` event so the reset is auditable.

**2. Re-labelling a block kind laundered loop memory.** `_route_block` counted recurrences only
when the block kind repeated (`prev_kind == kind`), so flipping `needs_input`→`dependency` (or any
re-label) reset the count to 1 and defeated the escalation limit entirely. Recurrence counting is
now kind-independent over blocked→unblocked→re-block cycles; pure dependency waits (blocked by
unmet parents) are still never counted, and `loop_counter_reset` clears the ledger.

Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_triage_loop_guard.py` — includes
`test_kind_change_does_not_launder_recurrences` and an end-to-end tick-skip test. 124 tests green
locally across the kanban block/decompose/dispatch/specify/notifier/review suites (Python 3.14);
ruff clean. The two changes ship as separate commits since they're independently reviewable.

prs.title: fix(kanban): keep block-loop triage out of the auto-decomposer (#79738)
prs.body:
## What & why

**Closes #79738.** A Kanban worker that blocks with `kanban_block(reason="review-required: ...")` can have its terminal handoff silently undone by the auto-decomposer:

1. `block_task`'s unblock-loop breaker routes a re-blocked same-cause task to `triage` (emitting `block_loop_detected`) — by design, a human-in-the-loop gate.
2. The gateway auto-decomposer (`list_triage_ids` → `decompose_task(author="auto-decomposer")`) cannot distinguish those recovery cards from fresh triage, so on the next tick it re-specifies them (rewrites title/body), promotes them to `ready`, and the `active_pr` respawn guard then blocks any spawn — leaving the card **non-terminal** for external observers polling `kanban show --json`.

This is the same root cause as #79728 (block-loop recovery triage auto-decomposed into duplicate work) and #75444. The open PR #75490 filters only `block_kind IS NOT NULL`, which **misses the exact #79738 case**: the reporter's worker omitted `kind`, so `block_kind` stays NULL and the card is still fed to the decomposer. This PR detects escalation from the event log instead, which covers both typed and untyped blocks.

## Fix

- **`list_triage_ids()`** — excludes block-loop-escalated cards: a `block_loop_detected` event with no newer `triage_escalation_recovered` event. The auto-decompose feed is clean.
- **`decompose_task()`** — refuses escalated cards when called by the auto-decomposer (defense in depth; the call path is identified via the shared `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_AUTHOR` constant, also used by the gateway tick). An explicit manual `hermes kanban decompose <id>` is the operator's human-in-the-loop decision: it acknowledges the escalation (audited `triage_escalation_recovered` event) and proceeds, per #79728's "manual decomposition must remain available".
- **`recover_escalated_triage_task()`** — new audited operator recovery action: clears `block_kind`, resets `block_recurrences` (fresh loop budget — without the reset, one re-block instantly re-hits `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` and re-escalates), and appends the recovery event.
- **`idx_events_task_kind`** — composite index on `task_events(task_id, kind)` serving the escalation predicate (per-tick cost is one indexed `EXISTS` per triage row); `IF NOT EXISTS` in the always-run schema block, so existing DBs pick it up on next init.
- **`hermes kanban unblock --recover-escalated`** — exposes the recovery path on the operator surface (the gap the maintainer review on #75490 called out). Defaults to off; existing unblock scripts are unaffected.
- **Docs** — `kanban-worker-lanes.md` gains a "Block-loop escalation and recovery" section (the events, the fresh-vs-escalated triage distinction, the recovery paths); `kanban.md` notes the auto-decompose exclusion.

## Verification

- Reproduced the reporter's exact chain on main (block kind=None → unblock → re-block → triage with `block_kind` NULL → listed by `list_triage_ids`): RED.
- 8 new tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose.py`: the kind=None chain, typed escalation, operator recovery, fresh-triage regression, manual decompose of an escalated card. All GREEN.
- Regression (local run): 55 kanban-related tests pass (kanban_db, block_kinds, blocked_sticky, specify, cli, decompose_db, gateway auto-decompose live, watchers mixin), re-verified after the review-fix round (44 focused tests).
- Full `tests/hermes_cli` + `tests/gateway -k kanban` batch shows the same 8 pre-existing order-dependent failures as unchanged main (root/write-guard/WAL tests) — no new failures.
- Cross-vendor review (Gemini 3.6 Flash + GPT-OSS 120B): two rounds — design/diagnosis validation then code review of the diff and the post-review delta; both approved, no BLOCKERs/SHOULD-FIXs remaining.

## Notes

- The zombie-worker leg of #79738 (a worker whose run is recorded ended stays alive) is tracked separately in #80512 and is out of scope here; with this fix the card never reaches `ready`, so the non-terminal-observer failure is gone regardless.
- The `active_pr` respawn-guard semantics are tracked in #80231 and friends; untouched here.
- Out of scope follow-ups: dashboard surface for `--recover-escalated` (CLI is the canonical operator surface for kanban recovery ops).

**Open question:** should `recover_escalated_triage_task` also be exposed via the dashboard API (plugins/kanban/dashboard), or is the CLI surface sufficient for this recovery action?

prs.title: fix(kanban): gate auto-decomposer past block_loop_detected cards (t_15b7ebc4 vector 2)
prs.body:
### Problem

`auto-decomposer` (gateway `kanban_watchers.py::_auto_decompose_tick`) iterated all triage tasks and called `decompose_task()`, which only checked if `task.status == "triage"`. It did NOT distinguish a freshly-created triage card from one routed to triage by **`block_loop_detected`** (the circuit-breaker that escalates recurring-block loops for human review). Cards routed for human decision got re-specified and auto-promoted past Frank's gate without any human involvement -- see jarvis-os/t_15b7ebc4 (vector 2).

This is the second core-machinery vector defeating a needs_input/frank gate on this card; the first was `apply_approvals` substring-match, fixed in sibling PR #12 (t_552cc9e1).

### Reproduced live

| time (UTC) | event |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-02 11:20:22 | `block_loop_detected` at recurrences=2 --> routed to triage for human decision |
| 2026-08-03 07:18:25 | auto-decomposer: `specified` + `promoted` --> spawned run 102808 (no human approved anything) |

### Fix

Added `_has_gate_history(conn, task_id) -> bool` in `hermes_cli/kanban_decompose.py`:

1. **Check last terminal event:** if `'block_loop_detected'` --> gate (human decision routing)
2. **Check open block_kind:** if `'needs_input'` or `'capability'` --> gate (human-authority hold)

When either returns True, `decompose_task()` skips with `ok=False` and reason `"card was routed to triage by block_loop_detected (needs human decision) -- skipped"`. Normal fresh triage cards proceed exactly as before.

### Why core

Auto-decomposer lives in `gateway/kanban_watchers.py` --> `hermes_cli/kanban_decompose.decompose_task` (NousResearch/hermes-agent). Fleet hooks cannot fix it. This is in the same category as t_552cc9e1 (apply_approvals fix) -- core machinery that must be patched upstream.

### Tests

All 8 tests pass in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose.py`:

| Test | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `test_decompose_with_fanout_creates_children` | Pre-existing: fan-out works |
| `test_decompose_fanout_false_invalid_llm_assignee_uses_default` | Pre-existing: assignee fallback works |
| `test_decompose_returns_false_when_task_not_triage` | Pre-existing: non-triage rejected |
| `test_decompose_skips_block_loop_detected_card` | NEW: gate-circuit card skipped |
| `test_decompose_skips_needs_input_block_on_triage_card` | NEW: needs_input hold skipped |
| `test_decompose_skips_capability_block_on_triage_card` | NEW: capability hold skipped |
| `test_decompose_fresh_triage_still_works_no_regression` | NEW: normal fan-out still works |
| `test_decompose_normal_triage_without_block_kind_passes` | NEW: single-task spec still works |

### Rollback

Pure tightening: only refuses previously-granted auto-clears; operator `unblock_task` path untouched. No schema change. `git revert` safe.

Fixes root cause class behind t_f6805f35 (this) and t_15b7ebc4.

prs.title: test(plugins): report-only import boundary lint between core and bundled modules
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The written rule is that plugins don't reach into Hermes internals and core doesn't hardcode specific plugins. Nothing checks it today, so it slips a little with every PR.

This adds a report-only import lint for both directions and records each crossing it finds today in a committed baseline. Existing violations never fail anything. CI fails when a crossing occurs more often than the baseline records, and the failure names that crossing and says how to accept an intended one (`--update`, with a reason in the PR). Each crossing is its own baseline line, keyed by the importing file and the target, so a new import that lands alongside a removed one is still caught. Two PRs that accept imports in different files add different lines: when those lines aren't next to each other the merge is clean and `main` stays green; when they sort next to each other git shows a visible conflict in the baseline, fixed by rerunning `--update`. One case still merges silently red: two PRs adding the same target in the same file. That's rare, and a CI rerun on the merged head right before merging catches it. A reduction only sticks once someone rewrites the baseline with `--update`.

| Direction | What counts as a violation | Count on `main` today |
|---|---|---|
| module → core internals | a bundled module imports a Hermes module or name that is **not** on the published plugin API (`hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json`), e.g. `gateway.run._profile_runtime_scope` | **830** |
| core → module | core code imports one specific bundled module, e.g. `tools/send_message_senders.py` importing `plugins.platforms.telegram.adapter` | **29** |

Definitions:

- **Module**: a directory under `plugins/` with a `plugin.yaml`, or a `plugins/<name>/` with a `dashboard/manifest.json` (kanban, achievements). That's 109 directories.
- **Plugin plumbing** (counted as core): everything else under `plugins/`, such as `plugin_loader.py`, `plugin_utils.py`, `plugins/memory/__init__.py` discovery and the kind-level `_common`/`_shared` helpers.
  - Maintainers: please confirm `_common`/`_shared` should count as core. 208 of the listed sites involve those helpers, so the choice moves the counts a lot.
- **Core**: every other file of the shipped packages (pyproject `packages.find`) plus the root `*.py` modules.
- **Not checked**: tests, `scripts/`, docs, `skills/` and `optional-skills/`. Skills are library content run as subprocesses, not modules the gateway loads.

The module → core rule doesn't write its own allow-list. It calls `private_import_findings()`, the same function `hermes plugins validate` uses to warn plugin authors. So the lint, the validate warning and the generated docs page all read one `plugin_api.json` and can't drift apart. A full-path import from one in-tree module into a module directory (`plugins.web.firecrawl.provider`) is left out of module → core: it's a module-to-module import, not a core one. Imports under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` are skipped in both directions, the same as validate.

Scope: this is the lint only. The per-contract conformance suites are a separate PR. No production code changes.

## Related Issue

Refs HACORE-116 (One Core P2: boundary lint and contract tests).

I found no existing issue or PR for this. Searches run, PRs and issues in all states: "boundary lint", "import boundary", "core internals import lint", "plugins import gateway.run", "import-linter", "layer import lint". Nearest is #146473 (a different check: the module-level dependency DAG and acyclicity).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

(A CI lint delivered as a script plus a test. No runtime behavior changes.)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/boundary_lint.py`: collects violations in both directions.
  - `--list` prints every site (`file:line target`).
  - `--check` exits 1 only when a crossing's count is above the baseline, and prints each such crossing (`module_to_core: plugins/web/exa/provider.py gateway.run._profile_runtime_scope (1, baseline 0)`) plus how to fix or accept it.
  - A crossing's key is `<importing file> <target>` (repo-relative path, line dropped) in both directions, and its value counts how often that file imports that target. Moving an import to another file reads as a swap and needs `--update`.
  - core → module counts each distinct module an import names: `import plugins.web.exa, plugins.web.firecrawl` and `from plugins.web import exa, firecrawl` are two sites each. Spellings of one alias that name the same module (`from plugins.web.exa.provider import A, B`) collapse to one.
  - `--update` rewrites the baseline from the current sites. Run it to record an intended import or to drop entries a change removed.
- `scripts/boundary_lint_baseline.json`: `{"module_to_core": {key: count}, "core_to_module": {key: count}}`, one line per crossing: 789 module → core keys (830 sites) and 21 core → module keys (29 sites), about 71 KB.
- `tests/scripts/test_boundary_lint.py`, seven tests:
  - the ratchet: no crossing's count may exceed the baseline;
  - a tmp-tree case for each direction, where public-API and plugin-plumbing imports are not counted;
  - dashboard-manifest modules, core-side relative imports (levels 1 and 2) and the core-side `TYPE_CHECKING` skip;
  - grouped core → module imports count each module once per import line;
  - a lower count is not a regression, a swap is, and the failure names the new crossing;
  - the per-crossing tally: keyed by importing file, a file importing one target twice counts 2;
  - two branches adding the same target from different files, with their baselines merged, are not a regression; the same target added in the same file by both still is (the known limit above).

This runs in the existing pytest CI job. No workflow files change, and nothing under `scripts/ci/` or `scripts/check` changes.

## How to Test

1. `python scripts/boundary_lint.py --list` prints both counts and every site. It exits 0 with 830 / 29 on this branch.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_boundary_lint.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_private_imports.py --file-retries 0` gives `2 files, 16 tests passed, 0 failed`.
3. Ratchet probe (reverted afterwards). I added `from gateway.run import GatewayRunner` inside a function in `plugins/web/exa/provider.py`, and `import plugins.web.exa.provider` inside a function in `tools/web_tools.py`. Results:
   - `test_boundary_violations_do_not_rise_above_the_baseline` failed with `assert not ['module_to_core: 831 violations, baseline 830', 'core_to_module: 30 violations, baseline 29']` (this probe was run on the earlier per-direction version; the per-crossing version names each crossing instead);
   - `--check` exited 1.
4. On base `ca4360692055`, with only the new test file copied in, all the tests fail with `FileNotFoundError: ... scripts/boundary_lint.py`: the lint doesn't exist there.

5. Grouped-import check: with the previous version of `scripts/boundary_lint.py` (one site per import line), `test_grouped_imports_count_each_module` fails with `At index 1 diff: 'tools/web.py:2 plugins.web.exa' != 'tools/web.py:1 plugins.web.firecrawl'`; the other 3 pass.
6. Two-branch merge, in a scratch clone. Branch X adds `from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope` to `plugins/web/exa/provider.py`, branch Y adds `from agent.conversation_compression_checkpoint import checkpoint_required_from_config` to `plugins/web/firecrawl/provider.py`. Each runs `--update` and passes `--check`, then X merges Y.
   - Per-direction baseline (98c8b7b1226b): the merge is clean, and `--check` on it prints `module_to_core: 832 violations, baseline 831` and exits 1.
   - Per-crossing baseline keyed by module (44cc55a3232d): the two `--update` runs add two different lines, the merge is clean, and `--check` exits 0.
   - Same target from different files, same scratch-clone flow: base adds `import plugins.platforms.telegram.adapter` in a new core file, X adds it in `tools/aa_x.py`, Y in `tools/zz_y.py`. With 44cc55a3232d's keys (core key = target only) the merge is clean and `--check` exits 1. On this branch the merge is clean and `--check` exits 0. With the two new files named `tools/zz_x.py` and `tools/zz_y.py` (adjacent baseline lines), the merge stops with a visible conflict in `scripts/boundary_lint_baseline.json` instead.
7. Mutation probe of `scripts/boundary_lint.py` at 44cc55a3232d (each reverted after its run), all 11 caught by `tests/scripts/test_boundary_lint.py`: regressions back on direction totals, `>=` for `>`, module key = file, core key including the file, module key without the target, a set instead of a Counter, the `dashboard/manifest.json` line dropped, `_absolute`'s level-2 slice off by one, level-1 resolved against the parent package, relative imports ignored, and the core-side `TYPE_CHECKING` skip dropped.
8. File-keyed baseline: with 44cc55a3232d's `scripts/boundary_lint.py` and this branch's tests, `test_two_branches_adding_one_target_from_different_files_merge_green` fails (`assert ['core_to_mod... baseline 2)'] == []`), `test_tally_keys_by_importing_file_and_counts_repeats` fails, and the ratchet fails on the regenerated baseline. All pass on this branch.

The full-repo scan takes about 15 s in one test.

## Compatibility

- Adds three new files and edits no existing file. Nothing imports the new script except its test.
- Reuses `private_import_findings`, `_imported`, `_type_checking_nodes` and `_hermes_packages` from `hermes_cli/plugin_validate_private_imports.py` without changing them. `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_private_imports.py` passes unchanged (in the 16 above).
- Report-only: the current 830 / 29 sites pass. The only new failure mode is a crossing occurring more often than the committed baseline records.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. I ran only the two related files: 16 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (kernel 6.8)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A (the script docstring documents the definitions and flags)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A

prs.title: feat(kanban): pre_attachment_store — a policy hook at the single attachment store seam
prs.body:
Closes #158785

## What

One programmable pre-store policy seam in front of **every** durable kanban attachment ingress, as a new fail-closed directive hook **`pre_attachment_store`**. A field incident (full RCA in the issue): a worker's `kanban_complete(metadata={"artifacts": [...]})` staged a captured `docker inspect` dump containing a live service key into the durable attachments dir — the completion-staging copy is made by the engine, so a `pre_tool_call` guard plugin never sees that door, and nothing in core could refuse the store.

## How

- **`hermes_cli/kanban_db_attachments.py` (new)** — the shared store lane. `store_attachment_bytes` (agent `kanban_attach` / `kanban_attach_url`, CLI `attach`) and new `store_attachment_file` (dashboard's streamed upload, adopted from a private `.part` file) both: size cap → safe name → `_require_task` (no blob written for an unknown task, which today creates a dir first) → policy gate → row. The completion/review staging in `kanban_db._persist_scratch_completion_artifacts` gates each `_copy_capped` copy through the same `run_attachment_policy`; a refusal raises `ArtifactPreservationError`, so the completion rolls back and the card stays retryable (the existing orphan-discipline already unlinks the staged copy).
- **The hook contract** — fired while the staged blob exists at mode `0600` and before its row: kwargs `task_id, board, filename, content_type, size, source, uploaded_by, path`. `{"action":"block","message": …}` refuses (blob unlinked, `attachment_policy_blocked` event with the subscriber's message truncated to 200 chars, uploader sees the message verbatim). A subscriber may **rewrite the file in place to redact and allow** — the row records the **post-hook** stat size, so a redaction can't leave a lying `size` column. Timeout/raise reuse the existing policy-hook machinery: the hook joins `_HOOK_TIMEOUT_FAIL_CLOSED_HOOKS` next to `pre_tool_call` (timeout message generalized per-hook; the `pre_tool_call` string is untouched). **Core ships no scanner and no secret parser** — the oracle is an operator plugin; with no subscriber the fast path is byte-identical to today (no scan, no chmod, no dispatch).
- **Why the file moved** — `kanban_db.py` is 4231 lines, over the FILE_LINES ratchet, and may only shrink; the sanctioned remedy (config.py: "offset the growth in the same PR by making a folder") is applied: the attachment write path leaves the facade (net −45 lines there), callers (`kanban_tools`, CLI, dashboard plugin) import the sibling.
- **Dashboard dedupe** — `upload_task_attachment` stops hand-rolling the blob write and calls `store_attachment_file`; this retires two private cross-boundary imports (`kanban_db._safe_attachment_name`, `._collision_free_path`) and adds one (`kanban_db_attachments`). `boundary_lint_baseline.json`: −2/+1 for `plugin_api.py`, nothing else touched.
- Docs: `hooks.md` catalog row, timeout bullet, registration example.

## Verification

- New suite `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_attachment_policy.py`, 12 behaviour tests, **all pass on head; the module is red on base `88a1c1f4`** (import/collection error on the absent store lane; the seam's existence is itself asserted by `test_base_defect_no_gate_existed_in_front_of_the_staging_copy`): block→no blob/no row/event+verbatim value-free message; payload shape + `0600` during callback + real staged bytes scanned; in-place redaction lands and the row carries the post-hook size; raising subscriber fails closed; any-block-wins + allowed blob ends at the same mode an un-scanned store gives it; unknown task refused before any blob write; completion-staging refusal rolls the completion back (task stays `running`, no attachments, no staged copy) and the allow path stages normally; dashboard 400 with policy message and no `.part` debris; dashboard allow roundtrip incl. post-redaction size; 413 leaves no staged file.
- Touched-lane cross-section: all 114 `test_kanban*` files under `tests/{hermes_cli,plugins,cron,tools}` + `test_plugins.py` + `test_docs_drift.py` — **992 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped** via `scripts/run_tests.sh` (Python 3.14 CI env).
- `python scripts/check`: **22 checks, ok** (health: 0 blocking; the one `ASYNC230` on the dashboard stream carries the existing documented waiver).
- `scripts/boundary_lint.py --check`: no regressions.

## Interim control downstream (context, not part of this PR)

The fleet that found this runs an estate `pre_tool_call` plugin (`attach-needle-guard`) against the tool-layer doors until this lands; it provably cannot cover the completion-staging door — which is the point of the seam.

prs.title: fix(redact): stop logging a token in the path of a CDP URL
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Some CDP gateways put the access token in the URL path, like `https://cdp.example.com/<64-character token>`. `redact_cdp_url` masks a query string and `user:password@`, but it leaves the path as it is, so `tools/browser_session_cdp.py` writes the token to the log at INFO level each time it resolves the endpoint.

`redact_cdp_url` now replaces any run of 32 or more characters that follows a `/` with `***`. The run stops at the next `/`, whitespace, `?`, `#`, a quote or `<>`. The host after `//` is never masked. The pattern runs over the whole text, not only over full URLs, because when `requests` can't reach the gateway, urllib3's error names only the path: `Max retries exceeded with url: /<token>/json/version`. `tools/browser_session_cdp.py` logs that error at WARNING level through `redact_cdp_url`.

A local Chrome serves its own target ID in the path too, as `/devtools/browser/<UUID>` or `/devtools/page/<32 hex characters>`. Both are long enough to look like a token, so an ID of exactly that shape right after `/devtools/<kind>/` is kept. Anything else in that place is masked, and so is a token before that part, like `wss://cdp.example.com/<token>/devtools/browser/<id>`.

The new tests are in a new file, `tests/agent/redact/test_cdp_url_path.py`. `tests/agent/test_redact.py` is already over the 2,000-line limit in `scripts/check`, and that check doesn't let it grow.

## Related Issue

Fixes #158758

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix, a non-breaking change that fixes an issue

## Changes Made

- `agent/redact.py`: a new `_CDP_PATH_TOKEN_RE` masks long path segments, and `redact_cdp_url` applies it after the query string pass. The function still masks them when `security.redact_secrets` is off, like the query string pass.
- `tests/agent/redact/test_cdp_url_path.py`: tests check that a token is masked when `/json/version` follows it, inside error text and next to punctuation, `==` padding, an uppercase scheme or a query string, in a real `requests.ConnectionError` built from urllib3's `MaxRetryError`, with redaction turned off, and before or in place of a `/devtools/browser/` ID. Other cases check that `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, its `/json/version` URL, Chrome's browser and page URLs, a 31-character segment and a long host name come back unchanged.

## How to Test

1. Run `python -c "from agent.redact import redact_cdp_url; print(redact_cdp_url('https://cdp.example.com/' + 'a' * 64))"` from the repository root. It prints `https://cdp.example.com/***`, and on `main` it prints the whole token.
2. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/redact tests/agent/test_redact.py tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_override.py tests/tools/test_managed_browserbase_and_modal.py`.
3. I ran those 4 test paths with pytest directly, not through `scripts/run_tests.sh` or `just`, because my machine has no PM test environment for this checkout, so the two `just` boxes below are unticked. All 353 tests passed on the branch. On `main` with the new test file copied in, the 14 masking tests failed and the other 339 passed. The other test files in `tests/agent` that mention redaction gave the same results on both. I also ran `python scripts/check --commit HEAD` directly. 21 of 22 checks passed, and the `shims` check failed the same way on `main` in my checkout.

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- **Async stages:** module handlers may be coroutines; an async failure

- **Degradation:** drafter disabled/failed → full host draft+shaping fallback;

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(security): harden host approvals and delegated-worker admission
prs.body:
## Summary

Applies owner-managed approval constraints and atomic host-account worker admission across synchronous, async, and lifecycle delegation. Reservations are retained through actual execution and cleanup; decisions fail closed on invalid authority state or uncertain process identity. Adds isolated behavioral contracts and observe-first rollout documentation. No live policy is activated by this change.

- Owner-managed host approval policy: host-authority precedence over profile/session state, bounded (≤24h, unique-permission) owner exceptions, fail-closed on malformed or unreadable policy, honest human-presence resolution, and `yolo`/standing-grant relaxation only when explicitly policy-authorized.
- Host-scoped delegated-worker admission: one reservation per concrete runnable child (orchestrators counted while awaiting descendants), atomic all-or-none batch admission, reservations held until the whole child lifecycle is quiescent (including the schema retry), reject-not-queue on capacity with occupancy/limit metadata.
- Identity safety: opaque reservation identities validated against process-birth and host identity; PID reuse, missing fingerprints, foreign namespaces, or uncertain liveness retain capacity and surface a repair-needed condition instead of manufacturing free slots.
- Windows: installed managed authority is explicitly refused pending an ACL-qualified implementation; absent authority preserves the existing unmanaged behavior.

## Test adaptation (second commit)

`test_real_binding_correlates_plugin_approval_denial_to_tool_metric` mocked `approval_context.get_current_session_key` with a zero-argument lambda. The managed gate calls the getter's documented `get_current_session_key(default="")`, so the mock raised `TypeError`, which the fail-closed plugin boundary swallowed — the test then asserted the gate-error block message (`BLOCKED: plugin approval gate failed`) instead of the user denial it exists to correlate. The mock now accepts the documented default.

## Validation

Validated at `42331a4e` (base `2bd378ed1b8`, v0.23.0) in a clean PM-built environment (frozen lock, Python 3.14.9, `dev`+`test` groups, all CI extras, isolated `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`):

- New hardening contracts: 100 passed, 3 host-specific skips.
- Focused approval/delegation/admission suites: 1,599 passed / 9 skipped; the single failure is the known macOS `/private/var/tmp` vs `/var/tmp` delegate assertion, which reproduces on the unmodified base.
- `scripts/check --base 2bd378ed1b8`: 14/14; code health over the 27 changed files: zero blocking or advisory findings.
- Full macOS default suite: 70,842 passed / 106 failed / 1,993 skipped, versus 104 identical failures on the unmodified baseline control (environmental/host-specific). The only current-only failures are the stale mock fixed by the second commit and one intermittent prepared-compaction flake observed under 6-worker load that passes in every serial rerun.
- With the mock adaptation, both relay integration files pass 59/59 serially under `scripts/run_tests.sh`.

## Rebase record

Rebased onto current `main` (`ac248c819a2`); head `add930bb145`. The only textual conflict was `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py` (`_defer_close_after_timeout`): the resolution keeps upstream's `contextvars` context binding and cleanup-tail dispatch and the hardening's `child._delegate_close_future` retention signal, resolving that Future in a `finally` so an admission reservation can never strand on a cleanup exception.

Re-validation on the rebased tree (fresh environment built from the rebased source; tests run from a checkout outside `~/.hermes` so the home-isolation guard stays meaningful):
- `scripts/check --base ac248c819a2`: 17/17 checks ok; code health over the 25 changed files: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
- Focused approval/delegate/admission/hardening selection, 186 files, 6 workers, no retries: 1,919 passed / 2 failed / 9 skipped (host-specific). Failures: the known pre-existing macOS `/private/var/tmp` vs `/var/tmp` delegate path assertion (reproduces on unmodified `main`), and `test_terminal_approval_batch[False-0]`, which times out under 6-worker load and passes 7/7 serially — the same load-sensitivity class as the prepared-compaction flake above.
- The relay integration file (with the adapted mock) and the prepared-compaction file both passed under the 6-worker run.

## Rollout

Observe-first: this PR activates nothing live — no config changes, no dependency changes, no enforcement. Enforcing rollout follows the separately documented staged plan (compatible runtime, old-process drain, host/session adoption checks, platform qualification).

prs.title: fix(update): rebase local fork commits onto upstream instead of skipping sync
prs.body:
## Problem

When the fork has local commits **and** upstream has new commits, `hermes update` previously **skipped upstream sync entirely** to avoid trampling local changes:

```
ℹ Your fork has N commit(s) not on upstream.
  Skipping upstream sync to preserve your changes.
```

The fork is then left permanently behind upstream — the sync only ever runs when the fork is strictly behind, which can't happen once a local commit lands. Users with local patches on their fork (e.g. downstream packaging, hotfixes waiting on upstream PRs) never receive official updates via the updater.

## Change

In `_sync_with_upstream_if_needed` (hermes_cli/update_cmd.py):

- **Fork ahead + upstream ahead**: rebase local commits on top of upstream/main (`git pull --rebase upstream main`).
- **Conflict safety**: if the rebase conflicts, abort it (`git rebase --abort` + capture_output) so the repo is never left in a broken mid-rebase state, and print manual-resolution instructions.
- **Fork ahead + upstream not ahead**: report `Upstream is up to date (N local commit(s) ahead)` instead of the misleading skip message.
- **Strictly behind (ff-only)**: unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` passes
- [x] Manual trace of all four branch states (ahead/behind x upstream ahead/not) via code review
- [ ] Unit coverage (none exists for this helper today — happy to add if maintainers want a specific harness)

Verified against upstream/main `fbd40c907d` — cherry-picked cleanly, single-file diff.

prs.title: fix(cli): show all messaging platforms in config, not just Telegram/Discord
prs.body:
## Summary

`hermes config` now shows **all** registered messaging platforms instead of only Telegram and Discord.

## Problem

`hermes config`'s `Messaging Platforms` section was hardcoded to check only `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. All other platforms — Email, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack, Feishu, WeCom, and many more — were silently omitted even when correctly configured via `.env` or plugin registration. This was misleading: a user could have Email fully configured and active in the gateway, yet `hermes config` would report nothing about it.

Reported in #8175. Previous PR #8238 attempted to fix this but used a static map rather than the shared platform registry, and was not merged.

## Fix

Replaces the hardcoded check with a query of `gateway.platform_registry.PlatformRegistry.all_entries()` — the shared source of truth that **all** platforms (built-in and plugin) register into:

1. Trigger plugin discovery (`get_plugin_manager().discover_and_load()`) so the registry is populated.
2. Render one row per registry entry, sorted by label, in a dedicated `_show_messaging_platforms()` helper.
3. Configured state comes from each entry's `required_env` contract — the same list `hermes setup` displays — **never** from `check_fn()`, which is a passive SDK-availability probe that must stay side-effect free (#79812). A platform with no env contract (e.g. A2A) needs nothing from the environment and renders as `configured (no env required)`.
4. Added a module-level `check_mark()` helper for consistent ✓/✗ rendering.

This single code path now automatically surfaces all 23 registered platforms, and stays correct as platforms are added or removed.

## Testing

- Regression tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py::TestShowConfigPlatforms` (row-scoped):
  - the IRC row flips `✗ not configured` → `✓ configured` when IRC's own env vars are set (asserted on the row, not a global substring)
  - a no-env-contract platform (A2A) renders `configured (no env required)`, not a false negative
  - registry output still includes Email (previously invisible) alongside Telegram and Discord
  - no Traceback/Error in config display
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py`: 123 passed, 4 skipped; `ruff check` clean.
- Rebased onto current main (was 21k commits behind); upstream's refactor of `show_config()` into section helpers is preserved — the messaging block is now its own `_show_messaging_platforms()` section function.

Closes #8175

prs.title: fix(email): honor explicit outbound subjects; cron reports start fresh conversations
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes cron/scheduled email reports being threaded into the recipient's
ordinary conversations with the sender.

The email adapter builds outbound subjects purely from per-sender thread
context. Cron deliveries have no inbound reply anchor, so a report sent to
someone you have been emailing arrives with "Re: <last conversation
subject>" plus References/In-Reply-To headers — Gmail then threads the
nightly backup into your "floor plans" thread. This PR lets the delivery
router stamp thread-less email cron deliveries with an explicit
"Cronjob Response: <job_name>" subject, and makes the adapter honor an
explicit metadata subject verbatim: no Re: prefix, no threading headers
(a guaranteed fresh conversation). Reply behavior is unchanged when no
explicit subject is present.

Two small related email fixes ride along, both verified in production:

- `splits_long_messages = True` on the adapter. Email has no practical
  length cap, but the gateway truncated long sends (large cron reports)

No issue is claimed (the cron-threading problem surfaced through local

prs.title: fix(gateway): an empty-response turn reaches the chat as one plain reply, not five retry lines (#101138, salvage #101157)
prs.body:
When the model answered empty three times, a Telegram chat got five technical messages, out of order: `retrying (1/3) in 6s`, edited to 2/3 and 3/3, then `❌ Model returned no content after all retries. No fallback providers configured.`, then the actual explanation. Now the chat gets only the explanation ("didn't produce a reply this time… Send `continue` to try again, or switch models with /model"). The CLI and local viewers still show every line.

| Live probe: real `gateway run` + Telegram Bot API stand-in, DM, the model answers empty on every call (4 calls) | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| messages sent to the chat | 2: `⚠️ Empty response from model — retrying (1/3) in 6s`, then the explanation | 1: the explanation |
| edits to those messages | 3: `retrying (2/3) in 15s`, `(3/3) in 25s`, `❌ Model returned no content after all retries. No fallback providers configured.` | 0 |
| final reply | `⚠️ No reply: fake-model didn't produce a reply this time, even after retries. Send `continue`…` | same |

- `gateway/run.py::_TELEGRAM_NOISY_STATUS_RE`: the `retrying\s+in\s+\d` alternative also accepts the counter the empty-response retry emits (`retrying (1/3) in 8s`, `agent/turn_empty_response.py::_retry_empty`). That is defect 1 of the issue. The pattern is the one from #101157 (@fangliquanflq, co-author).
- `agent/turn_empty_response.py::_terminal_empty`: the terminal "no content after all retries" and "reasoning but no visible response" statuses become `TerminalFailureText`. That is the marker `_prepare_gateway_status_message` already drops for the other turn-ending failures (#72131), since the final reply already says it.
- Defect 2 of the issue (the final reply bypassed the filter): on current main the final reply for an empty turn is no longer a raw diagnostic. Since 23036e20a665 `_hmwa_shape_agent_response` replaces `(empty)` with the localized `EMPTY_RESPONSE_EXPLANATION`, the same text the CLI and Desktop show. The reporter's sixth message ("switch model/provider, or inspect the tool output above") was the old copy. So this PR does not filter final replies. #101157 instead swapped them for a generic "Something went wrong" line, which would make chat copy differ from the CLI and Desktop (`tests/gateway/test_empty_sentinel_rewrite_copy.py` pins one text), so that part is dropped.
- Root cause: the retry counter was added to the emitter without updating the filter, and the terminal empty status was never tagged as turn-ending.

## Dropped hunks
- #101157's `_GATEWAY_RETRY_FINAL_DIAGNOSTIC_RE` final-reply replacement and its extra `empty response from model` / `model returned no content` / `no reply:` noise alternatives. The final reply is the explainer on main (see above), and the terminal status is now dropped by its type, not by its text.

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_empty_retry_chatter_filtered.py` covers the counted retry lines being dropped on chat and kept on the CLI, the terminal-empty status from the real `_terminal_empty` (both branches) being dropped on chat and kept on the CLI, and an unrelated warning still delivered. 4 of 6 red on the base, all green here. `test_telegram_noise_filter`, `test_warning_notification_contracts`, `test_empty_sentinel_rewrite_copy`, `test_failed_turn_site_codes` and `test_empty_response_fallback_refund` stay green (212 passed). `git merge-tree` is clean against #153458, #153101, #153087, #153196, #153247 and #153054.

Fixes #101138

prs.title: fix(modal): routed preflight reads only the serving profile's tokens
prs.body:
## What

`has_direct_modal_credentials()` now runs the routed-profile check first. For a routed profile it reads both Modal tokens strictly through `get_secret`, and treats an unscoped read as not ready. Single-profile selection is unchanged, including the host `~/.modal.toml` login.

## Why

This is a follow-up to #156051, from @unsupportedpastels's review comment r4628281709 (finding m1).

The token pair was read through `_scoped_credential`, which catches `UnscopedSecretError` and falls back to the launch process env. A multiplexed caller with no secret scope bound therefore got `selected_backend == "direct"` from the launch account's tokens, and `ModalEnvironment` then refused the start. Nothing ran on the wrong account, because the constructor makes no SDK call in that case. But readiness disagreed with the constructor.

```text
unbound multiplex caller, launch tokens present
main (4bf7516003): selector=direct; constructor refuses before the SDK
this PR:           selector=None;   constructor refuses before the SDK
```

With the selector at None, the caller now gets #156051's routed direct-mode refusal, which tells them to set both tokens in that profile.

## Authorship

The patch is @unsupportedpastels's as posted, applied with `git apply` and committed under their authorship, and it applied unchanged on main. I wrote only the commit message.

## Verification

- The new test `test_unbound_multiplexed_modal_preflight_does_not_offer_launch_tokens` fails on main's source (`assert 'direct' is None`) and passes with the fix.
- The whole guard file `tests/tools/test_modal_profile_client.py` passes: 29 tests.
- Both runs used an isolated interpreter: an empty env with an explicit `PYTHONPATH`.
- `scripts/check --staged`: 22 checks pass. ruff is clean.
- Hosted CI runs on this head.

prs.title: fix(cron): reopen the run ledger when Windows opens it read-only
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When another process holds `cron/executions.db` without write sharing at the moment the ledger opens it, SQLite on Windows falls back to a read-only handle without an error. Reads work, and the first write fails with `attempt to write a readonly database`, so the cron run fails. Antivirus, search indexers and backup tools can hold a file like that for a moment.

The ledger's transaction connection now catches `SQLITE_READONLY` when the transaction hasn't written anything yet. It opens a fresh connection, closes the read-only one and runs the statement again, up to 3 times, after 0.2, 0.5 and 1 second. If the file is still read-only, the error is logged and raised with a note that names the file and both likely causes: a permission or mount problem, or a program holding the file.

When the OS reports that this user can't write the file or its folder, waiting can't help, so the ledger raises at once with a note that says so. That covers permission bits and a read-only mount on Linux and macOS, and the read-only attribute on Windows. The waits run under the ledger's module lock, which every profile's ledger calls in the process share, so those cases don't hold that lock for 1.7 seconds on every write. On Windows, `os.access` doesn't read ACLs, so a file an ACL denies still waits out the 3 reopens before the error.

```text
execute(sql)
  run sql
  on SQLITE_READONLY, if no rows were written in this transaction
    if the OS says this user can't write the file or its folder: log and raise
    wait, open a new connection, close the old one
    run sql again (at most 3 reopens)
  after the last reopen, log and raise with the file path
```

Open pull request #156680 also changes `cron/executions.py`, but for `database is locked`. The two merge without a conflict, and neither retries the other's error. I kept the fix to the run ledger from the issue. `cron/incidents.py` writes its own table into the same file, and the other SQLite stores in `cron/` open their files the same way, so they may need the same reopen. That can be a separate change.

## Related Issue

Fixes #158757

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix, a non-breaking change that fixes an issue

## Changes Made

- `cron/executions.py`: `_transaction()` yields a `_LedgerConnection` wrapper that reopens a read-only handle before its first write. A new `_ledger_path()` helper is shared with `_connect()`, and `_readonly_give_up_reason()` decides when to stop and what the note says.
- `tests/cron/test_execution_ledger.py`: 6 new tests. Four cover a read-only open that recovers, one that stays read-only, a reopen that fails, and a file this user can't write. One checks that a read-only error after a write isn't retried. The last is a real Windows run where a second process holds the file without write sharing.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_execution_ledger.py`.
2. I ran this file on the branch and on `main` with the new test file copied in. All 30 tests passed on the branch. On `main`, 5 of the 6 new tests failed, and the recovery and Windows tests failed with `attempt to write a readonly database`. The sixth checks that a write isn't retried after rows were written, which `main` doesn't do either. The other 49 cron test files gave the same results on both.
3. My machine has no PM test environment for this checkout, so I couldn't use `scripts/run_tests.sh` or `just`, and the two `just` boxes below are unticked. I ran `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py`, the runner `run_tests.sh` calls, in the same clean environment, and it passed 51 tests with 0 failures across this file and the two other test files that use the ledger. I also ran `python scripts/check --commit HEAD`. 21 of 22 checks passed, and the `shims` check failed the same way on `main` in my checkout.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)

prs.title: fix(pm): probe pnpm version in its staged entry directory
prs.body:
## Summary
- Set `probe_cwd = True` on `Pnpm` in `pm/packages.py` so `BinaryPackage.verify()` runs `pnpm --version` with `cwd=native(binary.parent)` instead of inheriting the caller's working directory.
- Update the `BinaryPackage.probe_cwd` comment to document workspace-aware CLI isolation alongside `dlopen` backend resolution.
- Add a regression test in `tests/pm/test_pnpm_package.py` (`test_pnpm_verify_probes_in_entry_dir_not_callers_cwd`) verifying that `Pnpm.verify()` probes in the staged entry directory even when the caller's `cwd` contains a `package.json` pinning `npm`.

## Root Cause
`Pnpm` inherited `probe_cwd = False` from `BinaryPackage`, causing `verify()` to invoke `pnpm --version` in whatever directory Hermes was launched from. pnpm 12 reads the nearest `package.json` even for `--version` and exits with status 1 (`ERR_PNPM_OTHER_PM_EXPECTED`) when that project's `packageManager` field pins `npm`, breaking `hermes pm install pnpm` and launch-time dependency sync.

## Test Plan
- Ran `.venv/bin/pytest tests/pm/test_pnpm_package.py -v` (13 passed)
- Ran `.venv/bin/pytest tests/pm/test_pm_core.py -q` (43 passed, 1 skipped)

prs.title: fix(dashboard): refresh runtime-prefixed lazy assets with executable regression (#90068)
prs.body:
## Summary and original-author credit

**This is a credited refresh/salvage of MagnaCapax's #141502, not an independently invented fix.** Its original commit `05aedd244c44d73904c6dece507f48dee0841148` was cherry-picked with `-x`; the original author identity and authored date are preserved. The production implementation and documentation are MagnaCapax's. This refresh adds executable build-regression coverage and independent current-main/installed-source validation.

Fixes #90068.

Also credit to LeonardoLGDS for #90170, which addresses the same bug using a relative Vite base plus server anchoring of HTML URLs. This PR retains #141502's runtime-prefix approach, **does not mix the competing relative-base implementation into it**, and does not close or formally supersede either existing PR. It is offered as a freshly validated consolidation candidate for maintainers to choose.

## Why this is still needed

Rechecked upstream main `88a1c1f4b19d1bc2b9fe8db870dee9ba0803fad5` before publication. It still builds with Vite's default root base, without a runtime asset URL hook. The HTML/CSS rewrites do not cover URLs generated by the lazy preload helper in JavaScript. Merged #133903 fixes auth-prefix handling; #145357 handles stale chunks after updates. Neither changes this URL generation.

A prefixed document and its entry assets load successfully, then lazy preloads request origin-root `/assets/...`; failed CSS preload rejects the lazy route. A filename/minifier-specific nginx substitution can mask it, but breaks as soon as another build changes the bundle hash or helper name.

## Source decision

- Use Vite `experimental.renderBuiltUrl` only for JS-hosted asset URLs, resolving them against `globalThis.__HERMES_BASE_PATH__`.
- Leave HTML/CSS URL generation and the existing backend prefix rewriting unchanged. No backend, auth, MIME, or proxy-root fallback change.
- Empty/missing runtime prefix keeps root deployments working. One build works under independent prefixes and nested document paths.
- Known tradeoff: this uses Vite's experimental build hook; the regression executes emitted output so a future Vite change cannot silently bypass the integration.

## Regression improvement

The source PR's unit coverage is retained. Its minified-text integration assertion is replaced with an execution test: build a lazy JS+CSS fixture twice with changed module content, then run the emitted native ESM/preload code for missing, empty, two independent, and nested prefixes. Only the DOM/network boundary is simulated. Assert actual generated link paths and the lazy module's exported value, independent of minifier names, quotes, or content hashes.

With the Vite hook disabled, the unchanged new test fails:

```text
- "/hermes-1/assets/page-CqdXlfeY.css"
- "/hermes-1/assets/page-CD2v9lyW.js"
+ "/assets/page-CD2v9lyW.js"
+ "/assets/page-CqdXlfeY.css"
Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

Restoring the hook: 5/5 pass, including all ten built-output execution cases.

## Independent verification executed

Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, locked Vite 8.3.4:

- `pnpm --dir web run check`: **82 test files / 607 tests pass**, TypeScript passes, ESLint exits 0 (29 existing warnings).
- `python scripts/check --base 88a1c1f4b19d1bc2b9fe8db870dee9ba0803fad5`: **22 checks pass**, 0 blocking/advisory code-health findings.
- `HERMES_PYTHON=<isolated-test-python> scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_prefix.py -q`: **26 pass**.
- Real production builds before/after on upstream source and on **two separately exported installed frontend source snapshots**, each using its own lockfile/config/build inputs. The exact two-file production patch passes `git apply --check` on both snapshots; no snapshot-specific source adaptation is required.
- Real Chromium through an isolated TLS nginx prefix-stripping proxy with password auth, forwarded prefix/proto/original Host+port, **no JS response rewriting**, and no root `/assets` fallback:
  - Before, both installed-source builds: login succeeds and prefix is injected, but Chat has `#root` child count 0 and **15 root-asset 404s per mount**.
  - After, both installed-source builds: Chat sidebar and xterm DOM render; **zero wrong-prefix asset requests and zero asset failures**. Pointer-driven Sessions → Chat navigation also loads correctly.
  - Root deployment renders before and after, without asset failures.
  - Refreshed upstream build also renders through both prefixes.
- HTTP sweeps: **39/39 JS/CSS files per installed snapshot**, **41/41 per mount for upstream** (both prefixes and root), all 200 with correct MIME. Served JS matches built bytes exactly. Nested SPA fallback documents anchor assets correctly; protected `/api/auth/me` is 401 anonymously/200 after login; one prefix's cookie does not authenticate the other. A separate external-API stub remains under its own mount rather than taking dashboard `/api`.

## Limitations

The installed snapshots contain actual frontend/build inputs and exact installed asset-serving/prefix-normalization modules; remaining Python backend modules are from the validated upstream base. This is not a full installed-container clone. The local server disables agent/cron/gateway lifespan services and uses synthetic test credentials in isolated homes. No model/provider is configured: terminal/route rendering and asset loading are verified, not assistant conversations. No production deployment or restart was performed. No claim is made that current upstream was previously deployed. CI results are separate from these executed local checks.

## What does this PR do?

Lets model-provider plugins claim per-tenant gateway hostnames (`<tenant>.example.com`) for named custom providers instead of special-casing those hosts in core (two commits):
