prs.title: fix(key_cmd): cache, classify and recover key_cmd credentials correctly
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes three bugs that can strand a `key_cmd` provider on an expired or unmintable token until restart (three focused commits replacing #88536, #91109, and #91132, with prior review feedback addressed):

- **Use shortest advertised lifetime (`agent/command_token_source.py`):** take `min(expires_in, expiry - now, expiresOn - now)` instead of letting a helper's cached `expires_in` override an earlier absolute deadline.
- **Fail fast on mint errors (`agent/error_classifier.py`):** walk the exception cause chain in `_by_key_cmd_failure` ahead of `_by_transport` so `CommandTokenError` wrapped in `APIConnectionError` classifies as `auth_permanent` instead of retrying as a connection timeout.
- **Re-mint once on auth failure (`agent/command_token_source.py`, `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`):** add `CommandTokenSource.invalidate()` and `remint_after_auth_failure()` in the `pool is None` path so an auth rejection (including bare `401`, excluding bare `403`) forces one re-mint per credential instance without spinning, and re-arms on the next scheduled mint.

## Related Issue

Fixes #88535
Fixes #91108
Fixes #91119

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/command_token_source.py`, `agent/error_classifier.py`, `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` (line-neutral import merge for file-size limit)

- Updated `test_the_shortest_advertised_lifetime_wins` (replacing `test_expires_in_still_wins_when_both_present`) for both `expires_in < expiry` and `expiry < expires_in`.
- Classifier tests cover bare, SDK-wrapped, `__context__`, two-level wrapper chain, genuine connection errors, and cyclic causes.
- Re-mint bound lives on `CommandTokenSource` per credential instance, ignores failed mints and bare `403`s, never retries a token that already resulted from an auth re-mint, and re-arms after the next scheduled mint.

prs.title: A 429 saying the plan has zero allowance for the model no longer gets waited on and retried (port omp#19301)
prs.body:
When a provider's plan gives you no allowance at all for a model, it answers every request with "Rate limit exceeded" and a `x-ratelimit-limit-…: 0` header. Hermes used to treat that as a short rate limit and waited and retried a request that could never work; now it stops waiting and moves straight to another key or the fallback model.

Ported from can1357/oh-my-pi#19301 (https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19301), which hit it on a Mistral plan (`code: 1300`).

## What changes

- `agent/error_classifier.py::_status_429` returns the existing billing verdict (`retryable=False`, rotate credential, fall back) when any `x-ratelimit-limit-*` response header is `0`. New helper `_zero_allowance_header` reads the headers the classifier already pulls off the exception chain.
- A spent window with a real limit (`limit: 60, remaining: 0`) is unchanged: still `rate_limit`, still backs off.

| Real `hermes chat -q` against a local endpoint answering every POST with Mistral's 429 + `x-ratelimit-limit-req-minute: 0` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Classifier verdict | `rate_limit`, retryable | `billing`, not retryable, fallback |
| Agent log | `API call failed (attempt 1/3)` → `Retrying in 2.4s` → `Retrying in 4.6s` → `failed after 3 retries` | `API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable)` → `Non-retryable client error` |
| Wall time / requests to provider | 24.6 s / 7 | 13.1 s / 5 |

(The request counts include the CLI's model-metadata probes; the retry loop itself goes 3 → 1.)

**Ours vs theirs:** omp has to append a notice to the error text so its persisted-text classifiers see it, and adds exclusions in three retry layers. Hermes has one structured classifier that already sees response headers, so the port is one check at the 429 seam; every retry/rotation consumer reads that verdict.

**Live repro:** real `hermes chat -q` process (fresh fake HOME + HERMES_HOME per leg, gateway killed by PID after each), provider = local HTTP server replaying the 429. Numbers above from each leg's `logs/`. Not covered: a real zero-allowance Mistral key.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_error_classifier_zero_allowance.py` (real `openai.RateLimitError` over an `httpx.Response`) (limit 0 → billing, red on main; limit 60 → rate_limit, control).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/`: 15050 passed, 0 failed, 72 skipped; 1 collection error in `test_vault_key_storage.py` (`keyring` not installed in this local env, unrelated).

## Infographic

![Limit zero means no](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab3717c/LsK6l05YJARi1wbsB02sA_ToVhGqYG.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

1. Plant only the test hunks on `main`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary_reads.py` gives 3 failed, including `assert [] == ['owned']` and `test_activity_snapshot_requires_current_owner_objects`.
2. Same command on this branch: 4 passed.
3. Related files (`tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary*.py`, `test_subagent*.py`, `test_local_viewer*.py`, `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py`, 51 files): 418 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, 0 blocking health findings.

I've been running this change on a long-lived gateway since mid-October. Before it, a rebuilt parent left the CLI subagent monitor empty while its children kept running. With it, the children stay listed and steerable.

prs.title: feat(write-approval): one decision path and a public review API for staged writes
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the change clearly. What problem does it solve? Why is this approach the right one? -->

Staged memory and skill writes can only be decided through `/memory` and `/skills` today. A plugin that wants to list or decide them has to import private modules, and `hermes plugins validate` flags it for that. This PR routes every decision through one resolver and adds a small public API on top.

It's stacked on #142244. The first five commits are that PR unchanged, and this PR's changes are the last two: the resolver, then the public API. I'll rebase once #142244 merges.

- `resolve_pending(subsystem, id, decision, *, expect=None)` in `tools/write_approval.py` decides one pending write. It returns `applied`, `rejected`, `already_resolved` (with `prior`), `conflict` (nothing was written; a pending write stays pending) or `needs_review`. `/memory` and `/skills` approve and reject use it. Successful output is unchanged, a refusal says why, and the pending list gets a "Needs review" section when there's something in it.
- Each write is decided once. A decision holds a per-record OS lock from the claim until its outcome is saved to a small result file, so once an outcome is recorded, a second client or a retry gets `already_resolved` instead of a second apply. A competing decision waits up to 5 seconds, then returns `conflict`.
- Approvals are checked against what was staged or previewed. Staging records a revision for every file a skill write touches. `preview_pending` returns the ops, diffs from a single read of the files, and an `expect` value (record hash, file revisions, profile). With `expect`, an approval only writes if the files still match, checked under the appliers' own locks. Without it, as in the slash commands, the staged revisions decide. Memory keeps relying on the pinned `matched_entry`.
- Some batches are refused outright. Deletes and file removals always need their staged revision, even after a new preview, and one stale removal blocks its whole batch. A batch that names one skill two ways (`foo` and `cat/foo`) is refused, because each spelling would be checked on its own while the batch edits one folder. The check goes by leaf name, so it errs toward refusing. A batch that mixes `delete` with other ops is refused too, matching the batch tool.
- A non-destructive skill record queued by an older version has no revisions to check. The slash commands still approve it (`legacy_unchecked=True`), and the plugin API needs a fresh preview for it.
- An interrupted approval is never replayed. If the process dies mid-apply, the record becomes `needs_review` and leaves the queue, and `/memory pending` and `/skills pending` list it. After checking the files, `/memory reject <id>` or `/skills reject <id>` closes it as `rejected`. The outcome file keeps why it stopped, and the reply warns that the files may be partly changed and nothing was rolled back. Only a reject that names the id does this: `reject all` skips these writes, and `approve` keeps refusing them. A skill batch whose rollback fails ends up here too. This covers a crashed or killed process, not power loss.
- `tools/write_review_api.py` is the public API. It's documented in the plugin guide and registered in `hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json`:
  - `list_writes(kind="all", *, page=1, page_size=25)`: metadata only (no memory text), counts per kind, both gate states, and a separate count of writes that need review.
  - `preview_write(kind, pending_id)`: the structured preview, with an `expect` tied to that kind and id, and `created_at` (the staging time as a float, or `None`). The list and the preview clean `created_at` with the same helper, so they always agree; a bool, NaN, ±inf or an out-of-range value becomes `None`.
  - `decide_write(kind, pending_id, "approve" | "reject", *, expect)`: needs a preview's `expect` and passes the decision to the resolver.

  They act on the active profile for the call, never take a profile or home path, and leave authorization to the host.

For the examples in the issue: `pending_count` is `list_writes()["counts"]["total"]`, and "decide all" is a preview plus a decision per id, so each approval uses the revisions from that id's own preview.

Left for follow-ups:

- A "write staged" event, and a public `evaluate_gate` for memory providers (raised in the issue thread).
- Pruning lock and outcome files. Outcomes have to outlive retries, and a lock file can't be unlinked while another process may be waiting on it, so retention needs its own design.

## Related Issue

<!-- Link the issue this PR addresses. If no issue exists, consider creating one first. -->

Fixes #148313

Related: #142244 (base), #84189, #145505, #136738

## Type of Change

<!-- Check the one that applies. -->

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

<!-- List the specific changes. Include file paths for code changes. -->

- `tools/write_approval.py`: the resolver, claim lock and outcome files, file revisions, previews, and listing writes that need review.
- `tools/write_review_api.py` (new): the public API.
- `tools/skill_manager_batch.py`: reports a failed rollback, and stores the skill name resolved for each batch op so a replay doesn't depend on the caller's default name.
- `hermes_cli/write_approval_commands.py`: approve and reject go through the resolver; the pending list shows writes that need review, and `reject <id>` closes one.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md`: a "Review staged memory and skill writes" section that documents the API. `hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json` registers the three functions under it, and `public-api.md` is regenerated.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md` and `skills.md`: what "needs review" means and how to clear it.
- Tests: `tests/tools/write_approval/` is new (the resolver contract, races, files changing while a decision waits for a lock, SIGKILL recovery, and the public API). `tests/tools/test_write_approval.py` follows the applier hook the resolver now calls, and `tests/gateway/test_session_memory_review.py` stages minted ids.

## How to Test

<!-- Steps to verify this change works. For bugs: reproduction steps + proof that the fix works. -->

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/write_approval/ tests/tools/test_write_approval.py tests/tools/test_skill_pending_diff_batch.py tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py tests/e2e/core/security/test_store_traversal.py tests/gateway/test_session_memory_review.py tests/gateway/test_session_read_commands.py tests/plugins/conformance/test_published_plugin_api_resolves.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_private_imports.py`
2. `python scripts/gen_plugin_api_docs.py --check`
3. By hand: set `memory.write_approval: true`, let the agent stage a memory write, then run `/memory pending` and `/memory approve <id>`. Approving the same id again writes nothing.

Results on `0369a6fbc1` (Linux arm64, Python 3.14):

- Step 1: 354 passed, 0 failed.
- Step 2 is clean, and `just check` passes.
- A standalone plugin built only on the three public functions passes its 49 Python tests against this branch, including mounted tests through Hermes' web app, plus its render tests, and `hermes plugins validate` passes.

The claim lock uses `fcntl.flock` on POSIX and `msvcrt.locking` on Windows. The Windows path hasn't run on a Windows backend yet, so CI's Windows lane will be its first run.

prs.title: fix(scratch): prune even when a boot temp var already holds a value
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the 24h scratch prune fire from the boot hook even when `apply_scratch_tmp_env()` declines to repoint `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`.

On Windows + git-bash those three already hold `/tmp` before Hermes boots, so the guard reads them as a user override and returns `False`. `export_scratch_tmp_env()` only resets `tempfile.tempdir` in that case, and **nothing else on the boot path calls `get_scratch_dir(prune=True)`** — so `_prune_scratch_dir_once()` is never reached and the scratch dir is never pruned.

Observed on the reporting machine: the `.last_prune` stamp had not moved since 2026-11-13 while 20 idle entries accumulated through 11-22.

## Bug Cause

`hermes_constants.py`:

```python
ours = env.get(SCRATCH_DIR_MARKER_ENV, "")
for key in SCRATCH_TMP_ENV_VARS:
    value = env.get(key, "").strip()
    if value and value != ours:
        return False          # <-- git-bash's /tmp lands here
```

`get_scratch_dir(prune=True)` is the only thing that triggers the prune, and reaching it is gated on that unrelated decision.

Controlled repro on one machine and binary:

```
# with the git-bash default triple:
$ TMPDIR=/tmp TMP=/tmp TEMP=/tmp hermes --version >/dev/null
$ ls -l --time-style=full-iso cache/scratch/.last_prune
-rw-r--r-- 1 ... 2026-11-13 08:00:00 .last_prune      <-- unchanged

# with the vars cleared:
$ env -u TMPDIR -u TMP -u TEMP hermes --version >/dev/null
$ ls -l --time-style=full-iso cache/scratch/.last_prune
-rw-r--r-- 1 ... 2026-11-22 10:57:44 .last_prune      <-- advanced
```

Calling `prune_scratch_dir()` directly always works, so the pruner itself is fine — only its boot-time trigger is unreachable.

## Fix

Trigger the prune from the boot hook independently of the guard. Two statements plus a comment:

```python
    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
        _prune_scratch_dir_once(get_scratch_dir(prune=False))
```

No platform detection, no behaviour change when the guard does not fire. `_prune_scratch_dir_once` is already throttled (once per process, once per hour across processes via the stamp file) and hands the scan to a detached child, so this stays cheap for short-lived `hermes` invocations.

## Related Issue

Fixes #158752

Related, deliberately not addressed here:
- #127261 — the same guard makes temp files land outside scratch and the prompt's "TMPDIR points here" false. This PR does not repoint TMPDIR, so that stays open.
- #148451 — prune does not re-run inside a long-lived gateway (`_scratch_pruned_once` is process-scoped). This PR only guarantees the first call happens.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_constants.py` — `export_scratch_tmp_env()` triggers the prune regardless of the temp-var guard's verdict.
- `tests/test_scratch_dir.py` — `test_boot_hook_still_prunes_when_a_user_tmpdir_wins`: with `TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP=/tmp` set, `export_scratch_tmp_env()` must still hand the scratch dir to `spawn_prune`. Uses the existing `scratch_prune_spawns` fixture (no real detached child).

## How to Test

1. On any host, run `test_boot_hook_still_prunes_when_a_user_tmpdir_wins` — it fails on `main` with `AssertionError: boot hook never reached the prune`, and passes with this change.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_scratch_dir.py` — the whole file: 3 failed, 11 passed, 20 skipped **on Windows, and the same 3 fail identically on the base commit** (`test_a_short_lived_process_still_completes_its_due_prune`, `test_bootstrap_import_exports_scratch_to_process_and_children`, `test_prune_records_removals_and_kills_in_scratch_prune_log`). They look host-specific: a spawned `python.exe`'s pid does not match on this host, and one test splits a path containing a space. Not caused by, and not fixed by, this PR.

I have not run the full `scripts/check` suite locally; CI will. The change is two statements inside an existing function and touches no prompt surface, config key or tool list.

## Checklist

- [x] Proven red on the base commit (the new test fails without the fix)
- [x] No new dependency, env var, config key or prompt change
- [x] Test uses an existing fixture and writes nothing outside `tmp_path`

prs.title: fix(skills): preserve Office text replacement
prs.body:
## What changed

Word and PowerPoint now share one run-preserving, non-recursive replacement helper. It computes matches from the original text, applies them right-to-left, and never searches inserted replacement text again.

The integration also:

- includes Word runs nested in hyperlinks;
- avoids processing linked headers and merged table cells twice;
- preserves all `w:t` nodes, tabs and breaks while normalizing Word runs/comments;
- respects PowerPoint soft-break boundaries and edits text inside grouped shapes.

## User impact

Previously replacements such as `cat` → `cats` could loop in Word, text inside hyperlinks/groups was skipped, cross-run matches could lose formatting, and linked/merged content could be processed more than once.

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `office_text_replace`, Word hyperlink replacement, linked headers, merged cells, PowerPoint grouped text and soft-break replacement. No matching implementation was found. #158768 is complementary and only covers slide duplication safety.

- `python scripts/check`: 22 checks passed.

Tested on Linux with Python 3.14, python-docx 1.2.0 and python-pptx 1.0.2.

prs.title: fix(plugins): the remaining plugin state writers refuse a deleted or renamed profile home
prs.body:
## Problem

#158270 made plugin state writes refuse a **deleted or renamed profile home** — it added `mkdir_under_hermes_home()` as the guard and fixed seven sites. Three writers of the same class were left behind, and each one still recreates the home the operator just deleted:

| Site | What it writes |
|---|---|
| `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py` — `_command_sync_state_path()` / `_save_command_sync_state()` | Discord slash-command sync pacing state |
| `plugins/platforms/google_chat/adapter.py` — bot id cache | Google Chat bot id resolution cache |
| `hermes_cli/plugin_host_profiles.py` — model extraction cache | Cached model list per plugin host profile |

All three call `Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (or write straight through `atomic_json_write`) on a path under `get_hermes_home()`, so a profile that was deleted or renamed comes back as an empty directory tree with a cache file in it. `#158270` touched `plugins/platforms/discord/recovery.py`, not `adapter.py`, which is why this tail stayed open.

## Fix

Route every one of the three through the same guard the merged fix introduced, and keep the failure non-fatal:

- `mkdir_under_hermes_home(dir)` raises `FileNotFoundError` when the profile home is gone, instead of recreating it.
- **Discord**: the pacing state is best-effort — `OSError` is caught, logged at debug level, and the rest of the slash-command sync continues. A dead home no longer aborts a sync that would otherwise succeed.
- **Google Chat**: the mkdir is wrapped so a deleted/renamed home simply skips the write; `except Exception: pass` became `except OSError: pass` so genuine programming errors still surface.
- **`plugin_host_profiles`**: on `FileNotFoundError` the caller still gets its payload, the cache write is skipped.

No behaviour change on a live profile: the path already exists, so `mkdir_under_hermes_home()` is a no-op there.

## Tests

New: `tests/gateway/test_platform_state_writes_dead_profile_home.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host_profiles_dead_home.py` — each case runs against a **deleted** and a **renamed** home.

- Green: both files **8 passed / 0 failed**
- Red proof (the three source files reverted to `origin/main`, tests kept): **6 failed / 2 passed** — the six failures are the deleted/renamed assertions, not import errors.

## Duplicate check

- `#158270` (**merged**, 2026-11-21) is the same class of fix, and its file list does **not** include `discord/adapter.py`, `google_chat/adapter.py` or `plugin_host_profiles.py`.
- Symbol searches for `mkdir_under_hermes_home`, `plugin_host_profiles`, `"dead profile home"` across open PRs return no PR touching these three sites.
- `main` still has the unguarded writes.

## Notes for the reviewer

- 5 files, +135/−10; three source files, two test files. No unrelated changes.
- `ruff check` clean on all five.
- `merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` → rc=0 at the time of writing.
- CI on fork PRs starts as `action_required` — the numbers above are local runs, not CI results.

prs.body:
Re-pins `plugin-catalog/mock-review.yaml` from v2.1.0 to v2.3.0. v2.1.1 through v2.2.0 were never merged here, so this covers all of them.

- sha: `9ebf9d4b01555988f9cff88334349297b8752f37`, the v2.3.0 release commit (tag `v2.3.0`, https://github.com/apelabs-dev/hermes-mock-review/releases/tag/v2.3.0).
- version: `2.3.0`
- The image and screenshot raw URLs now point at the new sha. Both return 200.

**2.3.0**

- **Wake on every messaging platform, Hermes Desktop included.** A board now wakes the chat it was made in on every messaging platform Hermes hosts. `mock_review_create` reads that chat from the calling session, and an explicit `origin_*` argument still takes precedence. `hermes mockreview setup` creates the wake route and the notice route for every configured messaging platform, not only the first one.
- **How a Desktop chat is woken.** A Hermes Desktop chat has no webhook route. The board server inside the gateway instead queues the wake prompt into that chat's own session through Hermes's plugin `inject_message` API. Hermes allows this only with `plugins.entries.mock-review.allow_gateway_injection: true`. Setup asks for that consent and sets it with `hermes config set` only when the user answers yes at a terminal. Under `--yes` it only prints the command.
- **Desktop boards are gated.** The woken turn runs with that chat's own tools, so a Desktop board is refused while Send is not gated. Send counts as not gated when the server is on a non-loopback host, `public_url` is set, a Tailscale Funnel mapping exists, or the board is public.
- **Non-chat origins.** Origins that are not chats (`api_server`, `webhook`, and others) are refused at create, with the reason.
- **Resolved pins.** Resolved pins now stay on the board. The new setting `hide_resolved_pins` hides them.

**2.2.0** (included): the board shows live which pins Hermes is working on: a pulsing red dot on the pin, a chip on the block, a status row in the thread, a badge in the Comments list and a count in the header.

**2.1.1–2.1.4** (included): the board header shows the project's icon; the Desktop Mocks tab renders design-profile mocks with their CSS; plus docs, CI and test fixes.

**Entry text.** The description adds the 2.2 and 2.3 features and the Desktop wake path (`inject_message`, the consent key and its gating). Setup's `hermes` subcommands are still covered by `config get/set/unset`. There are no new outbound hosts, secrets or dependencies.

`scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/mock-review.yaml` passes.

prs.body:
## Summary

Systematic bug audit of `run_agent.py` identified and fixed 7 verified bugs. Each fix is minimal and targeted — no refactoring, no new features.

### Critical
- **Off-by-one in `_flush_messages_to_session_db`** — first new message after conversation history was skipped, never written to DB (`start_idx = len(history) + 1` → `len(history)`)
- **Stale interrupt flag on early returns** — 3 interrupt return paths didn't call `clear_interrupt()`, causing next `run_conversation()` call to exit immediately

### High
- **Uncaught `handle_function_call` exceptions** — quiet mode had `try/finally` without `except`, normal mode had no `try` at all. An exception would crash the agent and break the API contract (missing tool response)

### Medium
- **`flush_memories` identity check could wipe all messages** — `is not flush_msg` cleanup used Python identity comparison; if reference was lost, the while loop would pop every message. Replaced with sentinel marker

### Low
- **`_hydrate_todo_store` cleared global interrupt flag** — unrelated `_set_interrupt(False)` call removed
- **Retry loop off-by-one** — `while retry_count <= max_retries` allowed 7 retries instead of intended 6. Changed to `<`
- **Redundant `import re`** in `_clean_session_content` (already imported at module level)

## Changes

Single file: `run_agent.py` (+22, -10)

prs.title: MCP servers signed in through Microsoft Entra stay signed in past the first hour (port omp#19855)
prs.body:
MCP servers signed in through a Microsoft Entra app registration used to need a fresh browser sign-in about every hour, because the token refresh was refused. Now the refresh repeats the scope you originally signed in with, so Entra issues a new token and the server stays signed in.

Ported from can1357/oh-my-pi#19855 (https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19855).

## What changes

The MCP SDK builds the `refresh_token` grant with no `scope`. RFC 6749 §6 makes it optional, but Entra v2 requires it when the OAuth client is also the resource (the usual setup for an internal MCP server behind its own app registration) and answers `400 invalid_request AADSTS90009 ... requesting a token for itself`. Hermes then dropped the tokens and the next tool call went back to a browser sign-in.

- `tools/mcp_oauth_provider.py::HermesProviderMixin._with_grant_scope` adds the stored token's scope to the refresh form. The stored scope is the granted one (the SDK records the requested scope when the grant omits it), so the refresh never asks for more than was granted.
- No stored scope (and none configured) = request byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Applied inside `_refresh_token` under the existing refresh fence, so the OAuth manager path and device-flow servers both get it.

| Token endpoint behaviour (local stand-in, refuses scope-less refresh like Entra) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh with stored scope `api://app-1/access_as_user offline_access` | `400 {"error": "invalid_request", "error_description": "AADSTS90009: ..."}` | `200 {"access_token": "new", ...}` |
| Refresh with no stored scope | form without `scope` | unchanged, form without `scope` |

**Ours vs theirs:** omp saves the authorize request's scope on its credential record and threads it into its refresh helper. Hermes already persists `scope` on the stored `OAuthToken` (and backfills it from the requested scope), so the port is one hook at the shared refresh builder; no storage change.

**Live repro:** real `MCPOAuthManager` provider, real `httpx2` POST to a local token endpoint that rejects scope-less refresh grants: main 400 AADSTS90009, head 200. Not covered: a real Entra tenant (no credential here).

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth_user_agent.py::test_refresh_names_the_grant_scope` (red on main, green on head).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/ -k oauth`: 196 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped.

## Infographic

![MCP sign-in that lasts](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab37117/6yeuRELIOmCC-vb0uTIWJ_H8OVcxWB.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): mark onboarding tips seen in the profile they were read from
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When one gateway serves several profiles, the "First-time tip … This notice won't appear again" message never stops. It comes back on every steered or queued message, and the `/verbose` tip comes back on every long tool run.

The tip checks whether it has been shown in the **served profile's** `config.yaml`, but records that it was shown in the **launch profile's** `config.yaml`. The served profile never gets the flag, so the tip shows every time. The launch profile gets a flag it never asked for.

The fix records the flag in the same file it is read from, using `_gateway_config_home()`, which the read already uses. With only one profile, `_gateway_config_home()` returns the launch home, so nothing changes there.

This reworks devorun's #119493, which was closed without merging because of the open-PR limit, onto current `main`, and adds a test for the second tip. devorun is credited as co-author.

## Related Issue

Fixes #154977
Fixes #156007
Salvages #119493

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_busy.py`: the busy-input tip records its flag in `_gateway_config_home()`, not `_hermes_home`.
- `gateway/run_turn_progress.py`: the long-tool `/verbose` tip, same fix. @mgr-nick pointed this one out on #156007.
- `tests/gateway/test_busy_session_ack.py`: new test, served profile set with `set_hermes_home_override`. The flag must land in that profile's config, the next read must see it, and the launch home must stay untouched.
- `tests/gateway/test_tool_progress_hint_profile.py`: the same test for the `/verbose` tip. No gateway test covered `_progress_onboarding_hint` before.

I searched the rest of the code for other `is_seen` / `mark_seen` pairs. None of them reads and writes different files:

| Place | Why it is fine |
|---|---|
| `gateway/run_turn_prepare.py` (first-contact note) | Already reads and writes through `_gateway_config_home()` |
| `hermes_cli/cli_stream_mixin.py`, `cli_tui_mixin.py`, `cli_tui_runtime_mixin.py` | The command line runs one profile per process, so it reads and writes the same file |
| `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py` | Both sides follow the profile override |

## How to Test

1. Run a gateway that serves a second profile, with `display.busy_input_mode: steer`.
2. Start a long task in that profile, then send another message while it runs.
3. Before this fix, the first-time tip appears every time, and `onboarding.seen.busy_input_prompt` shows up in the launch profile's config, not the served one. After this fix, the tip appears once and the flag is in the served profile's config.

prs.title: fix(cli): let display.banner_hyperlinks disable the banner's OSC 8 release link
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The welcome banner wraps its version label in rich `[link]` markup pointing at the latest GitHub release tag. rich renders that as an OSC 8 hyperlink sequence that always carries an `id=` parameter:

```
ESC ] 8 ; id=<random> ; https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/vX.Y.Z ESC \
```

Terminals whose OSC parser truncates the parameter at the first `;` (reproduced on SecureCRT) consume `ESC ] 8 ; i` as the command and print the remainder as visible text — `d=<random>;https://github.com/...releases/tag/vX.Y.Z` — which overflows the Panel title, wraps the border, and garbles the whole banner.

Since rich unconditionally emits `id=` for `[link]` markup, there is no degraded (id-less) form to fall back to. The only reliable fix is to not emit the sequence at all on such terminals.

This PR adds a `display.banner_hyperlinks` config flag (default `true`, zero behavior change when unset). Setting it to `false` drops the OSC 8 bytes; the visible title text is identical either way.

## Related Issue

None found — searched issues/PRs for OSC / hyperlink / SecureCRT; no existing report. Happy to file one first if maintainers prefer.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/banner.py` — new `_banner_hyperlinks_enabled()` reads `display.banner_hyperlinks` (defaults true, config errors fall back to true); the title only gets `[link]` when enabled.
- `hermes_cli/cli_config_load.py` — register the key in display defaults.
- `cli-config.yaml.example` — document the key with the SecureCRT symptom.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_banner.py` — 3 tests: default emits OSC 8 `id=` sequence; flag off removes `]8;` bytes entirely; the flag reads the config key, defaults true, survives config errors.

## How to Test

1. Repro without the fix, in any terminal (two printf's, the second mimics what rich emits and what SecureCRT leaks — its OSC parser keeps `d=123;<URL>` as text):
   ```
   printf '\033]8;;https://example.com\033\\A-no-id\033]8;;\033\\'
   printf '\033]8;id=123;https://example.com\033\\B-with-id\033]8;;\033\\'
   ```
2. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_banner.py -q` — 8 passed (5 pre-existing + 3 new).
3. On a SecureCRT session: `display: {banner_hyperlinks: false}` in cli-config.yaml → banner title renders with a clean border, no leaked `d=<n>;https://…` text.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (OSC/hyperlink/SecureCRT: no hits)

- [x] I've run the banner tests: `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_banner.py` → 8 passed
- [x] Repo-pinned ruff (`--config ruff.toml`) passes on all touched files; pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes

prs.title: feat(regex): add the hermes_re facade over google-re2 and a doctor check for regex settings
prs.body:
Stacked on: #158716 (S0). Review only the commits after it; this PR targets main and shows S0's commits too until #158716 merges.

## Summary
Adds `hermes_re`, a first-party package with the stdlib `re` surface on top of Google RE2 (`google-re2`, added in
S0), so later stages migrate a module by changing only `import re` to `import hermes_re as re`. RE2 matches in
linear time (ReDoS-resistant). The package is stdlib-only at import and loads the engine on first use; `compile()`
validates at once and raises `hermes_re.error` (a subclass of `re.error`) for what RE2 cannot run. Without
`google-re2` the first match raises `ModuleNotFoundError(name="re2")`. **No product code uses it for matching yet.**

Also adds the D28 pre-upgrade check in `hermes doctor` so users can see, before any behaviour changes, which of
their regex settings the new engine will refuse.

## What changes for users
- `hermes doctor` gains the section "Regex Settings (RE2 engine change)": for the active profile it lists
  user-supplied regexes (shell-hook and outbound-webhook matchers, Matrix `ignore_user_patterns`, webhook route and
  subscription filters, platform mention patterns, env-var forms included) that RE2 will refuse (a manual issue:
  `hermes doctor` exits 1, like the neighbouring upcoming-change notices) or will read with ASCII word boundaries
  (warning). It rewrites nothing. Hooks are named by place, `hooks.<event>[<index>] matcher` / `hooks.outbound[<index>] matcher`;
  the hook's command, URL or name is never printed (it can carry a token). Without `google-re2` it prints
  `skipped: google-re2 not installed` (warning); with the package installed but failing to import it prints the
  cause (exception class and message) instead.
- Nothing else. Plugins may `import hermes_re as re` (new plugin-API entry).

## Plan stage and owner decisions
Plan stage S1 (facade package, tests, docs page, plugin-API entry, engine-missing test, doctor check). Implements
D24 (no module needs the engine to import: `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`), D28 (doctor check, exit 1 on a
refused pattern), the 64 MiB per-pattern memory budget, and the S0 "after S1" step (musl CI table check).

## Commits
1. `feat(regex): add the hermes_re facade over google-re2` — package, tests (108), table generator + JSON, docs page
   + sidebar, `packages.find`, plugin-API entry (+ regenerated `public-api.md`), package lists in the desktop
   fixture, two update tests and the neutral-imports allowlist.
2. `test(regex): check that modules import without the regex engine` — `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`.
3. `feat(doctor): report regex settings the RE2 engine will refuse` — `hermes_cli/doctor_regex.py`, doctor row,
   `webhook_filters.filter_regexes` walker (no behaviour change), CLI docs paragraph, tests.
4. `ci(pm): check the hermes_re tables against musl RE2` — musl job runs `gen_hermes_re_tables.py --check`;
   workflow triggers on `hermes_re/**`.
5. `fix(doctor): name regex hooks by index, never by command or name` — review fix: a hook command can carry a token.
6. `fix(doctor): report why an installed regex engine fails to import` — review fix: "not installed" only when it is.
7. `docs(doctor): state which lookarounds RE2 accepts` — review fix: RE2 refuses lookaround except a one-character
   lookbehind at the very start and one lookahead at the very end (a negative lookahead tests one character).

## Tests run (locally, isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME, Python 3.14)
- `tests/hermes_re/`: 108 passed. `scripts/gen_hermes_re_tables.py --check`: up to date.
- `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`: 4 passed. Doctor tests (`test_doctor*.py`, `test_doctor_regex_settings.py`)
  and `tests/gateway/test_webhook*.py`: all passed. STAGE_1 list (plugin API/docs imports, plugin conformance,
  neutral imports, update tests, tree layout) and `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py`: passed.
- `python scripts/check`: ok (22 checks; code health 0 findings).
- Re-checked after the review fixes in a per-worktree venv (editable install of this branch only, engine + all
  extras): doctor tests + `tests/hermes_re` + engine-optional + docs drift: 336 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped; check ok.
  The new doctor tests were red on the pre-fix code and green after.
- `tests/hermes_re/`, `test_doctor_regex_settings.py` and `test_regex_engine_optional.py` need `google-re2` (a core
  dependency from S0 on); on an interpreter without it they fail by design, not by flakiness.
- Without `google-re2`: `import hermes_re` works, compile works (a backreference or non-edge lookaround is refused at once), first match raises `ModuleNotFoundError(name="re2")`.

## Evidence level / known limits
The facade was differentially tested against stdlib `re` during planning (tens of millions of comparisons); this
PR's test runs are the first runs of the repository suite on it. Silent differences that remain by design (ASCII
`\b` away from simple edges, empty-match iteration, lone surrogates, repeated-empty-body groups) are documented in
`website/docs/developer-guide/regex.md`. Not run locally: the docs site build, the musl CI job, Windows/macOS lanes.
The doctor check covers the active profile only (`hermes -p <name> doctor` for others).
One deviation from the planned text: the table generator reads its JSON with `utf-8-sig` (the newer footguns lint).

prs.title: fix(gateway): a background subagent's approval after the parent's reply reaches the chat and /approve answers it (#133514, salvage #136199 #133522)
prs.body:
A background subagent that hit a command needing approval after the parent had already replied used to get a "pending approval" that no one could see: no card arrived and `/approve` said nothing was pending. Now the approval card (or the `/approve` text prompt) shows up in the chat the parent was started from, and a tap, `/approve` or `/deny` answers that subagent's command. Where no chat can show it (API server, webhooks, local viewers), the command is refused with an explicit "no approval channel" result, never a fake pending.

Fixes #133514

**Merge order:** land after or together with #153418. Its random card ids stop a card left over from before a gateway restart from approving a new command; this PR makes that case easier to hit, because background children post cards after the turn.

Stacked on #153247 (`fix/w5-approval`): this branch is that PR's three commits plus three commits of its own. The background transport uses #153247's `TurnContext` adapter resolver, so a card sent after a reconnect goes through the live adapter.

## Live probe: real `hermes gateway run` + Telegram adapter vs the Bot API stand-in, FakeLLMServer

The parent calls `delegate_task(background=True)` and replies. The child sleeps, then runs `rm -rf <victim>` (`approvals.mode: manual`).

| Leg | `origin/main` (77e16d5f) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| child asks after the parent replied, tap Once | child gets `pending_approval`, **no card**, file kept | card ~7 s after the reply, tap runs it, file gone |
| same, user sends `/approve` | `pending_approval`, `/approve`: nothing pending | `/approve` resolves 1, command runs |
| same, user sends `/deny` | (no card to answer) | `/deny` resolves 1, file kept, child gets BLOCKED |
| card shown while the parent still runs, tapped after the parent replied | card **withdrawn** when the parent ends; tap resolves 0, file kept | tap resolves 1, command runs |
| control: child asks and is answered while the parent turn is still running | works | works |

Head legs re-run on the final head after the review fix: all four pass.

Gateway logs on the head legs: `Exec approval card delivered` … `Telegram button resolved 1 approval(s)` / `User approved 1 dangerous command(s) via /approve` … `Approval wait ended (state=set, resolved=True, choice=once)`.

## Root cause
The parent turn's `finally` in `TurnRunner._run_conversation_with_approval` unregisters the session's approval notifier and wakes every queued wait (`tools/approval.py::unregister_gateway_notify`). A background child asking later found no notifier, so `_human_decision` fell through to `_pending_result`, which writes a store nothing reads and sends no card.

## What changed
- **Lease per background dispatch** (salvaged from #136199, @emi-ran, cherry-picked): `tools/approval_notify_lease.py` gives each `dispatch_async_delegation` unit a lease, bound to the worker through a contextvar. The child's queue entries carry their owner, so a parent turn ending no longer withdraws them. Interrupting the child, finishing it or `clear_session` (`/new`, `/stop`) releases the lease and withdraws its prompts.
- **A transport the turn publishes for its children** (`gateway/run_turn_runner_approval_transport.py`). It captures the chat, thread and the turn's adapter resolver, and renders through `_render_approval_sync(background=True)`. It does not touch the finished turn's typing or stream boundary, and it does not register on the turn's canonical execution generation, which has settled by then and would refuse the prompt. This is the part #136199 could not ship for messaging sessions: there every turn is authority-owned, so its background path failed closed and never sent a card.
- **The child always asks through that transport, even while the parent is still replying.** The prompt never registers on the parent's generation, so the parent settling mid-send cannot turn a delivered card into a failure, and the card stays answerable. Its timeout notice is bound to the child's context, so a newer turn in the chat does not suppress it. The presenter is built without `TurnRunner.__init__`, so no canonical owner can attach.
- **Fail closed where no chat can show the prompt** (credit #133522, @liuhao1024, for the outcome and wording). API-server/webhook/local-viewer turns publish no background transport, and a stranded child request now returns the `notify_failed` denial instead of `pending_approval`. A background text prompt that was not delivered raises, so the wait fails closed. Foreground handling is unchanged, and every `origin/main` approval test passes untouched.
- **Protected instruction files** (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, …): the write gate in `tools/file_tools_write_guards.py` asks through the same `_gateway_notify_cb()` as the command gates, so a child writing one after the parent replied gets a card instead of a refusal (755259e1). The ACP editor consent (`gateway/session_local_editor.py`) uses the same accessor.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/features/delegation.md` § Approvals from background children.

## Salvage
- Salvages #136199 (@emi-ran): commits `b9dad57f` (lease, owner-aware unregister, async dispatch wiring) and the tools half of `43af5210` (session-clear revoke) are cherry-picked with authorship kept. Its email is mapped in `contributors/emails/`.
- Salvages #133522 (@liuhao1024): its fail-closed result is ported as `Co-authored-by`. It was not cherry-picked, because it flipped `origin/main` tests (`test_guard_gateway_missing_notify_is_pending` and others) to fail closed for every gateway session with no notifier. Here it applies only to a background child's lease that has no transport, so those tests stay as they are.

## Dropped hunks
- #136199 `9e783f64` and later: a canonical dispatch-owner authority, exact-ID text-only prompts (`/approve request:<id>`), TUI/OpenRPC contract changes, and Telegram callback rebinding. They are not needed: the background card is a native card bound to its `request_id` (`resolve_gateway_approval_card` already resolves only its own request), and card ids are hardened separately in #153418. A canonical client gets no projection of a background prompt; the chat card and `/approve` are the answer surfaces.
- #136199's change that made every foreground text-prompt failure raise: kept for background prompts only, so foreground behaviour matches main.

## Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_background_child_approval_after_turn.py` (new) goes through the real `TurnRunner._run_conversation_with_approval` and `dispatch_async_delegation`, with the child asking after the parent's run returned. It covers card plus approve or deny, a reconnect after the turn (the card goes through the live adapter), and the API-server child failing closed. Red on base (3/3). Reverting only the `register_gateway_notify(..., approval_transport(self))` call site turns 2 of them red.
- `tests/tools/test_async_approval_lease.py` and `tests/gateway/test_background_approval_transport.py` (salvaged, adapted): approve, deny, timeout, cancel and missing-transport outcomes, cross-chat isolation, independent consent for concurrent children, cancellation of a queued worker, and session-clear revoke.
- `test_child_card_raised_mid_turn_survives_the_parent_settling`: the parent has a canonical owner that refuses once settled. The child's card goes out mid-turn, the parent settles, and a newer turn takes the chat before the 1 s timeout. The test asserts the owner was never consulted, the request stays pending, and the expired card is edited with the timeout notice.
- 153 related files (every test touching the notifier, queue, pending result, async dispatch or clear_session): 2682 passed, 2 skipped (local, fake HOME).

prs.title: memory(retaindb): skip ingest for incognito and burned sessions
prs.body:
## Problem
RetainDB automatic provider ingest leaks incognito-session content into durable memory. Canary-verified on Hermes v0.23.2 + hermes-incognito v1.0.1: an active incognito session was hidden from listings yet its turns were ingested into RetainDB (one memory marked durable).

## Change
- New ingest guard in plugins/memory/retaindb evaluated at BOTH enqueue and flush time (crash-replayed queue rows bypass enqueue):
  - skip sessions with an active hermes-incognito lease (plugin-data/incognito/leases.json, read-only)
  - skip burned sessions: no session row AND no message rows left in state.db (messages-only sessions are NOT misclassified as burned)
  - vetoes at flush delete the queued rows
  - any read failure fails open to prior behavior
- Opt out via memory.retaindb.skip_incognito_sessions (default true).

## Tests
- New tests/plugins/memory/test_retaindb_incognito_gate.py (19 cases incl. lease skip, burned skip, messages-only, fail-open, config disable, flush-time burn, crash replay): 19/19 pass.
- E2E canary through the real provider module + live RetainDB server: control session ingests (raw-store hit), incognito session does not (0 queue rows, 0 store hits), burn purges a pre-existing session memory.

Companion PR: nicolasbuelvas/hermes-incognito#5 (Gate 2: archive purge on burn).

issues.title: [Feature] Add LLMTR as an OpenAI-compatible provider
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

I'd like PicoClaw to ship a named `llmtr` provider in the model catalog.

LLMTR (https://llmtr.com) is an OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://llmtr.com/v1. One key reaches the models in its catalog. I can already point a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint at it, but a built-in catalog entry would let me choose `llmtr` and use `https://llmtr.com/v1` without overwriting another provider's settings.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Add `llmtr` to the provider metadata catalog (the same map as OpenRouter and LiteLLM): default API base `https://llmtr.com/v1`, creatable and usable as a default chat model, with `/models` fetch enabled. I am not proposing a built-in common-model list or a logo; catalog models should be pinned in `model_list`.

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

The change is a new entry in `pkg/providers/provider_metadata.go`, plus the providers guide, README provider tables, and a comment in `pkg/config/defaults.go`. No new HTTP client is needed; `httpAPI: true` uses the existing OpenAI-compatible transport.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

A custom OpenAI-compatible model entry with `api_base` set to `https://llmtr.com/v1` already works. That is what I use today. A named `llmtr` provider would keep those settings separate, the same way the OpenRouter catalog entry does.

## 💬 Additional Context

I am ready to open a PR after this issue. The change does not include a provider logo; a public asset could not be retrieved from llmtr.com for this work.

issues.title: skills install fails with "registry archive is not a valid skill" when another skill shares the frontmatter name
issues.body:
## Summary

`picoclaw skills install` (and the agent's `install_skill` tool) fail with:

```
failed to install "<slug>": registry archive is not a valid skill
```

whenever another already-installed skill uses the same `name` in its
`SKILL.md` frontmatter — even when the two skills are completely different
(different directories, authors and content).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a skill whose frontmatter `name` is `weather`:
   ```bash
   picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather-zhouli
   ```
2. Install a second, different skill that also declares `name: weather`:
   ```bash
   picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather23
   ```
   → fails with `registry archive is not a valid skill`.
3. Remove the first skill and retry → the install succeeds.

Both ClawHub ZIPs contain a byte-identical `SKILL.md`
(md5 `107ea6b0f12a145071ba29153699aa67`), so the failure is caused purely by the
shared `name`.

## Root cause

`pkg/skills/loader.go` → `ListSkills()` deduplicates globally by the frontmatter
`name`:

```go
if seen[info.Name] {
    continue
}
seen[info.Name] = true
```

The install validation re-scans the workspace through `ListSkills()` and then
looks for the newly installed directory:

- `workspaceHasValidInstalledSkill` in `pkg/tools/integration/skills_install.go`
- `workspaceHasValidSkillDirectory` in `cmd/picoclaw/internal/skills/helpers.go`

Because the new skill is deduplicated away (same `name` as an already-installed
skill), the lookup never finds it and the install is reported as invalid.

## Impact

- Two skills sharing a frontmatter `name` cannot be installed together.
- The second skill is also invisible to the agent (not listed, not loadable).
- Reproduced on `v0.3.1` and on `main`.

## Proposed fix

Deduplicate per root instead of globally by name: shadow a `name` only when it
appears in a **higher-priority** root (workspace > global > builtin), and list
distinct directories within the same root:

```go
firstRoot := make(map[string]int)

addSkills := func(dir, source string, rootIdx int) {
    // ... same as before ...
    if r, ok := firstRoot[info.Name]; ok && r != rootIdx {
        continue
    }
    firstRoot[info.Name] = rootIdx
    skills = append(skills, info)
}

// Priority: workspace > global > builtin
addSkills(sl.workspaceSkills, "workspace", 0)
addSkills(sl.globalSkills, "global", 1)
addSkills(sl.builtinSkills, "builtin", 2)
```

Verified locally against `v0.3.1`: with the patch, both `weather` skills install
and are listed, and `install_skill` works.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git `2cf030d2`), Go 1.25.11
- Linux amd64

Happy to open a PR if the fix looks good.

issues.title: [bug] Codex: a brief connection drop fails the reply even though Codex retries and recovers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

080bd7809 (main, 2026-11-21) with Codex 0.169.0

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

When the connection to the model drops for a few seconds in the middle of a turn, Codex sends an `error` event that says it will retry (`willRetry: true`, "Reconnecting... 2/5"), then retries on its own. NanoClaw treats that retry notice as a fatal error. It ends the turn, sends the user "Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer", and marks the message as handled, so it is never tried again. The real answer, which Codex would have given a few seconds later, is lost.

Any short outage can do this: a network blip, or a 502 from the model API or the credential gateway.

Related: #4014 (an earlier fix for the same bug, made for the old `providers` branch) and #3338 (a different retry that Codex does not report at all).

### What did you expect?

A retry notice should not end the turn. The user should get the agent's real reply once Codex reconnects. Only an error that Codex will not retry should fail the turn.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Install NanoClaw with the Codex provider (an OpenAI API key is enough) and a terminal agent.
2. Run `pnpm run chat "Run the shell command: sleep 20 (one call, and wait for it to finish). After it finishes, reply with exactly OK and nothing else."`
3. About 15 seconds in, cut the OneCLI container's outbound HTTPS for about 14 seconds: `sudo iptables -I DOCKER-USER -s <onecli container IP> -p tcp --dport 443 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset`, then remove the rule with `-D`.
4. When `sleep` ends, Codex's next model request gets a 502 and Codex starts to retry. The chat prints the "Sorry, something went wrong" notice instead of `OK`, and the agent container's log shows the turn ending on the retry notice.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64

### Install or update path

Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh

### Docker version

Docker 29.1.3

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Codex

### Agent model

gpt-6.1-sol

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
[poll-loop] Error: Reconnecting... 2/5: unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway: {"error":"resolution_failed","message":"OneCLI gateway failed to resolve rules for this request."}, url: wss://api.openai.com/…
[poll-loop] Error result notice — delivering to channel
[poll-loop] Errored batch will be acked completed — 1 message(s), no redelivery
```

### Last version that worked

_No response_

### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0 (main 080bd7809)

### Host platform

### What happened?

Codex agents fail when the OpenAI sign-in stored in the gateway stops working (a revoked API key, or a ChatGPT login whose refresh token was revoked). The add-codex skill's Troubleshooting says to re-run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`. That step prints "Your OpenAI account is already connected." and returns without a sign-in, so nothing changes and the agents keep failing.

The auth step only checks that the gateway holds a Codex secret (`store.has('codex')` in `.claude/skills/add-codex/payload/setup/providers/codex.ts`), not that the secret still works. Closed PR #2878 tried a fix on the old `providers` branch and was never merged.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Install NanoClaw with OneCLI, then Codex (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`).
2. Make the stored Codex secret stale: revoke the OpenAI API key, or store an invalid key as the OneCLI secret named `Codex`.
3. Message a Codex agent. The reply is the failure notice, and the container log shows `401 Unauthorized ... wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses`.
4. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex` again.
5. It prints "Your OpenAI account is already connected." and exits 0 with no sign-in prompt.

issues.title: [bug] Codex: a sub-agent finishing ends the main agent's turn early

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

080bd7809 (main, 2026-11-21) with Codex 0.169.0

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

When a Codex agent starts a sub-agent (Codex's built-in `spawn_agent` tool), NanoClaw treats the sub-agent's events as if they came from the main agent. When the sub-agent finishes, NanoClaw ends the main agent's turn and takes the sub-agent's text as the turn's result.

In our live test the user still got the right answer, by luck: the sub-agent's text had no `<message>` block, so nothing was sent, the runner pushed a "nothing was sent" nudge, and that nudge's turn picked up the main agent's real answer. Unit tests show cases that fail outright:

- if the sub-agent's turn fails, the main turn fails with the sub-agent's error;
- a message the user sends while the sub-agent runs is aimed at the sub-agent's turn;
- stopping the agent interrupts the sub-agent, not the main agent.

### What did you expect?

Only the main agent's own events should end its turn or become its reply. Sub-agent work should only count as activity.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Install NanoClaw with the Codex provider (an OpenAI API key is enough) and a terminal agent.
2. Run `pnpm run chat "Use spawn_agent to start one sub-agent that replies with exactly CHILD-1. Wait for it with wait_agent. Then reply: PARENT saw <its reply>."`
3. Read the agent container's log: `docker logs <ncl-... container>`.
4. You see `Result: CHILD-1` (the sub-agent's text) and "Wrap-nudge pushed" before the main agent's own result.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64

### Install or update path

Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh

### Docker version

Docker 29.1.3

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Codex

### Agent model

gpt-6.1-sol

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
[poll-loop] Result: CHILD-a2534a
[poll-loop] WARNING: agent output had no <message to="..."> blocks — nothing was sent
[poll-loop] Wrap-nudge pushed: nothing was sent this turn
[poll-loop] Result: <message to="local-cli">PARENT-2027e6 saw CHILD-a2534a.</message>
```

### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0 (also main 080bd7809)

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

`/update-nanoclaw` stops at `prepare` with a raw git failure (see logs) when the install is not on a branch. This happens after `git checkout v2026.11.0`, and on installs made by the e2e tools, which check out the commit under test detached.

The updater has a clearer message for this case, "Update requires a named branch, not detached HEAD", but never reaches it. `git symbolic-ref --quiet` exits 1 on a detached HEAD, so the call throws first (`currentBranch` in `scripts/update/transaction.ts`).

When the detached commit is newer than the latest release, the default stable channel fails even earlier with `ahead-of-release` and asks the user to pick a channel. The branch problem only shows up on the next run.

### What did you expect?

A plain error, before any channel question, that says HEAD is detached, where (the tag or commit), and the one command that fixes it. For example:

`Update needs a branch, but HEAD is detached at tag v2026.11.0. Make one here, then run the update again: git switch -c nanoclaw`

### How can we reproduce it?

1. `git clone https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw.git && cd nanoclaw`
2. `git checkout v2026.11.0`
3. Run `/update-nanoclaw` (or, after `pnpm install`: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts prepare --project-root "$PWD" --remote origin`)
4. See the `git symbolic-ref` error in the logs below.

macOS 26.6.1, arm64

### Install or update path

Something else

_No response_

Not channel-specific

Not provider-specific

_No response_

```shell
{
  "schema": "nanoclaw-update-error/v1",
  "error": "Command failed: git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD"

```

None. It has failed this way since the transactional updater landed (8772ec977).

issues.title: [bug] Telegram: voice notes reach the agent as plain audio, not as voice notes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0, with `channels` at 4a036385 (`@chat-adapter/telegram` 4.41.1)

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

A Telegram voice note reaches the host as an `audio` attachment, the same as a music file. Nothing marks it as a voice note:

- The agent sees it as plain audio, so it can't tell a voice note from a song.
- `isVoiceNote` is never set, so a transcription step that looks for it skips Telegram voice notes.

WhatsApp (since #4378) and iMessage mark voice notes with `type: 'voice'`, so Telegram is the odd one out.

The type is lost in the Telegram adapter package. `@chat-adapter/telegram` 4.41.1 builds both `message.voice` and `message.audio` with `createAttachment("audio", ...)` (`dist/index.js:2788`). Core's Chat SDK bridge passes that type on and keeps only a fixed set of attachment fields, so a voice flag can't be added after the bridge either.

### What did you expect?

A Telegram voice note arrives as `type: 'voice'` with `isVoiceNote: true`, like a WhatsApp voice note. A music file stays `audio`.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Install Telegram with `/add-telegram` (adapter 4.41.1).
2. Send the bot a voice note (hold the mic button), then send it an audio file.
3. Look at the attachments of the two inbound messages, or at the attachment lines in the agent's prompt.
4. Both are `type: "audio"`, and neither has `isVoiceNote`.

A test that sends both updates through the real adapter and bridge, with only the Telegram API faked, shows the same result.

### Install or update path

Development checkout

### Channel or interface

Telegram

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

issues.title: [bug] verify-agent-image fails when the old image pin can no longer be read

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main `a4903adb3`, `.github/workflows/verify-agent-image.yml`, step "Size delta is plausible". Seen on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4512 (run https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/actions/runs/44823655374).

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

The `verify` job failed on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4512, the main to channels sync. The sync moved the `channels` pin in `agent-images.json` from the 10-21 image to main's 11-14 image. The new image passed every real check: both platforms, lock matches, hardened. Then the size step ran `docker buildx imagetools inspect --raw` on the old 10-21 digest and got nothing back. The Python one-liner crashed with `JSONDecodeError`, and that failed the job.

### What did you expect?

If the old image can't be read, the size step should skip its comparison and pass. It is a rough tripwire, and its own guard already skips the check when the old size is 0.

### How can we reproduce it?

Open a PR that changes a pin in `agent-images.json` whose old digest can no longer be read from the registry. For example, merge main into a branch whose pin is several image rebuilds old, as #4512 did.

### Relevant redacted logs

```
Size delta is plausible | json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Size delta is plausible | ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

### Last version that worked

Not a regression. It only shows when the old image is gone, and the usual bump PRs (for example https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4500) compare against a recent image that still exists.

Fix idea: in `total()`, don't let a failed inspect crash. Add `|| true` after the `docker buildx imagetools inspect` call, and have the Python print 0 for empty input. `O=0` then skips the check through the existing `[ "$O" -gt 0 ]` guard.

issues.title: [bug] Agent image runs Claude Code 2.1.321, which misses resume and compaction fixes from 2.1.322 to 2.1.330

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
