issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0 (main at 7e5406d6a)

### Host platform

Any (the agent container is Linux)

### What happened?

Agent containers run Claude Code 2.1.321 with Agent SDK 0.3.321 (`container/cli-tools.json`, `container/agent-runner/package.json`). Claude Code's [changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) fixes these bugs in 2.1.322 to 2.1.330. Each is on a path our runner takes: it resumes the session on every container start, runs the NanoClaw MCP server from the SDK, auto-compacts long sessions, and reaches the API through the gateway proxy.

- 2.1.325: recent turns could go missing from a resumed session after Claude Code stopped without a clean exit.
- 2.1.327: headless sessions could lose stored messages on resume when a message was sent again with the same UUID after the process was killed.
- 2.1.330: `--resume` could open an empty session or fail when the last saved message had a missing or invalid timestamp.
- 2.1.328: automatic compaction reused the session's earlier system prompt instead of rebuilding it.
- 2.1.325: MCP tool calls from an SDK host could answer "Not connected" after the server had reconnected.
- 2.1.327: `claude -p` could hang before its first request when the fetch of a model's settings stalled at a proxy.

2.1.325 also fixes a security issue in how zstd-compressed responses are decoded.

### What did you expect?

The agent image runs a Claude Code release with these fixes.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. On main, read `container/cli-tools.json`: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` is `2.1.321`.
2. Compare with the 2.1.322 to 2.1.330 entries in Claude Code's changelog.

We have not reproduced each bug on NanoClaw itself.

### Agent provider

Claude

issues.title: [hardening] Restamp reads agent-writable files by path after a type check

labels.name: kind/hardening
labels.description: Defense-in-depth improvement; not exploitable across a trust boundary

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I confirm that this is not an exploitable vulnerability and can be discussed in public.

### What should be safer?

When a group already carries a plugin, `ncl groups create --template <ref>` plans an in-place update (restamp). The plan compares files that the agent container can write with the template's copies, in two places in `src/templates/restamp.ts`:

- Context files in the group folder (line 193): `statSync(target).isFile()`, then `readFileSync(target)`.
- Skill overlay files in `dirsEqual` (line 498): `lstatSync` while listing, then `readFileSync` on each path.

Both read by path after the check, so the check and the read can see two different files:

- If the agent swaps the file for a named pipe between the two calls, the read waits on the host's event loop. That is the hang GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj describes for the persona and provider files, fixed in #4440.
- `statSync` follows symlinks, so a context file replaced by a symlink is read through to its target for the compare.

This is narrower than the advisory. Restamp runs only when an operator starts or approves it, and the swap has to land between two calls.

Proposed: read both through one helper that opens with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, checks `fstat().isFile()` on the descriptor, and treats anything else as absent. That is how `readGroupPersona` reads `instructions.prepend.md` since #4440.

Suggested by @amit-shafnir while reviewing the fix for GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj.

### How can we verify the concern?

1. Stamp a group from a template that ships a context file and a skill.
2. Swap the context file (or a skill overlay file) for a named pipe at the moment restamp opens or reads it. A unit test can force this timing with a hook on `fs.openSync` and `fs.readFileSync`.
3. Run the restamp plan (`apply: false`).
4. On main the plan blocks until another process opens the pipe for writing.

For the symlink case, replace the context file with a symlink to a file that holds the new template's text. The plan reports the file as "unchanged".

Needs no host access or unsafe configuration. The agent only writes in its own group folder.

### Affected version

v2026.11.0 (main at 7e5406d6a)

### AI assistance

Yes. I verified it myself and can explain it

### AI assistance details

Claude Code wrote the test that reproduces it and drafted this text.

### Related trust boundary

Filesystem mounts

issues.title: [bug] Claude token parser can return a too-long token when the terminal repaints its end

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit
7e5406d6a (main)

### Host platform
macOS

### What happened?
`setup/lib/captured-token.ts` deletes escape codes from the `claude setup-token` capture and then joins what is left. If the terminal moves the cursor back and prints the end of the token again, both copies stay. The parsed token gets longer and is wrong. Setup then saves a token that can't call Claude.

### What did you expect?
The parser returns the token as the terminal shows it.

### How can we reproduce it?
1. `T="sk-ant-oat01-$(printf 'Ab3_-%.0s' $(seq 1 19))xyzAA"` (113 characters)
2. `printf '%s\033[5DxyzAA\r\n' "$T" > /tmp/cap` (cursor back 5 columns, same 5 characters again)
3. `pnpm exec tsx setup/lib/captured-token.ts claude /tmp/cap | wc -c`
4. It prints 118, not 113.

### Additional context
Found while building Sign in with Claude for NanoClaw Desktop, which had the same parser. The desktop fix reads the token from its terminal emulator's screen, with the old parser as a fallback. The parser is used by `add-onecli/scripts/register-claude-token.sh`, `add-iron-proxy/scripts/capture-claude-token.sh` and `setup/lib/claude-assist.ts`.

Suggested fix: one helper that runs the capture and replays it through a terminal emulator, because a correct read needs the terminal's width.

prs.title: feat(providers): add pi agent provider (/add-pi payload skill)
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - README, CONTRIBUTING, or docs only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (pi Coding Agent) as an optional agent provider, installable with the `/add-pi` skill. This is the restructured version of #3857, which targeted the `providers` branch. It now ships the way `/add-opencode` does on `main`: the skill carries its provider as a payload and needs no separate branch.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 1.3.0). No `pi serve` process and no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in process (stdio + Streamable HTTP, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, JSON-Schema `pattern` stripped because some model APIs reject the regex dialects MCP servers ship).
- `payload/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (host) + `payload/container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (runtime) — seam version 1. The host contract declares the `AGENTS.md` project document, the group's `.pi-shared` state volume mounted at the agentDir, pi's skill backings/views, and the `auth.json` stub file; the runtime contract declares the permission stance, `textDelivery: 'result'`, and XML slash-command formatting.
- `payload/setup/providers/pi.ts` — the setup picker entry, gateway auth hook, and install check.
- `payload/src/providers/pi.ts` — the host container-config adapter (`PI_AGENT_DIR`, plus optional `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS` / `PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` / `PI_DEFAULT_MODEL`).

**How the review points from #3857 are handled**

1. **Payload skill on `main`.** The whole provider lives under `.claude/skills/add-pi/` (`SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `REMOVE.md`, `apply-fixtures.json`, `payload/`). `SKILL.md` is a parser-applyable set of `nc:` directives: copy the payload, append five barrel imports (host/container providers, host/container contracts, setup), install the pinned runner dependency, build, test. No branch fetch, no `PI_REF`, no per-group overlay propagation. `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` lists the newly offered skill.
2. **Credentials come through the gateway.** No personal `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` is copied anywhere. The container writes fixed `gateway-managed` placeholders into the group's pi agentDir before each session open (`payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi-auth.ts`), and the selected gateway replaces them on the wire by destination host. ChatGPT subscription auth is pi's `openai-codex` provider, which reuses the gateway's Codex/ChatGPT login; because pi decodes the access token for the account id, the placeholder is a syntactically valid JWT carrying the placeholder claim. API-key providers get a placeholder `api_key` entry, and `provider-auth pi` stores the real key through `getCredentialStore().connection(target)` (observing the entry first, as the seam requires), recording the provider ids in `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS`. A real login already in the agentDir is never overwritten.
3. **`bun.lock` / npm registry.** The skill no longer commits `container/agent-runner/package.json` or `bun.lock`; the pinned dependency is installed at apply time by the `nc:dep` directive, and the pin is registered in `.github/skill-pins` so Dependabot tracks it and `skill-pins:sync` writes future bumps back into SKILL.md. Locally regenerating that install against the default npm registry produces a lock with zero `registry.npmmirror.com` URLs (the #3857 lock had 260).

**Model selection follows the SDK, not a hardcoded id.** Model ids change between pi releases (0.85.1 ships `deepseek-v4-flash`; 1.3.0 calls it `deepseek-flash`), so the provider resolves the start provider/model from pi's own runtime catalog (`getAvailableSnapshot` / `getModel`) and writes that into `settings.json`. Operator-authored values are never overwritten. Verified across both versions with no code change.

**Two things a reviewer should know**

- **The secret still has to be granted to the agent.** The credential seam stores secrets but never assigns them, and `/add-opencode` has the same manual step ("follow the selected gateway skill to grant it to agents"). OneCLI's `secretMode` is `selective`, so an ungranted key reaches the provider as `401 access restricted`. SKILL.md documents it.
- **Setup's own ping is not proof the model call worked.** It reports "Your assistant is ready" whenever the chat command exits 0 with any output, and a failed pi turn answers with the generic "The agent run failed" notice. Verify with a real reply and `continuation:pi` instead; SKILL.md says so explicitly.

**How it was tested**

- `scripts/provider-contract-verifier.ts --required-declared pi` — **passed** (host deps, runtime deps, host build, host provider-contract tests, runtime typecheck, runtime provider-contract tests, host/runtime contract inventories, runtime conformance test files).
- Container suite: **673 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**. Host suite: **3613 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**. `skill-pins:check` clean.
- End-to-end on a fresh clone of this branch: `bash nanoclaw.sh` → pick pi → DeepSeek key stored in the gateway → skill applied (14 files, 5 barrels, pin 1.3.0, image SDK 1.3.0) → group switched to pi → real reply, session continuation, and `continuation:pi` in the session's `outbound.db` `session_state`. A WeChat channel was installed onto the same install afterwards, so the channel/provider split was exercised too.
- Testing was done against a OneCLI gateway at 1.45.0 (newer than the 1.42.0 pin in `/add-onecli`), so the grant step used its `PUT /v1/agents/<id>/grants/secrets/<id>` API. This payload itself calls no gateway management API — only the credential seam — so the pinned 1.42.0 gateway is unaffected.

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Configure credentials with `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth pi` (ChatGPT via the gateway's Codex login, or a stored API key), then grant the secret per the gateway's skill. Model selection lives in the group's `data/v2-sessions/<group>/.pi-shared/settings.json`.

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow was stuck in `action_required` on #3857 (first-time contributor). It needs a maintainer approval click to run here too. #3857 is superseded by this PR; it can stay open until this one merges.

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased after #4104 (`/add-codex` payload), #4107 (`/add-cursor` payload), #4105, #4106 and #3980 landed. Two conflicts, both list-append in shared files: `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` now expects `codex, cursor, opencode, pi`, and `.github/skill-pins/package.json` carries this branch's pin alongside upstream's.

Upstream changes that touch this work, checked rather than assumed:

- **#3980 (first-chat ping)** fixed the very problem SKILL.md used to warn about: a failed pi turn's notice is now scored as a failed first chat instead of a green result. The doc now states the post-#3980 behaviour.
- **#4105 (shared exchange archive)** is for providers whose harness keeps no on-disk transcript. pi's session JSONL *is* its transcript — the continuation token is that file's path — so it needs no archiver, unlike Codex.
- **#4106 (credential connection path)** is unnecessary here: pi's provider entry is a key on exactly one host, so host-scoped injection is what we want.
- **#4104 / #4107** moved Codex and Cursor to the same payload-skill shape this PR uses, so the structure now matches three siblings.

Verification on the rebased branch: container `bun run typecheck` clean and the pi suites at 65 pass; host `tsc --noEmit` clean; host `vitest run` has one failure in `setup/gateways/selection.test.ts` ("detects an installed gateway from inside a nested pnpm") that reproduces on a clean `upstream/main` tree with this payload removed — it is a pre-existing flake under parallel load, not a regression here.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (274)
- [x] I tested this skill by applying it onto current `main`, running the provider-contract verifier, and completing a real end-to-end install on a fresh clone

prs.title: fix(mailbox): skip completed history when polling for new messages
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

This keeps the runner from reading through a session’s history every time it checks for new messages.

- **What I hit** — I tracked this down in a long-running DM on my install. It had about 42,000 messages. A single poll on copies of its databases went from 110.1 ms to 3.3 ms with the fix.
- **What changed** — The host adds an index so the runner can go straight to pending messages in order. The runner then checks acknowledgements only for those message IDs. Existing sessions get the index the next time the host opens their mailbox.

## Related work

Refs #3289. That issue and the earlier #3291 cover a large backlog of messages still waiting to be processed. I could hit this with just one new chat message and a lot of completed history. This PR still reads all due pending messages, so I’d leave #3289 open.

The merged #4245 shrinks old recurring-task payloads and keeps the rows for task stats. The open #4384 tackles similar reads on the host. This change handles the poll inside the container.

My other PR, #4534, clears late `ncl` replies. The two edits meet in the same function, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. I tried them together locally and all 14 message-selection tests passed.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- On upstream `main` and this branch, I timed 61 polls with 40,000 completed chats, their acknowledgements and one pending chat in memory. The median went from 7.65 ms to 0.02 ms. Every poll returned the new chat.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/mailbox` passed all 46 host mailbox tests, including index use on fresh and upgraded inboxes.
- `bun test --isolate` in `container/agent-runner` passed 691 tests with 3 skipped. The new cases check the actual acknowledgement query plan and message selection across lookup batches.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` both passed.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Checking for new messages is faster in long-running sessions with lots of completed history.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The host creates the inbox index. The runner uses its existing read-only access to the inbox and binds message IDs as SQL parameters.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-antigravity with its own payload
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-antigravity`, a provider skill that runs agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Gemini models, switchable per group with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`.
- **Problem**: there is no way to run a NanoClaw agent on Gemini through Google's own agent harness; OpenCode reaches Gemini models but not Antigravity's tools, planning and conversation store.
- **Fix**: a provider skill shaped like `/add-cursor`. All code and tests live in the skill's `payload/`; apply wires the five provider barrels and adds a pinned, sha512-checked `agy` 1.5.8 to the agent image. Auth is a Gemini API key held only by the credential gateway; the container sees a placeholder.
- **Out of scope**: Google-account (OAuth) sign-in, which Google's terms do not allow from a third-party harness; a generic manifest for native binaries (see "Core changes" below).

<details>
<summary>Core changes outside the skill, and why</summary>

agy is a native Go binary that is not published on npm, so `container/cli-tools.json` (npm only) cannot install it. The block has to run as root, before the setuid sweep and `USER node`, and is best placed above the often-bumped layers so a lockfile or Claude Code bump does not re-download 265 MB. No existing hook does that, so this PR adds one:

- `container/Dockerfile`: an empty `# >>> nanoclaw:provider-binaries` / `# <<< nanoclaw:provider-binaries` marker region just above `# ---- agent-runner deps`. With nothing installed it changes no layer.
- `docs/skill-directives.md`, `scripts/skill-directives.ts` (comment), `docs/skill-guidelines.md`, `docs/skills-model.md`: one line each naming the region as the native-binary path.
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: the scratch root gets a stub Dockerfile carrying the region, the same way it already stubs `cli-tools.json`.

Alternatives considered: a prose-only Dockerfile edit like `/add-mnemon` breaks setup's deterministic provider install (`setup/providers/install.ts` fails on any step it cannot apply); appending at end of file with `USER root`/`USER node` breaks on remove, which deletes by line and would also delete core's own `USER node`. A `json-merge` manifest for native binaries (url + sha512 per arch) would be cleaner long term but is a bigger core feature. I'm happy to split the marker into its own PR first, or to rework it into a manifest, if you prefer.

Other edits: the `registry-skills.yml` matrix entry, the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`, `.github/skill-pins/not-covered.json` (regenerated; `AGY_VERSION=1.5.8` now appears as a hand-checked binary pin), and README (Antigravity listed next to Codex, Cursor and OpenCode).

```release-note
New /add-antigravity skill: run agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (Gemini models) with a Gemini API key held by the credential gateway.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials:** the Gemini key goes only to the credential gateway, through `getCredentialStore().connection()` with a `GatewayCredentialTarget` that sets `provider: 'antigravity'`. Containers get `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, which agy sends as `x-goog-api-key`; the gateway swaps it for the real key on the wire. The key is never in `.env`, container env, argv, mounts or logs. The live runs scanned for it and found it nowhere.
- **Supply chain:** one exact build (1.5.8, execution id 4602374149505024) downloaded from `storage.googleapis.com`, a sha512 pinned per architecture and checked with `sha512sum -c` before extraction, a `--version` check that fails the build, and auto-update forced off. The tarballs are byte-identical to the assets on Google's GitHub release.
- **Egress:** model domains are `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` (agy telemetry, which 1.5.8 cannot turn off in API-key mode). Requests from antigravity groups pass without an approval card; with Iron Proxy, model domains are allowed install-wide (as for other providers).
- **Permissions:** agy runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and its terminal sandbox off (it needs user namespaces, which Docker's seccomp profile blocks), so the container is the boundary, as with the other providers. The image still ends as `node`, with no setuid binaries.
- **Prompt injection:** per-session instructions go in-band as a `<nanoclaw_system_context>` block in agy's first turn. Core's formatter escapes `<` in inbound text, so a chat message cannot forge that block.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keep abandoned `ncl` replies from taking up space in the next batch of messages for an agent.

- **Problem** — The CLI stops waiting after 30 seconds. A host reply that arrives later can stay pending and repeatedly take a slot that would otherwise hold conversation context.
- **Fix** — During the existing SQLite poll, exclude pending `cli_response` system messages older than ten minutes and acknowledge up to 500 per poll. Recent CLI replies and interactive question answers stay available to their callers.

## Related work

Related to #2976, which addresses repeated wakes from late interactive question answers. CLI replies already have their wake flag cleared. This fixes their effect on batch selection.

- `bun test --isolate src/db/messages-in.test.ts` passed all 12 tests. The regressions cover recent replies, older question answers, malformed rows, and 501 expired replies draining over two polls while real context remains available on both.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passed.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Confirm a WhatsApp link only after setup can verify the saved pairing.

- **Problem** — Baileys can open the socket before the final credentials write finishes. Setup could report success and exit `0` even if that write later failed.
- **Fix** — Give socket shutdown and outstanding writes a shared five-second deadline, including writes started before a pairing reconnect. Verify the saved account, then flush the terminal status to the setup wizard before exiting.

## Related work

The pairing tests use a simulated Baileys socket and exercise a slow write across reconnects, a rejected or hung write, a final update during shutdown, and delayed status delivery.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Make OneCLI setup exit non-zero when its gateway readiness check fails.

- **Problem**: `run()` rejects after emitting `STATUS: failed`, but the shared logger handles unhandled rejections without setting a failing exit code. Setup can therefore exit 0 and let the skill driver continue.
- **Fix**: catch rejections at the OneCLI CLI entry point, log the error, and set `process.exitCode = 1`.
- **Coverage**: launch the real setup CLI against loopback fixtures for a 404, a dropped `/v1/health` connection, and a healthy gateway. The tests use a disposable HOME and a fake OneCLI CLI.

## Related work

Closes #4408.

#4303 changes the entry-point path guard and leaves `void run(...)` unchanged. This changes the invocation inside that guard; the adjacent edits may need coordination.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Against unchanged main at `c0ec12952e8d9a4ebbd869015010daac804d5d11`, `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/readiness.test.ts` -> 2 failed, 3 passed. Both failing gateways emitted `STATUS: failed` but exited 0.
- With this fix, the same file -> 5 passed. Failed readiness exits 1; healthy readiness exits 0.
- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts setup/gateways setup/installer-shell.test.ts scripts/skill-apply.test.ts scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts scripts/skill-pins.test.ts` -> 639 passed in 18 files on Node 22.22.0 and Node 24.18.0, macOS, fresh clone.
- Host `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc` -> pass.
- Separate strict TypeScript check of `setup.ts` and `readiness.test.ts` -> pass; the root tsconfig does not include these files.
- Prettier on both changed files and `pnpm run format:check` -> pass.
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors, 209 warnings in unchanged `src/` files.
- `git diff --check` -> pass.
- Live OneCLI installation, Linux, and the full repository/container suites were not run. The CLI regression exercises reuse; the shared entry-point catch also handles rejected remote and fresh-install runs.

prs.title: fix: drop stale "Global Memory" instruction from main seed prompt
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What:** Removes the stale `## Global Memory` section from the main group's seed prompt (`groups/main/CLAUDE.md`).

**Why:** It instructed the agent to "read and write `/workspace/global/CLAUDE.md`", a path that no longer exists after the c8fc1da cutover (the mount was removed and `groups/global/` is deleted on every host boot). There is no agent-writable global-memory replacement (the shared base `container/CLAUDE.md` is read-only / host-managed), so an agent that followed the instruction would silently write to an unmounted, ephemeral path.

**How:** Delete the section (heading, body, and its trailing separator). The preceding `---` is kept, so the surrounding markdown stays well-formed.

**Tested:** `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes; the change is prompt-only markdown and no test references the section.

Related to #2312 (part of the same c8fc1da cutover cleanup).

Updates `vitest` from 5.0.5 to 5.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from vitest's releases.

v5.1.0

   🚀 Features

  • Add --last-failed to run only failed tests  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11558 (82f63)
  • Support Temporal.Instant and Temporal.ZonedDateTime in vi.setSystemTime()  -  by @​Prajwal2246, Prajwal2246, Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context), @​hi-ogawa and Codex (GPT-6) in vitest-dev/vitest#11321 (f150f)
  • Introduce --since-last-run flag  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11516 (08bd9)
  • Expose per-retry/repeat attempt result  -  by @​hi-ogawa, Codex (GPT-6) and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11232 (21be4)
  • Support fake timers for node:timers and node:timers/promise  -  by @​hi-ogawa, OpenCode and Codex (GPT-6) in vitest-dev/vitest#10899 (fbe97)
  • Allow coverage providers to store data in fs module cache  -  by @​AriPerkkio in vitest-dev/vitest#11747 (54a2b)
  • Interactively review failed snapshots  -  by @​macarie and @​hi-ogawa in vitest-dev/vitest#11325 (54e5b)
  • browser:
    • Mock modules through an import map  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11534 (707f8)
    • Drop experimental label from trace view  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11518 (44c3c)
    • Introduce experimental pointer API  -  by @​macarie in vitest-dev/vitest#10780 (5dc09)
    • Capture aria snapshot in trace view  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11492 (0cc39)
    • Show trace steps timeline on terminal on test failure  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11594 (973dc)
    • Add failure-only trace view mode  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11612 (d5d7d)
    • Enable failure-only trace view by default  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11766 (f37b6)
  • coverage:
    • V8 to support ignoreNode option  -  by @​erickserra and @​AriPerkkio in vitest-dev/vitest#11688 (e02db)
  • experimental:
    • Add trace timeline for node  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11753 (4e985)
    • Add message option to vi.waitFor and vi.waitUntil  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11754 (fd145)

   🐞 Bug Fixes

  • Rerun setup files after --changed filtering  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11621 (3a39c)
  • Return the mock to concurrent imports  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11623 (1453b)
  • Don't fail on console log pending at teardown  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11619 (a60b8)
  • Reference chai types in every d.ts chunk  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11618 (fb150)
  • Detect mock factory cycles that form later  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11642 (e9554)
  • Skip fs module cache for typed import.meta.glob  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11666 (79501)
  • Run tests that import a deleted file  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11669 (80aa1)
  • Keep syntax highlighting in code frames  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11705 (d39f5)
  • Respect CLI filters when prewarming browsers  -  by @​sheremet-va and Benjamin Tang in vitest-dev/vitest#11706 (10947)
  • Read cached source as utf-8  -  by @​juan-fernandez in vitest-dev/vitest#11682 and vitest-dev/vitest#11709 (867a5)
  • Inherit watch from the root config in projects  -  by @​nstepien and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11724 (77c12)
  • Prefix expect.poll message to all errors  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11756 (cab58)
  • Support api.port 0  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11641 (3667c)
  • Show attempts in test error logs of retried tests  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11696 (77a94)
  • Preserve rootDir in project paths  -  by @​btea in vitest-dev/vitest#11816 (bf96d)
  • browser:
    • Change default port to 23315  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11640 (a2ec4)
    • Advance fake timers in actions and expect.element  -  by @​julienw, @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11242 (68190)
    • Drop trace view warning without html reporter  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11665 (e6407)
    • Detect shared chunks via the optimizer  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11661 (e2e9c)
    • Clear screenshot stability timeout  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11659 (fbe37)
    • Measure prepare duration with one clock  -  by @​sheremet-va in vitest-dev/vitest#11667 (a3ed4)
    • Keep failure screenshot per attempt  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11694 (a5022)
    • Print trace timeline of each attempt  -  by @​hi-ogawa and Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in vitest-dev/vitest#11695 (27229)

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep the turn open on an error Codex will retry
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A short model outage that Codex retries on its own no longer fails the reply.

- **Problem**: before each automatic retry, Codex sends `error` with `willRetry: true` ([`bespoke_event_handling.rs:1083-1100`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1083-L1100)). `runOneTurn` ended the turn on every `error`. So a 502 or network blip failed the reply with "Reconnecting... 2/5" while Codex went on, and the message was acked with no retry.
- **Fix**: a `willRetry: true` error yields a `progress` event and leaves the turn open. Text the broken stream left half-written is dropped. A completed message stays only if it is an answer: a final answer or an unphased message, the same rule as Codex's turn summary ([`thread_state.rs:243-251`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_state.rs#L243-L251)). So commentary like "Checking the sample." is not kept as the reply (found by @poisdahl). Any other error still ends the turn.
- **From #4014** (by @poisdahl, carried over as their commit): `turn/completed` counts as a reply only with `status: 'completed'`. This is a guard: Codex 0.169.0 sets `failed` only with an error, which main already handles, and `interrupted` only after NanoClaw aborts.
- **10-minute limit (unchanged)**: Codex retries a lost connection without limit ([`responses_retry.rs:96-118`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs#L96-L118)). In a long outage the turn now ends at the existing 10-minute limit, not at the first retry. #4254 replaces that limit with an inactivity budget.
- **Not fixed**: Codex sends no notice for the first WebSocket retry ([`responses_retry.rs:146-160`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs#L146-L160)); that is #3338.
- **Not changed**: when commentary is the last thing the agent says before the turn ends, it is still the reply, as on main. Only a retry after it drops it.

## Related work

Closes #4530. Carries #4014.

Stacked on #4165, which changes the same handler. When #4165 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to main.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- add-codex container suites with the payload applied: 222 pass, `tsc -p container/agent-runner` clean; the 2 failures are the `cli-tools.json` tests the quick harness can't merge (main fails the same 2). `test-registry-skills.ts add-codex`: PASS.
- Tests in `codex.turns.test.ts`: a retry keeps the turn open and takes steered input; a completed answer survives a retry, even with commentary after it; half-written text, commentary, a partial answer and blank text do not; non-retried errors end the turn; a sub-agent's retry leaves the main turn alone; non-`completed` statuses fail; the turn deadline still applies during retries.
- Live on exe.dev (Codex 0.169.0, OpenAI API key, public wizard install of main `080bd7809`), OpenAI cut off for 14 s mid-turn: on main the first retry notice ended the turn and the user got "Sorry, something went wrong". With this PR, 4 retries showed as progress and the real reply arrived once the connection was back. A turn that spawns a sub-agent still ends with the main agent's answer.
- CI on this stacked PR runs only `label`, `template-compliance` and `verify`; the full suites run once it targets main.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Codex agents no longer fail a reply when the model connection drops briefly and Codex reconnects on its own. If it stays down, the reply fails at the 10-minute turn limit instead of right away. Thanks @poisdahl (#4014).
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. The change only affects provider event handling.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: add-codex changes `codex.ts` and its test in place. There are no new files, barrel lines or dependencies. `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes it.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep sub-agent thread events out of the parent turn
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex agents that start sub-agents keep their own turn: a sub-agent's events no longer end, fill or redirect it.

- **Problem**: Codex 0.169.0 (the current pin) streams every sub-agent thread it spawns on the same app-server connection ([`app-server/src/lib.rs:1349-1367`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs#L1349-L1367)), and sub-agents are on by default. `runOneTurn` ignored `threadId`. So a sub-agent's `turn/completed` or `error` ended the main turn, its `turn/started` moved the turn id that steer and interrupt target, and its text could become the reply.
- **Fix**: events from another thread now only yield `activity`, so the host doesn't mark a waiting parent stale. Codex always tags these events (`threadId` is required, e.g. [`ErrorNotification`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/notification.rs#L59-L69)); untagged events work as before. prs.title: fix(update): say where a detached HEAD is and how to fix it
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`/update-nanoclaw` on a detached HEAD now says where HEAD is and how to fix it, instead of failing with a raw `git symbolic-ref` error.

- **Problem**: `git symbolic-ref --quiet` exits 1 on a detached HEAD, so `prepare` threw "Command failed: git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD" before reaching its own branch message. When the detached commit was newer than the latest release, the stable channel failed even earlier with `ahead-of-release` and asked a channel question instead.
- **Fix**: read the branch with `git branch --show-current` (empty when detached) and refuse with `Update needs a branch, but HEAD is detached at tag v2026.11.0. Make a branch here with a name that is not taken yet, then run the update again. For example: git switch -c nanoclaw` (or `at commit <sha>`). CLI `prepare` runs this check before channel resolution, so `prepare` fetches nothing and no channel question comes first.
- **Reach**: the skill runs the controller from upstream `main`, so every install gets the new message on its next `/update-nanoclaw` after merge.
- **Out of scope**: updating while detached (the updater still needs a branch), and a checkout detached by hand between `prepare` and `cutover`, which main does not check either.

## Related work

Closes #4525

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New test in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`: `prepare` on a checkout detached at an annotated tag, then at a bare commit, names each one and creates no transaction, backup branch or tag. Fails on main with the raw error.
- New test in `scripts/update/channel.test.ts` runs the real controller CLI on a checkout detached at a commit newer than the latest release. It gets the branch message, not `ahead-of-release`, and fetches nothing. Fails on main, and fails again with only the CLI check removed.
- `scripts/update` tests: 131/131 pass. Prettier clean.
- Codex adversarial review, 3 rounds: 3 findings fixed (check order, stderr parsing, fetch proof in the test). The rest were refuted or left as minor: the cutover gap above is on main too, and `nanoclaw.sh` already needs git 2.22 for `--show-current`.
- E2E on a fresh exe.dev VM: headless install of main 080bd7809 (Claude, OneCLI, `PING: ok`), which leaves the checkout detached. Ran `prepare` with the controller archived from main and from this branch, the way the skill does:

  | Checkout | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Detached as installed, newer than v2026.11.0 | `ahead-of-release` | `detached at commit 110a625d` |
  | Same, `--channel edge` | raw `git symbolic-ref` error | `detached at commit 110a625d` |
  | `git checkout v2026.11.0` | raw `git symbolic-ref` error | `detached at tag v2026.11.0` |

  After `git switch -c nanoclaw`, this branch's `prepare` reached `prepared` (already on v2026.11.0), and `abandon` cleaned up.

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
/update-nanoclaw on a checkout that is not on a branch (for example after `git checkout v2026.11.0`) now names the tag or commit and gives the command to fix it, instead of a raw git error.
```

None. The check runs read-only git commands on the install's own checkout.

prs.title: fix(codex): let setup replace a stale OpenAI sign-in
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets Codex setup replace a stored OpenAI sign-in that stopped working, instead of saying "already connected".

- **Problem**: the Codex auth step skips sign-in whenever the gateway holds a Codex secret, so a revoked key or ChatGPT login can't be replaced. The add-codex Troubleshooting step (re-run `provider-auth codex`) does nothing.
- **Fix**: at a terminal, setup asks **Keep it** or **Sign in again**; without one it keeps the stored sign-in, as before. On OneCLI, signing in again updates the recorded secret's value in place (`PATCH /v1/secrets/<id>` on the install's management API). Groups keep their grant, no second `Codex` secret competes for the host, and the value never goes on argv (`onecli secrets update` only takes `--value`). OneCLI 1.45 re-derives the host and ChatGPT metadata from the new value, as on create. Iron already replaces its secrets in place.
- **Guards**: two recorded secrets on one host, or a recorded secret there that isn't an inline OpenAI login, stop the save with a pointer to OneCLI. A ChatGPT login missing a token or its workspace id never replaces a working one.
- **Not `store.connection()`** (the #2878 close note): OneCLI's connection stores API keys as `generic` and checks metadata strictly, so existing `openai`-type Codex secrets would be rejected. That's a migration, not this fix.

## Related work

Closes #4529. Rebuilds closed #2878 on main.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests, red on main and green here: keep, sign in again, no terminal and declined skip in the Codex payload's `codex.test.ts`; in-place update, same-host refusals, partial login and the unchanged create path in `add-onecli/scripts/credential-store.test.ts`. Those suites: 314/314 pass.
- exe.dev, one VM, OneCLI 1.45, a stale Codex API key in the vault: on main, setup says "already connected" and the Codex agent gets `401`. On this branch, setup offers **Sign in again**, updates the same secret id in place, and the agent replies, from a session that started before the update. Without a terminal it keeps the stored sign-in.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Codex sign-in can replace an expired or revoked OpenAI sign-in.** Re-running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex` now asks whether to keep the stored account or sign in again; it used to say "already connected" while agents kept failing.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Credentials: signing in again overwrites this install's recorded OneCLI secret through the management API named in `.env` (`ONECLI_URL`, `ONECLI_API_KEY`). The value never reaches argv or logs, and errors never echo the API's responses.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

No new files: the add-codex payload's `setup/providers/codex.ts` and the add-onecli scripts change in place. An installed Codex gets the new auth step from `provider-auth codex --refresh`; it applies from the next run.

prs.title: fix(codex): honor native retry and completion status
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Fix** - bug fix to source code

## Description

Honor the Codex app-server turn lifecycle in the container provider:

- Keep the existing turn alive when an `error` notification explicitly sets `willRetry: true`. Codex owns that retry; the provider can still steer, abort, or reach its existing deadline.
- Only emit an ordinary result when `turn/completed` has status `completed` and no native error. Interrupted turns and other noncompleted or malformed statuses use the existing terminal error path, preserving native error messages when supplied.

The official protocol defines transient retry notifications and the completed/failed/interrupted/inProgress statuses: [ErrorNotification](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/notification.rs#L41), [stream-error handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L955), and [TurnStatus](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/TurnStatus.ts).

This handles notifications the app-server emits; it does not address retries hidden inside Codex with no corresponding notification.

## Validation

- Bun 1.3.12: active-turn tests **21 passed**. Added cases cover recovery and steering on the same turn, eventual terminal failure, nonretrying errors, abort, the existing deadline, and partial text with interrupted or invalid completion status. Before the provider fix, these tests gave 10 pass / 11 fail.
- Other Codex runner tests: **34 passed, 5 skipped**, with the skips requiring the composed core or CLI-tools manifest.
- Both changed files pass Prettier; `git diff --check` passes.
- Standalone runner typecheck has the same nine contract/core incompatibility diagnostics on the unmodified `providers` branch (only line positions change). The existing provider-contract CI composes this payload with its compatible core and checks installs and refreshes.

prs.title: fix(setup): match auth errors only in flagged failure notices
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup's first-chat ping now reports a credential error only when the runner's flagged failure notice (or stderr) says so. A real reply that mentions "not logged in" no longer fails the first chat.

- **Problem**: the ping matches the auth patterns against every reply. A real reply that says "not logged in" (about GitHub, say) is scored `auth_error`, quoted as the error, and setup skips the first chat.
- **Fix**: `classifyPingResult` takes the flagged notices as their own argument and matches the auth patterns only there and on stderr. `pingOutcome` passes them in and takes the error line from them.
- **Why now**: this waited for an image repin past #3908, but the image does not decide the runner. The host mounts `container/agent-runner/src` from setup's own checkout and runs it, and setup restarts the host before the ping. The image only adds the Claude SDK; the e2e covers both pinned SDKs.
- **Out of scope**: a bad OAuth token still scores `agent_failure`, here and on main. The SDK's 401 text is not in the runner's exact-match list (`providers/claude.ts`), so the runner sends the generic notice.

## Related work

Follow-up to #3980: note 1 from @amit-shafnir's review ([comment](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3980#discussion_r4312007392)), held until the repin ([reply](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3980#discussion_r4313104656)). No issue: the case comes from that review, not a report.

- `setup/lib/agent-ping.test.ts`: the auth tests now pass the notice as flagged; 2 new tests (a plain reply that says "not logged in" scores ok, also in raw-lines form) fail on main.

prs.title: fix(router): a new thread does not wait for its siblings' mailboxes
prs.body:
## What

A new thread's first message no longer waits for its sibling sessions' mailboxes. The typing indicator shows before any context is gathered.

## Why

When a message opens a new per-thread session, the router seeds the session with the conversation's top-level talk before it writes the message: each hot sibling's root user message and its top-level agent posts (`backfillSession`). The backfill read those by opening up to eight sibling sessions whole. On a remote (S3) mailbox, a session that is not in the Host's memory is read whole, record by record, through one Host-wide pool of reads. So the message and the typing indicator waited for all eight.

Seen on a production Host, two and seven minutes after a Host restart, Slack DM:

| | "Session created" to "Message routed" |
|---|---|
| new thread 1 | 23.3 s |
| new thread 2 | 12.2 s |
| reply in an existing thread (no backfill) | 0.8 s |

Nothing else between those two lines takes time: wake context is held to 1.5 s and logged no slow warning, and the message write is one insert. The person saw nothing for that time; the reply came 60 s after the message.

## How

- **Record the talk where the Host sees it.** A small central table, `conversation_timeline` (migration 027), gets one row per top-level message:
  - the router records a new session's first message (same rules as the mailbox's `getConversationRoot`: a chat message on a real chat surface, never a Host-injected instruction);
  - delivery records each delivered top-level agent post (same rules as `getTopLevelOutbound`: no system, task-log or agent-to-agent rows, no thread or a thread id that names only the chat).
  Both writes are off the message's path and never throw.
- **Read it with one query.** The backfill reads the newest rows of the same hot siblings, with the same horizon (`ECHO_MAX_AGE_MS`), the same catch-up floor and the same limit (12). No sibling mailbox is opened. Labels, surfaces, row ids and the single write into the new session are unchanged.
- **Typing first.** The router starts the typing indicator in the wake branch before the backfill and wake context; the start after the write only refreshes it. It is a one-line helper call, so skills anchored on the wake branch's `startTypingRefresh(` block still match once.
- **Retention.** Rows older than the horizon are never read and are deleted when their conversation records its next row. A session's rows are deleted with the session (`deleteSession`, group delete, chat delete; no foreign key, like the host-coordination tables). Text is kept to 4000 characters, the most the backfill writes for a row.

No wait, timeout, retry, cache or setting is added.

## Limits, stated

- Talk from before this release is not in the table, so for up to three days (the backfill horizon) a new thread in an older conversation gets less of it. Slack chats with history reading on still get the platform's own timeline from the `channel-timeline` wake-context provider.
- A long-idle existing session still reads its own newest row to set its catch-up floor (one mailbox open of the session being woken, which a new thread never does).
- `getConversationRoot` and `getTopLevelOutbound` stay on the mailbox interface (the S3 mailbox in nanoco-recipes implements them); this PR no longer calls them.

## How it fits with other work

- nanoco-recipes#2432 (approved, not merged) stops the host sweep from opening idle sessions, which keeps the mailbox cache from churning. Its memo is in memory, so right after a Host restart every session is cold again; this PR removes the backfill's sibling reads altogether, cold or not.
- #4247 changes the same backfill (attachments on echo and backfill rows). Whichever merges second carries the other's change: here the rows come from the timeline, so attachment ids would be recorded with the row.
- The 18.6 s the same message also waited while its group's pod was replaced as stale is a separate fix.
- Governance's session delete keeps its own list of session tables: nanocoai/nanoco-recipes#2609 adds this table to it.

## Tests

Red first, each on `main` plus the new test:
- `backfill-timeline.test.ts`: two hot siblings whose mailbox opens never answer (a cold remote store), their root and post recorded. Red: the backfill is still waiting after 2 s. Green: both rows seeded, no sibling opened.
- `router-new-thread-wait.test.ts` (real `routeInbound`): the typing indicator starts while the backfill is still running (red: no typing until the backfill ends); a new thread's first message is recorded as the session's root (red: no row).
- `delivery-timeline.test.ts` (real `deliverToSessions`): a delivered top-level post is recorded, a reply in a thread is not (red: no row).
- `timeline.test.ts` (real central DB): what is and is not recorded, redelivery, text cap, horizon pruning, the read's order, floor and limit, deletion with the session.
- `backfill.test.ts`: the existing cases kept (hot set, labels, surfaces, floor, limit, horizon, row ids), now against the timeline read.

Local: `src` suite 2511 passed, 0 failed (201 files); typecheck and lint clean on the changed files. nanoco-recipes `check-recipe nanoco-k8s-nancy-v3` with this head pinned: compose (117 skills), install, typecheck and packaging ok. In that composed tree the related tests fail only where they fail on `main` too (no S3 endpoint for local tests).

Box proof: to follow in a comment.

prs.title: fix(templates): read restamp's live files without following or blocking
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Restamp now reads the agent-writable files it compares through one descriptor that cannot follow a symlink or wait on a named pipe.

- **Problem**: restamp's plan checked a context file or a skill overlay file, then read it by path. Both folders are container-writable, so the agent could swap in a named pipe between the two calls, and the read would wait on the host's event loop (the hang in GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj). `statSync` also followed a symlinked context file to its target.
- **Fix**: one helper, `readRegularFile`, opens with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, checks `fstat` on the descriptor, and takes the bytes and the mode from it. Anything else reads as absent, and so does an overlay entry that the container removes or replaces after the listing. A symlinked context file now plans as `create` and is never removed, the rule `readGroupPersona` already uses for the persona file.
- **Out of scope**: a symlinked parent folder is still followed by the compare, as before. The compare cannot block, and the writes already refuse that folder through `AnchoredDir`.

## Related work

Closes #4521

Follow-up to #4440 (GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj), suggested by @amit-shafnir while reviewing that fix. His other follow-up, a refused provider spawn file that names itself, already shipped in #4440.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 4 new tests in `src/templates/restamp.test.ts`, all failing on main: a symlinked context file plans as absent; a context file or overlay file that turns into a FIFO at the moment of the open does not block the plan; overlay entries that change after the listing do not abort it.
- Removing `O_NONBLOCK`, `O_NOFOLLOW`, the `fstat` check, the mode compare, the listing fix, or either new read fails at least one test.
- The FIFO tests cannot hang: a helper process frees a stuck read after 3 s, so a regression fails instead.
- `vitest run src`: 2503 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. `tsc`, `prettier` and `eslint` on the changed files: clean.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Restamp no longer follows symlinks or waits on named pipes when it compares an agent's files with its template.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Untrusted input: context files in the group folder and the skill overlay, which the agent container can write. Restamp's reads there now refuse anything that is not a regular file, without blocking. No change to writes, permissions, credentials, mounts or containers.

prs.title: fix(telegram): mark voice notes as voice notes
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Marks Telegram voice notes as voice notes, the same way WhatsApp does since #4378.

- **Problem**: `@chat-adapter/telegram` 4.41.1 builds a recorded voice note (`message.voice`) as `type: 'audio'`, the same as a music file. Core's bridge passes the type on and drops every other field. So the agent saw a plain audio file, and nothing that looks for `isVoiceNote` ever fired. (#4378's description said core already typed these as `voice`. It does not.)
- **Fix**: `telegram.ts` wraps the adapter's `extractAttachments`, so the `message.voice` attachment is typed `voice`. Then, on the way to the host, each `voice` attachment gets `isVoiceNote: true`. Music files and other audio stay `audio`.
- **Out of scope**: core's bridge, which still forwards a fixed set of attachment fields, and the SDK's own mapping.

## Related work

Closes #4517

Follow-up to #4378, from the review there.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves the `channels` branch off Baileys `7.0.0-rc.9`, which is affected by [GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/security/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg) (message spoofing).
- **Problem**: #4024 pinned rc14 in the `add-whatsapp` skill, but the `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `channels` still resolve rc.9 at `4a036385`, after the 2026.11.0 sync (#4512).
- **Why syncs miss it**: Baileys exists only in `channels`, so main→channels merges never touch this line.
- **Fix**: bump to `7.0.0-rc14` and regenerate the lockfile. As a side effect, `libsignal@6.0.0` now resolves from npm with an integrity hash instead of the git tarball, `whatsapp-rust-bridge@0.5.4` is added, and the `jimp` peer range is now `^1.6.1`.
- **Out of scope**: the registry checker (`dependencyProblems()` in `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts`) checks the `package.json` after a skill is applied, not the `package.json` on `channels` itself. That's why CI didn't flag this. Better as a separate change.

prs.title: docs: add optional Parallel Search MCP example
prs.body:
Adds an opt-in Parallel Search MCP example using NullClaw's native HTTP transport. Merge the server entry into your existing configuration, restart, and use `mcp_parallel_web_search` or `mcp_parallel_web_fetch`. No Parallel API key or local bridge is needed. Anonymous access has rate limits, and queries and fetched URLs are sent to Parallel. English and Chinese setup instructions explain configuration, discovery, and usage. Existing search defaults stay unchanged.

I work at Parallel. For context: [Artificial Analysis Search API benchmarks](https://artificialanalysis.ai/agents/search-api).

Tested: source build with Zig 0.16.0; full test suite (7,493 passed, 14 skipped); live anonymous discovery, search, and fetch through CLI agent turns with a scripted model fixture.

issues.title: feat: add LLMTR as a built-in OpenAI-compatible LLM provider
issues.body:
## Summary

Please add LLMTR as a first-class entry in the built-in provider catalog (`crates/domains/ironclaw_llm/assets/providers.json`), next to Groq, Together, Cerebras, and MiniMax.

LLMTR is an OpenAI-compatible gateway at `https://llmtr.com/v1`. Model IDs are namespaced `vendor/model` values such as `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash`. IDs under `llmtr/` are hosted in Turkey; other vendor/model IDs route to their vendors. Keys: https://llmtr.com/dashboard/keys.

## Problem

Users can already point the generic `openai_compatible` adapter at LLMTR, but that requires setting a base URL by hand and does not show up in the overview table or the setup wizard. A named catalog entry would make the same path a one-key setup (`LLMTR_API_KEY`), consistent with the other hosted OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Proposed shape

- `id`: `llmtr`
- `protocol`: `open_ai_completions`
- `default_base_url`: `https://llmtr.com/v1`
- `api_key_env`: `LLMTR_API_KEY`
- `base_url_env`: `LLMTR_BASE_URL`
- `model_env`: `LLMTR_MODEL`
- `default_model`: `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash`
- Docs row and a short section in `docs/capabilities/llm-providers.md`

This is a small catalog addition; no new protocol or runtime path is required.

I have a ready implementation and can open a PR that links this issue once you confirm it fits the roadmap.

issues.title: [Bug] 多分身配置下「梦境日记」面板恒为空：内置 runtime 2026.8.1 缺 doctor.memory.* 的 ambient-owner 回退（上游已修，待跟进）
issues.body:
### 环境

- LobsterAI **2026.9.23**（macOS 27.0 arm64）
- 内置 runtime：**OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (ea80657)**
- 配置：`agents.entries` 下 5 个 agent；`agents.ownership = "explicit"`；已设 `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId = "main"`

### 现象

**设置 → 梦境 → 日记（Diary）标签页恒显示「还没有梦境日记」**，但工作区的 `DREAMS.md` 一直在正常更新（当前 7.7KB，含每日梦境日记条目），`memory/dreaming/{light,rem,deep}/<日期>.md` 也在产出。

### 证据（网关日志）

```
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ doctor.memory.status      879ms
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ doctor.memory.dreamDiary    0ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST
     errorMessage=Multiple agents are configured, but doctor memory has no explicit owner.
                  Pass agentId to select a configured agent.
```

CLI 直调可稳定复现，且证明数据与接口本身正常：

```bash
# 不带 agentId → 报错（与面板一致）
openclaw gateway call doctor.memory.dreamDiary

# 带 agentId → 正常返回日记
openclaw gateway call doctor.memory.dreamDiary --params '{"agentId":"main"}'
# => {"found":true,"path":"DREAMS.md","updatedAtMs":...}
```

### 根因（上游已确认并修复，属内置 runtime 版本落后）

上游同名缺陷：**openclaw/openclaw#138369**（2026-09-04 提交，**2026-09-23 关闭为已修**）、相关 **#138341**。

修复内容（PR #156437，commit `930bd347472`，2026-09-23 进 `main`）：把 `doctor.memory.status` 已有的 **ambient-owner 回退**搬进共享的 `resolveDoctorMemoryTarget` —— 这样 dream diary 等 doctor memory 处理器在调用方（含"legacy embedded Control UI"这类不带 `agentId` 的客户端）未传 agentId 时，会解析到**配置的 system agent** 或唯一 agent。

官方结案原话：「…**Ships with the next release**」。本机内置 runtime 为 **2026.8.1**，早于该修复（也早于 v2026.8.2 的客户端侧修复），因此仍复现。

### 为什么用户无法自行绕过

`agents.ownership="explicit"` 与 legacy `agents.entries.<id>.default=true` **互斥**（schema 要求二选一）。实测：

```
unset agents.ownership                     → 校验失败：multi-agent rosters require ownership="explicit" or one legacy default=true marker
entries.main.default=true（ownership 未动）→ 校验失败：cannot be combined with a legacy default=true marker
```

即**必须原子改两个键**，`config patch` 做不到；且 App 每次同步都会写回 `ownership="explicit"`。配置层无解。

### 建议

1. **跟进内置 runtime 版本**（≥ 含 `930bd347472` 的构建）；或
2. 面板调用补 `agentId`（或复用与 `doctor.memory.status` 相同的解析路径——该 RPC 在当前版本可用）。

### 临时替代

直接查看工作区 `DREAMS.md`（内容完整）。

---

（上游 #126360 仍开着，讨论多分身 + `ownership="explicit"` 下若干 ambient 路径缺 agentId 的问题。）

prs.body:
## Summary

Restores three LobsterAI Plan model compatibility capabilities that were missing after the OpenClaw → DSH runtime migration:

1. **Per-model protocol dispatch & Anthropic proxy path fix (e.g., Claude Sonnet 5.5)**
   - Propagates per-model `apiFormat` from `serverModels` through `dshProviderSync` into `DshHostProviderModelSpec.api`.
   - Updates `lobster-model-bridge` to dispatch `stream` / `streamSimple` by `model.api` (instead of binding a single provider-level protocol), prevents OpenAI-only provider `compat` flags from leaking onto Anthropic models, and omits synthetic `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` for Anthropic models without `thinkingConfig`.
   - Normalizes `/v1/<lobster-plan-alias>/v1/messages` in `openclawTokenProxy` so Anthropic SDK requests forward to `/api/proxy/v1/messages` instead of `/api/proxy/v1/v1/messages`.

2. **Thinking-level control & `lobsterai_options` v1 (e.g., GLM-5.3-Flash)**
   - Adds `resolveEffectiveDshReasoningEffort` and wires it into DSH `resolveModelSelection` (including virtual preset resolution), `DshRuntimeAdapter.patchSession` (including reset-to-default), and `buildDshHostAgentSpecs`.
   - Builds exact `thinkingLevelMap` from `thinkingConfig.options` and uses `AsyncLocalStorage` across `PiAiAdapter.stream` / `prepareCall` in `lobster-model-bridge` to preserve explicit `'off'` vs unset, injecting `lobsterai_options: { version: 1, thinking: { level } }` on `lobsterai-options-v1` models.

3. **Kimi K3 runtime profile contract & safe output token defaults**
   - Resolves `ModelRuntimeProfile.MoonshotKimiK3` across plan (`kimi-k3-YoudaoInner`), built-in Moonshot, and custom OpenAI-compatible providers in `dshProviderSync`, applying `maxTokensField: "max_tokens"`, `supportsUsageInStreaming: false`, `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true`, and `thinkingLevelMap`.
   - Ports the Kimi K3 payload contract into `lobster-model-bridge` (`reasoning_effort: "max"`, fixed sampling field stripping, assistant tool-call `reasoning_content` backfill, fail-closed transport check).
   - Decouples Kimi K3's `1,048,576` catalog `maxTokens` from its per-request default (`defaultMaxTokens: 131,072`) and restores `32,768` as the default output budget for plan reasoning models without explicit `maxTokens`.

## Electron / Runtime Changes

- **Main process & local proxy**: `src/main/main.ts`, `src/main/libs/openclawTokenProxy.ts`, `src/main/libs/dsh/*`, `src/main/libs/agentEngine/dshRuntimeAdapter.ts` (no IPC schema or SQLite migration changes).
- **DSH host bundle plugin**: `dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/plugins/model-bridge.mjs` and `model-bridge-helpers.mjs` (no upstream DSH runtime patches).

## Verification

- `npm test -- dsh openclawTokenProxy modelRuntimeProfiles claudeSettings.serverModels` — 30 test files, 250 tests passed.
- `npm run compile:electron` & `npx tsc` — 0 errors.
- `node --check dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/plugins/model-bridge.mjs dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/plugins/model-bridge-helpers.mjs` — passed.
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored <touched files>` — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Wire-level smoke test against real `PiAiAdapter` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai` verified exact outbound HTTP paths and JSON payloads for Claude Sonnet 5.5, GLM-5.3-Flash (`off` / `max`), and Kimi K3.

## Summary
- Fixes an XML namespace compatibility bug where adding worksheets to an `openpyxl`-generated `.xlsx` (which declares `xmlns:r` locally on each `<sheet>` rather than on `<workbook>`) emitted new `<sheet ... r:id="..."/>` elements with an unbound `r` prefix, causing `openpyxl` and strict XML parsers to reject the saved workbook.
- Adds shared `namespacePrefixFor` / `ensureXmlNamespace` helpers in `src/renderer/services/office/sheet/xlsxXml.ts`.
- Ensures `rewriteWorkbookSheets` binds the relationship namespace on `<workbook>` (or locally on prefix collision) when adding sheets, and adds `ensureWorkbookSheetNamespaces` in `exportXlsx` to self-heal previously damaged files on save while keeping healthy files byte-identical.
- Unifies `<worksheet>` `xmlns:r` handling across `xlsxHyperlinks.ts`, `xlsxDrawings.ts`, and `xlsxNotes.ts` (and matches non-`r` prefixes when removing `legacyDrawing`).
- Adds unit/regression tests and strict `@xmldom/xmldom` XML namespace validation across `xlsxCodec.test.ts`.

## Electron-specific Notes
- Renderer-side Office spreadsheet codec only; no IPC, storage, runtime, windowing, or OpenClaw/DSH config changes.

  - Updated `PetAtlasPlayer`, `CompanionCharacter`, `CompanionOrb`, and `desktopCompanion.css` to apply calibrated canvas dimensions and `--atlas-offset-y`, and switched the initial canvas draw to `useLayoutEffect` to prevent a blank frame on transition.

prs.body:
## Summary
Restores and upgrades multi-agent collaboration on the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) runtime so any enabled LobsterAI agent can discover and delegate tasks to other configured specialist agents using their own workspace persona, long-term memory, skills, working directory, and model.

Design doc: `specs/features/agent-subagent-delegation/2026-11-21-dsh-multi-agent-delegation-design.md`

## Key Changes
- **DSH Host Bundle (`@lobsterai/dsh-bundle`)**:
  - Added `lobster-agent-delegation` plugin (`agent-delegation.mjs` + pure `agent-delegation-helpers.mjs`) mounted in `cordis.patch.yml` (zero patches to upstream DSH).
  - Injects a compact collaborator roster into runtime context and exposes `delegate_agent` (plus on-demand `list_collaborator_agents` when >20 collaborators), delegating directly onto native `ctx.subagents.startActivation({ provider: 'spawn', ..., maxDepth: 2, delivery: 'parent' })` with anti-cycle ancestry checks and explicit model route preflight/fallback.
  - Extended `ops-rpc.mjs` and `shared-state.mjs` with `syncAgents` / `syncSubagentBindings` and synchronous cold-resume context synthesis for delegated children.
- **Electron Main / Storage / Runtime**:
  - **Storage**: Added `agents.subagent_collaboration_mode` (`all` | `allowlist` | `disabled`, defaulting to `all` with one-time migration preserving non-empty legacy `subagent_allow_agent_ids` as `allowlist`) and `dsh_subagent_agent_bindings` table for durable child-to-agent and direct-parent mapping.
  - **Runtime & Bridge**: Added `dshAgentSync.ts`, `DshHostManager.syncAgents` / `syncSubagentBindings` (replayed on restart), and `/dsh-bridge/subagent-binding` callback route.
  - **Subagent Sessions & Adapter**: Included `delegate_agent` in `isDshSubagentSpawn`, recorded target `agentId` on `subagent_runs`, and enabled recursive depth-2 catalog sync & history reads in `DshSubagentSessions`.
  - **IPC / Preload**: Extended agent create/update payloads with `subagentCollaborationMode`.
- **Renderer UI & i18n**:
  - Upgraded the Collaboration tab in `AgentSettingsPanel` and `AgentCreateModal` with a shared 3-mode `AgentCollaborationSettings` component and full `zh`/`en` translations.
  - Updated `SubagentPanelContent` and `subagentDisplay.ts` to show the delegated specialist agent badge and initial without materializing extra sidebar sessions.

prs.body:
## PR Title

docs(teams): add optional public evidence handoff guide

## Description

Document how a researcher can look up public Python documentation and pass original URLs and short excerpts to a writer through TinyAGI's existing team handoff. The existing researcher example does not explain how to configure a workspace MCP connection or preserve its evidence in a teammate's reply.

Use the provider CLI's local MCP scope to expose optional Parallel web search only in the researcher's workspace. Include request budgets, failure handling, verification, and removal steps. This documentation change requires no TinyAGI runtime or dependency changes.

I work at Parallel. This contribution was prepared with AI assistance.

## Changes

- Add `docs/PUBLIC-RESEARCH.md` with a public documentation lookup using the existing agent, team, and messaging commands.
- Carry original source URLs and short supporting excerpts through the researcher's handoff and the writer's cited reply.
- Add one link under Team Collaboration in the README.

## Testing

- Run the real `tinyagi start`, reset, send, and stop commands through the API, SQLite queue, and provider CLI with temporary configuration directories and a deterministic local model-provider fixture. The researcher executed one live anonymous MCP search; the original Python documentation URL and excerpt reached the writer and its reply. The writer had no Parallel tool. This checks application plumbing; live model reasoning and answer quality were not tested. Interactive creation wizards were represented by equivalent isolated settings.
- Separately test real anonymous MCP initialization, a catalog containing only `web_search`, and a search using the setup URL and TinyAGI User-Agent from the guide. Verify the returned Python source URL with HTTP 200 and its creation command. Verify local MCP add/get/remove with the real client.
- Run `npm run build` successfully with a local unsaved `@clack/prompts@1.1.0` pin. An unpinned install resolved 1.9.0 and reproduced baseline symbol type errors; no dependency change is included.
- Check all four shell blocks with `bash -n`, local links, and `git diff --check`.

## Checklist
