issues.title: [Bug]: Console freezes on iOS WebKit in long conversations due to UserMessageAnchors layout thrashing and content-visibility:auto in column-reverse list
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`2.3.0.post1` (commit `ee58cb1a64f2b21e825c525f73dc44bc7941edea`, Console using `@agentscope-ai/chat` `^1.2.0-beta.1792133067831`)

## Description

On iOS Safari / WebKit, opening or continuing a long chat session with substantial context causes the Console UI to freeze / become unresponsive, even though initial DOM load itself is fast (~742ms).

Investigating both `console/src/pages/Chat/` and `@agentscope-ai/chat` points to **4 interacting root causes** that combine into severe layout thrashing / main-thread hang on iOS WebKit:

### 1. `UserMessageAnchors` still observes every bubble and forces synchronous layout in `navigator` mode
- `console/src/pages/Chat/longChatPerformance.ts` enables `LONG_CHAT_USER_MESSAGE_ANCHORS = { enabled: true, variant: "navigator" }`, with the comment assuming `navigator` mode does not observe or measure every bubble.
- However, in `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/AgentScopeRuntimeWebUI/core/Chat/MessageList/UserMessageAnchors/`:
  - `index.js:531-538`: Whenever there are ≥ 3 user messages (`visible === true`), even with `variant === 'navigator'`, it:
    1. Calls `observeMessageLayout(scrollEl, ...)` (`targetLayout.js:105-116`), which attaches a `ResizeObserver` to **every `[data-role][id]` bubble** in the scroll container.
    2. Attaches a `MutationObserver` with `{ childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true }` to the entire message scroll container.
    3. Listens to `scroll` events on the scroll container.
  - `index.js:454-463`: On every scroll frame, resize, or streaming character mutation, `measureAnchors()` queries all `[data-role][id]` bubbles and calls `target.getBoundingClientRect()` on **every single bubble** **before** the `if (variant === 'navigator') return;` early-return on line 463.
- On iOS WebKit, this triggers forced synchronous layout across the entire message list during streaming and momentum scrolling.

### 2. `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 160px` inside `flex-direction: column-reverse` on iOS WebKit
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/Bubble/Bubble.js:83-85` applies inline styles `contentVisibility: 'auto'` and `containIntrinsicSize: 'auto 160px'` to every bubble.
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/Bubble/style/list.js` renders the message list with `flex-direction: column-reverse` (`order="desc"`).
- On iOS 18+ WebKit, `content-visibility: auto` inside a `column-reverse` scroll container—especially when real bubble heights (long Markdown, Prism code blocks, tool cards) greatly exceed `160px` and `UserMessageAnchors` repeatedly calls `getBoundingClientRect()` and observes every bubble via `ResizeObserver`—causes severe layout thrashing, scroll anchor jumps, and WebContent hangs.

### 3. `setSessionMessages` in `Chat/index.tsx` omits `history: true` (bypassing SDK pagination), and SDK pagination never unmounts offscreen bubbles
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/AgentScopeRuntimeWebUI/core/Chat/MessageList/index.js:82-98` only paginates (`PAGE_SIZE = 10`) messages with `m.history === true`, and `loadMore` uses `flushSync` (line 102) without virtualizing/unmounting scrolled-away bubbles (related to #3923).
- While `ChatAnywhereSessionsContext.js:244-248` adds `history: true` on initial session load, `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` calls `chatRef.current?.messages.setSessionMessages(...)` with refreshed history messages (`recovered.messages` / `session.messages`, e.g. queue recovery and handoff refresh) without marking `history: true`, causing the entire session history to mount synchronously at once.

### 4. `ComposerAccessibilityLabels` observes the entire chat layout subtree
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ComposerAccessibilityLabels.tsx:112-115` attaches `MutationObserver({ childList: true, subtree: true })` to `-chat-anywhere-layout` (which wraps the entire `MessageList` as well as the composer), running `querySelectorAll("button")` over newly added message nodes during streaming/history loads.

**Related Issue(s):** #3923

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `2.3.0.post1` (`ee58cb1a64f2b21e825c525f73dc44bc7941edea`)
- **OS:** iOS (Safari / WKWebView)
- **Install method:** pip (`qwenpaw==2.3.0.post1`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session in QwenPaw Console on iOS Safari / WebKit with a long conversation history (many turns, long Markdown/code blocks/tool calls).
2. Scroll through the conversation or continue streaming new replies.
3. Observe UI responsiveness.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** Initial DOM load completes quickly (~742ms), then the page freezes / becomes unresponsive on iOS once the long conversation renders, scrolls, or streams.
- **Expected:** Long conversations remain responsive and scrollable on iOS WebKit without main-thread hangs.

## Suggested Fixes

### Console-side mitigations
1. Disable `userMessageAnchors` on iOS / iPadOS WebKit (or until `@agentscope-ai/chat` stops observing/measuring all bubbles in `navigator` mode).
2. Override bubble `content-visibility: visible; contain-intrinsic-size: none;` under `@supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none)` to avoid WebKit `column-reverse` + `content-visibility: auto` layout hangs.
3. Mark hydrated messages with `history: true` when calling `setSessionMessages` with refreshed session history in `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx`.
4. Scope `ComposerAccessibilityLabels`'s `MutationObserver` to the sender container (`-chat-anywhere-chat-sender` / `-sender`) instead of `-chat-anywhere-layout`.

### Upstream `@agentscope-ai/chat` SDK root fixes
1. In `UserMessageAnchors`: in `navigator` mode, do not attach `ResizeObserver` to every bubble or `MutationObserver({ subtree: true, characterData: true })` to the whole message list, and avoid measuring all bubbles with `getBoundingClientRect()` on every scroll/mutation frame.
2. Revisit `content-visibility: auto` on `Bubble` inside `column-reverse` lists on WebKit, and consider windowed/virtualized rendering for long histories instead of append-only `flushSync` pagination.

issues.title: Console: message list is not keyboard-focusable, so arrow/PageUp/PageDown never scroll the conversation
issues.body:
## Summary

In the Console chat view, the conversation cannot be scrolled with the keyboard. Arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End do nothing, because the scroll container is not focusable and clicking inside a message never moves focus to it.

This makes the chat unusable on machines without a mouse wheel (laptops using a TrackPoint or keyboard-only navigation), where wheel events are not available as a fallback.

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1, QwenPaw Desktop (Tauri webview)
- Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045)
- WebView2 / Chromium 126, viewport 1366 x 705, devicePixelRatio 1
- Conversation with long history (scroll range ~6900-8000 px)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a conversation long enough to scroll.
2. Click inside the message text.
3. Press ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp or PageDown.

## Expected

The conversation scrolls, or at minimum the list takes focus and then scrolls.

## Actual

Nothing scrolls. `document.activeElement` remains the composer input, so the keys are consumed by the chat input instead of the list.

## Root cause (measured)

The scrolling element is `.qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll` (the wrapper that Ant Design X's `Bubble.List` renders with `overflow:auto`, `flex-direction:column-reverse`, and a scrollTop range of `[-range, 0]`). It reports:

```
tabIndex: -1
```

so it can never receive focus, and clicking a message does not focus it.

Direct evidence from the running app, same conversation:

| Action | scrollTop |
| --- | --- |
| seed | -1500 |
| PageDown, list not focused | -1500 (no change) |
| set `tabIndex = 0` and `focus()` | -1500 |
| PageDown, focused | **-1059** (441 px page) |
| ArrowUp, focused | **-1099** (40 px line) |
| ArrowDown, focused | -1059 |

With focus the native keyboard scrolling works correctly, including the inverted (negative scrollTop) list. So the scroll maths are fine; only focusability is missing.

Wheel scrolling in the same build is unaffected: synthetic `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` wheel and a real `SendInput` `MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL` both scroll the list normally.

## Suggested fix

Give the scroll container a tab stop and keep keyboard scrolling working:

```jsx
<div className="qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll ..." tabIndex={0}>
```

plus a `:focus-visible` outline so the focus is visible, and optionally a `keydown` handler on the message area (Arrow/PageUp/PageDown/Home/End) so the keys work even when focus is on the page body.

Related but separate: the scrollbar's page area works (a track click jumps 441 px), and the round chevron at the bottom-right of the list is `qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll-to-bottom`, not a scrollbar arrow, which is easy to mistake for one.

issues.title: [Question]: 压缩失败提示建议 `/clear`，容易误导用户清除上下文导致信息丢失

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

issues.body:
## Question or topic

**位置**：`src/qwenpaw/agents/command_handler.py`，`_process_compact` 的失败分支（约 476-479 行）

```python
return await self._make_system_msg(
    f"❌ **Compact Failed!**\n\n- Reason: {e}\n"
    f"- Use `/clear` to reset the context if needed",
)
```

## 背景：官方对「压缩失败」的处理是丢弃上下文

AgentScope 的默认行为是 `compression_fallback_to_truncation=True`：摘要生成失败时回退到截断最旧上下文（失败不保上下文）。

所以官方这条提示在原生语义下是自洽的——反正压缩失败后上下文本来也要丢，建议 `/clear` 并不算多损失。

## 问题：换成自定义压缩策略后，这条提示变成误导

现在可以用插件替换压缩管线（比如替换第 5 步摘要生成）。这类插件常见的选择是**失败即中止、保留原上下文**：摘要生成失败时抛异常，驱逐不发生，历史一条不少。

但它抛出的异常最终仍由官方 `/compact` 的失败处理兜底——于是用户在「上下文其实完好」的情况下，看到官方那句 `Use /clear to reset the context if needed`。

用户照着做，等于因为一次可重试的失败（超时、限流、输出截断），把本来被完整保住的会话清空了。

## 建议

把提示改成比较安全的措辞，例如：

```
- 可稍后重试，或切换到其他模型后再试
```

## 复现

1. 启用一个「压缩失败即中止、保留上下文」的压缩插件
2. 让摘要生成失败（模型超时 / 限流 / 断网）
3. 执行 `/compact`，失败提示中出现 `Use /clear to reset the context if needed`
4. 此时 `/compact_str` 或对话历史可确认上下文并未丢失

## 影响

- 用户可能在上下文完好时误清空长会话，不可恢复
- 提示与实际状态不一致，属于会诱导数据丢失的体验问题

## Context

QwenPaw v2.3.1b1

## Tried so far


---

**Note:** For general questions or ideas, [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/discussions) may get more visibility. Use this template when the answer might lead to a bug report, feature request, or doc change.

issues.title: [Bug] console import map remaps the entry chunk to `?v=…`, so the bundle loads twice and plugin routes never register
issues.body:
## Summary

Frontend plugin apps fail with `PawApp <id> did not register its app route` even though the plugin registers its route correctly. The cause is in the served `console/index.html`: an import map (`id="qwenpaw-default-edit-unlock"`) rewrites the entry chunk URL to `?v=<hash>`, while the module `<script src>` keeps the bare URL. Same file, two URLs → two module instances → two route registries. The plugin writes to registry A, the app shell checks registry B.

## Environment

- QwenPaw `2.3.0.post1`, wheel install (`site-packages/qwenpaw/console/`)
- Entry chunk `assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js` (name is per build)
- Linux, Chromium via CDP
- Affected plugin: `qwenpaw-creator` 2.0.7, a frontend plugin with `entry_page = /apps/qwenpaw-creator`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install any frontend (PawApp) plugin that calls
   `window.QwenPaw.registerRoutes(pluginId, [{ path: '/apps/<id>', component }])`
   — this is the documented pattern, `qwenpaw-creator` does exactly that.
2. Open `/apps/<id>` in the console.
3. The console throws `PawApp <id> did not register its app route` and never renders the app. Retry does not help.

No plugin-side error appears; the plugin's own code runs fine (`console.info("[qwenpaw-creator] registered route …")` prints).

## Root cause

`console/index.html` ships with an import map:

```html
<script type="importmap" id="qwenpaw-default-edit-unlock">{"imports":{
  "/assets/AgentGallery-DvcKQ9WZ.js":"/assets/AgentGallery-DvcKQ9WZ.js?v=a5349397",
  "/assets/index-BpnNM-Op.js":"/assets/index-BpnNM-Op.js?v=34f1de5f",
  "/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js":"/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js?v=39706821"}}</script>
```

1. The entry is loaded with the **bare** URL:
   `<script type="module" crossorigin src="/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js">` → module instance A.
2. Lazy chunks import the entry with a **relative** specifier, e.g. `assets/registerBuiltinCards-9DK5RUxP.js` contains
   `import{…}from"./index-CBEGaFBC.js"`.
   The specifier resolves to `/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js`, which the import map rewrites to `?v=39706821` → module instance B.
   (Import maps apply to relative specifiers too, since matching happens after URL resolution.)
3. Instance A runs first and wins the guard `window.QwenPaw = window.QwenPaw || {…}`, so `window.QwenPaw.registerRoutes` closes over registry `Jo_A`.
4. The app shell that renders `/apps/:appId` is reached through a chunk in graph B, so its check
   `Jo.snapshot().some(a => a.source === pluginId && a.path.startsWith('/apps/'))` runs against `Jo_B`.
5. The plugin's route lives only in `Jo_A` → check false → misleading error is thrown.

The same split affects **every** registry-based plugin contribution (routes, menu items, slots, tool renderers): plugins write into A while React reads B. Route failures are just the loudest symptom; silently missing menu entries are the quiet one.

## Evidence

- Server access log shows the same file fetched twice per page load:
  `/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js` **and** `/assets/index-CBEGaFBC.js?v=39706821`.
- Runtime probe inside the bundle: `Jo === window.__joShim` → `false`.
  - `__joShim.snapshot()` (the registry `registerRoutes` wrote to) contains `{path:"/apps/qwenpaw-creator", source:"qwenpaw-creator"}`.
  - the registry used by the throwing code contains only core routes.
- Audit buffer: `route.add` recorded successfully for the plugin, followed by `route.conflict | duplicate route id; ignored` on subsequent executions — i.e. the route really was added to *some* registry.
- Same pattern exists for `AgentGallery-DvcKQ9WZ.js` and `index-BpnNM-Op.js`.

## Fix

Filenames are already content-hashed, so the `?v=` remap adds nothing:

```html
<script type="importmap" id="qwenpaw-default-edit-unlock">{"imports":{}}</script>
```

Verified locally: after this change `/apps/qwenpaw-creator` renders normally.

Better permanent fix in whatever build step emits this import map: map each specifier to itself, or if the query is needed for cache-busting, emit the *same* `?v=` value on the `<script type="module" src>` as well, so only one URL is ever used for a given module.

## Secondary suggestion

The thrown message blames the plugin ("did not register its app route") when the real failure is a registry mismatch. Consider checking whether the plugin appears in the *other* known registry, or logging the registry size, so this class of bug is diagnosable without patching the bundle.

issues.title: [Feature]: 希望可以添加 notice_after_complete （完成后通知）工具。让agent在等待 命令行或子agent任务时，可以回复用户其他问题

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

希望为 Agent 增加 `notice_after_complete` 工具/机制，使得 Agent 在发起一个长时间运行的任务（如执行命令行、调用子 Agent 或等待外部 API 响应）后，能够先回复用户“任务已启动，完成后通知您”，并继续处理用户在同一会话中提出的其他问题，待后台任务完成时再主动推送完成通知。

我推想的方案。  
agent 使用 shell 启动了进程，放在后台，并获得任务号。  
agent 调用 notice_after_complete(任务号) ，注册一个完成通知。  
agent 说 我已注册通知。  
用户 说 我们闲聊吧。  
agent 说 闲聊内容。  
任务完成了，自动用户侧推送一条信息，前缀是 [后台任务「任务号」完成通知] ，发送给agent。 （看起来和用户消息很像，只不过是框架发送的消息）  
agent 说 收到了通知，继续调用其他的工具，继续干活。  

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

当前 Agent 在执行某些阻塞型操作（例如运行耗时较长的 shell 命令、调用子 Agent 进行多轮推理、等待外部工具返回结果）时，会一直等待任务结束才回复用户。这导致：
- 用户体验差：用户必须等待任务完全结束才能收到任何回复，期间界面无响应或长时间“思考中”。
- 无法并行处理：在等待期间，Agent 无法处理用户穿插提出的其他简单问题（例如“当前进度如何？”或“帮我查另一个东西”），即使这些问题与后台任务无关。
- 资源浪费：对于长时间任务，用户往往希望先得到“已接收”的确认，而不是沉默等待。

此功能尤其适用于需要数分钟甚至更久的后台任务场景，如代码编译、大规模数据检索、复杂推理链等。

## Proposed Solution

增加一个名为 `notice_after_complete` 的工具（或内置能力），其工作流程如下：

1. Agent 检测到即将执行一个可能耗时的操作（如 `run_command`、`call_sub_agent`、`http_request` 等）。
2. Agent 调用 `notice_after_complete(task_id, description, callback_context)`，将该任务注册到后台执行队列。
3. 工具立即返回一个占位符（如 `task_id`），Agent 随即向用户回复一条确认消息，例如：“正在执行 [任务描述]，完成后我会主动通知您。您可以继续提问其他问题。”
4. Agent 进入“多任务模式”，可以继续响应当前会话中的其他用户消息，而该后台任务在独立协程/线程中继续运行。
5. 任务完成后，后台机制通过 `task_id` 触发回调，Agent 通过原有通道（如聊天界面）主动向用户推送一条完成通知，包含任务结果或摘要。
6. 如果任务失败，同样推送错误通知。

实现建议：
- 在 Core 层引入任务管理器（TaskManager），维护 `task_id` -> `future` / `callback` 映射。
- 为现有的执行函数（如 `run_command`）提供异步包装，支持 `detach=True` 参数。
- 会话上下文需支持“挂起任务”状态，确保通知能正确投递到对应会话。
- 通知格式可复用现有的消息发送接口（如 `send_message`）。

## Alternatives Considered

- **使用已有的 `send_message` 手动模拟**：用户可以通过在 prompt 中要求 Agent “先回复再执行”，但这不是通用机制，且 Agent 无法在等待后自动推送完成通知，仍需用户主动询问。
- **引入 `background` 修饰器**：让开发者标记函数为后台运行，但缺乏统一的任务 ID 和通知回调管理，不易与对话流集成。
- **依赖外部消息队列**：过于重量级，对于本项目而言增加复杂度和部署成本。

## Additional Context

- 类似设计在 Slack、Discord 的机器人框架中常见（如 `ephemeral` 回复 + `follow-up` 消息）。
- OpenAI 的 Assistants API 支持 `submit_tool_outputs` 的异步模式，但需轮询；我们更希望主动推送。
- 典型使用场景：
  - 用户：“帮我在代码库里搜索所有包含 TODO 的文件，并统计数量。”
  - Agent：调用 `notice_after_complete`，回复“搜索已开始，预计需要 2 分钟，完成后通知您。”
  - 用户：“好的，那顺便问一下，今天天气怎么样？”
  - Agent：调用天气工具，立即回复天气信息。
  - 2 分钟后，Agent 主动推送：“搜索完成，共找到 127 个文件包含 TODO。”

## Willing to Contribute

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

issues.title: [Feature]: QwenPaw 当前缺少与 AgentScope社区 的联动，希望增加 社区登录，信箱，快速反馈等社区功能

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

增加登录 和 社区反馈功能，可以把QwenPaw 本地关联上 AgentScope 社区，可以快速看到 社区里的讨论，Bug反馈。以及使用 QwenPaw 本身的 Agent 能力，进一步细化 反馈报告 的内容。

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [☑️] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

我写了多个插件，和 向多个插件作者反馈了Bug。如果我不专门打开 AgentScope 社区论坛，我就没法看到别人的Bug反馈，也看不到其他插件作者的回复。

## Proposed Solution

虽然不经常打开 AgentScope 社区网站，但我经常使用 QwenPaw 干活，我希望增加登录功能，把社区连入本地的QwenPaw UI 。

增加登录 和 社区反馈功能，可以把QwenPaw 本地关联上 AgentScope 社区，可以快速看到 社区里的讨论，Bug反馈。以及使用 QwenPaw 本身的 Agent 能力，进一步细化 反馈报告 的内容。

prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Set the deployment prefix via `<base href>` in the prebuilt `index.html`. Current builds do not require inline JavaScript to bootstrap, so `script-src 'self'` works without `unsafe-inline`. The server still recognizes the old token for older Console bundles; it does not rewrite JavaScript or CSS responses.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

### Review follow-up (`286c6556`)

- A mount may itself end in `/api`. Local clients now distinguish the deployment URL from an explicit `--base-url`: for `/tenant/api`, cron requests go to `/tenant/api/api/cron/jobs`. Desktop/Tauri's private backend stays at `/` without changing the saved Web configuration.
- The Data Context bridge preserves the original `Request.signal` when omitted or `undefined`. An explicit live signal or `null` overrides it; an already-aborted request never reaches the API.
- For existing Chrome or Voice installations, upgrade the relevant plugin to `0.1.2` or later **before** enabling a prefix. Restart QwenPaw and rerun Chrome Bridge setup if used. The manifest versions changed; no plugin release is part of this update.

prs.title: fix(memory): OpenViking follow-up cleanup, compatibility, and shutdown fixes
prs.body: ## Description Follow-up to #7613. This PR applies the plugin-local cleanups suggested during review, adapts automatic-recall budgeting to the host's current `HintBlock` format, and addresses the shutdown edge case accepted as a non-blocking follow-up in #7613. All changes are confined to `plugins/memory/openviking/`. **Related Issue:** Relates to #7613 **Security Considerations:** [If applicable, e.g. channel auth, env/config handling] ### Automatic-recall budgeting - Account for the actual `HintBlock.hint` content when reserving space for the host-generated recall wrapper. - Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and bound the full injected recall text, rather than only the retrieved body. - Update budget tests to measure the actual hint content instead of fields from the previous message format. - Remove the hard-coded request-budget expectation derived from the old host prompt. Existing boundary tests verify the complete-message budget. - Update the toolkit-builder test's mock configuration to include `coding_mode.enabled`. ### Shutdown lifecycle - Store and reuse a single HTTP cleanup task across repeated and concurrent `close()` calls, rather than treating a cleared client reference as proof that cleanup completed. - Use `asyncio.shield()` so cancelling a caller's wait does not cancel the underlying cleanup. Cancellation still propagates to the caller. - Preserve the actual cleanup result. If HTTP cleanup fails, subsequent `close()` calls continue to return `False` instead of incorrectly reporting success. - Add regression coverage for repeated close after failure, caller cancellation followed by successful or failed cleanup, concurrent close calls, and repeated close after success. Preserve credential redaction in failure logs. ### Review follow-up **Item 1 — Reuse the base automatic-recall flow** The session-aware `auto_memory_search()` override is retained in this PR. I agree that the base flow could serve the current default configuration with query expansion disabled. The retained override passes the current QwenPaw session ID to OpenViking, allowing session-based query expansion when `query_expansion="auto"` is enabled through the documented source change. The READMEs now clarify that query expansion remains disabled by default, requires editing source and redeploying, and depends on available session history or an archive overview. No Console or Agent configuration switch is introduced. **Item 3 — Use one UTF-8 clipping implementation** Reuse `_clip_utf8()` for both automatic recall and explicit search. When truncation cannot retain meaningful text, return an empty string rather than a marker-only result. Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and multibyte character boundaries. **Item 4 — Flatten persistence filtering** Combine role, persisted-ID, and pending-ID filtering into one pass, and calculate the `every_turn` condition once. Preserve the existing separation between successful append and successful commit progress. **Item 5 — Reduce test coupling** Move shared fixtures into `conftest.py` and centralize manager cleanup. Budget tests measure the complete injected message and check the intact notice and nonempty recalled body, rather than relying on hard-coded values derived from host prompt wording. ### Additional small cleanups - Use a direct relative import in `plugin.py`. - Return `await self._request(...)` directly in the two forwarding client methods. - Catch `httpx.RequestError` alone, since it already includes `TimeoutException`. The explicit-search small-budget guard is retained as a defensive useful-body check if the fixed source limits are reduced, with boundary-test coverage. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [x] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.) - [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes - [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery) - [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py` - [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/` ## Testing The tests cover complete-message recall budgets, oversized and multibyte results, intact safety notices, empty-result handling, persistence retries and deduplication, bounded caches, and shutdown lifecycle behavior. Shutdown regression tests verify that repeated or concurrent calls cannot report success before cleanup completes, caller cancellation does not cancel the shared cleanup task, and genuine cleanup failures remain reported as failures. ## Evidence ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD" \ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \ PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ plugins/memory/openviking/tests ``` ```text 146 passed in 1.21s ``` ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --all-files git diff --check ``` All applicable hooks passed. ### OpenViking v0.5.2.1 — session-based query expansion For this verification, the request was changed in source to `query_expansion="auto"` and the commit policy was set to `auto`. The user first established the current project, then asked a follow-up using only “它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？” After switching from R3 to R4, the server’s expansion followed the new project. Selected response fields from the OpenViking v0.5.2.1 query-expansion verification: ```json { "query_expansion": "used", "planned_queries": [ "它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？请直接回答，不要主动调用工具，也不要读取本地文件。", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 设备编号", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 维护窗口" ] } ``` The corresponding answer returned `OV-UP-B610E899` and Sunday at 20:45. Additional checks confirmed that recall remained functional after a message-count-triggered commit retained recent messages, and a fresh session did not borrow the previous session’s history for query expansion. Long-term memory remains shared across those conversations. The `used` status alone is not treated as proof of query rewriting; the expanded `planned_queries` above provide that evidence. ## Additional Notes 1. The plugin keeps its own automatic-recall method to pass the current session ID to OpenViking. If `query_expansion` is changed from `"off"` to `"auto"` in the source code, OpenViking can use the current conversation's history to expand search queries. 2. Extracting the shared recall-budget helper into `BaseMemoryManager`, and updating both OpenViking and PowerContext to inherit it, is intentionally deferred to a separate follow-up PR.

prs.title: fix(agents): fall back when a saved model provider is disabled
prs.body:
Fixes #8579

## Description

**Cause.** `agent.json` keeps the last selected `active_model` after its provider is switched off on the Models page. `create_model_and_formatter` then hit `if not provider.enabled: raise ProviderError("Provider is disabled")` with no fallback, so every channel run for that agent failed with "Internal error" even though an enabled global active model exists.

**Fix.** For a persisted agent slot (not an explicit per-request `model_slot_override`) whose provider is disabled, fall back to the global active model when it names a different, enabled provider, and log a warning naming the agent and both models. This is the same path as an agent with no model set, as suggested in the issue. An explicit override of a disabled provider still raises, as does the case with no usable global model.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8579

**Security Considerations:** None; an explicit override is never rewritten.

prs.title: fix(console): scroll wide Markdown tables inside the bubble
prs.body:
## Description

Markdown tables wider than the message bubble overflow the conversation and cannot be scrolled. The console applied `overflow-x: auto` directly to `.x-markdown table`, but a table box is not a scroll container, so the rule had no effect; the overflowing columns were painted past the message list and were unreadable.

This makes the table itself a block-level scroll container:

- `display: block` lets the table act as a scroll container;
- `width: max-content` keeps narrow tables compact;
- `max-width: 100%` caps the scroll box to the bubble width;
- `overflow-x: auto` adds the horizontal scrollbar.

Small tables keep their normal appearance; wide tables now scroll inside the bubble instead of bleeding out of it.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8845

prs.title: docs(config): document envs merge, replace and reset semantics
prs.body:
## Description

The environment variables section of the config docs reduced the `/envs` API to `GET/PUT/DELETE /envs`. That is incomplete and actively misleading:

- `PUT /envs` replaces the whole stored set, so submitting only one key deletes every other stored variable.
- `PATCH /envs` (merge, keeps omitted keys) and `GET /envs/catalog` were not documented.
- `DELETE /envs/{key}` returns 400 for known settings; those must use `POST /envs/{key}/reset`, which was not documented.

The QA agent and the guidance skill point users at these docs. With only `PUT /envs` documented, the agent recommended a single-key `PUT` when asked how to add one variable, silently removing the user's other credentials. It also recommended `DELETE` for known settings, which returns 400.

This PR documents the actual router behavior in both the English and Chinese docs. No API change.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8843

**Security Considerations:** Prevents documentation-driven loss of stored environment variables (credentials). No code or API behavior changed.

issues.title: [Bug]: Agent cards show "<$0.01" for an agent that has spent nothing
issues.body:
### Affected component

web dashboard

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

An agent whose recorded spend is exactly $0 (for example, all of its calls went to a free local model) shows "<$0.01 this month" on its card on the Agents page and in its drawer, instead of "$0.00".

`formatUsd` in `web/src/lib/format.ts` returns "<$0.01" for any value under 0.01, and 0 is under 0.01 ([`format.ts` L3-L7](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/d1a44f697beac5118a589c053d4a4344435f1548/web/src/lib/format.ts#L3-L7)). The formatter has behaved this way since it was added in #7665. The dashboard's metrics row uses its own formatter, which already returns "$0" for zero.

### Expected behavior

No spend shows as "$0.00"; "<$0.01" is only for spend that is above zero but under a cent.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Use an agent only with a model that has no configured cost (a free local
   model), so its recorded calls cost $0.
2. Open the Agents page.
3. The agent's card shows "<$0.01 this month".
```

### Impact

Suggests a small charge where there is none, which is confusing for people running free local models.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

v0.9.0 (with some open web PRs merged locally; none touches this formatter). The code reference is from current `master` (`d1a44f697`).

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux server (amd64); desktop browser

### Regression?

Unknown

- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

## Summary

- Centralize `chacha20poly1305` at 0.11 as a workspace dependency and migrate the secret store (`zeroclaw-config`) and CA key encryption (`zeroclaw-tls`) from 0.10 to that dependency.
- Drop the direct `chacha20poly1305` dependencies from `zeroclaw-providers` and `zeroclaw-runtime`. In the provider OAuth helper, `random_base64url` now fills its buffer from the operating system through `rand::rngs::SysRng`. The requested byte length and URL-safe Base64 output are unchanged.
- Replace the Telegram photo test’s live API call with a local Wiremock server that returns a controlled rejection. This changes only the test.
- Related to #11847. This update can merge independently of XMPP and #12322.

## Testing

- `enc2_ciphertext_from_chacha20poly1305_010_remains_compatible` decrypts a synthetic 0.10.1 secret-store fixture, verifies the key file is unchanged, and compares the ciphertext produced by 0.11 against the fixture with the same key and nonce.
- `ca_key_envelope_from_chacha20poly1305_010_remains_compatible` decrypts a synthetic 0.10.1 encrypted CA key envelope and verifies that 0.11 produces the same ciphertext with the same inputs. It also checks that tampered and truncated envelopes are rejected.
- The Telegram test uses a local mock to exercise both photo submissions, with and without a caption, and verifies the expected error path.
- Local checks previously recorded include formatting, locked Cargo metadata and diff validation. See this PR’s Checks tab for results on the current head.

## Security and Privacy

The secret store and CA key paths continue to use authenticated encryption. OAuth random bytes still come from the operating system. The compatibility fixtures contain synthetic data, and the Telegram test uses a fake token and makes no external API request.

## Compatibility and Rollback

The `enc2` and encrypted CA key formats are unchanged. The fixed-input fixtures verify that the new implementation reads old data and generates the same ciphertext for those formats. Reverting this PR requires no data migration for either format. The SQLite bridge is outside this PR, and the shared advisory is tracked in #12320.

None.

prs.title: feat(web): enable browser voice for OIDC sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Includes the merged #12269 through master.
- Enable browser dictation and narration for an OIDC dashboard operator without a paired-device token.
- Store voice choices in the current browser profile under a SHA-256 digest of the verified principal ID. The paired-device API remains the source of truth for paired browsers.
- Clear capture and narration state when the signed-in principal changes. Use the existing global silence setting and dashboard permission checks.

### What this does, simply

An OIDC operator with Chat and Config access can enable the microphone and speaker in **Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio**. Each account in the browser has its own opt-in choices.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested? Yes.
- Interface: `web`, dashboard chat and voice settings.
- Setup: HTTPS dashboard with an OIDC operator and an unpaired browser profile.
- Sign in, open **Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio**, enable dictation and reading, and choose a voice. Open chat, dictate, pause for the configured interval, and listen to the reply. Change to a different OIDC account in the same browser and verify its initial settings.
- After: controls work without pairing, the transcript is sent once and another account starts with its own preferences.
- On the parent PR: the voice preferences require a paired-device record.

### How I tested

#### Markdown narration regression

Narration reads Markdown content. It omits heading, list, emphasis, and horizontal-rule markers, and preserves the text inside HTML tags. It reads referenced GFM footnotes once after the reply, in first-reference order, and skips unused definitions. Literal punctuation in code is preserved.

The Windows equivalent of npm run test:voice passed 41/41 tests at 7baa195. The new regression exercises Markdown formatting, visible HTML text, and repeated and unused footnotes. Audible playback evidence from earlier revisions is recorded separately.


- Focused component suite: 33 passed. The OIDC test exercises settings, fake recognition and playback in an unpaired session, denies stale capture after switching accounts, and checks that no paired-device route was called.
- CI relied on: Web Permission Tests and CI Required Gate. The voice suite was run directly, as shown below. 
- Coverage gap: the new deployment smoke test did not exercise real speech input or audio output. The localized preview is covered by the voice suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New capabilities? Yes. Voice controls are available in an existing chat session. Browser audio permissions and gateway permissions still apply. Account-scoped storage holds only voice choices.
- New external network calls? No. The existing recognition mode remains an explicit user choice.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. At runtime, browser storage associates preferences with the SHA-256 digest of the verified account ID, which is a persistent pseudonymous identifier. The raw account ID and session credentials are excluded from the new storage key.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced or changed? No. Dictation continues through the ordinary composer.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

- Revert this PR and rebuild the dashboard assets.
- Feature flags or config toggles: none added.
- Observable failure symptoms: missing controls for an opted-in OIDC account, or settings shared across accounts.

### Live OIDC acceptance

An operator tested an unpaired browser against a deployed dashboard using Keycloak. Dictation, single send after the configured silence, and audible narration worked before and after closing the window and signing in again. The test identified an English preview for a Portuguese narrator. The follow-up selects sample text and utterance language from the narrator locale. The automated suite verifies a Portuguese sample with an English WebUI and verifies that the saved automatic-reading default is restored for the same principal. The chat-local long press remains scoped to the conversation.


## Scope boundary and blast radius

Historical validation before #12269 merged. Head `3930bb832` incorporates #12269 at `d6cdf58ec`. The OIDC-specific diff still covers the same six files. All 35 voice tests and the production WebUI build passed locally on the aligned head. The OIDC branch applies only when the session has Chat and Config access. The paired-device persistence path continues through its existing API. In an authorized browser profile, an existing preference for the same OIDC account is migrated to the digest key.

## Current interface evidence

Captured production components from PR head `25431a005` in headed Chrome with a synthetic OIDC session, preferences and conversation. The settings view shows that the paired-device picker is absent. The chat view shows the microphone and speaker. The fixture also verified that localStorage uses a SHA-256 key.

![OIDC browser voice settings without device pairing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/c2eef22421000bc322ad71e45bbdf6b668f29243/.pr-evidence/voice-oidc-settings-25431a005.png)

![OIDC chat microphone and speaker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/c2eef22421000bc322ad71e45bbdf6b668f29243/.pr-evidence/voice-oidc-chat-25431a005.png)

## Test output and live smoke test

```text
npm run test:voice
✔ OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts
ℹ tests 35
ℹ pass 35
ℹ fail 0
```

The OIDC test also checks that a Chat-only principal sees no controls and cannot write preferences. The integrated Jarvis WebUI build `66086f10f` passed `npm run build` and was deployed as static assets. In a fresh, unpaired Chrome profile, Keycloak sign-in reached the voice settings. Both toggles persisted after reload, the chat showed the microphone and speaker, and the browser stored a digest key. No microphone capture or playback was attempted during this smoke test.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Restack after #12269 merged

The current branch is based on master at fa48765b, which contains #12269. The diff now contains just six OIDC documentation, frontend, and test files. At 32b613b0b, npm run test:voice passed 41/41 on Linux with Node 24, including the unpaired OIDC access and account isolation case.

## Current-head validation and OIDC interface evidence

The branch is aligned with master after #12269 merged. The current diff is the OIDC voice follow-up and a narration separator regression. Only OIDC sessions with both Chat and Config access can enable voice controls. The paired-device path is unchanged. Browser-local preferences are keyed by a SHA-256 digest of the verified OIDC principal ID. The key does not contain the issuer, subject, CSRF token or paired bearer token.

At `8d1f14ca2b0fd6d31647ce40faca7f4340e4eac9`, Linux Node 24 `npm run test:voice` reported:

```text
✔ OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts
✔ narration speaks HTML text and referenced footnotes without formatting
✔ narration separates HTML lines and table cells without splitting inline words
ℹ tests 42
ℹ pass 42
ℹ fail 0
```

The hosted Web Permission Tests and CI Required Gate are tracked on the PR Checks tab for this head.

The captures below are from the deployed Jarvis integration, whose frontend source revision is `aadd4f027` and asset is `index-Cwr3ds5v.js`. A fresh Chrome profile signed in through Keycloak with no paired token. The captures show desktop and 390px mobile configuration, and the microphone and speaker in the same OIDC chat session. The crops omit account identifiers and browser chrome. This is a visual check of the deployed integration. The exact PR head was tested separately above. No new microphone capture or audible playback was run.

- [Desktop OIDC voice settings](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/bc90a43a9a99d403557fb3f9aaa3bafb75c14407/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-settings-desktop-20261122.png)

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Rust XMPP with optional legacy OMEMO
prs.body:
<!-- replay-cache-fix-20261110 -->
## TLS replay cache follow-up

Revision `f5b5735eb` classifies new TLS-only message IDs at insertion and evicts only that class. Older and encrypted markers remain in the shared replay table, preserving cross-mode deduplication and reviewed inbox release. The private store recognizes the exact legacy and classified schemas.

The old query reproduces a missing encrypted replay marker after exceeding the TLS retention limit. The new regression drives the real private store and offline review/release command through TLS eviction; fresh TLS-to-OMEMO initialization and earlier socket deadline regressions also pass. Integrated XMPP, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI remains authoritative.

<!-- control-write-fix-20261110 -->
## Control-write deadline follow-up

Revision `5e1f62ae7` includes `adbc57d18` and master `a4beef9a6`. Control stanzas now have a 60-second write deadline. A stalled or failed control write returns an error from the connection writer, which releases queued replies and lets the existing listener supervisor reconnect. The writer does not replay uncertain sends.

A regression driving the real writer with a stalled sink fails before the fix and passes after it. Healthy and broken control writes are also covered. Integrated XMPP, HTTP-cache and runtime tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI on this revision remains authoritative.

<!-- review-fix-20261110:start -->
## Review follow-up (2026-11-10)

Published head: 1d062fc50eb74070a6267b4d838875edf763e892. Updated with master 6877da56d.

Atomic peer-device index cleanup for reviewed offline OMEMO session reset, with index-bound review tokens and an actual encrypted send to the surviving device.

Local integration regression tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed. Hosted CI for this exact head is pending; earlier CI/approval does not validate the new revision. Detailed boundary evidence is in the reply to the corresponding review thread.
<!-- review-fix-20261110:end -->

## Summary



Base branch: `master`.



Implement feature-gated native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO. Related #9814. Depends on #12015.



### What this does, simply



The native channel owns encrypted receipts independently of the socket. Reconnect reuses the exclusive store; completed runtime and control receipts can be recorded while offline. First-contact key publication explicitly requests readable public nodes.



<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at f120f8722. Retained scoped-chat authorization and XMPP policy coverage. Canonical API generation, npm run test:auth (including xmppPolicy.test.ts), and the production build passed. Native XMPP/OMEMO validation remains covered by the published commit's CI. The dependency on #12015 remains.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



Run the `xmpp` and `native_ingress_` channel-library filters with `--no-default-features --features channel-xmpp`; then run `crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/xmpp_native/managed_server.py` using the documented disposable loopback-only fixture.



### Earlier validation (historical)



Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 47f16954424bcc3787379e5e1d2c21df52daf100, including every source-image build. The inherited master root-fixture packaging fix is confirmed across the current Dockerfile/Containerfile source matrix. Integrated validation passed 69 XMPP tests (4 separately marked ignored), 5 shared-ingress tests, all four real encrypted interoperability scenarios and strict channel/test and root binary Clippy. Fresh-account scenarios remove pre-created bot nodes and verify public key discovery without roster subscription. Offline receipt completion, explicit publication policy/refusal, live admission filtering, queue overflow and deferred authorized ping ordering are covered. Human changes-requested review has not been dismissed; re-review is requested.



Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



OMEMO identity keys, signed prekeys and ratchet state are stored as JSON in the private omemo.sqlite3 database with mode 0600 and exclusive ownership; they are not encrypted at rest by the vault. The vault is required for new identity creation and encrypts queued ingress payloads. The account password uses the existing secret configuration field. Uncertain admitted work remains unreleasable. Public device lists and bundles request open access; these contain public keys, while live peer allowlists and fingerprint pins still gate message admission. Server publication refusal fails explicitly. No private deployment information, real identities, credentials, or messages are included.



- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: Yes â€” the optional channel owns a private mode-0600 OMEMO database and existing-vault access for identity creation and ingress sealing.

- New external network calls: Yes â€” configured XMPP service and bounded protocol exchanges.

- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes â€” the account password is a secret field; queued ingress uses vault ciphertext, while long-term OMEMO keys and ratchet state use the private database described above. Fingerprint pins authorize peer devices; they do not encrypt the local key store.

- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.

- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No â€” protocol content remains inside the existing shared dispatch/policy boundary.



## Compatibility (required)



Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO remains distinct from OMEMO v2. The existing migration and replay-protection boundaries remain documented. Offline administration requires stopping the channel owner, including while its socket is disconnected. Existing nodes with incompatible publication policy require owner reconciliation. No toolchain-floor change.



## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)



Disable the XMPP feature/configuration or revert the code subject to documented state compatibility. Preserve newer ratchets, replay markers and uncertain admitted records. Stop the channel owner before supported offline inspection/release. Observe explicit publication errors, refused admission and unreleasable completed receipts.



## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)



None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.


SQLite scope correction: #12322 remains draft pending a published Matrix storage dependency (matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk#7456). Its workspace-only bridge was removed from this PR; registry compatibility is preserved and #12320 remains the shared advisory tracker. No SQLite waiver is added here.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
The discovery exchange now waits for outbound queue capacity inside its existing 10-second budget; queue admission and response share one deadline. Peer timeout remains a typed inbound rejection. Added regressions cover full queue admission, the shared deadline, and cancellation without a late IQ. Integrated validation: 76 XMPP tests pass (4 lab-only ignored).

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Security maintenance — remove the XMPP chrono dependency

This PR includes the parser correction directly in its branch, commit f7e041a. The XMPP dependency path is now tokio-xmpp → the locally patched xmpp-parsers → time. Its resolved dependency subtree contains neither chrono nor chrono-tz.

The motivation is RustSec RUSTSEC-2026-0543 and the security-maintenance work tracked in #12505. The former Utc::now()/timestamp() calls are supported APIs. The advisory identifies chrono as unmaintained. This change removes that dependency from the new XMPP transport.

The patch preserves the parser's MPL-2.0 license, copyright notices, source commit and original registry checksum. The imported parser is about 1 MB. Functional changes cover its date/time APIs, corresponding parser tests and manifests, plus rejection of unsupported CID algorithms and panic-free handling of malformed CSS declarations and nested unknown XHTML tags. PATCH.md documents the public type changes, source provenance, test commands and eventual removal of the local override. Upstream xmpp-rs currently declines AI-assisted contributions, so this correction is carried in this PR.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.98.1

- Default parser suite passed 640 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- Strict XML (pedantic) suite passed 669 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --tests passed.
- cargo fmt --all -- --check passed.
- Dependency-tree inspection confirmed the tokio-xmpp subtree has no chrono or chrono-tz.
- A channel regression test parses delayed-delivery XML and checks nanosecond precision, negative sub-hour offsets and rejection of malformed dates.

The security gate still audits existing workspace dependencies. Other chrono/chrono-tz consumers and the separate ZIP advisory retain their existing tracking. Production deployment of this parser update remains pending.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Shared HTTP pool prerequisite

Depends on #12323 for the shared Tokio-runtime HTTP pool ownership repair. That repair is intentionally kept in its dedicated approved PR rather than copied into this feature diff. The integrated test deployment composes that PR separately and retains the fix. If master-based pooled-dispatch tests fail before #12323 lands, report/rerun that shared prerequisite failure rather than restoring unrelated cache changes here.

## Archived XMPP evidence

Artifacts are retained at the immutable pre-cleanup commit.

prs.title: test(gateway): skip the reply-end write-deadline test on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends` has failed in every scheduled Windows run since #12244 added it. That includes run 42952365996 on 1a79f89d1e, the run on the v0.9.0 release commit (43147792721 on 6c78ba59bc), and the latest, 44009787866 on cda933e6b9. Each fails after about 32 s with `a chat that could not write its reply's end closes its conversation: still live: [...]`.
  - The test pins both socket buffers to 64 KiB. It lets the browser read a 7 MB `chunk` frame and then stop reading, and expects the 7 MB `done` frame's write to stall until the chat gives up at `WRITE_DEADLINE`.
  - Windows doesn't stall that write. Winsock accepts a send of any size while less than `SO_SNDBUF` is queued. Once the browser has read the chunk, the whole `done` frame is accepted, the write completes, and the conversation correctly stays live because the browser's socket is still open.
  - This PR gates the test to non-Windows targets with `#[cfg(not(windows))]` and a comment that gives the reason.
  - I didn't force the stall some other way, for two reasons:
    - A zero `SO_SNDBUF` on a non-blocking Windows socket has no documented behaviour, so it couldn't be shown to be deterministic.
    - Stopping the read before the chunk drains would move the stall on Linux onto the chunk write. That is a different branch from the turn-end write this test exists to cover.
- **Scope boundary:** Test-only. The write deadline (`chat_core.rs`, `tokio::time::timeout(WRITE_DEADLINE, self.sink.send(message))`) and all other product code are unchanged. Every other platform still compiles and runs the test, and Linux CI runs it on every PR. The other two failures in the same Windows job, #12483 and #12484, are not touched.
- **Blast radius:** One `#[cfg(test)]` module in `zeroclaw-gateway`. The small-buffer helpers and `mount_flood` keep other callers, so nothing becomes unused on Windows. No released binary changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12400. Related #12244.

### What this does, simply

The dashboard chat gives up on a browser that has stopped reading, so a stuck tab can't hold a conversation open forever. One test checks this by making the network buffers tiny, so that the end of a long reply can't be delivered, and then waiting for the chat to give up.

On Windows that trick doesn't work: Windows accepts the whole reply into its own memory however small the buffers are set. The reply is delivered, nothing is stuck, and the chat rightly carries on, so the test fails. Nothing is wrong with the chat itself.

This PR stops running that one test on Windows and records why. Linux CI keeps running it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, but only on Windows, through the `ci:windows` label. No local steps are needed.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None. No user-facing surface changes; the test belongs to the gateway side of the `web` dashboard chat.
- **Setup / preconditions:** add the `ci:windows` label to this PR. The "Advisory Windows test selection" job should choose `mode=scoped`, packages `fill-translations`, `xtask`, `zeroclaw` and `zeroclaw-gateway`, with `needs_plugin_host=true`. That is what the selector printed locally for this change.
- **Steps to run:** open the job `Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=true)` and search its log for `a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** no match in either gateway run: the scoped baseline step, or the `-p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib` plugin-host step. The other `dashboard_core::tests::` tests still pass, including `queued_chat_output_cannot_starve_permission_checks`, which uses the same small-buffer helpers.
  - The job's overall status isn't the signal. It is advisory, and #12483, a different gateway test that fails on Windows, is still open.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the test is listed as `FAIL [ ~32s]` with the panic at `dashboard_core.rs:2417:13`, as in the scheduled `Platform Test (Windows)` job of run 44009787866.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the CI Required Gate on this PR's head, once it runs: fmt, Clippy and the Linux tests. The local runs below cover the same commands for the one changed crate. PR CI runs no Windows tests, which is the gap below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows. Only the `ci:windows` run above, or the nightly scheduled run after merge, shows the test gone from the Windows list. macOS isn't covered either: the scheduled macOS job has failed at "Install cargo-nextest" since 2026-10-31, so it hasn't run this test since it landed. That failure is unrelated to this PR.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, at this head.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 11s   (no warnings)

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends -- --exact   # 3 runs
  test dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 915 filtered out; finished in 11.20s
  (11.18s and 11.16s on the other two runs)

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
  unittests src/lib.rs:              test result: ok. 915 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
  tests/golden_frames.rs:            test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored
  tests/nodes_mdns.rs:               test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  tests/relay_dashboard_ingress.rs:  test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  ```

  On Linux the test takes about 11 s, the 10 s write deadline plus setup. So there the write does stall and the deadline does end the conversation.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - That nothing becomes unused when the test is compiled out, as on Windows. I temporarily replaced `#[cfg(not(windows))]` with the always-false `#[cfg(any())]` and ran `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`. It finished with no warnings, and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- --list` listed 915 tests without this one. I then restored the file.
  - Not verified:
    - Anything on Windows itself.
    - A Windows-target build: `cargo +1.96.1 check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests` stopped in the `ring` and `libsqlite3-sys` build scripts (`failed to find tool "lib.exe"`), because no MSVC toolchain was available, before reaching any ZeroClaw crate.
    - The precise Winsock buffering mechanism. The diagnosis is inferred from the CI symptom.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head on base cda933e6b9; `cargo test` output above; scheduled Windows runs 42952365996 through 44009787866 for the failure.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the output tails above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** on Linux the test still runs and passes. With the cfg forced false, as on Windows, it is absent and the module still builds clean.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - No workspace-wide Clippy with `--features ci-all`: the change is one attribute in one crate's test module, and CI's Lint job runs that.
  - No Windows run: none was available. The `ci:windows` label is the check.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk, test-only: `git revert <sha>` is the plan.

### Current hosted Windows evidence

At `bf10df4fc90ea04252ef27c90df27ff8ab2ef28b`, [the advisory Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44482561096/job/135418393950) lists no occurrence of the excluded test and passes `queued_chat_output_cannot_starve_permission_checks` in both gateway selections. Other tests still fail; this does not claim an entirely green Windows job. The local-testing limitations above describe the original author run.

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

When RPC deletion has admitted the matching gateway durable session, it fences that gateway lifecycle so an open WebSocket cannot recreate the deleted session. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Opt-in durable metadata and current-session tools. Admission/transactional ownership checks prevent stale or cross-session mutations.
- New external network calls? **No.** Session-prompt approval previews use existing transports without marker expansion/upload. Matrix clients may independently fetch URL previews; disable those in the reviewing client when appropriate. A relay-terminated dashboard exposes previews and list results to that configured relay.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Opaque bounded text intentionally enters the system prompt, beneath immutable host/safety authority.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Exact default-required single-use approval, current-session incarnation ownership, direct-only dispatch, complete prompt-budget checks and output masking contain the risk. `disabled` relaxes additional content-bound confirmation, not ordinary authorization, and can permit auto-approved writes without operator preview. Hooks cannot read sensitive bodies/results. Content hashes can permit low-entropy guessing; masking is not secrecy. Sensitive text-mode exchanges omit unrepresentable media declarations; ordinary rounds/native carriers retain upstream behavior. Previously stored opaque transcripts are not retroactively scrubbed.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for Rust source APIs; additive/defaulted wire and configuration fields.** Feature-off users retain ordinary session operations but are affected by the explicit lifecycle, retention, reserved-name and native-prompt changes below.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** `[channels].session_prompts_enabled` defaults to `false`; global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval` accepts `required`/`disabled`, global default `required`, profile default inheritance. SQLite only; enabled JSONL is rejected. When session prompts are enabled, operator WebSocket Chat needs gateway persistence or fails with `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED` before dispatch; scoped signed-in dashboard Chat uses the daemon RPC session backend.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- **If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users:** Back up SQLite, rebuild out-of-tree Rust consumers, match Web/ZeroCode clients to the daemon and restart after enabling persistence. Existing WebSockets need reconnect after policy changes; channels need restart. RPC resolves current policy at primary-turn entry and again at protected session/storage effects after waits; the durable attachment owner remains bound to the admitted turn. Add `Config.session_prompt_approval = Required`, `ChannelsConfig.session_prompts_enabled = false`, and `RiskProfileConfig.session_prompt_approval = None` to struct literals to preserve defaults.

For all scoped dashboard approvals, an unacknowledged answer now emits an error, and an RPC delivery failure closes the socket and refuses outstanding approvals. A `retryable: true` RPC response only confirms a bound strict request was pending at response time; it may expire before the next answer. Missing status is treated as unconfirmed. Replaying a retryable preview restarts the Web countdown with its original duration, so the displayed countdown can overstate remaining time; the core deadline still controls the decision.

**Observable changes, including with attachments disabled:**

- `sessions_reset` invokes whole-session reset, clearing attachments and rotating incarnation atomically in SQLite. Its "already empty" wording still counts removed messages, not attachment removal. Message-only clear preserves attachments.
- Durable `/new` deletion failure keeps existing history and reports `channel-runtime-new-session-failed` instead of claiming success. Legacy JSONL can treat a transcript it cannot inspect as absent. Without an attached backend and with prompt injection disabled, ordinary ephemeral behavior remains.
- Chat RPC deletion considers the raw, `rpc_` and `gw_` keys but refuses distinct candidate sessions rather than deleting all aliases. A scoped owner may delete an authorized live-only RPC session when the backend is unavailable; no gateway turn is cancelled without a proven shared durable identity. Guarded JSONL RPC and gateway deletion require an exact, single-link file with an unambiguous complete filename on positively identified Linux ext storage with casefold disabled. Names containing underscores, including ordinary `rpc_` and `gw_` keys, are refused on every platform; persistent JSONL deletion through these paths is refused on macOS and other unproved filesystems. This conservative restriction applies even with session prompts disabled. Use SQLite for supported guarded persistent-session deletion; JSONL file cleanup is non-transactional and external writers are not coordinated. The operator Dashboard directs operators to the owning interface for RPC or channel sessions. On JSONL, the Delete button can still appear enabled for a gateway row. The backend returns a conflict and preserves the transcript. Custom backends that cannot provide identity-bound admission fail closed. ACP remains separate. Queue admission can report `SESSION_BUSY`; a deleted gateway connection must reconnect. A cancellation delivered before a subsequent failure cannot be undone.
- Current-session views, strict previews, turn spans and delegate forensic principal identity use the canonical storage key. Public RPC/cost/OpenCode/shell identity remains separate; `ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID` prefers caller-visible identity. ACP identity is unchanged.
- The three session-prompt tool names are reserved for plugins/skills even when disabled, including prepared-skill registration. Rename conflicts. They also follow master's built-in selection: default full includes eligible prompt tools; minimal requires their explicit names in `[tools].optional` and a reload. This selection changes availability, not authorization or injection of already-stored prompts into an enabled primary Chat turn. Deferred MCP tools must use full `server__tool` names rather than conflicting bare suffixes. Indirect `unfiltered_tool_arcs` excludes prompt tools; use canonical direct calls.
- Native tool framing changes from 42 to 36 characters ("Use tools when this request needs it") for exact budget substitution, including feature-off turns. Native prompt fingerprints consequently change. Complete native/XML prompt framing is paired; nonempty attachment overflow fails closed without truncating host context.
- Strict mutation previews visibly encode Unicode 17 format/default-ignorable characters, including legitimate joiners and variation selectors. This can change how joined text and emoji look in the preview; stored text, content hashes and provider context keep the original bytes. This is display encoding, not a new restriction on valid prompt text.
- Channel retention preserves upstream selection after the last user-role row, including synthetic text-tool results. Text-protocol call/result exchanges are omitted from retained history; native-tool retention remains unchanged. Privacy projection scans the complete exchange before selection so host-marked results can identify sensitive calls. Provider working history is unchanged.
- Export recovery separately recognizes malformed JSON/XML/MiniMax prompt-tool material before ordinary diagnostic output; shared streamed detection retains master's name-based behavior. Recovery is best-effort, not approval or execution. Unrepresentable text media carriers are omitted only for marked sensitive rounds; ordinary media behavior remains upstream.
- Programmatic `HookHandler::before_llm_call` is skipped when the request or active scope carries private session-prompt content, including max-iteration summaries. Its transforms, cancellation and model selection do not apply to these requests; ordinary requests retain them. Ordinary unmarked invocation examples retain hook processing when the feature is disabled; host-marked sensitive results remain protected. Observational input masking remains separate, and provider working history is never replaced with a masked hook projection.
- With single-tool rounds enabled, the host instruction is inserted before the private Session Prompts suffix. Diagnostic exports retain that instruction, and host protocol replacement leaves opaque attachment bytes unchanged. Trim reconstruction preserves the canonical host prompt before reapplying the transient instruction. Ordinary no-attachment and no-system behavior is preserved. The guide documents a reserved-heading limitation: host text (workspace files, skill/tool descriptions) with a standalone `## Session Prompts` after a blank line can be mistaken for the private suffix, leaving later tool-format/framing instructions unchanged and masking later host text in diagnostic/export views. Dispatch still rejects disallowed multi-tool calls; a failed turn may need a client retry. Use another heading in host text. This sync documents the limitation without changing runtime behavior.
- Independent child transcripts withhold attachment-bearing parent protocol scope, while same-agent inline SOP continues the primary transcript without attachment tools. Ordinary non-attachment child protocol inheritance is pre-existing and intentionally unchanged by this repair; this is not general child-context isolation.

The additive incarnation migration adopts valid unbound legacy attachments and removes mismatches/orphans. Historical legacy ownership cannot be proved retroactively; reset questionable old sessions. Feature-off does not delete stored attachments or scrub old histories. Downgrading and clearing history with an older binary can leave attachments that reappear after re-upgrade; reset affected sessions before downgrade and retain the backup.

`ToolResultMessage` adds the public `session_prompt_tool_result: bool` field.
Out-of-tree Rust struct literals must initialize it: use `false` for ordinary
results and preserve the host-derived value when replaying existing results.
Exhaustive patterns must bind the new field or use `..`; forwarding code must
preserve the flag.
The reserved key is exported as
`zeroclaw_api::model_provider::SESSION_PROMPT_HISTORY_RESULT_KEY`. Absent
serialized fields default to `false`; ordinary serialized results omit the
field. Marked results retain the existing native host key or text privacy
marker through Chat replay, including when a tool hook changed the original
call name. This is privacy provenance, not a capability or ACP prompt support.

The legacy public `SessionBackend::delete_session_owned` SQLite implementation retains master's two-autocommit deletion behavior. Runtime Chat now uses the identity-bound `admit_session_deletion` handle; external Rust consumers must select an operation matching their authorization and lifecycle requirements. Retiring or transactionally repairing the legacy method is deferred to a separate follow-up.

The runtime loop facade additionally exposes `scope_required_session_prompt_section` for channel orchestration. This is an additive Rust API; it grants no tool capability or wire access.

A stalled, non-reading dashboard client can delay sign-out close processing while the server sends the rejection of a forbidden Always approval. The existing SOP-frame reply path has the same timing limitation. Later input is still checked against current authority; this integration leaves that broader transport hardening for follow-up.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Reset/delete affected sessions with this version first when stored attachments must be removed; back up SQLite and restore the previous known-good binary/client pair. Reverting this feature restores previous source behavior but does not retroactively clean stored data. Keep the backup for migration recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = false` and restart. This stops injection/tools, not attachment persistence, redaction of previously marked history or the feature-off lifecycle/retention changes described above. Reset/delete is required to remove attachments.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_BUSY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `channel-runtime-new-session-failed`, strict-preview refusal or prompt-budget errors before provider dispatch. Modifying-hook callbacks not firing for classified private requests is intentional; deployments relying on hook transforms/cancellation/model selection must account for this exclusion and host-marked sensitive results retained across feature disablement. Inspect lifecycle/approval metadata without dumping prompt bodies. An idle old WebSocket refusing after committed deletion is expected behavior, not a reason to bypass the owner fence.
