prs.title: docs(runtime): record bounded managed HTTP credential write guard
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** propose one bounded ADR-016 record for the managed HTTP credential write guard required by #12408 and inherited by #12490.
- **Scope boundary:** documentation only. This PR grants no exception before independent Core Team review and merge.
- **Blast radius:** the runtime holding-crate exception table only.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12408 and #12490; Related RFC #12422.

### What this does, simply

A generic configuration writer must not bypass the dedicated operator credential API by inserting or replacing encrypted HTTP aliases through RPC single/batch/detached writes. The feature keeps those checks. This separate record names their bounded runtime adapter, canonical admitted config and writer guard, planned `zeroclaw-kernel` IPC destination and review conditions. The credential API, secret handling and HTTP use stay in their existing gateway/config/tools owners.

The authority cell is explicitly **Pending Core Team approval on this pull request**. The feature PRs depend on this record landing; they do not grant themselves an exception.

## Testing

### How you can test

N/A: documentation-only. Compare the row against ADR-016 and both save paths in #12408's `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`. Verify it covers the localized refusal and focused non-admin single/batch regression, but no secret resolution or new authority.

### How I tested

`git diff --check` passes. The existing real runtime non-admin single/batch mutation regression passed in the feature checkout; that is receiving-caller evidence, not a claim this documentation PR changes runtime behavior. Hosted Docs Style and structure checks will validate this head.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** documentation only; the separately reviewed feature refuses generic mutation.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? **Yes.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** revert the one-row documentation change before its dependent features merge, or reconsider the record together with those features afterwards.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** inaccurate placement guidance; no runtime behavior changes in this PR.

Depends on #12577 for the shared RustSec dependency updates. This PR excludes those updates from its diff.

prs.title: fix(web): show a detached chat turn and load its answer when it ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running, the page reloads the transcript once, before the turn is stored, and nothing reloads it again: the answer stays missing until a page reload or a conversation switch (#12107).
  - Hydration now asks `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` before it loads the stored transcript (asked after it, a turn ending between the two reads would leave its answer unloaded). While the turn is `running` there, the page shows it as running (before the composer unlocks, so it does not offer to send into it) and asks again every 2 s. Once the state leaves `running`, it loads the transcript once more. The gateway sets `idle` or `error` only after it has persisted the turn (`ws.rs`), so that load has the answer, or the stored outcome of a failed turn.
  - The watch ends without a reload on the next hydration, a conversation switch or clear, a model switch (a clear or model switch also stops one that has not started yet, while the first check or the transcript load is still out), unmount, and when its socket closes (the reopen reloads and asks again). A check still in flight when the watch ends is ignored. A failed check, including the 404 of a gateway without session persistence, reads as "not running": the page keeps today's single load and never retries in a loop. So does a check without an answer within 10 s (`STATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`): each check has its own deadline, and the page stops awaiting it at the deadline or when the watch ends, so a stuck request can neither keep the composer locked nor keep the turn shown as running. A daemon restarted mid-turn settles the abandoned turn to `error` (`recover_abandoned_session_turns`), which also ends the watch.
  - Because the check runs after any hydration, a page loaded while its conversation's turn runs (a reload, or a return from another conversation) also shows the turn and loads the answer when it ends.
  - A stored `running` state can outlive its turn: the gateway ignores errors on its state writes (`let _ = backend.set_session_state(...)` in `ws.rs`), so a failed `idle` write leaves `running` until the next restart. A page watching such a turn would stay locked, and Stop did nothing, because the abort route's `no_active_response` answer was discarded. Stop now reads that answer. The gateway also gives it in the moment between a turn's end (its cancel token removed) and its `idle` write, so the answer alone does not end the watch: two state checks that both start after it must still read the same turn id `running` (a check already out when Stop was refused does not count). Then the watch ends like a finished turn, with one reload, and later loads on this page do not lock on that turn id again. A different turn, or one without a turn id, is never treated as stale. This assumes the gateway's tail from token removal to the `idle` write takes well under one poll interval (2 s); it is a transcript write and a state write.
- **Scope boundary:** Web dashboard only (`web/src`); no gateway or API change: the state route already exists. A turn streaming on the page's own socket is not watched. A conversation switch still does not abort a detached turn (it aborts a live one, as before); Stop aborts a watched turn through the existing abort route, and the watch then loads the outcome. Accounts whose chat goes through the core (one conversation per socket) are unchanged: there is nothing to reload. No partial-answer replay while the turn runs; the answer appears when it is stored. Not covered, as possible follow-ups: an "outcome unknown" notice or tool-card settling across a reload; a deadline on the transcript load itself (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, unchanged here and signal-less on master); a turn that another client starts in the same conversation, which this page does not see live at any time (a dashboard socket receives turn frames only for its own prompts; the multi-viewer direction is #9002 and #11185), so a turn started while the transcript loads is shown at the next load, as one started just after it would be; and the known limit pinned in `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` (#11571), where a prompt another client committed with identical text hides the same prompt in flight here: transcript rows carry no turn id, so that needs a server change. A stale `running` state is handled per page: a reload, another tab or another device locks again until Stop is pressed there too; settling such a row on the server (for example in the abort route when no turn is registered) is a separate gateway change.
- **Blast radius:** `AgentContext` hydration, the socket close handler, and Stop's handling of the abort answer. One extra `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` per transcript load (a gateway without session persistence answers it with 404), plus one every 2 s only while a detached turn runs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12107. Related #9002 (the wider reconnect contract), #11571 (keeps the in-flight prompt on reload), #11965 (introduced the reload on reopen), #11185 (server-side session-owned turns for RPC clients; no dashboard change).

### What this does, simply

The gateway keeps working on a chat turn after the browser loses its connection, but it saves the turn only when it finishes. If the browser reconnected before that, it fetched the conversation too early, got no answer, and never looked again, so the chat sat idle with the answer missing. Now the browser asks the gateway whether the turn is still running, shows it as running if so, and fetches the conversation again as soon as the gateway reports it finished. It stops asking when the turn ends, when the user moves on, or when anything goes wrong, so it cannot loop. If the gateway's record wrongly says a turn is still running, pressing Stop now unlocks the chat after two checks instead of leaving it stuck.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Session persistence on (the default) and a turn that runs at least ~20 s (for example a shell tool running `sleep 20`).
- **Steps to run:** Send the turn. While it runs, drop the connection briefly (devtools offline for a few seconds, or restart a proxy in front of the gateway) so the socket closes and reopens. Wait for the turn to finish. Separately: reload the page while a turn runs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** After the reopen (or reload) the turn shows as running and the composer stays locked; when the turn finishes, the answer appears on its own and the composer unlocks. The prompt appears once.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** After the reopen the page stops showing the turn; the answer does not appear until the page is reloaded or the conversation switched.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the web test jobs run `test:contexts`, which includes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`, where the new tests live next to the existing reopen test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no browser test; the network-drop behaviour is covered by the manual browser check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (on this head, Node with the generated API files from an xtask web build)
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean
  - `npm run test:contexts`: `ℹ pass 159` / `ℹ fail 0` (`sessionLifecycle.test.ts`: 91 pass, 28 new)
  - `npm test`: 174 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:auth`: 247 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:navigation`: 9 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:permissions`: 34 pass, 0 fail
  - `git diff --check`, `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` on the changed files: clean
- **Rebased 2026-11-17 onto master `cda933e6b` (head `263acc119`), then server-side onto `1c8f2b59b` on 2026-11-19 (head `f84cfd0d9`, all three commits patch-identical by `git range-diff`) for the advisory fix in #12516.** Two conflicts with master, both in tests: the `/api/config/list` mock in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` (kept master's `configListEntries` and this PR's abort route), and the runtime mock in master's new `contextMeter.dom.test.ts` (#12074), which lacked this PR's `getState`; it now answers `idle`, folded into the first commit so every commit type-checks. The second commit is unchanged (`git range-diff`). On this head: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 180 pass; `npm run test:auth` 250 pass; `npm run test:contexts` 169 pass; `npm run test:permissions` 34 pass; `npm run test:navigation` 9 pass; 0 fail in all; `git diff --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` clean. The browser and gateway results below are from before this rebase.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new tests fail against master's `AgentContext.tsx` (same tests, master's production file): the reopen, page-load, Stop, switch and close scenarios fail at the first "shows the turn as running" assertion.
  - Reverting each guard one at a time (live-turn guard; switch keeps a detached turn; close, clear, model switch and unmount end the watch; the abort checks after the wait and after the last check; a failed check reads as not running; the reload when the turn ends; the per-check deadline, the race that stops awaiting a stuck request, the cancellation of a check when the watch ends; a hydration's pending check registered, and cancelled by clear and by model switch; no watch once cancelled before the load) fails at least one test each: 17 of 17.
  - Stale state (third commit): the tests for Stop on a turn the gateway is not running (unlock after two checks, no re-lock on the same turn id, re-lock on a new one), a check already out when Stop is refused, and a turn without an id fail against the previous head `44618fc9d` or the commit's first draft; a refusal followed by another running turn, Stop accepted, and Stop just as a turn ends (its answer still loads) pin the unchanged paths.
  - The tests also assert the prompt shows exactly once while the turn runs and after the answer loads, and that the page never re-sends it.
  - A turn that ends while the transcript loads (the test's gateway flips to `idle` when the snapshot is read) still gets its answer loaded; this fails with the state asked after the load.
  - **Server-side rebased 2026-11-19 onto master `dfc70a2b4` (head `a85e44959`)** for the Security fix in #12577; all three commits unchanged by `git range-diff`. The browser results below are from `7b47bd716` and the earlier gateway trials; the test results for the current head are in the first-turn note below.
  - A state check that never answers: hydration finishes at the deadline with the single load (no watch), and a stuck check during the watch ends it with one reload; the stuck request's signal is aborted in both, and on a conversation switch.
  - **First-turn "conversation started over" notice (reported by @GaijinSystems on this PR): explained and fixed in `61103768f`, hardened in `0f8d0602e`.** The gateway stores a turn's transcript only when the turn ends, so a socket that reopens during a conversation's first turn receives `session_start` with `message_count: 0`. If that frame arrived while the reopen's reload was still waiting on its `/state` check, the started-over check (`message_count === 0`, messages on screen, no turn shown as running) fired: it replaced the transcript with the notice and, by bumping `localMessageMutationVersionRef`, made the reload skip its transcript update — matching both the report's wording and the flake seen once in 8 browser runs above. That notice decision now waits for the reopen's state check: a running turn proceeds with no notice (the detached-turn watch shows it and loads the answer when it ends), and a check that reports no running turn shows the notice only if the reloaded transcript is still empty (so a first turn that ended during the outage still loads, without a notice). Four tests in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` pin this (notice deferred while the check is out; no notice and the answer loads when the turn turns out to be running; notice shown when the first turn really ended during the outage; a same-page reload during a running first turn). `0f8d0602e` closes two remaining paths: a deferred decision whose load failed without a retry no longer fires on a later reload, and a `session_start` after a failed load waits for the retry it triggers instead of flashing the notice; three more tests cover these (the deferred decision is still made by a retry, so a conversation that really started over keeps its notice). All seven fail with `AgentContext.tsx` at `a85e44959`; with it at `61103768f`, exactly the two hardening tests fail. When the state check has already answered that no turn is running, the notice still shows at once: the pre-existing "a reload in the middle of a turn that ended the conversation keeps only the notice" test is unchanged and passes. Validated on this head: `cargo web check` (generated API + `tsc -b`) clean; `npm run test:contexts`, `test:permissions`, `test:sops`, `test:sop-editor`, `test:auth`, `pretest:contexts` pass, 0 fail.
  - **Browser check against a real gateway with a real network drop** (added 2026-11-15; headless Chromium, isolated `zeroclaw gateway` built from this PR's first two commits, patch-id identical, plus unrelated carried changes). A fake OpenAI-compatible model streams a fixed answer over 20 s; a TCP proxy between browser and gateway drops every connection, with no close frames, and refuses new ones for a set time. Each trial opens `/agent/<alias>`, sends a message, cuts the network once the model's first words are on screen, then waits for the complete answer without any reload or navigation. Control: the same tree with this PR's two commits reverted and nothing else.

    | Network outage | Without this PR | With this PR |
    |---|---|---|
    | 3 s (the socket reopens while the turn still runs) | 0/5: one transcript load while the turn runs, the composer back to "Type a message...", the answer never shown | 5/5: "Running…" shown, `/state` polled every 2 s, the answer loaded when the turn ends |
    | 12 s (the turn ends during the outage) | 2/2 | 2/2 |

  - **Gateway side, without a browser:** over 30 drop-and-reopen trials (clean close, close then reopen, abrupt TCP drop), `/state` stayed `running` during the detached turn, and at the first non-`running` read (polled every 50 ms) `/messages` already held the complete answer: the turn is stored before the state reports `idle`, which this change relies on.
  - **Browser scenarios on this head (`7b47bd716`)**, same harness, one run each (the gateway's state row edited by hand for the stale case):
    - socket reopened mid-turn: "Running…" shown, the full answer loaded about 4 s after the reopen, the prompt shown throughout;
    - a second browser opening the conversation mid-turn: the composer locks, the answer loads without a reload; Stop from that browser stops the turn (state `idle`) and both pages unlock;
    - stored state `running` with no turn running: locked on load; after Stop unlocked within 8 s, answer kept, no `/state` request in the next 10 s (the previous head, as deployed, was still locked and polling);
    - gateway killed mid-turn and restarted: state `error`, the page unlocks.
    - Once in 8 runs of the reopen scenario across builds, under heavy host load, the page briefly (about 2-4 s) showed the "conversation started over" notice and hid the prompt before the answer loaded; it did not reproduce in the other runs. It is now explained and fixed (see the first-turn notice note below).
  - Not covered: mobile background-tab timer throttling and tab eviction.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output. No new UI: the change only drives the existing running state (`typing`); one test renders the real chat page (`AgentChatInner`) and asserts the composer is disabled while the detached turn runs and enabled once its answer has loaded.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `7b47bd716c61b623cbc55a5cbd448ec358b78c81`, `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` ("a page that loads while its turn runs shows the turn and loads the outcome once it ends"); the first-turn notice tests above are on head `0f8d0602e`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the assertions above, on the rendered `AgentChatInner` textarea's `disabled` prop.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** turn running on the gateway at hydration → composer disabled, running state shown; state leaves `running` → transcript reloaded, answer shown, composer enabled.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust checks: no Rust file changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (an existing same-origin route, with the page's existing auth)

prs.title: chore(lint): fix clippy lints introduced by Rust 1.99
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - CI pins Rust 1.98.0, where the workspace is clippy-clean. On Rust 1.99.0, `scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace` fails on existing code, so the next toolchain bump would be blocked by unrelated lint fallout. This clears it ahead of time.
  - `fetch_update` on atomics is deprecated in 1.99 in favour of `try_update`, which has the same signature and semantics. 4 call sites, plus one comment that names the method.
  - `needless_borrows_for_generic_args`: 4 capture-free (`Copy`) closures passed as `&f` are now passed by value.
  - `assert_is_empty` (pedantic; only the root crate opts into `clippy::pedantic`): 40 flagged `assert!(x.is_empty())` test assertions now print the value on failure, which is the lint's point (CI failures show *what* was there). Call results are bound to a `let` first so the message does not re-evaluate the call.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not bump the CI toolchain or MSRV, does not add any `#[allow]`, and touches no production logic beyond the two behaviour-preserving mechanical edits above. Only the exact lines clippy flagged were changed: unflagged `is_empty()` assertions on non-slice types were left alone.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Test failure messages for the rewritten assertions now include the offending value.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12642 (spotted while validating that PR on a local 1.99 toolchain)

### What this does, simply

The Rust toolchain on newer machines (1.99) added and changed some lint rules. CI still uses 1.98, so nothing is failing today, but anyone on 1.99 sees `cargo clippy` fail on code nobody touched, and the next CI toolchain bump would hit the same wall. This PR fixes those lint findings. Two are pure renames or simplifications with identical behaviour. The rest are test assertions that, when they fail, will now print the unexpected value instead of just "assertion failed".

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: lint-only change; the evidence is clippy on three toolchains plus the crates' own test suites, listed below.

Ran CI's exact clippy invocation (`scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace` → `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings`) on the new toolchain, the CI-pinned toolchain, and the MSRV.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

prs.title: fix(rpc): refuse config writes and session/configure on a mid-turn session
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A running turn holds its session's `model_provider_update` guard for the whole turn. Config writes that must refresh that session (every `prepare_live_sessions_refresh` caller: `config/set`, `config/set-many`, deletes, …) and `session/configure` waited on that guard **without a bound**, inline on the issuing connection's sequential dispatcher, while holding the daemon-wide `config_write_lock`.
  - zerocode's RPC call times out after 5s, but the daemon stays parked, so every later frame from that client queues behind it. If the busy turn is itself waiting on a frame from the same client (e.g. a tool-approval reply), it is a deadlock: the zerocode config editor hard-locks instead of showing an error, and every other config writer on the daemon stalls.
  - Both sites now use the existing `lock_model_provider_update_with_timeout` with one shared bound, `SESSION_PROVIDER_UPDATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (3s, inside zerocode's 5s RPC budget), and refuse with a retryable `SESSION_BUSY` on timeout. A refusal drops the candidate config and every guard already taken, so nothing commits and the writer lock is released.
  - Short holders are still absorbed, so the existing queued-ordering guarantees (and their tests) are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change lock ordering, what a config write refreshes, or `session/prompt` (already bounded at 30s, and spawned rather than inline). `reconcile_rehydrated_session` keeps its unbounded wait: it is a background task with no client parked on it. No zerocode client changes; it already surfaces both errors (`zc-config-status-set-failed`, `zc-model-switch-failed`).
- **Blast radius:** Clients that edit a setting in scope of a mid-turn session now receive `SESSION_BUSY` after ~3s instead of the write being applied after the turn ends. Affects zerocode, the gateway, and any RPC client calling config writes or `session/configure`. Edits that do not touch a busy session are unaffected (those already skipped busy out-of-scope sessions).
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed.

### What this does, simply

When you change a setting in zerocode that an agent is using *right now* (say, the model of the provider a running chat turn is talking to), the daemon used to wait for that turn to finish before answering. It waited with no time limit, and while waiting it blocked everything else from that zerocode window. If the running turn needed an answer from that same window (like approving a tool call), nothing could ever move again, so the UI froze.

Now the daemon waits at most 3 seconds. If the session is still busy, it says so with a normal error ("…while it is running a turn; retry after the turn finishes"), saves nothing, and the UI stays responsive. Once the turn ends, the same edit works. The same fix applies to `session/configure` (zerocode's `/model` switch), which had the identical problem.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui` (zerocode); `channel`: `rpc`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A daemon with one agent bound to a model provider, and a zerocode session on that agent. Use a prompt that makes the turn wait on a tool approval (or any long-running turn).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Start a turn and leave it waiting on the tool-approval prompt.
  2. Open the config editor and change that agent's provider model (`providers.models.<type>.<alias>.model`), then save.
  3. Separately, run `/model <other>` while a turn is running.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** After ~3s the editor shows a "set failed … SESSION_BUSY / running a turn" status (and `/model` shows a model-switch-failed info message). The UI stays responsive, the approval can still be answered, and after the turn ends the same save succeeds.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The save never returns. zerocode stops responding to further config/list and approval traffic, and other config writes on the daemon stall.

### How I tested

Added two regression tests at the real handler boundary, each holding the session's `model_provider_update` guard the way a running turn does:

- `config_set_in_scope_of_busy_session_fails_busy_instead_of_hanging`
- `session_configure_on_busy_session_fails_busy_instead_of_hanging`

Each asserts: `SESSION_BUSY` within 5s; the config writer lock is released; nothing is committed (config value / session override unchanged); and the same request succeeds once the guard is dropped. **Both failed on the unpatched handlers** (the call parked until the test's outer timeout: `Elapsed(())`) and pass with the fix.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`, the only changed crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None. CI's pinned toolchain (1.98.0) is clippy-clean for this change. Locally I ran clippy on Rust 1.99.0, which flags pre-existing lints unrelated to this diff (`fetch_update` deprecation, `needless_borrows_for_generic_args`, `assert_is_empty`); those are fixed separately in #12644 so this PR stays single-concern.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib busy_session_fails_busy   # before session/configure fix
test rpc::dispatch::tests::config_set_in_scope_of_busy_session_fails_busy_instead_of_hanging ... ok
test rpc::dispatch::tests::session_configure_on_busy_session_fails_busy_instead_of_hanging ... FAILED
  panicked: session/configure must not park behind a busy session's turn: Elapsed(())

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 6265 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 26.02s

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
(Rust 1.99.0 locally) only pre-existing 1.99-only lints outside this diff, fixed in #12644; none in changed hunks
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Read the existing ordering tests (`model_provider_update_blocks_session_configure`, `session_prompt_waits_for_queued_provider_update_transaction`, `model_provider_update_preserves_newer_session_override`) to confirm they release the guard well inside the bound; all pass. Confirmed zerocode renders both errors through its existing status/info paths. Did **not** run a live daemon + zerocode end-to-end session.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no rendering change; the existing error-status paths are reused)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `bb8a24d8aa`, handler-level tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Config write / configure against a mid-turn session → `SESSION_BUSY` in ~3s, nothing committed, writer lock free.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace `cargo test`: only `zeroclaw-runtime` changed, and its full lib suite was run. Full-workspace clippy was not run on the CI-pinned 1.98.0 toolchain locally; the CI `Clippy` job covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. `SESSION_BUSY` is an existing, documented retryable code; clients already handle it for `session/prompt`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert bb8a24d8aa` (single commit, single file)
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Config edits or `/model` switches failing with `SESSION_BUSY` / "while it is running a turn" when no turn is actually running would indicate the bound is too tight for some legitimate short holder.

prs.title: fix(log): remove the rolling trim's temp file on failure and skip the startup directory scan
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The rolling trim copies the retained tail into a sibling `runtime-trace.tmp.<pid>.<nanos>` file and renames it over
    the active log. Any error between creating that file and the rename returned early and left it behind, so a trim
    that kept failing leaked one file per appended event. The temp file is now owned by a scope guard that removes it
    unless the rename succeeded.
  - The guard already existed inside the legacy-log migration. The first commit moves it, unchanged, to a private module
    of `zeroclaw-log` so both writers share it.
  - Writer startup listed the whole log directory to seed the next archive number under every storage policy, although
    only `rotating` creates archives and reads that number. With the default `rolling` policy that cost grows with the
    number of entries in the directory and runs while the daemon holds config ownership. The listing now happens only
    when the policy owns archives.
- **Scope boundary:** does not remove temp files that are already on disk, nor those left by a killed process or by a
  panic in a build that aborts on panic (`panic = "abort"` in the release profiles, so `Drop` does not run there). Does
  not change the directory listing under `rotating` (startup, retention, queries). Does not determine why the trim
  failed on the reporter's machine. Other temp-then-rename sites in the repo were not audited.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-log` only (`writer.rs`, `migrate.rs`, a new private `temp_guard.rs`) plus one table row and
  one paragraph in `docs/book/src/architecture/logging.md`. The public API of the crate is unchanged. Under
  `rolling`/`full`/`none`, `next_archive_seq` now starts at `1` instead of the disk-derived value; it is read only by
  `rotate_active`, which is reached only under `rotating`, and a `debug_assert!` checks that. The assert is compiled out
  of release builds.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12570 (this PR does not close it: the points above remain). Related #10073, which
  proposes retiring `StoragePolicy::Rolling`; if that lands, the trim part of this PR goes with it.

### What this does, simply

When the log is in `rolling` mode, every new event makes ZeroClaw rewrite the tail of the log into a temporary file and
swap it in. If something goes wrong half-way, that temporary file used to stay in the log directory forever; repeated
failures piled up, as reported in the linked issue (I did not reproduce the failure that caused it). Now a failed trim cleans up after itself and leaves the real log untouched. Separately,
on startup the writer no longer scans the log directory unless it is in the one mode (`rotating`) that needs to know which
archives are there.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the behavior is covered by unit tests that inject the failure; there is no
  user-visible interface change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Lint` job (rustfmt, clippy, comment-hygiene gate) and
  whichever CI job runs the `zeroclaw-log` unit tests, which is where the five new tests live (I have not confirmed
  which job that is).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** I did not verify that a Windows job runs the `zeroclaw-log` tests; the guard's
  behavior on Windows is untested by me.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux/WSL, on the pushed head):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-log --lib --locked -- --test-threads=1` → `test result: ok. 174 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → rc 0
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` → `58 passed, 0 failed`; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-log --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` → rc 0
  - Narrower than the CI's workspace clippy (`run_clippy.sh --scope workspace`), which I did not run.
- **Do the new tests fail without the change?** Checked by temporarily reverting each half locally:
  with the guard made inert, `failed_trim_removes_its_temp_file_and_keeps_the_log` fails; with `initial_archive_seq`
  always reading the directory, `only_a_policy_that_owns_archives_reads_the_directory_for_the_sequence` fails. The
  reverts were not committed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing at runtime beyond the tests above. By reading the code I checked
  that `rotate_active` is reached only from `maybe_rotate_for_*`, which `write_one` calls only under
  `StoragePolicy::Rotating` (search `maybe_rotate_for|WorkerState \{|rotate_active\(` in `crates/zeroclaw-log`, which
  finds the definitions and every call site), and that `WorkerState` is a private struct of `writer.rs`. The rotation
  tests in the 174 above ran with the `debug_assert!` active (debug test profile) and it did not fire. I did not verify
  the guard's behavior on Windows.
- **What the tests cover and do not:**

prs.title: fix(web): cancel the voice auto-send when the draft is edited
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When the browser ends recognition on its own after a final phrase, the silence timer stays armed. When it fires, the chat page sends whatever is in the composer at that moment. Nothing cancelled that pending send when the person edited the draft, so text typed after the mic turned off could go to the agent without a click.
  - `BrowserVoiceControls` now exposes a second handle, `autoSendCancelRef`, next to `captureRef`. It moves the existing submit-cancellation epoch on, the same check a manual mic click uses, and clears the silence timer if capture has already ended.
  - `AgentChat` calls it from `handleTextareaChange`, so any typed, pasted or deleted text cancels the automatic send for that dictation. Dictated text reaches the composer through `applyInput`, not the textarea's change handler, so dictation never cancels itself.
  - If the mic is still live when the person types, it keeps listening and still ends after the silence timeout, but that dictation doesn't send on its own. The next dictation, with no edit, sends as before.
  - The dictation's cancellation epoch is now taken at the mic click, before the on-device language check, so an edit made while the mic is starting also counts.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the silence timeout, its revalidation, the manual mic stop, or Send. An image attachment or a slash-command pick doesn't cancel the send. Attaching an image is a deliberate step toward sending the message, where typing usually corrects what was heard, so the dictation still goes out with the image. Slash commands are never auto-sent anyway.
- **Blast radius:** The chat composer's voice auto-send in `AgentChat.tsx` and `BrowserVoiceControls.tsx`. A new page test runs in the existing `Voice tests` CI step.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12632. Related #12269.

### What this does, simply

With dictation on, ZeroClaw sends your message by itself after 15 seconds of silence. Some browsers, mostly on phones, turn the mic off early after a short pause, but the 15-second countdown kept running. If you started fixing or rewriting the message in that time, ZeroClaw sent your half-finished text when the countdown ran out. Now any typing in the message box cancels that automatic send, and the message waits for you to press Send.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard chat, voice dictation)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a paired browser with dictation on in Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio, and `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` at its default of 15. The early end is easiest to see in a mobile browser, which ends recognition on a short pause.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Click the microphone, say a short phrase, and stop talking. Wait for the mic button to turn off by itself.
  2. Before 15 seconds pass, change the text in the message box.
  3. Wait 20 seconds.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the edited text is still in the message box, unsent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the edited text is sent when the timer fires.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Web Permission Tests`: `cargo web check` typechecks both files, and `Voice tests` (`npm run test:voice`) now runs `BrowserVoiceControls.test.ts` and the new `agentChat.voiceAutoSend.test.ts`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests fake the browser speech API, the WebSocket and the gateway's HTTP API. No real recognizer runs.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on macOS with Node 24, at this head:
  ```text
  $ npm run test:voice
  BrowserVoiceControls.test.ts:     tests 43, pass 43, fail 0
  agentChat.voiceAutoSend.test.ts:  tests 3, pass 3, fail 0
  $ npm test                  (exit 0)
  $ npm run typecheck         (exit 0)
  $ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh && scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```
  With the change to `AgentChat.tsx` taken out, the page test fails on master's behaviour:
  ```text
  ✖ typing after the browser ends dictation early cancels the automatic send
    + [ '{"type":"message","content":"Wait, do not deploy yet, first"}' ]
  ✖ typing while the microphone is live keeps the draft from being sent on silence
    + [ '{"type":"message","content":"Deploy the staging build after the"}' ]
  ✔ with no edit, the silence timeout still sends the dictated text
  ```
  With the handle's body emptied in `BrowserVoiceControls.tsx`, the new component tests fail (`actual: 1, expected: 0` sends). The startup-edit test failed the same way at 24ed0976fb, before the epoch moved.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The page test mounts the real chat page (`AgentChat`, `ChatWorkspace`, `AgentProvider`, `BrowserVoiceControls`) and types through the textarea's own `onChange`. Its control test checks that a dictation with no edit still sends after exactly 15 seconds. Not verified: a real browser recognizer, Safari, or a phone.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. Nothing about layout or rendering changes; the change is whether a send happens.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch at 7dfc991ce2, on `master` at 39478aa505.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the test output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** typing after dictation, then waiting past the timeout, leaves the edited draft unsent.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo web check` wasn't run as one command. Its two steps were: the API client built from `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- spec-dump` and `openapi-typescript`, then `npm run typecheck`. No Rust files change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. It's web-only, with no data or config migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs = 0` turns automatic sending off completely, so every dictated draft waits for Send.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** client-side only, with no log or metric. Either a dictated draft with no edit stops sending after the timeout, or an edited draft is still sent without a click.

prs.title: fix(gateway/web): keep voice settings changed elsewhere when one is saved
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The voice settings screen saved the whole record it last read (`{ ...prefs, ...patch }`), and the gateway replaced the stored JSON with it. A screen that hadn't reloaded therefore undid any change made elsewhere in the meantime, the recognition mode included. The screen reloads on window focus, when the tab becomes visible, and when another tab in the same browser saves, but a screen that gets none of those keeps its old copy. One example is a tablet or a second monitor left on the page while an operator changes the device from another computer.
  - `PUT /api/devices/me/voice` and `PUT /api/devices/{id}/voice` now take a `VoicePreferencesUpdate`, in which every field is optional. The gateway reads the stored record inside the existing `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write transaction and applies only the fields in the body. A concurrent save of another field is kept, not replaced.
  - Validation now checks only the fields present. Stored values were checked when they were written. Unknown fields are still refused (`deny_unknown_fields`).
  - The settings screen sends only the field that changed. Its optimistic draft and the response handling are unchanged, so after a save the screen shows the merged record the gateway returns, including the other computer's change.
- **Scope boundary:** No version or ETag check. Two screens that change the same field still resolve last-write-wins, which is the expected result for a single setting. No change to reads, device authorization, the operator admission path, or where preferences are stored.
- **Blast radius:** the two voice preference `PUT` routes in `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_pairing.rs`, and `saveVoicePreferences` in `web/src/lib/browserVoice.ts`, whose only caller is `BrowserVoiceSettings.tsx`. A body that names every field, as master's dashboard sends, still replaces the whole record. Only a partial body behaves differently: missing fields used to be reset to their defaults, and now they keep their saved values.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12633. Related #12269.

### What this does, simply

Each paired browser has its own voice settings, which you can change from that browser or, as an operator, from another computer. When you changed one setting, the settings page saved every setting as it last saw them. If the page had been open for a while and someone else had changed something in the meantime, your save quietly put their change back. Switching a device to on-device recognition could be undone this way, which starts sending its microphone audio to the browser's online service again. Now the page sends only the setting you changed, and the gateway keeps everything else as it is.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a gateway with pairing on and two signed-in screens on different computers. Screen A is a paired browser on its own device record, with recognition set to the browser service.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the voice settings on screen A, and leave it in the foreground without switching windows or tabs.
  2. On screen B, select screen A's device and switch it to on-device recognition.
  3. On screen A, move only the speech rate slider.
  4. Reload screen A.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the new rate is saved, and recognition is still on-device.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the new rate is saved, and recognition is back on the browser service.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the gateway's unit tests (the new `a_partial_voice_write_keeps_fields_another_screen_saved` and `an_invalid_partial_voice_write_changes_nothing`, plus the existing voice tests, now writing through the update type). `Web Permission Tests`: `cargo web check` typechecks the screen, and `Voice tests` runs the new screen test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the gateway tests call the handler functions directly, not over HTTP. The existing `dashboard_session` cookie-write test still sends a full record over the router and passes.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  Gateway, on Linux at this head:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output)
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 17s
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib voice
  test api_pairing::tests::a_partial_voice_write_keeps_fields_another_screen_saved ... ok
  test api_pairing::tests::an_invalid_partial_voice_write_changes_nothing ... ok
  test dashboard_session::tests::voice_write_rechecks_cookie_permissions_after_body_admission ... ok
  test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 924 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
  test result: ok. 931 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```
  Web, on macOS with Node 24, at this head:
  ```text
  $ npm run test:voice
  BrowserVoiceControls.test.ts: tests 41, pass 41, fail 0
  $ npm test                  (exit 0)
  $ npm run typecheck         (exit 0)
  $ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh && scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```
  With the screen change taken out, the new web test fails on master's behaviour: the body is the whole record, `recognition: 'browser'` included, not `{ rate: 1.5 }`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The screen test mounts the real `BrowserVoiceSettings` and `browserVoice.ts`. The other computer's save is applied at the fake server, and the screen gets no focus, visibility or same-browser notice; it then moves the rate slider. The fake server now merges as the gateway does. Not verified: two real computers against a running gateway.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. Nothing on screen changes; the change is what a save sends and stores.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch at 093c713706, on `master` at 39478aa505.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the test output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** a rate change from a screen that hasn't reloaded keeps a recognition change made elsewhere.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo web check` wasn't run as one command. Its two steps were: the API client built from `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- spec-dump` and `openapi-typescript`, then `npm run typecheck`. The voice routes aren't in the OpenAPI spec, so the generated client doesn't change. The full workspace `cargo test` wasn't run; only `zeroclaw-gateway` changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The privacy effect is the fix itself: a stale save can no longer move a device from on-device recognition back to the browser's online service.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A full-record body behaves as before. A partial body keeps the fields it leaves out, where master reset them to defaults; master's dashboard never sent one.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`, then redeploy the gateway and `web/dist` together and reload any open dashboard tabs. The stored record's shape doesn't change, so there's nothing to migrate back.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `PUT /api/devices/me/voice` or `/api/devices/{id}/voice` returning 500 "Could not save voice preferences", with the `Failed to persist device voice preferences` error event. After a partial rollback (old gateway, new dashboard still open), saving one voice setting resets the device's other voice settings to their defaults.

prs.title: feat(gateway): use the long-running timeout for webhook turns
prs.body:
resolve: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11930

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Move `POST /webhook` (docs: [Generic Webhook Gateway HTTP API](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/4efcc4b6286d83c3d69cdc6c2416ec93ab077b47/docs/book/src/gateway/api.md#generic-webhook-request-timeout)) to the existing long-running router so synchronous agent calls can finish beyond the ordinary gateway deadline. Reuse the typed timeout configuration and existing body-size limit.
- **Scope boundary:** No new configuration fields, dependencies, execution state, retry mechanism, or queue. Provider/tool deadlines and SSE body lifetime/cancellation ownership are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** All generic webhook branches use the longer response-creation deadline, including body extraction and SOP/SSE admission. Ordinary routes and separate channel/plugin/SOP webhook routes retain their existing timeout selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11930.

### What this does, simply

An HTTP client sending a non-streaming message to `/webhook` waits for the agent's final JSON answer. A slow model or several tool calls can exceed the ordinary 30-second request deadline. This change uses `gateway.long_running_request_timeout_secs`, default 600 seconds, without extending ordinary gateway requests. Early answers still return immediately.

This concerns the gateway's `POST /webhook`, **not the separate `[channels.webhook]` adapter** documented in [Channels → Webhooks](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/c2f6b3f4cdd55f485d91bcca0a107c9c1989ea81/docs/book/src/channels/webhook.md). That adapter accepts inbound messages and can deliver replies later through `send_url`. In the gateway's non-streaming chat path, [the handler awaits the agent turn and returns the final JSON answer in the same HTTP response](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/4efcc4b6286d83c3d69cdc6c2416ec93ab077b47/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs#L3697). Here, synchronous describes the caller's request/response contract, not blocking a server thread. SOP dispatch and optional SSE remain distinct branches.

A controlled HTTP client can therefore receive the result of a slow model or multi-tool turn without raising deadlines for unrelated gateway routes or adopting a streaming response. This does not change external webhook senders' acknowledgement deadlines or promise that client/proxy timeouts will allow the same wait.

This PR implements the whole-route option discussed in #11930. Maintainer assessment is requested on sharing the existing 600-second default, allowing body receipt to use that deadline, and the retry implications below. These are proposed choices, not an already accepted issue decision.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated boundary tests start the real gateway, drive HTTP requests, and replace only the external model API with a controlled loopback provider.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Completed on rebased head 4efcc4b6286d83c3d69cdc6c2416ec93ab077b47. The [CI Required Gate passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39702156404/job/119579059135). The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39702156404/job/119574151067) passed all eight `webhook_timeout` integration tests, including the synchronized overlapping-retry test; its main workspace suite reported 19,303 passed and 41 skipped. [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39702156404/job/119574151083), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39702156404/job/119574151149), Format, Docs Style, MSRV, default/no-default feature checks, plugin checks, Linux build, macOS check, Windows compile/service smoke and the remaining selected Quality Gate jobs passed. Semgrep and the Greptile Review check also succeeded. Conditional jobs marked skipped were not executed; earlier cancelled risk-report runs are followed by a successful run. Local follow-up validation below predates the rebase.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows compile/service checks do not establish that the webhook integration suite ran on Windows. No live external provider was used.
- **Commands run for the test synchronization follow-up (macOS/aarch64):**

```text
cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --test webhook_timeout
  8 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-default-features --test webhook_timeout
  8 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --test webhook_timeout --no-deps -- -D warnings
  PASS
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  PASS
git diff --check
  PASS
```

The initial sandboxed test attempt could not bind loopback sockets; both suites passed after rerunning with loopback access. The retry fixture now withholds both provider responses until two calls are observed, retaining real time only for duplicate-marker expiry. Other timeout tests retain their delayed provider.

Earlier local validation at e2e2b47e6 included the complete gateway package (681 passed, 7 ignored), scoped all-target Clippy, and documentation style/link gates. Dependency-inclusive local Clippy on Rust 1.99 reported unchanged provider `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` diagnostics; hosted Lint on that revision passed. The local toolchain also reports an existing runtime deprecation and macOS linker unwind-table warning.

HTTP tests cover success beyond the ordinary deadline, timeout under the shorter long-running budget, ordinary/SOP deadlines, webhook body receipt, authentication, rate limiting, oversized bodies, duplicate suppression, SOP-first dispatch, SSE completion, and overlapping retries after marker expiry. No live external provider was used.

The default 300-second idempotency marker can expire during a 600-second turn. This also affects existing deployments that raise the ordinary timeout; the route move makes it relevant under defaults. prs.title: feat(channels): process Telegram edited_message updates with latest-wins coalescing
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why.** Telegram delivers every message edit as an `edited_message` update; ZeroClaw currently ignores this update type entirely, so an edit never reaches the agent. Two gaps close here: (1) the long-poll subscribes with `allowed_updates: ["message", "callback_query"]`, so Telegram never even delivers edits — the subscription now includes `edited_message` when the alias opts in; (2) the update was not parsed — it now flows through the exact pipeline of an ordinary message (authorization, mention gate, reply-to-bot bypass, attachments) with a small edit policy applied in the orchestrator.
- **The edit policy (design):**
  - An edit *replaces the meaning* of the original message (same `message_id`). Three cases follow: an edit that makes the message **addressed** (adds mention/reply) must trigger; an edit that **clarifies** an already-addressed message must trigger with the previous exchange as context; an edit that **removes** addressing must not trigger.
  - **Freshness gate:** an addressed edit triggers an agent turn only when the *original* message is younger than 600s (`EDIT_FRESHNESS_SECS`, measured from `date`, not `edit_date`). Editing an old message is a clarification of history, not a live prompt — it is recorded as passive context without a turn. This bounds cost and prevents necrobumping.
  - **Latest-wins coalescing:** rapid consecutive edits of one message collapse into a single dispatch carrying the latest content. The shared `MessageDebouncer` concatenates messages with `\n`, which is wrong for edits (superseded versions must vanish), so a small dedicated pending-edit map is used: key `(reply_target, sender, message_id)`, timer = the channel's effective debounce window, each new edit replaces content and resets the timer (generation counter — a superseded timer never dispatches). Coalescing is active only with a non-zero `[channels].debounce_ms`: at the global default of `0` every edit dispatches immediately as its own turn (freshness marking still applies). A bounded map (`PENDING_EDITS_LIMIT = 128`) falls through to immediate dispatch when full.
  - **Interrupts follow the alias policy:** the coalesced edit re-enters the standard dispatch path; with `interrupt_on_new_message` on for the alias it supersedes the active turn like any other message, otherwise it queues behind it. (Carrying suppression through the second pass is a known follow-up.)
  - **History marker:** the dispatched content is prefixed with `[edited] `. Session history is not rewritten — the model sees the original message, its previous answer, and the correction as an evolution, which models handle naturally.
- **Opt-in:** `channels.telegram.<alias>.edited_messages = true` (default `false`). Zero behavior change without the flag; with the flag off, edited updates are acked and skipped exactly as today.
- **Scope boundary.** No changes to the shared `MessageDebouncer`, no session-history surgery, no SOP-trigger changes for stale edits (a stale addressed edit is recorded, not dispatched, so it cannot fire SOP events). Album-member edits are processed as single attachments; the album aggregation path is untouched.
- **Blast radius.** Telegram channel (new gate + `edited` flag on `ChannelMessage`), orchestrator dispatch loop (one new branch before SOP-event dispatch), config schema (one defaulted bool). Other channels are unaffected; `ChannelMessage.edited` defaults to `false` everywhere.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11713 (edits adding a mention stay unanswered without opting in). Related behavior: mention-gate reply-to-bot bypass (existing). Note: #11781 is an alternative edited_message design, not a stack — the two conflict textually and only one should land.

### What this does, simply

Telegram lets users edit sent messages. Every edit arrives as a separate update of type `edited_message`. Today ZeroClaw does not look at this update type at all — as if the edit never happened. Worse, the long-poll subscribes only to `message` and `callback_query` updates, so Telegram does not even deliver edits to the bot. That is mostly harmless, except in one painful case: a user in a mention-gated group sends a photo or a question *without* the bot's @-mention (correctly ignored), then edits it to add the mention. The bot stays silent forever, because the only version that addresses it is the edit, and edits never arrive.

This PR first widens the subscription to include `edited_message` when the alias opts in, then teaches the Telegram channel to parse edits with the same rules as fresh messages (same authorization, same mention gate, same reply bypass, same attachment handling), and teaches the orchestrator three things about edits: an addressed edit of a *recent* message is a live prompt (process it, but collapse bursts of edits into one turn carrying only the final text); an addressed edit of an *old* message is history clarification (record it as context, don't spend a turn); an unaddressed edit changes nothing (same passive/drop path as always). The model is told a message was edited via a one-word `[edited]` marker rather than by rewriting conversation history.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the behavior is user-visible and timing-dependent (coalescing window).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (Telegram).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Telegram group with `mention_only = true` and `edited_messages = true` on the alias; a vision-capable model is NOT required.
- **Steps to run:** (1) send a message without the bot's @-mention — expect silence (unchanged); (2) edit it to add the mention — on this branch the bot answers after the debounce window; (3) edit the same message three times quickly — expect exactly one answer, reflecting the final text; (4) edit a week-old message to add the mention — expect no turn, the text lands in session context only.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** steps 2–4 behave as described.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** steps 2–4 all produce silence; `edited_message` updates are never parsed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (Test, Lint, Format, clippy) — the change is channel + orchestrator logic covered by the workspace matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check        # clean
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels   # Finished OK
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels edited   # 10 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config telegram   # passed (incl. new default-off/deserialize tests)
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets   # exit 0; no new warnings in touched files
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Unit-level: parse gates for edited updates (mention required in mention_only group, mention passes, reply-to-bot bypass, flag-off skip, timestamp pinned to original `date`), the long-poll subscription (`allowed_updates` contains `edited_message` only when the flag is on), policy tests (fresh addressed edit dispatches once with `[edited] `, stale addressed edit records only, two consecutive edits produce one dispatch with the latest content — no concatenation). Live-verified on a production contour: without the subscription fix the parse code is unreachable (Telegram simply never delivers the edit); with it, an edit that adds the @-mention triggers a single answer after the debounce window.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head `9064bfe226`; evidence: unit tests in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs` and `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` — pre-existing warnings outside the touched crates; the changed crate is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No** — edits flow through the existing authorization and mention gates; attachment handling is the existing pipeline.
- New external network calls? **No** — `edited_message` arrives via the existing long-poll; media replacement re-uses the existing download path.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No** — tests use synthetic ids/usernames.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — edited text is gated exactly like fresh text; the `[edited] ` marker is fixed.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — opt-in per alias; default behavior byte-identical (edited updates acked and skipped).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — new optional key `channels.telegram.<alias>.edited_messages` (default `false`).
- Rust/MSVC/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Upgrade steps: none required; set `edited_messages = true` on the desired aliases to enable.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert 9064bfe226` — additive, gated by a default-off flag.
- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 9064bfe226` or set `edited_messages = false`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.telegram.<alias>.edited_messages` (default `false`).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** duplicate answers after rapid edits (coalescing broken — grep trace for consecutive dispatches of the same `message_id`); answers to stale edits (freshness gate broken — grep for agent turns with `[edited]` content older than 600s).
