prs.title: feat(channels): route external peers to an explicit destination
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #12116: the first commit is #12116's head (patch-identical), and this PR's change is the second commit. Review the second commit, or the diff after #12116 merges.
- **Reshaped after @JordanTheJet's review of 2026-11-20:** the route is generic, the channel declares whether routes apply, and the channel renders the mention. No shared crate names a channel type: the Discord branches in `send_message_to_peer` (including #12116's `channel_ref_is_discord`), `send_via` and route validation are gone. This is the split from the review: the generic route plus Discord as the first channel that supports it; other channels can declare support later.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Some channels identify an external peer by user rather than by a place to post. On Discord an `external_peers` entry is a user ID, but messages are posted to channels and threads, and bots cannot DM other bots. `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via` used that user ID (for `send_via`, the group's *first* entry) as the destination, so sends failed with Discord's 404 `Unknown Channel`, and which peer `send_via` picked depended on list order.
  - This adds an operator-chosen per-peer route, `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer>"]`, with `destination` (where to post, in the channel's own format) and an optional `mention`, following the decisions in #10926 (comment of 2026-11-06).
  - `Channel::supports_peer_routes()` (default `false`, Discord `true`) is the declaration, next to `supports_native_polls` and `supports_outbound_send`. A delivery is checked against it before anything is sent, through `PeerAddressing` (`Direct`, `Peer`, `Routed`): an unrouted peer on a channel that needs routes is refused with guidance, and a route on a channel that doesn't support them is refused instead of ignored.
  - `SendMessage` carries the routed peer (`routed_peer`) next to `allowed_mentions`. `with_routed_peer` sets the ping rule: nobody, or with `mention = true` only the routed peer. The channel renders the mention and owns the rule: Discord derives it from the routed peer itself rather than trusting the caller, sends the peer ID in Discord's form (a route key may be written with a leading `@`), applies it to every chunk and attachment payload, prefixes `<@id>`, and refuses a routed message aimed at an interaction reply.
- **The route rules are unchanged, with their tests:** admission stays in `external_peers`, a wildcard can't be routed, an ignored peer isn't routable, a route only applies through groups the sending agent is in, conflicting routes across two groups fail and name both, and a routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only with `mention = true`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Discord is the only channel that declares peer routes. Other channels keep delivering to the external peer itself; Matrix and Signal are left to separate slices.
  - No peer selector and no group default for `send_via`: a group or channel target posts only when exactly one eligible routed peer exists. Explicit per-peer sends stay with `send_message_to_peer`.
  - The route is not checked against the Discord channel's `channel_ids`, which keeps its meaning as the listening filter. No `thread` field: `destination` is the ID the sender posts to.
  - Unrouted sends and sends on other channels keep their payloads; `allowed_mentions` is omitted unless a route sets it.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-api`: `SendMessage` gains `allowed_mentions` and `routed_peer` (both `None` by default, set by both constructors), so struct-literal sites get two more fields. New `RoutedPeer`, `PeerAddressing`, `PeerRouteError`, and the defaulted `Channel::supports_peer_routes`.
  - The cron/announcement `DeliveryFn` gains a final `PeerAddressing` argument. `deliver_announcement` keeps its signature and passes `Direct`; the new `deliver_announcement_addressed` carries the rest.
  - The Discord sender builds every chunk through one helper, `chunk_payload`. For plain chunks it produces the same request body as the previous `DiscordOutgoing::text` path (tested).
  - Config validation no longer checks Discord ID formats or rejects routes on other channel types: config can't see a channel's declaration, so that check moved to send time. On such a channel `send_via` refuses a route for the recipient in any of the agent's groups covering it, and names the group that sets it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926. Depends on #12116.

### What this does, simply

A peer group lists who an agent may talk to on a channel. On Discord, an outside participant (another bot or a person) is listed by user ID, but a bot can't post to a user ID: it posts into a channel or thread, and bots can't DM other bots. So asking an agent to message such a peer failed with a confusing "Unknown Channel" error.

With this change, the operator says where messages for that peer should go:

```toml
[peer_groups.discord_peers]
channel = "discord.main"
agents = ["assistant"]
external_peers = ["111111111111111111"]

[peer_groups.discord_peers.routes."111111111111111111"]
destination = "333333333333333333"   # channel or thread ID to post in
mention = true                       # optional: start with a ping of the peer
```

`send_message_to_peer` to that peer, or `send_via` to that group, then posts in the configured channel or thread. The result names the destination, so the agent knows it posted in a shared place rather than a private message. The route never lets anyone new in, can't be used for an ignored peer, and only applies through groups the sending agent is in. If two of the agent's groups route the same peer to different places, the send fails and names both groups. A routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only when `mention = true`.

The Discord channel says it needs routes; no code outside it mentions Discord. Another channel with the same problem only has to declare support and render its own mention.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional; unit coverage is focused, and a live Discord check shows the end-to-end effect.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord` (agent tool calls `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord bot in a server with a test channel or thread. An agent on `discord.<alias>`, and a peer group containing that agent with another bot or user ID in `external_peers`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Without a route, ask the agent to `send_message_to_peer` the external peer on the Discord channel ref.
  2. Add the `routes."<peer ID>"` block above with your channel or thread ID, reload, and repeat.
  3. Optionally set `mention = true`, and include `@everyone` or another user's mention in the message text.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 1 fails with an error explaining how to add a route. Step 2 posts in the destination, and the tool result names it. In step 3 the message starts with the peer's mention, and only the peer is pinged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 1 fails with Discord's `404 Unknown Channel`, because the user ID is used as a channel ID (#12116 replaces this with an actionable error). There is no way to route.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs cover the API, config, tools, channels, runtime and gateway changes; Docs Style and the links gate cover the two Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord API call in CI; the payload shape is covered by unit tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1, on `425b93579` over master `665904f6d`; suites on a 20-core build host, fmt and docs gates also on the author's host. The current head `936a112ed` differs only by one doc-comment link (CI's `cargo doc` rejected a redundant explicit link target); on it, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, `cargo fmt --check` and clippy on `zeroclaw-channels` are clean):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> clean
cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -> clean
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-channels \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings -> clean
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api --lib
  test result: ok. 324 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- route peer_group multi_agent
  test result: ok. 84 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- send_via i18n
  test result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord orchestrator::tests::routed announcement_delivery deliver_announcement whatsapp
  test result: ok. 351 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- send_message_to_peer cron i18n locale fluent
  test result: ok. 436 passed; 0 failed   (route tests also run in isolated child processes, each required to report "1 passed")
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh    -> Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh      -> Checked 1 local docs link target(s)
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh -> passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `send_message_to_peer`'s route tests run in an isolated child process with a delivery stand-in that checks `PeerAddressing` the way the orchestrator does; the orchestrator test checks the real `deliver_announcement_addressed` against a recording channel that declares or doesn't declare routes.
  - Routed replies queued by `send_via` always leave through `send_final` with the routed peer attached, never through draft finalization (a peer route is only recorded together with a resolved target channel). This was checked in the code; there is no end-to-end turn test for it.
  - Not verified: a live Discord post from this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (tool results and Discord message payloads only; no UI change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `425b93579` and `936a112ed` (doc-comment change only), the commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded locally because its GTK system libraries are not on this host (CI excludes it too). The full workspace `cargo test` was not run; the workspace builds with all targets, and the focused suites above cover the changed modules.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** A configured route can post outside the Discord channel's `channel_ids` listening filter. It is operator-configured only. It applies only to a peer the sending agent's own groups already admit and do not ignore, and conflicting routes fail closed. The docs state that everyone with access to the destination can read routed messages.
- New external network calls? No. Same Discord message endpoint, to a different operator-chosen channel.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. IDs are synthetic, e.g. `111111111111111111`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new untrusted input. Routed message text comes from the agent as before, and the explicit `allowed_mentions` policy stops it from pinging anyone except the routed peer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, with one Discord behavior change.** `send_via` to a Discord peer group, or to a Discord channel one group covers, that has external peers but no single routed peer now fails with guidance instead of posting to the first external peer's user ID. That post already failed with `404 Unknown Channel`. Groups with no external peers keep their existing rejection, and other channels are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer>"]` with `destination` and `mention`. Existing configs load unchanged; a route outside `external_peers`, a wildcard or duplicate key, or an empty destination is a load-time error, and a route on a channel that doesn't support routes fails at send time.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: none needed. To deliver to a Discord external peer, add a route as shown above.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this PR's commit. Routes are opt-in config; without them, the only change is the clearer `send_via` rejection described above.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Matrix delivers an edit as a new `m.replace` replacement event whose own body is the fallback containing the corrected text (prefixed with `*`). Letting it through the inbound pipeline started a duplicate agent turn from the fallback.
  - `MatrixConfig.edited_messages` (default `false`): replacement events are dropped on ingress unless the alias opts in — this changes master’s behavior, which admitted replacements as new messages.
  - When enabled, the corrected `m.new_content` body flows through the ordinary pipeline, and `ChannelMessage.edited` marks the delivery so downstream consumers can tell an edit from a new message.
  - Replacements of non-text messages (media, polls) are dropped in both modes — an edit never fabricates partial media state.
- **Scope boundary:** outbound editing (sending edits back to Matrix) is unchanged; no other channel's ingress changes (they set `edited: false`); no session/history semantics change.
- **Blast radius:** Matrix channel ingress plus the shared `ChannelMessage` struct, which gains `edited: bool` with `#[derive(Default)]` semantics. All struct literals across the workspace were audited: the overwhelming majority already spread `..Default::default()`; two feature-gated full literals (`whatsapp-web`, `channel-linq` test helper) are updated in this branch so every feature combination compiles.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12371 (Telegram edited-message coalescing — same ingress concern, different channel; no code overlap)

### What this does, simply

In Matrix, when a user edits a message, the homeserver does not rewrite history — it sends a new "replacement" event that points at the original. ZeroClaw's Matrix channel previously treated every such replacement as a brand-new message, so one edit produced a second agent turn using the fallback text (the replacement event's own body contains a fallback copy of the correction prefixed with `*`). With this PR replacements are dropped by default. An operator who wants the bot to see corrections can set `edited_messages = true` on the Matrix alias; the agent then receives the corrected text through the normal pipeline, marked with `edited = true`. Edits of non-text messages (photos, polls) are always ignored — a text-only channel cannot represent them faithfully.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — channel ingress is covered by unit tests at the sync boundary; meaningful manual verification needs a live homeserver, which CI does not provide.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (matrix)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features channel-matrix   # 2308 passed, 0 failed (incl. the 3 new edited-message tests)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                               # 1940 passed, 1 pre-existing failure
cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web
cargo check -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq --tests
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        # clean (cargo +1.98.0 fmt)
```

- Correction on an earlier revision of this body: the first validation run reported 2042 channel tests but did not enable `channel-matrix`, so the matrix module — including this change — was never compiled. Caught during live-test preparation; fixed in `d404d0d4cf` (the new ingress symbols are qualified through `mod inbound`, where the base file layout places them, plus one `MatrixConfig` test literal) and re-validated with the feature enabled. The 3 new tests are now confirmed running and green: `sync_ingress_drops_text_replacement_by_default`, `sync_ingress_delivers_text_replacement_body_when_enabled`, `sync_ingress_drops_non_text_replacement_even_when_enabled`.

- New tests: `sync_ingress_drops_text_replacement_by_default`, `sync_ingress_delivers_text_replacement_body_when_enabled`, `sync_ingress_drops_non_text_replacement_even_when_enabled` — they drive the real `handle_message` ingress with raw replacement events (`m.replace` + `m.new_content`) and assert the delivered `ChannelMessage`.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (workspace build/test/clippy across the feature matrix) compiles `channel-matrix` and covers the two feature-gated constructors updated here.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known for this diff — the feature-gated matrix module is compiled and tested with `--features channel-matrix` (see the correction above); the `zeroclaw-config` run has one failure — `platform::native::tests::powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics` — which reproduces on unmodified `master` (Windows console encoding in the test harness, unrelated to this diff).
- **Commands run and tail output:** channels lib 2042/2042 green; `cargo clippy` introduces zero new lints against the diff (3 Windows-only pre-existing lints reproduce on clean master: `platform/docker.rs` dead field, `platform/native.rs` dead field, `secrets/windows_key_file.rs` collapsible_if — none touched here).
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Full-workspace audit of every `ChannelMessage` literal (329 sites) to confirm the new field cannot break any feature-gated or test-only constructor; not verified: a live homeserver round-trip (that is the NB-pilot step and will be reported separately).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (No)
- New external network calls? (No — the same sync loop against the same homeserver; no new endpoint or credential use)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (No)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (No)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (Yes)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: when `edited_messages = true`, the corrected `m.new_content` body (user-generated channel text from the same sender and room) reaches the agent instead of the fallback body that master already delivered as a duplicate turn. No new trust boundary is crossed — the text source and admission gates (allowed senders, mention/room rules) are identical; only freshness improves. The flag defaults to off, so operators opt in explicitly.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (No — behavior change in both modes. On master every edit starts a second turn with the `* …` fallback body; with this PR edits are dropped unless the alias opts in via `edited_messages = true`, exactly as #12439 calls out for the same path)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (Yes — one new optional key `[channels.matrix.<alias>] edited_messages`, default `false`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (No)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: to opt in, add `edited_messages = true` under the Matrix alias in `config.toml` and restart. No migration needed; the key only controls whether edits are processed, not any state.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` — single commit, no migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `edited_messages` on the Matrix alias (default `false` is the rollback posture).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** with the flag on, edits delivered with the literal `* ` fallback body or edits re-triggering duplicate turns (pre-PR behavior returning); a missed `edited` field compile error in any future full `ChannelMessage` literal surfaces immediately at build time.

prs.title: feat(cli): show Codex subscription usage
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Add `zeroclaw auth usage --model-provider openai.<alias>` so an operator can check Codex subscription usage before running inference. Show five-hour and weekly utilization and UTC reset times when the service reports them; `--json` keeps missing fields as `null` rather than inventing zeroes.
- **Scope boundary:** CLI only. No WebUI, slash command, routing policy, background polling, config schema change, or new dependency. API-key and custom-endpoint routes aren't supported by this command.
- **Blast radius:** The explicit command adds one read-only request for a native Codex route. It reuses the route's ZeroClaw OAuth profile selection, reads the access token from the same auth snapshot, and does not refresh or fall back to another profile. Existing inference paths are not intended to change.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

If you use Codex through ZeroClaw, check how much of your subscription's usage windows is consumed and when the windows reset. This checks the ZeroClaw login, which may not be the same account as a separate Codex CLI login. It calls the same direct ChatGPT usage endpoint (`GET /backend-api/wham/usage`) as the [open-source Codex client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/f12fa0fbc5c39eb59a4ad9d894b306a91ee8867c/codex-rs/backend-client/src/client/rate_limit_resets.rs#L128-L133). OpenAI documents `account/rateLimits/read` for the [Codex App Server](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server), not a public API contract for this direct HTTP endpoint. ZeroClaw reuses its own OAuth login without running the App Server, so the endpoint’s availability and response shape can change independently of ZeroClaw. The result is informational; it doesn't promise that a later turn will be accepted.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if you have a configured native Codex route and want to verify the live endpoint.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A configured native Codex route, e.g. `openai.coding`, and its existing usable ZeroClaw OAuth profile. The separate Codex CLI is not required.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw auth usage --model-provider openai.coding --json`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One JSON document with `five_hour` and `weekly`; when reported, each contains `used_percent` and `resets_at`. If at least one recognized window is present, the other window or individual fields may be `null`. If the response contains neither recognized window, the profile is unusable, or the endpoint fails, the command exits nonzero. No inference starts.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `auth usage` is not a recognized subcommand.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why:** The [required CI gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44963756531/job/137030854771) passed on `ea56e7cb8`, including hosted build, lint, test, and Security checks. The focused local tests below exercise the changed command and provider boundaries.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Mock HTTP tests cannot establish availability or compatibility of the live direct HTTP endpoint.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  git diff --check
  cargo test --locked --offline -j2 -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- openai_codex::usage::tests:: auth::profiles::tests::read_oauth_access_only auth::tests::select_profile_prefers --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 33 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test --locked --offline -j2 --bin zeroclaw -- auth_usage codex_usage --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test --locked --offline -j2 --test component -- component::auth_usage_cli:: --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
  cargo clippy --locked --offline -j2 -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
  ```

  The provider-guide Markdown gate reported `0 error(s)`; the added-link gate found no added links.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An isolated candidate executable showed the expected help and missing-profile behavior. One live invocation using a configured native Codex route succeeded: stdout was one JSON document, both usage percentages were present, and both reset times were UTC. Monitored config, auth, and OTP file metadata was unchanged. No inference, retry, or token refresh was performed. Actual quota values and account details are intentionally omitted. Independent exact-head reviews returned `READY` with advisory findings, not maintainer approval.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output from the noninteractive, unstyled `cli` command.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `faaefa5363d112490a8bc6496879651d29e20f7f`; `cli`; English; isolated final-interface stderr for a synthetic missing-profile case. The current head `ea56e7cb8bf0c80a9d8fab87ee32d578be080eef` is an attribution-only rewrite: both commit trees were verified identical to their tested counterparts. The local tests, live smoke check, and independent exact-head reviews ran on `faaefa5363d112490a8bc6496879651d29e20f7f`, not on the new SHA.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

  ```text
  Error: No OpenAI Codex OAuth profile found; run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`.
  ```
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The missing-profile invocation exited 1, left stdout empty, and created no auth or OTP files. The live invocation exited successfully and returned both usage windows with UTC reset times.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The local suite is scoped to touched behavior; the wider workspace suite is left to hosted CI. No deployment is required for the live smoke check.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes, an explicit CLI capability reads an existing ZeroClaw auth snapshot; no added permissions, new credential store, or broader directory scope.
- **New external network calls?** Yes, one opt-in GET to the fixed first-party ChatGPT usage endpoint. Custom endpoints are rejected; time and body size are bounded, with no redirects or retries.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** Yes, the usage path reads only the selected profile's OAuth access token from one snapshot and sends it to the fixed first-party HTTPS endpoint. It does not refresh or log it, and checks account consistency when the response identifies an account.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No. Examples and fixtures are synthetic; actual usage values are not included in this PR.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No. The command doesn't call the model; output contains only normalized quota fields.

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Yes.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** Yes, an additive `auth usage` subcommand with `--model-provider` and `--json`. No config or environment changes.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing users. To opt in, run the command with an already configured native Codex route and usable ZeroClaw OAuth profile.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Stop invoking `auth usage`; to remove the feature, revert the PR's merge commit or reinstall the prior binary. No schema or credential migration to undo.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The command only runs on explicit invocation.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Nonzero exit for auth, transport, or parse errors; missing windows or fields appear as `null` when otherwise valid data is returned.

prs.title: fix(web): show the typed prompt and stored times in a reloaded chat
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When the dashboard rebuilds a chat from the stored transcript (for example after leaving the chat page and coming back), user messages from the agent path showed the runtime's `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix. The chat view already strips a leading channel-style `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ]`, but not this labeled form. `displayMessageText` in `web/src/lib/chatMessageText.ts` (the shared display helper #12269 added) now strips exactly one server prefix from a server-sourced user message: the labeled one when present (through the existing `normalizeServerUserContent`), otherwise the channel-style one as before. Stripping only one keeps a bracketed datetime the user typed at the start of their message.
  - The rebuilt bubbles also got synthetic times (one second apart, ending just before the reload). `mapServerMessagesToPersisted` now uses each row's `created_at`, which the messages API already returns, and keeps the synthetic time only when a row has none or it doesn't parse.
- **Scope boundary:** Display and copy only. `msg.content` stays the raw server text, so the hydration comparison in `chatHydration.logic.ts` is unchanged. No change to what the runtime stores, to the messages API, or to locally typed or live messages. Not addressed here: the SQLite backend giving every stored row the time of the last write (#11420, addressed by the open #11676), and thinking and tool rows not being stored (#8794).
- **Blast radius:** The chat view's message text and copy button for server-sourced user messages, and the timestamps of rebuilt messages. The helper is also used by the browser voice controls, which read only agent replies aloud, so they are unaffected. Nothing else reads message timestamps: they are only displayed (and saved with the browser's local copy of the chat).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12507. Related #11676, #11420. #12269 landed first and moved the chat view's prefix stripping into `web/src/lib/chatMessageText.ts`, so the display change now lives in that helper; `AgentChat.tsx` is unchanged by this PR.

### What this does, simply

When you chat with an agent, the runtime adds a line like `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: 2026-11-17 18:30:21 +00:00]` to each of your messages before it stores it, so the model knows the time. The dashboard showed that line at the top of your own messages whenever it reloaded a chat from the server, as if you had typed it. It also replaced each message's time with made-up times a second apart. Now the reloaded chat shows your messages as you typed them, and the times the server stored for them.

Until #11676 is merged, the SQLite backend gives all earlier messages in a chat the time of the latest turn, so those times will look the same; with #11676 they become per turn.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard chat)
- **Setup / preconditions:** an agent on the structured Agent path (any provider), SQLite session persistence (the default).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the agent's chat and send two short messages.
  2. Click Dashboard in the sidebar, then go back to the chat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the two messages read exactly as typed, and the copy button copies them without a prefix. Their times are the stored ones (until #11676 lands, the time of the latest turn).
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** each user message starts with `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]`, and all bubbles show times one second apart, ending just before you came back to the chat.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Web Permission Tests` job, required by `CI Required Gate`: its `cargo web check` step typechecks the changed files (`tsc -b`), and its `npm run test:contexts` step runs `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`, with the new test, through `pretest:contexts`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the test renders the chat through the existing react-test-renderer harness, not a browser; the browser check below covered that at an earlier revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a Node 24 container at this head (`d90646786`), after generating the API client files with `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- spec-dump --out <dir>` and `openapi-typescript`:
  ```text
  $ npm run typecheck      (exit 0)
  $ npm run build          (exit 0)
  $ npm test               (exit 0)
  $ npm run test:contexts  (exit 0)
  $ npm run test:auth      (exit 0)
  ✔ a chat rebuilt from the stored transcript shows the typed prompt and stored times
  ```
  The new test rebuilds a chat from a transcript with a prefixed user row, a row without `created_at`, a prefixed row whose text starts with a bracketed datetime, and an agent reply that quotes the label. It checks that the rows take their `created_at`, that the row without one keeps a synthetic time, that the label isn't rendered on user rows, and that the typed datetime and the agent reply's quoted label are. It fails without the display change ("the runtime's date prefix must not be displayed") and without the timestamp change ("hydrated bubbles must take the rows' created_at").
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On my own server, running current `master` plus an earlier revision of this branch (before review fixes that only change the case of a message starting with a bracketed datetime) and other open PRs that don't touch chat hydration: after leaving the chat page and coming back, the user messages no longer showed the prefix, and the times were the stored ones (all the time of the latest turn, as expected without #11676). Not verified: a channel-sourced conversation opened in the dashboard, Safari, or a phone.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** a slim daemon built from this branch (the tree of `034e53d3c`, the first commit of this branch, before the merges of `master`; the display rule has since moved into `chatMessageText.ts` with #12269 and is covered at the current head by the new test, which renders through it) and one built from `master` at `cda933e6b`, each with its embedded dashboard, SQLite session storage and a stub provider that answers "ok". A Playwright script in headless Chromium (locale `en-US`, time zone UTC) opened the chat, sent `first prompt` and `[2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC] typed datetime`, clicked Dashboard, went back, and read the text of each message row.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the rows' visible text after coming back to the chat (line breaks inside a row shown as two spaces, times aligned):
  ```text
  master (cda933e6b)
    [CURRENT DATE & TIME: 2026-11-17 18:30:21 +00:00]  first prompt   6:30:24 PM
    ok                                                                 6:30:25 PM
    [CURRENT DATE & TIME: 2026-11-17 18:30:24 +00:00]  [2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC] typed datetime   6:30:26 PM
    ok                                                                 6:30:27 PM
  this branch at 034e53d3c
    first prompt                                                       6:31:25 PM
    ok                                                                 6:31:25 PM
    [2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC] typed datetime                           6:31:25 PM
    ok                                                                 6:31:25 PM
  ```
  The messages API returned the same `created_at` for all four rows in both runs (the time of the second turn's write, #11420), which is the time this branch shows. On `master` the times were the synthetic ones counted back from the reload; the messages had been sent at 6:30:21 and 6:30:24.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** as above. Before leaving the chat, both builds showed the messages as typed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo web check` was not run directly; its generation and `tsc -b` steps were reproduced as described above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(transcription): add default_provider fallback for agents without a transcription alias
prs.body:
## Problem

`TranscriptionManager::transcribe()` fails loud when the runtime agent has no `transcription_provider` configured — there is deliberately no global default. In practice this means voice transcription silently (well, loudly) does nothing for every agent until each one is given its own alias, even when the deployment has exactly one transcription provider and the operator considers it deployment-wide.

## Change

- New optional `[transcription].default_provider`: when set, agents without their own `transcription_provider` fall back to it; agents with their own alias are unaffected. When neither is set, the existing fail-loud behavior is unchanged.
- `TranscriptionManager` gains `resolved_agent_alias()` (agent alias → `default_provider` → empty); `transcribe()` dispatches through it, and the unbound-agent error now points at `[transcription].default_provider` as the remediation.
- The voice path in `telegram.rs` resolves via the same API (`transcribe_with_provider`), keeping its warn-and-skip disposition when nothing is bound.
- The current config loader preserves `[transcription].default_provider` by removing only its retired-key and old-layout markers. The unrelated retired default aliases remain retired.

Note: `TranscriptionManager::new`/`from_sections` take the new value as a parameter (all in-repo call sites updated). Happy to switch to reading it from `TranscriptionConfig` inside the constructor if the maintainers prefer a smaller public diff.

## Tests

- `resolved_agent_alias_prefers_agent_then_default_then_empty`
- `transcribe_dispatches_to_agent_alias_when_set` (no behavior change)
- `transcribe_falls_back_to_default_provider_when_agent_unbound`
- `transcribe_fails_loud_when_agent_unbound_and_no_default_provider`

prs.title: fix(rpc): rehydrate reaped ACP sessions on provider switch
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A failed ZeroCode Code-pane turn drops the live ACP incarnation so the next prompt can rebuild provider-safe history from the durable row.
  - `/model-provider` is `session/configure`. That handler only looked at the live map, so a switch after a provider rate-limit returned `-32000` `Session not found` for a session that still existed in the ACP store.
  - `session/configure` now restores that reaped row, under the configure method's leases, before applying the provider override.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change prompt admission, checkpoint recovery rules, or when a failed turn drops the live incarnation. Does not change provider failover itself.
- **Blast radius:** `session/configure` on a reaped ACP session now rebuilds the agent before writing overrides. Live sessions and chat-mode sessions take the existing path. Rehydration leases are parameterized by the calling method instead of being hard-wired to `session/prompt`. configure's pending-binding wait now runs after the optional restore instead of before it, so it also covers a session another request restored.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A Code pane keeps its conversation in the ACP store. When the model provider fails the turn, for example an OpenAI Codex rate limit, ZeroClaw removes the in-memory session on purpose. The next prompt knows how to put that session back. Changing the provider with `/model-provider` did not. It looked only at the in-memory map, decided the session was gone, and refused the switch with `-32000`.

This PR makes the provider-switch call restore the saved Code-pane session first, then apply the new provider. A session that was never saved, or that was killed, still gets `Session not found`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The reliable reproduction is the new unit test; a manual A/B needs a failed Code-pane turn.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` Code pane (`channel` `rpc`, chat mode ACP) via `/model-provider` (`session/configure`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Code pane session whose provider can fail a turn (the reported case was an OpenAI alias with Codex auth, then `/model-provider` to an xAI alias). The automated test uses the persistence dispatcher and does not need live credentials.
- **Steps to run:** On a Code pane, send a prompt that ends in a failed turn, then run `/model-provider <other-provider>`. Automated: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_` (covers the restore path and both concurrent-restore interleavings).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The switch succeeds and later prompts use the selected provider. The unit test asserts the reaped session is live again and its route resolver names `openai.provider-b`. The two interleaving regressions assert that when another request restores the session with a pending binding, configure waits for reconciliation, and the reported selection, stored override and live route all name `openai.provider-b` afterwards.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `/model-provider` returns `-32000` `Session not found` even though the ACP row is still in the store.

### How I tested

Focused runtime tests cover the new restore path, both concurrent-restore interleavings from review, and the existing rehydration and configure paths that share the edited function. The full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib suite and crate clippy on CI's pinned toolchain were run locally on `c98b20fc4`. Workspace-wide clippy and `cargo test` were not; required CI on this head covers them.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet for `c98b20fc4`. Do not treat pending checks as evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local evidence does not include workspace clippy or the workspace test suite. CI lint and test jobs cover that gap once they run on this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0, no output

cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 00s

# Before the fix (new tests + test hook on ee958454a handler):
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_waits_for_binding_restored -- --test-threads=1
# ..._restored_before_live_lookup ... FAILED
#   reconciliation must not revert the provider configure reported as selected
#   left: "openai.test-provider"  right: "openai.provider-b"
# ..._restored_during_admission_wait ... FAILED
#   configure must wait for the binding another request restored

# After the fix (c98b20fc4):
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_ -- --test-threads=1
# test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6185 filtered out

# Stress: the two interleaving regressions, default parallel harness, 25 runs
# pass=25 fail=0

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
# test result: ok. 6185 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The failing path was identified from a Code-pane rate-limit turn (`openai` + Codex auth) followed by `/model-provider` to xAI, which returned `-32000`. I did not re-run that live provider switch after the patch. The unit tests reproduce the dropped live incarnation, the configure call, and both concurrent-restore interleavings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No presentation-sensitive interface state changed. The user-visible change is whether the slash command succeeds.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `c98b20fc4`. Automated evidence is the `zeroclaw-runtime` lib tests above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test tails above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `session/configure` on a reaped ACP session restores the agent and installs the requested provider override. When another request restored it with a pending binding, configure waits for reconciliation first, so the override is not reverted.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and workspace `cargo test` were skipped locally because this change is one RPC handler plus regression tests in one crate. Crate clippy was run on CI's pinned 1.98.0; local stable 1.99.0 reports new lints in untouched code (`zeroclaw-providers`, `fetch_update` deprecations), unrelated to this PR. CI on this head is the intended coverage for the rest.

prs.title: feat(channels): opt-in owner notice for turned-away Matrix senders
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A Matrix message turned away by the sender allowlist is dropped silently: the sender gets no stub, and the operator learns about the attempt only from DEBUG logs. This adds an opt-in `owner_user_id` field to `[channels.matrix.<alias>]`; when set, the channel also delivers a short heads-up DM to that user (typically the operator) naming the sender MXID, the source room, and a bounded preview of the turned-away message, plus a `peer_groups` authorization hint.
  - The DM room is created lazily (`is_direct`, encrypted under the SDK's e2e feature), cached, and re-resolved when the configured owner changes; an existing DM with the owner is reused.
  - Notices are throttled to one per (sender, room) pair per 5 minutes. Matrix has no transport-level flood gate like Telegram's Bot API, so without this a determined spammer could turn the operator's DM into a firehose.
- **Scope boundary:** trigger v1 is the sender-allowlist drop only — room-allowlist drops (operator configuration errors) and mention-gate drops (polite group silence) do not notify. No public stub is sent to the turned-away sender; authorization decisions, peer resolution, and other channels are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Matrix channel ingress only. `HandlerCtx` and the channel struct gain shared owner-notice state; two test-only `HandlerCtx` literals and one full `MatrixConfig` test literal are updated.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12346 (Telegram `owner_chat_id` owner notice — same design vocabulary, deliberately adapted)

### What this does, simply

In Matrix, when someone who is not on the bot's peer list writes to a room the bot watches, the message is currently dropped with only a DEBUG log line — neither the sender nor the operator hears anything. With this PR an operator who sets `owner_user_id = "@you:your-server"` on the channel alias gets a direct message from the bot: who tried, from which room, a 160-character preview of what they said, and a hint that authorizing means adding their MXID to the channel's `peer_groups` entry. The notice is deliberately sent even when the operator themselves is the turned-away sender (unlike the Telegram version, which skips that echo) because Matrix sends no public reply at all — the DM is the only signal, and an operator testing from an unauthorized account wants to see it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — ingress behavior is covered by unit tests at the decision layer; end-to-end DM delivery needs a live homeserver and was verified against a real Synapse (see below).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (matrix)

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features channel-matrix        # full channel suite incl. new owner_notice_gates module
cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-matrix --tests     # feature-gated compile gate
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                             # clean (cargo +1.98.0 fmt)
```

- New `owner_notice_gates` tests pin the pure decision layer: preview collapse/truncation with ellipsis, throttle admit/suppress/readmit per (sender, room) pair, notice composition naming sender/room/preview/alias, and `prepare_owner_notice` gating (no owner, blank owner, no logged-in client all yield no notice).
- The full channel suite was run **with `--features channel-matrix`** so the feature-gated matrix module is actually compiled and exercised (an earlier PR of ours missed this — see #12426 — and the lesson is applied here).
- Delivery itself (DM creation, encrypted send) requires a logged-in client; it was verified end-to-end against a live Synapse 1.165 stand during development (turned-away sender → operator DM received, throttle suppressing rapid repeats). A homeserver is not available in CI for this path.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI builds the workspace across the feature matrix, compiling `channel-matrix` and the updated config schema.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** DM delivery has no CI integration test (no homeserver); the decision layer is unit-covered and delivery is a thin `get_dm_room`/`create_dm` + `room.send` wrapper with failure logging.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Live Synase stand: unauthorized sender → owner DM delivered with correct fields; repeat attempt within 5 minutes produced no second DM; the DM room was reused (no duplicate room created). Not verified: owner switching mid-run against a live server (covered by cache-key design, exercised only at unit level).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (No)
- New external network calls? (No — the DM send goes to the already-configured homeserver, like every other channel send)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (No)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (No — examples use `example.org` placeholders)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (No — the notice text is delivered to the configured operator only; message bodies reach the notice preview unchanged from what the sender wrote, and the notice is never fed back into an agent turn)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (Yes — default off; without `owner_user_id` the drop stays exactly as silent as before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (Yes — one new optional key `[channels.matrix.<alias>] owner_user_id`, default unset)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (No)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: to opt in, add `owner_user_id = "@you:your-server"` under the Matrix alias in `config.toml`; the change is visible to the next turn-away event without a restart when the config is published through the live-config authority.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` — single commit, no migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `owner_user_id` from the alias (or set it to an empty value) — the notice path disables immediately on the next read.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** operator receives owner DMs for ordinary traffic (misconfigured `owner_user_id` pointing at a user who is also an authorized sender — the notice only fires on allowlist drops, so this means the allowlist is wrong, not the notice); WARN records `matrix: owner notice delivery failed` when the homeserver rejects DM creation or send.

prs.title: fix(web): draw the Cost Overview bars against the configured limits
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The Overview tab's Cost Overview bars were each scaled to the largest of the card's three amounts. The month's spend includes the day's, so with the default Today window the Monthly bar was full whatever share of `[cost].monthly_limit_usd` had been spent, and with no spend every bar still showed a 2% sliver. The "Session" row was the total for the window selected on the Cost tab, not a session (#12568).
  - `GET /api/cost` now also returns `budget`: `tracking` (a tracker runs and `[cost].enabled` is on), `daily_limit_usd`, `monthly_limit_usd` and `warn_at_percent` (capped at 100, as the budget check caps it). They come from the running tracker's config (the one its budget check reads), or the live `[cost]` section when the gateway holds no tracker. The limits are nullable (`null` for a non-finite value today), so an unset limit, as in #12512, needs no new response shape.
  - The card shows Daily and Monthly against their limits, with the limit next to the amount. The bar is 0% with no spend, turns the warning colour from `warn_at_percent`, and is full and red once the limit is reached. A zero or negative limit allows no spend, matching the budget check's `projected > limit`: with a zero limit any spend fills the bar, and a negative one is full from the start. Without tracking or without a limit, the card shows the amount and no bar. The Session row is removed.
  - The bar rules live in `web/src/pages/costBudget.logic.ts`, with tests.
  - `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md` describes the new response and no longer points to the removed Session row.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to cost tracking, the budget check, enforcement, the `cost` part of the response, the Cost tab, or the card's Total tokens and Requests lines (still the selected window's totals). How to present disabled enforcement (`[cost.enforcement]`) is left open, as suggested in #12568; the bars show whenever tracking is on and a limit is set.
- **Blast radius:** The Overview tab's Cost Overview card, a new field in the `/api/cost` response, whose only reader is the dashboard, and two passages of the cost tracking guide. `getCost`, used elsewhere, is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12568. Related #12512, which makes the limits optional: once `cost_budget` and its two tests are adapted to `Option<f64>` (e.g. `cost.daily_limit_usd.filter(|v| v.is_finite())`), an unset limit is reported as `null`, and the card already shows such a period without a bar. Whichever lands second adapts the other.

### What this does, simply

The dashboard's cost bars now show how much of your daily and monthly spending limits you've used. Before, the monthly bar was usually full, so it looked as if you'd hit your limit when you hadn't. The bars turn amber near the limit and red once it's reached, and they don't change when you pick a different time window on the Cost tab.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard Overview)
- **Setup / preconditions:** cost tracking on (the default), with some spend recorded today and this month.
- **Steps to run:** open the dashboard's Overview tab; then choose "All time" on the Cost tab and go back to Overview.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Daily and Monthly show spend / limit, with bars at that share; switching the window doesn't change them.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the Monthly bar is full; Daily is drawn as a share of the month; with "All time", the Session row becomes the full bar and the others shrink.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the gateway tests (`api_cost_reports_the_limits_without_a_tracker`, `api_cost_reports_the_running_trackers_limits`) cover the new `budget` field, including an explicit zero limit, the capped warning percentage and tracking off. The `Web Permission Tests` job's `cargo web check` typechecks the dashboard. `Docs Style` covers the changed guide.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `npm test`, where the new `costBudget.logic.test.ts` is registered alongside the other logic suites, is not run by CI; I ran it locally (6 pass). It covers the two cases from #12568 (no spend against a positive limit draws 0%; $4 of $10 daily and $55 of $100 monthly stay at 40% and 55% whatever the window total), the warning and reached tones, zero and negative limits, and the no-bar cases. The card's rendering isn't tested in CI; see the browser check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in podman (`zc-build:1.98.0`, Rust 1.98) and a Node 24 container:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      (ok)
  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings   (no warnings)
  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_cost
  test api::tests::api_cost_reports_the_limits_without_a_tracker ... ok
  test api::tests::api_cost_reports_the_running_trackers_limits ... ok
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
  $ npm run typecheck      (exit 0)
  $ npm run build          (exit 0)
  $ npm test               (exit 0; costBudget.logic.test.ts: 6 pass)
  $ npm run test:contexts  (exit 0)
  $ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   (0 errors)
  $ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     (no added links)
  ```
  (clippy and the gateway tests ran on a revision whose Rust differs from the head only in a doc comment; fmt and the web and docs checks ran at the head.)
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The card in a browser, below. Not verified: Firefox, Safari, a phone, or a tracker with real provider pricing (the spend was seeded into the ledger).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** slim daemons with the embedded dashboard, one built from `master` at `39478aa50` and one from an earlier revision of this branch (differing from the head only in code comments and in drawing a negative limit as full, which the logic tests cover), with the default limits ($10 daily, $100 monthly, warning at 80%) unless noted. Each run's cost ledger (`state/costs.jsonl`) was seeded with $4 today, $51 earlier this month and $185 last month (UTC), so the month is $55 and all time is $240. A Playwright script in headless Chromium 136 (1400×1000, time zone UTC) read each row's text, bar width and colour on the Overview tab, then chose "All time" on the Cost tab and read them again.

prs.title: feat(oidc): make requested OAuth scopes configurable per provider
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `[oidc.<alias>] scopes` (device grant + browser Authorization Code, including dashboard sign-in) and `service_scopes` (`client_credentials`). Every flow previously hard-coded `scope=openid`.
  - Entra ID derives the access token's audience from the requested scope, and its `client_credentials` grant accepts only `api://<app>/.default` (no `openid`). With a fixed `openid`, Entra cannot issue a token for ZeroClaw's audience at all, which blocks the v1.0 Okta + Entra ID requirement recorded in #12496. Two lists are needed because the interactive and service flows want incompatible scope sets on Entra.
  - Validation fails closed: each entry must be an RFC 6749 §3.3 scope-token (rejects blank, whitespace that would split one entry into two scopes, `"`, `\`, control, and non-ASCII), no duplicates, and interactive `scopes` must include `openid` because browser sign-in validates an ID token. No scope, including `offline_access`, is ever added implicitly (its meaning differs by issuer; on Keycloak it yields an offline token that outlives the SSO session).
  - Removes the "No configurable scopes" limitation from `identity-providers.md` and updates the two lines that depended on it.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change token verification (Okta/Entra token-format compatibility is a separate PR), does not add RFC 8707 `resource`, and does not touch refresh tokens. Defaults are unchanged: an entry without the new keys sends exactly `scope=openid` as before.
- **Blast radius:** `Enrollment` request building, used by gateway device/browser enrollment, dashboard sign-in, and `zeroclaw oidc login|token`. `OidcConfig` gains two `#[serde(default)]` fields; the field reference in `authentication.md` is rendered from their doc comments via `{{#config-fields oidc}}`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12608 (ADR-016 exception for `enrollment.rs`). Related #8289, Related #12496

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw asks an identity provider to sign someone in, it says what it wants access to through "scopes". Until now it always asked for just `openid`. That's enough for Keycloak, but Microsoft Entra ID decides who a token is *for* from the scopes requested, so with only `openid` Entra hands back a token for Microsoft's own APIs that ZeroClaw rightly refuses. This lets an operator list the scopes per provider, separately for people signing in and for headless service accounts. Nothing changes for existing setups.

prs.body:
> **Refreshed (`e57e860fbf`):** #12608 has merged, so `master` was merged in. This PR now adds only the refresh-grant row, unchanged from `5f6c8ee82f`, after #12608's two Okta/Entra rows.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds the `zeroclaw-runtime` exception row for the refresh-grant implementation that the ADR-017 amendment (#12496, approved) records. The existing #12317 OIDC row explicitly excludes "refresh-token storage", and #12496 now states that each implementing PR touching the auth-provider owner in the holding crate needs its own row first. Proposed ahead of the implementation, as ADR-016 requires and as the plugin-admission row did.
  - Scope names exact paths and limits: retaining the refresh token the existing device-grant and browser responses already return (`EnrolledToken::refresh_token`), a refresh request that omits `scope`, RFC 7009 revocation, never-sent vs unknown-outcome classification (`enrollment.rs`); a new `refresh_grant.rs` module *inside the existing auth-provider subsystem* for the pending grant (keyed by a hash of its paired access token) and the durable, `SecretStore`-sealed grant with version, single-flight, in-flight marker and uncertain state, registered in `auth_provider/mod.rs` limited to declaring the module and re-exporting its public types; a grant table in the existing ledger database so the claim commits in the same transaction as `record_issued`, plus deletion on revocation or unrenewed lapse (`cert_ledger.rs`); and a pre-auth refresh method admitted like `cert/renew`, sign-out, and grant deletion on provider removal/repoint (`rpc/{auth,dispatch,types}.rs`).
  - Explicit exclusions: no dashboard refresh or client-held refresh token, no OAuth flow beyond refresh and revocation, no change to introspection or `initialize`, no new subsystem. Encryption reuses `zeroclaw_config::secrets::SecretStore` (ADR-013) rather than adding crypto to runtime. Gateway hand-off, the Zerocode trigger, and `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` method names stay in their own crates.
- **Scope boundary:** Governance record only; no code. Does not cover #12497/#12498 (that's #12608).
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Gates the refresh implementation PRs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12608. Related #12496, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

The ADR now says how ZeroClaw will keep a laptop's sign-in alive across sleep: the daemon holds the identity provider's refresh token, and the device certificate lets Zerocode ask for a fresh access token. Most of that code has to touch sign-in code in a temporary "holding" crate, which needs a written, approved exception before anything lands there. This is that exception, drawn tightly around what the refresh work needs and nothing more, so the implementation can be reviewed against a fixed boundary.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `formatUsd` (`web/src/lib/format.ts`) returned "<$0.01" for any value under a cent, including exactly zero. Zero (and anything below it) now formats as "$0.00"; "<$0.01" stays for spend above zero but under a cent.
  - A small test, `web/src/lib/format.test.ts`, covers null, zero, a negative value, under a cent, a cent, and a larger amount. It stands in the browser globals that the i18n module's imports read on load, as `apiAuth.test.ts` does.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `formatUsd`. The dashboard's metrics row has its own formatter, which already shows zero as "$0", and the Cost Overview card's four-decimal `formatUSD` is unaffected. prs.title: chore(channels)!: move IRC and Twitch out of the binary into registry plugins
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remove the compiled-in IRC and Twitch channels. Both now ship as the `irc` and `twitch` WASM plugins, which a stock host installs without a rebuild. Twitch was a thin adapter over the IRC channel, so the two leave together. This takes the raw-TCP IRC channel out of the "retain built-in" list in #8850, now that a compatible, validated package exists.
  - `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` become **retired config keys**, the same mechanism WATI used. Each load drops the section and prints a notice that names the plugin and its install and bind commands. The next save removes it from disk, secrets included.
  - `ChannelKind::Irc` and `ChannelKind::Twitch` stay in the attribution enum so historical records deserialize. They are marked not inbound-capable, so they leave the SOP trigger registry, as WATI did.
  - Keep `OutboundContentFormat::PlainText` for migrated `plugin.<alias>` bindings whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>].package` is `irc` or `twitch` (and fall back to `PlainText` for bare `"plugin"` or unresolved plugin aliases whenever an enabled plain-text plugin binding exists), so Markdown link destinations are still scanned by the outbound leak redactor across drafts, multi-message narration flushes, final replies (including `send_via` redirects), and announcements.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No other channel changes, and no plugin-runtime changes.
  - No automatic conversion of an old section into a plugin binding. The plugin must be installed first, and the encrypted credentials belong to a different config row.
  - The schema version is not bumped (see the reviewer question below).
- **Blast radius:**
  - Release archives never included IRC or Twitch: neither is in the dist feature set. They shipped only in `channels-full` source builds and the `all-features` image. That image and `--preset full` also build the plugin runtime, so every install that had these channels can install the plugins.
  - A plain `cargo build --features channels-full` without `plugins-wasm` loses them, and needs `plugins-wasm` added.
  - Generated installer surfaces (`Containerfile`, `setup.bat`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`) were checked against `cargo generate installers`: no drift.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8850. Depends on zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174 (merged and published), which publishes the `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 packages this PR points operators to.

### Reviewer decision: `retired_in: 4`, no schema bump

The `RETIRED_KEYS` policy comment asks for a version bump when no pending version covers a retirement. V4 shipped in v0.9.0. I used `retired_in: 4` without a V5 bump because:
- Every load already applies every retired key, whatever version the file declares, so operators see the same thing either way.
- A V5 bump would make every config saved by this binary unreadable by v0.9.0 ("newer than this binary supports"). That's a large side effect for a channel removal, and it would be the first V5 change.

If maintainers prefer the bump, it's a mechanical follow-up: a `MIGRATION_STEPS` entry, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5`, and a regenerated fixture.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw used to carry IRC and Twitch support inside its binary, but most installs (every release download) didn't include them, and getting them meant rebuilding ZeroClaw. They are now plugins you install with one command. This PR removes the old built-in copies. If an existing config still has an IRC or Twitch section, ZeroClaw says exactly what to do instead of silently ignoring it, and the rest of the config keeps working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the upgrade path.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config`, `zeroclaw plugin`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift,channels-full`, and a config dir whose `config.toml` holds `schema_version = 4`, a provider, `[agents.assistant] channels = ["irc.libera"]`, a `[channels.irc.libera]` section with a `sasl_password`, a peer group on `irc.libera`, and `[plugins] enabled = true`. Both `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 are published in the plugin registry (zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --config-dir D config get agents.assistant.channels`
  2. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin install irc`
  3. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin bind irc --channel-alias libera`
  4. Set `server`, `nickname`, and `channels` on the printed `plugins.entries.<key>.config.*` paths, and the server on `.egress_hosts`, with `config set --no-interactive`.
  5. `config set --no-interactive agents.assistant.channels '["plugin.libera"]'`
  6. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin info irc`
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Step 1 exits 0. It prints the retired-key warning naming the `irc` plugin and its install and bind commands, then a `config migrate` hint, on stderr, with no secret value shown. The complete output is in **Migration receipt** below.
  - Steps 2 to 5 succeed even though the agent still references `irc.libera`.
  - After the first save, `config.toml` no longer holds `[channels.irc]` or its secret.
  - Step 6 reports `plugin.libera configuration validates against the package schema.`, `The activation plan admits plugin.libera`, and `Loads: yes`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the built-in IRC channel loads from `[channels.irc.libera]`.

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps:
  1. Note the non-secret settings of each `[channels.irc|twitch.<alias>]` section. Secrets are encrypted in the file, so re-enter them from their source.
  2. Build with a WASM plugin backend if this is a custom source build (`--preset full` already has one).
  3. `zeroclaw plugin install irc` (or `twitch`), then `zeroclaw plugin bind irc --channel-alias <alias>` (Twitch: add `--egress declared`).

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the commits on this PR restores both channels and their config sections. A config whose retired section was already dropped by a save needs the section re-entered.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `dropped retired config key \`channels.irc\`` / `\`channels.twitch\`` on the CLI and `removed retired config key …` in logs at load; `agents.<agent>.channels[...] = "irc.<alias>" but channels.irc.<alias> is not configured` validation warnings until references are updated.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add host-mediated agent wake dispatch (dispatch.wake)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` interface `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` (`wake(target-agent, prompt) -> result<_, dispatch-error>`) and gated `import dispatch;` on `world tool-plugin` (`wit/v0/tool.wit`), gated by `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`).
  - Adds `AgentWakeBackend` / `AgentWakeService` on `PluginHostServices` (`zeroclaw-plugins`), `OptionalImports::dispatch` linker gating + coherence checks, `PluginState::wake_agent` (enforcing `ToolExecute` call-frame phase, host-call budget, grant, and target/prompt grammar), and host-owned `WasmTool::caller_alias`.
  - Adds operator grant fields `PluginEntryConfig::{dispatch_agents, dispatch_rate_per_min}` in `zeroclaw-config` (default-closed `[]` and `30`/min, strict alias/padding/bounds validation), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` in `zeroclaw-api`, and `manifest_owns_instance_state` row seeding so `agent_dispatch`-only manifests receive a `[[plugins.entries]]` row on install.
  - Implements `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/plugin_wake.rs` and wires `plugin_host_services_with_wake` / `register_plugin_tools` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` under the ADR-016 exception approved in #12417: live-config target authorization, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance continuous token bucket, per-`(instance, target)` wake coalescing, `AgentExecutionCapability` admission, `TaskKind::PeerInbox` durable `TaskRecord` registration/settlement, and `CostTracker` scoping.
  - **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):** Increments the hardcoded `wit/v0/` input-inventory assertion in `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`Run runtime plugin admission regressions`, line 1241) from `17` to `18` to account for the new `wit/v0/dispatch.wit`, matching the `expected_inputs` update in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Appends `--test dispatch_plugin_e2e` to the existing `Run plugin component tests` step and adds a `Run runtime plugin wake dispatch tests` step to the cranelift runtime leg (`cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib tools::plugin_wake`). No workflow triggers, runner labels, permissions, pinned actions, or secrets changed.
  - Adds `tool-dispatch-fixture` WASM guest + `dispatch_plugin_e2e`, unit tests across all touched crates, and documentation (`plugin-protocol.md`, `plugin-manifest-fields.md`, `writing-a-tool-plugin.md`, `CHANGELOG-next.md`).
- **Scope boundary:** `tool-plugin` world only; `channel-plugin` and `memory-plugin` do not import `dispatch`. No synchronous plugin-to-agent RPC, no ambient target grants, no edits to `send_message_to_peer.rs`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes only the `len(inputs) != 18` inventory count and the two test selections above. A dispatch-granted `WasmTool` reports `requires_unrestricted_principal`, so restricted (non-admin) principals never receive it. `wit/v0` remains experimental (no `.frozen` marker); `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` keeps existing `wit/v0` plugins linking unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Additive WIT import, optional `PluginEntryConfig` fields, `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool`, runtime adapter wiring, and the `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` inventory entry in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Default-closed (`dispatch_agents = []`) until an operator explicitly grants target aliases for an `agent_dispatch` plugin.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416, Related #12417

### What this does, simply

Tool plugins run in a fresh store per call with no network listener or access to the agent loop. This adds a gated `dispatch.wake(target-agent, prompt)` host import so an operator-authorized tool plugin can nudge a target agent into an asynchronous turn—coalescing burst wakes onto at most one queued follow-up turn, capping recursion at 2 hops, and enforcing live per-instance rate limits and target allowlists. It also updates the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and its matching `r5_namespace_tests.rs` list) to expect 18 WIT input files instead of 17 now that `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated WASM component E2E (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and runtime mock-provider coalescing/panic/cost tests (`plugin_wake`) exercise the full boundary directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI runs workspace format, clippy (with CI's pinned toolchain), `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-plugins`, `zeroclaw-runtime` (including the `r5_namespace_tests` fixture-receipt proof), architecture runner-label checks, and docs/links checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after this head. Earlier revisions had one: required CI selected neither `dispatch_plugin_e2e` nor the runtime `tools::plugin_wake` tests, because the default-feature Test job does not enable `plugins-wasm-cranelift` and the cranelift runtime leg selects modules explicitly. This head adds both selections to the plugin backend job.
- **Commands run and tail output (on head `f72f78a8ff` / prior `8ac25c5f9b` before the 2-line inventory update):**

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (exit 0)

  $ python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"
  (exit 0)

  $ cargo test --test architecture ci_runner_labels
  test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 80 filtered out; finished in 0.01s

A wake issued from a headless SOP step carries that step's tool scope into the woken turn (per wake, coalesced follow-ups included), and a wake is accepted onto a slot only once a worker owns it, so a failed setup never drops a wake that already returned success; a follow-up whose durable registration fails transiently is requeued and retried with capped backoff, re-checking the live grant and target before each attempt; the finished turn's lifecycle lease is released before draining, so an idle target stays deletable during that wait.

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. A granted tool plugin supplies a prompt the target agent sees. Operator target grants, the 1024-byte bound, and the target agent's risk profile limit its reach; the prompt remains untrusted input.

## Compatibility (required)
