- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes (`[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_agents` and `[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_rate_per_min`, both optional with fail-closed defaults).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No action required for existing installs; operators enabling an `agent_dispatch` plugin explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<key>.dispatch_agents` (and optionally `dispatch_rate_per_min`) to allow target wakes.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `dispatch_agents = []` on the affected `[[plugins.entries]]` rows in live config; new plugin wakes are denied without a rebuild. For a code rollback after merge, revert the merged PR commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.entries[].dispatch_agents = []` (default) disables all wake targets; WIT surface is gated behind `plugins-wit-v0-dispatch`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Wakes return `dispatch-error::access-denied` (`dispatch_agents` empty/missing) or `rate-limited` / `unavailable`, logged via `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::plugin_wake` with `action = Reject` or `Dispatch`.

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before. ZeroCode and Telegram wait the full 10 minutes; ACP waits the shorter of 10 minutes and `acp.session_timeout_secs`, because the ACP channel uses the trait's default timeout; other chat channels keep their own `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s by default), so there the shorter wait applies.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is kept in memory only. It ends at the next UTC day or month rollover, or when the daemon restarts, and a restart restores enforcement. Nothing is written to `state/cost-overrides.json`; a file left by an earlier build is ignored.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it. If the daemon refuses the answer (for example `FORBIDDEN`), the notice comes back with the error so the user can answer again; a timeout shows the error without bringing the notice back, because the daemon may already have the answer.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the #11589 row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` covers `src/agent/{approval_bridge,cost}.rs`, `src/agent/turn/{approval_gate,mod,provider_call}.rs`, `src/rpc/approval_channel.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`. It doesn't yet cover the RPC enforcement adapter in `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local}.rs`, or the attribution-only edits in `src/agent/agent.rs`, `src/daemon/mod.rs` and `src/integrations/registry.rs`. The ancestry, admission and binding rules themselves live in `zeroclaw-config` (`cost::override_grant`). A row amendment that covers these files and states the memory-only grant is drafted on fork branch `docs/runtime-exception-11589` (`e7868ca2a`, on `master` `1c1cd118a`). Like #11697, it needs its own Core Team-approved PR; this PR can't grant it.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends or the daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot ask still stop at an enforced limit on their own, but they benefit from a grant made elsewhere—the lift is daemon-wide for every session, delegation, and unattended scheduled or cron job using that shared tracker. Other shared limits and per-agent or per-hop ceilings still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a daemon restart the limit is enforced again and the next turn asks again. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

- **Authority recheck after the peer lookup (head `5d2ca670b747`):** `session/approve` for a cost-override prompt now rechecks the admitted session, the caller's current `SessionApprove` grants and ownership, and the pending request's session binding after the peer-process lookup. It holds the authority lease through delivery, so no await sits between the last check and `resolve_from_operator`. A caller who lost `sessions:update` during the lookup gets `FORBIDDEN`, the prompt stays pending and no override is granted. New tests: `rpc::dispatch::tests::cost_override_approve_rechecks_authority_after_peer_lookup` pauses the lookup, revokes the grant and checks for no approval and no grant. `cost_override_approve_accepts_unchanged_authority_after_peer_lookup` is the control: the approval is acknowledged and the real budget gate grants the override. With only the test commit applied to `ab919d606c`, the revocation test fails (the old handler answers `acknowledged: true`) and the control passes. On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5902 passed; 2 failed`, the two being the `relay::local_dial_tests` loopback-stall tests that also fail on the base; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no automated end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate. The gate tests use a scoped tracker with a scripted channel. The live run above covers that path by hand at the current head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** historical focused run on `2830dc912` (superseded by current head `fb2af71c36ed`) (`d01ad8eb1ad9` plus two ZeroCode-only fixes. Greptile 4429329518: a refused cost-limit answer brings the notice back and shows the error. Greptile 4429693704: a restored notice is cleared when its turn ends, so a refusal that also stopped the turn doesn't leave it up), Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree):
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1566 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`, including `refused_cost_limit_answer_restores_the_notice_and_shows_the_error` (the daemon answers `FORBIDDEN`; the notice and request id come back, and the error text is shown; a following `TurnComplete` then clears the notice).
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` → clean.
  - The runtime, config and api crates are unchanged since `d01ad8eb1ad9`, so the results below still apply to them.
- Previous head `d01ad8eb1ad9` (`d0297b2c4` narrow-pane fix plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --lib` → runtime `5905 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, config `1834 passed; 0 failed`, api `322 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1564 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on `master` on this host. `cost_limit_notice_keeps_full_scope_timeout_and_buttons_visible` passes at widths 30, 40, 76 and 100.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --check` → clean.
  - Historical note only: that paragraph described an older head. On 138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7, CI Required Gate passes. This PR does not change Cargo.lock or deny.toml.
  - The earlier head `5d2ca670b7` had a green CI Required Gate.
- **Greptile round 3 (on the master merge `e7c4aa6b3f68`):** the typing wrapper now resumes typing when another session's grant releases a waiting prompt, and keeps it off for a cancelled turn (`abandoned_approval_resumes_typing_unless_the_turn_was_cancelled`, which fails with the guard disarmed). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-runtime`; channels `approval_typing abandoned_approval approval_wait_resumes unsupported_approval_resumes` 5 passed; rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; a restart restoring enforcement (grants are memory-only), cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** historical live run on `d01ad8eb1ad9` (not exact-head for `fb2af71c36ed`) (real X11 window captures, daemon and ZeroCode from the same debug build, priced local stub provider). [Manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/MANIFEST.txt):
  - [Cost-limit prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L01-cost-limit-prompt-150x42.png); [Stop ends only that turn, no further provider call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L02-stop-ends-turn-150x42.png).
  - **Child-client IPC:** the daemon's `shell` tool opens a ZeroCode client (pid 3991336, a descendant of the daemon; see [ancestry](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/child-ancestry.txt)). Ctrl+O there [is refused and the turn stops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L05-child-client-ctrl-o-refused.png). The trace records `RPC cost override refused: independent operator process required` (`cost_override_untrusted_process`, `peer_pid` 3991336).
  - **Cross-session release:** with the child and a second, independent client both waiting, [Ctrl+O in the second client releases both turns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L07-grant-in-second-releases-child-desktop.png). It emits one `Approve` event, and [the main turn continues under the same grant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L08-main-turn-continues-under-grant-150x42.png).
  - **Narrow pane:** in a pane about 42 columns wide, [Stop and Override stack on separate rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L09-narrow-pane-stacked-buttons-42col.png), and [clicking the stacked Override continues the turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L10-narrow-pane-override-click-continues-42col.png).
  - Earlier macOS screenshots of `ab919d606c`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6514704152. Earlier build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6160109618.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current head `138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7` (includes this morning's master merge). Historical ZeroCode tests were on `2cd669c27`; historical runtime tests and the live X11 run linked above were on `d01ad8eb1ad9` / `2830dc912` (ZeroCode Chat pane over local RPC, `zeroclaw daemon`)—those captures remain labelled historical, not exact-head proof of this SHA. Older local runs on `225c52bb636f` (master `f12da7462a0f`, remote macOS arm64 builder). Earlier live run: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the captures, trace lines (`trace-child-refusal.jsonl`, `trace-grant.jsonl`), stub request log and config excerpt are all in the manifest folder linked above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (grants are memory-only; no new file is written)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one new key, `channels.telegram.<alias>.cost_override_operators` (numeric Telegram user IDs allowed to override in group chats; defaults to empty, which denies group overrides; no wildcards or usernames). Also one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`. Before merge, do not revert master merges. Current head is `138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7`. Earlier feature commits on this branch (for example `a8857fb9b1`…`d0297b2c4`, `2cd669c27`, `2830dc912`, `a4f77e75a7`) are historical; use the live head when naming rollback targets.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.allow_override = false` restores the hard stop without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** turns stuck waiting at the limit; grep the runtime trace for `cost limit overridden by the operator` and `cost limit override prompt failed`.

prs.title: test(ci): fail a stopped parallel runtime pass at a deadline
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a test in the parallel runtime gate stops making progress, nothing ends it until the job's 30-minute timeout cancels the whole job. #12350 records three such Telegram hangs on 2026-11-09 alone. Each ran into the 30-minute timeout and failed `CI Required Gate` with a cancellation instead of a test failure.
  - `scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` now compiles each crate's test binary first (`--no-run`) and then runs every pass under `timeout`. The deadline is `ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_PASS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 300 by default. A pass that misses it fails with exit status 124 and an error naming the crate and pass. The test harness's "has been running for over 60 seconds" line above it names the test that stopped.
  - Compilation sits outside the deadline because the first pass of each crate spends about three minutes compiling. In job 133741439431 (2026-11-17), the passes themselves took 41.6 s (`zeroclaw-runtime`) and 11.4 s (`zeroclaw-channels`), so 300 s leaves about seven times the normal pass time.
  - Where `timeout` isn't installed (stock macOS), the gate says so and runs without a deadline, as before.
- **Scope boundary:** It doesn't fix the hang in #12350 or the flaky test in #12351; it makes them cheaper and easier to read. No change to which tests run, how often, or with how many threads.
- **Trade-off:** a healthy pass that took longer than 5 minutes would now fail; today the slowest takes 42 s. A hang still fails the gate, only sooner and with the test named.
- **Blast radius:** `Parallel Runtime Test` in the Quality Gate, and anyone running the gate script locally.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12350, Related #12351

### What this does, simply

One CI job runs the runtime and channel test suites three times each, all tests at once, to catch tests that interfere with each other. When one of those tests got stuck, the job waited out its full 30 minutes and was cancelled, and the log didn't say clearly which test was to blame. Now each repetition gets five minutes, which is several times what a healthy one needs. A stuck repetition fails after that with a message saying which one it was.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the script's test now covers a stopped pass, and this PR's own CI runs the gate on real passes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** this PR changes the gate script, which selects `Parallel Runtime Test` with scope `all`. The job runs all six real passes under the deadline. The Quality Gate also runs `parallel_runtime_test_scope.test.sh`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for the gate. A real hang can't be produced on demand; the test uses a stand-in `cargo` that sleeps.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run on `dfe8ab35bd` with this patch applied:

```text
$ shellcheck scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_scope.test.sh
(no output)
$ bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_scope.test.sh
parallel runtime test scope tests: pass
```

  The new cases: a zero deadline exits 2 before Cargo runs, and a pass that sleeps past a 1-second deadline exits 124 with `zeroclaw-channels run 1/2 did not finish within 1s`, without starting run 2.

  Revert check: with the old gate script and the new test, the test fails at its first assertion (`FAIL: unexpected Cargo calls for channels scope`).

  Without `timeout`, under `/bin/bash` 3.2 with a stand-in `cargo`:

```text
timeout is not installed; passes run without a deadline.
==> parallel runtime regression: zeroclaw-channels run 1/1 (16 threads, no deadline)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Pass times in a recent successful job (above), to choose the default deadline.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full gate wasn't run locally; this PR's CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: an optional environment variable for the gate script, `ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_PASS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, documented in `docs/book/src/contributing/testing.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none needed; the default applies when the variable is unset.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: perf(ci): fetch only the history each Quality Gate job reads
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Six Quality Gate jobs cloned the repository's full history. When a clone ran slow, the 5-minute jobs among them were cancelled inside `actions/checkout`, and a cancelled job fails `CI Required Gate`. In run data for 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-17, 54 jobs in 20 runs were cancelled 303 to 305 seconds after starting, inside `actions/checkout`, all on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. One example is run 42142914074, a push to `master` on 2026-11-06, where `Detect crates.io version bump` was cancelled after 5m04s.
  - #12219 made five change detectors shallow. This does the same for the six jobs that still take full history. Each now fetches only the history it reads:
    - **`history-guard`:** the full commit graph as a treeless clone (`filter: tree:0`). `git merge-base` needs commits only.
    - **`docs-style`:** a blobless clone (`filter: blob:none`). The docs gates need `git merge-base` and a diff, and fetch only the blobs they read.
    - **`check-plugin-backends` and `crates-preflight-changes`:** depth 2, which keeps both parents of the test merge commit, plus a depth-1 fetch of the one base commit they compare against.
    - **`lint`:** the default shallow checkout. Nothing in the job reads history.
    - **`zerocode-rpc-boundary`:** no history. Its gate parses one manifest in well under a second, so it now runs on every event instead of fetching history to decide whether to run.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to what any gate checks, and no change to job timeouts. On `pull_request`, `merge_group` and `push`, each detector selects the same work as before, except that the Zerocode gate now always runs.
- **Trade-off:** the merge-queue paths of `crates-preflight-changes` and `check-plugin-backends` first run for real once a pull request is queued. A mistake there would turn the queue red until reverted; both fail closed rather than skip. A git command added to these jobs later that walks a lot of history would also run slower in a partial clone.
- **Blast radius:** Required Quality Gate jobs: Common Ancestor, Lint, the plugin backend checks, Docs Style, Zerocode RPC Boundary, and Detect crates.io version bump.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12218, Related #12219

### What this does, simply

Several required CI jobs downloaded the project's entire history before doing a few seconds of work, and a job with a 5-minute limit was cancelled whenever that download ran slow. A cancelled job turns the required gate red, which blocks the pull request or ejects it from the merge queue for reasons unrelated to the change. Each job now downloads only what it uses: the commit list, or the two or three commits it compares. The checks themselves are unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this PR changes `ci.yml`, so its own Quality Gate run executes all six changed jobs on the `pull_request` path.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** this PR's Quality Gate run. A `ci.yml` change selects the docs and plugin-backend job families, so all six jobs run with the new checkouts.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the `merge_group` and `push` paths of `crates-preflight-changes` and `check-plugin-backends` run only in the queue and after merge. Both were reproduced locally against real refs; see below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run on `dfe8ab35bd` with this patch applied:

```text
$ actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml
(no output)
$ bash scripts/ci/common_ancestor_guard.test.sh
common ancestor guard tests passed
$ bash scripts/ci/crates_preflight_trigger.test.sh
crates_preflight_trigger: ok
$ bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh
plugin backend change filter tests: pass
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh .github/workflows scripts/ci docs/book/src/maintainers
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

  Each new fetch shape, reproduced from a workstation against an open PR's test merge ref (`refs/pull/12323/merge`, base `6e83982340`):

```text
depth 2 + base fetch:   HEAD parents present; crates_preflight_trigger.sh pull_request -> run=false;
                        merge_group (base = master~3) -> run=false; push (no base) -> run=false;
                        plugin_backend_change_filter.sh on the diff -> run=true
treeless, full depth:   common_ancestor_guard.sh origin/master <head> -> "Common ancestor with origin/master: 6e83982340..."
blobless, full depth:   git merge-base origin/master HEAD -> 69ea0ae1ae; content diff against it succeeds
clone of master alone:  full 135 s / 194 MB; blobless 2 s / 11 MB; treeless 1 s / 5.3 MB
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** For each job, which git commands its steps and scripts run, and that the new checkout satisfies them. Not verified: the `tests/architecture` suite was not run locally. CI's Test job runs it, and its one assertion on these jobs (the `crates-preflight-changes` block in `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`) matches by substring and still holds.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo test --test architecture` (see above).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The added fetches go to the same remote `actions/checkout` already uses.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` restores the full-history checkouts.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a red `Detect crates.io version bump` or plugin `Check` job in the merge queue, or `Common Ancestor` / `Docs Style` failing at a git step.

prs.title: ci(release): retry the Discord announcement and website redeploy
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Discord answered the release announcement with HTTP 504 in two of the last three releases (`Discord webhook failed (HTTP 504)` in both job logs). Both times, the step failed after the release was already public: v0.8.6 in run 39095722409, re-sent by hand in 39103789968, and v0.9.0 in run 43098585102, re-sent in 43152248599. The Discord job runs after `publish`, so each failure also marked a successful release run `failure`.
  - The webhook call now uses curl's own retry: `--retry 4 --retry-max-time 120`. That retries 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 and honours `Retry-After`; anything else, a bad webhook URL among them, still fails at once. `-s` becomes `--no-progress-meter`, so each retry leaves a line in the log.
  - The website redeploy dispatch gets the same treatment (`--retry 3 --retry-max-time 60`). Dispatching it twice only rebuilds the site twice.
  - A failure after the retries still fails the run. If the announcement didn't go out, the run should say so.
- **Scope boundary:** The tweet job, which already checks for a duplicate before posting, and the message itself are unchanged.
- **Trade-off:** if Discord posts the message and still answers 5xx, the retry posts it twice. That is already true of a manual re-send.
- **Blast radius:** `discord-release.yml`, whether called by `Release Stable` or dispatched by hand, and the `redeploy-website` job.
- **Linked issue(s):** None

### What this does, simply

After a release is published, CI posts the announcement to Discord and asks the website to rebuild. Twice now, Discord's servers had a moment of trouble, the post failed, someone had to send it by hand, and the release run showed red although the release was fine. Both calls now try again a few times first.

**One trade-off:** a 5xx can arrive after Discord has actually posted the message, so a retry can post it twice. That was already true of the manual re-send, and a duplicate is cheaper than a release nobody heard about.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the post runs only at release time. A manual dispatch with `dry_run` composes the message without calling the webhook.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** none run the webhook call; see below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The webhook path runs only in a release or a manual non-dry-run dispatch.
- **Commands run and tail output:** the same curl flags, against a local stand-in webhook that answers from a fixed list of status codes:

```text
answers 504, 504, 204         -> final HTTP 204 after 3 s; 3 requests
answers 429 (Retry-After 2), 204 -> final HTTP 204 after 2 s; 2 requests
answers 401                   -> final HTTP 401 after 0 s; 1 request
with --no-progress-meter:     "Warning: Problem : HTTP error. Will retry in 1 seconds. 4 retries left."
$ actionlint .github/workflows/discord-release.yml
(no output)
```

  (curl 8.7.1; `--retry` honours `Retry-After` since 7.66 and `--no-progress-meter` exists since 7.67.)

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The failed step and HTTP status in the two release runs above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live webhook call, to avoid posting to the release channel.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The same calls, repeated on a transient failure.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the squash commit. Workflow-only, no state to unwind.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `Warning: Problem : HTTP error. Will retry in …` lines in the Discord Announcement job log, a duplicate release post in Discord after an ambiguous 5xx, or a website dispatch that retried (`curl: (22)` lines in the Trigger Website Redeploy log).

prs.title: ci(release): retry Apple notarization and stapling of the macOS installer
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The v0.9.0 release run (43098585102) lost its first attempt in the last minute of `Build Desktop App (macOS Universal)`. Notarization of the `.dmg` came back `Accepted`; `xcrun stapler staple` then failed with `NSURLErrorDomain Code=-1005 "The network connection was lost."` and exit 68. That was after 2h57m of building, and re-running the failed jobs took another 1h21m.
  - The notarize-and-staple step now retries both Apple calls: `notarytool submit --wait` up to 3 times and `stapler staple` up to 5 times, waiting 30, 60, 90 and 120 seconds between attempts. Each retry leaves a warning on the run.
  - Both calls are safe to repeat. A resubmitted `.dmg` is simply notarized again, and stapling fetches the same ticket. A rejected notarization still fails the job: it leaves no ticket, so stapling fails on every attempt.
- **Scope boundary:** `stapler validate` and the order of prepare, notarize, staple, validate and upload are unchanged. Two things stay for follow-ups: moving notarization into its own job, so a failure there no longer forces a rebuild, and retrying the code-signing timestamp inside `cargo tauri build` (where the v0.8.7 run failed).
- **Trade-off:** a genuine rejection or bad credentials now fails several minutes later, because each retry waits for Apple again. This touches the release workflow, so it is best merged when no release run is in progress.
- **Blast radius:** The macOS desktop job of `Release Stable`, only when Apple credentials are set.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11839

### What this does, simply

Before a release goes out, the macOS installer is sent to Apple to be checked, and the approval is then attached to the file. Both steps talk to Apple's servers, and in v0.9.0 the connection dropped at the very last step, after almost three hours of building. Each step now tries again a few times before failing the job.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: notarization runs only in a release with Apple credentials.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `architecture` test `macos_desktop_release_notarizes_published_dmg` (`tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`) runs in the Test job. It pins this step's commands and their order.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The Apple calls themselves are not exercised before the next release.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run on `dfe8ab35bd` with this patch applied:

```text
$ actionlint .github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml
(four existing info notes, SC2016 and SC2094, in the publish job; the same four appear on master; none in this step)
```

  The contract test's required strings, checked by the same substring rules: all present, in order, with one `MACOS_DMG_PATH:` source.

  The retry function, run with stand-in commands:

```text
::warning::Stapling failed (attempt 1/5); retrying in 0s.
::warning::Stapling failed (attempt 2/5); retrying in 0s.
succeeded on call 3
::warning::Notarization failed (attempt 1/3); retrying in 0s.
::warning::Notarization failed (attempt 2/3); retrying in 0s.
::error::Notarization failed after 3 attempts.
gave up with status 1
```

  (The delays were set to 0 for this run; the workflow waits 30, 60, 90 and 120 seconds.)

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The failure in the v0.9.0 job log: notarization `Accepted`, then the staple error above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo test --test architecture` was not run locally; CI's Test job runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The same Apple calls, repeated on failure.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The credentials are passed exactly as before.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No release run should be in progress when it merges or reverts.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The step still runs only when `APPLE_ID` is set.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `::warning::Notarization failed (attempt n/3)` / `::warning::Stapling failed (attempt n/5)` annotations on a Release Stable run, then `::error::<label> failed after N attempts.` and a failed `Notarize and staple the .dmg` step.

prs.title: ci(workflows): retry tool downloads instead of failing the job
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - CI downloads `cargo-nextest`, `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` with a single `curl` piped into `tar`, so one 5xx or dropped connection fails the job before any code runs. On 2026-11-09, merge-queue run 42569447258 (the entry for #12100) failed seven test jobs at `Install cargo-nextest`, and the next queue run, 42571610051, lost `Test (channel Matrix)` at the same step 23 minutes later.
  - Each of the nine downloads now goes to a file with `curl --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 --retry-all-errors` and is extracted afterwards. Extracting from a file is what makes the retry safe: a retried transfer restarts the file, whereas a pipe would have fed `tar` half an archive.
  - Covered: the six Linux `cargo-nextest` installs and the `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` installs in `ci.yml`; `cargo-audit` in `daily-audit.yml`; the macOS and Windows `cargo-nextest` installs in `platform-tests.yml`. Git Bash's `tar` reads `D:\...` as a remote host, so the Windows leg converts the path with `cygpath`, as `windows-tests.yml` already does.
- **Scope boundary:** No version changes. `cargo-nextest` still comes from `get.nexte.st/latest`, and `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` keep their pinned releases. The advisory Windows job's pinned, checksummed download is untouched.
- **Trade-off:** a download that is really broken, such as a moved URL, now takes about 15 seconds longer to fail.
- **Blast radius:** The install steps of the required test jobs and `Security`, the scheduled platform tests, and the daily advisory scan.
- **Linked issue(s):** None

### What this does, simply

Several CI jobs download a testing or auditing tool at the start. prs.title: fix(runtime): honor cost.enforcement.mode when a budget limit is exceeded
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The budget gate (`enforce_tool_loop_budget`) never read `[cost.enforcement] mode`. Every exceeded daily or monthly limit ended the turn, whatever the mode said, so `warn` behaved like `block` and `route_down` never substituted a model.
  - The gate now reads the mode from the scoped tracker's live cost config, the same place the limits come from. `block` stops the turn. `warn` records a warn-level event and lets the call through.
  - The default is now `block`, which is what every install has actually had. An install that never set the mode sees no change, and `warn` becomes an opt-in that works. The config schema used to say `warn` was the default, but the gate never read the mode, so that default never took effect.
  - `route_down` has no model substitution in the turn loop yet. It stops the turn as `block` does and logs that it fell back to `block`. Unrecognized values do the same, so a typo can never loosen the control.
  - The mode covers the shared `daily_limit_usd` and `monthly_limit_usd` limits only. A delegated agent's per-hop ceiling (`max_cost_per_day_cents`) still stops that agent's own calls in every mode. `check_budget` returns at the first exceeded limit it finds, before it reads those ceilings, so the tracker gains `check_ceilings()`, which the gate asks before `warn` lets an exceeded shared limit through.
- **Scope boundary:** No model substitution for `route_down` (#12626). No session notice for a call that `warn` lets through past the limit (#12628). No change to the gap where a sub-agent started with `spawn_subagent` inside a bounded delegation runs on the process-wide tracker, outside the delegate's ceiling (#12627). No change to `allow_override`, config-reload plumbing, `warn_at_percent` notices, or how spend is priced and recorded. No new config keys. `check_budget` keeps its signature and results; its per-agent loop moves into a helper that `check_ceilings` shares.
- **Blast radius:** Every turn that runs in a cost-tracking scope: CLI `agent`, gateway chat and webhook turns, channel turns, cron, delegated sub-loops, and the one-shot `run_model_query` seam (skill reflection, graceful summary). Behavior changes only where an operator sets `mode = "warn"`. Those turns no longer stop at the shared daily or monthly limit.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12477. Model substitution for `route_down`, which #12477 also lists, is tracked in #12626. Depends on #12629, which records the holding-crate exception for the runtime budget gate. Related #12512, #11585 and #11589.
  - #12512 removes the default dollar limits. With `block` as the default here, a limit an operator sets under #12512 stops spend as its body says. The two PRs conflict only in `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md` and `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`. Whichever lands second keeps the other's paragraphs, and the two `f64` limit literals in this PR's `check_ceilings` test become `Some(1.0)`.
  - #11589 adds an approval-based override of an exceeded limit. It shares no lines with this change, and `git merge-tree` combines the two without conflicts. If both land, its override prompt should be offered only in `block` mode, because `warn` already lets the call through.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop spending when a daily or monthly cost limit is reached. `[cost.enforcement] mode` is meant to choose what happens then: `block` refuses further calls, `warn` logs it and carries on, and `route_down` switches to a cheaper model. The setting was parsed but never used, so every limit acted like `block`.

With this change the setting works. `block` is the default, so nothing changes unless you choose otherwise. If you would rather keep working past the limit and watch the log, set `mode = "warn"`. `route_down` still refuses, because the model swap it describes isn't built yet, and it now says so in the log. Per-agent spending ceilings on delegated agents keep stopping those agents' own calls whatever the mode is.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. `warn` changes from stopping to continuing, and an A/B run against a loopback mock shows it in a minute.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `cli` (`zeroclaw agent`). The `web` surface (gateway webhook SSE) is covered by a test, not by a manual step.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A loopback OpenAI-compatible mock that answers every chat request with `usage.prompt_tokens = 10000`, a throwaway config dir, and this config:

  ```toml
  schema_version = 4
  [providers.models.openai.mock]
  model = "mock-model"
  uri = "http://127.0.0.1:18765/v1"
  api_key = "dummy"
  [agents.repro]
  enabled = true
  model_provider = "openai.mock"
  risk_profile = "default"
  runtime_profile = "default"
  [risk_profiles.default]
  [runtime_profiles.default]
  [cost]
  daily_limit_usd = 0.01
  [cost.enforcement]
  mode = "warn"        # then "block", then "route_down", then remove the section
  [cost.rates.providers.models.openai."mock-model"]
  input_per_mtok = 100.0
  output_per_mtok = 100.0
  cached_input_per_mtok = 100.0
  ```

- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level warn --config-dir ./cfg agent -a repro -m "hi"` twice for each mode, starting from a fresh config dir each time.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `warn`: turn 2 prints `ok` and exits 0, the mock sees 2 POSTs, and stderr shows a WARN `note` record with `{"current_usd":1.0005,"enforcement_mode":"warn","limit_usd":0.01,"period":"Day"}` and `cost limit exceeded; the call proceeds because cost.enforcement.mode is warn`. `block`, and no `[cost.enforcement]` section at all: turn 2 exits 1 with the same `Budget exceeded` error as before, 1 POST, and the `reject` record now carries `"enforcement_mode":"block"`. `route_down`: the same refusal and 1 POST, plus a WARN `note` with `"enforced_as":"block","enforcement_mode":"route_down"`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** In every mode, turn 1 prints `ok` and records $1.0005. Turn 2 exits 1 with `Error: Budget exceeded: $1.0005 of $0.01 Day limit. Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.` and the mock sees one POST in total. The v0.9.0 release binary behaves the same.

### How I tested

Ran on Linux x86_64 with rustc 1.98.0, on `master` dfe8ab35bd plus this branch's changes. The tested tree is 17c820fe0d, the tree of 2394d3072a.

Tests at the behavior boundary:

- `agent::turn::provider_call::tests`: the budget gate in a cost scope.
  - With no mode set, `the_default_mode_is_block_and_stops_an_exceeded_shared_limit` checks that the default stops the turn and records `enforcement_mode: "block"`. `block` set explicitly stops it too.
  - `warn` lets an exceeded shared limit through and records it.
  - `route_down` and an unrecognized value (`"Warn"`) stop it and record the fallback.
  - The mode is read live (warn → block → warn on one tracker).
  - Under `warn`, a delegated agent is still stopped by its own ceiling and by the shared-capped ceiling, and goes ahead when those ceilings hold. Under `block`, the shared limit stops it whatever its ceiling.
- `agent::loop_::tests::warn_mode_turn_past_the_daily_limit_still_reaches_the_provider`: a full `run_tool_call_loop` turn past the limit under `warn` returns the provider's answer. `budget_rejection_emits_no_waiting_on_model_lifecycle` runs the same turn on the default and still stops.
- `tests::webhook_sse_production_warn_mode_past_the_budget_reaches_provider` (gateway): a webhook SSE turn past the limit under `warn` reaches the provider and ends with `done`. The existing budget-exhaustion test runs unchanged on the default.
- `cost::tracker::tests::check_ceilings_reads_only_the_ceilings_behind_an_exceeded_shared_limit`: the new tracker method across shared, per-agent, ancestor-chain, shared-capped and disabled scopes.

The existing tests that rely on an exceeded limit stopping the turn are unchanged from `master`. Red first: with this branch's tests and the default put back to `warn`, 13 tests fail. They are the two schema default tests, the new default gate test, and the ten existing tests that pin the stop (in `loop_.rs`, `max_iter.rs`, `skills/creator.rs`, `tools/delegate.rs`, `tools/send_message_to_peer.rs` and the gateway):

```text
test schema::tests::cost_enforcement_config_defaults ... FAILED      left: "warn"  right: "block"
test agent::turn::provider_call::tests::the_default_mode_is_block_and_stops_an_exceeded_shared_limit ... FAILED
  the exceeded limit must stop the turn: ()
test agent::loop_::tests::budget_rejection_emits_no_waiting_on_model_lifecycle ... FAILED
  should fail with budget exceeded: "the provider answered"
test tools::delegate::tests::sync_delegate_shared_daily_limit_still_binds ... FAILED
  the shared global daily limit must still bind: ToolResult { success: true, ... "delegate cost flow done" ...
test tests::webhook_sse_production_budget_exhaustion_skips_provider_request ... FAILED
  an exhausted budget must reject before the provider request  left: 1 right: 0
zeroclaw-config 54 passed, 2 failed; zeroclaw-runtime 323 passed, 10 failed; zeroclaw-gateway 1 passed, 1 failed
```

Green, on this branch:

```text
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -E 'test(/^schema::tests::cost_/) | test(/^cost::tracker::tests::/)'
     Summary 56 tests run: 56 passed, 1941 skipped
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E '<the gate, loop, max_iter, creator, delegate and send_message_to_peer budget tests>'
     Summary 333 tests run: 333 passed, 5922 skipped
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  # exit 0
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 12s
$ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-deps
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 13s
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config
     Summary [  11.767s] 2128 tests run: 2128 passed, 0 skipped
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
     Summary [ 165.771s] 943 tests run: 943 passed (1 slow), 8 skipped
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime
     Summary [  97.250s] 6301 tests run: 6301 passed (1 slow), 10 skipped
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --doc   # ok, 0 doc-tests
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 12s
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     # Checked 1 local docs link target(s). No added HTTP(S) links detected
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed files>   # Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Required Gate (Lint, fmt, tests) once it runs on this head; it covers the same three crates. Everything above is from local runs made before CI.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known. The changed code is on every platform's common path. The binary A/B run under "How you can test" adds what unit tests can't show: CLI exit codes and the log records an operator sees.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The A/B binary run under "How you can test", in all four cases (`warn`, `block`, `route_down`, no `[cost.enforcement]` section), on the v0.9.0 release binary (before) and a debug build of this branch (after). Before, every case refused turn 2 with one POST. After, `warn` answered turn 2 (exit 0, 2 POSTs, the `note` record above), and `block`, the unset case and `route_down` refused as before, with the reject record carrying `"enforcement_mode":"block"` for the first two and `"route_down"` plus the fallback `note` for the third. It ran in an isolated network namespace with a loopback mock, a throwaway HOME and a throwaway config dir. I also merged this branch with #12512 locally (89a73c994b) to check how the two fit. With the two docs files resolved, the only compile errors were the two `f64` limit literals in `check_ceilings_reads_only_the_ceilings_behind_an_exceeded_shared_limit`. With those set to `Some(1.0)`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passed, and so did the cost, tracker and policy tests in `zeroclaw-config` (355), the runtime budget tests (334) and the gateway SSE tests (5). Not verified: real paid providers; channels other than the CLI and the gateway webhook (Telegram, Discord, cron and ACP run the same gate); Windows and macOS; the dashboard UI.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output` (stderr records and stdout of `zeroclaw agent`, quoted above).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree 17c820fe0d, `cli` surface, `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level warn --config-dir <dir> agent -a repro -m hi`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the turn-2 lines quoted under "Expected on this branch".
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** the second turn past a $0.01 daily limit. `warn` answers; `block`, no mode set, and `route_down` refuse.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--all-features` clippy run; clippy ran with default features on the three touched crates. `zeroclaw-desktop` was excluded from the workspace check (it needs desktop toolchains).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: None are `Yes`. One cost-control note: the default stays `block`, so a set limit still stops spend unless the operator opts into `warn`. Per-agent ceilings still stop delegated agents' own calls in every mode, and `route_down` and unrecognized values fail closed to `block`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With no mode set, `block` or `route_down`, an exceeded limit stops the turn as it does on `master`. A config that sets `mode = "warn"` now gets what `warn` documents: the call goes ahead past the shared limit, with a warn-level `cost limit exceeded` record.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The existing `[cost.enforcement] mode` now takes effect, and its default is `block` (the schema said `warn`, which was never applied).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None needed to keep today's behavior. To opt into `warn`, check that `config.toml` has:

  ```toml
  [cost.enforcement]
  mode = "warn"
  ```

  Earlier releases dropped `mode = "warn"` from `config.toml` on save, because it equaled the old default. So a key you wrote may no longer be there.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Without a new build, an operator can undo `warn` by removing the key or setting `[cost.enforcement] mode = "block"`, which applies at the next check, with the same reload rules as the limits.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[cost.enforcement] mode` (`block`, the default, or `warn`).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** In `warn` mode, WARN records `cost limit exceeded; the call proceeds because cost.enforcement.mode is warn` with `current_usd`, `limit_usd` and `period`. A refusal is still the WARN `tool-call loop budget exceeded` record, which now carries `enforcement_mode`. A `route_down` or unrecognized mode adds the WARN `... so the exceeded limit is enforced as block`. A failed ceiling check logs `cost ceiling check failed; ...` and refuses.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** This adds one row to the holding-crate exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, so that #12500 can merge under ADR-016. #12500 makes the runtime budget gate honor the documented `[cost.enforcement] mode` when a shared daily or monthly limit is exceeded. `block`, the default, stops the turn as today. `warn` lets the call through with a log record unless a per-agent or per-hop ceiling binds. `route_down` and unrecognized values stop the turn and log the fallback. The two existing cost rows (#11589, #11692) were recorded for honoring keys that were already documented, and this is the same kind of change.
- **Scope boundary:** The row covers `src/agent/cost.rs` and `src/agent/turn/provider_call.rs`, with focused tests there and in `src/agent/loop_.rs`. The limits, the ceilings and their arithmetic stay with `CostTracker` in `zeroclaw-config`. This PR contains no feature code and does not approve itself.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime contribution policy for this one feature.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12500 and #12477.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is being split into smaller crates, so new behavior there needs a recorded exception. #12500 changes what the existing budget gate does once a cost limit is exceeded: it now follows the configured mode instead of always stopping. prs.title: fix(config): refuse a decimal setting that is not a finite number
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `str::parse::<f64>` reads `inf`, `Infinity`, `NaN` and out-of-range text such as `1e999` (as infinity), and every path that sets a config property from text stored the result: `zeroclaw config set memory.vector_weight inf` writes `vector_weight = inf`. A limit stored as infinity compares above every value, and `NaN` compares false with everything. `parse_prop_value` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/helpers.rs`), which `set_prop` uses for `zeroclaw config set`, RPC `config/set`, environment overrides and the gateway `PATCH`, and `coerce_for_set_prop` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/typed_value.rs`), which `PATCH` and `zeroclaw config patch` use for a JSON string, now refuse them with the same error as text that is not a number.
  - `channels.voice_wake.<alias>.energy_threshold` is the one `f32` setting. `1e39` is finite as an `f64` and became infinity when the section was deserialized. `serde_set_prop` now refuses a float whose stored value would not be finite and keeps the value already set; the config API reports it as `value_type_mismatch`, like other text that is not a usable number.
  - ZeroCode's config editor (`apps/zerocode/src/config_manager.rs`) applies the `f64` rule before it sends an edit.
- **Scope boundary:** Loading `config.toml` is unchanged: a hand-written `inf` still loads. The dashboard's form code is unchanged. JSON numbers cannot be non-finite, so as JSON numbers these values only reach the new `f32` check.
- **Blast radius:** every text path that sets a float property (`zeroclaw config set`, `zeroclaw config patch`, `PATCH /api/config`, RPC `config/set`, environment overrides, quickstart field writes) and ZeroCode's scalar validation. A `ZEROCLAW_…` environment override set to one of these values now stops the config from loading with `Invalid float value`, as a non-number override already did (checked: `ZEROCLAW_memory__vector_weight=inf` exits 1 on this branch and loads `inf` on `master`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12559.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's decimal settings, such as spending limits, accepted `inf`, `NaN` and absurdly large numbers. A limit set to infinity never stops anything, and nothing warned you. These values are now refused with the same "invalid float value" error as a typo, and the setting keeps its previous value.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** an empty config directory in `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR`.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive -- memory.vector_weight inf`, then `grep '^vector_weight' "$ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml"`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the command exits 1 with `Error: Invalid float value 'inf'`, and `config.toml` holds no `inf`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the command exits 0 and the file holds `vector_weight = inf` (`NaN` gives `nan`, `1e999` gives `inf`).

### How I tested

All jobs ran on a Linux x86_64 build host; test jobs ran in a private network and mount namespace with a throwaway `HOME`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test, clippy and fmt jobs cover the code; no docs page changed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `375ebd68f7`)

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    # pass
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings   # pass
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zerocode
       Summary 4770 tests run: 4770 passed (1 leaky), 10 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime
       Summary 6255 tests run: 6255 passed, 10 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --lib --bins --test component --test integration --test architecture
       Summary 1350 tests run: 1349 passed, 1 failed
  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh, docs_links_gate.sh, comment_hygiene_gate.sh   # pass
  cargo fluent check; cargo generate openrpc --check                            # pass
  ```

  The one failure is `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` ("expect must be installed for the PTY regression test"); `expect` is not installed on the build host and the test fails the same way on `master`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - On a build of `master` `69ea0ae1ae` (the parsing code is unchanged on `cda933e6b9`), `zeroclaw config set` of `inf`, `NaN` and `1e999` exits 0 and writes `inf`, `nan` and `inf`.
  - New tests cover each path with `inf`, `+inf`, `-inf`, `Infinity`, `infinity`, `NaN`, `nan`, `1e999` and `-1e999`, on a plain float (`memory.vector_weight`) and an optional one (`runtime.docker.cpu_limit`), and check the stored value is unchanged in memory and on disk: `set_prop` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`), the gateway `PATCH` including atomicity and the error code (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs`), RPC `config/set` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`), and the real binary's `config set` and `config patch` (`tests/component/config_patch_cli.rs`). Finite edge values (`-0.0`, `5e-324`, `f64::MAX`, `5`) still store bit-exact. The `f32` case is covered through `set_prop` and the gateway, as a JSON string and a JSON number.
  - Each guard was disabled on its own and a covering test failed on an assertion: the finite check in `parse_prop_value`, the one in `coerce_for_set_prop`, the overflow check in `serde_set_prop`, and ZeroCode's. With the first disabled, the `set_prop` tests still pass because the overflow check also catches non-finite values; the unit test on `parse_prop_value` fails.
  - The new tests ran five times in a row and passed every time.
  - Not verified: ZeroCode in a real terminal (its change is covered by a unit test on the validation).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `375ebd68f7`, `zeroclaw config set`, `tests/component/config_patch_cli.rs`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

  ```text

  Error: Invalid float value 'inf'
  ```

prs.title: feat(memory)!: retire the local LLM response cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The local LLM response cache almost never served a reply, so it is removed. A hit needed all of these: temperature exactly `0.0`; an agent with no tools; no hooks, memory injection, native-thinking override or images; and a single provider with no fallbacks. Every `Agent` turn also stamps the user message with the time to the second (`[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]`) before the key is computed, so even a qualifying turn hit only when the same conversation arrived within the same second. Channel turns run through `run_tool_call_loop`, which never read the cache.
  - The code that existed only to guard it goes too:
    - `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity` and its wrapper implementations;
    - the provider context-truncation flag (`take_last_provider_context_truncation`), whose only reader was the cache write guard;
    - `ObserverEvent::CacheHit` and `CacheMiss`, plus the three Prometheus counters fed by them.
  - The four `memory.response_cache_*` keys are retired through `RETIRED_KEYS` with a shared reason in every CLI locale. A config that still has them loads with a `Removed` notice and the next save drops them, instead of the keys being silently ignored.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Provider prompt caching does not change: Anthropic `cache_control` and `cache_ttl`, compatible-provider `cache_passthrough`, Bedrock `cachePoint`, OpenRouter markers.
  - `VisionOverrideProvider::factory_leaf` still wraps every factory-built provider. With the identity mark gone, that wrapper is a pass-through when no `vision` override is set. Going back to wrapping only when `vision` is set is left for a follow-up.
  - Existing `response_cache.db` files are not deleted. `V2_MEMORY_DATA_NAMES` still lists the file so the V2 → V3 directory migration keeps moving it.
- **Blast radius:**
  - **Agent turn paths:** both `Agent::turn` and `turn_streamed` lose a branch that ran a skip check every turn and never fired in ordinary use.
  - **Config load and migration:** configs that set `[memory] response_cache_*`.
  - **Prometheus scrapes:** `zeroclaw_cache_hits_total`, `zeroclaw_cache_misses_total` and `zeroclaw_cache_tokens_saved_total` disappear.
  - **Rust API consumers:**
    - `AgentBuilder::response_cache`;
    - `zeroclaw_memory::{ResponseCache, create_response_cache}`;
    - `ModelProvider::has_stable_request_identity`;
    - `ObserverEvent::CacheHit` and `CacheMiss` (the enum is already `#[non_exhaustive]`);
    - `zeroclaw_providers::reliable::take_last_provider_context_truncation`.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Closes #12611.
  - Related #8321: its cache-policy question has no subject once this lands.
  - Related #12460: open; it adds tests for the module this deletes.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw could save a model's reply on disk and hand it back when exactly the same request came in again. In practice, almost nothing qualified. Ordinary agents have tools, the setting was off by default, and every message carries the current time to the second, so two requests matched only if they arrived within the same second.

The feature still cost something. It added a check to every turn, kept a file of prompts and replies on disk, and needed several pieces of supporting code in the provider layer. It also had its own share of bug fixes.

This PR removes the feature and its supporting code. If your config still sets the old keys, ZeroClaw tells you they were removed and carries on. Provider-side prompt caching, which is where repeated prompts actually save money, is unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`, for the config retirement notice; the rest is a removal covered by tests.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a scratch config directory with a current (`schema_version = 4`) config whose `[memory]` table sets `response_cache_enabled = true`.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> config migrate`, then `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> config get memory.response_cache_enabled`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `migrate` prints `warning: dropped retired config key `memory.response_cache_enabled` …: the local LLM response cache was removed; provider prompt caching still applies` and removes the key from the file; `config get` reports `Unknown property`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the keys are ordinary schema fields, so `migrate` keeps them and `config get` prints the stored value.

### How I tested

All Rust and docs gates ran on dev-box (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0), inside a throwaway `HOME` with a private network namespace for the test runs.

**At `446612a351` (this head):**

```text
cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                        -> clean
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
                                                          -> Finished, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib              -> test result: ok. 1998 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
```

**At `f5f2881f7a`:** the docs gates, plus the clippy command above, also clean. That commit differs from this head only by one test in `migration.rs`.

```text
DOCS_FILES=<the 2 changed pages> BASE_SHA=dfc70a2b49 scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. Linting: 2 file(s). Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  -> Collected 1 added link(s) from 2 docs file(s). Checked 1 local docs link target(s).
```

**At `5412d514ab`:** this head minus the two new `zeroclaw-config` tests (+43 lines, test-only).

```text
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets --no-default-features --features "$(xtask cli-only feature set)" -- -D warnings
                                                          -> Finished, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
  -> 142 test binaries: 20544 passed; 4 failed; 47 ignored
```

None of the four failures comes from this branch. Each was rerun alone, and the two that still failed were also run on `master` `dfc70a2b49`:

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The root crate declares most `src/` modules twice: in the library (`src/lib.rs`) and again in the `zeroclaw` binary (`src/main.rs`). Six of them have no user in either target. Each was a single `pub use` re-export of an owning crate, and three also carried copies of that crate's tests. This PR deletes them: `src/approval/`, `src/health/`, `src/heartbeat/`, `src/multimodal.rs`, `src/platform/` and the root `src/verifiable_intent/` shim.
  - Eight more modules are used only by the binary: `auth`, `commands`, `cost`, `daemon`, `doctor`, `peripherals` and `sop`, whose callers are in `src/main.rs`, and `security`, whose callers at this head are `src/main.rs`, `commands/self_test.rs` and `quickstart_plugins/mod.rs`, all compiled only by the binary. On `master`, `src/approval/mod.rs` also used `crate::security`; this PR deletes that copy. This PR removes their `src/lib.rs` declarations, so the library stops compiling them and stops running their tests a second time. The binary keeps its own `mod` for each, so the code and its tests stay.
  - The `#[cfg(test)]` blocks in `src/security/mod.rs` and `src/memory/traits.rs` copy tests that already run in `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-api`. Each deleted test is identical to the owning crate's test of the same name, or a strict subset of it, so no assertion is lost. The `src/memory/traits.rs` re-export lines stay. The root traits module also exports `async_trait`, which `zeroclaw_memory::traits` does not, so keeping it preserves `zeroclaw::memory::traits::async_trait`.
  - Routing and text that named the deleted paths are updated here so they don't go stale:
    - The `/src/{approval,health,platform,verifiable_intent}/**` lines are removed from `.github/CODEOWNERS`.
    - The `src/{health,heartbeat}/**` globs are removed from `.github/labeler.yml` and from the label table in `docs/book/src/maintainers/labels.md`. The `health` and `heartbeat` labels keep their `crates/zeroclaw-runtime` globs.
    - `NOTICE` now names `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/verifiable_intent/`.
    - The comment above `pub mod traits` in `src/memory/mod.rs` no longer refers to the removed `#[cfg(test)]` block. It now says the module keeps `zeroclaw::memory::traits` importable, including its `async_trait` re-export, so a later cleanup keeps that re-export.
- **Scope boundary:** Not touched:
  - the `trust`, `tunnel` and `routines` shims (a separate branch handles those);
  - the crate-side Verifiable Intent module in `zeroclaw-runtime` (#9328 owns it);
  - the `#[allow(unused_imports)]` lines in the seven modules the binary keeps (separate #12613 batch);
  - the `zeroclaw-acp-bridge` binary;
  - every routing entry for paths that still exist.
- **Blast radius:** No in-tree caller uses the removed library paths. The next 0.9.x patch removes six published Rust module paths: `zeroclaw::{auth, commands, peripherals, platform, sop, verifiable_intent}` (see Compatibility). The other eight removed library declarations were `pub(crate)`, so they were never public API. CLI, config and runtime behavior are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12613

### What this does, simply

The `zeroclaw` package builds a library and the `zeroclaw` program from the same `src/` folder. It also builds a small `zeroclaw-acp-bridge` helper, which this PR does not touch. Over time, many folders were registered with both the library and the program. Some do nothing in either: they only point at code that now lives in other crates, plus copies of those crates' tests. Others are used only by the program, but the library builds them as well, so their tests run twice.

This PR deletes the folders that do nothing, stops the library building what only the program uses, and removes the duplicate test copies. The program behaves the same as before. The 175 help pages visited in the default Linux build matched byte for byte, and every test that still covers this code runs once. The trade-off is on the Rust library side. Six module paths that the published `zeroclaw` crate exported are gone. Nothing in this repository or on crates.io uses them, but an unpublished downstream crate could stop compiling (see Compatibility).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the CLI, config and runtime are unchanged and the help-tree comparison below covers the help pages it visited. The library API change is covered by the repository and crates.io searches, not by a manual step.

### How I tested

Every Rust gate below ran on this head, `cd222ad046`, on Linux x86_64. The help comparison and the test inventory ran on the first revision, `3432c410aa`. Since then the PR has added only `NOTICE`, comment and routing edits, plus the removal of the library's `security` declaration, and the Rust gates were rerun after that removal.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Lint` (workspace clippy with `ci-all`), `Check (no default features)`, `Check (default features, all targets)` and `Test (CLI-only build)` compile the library and the `zeroclaw` binary on their feature sets. Compilation catches unresolved imports on the selected feature sets. The repository searches below cover uses of the removed public paths.
  - `Test` (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`) runs the binary's unit tests, which is where the `commands` and `sop` tests run now. The owning crates' tests for approval, health, heartbeat, security and memory traits run in those crates' suites.
  - Routing: the existing routing and docs gates passed, but no assertion in them targets the edited rules. The evidence for the routing edits is direct. The four owner rules matched only files deleted here: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> -- src/approval src/health src/platform src/verifiable_intent` lists four `mod.rs` files at `dfc70a2b49` and none at this head. The `health` and `heartbeat` labels keep their runtime globs.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `fuzz/` is not a workspace member and no CI job builds it. `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_command_validation.rs:3` imports `zeroclaw::security::SecurityPolicy`, which was already invalid on `master`: `security` has been `pub(crate)` in `src/lib.rs` since #985. This PR removes that private declaration from the library, which leaves the import exactly as broken as before. No other fuzz target names a removed module. Unpublished downstream crates are not covered by anything.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

Reproduce the "nothing uses it" evidence (run from the repo root on `master`):

```sh
# The six deleted modules have no path user anywhere in src/ (lib or bin), outside their own files:
for m in approval health heartbeat multimodal platform verifiable_intent; do
  rg -n "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_:])(crate::|super::|self::)?$m::|crate::$m\b|super::$m\b" src \
    --glob "!src/$m/**" --glob "!src/$m.rs"
done
# -> no output

# The library-only removals are used only from binary-only files
# (security: src/commands/self_test.rs and src/quickstart_plugins/mod.rs, both binary-only):
for m in auth commands cost daemon doctor peripherals security sop; do
  rg -n "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_:])(crate::|super::|self::)?$m::|crate::$m\b|super::$m\b" src \
    --glob "!src/$m/**" --glob "!src/$m.rs" | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u
done
# -> src/main.rs for each of the seven; for security at this head, src/main.rs, src/commands/self_test.rs and
#    src/quickstart_plugins/mod.rs (on master, src/approval/mod.rs:8 also matches; this PR deletes it)
```
